# Rigveda Samhita — Volume 16 (Kannada → English translation)

### Printed p. 2

*[The window begins in the middle of Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 7 (the earlier part is on p. 1, outside this window). The Sanskrit fragment below is copied from kn.md as supplied; the first word is cut at the start of the page.]*

पिजवनः पुनः स्पर्धनीयजवो वामिश्रीभावगतिर्वा ॥ स वित्तं गृहीत्वा विपाट् छुतुद्रोः संभेदमाययौ । अनुययुरितरे । स विश्वामित्रो नदीस्तुष्टाप-गाधा भवत-इति । आपि द्विवदपि बहुवत् तद्यद्द्वदुपरिष्टात्त- द्व्याख्यास्यामः ॥ (*pijavanaḥ punaḥ spardhanīyajavo vāmiśrībhāvagatirvā ‖ sa vittaṃ gṛhītvā vipāṭ chutudroḥ saṃbhedamāyayau | anuyayuritare | sa viśvāmitro nadīstuṣṭāpa-gādhā bhavata-iti | āpi dvivadapi bahuvat tadyaddvadupariṣṭātta- dvyākhyāsyāmaḥ ‖*) (printed సి. 2-24, the abbreviation in Telugu script as supplied)

Gist: the passage gives the story of Viśvāmitra, who takes the wealth, comes to the confluence of the Vipāś and the Śutudrī, and praises the rivers so that they become fordable; the other (Bharatas) follow him.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** Thus an old story is told. "Viśvāmitra" means that this seer is a friend to all, or that all are his friends; this is the etymological sense of the word. This seer was the priest ([sic] the supplied text reads पुरोतनागिद्दनु (*purotanāgiddanu*), evidently for *purohita*) of the king named Sudāsa, the son of Pijavana. Once, taking the wealth given by that king and setting out to go to his hermitage, he came to the confluence of the rivers Vipāś and Śutudrī (the present Beas and Sutlej of the Punjab). Thieves who wished to seize the wealth he carried were following him. Knowing this, Viśvāmitra tried by some means to cross these rivers that lay across his path, but they were very deep with the water of the flood and he could not. Then the seer prayed to the rivers and praised them, that they should reduce their water and make it convenient for him to pass; this is said in the 33rd sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33) and in verses 9-11 of Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53.

This seer Viśvāmitra in the sūkta above, that is, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-5, calls himself the son of Kuśika. In the Rāmāyaṇa, the Bhārata and other Purāṇas it is said that there was enmity and ill-will between Viśvāmitra and the seer Vasiṣṭha. There is some support for this in a few places in the Ṛgveda ([sic] the supplied text reads आधांवू (*ādhāṃvū*), evidently for आधारवू (*ādhāravū*), "support"). That will be discussed in the Pīṭhike (introduction) of this part.

The names of Viśvāmitra and of this seer's descendants are read in the mantras Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-21; 3-18-4; 3-53-13; 10-89-17; Atharvaveda 18-3-6; 18-4-54; Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa 3-15-1 and others. In the story of Śunaḥśepa the part of Viśvāmitra is very important; we have described it at length in Part 2 of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā. That Viśvāmitra is a principal seer is described in Aitareya (printed ऐतरेय वर्णक (*aitareya varṇaka*), "Aitareya varṇaka") 2-2-1; Ai. Brā. 6-18-1; 6-20-3; Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-1-2; 3-1-7-3; 5-2-3-4; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 16-19; 20-9; Maitrāyaṇīya Saṃhitā 2-7-19; Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 15-1; 26-14; 28-1,2; 29-3; Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 14-3-12; Bṛ. U. 2-2-4; Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa 3-3-13; 3-15-1 and other places.

In the Purāṇas and the like Viśvāmitra is said to have been a king who became a Brāhmaṇa by austerity. In the Ṛgveda there is no support at all for this. But in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-24) it is said that Viśvāmitra was the son of a king named Kauśika; and in the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa also (Paṃ. Vi. Brā. 21-12-2) Viśvāmitra is said to have been a king. In the Ṛgveda alone there is no support for this.

## Sūkta 7 (Maṇḍala 3)

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta** (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोमस्येत्यनवाके द्वादश सूक्तानि । तत्र प्र य आरुरित्येकादशर्चं स-
> प्तमं सूक्तं , मंडलद्रष्टा विश्वामित्र ऋषिः ' अनुक्तत्वात् त्रिष्टुप्छंदः । मं-
> डलादिपरिभाषयाग्निर्देवता ! प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोः सूक्तत्रयस्य प्रत्यग्निरुषस-
> स्त्रीणीति विनियोग उक्तः । तदेकं तृतीयं सूक्तं ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** In the third maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, in the first anuvāka, beginning with सोमस्य (*somasya*), there are twelve sūktas. Among them the sūkta beginning प्र य आरुः (*pra ya āruḥ*) is the seventh; it has eleven ṛks (as printed here; the head-lines below give 20). As Viśvāmitra is the seer of this whole third maṇḍala, he is the seer of this sūkta also. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The deity is Agni. As it has been said before that the three sūktas beginning प्रत्यग्निरुषसः (*pratyagniruṣasaḥ*) (the 5th, 6th and 7th sūktas) are applied to the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka mantras and the Āśvina śastra mantras, and as this is the third of those three sūktas, the same application given above holds for this sūkta also.

Sūkta—7. Maṇḍala—3. Anuvāka—1. Sūkta—7. Aṣṭaka—3. Adhyāya—1. Varga—1, 2. Number of ṛks in the sūkta—20. Ṛṣi—Viśvāmitra. Devatā—Agni. Chandas—Triṣṭubh.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र य आ॒रुः शि॑तपृ॒ष्ठस्य॑ धा॒सेरा मा॒तरा॑ विविशुः स॒प्त वाणीः॑ ।  
> प॒रि॒क्षिता॑ पि॒तरा॒ सं च॑रेते॒ प्र स॑स्र्राते दी॒र्घमायुः॑ प्र॒यक्षे॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । ये । आरुः । शित्तिपृष्ठस्य । धासेः । आ । मातरा । विवितुः । सप्त । वाणीः ।  
> परिक्षिता । हितरा । सं । चरेते इति । प्र । सर्स्राते इति । दीर्घं । आयुः ।  
> प्रयक्षे ॥ १ ॥

> *pra | ye | āruḥ | śittipṛṣṭhasya | dhāseḥ | ā | mātarā | vivituḥ | sapta | vāṇīḥ |*  
> *parikṣitā | hitarā | saṃ | carete iti | pra | sarsrāte iti | dīrghaṃ | āyuḥ |*  
> *prayakṣe ‖ 1 ‖*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni's rays have entered heaven and earth and the flowing rivers; heaven and earth, surrounding, move together with Agni and spread long life or abundant food for the sake of sacrifice; or they give the sacrificer long life.

The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya (accent and formation of आरुः (*āruḥ*), शितिपृष्ठस्य (*śitipṛṣṭhasya*), धासेः (*dhāseḥ*), मातरा (*mātarā*), विविशुः (*viviśuḥ*), सप्त (*sapta*), क्षिता (*kṣitā*), चरेते (*carete*), सस्राते (*sasrāte*), आयुः (*āyuḥ*), प्रयक्षे (*prayakṣe*), citing Uṇ. 2-96, Uṇ. 1-56 and Pā. 1-3-54) is noted here but not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

*[Before the Pratipadārtha the supplied text has the stray letters क, ति, स, व, ध, ग (*ka, ti, sa, va, dha, ga*), kept in kn.md as supplied. The first word is printed तिशिपृष्ठस्य (*tiśipṛṣṭhasya*) in the Pratipadārtha, but शितिपृष्टस्य (*śitipṛṣṭasya*) in the bhāṣya; both are kept as supplied.]*

Śitipṛṣṭhasya : of the blue-backed one; dhāseḥ: of Agni, the support of all; ye raśmayaḥ: whichever rays; pra āruḥ: go forth upward abundantly; (te): those rays; mātarā: the parents, the mother and father, heaven and earth; ā viviśuḥ: have entered from all sides; (and) sapta: of flowing nature; vāṇīḥ: the worship-worthy rivers also (have entered); parikṣitā: surrounding; pitarā: heaven and earth, standing in the place of parents; saṃ carete

### Printed p. 5

(with Agni) deal well together; (and) prayakṣe: for the sake of abundant performance of sacrifice; dīrghaṃ āyuḥ: (to Agni) long life [or abundant food]; prayakṣe: abundantly and constantly, for the sake of performing sacrifices; dīrghaṃ āyuḥ: (to the sacrificer) long life [or abundant food]; pra sasrāte: spread (grant ... the supplied text breaks off here with an unfinished word, ऒदगि (*òdagi*), with no closing bracket).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The rays of Agni, the blue-backed and all-supporting, going out from Agni, have pervaded everywhere the world and the parents, व्याघ्रापृथिविगळन्नु (*vyāghrāpṛthivigaḷannu*) ([sic] as supplied; evidently *dyāvāpṛthivī*, heaven and earth); in the same way the flowing and worship-worthy rivers also are pervaded. The all-pervading heaven and earth, so that sacrifices may go on in abundance, grant long life to Agni and abundant food to the sacrificer, and सिद्धरिसुत्तवॆ (*siddharisuttavè*) (as supplied; the sense seems to be "work together") with Agni.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The (rays) of the blackbacked, all-sustaining (Agni) have arisen, and pervaded the parents (earth and heaven) and the flowing rivers ; the surrounding parents co-operate with him, and bestow long life for the sake of assiduous worship.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धासेः— सर्वस्य धारयितुः । (*dhāseḥ— sarvasya dhārayituḥ |*) The author of the Nirukta reads the word धासिः (*dhāsiḥ*) among the twenty-eight names of food (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa has explained the sense as "Agni bears everything". He also gives the meaning that the rays of this Agni shine greatly.

मातरा विविशुः सप्तवाणीः (*mātarā viviśuḥ saptavāṇīḥ*): the word वाणी (*vāṇī*) is read in the Nirukta among the twenty-seven names of speech (Ni. 2-23). Here the meaning "rivers" is given, and it is explained that the rays of Agni pervade the rivers. The sense that the word सप्त (*sapta*) is not a numeral is indicated here; the word is explained as "of pervading nature", and the nature of the rays is described. Though the word मातरा (*mātarā*) is not stated among the names of heaven and earth in the Nirukta, here the word is explained as heaven and earth, and it is described that the rays of Agni pervade heaven and earth (earth and the middle region). The fact that heaven and earth, like mother and father, are the nourishers of all is stated in the ṛks.

परिक्षिता पितरा—परितो वर्तमाने पितरौ द्यावापृथिव्यौ । (*parikṣitā pitarā—parito vartamāne pitarau dyāvāpṛthivyau |*) The meaning is: heaven and earth (earth and the middle region), who are the mother and father of the world, pervade everything, and they co-operate in the world with Agni.

### Printed p. 6

(Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.) Regarding the sentence प्रसर्स्राते दीर्घमायुः प्रयक्षे (*prasarsrāte dīrghamāyuḥ prayakṣe*), Sāyaṇa has explained two kinds of meaning. In the first meaning, heaven and earth are described as bringing about the abundant food needed for the sacrifice, so that the sacrifice may proceed without obstacle, and Agni as bringing about a proper state and continuance while the sacrifice is going on. The word आयुः (*āyuḥ*) is read among the twenty-eight names of food (Ni. 3-9); from this Sāyaṇa gives the meaning "abundant food". In the second meaning, introduced by the Sanskrit words below, it is explained that heaven and earth grant to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice at all times an increase of आयुस्सु (*āyussu*) (lifetime), so that he may live for a long time:

द्यावापृथिव्यौ प्रकर्षेण सततं यष्टुं यजमानस्य दीर्घमायुः संपादयतः (*dyāvāpṛthivyau prakarṣeṇa satataṃ yaṣṭuṃ yajamānasya dīrghamāyuḥ saṃpādayataḥ*) (as supplied: प्रक-र्षेण (*praka-rṣeṇa*) is split across a line end).

The author of the Nirukta, on the matter of heaven and earth being mother and father, cites the following ṛk (the reference is printed य. सं. (*ya. saṃ.*) "Ya. Saṃ." 1-164-33, as supplied):

दौर्मे पिता जनिता नाभिरत्र बंधुर्मे माता पृथिवी महीयं । (*daurme pitā janitā nābhiratra baṃdhurme mātā pṛthivī mahīyaṃ |*)
उत्यासयोश्चमै ३ र्योनिरंतरत्रा पिता दुहितुर्गर्भमाधात् ॥ (*utyāsayoścamai 3 ryoniraṃtaratrā pitā duhiturgarbhamādhāt ‖*)

Durgācārya (comments):

उडकं हि द्युलोकात् पतितं पार्थिवेन धातुना संपृक्तं ओषधीभावमागम्य शरीरभावेन अवतिष्ठते इत्येतदपेक्ष्य सर्वभूतानां द्यावापृथिव्यौ मातापितरौ उच्येते (*uḍakaṃ hi dyulokāt patitaṃ pārthivena dhātunā saṃpṛktaṃ oṣadhībhāvamāgamya śarīrabhāvena avatiṣṭhate ityetadapekṣya sarvabhūtānāṃ dyāvāpṛthivyau mātāpitarau ucyete*) .

The meaning is explained thus: the water that falls from the heaven-world (the firmament) onto the earth in the form of rain, joining with the earth, takes the form of plants and the like and then the form of the bodies of living beings; therefore the earth and the firmament (heaven and earth) have the character of mother and father to all beings. Having explained this, he cites the ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-15):

द्वे स्रुती अश्वणवं पित्थाणांमहं देवानामुत मर्त्यानां (*dve srutī aśvaṇavaṃ pitthāṇāṃmahaṃ devānāmuta martyānāṃ*)
ताभ्यामिदं विश्वमेजत्समेति यदंतरा पितरं मातरं च ॥ (*tābhyāmidaṃ viśvamejatsameti yadaṃtarā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca ‖*)

and (continues):

तत्कृतस्य उपकारस्याभावे सतीतरौ मातापितरावकिंचित्करावेव भवतः । तस्मादुपपद्यते द्यावापृथिव्योः मातापितृभावः । एवं द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां अंतरिक्षेण च अवकाशदानेन अनुगृह्यमाणेन एतानि अस्मदादीनि भूतान्युत्पद्यंत इति अनेक मंत्रेण मंत्रदैशा स्थापितं (*tatkṛtasya upakārasyābhāve satītarau mātāpitarāvakiṃcitkarāveva bhavataḥ | tasmādupapadyate dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ mātāpitṛbhāvaḥ | evaṃ dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ aṃtarikṣeṇa ca avakāśadānena anugṛhyamāṇena etāni asmadādīni bhūtānyutpadyaṃta iti aneka maṃtreṇa maṃtradaiśā sthāpitaṃ*) .

The meaning is explained thus: in the world, if there were not the help of this heaven and earth, the mother and father who are the cause of the birth of living beings would be doers of no kind of work whatever. Because heaven and earth have granted space, the bodies of living beings come into being; the seer who saw the mantra has understood the mantra teaching this meaning directly and stated it here.

Sāyaṇa's gloss, quoted here: द्यावापृथिव्यौ यॆष्टुं (दीर्घमायुः) जीवनं प्रभूतं अन्नं वा (प्रसारयतः) संपादयतः (*dyāvāpṛthivyau yèṣṭuṃ (dīrghamāyuḥ) jīvanaṃ prabhūtaṃ annaṃ vā (prasārayataḥ) saṃpādayataḥ*) (as supplied; यॆष्टुं (*yèṣṭuṃ*) for the bhāṣya's यष्टुं (*yaṣṭuṃ*)). Heaven and earth produce abundant food and lifetime so that the sacrifice may go on. In this sense the author of the Nirukta cites

the ṛk

द्यावा नः पृथिवी इमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्पृतं । (*dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī imaṃ sidhramadya divispṛtaṃ |*)
यज्ञं देवेषु यच्छतां ॥ (*yajñaṃ deveṣu yacchatāṃ ‖*)

and explains: द्यावापृथिव्यौ न इमं साधनमद्य दिविस्कृतं यज्ञं देवेषु नियच्छतां (*dyāvāpṛthivyau na imaṃ sādhanamadya diviskṛtaṃ yajñaṃ deveṣu niyacchatāṃ*) . "May these heaven and earth make our sacrifice, the means of welfare, such that the gods are pleased." Since in this ṛk it is described that Agni enters heaven and earth, the purport is indicated that heaven and earth, pervaded by the rays of Agni, are beneficial to the world.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni's red flame-horses, pervading the sky, are his milch cows; he reaches the shining, sweet-water-bearing rivers; a single voice of the firmament waits on you, Agni, who desire a dwelling in the waters' abode.

The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya (formation and accent of दिवक्षसः (*divakṣasaḥ*), धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*), वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*), अश्वाः (*aśvāḥ*), तस्था (*tasthā*), मधुमत् (*madhumat*), त्वा (*tvā*), क्षेमयंतं (*kṣemayaṃtaṃ*), एका (*ekā*), वर्तनिं (*vartaniṃ*), गौः (*gauḥ*), citing Uṇ. 2-107 and Uṇ. 2-67 as printed) is noted here but not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Vṛṣṭaḥ (वृष्टः (*vṛṣṭaḥ*) as supplied; the bhāṣya has वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)): of Agni, the bestower of desires; aśvāḥ: the red-coloured flames, serving as vehicles; divakṣasaḥ: pervading the firmament; dhenavaḥ: they become the givers of delight to Agni; (such Agni) madhumat: water full of sweetness; vahantīḥ: carrying; devīḥ: luminous rivers; ā tasthau: reaches. (He agne: O Agni) ekā gauḥ: one (praise-form) utterance; ṛtasya: of the water; sadasi: in the abode, the firmament; kṣemayantam: seeking a dwelling; vartanim: sending out flames; tvā: you; pari carati: serves.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The red-coloured flames of Agni, the bestower of desired boons, serving as his vehicles, pervade even the firmament and give delight to Agni; this Agni resorts to the rivers, which carry sweet water and are luminous. Thus, O Agni, a voice in the form of praise serves you, who desire to dwell in the firmament, the abode of the waters, and who are the cause of flames (we make you known by praises).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sky-traversing steeds of the showerer (of benefits) are the milch cows (of Agni); as he attains the divine (rivers), bearers of sweet (water). One sacred sound glorifies you (Agni), who are desirous of repose, pecifying [sic] your flames) in the abode of the water (the firmament),

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वृष्णः— कामानां वर्षितु: (*vṛṣṇaḥ— kāmānāṃ varṣitu:*) (*vṛṣṇaḥ: of the showerer of desires*). The meaning is that Agni fulfils all the wishes of those who perform sacrifice.

अश्वा—वाहनरूपाः रोहिताः (*aśvā—vāhanarūpāḥ rohitāḥ*) (*aśvā: vehicle-like red ones*). The authors of the Nirukta (say):

हरी इंद्रस्य । रोहितोऽग्नेः । हरित आदित्यस्य । रासभावश्विनोः । अजाः (*harī iṃdrasya | rohito 'gneḥ | harita ādityasya | rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ | ajāḥ*)
पूष्णः । पृषश्यो मरुतां । अरुण्यो गाव उषसः । श्यावाः सवितुः । विश्व (*pūṣṇaḥ | pṛṣaśyo marutāṃ | aruṇyo gāva uṣasaḥ | śyāvāḥ savituḥ | viśva*)
रूपा बृहस्पतेः । नियुतो वायोः । (*rūpā bṛhaspateḥ | niyuto vāyoḥ |*) (Ni. 2-28)

(Gloss mine and tentative: the two bay horses are Indra's; the red one is Agni's; the green ones are the Sun's; the two asses belong to the Aśvins; the goats to Pūṣan; the spotted ones to the Maruts; the ruddy cows to Uṣas; the dark ones to Savitṛ; the many-formed ones to Bṛhaspati; the नियुत् (*niyut*) team to Vāyu. The passage is quoted as supplied, with the विश्व-रूपा (*viśva-rūpā*) split across a line end; the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 continue on the next page.)

### Printed p. 11

(Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 10.) Since the vehicles of the respective deities are thus indicated, the vehicle of Agni is known to be the red one (रोहित (*rohita*)). Sāyaṇa has explained it here as रोहिताः अश्वाः (*rohitāḥ aśvāḥ*) ("the red horses").

धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)— अग्नेः प्रिणयित्र्यः (*agneḥ priṇayitryaḥ*) (delighters of Agni). The word धेनु (*dhenu*) is read among the twenty-eight names of speech (Ni. 2-23; the supplied text prints the abbreviation as "ಸಿ", evidently Ni., as printed). Just as words give delight in the world, the red horses, the vehicles of Agni, give delight to Agni; thus the meaning is explained (resorting to a figurative usage).

ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—उदकस्य (*udakasya*). The word ऋत (*ṛta*) is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24) and also in the sense of a particular time. Here the meaning is explained as water.

क्षेमयंतं (*kṣemayaṃtaṃ*) — क्षेमं आवासमिच्छंतं (*kṣemaṃ āvāsamicchaṃtaṃ*). The meaning is that Agni, imagining (and pervading the water to make) a pleasant dwelling-place in the rivers that bear sweet (tasty) waters, abides there. By this both the Aurva fire (the submarine fire) and the lightning-fire that is in the midst of the clouds are made known.

गौः (*gauḥ*)—माध्यमिका वाक् (*mādhyamikā vāk*) (the speech of the firmament). The word गो (*go*) is stated among the twenty-one names of the earth (Ni. 2-5). The Nirukta sentence गौरिति पृथिव्या नामधेयं (*gauriti pṛthivyā nāmadheyaṃ*) explains this meaning. अथापि पशुनामेह भवत्वेतस्मादेव (*athāpi paśunāmeha bhavatvetasmādeva*): since the word गौः (*gauḥ*) is derived from a root (given in the supplied text as गाज् गत् (*gāj gat*)), it conveys the meaning "animal"; the meaning is cows.

In the Ṛk

सुपर्णं वस्ते मृगो अस्या दंतो गोभिस्सन्नद्धा पतति प्रसूता यत्रा नरः सं च वि च द्रवंति तत्रास्मभ्यमिषवः शर्म यंसन् (*suparṇaṃ vaste mṛgo asyā daṃto gobhissannaddhā patati prasūtā yatrā naraḥ saṃ ca vi ca dravaṃti tatrāsmabhyamiṣavaḥ śarma yaṃsan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-11)

it is described that the word गो (*go*) means sinew and phlegm.

In the Ṛk

वृक्षेवृक्षे नियता मीमयद्दौस्ततौ वयः प्र पर्ता पूरुषादः । अथेदं विश्वं भुवनं भयात इंद्राय सुन्वदृषये च शिक्षत् (*vṛkṣevṛkṣe niyatā mīmayaddaustatau vayaḥ pra partā pūruṣādaḥ | athedaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhayāta iṃdrāya sunvadṛṣaye ca śikṣat*) (the supplied text prints the abbreviation as "ಮಿ. ಸಂ-", evidently Ṛ. Saṃ., as printed: 10-27-22)

the meaning "bowstring" (ज्या (*jyā*)) is given for the word गो (*go*).

In

उतादः परुषे गवि सूरश्चक्रं हिरण्ययं । नैरयद्रथीतमः (*utādaḥ paruṣe gavi sūraścakraṃ hiraṇyayaṃ | nairayadrathītamaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-56-3)

since the meaning is given as आदित्योऽपि गौरुच्यते (*ādityo 'pi gaurucyate*) ("the sun too is called gauḥ"), the authors of the Nirukta say that the sun also is a meaning of the word गो (*go*).

In

ता नां वास्तून्युष्मसि गमध्यै यत्र गावो भूरिशृंगा अयासः । आत्राह तदुरुगायस्य वृष्टः परमं पदमव भाति भूरि (*tā nāṃ vāstūnyuṣmasi gamadhyai yatra gāvo bhūriśṛṃgā ayāsaḥ | ātrāha tadurugāyasya vṛṣṭaḥ paramaṃ padamava bhāti bhūri*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-6)

the meaning "ray" is given for the word गो (*go*) with the words सर्वॆऽपि रश्मयः गाव उच्यंते (*sarvè 'pi raśmayaḥ gāva ucyaṃte*) ("all the rays are called gāvaḥ"). Since Durgācārya has commented सुषुम्मो रश्मिरेक एव गौः इति उच्यते (*suṣummo raśmireka eva gauḥ iti ucyate*) ("the one ray Suṣumna alone is called gauḥ"; सुषुम्मो (*suṣummo*) as supplied), the ray of the Suṣumnā (nāḍī) etc. is also a meaning of the word गो (*go*). The word गो (*go*) has the earth, cows,

### Printed p. 12

sinew, phlegm, Maurvī (bowstring), the sun, rays, and the ray of the Suṣumnā nāḍī, among many meanings. Sāyaṇa, having commented

गोशब्दो माध्यमिकवाग्वाची माध्यमिकां वाचमिति नैरुक्ता इत्यभिधानात् । एका गौः काचिदुक्तविधा वाक् वर्तनिं ज्वालाः प्रवर्तयंतं त्वां परिचरिति सेवते (*gośabdo mādhyamikavāgvācī mādhyamikāṃ vācamiti nairuktā ityabhidhānāt | ekā gauḥ kāciduktavidhā vāk vartaniṃ jvālāḥ pravartayaṃtaṃ tvāṃ paricariti sevate*)

has made the meaning that the speech of the firmament serves Agni. In regard to the utterance of speech by living beings, the Vaiśvānara fire, impelled by the vital breath (prāṇa-vāyu), is the producer of the manifestation of speech: the meaning is thus described in an involved manner.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the finder of the best wealth among riches and the knowing lord of horses, mounts the easily controlled mares; the blue-backed, many-formed one makes them rest to nourish his ceaseless going.

The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya (formation and accent of सीं (*sīṃ*), अरोहत् (*arohat*), सुयमाः (*suyamāḥ*), पतिः (*patiḥ*), चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*), रयिवित् (*rayivit*), रयीणां (*rayīṇāṃ*), नीलपृष्ठः (*nīlapṛṣṭhaḥ*), आतसस्य (*ātasasya*), आवासयत् (*āvāsayat*), citing Uṇ. 117 as printed) is noted here but not explained. The Pratipadārtha and the rest of Ṛk 3 follow on the next page.

> पुरुधप्रतीकः । पुरुशब्द इह संख्यावाची । संख्याया विधार्थे धेति धाप्रत्ययः ।
> बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । ह्रस्वश्चांदसः ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

rayīṇām — (in the midst) of riches; rayivit — the one who supplies the best wealth; cikitvān — the wise one; patiḥ — the lord of horses, Agni; sīm — in every way; suyamāḥ — easily controlled; bhavantīḥ (yāḥ) — you who are mares (O horses), whom; ā arohat — he mounts; tāḥ — those horses; nīlapṛṣṭhaḥ — he whose back is dark blue; purudhapratīkaḥ — he whose limbs are scattered in many ways (Agni); atasasya — of the ceaseless going; dhāseḥ — for the nourishment (of it); pra āvāsayat — makes them rest.

(Printed as supplied: शीं (*śīṃ*) for sīm, पुरुषप्रतीकः (*puruṣapratīkaḥ*) for purudhapratīkaḥ, अतसस्य- सतत (*atasasya- satata*) with a stray hyphen; left as supplied.)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mares, the vehicles of Agni! Agni, who bestows the most excellent wealth, who is wise, and who is the lord of horses, mounts you in every way, you who are easily controlled. But that dark-backed Agni, of scattered limbs, in order that the nourishment needed for the unwearied going from you may reach you, in advance makes you rest.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Their lord has mounted on his well-trained mares; the sagacious selector of treasures, the blackbacked, manylimbed (Agni) has granted them a place of rest for the cherising [sic] of (their) rapid speed.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

रयीणां रयिवित् (*rayīṇāṃ rayivit*) — धनानां मध्यॆ विशिष्टधनस्य लंभयिता (*dhanānāṃ madhyè viśiṣṭadhanasya laṃbhayitā*). The word *rayi* denotes water (Ni. 2-24) and also wealth (Ni. 3-9); and since it is said, at "nū ca purā ca sadanaṃ rayīṇām", "*rayi* is a name for wealth, from *rā*, in the sense of giving" (Ni. 4-17), it conveys the meaning wealth. The meaning is that Agni obtains for those who perform the sacrifice all that is known as wealth.

पुरुधप्रतीक: (*purudhapratīka:*) — पुरुशब्द इह संख्यावाची । बहुधा विक्षिप्तांगः (*puruśabda iha saṃkhyāvācī | bahudhā vikṣiptāṃgaḥ*). It is explained that Agni pervades all places.

धासेः ताः प्र अवासयत् (*dhāseḥ tāḥ pra avāsayat*) — पोषणार्थं आश्वा: प्रकर्षेण वासयेति स्म (*poṣaṇārthaṃ āśvā: prakarṣeṇa vāsayeti sma*). Because Agni is the lord of the horses, he is described as the helper by whom the horses (for their nourishment) may grow,

### Printed p. 16

and, having removed their weariness, may move about always, and may also be at ease.

चिकित्त्वा (*cikittvā*) (as printed; the bhāṣya has चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)) — knowing. The meaning is that Agni has spiritual knowledge.

सीं (*sīṃ*) — everywhere, in all regions. The authors of the Nirukta, on the word सीं (*sīṃ*), say सीमिति परिग्रहार्थियो वा पादपूरणे वा (*sīmiti parigrahārthiyo vā pādapūraṇe vā*): the particle *sīm* is used in the sense of "taking in all round" and also as a verse-filler. Then, at विशीमतः सुरुचो-वेन आवः व्यवृणोत् सर्वत आदित्यः (*viśīmataḥ suruco-vena āvaḥ vyavṛṇot sarvata ādityaḥ*) , they explain *sīm* as सर्वतः (*sarvataḥ*) (on all sides), and सीम्न: सीमतः सीमतो मर्यादातः सीमा मर्यादा (*sīmna: sīmataḥ sīmato maryādātaḥ sīmā maryādā*) as limit, boundary.

Sū. 84), अरोहत् (*arohat*) (root *ruh*; laṅ third singular; all-unaccented after a non-finite form), सुयमाः (*suyamāḥ*) (root *yam*; khal ending by ईषद्दुः सुषु (*īṣadduḥ suṣu*), Pā. 3-3-126; accent of the compound by the *kṛdutta-rapada* rule), पतिः (*patiḥ*) (root *pā*; ḍati ending by पातेर्दतिः (*pāterdatiḥ*), Uṇ. 4-497 as printed; loss of the ṭi; ending accented first), चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*) (root *kit*; kvasu replacing liṭ by Pā. 3-2-107; reduplication; ending-accent), रयिवित् (*rayivit*) (root *vid*; kvip by Rā. Sū. 3-2-76 [sic, as printed]), रयीणाम् (*rayīṇām*) (genitive plural; ending accented by नामन्यतरस्याम् (*nāmanyatarasyām*), Pā. 6-1-177), नीलपृष्ठः (*nīlapṛṣṭhaḥ*) (*nīla* is in the *vṛṣādi* list, hence initial accent by वृषादीनांच (*vṛṣādīnāṃca*), Pā. 6-1-213; accent of the first member in the bahuvrīhi by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*), 6-2-1), दासेः (*dāseḥ*) (as printed; said to be explained already in the first Ṛk).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वहंति ।  
> व्यंगे॑भिर्दिद्युता॒नः स॒धस्थ॒ एका॑मिव॒ रोद॑सी॒ आ वि॑वेश - ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । अंगेभिः । दिद्युतानः । सधस्थे । एकांइव । रोदसी इति । आ । विवेश ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The mighty rivers, making the strengthless strong, carry Agni, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, who wishes to support the worlds; blazing with his limbs by the water's side, he entered heaven and earth as a man enters a woman.

The bhāṣya is cut off at the end of printed p. 17 in the middle of its grammatical tail (on त्वाष्ट्रं (*tvāṣṭraṃ*) and स्तभूयमानं (*stabhūyamānaṃ*)); the stray character "3" at its end in the supplied text is left as supplied. The Pratipadārtha and the rest of Ṛk 4 follow on the next page.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Ūrjayantīḥ — those that make the strengthless strong; vahataḥ — rivers that are intent on carrying; mahi — the great one; tvāṣṭram — the son of Tvaṣṭṛ; ajuryam — one not liable to old age; stabhūyamānam — one who wishes to support the world: Agni; vahanti — they bear; sadhasthe — near the water; aṅgebhiḥ — (together) with his limbs; didyutānaḥ — Agni, shining; rodasī — heaven and earth; ekām iva — (as a man enters) a single woman (in many forms); vi ā viveśa — enters in manifold forms.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The rivers, which give strength to the weak and are intent on carrying, bear Agni, the great one, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, not liable to old age, who wishes to support the world. Thus, shining with all his limbs kindled near the water, Agni enters heaven and earth in many forms, as a man approaches a single woman in different forms.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The flowing (rivers) invigorating him, bear along the great son of Twashtri, the undecaying upholder (of the world), radiant with various forms in the vicinity (of the firmament): Agni is associated with heaven and earth, as (a husband with) one only wife.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऊर्जयंतीः (*ūrjayaṃtīḥ*) — अबलं बलिनं कुर्वत्यः (*abalaṃ balinaṃ kurvatyaḥ*) (making the strengthless strong). The word ऊर्क् (*ūrk*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). The word *ūrja* is also used in the sense of strength. For example—

### Printed p. 19

देवी ऊर्जाहुती इषमूर्जमन्यावक्षत् सद्धिं सपीतिमन्या नवेन पूर्वं दयमानाः स्याम पुराणेन नवं तामूर्जमूर्जाहुती ऊर्जयमाने आधातां वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज (*devī ūrjāhutī iṣamūrjamanyāvakṣat saddhiṃ sapītimanyā navena pūrvaṃ dayamānāḥ syāma purāṇena navaṃ tāmūrjamūrjāhutī ūrjayamāne ādhātāṃ vasuvane vasudheyasya vītāṃ yaja*) (Yaj. Vā. Saṃ. 28-16). Durgācārya has commented that in this mantra the word *ūrja* is used in the sense of strength. Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as: the rivers produce strength even for those who have no strength.

वहतः स्तभूयामानं वहंति (*vahataḥ stabhūyāmānaṃ vahaṃti*) — वहनपराः नद्यः लोकानां धारणमिच्छंतमग्निं धारयंति (*vahanaparāḥ nadyaḥ lokānāṃ dhāraṇamicchaṃtamagniṃ dhārayaṃti*): the rivers, flowing ever with abundant currents, pervade all the worlds and bear Agni, who desires to protect everything. By the Śruti अग्नेरापः (*agnerāpaḥ*) ("the waters are from Agni"), the waters originate from Agni; therefore Agni's entry is in the waters. This is the meaning.

अजुर्यं-जरयितुमनॆर्हं (*ajuryaṃ-jarayitumanèrhaṃ*) — the meaning is that Agni is not fit to be consumed (quenched) by anyone.

रोदसी एकामिव आ विवेश (*rodasī ekāmiva ā viveśa*) — द्यावापृथिव्यॆ विविधं प्रविष्टर्वा यथा पुर्मा एकां स्त्रीयं तद्वत् (*dyāvāpṛthivyè vividhaṃ praviṣṭarvā yathā purmā ekāṃ strīyaṃ tadvat*) : Agni, having entered the waters, has pervaded heaven and earth in many ways. Just as in the world a man, attached to a woman and in many ways becoming the object of her affection, pervades her mind, so the entry of Agni into heaven and earth is stated here by way of simile. The word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is read among the twenty-four names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22). And—

रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हुनामहे । आ यस्मिन् तस्थौ सुरहानिबिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥ (*rathaṃ nu mārutaṃ vayaṃ śravasyumā hunāmahe | ā yasmin tasthau surahānibibhratī sacā marutsu rodasī ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 5-6-8, as printed).

Yāska, citing this Ṛk, explains here that रोदसी (*rodasī*) means the wife of Rudra; Durgācārya explains it as the manifestation (विभूतिः (*vibhūtiḥ*)) of Rudra.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

People know the comfort of Agni, the showerer, free of enemies; they delight under his command; those whose praise of him is honoured become radiant light-givers of heaven.

The bhāṣya (Sanskrit, not rendered) continues with its grammatical tail on जानंति (*jānaṃti*), अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*), शेवं (*śevaṃ*), शासने (*śāsane*), दिवोरुचः (*divoruchaḥ*), सुरुचः (*suruchaḥ*), इळा (*iḷā*), गण्या (*gaṇyā*), माहिना (*māhinā*) and गीः (*gīḥ*), not explained; it also cites a mantra (ma 1-60-2, as printed).

### Printed p. 22

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Vṛṣṇaḥ — of the one who showers desires; aruṣasya — of the one without enemies (and therefore shining), Agni; śevam — the comfort that has him as refuge; jānanti — (people) come to know; uta — and (those people who know that comfort); bradhnasya — of Agni, of great majesty; śāsane — under the rule; raṇanti — rejoice (and); yeṣām — whichever men; māhinā — greatness-possessing; iḷā gīḥ — (Agni's) speech in the form of praise; gaṇyā — worthy of honour; te — they; divorucaḥ — (dear to heaven) those who bring heaven into light; surucaḥ — of fine brilliance; rocamānāḥ — shining brightly (become).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

People come to know the comfort that arises from taking refuge in Agni, who grants what is wished for and has no enemies; coming under the rule of that Agni of great majesty, they live happily. Those who regard as worthy of honour the praise relating to Agni, full of great majesty, become exceedingly radiant and guides toward the attainment of heaven.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Men comprehend the service of the uninjurable showerer (of benefits) and exult in the commands of the mighty (AGNI) : their frequent and earnest hymns of praise, bright and radiant, are illuminating heaven.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*) — रोषंतीति रुषा हिंसकाः (*roṣaṃtīti ruṣā hiṃsakāḥ*) : the word *ruṣāḥ*, formed from the root *ruṣ*, which conveys "to injure", is explained as "those who injure"; since there are no such injuring enemies, Agni shines. The word *aruṣam* is read among the names of form (Ni. 3-13). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as "one free of those who injure".

शेवं (*śevaṃ*) — आश्रयविषयं सुखं (*āśrayaviṣayaṃ sukhaṃ*): the word *śeva* is read among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-13). Nirukta (10-17) says: शेव इति सुखनाम शिष्यतेर्वकारो नामकरणो अंतस्थांतरोपलिंगी विभाषितगुणः शिवमित्यप्यस्य भवति (*śeva iti sukhanāma śiṣyatervakāro nāmakaraṇo aṃtasthāṃtaropaliṃgī vibhāṣitaguṇaḥ śivamityapyasya bhavati*) (the text is given as supplied and is not rendered). The word is formed from the root *śiṣ*: in place of the *ṣ* of *śiṣ* a *v* comes, guṇa follows, and the form is *śeva*. The meaning is that those who take refuge in Agni know the comfort arising from that refuge.

ब्रध्नस्य शासने रणंति (*bradhnasya śāsane raṇaṃti*) — महतो अग्नेः आज्ञायां सर्वॆ जनाः रमंते (*mahato agneḥ ājñāyāṃ sarvè janāḥ ramaṃte*). The word *bradhna* is read among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27); it is also read among the names of the great (Ni. 3-13)

### Printed p. 23

(the passage continues from p. 22) Sāyaṇa explains the meaning thus: all people who follow the command of Agni, filled with a greatness fit to be honoured by all, live happily; and he describes this matter as also established by the Ṛk

अस्य शासुरुभयासस्सचंते हविष्मंत उशिजो ये च मर्ताः (*asya śāsurubhayāsassacaṃte haviṣmaṃta uśijo ye ca martāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-60-2).

येषां माहिना इळा गीः (*yeṣāṃ māhinā iḷā gīḥ*) — येषां मनुष्याणां अग्नि विषया महती स्तूतिरूपा वाक्, ते गण्याः (*yeṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ agni viṣayā mahatī stūtirūpā vāk, te gaṇyāḥ*): those who recite the praise that is full of the greatness (found in Agni) are honoured, make the heaven-world shine and have abundant brilliance; thus the glory of Agni is revealed. The word *iḷā* is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5), of speech (Ni. 2-23) and of food (Ni. 3-9).

अभि न इळा यूथस्य मातास्मन्नदीभिरुर्वशी ना गृणातु (*abhi na iḷā yūthasya mātāsmannadībhirurvaśī nā gṛṇātu*) (Mi. Saṃ. 5-41-19, as printed): here *iḷā* (or *iḍā*) is explained as a deity of the middle region. Sāyaṇa has explained it as speech in the form of praise.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The worshippers bring to Agni the delight proclaimed by heaven and earth; Agni, the rain-shedder, brings near to the praiser his own radiance that invests the night. The grammatical tail (accents of ghoṣam, mahaḥ, anayanta, ukṣā, aktoḥ, vavakṣa) is transcribed, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Uto — and. Yatra — among whichever worshippers. Ukṣā — Agni, the one who sprinkles water (by producing rain). Aktoḥ — of the night. Pari dhānam — (like a covering) the holder. Svaṃ dhāma — his own radiance. Jaritum — of the praiser (for hearing the praise). Anu vavakṣa ha — (makes it present) brings it near. (Te — those worshippers.) Maho mahadbhyāṃ — greater than the great. Pitṛbhyāṃ — the parents, heaven and earth. Pravidā — by making known. Anu ghoṣaṃ — that is proclaimed. Śūṣaṃ [sic: the supplied text reads *Kūṣaṃ*] — the delight. Anayanta — (to Agni) caused to reach.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who causes water to be sprinkled by means of rain, becomes present, with the purpose of hearing the praise of the praiser, in the form of his own radiance that, like a covering, holds the night. The praisers too, by glorifying heaven and earth, greatest among the great, bring delight to Agni.

### Printed p. 26

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Verily (men) bring great delight to Agni by glorifying aloud the mighty parents (heaven and earth), when the shedder of rain approximates his own radiance to the worshipper, (wherewith) to invest the night.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

महः महद्भ्यां (*mahaḥ mahadbhyāṃ*)—महतो महद्भ्यां (*mahato mahadbhyāṃ*). The word *mahaḥ* is also read among the names of water (21-24).

पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीं । यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥ (*pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīṃ | yasya trito vyojasā vṛtraṃ viparvamardayat ‖*) (Pu. Saṃ. 1-187-1). In this Ṛk, since the meaning of *mahaḥ* is explained as महतः बलस्य धारयितारं (*mahataḥ balasya dhārayitāraṃ*) ("the holder of great strength", one who bears exceeding strength), the word *mahaḥ* is understood in the sense *mahat* (superior).

त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति । यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश ॥ (*tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇotītīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 10-17-1). In this Ṛk also, since the meaning is explained as महः महतः जाया एवस्वतः (*mahaḥ mahataḥ jāyā evasvataḥ*) ("the wife of the sun, filled with greatness"), the word *mahaḥ* is used here in the sense *mahat*.

पितृभ्यां (*pitṛbhyāṃ*)—द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां (*dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ*). Yāska explains the word *pitṛ* as पिता पाता ना पालयिता वा (*pitā pātā nā pālayitā vā*) (Ni. 4-21), that it conveys the sense "protector". Here the meaning is taken as heaven and earth.

शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*)—सुखं (*sukhaṃ*). The word *śūṣa* is stated both among the twenty-eight names of strength (Ni. 3-9) and among the twenty names of happiness beginning with *śimbātā*, *śatarā* (Ni. 3-13). Here the meaning is happiness.

Here, महद्भ्यां पितृभ्यां प्रविदा अनुघोषं शूषं (*mahadbhyāṃ pitṛbhyāṃ pravidā anughoṣaṃ śūṣaṃ*) is explained thus: heaven and earth, filled with greatness, well knowing the abundance of the happiness arising from Agni, proclaim it; and the sacrificing worshippers, having obtained such happiness through the worship of Agni, express the wish that the same happiness may come to Agni who bestowed happiness on them, and thus have caused it to come to Agni.

### Printed p. 27

उक्षा (*ukṣā*)—वृष्ट्यत्पादनेन उदकस्य सेक्ता (*vṛṣṭyatpādanena udakasya sektā*) ("the sprinkler of water by producing rain"). The word *ukṣā* is stated among the twenty-five names of the great, beginning with *mahat*, *bradhnaḥ* (Ni. 3-13). And Yāska, citing the Ṛk

वृषाकपायि रेवति सुपुत्र आदु सुस्नुषे । घसत्त इंद्र उक्षणः प्रियं काचित्करं हविर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ (*vṛṣākapāyi revati suputra ādu susnuṣe | ghasatta iṃdra ukṣaṇaḥ priyaṃ kācitkaraṃ havirviśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 10-86-13),

explains उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*) as उक्षतेर्वृद्दिकम=णः, उक्षंत्युदकेनेति वा (*ukṣatervṛddikama=ṇaḥ, ukṣaṃtyudakeneti vā*) : to the word *ukṣā*, formed from the root *ukṣ* that conveys growth, he gives the meaning "one who grows", or "one who pours water, hence *ukṣā*". Here Sāyaṇa explains that Agni too is denoted by the word *ukṣā* because he produces rain. The purport is that Agni produces rain to the advantage of those who perform the sacrifice.

अक्तुः (*aktuḥ*)—रात्रेः (*rātreḥ*): night. The word *aktuḥ* is stated (Ni. 2-18) among the twenty-three names of night beginning with *śyāvī*, *kṣapā*. Sāyaṇa explains: अक्तुशब्दो रात्रिमाचष्टे अज्यते सिच्यते नीहारेण जगदस्यामिति व्युत्पत्तेश्व (*aktuśabdo rātrimācaṣṭe ajyate sicyate nīhāreṇa jagadasyāmiti vyutpatteśva*) — night is called *aktu* because it wets the whole world with mist.

जरितुः (*jarituḥ*)—स्तोतुः (*stotuḥ*): of the praiser. The word *jaritṛ* is explained by Yāska as जरिता—गरिता (*jaritā—garitā*) (Ni. 1-7). It is read among the names of the praiser as रेभः जरिता (*rebhaḥ jaritā*) (Ni. 3-19).

From the sentence उक्षा अक्टोः परिधानं स्वं धाम जरितुः ववक्ष (*ukṣā akṭoḥ paridhānaṃ svaṃ dhāma jarituḥ vavakṣa*) the meaning is explained thus: Agni makes his radiance, which covers the night, present (visible) for those who praise him (for the hearing of the praise).

Words treated: उतो (उतो (*uto*)) (ending in o, a particle; pragṛhya designation by Pā. Sū. 1-1-15, *ot*; prakṛtibhāva by the rule *plutapragṛhyā aci nityam*; being among the *evādi* words, final accent by *evādīnām antaḥ*, Phi. Sū. 82), प्रविदा (प्रविदा (*pravidā*)) (root *vid* "to know"; kvip; prādi compound; accent of the stem by the rule for the latter member being a kṛt; instrumental singular), घोषम् (घोषम् (*ghoṣam*)) (root *ghuṣ*, "to sound"; ghañ in the object sense; guṇa of the light penultimate, Pā. Sū. 7-3-86 as printed).

> तेर्हिरिति हिरादेशः । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । वेः । वी कांतिगत्यादिशु ।
> अस्माद्विच् । सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः । सा. ७-३-८४ । इति गुणः । जसिजसोश्चेशि
> पूर्वरूपत्वं । प्रांचः i अनिगंतोऽंचताविति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । मदंति ।
> मदी हर्षॆ । निघातः । गुः i इण् गतावित्यस्माल्लुजि रूपं । इणो गा लुजीति

> निहन्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The twelve priests other than the Udgātṛ group: seven offer the vaṣaṭ, five lead the sacrifice; together they guard Agni's dear station, the Āhavanīya, and rejoice, following the gods' rites. The grammatical tail (rakṣante, nihitam, veḥ, prāñcaḥ, madanti, guḥ) is transcribed, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Pañcabhiḥ adhvaryubhiḥ — (accompanied) by five priests of the Adhvaryu group. Sapta viprāḥ — seven wise priests of the Hotṛ group. Veḥ — to Agni, of swift-moving nature.

### Printed p. 30

Priyam — dear. Nihitaṃ padam — the prepared station (called Āhavanīya). Rakṣante — protect. Prāñcaḥ — those facing east (for drinking the Soma), ajuryāḥ — not subject to old age, ukṣaṇaḥ — sprinklers of the Soma juice. Devāḥ — the praisers (priests). Madanti — rejoice (and those priests). Devānām — (belonging) to the gods. Vratā — the rites (sacrifices). Anu guḥ — follow. Hi — it is well known.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seven wise priests of the Hotṛ group, accompanied by the five priests of the Adhvaryu group, guard the station of the Āhavanīya fire, dear to the swift-moving Agni; the priests, facing east for the drinking of the Soma, not subject to old age, sprinklers of the Soma juice, rejoice, praising Agni; [distinguished by] the oblations favoured by the pleased Agni, they undertake the other rites of the gods.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Seven sages with five ministering priests attend the station that is pre-pared [sic] for the rapid (Agni): the undecaying divine (sages), with their faces to the east, sprinkling (the libations), rejoice as they celebrate the worship of the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पंचभिः अध्वर्युभिः सप्त विप्राः (*pañcabhiḥ adhvaryubhiḥ sapta viprāḥ*): उद्गातृवर्गव्यतिरिक्ताः द्वादशर्त्विजो भवंति । तत्र सप्तवषट्कर्तारः । पञ्चान्ये अध्वरं नयंति : सप्त मेधाविनो होत्रकाः (*udgātṛvargavyatiriktāḥ dvādaśartvijo bhavanti; tatra saptavaṣaṭkartāraḥ; pañcānye adhvaraṃ nayanti; sapta medhāvino hotrakāḥ*) (the Sanskrit as supplied; the supplied text has *saptavaṣaṭkartāraḥ* and *pañcānye*, with a colon where a danda is expected). The people who are appointed to perform the duties necessary in a sacrifice while it is being performed are called priests (*ṛtvij*). Since the sacrifice is a rite carried on by the several priests who have studied the four Vedas, those who have studied each Veda perform the rites of that Veda; so the priests connected with the performance of the sacrifice fall into four groups: the Hotṛ group, the Adhvaryu group, the Udgātṛ group and the Brahman group. The priests of the Hotṛ group are those who have studied the Ṛgveda; with the respective mantras they invoke the respective gods. Those of the Adhvaryu group have studied the Yajurveda; in the manner prescribed they prepare the oblation-substances for the gods invoked by the Hotṛ, according to the order prescribed, and after hearing the Hotṛ's *vaṣaṭ* call they perform the respective offerings. Those of the Udgātṛ group have studied the Sāmaveda; in the respective sacrifice they

### Printed p. 31

(Special Topics continued from p. 30.) ... perform the respective sāmans in the order prescribed. The priests of the Brahman group (the Upadraṣṭṛ and the others) see that the sacrifice is completed in the prescribed manner by carrying out the proper expiations for deficiencies and excesses in the necessary duties of the sacrifice. The four groups together make sixteen persons. Among these sixteen (leaving aside the priests of the Udgātṛ group, the Brahman, the priests of the Brahman group, and the sacrificer) seven priests belong to the group of those who utter the *vaṣaṭ*. Sāyaṇa has described this point by the words उद्धातृ वर्ग व्यतिरिक्ताः द्वादश ऋत्विजः (*uddhātṛ varga vyatiriktāḥ dvādaśa ṛtvijaḥ*), "twelve priests apart from the priests of the Udgātṛ group". Of these, the seven who make the *vaṣaṭ* call, including those of the Hotṛ group, he has explained by सप्त वषट्कर्तारः (*sapta vaṣaṭkartāraḥ*). पंचाध्वर्यवः (*paṃcādhvaryavaḥ*): the five, including the priests who assist in performing the work of the Adhvaryu, are described as Adhvaryus. In all, the twelve priests carry out their respective rites without break, in the prescribed manner of the sacrifice. The Nirukta says:

गायत्रमेको गायति शक्वरीषूद्घाता (*gāyatrameko gāyati śakvarīṣūdghātā*) ... ब्रह्मैको जाते जाते विद्यां वदति (*brahmaiko jāte jāte vidyāṃ vadati*) ब्रह्मा सर्वविद्यः सर्वं वेदितुमर्हति (*brahmā sarvavidyaḥ sarvaṃ veditumarhati*) ... यज्ञस्य मात्रां विमिमीत एकोऽध्वर्युः (*yajñasya mātrāṃ vimimīta eko 'dhvaryuḥ*) अध्वर्युरध्वरयुरध्वरं युनक्त्यध्वरस्य नेताध्वरं कामयत इति वा (*adhvaryuradhvarayuradhvaraṃ yunaktyadhvarasya netādhvaraṃ kāmayata iti vā*) ... अध्वर इति यज्ञनाम (*adhvara iti yajñanāma*) ध्वरतिर्हिंसाकर्मा तत्प्रतिषेधः (*dhvaratirhiṃsākarmā tatpratiṣedhaḥ*) (the passage is given with its ellipses and punctuation as supplied).

The root *dhvar* conveys the sense "to injure"; since the injury done in a sacrifice is directed to the deity, it is established that it is not injury. Hence the word *adhvara* denotes the sacrifice, the purifying rite. In this rite the so-called Udgātṛ sings the sāman called Gāyatra. The priest called Brahman is the one who knows all the rites performed in the sacrifice; he informs the other priests of the order in which the respective rites are performed. The priest called Adhvaryu is the one who carries out the rites of the sacrifice, or who carries the sacrifice forward, or who desires that the sacrifice proceed until it is completed; thus the Nirukta explains the duties of the Adhvaryu, Brahman and Udgātṛ.

Durgācārya: यदृचैव हौत्रं क्रियते (*yadṛcaiva hautraṃ kriyate*) (Ai. Brā. 5-5-8) एतत्तावदृगध्ययॆनकर्म तस्मिन् होतरि विनियुक्तं (*etattāvadṛgadhyayènakarma tasmin hotari viniyuktaṃ*). Since the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passage teaches that the Hotṛ performs the rites of the sacrifice with the Ṛgveda itself, all the rites of the sacrifice that belong to the Ṛgveda are the concern of the priest called Hotṛ. साम्योद्गीथं (*sāmyodgīthaṃ*) (Ai. Brā. 5-5-8) — उद्गाता (*udgātā*) तस्मिन्नप्येतत्सामगानकर्म विनियुक्तं (*tasminnapyetatsāmagānakarma viniyuktaṃ*): the Udgītha is to be performed with the Sāmaveda; the one who performs this rite is called the Udgātṛ; the sāman-singing rite connected with the sacrifice is assigned to him.

### Printed p. 32

ब्रह्मा नाम एक ऋत्विक् जाते प्रायश्चित्ते विद्यां वदति इतरेभ्यः ऋत्विग्भ्यः इदमत्र कुरुतेति (*brahmā nāma eka ṛtvik jāte prāyaścitte vidyāṃ vadati itarebhyaḥ ṛtvigbhyaḥ idamatra kuruteti*): the priest called Brahman, when a deviation arises in the performance of the sacrificial rites, instructs the other priests in the manner of performing the expiation to remedy it. तत्रापि ह्येतत्कर्मविनियुक्तं (*tatrāpi hyetatkarmaviniyuktaṃ*): this duty is assigned to the Brahman among the rites of the sacrifice. अथ केन ब्रह्मत्वं क्रियत इति त्रय्या विद्यया (*atha kena brahmatvaṃ kriyata iti trayyā vidyayā*) (Ai. Brā. 5-5-8): the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says that to perform the Brahman's office he must also have knowledge of the three Vedas. या काचिदिति कर्तव्यता यज्ञस्य, तां विमिमिते अध्वर्युः, नानाप्रकारं करोति (*yā kāciditi kartavyatā yajñasya, tāṃ vimimite adhvaryuḥ, nānāprakāraṃ karoti*): the commentary on the Nirukta explains that the Adhvaryu performs all the remaining necessary duties of the sacrifice, other than the rites to be performed by the Brahman, the Hotṛ and the Udgātṛ.

Sāyaṇa has repeated the word देवाः (*devāḥ*) and given the word *deva* two kinds of meaning. First: प्रांचः अजुर्याः उक्षणः देवाः मदंति (*prāṃcaḥ ajuryāḥ ukṣaṇaḥ devāḥ madaṃti*) — the praisers, going facing east for the drinking of the Soma, are joyful; this is the meaning explained. Second: देवाः ऋत्विजः देवानां व्रतानि अनु गुः (*devāḥ ṛtvijaḥ devānāṃ vratāni anu guḥ*) — the priests carry out the joy-giving works of the sacrifice that bring satisfaction to the gods. From this he has explained the meaning: आग्नेः प्रसादात् हनिर्लक्षणान्नवंतो देवाः यज्ञान् लब्धवंतः (*āgneḥ prasādāt hanirlakṣaṇānnavaṃto devāḥ yajñān labdhavaṃtaḥ*) — by Agni's favour the gods, who obtain food in the form of the oblation, obtain it through the sacrifice. प्रांचः मदंति—सोमपानार्थं प्राज्मुखा गच्छंतः (*prāṃcaḥ madaṃti—somapānārthaṃ prājmukhā gacchaṃtaḥ*): the seven Hotṛs and the five Adhvaryus, guarding the fire called Āhavanīya, go facing east for the drinking of the Soma; thus the meaning is explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Words treated (with the Pāṇinian sūtras as printed): रक्षंते (*rakṣaṃte*) (root *rakṣ* "to protect"; ātmanepada by the rule *vyatyayo bahulam*; laṭ third plural; nighāta accent after a finite verb), निहितम् (*nihitam*) (root *ḍudhāñ* "to hold, to nourish"; kta in the passive sense, *niṣṭhā* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-102); replacement *hi*, *dadhāter hiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42); prefix accent by *gatiranantaraḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49)), वेः (*veḥ*) (root *vī* "to shine, to go"; vic suffix; guṇa by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84)

### Printed p. 33

Grammar page continued, noted briefly: the guṇa of the root's *i* gives the stem *ve*; before the genitive singular ending *jas*, *jasijasoś ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-110) gives the earlier form; rutva and visarga; udātta accent. प्रांचः (*prāṃcaḥ*) (prefix *pra* with the root *añc* ending in kvin; prādi compound; the accent of the first member, *anigantoñcau* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-52)). मदंति (*madaṃti*) (root *madī* "to rejoice"; laṭ third plural; all-anudātta after a finite verb). उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*) (nominative plural; optional lengthening of the penultimate, *pāpapūrvasya nigame* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-9)). व्रता (*vratā*) (neuter plural; *śi* replacement, then elision of *śi*, *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70)). गुः (*guḥ*) (root *iṇ* "to go"; adādi; luṅ; replacement *gā*, *iṇo gā luṅi* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-45); luk of the sic, *gātisthāghupā* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77); *jus* for *jhi*, *ata* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-110); the augment *aṭ* does not occur, *bahulaṃ chandasy* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75); because of the connexion with *hi*, the lowering of accent is prevented, *hi ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34), and the word is udātta).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two chief divine Agnis, the accomplishers of the oblation, are propitiated by the seer Viśvāmitra; the seven Hotṛs rejoice with Soma and, guarding the rite, declare Agni the truth in every rite. The grammatical tail (yañje, svadhayā, āhuḥ, dīdhyānāḥ) is transcribed, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Daivyā — those of divine form. Hotārā — the accomplishers of the oblations. Prathamā — the chief; the two Agnis. Ni ṛñje — (I) praise. Sapta pṛkṣāsaḥ — the seven Hotṛs. Svadhayā — with the Soma oblation. Madanti — they satisfy. Ṛtam — (Agni's) praise. Śaṃsantaḥ — those praising, guardians of the sacrifice, radiant ones. Te — those priests. Anuvrataṃ — in every rite. Ṛtam it — Agni alone, of the nature of truth. Āhuḥ — they declare (as the aim of the sacrifice).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise the two chief Agnis, of divine form and accomplishers of the oblations; the seven Hotṛs gladden Agni with the Soma oblation; those priests, who praise Agni, guard the sacrifice and are radiant, declare in every rite that Agni, of the nature of truth, is the one aimed at.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I propitiate the two first divine offerers of sacrifice ; the seven (priests) rejoice with the libation ; the illustrious celebrators of holi [sic] worship, reciting (his) praises, have called AGNI the true (object) of every rite.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*) — दैवौ देवतारूपौ होतार् होमनिष्पादकौ (*daivau devatārūpau hotār homaniṣpādakau*). The two priests called Hotṛ and Maitrāvaruṇa perform the oblations connected with the sacrifice, (the Special Topics continue on the next page).

### Printed p. 35

...has been described. Here the word दैव्या (*daivyā*) is stated as an adjective of the word होतारा (*hotārā*). The Nirukta-writers explain its sense thus: "दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*): the two divine Hotṛs, Agni and the middle one (Vāyu)", and they cite the Ṛk "दैन्व्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा … (*dainvyā hotārā prathamā suvācā …*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-7) and explain their greatness. (The supplied text prints the reference twice, once as "Ma. Saṃ." and once as "Ṛ. Saṃ.", both 10-110-7; the first is evidently a misreading.) Durgācārya explains the word होतारा (*hotārā*) as the Hotṛ and Maitrāvaruṇa priests, and since the word दैवौ (*daivau*) is their adjective, these Hotṛ-Maitrāvaruṇas are human Hotṛs. The divine Hotṛs who invoke the gods, Vāyu and Agni, are the chief ones. This priest called Maitrāvaruṇa, attaining identity with Vāyu, the divine Hotṛ, constantly urges Agni, like a Hotṛ, towards the sacrifice; therefore he explains: तावेव देवानामाह्वातारौ उच्चेते (*tāveva devānāmāhvātārau uccete*), "they urge the gods to the sacrifice."

प्रथमा नृइच्छॆ (*prathamā nṛicchè*) — प्रथमौ मुख्याविमं चामुं चाग्नी मंत्रद्रष्टा विश्वामित्रोऽहं प्रसाधयामि (*prathamau mukhyāvimaṃ cāmuṃ cāgnī maṃtradraṣṭā viśvāmitro 'haṃ prasādhayāmi*). Since the divine Hotṛs, Vāyu and Agni, are designated by the word Hotṛ, the Hotṛ-Maitrāvaruṇas who attain identity with them are meant here. It is described that the seer Viśvāmitra, who knows the greatness of this mantra, praises them to obtain the favour of these two, the chief priests among those who perform the sacrifice. The Nirukta-writer says: ऋञ्चितः प्रसाधनकर्मा (*ṛñcitaḥ prasādhanakarmā*) (Ni. 6-21), explaining that the root ऋञ्चित (*ṛñcita*) [sic, as supplied] conveys the sense of "propitiating" (making glad), and gives the example आव ऋञ्चसे ऊर्जां व्युष्टिषु (*āva ṛñcase ūrjāṃ vyuṣṭiṣu*). Even when connected with the prefix नि (*ni*), the root conveys the same meaning.

सप्त पृक्षासः स्वधया मदंति (*sapta pṛkṣāsaḥ svadhayā madaṃti*) — सप्तहोतृकाः सोमेन हृष्यंति (*saptahotṛkāḥ somena hṛṣyaṃti*). The word पृक्ष (*pṛkṣa*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9); here its meaning is explained as Hotṛs. स्वं लोकं यजमानस्य दधाति विदधाति इति स्वधा सोमः (*svaṃ lokaṃ yajamānasya dadhāti vidadhāti iti svadhā somaḥ*): because Soma grants the sacrificer a dwelling in the world where he himself dwells, Soma is denoted by the word स्वधा (*svadhā*). The meaning is that the seven Hotṛs are joyful from drinking the Soma.

व्रतपाः (*vratapāḥ*) — व्रतस्य यज्ञकर्मणो रक्षितारः (*vratasya yajñakarmaṇo rakṣitāraḥ*). The Nirukta-writers: व्रतमिति कर्मनाम वृणोतीति सतः । इदमपीतरत् व्रतमेतस्मादेव निवृत्तिकर्म वारयतीति सतः । अन्न- (*vratamiti karmanāma vṛṇotīti sataḥ | idamapītarat vratametasmādeva nivṛttikarma vārayatīti sataḥ | anna-*)

### Printed p. 36

मपि व्रतमुच्यते यदावृणोति शरीरं (*mapi vratamucyate yadāvṛṇoti śarīraṃ*) — thus they state the meaning of the word व्रत (*vrata*). From the root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*) the word व्रत (*vrata*) is formed in the agent sense: वृणोतीति व्रतं (*vṛṇotīti vrataṃ*). Because it attaches to the one who has done an act, whether good or bad, one kind of meaning of the word व्रत (*vrata*) is "action". Secondly, since it keeps off (prevents) others from approaching the fire (the altar), it may mean व्रत (*vrata*) in that sense; also, since it turns one away from pleasures of the senses such as intercourse with women, it is व्रत (*vrata*); or, since food, the cause of growth of the seven constituents of the body, covers the body, व्रत (*vrata*) is explained as food. Sāyaṇa has explained व्रत (*vrata*) as sacrificial action, and the word व्रतपाः (*vratapāḥ*) as the priests who protect it.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Words treated: दैव्या (*daivyā*) (suffix यञ् (*yañ*) in the sense of relation to a god by "देवाद्यञ्ञौ (*devādyaññau*)"; ādivṛddhi and initial-udātta accent; the dual ending replaced by ā by "सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*)"; likewise in होतारा (*hotārā*)). ऋंजे (*ṛṃje*) (root ऋजि भृजी भर्जने (*ṛji bhṛjī bharjane*); with the prefix नि (*ni*) the sense becomes "to adorn"; Yāska: ऋंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा (*ṛṃjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā*); augment नुम् (*num*) by इदितोनुम् धातोः (*iditonum dhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58); laṭ first person singular; finite-verb nighāta accent). पृक्षासः (*pṛkṣāsaḥ*) (आसुक् (*āsuk*) augment to जस् (*jas*) by अज्जसेरसुक् (*ajjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50)). स्वधया (*svadhayā*) (स्वं लोकं यजमानस्य दधाति विदधाति इति स्वधा सोमः (*svaṃ lokaṃ yajamānasya dadhāti vidadhāti iti svadhā somaḥ*), "Soma gives the sacrificer his divine world"; suffix क (*ka*) on the root धाज् (*dhāj*) by अतोनुपसर्गेकः (*atonupasargekaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-3); elision of the root's ā; feminine टाप् (*ṭāp*); accent of the final member by गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*)). शंसंत: (*śaṃsaṃta:*) (root शंसु स्तुत् (*śaṃsu stut*); शतृ (*śatṛ*) for laṭ; the sārvadhātuka is anudātta by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*), so the root accent remains; nominative plural). आहु: (*āhu:*) (root ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*); laṭ third plural; उस् (*us*) substituted for झि (*jhi*) and अह (*aha*) for the root by ब्रुवः पंचानामादित अहो ब्रुवः (*bruvaḥ paṃcānāmādita aho bruvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-84); para-rūpa; all-anudātta after a non-finite word). व्रतपा: (*vratapā:*) (व्रतं पांति इति व्रतपाः (*vrataṃ pāṃti iti vratapāḥ*); root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*), suffix विच् (*vic*); accent of the final member).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the great, wonderful one, is the showerer; his many extended rays act like rain-givers; the wise, most gladdening Hotṛ is asked to bring the great gods and heaven and earth to this rite. (The bhāṣya continues on the next page; the window ends in its grammatical tail on वृषायंते (*vṛṣāyaṃte*) and महे (*mahe*), transcribed, not explained.) Note: the supplied text shows a figure marker before the Saṃhitā; the Saṃhitā reads वृष्टायंते (*vṛṣṭāyaṃte*) against the Pada and bhāṣya वृषयंते (*vṛṣayaṃte*)/वृषायंते (*vṛṣāyaṃte*), and चरित्वान् (*caritvān*) in the Pada against चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*) expected; all as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*) — the shining one
- होतः (*hotaḥ*) — O Agni, who calls the gods to the sacrifices
- महे (*mahe*) — the worshipful
- अत्याय (*atyāya*) — who surpasses all
- चित्राय (*citrāya*) — of many hues (worshipful to the gods)
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*) — the showerer of desires, (for you)
- सुयामाः (*suyāmāḥ*) — exceedingly extended; पूर्वीः रश्मयः (*pūrvīḥ raśmayaḥ*) — countless rays
- व्यपायंते (*vyapāyaṃte*) [sic, as supplied] — act like Parjanya (by producing rain), and
- मंद्रतरः (*maṃdrataraḥ*) — the best among those who gratify
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*) — possessed of knowledge, you
- महः (*mahaḥ*) — the worshipful
- देवान् (*devān*) — the gods
- रोदसी (*rodasī*) — heaven and earth
- इह (*iha*) — to this rite; आ वह (*ā vaha*) — bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, shining one, who calls the gods to the sacrifices! To you, of great glory, mighty, of many hues (worshipful), showerer of desires, the countless, greatly extended flames become sprinklers by providing room for the casting in of ghee and other oblations; you, the best among those who gladden the worshippers, the wise one, bring to this Vedic rite the gods who are worthy of worship in the sacrifices, and heaven and earth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Divine invoker of the gods, the vast and widespread rays shed (moisture) for you the mighty, the victorious, the wonderful, the showerer (of benefits): you are all-knowing, joy-bestowing ; bring hither the great gods, and heaven and earth.

### Printed p. 39

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**देव होतः (*deva hotaḥ*)** — "the shining one, the invoker of the gods". Here Agni is described as blazing with abundant radiance and as the one who invites the gods to the sacrifice. In the passage "अस्य वामस्य फलितस्य होतुः (*asya vāmasya phalitasya hotuḥ*)" the word Hotṛ was explained as "the one who is invoked". For the word होतुः (*hotuḥ*) in "होतुश्चित्पूर्वे हविरद्यमाशत (*hotuścitpūrve haviradyamāśata*)" Durgācārya explains "होतुरपि अग्नेः (*hoturapi agneḥ*)": of Agni, who is in the form of a human Hotṛ; and (he states that) the greatness of the gods is described in four ways: the mantras are of the kinds पौरुषविध्यं (*pauruṣavidhyaṃ*), अपौरुषविध्यं (*apauruṣavidhyaṃ*), कर्मार्थात्मोभयविध्यं (*karmārthātmobhayavidhyaṃ*) and नित्यमौभयविध्यं (*nityamaubhayavidhyaṃ*) [all as supplied], and by these kinds the glory of the gods is made manifest. The gods are endowed with a power consisting of abundant lordship (aiśvarya) and act in the manner fitting their respective duties; the seers, beholders of the mantras, saw this directly and praised each in his own way; and the glory of the gods is described as mūrtā (having form), amūrtā (formless), ekadhā (of one kind), dvidhā (of two kinds) and bahudhā (of many kinds). Here Agni's power is described as his having attained identity with the human Hotṛ who invokes the gods.

**चित्राय (*citrāya*)** — "नानाविधवर्णाय यद्वा देवैश्चायनीयाय पूज्याय (*nānāvidhavarṇāya yadvā devaiścāyanīyāya pūjyāya*)". Sāyaṇa gives two meanings: first, that Agni has many kinds of colours through his rays; second, that Agni, receiving the oblation-portions even from the gods, is worshipful. The Nirukta-writers explain the word citra as "चायनीयं महनीयं पूजनीयं (*cāyanīyaṃ mahanīyaṃ pūjanīyaṃ*)", giving the sense of "worshipful, deserving honour".

**चित्रस्य रश्मयः वृषायंते (*citrasya raśmayaḥ vṛṣāyaṃte*)** — सर्वतः व्याप्ताः ज्वालाः वृषेवाचरंति सेचका इव भवंति । होतारः ज्वालाभिः समिद्धमग्निं दृष्ट्वा सोमाज्यपयःप्रभृतीनि हवींषि तत्र प्रक्षिपंतीति ज्वालानां वृषत्वं । यद्वा षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । तथा च महतो अत्यस्य चित्रस्य वृष्टो अग्नेः बहवो रश्मयः वृषेवाचरंति । वृष्टुत्पादनद्वारा पर्जन्यवदाचरंति । (*sarvataḥ vyāptāḥ jvālāḥ vṛṣevācaraṃti secakā iva bhavaṃti | hotāraḥ jvālābhiḥ samiddhamagniṃ dṛṣṭvā somājyapayaḥprabhṛtīni havīṃṣi tatra prakṣipaṃtīti jvālānāṃ vṛṣatvaṃ | yadvā ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī | tathā ca mahato atyasya citrasya vṛṣṭo agneḥ bahavo raśmayaḥ vṛṣevācaraṃti | vṛṣṭutpādanadvārā parjanyavadācaraṃti |*) (The supplied text reads "ಚಿತ್ರಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ" and "ಚಿತ್ರಸ್ಯ ರಶ್ಮಯಃ" at this point, and "ವೃಷ್ಟೋ ಅಗ್ನೇಃ" in the quotation; all as supplied.) This is the same bhāṣya passage already summarised under the Ṛk: the flames spread on all sides act as showerers (sprinklers), since the Hotṛs, seeing Agni kindled by the flames, cast Soma, ghee, milk and other oblations into it; or the dative is in the sense of the genitive, so that the many rays of the great, wonderful, showering Agni act like a rain-giver.

A verse on the seven tongues of Agni follows (as supplied, with a gap of dots in the first line):

काळी कराळीचॆ मनोजवाच..................सुधूम्रवर्णा । (*kāḷī karāḷīcè manojavāca..................sudhūmravarṇā |*)
स्पुलिंगिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥ (*spuliṃginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ‖*)

### Printed p. 40

The various flames of Agni, or the rays described in this mantra, spreading everywhere and fulfilling the wishes of the sacrificers, act like Indra, who fulfils the wishes of those who serve him. The Hotṛ and other priests, pouring Soma juice, ghee (clarified butter), oblations and the like into the well-kindled fire, obtain their desired ends; therefore Sāyaṇa explains, as one meaning, that the flames of Agni grant what is desired and, like Indra, bestow wishes. In the second meaning, the dative case in चित्राय (*citrāya*) stands in the sense of the genitive, so that it is चित्रस्य ज्वालाः (*citrasya jvālāḥ*): the flames of the worshipful Agni, shining in many ways and accepting the oblation-portions offered by the sacrificers, become rain-producers (since they cause rain to fall) and do the work of Indra, the production of rain. Hence he explains वृषायंते वृषेवाचरंति (*vṛṣāyaṃte vṛṣevācaraṃti*). Thus the sense is given in two ways: because Agni's flames, kindled and widely spread, accept the oblations offered by the sacrificers and fulfil their wishes, or because, endowed with many colours, they produce rain, they do for Agni and for the world the work of Indra, the fulfilment of desired ends.

**मंद्रतरः (*maṃdrataraḥ*)** — "यजमानस्य मादयितृतमः (*yajamānasya mādayitṛtamaḥ*)". Because Agni fulfils the wishes of the sacrificers, he makes them joyful and exhilarated; this is the meaning. It is said: "मंद्रा मदना हर्षकरी तर्पयित्री वा लोकस्य (*maṃdrā madanā harṣakarī tarpayitrī vā lokasya*)" (Ni. 11-30).

**महः देवा, रोदसी इह आ वह (*mahaḥ devā, rodasī iha ā vaha*)** — By this sentence, since Agni also performs the Hotṛ's function (inviting the gods to the sacrifice), he is prayed to invite to the sacrificial rite the gods who are worshipful and worthy of sacrifice, and also heaven and earth. The word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is read among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

वृषायंते (*vṛṣāyaṃte*): "वृषा इव आचरंति (*vṛṣā iva ācaraṃti*)"; from the sūtra "उपमानादाचारे (*upamānādācāre*)" with उपमानात् (*upamānāt*) continuing, the suffix क्यज् (*kyaj*) comes after the word वृष (*vṛṣa*) by "कर्तुः क्यज् सलोपश्च (*kartuḥ kyaj salopaśca*)" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-11); lengthening of the preceding vowel by "अकृत् सार्वधातुकयोर्दिर्घः (*akṛt sārvadhātukayordirghaḥ*)" (Pā. Sū. 7-4-25); by "सनाद्यंताधातवः (*sanādyaṃtādhātavaḥ*)" the form वृषाय (*vṛṣāya*) gets the name dhātu; the laṭ third-person plural form stands at the beginning of a pāda, so the nighāta accent does not arise; the root accent remains.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, ever-moving, is addressed; the dawns, with abundant oblation-foods, fair speech (morning recitations) and clear signs by the sounds of birds and men, are to dawn for us bringing wealth; and he is asked to destroy whatever sin, such as injury to living creatures, has been committed, by the greatness of his wide flame, for the worshipper. The grammatical tail (दविणः, सुवाचः, रेवत्, ऊषुः, पृथिव्याः) is transcribed, not explained; the bhāṣya continues on the next page.

### Printed p. 43

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> न्नियोगेन धातोः संप्रसारणं । षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्चति जीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतो-
> दात्तः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । दशस्य । निघातः ॥

*Note: the grammatical tail ends with पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*) and दशस्य (*daśasya*); transcribed, not explained.*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O) ever-moving one (द्रविणः (*draviṇaḥ*)), O Agni; the dawns (उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)) that have much oblation-food and the like offered in the fire (प्रैक्षप्रयजः (*praikṣaprayajaḥ*) [sic, as supplied]); that are possessed of fair speech such as the morning recitation (सुवाचः (*suvācaḥ*)); that are indicative by words such as the "prakṣa" cries (सुकेतवः (*suketavaḥ*)); rise (ऊषुः (*ūṣuḥ*)) endowed with wealth (that is to be given to us) (रेवत् (*revat*)). And (उतो चित् (*uto cit*)), O Agni (अग्ने (*agne*)), for me, the respected (sacrificer) (महे (*mahe*)), whatever sin (चित् एनः (*cit enaḥ*)), such as injury to living creatures, that has been accumulated (कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)), by the greatness (महिना (*mahinā*)) of your exceedingly wide flame (पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)), destroy completely (सं दशस्य (*saṃ daśasya*)).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O ever-moving Agni, may the dawns, endowed with the morning recitations and other praises, with oblations and the like offered in the fire, and with the awakening "prakṣa" cries and the like, rise for us as givers of wealth and the rest; and, O Agni, whatever sin, such as injury to living creatures, has been committed by us, destroy it for me, the respected one, by your greatly extended flame.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ever-moving (Agni) may the mornings rise for us, abounding with oblatio ns [sic], with pious prayers, and with auspicious signs, and conferring wealth ; and with the might of your (diffusive flame), consume all sin on behalf of your respectable (worshipper).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**द्रविणः (*draviṇaḥ*)** — "द्रवति सततं गच्छति इति द्रविणशब्देन अग्निरभिधीयते (*dravati satataṃ gacchati iti draviṇaśabdena agnirabhidhīyate*)". The word द्रविण (*draviṇa*), formed from the root द्रु (*dru*) meaning "to go", means "one who is always moving"; so the meaning given here is that Agni has the nature of ever moving about. The Nirukta-writers read the word द्रविण (*draviṇa*) among the names of strength and also among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9).

**पृक्षप्रयजः (*pṛkṣaprayajaḥ*)** — "पृक्षाणि हविर्लक्षणान्नानि प्रकर्षेण यष्टुं प्रक्रम्यते यासु उषस्सु ताः (*pṛkṣāṇi havirlakṣaṇānnāni prakarṣeṇa yaṣṭuṃ prakramyate yāsu uṣassu tāḥ*)". The Nirukta-writers read the word पृक्ष (*pṛkṣa*) among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa explains पृक्ष (*pṛkṣa*) as food in the form of oblation, and explains that the time at which this oblation-food is offered abundantly (excessively) in the fire is the time of dawn.

### Printed p. 44

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**सुवाचः (*suvācaḥ*)** — "प्रातरनुवाकादिशोभना वाचो यासां ताः (*prātaranuvākādiśobhanā vāco yāsāṃ tāḥ*)". The time at which the priests recite in the sacrifice the mantras belonging to the morning, and the (auspicious) words of good meaning recited to wake Agni, is full of such utterances; hence the word सुवाचः (*suvācaḥ*) is used as an epithet of the dawn.

**सुकेशवः (*sukeśavaḥ*)** [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā word is सुकेतवः (*suketavaḥ*)] — The word केतु (*ketu*) is read among the names of intelligence (Ni. 3-13). In अह्नां केतुः (*ahnāṃ ketuḥ*) the word केतु (*ketu*) means "mark, sign" (Ni. 11-6). केतुना कर्मणा प्रज्ञया वा (*ketunā karmaṇā prajñayā vā*) (Ni. 11-27): by केतु (*ketu*) is meant action or intelligence. In देवं वहंति केशवः (*devaṃ vahaṃti keśavaḥ*), केशवः रश्मयः (*keśavaḥ raśmayaḥ*) (Ni. 12-17) gives "rays". So the word has several meanings: intelligence, action, mark, ray. Sāyaṇa, taking the word as an epithet of the dawn, says वयसां मनुष्याणां च शब्दैः सुप्रज्ञानाः (*vayasāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ca śabdaiḥ suprajñānāḥ*): at dawn men and birds make sounds, the whole world wakes, and so it is the time that gives all the world the knowledge needed for its business.

**उषसः रेवत् ऊषुः (*uṣasaḥ revat ūṣuḥ*)** — "एवंविधाः उषसः अस्माकं धनयुक्तं यथा भवति तथा व्युच्छंति (*evaṃvidhāḥ uṣasaḥ asmākaṃ dhanayuktaṃ yathā bhavati tathā vyucchaṃti*)". The word उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) is explained (Ni. 2-19): उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति, सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (*uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti, satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ*). Formed from the root उच्छ (*uccha*) meaning "to dispel" (vivāsana), उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) is the last part of the night, which destroys darkness. The dawns, according to the epithets given here, act so that the sacrificers become wealthy.

**पृथिव्या: (*pṛthivyā:*)** — "विस्तीर्णायाः ज्वालायाः (*vistīrṇāyāḥ jvālāyāḥ*)". The word पृथ्वि (*pṛthvi*) is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5) and of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). Here the word पृथ्वी (*pṛthvī*), formed from the adjective पृथु (*pṛthu*), is used as पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*) by Vedic usage. The meaning can be explained as: Agni's flame is abundant, spread everywhere.

**एनः (*enaḥ*)** — "प्राण्युपघातलक्षणं पापं (*prāṇyupaghātalakṣaṇaṃ pāpaṃ*)". When explaining the words किल्पिषं (*kilpiṣaṃ*) and एनः (*enaḥ*) the Nirukta-writers say सुकृतकर्मणो भयं एनः (*sukṛtakarmaṇo bhayaṃ enaḥ*): it destroys meritorious acts. एनः एतेः (*enaḥ eteḥ*) (Ni. 11-25): the word एनः (*enaḥ*), from the root इण् (*iṇ*) "to go", is explained as what unfailingly comes and joins at the proper time. Accordingly Sāyaṇa explains that sin checks the force of meritorious action and brings the creature into trouble.

**अग्ने (*agne*)** — "पृथिव्याः ज्वालायाः महिना चित् एनः महे संदशस्य विस्तीर्णायाः ज्वालायाः महत्वेन यत्किंचित् पापं महते यजमानाय मह्यं संक्षपय (*pṛthivyāḥ jvālāyāḥ mahinā cit enaḥ mahe saṃdaśasya vistīrṇāyāḥ jvālāyāḥ mahatvena yatkiṃcit pāpaṃ mahate yajamānāya mahyaṃ saṃkṣapaya*)"

### Printed p. 45

Addressing Agni, the prayer is that he destroy the sacrificer's sins by the greatness of his abundant flames.

The Nirukta-writers explain the word Agni thus: अग्निः कस्मात् अग्रणीर्भवति अग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणेयते अंगं नयति सन्नममानः (*agniḥ kasmāt agraṇīrbhavati agraṃ yajñeṣu praṇeyate aṃgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ*). Durgācārya explains the analysis अग्रं नयति अग्रणीः भवति (*agraṃ nayati agraṇīḥ bhavati*): the word अग्र (*agra*) means "chief"; सर्वेष्टर्थेषु असावात्मानं अग्रं नयति सेनां वा अग्रे नयति अग्निर्वैदेवानां सेनानीः इति श्रुतेः (*sarveṣṭartheṣu asāvātmānaṃ agraṃ nayati senāṃ vā agre nayati agnirvaidevānāṃ senānīḥ iti śruteḥ*). He takes the first place in all necessary duties; or, being the commander of the gods' armies, Agni leads the gods' army. This is one kind of meaning. Secondly, in sacrifices the fire is prepared first, before all necessary duties; hence the meaning अग्रं प्रणीयते इति अग्निः (*agraṃ praṇīyate iti agniḥ*). Thirdly, wherever he enters he himself is chief and brings all else under his control; hence अंगं नयतीति अग्निः (*aṃgaṃ nayatīti agniḥ*). In all worldly and Vedic works, and even in grass and wood, when Agni has entered and is connected, he keeps the position of being chief; whatever is connected with Agni stays subordinate to him. This is the purport.

The teacher Sthaulāṣṭhivi [sic, as supplied] says अकोपनो भवति न स्नेहयति (*akopano bhavati na snehayati*), and describes Agni's quality: he makes the thing that joins him (that is connected with him) take another form. The teacher Śākapūṇi explains the formation of the word Agni: it is from इतात् (*itāt*), अक्ताद्वा दग्धाद्वा नीतात् (*aktādvā dagdhādvā nītāt*), that is, from the three roots इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*), अंजू व्यक्तिश्लक्ष्ययोः (*aṃjū vyaktiślakṣyayoḥ*), दह भस्मीकरणे (*daha bhasmīkaraṇe*), with the element नी (*nī*) from the root णीज् प्रापणे (*ṇīj prāpaṇe*) added, the form अग्नि (*agni*) results. The Nirukta-writers quote the Ṛk

> ⟦अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्वजं । होतारं रत्नधातमं ॥⟧ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1)

> *⟦agnimīḷe purohitaṃ yajñasya devamṛtvajaṃ | hotāraṃ ratnadhātamaṃ ‖⟧ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1)*

and say that this Agni is called the terrestrial fire, while the other forms of Agni, such as Jātavedas, are spoken of as middle and highest. In this terrestrial fire the sacrificers invoke the other fires according to the respective rites, to suit their sacrifice. Hence Agni has the identity of all the gods; the Brāhmaṇa sentence अग्निः सर्वा देवताः (*agniḥ sarvā devatāḥ*) and

### Printed p. 46

> ⟦इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान् । एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदंत्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ॥⟧ (Ma. [sic, as supplied] Saṃ. 1-164-46)

> *⟦iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuratho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān | ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadaṃtyagniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānamāhuḥ ‖⟧ (Ma. [sic, as supplied] Saṃ. 1-164-46)*

this mantra too make clear that Agni has the nature of all the gods.

But: यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरुप्यते आयमेव सोऽग्निः। निपातमेवैते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी एतेन नामधेयेन भजेते (*yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirupyate āyameva so 'gniḥ| nipātamevaite uttare jyotiṣī etena nāmadheyena bhajete*) (Ni. 2-7-18). The Agni who is chiefly praised in the various rites, and for whom oblations are prepared with Vedic mantras, is spoken of as the terrestrial fire. The other fires, though in the position of highest and middle (the lightning fire, Jātavedas), are not so spoken of in the world by sentences such as अग्निमानय (*agnimānaya*) ("bring fire"); and अग्नियेषु सूक्तेषु हविः संप्रदानेषु स्तुत्यत्वेन भोक्तृत्वेन चैतदेवोपासीत (*agniyeṣu sūkteṣu haviḥ saṃpradāneṣu stutyatvena bhoktṛtvena caitadevopāsīta*): this terrestrial fire, which is praised in the hymns that describe Agni and is the recipient in the giving of oblations, is to be worshipped, so the injunction says. तस्मादग्निशब्देन पार्थिवस्य ज्योतिषः मुख्यस्संबंधः गौण इतरयोर्मध्यमोत्तमयोः (*tasmādagniśabdena pārthivasya jyotiṣaḥ mukhyassaṃbaṃdhaḥ gauṇa itarayormadhyamottamayoḥ*). Hence the chief sense of the word Agni is that the terrestrial fire is worshipped; the middle and highest rank of the other deities, designated through Agni's all-selfhood, is secondary here, as Durgācārya explains.

**चित् (*cit*)** — The Nirukta-writers say अप्युपमार्थेऽपि कर्मोपसंग्रहार्थेऽपि पदपूरणाः (*apyupamārthe 'pi karmopasaṃgrahārthe 'pi padapūraṇāḥ*): particles may convey comparison, or some meaning, or merely fill out the sentence — three uses. Then चिदितैषो अनेककर्मा, आचार्यश्चिदिदं ब्रूयादिति पूजायां, दधिचिदित्युपमार्थे, कुल्माषांश्चिदाहरेति अवकुत्सिते (*ciditaiṣo anekakarmā, ācāryaścididaṃ brūyāditi pūjāyāṃ, dadhicidityupamārthe, kulmāṣāṃścidāhareti avakutsite*): the particle चित् (*cit*) has several functions: comparison in ददि चित् (*dadi cit*) [sic, as supplied], respect in आचार्यश्चित् (*ācāryaścit*), contempt (disparagement) in कुल्माषांश्चित् (*kulmāṣāṃścit*). In places other than these it conveys only the general filling-out of the sentence; the supplied text ends this passage with a sentence that it prints as "इल्ल पदपूरणफलकवागि अनर्थकवागुवुदु (*illa padapūraṇaphalakavāgi anarthakavāguvudu*)" (as supplied: it becomes meaningless as a mere filler).

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इळा॑मग्ने पुरु॒दंसं॑ स॒निं गोः श॑श्वत्त॒मं हव॑मानाय साध ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

(The Pada reads तश्वर्तमं (*taśvartamaṃ*) where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya read शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*); noted as supplied.)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is asked to grant the sacrificer the cow-formed deity Iḷā, giver of cattle and doer of many works, perpetually; and that sons and grandsons be ours and his good will be fruitful for us. The grammatical tail treats śaśvattamam, sādha, vijāvā and bhūtu; transcribed, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O) Agni (अग्ने (*agne*)): endowed with many works (पुरुदंसं (*purudaṃsaṃ*)), and the giver of cattle such as cows (गोः सनिं (*goḥ saniṃ*)), the deity named Iḷā in the form of a cow (इळां (*iḷāṃ*)); perpetually (शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)), to me who am performing the sacrifice (हवमानाय (*havamānāya*)), accomplish (grant) (साध (*sādha*)). To us (नः (*naḥ*)), may there be a son (सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)) and a grandson (तनयः (*tanayaḥ*)) (so) (स्यात् (*syāt*)). O Agni (अग्ने (*agne*)), whatever good will (सुमतिः (*sumatiḥ*)) you have (ते (*te*)), that (सा (*sā*)) for our sake (अस्मे (*asme*)) may be unbarren (विजावा (*vijāvā*)), may it become so (भूतु (*bhūtu*)).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, make the earth, named Iḷā and in the form of a cow, who gives cattle and the like that are helpful to many rites, favourable to us who are engaged in the continuous performance of sacrifice; and, O Agni, may that gracious intention of yours to bestow sons, grandsons and the like on the worshippers be ever unbarren (fruitful) for us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Grant, Agni, to the offerer of the oblation, earth the bestower of cattle, the means of many (pious rites), such that it may be perpetual : may there be to us sons and grandsons, and may your good-will ever be productive of benefits to us.
