##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Hē yūpa — O yūpa) समिद्दस्य (*samiddasya*) [sic, the Saṃhitā has samiddhasya]: of the kindled Āhavanīya fire. पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*): in front, to the east. श्रयमाणः (*śrayamāṇaḥ*): being (there). अजरं (*ajaraṃ*): free from decay (loss). सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*): endowed with good sons and the like. ब्रह्म (*brahma*): food. वन्वानः (*vanvānaḥ*): giving. अस्मदमतिं (*asmadamatiṃ*): our enemy. आरे (*āre*): far away. बाधमानः (*bādhamānaḥ*): driving (him away). महते (*mahate*): for great. सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*): wealth and other prosperity. उत् श्रयस्व (*ut śrayasva*): be raised up (stand up).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O yūpa, established in the east of the kindled Āhavanīya fire, bestow on us food that is imperishable and joined with good offspring; keep our enemy far away and (there) destroy him; and stand up as the giver to us of great wealth and the like. (Stand up.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Standing on the east of the kindled (fire), dispensing food (as the source) of undecaying (health) and excellent progeny, keeping off our enemy at a distance, stand up for great auspiciousness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

समिद्धस्य श्रयमाणः पुरस्तात् (*samiddhasya śrayamāṇaḥ purastāt*) — दीप्यमानस्याहवनीयाग्नेः प्राच्यां दिशि वर्तमानः (*dīpyamānasyāhavanīyāgneḥ prācyāṃ diśi vartamānaḥ*) (being in the east of the kindled Āhavanīya fire). In the sacrificial hall the fire is divided and set in three places. Gārhapatya, (the passage stops at the end of this page and continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 83

(Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 82.) Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇāgni are the names of these three fires. Of these, the fire called Āhavanīya is well kindled in the eastern part of the vedi. The meaning is that the yūpa stands to the east of it.

अजरं (*ajaraṃ*) — जरारहितं समृद्धं (*jarārahitaṃ samṛddhaṃ*) (free from decay, prosperous). The author of the Nirukta explains the word ajara as अजरणधर्माणं (*ajaraṇadharmāṇaṃ*) , "that which does not grow old" (Ni. 4-27). Sāyaṇa too gives the meaning "that which is free from old age and is increasing (prosperous)".

सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*) — The author of the Nirukta (the supplied text prints निमुक्तकाररु (*nimuktakāraru*), evidently a misprint for Nirukta-kāra) explains the word vīra: वीरवंतः कल्याणवीरा वा वीरो वीरयत्यमित्रान् वेतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मणः वीरयतेर्वा (*vīravaṃtaḥ kalyāṇavīrā vā vīro vīrayatyamitrān vetervā syādgatikarmaṇaḥ vīrayatervā*) (Ni. 1-7): one who harasses enemies in many ways, one who marches against the enemies, one endowed with valour. In

वनस्पते वीड्वंगो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणस्सुवीरः (*vanaspate vīḍvaṃgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇassuvīraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-26, as given in the supplied text, "ಮ. ಸಂ.")

the meaning "suvīra = of good valour" is given. Durgācārya explains it as "one who is not timid, who does not fall under the control of others". Sāyaṇa here takes the word as an adjective of the word brahma and explains शोभनापत्ययुक्तं (*śobhanāpatyayuktaṃ*) as food that produces excellent sons.

ब्रह्म (*brahma*) — food. The word brahman is listed among the names of food (Ni. 3-7) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). Here the meaning "food" is given, and it is prayed that the fire within the yūpa, spoken of by the word vanaspati, should produce such food. Further: "driving away our enemy" (अस्मदमतिं बाधमानः (*asmadamatiṃ bādhamānaḥ*)) means destroying the sacrificers' enemy called hunger; "for great good fortune" (महते सौभगाय (*mahate saubhagāya*)) means "be capable of producing exceptional wealth"; thus it is invoked. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passage explains the purport of this Ṛk (the passage is given in the bhāṣya also; the supplied text prints it in Kannada script, with the readings ब्रह्मवन्वानो आजरं (*brahmavanvāno ājaraṃ*) and बाधदान (*bādhadāna*) as supplied, which differ from the Sanskrit bhāṣya above, ब्रह्म वन्वानो अजरं and बाधमानः):

समिद्धस्य श्रयमाणः पुरस्तादिति समिद्धस्य ह्येष एतत् पुरस्ताच्छ्रयते (*samiddhasya śrayamāṇaḥ purastāditi samiddhasya hyeṣa etat purastācchrayate*) ब्रह्मवन्वानो आजरं सुवीरमित्याशिषमेवाशास्त्र आरे अस्मदमतिं (*brahmavanvāno ājaraṃ suvīramityāśiṣamevāśāstra āre asmadamatiṃ*) बाधदान इत्यशनाया वै पाप्मामतिस्तामेव तदारान्नुदते (*bādhadāna ityaśanāyā vai pāpmāmatistāmeva tadārānnudate*) इत्याशिषमेवाशास्त्रे (*ityāśiṣamevāśāstre*) (Ai. Brā. 2-2, as printed इ. ब्रा. २-२ (*i. brā. 2-2*)). (Meaning: it asks the blessing for the sacrificer; hunger is the sinful enemy; the yūpa drives it far from the sacrifice and the sacrificer.)

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes (pp. 83–85), noted briefly. On p. 83: समिद्धस्य (*samiddhasya*), printed समिद्दस्य (*samiddasya*) in the supplied text: prefix sam, root इइंधी दीप्तौ (*iiṃdhī dīptau*), the past participle suffix (nishthā, Pā. 3-2-102); because the root has long ī marked (ītit) the augment iṭ does not come (Pā. 7-2-14, on p. 84).

### Printed p. 84

(Grammar notes, continued.) Loss of the nasal of the root, dh for t of the suffix (jhaṣastathoḥ), the gati takes the udātta (Pā. 9-2-49, as printed). श्रयमाणः (*śrayamāṇaḥ*): root śriñ sevāyām, śānac for laṭ, śap, guṇa, ayādeśa, muk augment (Pā. 7-2-82), ṇatva; the root accent remains (Pā. 6-1-186). पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*): the suffix astāti (Pā. 5-3-27), substitute pura for pūrva (Pā. 5-3-40). ब्रह्म (*brahma*): initial udātta by the Phiṭ rule 29 . वन्वानः (*vanvānaḥ*): root vanu yācane, used here in the sense of giving (the supplied text says दीनार्थ (*dīnārtha*), as supplied); śānac; final udātta (Pā. 6-1-183). अजरम् (*ajaram*): Pā. 6-2-116, initial udātta of the latter member. सुवीरम् (*suvīram*): Pā. 6-2-120. आरे (*āre*): from the group evamādi, final udātta. अस्मत् (*asmat*): Uṇ. 1-136, suffix madik; luk of the case ending. अमतिम् (*amatim*): negative tatpuruṣa, Pā. 6-2-2, accent of the first member. उत् (*ut*): nipāta, initial udātta. श्रयस्व (*śrayasva*): root śriñ sevāyām, loṭ, thās, replaced by se (supplied as पा. दू. ३-४-८० (*pā. dū. 3-4-80*)), then va for e (Pā. 3-4-91 on the next page), guṇa and ayādeśa, nighāta accent as it follows a non-verb... (as supplied: it stands after a finite verb-form).

### Printed p. 85

(Grammar notes, concluded.) महते (*mahate*): root maha pūjāyām; Uṇ. 2-2-41, "mahat" is made by nipāta, hence final accent; the case ending in the dative singular is udātta by the vārttika on bṛhat and mahat. सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*): the suffix añ (Pā. 5-1-129), vṛddhi of the first member (Pā. 7-3-19), but vṛddhi of the latter member does not occur, since all rules are optional in the Veda; initial udātta; a form of the dative singular.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

(begun on this page; the sense is quoted from the Brāhmaṇa)

> हे वनस्पते यूप पृथिव्या अधि पृथिव्यां वर्ष्मन् उत्कृष्टे देवयज-
> नाख्ये देश उच्छ्रयस्व । उच्चैतो भव । सुमिती शोभमानिया बुद्धा अथवा
> शोभनेन परिमाणेन मीयमान इयत्तया परिच्छिद्यमानस्य यज्ञवाहसे
> यज्ञनिर्वाहकाय यजमानाय वर्चो धाः । अन्नं धेहि । अयमेवार्थो
> ब्राह्मणेन दर्शितः । उच्छ्रयस्व वनस्पत इत्युच्छ्रियमाणायाभिरूपा यद्यज्ञेऽभि-
> रूपं तत्समृद्धं । वर्ष्मन्पृथिव्या अधीत्येतद्वै वर्ष पृथिव्यै यत्र यूपमुन्नि-
> न्वंति सुमिती मीयमानो वर्चो धा यज्ञवाहस इत्याशिषमाशास्ते । ऐ. प्रा.
> २-२ ॥ वनस्पते । अपादादित्वादाष्टमिकमनुदात्तत्वं । पृथिव्याः । उदात्तयणो

(Gist: O yūpa, vanaspati, rise up on the earth in the excellent sacrificial place; being well measured, bestow food on the sacrificer. The bhāṣya continues on the next page; its grammatical tail begins with वनस्पते (*vanaspate*) and पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*).)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(He vanaspate — O yūpa, you) पृथिव्या अधि (*pṛthivyā adhi*): upon the earth. वर्ष्मन् (*varṣman*): in the excellent sacrificial hall. उच्छ्रयस्व (*ucchrayasva*): stand up, rise. सुमिती (*sumitī*): by an auspicious intellect (or by a good measure). मीयमानः (*mīyamānaḥ*): being measured (so that it is just so much). यज्ञवाहसे (*yajñavāhase*): to the sacrificer, the one who accomplishes the sacrifice. वर्चःधाः (*varcaḥdhāḥ*) : bestow food.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O yūpa, stand up in this excellent sacrificial house on the earth. Cut to the proper measure, bestow food and the like upon the performer of the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Be exalted, VANASPATI, upon this sacred spot of earth. being [sic, lower case after the full stop, as printed] measured with careful measurement, and bestow food upon the offerer of the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वर्ष्मन्—उत्कृष्टे देवयजनाख्ये देशे (*varṣman—utkṛṣṭe devayajanākhye deśe*) — Since Sāyaṇa takes this word to be in the locative case, he explains the meaning as: in the excellent region of the sacrificial altar on the earth (above, on the surface). The region where oblations are offered to the gods is well known as the devayajana-deśa ("place of worship of the gods"). The meaning is that in this region the yūpa shines, standing high with its height.

सुमिती मीयमानः—शोभनया बुद्ध्या अथवा शोभनेन परिमाणेन इयत्तया परिच्छिद्यमानः (*sumitī mīyamānaḥ—śobhanayā buddhyā athavā śobhanena parimāṇena iyattayā paricchidyamānaḥ*) — Sāyaṇa gives a twofold meaning here. First he makes the word sumiti mean sumati, an auspicious intellect; second, an excellent measure consisting of height; and in both ways he describes the yūpa as being limited (measured).

### Printed p. 87

यज्ञवाहसे वर्चोधाः—यज्ञनिर्वाहकाय यजमानाय अन्नं धेहि (*yajñavāhase varcodhāḥ—yajñanirvāhakāya yajamānāya annaṃ dhehi*) — It is desired that the fire within the yūpa should grant food to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice. The word वर्चः (*varcaḥ*) is listed among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). And Sāyaṇa quotes the following passage, which conveys this meaning:

उच्छयस्व वनस्पत इत्युच्चीयमाणायाभिरूपा यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं वर्ष्मन् पृथिव्या अधीत्यैतद्वै वर्ष पृथिव्यै यत्र यूपमुन्मिन्वंति सुमिती मीयमानो वर्चो धा यज्ञवाहस इत्याशिषमाशस्ते (*ucchayasva vanaspata ityuccīyamāṇāyābhirūpā yadyajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ varṣman pṛthivyā adhītyaitadvai varṣa pṛthivyai yatra yūpamunminvaṃti sumitī mīyamāno varco dhā yajñavāhasa ityāśiṣamāśaste*) (Ai. Brā. 2-2).

He cites this Brāhmaṇa passage.

अधि पृथिव्यां (*adhi pṛthivyāṃ*) — The word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) is stated both in the sense of earth (Ni. 2-5) and in the sense of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). Citing the Ṛk

बळित्था पर्वतानां खिद्रं बिभर्षि पृथिवि । प्र या भूमिं प्रवत्वति मह्ना जिनोषि मॆहिनि । (*baḷitthā parvatānāṃ khidraṃ bibharṣi pṛthivi | pra yā bhūmiṃ pravatvati mahnā jinoṣi mèhini |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-84-1)

the author of the Nirukta (the passage as supplied lacks its closing bracket) explains:

सत्यं त्वं पर्वतानां मेघानां खेदनं छेदनं भेदनं बलममुत्र धारयसि पृथिवि प्रजिन्वसि या भूमिं प्रवणवति महत्त्वेन महतीत्युदकवशीति वा (*satyaṃ tvaṃ parvatānāṃ meghānāṃ khedanaṃ chedanaṃ bhedanaṃ balamamutra dhārayasi pṛthivi prajinvasi yā bhūmiṃ pravaṇavati mahattvena mahatītyudakavaśīti vā*) (Ni. 11-39).

The meaning is explained thus: the middle-region deity called Pṛthivī endures the splitting of mountains and clouds; besides being endowed with abundant strength, she makes the earth rich in water and is full of majesty.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes, noted briefly. वनस्पते (*vanaspate*): being listed in the pāraskara group it receives the augment suṭ; in the vocative, standing at the beginning of the pāda, the amantrita nighāta accent applies. वर्ष्मन् (*varṣman*): root वृषु सेचने (*vṛṣu secane*), suffix manin; guṇa of the light penultimate vowel (puganta-laghūpadhasya ca); initial udātta because the suffix is marked ṇit; luk for the locative ending by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. 7-1-39). पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*): udātta on the case ending by उदात्तयणो हल् पूर्वात् (*udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt*) (Pā. 6-1-174). सुमिति (*sumiti*): root माज् माने (*māj māne*), suffix ktin (Pā. 3-3-94); by dyatisyatimāsthā (Pā. 7-4-40) the root vowel is replaced by i before a suffix beginning with t and marked k; the udātta of the preceding gati (su) remains (Pā. 6-2-360, as printed); in the instrumental singular the preceding-similar long vowel replaces by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*).

### Printed p. 88

(Grammar notes, continued; the p. 87 sentence on सुमिति (*sumiti*) ends at the top of this page with the word प्रत्यय (*pratyaya*).) मीयमानः (*mīyamānaḥ*): root माज् माने (*māj māne*); śānac for laṭ in the passive; yak (Pā. 3-1-67); ī for the root vowel (Pā. 6-4-66, as printed); muk augment; the yak accent remains since śānac is anudātta. धाः (*dhāḥ*): root डुधाज् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāj dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); luṅ in the sense of loṭ in the Veda; sip in the second person singular; loss of its i (Pā. 3-4-100); loss of sic (Pā. 2-4-77); no augment aṭ (Pā. 6-4-75); nighāta accent after a finite verb. यज्ञवाहसे (*yajñavāhase*): यज्ञं वहति (प्राप्नोति) यज्ञवाहाः तस्मै (*yajñaṃ vahati (prāpnoti) yajñavāhāḥ tasmai*); root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*); suffix asun (Uṇ. 4-660); ṇidvadbhāva by anuvṛtti of ṇit; vṛddhi of the penultimate a (Pā. 7-2116, as printed); accent of the first member (Uṇ. 4-666); a dative singular form.

Gist: the yūpa is strong-limbed (youthful) and well clad, girt about with the rope; it comes and becomes the best of all trees, and the wise priests, desiring the gods, raise it up. The Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa passage is cited (Ai. Brā. 2-2, printed ऐ. ब्रा. २-२ (*ai. brā. 2-2*)). The grammatical tail covers युवा (*yuvā*), सुवासाः (*suvāsāḥ*), परिवीतः (*parivītaḥ*), अगात् (*agāt*), श्रेयान् (*śreyān*), स्वाध्यः (*svādhyaḥ*) and देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*) (not transcribed further here).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

युवा (*yuvā*): strong-limbed. सुवासाः (*suvāsāḥ*): having good cloth (rope). परिवीतः (*parivītaḥ*): (by it) surrounded; the yūpa so described. आगात् (*āgāt*): comes. सः उ (*saḥ u*): that very yūpa. श्रेयान् जायमानः भवति (*śreyān jāyamānaḥ bhavati*): is excellent (above all trees). तं (*taṃ*): that yūpa. धीरासः (*dhīrāsaḥ*): the wise. मनसा (*manasā*): with the mind. देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*): desiring the gods. स्वाध्यः (*svādhyaḥ*): those who meditate well. कवयः (*kavayaḥ*): the far-seeing adhvaryus and others. उत् नयंति (*ut nayaṃti*): raise upward.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The strong yūpa, covered with good cloth, comes; that same yūpa is regarded as the most excellent of all trees; this very yūpa, the wise ones, who desire the gods to come to the sacrifice, who are intent on meditation, far-seeing, the adhvaryu

### Printed p. 90

(Bhāvārtha, continued from p. 89:) and others, raise upward.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Well clad and hung with wreaths comes the youthful (pillar): most excellent it is as soon as generated : steadfast and wise venerators of the gods. meditating [sic, lower case after the full stop, as printed] piously in their minds raise it up.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

युवा—दृढांग: अष्टाश्रादिलक्षणलक्षितः (*yuvā—dṛḍhāṃga: aṣṭāśrādilakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ*) — The tree brought from the forest for the yūpa is hewn so that it has eight corners and is then planted. This is what Sāyaṇa explains as "having strong limbs (aṅga, parts)" and as having eight edges, being in the prescribed manner.

सुवासाः—शोभनेन वाससा रशनया युक्तः (*suvāsāḥ—śobhanena vāsasā raśanayā yuktaḥ*) — The yūpa, surrounded with excellent cloth and with rope, सर्वेभ्यो वनस्पतिभ्य उत्कृष्टतया संपद्यमानो भवति (*sarvebhyo vanaspatibhya utkṛṣṭatayā saṃpadyamāno bhavati*): the meaning is described as being better than all the trees in the forest.

कवयः मनसा देवयंतः स्वाध्यः उन्नयंति (*kavayaḥ manasā devayaṃtaḥ svādhyaḥ unnayaṃti*) — By this sentence the meaning is explained: the wise priests, the adhvaryu and others, meditating on the gods and invoking them to the sacrifice, regard this yūpa as most excellent and lift it up in order to plant it. The word kavi is listed among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). मेधावी कविः क्रांतदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्वा (*medhāvī kaviḥ krāṃtadarśano bhavati kavatervā*): thus the word kavi is explained (Ni. 12-13). Sāyaṇa cites the following passage of the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa for this meaning:

एतस्मिन्नर्थेब्राह्मणं भवति—युवा सुवासाः परिवीत आगादित्युत्तमया परिदधाति प्राणो वै युवा सुवासाः सोऽयं शरीरैः परिवृतः स उ श्रेयान् भवति जायमान इति श्रेयाञ्प्रेयान्हैष एतद्भवति जायमानस्तं धीरासः कवय उन्नयंति स्वाध्यो मनसा देवयंत इति ये वा अनूचानास्ते कवयस्त एवैनं तदुन्नयंति (*etasminnarthebrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati—yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgādityuttamayā paridadhāti prāṇo vai yuvā suvāsāḥ so 'yaṃ śarīraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sa u śreyān bhavati jāyamāna iti śreyāñpreyānhaiṣa etadbhavati jāyamānastaṃ dhīrāsaḥ kavaya unnayaṃti svādhyo manasā devayaṃta iti ye vā anūcānāste kavayasta evainaṃ tadunnayaṃti*) (printed इ. ब्रा. २-२ (*i. brā. 2-2*), i.e. Ai. Brā. 2-2, with "I." for "Ai." as printed).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes, noted briefly. युवा (*yuvā*): root यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः (*yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ*), suffix kanin by कनिन्युवृषि (*kaninyuvṛṣi*) (Uṇ. 1-156); because the suffix is marked k there is no guṇa of the root vowel; replacement uva by अचिश्नुधातु (*aciśnudhātu*) (Pā. 6-4-77); the word yuvan; initial udātta because the suffix is marked ṇit.

### Printed p. 91

(Grammar notes, continued.) सुवासाः (*suvāsāḥ*): root वस आच्छादने (*vasa ācchādane*), asun carried over by anuvṛtti; by वसेर्णित् (*vaserṇit*) (Uṇ. 4-657) it acts as ṇit; vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. 7-2-116); in the compound, ending in asun, initial udātta of the latter member by सोर्मनसी (*sormanasī*) (Uṇ. 6-2-107, as printed). परिवीतः (*parivītaḥ*): root व्येञ् संवरणे (*vyeñ saṃvaraṇe*), kta in the passive; samprasāraṇa by वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (*vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti*) (Pā. 6-1-15); lengthening of the earlier form; the gati (pari) keeps its own accent by गतिरनंतर: (*gatiranaṃtara:*) (Pā. 6-2-49, as printed). अगात् (*agāt*): root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*); luṅ, sip, loss of i; gā substitution by इणोगालुजि (*iṇogāluji*) (Pā. 2-4-45); loss of sic by गातिस्थाघुपा (*gātisthāghupā*) (Pā. 2-4-77); augment aṭ (the printed word "ಅರಿಗಕ್ಕೆ" is unclear [sic]); finite-verb nighāta accent.

श्रेयान् (*śreyān*): when the sense "most praiseworthy" is intended, suffix īyasun by द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे (*dvivacanavibhajyopapade*) (Pā. 5-3-57); śra substituted for the base by प्रशस्यस्य श्र (*praśasyasya śra*) (Pā. 5-3-60); guṇa; initial udātta because the suffix is marked ṇit. धीरासः (*dhīrāsaḥ*): nominative plural jas; augment asuk by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (Pā. 7-1-50). नयंति (*nayaṃti*): root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*); laṭ, third person plural; finite-verb nighāta accent.

साध्यः (*sādhyaḥ*) [sic, as supplied for स्वाध्यः (*svādhyaḥ*) of the Saṃhitā]: root ध्ये चिंतायां (*dhye ciṃtāyāṃ*); with the preverbs su and ā before it, suffix kvip by अन्येभ्योपिदृश्यते (*anyebhyopidṛśyate*) (Pā. 3-2-178); samprasāraṇa of the y of the root (the supplied text reads दृतिग्रहणसामर्थ-दिंद (*dṛtigrahaṇasāmartha-diṃda*), "by the force of the word dṛti-grahaṇa" [sic]); earlier form i by संप्रसारणाच्च (*saṃprasāraṇācca*); lengthening by हलः (*halaḥ*) (Pā. 6-4-2); before jas, yaṇ substitution by एरनेकाचो (*eranekāco*) (Pā. 6-4-82) (the word is given as स्वाधी (*svādhī*)); the accent of the base after the kṛt-latter member; since a following anudātta arises after the yaṇ substitution, it takes svarita by उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ*) (Pā. 8-2-4).

देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*): देवं आत्मनः इच्छंतः (*devaṃ ātmanaḥ icchaṃtaḥ*); suffix kyac by सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*) (Pā. 3-1-8); after the kyac-ending, laṭ gets the śatṛ substitution; by शास्यनुदात्तेत् (*śāsyanudāttet*) it is anudātta, so the accent of kyac remains; nominative plural.

Gist: the yūpa, born on earth, grows at the sacrifice attended by men, adorned with ghee, ointment and rope, and makes the days good; skilled priests purify it and the wise hotṛ recites praise of it. The Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa passage is cited (Ai. Brā. 2-2, printed ऐ. ब्रा. २-२ (*ai. brā. 2-2*)). The grammatical tail covers सुदिनत्वे (*sudinatve*), समर्यॆ (*samaryè*), पुनंति (*punaṃti*), देवयाः (*devayāḥ*) and इयर्ति (*iyarti*) (not transcribed further here).

### Printed p. 93

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

जातः (*jātaḥ*): arisen (first on earth; the yūpa). समर्यॆ (*samaryè*): accompanied by men (priests and others). विदथे (*vidathe*): in the sacrifice. आ वर्धमानः (*ā vardhamānaḥ*): grown on all sides (by ghee, ointment and the like). अह्नां (*ahnāṃ*): of the days. सुदिनत्वे (*sudinatve*): (by being the accomplisher of the sacrifice through the tying of animals and the like) in the goodness of the days. जायते (*jāyate*): (as the cause) becomes. अपसः (*apasaḥ*): devoted to ritual works. धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*): and wise, the adhvaryus and others. मनीषा (*manīṣā*): with intelligence. पुनंति (*punaṃti*): (by washing and the like) make pure. देवयाः (*devayāḥ*): the worshipper of the gods (or the one who offers the oblation to the gods). विप्रः (*vipraḥ*): the intelligent hotṛ. वाचं (*vācaṃ*): (praise-like, concerning the yūpa) speech. उत् इयर्ति (*ut iyarti*): sends forth (utters).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The yūpa, arisen on the earth, adorned with ghee, ointment and the like in the sacrifices performed by men, becomes the cause of the sanctity of the sacrificial days; the adhvaryus and others, devoted to ritual and wise, make it pure with intelligence through washing and the like; the devout hotṛ praises it.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
5. Born (in the forest), and beautiful in the sacrifice celebrated by men, it is (again) engendered for the sanctification of the days (of sacred rites); steadfast, active, and intelligent (priests) consecrate it with intelligence, and the devout worshipper recites its praise.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

समर्यॆ— मर्य इति मनुष्यनाम । तैसहिते (*samaryè— marya iti manuṣyanāma | taisahite*). The word मर्य (*marya*) is listed among the names of man (Ni. 3-8) and is explained as मर्यो मनुष्यो मरणधर्मा (*maryo manuṣyo maraṇadharmā*) (Ni. 3-15) [the printed references are as supplied]; and—

कोनु मर्या अविःथितः सखा सखायमब्रवीत् । जहा को अस्मदीषते ॥ (*konu maryā aviḥthitaḥ sakhā sakhāyamabravīt | jahā ko asmadīṣate ‖*) [the verse is as supplied; the word अविःथितः (*aviḥthitaḥ*) looks like a misreading in the supplied text, left as supplied]

Here मर्याः इति मनुष्यनाम मर्यादाभिधानं वास्यात् । मर्यादा मर्य्य रादीयते मर्यादा मर्यादिनोर्विभागः (*maryāḥ iti manuṣyanāma maryādābhidhānaṃ vāsyāt | maryādā maryya rādīyate maryādā maryādinorvibhāgaḥ*) (Ni. 4-2) : the word मर्या (*maryā*) denotes men, or it may be a boundary. Men divide a boundary. Therefore, the Nirukta-writers have explained that the difference of meaning between the word मर्यादा (*maryādā*) and the word for "those having a boundary" is thus. Sāyaṇa gives the meaning "man" and explains that the sacrifice is accompanied by men.

### Printed p. 94

विदथे आ वर्धमानः (*vidathe ā vardhamānaḥ*)—The word विदथ (*vidatha*) is used among the names of the sacrifice (Ni. 3-19), as विदथेषु यज्ञेषु (*vidatheṣu yajñeṣu*) (Ni. 8-12) and यज्ञे विदथे (*yajñe vidathe*) (Ni. 9-3), in the sense of "sacrifice", and in

होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेशि मायया । विदथानि प्र चोदयॆन् । (*hotā devo amartyaḥ purastādeśi māyayā | vidathāni pra codayèn |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-7)

in the sense विदथानि विज्ञानानि (*vidathāni vijñānāni*), "kinds of knowledge". Sāyaṇa explains it as "in the sacrifice", and explains the yūpa as धृतांजनरशनापरिव्ययणादिना सर्वतश्योभमानः (*dhṛtāṃjanaraśanāparivyayaṇādinā sarvataśyobhamānaḥ*) : shining on all sides through sacrificial rites such as smearing ghee on it and winding the rope round it. And this yūpa, पशुनियोजनादिद्दारेण यज्ञनिर्वाहकतॆया अह्नानि सुदिनानि करोति (*paśuniyojanādiddāreṇa yajñanirvāhakatèyā ahnāni sudināni karoti*) : being the means for such works as tying the sacrificial animal, it makes the days on which the sacrifice goes on good, worthwhile days for the sacrificers; thus the excellence of the yūpa is described.

अपसः धीराः पुनंति (*apasaḥ dhīrāḥ punaṃti*)—Among the twenty-six words for works, the word अपस् (*apas*) is stated (Ni. 3-2), the words being अपः अप्पः दंसः (*apaḥ appaḥ daṃsaḥ*) . The word धीरः (*dhīraḥ*) is stated among the names of the intelligent (Ni. 3-19) and used in the sense धीरो धीमान् (*dhīro dhīmān*) (Ni. 3-12). Sāyaṇa interprets the word धीर (*dhīra*) as "knowing, wise" and explains that the learned priests, the adhvaryu and others, make the yūpa pure (cleansed) in the sacrificial works by the respective rites.

देवयाः विप्रः वाचमुदियर्ति (*devayāḥ vipraḥ vācamudiyarti*)—The word विप्र (*vipra*) is stated among the names of the intelligent (Ni. 3-12). The word देवयाः (*devayāḥ*) is explained in two ways: देवानां यष्टा (*devānāṃ yaṣṭā*), one who performs the sacrifice with the gods in view, or देवानां हवींषि प्रापयिता वा (*devānāṃ havīṃṣi prāpayitā vā*), one who offers the oblations to the gods through Agni. The intelligent sacrificer is described as reciting the praise concerning the yūpa. Sāyaṇa cites the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa passage

जातो जायते सुदिनत्वे अह्नामिति जातो ह्येष एतज्जायते समर्य आ विदथे वर्धमान इति वर्धयंत्येवैनं तत्पुनंति धीरा अपसो मनीषेति पुनंत्येवैनं तद्देवया विप्र उदियर्ति वाचमिति देवेभ्य एवैनं तन्निवेदयति (*jāto jāyate sudinatve ahnāmiti jāto hyeṣa etajjāyate samarya ā vidathe vardhamāna iti vardhayaṃtyevainaṃ tatpunaṃti dhīrā apaso manīṣeti punaṃtyevainaṃ taddevayā vipra udiyarti vācamiti devebhya evainaṃ tannivedayati*) (Ai. Brā. 2-2)

as teaching this very meaning. [The supplied text has a stray "_" after सायणरु (*sāyaṇaru*).]

मनीषा—बुद्ध्या (*manīṣā—buddhyā*). The word मनीषा (*manīṣā*) is used, as मनीषया मनस ईषया स्तुत्या प्रज्ञया वा (*manīṣayā manasa īṣayā stutyā prajñayā vā*) (Ni. 2-25) (Ni. 9-11), in the senses of the mind's resolve, praise, and intelligence. Sāyaṇa has taken the sense "intelligence".

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes, noted briefly. जायते (*jāyate*): root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*); laṭ, third person singular; by ज्ञाजनोर्जा (*jñājanorjā*) (Pā. 7-3-79) the root gets the substitute jā; finite-verb nighāta accent. सुदिनत्वे (*sudinatve*): सुदिनानां भावः सुदिनत्वं (*sudinānāṃ bhāvaḥ sudinatvaṃ*), by तस्यभावस्त्वतल् (*tasyabhāvastvatal*) (Pā. 5-1 119, as printed) the suffix tva in the sense of "state"; final udātta by the suffix accent.

समर्यॆ (*samaryè*): root मृज् प्राणत्यागे (*mṛj prāṇatyāge*) ; by छंदसि निष्कर्ष्यदेव (*chaṃdasi niṣkarṣyadeva*) (Pā. 3-1-123) it is irregularly formed with the suffix kya; by the force of the irregular formation guṇa of the root ṛ occurs although the suffix is marked k. मर्यैः सहितः (सहवर्तते) समर्यः (*maryaiḥ sahitaḥ (sahavartate) samaryaḥ*); final udātta by समासस्य (*samāsasya*) (Pā. 6-1-223); a locative singular form.

पुनंति (*punaṃti*): root पूञ् पवने (*pūñ pavane*), kryādi class; laṭ, third person plural, replacement of jhi by anta; vikaraṇa śnā by क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना (*kryādibhyaḥ śnā*) (Pā. 3-1-81); shortening of the root before the vikaraṇa by प्वादिनां ह्रस्वः (*pvādināṃ hrasvaḥ*) (Pā. 7-3-80); loss of the a of the vikaraṇa by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Pā. 6-4-112); being at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta accent; the initial udātta of the suffix.

मनीषा (*manīṣā*): by the sūtra सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) the case ending is replaced by a single long vowel of the earlier form.

देवयाः (*devayāḥ*): देवान् यूपयतीति देवयाः (*devān yūpayatīti devayāḥ*) ; root या प्रापणे (*yā prāpaṇe*); suffix vic by आतो मनिन् क्विनिब् (*āto manin kvinib*) (Pā. 3-2-24); total loss; the accent of the first member kept by the rule गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*); nominative singular.

इयर्ति (*iyarti*): root ऋ गत् (*ṛ gat*) ; juhotyādi class; laṭ, third person singular, tip; reduplication of the root when the vikaraṇa ślu comes; ī for the reduplicative by आर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च (*ārtipipartyośca*) (Pā. 7-4-77); since a non-homogeneous vowel (ṛ) follows, iyaṅ substitution by अभ्यासस्यासवर्णॆ (*abhyāsasyāsavarṇè*) (Pā. 6-4-78); guṇa with raparatva of the root's ṛ because of tip; being after a non-finite word, nighāta accent.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यान्नो॒ नरो॑ देव॒यंतो॑ निमि॒म्युर्वन॑स्पते॒ स्वधि॑तिर्वा॒॑  
> ततक्ष ।  
> ते दे॒वासः॒ स्वर॑वस्तस्थि॒वांसः॑ प्र॒जाव॑द॒स्मे दि॑धिषंतु॒ रत्नं॑ ॥  
> ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यान् । वः । नं: । देवयंतः । निमिम्युः । वनस्पते । स्वधितिः । वा । ततक्ष ।  
> ते । देवासः । स्वरवः । तस्थिवांसः । प्रजावत् । अस्मे इति । दिधिषंतु । रत्नं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यूपा देवयंतो देवान्कामयमाना नरः कर्मणां नेतारोऽध्व-
> र्यादयो यान्वो यान्युष्मान्निमिम्युः । अवटेषु प्रचिक्षिपुः । ना अपि च हे
> वनस्पते स्वधितिः परशुस्त्वदीयान्यूपांस्ततक्ष बिच्छेद देवासो दीप्यमानाः स्वरवः ।
> स्वरुशब्दः स्वशकलवाची । तद्वंतः । लुप्तमत्त्वर्थियः । तस्थिवांसस्तिष्ठंतस्ते तादृशा
> यूपा आस्मे अस्मै यजमानाय प्रजावत् अपत्यसहितं रत्नमुत्तमं धनं दिधि-
> षंतु । धारयंतु । प्रयच्छंत्यर्थः ॥ निमिम्युः । डुमिञ् प्रक्षेपण इत्यस्य लि-
> ट्मुसि असंयोगाल्लिट् किदिति किद्वद्भावाद्दुणाभावः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । सति
> शिष्टः स्वरो बलीयानिति वचनात्प्रत्ययस्वरः । स्वधितिः । स्वशब्दोपपदाद्दा धारण इ-
> त्यस्मात् क्तिन् । स्वा स्वकीया निशितधारा धीयते प्रक्षिप्यतेऽनेनेति स्वधितिः खड्गः ।
> ततक्ष । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरण इत्यस्माल्लिटि णलि रूपादनिघातः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्तूर्व
> स्योदात्तत्वं । स्वरवः । स्व शब्दोपतापयोरित्यस्मान्निदित्यनुवृत्तौ श्वस्वस्निहित्री-
> त्यादिना उ प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तस्थिवांसः । ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तावित्यस्माच्छंदसि
> लिट् । तस्य क्वसुः । वस्वेकाजाद्भसामितीडागमः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । प्रजावत् । जनी
> प्रादुर्भाव इत्यस्मादुपसर्गे च संज्ञायामिति डः । ततष्टाप् । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् ।
> तस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । एकादेशस्वरः । अस्मे । अस्मच्छब्दस्य सुपां सुलुगिति शे आ-
> देशः । दिधिषंतु । धिष धारणे । जुहोत्यादिः । निघातः ॥

Gist: O yūpas, the posts which the priests, desiring the gods, set up in the pits, and which the axe of the vanaspati (tree) trimmed, standing resplendent with their own parts, may they bestow on this sacrificer excellent wealth with progeny. The grammatical tail (not transcribed further here) covers निमिम्युः (*nimimyuḥ*), स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*), ततक्ष (*tatakṣa*), स्वरवः (*svaravaḥ*), तस्थिवांसः (*tasthivāṃsaḥ*), प्रजावत् (*prajāvat*), अस्मे (*asme*) and दिधिषंतु (*didhiṣaṃtu*).

### Printed p. 97

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Hē yūpāḥ: O yūpas) — yān vaḥ: which you; devayantaḥ: those who desire the gods; naraḥ: the leaders of the sacrifice, the adhvaryus and others; nimimyuḥ: cut; vā: and; (he) vanaspate: O vanaspati; svadhitiḥ: the axe; tataksa: (the posts relating to me) has shaped (trimmed); te: such; devāsaḥ: (resplendent ones); svaravaḥ: possessed of their own parts (entire); tasthivāṃsaḥ: standing (the posts); asme: to this sacrificer; prajāvat: accompanied by offspring; ratnaṃ: jewels and the like; didhiṣantu: let them bear (let them bestow).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O yūpas, the adhvaryus and others, who carry on the sacrifice and are full of faith, cut you from the vanaspatis (trees) and shaped you with the axe; standing resplendent, endowed with all your parts (entire), bestow on this sacrificer wealth and the like together with offspring.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May those (posts) which devout men have cut down, or which, Vana-spati, the axe has trimmed, may they standing resplendent with all their parts (entire) bestow upon us wealth with progeny.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नरः (*naraḥ*) — This word is stated among the names of men (Ni. 3-7) and explained as नराः मनुष्याः नृत्यंति कर्मसु (*narāḥ manuṣyāḥ nṛtyaṃti karmasu*) ("men dance in works"). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as कर्मणां नेतारो अध्वर्यादयः (*karmaṇāṃ netāro adhvaryādayaḥ*), that is, the ṛtvijs such as the adhvaryu who perform the works of the sacrifice without deficiency or excess.

स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*) — स्वा स्वकीया निशितधारा धीयते प्रक्षिप्यते अनेनेति स्वधितिः खड्गः (*svā svakīyā niśitadhārā dhīyate prakṣipyate aneneti svadhitiḥ khaḍgaḥ*). Its sharp edge (blade) is driven against another object for cutting, and so it is called svadhiti, a knife; Sāyaṇa so explains and gives the meaning "axe" (paraśu) [the printed "ಹೇಳಿದಾರೆ" as supplied]. The word svadhiti is stated among the eighteen names of the thunderbolt, beginning दिद्युत् नेमिः (*didyut nemiḥ*) (Ni. 3-11).

देवासः स्वरवः (*devāsaḥ svaravaḥ*) — स्वरु शब्दः स्वशकलवाची । लुप्तमत्त्वर्थीयः (*svaru śabdaḥ svaśakalavācī | luptamattvarthīyaḥ*). Because it is a part belonging to the vanaspati (tree), the yūpa is used here in the sense of śakala (chip, piece). Since the adjective देवासः (*devāsaḥ*) is given to this word, the explanation is that this piece shines like the gods (देवा इव दीप्यमानाः (*devā iva dīpyamānāḥ*)). In the Mahākratus

*(page break)*

### Printed p. 98

many yūpas are used; this point is indicated here by the plural word ते (*te*). Because the yūpa is spoken of as a yūpa-piece, it is here denoted by the word स्वरु (*svaru*), which means a piece.

रत्नम् (*ratnam*) — This word is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). By the sentence प्रजावदस्मे दिधिषन्नु रत्नं (*prajāvadasme didhiṣannu ratnaṃ*) [sic, as supplied: the Saṃhitā has दिधिषंतु (*didhiṣaṃtu*)] it is prayed that these yūpas may bestow on the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice excellent sons and wealth.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes, noted briefly. निमिम्मु: (*nimimmu:*) : root डुमिञ् प्रक्षेपणे (*ḍumiñ prakṣepaṇe*); liṭ, third person plural, substitution of us by परस्मैपदानां (*parasmaipadānāṃ*) (Pā. 3-4-82); reduplication of the root; by असंयोगाल्लिट्‌कित् (*asaṃyogālliṭkit*) (1-2-5) the suffix is treated as k-marked, so no guṇa; yaṇ substitution; by यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (*yadvṛttānityam*) (Pā. 8-1-66) nighāta is prohibited; by the paribhāṣā सतिशिष्टः स्वर बलीयस्त्वम् (*satiśiṣṭaḥ svara balīyastvam*) the suffix accent prevails, so the word is final-udātta; by तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (Pā. 8-1-71) the gati (ni) is anudātta.

स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*): root धि धारणे (*dhi dhāraṇe*) ; with sva as upapada, suffix ktin by स्त्रियांक्तिन् (*striyāṃktin*); स्वा स्वकीया निशितधारा धीयते प्रक्षिष्यते अनेन इति स्वधितिः=खड्ग (*svā svakīyā niśitadhārā dhīyate prakṣiṣyate anena iti svadhitiḥ=khaḍga*); initial udātta by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*).

ततक्ष (*tatakṣa*): root तक्षू त्वक्कू तनूकरणे (*takṣū tvakkū tanūkaraṇe*) ; liṭ, third person singular. Because of the connection with वा (*vā*), nighāta is prohibited by चवा (*cavā*) (Pā. 8-1-59); by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. 6-1-193) the syllable before the suffix takes udātta.

स्वरवः (*svaravaḥ*): root स्व शब्दोपतापयोः (*sva śabdopatāpayoḥ*); suffix u by श्व स्वस्निहितृपि (*śva svasnihitṛpi*) (Uṇ. 1-10) ; guṇa of the root's ṛ with raparatva, giving स्वरु (*svaru*); nit carried on from the previous sūtra, so initial udātta by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*); nominative plural.

तस्थिवांसः (*tasthivāṃsaḥ*): root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*); liṭ in the sense of the present by छंदसिलुज् (*chaṃdasiluj*) ; replacement by kvasu by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*) (Pā. 3-2-107); since the root is monosyllabic, iṭ augment of the following suffix by वस्वेकाजा (*vasvekājā*) (Pā. 7.2-67, as printed); reduplication of the root; the ā is udātta by the suffix accent; nominative plural.

### Printed p. 99

Grammar page continued (Ṛk 6), noted briefly: प्रजावत् (*prajāvat*): root जनी (*janī*) in the sense of appearing, with the upasarga *pra* before it; suffix ḍa by उपसर्गे चसंज्ञायाम् (*upasarge casaṃjñāyām*) (Pā. 3-2-99); the *ṭi* part of the root is dropped because the suffix is ḍ-marked; feminine ending ṭāp, giving *prajā*; then suffix matup by तदस्यास्ति (*tadasyāsti*) (Pā. 5-2-94), which is anudātta because it is p-marked. अस्मे (*asme*): the word *asmad*; when the dative case-ending comes, *śe* is substituted, by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. 7-1-39). दिधिषंतु (*didhiṣaṃtu*): root *dhiṣ* in the sense of holding (juhotyādi class); loṭ, third person plural; the nighāta accent comes because it stands after a word that is not a finite verb [as the text says: "ಅತಿಜಂತದ ಪರದಲ್ಲಿ"].

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये वृ॒क्षासो॒ अधि॒ क्षमि॒ निमि॑तासो य॒तस्रु॑चः ।  
> ते नो॑ व्यंतु॒ वार्यं॑ देव॒त्रा क्षे॑त्र॒साध॑सः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । वृक्षासः । अधि । क्षमि । निमितासः । यतस्रुचः ।  
> ते । नः । व्यंतु । वार्यं । देवत्रा । क्षेत्रसाधनः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्रुच इति ऋत्विग्वाची यतस्रुचो मरुत इति ऋत्विज्ञामसु पठितत्वात् । यताः
> स्रुचो यैस्ते यतस्रुचः । तैर्यत्विग्निर्निमितासोवटेषु नितरां प्रक्षिक्ताः क्षेत्र-
> साधसः क्षेत्रस्य यज्ञस्य साधकाः । यथा क्षेत्रं सस्यादिद्वारा फलं प्रयच्छति तथा

> वित्यस्य लोटि रूपं । इकारलोपश्रांदसः । आयमंतर्भावितण्यर्थः । वार्यं ।

Gist: The posts (yūpas) that were cut down on the earth with the axe and fixed by the priests who hold their ladles are the accomplishers of the sacrifice; let them take our choice oblation to the gods. The grammatical tail covers कृष्णासः (*kṛṣṇāsaḥ*) [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has वृक्षासः (*vṛkṣāsaḥ*)], क्षमि (*kṣami*), निमितासः (*nimitāsaḥ*), यतस्रुचः (*yatasrucaḥ*), व्यंतु (*vyaṃtu*), वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*), देवत्रा (*devatrā*) and क्षेत्रसाधसः (*kṣetrasādhasaḥ*) (not transcribed further here).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Ye: which yūpas) — adhi kṣami: on the earth; vṛkṣāsaḥ: cut with the axe; yatasrucaḥ: by the priests who have prepared and hold their ladles; निमिशासः (*nimiśāsaḥ*) [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has निमितासः (*nimitāsaḥ*)]: thrown (into the pits) or (alternatively) fashioned; kṣetrasādhasaḥ: accomplishers of the sacrifice (which they are); te: those yūpas; naḥ: our; vāryam: choiceworthy oblations and the like; devatrā: among the gods; vyantu: let them make (them) go, so as to join (the gods).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the yūpas, which have been cut down with the axe and felled on the earth, and then fashioned (into the shape of yūpas) by the priests and so made accomplishers of the sacrifice, carry the excellent oblations offered by us to the gods.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May those posts which have been cut down upon the earth, and which have been fabricated by the priests. those which are the accomplishers of the sacrifice, convey our acceptable (offering) to the gods. [Printed "priests. those" with a full stop and lower-case "those" [sic].]

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अधि क्षमि (*adhi kṣami*) — क्षमायां भूम् (*kṣamāyāṃ bhūm*) . The word *kṣamā* is stated among the twenty-one names of the earth (Ni. 2-5). The meaning is explained thus: the posts, cut on the earth with the axe or similar tools, are useful in the sacrifice.

यतस्रुचः (*yatasrucaḥ*) — This word is stated among the eight names of priests beginning with *bhāratāḥ kuravaḥ* (Ni. 3-19). यताः स्रुचः यैस्ते (*yatāḥ srucaḥ yaiste*): the priests who have prepared and hold the ladles for pouring the oblation in the sacrifice; the meaning is thus given, and it is explained that the yūpas have been planted in the earth by the priests.

क्षेत्रसाधनः (*kṣetrasādhanaḥ*) [as supplied; the Saṃhitā has क्षेत्रसाधसः (*kṣetrasādhasaḥ*)] — क्षेत्रस्य यज्ञस्य साधकाः । यथा क्षेत्रं सस्यादिद्वारा फलं प्रयच्छति तथा यज्योऽपि अपूर्वद्वारा स्वर्गादिफलं ददातीति क्षेत्रं (*kṣetrasya yajñasya sādhakāḥ | yathā kṣetraṃ sasyādidvārā phalaṃ prayacchati tathā yajyo 'pi apūrvadvārā svargādiphalaṃ dadātīti kṣetraṃ*) [sic, यज्योऽपि (*yajyo 'pi*) as supplied]. The Nirukta-author explains the word *kṣetra* as क्षेत्रं क्षियतेः निवासकर्मणः (*kṣetraṃ kṣiyateḥ nivāsakarmaṇaḥ*), and, from the root क्षिज्‌क्षये (*kṣijkṣaye*) , which has the meaning "to dwell" (*ṣi*), he explains the word *kṣetra* so formed as meaning a dwelling-place (printed page break; the sentence continues on p. 101).

*(page break)*

### Printed p. 101

Sāyaṇa here explains the word *kṣetra* as denoting the sacrifice: as the field (the earth) increases the crops and the like and does what is useful to people, so the sacrifice gives the sacrificers who perform it the fruit of the sacrifice, heaven and so on, by means of what is called *apūrva*; and since the yūpas bring the sacrifice to completion, he explains them as accomplishers of the sacrifice. [The supplied text reads "ಸಸ್ತಾದಿಗಳನ್ನು" and "ಯೂಪಿಗಳು", left as supplied.]

वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*) — वरणीयं संभजनीयं हविः (*varaṇīyaṃ saṃbhajanīyaṃ haviḥ*). The Nirukta-author has explained the word *vārya* by वृणोतेरथापि वरतमम् (*vṛṇoterathāpi varatamam*) (*vṛṇoter athāpi varatamam*). Durgācārya, by यद्वरयितव्यं भवति तद्वार्यमित्युच्यते। अथापि कदाचित्—वार्यशब्देन यत् वरतमं श्रेष्ठतमं किंचिद्भवति तदुच्यते (*yadvarayitavyaṃ bhavati tadvāryamityucyate| athāpi kadācit—vāryaśabdena yat varatamaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ kiṃcidbhavati taducyate*) , explains the word *vārya*, formed from the root वृञ (*vṛña*) meaning "to choose", as "that which is to be desired" (the supplied text reads अभीलपणीय (*abhīlapaṇīya*) [sic]), and says that in some places the sense of "the most excellent" may also be indicated by the word *vārya*. Sāyaṇa describes it as the choiceworthy oblation, that is, the one most dear to the gods (the supplied text reads "ಹನಿಸ್ಸೆಂಬ" and "ವಿರ್ಣಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ" [sic]).

देवत्रा व्यंतु (*devatrā vyaṃtu*) — देवेषु गमयंतु (*deveṣu gamayaṃtu*). The meaning is explained thus: may the yūpas favour the sacrificers so that the gods receive the choice oblations offered by them. For the word *devatrā* the Nirukta-author cites the Ṛk
वनस्पते रशनया नियूय पिष्टतमया वयुनानि विद्वान् । वहा देवत्रा दिधिषो हवींषि प्र च दातारममृतेषु वोचः ॥ (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūya piṣṭatamayā vayunāni vidvān | vahā devatrā didhiṣo havīṃṣi pra ca dātāramamṛteṣu vocaḥ ‖*)
(my gloss, mine and tentative: "O vanaspati, bound with the girdle, knowing the rites, carry the oblations to the gods, and speak of the giver among the immortals"), and explains *devatrā* as देवत्रा देवान् (*devatrā devān*). Sāyaṇa describes it as the sacrificer's wish and request: अस्मदीयं हविः देवाधीनं कुर्वंतु (*asmadīyaṃ haviḥ devādhīnaṃ kurvaṃtu*) (the supplied text reads "ಅಸ್ಮ-ದೀಯಂ" with a hyphen at the line end).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar page, noted briefly. वृक्षासः (*vṛkṣāsaḥ*): root ओव्रश्च छेदने (*ovraśca chedane*) (to cut); optional iṭ because the root is ū-marked; suffix kta by *niṣṭhā*; being k-marked, by ग्रहिज्यावयि (*grahijyāvayi*) (Pā. 6-1-16) *samprasāraṇa* of the *r* of the root; pūrvarūpa; by स्कोःसंयो (*skoḥsaṃyo*) the initial sibilant of the conjunct is dropped; by चोःकुः (*coḥkuḥ*) *c* becomes *k*; since the root is o-marked, by ओदितश्च (*oditaśca*) (Vā. 8-2-45, as printed) *n* replaces the *t* of the suffix; by यस्यविभाषा (*yasyavibhāṣā*) (Pā. 7-2-15) the augment iṭ does not come to the *niṣṭhā* suffix; *ṇatva* of *n* after *ṛ*, giving *vṛkṣa*; before the ending *jas*, the augment asuk by अज्जसेरसुक् (*ajjaserasuk*) (Gā. 7-1-50, as printed).
क्षमि (*kṣami*): the word *kṣamā*; when the locative singular follows, in आतोधातोः (*ātodhātoḥ*) (Pā. 6-4-140), the division of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) as *ataḥ* means that even though it is not a root, the *a* of what ends in ā, having the name *bha*, is dropped.

### Printed p. 102

Grammar page continued (Ṛk 7), noted briefly. निमितासः (*nimitāsaḥ*): root डुमिञ् (*ḍumiñ*) in the sense of throwing; suffix kta in the passive; as the word ends in kta in the passive, by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. 6-2-49) the prefix (*ni*) takes the udātta accent; before *jas* the augment *asuk* by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*).
यतस्रुचः (*yatasrucaḥ*): यताः स्रुचः यैस्ते यतस्रुचः (*yatāḥ srucaḥ yaiste yatasrucaḥ*), a bahuvrīhi; by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyāpūrvapadam*) (Gā. 6-2-1) the first member keeps its natural accent.
व्यंतु (*vyaṃtu*): upasarga *vi*, root इण् (*iṇ*) in the sense of going; imperative (loṭ) third person plural, with the substitute *anta* and *utva*; by इणोयण् (*iṇoyaṇ*) *yaṇ* for the *i* of the root; the *i* of the upasarga is dropped in the Veda (chāndasa); nighāta accent; since the activity of the instigator is shown, the root has an implied causal sense.
वार्यम् (*vāryam*): root वृज् (*vṛj*) in the sense of sharing; by ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (*ṛhalorṇyat*) (Pā. 3-1-124) the suffix *ṇyat* in the passive; being *ṇ*-marked, vṛddhi of the root's *ṛ* (the supplied text gives the rule as अचोञ्छति (*acoñchati*) [sic, as supplied]); by ईडवृंद वृ शंसदुहा (*īḍavṛṃda vṛ śaṃsaduhā*) (the number is printed "6 1-214" without the second hyphen) the first syllable takes the udātta.
देवत्रा (*devatrā*): when *trā* is carried over, by देवमनुष्यपुरुषपुरुमर्त्येभ्यः (*devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyebhyaḥ*) (Pā. 5-4-56) the suffix *trā* in the locative sense; by the suffix accent the word is final-udātta.
क्षेत्रसाधस (*kṣetrasādhasa*): root राध साध संसिद्धौ (*rādha sādha saṃsiddhau*); by सर्वधातुभ्य आसुन् (*sarvadhātubhya āsun*) (Uṇ. 4-666, as printed) the suffix *asun*; by the *gatikāraka* rule the accent of the compound follows the last member (*kṛduttarapada*); nominative plural form.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒दि॒त्या रु॒द्रा वस॑वः सुनी॒था द्यावा॒क्षामा॑ पृथि॒वी अं॒तरि॑क्षं।  
> स॒जोष॑सो य॒ज्ञम॑वंतु दे॒वा ऊ॒र्ध्वं कृ॑ण्वंत्वध्व॒रस्य॒॑  
> केतुं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आदित्याः । रुद्राः । वसवः । सुनीथाः । द्यावाक्षमा । पृथिवी । अंतरिक्षं ।  
> सजोषसः । यज्ञं । अवंतु । देवा: । ऊर्ध्वं । कृण्वंतु । अध्वरस्य । केतुं ॥

### Printed p. 103

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुनीथा यज्ञस्य सुष्टु नेतार आदित्या द्वादशादित्या रुद्रा एकादशरुद्रा
> वसवोऽषौ वसवः । यद्वा सुष्टु नीथाः सुष्टुतयः । स्तुतशस्त्राणि नीथानि चोत्करा-
> मदानि च । ऐ. ब्रा. २-३८ । इति हि श्रूयते । द्यावाक्षामा द्यावापृथिव्यौ । पृथिवी ।
> सुब्बत्ययः । पृथु विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षं च । सजोषस एते सर्वे देवा ऐकमत्येन
> परस्परं संगता भूत्वेममस्मदीयं यज्ञमवंतु । रक्षंतु । किंच । अध्वरस्य
> यज्ञस्य केतुं ध्वजभूतं प्रज्ञापकं वेमं यूपमूर्ध्व० कृण्वंतु । उच्चृतं
> कुर्वंतु ॥ आदित्याः । अदितेरपत्यानि । दित्यदित्यादित्यपत्युत्तरपदादिति ण्यः । णित्त्वादा-
> दिवृद्धिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । रुद्राः । रोदयंति सर्वानंतकाले । रोदेर्णिलुक् चेति
> रक्षृत्ययः । तत्संनियोगे णिलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । जसः सुप्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे एका-
> देश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्येकादेशस्याप्युदात्तत्वं । वसवः । वस निवासे । निदित्यनुवृत्तौ
> श्यस्वस्तिहित्रप्यसिवसीत्यादिनोप्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सुनीथाः । णीञ्
> प्रापणे । हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्य इति क्धन् । कित्त्वादगुणः । थाथघइत्तेत्युत्तरपदां-
> तोदात्तत्वं । द्यावाक्षामा । द्यौश्च क्षामा च । दिवो द्यावेति द्यावादेशः । देवता-
> द्वंद्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । पृथिवी । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथेः शिवन् संप्र-
> सारणं चेति षिवन् संप्रसारणं च । षिद्धौरादिभ्यश्चेति जीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतो-
> दात्तः । अवंतु । अव रक्षणे । निघातः । कृण्वंतु । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोरित्यस्मा-
> ल्लोटि धिन्विकृष्णोरच्छेत्युप्रत्ययः । अकारश्चांतादेशः । निघातः ॥

Gist: The well-guiding twelve Ādityas, eleven Rudras, eight Vasus, Heaven and Earth, Earth and the firmament, united in mind, are to protect our sacrifice and raise the yūpa, the banner of the sacrifice, aloft. The bhāṣya quotes Ai. Brā. 2-38 on नीथानि (*nīthāni*). The grammatical tail covers आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*), रुद्राः (*rudrāḥ*), वसवः (*vasavaḥ*), सुनीथाः (*sunīthāḥ*), द्यावाक्षामा (*dyāvākṣāmā*), पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*), अवंतु (*avaṃtu*) and कृण्वंतु (*kṛṇvaṃtu*) (not transcribed further here).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुनीथा (*sunīthā*): (the sacrifices) auspiciously conducting
- आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*): the twelve Ādityas
- रुद्राः (*rudrāḥ*): the eleven Rudras
- वसवति (*vasavati*) [sic, as supplied
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*) expected]: the eight Vasus
- (सुनीथाः (*sunīthāḥ*): good praises)
- द्यावाक्षामा (*dyāvākṣāmā*): Heaven and Earth
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*): the extensive
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*): the firmament (and the others)
- देवाः (*devāḥ*): the gods
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*): of equal affection (united with one another)
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*): this our sacrifice
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*): may they protect; (and) अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*): of the sacrifice
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*): banner-like (indicating) this yūpa; ऊर्ध्वं कृण्वंतु (*ūrdhvaṃ kṛṇvaṃtu*): may they lift up (make it raised)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods, the leaders of the sacrifice: the twelve Ādityas, eleven Rudras, eight Vasus, Heaven and Earth, the wide firmament and the rest, united in agreement with one another, protect our sacrifice, and lift up this yūpa-post, the banner of the sacrifice.

*(page break)*

### Printed p. 104

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the leaders of the rite, the divine Adityas, Rudras, Vasus, Heaven and Earth, the Earth, the firmament, well pleased, protect our sacrifice: let them raise aloft the standard of the ceremony.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सुनीथा (*sunīthā*) — सुष्टु यज्ञस्य नेतारः (*suṣṭu yajñasya netāraḥ*). Sāyaṇa explains the meaning as: those who conduct the sacrifice, without any obstacle and in the prescribed order, until it is complete.

In the Ṛk श्वामिंद्र मतिभिस्सुते सुनीथासो वसूयवः । गोभिः क्राणा अनूषत ॥ (*śvāmiṃdra matibhissute sunīthāso vasūyavaḥ | gobhiḥ krāṇā anūṣata ‖*) (as supplied; the first word looks garbled, so no gloss is given) Durgācārya (Ni. 4-19) explains सुष्ठ स्तोतुं ये शक्नुवंते सुनीथाः (*suṣṭha stotuṃ ye śaknuvaṃte sunīthāḥ*) as: those who are skilled in praising well. The Nirukta also says that the word सुनीथः (*sunīthaḥ*) is stated among the ten words for praise beginning with अस्रेवाः (*asrevāḥ*) अनेमाः (*anemāḥ*) (Ni. 3-13) and denotes the excellent.

आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*) — द्वादशादित्याः (*dvādaśādityāḥ*). In explaining the word *āditya* the Nirukta-author says आदिश्यः कस्मात् आदत्तॆ रसान्, आदत्ते भासं, ज्योतिषामादीपो भासेति वा आदितेः पुत्र इति वा । अल्पप्रयोगं तस्यैतवार्जाभ्याम्नाये सूक्तभाक् सूर्यमादितेयमदितेः पुत्रं (*ādiśyaḥ kasmāt ādattè rasān, ādatte bhāsaṃ, jyotiṣāmādīpo bhāseti vā āditeḥ putra iti vā | alpaprayogaṃ tasyaitavārjābhyāmnāye sūktabhāk sūryamāditeyamaditeḥ putraṃ*) (as supplied; the first word reads आदिश्यः (*ādiśyaḥ*)). He explains that the meaning of *āditya* is: that which draws up the waters on the earth, takes to itself all the other lights, gives lustre to the other radiances, surpasses everything in brilliance, or is the son of the goddess Aditi; and he adds that the Ṛks praising this Āditya are few, while the hymns to the Āditya-varieties Savitṛ, Bhaga and Pūṣan are many; and he continues:

एवमन्यासामपि देवतानामादिक्यप्रवादाः स्तुतयो भवंति । तद्यथैतन्नित्रस्य वरुणस्यार्यमोण्ण दक्षस्य भगस्यांशस्येति ॥ (*evamanyāsāmapi devatānāmādikyapravādāḥ stutayo bhavaṃti | tadyathaitannitrasya varuṇasyāryamoṇṇa dakṣasya bhagasyāṃśasyeti ‖*) (Ni. 2-13) (as supplied, with doubtful letters: आदिक्यप्रवादाः (*ādikyapravādāḥ*), अर्यमोण्ण (*aryamoṇṇa*)).

That is: in the same way, in the case of the other deities too, namely Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Dakṣa, Bhaga and Aṃśa, the usage and praise as "Āditya" occurs; and he gives an example of the use of the word *āditya* in Ṛks addressed to these deities:

ता सम्राजा धृतासुती आदित्या दानुनस्पती । सचेते अनवह्वरं ॥ (*tā samrājā dhṛtāsutī ādityā dānunaspatī | sacete anavahvaraṃ ‖*) (Pu. Saṃ. 2-41-6, as printed). (No gloss given.)

In these children [sic, as supplied; probably "in this Ṛk"] Mitra and Varuṇa are praised by the word *āditya*, and … (the sentence continues on p. 105).

### Printed p. 105

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

(continued)

प्र स मित्र मर्तो आस्तु प्रयस्वान्यस्त आदित्य शिक्षति व्रतेन । न हन्यते न जीयते त्वोतो नैनमंहो अश्नोत्यंतितो न धूरात् (*pra sa mitra marto āstu prayasvānyasta āditya śikṣati vratena | na hanyate na jīyate tvoto nainamaṃho aśnotyaṃtito na dhūrāt*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-2; the line is printed twice, the second time as "Ma. Saṃ. 3-59-2"). In this Ṛk the deity Mitra is praised by the word आदित्य (*āditya*), and likewise,

उदुत्तमं वरुण पाशमस्मदवाधमं वि मध्यमं श्रथाय । अथा वयमादित्य व्रते तवानागगो अदितये स्याम ॥ (*uduttamaṃ varuṇa pāśamasmadavādhamaṃ vi madhyamaṃ śrathāya | athā vayamāditya vrate tavānāgago aditaye syāma ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 1-24-15). In this Ṛk Varuṇa is addressed by the word आदित्य (*āditya*). After giving the meaning of the word आदित्य (*āditya*), the Nirukta-author cites,

स्वरादित्योभवति । वृश्निरादित्यो भवति । नाक आदित्योभवति । गौरा-दित्योभवति । विष्टबादित्यो भवति । नभ आदित्यो भवति ॥ (*svarādityobhavati | vṛśnirādityo bhavati | nāka ādityobhavati | gaurā-dityobhavati | viṣṭabādityo bhavati | nabha ādityo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 9-15),

and so illustrates the secondary (figurative) grounds of application in the matters denoted by the word आदित्य (*āditya*). The meaning is that by the words स्वः (*svaḥ*), पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*) [as printed in the Sāyaṇa quotation: वृश्नि (*vṛśni*)], नाकः (*nākaḥ*), गौः (*gauḥ*), विष्टप् (*viṣṭap*), heaven (the firmament) is denoted by the word आदित्य (*āditya*).

यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्ञॆयासो दिवि देवा: सूर्यमादितेयं । यदा चरिष्णू मिथुनावभूतामादित्सा पश्यन् भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ (*yadedenamadadhuryajñèyāso divi devā: sūryamāditeyaṃ | yadā cariṣṇū mithunāvabhūtāmāditsā paśyan bhuvanāni viśvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-11). Since in this Ṛk it is stated in the Brāhmaṇa sentence यदस्य दिवि त्कृतीयं तवसावादित्य इति हि ब्राह्मणं (*yadasya divi tkṛtīyaṃ tavasāvāditya iti hi brāhmaṇaṃ*) (as printed, doubtful letters), the use of the name Āditya for Agni also occurs.

इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो धृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि । शृणोतु मित्रो आर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥ (*imā gira ādityebhyo dhṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi | śṛṇotu mitro āryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 2-27-1). In this Ṛk, from the sentence आदित्येभ्यः जुह्वा जुहोमि (*ādityebhyaḥ juhvā juhomi*), together with

अथातो द्युस्थाना देवगणाः तेषामादिश्याः प्रथमागामिनो भवंति । (*athāto dyusthānā devagaṇāḥ teṣāmādiśyāḥ prathamāgāmino bhavaṃti |*) (Ni. 12-35),

it is said that among the groups of gods dwelling in the heavenly region the Ādityas are the chief; hence the name Āditya is applied figuratively to all the deities. Sāyaṇa here explains that the Ādityas are twelve deities beginning with Mitra, and that they are all varieties of the Āditya.

*(page break)*

### Printed p. 106

रुद्रा: (*rudrā:*) (*rudrāḥ*) — एकादशरुद्राः (*ekādaśarudrāḥ*), the eleven Rudras. The word रुद्र (*rudra*) is stated among the names of praisers (Ni. 3-19). The Nirukta-authors explain: रुद्रो रौतीति सतः, रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा “यदरुदत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम्” इति हारिद्रविकम् (*rudro rautīti sataḥ, rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā “yadarudat tadrudrasya rudratvam” iti hāridravikam*) (*rudro rautīti sataḥ, rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā "yadarudat tadrudrasya rudratvam" iti hāridravikam*) [as supplied; सतः (*sataḥ*) doubtful]; and in the Kāṭhaka-brāhmaṇa, “ स किल पितरं प्रजापतिमिषुणा निध्यंतमनुशोचन्नरुदत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं ” (*“ sa kila pitaraṃ prajāpatimiṣuṇā nidhyaṃtamanuśocannarudat tadrudrasya rudratvaṃ ”*) — "he saw his father Prajāpati pierced by an arrow and wept; therefore he is named Rudra" is said; and the Maitrāyaṇa branch has the name Hāridrava, in which also the derivation of the word रुद्र (*rudra*) is stated in the same way, say the Nirukta-authors. They go on to cite

इमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिरः क्षिप्रेषवे देवाय स्वधान्ने । आषाळ्दाय सहमानाय वेधसे तिग्मायुधाय भरता शृणोतु नः ॥ (*imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane giraḥ kṣipreṣave devāya svadhānne | āṣāḷdāya sahamānāya vedhase tigmāyudhāya bharatā śṛṇotu naḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-46-1),

and describe the quality and greatness of Rudra with this Ṛk. Sāyaṇa explains that these Rudras are eleven deities; and he gives the meaning that, since रोदयंति सर्वमंतकाले (*rodayaṃti sarvamaṃtakāle*) [sic, as supplied] — at the time of dissolution they make everyone weep — they are Rudras.

वसव: (*vasava:*) (*vasavaḥ*) — अष्टौ वसवः (*aṣṭau vasavaḥ*), the eight Vasus. The Nirukta-author says: वसवो यद्विवसते सर्वमग्निः वसुभिर्वास, वइति समाख्या तस्मात् सृधिवीस्थानाः । इंद्रोर्वसुभिर्वासव इति समाख्या तस्मात् मध्यमस्थानाः । वसव आदित्यरश्मयः विवासनात्तस्मात् द्युस्थानाः । (*vasavo yadvivasate sarvamagniḥ vasubhirvāsa, vaiti samākhyā tasmāt sṛdhivīsthānāḥ | iṃdrorvasubhirvāsava iti samākhyā tasmāt madhyamasthānāḥ | vasava ādityaraśmayaḥ vivāsanāttasmāt dyusthānāḥ |*) (as supplied; सृधिवीस्थानाः (*sṛdhivīsthānāḥ*) and the split वसुभिर्वास, वइति (*vasubhirvāsa, vaiti*) look garbled).

The word वसु (*vasu*), formed from the root वस निवासे (*vasa nivāse*), has two kinds of meaning: "dwell", and "make to dwell happily". Hence one meaning: because terrestrial fire nourishes the whole world so that it lives happily, it is the sense of the word *vasu*, and because this fire pervades only the earth it has the earth as its region. Because Indra, by his wealth (riches), makes the whole universe dwell happily, he is a *vasu* and a god of the middle region: the second meaning. Because the rays of the Sun protect the whole world happily, they are gods of the heavenly region: the third meaning. Thus the meaning of the word वसवः (*vasavaḥ*) is stated in three ways, as Agni, Indra and the rays of the Sun [the Kannada has "the wives of the Sun" सूर्यपत्निगळु (*sūryapatnigaḷu*), as supplied; the context suggests "rays"]. Then,

ज्मया अत्र वसवो रंत देवा उरावंतरिक्षे मर्जयंत शुभ्राः । अर्वाक्षथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य ॥ (*jmayā atra vasavo raṃta devā urāvaṃtarikṣe marjayaṃta śubhrāḥ | arvākṣatha urujrayaḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ śrotā dūtasya jagmuṣo no asya ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 7-39-3).

Citing this Ṛk, he explains: Agni, being on the earth the chief god for the increase of sacrificial rites, is the one pervading the earth-region; likewise Indra, because he protects everything, is the god of the middle region; and the rays of the Sun, dwelling in the firmament and producing light, are gods of the heavenly region. And,

*(page break)*

### Printed p. 107

सुगावो देवाः सुपथा अकर्म य आजग्मुः सवनमिदं जुषाणः । जक्षिवांसः पपिवांसश्च विश्वेऽस्मॆ धत्त वसवो वसूनि ॥ (*sugāvo devāḥ supathā akarma ya ājagmuḥ savanamidaṃ juṣāṇaḥ | jakṣivāṃsaḥ papivāṃsaśca viśve 'smè dhatta vasavo vasūni ‖*) (Pā. Saṃ. 8-18, as printed).

In this Ṛk he gives the meaning that these deities, denoted by the word *vasu*, may bestow वसु (*vasu*), that is wealth, and describes their greatness. Hence the meaning "wealth" for the word वसु (*vasu*) is stated in the Nirukta (Ni. 3-9); and वसवः (*vasavaḥ*) as the rays of the Sun (Ni. 2-15) is also stated.

सुगुरसत्सुहिरण्यः स्वश्वो बृहदस्मै वय इंद्रो दधाति । यस्त्वायंतं वसुना प्रातरित्वो मुक्षीजयेव पदिमुत्सिनाति ॥ (*sugurasatsuhiraṇyaḥ svaśvo bṛhadasmai vaya iṃdro dadhāti | yastvāyaṃtaṃ vasunā prātaritvo mukṣījayeva padimutsināti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-125; and again "Pu. Saṃ. 1-125-2", as printed).

Here Durgācārya has commented वसुना अन्नेन (*vasunā annena*), "by food"; hence the word *vasu* also means food. A meaning not stated by the Nirukta-authors in the Nirukta is stated in other Vedas. Following that, Sāyaṇa explains that the Ādityas are twelve persons, the Rudras (eleven, एकादश (*ekādaśa*)) eleven persons, and the Vasus eight persons. This matter is expounded in the first part (Vol. 1) of this Ṛgveda. He says that they are सुनीथाः (*sunīthāḥ*), सुष्टुतयॆः (*suṣṭutayèḥ*) (*suṣṭutayeḥ*) [sic, as supplied], those having excellent praises, or those much praised, and cites the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa sentence स्तुतशस्त्राणि नीथानि चोक्षामदानि च (*stutaśastrāṇi nīthāni cokṣāmadāni ca*) (Ai. Brā. 2-8), describing their greatness.

द्यावाक्षामा (*dyāvākṣāmā*) — द्यौश्च क्षामा च (*dyauśca kṣāmā ca*): the firmament and the earth. Although this word is not explained in the Nirukta among the words for Heaven-and-Earth, Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning "heaven and earth".

पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) — for this word, saying that it means पृथु विस्तीर्णं (*pṛthu vistīrṇaṃ*), extensive or large, Sāyaṇa has explained it as an epithet of the word अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*).

सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*) — संगताः (*saṃgatāḥ*), united, assembled together.

आ रुद्रास इंद्रवंतः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गंशन । इयं वो अस्मत्पति दर्यते मतिस्तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उपन्यवे ॥ (*ā rudrāsa iṃdravaṃtaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gaṃśana | iyaṃ vo asmatpati daryate matistṛṣṇaje na diva utsā upanyave ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-57-1).

Here the Nirukta-authors' explanation is सजोषसः सह जोषणाः (*sajoṣasaḥ saha joṣaṇāḥ*). Durgācārya describes the meaning as परमैश्वर्येण नित्यमासेविताः (*paramaiśvaryeṇa nityamāsevitāḥ*): those constantly served by supreme lordship.

अजुक्तान ईड्यो वंद्यश्च याद्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः ॥ (*ajuktāna īḍyo vaṃdyaśca yādyagne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-3).

Here it is interpreted: सजोषाः सहजोषणः समानप्रीतिः (*sajoṣāḥ sahajoṣaṇaḥ samānaprītiḥ*), one of one and the same affection. The Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus, the firmament, and all these deities, in agreement (ऐकमत्येन (*aikamatyena*)) ... (the sentence continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 108

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

(continued)

… "mutually united" (परस्परं संगताः (*parasparaṃ saṃgatāḥ*)): that is, assembled together, may they protect the sacrifice that the sacrificer and the priests perform in co-operation; so it is described.

अध्वरस्य केतुं (*adhvarasya ketuṃ*) — यज्ञस्य ध्वजभूतं प्रज्ञापकं वा इमं यूपं (*yajñasya dhvajabhūtaṃ prajñāpakaṃ vā imaṃ yūpaṃ*): this post (yūpa), which is the banner of the sacrifice or its indicator. The word केतु (*ketu*) is stated (Ni. 3-13) among the names of knowledge [the supplied text has पद्धज्ञानामगळल्लि (*paddhajñānāmagaḷalli*), "padd-jñāna-names"; probably *prajñā*; as supplied, [sic]].

नवो नवो भवति जायमानोऽह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रं । भागं देवेभ्यो विदधात्यायन् प्र चंद्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः ॥ (*navo navo bhavati jāyamāno 'hnāṃ keturuṣasāmetyagraṃ | bhāgaṃ devebhyo vidadhātyāyan pra caṃdramāstirate dīrghamāyuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-19). Here the word केतुः (*ketuḥ*) is used in the sense of लक्षणं (*lakṣaṇaṃ*), "mark, sign".

महो अर्णस्सरस्वती प्र चेतयति केतुना । धियो विश्वा वि राजति ॥ (*maho arṇassarasvatī pra cetayati ketunā | dhiyo viśvā vi rājati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-12). Here केतुना कर्मणा प्रज्ञया वा (*ketunā karmaṇā prajñayā vā*) explains the sense as action (karma) or knowledge (prajñā).

उदुत्यं जातवेदसं देवं वहंति केतवः । दृशे विश्वाय सूर्यं ॥ (*udutyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahaṃti ketavaḥ | dṛśe viśvāya sūryaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-1). Here केतवः रश्मयः (*ketavaḥ raśmayaḥ*) gives the sense "rays". Although the Nirukta states for the word *ketu* the senses knowledge, ray, mark and action, Sāyaṇa here explains the sense "banner" and "indicator", and describes the prayer that the gods make the post, the indicator of the sacrifice, shine out nobly, with loftiness.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar page, noted briefly. आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*): the male descendants of Aditi; the suffix ṇya in the sense of descendant by दित्यदित्यादित्यपत्युत्तरपदात् ण्यः (*dityadityādityapatyuttarapadāt ṇyaḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-1-85); because the suffix is ṇit, vṛddhi of the first vowel by तद्धितेष्वचामदेः (*taddhiteṣvacāmadeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-1117, as supplied [sic]); final udātta by the suffix accent. रुद्राः (*rudrāḥ*): "those who make all weep at the end of time"; root रुदिर् अश्रुविमोचने (*rudir aśruvimocane*); after the causative, the suffix rak by रोदेर्णिलुक्च (*roderṇilukca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-179); loss of ṇic; because the suffix is k-marked there is no laghūpadha guṇa; the suffix accent remains; when the ending jas becomes anudātta, the single replacement is udātta by एकादेशउदात्तेनोदात्तः (*ekādeśaudāttenodāttaḥ*). वसवः (*vasavaḥ*): root वस निवासे (*vasa nivāse*); suffix u by शृ स्वृ स्निहि त्रप्यसि (*śṛ svṛ snihi trapyasi*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-10); ṇit carried on from the preceding sūtra, hence initial udātta.

### Printed p. 109

(Grammar notes, continued.) सुनीथाः (*sunīthāḥ*): root णीञ् प्रापणी (*ṇīñ prāpaṇī*) (*ṇīñ prāpaṇī*, as supplied); suffix kvan [the supplied text has क्सन् (*ksan*), *ksan*, [sic]] by हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः (*hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-159); because it is k-marked there is no guṇa of the root ī; final-syllable-of-the-latter-member udātta by थाथघञ् क्ता (*thāthaghañ ktā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-144); nominative plural form. द्यावाक्षामा (*dyāvākṣāmā*): द्यौश्च क्षामा च (*dyauśca kṣāmā ca*); by दिवोद्यावा (*divodyāvā*) the word *div* becomes *dyāvā*; by देवताद्वंद्वेच (*devatādvaṃdveca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-141) both members keep their natural accent; by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the case-ending is replaced by ā. पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*): root प्रथ प्रख्याने (*pratha prakhyāne*); suffix ṣivan with samprasāraṇa by प्रथेः शिवन् संप्रसारणंच (*pratheḥ śivan saṃprasāraṇaṃca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-148); samprasāraṇa of the r of the root; because it is ṣit, the feminine suffix jīṣ by षिड्गौरादिभ्यश्च (*ṣiḍgaurādibhyaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-41); final udātta by the suffix accent. आवंतु (*āvaṃtu*) (*avantu*): root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*); loṭ, third person plural; finite-verb nighāta accent. कृण्वंतु (*kṛṇvaṃtu*) (*kṛṇvantu*): root कृवि हिंसाकारणयोश्च (*kṛvi hiṃsākāraṇayośca*) (*kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*); loṭ, third person plural, with replacement of the ending (as supplied: अंदेश उत्व (*aṃdeśa utva*)); loss of a by धिन्विकृण्वोरच (*dhinvikṛṇvoraca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-80); because the root is i-marked the augment num; ṇatva after ṛ; yaṇ substitution; nighāta accent because it stands after a word that is not a finite verb (the supplied text has निघासस्वर (*nighāsasvara*) [sic]).

> यूपा अतिदैर्घ्यादंतरिक्षं व्याप्य वर्तंत इत्यर्थः ॥ हंसा इव । इवेन विभक्त्य-
> लोप इति वचनात्तूर्वपदस्वरः । श्रेणितः । बह्वल्पार्थादिति शस् । प्रत्ययस्वरः ।
> श्रेणिशः । बहुल्पार्थादिति शस् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । शुक्रा । शुच दीप्तावित्यस्मादृजेंद्रा
> ग्रेत्यादिना रन्प्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातनादंतोदात्तः । अगुः । इण् गतौ । आस्माल्लुजि
> रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The shining pillars, clad in bright garments and arrayed in rows like flying swans, have come to us; set up by wise priests in front of the Āhavanīya fire, they reach the gods' region, the atmosphere. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: हंसा इव (*haṃsā iva*), श्रेणिशः (*śreṇiśaḥ*), शुक्रा (*śukrā*), अगुः (*aguḥ*), root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*). The supplied text has बहुल्पार्थादिति (*bahulpārthāditi*) the second time for बह्वल्पार्थादिति (*bahvalpārthāditi*) and the clause श्रेणिशः । बहुल्पार्थादिति शस् । प्रत्ययस्वरः (*śreṇiśaḥ | bahulpārthāditi śas | pratyayasvaraḥ*) twice; as supplied, [sic].

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुक्रा (*śukrā*) — shining (white, bright) [garments called *raśanā*]
- वसानाः (*vasānāḥ*) — wearing
- स्वरवः (*svaravaḥ*) — together with their own parts
- श्रेणिशः (*śreṇiśaḥ*) — in rows
- यतानाः (*yatānāḥ*) — moving; हंसा इव (*haṃsā iva*) — like swans (shining as they shine)
- श्रेणिशः (*śreṇiśaḥ*) — in row upon row (the posts that proceed)
- नः (*naḥ*) — to us
- आगुः (*āguḥ*) — have arrived; (and) कविभिः (*kavibhiḥ*) — by the wise priests such as the Adhvaryu [the supplied text has आध्वय्यादि (*ādhvayyādi*), [sic]]
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*) — on the east of the Āhavanīya fire; उत् नीयमानाः (*ut nīyamānāḥ*) — erected
- देवाः (*devāḥ*) — those shining posts
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*) — of the gods
- पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) — the region, the atmosphere; आपि यंति (*āpi yaṃti*) — pervade [the supplied text has आपि (*āpi*) for अपि (*api*), as supplied]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The posts, clad in bright garments called *raśanā*, endowed with all their parts, shining in row upon row like rows of swans, have arrived (are shining); set up by the wise priests, the Adhvaryu and the others, in front of the Āhavanīya fire, they grow tall and touch even the atmosphere, the abode of the gods.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Arrayed in bright (garments), entire (in their parts), these pillars ranging in rows like swans, have come to us erected by pious sages on the east (of the fire); they proceed resplendent on the path of the gods.

### Printed p. 111

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हंसा इव श्रेणिशो यतानाः (*haṃsā iva śreṇiśo yatānāḥ*) — पङ्क्तः प्रवर्तमानाः हंसा इव (*paṅktaḥ pravartamānāḥ haṃsā iva*): moving in rows, like swans. यथा नभसि पङ्क्तः पतंतो हंसाः शोभंते तद्वत् शोभमानास्ते यूपाः (*yathā nabhasi paṅktaḥ pataṃto haṃsāḥ śobhaṃte tadvat śobhamānāste yūpāḥ*): as swans flying in rows in the sky shine, so those posts shine. The Nirukta writers have stated the word हंसासः (*haṃsāsaḥ*) among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27). And:

ईर्मांतासः सिलिकमध्यमासः सं शूरणासो दिव्यासो अत्याः । हंसा इव श्रेणिशो यतंते यदाक्षिषुर्दिव्यमज्ममश्वाः ॥ (*īrmāṃtāsaḥ silikamadhyamāsaḥ saṃ śūraṇāso divyāso atyāḥ | haṃsā iva śreṇiśo yataṃte yadākṣiṣurdivyamajmamaśvāḥ ‖*) (the supplied text has पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) [sic] 1-163-10).

Having cited this Ṛk, they explain हंसाः हंतेर्घ्नंत्यध्वानं (*haṃsāḥ haṃterghnaṃtyadhvānaṃ*): the word हंस (*haṃsa*), derived from the root हन (*hana*) in the sense of going, means "one that travels the road". They also describe the word श्रेणि (*śreṇi*) in श्रेणितः (*śreṇitaḥ*) as derived from the root श्रिज् (*śrij*) , with the sense of "being in a row". Sāyaṇa has explained it by comparing the posts to rows of swan-birds flying in the sky, which shine.

शुक्रा वसानाः (*śukrā vasānāḥ*) — शुक्राणि दीप्तानि रशनाख्यानि वासांसि आच्छादयंतः (*śukrāṇi dīptāni raśanākhyāni vāsāṃsi ācchādayaṃtaḥ*): covering themselves with shining garments called *raśanā*. The word शुक्र (*śukra*) is stated among the names of water (Ni. 2-24).

आ सुष्वयंती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योन् । दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपितं दधाने ॥ (*ā suṣvayaṃtī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yon | divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapitaṃ dadhāne ‖*) (the supplied text has पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) [sic] 10-110-6).

Here शुक्रं शोचतेर्ज्वलतिकर्मणः (*śukraṃ śocaterjvalatikarmaṇaḥ*) (the supplied text has दीप्तर्थवन्नु (*dīptarthavannu*) for the sense "shining" [sic]): the word शुक्र (*śukra*) is derived from the root शुच (*śuca*), which conveys the sense of shining, and the meaning "lustrous" is given. Durgācārya explains the meaning as शुक्लरूपां श्रियं (*śuklarūpāṃ śriyaṃ*) (white-formed splendour).

शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि । विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥ (*śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadviṣurūpe ahanī dyaurivāsi | viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣanniha rātirastu ‖*) (the supplied text has म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*) [sic] 6-58-1).

Here the word शुक्रम् (*śukram*) is given the sense "white" (शुक्ल (*śukla*)). The meaning is that the posts, clad in garments called *raśanā*, white (of a white colour) and lustrous, shine.

कविभि: पुरस्तादुन्नियमाना: (*kavibhi: purastādunniyamānā:*) [colons as supplied] — the word कवि (*kavi*) is stated among the names of the intelligent (Ni. 3-19). The meaning is that the priests such as the Adhvaryu have set the posts up, shining, in the sacrificial hall on the eastern side of the Āhavanīya fire.

देवानां पाथः अपियंति (*devānāṃ pāthaḥ apiyaṃti*) — देवानां स्थानमंतरक्षं प्राप्नुवंति (*devānāṃ sthānamaṃtarakṣaṃ prāpnuvaṃti*) (the supplied text has अंतरक्षं (*aṃtarakṣaṃ*) [sic] for अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)): they reach the atmosphere, the abode of the gods. The Nirukta writer, (continued on the next page)—

यत्रा चक्रुरमृता गातुमस्मै श्येनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः । प्रति वां सूर उदिते विधेम नमोभिर्मित्रावरुणोत हव्यैः ॥ (*yatrā cakruramṛtā gātumasmai śyeno na dīyannanveti pāthaḥ | prati vāṃ sūra udite vidhema namobhirmitrāvaruṇota havyaiḥ ‖*) (the supplied text has पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) [sic] 7-63-5).

Having cited this Ṛk, he explains पाथः अंतरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यानतं (*pāthaḥ aṃtarikṣaṃ pathā vyākhyānataṃ*) [as supplied; the sense is "pāthaḥ is the atmosphere, explained by 'path'"], giving the meaning "way". Then:

वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् । स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्धवींष्यवतां द्यावापृथिवी हवं मे ॥ (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān | svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavaddhavīṃṣyavatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī havaṃ me ‖*) (10-70-10, as supplied).

For the word पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) in this Ṛk he explains अन्नमपि पाथ उच्यते पानादेव (*annamapi pātha ucyate pānādeva*) ("food too is called pātha, from drinking"); the supplied text has वाख्यानमाडि (*vākhyānamāḍi*) [sic] for "explained". Durgācārya has explained the meaning as हवनसंबंधादन्नं पाथ उच्यते पानादेव (*havanasaṃbaṃdhādannaṃ pātha ucyate pānādeva*) ("food connected with the oblation is called pātha, from drinking").

उपावसृज त्मन्या समंजन् देवानां पाथ यतुथा हवींषि । हनस्पतिश्यमिता देवो अग्निः स्वदंतु हव्यं मधुना धृतेन ॥ (*upāvasṛja tmanyā samaṃjan devānāṃ pātha yatuthā havīṃṣi | hanaspatiśyamitā devo agniḥ svadaṃtu havyaṃ madhunā dhṛtena ‖*) (the supplied text has म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*) [sic] 10-110-10; it also has हनस्पति (*hanaspati*) [sic]).

In this Ṛk too the word पाथ (*pātha*) is explained as "food". Sāyaṇa explains (अध्वय्यादिभिः उच्छ्रीयमाणा यूपा अतिदैर्घ्यादंतरिक्षं व्याप्य वर्तंते (*adhvayyādibhiḥ ucchrīyamāṇā yūpā atidairghyādaṃtarikṣaṃ vyāpya vartaṃte*)): the posts, consecrated by the Adhvaryu and other priests, shine in the atmosphere, the abode of the gods, by their height.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar page, noted briefly. हंसा इव (*haṃsā iva*): root हसे हसने (*hase hasane*) , suffix ac; being in the Pṛṣodarādi group it takes the anusvāra augment; by the statement इवेनसमासो विभक्त्यलोपश्च (*ivenasamāso vibhaktyalopaśca*) the case-ending is not elided in the compound; the accent of the first member remains. श्रेणितः (*śreṇitaḥ*): suffix śas by बह्वल्पार्थात् शस् का (*bahvalpārthāt śas kā*) (Pā. Sū. 5-4-42); final udātta by the suffix accent. यताना: (*yatānā:*) [colon as supplied]: root यती प्रयत्ने (*yatī prayatne*); replacement of liṭ by śānac; luk for the vikaraṇa by बहुलंछंदसि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasi*); तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) keeps the root accent. शुक्रा (*śukrā*): root शुच दीप्तौ (*śuca dīptau*); suffix rat by ऋज्रेंद्राग्र (*ṛjreṃdrāgra*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-180), final udātta. स्वरमः (*svaramaḥ*) [sic, as supplied]: said to be explained in the sixth mantra of this same sūkta.

### Printed p. 113

(Grammar notes, continued.) अगुः (*aguḥ*): root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) , luṅ; the root becomes gā by इणोगालुजि (*iṇogāluji*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-45); by गातिस्थाघुपा (*gātisthāghupā*) (Vā. Sū. 2-4-77) sic is dropped; the ending jhi becomes us by आतः (*ātaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-110); the augment aṭ; nighāta accent. उन्नीयमानाः (*unnīyamānāḥ*): root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*); śānac in the passive; yak by सार्वधातुके यक् (*sārvadhātuke yak*); augment muk by आनेमुक् (*ānemuk*); the yak accent remains; in the prādi compound the accent of the latter member of a kṛt compound. यंति (*yaṃti*): root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), laṭ third person plural; nighāta accent. पाथः (*pāthaḥ*): root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*); suffix asun and the augment thuṭ are taught as irregular by अन्नेच (*anneca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-644); here it conveys the meaning "atmosphere" (the supplied text has इर्थ (*irtha*) [sic] for "meaning").
