##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The posts, eight-cornered and smooth, are seen on the earth like the horns of horned animals, and, hearing the praise uttered by the priests at the sacrifice, may protect us in battles. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: शृंगाणि (*śṛṃgāṇi*), ददृश्रे (*dadṛśre*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वरवः (*svaravaḥ*) — possessing their parts
- चषालवंतः (*caṣālavaṃtaḥ*) (*caṣālavantaḥ*) — free of thorns, the posts
- पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*) — on the earth
- शृंगिणां (*śṛṃgiṇāṃ*) (*śṛṅgiṇāṃ*) — of horned ones such as buffaloes; शृंगाणि इव इत् (*śṛṃgāṇi iva it*) (*śṛṅgāṇi iva it*) — just like horns; सं ददृश्रे (*saṃ dadṛśre*) — are well seen
- वा (*vā*) — and
- विहवे (*vihave*) — in the sacrifice where oblations of various kinds are offered
- वाघद्भिः (*vāghadbhiḥ*) — by the priests (the sound in the form of praise made by them)
- श्रोषमाणाः (*śroṣamāṇāḥ*) — those hearing (the posts)
- पृतनाज्येषु (*pṛtanājyeṣu*) — in battles (wars)
- अस्मान् (*asmān*) — us, the performers of the sacrifice
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*) (*avantu*) — may they protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The posts, complete in their parts and free of thorns and the like, are seen on the earth like the horns of buffaloes and other horned animals. And these posts, which listen to the praise uttered by the priests at the sacrifices, may they protect us in battles.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Entire in all parts and girded with rings, they appear upon the earth like the horns of horned cattle; bearing (their praises) by the priests: may they protect us in battles.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स्वरव: (*svarava:*) [colon as supplied] — स्वरुमंतः (*svarumaṃtaḥ*) : the meaning is that the posts are made eight-cornered (with eight edges) [the supplied text has an underscore and a bracket here].

चषालवंतः (*caṣālavaṃtaḥ*) — प्रतिमुक्तकंटका: (*pratimuktakaṃṭakā:*): the meaning is that they are smooth, as if free of thorns (जंटकगळु (*jaṃṭakagaḷu*) [sic] for "thorns").

शृंगाणीवेत् (*śṛṃgāṇīvet*) — here, in the three words शृंगाणि इव इत् (*śṛṃgāṇi iva it*) (the supplied text has कदगळल्लि (*kadagaḷalli*) [sic] for "words"), the word इत् (*it*) is used in the sense of a mere filler of the line. The Nirukta writers state अथ ये प्रवृत्तेर्थे (*atha ye pravṛtterthe*) ... and the quotation is cut off at the end of this page (continued in the next window).

### Printed p. 115

The Nirukta writers explain that the particles (the text has निखातगळु (*nikhātagaḷu*) [sic], evidently for *nipāta*) कं (*kaṃ*), ईं (*īṃ*), इत् (*it*) and उ (*u*) are used in prose works for completing the sentence and in metrical works for filling the pāda.

पृथिव्यां शृंगिणां शृंगाणीव संददृश्रे (*pṛthivyāṃ śṛṃgiṇāṃ śṛṃgāṇīva saṃdadṛśre*) — the sense is explained thus: the yūpas shine like the horns of horned animals such as buffaloes.

विहवे (*vihave*) — विविधं हूयंते हवींष्यत्रेति विहवो यज्ञः (*vividhaṃ hūyaṃte havīṃṣyatreti vihavo yajñaḥ*): the sacrifice, the rite in which many kinds of oblations offered to Agni are poured in many ways, is called *yajña*; this is the meaning explained here.

वाघद्भिः (*vāghadbhiḥ*) — the word वाघत् (*vāghat*) is stated among the names of priests (Ni. 3-19). The meaning is: the priests who perform the sacrificial rites.

पृतनाज्येषु (*pṛtanājyeṣu*) — the word पृतनाज्य (*pṛtanājya*) is stated among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9), and the Nirukta writers, citing the Ṛk इमं तं पश्य वृषभस्य युंजं काष्ठाया मध्ये द्रुघणं शयानं । येन जिगाय शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः पृतनाज्येषु ॥ (*imaṃ taṃ paśya vṛṣabhasya yuṃjaṃ kāṣṭhāyā madhye drughaṇaṃ śayānaṃ | yena jigāya śatavatsahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pṛtanājyeṣu ‖*) (Pu. Saṃ. 10-102-9, as printed), comment: पृतनाज्यमिति संग्रामनाम पृतनानाम जनाद्वा जयनाद्वा ! (*pṛtanājyamiti saṃgrāmanāma pṛtanānāma janādvā jayanādvā !*) (the text has वाख्यानमाडिद्दारॆ (*vākhyānamāḍiddārè*) [sic] for "explained"). Durgācārya explains the sense thus: पृतनः (*pṛtanaḥ*), men, अंजंति (*aṃjaṃti*) गच्छंति (*gacchaṃti*), go, where they perish, or पृतनः (*pṛtanaḥ*) men जयंति (*jayaṃti*) become victorious; and he says that because there arises a situation, a war, in which men perish or men conquer others, battle is expressed by the word पृतनाज्य (*pṛtanājya*). Sāyaṇa describes the meaning with पृतनाज्यशब्दः संग्रामवाची पृतनाज्येषु संग्रामेषु वधस्थलेष्टिति यावत् (*pṛtanājyaśabdaḥ saṃgrāmavācī pṛtanājyeṣu saṃgrāmeṣu vadhasthaleṣṭiti yāvat*), and says that the meaning is: may the posts (the text has यूषगळु (*yūṣagaḷu*) [sic] for यूपगळु (*yūpagaḷu*)) protect the sacrificers in these places of slaughter.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar page, noted briefly. शृंगाणि (*śṛṃgāṇi*): root शृ हिंसायां (*śṛ hiṃsāyāṃ*); by शृणातेः ह्रस्वश्च (*śṛṇāteḥ hrasvaśca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-123, as printed here; the bhāṣya tail gives a different last number) the suffix gan; augment nuṭ; the root vowel is shortened, giving शृंग (*śṛṃga*). By निर्त्यं (*nirtyaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) the suffix having an n-marker, the initial udātta accent comes. In compound with इव (*iva*), as before, the accent of the first member. ददृश्रे (*dadṛśre*): root दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे (*dṛśir prekṣaṇe*); by छंदसि लुज्लज्लिटः (*chaṃdasi lujlajliṭaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) liṭ in the passive in the present sense, third person plural, affix झ (*jha*) (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 116

(Grammar notes, continued.) ददृश्रे (*dadṛśre*): by the sūtra लिटस्तझयो (*liṭastajhayo*) (the text gives only these words) the substitute इरेच् (*irec*) comes; then by इरयोरे (*irayore*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-76) the substitute रे (*re*) for it. The root is doubled because of liṭ, etc. Because it stands after an *atijanta* the nipāta accent comes (the bhāṣya says nighāta). विहवे (*vihave*): root हु दानादनयोः (*hu dānādanayoḥ*); affix घ (*gha*) in the sense of the locus; taking it as the occasion, guṇa and अव् (*av*) substitution for the उ (*u*) of the root; by the accent of the affix it is acute on the final; in the prādi compound the accent of the latter member of a kṛt compound; locative singular form. श्रोषमाणाः (*śroṣamāṇāḥ*): root श्रु श्रवणे (*śru śravaṇe*); by vyatyaya it takes the ātmanepada; liṭ gets the substitute शानच् (*śānac*); by vyatyaya the vikaraṇa शप् (*śap*). By सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-38) the power of the word *bahula* brings सिप् (*sip*) here also; taking it as the occasion, guṇa of the उ (*u*); ṣatva and the augment मुक् (*muk*) for it. Because the laśārvadhātuka becomes anudātta by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*), the root accent remains. अवंतु (*avaṃtu*): root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*); loṭ third person plural; tiṅanta, so the nighāta accent.

#### Ṛk 11

> यं त्वाम॒यं स्वधि॑ति॒स्तेज॑मानः प्रणि॒नाय॑ मह॒ते सौभ॑-  
> गाय ॥ ११ ॥

> यं । त्वां । आयं । स्वधितिः । तेजमानः । प्रनिनाय । महते । सौभगाय ॥ ११ ॥

> हादुर्भूतो भव । वयमपि सहस्रवल्याः पुत्रपौत्रादिसंतानपरंपरया सहस्रशाखाः
> संतो विरुहेम । विशेषेण प्रादुर्भूता भवेम । तेजमानो निशितधारोऽयं
> स्वधितिः परशुः हे स्थानो यं त्वां महते सौभगाय महत्सौभाग्यं बहुशाखत्व-
> लक्षणं प्रणिनाय । प्रकर्षेण प्रापयामास ॥ सहस्रवल्याः । सहस्रशब्दः कर्दमादि-
> श्वान्मध्योदात्तः । बहुव्रीह पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । रुहेम । रुह प्रादुर्भाव इत्य.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O stump of the broken-off yūpa, grow with a hundred branches, and may we grow with a thousand; the sharp axe has brought you for great good fortune. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: रुहेम (*ruhema*), प्रणिनाय (*praṇināya*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) वनस्सते (*(he) vanassate*) [sic, as supplied for वनस्पते (*vanaspate*)] — O stump (post) whose root is cut off; यं त्वां (*yaṃ tvāṃ*) — you whom
- तेजमानः (*tejamānaḥ*) — with sharpened edge, अयं स्वधितिः (*ayaṃ svadhitiḥ*) — this axe
- महते (*mahate*) — great
- सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*) — for good fortune; प्र निनाय (*pra nināya*) — has cut and brought
- (सः (*saḥ*) — such a you)
- शतवल्यः (*śatavalyaḥ*) — having hundreds of branches
- विरोह (*viroha*) — appear (grow); वयं (अपि) (*vayaṃ (api)*) — we also
- सहस्रवल्याः (*sahasravalyāḥ*) — having a thousand offspring such as sons and grandsons; वि रुहेम (*vi ruhema*) — may we prosper (the text has अभिवृद्ध रागोण (*abhivṛddha rāgoṇa*), with a stray space)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O stump of the yūpa, whose root is cut off: this axe with its sharp edge has cut you and brought you to the sacrifice so that you may bestow good fortune. May you, such as you are, grow with hundreds of branches, and grant that we too may prosper, having thousands of branches in the form of sons, grandsons and the like.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
VANASPATI, mount up (grow) with a hundred branches, that we may mount with a thousand, you whom the sharpened hatchet has brought for great auspiciousness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वनस्पते शतवल्वो विरोह (*vanaspate śatavalvo viroha*) — the meaning of the word *vanaspati* has been explained (in the Pīṭhikā). Here, with भिन्नमूल स्थाणो (*bhinnamūla sthāṇo*), the base of the tree that remains with its roots after the tree is cut, the stump, is addressed by the word वनस्पति (*vanaspati*). And the wish is expressed that this rooted stump, having many branches, may attain the state of a great tree.

The sacrificers, by the grace of the Agni present in the yūpa, express the hope सहस्रवल्याः वि रुहेम पुत्रपौत्रादिसंतानपरंपरया सहस्रशाखाः संतः विशेषेण प्रादुर्भूता भवेम (*sahasravalyāḥ vi ruhema putrapautrādisaṃtānaparaṃparayā sahasraśākhāḥ saṃtaḥ viśeṣeṇa prādurbhūtā bhavema*): that we may prosper in many ways in the order of sons and grandsons (the text has पुत्ररू (*putrarū*) मक्कळू (*makkaḷū*) मॊम्मक्कळू (*mòmmakkaḷū*)).

तेजमानः स्वधितिः महते सौभगाय प्रणिनायि (*tejamānaḥ svadhitiḥ mahate saubhagāya praṇināyi*) (as supplied; the text then has an underscore) — the yūpa connected with the vanaspati has been cut by the sharp axe and brought here, in order to bring us much welfare. This meaning (continued on the next page)

### Printed p. 118

is described with the explanation निशितधारः परशुः महत्सौभाग्यं बहुशाखत्वलक्षणं प्रकर्षेण प्रापयामास (*niśitadhāraḥ paraśuḥ mahatsaubhāgyaṃ bahuśākhatvalakṣaṇaṃ prakarṣeṇa prāpayāmāsa*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

रोह (*roha*): root रुह बीजजन्मनि प्रादुर्भावे च (*ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca*); loṭ second person singular. Because it stands after an *atijanta* , the nighāta accent comes. सहस्रवल्याः (*sahasravalyāḥ*): because the word सहस्र (*sahasra*) is read in the group beginning कर्दम (*kardama*), it has the accent on the middle syllable. By बहुप्रीहौप्रकृत्यापूर्वपदम् (*bahuprīhauprakṛtyāpūrvapadam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member keeps its own accent in the bahuvrīhi compound. रुहेम (*ruhema*): root रुह प्रादुर्भावे (*ruha prādurbhāve*), first person plural of the āśīrliṅ, मस् (*mas*); by नित्यंजितः (*nityaṃjitaḥ*) loss of the स (*sa*); by लिज्याशिष्यज् (*lijyāśiṣyaj*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-86) the affix अज् (*aj*); the liṅ takes the augment यासुट् (*yāsuṭ*); by आतोयेयः (*ātoyeyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-80) the substitute इय् (*iy*); guṇa; by लोपोव्योर्वलि (*lopovyorvali*) loss of the य् (*y*) of इय् (*iy*); tiṅanta nighāta accent. प्रणिनाय (*praṇināya*): upasarga प्र (*pra*); root णिञ् प्रापणे (*ṇiñ prāpaṇe*); liṭ third person singular, when तिप् (*tip*) comes, the substitute णल् (*ṇal*); doubling of the root; because the affix is ṇit, vṛddhi of the इ (*i*) of the root by अचो-इत्ति (*aco-itti*) ; substitute आय् (*āy*). Because it stands at the beginning of the pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. Because the affix is lit, by लिति (*liti*) the syllable before the affix gets the udātta. By तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) the gati (प्र (*pra*)) gets the udātta, since a tiṅanta with an udātta follows. महशे (*mahaśe*) [sic, evidently for महते (*mahate*)]: by बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानम् (*bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānam*) the dative ending gets the udātta.

## Sūkta 9 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The ninth sūkta**

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta** (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सखायस्त्वति नवर्चं नवमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं । आश्रेयमनुक्रमणिका ।
> सखायो नव बार्हतं त्रिष्टुबंतमिति । अंत्या त्रिष्टुप् । शिष्टा अष्ट् बृहत्यः ॥ प्रात-
> रनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्बार्हते छंदस्यस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगः । अथैतस्या इति खंडे
> सूत्रितं । सखायस्त्वियमग्निरग्न आ याहि । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning सखायस्त्वा (*sakhāyastvā*) is the ninth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: सखायो नव बार्हतं त्रिष्टुबंतमिति (*sakhāyo nava bārhataṃ triṣṭubaṃtamiti*). The last ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining eight ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre. At the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka mantras and of the Āśvina śastra mantras, for the recitation of the ṛks in the Bṛhatī metre, this sūkta's (the Anuvāda breaks off here at the end of p. 118; the application continues on p. 119, together with the sūkta data and Ṛk 1).

### Printed p. 119

*[Continuation of the Anuvāda of Sūkta 9 from the previous page.]*

… has its application (viniyoga), as is made clear by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the section beginning अथैतस्या (*athaitasyā*) [sic, as supplied], in the sūtra सखायस्त्यामग्निरग्न आ याहि (*sakhāyastyāmagniragna ā yāhi*) (Ā. 4-13).

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 9. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 9. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 1; Varga 5, 6. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 9. Ṛṣi: Viśvāmitra. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: "8, Bṛhatī; 9 Triṣṭubh" (as printed; evidently ṛks 1–8 Bṛhatī, 9 Triṣṭubh, in agreement with the Anukramaṇikā quoted above).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सखा॑यस्त्वा ववृमहे दे॒वं मर्ता॑स ऊ॒तये॑ ।  
> अ॒पां नपा॑तं सु॒भगं॑ सु॒दीदि॑तिं सु॒प्रतू॑र्तिमने॒हसं॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सखायः । त्वा । ववृमहे । देवं । मर्तासः । ऊतये ।  
> अपां । नपातं । सुभगं । सुदीदितिं । सुप्रतूर्तिं । अनेहसं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वामित्रः सौति । हे आग्ने सखायः सोमाज्यादिहविस्पदानेनोपकारक-
> त्वान्मित्राणि मर्तसो मनुष्या ऋत्विजो वयमपां नपातमपां नप्तारं सुभगं
> शोभनधनयुक्तं कुदीदितिं शोभनदीप्तिं सुप्रतूर्तिं शोभनप्रतरणं कर्मानु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, we priests, your friends through our oblations, choose you, the grandson of the waters, rich, bright, easily approached and free from harm, for protection. (The grammatical tail, on सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*), ववृमहे (*vavṛmahe*) and ऊतये (*ūtaye*), is transcribed, not explained; it continues on the next page. The bhāṣya reads कुदीदितिं (*kudīditiṃ*) [sic] where the Saṃhitā and Pada have सुदीदितिं (*sudīditiṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे आग्ने (*he āgne*) — O Agni)
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*) — friends (by offering oblations such as soma and ghee)
- मर्तासः (*martāsaḥ*) — we, men in the form of priests; अपां नपतं (*apāṃ napataṃ*) [sic, the Saṃhitā has नपातं (*napātaṃ*)] — the grandson of the waters
- सुभगं (*subhagaṃ*) — endowed with excellent wealth
- सुदीधितिं (*sudīdhitiṃ*) [sic, the Saṃhitā has सुदीदितिं (*sudīditiṃ*)] — of good brilliance
- सुप्रतूर्तिं (*supratūrtiṃ*) — one who gives auspicious gifts (or: easily reached by those who perform the rites)

- ऊतये (*ūtaye*) — for protection
- ववृमहे (*vavṛmahe*) — we call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, grandson of the waters, rich in excellent wealth, of fine radiance, a good giver (easy of access to those who perform the rites), free from harm, of divine nature: we, who are your friends because we offer oblations to you, and who are men in the form of priests, desire protection and call you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We your mortal friends have recourse for our protection to you the divine, the grandson of the waters, the auspicious, the resplendent, the acces- sible [sic, "acces- sible" for "accessible"], the sinless.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सखायः— सोमाज्यादिहविष्पदानेन उपकारत्वात् मित्राणि (*sakhāyaḥ— somājyādihaviṣpadānena upakāratvāt mitrāṇi*) — for this word Yāska has given the meaning समानख्याना ऋत्विजः (*samānakhyānā ṛtvijaḥ*) (priests of the same utterance). Sāyaṇa explains that because the priests offer to Agni oblations such as soma and ghee, and perform the work of friends (protection), they are friends of Agni.

मर्तासः—मनुष्याः ऋत्विजः (*martāsaḥ—manuṣyāḥ ṛtvijaḥ*) — since the word मर्त (*marta*) is stated among the names of men (Ni. 3-8), he gives the meaning मनुष्याः ऋत्विजः वयं (*manuṣyāḥ ṛtvijaḥ vayaṃ*), "we priests who are men".

अपांनपातं-अपां नप्तारं (*apāṃnapātaṃ-apāṃ naptāraṃ*) — the meaning is "grandson of the waters". Yāska explains this with अपान्न पात् तनूनप्ता, व्याख्यातः (*apānna pāt tanūnaptā, vyākhyātaḥ*) (the text has याग्तरु (*yāgtaru*) [sic] for "Yāska"), and

### Printed p. 121

… having explained it so, he cites the Ṛk (the text has मक्कळन्नु (*makkaḷannu*) [sic], evidently for "Ṛk"):

यो अनिध्मो दीदयदप्स्व १ स्तर्यं विप्रास ईळते अध्वरेषु । अपां नपान्मधुमतीरपो दा याभिरिंद्रो वावृथे वीर्याय ॥ (*yo anidhmo dīdayadapsva 1 staryaṃ viprāsa īḷate adhvareṣu | apāṃ napānmadhumatīrapo dā yābhiriṃdro vāvṛthe vīryāya ‖*) **NOTE** (Pu. Saṃ. 10-30-4, as printed; a stray digit १ (*1*) stands inside the quoted word अप्स्व १ स्तर्यं (*apsva 1 staryaṃ*) in the supplied text, left as supplied)

and, citing this ṛk (the text again has मक्कळन्नु (*makkaḷannu*) [sic]):

तनूनपात् पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समंजन्त स्वधया सुजिह्व । मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृंधन् देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥ (*tanūnapāt patha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samaṃjanta svadhayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛṃdhan devatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 10-110-2, as printed)

For the word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) in this ṛk Yāska states the opinions of two authorities: तनूनपादाज्यमिति कात्क्यः अग्निरितिशाकपूणिः (*tanūnapādājyamiti kātkyaḥ agniritiśākapūṇiḥ*), "Kātkya says ghee, Śākapūṇi says Agni". Then, गौरत्र तनुरुच्यते, नपादित्यनंतरायाः प्रजाया नामधेयं (*gauratra tanurucyate, napādityanaṃtarāyāḥ prajāyā nāmadheyaṃ*): here तनु (*tanu*) is said to be the cow (गौः (*gauḥ*)), and नपात् (*napāt*) is a name for a descendant not immediately next. He points out the awkwardness of Kātkya's view, which gives the word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) the meaning "ghee" on the ground that ghee is produced from the cow through the milk (the text has वयस्सिन मूलक (*vayassina mūlaka*), "through age", which seems out of place; left as supplied). Then he explains: आपोऽत्र तन्न उच्यंते, तता अंतरिक्षे ताभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायंते ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्यः एष जायते (*āpo 'tra tanna ucyaṃte, tatā aṃtarikṣe tābhya oṣadhivanaspatayo jāyaṃte oṣadhivanaspatibhyaḥ eṣa jāyate*) (the text has तन्न (*tanna*) and तता (*tatā*) [sic]). Durgācārya, on नपात् इति अनन्तरायाः प्रजायाः नामधेयं (*napāt iti anantarāyāḥ prajāyāḥ nāmadheyaṃ*), says: one produced from the father is the son; one produced from the son is next in order (anantara) and is lower than the son. Hence, on the view of those who take the word तनु (*tanu*) as "cow", the view of Kātkya that ghee and the like come from the cow and Agni from ghee and the like is not acceptable to Yāska. He describes, further, the view of Śākapūṇi: since the waters are the meaning of the word अप् (*ap*), the waters are spread in the atmosphere; from these waters come the plants and trees, and from these Agni; therefore Agni is designated both by the word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) and by the word अपान्न पात् (*apānna pāt*). From this the meaning is that Agni is the grandson of the waters (the text has नॊम्मगनु (*nòmmaganu*) [sic] for "grandson").

सुप्रतूर्तिं (*supratūrtiṃ*) — because Agni is worthy of being easily worshipped by those who perform sacrifices and other rites, it is explained that he is सुप्रतरण (*suprataraṇa*), the remover of the troubles of the sacrificers.

सुभगं अनेहसं सुदीदितिं देवं ऊतये ववृमहे—शोभनधनयुक्तं शोभनदीप्तिं, उपद्रवरहितं रक्षणाय वृणीमहे (*subhagaṃ anehasaṃ sudīditiṃ devaṃ ūtaye vavṛmahe—śobhanadhanayuktaṃ śobhanadīptiṃ, upadravarahitaṃ rakṣaṇāya vṛṇīmahe*) — it is explained: Agni, the god, who has excellent wealth and gives it to the sacrificers, who shines with auspicious brilliance, who is free from every trouble, to protect us, we priests choose (the text has वंसिसुत्तेवॆ (*vaṃsisuttevè*) [sic], for "we choose").

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar page, noted briefly. सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*): root ख्या प्रकथने (*khyā prakathane*); by समाने ख्यश्चोदात्तः (*samāne khyaścodāttaḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-576, as printed) the affix इण् (*iṇ*) for this root when समान (*samāna*) stands as upapada; the affix being डित् (*ḍit*), the account goes on: "by the preceding …" (the page breaks off here; continued on the next page). (A stray "16" ends this page in the supplied text; left as supplied.)

### Printed p. 122

Continuing सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*): as the sūtra carries on by anuvṛtti, the ṭi of the root is dropped by the force of the affix being ḍit, and the y with it; by समानस्य छंदसि (*samānasya chaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6 3-74, as printed) समान (*samāna*) becomes स (*sa*)-; the word becomes सख (*sakha*), the upapada takes the udātta accent; before जस् (*jas*) the rule सुख्युरसंबुद्धौ (*sukhyurasaṃbuddhau*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-97, as printed) makes it ṇit-like, vṛddhi of the i and ayādeśa follow, and the word is ādyudātta. ववृमहे (*vavṛmahe*): root वृज् संभक्तौ (*vṛj saṃbhaktau*); छंदसि लुज्ज्‌लज्‌लिटः (*chaṃdasi lujjlajliṭaḥ*) gives liṭ in the present sense, the affix महिज् (*mahij*) in the first person plural, ṭi becomes e; कृसृभृवृ (*kṛsṛbhṛvṛ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-13) forbids the iḍ-augment; reduplication of the root; nighāta accent (reason given as in the text). मर्तासः (*martāsaḥ*) (the text's headword reads मर्शासॆ (*marśāsè*) [sic]): root मृज् प्राणत्यागे (*mṛj prāṇatyāge*) [sic] with an Auṇādika affix तन् (*tan*), guṇa of the ṛ with r following, and असुक् (*asuk*) added to जस् (*jas*) by अज्जसेरसुक् (*ajjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50). ऊतये (*ūtaye*): root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*); as ऊतियूतिजूति (*ūtiyūtijūti*) (Pā. Sū. 3-0-97, as printed) is a nipātana ending in क्तिन् (*ktin*) it is antodātta; dative singular. अपां (*apāṃ*): genitive plural; by ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the case-ending takes the udātta. सुभगं (*subhagaṃ*): bahuvrīhi; by आद्युदात्तं द्व्यज् छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvyaj chaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119) the latter member is ādyudātta. सुप्रतूर्तिं (*supratūrtiṃ*): also bahuvrīhi, in the क्रत्वादि (*kratvādi*) group, so by क्रत्वादयश्च (*kratvādayaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-118) the latter member is ādyudātta.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, desiring the forests you went to the waters, your mothers, and became calm there; yet by churning you appear at once in our kindling-sticks, so your staying far off pleases us not. (Yāska is quoted; the grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained. The Saṃhitā block as supplied reads मात्वरजगन्नपः (*mātvarajagannapaḥ*) where the Pada and bhāṣya read मात्यः (*mātyaḥ*) / मात्यरपो (*mātyarapo*): an OCR variant of the supplied text, left as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(हे (*he*)) अग्ने (*agne*) — O fire. वना (*vanā*) — the forests. कायमानः (*kāyamānaḥ*) — desiring. त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you. यत् (*yat*) — for which reason. मातृः (*mātṛḥ*) — (to you) of the nature of mothers [the supplied text has a garbled word here, not reproduced]. अपः (*apaḥ*) — the waters (toward). अजगन् (*ajagan*) — you went; and यत् (*yat*) — for which reason. दूरे सन् (*dūre san*) — being far away (invisible within the water, you). इह (*iha*) — here (in the kindling-sticks, the aranis, that are ours). अभवः (*abhavaḥ*) — are present. तत् (*tat*) — for that reason. ते (*te*) — your. निवर्तनं (*nivartanaṃ*) — constant dwelling (in the water; destruction). न प्रमृषे (*na pramṛṣe*) — is not tolerated.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who wish to be in the forests left them, joined the waters and became calm; and though thus invisible in the water, you appear in our kindling-sticks (as soon as you are churned). Therefore your dwelling far off (in the midst of the water) does not please us.

### Printed p. 124

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Desirous as you are of the forests since you have repaired to the maternal waters, Agni, your tarrying so far away is not to be endured ; (in a moment) you are here with us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वना—काननानि (*vanā—kānanāni*) — the word वन (*vana*) is also stated among the names of rays (Ni. 2 15, as printed). And in नियद्वृणक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्कस्य चिद्वृंदिनो रोरुवद्वना (*niyadvṛṇakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣkasya cidvṛṃdino roruvadvanā*) (no source given in the text; the Ṛk is quoted as supplied) Yāska has explained the word वना (*vanā*) as वनानि इति वा वधेनेति वा (*vanāni iti vā vadheneti vā*); accordingly Sāyaṇa gives the meaning वनानि (*vanāni*) "forests", and for कायमानः (*kāyamānaḥ*) the meaning कामयमानः (*kāmayamānaḥ*), "one who wishes for".

अपः अजगन्—मातृभूताः अपः गतवानसि (*apaḥ ajagan—mātṛbhūtāḥ apaḥ gatavānasi*) — by the word अपांनपात् (*apāṃnapāt*) it was shown that water is the mother-place of Agni. Therefore Agni has entered the waters, which are like a mother to him and nourish through the herbs and trees produced from water; and the words अप्पु प्रविष्टत्वात् शांतोऽसि (*appu praviṣṭatvāt śāṃto 'si*) [sic, अप्पु (*appu*) for the bhāṣya's अप्सु (*apsu*)] are explained thus: since Agni is in the waters, he is in a state of calm.

निवर्तनं न प्रमृषे—नितरां तत्त्रैव वर्तनं तेन च विनाशो लक्ष्यते । सविनाशः न प्रमृष्यते न सह्यते (*nivartanaṃ na pramṛṣe—nitarāṃ tattraiva vartanaṃ tena ca vināśo lakṣyate | savināśaḥ na pramṛṣyate na sahyate*) — the word वर्तन (*vartana*) is formed from the root वृतु (*vṛtu*) and is used here with the prefix नि (*ni*). As stated in उपसर्गेण धात्वर्थो बलादन्यत्र नीयते । प्रहाराहारसंहारविहारपरिहारवत् (*upasargeṇa dhātvartho balādanyatra nīyate | prahārāhārasaṃhāravihāraparihāravat*) (gloss mine and tentative: "by a prefix the meaning of the root is forcibly led elsewhere, as in prahāra, āhāra, saṃhāra, vihāra, parihāra"), the word वर्तन (*vartana*) with the prefix नि (*ni*) conveys the meaning "destruction", and also the state that precedes destruction. By this, Agni's staying in the waters is not tolerated by the sacrificers; that is, Agni's becoming invisible is not to be tolerated.

यत् दूरे सन् इह अभवः । अदृश्यतया वर्तमानः अग्नि: अस्मत्संबंधिषु अरणिरूपेषु काष्ठेषु मंथनात् क्षणमात्रेण अस्माकं समीपे भवति तस्मात् अग्नेः दूरतः वर्तनं अस्माकं न रोचते (*yat dūre san iha abhavaḥ | adṛśyatayā vartamānaḥ agni: asmatsaṃbaṃdhiṣu araṇirūpeṣu kāṣṭheṣu maṃthanāt kṣaṇamātreṇa asmākaṃ samīpe bhavati tasmāt agneḥ dūrataḥ vartanaṃ asmākaṃ na rocate*) — it is explained that Agni's being in the waters in an invisible form (a form not seen by the eye) is his manner of being far away, and that his appearing visibly at that very moment, when churned in the kindling-sticks of those who perform the sacrifice, is his manner of being near. Of the two, the sacrificers prefer Agni to be near rather than far. Yāska quoted this same Ṛk in the Nirukta and stated his own view clearly:

कायमानश्चायमानः कामयमान इति वा वनानि त्वं यन्मात्यरपोगम उपशाम्यन् न तत्ते अग्ने प्रमष्यते निवर्तनं दूरे यत्सन्निह भवसि जायमानः (*kāyamānaścāyamānaḥ kāmayamāna iti vā vanāni tvaṃ yanmātyarapogama upaśāmyan na tatte agne pramaṣyate nivartanaṃ dūre yatsanniha bhavasi jāyamānaḥ*) (A. 4-14, as printed; the text has मात्यरपोगम (*mātyarapogama*) and प्रमष्यते (*pramaṣyate*) [sic] where the bhāṣya has मात्यरपोऽगम (*mātyarapo 'gama*) and प्रमृष्यते (*pramṛṣyate*)). Sāyaṇa has explained this same view stated in the Nirukta.

Grammar page, noted briefly. कायमानः (*kāyamānaḥ*): root कमु कांत् (*kamu kāṃt*) [sic, as supplied]; by कमेर्णिज् (*kamerṇij*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-30) the affix णिज् (*ṇij*) in the root's own sense; vṛddhi of the penultimate by आत उपधायाः (*āta upadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116); the णिजंत (*ṇijaṃta*) is a root; लट् (*laṭ*) is replaced by शानच् (*śānac*); guṇa and ayādeśa; आनेमुक् (*ānemuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82) gives the augment मुक् (*muk*); the m of the root is dropped in the Veda; the root accent remains. वना (*vanā*): neuter plural; शि (*śi*) is dropped by छंदसि बहुलं (*chaṃdasi bahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70). अजगन् (*ajagan*): root गमल्य गतौ (*gamalya gatau*) [sic, as supplied]; लज् (*laj*) with तिप् (*tip*); इतश्च (*itaśca*) drops the i; शप् (*śap*) becomes शु (*śu*) by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*); the ending is dropped; मोनो धातोः (*mono dhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-64) changes m to n; augment अड् (*aḍ*); because the word यत् (*yat*) is connected there is no nighāta; ādyudātta by the udātta augment. प्रमृषे (*pramṛṣe*): root मृष तितीक्षायां (*mṛṣa titīkṣāyāṃ*); लट् (*laṭ*) in the passive, त (*ta*) ending, e by टित आत्मने (*ṭita ātmane*); no यक् (*yak*) by vyatyaya; the a of the ending dropped by लोपस्त आत्मने पदेषु (*lopasta ātmane padeṣu*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-41); no nighāta because of न (*na*); तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71, as printed, with पा (*pā*) and सू. (*sū.*) split by a line break) makes प्र (*pra*) anudātta. निवर्तनं (*nivartanaṃ*): root वृतु वर्तने (*vṛtu vartane*); ल्युट् (*lyuṭ*) in the sense of the action; युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) gives अन (*ana*); लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) gives udātta before the affix; as a prādi-compound it takes the accent of the kṛdanta latter member. अभवः (*abhavaḥ*): root भू सत्तायां (*bhū sattāyāṃ*); by छंदसि (*chaṃdasi*) … (Pā. Sū. 3-4.6, as printed) … (the page breaks off here, mid-word: ऎंबु (*èṃbu*); continued on the next page).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अति॑ तृ॒ष्टं व॑वक्षि॒थाथै॒व सु॒मना॑ असि ।  
> प्रप्रा॒न्ये यंति॒ पर्य॒न्य आ॑सते॒ येषां॑ स॒ख्ये असि॑ श्रि॒तः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अति । तृष्टं । ववक्षिथ । अथ । एव । सुमनाः । असि ।  
> द्रप्र । अन्वे । यंति । परि । अन्वे । आसते । येषां । सख्ये । आसि । श्रितः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने तृष्टं स्तोतुस्त्वाभिलाषं तदुचितफलप्रदानेन सफलं कर्तु-

> वर्तसे तेषां मध्येऽन्येऽध्वर्युप्रभृतयो द्वादशर्त्विजः प्रयंति । प्रकर्षण
> होतुं गच्छंति । अन्य उद्गातृप्रभृतयश्चत्वारः पर्यासते । परित आसीना वर्तंते॥
> ववक्षितथ । वह प्रापण इत्यस्य सनि रूपं । अभ्यासस्य सन्यत इतीत्वाभावश्कांदसः । तदं-
> ताद्वर्तमाने लिट् । फल अर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेरितीट् । कास्पत्ययाडामित्याम्
> न भवति मंत्रत्वात् । निघातः । प्रप्र । प्रसमःपोद इति द्विवचनं । यंति । इष्
> गतावित्यस्य लटि रूपं । एकान्याभ्यां समर्थाभ्यामित्यन्यशब्दयोगात्पूर्वस्य निघाता-
> भावः । आसते । आस उपवेशने । उत्तरत्वान्नि घातः । असि । आस भुवि । शासस्तो-
> र्लोप इति सकारलोपः । यद्वृत्तयोगान्न निहन्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you wish to bear the worshipper's desire to fulfilment and so are well-pleased; of the sixteen priests in whose friendship you rest, twelve go forth to offer and four sit around. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: ववक्षिथ (*vavakṣitha*), प्रप्र (*prapra*), यंति (*yaṃti*), आसते (*āsate*), आसि (*āsi*). The text prints ववक्षितथ (*vavakṣitatha*) in the tail where the Pada has ववक्षिथ (*vavakṣitha*), तृष्टं (*tṛṣṭaṃ*) where the printed English later suggests तृष्णं (*tṛṣṇaṃ*), and द्रप्र (*drapra*) in the Pada for प्रप्र (*prapra*): OCR variants of the supplied text, left as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(हे अग्ने (*he agne*) — O Agni) तृष्टं (*tṛṣṭaṃ*) — the thirst (desire) of the worshipper (to make fruitful). अति ववक्षिथ (*ati vavakṣitha*) — you wish to bear greatly. अथ एव (*atha eva*) — for that very reason. सुमनाः आसि (*sumanāḥ āsi*) — you are of a contented mind; (and) येषां (*yeṣāṃ*) — of which sixteen priests. सख्ये (*sakhye*) — in friendship. श्रितः आसि (*śritaḥ āsi*) — you are resting. (तेषां (*teṣāṃ*) — among them)

### Printed p. 127

अन्ये (*anye*) — some (the twelve priests beginning with the Adhvaryu). प्र प्र यंति (*pra pra yaṃti*) — go forth (to offer the oblation). अन्ये (*anye*) — (and) some others (the four beginning with the Udgātṛ). परि आसते (*pari āsate*) — sit all around.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you are well-pleased [the text reads "ಪೂರ್ಣಮಾಡುವುದಕ್ಕೋಸ್ಕರಲೇ" with a stray letter; sense: for the very purpose of fulfilling the worshipper's desire]; of the sixteen priests regarded by you as friends, the twelve beginning with the Adhvaryu have set out to make the offering in abundance, and the remaining four (beginning with the Udgātṛ) sit all around. (They are seated.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
you wish exceedingly to convey satisfaction (to your worshipper) and are thereto well-disposed ; of those in whose friendship you are cherished some precede whilst others sit around.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तृष्णं ववक्षिथ (*tṛṣṇaṃ vavakṣitha*) — [as supplied; the Saṃhitā reads तृष्टं (*tṛṣṭaṃ*)] With this sentence Agni is addressed: स्तोतुः तृष्णाभिलाषं सफलं कर्तुं तत्तदुचितफलप्रदानेन अतिशयेन वोढुमिच्छसि (*stotuḥ tṛṣṇābhilāṣaṃ saphalaṃ kartuṃ tattaducitaphalapradānena atiśayena voḍhumicchasi*). It is described that he is desirous of bearing abundant oblation from the sacrificer, in order to give the fruit corresponding to the desire of the sacrificer who praises him, in order to make the sacrificer one who has gained his purpose, and in order to show his own affection for the sacrificer. And सुमना असि (*sumanā asi*) is further explained as: he is of a mind that is joyful toward the sacrificer.

अन्ये प्रयंति अन्ये परि आसते (*anye prayaṃti anye pari āsate*) — Agni is affectionate toward all sixteen priests of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ and the others, because they serve him. Among them अध्वर्युप्रभृतयो द्वादश ऋत्विजः प्रकर्णण होतुं गच्छंति (*adhvaryuprabhṛtayo dvādaśa ṛtvijaḥ prakarṇaṇa hotuṃ gacchaṃti*) [sic, प्रकर्णण (*prakarṇaṇa*) as supplied; the bhāṣya reads प्रकर्षण (*prakarṣaṇa*)] — the twelve priests beginning with the Adhvaryu are ready to offer oblations and perform the homa to satisfy Agni. अन्ये उद्गातृप्रभृतयः चत्वारः परित आसीना वर्तंते (*anye udgātṛprabhṛtayaḥ catvāraḥ parita āsīnā vartaṃte*) — the four priests beginning with the Udgātṛ, as praisers of Agni, sit around him in the sacrificial hall, ready to chant. Thus the duties performed by the priests belonging to the sacrifice are briefly indicated here.

सख्यॆ (*sakhyè*) — मित्रत्व (*mitratva*); the meaning is the state of friendship. The Nirukta authors—

(continuing the Nirukta citation) सक्तुमिव तितउना पुनंतो यत्र धीरा मनसा वाचमक्रत । अश्रा सखायस्सख्यानि जानते भद्रैषां लक्ष्मीर्निहिताधि वाचि ॥ (*saktumiva titaunā punaṃto yatra dhīrā manasā vācamakrata | aśrā sakhāyassakhyāni jānate bhadraiṣāṃ lakṣmīrnihitādhi vāci ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-2, as printed; the text's तितउना (*titaunā*) is as supplied — a gloss would be mine and tentative: "as one purifies barley-meal with a sieve, where the wise fashioned speech with the mind; there friends know the marks of friendship; their auspicious mark is placed in speech"). In this Ṛk, the meaning सखायः सख्यानि संजानते (*sakhāyaḥ sakhyāni saṃjānate*), "friends recognise the states of friendship", is explained. Durgācārya (explains): समानख्यानाः समानख्यानानामेव सखायः, वैयाकरणानां वैयाकरणा एव नैरुक्तानां नैरुक्ता एव सखिभावान् संजानते विज्ञानानि संजानते इतरेतरस्य यो विज्ञानप्रकर्षः तं जानते (*samānakhyānāḥ samānakhyānānāmeva sakhāyaḥ, vaiyākaraṇānāṃ vaiyākaraṇā eva nairuktānāṃ nairuktā eva sakhibhāvān saṃjānate vijñānāni saṃjānate itaretarasya yo vijñānaprakarṣaḥ taṃ jānate*). Those who have one kind of knowledge are friendly with those equally skilled; those who know grammar recognise each other's excellence of knowledge among grammarians, and those who know the Nirukta among the Nirukta-scholars. From this, affection arises among them. In the same way Agni, being renowned as the Hotṛ, is friendly with the priests; thus the meaning is explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar page, noted briefly. ववक्षथ (*vavakṣatha*) [sic, as supplied; the bhāṣya reads ववक्षिथ (*vavakṣitha*)]: root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*); the affix सन् (*san*) in the sense of wishing by धातोःकर्मणः (*dhātoḥkarmaṇaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-6, as printed); doubling of the root by सन्यजोः (*sanyajoḥ*); the i that सन्यतः (*sanyataḥ*) would give to the reduplicative syllable does not occur in the Veda; होढः (*hoḍhaḥ*) changes h to ḍh, षढोःकसि (*ṣaḍhoḥkasi*) then gives ka, and ṣatva of the s follows; the form in सन् (*san*) is a root by सनाद्यंताधातवः (*sanādyaṃtādhātavaḥ*), takes लिट् (*liṭ*); the second person singular सिप् (*sip*) becomes थल् (*thal*) by परस्मैपदानां (*parasmaipadānāṃ*); the इड् (*iḍ*)-augment by अर्धधातुकस्येद्वलादेः (*ardhadhātukasyedvalādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35, as printed, text अर्धधातुकस्यॆद्वरादेः (*ardhadhātukasyèdvarādeḥ*)); आम् (*ām*) does not occur, the prohibition अमंत्रे (*amaṃtre*) in कास्प्रत्ययादाममंत्रेलिटि (*kāspratyayādāmamaṃtreliṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-35) applying to the Veda; अतोलोपः (*atolopaḥ*) drops the a of the sanning (text: "ಲೋರ" [sic]); the nighāta accent arises as the word follows [a word garbled in the text: "ಅತಿ ಚಿಂತದ" — **NOTE**]. सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*): शोभनं मनः यस्य सः (*śobhanaṃ manaḥ yasya saḥ*); since the latter member ends in अस् (*as*), सोर्मवसी (*sormavasī*) [as supplied, with a stray underscore] (Pā. Sū. 6-2-117, as printed) gives the latter member's initial udātta. प्रप्र (*prapra*): in filling the pāda, doubling of प्र (*pra*) by प्रसमुपोद (*prasamupoda*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-6, text without full stops); the second is called amreḍita and made udātta by अनुदात्तंच (*anudāttaṃca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3). यंति (*yaṃti*): root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) [sic, as supplied]; लट् (*laṭ*) third plural, अंत् (*aṃt*) substituted; लुक् (*luk*) for शप् (*śap*); इणोयण् (*iṇoyaṇ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-81) gives यण् (*yaṇ*); because the word अन्य (*anya*) is connected, एकान्याध्यांसमर्थाभ्याम् (*ekānyādhyāṃsamarthābhyām*) [sic, as supplied] (Pā. Sū. 8-1-65) forbids the tiṅanta nighāta, so the ending's ādyudātta accent remains.

### Printed p. 129

आसते (*āsate*)—root आस (*āsa*) in the sense of sitting; the present (laṭ) third person plural form. Although another word (अन्य (*anya*)) is in construction, the prohibition of nighāta does not apply because the word stands in the latter part of the sentence. By तिज्जतिजिः (*tijjatijiḥ*) [sic, as supplied] the all-anudātta accent arises.

असि (*asi*)—root अस (*asa*) in the sense of being; the affix sip in the present second person singular. By तासस्तो र्लोपः (*tāsasto rlopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-50) the s of the root is dropped. Because the relative word यत् (*yat*) is connected, the all-anudātta accent does not arise; the root accent remains.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ई॒यि॒वांस॒मति॒ स्रिधः॒ शश्व॑ती॒रति॑ स॒श्चतः॑ ।  
> अन्वी॑मविंदन्निचि॒रासो॑ अ॒द्रुहो॒प्सु सिं॒हमि॑व त्रि॒तं ॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ईयिवांसं । अति । स्रिधः । तत्वतीः । अति । सच्चतः ।  
> अनु । ईं । अविंदन् । निचिरासः । अद्रुहः । अप्सु । सिंहंइव । श्रितं ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अद्रुहोऽद्रोद्धारो निचिरासो नितरां चिरासश्शिरंतना विश्वे
> देवाः स्रिधः शोषकाञ्त्रून्बलेनातिक्रम्येयिवांसं गच्छंतं तश्वतीर्बह्वीः सश्चतः
> संगतिकारिणीः सेनाश्चात्यतिक्रम्य गच्छंतमप्पु श्रितं तिरोहितमत एव सिंहमिव गुहा-
> प्रविष्टं सिंहमिव भीममीमेनं त्वामन्वविंदन् । अनुगम्यालभंत ॥ ईयिवांसं ।
> इण् गतावित्यस्य क्वसावुपेयिवाननाश्वाननूचानश्च । पा. ३-२-१०९ । इति निपातितः ।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । स्रिधः । स्रिधेः क्षयार्थस्य शोषणार्थस्य वा क्विड् चेति क्विप् । धातु-
> स्वरः । सश्चतः । षस्थ गत् । जकारस्य व्यत्ययेन चकारः । लटः शतादेशः । प्रत्यय-
> स्वरः । अविंदन् । विद्ल लाभ इत्यस्य लजि रूपं । निजिरासः । नितरां चिराः । आज्जसे-
> रसुगित्यसुक् । समानस्वरः । अद्रुहः । द्रुह जिघांसायां । संपदादित्वाद्भावे
> क्विप् । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं । श्रितं । श्रिञ् सेवायामि-
> त्यस्य श्रुकः कितीतीट्प्रतिषेधः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ever-ancient, benevolent gods, passing beyond the drying-up foes and their assembled hosts, found Agni, hidden in the waters like a lion in a cave. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: ईयिवांसं (*īyivāṃsaṃ*), स्रिधः (*sridhaḥ*), सश्चतः (*saścataḥ*), अविंदन् (*aviṃdan*), निचिरासः (*nicirāsaḥ*), अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*), श्रितं (*śritaṃ*). The printed text has "17" after the bhāṣya, a signature number of the press. Variants of the supplied text, left as supplied: the Pada reads तत्वतीः (*tatvatīḥ*) where the Saṃhitā has शश्वतीः (*śaśvatīḥ*); the Pada reads श्रितं (*śritaṃ*) for the Saṃhitā स्रितं (*sritaṃ*); the bhāṣya reads लजि (*laji*) and निजिरासः (*nijirāsaḥ*) in the tail; the Pada has "ಸಿಂಹಂಇವ" joined.

### Printed p. 130

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे अग्ने (*he agne*)—O Agni) अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)—those who are not hostile (the benefactors) and निबिरासः (*nibirāsaḥ*) [sic, as supplied; the bhāṣya has निचिरासः (*nicirāsaḥ*)]—the ever-ancient gods
- स्रिधः (*sridhaḥ*)—the drying-up (withering) enemies
- ईयिवांसं (*īyivāṃsaṃ*)—him who goes (passing beyond them by strength), and शश्वतीः (*śaśvatīḥ*)—the countless, and सश्चतः (*saścataḥ*)—(gathered in one place) assembled armies
- अति (*ati*)—who goes passing beyond
- अप्सु (*apsu*)—in the waters
- श्रितं (*śritaṃ*)—who dwells; सिंहं इव (*siṃhaṃ iva*)—who is like a lion (hence like a lion sheltered in a cave)
- ईं (*īṃ*)—you; अनु अविंदन् (*anu aviṃdan*)—followed after and obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, all the gods, benefactors and ever-ancient, sought you out and at last reached you (came near you): you who confront the countless armies of the enemies gathered together, and who are hidden in the waters as a lion lodges in a cave.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The benignant and long-lived deities have discovered you, Agni, when required to go against their constant and assembled foes, hidden in the waters like a lion (in a cave).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)—अद्रोग्दारः (*adrogdāraḥ*): the meaning is those who have no mind to do harm to others. The Nirukta authors, in the Ṛk आ वामुपस्थमद्रुहा देवाः सीदंतु यज्ञियाः । (*ā vāmupasthamadruhā devāḥ sīdaṃtu yajñiyāḥ |*) इहाद्य सोमपीशये ॥ (*ihādya somapīśaye ‖*) have described अद्रुह: (*adruha:*) as having the sense अद्रोग्यवे (*adrogyave*) [sic, as supplied].

निचिरासः (*nicirāsaḥ*)—नितरां चिरासः चिरंतनाः विश्वेदेवाः (*nitarāṃ cirāsaḥ ciraṃtanāḥ viśvedevāḥ*). Sāyaṇa has explained this word to mean: the very ancient, all the gods, or the Viśvedevas, worshipped (praised) Agni, who confronts the enemies by his own strength, or confronts the armies by his own power.

शत्वतीः (*śatvatīḥ*) [sic, as supplied; the Pada reads तत्वतीः (*tatvatīḥ*), the Saṃhitā शश्वतीः (*śaśvatīḥ*)]—बह्वीः (*bahvīḥ*)—the word शश्वत् (*śaśvat*) is listed among the names for "many" (Ni. 3-13). Here the meaning "many armies" is given.

अप्पु श्रितं सिंहमिव (*appu śritaṃ siṃhamiva*)—अप्पु तिरोहितं गुहाप्रविष्टं सिंहमिव भीमं । (*appu tirohitaṃ guhāpraviṣṭaṃ siṃhamiva bhīmaṃ |*) Because Agni exists in the waters in an invisible form, he is compared to a lion, as one hidden in the water like a lion concealed in a cave.

### Printed p. 131

The particle ईं (*īṃ*) is employed to fill out the pāda, it is stated (Ni. 1-9) [the text reads "ಪರಿತವಾಗಿದೆ", as supplied]. And the particles हरि (*hari*), ईं (*īṃ*), सी (*sī*) are explained as pāda-fillers (Ni. 5-18). Since Sāyaṇa has commented (Ni. 1-4) अथ निपाताः उच्चावचेष्टर्थेषु निपतंति । अनेकप्रकारेष्टर्थेषु निपतंति (*atha nipātāḥ uccāvaceṣṭartheṣu nipataṃti | anekaprakāreṣṭartheṣu nipataṃti*)—that particles also have the power of conveying many kinds of meaning—here for the word ईं (*īṃ*) he has given the sense एनं (*enaṃ*): "this Agni".

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar page, noted briefly.

ईयिवांसम् (*īyivāṃsam*): root इण् (*iṇ*) in the sense of going. When liṭ comes, by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-107) kvasu is substituted for it; by उपेयिवाननाश्वाननूचानश्च (*upeyivānanāśvānanūcānaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-109) the form ending in the kvasu affix is irregularly formed [the text reads "ನಿಷಾ ತ", as supplied]; the affix accent arises; in the accusative singular the form ईयिवांसम् (*īyivāṃsam*) results.

स्रिधः (*sridhaḥ*): root स्रिध (*sridha*) in the sense of decay (drying up); by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) the affix kvip; the root accent remains; form of the nominative plural.

सश्चतः (*saścataḥ*): root षस्थ गत् (*ṣastha gat*) [sic, as supplied]. By व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*) the j of the root is replaced by c; by धात्वादेःषःसः (*dhātvādeḥṣaḥsaḥ*) the initial becomes s. When laṭ comes, śatṛ is substituted for it; the ādyudātta accent of the affix arises.

अविंदन् (*aviṃdan*): root विद्‌ल्य लाभे (*vidlya lābhe*) [sic, as supplied]. The ending अंत् (*aṃt*) replaces the third person plural of laṅ; by इतश्च (*itaśca*) the final i is dropped, and by the loss of the final conjunct the t is dropped. Vikaraṇa śa. By शेमुचादीनाम् (*śemucādīnām*) the root takes the augment num, which becomes anusvāra and parasavarṇa. The base takes the augment aṭ. The all-anudātta accent arises.

निचिरासः (*nicirāsaḥ*): नितरां चिराः निचिराः (*nitarāṃ cirāḥ nicirāḥ*), a prādi compound. When jas follows, by अज्जसेरसुक् (*ajjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50) it takes the augment asuk. By the compound accent the vowel a after r becomes udātta.

अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*): root द्रुह जिघांसायां (*druha jighāṃsāyāṃ*); since it belongs to the sampadādi group, the affix kvip in the abstract sense. In the bahuvrīhi compound, by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the latter member's final udātta accent arises. Form of the nominative plural.

श्रितम् (*śritam*): root त्रिञ् सेवायाम् (*triñ sevāyām*) [sic, as supplied; the bhāṣya reads श्रिञ् (*śriñ*)]. By निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) the affix kta. Because त्रिज्ञान (*trijñāna*) [sic, as supplied] follows, by श्रुकः किति (*śrukaḥ kiti*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-11) the iṭ-augment is prohibited. By the affix accent the word ends in an udātta.

### Printed p. 132

सिंहमिव (*siṃhamiva*)—root हिसि (*hisi*) in the sense of injuring (हिंसायां (*hiṃsāyāṃ*)). Because the root has the marker इ (*i*) the num-augment is added; the affix is ac. Because the word is read in the पृषोदरादि (*pṛṣodarādi*) group, a change of letters occurs. When it is compounded with इव (*iva*) the case ending is not elided. The first member keeps its natural (prakṛti) accent.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒स्य॒वांस॑मिव॒ त्मना॒ग्निमि॒थ्या ति॒रोहि॑तं ।  
> ऐनं॑ नयन्मात॒रिश्वा॑ परा॒वतो॑ दे॒वेभ्यो॑ मथि॒तं परि॑ ॥५॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सस्यवांसंइव । त्मना । अग्निं । इत्था । तिरःऽहितं ।  
> आ । एनं । नयत् । मातरिश्वा । परावतः । देवेभ्यः । मथितं । परि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मातरिश्वा वायुरित्थेत्थं त्मना स्वच्छयाप्सु प्रवेशेन तिरोहितं निलीनं
> परि परितो मथितं मंथनेन निष्पादितमेनमग्निं देवेध्यः । तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ।
> देवार्थं परावतो दूरदेशादानयत् । अनीतवान् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सस्यवांस-
> मिव । यथा स्वाच्छंद्येन सस्यवांसं सरंतं गच्छंतं पुत्रं पिता बलादानयति
> तद्वत् ॥ सस्यवांसमिव । सृ गतावित्यस्माल्लिट् । तस्य क्वसुः । इवेन विभक्त्यलोप
> इत्युक्तत्वात्पत्ययस्वरः । त्मना । आत्मन्शब्यस्य मंत्रेष्टाज्यादेरात्मन इत्याकार-
> लोपः । इत्था । था हेत् च छंदसीति व्यत्ययेन थाप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । एनं ।
> अन्यादेशे द्वितीयाटौष्णेन इत्येनादेशः । अनुदात्तश्च । नयत् । णेञ् प्रापण
> इत्यस्य लजि रूपं । अडभावश्चांदसः । मातरिश्वा। मातर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसितीति त्वन्नु क्षन्नि-
> श्यादिना निपातितः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mātariśvan (Vāyu) brought Agni, hidden in the waters of his own will and produced by churning, from afar for the gods, as a father forcibly brings back a son who wanders at will. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: सस्यवांसमिव (*sasyavāṃsamiva*), त्मना (*tmanā*), इत्था (*itthā*), एनं (*enaṃ*), नयत् (*nayat*), मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*). Variants of the supplied text, left as supplied: the bhāṣya reads देवेध्यः (*devedhyaḥ*) for देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*), आत्मन्शब्यस्य (*ātmanśabyasya*) (sic), and लजि (*laji*) in the tail; the Pada reads तिरःऽहितं (*tiraḥ 'hitaṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)—Vāyu (the wind)
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in the manner stated before
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—of his own will
- तिरोहितं (*tirohitaṃ*)—(having entered the water) hidden; परि मथितं (*pari mathitaṃ*)—produced by thorough churning; एनं अग्निं (*enaṃ agniṃ*)—this Agni
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods
- सस्यवांसमिव (*sasyavāṃsamiva*)—like a son who roams at will (whom the father brings back by force)
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—from a very distant region; आ नयत् (*ā nayat*)—has brought

### Printed p. 133

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vāyu has brought this Agni here for the gods: Agni who, as said before, lay hidden in the waters of his own will, and who was produced by churning; as a father forcibly seizes and brings back a son who roams at will.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Matarishwan therefore brought for the gods from afar, Agni, hiding of himself, and generated by attrition, as (a father brings back) a fugitive (son).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)—वायुः (*vāyuḥ*). Sāyaṇa has explained this word as meaning Vāyu. The Nirukta authors, after citing the Ṛk (Ma. Saṃ. 6-8-4, "ಮ. ಸಂ." as supplied)

आपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्यत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुर्यग्नियम् । (*āpāmupasthe mahiṣā agṛbhyata viśo rājānamupa tasthuryagniyam |*) आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥ (*ā dūto agnimabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ ‖*) (my gloss, mine and tentative: "In the lap of the waters the great ones seized him; the clans stood by the king ...; the messenger of Vivasvat brought Vaiśvānara Agni from afar, Mātariśvan")

have explained, with मातर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति (*mātaryaṃtarikṣe śvasiti*) (he breathes/moves in the mother, the sky)—because he moves without any obstruction in the sky, which is the mother of all beings in the world, or with मातरि आतु अनिति (*mātari ātu aniti*)—because he moves swiftly in the sky—that Vāyu is denoted by the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*).

त्मना (*tmanā*)—स्वेच्छया आप्सु प्रवेशेन (*svecchayā āpsu praveśena*). It is the instrumental singular of the word आर्त्मन (*ārtmana*) [sic, as supplied]. The word त्मना (*tmanā*), used in the Veda with the ā dropped (the text reads "ಅಕಾರವನ್ನು ಉಳಿದು", as supplied), is rendered "by his own will". The sense given is that Agni (printed "ಆಗ್ನಿಯು" [sic, as supplied]) entered the waters as he pleased. The Nirukta authors have cited the use of this word in the same sense. For example:

कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरायोः कथा जाते कवयः को वि वेद । (*katarā pūrvā katarāparāyoḥ kathā jāte kavayaḥ ko vi veda |*) विश्वं त्मना बिभृतो यद्ध नाम वि वर्तेते अहनी चक्रियेव ॥ (*viśvaṃ tmanā bibhṛto yaddha nāma vi vartete ahanī cakriyeva ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-185-1) (my gloss, mine and tentative: "Which of the two is earlier, which later? How were they born, O sages? Who knows? Of their own accord they bear every name, and the two days [day and night] turn like wheels")

Here त्मना (*tmanā*) is explained as आत्मना (*ātmanā*). Examples of the same kind have been cited separately in various places.

परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—दूरदेशात् (*dūradeśāt*). Among the five names for "far", आके (*āke*), पराके (*parāke*), पराचैः (*parācaiḥ*) and so on, the word परावतः (*parāvataḥ*) is stated (Ni. 4-20) [the text reads "ತಬ್ದವು" for "ಶಬ್ದವು", as supplied].

### Printed p. 134

एतदस्या अनः शये सुसंपिष्टं विपाश्या । ससार सीं परावतः ॥ (*etadasyā anaḥ śaye susaṃpiṣṭaṃ vipāśyā | sasāra sīṃ parāvataḥ ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 4-30-11, "ಮ. ಸಂ." as supplied) (my gloss, mine and tentative: "This cart of hers lies well crushed in the Vipāś; she fled far away")

Here परावतः प्रेरितवतः परागताद्वा (*parāvataḥ preritavataḥ parāgatādvā*) is given as one kind of meaning. Durgācārya has also explained the meaning as दूराद्दूरतरं (*dūrāddūrataraṃ*). Because Agni has entered the waters and is therefore far away, Sāyaṇa explains that Mātariśvan fetched him, produced by churning with the araṇis, from a distant region for the delight of the gods, for the sacrifice. In this matter the simile सस्यवांसमिव (*sasyavāṃsamiva*) is stated. For this word [Sāyaṇa's explanation] यथा स्वाच्छंद्येन सरंतं गच्छंतं पुत्रं पिता बलादानयति तद्वैत् (*yathā svācchaṃdyena saraṃtaṃ gacchaṃtaṃ putraṃ pitā balādānayati tadvait*) [the bhāṣya has तद्वत् (*tadvat*); as supplied here] is compared: as a father by force brings back and sets right a son who wanders at will. Because, by the śruti text वायोरग्निः (*vāyoragniḥ*), Agni is born of Vāyu, the relation of father and son (producer and produced) between Vāyu and Agni is appropriate in the illustration.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

सस्यवांसमिव (*sasyavāṃsamiva*)—root सृ (*sṛ*) गत् (*gat*) [sic, as supplied]. When the perfect (liṭ) comes, by क्वसुश्व (*kvasuśva*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-107) the substitution of kvasu (printed "ಕ್ರಸುರಾದೇಶ" [sic, as supplied]); on that basis reduplication of the root and so on. The affix accent remains. By the rule इवेन समासो विभक्त्यलोपश्च (*ivena samāso vibhaktyalopaśca*), when compounded with इव (*iva*), by सुप्रोधातुप्रादिपदिकयोः (*suprodhātuprādipadikayoḥ*) the case ending is not elided. Since the first member keeps its natural accent, the ā after the v becomes udātta.

त्मना (*tmanā*)—when the form आत्मना (*ātmanā*) results, by मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरात्मनः (*maṃtreṣvājyāderātmanaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-141) the ā is elided.

इत्था (*itthā*)—the word इदम् (*idam*). By थाहेतौच छंदसि (*thāhetauca chaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-26) the affix thā is prescribed; by vyatyaya it comes here too. By the affix accent the word is ending-udātta.

एनम् (*enam*)—the taking up again, for another purpose, of a person already once mentioned is called anvādeśa. When anvādeśa appears, for the word इदम् (*idam*), by द्वितीयाटौस्वेनः (*dvitīyāṭausvenaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-5-34) , when the accusative singular follows, there is the substitute ena, and it is all-anudātta.

नयत् (*nayat*)—root णीञ् (*ṇīñ*) प्रापणे (*prāpaṇe*). The affix tip in the third person singular of the imperfect (printed "ಲಜ್" [sic, as supplied]). By इतश्च (*itaśca*) the elision of i; the vikaraṇa śap; on that basis guṇa of the root vowel i; ayādeśa. By बहुलंछंदस्यमाज्‌योगेऽपि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasyamājyoge 'pi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75) the aṭ-augment does not come. The tiṅanta nighāta accent arises.

मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)—मातरि अंतरिक्षे श्वसिति इति मातरिश्वा (*mātari aṃtarikṣe śvasiti iti mātariśvā*). By त्वन्नुषन् (*tvannuṣan*) (U. Sū. 1-57) it is formed irregularly with the affix kanin. The form is nominative singular.

### Printed p. 135

मथितम् (*mathitam*)—root मंथ (*maṃtha*) विलोडने (*viloḍane*). By निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) the affix kta; the iṭ-augment. By अनिदितांहल (*aniditāṃhala*)—[sūtra as supplied, incomplete] the penultimate n is elided. By the affix accent the word is ending-udātta.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं त्वा॒ मर्ता॑ अगृभ्य त दे॒वेभ्यो॑ हव्यवाहन ।  
> विश्वा॒न्यद्य॒ज्ञा अ॑भि॒पासि॑ मानुष॒ तव॒ क्रत्वा॑ यविष्य ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । त्वा । मर्ताः । अग्नृभ्यत । देवेभ्यः । हव्यवाहन ।  
> विश्वान् । यत् । यज्ञान् । अभिपासि । मानुष । तव । क्रत्वा । यविष्य ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे हव्यवाहन हव्यानां वोढर्हे अग्ने मर्ता मनुष्या अध्वर्युप्रभृ-
> तयस्तं तादृशमप्पु तिरोहितं त्वा त्वां देवेभ्यो यष्टव्यदेवतार्थमगृभृत ।
> अगृहृत । मानुष मनुष्याणां हितकारन्यविष्ठ युवतम हे अग्ने तव क्रत्वा तव
> कर्मणा माहात्म्यन विश्वान्सर्वानस्माभिः क्रियमाणान्यज्ञान्यद्यस्मात्कारणादभिपासि
> सर्वतः पालयसि तस्मात्वामगृभृतेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ अगृभृत । ग्रह उपादाने
> क्रादिश्वाच्छा । ग्रहिज्यावयिति संप्रसारणं। हृग्रहोर्भश्चंदसीति हकारस्य भकारः।
> तिज्जतिज इति निघातः । हव्यवाहन । वह प्रापण इति धातोर्ञ्युडित्यनुवृत्तौ । हव्य-
> हव्येनंतःपादमिति त्र्युट् । उपधावृद्धिः । योरनादेशः । अपादादित्वादाष्टमिक-
> मनुदात्तत्वं । विश्वान् । विश प्रवेशन इत्यस्मादशिपुषिलटरणिकणिखटिविशिभ्यः क्वन्निति
> क्वन् । कित्वाद्गुणाभावः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । अभिपासि । पा रक्षणॆ । अस्य धातो
> रक्षणार्थत्वान्न शिबादेशः । यच्छब्दयोगान्न निघातः । धातुस्वरः । क्रत्वा । टा ।
> जसादयश्चंदसि विकल्प्यंत इत्यत्र नादेशाभावः । यणादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ।
> यविष्य । युवशब्दादतिशायने तमबिष्ठनावितीष्ठन् । स्कूलदूरयुवेति यणादि
> परं लुप्यते पूर्वस्य च गुण: । वस्वादित्वात्स्वार्थिको यप्रश्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, carrier of oblations, because by your power you protect on every side all the sacrifices performed by us, mortals such as the Adhvaryu took you, hidden in the water, for the gods. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: अगृभृत (*agṛbhṛta*), हव्यवाहन (*havyavāhana*), विश्वान् (*viśvān*), अभिपासि (*abhipāsi*), क्रत्वा (*kratvā*), यविष्य (*yaviṣya*). Variants of the supplied text, left as supplied: the Saṃhitā reads अगृभ्य त (*agṛbhya ta*) (with a space), the Pada अग्नृभ्यत (*agnṛbhyata*), the bhāṣya अगृभृत (*agṛbhṛta*); the Saṃhitā and Pada read यविष्य (*yaviṣya*), the bhāṣya यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मानुष (*mānuṣa*)—beneficial to men
- यविष्ठ्य (*yaviṣṭhya*) [as supplied; the Saṃhitā has यविष्य (*yaviṣya*)]—exceedingly young, O Agni; तव क्रत्वा (*tava kratvā*)—by your deed (greatness)
- विश्वान् (*viśvān*)—(performed by us) [the sentence breaks off at the end of printed p. 135 and continues on p. 136]

### Printed p. 136

*[Continuation of the Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 6; the first word is cut at the page boundary in the supplied text, "…ವಾದ)", and the text continues:]* …all (the sacrifices performed by us). यज्ञान् (*yajñān*)—the sacrifices. यत् (*yat*)—for which reason. अभिपासि (*abhipāsi*)—you protect on every side. (तत् (*tat*)—for that reason.) (हे (*he*)) हव्यवाहन (*havyavāhana*)—O Agni, bearer of oblations to the gods. मर्ताः (*martāḥ*)—men such as the Adhvaryu. तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*)—you, hidden in the water. देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the sake of the worshipful gods. आगृभ्यत (*āgṛbhyata*) *[as supplied; the Saṃhitā has अगृभ्यत (*agṛbhyata*)]*—took, grasped.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, beneficial to men and the best among the young: all the sacrifices that we perform are protected on every side by your greatness; therefore the Adhvaryu and the others accept (welcome) you, who bear the oblations to the gods and were hidden in the water, for the worship of the gods.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Bearer of oblations, men apprehend you (thus concealed) for the service of the gods. and that you, youugest [sic] (of the deities) and friendly to mankind, may recompense by the acts all their pious rites.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हव्यवाहन (*havyavāhana*)—हव्यानां वोढर्हे अग्नॆ (*havyānāṃ voḍharhe agnè*). The Nirukta authors, in the Ṛk प्र तद्वोचेयं भव्यायेंदवे हव्यो न य इषर्वा मन्म रेजति रक्षोहा मन्म रेजति (*pra tadvoceyaṃ bhavyāyeṃdave havyo na ya iṣarvā manma rejati rakṣohā manma rejati*) (Pu. Saṃ. 1-19-6, "ಪು. ಸಂ." as supplied), have explained the word हव्यो न (*havyo na*) as हवनार्ह इव (*havanārha iva*) (like one worthy of invocation). Durgācārya, at यः यज्ञेन च पुनराहूयते अहवर्धाक्त्वादेव (*yaḥ yajñena ca punarāhūyate ahavardhāktvādeva*) , has described the sense: Agni, on account of the sacrifice, is invoked many times by the sacrificers, as if he were calling the gods who receive the oblations, though he himself has no share of the oblation.

In the Ṛk ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियंधा: स्वदंति देवा उभयानि हव्या (*ye sukratavaḥ śucayo dhiyaṃdhā: svadaṃti devā ubhayāni havyā*) the word हव्या (*havyā*) is explained as हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*). Agni is thus addressed as one who receives the oblations offered by those who sacrifice for the gods and hands them over to the gods.

मर्ताः (*martāḥ*)—this word is stated among the names of men (Ni. 3-8) and is explained as मनुष्या: (*manuṣyā:*) . अध्वर्य प्रभृतयः (*adhvarya prabhṛtayaḥ*)—the priests beginning with the Adhvaryu. These priests, it is said, accept (take) Agni, who has entered the waters and remains in an invisible form, in order to invite to the sacrifice the gods who receive the oblations, and to bring him to the sacrifice.

*[Printed p. 137 begins here.]*

### Printed p. 137

मानुष (*mānuṣa*)—मनुष्याणां हितकारिन् (*manuṣyāṇāṃ hitakārin*). Agni is addressed as one who brings benefit to men.

यविष्ट (*yaviṣṭa*) *[as supplied; the Saṃhitā has यविष्य (*yaviṣya*)]*—युवतम (*yuvatama*). Agni, being always free of childhood and old age and ever possessed of the vigour that belongs to youth, is addressed as the best even among the young.

कृत्वा (*kṛtvā*) *[as supplied; the Ṛk has क्रत्वा, see the Saṃhitā]*—कर्मणा मात्र्येन (*karmaṇā mātryena*) . Because Agni protects, by his greatness and by favouring the sacrificers, all the sacrificers and the sacrifices, the priests bring him, though he is in a distant region; so it is explained. On this point Sāyaṇa's comment is: सर्वानस्माभिः क्रियमाणा यज्ञान् यस्मात् कारणात् सर्वतः पालयसि तस्मादगृभत (*sarvānasmābhiḥ kriyamāṇā yajñān yasmāt kāraṇāt sarvataḥ pālayasi tasmādagṛbhata*) , and so it stands.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

मर्ताः (*martāḥ*)—root मृज् (*mṛj*) (प्राणत्यागे (*prāṇatyāge*), in the leaving of life); an affix of the औषादिकतन् (*auṣādikatan*) kind; guṇa of the ṛ by सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*); the udātta accent on the final syllable (आम्यवात्तस्वर (*āmyavāttasvara*) as supplied) arises because the affix has an n.

अगृभ्यत (*agṛbhyata*)—root ग्रह (*graha*) (उपादाने (*upādāne*)), of the क्रादि (*krādi*) class; the affix jha in the third person plural of the imperfect (printed लज् (*laj*) [sic, as supplied]); by आत्मनेपदेष्टनतः (*ātmanepadeṣṭanataḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-5) the substitute ata; vikaraṇa śnā by क्रादिभ्यःश्ना (*krādibhyaḥśnā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-81); by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Gā. Sū. 6-4-112, "ಗಾ. ಸೂ." as supplied) elision of the ā/i of the vikaraṇa; samprasāraṇa of the r of the root by ग्रहिज्यावयिव्यधि (*grahijyāvayivyadhi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-16); the form with pūrvarūpa; by the statement हृग्रहोर्भंदसि (*hṛgrahorbhaṃdasi*) bha for the ha of the root; the aṭ augment of the stem; and since it stands after an ati-ending verb, the nighāta accent by तिज्जतिजिः (*tijjatijiḥ*) .

हव्यवाहन (*havyavāhana*)—root वह (*vaha*) (प्रापणे (*prāpaṇe*)); with the ñyuṭ affix carried over from the preceding sūtra, by हव्येनंतः पादम् (*havyenaṃtaḥ pādam*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-66) when the word havya is the upapada; because the affix is a *ṭ*-affix, vṛddhi of the upadhā a by आतउपधायाः (*ātaupadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116); by युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the substitute ana for the affix. In the vocative, since the word is not at the beginning of a pāda, by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the all-anudātta accent comes.

### Printed p. 138

*[Stray line at the foot of p. 137: "18" (the signature number); kept.]*

विश्वान् (*viśvān*)—root विश (*viśa*) (प्रवेशने (*praveśane*)); the affix kvan by अशिपुषिलटरणिकणिखटिविशिभ्यः क्वन् (*aśipuṣilaṭaraṇikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan*) (U. Sū. 1-149); because it is a *k*-affix there is no guṇa of the light penultimate vowel; because it is an *n*-affix the initial-udātta accent arises; the form is accusative plural.

अभिपासि (*abhipāsi*)—root पा (*pā*) (रक्षणे (*rakṣaṇe*)), second person singular of the present; since the root has the sense of protecting, the substitute piba does not come; because of the connection with the word यत् (*yat*) the all-anudātta accent does not come; since the affix sip has a p it is anudātta, so the root accent remains; because an accented verb follows, by तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) *[as supplied; the sūtra number printed is "8-1-71"]* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) the word अभि (*abhi*) becomes all-anudātta.

कृत्वा (*kṛtvā*) —by कृञ् क्रतुः (*kṛñ kratuḥ*) (U. Sū. 1-77) the affix kratu after the root कृञ् (*kṛñ*), giving क्रतु (*kratu*); in the instrumental singular, by जसादिषु छंदसि वा वचनम् (*jasādiṣu chaṃdasi vā vacanam*) the ending does not take nā; yaṇ substitution; initial udātta by the affix accent.

यविष्य (*yaviṣya*)—अतिशयेन युवा यविष्यः (*atiśayena yuvā yaviṣyaḥ*). By अतिशायने तमभिष्ठन् (*atiśāyane tamabhiṣṭhan*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55) the affix iṣṭhan after the word युवन् (*yuvan*) in the sense of excess; when it follows, by स्कूलदूरयुव (*skūladūrayuva*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156) the part after the yaṇ-sound (van) is elided, guṇa of the preceding u, avādeśa; since it is read in the vasu-class, the affix ya in its own sense; the vocative accent follows.

> झस्यादेशः । यद्योगादनिघातः । तिजि चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः । धातुस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, this auspicious sacrificial work of yours (the Agnihotra and the like) honours even the ignorant sacrificer, like a child, with cattle and sons, because at the beginning of the night animals of both kinds sit around you kindled. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*), पाकाय (*pākāya*), छदयति (*chadayati*), समासते (*samāsate*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे (*he*)) अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- अपितर्वरे (*apitarvare*) —at the beginning of the night (at the time of the Agni's wandering)
- समिद्धं (*samiddhaṃ*)—kindled
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- पशवः (*paśavaḥ*)—(two-footed and four-footed) all living beings; सं आसते (*saṃ āsate*)—worship well
- (तत् (*tat*)—therefore)
- तव (*tava*)—belonging to you (and)
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—auspicious
- दंसना (*daṃsanā*)—this work, the Agnihotra and the like
- पाकायचित् (*pākāyacit*)—(like a child) the ignorant, or the praiseworthy, sacrificer
- छदयति (*chadayati*)—(by granting its fruit) honours. *[A stray "!" stands after "ಮತ್ತು" in the supplied text.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, all beings, two-footed and the rest, worship you who are kindled at the beginning of the night (the time of the Agni's wandering); therefore the auspicious works such as the Agnihotra, performed with you in view, bestow the fruit of cattle, sons and the like even on the ignorant.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Auspicious is yuro [sic] worship for it prospers the ignorant (worshipper), wherefore animals reverence you Agni, kindled in the beginning of the night- *[the sentence is cut at the foot of p. 139; its continuation, which should stand at the head of p. 140, is missing from the supplied text]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शत् भद,ं दंसना पाकाय चित् छदयति—हे अग्ने तव संबंधि इदं शोभनं अग्निहोत्रादिकं कर्म अर्थकं पशुपुत्रादिभिः परिवृतं करोति । यद्वा । पाकशब्दः प्रशस्यं वक्ति । पाकः वामः इति तन्नामसु पठितत्वात् । तद्भदं प्रशस्यं यजमानमभिमतफलप्रदानेन पूजयति ॥ (*śat bhada,ṃ daṃsanā pākāya cit chadayati—he agne tava saṃbaṃdhi idaṃ śobhanaṃ agnihotrādikaṃ karma arthakaṃ paśuputrādibhiḥ parivṛtaṃ karoti | yadvā | pākaśabdaḥ praśasyaṃ vakti | pākaḥ vāmaḥ iti tannāmasu paṭhitatvāt | tadbhadaṃ praśasyaṃ yajamānamabhimataphalapradānena pūjayati ‖*) *[quoted as supplied; the beginning "ಶತ್ ಭದ,ಂ" and "ತದ್ಭದಂ" look corrupt, and "ಪಾಕಃ ವಾಮಃ" and "ಅರ್ಥಕಂ" differ from the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of this Ṛk, which has "ತತ್ ಭದ್ರಂ", "ತದ್ಭದ್ರಂ", "ಪಾಕೋ ನಾಮ" and "ಅರ್ಭಕಃ"; not corrected] **NOTE***

दंस (*daṃsa*)—this word is stated among the names of works (Ni. 3-2); the sense "works such as the Agnihotra" is thus explained. The word भद्र (*bhadra*) (Ni. 4-9) is explained thus: भजनीयं भूतानामभिद्रवणीयं भवद्रममयतीति वा भाजनवद्वा (*bhajanīyaṃ bhūtānāmabhidravaṇīyaṃ bhavadramamayatīti vā bhājanavadvā*) ; that is, what is fit to be attained by beings, what gladdens beings, and what attracts the minds of beings: so the sense of the word bhadra is explained. Since the word पाकः (*pākaḥ*) is stated among the names of what is praiseworthy (Ni. 3-13), the sense "praiseworthy" is explained here. And in the passage धीरः पाकमत्राविवेश (*dhīraḥ pākamatrāviveśa*) the sense "a fool who knows nothing" is given to the word pāka: पाकः पक्षव्यो भवति (*pākaḥ pakṣavyo bhavati*) . Here Sāyaṇa has explained the sense in two ways. First, addressing Agni, he explains that the work of the Agnihotra (offering in Agni), being worthy of honour, brings about for the dull and ignorant the increase of sons, grandsons and the like. Second, taking the word pāka as an epithet of bhadra and accepting the sense "praiseworthy", he describes that the Agnihotra and the rest produce the desired, praiseworthy welfare for the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, and so bring honour to the sacrificers.

अपितर्वरे समिद्धं पशवः समुपासते शवर्रीमुखे अग्नि विहरणकाल एव दी प्यमानं त्वां द्विपदाश्च तुष्पदाश्चोभये पशतु पर्युपासते । (*apitarvare samiddhaṃ paśavaḥ samupāsate śavarrīmukhe agni viharaṇakāla eva dī pyamānaṃ tvāṃ dvipadāśca tuṣpadāścobhaye paśatu paryupāsate |*) *[as supplied; the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya has ಶರ್ವರೀಮುಖೇ, ಚತುಷ್ಪದಾಶ್ಚ, ಪಶವಃ, ಸಮಾಸತೇ; not corrected]* The word शवर्री (*śavarrī*) is stated among the names of night (Ni. 2-28). Here the word śarvara is given the sense śavarrī (night); he explains that Agni is kindled at the beginning of the night, and that then men (human beings) and other creatures also serve him; and तदिदं पश्वादिलक्षणं फलं यजमानाय प्रयच्छति (*tadidaṃ paśvādilakṣaṇaṃ phalaṃ yajamānāya prayacchati*): Agni, worshipped by all, bestows on the sacrificers the fruit consisting of servants, men and women, and of cattle and the like.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

भद्रम् (*bhadram*)—root भदि (*bhadi*) (कल्याणे सुखेच (*kalyāṇe sukheca*)); the affix rak is given as irregular by the sūtra स्थायितंचि (*sthāyitaṃci*) (U. Sū. 1-186), hence final-udātta. पाकाय (*pākāya*)—root पा (*pā*) (रक्षणे (*rakṣaṇe*)); the affix kan by इण् भीकापाशलि (*iṇ bhīkāpāśali*) (U. Sū. 3-323); पायते रक्ष्यते राजादिभिः इति पाकः (*pāyate rakṣyate rājādibhiḥ iti pākaḥ*) (the one protected by kings and others); the explanation of the accent continues on p. 141.

### Printed p. 141

Because the affix has an n, the initial-udātta accent comes by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 *[as printed; the number is the same as the next one]*); the form is the dative singular.

छदयति (*chadayati*)—root छद (*chada*) (अपवारणे (*apavāraṇe*) *[the bhāṣya has ಆಪವರಣೇ]*); ṇic in its own sense; since the root ends in a, elision of the a by अतोलोपः (*atolopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48); by अचःपरस्मिन् पूर्वविधौ (*acaḥparasmin pūrvavidhau*) (Pā. Sū. 1-1-57) the elided a counts as still present, so no vṛddhi of the penultimate syllable comes on account of ṇic; lat after the ṇic-ending root, tip in the third person singular, śap, guṇa of the ṇic, ayādeśa; since it stands after an ati-ending verb the nighāta accent comes.

समासते (*samāsate*)—prefix सम् (*sam*); the root आस (*āsa*) (उपवेशने (*upaveśane*)) of the adādi class; lat, third person plural, the affix jha; elision (luk) of śap by आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः तपः (*ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ tapaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72); the substitute ata for jha by आत्मनेपदेष्टनतः (*ātmanepadeṣṭanataḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-5); because of the connection with yat the nighāta accent does not come; by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the ending after the anudātta-it root is anudātta, the root accent remaining; by तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) the prefix सम् (*sam*) becomes anudātta before an accented verb.

समिद्धम् (*samiddham*)—root इंधी (*iṃdhī*) (दीप्तौ (*dīptau*)), affix kta; by अनिदितांहल (*aniditāṃhala*) *[as supplied, the rest of the sūtra not printed]* elision of the n of the root; by झषस्तथो (*jhaṣastatho*) dha for the affix; by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the prefix सम् (*sam*) takes the udātta accent.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer urges the priests: gratify with oblations this Agni, who has a purifying flame, lies hidden in wood and plants, and has a good sacrifice; he is swift, a messenger of the gods, ancient and worthy of praise; honour him quickly. (The grammatical tail is transcribed, not explained: जुहोत (*juhota*), स्वध्वरं (*svadhvaraṃ*), शीरं (*śīraṃ*), पावकशोचिषं (*pāvakaśociṣaṃ*), आशुं (*āśuṃ*), अजिरं (*ajiraṃ*), प्रत्नं (*pratnaṃ*), ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*), सपर्यत (*saparyata*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे ऋत्विजः (*he ṛtvijaḥ*)—O priests)
- पावकशोचिसं (*pāvakaśocisaṃ*) —he who has a purifying flame
- शीरं (*śīraṃ*)—he who lies hidden (in wood and plants)
- स्वध्वरं (*svadhvaraṃ*)—he who has an auspicious sacrifice; this Agni; आ जुहोत (*ā juhota*)—gratify well (with oblations); (and further) अशुं (*aśuṃ*) —he who pervades the work
- दूतं (*dūtaṃ*)—messenger (because he calls the gods)
- अजिरं (*ajiraṃ*)—swift (in coming)
- प्रत्नं (*pratnaṃ*)—ancient
- ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*)—worthy of praise
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—shining; this Agni
- श्रुष्टि (*śruṣṭi*)—quickly
- सपरत (*saparata*) —honour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, gratify well with oblations Agni, who has a flame that makes pure, who is present in wood and the like, and who pervades works, who calls the gods *[the supplied text, and with it this window, breaks off here in mid-word: "ಕರೆಯುವವ…"; the rest of the Bhāvārtha follows in the next window]*

### Printed p. 143

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

*(continued from p. 142; the word broken off there, "ಕರೆಯುವವ…", is completed by the first letters of this page: "ಕರೆಯುವವನಾದುದರಿಂದ")*

— and since he is thus one who calls the gods, he is called by the word "messenger"; he who comes swiftly to the sacrifices, the ancient one, worthy of praise, the shining one: worship such Agni quickly.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Offer oblations to the object of holy sacrifice, the brilliant purifier, who is dormant (in fuel) : worship quietly the pervader (of the rite) the messenger (of the gods), the rapid, the ancient deity who is entitled to laudation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पावकशोचिसं (*pāvakaśocisaṃ*) *[as supplied; the Saṃhitā has "ಪಾವಕಶೋಚಿಷಂ" in the bhāṣya]*—शोचिषमित्यत्र पवनं पावः शुद्धिः तं कायतीति पावकः । शोधकदीप्तिं । (*śociṣamityatra pavanaṃ pāvaḥ śuddhiḥ taṃ kāyatīti pāvakaḥ | śodhakadīptiṃ |*) The sense is explained as: Agni has flames (rays) that produce purification, and is therefore brilliant.

शीरं (*śīraṃ*)—काष्ठोषधीषु जानुशायिनं. (*kāṣṭhoṣadhīṣu jānuśāyinaṃ.*) The meaning is that Agni pervades the pieces of wood and the herbs. The Nirukta-writers (Yāska) cite the Ṛk:

शीरं पावकशोचिसं ज्येष्ठो यो दमेष्वा । दीदाय दीर्घश्रुुत्तमः ॥ (*śīraṃ pāvakaśocisaṃ jyeṣṭho yo dameṣvā | dīdāya dīrghaśruuttamaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-102-11, printed "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೮-೧೦೨-೧೧"; the text is quoted as supplied, with the doubled श्रुु (*śruu*), [sic])

and, having cited this Ṛk, explain: पावकदीप्तं अनुशायिनमिति वाशिनमिति वा । (*pāvakadīptaṃ anuśāyinamiti vāśinamiti vā |*) The words अनुशायि (*anuśāyi*) and आशि (*āśi*) are explained as "one who pervades"; and पावयित्रि यस्य तोचिः दीप्तिः (*pāvayitri yasya tociḥ dīptiḥ*) *[as supplied, "ತೋಚಿಃ" for "ಶೋಚಿಃ"]*: since the splendour of Agni produces purification, Agni is explained as the one who purifies.

स्वध्वरं (*svadhvaraṃ*)—शोभनयज्ञोपेतं । (*śobhanayajñopetaṃ |*) Since Agni is the means of sacrifices that bring excellent and auspicious fruit, he is described as one endowed with sacrifices.

दूतं (*dūtaṃ*)—देवानां आज्ञानकारितेन दूतं (*devānāṃ ājñānakāritena dūtaṃ*) . Because he invites the gods to the sacrifice and delivers to each their respective shares of the oblation, Agni is described as the messenger of the gods.

अजिरं (*ajiraṃ*)—क्षिप्रं गंतारं. (*kṣipraṃ gaṃtāraṃ.*) The word अजिर (*ajira*) is stated among the names of "swift" (Ni. 3-9). It is explained that Agni moves quickly (or rapidly).

ईड्यं देवं श्रुष्टि सपर्यत (*īḍyaṃ devaṃ śruṣṭi saparyata*)—The word श्रुष्टि (*śruṣṭi*) is read among the names of "swift" (Ni. 3-9). The seer of the mantra commands, in the form of an order: worship quickly Agni, who is very brilliant and worthy of the praise of all, and satisfy him with those oblations (जुहोत (*juhota*) [sic, as supplied: the text has "ಆ ಜುಹೋತ ಅಹುತಿಗಳಿಂದ"]); thus the seer describes the abundant greatness of Agni.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Words treated (Pāṇinian sūtras as printed): जुहोत (*juhota*) (root हु (*hu*) in the sense of giving and eating; laṭ-type imperative, second person plural, affix tha; the substitute ta by तस्‌थस्‌थमिपां (*tasthasthamipāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101); śluvikaraṇa by जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः (*juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-75); reduplication; the substitute tap for the affix by तप्तनप्तनथ-नाश्च (*taptanaptanatha-nāśca*) (Pā. ##### Gist of the bhāṣya
