##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the priest set in front, is the special seer of the sacrifice and knows the Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices in their due order; the rest explains the grammar of *veda* and *ānuṣak*.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

होता (*hotā*)—the invoker of the gods. पुरोहितः (*purohitaḥ*)—the priest of the gods, or one who, giving the desired fruit beforehand, brings about good, or one established in front (in the eastern part) in the form of the Āhavanīya fire. अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the sacrifice. विचर्षणिः (*vicarṣaṇiḥ*)—the special seer. सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*)—that Agni. आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—performed in due order. यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice such as the Agniṣṭoma. वेद (*veda*)—knows.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who calls the gods to the sacrifices, who is the priest of the gods (who, in advance, grants what is desired and is beneficial to the people, or who is installed in the eastern part of the sacrificial hall in the form of the Āhavanīya), and who has special knowledge of the sacrifice, knows in due order the sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the invoker of the gods, the niinister [sic] (of the gods), the supervisor of the sacrifice, understands the solemn rite in its due course.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**पुरोहितः (*purohitaḥ*)**—पुरत एवाभिमतफलसंपादकत्वेन हितकारी यद्वा पुरः पूर्व (*purata evābhimataphalasaṃpādakatvena hitakārī yadvā puraḥ pūrva*) भागे आहवनीयरूपेण निहित इति पुरोहितः (*bhāge āhavanīyarūpeṇa nihita iti purohitaḥ*) (the print breaks the line inside the compound *pūrvabhāge*, so the supplied text shows it as two words). Yāska has explained it as पुर एनं दधाति (*pura enaṃ dadhāti*) (Ni. 2-12). Sāyaṇa has explained two kinds of meaning: that Agni, by granting the sacrificers what they wish, is one who brings about benefit in the future; or that he is placed (installed) in the eastern part of the sacrificial hall under the name Āhavanīya.

**अध्वरस्य विचर्षणि (*adhvarasya vicarṣaṇi*)**—The word *adhvara* is spoken among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19) and also among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). The word *vicarṣaṇi* is spoken among the eight "seeing" verbs, चिक्कत् (*cikkat*), जाकनत् (*jākanat*) (as supplied; both look garbled) and the rest, the sentence running over into the next page.

### Printed p. 179

*[The Special Topics sentence continues from p. 178.]* …(these eight) verbs of seeing (Ni. 3-13). Because Agni does the act of offering the oblation both to the gods and to himself, and because he is the cause of the welfare of the world by rain and the like, the meaning is described as: Agni is the one who looks upon the sacrifice with special care.

**अग्निरानुषक् (*agnirānuṣak*)**—आ समंतात् आनुषजतीति (*ā samaṃtāt ānuṣajatīti*). Agni, who has full knowledge that all the rites to be performed in the sacrifice go on rightly in the order prescribed, is said to have the knowledge of performing the rites (*kratu*) such as the Agniṣṭoma.

**होता (*hotā*)**—देवानां आह्वाता (*devānāṃ āhvātā*)—it was explained earlier that Agni invokes the gods for the sacrifice.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- पुरोहितः (*purohitaḥ*): by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. 6-2-49) the stem accent comes on the *gati* (*puraḥ*).
- वेद (*veda*): root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*). In the *laṭ* third person singular the affix *tip*; by विदोलटोवा (*vidolaṭovā*) (Pā. 3-4-83) the substitute *ṇal* for it. By पुगंतलघूपधस्य च (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasya ca*) (Pā. 7-3-86) the light penultimate of the root takes guṇa, and the form is *veda*. Since it follows a non-finite-verb word (the supplied text has "ಅತಿಣಂತದ", as supplied), the *nighāta* accent comes.
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*): आ समंतात् अनुषजति इति आनुषक् (*ā samaṃtāt anuṣajati iti ānuṣak*). Root षज्ञ संगे (*ṣajña saṃge*) . By धात्वादेः षःसः (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥsaḥ*) (Pā. 6-1-64) *s* is substituted for *ṣ*. By क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) (Pā. 3-2-76) the affix *kvip*. By अनिदितांहलउपधा (*aniditāṃhalaupadhā*) (Pā. 6-4-24) the penultimate nasal of the root is elided, and the form *saj* results. By उपसर्गात्सुनोति (*upasargātsunoti*) (Pā. 8-3-65) the retroflex *ṣ* comes, since *s* follows the cause in the preverb. In the nominative singular, when *su* comes it is elided by the rule beginning हल् ज्याभ्यो (*hal jyābhyo*) (the rest of the name is not given). By चोःकुः (*coḥkuḥ*) (Pā. 8-2-30) the substitute *g* for *j*. By वावसाने (*vāvasāne*) (Pā. 8-4-56) optionally *k*. The accent of the final member of the krt compound comes.

> स हव्यवाट् हविषो वोढामर्त्यो मरणधर्मरहित उतिक् हविः काम-
> यमानो दूतो देवानां दूतश्चनसे हविर्लक्षणायान्नाय हिते निहितः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, bearer of the oblation, deathless, desiring the oblation, messenger of the gods, placed for the food in the form of the oblation (or: whose welcome food is the oblation), is joined with understanding; the rest explains the grammar of the words.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*)—the bearer of the oblation (to the gods). अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—free from death. उशिक् (*uśik*)—the one who desires (the oblation). दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—the messenger (of the gods). चनः हितः (*canaḥ hitaḥ*)—established for the sake of the food in the form of the oblation, or fond of the food in the form of the oblation (the supplied text has the line broken at "ಹವೀರೂಪಾನ್ನಕ್ಕೋ / ಸ್ಕರ", as supplied). सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*)—that Agni. धिया (*dhiyā*)—with understanding (in the matter of the rite). सं ऋण्वति (*saṃ ṛṇvati*)—becomes united.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the bearer of the oblation, free from death, desirous of the oblation, the messenger of the gods, established for the very purpose of receiving the food in the form of the oblation, becomes endowed with knowledge of the rites such as the Agniṣṭoma. (May such an Agni be the giver of knowledge of the rites to us also.) (The supplied text has "ಅಂತಹ!" with an exclamation mark, as supplied.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
That Agni, who is the bearer of oblations, the immortal, the desirer (of offerings), the messenger (of the gods), and is the receiver of sacrificial viands, is associated with understanding.

### Printed p. 181

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**उशिक् (*uśik*)**—हविःकामयमानः (*haviḥkāmayamānaḥ*). The word *uśik* is spoken among the eighteen words of lustre (the print names वश्मि (*vaśmi*) and उत्सि (*utsi*) among them; Ni. 3-9). The word *uśik* is derived from the root *vaś*, which conveys the sense of desire/lustre. Here the meaning is described as: Agni desires the oblation.

**दूतः, देवानां दूतः (*dūtaḥ, devānāṃ dūtaḥ*)**—Because Agni calls the gods to the sacrifice and carries to each of them his portion of the oblation, he is described as the messenger (servant) of the gods.

**चनोहितः (*canohitaḥ*)**—चनसे हविर्लक्षणायानाय हितः । यद्वा चनोन्नं हविर्ल (*canase havirlakṣaṇāyānāya hitaḥ | yadvā canonnaṃ havirla*) क्षणं हितमस्येति (*kṣaṇaṃ hitamasyeti*) (the print breaks the line inside *havirlakṣaṇam*; the supplied text has हविर्लक्षणायानाय (*havirlakṣaṇāyānāya*) where the bhāṣya has "ಹವಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಣಾಯಾನ್ನಾಯ", as supplied). The word *canas* has been explained by Sāyaṇa as "ಚನ್ನೋನಂ" (as supplied, i.e. food). Yāska's explanation is चन इत्यन्ननाम (*cana ityannanāma*) (Ni. 6-16). Taking the two words दूतः चनोहितः (*dūtaḥ canohitaḥ*) together, one meaning given here is that Agni is a messenger placed by the gods (for the sake of food); another is that, since the food in the form of the oblation nourishes Agni and is agreeable to him, Agni is designated by this word.

**धिया समृण्वति (*dhiyā samṛṇvati*)**—प्रज्ञया संगच्छते । कर्मविषयप्रज्ञानितो अग्निरस्मानपि (*prajñayā saṃgacchate | karmaviṣayaprajñānito agnirasmānapi*) तादृक् प्रज्ञान्वित्वान् करोत्वित्याशास्ते (*tādṛk prajñānvitvān karotvityāśāste*) (the print breaks the line after *asmānapi*; the supplied text has ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಿತೋ and ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ್ವಿತ್ವಾನ್ where the bhāṣya reads differently, as supplied). The word *dhī* is spoken among the names of action (Ni. 3-2) and among the names of understanding (Ni. 3-13). Here the meaning is explained as understanding concerned with the rite: may Agni, endowed with understanding of the rites, make the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice likewise endowed with understanding; thus the wish is expressed.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*): हव्यं वहति इति हव्यवाट् (*havyaṃ vahati iti havyavāṭ*). By वहश्च (*vahaśca*) (Pā. 3-2-64) the affix *ṇi*. By अतउपधायाः (*ataupadhāyāḥ*) vṛddhi of the penultimate of the root. By होढः (*hoḍhaḥ*) the substitute *ḍh* for *h*. By झलांजशोंते (*jhalāṃjaśoṃte*) (Pā. 8-2-39) the substitute *ḍ* for it at the end of the word. By नावसाने (*nāvasāne*) the substitute *ṭ*. Since the first member is a *kāraka*, the accent of the final member of a krt compound comes.
- उशिक् (*uśik*): root वश कांतौ (*vaśa kāṃtau*). When इजिः (*ijiḥ*) continues from the preceding sūtra, by वशेः किच्च (*vaśeḥ kicca*) (Uṇ. 2-229) the affix *iji*. Because *k*-marking is prescribed, by the rule ज्यावयिव्यधि (*jyāvayivyadhi*) (Pā. 6-1-16; the name begins with ಗ್ರಹಿ at the end of the preceding line) the root's *v* undergoes *samprasāraṇa* (*u*), and by the rule beginning संप्र (*saṃpra*) साराणाच्च (*sārāṇācca*) (split by the line break) the earlier form comes. The word becomes उशिज् (*uśij*). By the affix accent the *i* becomes udātta. The final *j* takes *k* and the substitution for the final stop. *[The grammar notes continue on p. 182.]*

### Printed p. 182

Grammar notes of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 181 (noted briefly; the supplied text has several slips in the sūtra names and technical terms, kept as supplied):

- चनोहितः (*canohitaḥ*): the word चनः (*canaḥ*) is formed from the root चाय्क्य (*cāykya*) (printed so; पूजानिशामनयोः (*pūjāniśāmanayoḥ*)) when it has the sense of food, by चायतेरन्ने प्रस्वश्च (*cāyateranne prasvaśca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-639): the affix *asun* with the augment *ṇuḍ* (printed "ಮಡಾಗಮ"), and shortening of the root; the *y* of the root is elided when the affix comes. Because *asun* has the marker *n*, चनः (*canaḥ*) is initial-udātta. हितः (*hitaḥ*) comes from the root धा (*dhā*) with the affix *kta*, by धधातेर्हिः (*dhadhāterhiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42) the substitute हि (*hi*). By the statement पुनश्चनसोश्चंदसि गतिसंज्ञावक्तव्या (*punaścanasoścaṃdasi gatisaṃjñāvaktavyā*) (Pā. Sū 1-4-60.2) चनः (*canaḥ*) receives the name *gati*; since a word ending in *kta* is the latter member, by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū 6-2-49) चनः (*canaḥ*) keeps its natural accent, and so चनोहितः (*canohitaḥ*) is initial-udātta. In the second explanation (a *bahuvrīhi* compound) the accent of the first member comes by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1).
- धिया (*dhiyā*): instrumental singular; by सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā.Sū. 6-1-168) the case ending takes the udātta.
- ऋण्वति (*ṛṇvati*): root ऋणु गतौ (*ṛṇu gatau*). In the *leṭ* third person singular the affix *tip*; by लेटोडाटौ (*leṭoḍāṭau*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-93) the augment *aḍ*. By तनादिकृञ्भ उः (*tanādikṛñbha uḥ*) (no number printed) the *vikaraṇa* *u*, and the substitution *yaṇ* (printed "ಯಣಾದೇಶ"). Since it follows a non-finite-verb word (the supplied text has "ಅತಿಜಂತದ", as supplied) the *nighāta* accent comes.

> यज्ञस्याग्निष्टोमादेः केतुः प्रज्ञापकः पूर्व्यः पूर्वे भवश्चि-

> कुषिगर्तिभ्यस्थन्निति थन् । गुणः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । तरणि । त्वा प्लवनतरणयोः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the ancient indicator of the sacrifice, knows everything by his understanding; the radiance of this moving Agni is the remover of the darkness. The rest gives the grammar of the words (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma. केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—the giver of knowledge. पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)—the ancient one. सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*)—that Agni. धिया (*dhiyā*)—with (his) power of grasping. चेतति (*cetati*)—knows (everything); (of such an Agni) अर्थं (*arthaṃ*)—the radiance endowed with the nature of movement. अस्य (*asya*)—of this (visible) darkness. शरणि हि (*śaraṇi hi*) (printed so; the Saṃhitā and Pada have तरणि (*taraṇi*))—is indeed the warder-off (printed "ವಾರಕ", as supplied).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the giver of knowledge concerning the sacrifices, the ancient one, can know everything by his power of grasping; the radiance of such an Agni is indeed the remover of darkness.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the ancient banner of sacrifice, knows (all things) through understanding : his radiance traverses (the darkness).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**यज्ञस्य केतुः (*yajñasya ketuḥ*)**—अग्निष्टोमादेः प्रज्ञापकः (*agniṣṭomādeḥ prajñāpakaḥ*). The word *yajña* is spoken among the fifteen sacrifice-names beginning with *vena*, *adhvara* (Ni. 3-19). Although the word *ketu* has the senses "action", "banner" and so on, here it is used in the sense of "indicator", so Agni is the one who makes known (the rites) such as the Agniṣṭoma; the meaning is explained as: he impels (people) to perform rites such as the Agniṣṭoma.

**पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)**—पूर्वे भवः चिरंतनः (*pūrve bhavaḥ ciraṃtanaḥ*). Among the six names of the ancient (printed "ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಂ, ಪ್ರದಿವಃ ಮೊದಲಾಪ", as supplied, apparently *pratnam*, *pradivaḥ* and so on; Ni. 3-20) the word *pūrvya* is read. Because Agni arose at the beginning of creation, he is described as *ciraṃtana*, one who has existed for a long time.

**धिया चेतति (*dhiyā cetati*)**—The word *dhī* is spoken both among the names of action (Ni. 3-2) and among the names of understanding. Here the meaning is that Agni, by his excellent knowledge, knows everything and has attained the state of being all-knowing (printed "ಸವಜ್ಞ", as supplied).

**अर्थं (*arthaṃ*)**—गमनस्वभावं तेजः (*gamanasvabhāvaṃ tejaḥ*). The Nirukta authors (the supplied text has "ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು", followed by the verse):

स्थाणुरयं भारहरः किलाभूदधीत्य वेदं न विजानाति योर्थं । (*sthāṇurayaṃ bhāraharaḥ kilābhūdadhītya vedaṃ na vijānāti yorthaṃ |*)

योर्थज्ञ इत्सकलं भद्रमश्नुते नाकमेति ज्ञानविधूतपाप्मा । (*yorthajña itsakalaṃ bhadramaśnute nākameti jñānavidhūtapāpmā |*)

### Printed p. 184

(Special Topics continued.) The sentence just quoted is explained as अर्थोऽर्तॆररणस्थो वा (*artho 'rtèraraṇastho vā*) . Durgācārya says of the word *artha*, derived from the root *ṛ* which conveys movement: अर्यते ह्यसावर्थिभिः (*aryate hyasāvarthibhiḥ*)—since it is carried off by petitioners, the *dīnāra* and similar (gold coins) are called by the word *artha*. Sāyaṇa explains the sense as "the radiance of Agni", because the nature of moving is also in radiance.

**तरणि (*taraṇi*)**—कारकं (*kārakaṃ*) (as supplied; the bhāṣya text reads शारकं (*śārakaṃ*) and the Pratipadārtha "ವಾರಕ", all as supplied, with the sense "warder-off, remover"). The word *taraṇi* is spoken among the names of the swift (printed "ಸಿ. ೩-೯", as supplied for "Ni. 3-9"). The word *taraṇi*, formed from the root conveying crossing and floating (printed "ದ್ವಿಧಾತು", as supplied), is explained as "one who causes crossing" (*tāraka*). The meaning is explained thus: the all-pervading radiance of Agni destroys the darkness spread in the atmosphere.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- चेतति (*cetati*): root चीती संज्ञाने (*cītī saṃjñāne*) . In the *laṭ* third person singular the form is चेतति (*cetati*). Since it follows a non-finite-verb word (printed "ಅತಿಜಂತದ", as supplied), the all-unaccented (*sarvānudātta*) accent comes.
- अर्थम् (*artham*): root ऋ गतौ (*ṛ gatau*); by उषिकुषिगार्तिभ्यस्थन् (*uṣikuṣigārtibhyasthan*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-161) the affix *than* comes to it. The sentence "ಅದನ್ನು ನಿಮಿತ್ತೀಕಂಸಿ ಧಾತುವಿಗೆ ಗುಣ ರಸವಾಗಿ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ" is garbled in the supplied text (it means that guṇa comes to the root); kept as supplied. Because the affix has the marker *n*, the initial-udātta accent comes.
- तरणि (*taraṇi*): root त्वा प्लवनतरणयोः (*tvā plavanataraṇayoḥ*) . By आर्ति सृभृधृधमि (*ārti sṛbhṛdhṛdhami*) (Uṇ. Sū 2-259) the affix *ani*. By सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū 7-3-84) guṇa for the root's *ṛ*. The text then has अट् कुप्वाज् (*aṭ kupvāj*) (the rule is named with no number) for the *n* (the sentence is incomplete in the supplied text, "ನಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಇತ್ವ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಯದ ಆದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತಸ್ವರ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ", as supplied); the initial-udātta accent of the affix comes.

*[Stray line after the grammar notes, as supplied: "ಸಂ: ಹಿಮಾಚಲ" (apparently an editor's initial/name, "Saṃ: Himācala"); kept.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहसः सूनुं बलस्य पुत्रं मथनरूपेण बलेन निष्पाद्यमानत्वात् सनश्रुतं
> सनातनत्वेन प्रसिद्धं जातवेदसं जातप्रज्ञं कमिममग्निं देवा हविर्भुजो देवा
> हविषां वोढारमकृण्वत । अकुर्वत ॥ सनश्रुतं । शु श्रवणे । कर्मणि क्तः ।
> कृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । वह्निं । वह प्रापणे । निरित्यनुवृत्तौ

> कृण्वोरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः । आकारश्चांतादेशः । लजि व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । निघातः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, the eaters of oblations, made Agni, the son of strength (because he is produced by the force of churning), ancient and all-knowing, the bearer of their oblations. The rest gives the grammar of the words (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

सहसः सूनुं (*sahasaḥ sūnuṃ*)—(because he is produced by strength at the time of churning) the son of strength. सनश्रुतं (*sanaśrutaṃ*)—renowned as the eternal one. जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—possessing knowledge (of all things). अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni. देवा: (*devā:*)—the gods, the eaters of oblations. वह्निं (*vahniṃ*)—as the bearer of the oblations. अकृण्वत (*akṛṇvata*)—made.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, the eaters of oblations, made for themselves their bearer of oblations that Agni who (because he is produced by strength at the time of churning) is renowned as the son of strength and as the eternal one, and who has knowledge of all things that are born.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The gods have made Agni, who is the son of strength, the eternally-renowned, the knower of all that is born, the bearer (of oblations).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Because Agni arises from the churning in the two *araṇis* (fire-sticks), he is spoken of as सहसःसूनु (*sahasaḥsūnu*)—the son of strength. Because he has existed for a long time he is सनश्रुत (*sanaśruta*), that is, one who exists always. Because he knows everything that has come into being, he is जातप्रज्ञ (*jātaprajña*) (one of born knowledge) and is denoted by the word जातवेद (*jātaveda*). The meaning is explained thus: the gods have made such an Agni, of abundant greatness, the bearer of their respective oblations.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- सनश्रुतम् (*sanaśrutam*): root श्रु श्रवणे (*śru śravaṇe*). By निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-102) the affix *kta* in the passive sense. By तृतीयाकर्मणि (*tṛtīyākarmaṇi*) (Pā. Sū 6-2-48) the accent of the first member comes.

*[Stray line at the foot of the page, as supplied: "24" (apparently a signature or sheet number).]*

### Printed p. 186

- वह्निम् (*vahnim*): root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*). When निः (*niḥ*) continues from the preceding sūtra, the affix *ni* comes to it by तहिश्रिश्रुयु (*tahiśriśruyu*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-491) (as supplied; the bhāṣya quotes the rule as वहिश्रीत्यादिना (*vahiśrītyādinā*)). Since *nit* continues, the initial-udātta accent comes.
- अकृण्वत (*akṛṇvata*): root कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च (*kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca*). By इदितोनुम्‌धातोः (*iditonumdhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) the augment *num*. In the *laṅ* third person plural, by *vyatyaya* the affix *jhu*. By आत्मनेपदेष्टनतः (*ātmanepadeṣṭanataḥ*) the substitute *ata* for it . By धिन्विकृण्वरच (*dhinvikṛṇvaraca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-80) the affix *u* and the substitute ending in *a*. By अतोलोपः (*atolopaḥ*) the *a* is elided; since it is treated as the original (*sthānivadbhāva*), the guṇa of the penultimate short vowel does not come. Because *ṛ* follows, the *n* of the *num* becomes *ṇ*; *yaṇ* substitution. The verb-accent (*nighāta*) of a finite verb comes (printed "ಅತಿಜಂತದ", as supplied).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अदा॑भ्यः पुरए॒ता वि॒शाम॒ग्निर्मानु॑षीणां ।  
> तूर्णी॒ रथः॒ सदा॒ नवः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आदाभ्यः । पुरःऽएता । विशां । अग्निः । मानुषीणां ।  
> तूर्णिः ; रथः । सदा । नवः ॥ ५ ॥

> *ādābhyaḥ | puraḥ 'etā | viśāṃ | agniḥ | mānuṣīṇāṃ |*  
> *tūrṇiḥ ; rathaḥ | sadā | navaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

*[The Pada prints पुरःऽएता (*puraḥ 'etā*) with the compound mark, and तूर्णिः ; (*tūrṇiḥ ;*) with a semicolon in place of the danda; all as supplied. The Pada also reads आदाभ्यः (*ādābhyaḥ*) where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya have अदाभ्यः (*adābhyaḥ*) (as supplied).]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मानुषीणांमनोर्जातानां विशां प्रजानां पुरएता सन्मार्गप्रदर्शनेना-
> ग्रतो गंतात एव तूर्णिस्ताः प्रजा वैदिककर्मप्रवर्तकत्वेनानुग्रहीतुं त्वरायुक्त
> अलस्यरहितो रथो हविषां वहनाद्रथसदृशः सदा सर्वदा तत्कर्मणि नवो नूतनः
> पुनर्मथनादभिनव एवविधोऽग्निंदाभ्यः । अहिंस्यः । न केनापि तिरस्कार्य इत्यर्थः ॥
> अदाभ्यः । दंधु दंभे । दभेश्चति वक्तव्यमिति कर्मणि ण्यत् । उपधावृद्धिः । न
> दाभ्योऽदाभ्यः । नञ्मासे तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थेति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । पुरएता।
> इण् गत् । ण्वुल्बचाविति तृच् । गुणः । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । मानुषीणां । मनो-
> र्जातावण्यत् शुक् चेत्यञ् । टिड्ढाणञ्ति जीप् । इत्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तूर्तिः ।
> इत्वरा संभ्रम इति धातोर्निरित्यनुवृत्तौ वहिश्रिश्रुयुद्रुग्लाहात्वरिभ्यो निदिति
> निप्रत्ययः । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना ऊर् । तस्य नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । संहितायां ढ्रलोपे
> पूर्वस्यॆति दीर्घः । रथः । हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्य इति कन्पत्ययः । कित्वादनुदा-
> त्तोपदेतेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । सदा । स्वरादिष्वाद्युदात्त-
> श्चैन दरितत्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is the forerunner of the human tribes, showing them the good path; he is swift and untiring, like a chariot in carrying the oblations, ever new because churned afresh, and not to be harmed or slighted by anyone. The rest gives the grammar of the words (transcribed, not explained).

### Printed p. 187

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

मानुषीशां (*mānuṣīśāṃ*) (printed so, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*))—born of Manu. विशां (*viśāṃ*)—to the people. पुरः एता (*puraḥ etā*)—(as the guide on the good path) the one who goes in front. तोर्णिः (*torṇiḥ*) (printed so, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has तूर्णि (*tūrṇi*))—(therefore, to make them perform the Vedic rites) hasty (untiring). रथः (*rathaḥ*)—(through carrying the oblations) like a chariot. सदा (*sadā*)—at all times. नवः (*navaḥ*)—(because he arises again and again, churned afresh) new. अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni. अदाभ्यः (*adābhyaḥ*)—not to be harmed (not slighted by anyone).

*[The label of the next section is garbled in the supplied text ("ಧಾವರ್ಧ."); it is restored in kn.md as the Bhāvārtha label, structure only.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who goes in front as the guide on the good path of all the people born of Manu's line, who is hasty (so that they may perform that rite), who is like a chariot through the work of carrying the oblations, and who is always new because he is born again and again by being churned, cannot be slighted by anyone (he is to be honoured by all).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the preceder of human beings, (ever) alert, the vehicle of their offerings, is ever new, is unsusceptible of harm.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**मानषीणां विशां पुर एता (*mānaṣīṇāṃ viśāṃ pura etā*)** (मानषीणां (*mānaṣīṇāṃ*) printed so, as supplied)—मनोर्जातानां प्रजानां सन्मार्गप्रदर्शनेन अग्रतो गंता (*manorjātānāṃ prajānāṃ sanmārgapradarśanena agrato gaṃtā*). The word विशः (*viśaḥ*) is spoken among the names of man (Ni. 3-7). The Nirukta author has explained the meaning of the name of man as मनोरपत्यं मनुषो वा (*manorapatyaṃ manuṣo vā*) (Ni. 3-7). And:

जराबोध तद्विविड्डि विशेषिविशे यज्ञियाय । स्तोमं रुद्राय दृशीकं ॥ (*jarābodha tadviviḍḍi viśeṣiviśe yajñiyāya | stomaṃ rudrāya dṛśīkaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ 1-27--10) (references as supplied, with the double hyphen)

Here, for the word विशेविशे (*viśeviśe*) they have explained the meaning as मनुष्यस्य मनुष्यस्य (*manuṣyasya manuṣyasya*). To avoid this repetition Sāyaṇa gave the word विशां (*viśāṃ*) the meaning प्रजानां (*prajānāṃ*), and described Agni as the one who goes in front of the people born of Manu, because he teaches them the good path.

**तूर्णि: (*tūrṇi:*)**—The Nirukta authors read this word among the names of the swift (Ni. 3-9) and explained its meaning as त्वरमाणः (*tvaramāṇaḥ*) (Ni. 7-18). It is explained that Agni is eager to favour the people of Manu so that they engage in the rites enjoined by the Veda.

### Printed p. 188

*(Special Topics on Ṛk 5, continued from p. 187.)*

रथः (*rathaḥ*)—हविषां वहनात् रथसदृशः (*haviṣāṃ vahanāt rathasadṛśaḥ*). Yāska has described the word *ratha*, with explanation of its meaning, thus: रथो रंहतेर्गतिकर्मणः स्थिरतेर्वा विषरीतस्य रममाणोऽस्मिन् तिष्ठतीति वा रपशीर्वा रसतेर्वा (*ratho raṃhatergatikarmaṇaḥ sthiratervā viṣarītasya ramamāṇo 'smin tiṣṭhatīti vā rapaśīrvā rasatervā*) (Ni. 9-12): it is formed either from the root रंह (*raṃha*), which conveys the meaning "going" (walking), or, as in the saying of the authorities स्थिरसर्स रथ इत्युक्तः (*sthirasarsa ratha ityuktaḥ*) , from the opposite of the word स्थिर (*sthira*) (firm), the chariot being a means in which one never fails to take joyful pleasure; or from the root रप (*rapa*) or the root रस (*rasa*). The meaning is described in a figurative way: because Agni carries the shares of the gods in the oblations, he is like a chariot, a vehicle for carrying things.

सदा नवः अदाभ्यः (*sadā navaḥ adābhyaḥ*)—सर्वदा तत्कर्मणि नवः नूतनः पुनर्मथनादभिनवः । (*sarvadā tatkarmaṇi navaḥ nūtanaḥ punarmathanādabhinavaḥ |*) आहिंस्यः न केनापि तिरस्कार्यः । (*āhiṃsyaḥ na kenāpi tiraskāryaḥ |*) (आहिंस्यः (*āhiṃsyaḥ*) as supplied.) Two kinds of meaning are given for the word *sadānava*: that Agni is always eager in the work of carrying the oblations to the gods, and that, being produced by churning in the two *araṇis*, he is always new. And the nature of Agni is explained: he is one who cannot be harmed by anyone (is impossible to injure) and is not one to be slighted.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- अदाभ्यः (*adābhyaḥ*): root दंभु दंभने (*daṃbhu daṃbhane*). By the statement दभेश्चतिनक्तव्यव् (*dabheścatinaktavyav*) the affix *ṇyat* in the passive sense. When the penultimate nasal is elided, vṛddhi by आतउपधायाः (*ātaupadhāyāḥ*) ; the form is दाभ्य (*dābhya*). न दाभ्यः अदाभ्यः (*na dābhyaḥ adābhyaḥ*): *nañ*-tatpuruṣa compound. By the rule *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the accent of the first member comes.
- पुरएता (*puraetā*): the root is printed इष् गत् (*iṣ gat*) (as supplied; an underscore stands before it in the text). By the rule *ṇvul-tṛcau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-133) the affix *tṛc* in the agent sense. By सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) guṇa for the root. By चितः (*citaḥ*) the final-udātta accent comes. In the compound the accent of the final member after a *kṛt* comes.
- विशाम् (*viśām*): genitive plural form. By the rule *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168) the udātta accent on the case ending comes.
- मानुषीणाम् (*mānuṣīṇām*): मनोर्जाताः मानुष्यः (*manorjātāḥ mānuṣyaḥ*) ("born of Manu"). By the rule on words meaning "born of Manu" (Pā. Sū. 4-1-161) the affix *añ* and the augment *śuk* come to the word *manu*. By the rule *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-117) vṛddhi of the first vowel. Since the word ends in *a*, in the feminine the affix *ṅīp* by the rule *ṭiḍḍhāṇañ…* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-15). By यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) the preceding *a* is elided. Since *ṅīp* and *sup* have the *p* marker the case ending is anudātta; since *añ* has the *ñ* marker, by the rule *ñnityādir nityam* (as supplied: "ಇನ್ಯಾದಿರ್ನಿತ್ಯಮ್") the initial-udātta accent comes. Genitive plural form.

### Printed p. 189

- तूर्णिः (*tūrṇiḥ*): root इत्वरा संभ्रमे (*itvarā saṃbhrame*) . When *niḥ* continues, the affix *ni* comes by the rule *vahiśriśruyu…* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-491). By the rule *jvaratvarasrivyavi…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-20) *ūṭh* substitution for the *va* and the penultimate. By the rule *raṣābhyāṃ ṇo naḥ samānapade* the affix gets *ṇ*. The form is तूर्णि (*tūrṇi*). Since the affix is laid down as *nit*, the initial-udātta accent comes. When *su* is added, *ruttva* at the end of the word. By रोरि (*rori*) the preceding *r* is elided because an *r* follows. By the rule *ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ* (as supplied: Pā. Sū. 6-0-111) the preceding *i* is lengthened.
- रथः (*rathaḥ*): root रमु क्रीडायां (*ramu krīḍāyāṃ*). By the rule *hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ…* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-159) the affix *kthan* to it. Since it has the *k* marker, by the rule *anudāttopadeśa-vanati…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) the *m* of the root is elided. Since the affix is *nit*, the initial-udātta accent comes.
- सदा (*sadā*): since it is read as initial-udātta in the *svarādi* group, it is initial-udātta.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सा॒ह्वान्विश्वा॑ अभि॒युजः॒ क्रतु॑र्दे॒वाना॒ममृ॑क्तः ।  
> अ॒ग्निस्तु॒विश्र॑वस्तमः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सह्वान् । विश्वाः । अभियुजः । क्रतुः । देवानां । अमृक्तः ।  
> अग्नि: । तुविश्रवःतमः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभियुजोऽभियोक्रीर्विश्वाः सर्वाः सेनाः साह्वान्सहमानः स्वबलेन तिर-
> स्कुर्वाणोऽत एवामृक्तः शत्रुभिरहिंसितो देवानां क्रतुः कर्ता हविष्पदानेन
> पोषक एवंभूतोऽग्निस्तुविश्रवस्तमः । तुविशब्दो बहुवाची । तुवि पुरु इति तन्ना-
> मसु पाठात् । श्रवःशब्दोऽन्नवाची । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम श्रूयते । नि. १०-३ । इति
> निरुक्तेऽभिधानात् । अतिशयेन बहुविधान्नोपेतो वर्तते । यस्मादेवं तस्माद-
> स्मानपि बहुविधान्नोपेतान्नरोत्विति भावः ॥ साह्वान् । षह मर्षण इत्यस्य क्वसौ
> दाश्वान्साह्वान्मीढ्वांश्चति निपातनाद्विर्वचनमिडागमश्च न भवति परस्मैपदं च भवति।
> क्वसुस्वरः । क्रतुः । कृञाः कतुः । कित्ताद्गुणाभावः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । तुविश्रवस्तमः ।

### Printed p. 190

> कु वृत्तिहिंसापूर्तिषु । अस्मादौणादिकः किप्रत्ययः । कित्वाद्गुणाभावः । उवजा-
> देशः । अंशोदात्तः । श्रवः । श्रु श्रवणे । श्रूयतेऽन्नमिति कर्मण्यसुन्प्रत्ययः ।
> अतिशयेन तुविश्रवा इत्यतिशायने तमबिति शमप् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृति-
> स्वरत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni overcomes all hostile armies by his own strength, is unharmed, is the nourisher of the gods through oblations, and has food of many kinds; may he give us many kinds of food too. The rest gives the grammar of the words (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अभियुजः (*abhiyujaḥ*)—of those who come against (him, the enemies). विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all armies. साह्वान् (*sāhvān*)—(by his own power) the one who endures. अमृक्तः (*amṛktaḥ*)—(therefore) the unharmed. देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods. क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*)—the one who brings about (nourishment through the giving of oblations). अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni. तुविश्रवस्तमः (*tuviśravastamaḥ*)—is possessed of food of many kinds.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is able to overcome by his own power all the hostile armies that come against him, who (therefore) is unharmed by anyone, and who is the nourisher of the gods through the giving of oblations, is possessed of food of many kinds. (Therefore may such an Agni grant to us too food of various kinds.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the most liberal contributor of food, is able to resist all assailants unharmed, the nourisher of the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अभियुजः विश्वाः साह्वान्, अमृक्तः (*abhiyujaḥ viśvāḥ sāhvān, amṛktaḥ*)—अभियोक्रीः सर्वाः सेनाः सहमानः आत एव शत्रुभिरहिंसितः । (*abhiyokrīḥ sarvāḥ senāḥ sahamānaḥ āta eva śatrubhirahiṃsitaḥ |*) One who comes in front of others with the intention of killing them is called an enemy. An enemy of this kind is designated here by the word *abhiyuj*. It is described that Agni overcomes all the enemy armies by his own power and is one who does not suffer harm from enemies. (In the Kannada the sentence begins with "ತನು" where "ಅವನು" would be expected; as supplied.)

देवानां क्रतुः तुविश्रवस्तमः (*devānāṃ kratuḥ tuviśravastamaḥ*)—The word तुवि (*tuvi*) is stated among the names for "many" (Ni. 3-13). The word श्रवः (*śravaḥ*) is stated among the names for wealth (Ni. 3-9), and in आतूर्तो राजा श्रव इच्छमानः (*ātūrto rājā śrava icchamānaḥ*) it is used in the sense of "praise" (Ni. 9-11); and as श्रव इत्यन्ननाम श्रूयत इति सतः (*śrava ityannanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ*) (Ni. 10-3) (सतः (*sataḥ*) as supplied) it is used in the sense of "food". Sāyaṇa has explained that Agni nourishes the gods by giving oblations and is possessed of abundant food of many kinds; therefore may he make the sacrificing householders also possessed of food of many kinds; this is the meaning, and the one who teaches it, अतित. (*atita.*) (as supplied; garbled), has given the commentary: येन बहुविधानोपेतो वर्तते । यस्मादेवं तस्मादस्मानपि बहुविधानोपेशान् करोतु (*yena bahuvidhānopeto vartate | yasmādevaṃ tasmādasmānapi bahuvidhānopeśān karotu*) (here बहुविधानोपेशान् (*bahuvidhānopeśān*) as supplied, where the bhāṣya block has बहुविधान्नोपेतान् (*bahuvidhānnopetān*)).

### Printed p. 191

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- साह्वान् (*sāhvān*): root सह मर्षणे (*saha marṣaṇe*). When *kvasu* is substituted for the *liṭ* that follows it, the form is irregularly fixed as साह्वान् (*sāhvān*) by the rule *dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-12) ; therefore it takes the parasmaipada. The augment *iṭ* and the doubling do not come. The affix accent remains.
- अभियुजः (*abhiyujaḥ*): root युजिर् योगे (*yujir yoge*). Affix *kvip*. The accent of the final member after a *kṛt* comes. Accusative plural form.
- क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*): root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*). It is established by कृञाःक्रतुः (*kṛñāḥkratuḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-77) . Since the affix has the *k* marker guṇa does not come; *yaṇ* substitution. The initial-udātta accent of the affix comes.
- तुविश्रवस्तमः (*tuviśravastamaḥ*): root तु वृत्तिहिंसापूर्तिषु (*tu vṛttihiṃsāpūrtiṣu*). To it the Uṇādi affix *ki*. Since it has the *k* marker, guṇa of the *u* of the root does not come (बरुवुनिल्ल (*baruvunilla*) as supplied). By अचिश्नुधातुभ्रुवां (*aciśnudhātubhruvāṃ*) the substitute *uva*; by the accent of the affix it is final-udātta (the text reads उवजादेत (*uvajādeta*) as supplied). श्रवः (*śravaḥ*): root श्रु श्रवणे (*śru śravaṇe*). श्रूयते अन्नमिति श्रवः (*śrūyate annamiti śravaḥ*). The Uṇādi affix *asun* comes in the passive sense by the word *bahula*. अतिशयेन तुविश्रवाः तुविश्रवस्तमः (*atiśayena tuviśravāḥ tuviśravastamaḥ*); by the rule *atiśāyane tamap* the affix is given as *śamap* . In the bahuvrīhi the accent of the first member comes.

*[Stray line as supplied: "ಸಂಪಾದಕ" (apparently a running word of the editor, "the editor"), standing between the grammar notes and the next Ṛk.]*

> अ॒भि प्रयां॑सि॒ वाह॑सा दा॒श्वा अ॑श्नोति॒ मर्त्यः॑ ।

> क्षयं । पावकशोजिषः ॥ ७ ॥

> वाहकेनाग्निना प्रयांस्यन्नान्यभ्यश्नोति। अभितः सर्वतः प्राप्नोति । किंच पावकशो-
> चिषः शोधकदीप्तेरग्ने: सकाशात् क्षयं गृहं जाभ्यश्नोति ॥ प्रयांसि । प्रीञ् त-
> र्पणे । अस्माद्दातोरंतर्भावितण्यर्थादसुन्प्रत्ययः । प्रीणयंति भक्षमिति प्रयां-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The giver of oblations, a mortal, obtains foods through Agni, the carrier of the oblations, from every side, and also obtains a home from Agni of purifying brightness. The bhāṣya continues (with the grammar of the words) on the next page; the supplied text of this window ends in the middle of it, at the word प्रयांसि (*prayāṃsi*).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

*(continued from p. 191)*

> स्यन्नानि । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । वाहसा । णिदित्यनुवृत्तौ वहिहाधाङ्छंदसीत्यसुन् ।
> णेत्वादुपधावृद्धिः । नित्स्वरः । दाश्वान् । दातृ दान इत्यस्य क्वसौ दाश्वानाह्वानिति
> निपातनादिडागमो द्विर्पचनं क्वच न भवति । क्वसुन्प्रत्ययस्वरः। अश्नोति । अतू

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The rest of the bhāṣya on Ṛk 7 gives only the grammar of the words prayāṃsi, vāhasā, dāśvān and aśnoti (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

दाश्वान् (*dāśvān*)—the giver of oblations. मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—the sacrificer, a man. वाहसा (*vāhasā*)—by Agni, the carrier of the oblations. प्रयांसि (*prayāṃsi*)—foods. अभि अश्नोशि (*abhi aśnośi*) —obtains in every manner; (and) पादकशोचिसः (*pādakaśocisaḥ*) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has पावकशोचिषः (*pāvakaśociṣaḥ*))—of Agni who has purifying radiance (by his favour) क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)—the house too. (अभि अश्नोशि (*abhi aśnośi*)—he obtains.)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who offers oblations and the like for the gods obtains food, and also a house, through the favour of Agni, who carries the oblations and is endowed with purifying radiance.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
From Agni, of purifying radiance the mortal presenter (of offerings) obtains by his conveyance (of them to the gods) abundant viands and a dwell-ing [line-break hyphen as supplied].

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दाश्वान् (*dāśvān*)—हविषां दाता (*haviṣāṃ dātā*). The meaning is given that Agni is the one who gives (carries) to the gods the food in the form of the oblation. The Niruktakāra, quoting the Ṛk ओमासश्चर्षणीधृतो विश्वे देवास आ गत । दाश्वांसो दाशुषस्सुतं (*omāsaścarṣaṇīdhṛto viśve devāsa ā gata | dāśvāṃso dāśuṣassutaṃ*) (Pu Saṃ. 1-3-7), explains दाश्वांस:-दत्तवंतः (*dāśvāṃsa:-dattavaṃtaḥ*) as those who give, the liberal ones, and दाशुषः-दत्तवतः (*dāśuṣaḥ-dattavataḥ*) as to the liberal ones.

मर्त्य:-मनुष्य यजमानः (*martya:-manuṣya yajamānaḥ*). Although the word मर्त्य (*martya*) is read among the names of man (ಽ 3-7 [sic: the reference is printed with a stray sign]), here the meaning "the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice" is made clear.

वाहसा प्रयांसि अभ्यश्नोति (*vāhasā prayāṃsi abhyaśnoti*)—the word प्रयस् (*prayas*) [printed प्रयश्यब्द (*prayaśyabda*) as supplied]: प्रीणयंति भोक्तूनिति प्रयांसि अन्नानि (*prīṇayaṃti bhoktūniti prayāṃsi annāni*) — foods are so named because they gratify those who eat; and the word प्रयस् (*prayas*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa explains: यजमानः हविषां वाहकेन अग्निना अभितः सर्वतः प्राप्नोति (*yajamānaḥ haviṣāṃ vāhakena agninā abhitaḥ sarvataḥ prāpnoti*) — that is, the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice obtains food in many ways from Agni, who carries the oblations to the gods.

### Printed p. 193

पावकशोचिषः क्षयं (*pāvakaśociṣaḥ kṣayaṃ*)—शोधकदीप्तेः अग्नेः सकाशात् गृहं च अभ्यश्नोति (*śodhakadīpteḥ agneḥ sakāśāt gṛhaṃ ca abhyaśnoti*). Although the word क्षय (*kṣaya*) is not stated among the names of the house, it is used in the sense of a dwelling-place. It is explained that the sacrificer obtains a lasting dwelling-place through the favour of Agni, who has purifying radiance (the Kannada reads "ಯಜ್ಞ ಮಾಡ ವ" with a space, as supplied).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- प्रयांसि (*prayāṃsi*): root प्रीञ् तर्पणे (*prīñ tarpaṇe*). As it shows causation, it is a root with the causative sense included. The affix *asun* comes to it by सर्वधातुभ्य असुन् (*sarvadhātubhya asun*). प्रीणयंति भोक्त्यानिति प्रयांसि अन्नानि (*prīṇayaṃti bhoktyāniti prayāṃsi annāni*) (food gratifies those who eat). Because the affix has the *n* marker, the initial-udātta accent comes.
- वाहसा (*vāhasā*): root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*). The affix *asun* by वहिहाधाञ्भ्यश्चंदसि (*vahihādhāñbhyaścaṃdasi*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-660) . As णित् (*ṇit*) is carried on, it has the *ṇ* marker; vṛddhi of the penultimate by अतउपधायाः (*ataupadhāyāḥ*). The stem *vāhas* results. The initial-udātta accent comes. Instrumental singular.
- दाश्वान् (*dāśvān*): root दाश्य दाने (*dāśya dāne*) . When the affix *kvasu* comes, it is fixed irregularly by दाश्वान् साह्वान् (*dāśvān sāhvān*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-12), so the doubling and the augment *iṭ* do not come. The affix accent comes.
- अश्नोति (*aśnoti*): root अशू व्याप्तौ (*aśū vyāptau*). By व्यत्ययोबहुलं (*vyatyayobahulaṃ*) the parasmaipada is used. Present tense, third person singular. The accent of a finite verb (*nighāta*) comes.

> स्त्वमग्नेवोजितमिति तद्विशेषणत्वं युक्तं ॥ सुधिता । डुधाण् धारणपोषण-
> योरित्यसाद्मातोर्निष्ठायां छंदसीत्यनवृत् सुधितवसुधितेत्यादिना निपातितः ।
> शेषृंदसि बहुलमिति शेर्लुल् । गतरनंतर इति गते: प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अश्याम । अशू
> व्याप्तौ । बहुलं छंदसीति श्नुप्रत्ययस्य लुक् । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । यासुट्
> परस्मैपदेषूदात्त इति यासुट् । लिज: सलोप इति सलोपः । अदंतत्वाभावादि-
> यादेशो न भवति । मसः सकारस्य नित्यं जित इति लोपः । निघातः । मन्मभिः ।
> मनु अवबोधने । अन्वेभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति मनिन् । नित्सरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the wise priests such as the Hotṛ, may obtain on every side all the good things we desire through the praises of Agni, the all-knowing; *jātavedas* is an epithet of Agni. The rest is the grammar of sudhitā, aśyāma and manmabhiḥ (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(जातवेदसः (*jātavedasaḥ*)—possessed of knowledge) विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—wise (priests such as the Hotṛ), we. जातवेदसः (*jātavedasaḥ*)—of the all-knowing. अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—Agni's. मन्मभिः (*manmabhiḥ*)—by praises. विश्वाणि (*viśvāṇi*) [Saṃhitā विश्वानि (*viśvāni*), as supplied]—all. सुधिता (*sudhitā*)—very beneficial desired riches. परि आश्याम (*pari āśyāma*) —let us obtain.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, we who are of the nature of Hotṛ and the like, and wise, praise you, the all-knowing, and wish to obtain all the desired riches and other things.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May we, endowed with intelligence, obtaiu [sic] all good things by our praises of Agni, to whom all is known.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here, for the word जातवेदश्यब्द (*jātavedaśyabda*) one kind of meaning is given, जातप्रज्ञः जातानि सर्वाणि वेत्ति (*jātaprajñaḥ jātāni sarvāṇi vetti*) and another kind of meaning, जातप्रज्ञाः विप्राः (*jātaprajñāḥ viprāḥ*); but since जातवेदसः अग्नेः (*jātavedasaḥ agneḥ*) makes the word जातवेदश्यब्द (*jātavedaśyabda*) an epithet of the word Agni (जातवेदश्यब्द (*jātavedaśyabda*)), the second meaning is explained. Since the word विप्राः (*viprāḥ*) is stated among the names of the wise, the meaning "the wise priests such as the Hotṛ" is explained. And

मध्वः—मननीय्यैः स्तोम्यैः (*madhvaḥ—mananīyyaiḥ stomyaiḥ*) . The Niruktakāra: *(the supplied text of this window ends here, at "ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರಃ—"; the passage continues on the next page)*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*(continued from p. 194)*

उप प्रागात्सुमन्नेऽधायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्टः । (*upa prāgātsumanne 'dhāyi manma devānāmāśā upa vītapṛṣṭaḥ |*) अन्वेनं विप्रा यषयो मदंति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबंधुं ॥ (*anvenaṃ viprā yaṣayo madaṃti devānāṃ puṣṭe cakṛmā subaṃdhuṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-7). In this Ṛk the word मन्म (*manma*) is explained as मननीयमर्थजातं (*mananīyamarthajātaṃ*), "things worthy of meditation"; and in

शवं हु समना गिरा पित्थूणां च मन्मथिः । (*śavaṃ hu samanā girā pitthūṇāṃ ca manmathiḥ |*) नाभाकस्य प्रशस्तिभिर्यस्सिंधूनामुपोदये सप्तस्वसा स मध्यमो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥ (*nābhākasya praśastibhiryassiṃdhūnāmupodaye saptasvasā sa madhyamo nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-41-2) *(the Sanskrit is given exactly as supplied; the supplied text has a line-end hyphen in नभं-तामन्यके (*nabhaṃ-tāmanyake*), joined here)*

the words मननीयाः मननार्हाः बहुमानाः स्तोमनाः (*mananīyāḥ mananārhāḥ bahumānāḥ stomanāḥ*) (स्तोमनाः (*stomanāḥ*) as supplied) are given, that is, praises worthy of being meditated on and worshipped; thus the word मन्म (*manma*) has been given its meaning. From this the sense is that we, the wise priests such as the Hotṛ, skilled in performing the rites that concern the deities and possessed of knowledge, meditate on and worship Agni by his worshipful and praiseworthy greatnesses, and so wish to obtain in every way everything that is desirable to us and beneficial. This is the first meaning.

In the second meaning, where the word जातवेदसः (*jātavedasaḥ*) is stated as an epithet of Agni, the all-knowing Agni, knowing his own greatnesses, is gracious to fulfil in every way all (every kind of) wishes of the priests such as the Hotṛ who worship him and meditate on him. Therefore we, the wise priests, wish to obtain this by gaining the favour of Agni. Having thus explained the meaning, the bhāṣya says एतादृशं जातवेदस्तं अग्नेरेवोचितमिति तद्विशेषणत्वं युक्तं (*etādṛśaṃ jātavedastaṃ agnerevocitamiti tadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ yuktaṃ*) — since such omniscience, with greatness of this kind, belongs fittingly to Agni, it is proper to state this word as his epithet; so the meaning is described.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- सुधिता (*sudhitā*): root डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). The affix *kta* comes to it by निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*). When this follows, with छंदसि (*chaṃdasi*) carried on from before, it is irregularly fixed by सुधितवसुधित (*sudhitavasudhita*)… (Pā. Sū. 7-4-45). In the neuter plural, when the form सुधितानि (*sudhitāni*) results, the *śi* is elided by शेश्छंदसि बहुलम् (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-20). When a final member ending in *kta* follows, the preverbal element (सु (*su*)) keeps its own accent by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49).
- अश्याम (*aśyāma*): root आशू व्याप्तौ (*āśū vyāptau*) *(printed आशू (*āśū*), as supplied)*. In the *liṅ*, first person plural, the *parasmaipada* ending *mas* comes by व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85). The *s* is elided by नित्यंजितः (*nityaṃjitaḥ*). The *vikaraṇa* (*śnu*) is elided by *luk* by बहुलंछंदसि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasi*). The augment *yāsuṭ* comes to the ending by यासुट्परस्मैपदेषु (*yāsuṭparasmaipadeṣu*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-103). The *s* is elided by लिजःसलो- (*lijaḥsalo-*) *(the sūtra is split by the page break: p. 196 continues with पोवंत्यस्य (*povaṃtyasya*))*

### Printed p. 196

पोवंत्यस्य (*povaṃtyasya*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-29): the *s* is elided. Since the *ā* does not come after an *at*-ending stem, the substitute *iya* does not come for या (*yā*). The form अश्याम (*aśyāma*) results. Because it follows अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*) *(as supplied: "after a finite verb", the Kannada reads अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*))* the *nighāta* accent comes.
- मन्मभि (*manmabhi*): root मनु अवबोधने (*manu avabodhane*). The affix *manin* by अन्वेभ्योपिदृश्यंते (*anvebhyopidṛśyaṃte*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75). As it has the *n* marker, the initial-udātta accent comes by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197). The form is of the instrumental plural.
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*): when *jas* follows, the augment *asuk* comes to it by अज्जसेरसुक् (*ajjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ विश्वा॑नि॒ वार्या॒ वाजे॑षु सनिषामहे ।  
> त्वे दे॒वास॒ एरि॑रे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । विश्वानि । वार्या । वाजेषु । सनिषामहे ।  
> श्वे इति । देवासः । आ । ईरिरे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने वार्या वरणेयानि संभजनीयानि विश्वानि सर्वाणि धनानि वाजेषु
> युद्धेषु सनिषामहे । वयं संभजामहे । यतः कारणाद्देवासः पूर्वमस्माभि-
> रिष्टा देवा अस्मदभिमतफलप्रदानाय त्वे त्वय्येरिरे । आ समंतादगमन् । त्वयि
> प्रविष्टा इत्यर्थः । सर्वथापि त्वत्सकाशात् फलं लभेमहीति भावः ॥ वार्या । वृज्
> संभक्तौ । महलोर्ण्यदिति ण्यत् । शेश्चंदसि बहुलमिति शेर्लुक् । ईडवंदेत्यादि-
> नाद्युदात्तः । वाजेषु । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । सनिषामहे । वनषण संभक्तौ ।
> धात्वादेः षः सः । लेटि सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् । सिप अर्धधातुकत्वादिदागमः । लेटोः-
> डाटावित्यडागमः । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । निघातः । त्वे । युष्मच्छब्दस्य सप्तम्यां-
> श्वादेशः । सुपां सुलुगिति शेआदेशः । शे । पा. १-१-१३ । इति प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा ।
> ईरिरे । ईर गताविश्यस्मात्परस्य लिटो झस्य इरेजादेशः । इजादेश गुरुमत
> इत्याम्म भवति मंत्रत्वात् । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, we obtain in battles all choice riches; the gods once worshipped by us have entered into you, so we get the fruit from you. The rest is the grammar of vāryā, vājeṣu, saniṣāmahe, tve and īrire (transcribed, not explained).

### Printed p. 197

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(हे (*he*)) अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—(the gods worshipped by us), all of them. त्वे (*tve*)—in you. आ ईरिरे (*ā īrire*)—(in order to grant us our wish) have arrived; (therefore) वार्या (*vāryā*)—(desirable), the choice. विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all wealth. वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—in battles. सनिषामहे (*saniṣāmahe*)—let us obtain.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, all the gods worshipped by us are gathered in you alone; therefore we wish to obtain all the choice wealth and other things in battles (only through your favour).

*[The Kannada label of this section was printed/read as "ಕಾವ್ಯ." in the supplied text; restored to the standard Bhāvārtha label, structure only.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May we obtain, Agni, all precious things (as booty) in battles, since the gods concentrated in you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वार्या (*vāryā*)—वरणीयानि संभजनीयानि (*varaṇīyāni saṃbhajanīyāni*) — this word is used as an epithet of the word विश्वा (*viśvā*). The meaning given is that we priests shall, through the favour of Agni, obtain in battles all kinds of wealth that is desired by all and is worthy of being necessarily obtained.

वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—युद्धेषु (*yuddheṣu*). The word वाज (*vāja*) is found to denote many things: among the names of food (Ni. 3-9); as वाजे (*vāje*) among the names of battle (3-0-9, as supplied); वाजे संस्कृते हविषि (*vāje saṃskṛte haviṣi*) (Ni. 10-34), a prepared, satisfying oblation; as the name of a person (Ni. 11-17); वाजिनीवती - हविषा उदकेन वा तद्वती (*vājinīvatī - haviṣā udakena vā tadvatī*) (Ni. 11-27), oblation or water. Here Sāyaṇa has described the meaning "battle". *(The supplied text has परिशतवागिदॆ (*pariśatavāgidè*), "is found", as supplied.)*

देवासः एरिरे (*devāsaḥ erire*) — पूर्वमस्माभिरिष्टा देवाः अस्मवभिमतफलप्रूजनाय समंतादगमन् त्वयि प्रविष्टाः सर्वथापि त्वत्सकाशात् फलं लभेमहि (*pūrvamasmābhiriṣṭā devāḥ asmavabhimataphalaprūjanāya samaṃtādagaman tvayi praviṣṭāḥ sarvathāpi tvatsakāśāt phalaṃ labhemahi*) *(Sanskrit as supplied; it differs in spelling from the bhāṣya's अस्मदभिमतफलप्रदानाय (*asmadabhimataphalapradānāya*), and प्रूजनाय (*prūjanāya*) looks like a misprint, [sic])*. Having given to the word वेवाः (*vevāḥ*) *(sic, for देवाः (*devāḥ*) as supplied)* in this sentence the meaning "the gods who fulfil the wishes of the priests" *(the supplied text has ऎंड्स (*èṃḍsa*) [sic] for "ಎಂದು")*, he explains that since all those gods entered Agni even before the sacrifice, in order to grant the wish, Agni is made of all the deities. Since, by the favour of this very Agni, who is full of such abundant greatness, every kind of fruit comes to the priests such as the sacrificer, "we shall obtain it" *(the supplied text has हॊंपुत्तेवॆ (*hòṃputtevè*), as supplied)*; so the wish is expressed.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- वार्या (*vāryā*): root वृज् संभक्तौ (*vṛj saṃbhaktau*). The affix *ṇyat* comes to it by ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (*ṛhalorṇyat*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-124) *(sūtra as supplied)*. Since it is marked चित्तानुदरिंद (*cittānudariṃda*) , by अचोञ्जाति (*acoñjāti*) the preceding vowel takes vṛddhi *(the supplied text of this window ends here, at "ವೃದ್ಧಿ"; the note on वार्या (*vāryā*) continues on the next page)*.

*[The window opens in the middle of the grammar notes of Ṛk 9, continuing the note on the first word of the Ṛk that broke off at "ವೃದ್ಧಿ" at the end of p. 197. The supplied text of p. 198 begins mid-sentence with रहरवागि बरुत्तदॆ (*raharavāgi baruttadè*) ("... comes ..."), and the word रहर (*rahara*) is unintelligible [?]; the connecting words are not in the supplied text.]*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(continued)*

- *(Note begun on p. 197, continued)* "... comes." In the neuter plural, by शेश्शंदसि बहुलम् (*śeśśaṃdasi bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-20) the *ti* is elided *(as supplied: "ತಿಗೆ ಲೋಪ"; the sūtra is quoted in the shape "ಶೇಶ್ಶಂದಸಿ")*. By ईडवंदवृ (*īḍavaṃdavṛ*)— (Pā. Sū. 6-2-214) the initial-udātta accent comes.
- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*): since this word belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group, the initial-udātta accent comes by वृषादीनांच (*vṛṣādīnāṃca*) (Pā. Sū 6-1-203).
- सनिषामहे (*saniṣāmahe*): root वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*). By धात्वादेःषःसः (*dhātvādeḥṣaḥsaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) the initial *ṣ* becomes *s*. *Leṭ*. By व्यत्ययोबहुलम् (*vyatyayobahulam*) it takes the *ātmanepada*. In the first person plural the affix *mahiṅ*. By टितआत्मनेपदानां टेरे (*ṭitaātmanepadānāṃ ṭere*) the *ṭi* (*i*) becomes *e*. By लेटोडाट् (*leṭoḍāṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-64) it takes the augment *aḍ* *(as supplied, "ಎಂಬುದರಿರದ")*. By सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) it takes *sip* *(as supplied, "ಎಂಬದರಿಂದ")*. Since this has the *ardhadhātuka* designation, the augment *iḍ* comes by अर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (*ardhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ*). By आदेशप्रत्यययोः (*ādeśapratyayayoḥ*) it takes *ṣatva*; the form सनिषामहे (*saniṣāmahe*) results. Because it stands after a अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) *(as supplied, "ಅತಿಜಂತದ ಪರದಲ್ಲಿರುವುದರಿಂದ")*, the all-unaccented (*sarvānudātta*) accent comes by तिज्जतिजिः (*tijjatijiḥ*) .
- त्वे (*tve*): the word युष्मद् (*yuṣmad*). When it ends in the locative singular, by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*)— (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute शे (*śe*) comes to it; the substitute त्व (*tva*) replaces up to the *m*. By शे (*śe*) (Pā Sū. 1-1-13) the designation *pragṛhya* comes.
- ईरिरे (*īrire*): root ईर गतौ (*īra gatau*). For the *liṭ* third person plural, by लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच् (*liṭastajhayoreśirec*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81) the substitute *irec*. Because it is prohibited in the mantra, *ām* does not come by इजादेशगुरुम (*ijādeśaguruma*)— (Pā.. Sū. 3-1-36) *(as supplied; the sūtra is garbled and has a doubled full stop in "ಪಾ..")*. Reduplication; the vowel is long at the beginning *(as supplied: "ದೀರ್ಘಾದಿ")*. By तिज्जितजिः (*tijjitajiḥ*) the *nighāta* accent comes.

*The eleventh sūkta is complete.* (हन्नॊंदनॆय सूक्त समाप्तवु (*hannòṃdanèya sūkta samāptavu*))

*The twelfth sūkta.* (हन्नॆरडनॆय सूक्तवु (*hannèraḍanèya sūktavu*))

## Sūkta 12 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twelfth sūkta**

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta** (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्राग्नी इति नवर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रमैंद्राग्नं । तथा चानु-
> क्रम्यते । इंद्राग्नी ऐंद्राग्नमिति । गायत्रं त्विति तुशब्दादिदमपि सूक्तं गायत्रं ।
> इंद्राग्नी देवता ॥ अभिप्लविकेष्टहरुसु प्रातःसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्र आवापार्थमिदं
> सूक्तं । अभिप्लवपृष्ट्याहानीति खंडे सूत्रितं । इंद्राग्नी आ गतं ता हुवे ययो-
> शिदं । अ. ७ ५ । इति ॥ अग्निष्टोमेच्छावाकशस्त्र इंद्राग्नी आ गतमिति स्तोत्रिय-
> तृचः । तस्यैवाच्छावाकस्याद्या शस्त्रयाज्या । इंद्राग्नी आ गतं सुतमिति याज्या ।

*[The introduction continues on p. 199.]*

> आ. ५ १० । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ चतुर्विंशेऽहनि प्रातःसवनेऽच्छावाकशस्त्र इंद्राग्निः
> आ गतं सुशमिति षळहस्तोत्रियः इंद्राग्नी आ गतमिंद्रे अग्ना नमो बृहत् । अ.
> ७.२ । इति सूत्रितं ॥ अग्निष्टोमाच्छावाकशस्त्रे तोता वृत्रहणा हुव इत्याद्यास्ति स्रः ।
> सूत्रितं च । तोशा वृत्रहणा हुव इत्याद्यास्ति स्रः । आ. ५-१० । इति ॥ अग्निष्टोमेऽ-
> च्छावाकशस्त्र इंद्राग्नी अपसस्परीत्यनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । इंद्राग्नी आ गतं सुशमिं-
> द्राग्नी अपसस्परि । आ ५-१० । इति ॥

> *ā. 5 10 | iti sūtritatvāt ‖ caturviṃśe 'hani prātaḥsavane 'cchāvākaśastra iṃdrāgniḥ*
> *ā gataṃ suśamiti ṣaḷahastotriyaḥ iṃdrāgnī ā gatamiṃdre agnā namo bṛhat | a.*
> *7.2 | iti sūtritaṃ ‖ agniṣṭomācchāvākaśastre totā vṛtrahaṇā huva ityādyāsti sraḥ |*
> *sūtritaṃ ca | tośā vṛtrahaṇā huva ityādyāsti sraḥ | ā. 5-10 | iti ‖ agniṣṭome '-*
> *cchāvākaśastra iṃdrāgnī apasasparītyanurūpaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ suśamiṃ-*
> *drāgnī apasaspari | ā 5-10 | iti ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*) is the twelfth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta; Indra and Agni are the deities. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said इंद्राग्नी ऐंद्राग्नं (*iṃdrāgnī aiṃdrāgnaṃ*). Because the word तु (*tu*) is used, it is indicated that this sūkta too, like the preceding one, is in the Gāyatrī metre. On the days of sacrifice connected with the abhiplava, at the time of the morning pressing, this sūkta has its application for the āvāpa *(the supplied text has "ಅಪಾಪಾರ್ಥ", as supplied)* of the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Acchāvāka; this is set out by the sūtra इंद्राग्नी आ गतं ता हुवे ययोरिदं (*iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ tā huve yayoridaṃ*) in the section of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra called अभिप्लवसृष्टाहानि (*abhiplavasṛṣṭāhāni*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has अभिप्लवपृष्ट्याहानी (*abhiplavapṛṣṭyāhānī*))* (Ā. 7-5). In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, among the śastra mantras to be recited by the Acchāvāka priest, the three ṛks beginning इंद्राग्नी आ गतं (*iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ*) are to be recited as the stotriya tṛca, and the ṛk इंद्राग्नी आ गतं (*iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ*) as the first yājyā mantra of the śastra *(as supplied: "ಯಾಜ್ಞಾಮಂತ್ರ")*; this is set out by the sūtra इंद्राग्नी आ गतं सुतमिति याज्ञा (*iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ sutamiti yājñā*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 5-10). And on the twenty-fourth day of the sacrifice, at the morning pressing, the Acchāvāka priest is to recite the ṛk इंद्राग्नी आ गतं सुतं (*iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ sutaṃ*) as a stotrīya mantra *(the supplied text has "ಪಠಣ ಸ್ತೋತ್ರೀಯಮಂತ್ರವನ್ನಾಗಿ ಪಠಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು", as supplied)*; this is set out by the sūtra इंद्राग्नी आ गतमिंद्रॆ आग्ना नमो बृहत् (*iṃdrāgnī ā gatamiṃdrè āgnā namo bṛhat*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 7-2). And in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice the Acchāvāka priest is to recite as śastra mantras the three ṛks of this sūkta beginning तोशा वृत्रहणा हुवे (*tośā vṛtrahaṇā huve*) ; this is set out by the sūtra तोशा वृत्रहणा हुवा इत्यद्यास्ति स्रः (*tośā vṛtrahaṇā huvā ityadyāsti sraḥ*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 5-10). And in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice the Acchāvāka priest, at the time of reciting the śastra mantras, is to recite the first ṛk of the sūkta इंद्राग्नी आ गतं सुतं (*iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ sutaṃ*) and the seventh ṛk इंद्राग्नी अपसस्सिरि (*iṃdrāgnī apasassiri*) as anurūpa ṛks; this is set out by the sūtra इंद्राग्नी आगतं सुतमिंद्राग्नी अपसस्सिरि (*iṃdrāgnī āgataṃ sutamiṃdrāgnī apasassiri*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (printed "ಅ. ೫-೧೦", with "ಅ" for "ಆ", as supplied: Ā. 5-10).

#### Ṛk 1

*[The label of the Saṃhitā is garbled in the supplied text (printed "ಸಂವಾದಃ"); the Saṃhitā block follows in the standard place. In the Saṃhitā the supplied text reads गीर्भिनर्नभो (*gīrbhinarnabho*) (as supplied) and धियेषिता (*dhiyeṣitā*).]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ आ ग॑तं सु॒तं गी॒र्भिनर्नभो॒ वरे॑ण्यं ।  
> अ॒स्य पा॑तं धि॒येषि॒ता ॥ १ ॥

> *iṃdrāgnī ā gataṃ sutaṃ gīrbhinarnabho vareṇyaṃ |*  
> *asya pātaṃ dhiyeṣitā ‖ 1 ‖*

*[The label of the Pada is garbled in the supplied text (printed "ಕಡಂಬಃ"). The Pada reads गीभिः (*gībhiḥ*), नॆभः (*nèbhaḥ*) and इषिका (*iṣikā*), which differ from the Saṃhitā गीर्भिनर्नभो (*gīrbhinarnabho*) and धियेषिता (*dhiyeṣitā*) and from the bhāṣya's इषिता (*iṣitā*); as supplied.]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । आ । गतं । सुतं । गीभिः । नॆभः । वरेण्यं ।  
> अस्य । पातं । धिया । इषिका ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रश्चाग्निश्चेंद्राग्नी हे इंद्राग्नी देवौ सुतमभिषवादिसंस्कारैः संस्कृत-
> मत एव वरेण्यं परणेयं संभजनीयमिमं सोमं प्रति गीर्भिरस्मदीयाभिः
> स्तुतिरूपाभिर्वाग्निराहुत् संतौ नभो नभसः स्वर्गस्थानादागतं । आगच्छतं । अगत्य
> च धियस्माभिः क्रियमाणे कर्मणेषिता प्रेरितौ युवामस्य पातं । इमं सोमं
> पिबतं । यद्वा धियास्मदीयया । बुद्धेषितौ प्राप्तावस्मदृक्त्या प्रेरितौ युवा-
> मिमं सोमं पिबतं ॥ इंद्राग्नी । इंद्रश्चाग्निश्च द्वंद्वे घि । पा. २-२-३२ । इत्नग्नि-
> तद्व्य पूर्वनिपाते प्राप्ने अजाद्यदंतं । पा. २-२-३३ । इतींद्रशब्दस्य पूर्वनिपातः।
> पादादिश्वान्निघातप्रतिषेधः । षाष्ठिकस्वरः । गतं । गम्ल्य सृप्‌ल्य गतौ । बहुलं
> छंदसीति शपो लुकि सत्यनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिना मकारलोपः । निघातः । वरेण्यं ।
> वृज् संभक्तौ । वृज एण्यः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । पातं । पा पाने । सर्वे विध-
> यॆत्कंदसि विकल्प्यंत इति न पिबादेशः । इषिता । इष गतावित्यस्माद्धातोर्निष्ठायां
> तीपसहेतीडागमः । आगमा अनुदात्ता इतीटोऽनुदात्तत्वात् क्तस्वरः शिष्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, invoked by our praises, come from heaven to this Soma, prepared by pressing and desirable; impelled by our rite or devotion, drink it. The rest is the grammar of इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*), गतं (*gataṃ*), वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*), पातं (*pātaṃ*) and इषिता (*iṣitā*) (transcribed, not explained).

### Printed p. 201

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(ಹೇ) इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni, gods. सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—prepared by the sacrificial processes such as pressing, and वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*)—(therefore) acceptable (this Soma juice, with reference to it). गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—(our praises) by these words (invoked). नभः (*nabhaḥ*)—from (your own place) the world of heaven. आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—come; (then) धिया (*dhiyā*)—in the rite performed by us, or by our intellect (devotion). इषिता (*iṣitā*)—(you two) impelled. अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma juice. पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, gods, with reference to this Soma juice, which is acceptable because it is prepared by processes such as अभिनवादि (*abhinavādi*) *(sic, as supplied; the bhāṣya has अभिषवादि (*abhiṣavādi*))*, come from heaven, your place, invoked by our praises; pleased with our devotion, drink this Soma juice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra and Agni, come to this acceptable libation, (brought) by our praises from heaven, and induced by (our) devotion to drink of it.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

**सुतं— अभिषवादिसंस्कारैः संस्कृतं (*sutaṃ— abhiṣavādisaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ*)** — Those who perform the sacrifice consecrate the soma plant with mantras when they bring it for the sacrifice. After it has been brought, when the juice is extracted from it by pounding it with stones, they recite mantras and press the juice. By this it is described here that the soma juice is prepared (*saṃskṛta*).

**वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*)** — वरणेयं संभजनीयं (*varaṇeyaṃ saṃbhajanīyaṃ*) — "अभिलवणीयवादुदु (*abhilavaṇīyavādudu*)" *(as supplied, [sic])* or "that which is worthy of being necessarily obtained" is the meaning. The Nirukta authors, in the ṛk

विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चत्पुषदे । (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catpuṣade |*)
वि नाकमख्यत् सविता वरेण्योऽनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥ (*vi nākamakhyat savitā vareṇyo 'nu prayāṇamuṣaso vi rājati ‖*)

(printed "ಯ. ಸಂ. ೫-೮೧-೨", i.e. Ya. Saṃ. 5-81-2 as supplied), have explained the sense of the word वरॆण्यं (*varèṇyaṃ*) as वरणीयं (*varaṇīyaṃ*).

**गीर्भि: (*gīrbhi:*)** — अस्मवीयाभिः स्तुतिरूपाभिर्वाग्निराहूत् (*asmavīyābhiḥ stutirūpābhirvāgnirāhūt*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has "asmadīyābhiḥ" in its own spelling)*. The word गीः (*gīḥ*) is stated in the वाज्ञा मगळल्लि (*vājñā magaḷalli*) **NOTE** *(garbled in the supplied text; presumably the list of names of speech)* (Ni. 2-23). In the ṛk

मा त्वा सोमस्य गल्दया सदा याचन्नहं गिरा । (*mā tvā somasya galdayā sadā yācannahaṃ girā |*)
भूर्णि मृगं न सवनेषु चुक्रुदं क ईशानं न याचिषं ॥ (*bhūrṇi mṛgaṃ na savaneṣu cukrudaṃ ka īśānaṃ na yāciṣaṃ ‖*)

(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೮-೧-೨೦", as supplied: Ma. Saṃ. 8-1-20) the meaning is described, for स्तुत्या गीशन्य (*stutyā gīśanya*) , as "by praise or by song". And—
