### Printed p. 202

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*(continued from p. 201)*

तमिद्वर्धंतु नो गिरो वत्सं संशिश्वरीरिव । (*tamidvardhaṃtu no giro vatsaṃ saṃśiśvarīriva |*)
य इंद्रस्य हृदंसनिः ॥ (*ya iṃdrasya hṛdaṃsaniḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-61-14). In this ṛk स्तुतयः (*stutayaḥ*) (praises) is the meaning of गिरः (*giraḥ*); the word गिरः (*giraḥ*) is formed from the root गृणातेः (*gṛṇāteḥ*) (the supplied text has "ಗೃಣಾತೇಃ_ಗಿರಃ" and names the root as "ಗ್ಯ", as supplied [sic]). Since the Niruktakāras describe its meaning as "praises", it is expressed here that Indra and Agni, invoked by our praises, should come from heaven to our sacrifice.

धिया इषिता अस्य पातं (*dhiyā iṣitā asya pātaṃ*)—अस्माभिः क्रियमाणे कर्मणि प्रेरितौ युवां इमं सोमं पिबतं (*asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇe karmaṇi preritau yuvāṃ imaṃ somaṃ pibataṃ*) । यद्वा धिया अस्मदीयया बुद्ध्या इषितौ प्राप्तौ अस्मद्भक्त्या प्रेरितौ युवामिमं सोमं पिबतं (*yadvā dhiyā asmadīyayā buddhyā iṣitau prāptau asmadbhaktyā preritau yuvāmimaṃ somaṃ pibataṃ*) ॥ Because the word धी (*dhī*) is used in both senses, "rite" and "intelligence", a twofold meaning of this sentence is explained here. The first meaning: Indra and Agni, invoked by the praise-words of the priests and impelled by our praises in the rites, should come to the sacrifice and drink the Soma juice. Or: made the object of our meditation by the priests, and impelled by our devotion or meditation, Indra and Agni should come to the sacrifice and drink the Soma juice; so it is prayed. (The supplied text has "ಸೋಮರಸನ್ನು" for "ಸೋಮರಸವನ್ನು", as supplied.)

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*): इंद्रश्च अग्निश्च इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdraśca agniśca iṃdrāgnī*). By द्वंद्वेघि (*dvaṃdveghi*) (Pā. Sū. 2-2-32) a word ending in *i* must be placed first in a dvandva compound; but by आजाद्यदंतं (*ājādyadaṃtaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-2-33) there is a rule that a word beginning with a vowel and ending in short *a* is to be said first, so the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) gets the prior position. Because it stands at the beginning of the pāda the *āmantrita* *nighāta* accent does not come; by आमंत्रितस्य (*āmaṃtritasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) the initial-udātta accent comes.
- गतम् (*gatam*): root गमल्य गतौ (*gamalya gatau*) . In the *loṭ*, second person dual, the substitute *tam* (since the affix is treated like *laṭ*, as supplied "ಲಜ್ವದ್ಭಾವ"). By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) *luk* of *śap*. Because the affix has the marker *c* (as supplied "ಚಿತ್ತ"), by अनुदात्तोपदेश (*anudāttopadeśa*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) the *m* of the root is elided. The finite-verb *nighāta* accent comes.
- वरेण्यम् (*vareṇyam*): root वृज् संभक्तौ (*vṛj saṃbhaktau*). By वृज एण्यः (*vṛja eṇyaḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-378) the affix *eṇya*. By सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) guṇa of the root's *ṛ*, which stands with *r* following. Because the word is read in the वृषादिगण (*vṛṣādigaṇa*) the initial-udātta accent comes.
- पातम् (*pātam*): root पा. पाने (*pā. pāne*). In the *loṭ*, second person dual, the substitute *tam*. By the statement सर्वेविधयःछंदसि विकल्प्यंते (*sarvevidhayaḥchaṃdasi vikalpyaṃte*) (as supplied, the two words run together) the substitute *piba* does not come for the root. The finite-verb *nighāta* accent comes.

### Printed p. 203

Grammar notes of Ṛk 1, continued from p. 202:

- इषिका (*iṣikā*) (as supplied; the bhāṣya has इषिता (*iṣitā*)): root इष गतौ (*iṣa gatau*). By निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-102) the affix *kta*. By तीषसहलुभ (*tīṣasahalubha*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-48) the augment *iḍ*, since the affix beginning with *t* is an *ārdhadhātuka*. By the statement आगमा अनुदात्ताः (*āgamā anudāttāḥ*) the *iṭ* is anudātta, so by the accent of the affix the word is final-udātta. When the dual ending (*au*) follows, by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) it is replaced by *ā*.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी जरि॒तुः सचा॑ य॒ज्ञो जि॑गाति॒ चेत॑नः ।  
> अ॒या पा॑तमि॒मं सु॒तं २ ॥

> *iṃdrāgnī jarituḥ sacā yajño jigāti cetanaḥ |*  
> *ayā pātamimaṃ sutaṃ 2 ‖*

*[The Saṃhitā ends "ಸುತಂ ೨ ॥" in the supplied text, with no second danda before the number, as supplied.]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । जरितुः । सचा । यज्ञः । जिगाति । चेतनः ।  
> अया । पातं । इमं । सुतं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी जरितुः स्तोतुः सचा स्वर्गादिलक्षणफलप्राप्तौ सहायभूतो
> यज्ञो ज्योतिष्टोमादियज्ञसाधनभूतश्चेतन इंद्रियाणां चेतयिताप्यायन-
> कारी सन् असौ सोमो जिगाति । युवामभिगच्छति । आयास्मदीयया स्तुतिलक्षण-
> यानया वाचाहसत् संतौ सुतमभिषवादिसंस्कारोपेतमिमं सोमं पातं ।
> पिबतं ॥ जिगाति । गा स्तुताविश्ययं धातुरत्र गमने वर्तते । छंदसि जुहोत्यादिः ।
> बहुलं छंसीत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । निघातः । चेतनः । चिती संज्ञाने । कर्तरि बहुलवच-
> नाल्कुट् । लितीत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । अया ! इदंशब्दस्य तृतीयायाः स पां सुलुगिति
> याजादेशः । अनादेशप्राप्तौ हलि लोपः । पातं । पा पाने । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the Soma, helper of the worshipper in gaining heaven and the means of the sacrifice, refreshing the senses, goes to you; invoked by our speech, drink this pressed Soma. The rest is the grammar of जिगाति (*jigāti*), चेतनः (*cetanaḥ*), अया (*ayā*) and पातं (*pātaṃ*) (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(हे (*he*)) इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni. जरितुः (*jarituḥ*)—to the worshipper (the supplied text has "ಸ್ತೋಶೃವಿಗೆ", as supplied). सचा (*sacā*)—helper (in obtaining the fruit such as heaven). यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—the means of sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma. चेतनः (*cetanaḥ*)—a giver of vigour (refreshment) to the senses (this Soma juice). जिगाति (*jigāti*)—goes (in your direction). अया (*ayā*)—by this speech (of ours, in the form of praise; invoked). सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—well prepared. इमं (*imaṃ*)—this Soma juice. पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink.

### Printed p. 204

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, this Soma juice, which is a helper of the worshipper in gaining the fruit such as heaven, a means of sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, a giver of vigour to the senses, which goes forth with you as its aim and is well prepared by the processes such as pressing: invoked by our praise-words, come and drink it.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra and Agni, the conscious sacrifice associated with the worshipper proceeds to you : (summoned) by this (invocation), drink the libation

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

जरितुः सचा (*jarituḥ sacā*)—स्तोतुः स्वर्गादिलक्षणफलप्राप्तौ सहायभूतः (*stotuḥ svargādilakṣaṇaphalaprāptau sahāyabhūtaḥ*). The word जरिता (*jaritā*) is stated among the names of the worshipper (Ni. 3-19). And in नूनं साते प्रति वरं जरित्रे (*nūnaṃ sāte prati varaṃ jaritre*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-21) the word जरिता (*jaritā*), गरिता (*garitā*) means one who praises (the supplied text has "ಸ್ತುತಿಮಾಡುನವನೆಂದು", as supplied). सचा (*sacā*)—this word is explained by Yāska (Ni. 5-5) as सचा सहेत्यर्थः (*sacā sahetyarthaḥ*), and in the ṛk

अग्निनेंद्रेण वरुणेन विष्णुनादित्यै रुद्रैर्वसुभिस्सचा भुवा । (*agnineṃdreṇa varuṇena viṣṇunādityai rudrairvasubhissacā bhuvā |*)
सजोषना उषसा सूर्येण च सोमं पिबतमश्विना ॥ (*sajoṣanā uṣasā sūryeṇa ca somaṃ pibatamaśvinā ‖*)

(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೮-೩೫-೧", i.e. Ma. Saṃ. 8-35-1) it conveys the sense of "together": वसुभिस्सहभुवा (*vasubhissahabhuvā*), "those who are together with the Vasus". Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning thus: since Soma is a means of satisfying the gods, it helps the priests who praise the gods in the sacrifice to obtain the favour of the gods (so that fruit such as heaven results).

यज्ञः चेतनः जिगाति (*yajñaḥ cetanaḥ jigāti*)—although the word यज्ञ (*yajña*) in this sentence is stated and explained among the names of the sacrifice (Ni. 3-19; the same reference as for the worshipper's names above, as supplied), Sāyaṇa explains it by ज्योतिष्टोमादियज्ञसाधनभूतः (*jyotiṣṭomādiyajñasādhanabhūtaḥ*): the Soma plant is the instrument for performing the sacrifice when sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma are performed. For the word चेतनः (*cetanaḥ*) he explains इंद्रियाणां चेतयिता अप्पायनकारी सन् आसौ सोमः (*iṃdriyāṇāṃ cetayitā appāyanakārī san āsau somaḥ*) (as supplied, "ಅಪ್ಪಾಯನ", "ಆಸೌ"): the Soma (juice) gives keenness to the senses, does good to the mind, and so is offered to Indra and Agni.

आया (*āyā*)—this word has been explained by Durgācārya as the Vedic form of अनया (*anayā*) (the Saṃhitā has अया (*ayā*); as supplied). Yāska (printed "ಸಿ. ೩.೨೧", i.e. "Si." for "Ni." [sic], 3.21) reads अयेनेत्युपदेशस्य (*ayenetyupadeśasya*) and says that the words अया (*ayā*) and एना (*enā*) are used in all three genders. अस्मदीयस्तुशिलक्षणया अनिया वाचा आरूतौ (*asmadīyastuśilakṣaṇayā aniyā vācā ārūtau*) (as supplied; the bhāṣya reads differently): "by this speech of ours, in the form of praise, … the priests …" (the supplied text breaks off here in the middle of the word वाक्कुग (*vākkuga*) "this speech", at the end of the window; the passage continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 205

Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 (the passage broke off at the end of p. 204 in the word ವಾಕ್ಕುಗ…; here it continues ಳಿಂದ, together "ವಾಕ್ಕುಗಳಿಂದ", "by words"): … "invoked by words" — having given this sense, he has described the meaning thus: may Indra and Agni drink the Soma juice (सोमंसवन्नु (*somaṃsavannu*), as supplied) which is endowed with the preparatory rites such as pressing (*abhiṣava*, squeezing out).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

of Ṛk 2

- जरितु (*jaritu*): the root is given in the supplied text as "ಜ್ಯಷ್ ವಯೋಹಾನ್" (as supplied; not corrected). Here it is used in the sense of praising. The affix तृच् (*tṛc*) in the agent sense; the augment इडागम (*iḍāgama*); guṇa because of the affix. Because the affix is marked चित् (*cit*) (the supplied text has "ಚಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ"), the word is final-udātta. It is a form of the genitive singular (the supplied text has "ಪಷ್ಟೀ", as supplied).
- जिगाति (*jigāti*): from the root गा स्तुतौ (*gā stutau*). Since roots have many meanings, it is used here in the sense of going. A root used in the Veda only (छंदोमात्र (*chaṃdomātra*)), of the juhotyādi class. In the third person singular of the present (लट् (*laṭ*)) the lengthened/reduplicated form arises through the substitute of the affix (the supplied text has "ವಿಪ್ ಶ್ಲು", as supplied) so the root is doubled; by बहुलंछंदसि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasi*) the reduplicate takes *i*. The form is जिगाति (*jigāti*); the verbal accent तिजंतनिघातस्वर (*tijaṃtanighātasvara*) results.
- चेतनः (*cetanaḥ*): the root is given as "ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಸಂಜ್ಞಾನೇ" (as supplied; the bhāṣya reads the root differently). By the extension "bahula" the affix ल्युट् (*lyuṭ*) is used in the agent sense. By पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) guṇa for the light penultimate vowel of the root. By युवोरनाक् (*yuvoranāk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the affix is replaced by *ana*. By लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent falls on the syllable before the affix.
- अया (*ayā*): the word इदं (*idaṃ*). When the instrumental singular follows, by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the substitute *yāc* (याजादेश (*yājādeśa*); as supplied). If the substitute *ana* were to apply to the base, then, as the ending begins with a consonant, by हलिलोपः (*halilopaḥ*) the *id* is dropped; the *ā* that comes from the त्यदादि (*tyadādi*) rule remains; because the ending is marked चित् (*cit*) the final-udātta accent results.
- पातम् (*pātam*): the root पा पाने (*pā pāne*); explained in the previous mantra. The verbal accent तिजंतनिघातस्वर (*tijaṃtanighātasvara*) results.
- सुतम् (*sutam*): the root षुञ् अभिषवे (*ṣuñ abhiṣave*). The affix क्त (*kta*) in the passive sense. The initial of the root becomes *s* (सत्व (*satva*), as supplied); since the affix is कित् (*kit*) there is no guṇa; by the accent of the affix it is final-udātta (आंतोदात्त (*āṃtodātta*), as supplied). A form of the accusative singular.

(End of the grammar notes of Ṛk 2.)

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑मु॒ग्निं क॑वि॒च्छदा॑ य॒ज्ञस्य॑ जू॒त्वा वृ॑णे ।  
> ता सोम॑स्ये॒ह तृं॑पतां ॥ ३ ॥

> *iṃdramugniṃ kavicchadā yajñasya jūtvā vṛṇe |*  
> *tā somasyeha tṛṃpatāṃ ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 206

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रं । अग्निं । कविछदा । यज्ञस्य । जूत्या । वृणे ।  
> ता । सोमस्य । इह । तृंपतां ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य यज्ञस्य साधनभूतस्य सोमस्य जूत्या । जूतिः प्रेरणं । सोमस्ता-
> वद्यजमानं प्रेरयति । साधनमुपलभ्य तत्साध्यक्रता यजमानः प्रवर्तत इति हि तस्य
> प्रेरकत्वं । तया प्रेरणरूपया जूत्या प्रेरितोऽहं कविच्छदा कवीनां स्तोत्कृ-
> णामुचितफलप्रदानेनोपच्चंदकाविंद्रमग्निं च युवां वृणे । सोमपानार्थ-
> मिह कर्मण्यागच्छतमिति संभजे । ता आगतौ च ताविंद्राग्नी इह कर्मणि सोमस्य
> सोमदानेन तृंपशां । तृप्ततां ॥ इंद्रं । इदि परमैश्वर्य इत्यस्माद्दातोर्ऋ-
> जेंद्राग्रेति रन् प्रत्ययांतत्तेन निसातनादाद्युदात्तत्वं' कविच्छदा । छदि अपवारणे!
> अस्मात् क्विप् । सुपां सुलुगिति सुपो डादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । जूत्या ।
> जू इति सौत्रो धातुः । अस्मादुदात्त इत्यनुवृत्तावूतियूतिजूतीत्यादिना निपातनादं-
> तोदात्तत्वं । उदात्तयणो हल् पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । वृणे । वृज्
> संभक्तौ । श्नाप्रत्ययः । टित आत्मनेपदानामिति टेरेत्वं । निघातः । ता । सुपां
> सुलुगिति डादेशः । सोमस्य । सुञ् अभिषवे । अस्मादर्तिस्तुसुमसृधृक्षीत्यादिना म-
> स्प्रत्ययः । नित्सर्ः । तृंपतां । तृप प्रीणने । लोट मुचादित्वान्नुमागमः ।
> निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Urged by the impulse of the Soma, the means of the sacrifice, I choose Indra and Agni, who gratify the poets, to come to this rite; may they be satisfied with the Soma here. The rest is the grammar of इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*), कविच्छदा (*kavicchadā*), जूत्या (*jūtyā*), वृणे (*vṛṇe*), ता (*tā*), सोमस्य (*somasya*) and तृंपतां (*tṛṃpatāṃ*) (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the Soma juice that is the means of the sacrifice (the supplied text has "ಮಜ್ಜಸಾಧನಭೂತವಾದ", as supplied). जूत्या (*jūtyā*)—by the impulse (I who am impelled). कविच्छदा (*kavicchadā*)—protectors of the praisers. इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*) अग्निं (*agniṃ*) (the supplied text has "ಅಗ್ನಿಂ(ಚೆ)", as supplied)—you two, named Indra and Agni. वृणे (*vṛṇe*)—I pray (that you come for the drinking of Soma). ता (*tā*) (printed "ಶಾ", as supplied)—(so entreated, having come) Indra and Agni. इह (*iha*)—in this rite. सोमस्य (*somasya*)—of the Soma juice (from drinking). तृंपतां (*tṛṃpatāṃ*)—may they be satisfied.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Inspired by the impulse of the Soma juice, the means of the sacrifice, I pray to you two, named Indra and Agni, protectors of the praisers, to come to drink Soma. Having come, may you both drink Soma at this our sacrifice and be satisfied.

### Printed p. 207

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Urged by the energy of the sacrifice, I have recourse to Indra and Agni, the protectors of the pious: may they be satiated with the Soma here pre-sented (line-end hyphen of the print).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यज्ञस्य जूत्या (*yajñasya jūtyā*)—यज्ञसाधनभूतस्य सोमस्य जूत्या जूताः प्रेरणं (*yajñasādhanabhūtasya somasya jūtyā jūtāḥ preraṇaṃ*) (as supplied; the bhāṣya has जूतिः प्रेरणं (*jūtiḥ preraṇaṃ*)). The author of the Nirukta, having cited the ṛk

त्यमू षु वाजिनं देवजूतं सहावानं तरु तारंरथानां (*tyamū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtaṃ sahāvānaṃ taru tāraṃrathānāṃ*)
अगिष्वनेमिं पृतनाजमाकुं स्वस्तये तार्क्ष्यमिहा हुवेम (*agiṣvanemiṃ pṛtanājamākuṃ svastaye tārkṣyamihā huvema*)

(the supplied text has a stray "(ಋ. ಸಂ." and then "(ಪು. ಸಂ. ೧೦-೧೭೮-೧)", i.e. "Pu. Saṃ. 10-178-1", as supplied; the verse is quoted as supplied), has explained: जूतिर्गतिः प्रीतिर्वा देवजूतं-देवगतं देवप्रीतं वा (*jūtirgatiḥ prītirvā devajūtaṃ-devagataṃ devaprītaṃ vā*)—giving to the word जूति (*jūti*) the sense of "going" or "love", and explaining that देवजूत (*devajūta*) means the going or the love of the gods. Sāyaṇa has given the sense *preraṇa*, "urging", and says : सोमस्तावत् यजमानवं प्रेरयति साधनमुपक्रम्य तत्साध्यक्रता यजमानः प्रवर्तक इति हितस्य प्रेरकत्वम् (*somastāvat yajamānavaṃ prerayati sādhanamupakramya tatsādhyakratā yajamānaḥ pravartaka iti hitasya prerakatvam*) (this differs in several words from the bhāṣya of this Ṛk; noted, not corrected). Because Soma produces joy for the gods, it urges the sacrificer to perform the sacrifice: when the materials needed for the sacrifice are ready, the sacrificer engages in the performance of the sacrifice accomplished by them, and therefore Soma is the impeller of the sacrifice (the supplied text has "ಯಜ್ಞಪ್ರೇರವಾಗಿರುವುದು", as supplied). By this he has explained that the sacrificer is impelled.

कविच्छदा (*kavicchadā*)—कवीनां स्तोतृणामुचितफलप्रदानेन उपच्छंदका (*kavīnāṃ stotṛṇāmucitaphalapradānena upacchaṃdakā*). The word कवि (*kavi*) is stated among the names of the intelligent (Ni. 3-19), and in the ṛk

विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुप्पदे (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catuppade*)
वि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति (*vi nākamakhyatsavitā vareṇyonu prayāṇamuṣaso vi rājati*)

(printed "ಪು. ಸಂ. ೫-೧೧-೨", i.e. Pu. Saṃ. 5-11-2, as supplied; the verse is quoted as supplied), here कवि: मेधावी क्रांतदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्वा (*kavi: medhāvī krāṃtadarśano bhavati kavatervā*) (Ni. 12-13). Since the word *kavi*, derived from a root (the supplied text has "ಕುಧಾವಿನಿಂದ", as supplied), is explained as *krāntadarśin* ("one who has seen to the end of knowledge") and as the intelligent one, Sāyaṇa has taken "kavis" to mean the intelligent praisers. It is described that Indra and Agni increase the zeal of those who praise them, by granting them a fitting reward. And further, that the priests, to the sacrifice of such greatness, "come to the sacrifice" and for the purpose of drinking Soma (the supplied text breaks off here at the end of the window with the hyphenated word सोमपानार्थ- (*somapānārtha-*); the passage continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 208

Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 (the passage broke off at the end of p. 207 in the hyphenated word "somapānārtha-" (the Kannada-script word is quoted in the previous window); here it continues मिहकर्मणि आगच्छतमिति संभजे! (*mihakarmaṇi āgacchatamiti saṃbhaje!*) (the "!" as supplied). Then, आगतौ च तौ इह कर्मणि सोमपानेन तृप्यतां (*āgatau ca tau iha karmaṇi somapānena tṛpyatāṃ*)—the Ṛṣi, the seer of the mantra, has described his wish that Indra and Agni, who have come to the sacrifice, may drink the Soma and be satisfied.

सोमस्य (*somasya*)—The author of the Nirukta (says): ओषधिस्सोम: सुनोतेर्यदेनमभिषुण्वंति (*oṣadhissoma: sunoteryadenamabhiṣuṇvaṃti*)—a herb famous by the name Soma. About it (the text goes on), in the ṛk

आदाय श्येनो अभरत्सोमं सदस्रं सवा आयुतं च साकं । (*ādāya śyeno abharatsomaṃ sadasraṃ savā āyutaṃ ca sākaṃ |*)
अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥ (*atrā puraṃdhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūraḥ ‖*)

(printed "ಪು. ಸಂ. ೪-೨೬-೭", i.e. Pu. Saṃ. 4-26-7, as supplied), it is described that the Gāyatrī metre, taking the form of the Śyena bird, brought it from heaven to the earth, and that on the occasions of Indra's drinking this Soma the sacrificers, performing sacrifices with a thousand pressings, gave a gift (dakṣiṇā) numbering ten thousand (*ayuta*): thus the greatness of Soma is explained. And बहुलमस्य नैघंटुकं वृत्तं आश्चर्यमिव प्राधान्येनॆ (*bahulamasya naighaṃṭukaṃ vṛttaṃ āścaryamiva prādhānyenè*)—the praise of this Soma indicates its importance; and it is wonderful in character (the text then says), "as is read in the ninth Maṇḍala"; and the greatness of this Soma is stated in this book in the form of praise in

स्वादिष्ठया मदिष्टया पवस्व सोम धारया । इंद्राय पातने सुतः । (*svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭayā pavasva soma dhārayā | iṃdrāya pātane sutaḥ |*)

(printed "ಪ. ಸಂ. ೯೧೧", i.e. "Pa. Saṃ. 911", as supplied).

In the ṛk

सोमं मन्यते पपिवान् यत्संपिषंत्योषधिं । (*somaṃ manyate papivān yatsaṃpiṣaṃtyoṣadhiṃ |*)
सोमं यं ब्राह्मणो विदुर्न तस्याश्नाति कश्चन ॥ (*somaṃ yaṃ brāhmaṇo vidurna tasyāśnāti kaścana ‖*)

(printed "(ಖ). ಸಂ. ೧೦-೮೫-೩)", i.e. Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-3 with a stray bracket and full stop, as supplied) the word *soma* also means the moon. This ṛk praises both the Soma plant and the moon. But the author Yāska has described in the following way the greater importance, over the famous moon, of this Soma:

सोमं मन्यते पपिर्वा यत्संपिषंत्योषधिमिति वृथाशुतमसोम-माह सोमं यं ब्रह्माणो विदुरिति न तस्याश्नाति कश्चनायज्येत्य-धियज्ञं । अथाधिदैवतं सोमं मन्यते पपिर्वा यत्संपिषंत्यो-षधिमिति यजुस्सुतमसोममाह सोमं यं ब्रह्माणो विदुक्चंद्र-मसं न तस्याश्नाति कश्चनादेव इति । (*somaṃ manyate papirvā yatsaṃpiṣaṃtyoṣadhimiti vṛthāśutamasoma-māha somaṃ yaṃ brahmāṇo viduriti na tasyāśnāti kaścanāyajyetya-dhiyajñaṃ | athādhidaivataṃ somaṃ manyate papirvā yatsaṃpiṣaṃtyo-ṣadhimiti yajussutamasomamāha somaṃ yaṃ brahmāṇo vidukcaṃdra-masaṃ na tasyāśnāti kaścanādeva iti |*) (printed "ಸಿ. ೧೧-೪", i.e. "Si. 11-4", as supplied; the quotation differs in some words from the ṛk quoted above, e.g. ब्राह्मणो (*brāhmaṇo*) and ब्रह्माणो (*brahmāṇo*), पपिवान् (*papivān*) and पपिर्वा (*papirvā*); noted, not corrected; line-end hyphens of the print are kept)

Those who make rasāyana (elixirs) and the like bring the Soma, press out its juice and drink it; yet, since they do not become famous as *somapas* (Soma-drinkers) who drink the Soma in the sacrifice, and since it is employed as a part of the sacrifice, [the passage continues on the next page: उप (*upa*) + योगिसल्पट्ट (*yogisalpaṭṭa*) "employed"] (the sentence breaks off here at the end of p. 208).

### Printed p. 209

Continuation (the word उप (*upa*) at the end of p. 208 continues as योगिसल्पट्ट (*yogisalpaṭṭa*), together "employed"): … the Soma gives to the sacrificer alone, by the prescribed manner, the fame of being a Soma-drinker; so it is praised. In the view of the deities (*adhidaivata*) also (where the word *soma* is explained as the moon) the Soma that is a part of the sacrifice is denoted by the word *soma*. By the Śruti sentence सोमो नूनमेष यद्देवानामन्नं (*somo nūnameṣa yaddevānāmannaṃ*) , although the moon is denoted by the word *soma*, he is food for the gods alone. Therefore, although by the mantra सोमं-मन्यते (*somaṃ-manyate*) two kinds of meaning, *adhiyajña* (relating to the sacrifice) and *adhidaiva* (relating to the deities), are given to the word *soma*, the importance in the sacrifice performed by the sacrificial priests is stated for the Soma that is a herb.

In the ṛk

यत्त्वा देव प्रपिबंति तत आ स्वायसे पुनः । (*yattvā deva prapibaṃti tata ā svāyase punaḥ |*)
वायुस्सोमस्य रक्षिता समानां मास आकृतिः ॥ (*vāyussomasya rakṣitā samānāṃ māsa ākṛtiḥ ‖*)

(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೧೦-೮೫-೫", i.e. "Ma. Saṃ. 10-85-5", as supplied; स्वायसे (*svāyase*) is the supplied spelling), the Nirukta says:

यत्ना देव प्रपिबंति तक आप्यायसे पुनरिति नाराशंसानभिप्रेत्य पूर्वपक्षापरपक्षा-विति वा वायुस्सोमस्य रक्षिता वायुमस्य रक्षितारमाह साहचर्यार्त रसहरणाद्वा । (*yatnā deva prapibaṃti taka āpyāyase punariti nārāśaṃsānabhipretya pūrvapakṣāparapakṣā-viti vā vāyussomasya rakṣitā vāyumasya rakṣitāramāha sāhacaryārta rasaharaṇādvā |*)
समानां संवत्सराणां मास आकृतिः सोमो रूपविशेषैरोषधिश्चंद्रमा वा ! (*samānāṃ saṃvatsarāṇāṃ māsa ākṛtiḥ somo rūpaviśeṣairoṣadhiścaṃdramā vā !*)

(the supplied text has "!" for the final danda; the quotation differs in letters from the ṛk just quoted, यत्ना (*yatnā*) for यत्त्वा (*yattvā*), तक (*taka*) for तत (*tata*); noted, not corrected).

In the sense relating to the sacrifice (*adhiyajña*) the Soma is drunk at the three pressings (*savana*) by the sacrificer and the other priests (*ṛtvij*). Because of this, this Soma is one who causes increase (*āpyāyana*). Although the wind sucks the juice of the herbs, it does not suck the Soma juice, and so it is its protector. The rasāyana makers who know the Āyurveda (say) that this Soma, according to the lunar days (*tithi*) in the bright fortnights of each month, gains an increase of its leaves (*parṇa*), and according to the lunar days of the dark fortnights, a decrease (*apacita*) of the leaves (the supplied text has "ಹಾಸ", as supplied). In the sense relating to the deities, the moon, denoted by the word *soma*, by his phases (*kalā*) according to the respective lunar days, is the nourisher of the gods. The gods also drink the phases of the moon; in the respective fortnights the moon gains increase and decrease through his phases. Thus, in both the ways, *adhiyajña* and *adhidaiva*, the likeness (similarity of state) of the moon to the Soma plant is stated, the Soma-nature is established, and the Soma plant is praised as "filled with abundant greatness" (the supplied text has "ಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ", as supplied).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

of Ṛk 3

- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*) (*indra*)—root इदि (*idi*) in the sense of supreme lordship. By ऋजेंद्रागृ (*ṛjeṃdrāgṛ*) (Uṇ. 2-180) it is formed with the ending *ran* by nipāta, and hence is ādyudātta.
- कविच्छदा (*kavicchadā*)—root छदि (*chadi*) in the sense of covering (*apavāraṇa*); the ending *kvip* by क्विप्‌च (*kvipca*); the accent of the base of the latter member of a compound with a kṛt-ending; by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the case ending is replaced by *ḍā*. The form becomes कविच्छवा (*kavicchavā*) (as supplied; the word is कविच्छदा (*kavicchadā*) above).

### Printed p. 210

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 3):

- जूत्या (*jūtyā*)—जू (*jū*) is a root given in a sūtra (*sautra*). As "udāttaḥ" continues from the previous sūtra, by ऊतियूतिजूति (*ūtiyūtijūti*) … (Pā. Sū. 3-3-97) it is formed with the ending *ktin* by nipāta, so the final syllable is udātta. In the instrumental singular there is the substitution *yaṇ*; since an anudātta case ending follows the *yaṇ* that stands in the place of an udātta, by उदात्तयणो हल् पूर्वात् (*udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) the case ending also becomes udātta.
- वृणे (*vṛṇe*)—root वृज् (*vṛj*) in the sense of संभक्तौ (*saṃbhaktau*) ; of the *krayādi* class. In the present (*laṭ*) first-person singular the ending *iṭ* ; by टतआत्मनेपदानां (*ṭataātmanepadānāṃ*) *e* replaces it. By क्रादिभ्यः श्ना (*krādibhyaḥ śnā*) the *śnā* vikaraṇa. Since the ending is marked (the supplied text has "ಜಿತ್ವ", as supplied), by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112) the ā of the vikaraṇa is dropped. Because the vikaraṇa is so marked, guṇa does not occur for the ṛ of the root. Because of the following ṛ, the n has *i* (as supplied: "ಇತ್ವ"). Because it follows a finite verb form (*atiṅanta*, as supplied), the nighāta accent occurs.
- ता (*tā*)—the word तद् (*tad*). For the nominative dual (*au*), by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-30) the substitute is *ā*.
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—root षुञ् (*ṣuñ*) in the sense of pressing (*abhiṣava*). By आर्तिस्तुसुहुस्पृधृक्षि (*ārtistusuhuspṛdhṛkṣi*) (Uṇ. 1-137) the ending *man*; taking it as the cause, guṇa of the u of the root; since the ending is marked *nit*, the first-syllable-udātta accent comes. Form of the genitive singular (the supplied text has "ಷಷ್ಠೀ", as supplied).
- शृंपराम् (*śṛṃparām*) (the supplied spelling; the word of the ṛk, last in its Saṃhitā, is *tṛṃpatāṃ*; not corrected)—root तृप (*tṛpa*) in the sense of satisfying (*prīṇana*). For the third-person dual of the imperative (*loṭ*) the substitute *tām*. Since the root is read in the *muc*-class (the supplied text has "ಮುಚಾದಿ", as supplied), by शेमुजादीनाम् (*śemujādīnām*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-59) the augment *num* comes to the root. Because it follows a finite verb form, the nighāta accent occurs.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In this rite I call Indra and Agni, who oppress foes, slay Vṛtra (sin), are equally victorious, unconquered and givers of abundant food, to drink Soma. The rest is grammar of वृत्रहणा (*vṛtrahaṇā*), हुवे (*huve*), सजित्वाना (*sajitvānā*), अपराजिता (*aparājitā*) (the bhāṣya spells it so), इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*) and वाजसातमा (*vājasātamā*) (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

तोशा (*tośā*)—oppressors of foes. वृत्रहणा (*vṛtrahaṇā*)—destroyers of sin. सजित्वाना (*sajitvānā*)—equally victorious. अपराजॆता (*aparājètā*) (the supplied spelling; the Saṃhitā has अपराजिता (*aparājitā*))—who cannot be conquered (by anyone). वाजसातमा (*vājasātamā*)—givers of abundant food; such. इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni (you two). हुवे (*huve*)—(that you may come to this our sacrifice and drink Soma) I call.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

*(The label is printed "ಭಾಷೆ." in the supplied text; written here as the standard label.)*

O Indra and Agni, who cause affliction to foes, who remove sin, who are equally victorious, who cannot be conquered by anyone, and who give food as one wishes, I invite you two to come to this our sacrifice and drink Soma.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I invoke Indra and Agni, the discomfiters of foes, the destroyers of Vritra, the victorious, the invincible, the bestowers of most abundant food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*(The label is printed "ವಿಶೇಷವಸ್ತುಗಳು." in the supplied text; written here as the standard label.)*

तोशा-शत्रुणां बाधकौ (*tośā-śatruṇāṃ bādhakau*) (the bhāṣya has तोशा शत्रूणां बाधकौ (*tośā śatrūṇāṃ bādhakau*); as supplied). The meaning is described: Indra and Agni restrain foes.

### Printed p. 212

वृत्रहणा—वृत्रस्य पापस्य हंतागौ (*vṛtrahaṇā—vṛtrasya pāpasya haṃtāgau*) (the bhāṣya has हंतारौ (*haṃtārau*); as supplied). The authors of the Nirukta have explained the meaning of the word *vṛtra* in this way:

इत्को वृत्रः मेघ इति नैरुक्ताः त्वाष्टोऽसुर इत्यैतिहासिकाः अपां च ज्योतिषश्च मिश्रीभावरिर्मणे वर्षकर्म जायते। शत्रोपमार्थेन युद्धवर्णा भवंति । अहिवत्तु खलु मंत्रवर्णा ब्राह्मणवादाश्च । विवृद्धा शरीरस्य स्रोतांसि निवारयां चकार । शस्मिन् हते प्रसस्यंदिर आ८४ । (*itko vṛtraḥ megha iti nairuktāḥ tvāṣṭo 'sura ityaitihāsikāḥ apāṃ ca jyotiṣaśca miśrībhāvarirmaṇe varṣakarma jāyate| śatropamārthena yuddhavarṇā bhavaṃti | ahivattu khalu maṃtravarṇā brāhmaṇavādāśca | vivṛddhā śarīrasya srotāṃsi nivārayāṃ cakāra | śasmin hate prasasyaṃdira ā84 |*) (Ni. 2-16) वृत्रं जघ्निवान् अपववार तत् । वृत्रो वृणोतीर्वा वर्तशीर्वा वर्थतीर्वा यदवृणोत् तद् वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वं इति विज्ञायते । यदवर्तश तत् वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वमिति विज्ञायते । (*vṛtraṃ jaghnivān apavavāra tat | vṛtro vṛṇotīrvā vartaśīrvā varthatīrvā yadavṛṇot tad vṛtrasya vṛtratvaṃ iti vijñāyate | yadavartaśa tat vṛtrasya vṛtratvamiti vijñāyate |*) (Ni. 2-17).

Those who study the Nirukta, which explains the meaning of words according to their etymology, are called Nairuktas. They say that the cloud is what is denoted by the word *vṛtra*. But there is a Smṛti saying:

इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां वेदं समुपबृंदयेत् । (*itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vedaṃ samupabṛṃdayet |*)
बिभेत्यल्पश्रुताद्वेदो मामयं प्रतरेदिति ॥ (*bibhetyalpaśrutādvedo māmayaṃ pratarediti ‖*)

. That is: the meaning of the Veda should be settled by examining what is said in the Itihāsas and Purāṇas; the Veda is afraid of a man of scanty learning, thinking "he will wrong me". The Itihāsa which teaches that the son of Tvaṣṭṛ (the supplied text has "ತ್ವಷ್ಟವಿನ ಪುತ್ರನು", as supplied) is the Asura Vṛtra is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā and in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. Following this, Yāska has said मुख्यं कारणत्वं इतिहासज्ञानस्यॆव (*mukhyaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ itihāsajñānasyèva*) (as supplied; the sentence is broken by a line-end hyphen): in settling the meaning of the Veda, knowledge of the Itihāsa is the chief cause. Their main opinion is that when there is no other means of settling the meaning of the Veda, the Aitihāsika view should be accepted, and that अगतिकगतिकल्पना (*agatikagatikalpanā*) is justified. In this matter, quoting (the supplied text has "ದಹರಿಸಿ", as supplied) this mantra,

यदचरस्तन्वा वावृधानो बलानींद्र प्रब्रुवाणो जनेषु । (*yadacarastanvā vāvṛdhāno balānīṃdra prabruvāṇo janeṣu |*)
मायेत्सा ते यानि युद्धान्याहुर्नाद्य शत्रुं ननु पुरा विवत्से ॥ (*māyetsā te yāni yuddhānyāhurnādya śatruṃ nanu purā vivatse ‖*)

(printed "ಋ. ಸಂ. ೧೦-೫೪-೨", i.e. Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-54-2, as supplied; the verse is quoted as supplied), (the explanation runs): Indra grows in many ways; having a body grown in each of those ways, Indra is famous through his own power; when Indra fights many battles he assumes forms of many kinds; all this is the glory of his *māyā*. For Indra there is no enemy. वीर्यमिंद्रः वीर्यं वै प्राणाः इति ह विज्ञायते । (*vīryamiṃdraḥ vīryaṃ vai prāṇāḥ iti ha vijñāyate |*) Indra is the life-breath; Indra is vigour (*vīrya*), so the Śruti teaches. Therefore all that Indra has done in fighting is mere *māyā*. तस्मादाहुर्नैतदस्ति यद्देवासुरमिति विज्ञायते (*tasmādāhurnaitadasti yaddevāsuramiti vijñāyate*) (the supplied text has the line-end hyphen "ನೈತ-ದಸ್ತಿ"): the Śruti "tasmād āhuḥ" teaches that there is no such opposition and no fight as "gods and Asuras". Having thus discussed, he says that through the mixing of waters and light with each other (the sentence continues on the next page)

### Printed p. 213

(… "anyonya-" of the previous page continues: "mutually") rain (*varṣa*, *vṛṣṭi*) arises; and that although in other Vedic Śākhās and in various Brāhmaṇa sentences an Asura named Vṛtra and a fight with him are described, they should be set aside on the strength of the Śruti and reasoning set out above. In his view the thickening of water (*udaka ghanībhāva*) is what is called the growth of the body; this holds back the waters; if this is removed, the waters reach the earth in the form of rain. वृत्रं जघ्निर्वाक् (*vṛtraṃ jaghnirvāk*) means: he struck Vṛtra, or the cloud, which was an obstacle to rain, or he prevented the clouds from obstructing the rain. When the way by which rain comes from the clouds is blocked, Indra strikes the cloud and opens its path so that the waters fall to the earth. This is what is said by आपः प्रसस्यंदिरे (*āpaḥ prasasyaṃdire*) .

If the word वृत्र (*vṛtra*) is derived from the root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*) it conveys the sense of "covering" (the supplied text has "ಅವಂಸುವುದು", as supplied). If it is said to be derived from the root वृतु वर्तनॆ (*vṛtu vartanè*) , it means that he caused अपः (*apaḥ*) (the waters) वृष्टिभावेन (*vṛṣṭibhāvena*) (in the form of rain) अवर्तयत् प्रावर्तयत् (*avartayat prāvartayat*) (produced). When it is derived from the root वृधु वृद्धौ (*vṛdhu vṛddhau*), it means that the cloud has grown to a very great measure. Thus, after discussing the meaning of the word वृत्र (*vṛtra*) through its formation, he has also quoted the Brāhmaṇa sentences in the respective places.

Sāyaṇa has given for the word वृत्रहणा (*vṛtrahaṇā*) the meaning "Indra and Agni, who remove sins". In his view the word वृत्र (*vṛtra*), derived from the root वृञ् (*vṛñ*), conveys the sense of covering knowledge.

सजित्वाना (*sajitvānā*)—those who conquer foes alike; that is, Agni too, like Indra, conquers the foe. अपराजिता (*aparājitā*)—these two are not defeated by anyone; and वाजसातमा (*vājasātamā*)—they are bestowers of abundant food. Therefore I invite these two to the sacrifice for the drinking of Soma: thus, it is described, the Ṛṣi, the seer of the mantra, has said.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

of Ṛk 4

- वृत्रहणा (*vṛtrahaṇā*)—वृत्रं हतवंतौ (*vṛtraṃ hatavaṃtau*), "the two who struck Vṛtra"; root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*). With the word वृत्र (*vṛtra*) as upapada, by ब्रह्मभ्रूणवृत्तेषु क्विप् (*brahmabhrūṇavṛtteṣu kvip*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-87; the supplied text has "ವೃತ್ತೇಷು", as supplied) the ending *kvip* in the past sense. Because a word of one vowel is the latter member, by एताजुत्तरपदेणः (*etājuttarapadeṇaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-9-12, as printed; the bhāṣya has 8-4-12) the change of the root's *n* is stated (the supplied text has "ಇತ್ವ", as supplied). By गतिकारको (*gatikārako*) (the sūtra name breaks off at the end of the page in the supplied text) … (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the base of the latter member with a kṛt-ending comes. By सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the dual ending is replaced by *ā*.

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 4):

- (End of the previous word, the sūtra continues:) —(पा. सू. ६-२-१३९) (*—(pā. sū. 6-2-139)*) as supplied (the sūtra name before the page break is broken off, see above).
- हुवे (*huve*)—root ह्वेण् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च (*hveṇ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*). By व्यत्यय (*vyatyaya*) it takes the ātmanepada (the supplied text has "ಆತ್ಮನೇಪದಿಯಾಗುತ್ತಬೆ", as supplied). In the present (*laṭ*) first-person singular the ending *iṭ*; for it, by टिशआत्म (*ṭiśaātma*) (as supplied, the sūtra is incomplete) *e* comes. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) the *luk* of the vikaraṇa. While ह्वः संप्रसारणम् (*hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam*) continues, by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) the root takes *saṃprasāraṇa*, with the earlier form (*pūrvarūpa*). By अचिश्नुधातुभ्रुवां (*aciśnudhātubhruvāṃ*) the substitution *uvaṅ* (the supplied text has "ಉವಡಾದೇಶ", as supplied). By तिज्जतिजः (*tijjatijaḥ*) the nighāta accent comes.
- सजित्वाना (*sajitvānā*)—root जि जये (*ji jaye*). By शीज् क्रुशिरुहिजिक्षिसृधृभ्य (*śīj kruśiruhijikṣisṛdhṛbhya*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-553, as printed; the bhāṣya has 4-113) the ending *kvanip*. Since it is *kit*, no guṇa for the *i* of the root; since it is *pit*, by ह्रस्वस्य पितिकृतितुक् (*hrasvasya pitikṛtituk*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-71) the augment *tuk*. By समानस्यछंदस्य (*samānasyachaṃdasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-84) *sa* replaces समान (*samāna*); the word *sajitvan*; *ā* in the dual; the accent of the base of the latter member with a kṛt-ending.
- आपराजिता (*āparājitā*) (the supplied spelling; the bhāṣya and Saṃhitā have अपराजिता (*aparājitā*))—न पराजितौ (*na parājitau*), a *nañ*-tatpuruṣa compound. By तत्पुरुषेतुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣetulyārtha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the accent of the first member. As before, *ā* in the dual.
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—इंद्रश्च अग्निश्च इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdraśca agniśca iṃdrāgnī*). By अजाद्यदंतम् (*ajādyadaṃtam*) the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) is placed first. When by देवताद्वंद्वेच (*devatādvaṃdveca*) the accent of both members is due, it is prohibited by नोत्तरपदेनुदात्तादौ (*nottarapadenudāttādau*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-142); so by समासस्य (*samāsasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223) the final-udātta accent comes.
- वाजसातामू (*vājasātāmū*) (the supplied spelling; the Saṃhitā has वाजसातमा (*vājasātamā*))—root षणु दाने (*ṣaṇu dāne*). By जनसनखनक्रम (*janasanakhanakrama*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-67) the ending *viṭ*. When it follows, by विद्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् (*vidvanoranunāsikasyāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-41) *ā* replaces the *n* of the root. After it, to show excess, by अतिशायने तमप् (*atiśāyane tamap*) the ending *tamap*; since it is *pit* it is anudātta, so the accent of the root remains. In the compound, the first member being a kāraka, the accent of the base of the latter member with a kṛt-ending comes. By सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the case ending is replaced by *ā*.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the priests who possess the *ukta* (the recitation, *śastra*) worship you with praises, and the singers skilled in the Sāmans do likewise; I too choose you both for the gain of food. The rest is grammar of the words वां (*vāṃ*), अर्चंति (*arcaṃti*), उक्किनः (*ukkinaḥ*), नीथाविदः (*nīthāvidaḥ*), इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*), वृणे (*vṛṇe*) (as supplied; the supplied text has several slips in this bhāṣya, e.g. "ಉಕ್ಕಂ", "ನೀಥ್ಯವಿದಃ" in the Pada, kept as supplied).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni. उक्किनः (*ukkinaḥ*)—the priests, such as the Hotṛ, who know the *śastra* mantras. वां (*vāṃ*)—you two. प्र अर्चंति (*pra arcaṃti*)—(with words of praise) worship specially; (in the same way) नीथाविदः (*nīthāvidaḥ*)—those who know the hymns (skilled in the singing of Sāmans), जरितारः (*jaritāraḥ*)—the singers of praise (the Udgātṛ and others), वां अर्चंति (*vāṃ arcaṃti*)—worship you two with praises. (अहं अपि (*ahaṃ api*)—I also.) इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—of food (for the gain of). आ वृणे (*ā vṛṇe*)—I take refuge (in Indra and Agni).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, the priests such as the Hotṛ who know the *śastra* mantras, and the Udgātṛ and others who are skilled in the singing of Sāmans, worship you both with words of praise; I too take refuge in you alone for the gain of food.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The reciters of prayers, the repeaters of praise, who are skilled in sacred song, worship you both : I have recourse to Indra and Agni for food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उक्तिनः (*uktinaḥ*)—the bhāṣya says उक्तं शस्त्रं तद्वंतः शस्त्रिणो होत्रादयः । (*uktaṃ śastraṃ tadvaṃtaḥ śastriṇo hotrādayaḥ |*) उक्तं शस्त्रं येषां ते ! (*uktaṃ śastraṃ yeṣāṃ te !*) (the "!" as supplied). The word *ukta* is explained as *śastra*. Works such as the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa say that the meaning of the word *śastra* is a praise describing the qualities or glory of the respective deities, and explain that the words *ukta* and *śastra* are synonyms in Vedic usage. Here Sāyaṇa explains the sense as the priests, the Hotṛ and others, who know the praises describing the qualities of the respective deities; and for वां प्र आर्चंति (*vāṃ pra ārcaṃti*) (printed with a line-end hyphen, "ಆ-ರ್ಚಂತಿ") he explains the Indra and Agni are worshipped स्तुतिरूपाभिर्वाग्गिः पूजयंति (*stutirūpābhirvāggiḥ pūjayaṃti*) (the supplied text has "ವಾಗ್ಗಿಃ", the bhāṣya "ವಾಗ್ಭಿಃ"; as supplied), that is, they worship with words in the form of praise.

नीथाविदः (*nīthāvidaḥ*) (printed "ನೀಥಾವಿದು:", as supplied)—सामगानकुशलाः स्तोत्राभिज्ञाः (*sāmagānakuśalāḥ stotrābhijñāḥ*). He explains that the word *nīthā* denotes a variety of Sāmans in the Sāmaveda, and the meaning that they are skilled in singing Sāmans and, through singing Sāmans, are wise in praising the respective deities.

जरितारः (*jaritāraḥ*)—the word *jaritā* is explained as *garitā* (Ni. 1-7). Although the general meaning of this word is "praisers", he explains it as the priests, the Udgātṛ and others, who recite praise with the Sāmaveda, and says that to obtain their several desired ends they praise and worship Indra and Agni by Sāman-singing. (The supplied text has "ಉದ್ಧಾತೃ" for the Udgātṛ and "ಆರ್ಥವಾದರೂ", as supplied.)

अहमपि इषः आ वृणे (*ahamapi iṣaḥ ā vṛṇe*)—अन्नस्य लाभार्थं इंद्राग्नी सर्वतः संभजे । (*annasya lābhārthaṃ iṃdrāgnī sarvataḥ saṃbhaje |*) The word इषम् (*iṣam*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). In the Ṛk

यवं वृकेणाश्विना वरंतेषं दुहंता मनुषाय दस्रा । (*yavaṃ vṛkeṇāśvinā varaṃteṣaṃ duhaṃtā manuṣāya dasrā |*)
अभि दस्युं बकुरेणा धमंतोरु ज्योतिश्चक्रतुरार्याय । (*abhi dasyuṃ bakureṇā dhamaṃtoru jyotiścakraturāryāya |*)

(printed "ಪು. ಸಂ. ೧-೧೧೭-೨೧", i.e. Pu. Saṃ. 1-117-21, as supplied; the verse is quoted as supplied), the words इषं दुहंता (*iṣaṃ duhaṃtā*) are explained as अन्नं दुहंत् (*annaṃ duhaṃt*) , "those who give food". The seer of the mantra declares: "I serve Indra and Agni in order to obtain food." This is the sense explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- वाम् (*vām*)—the word युष्मद् (*yuṣmad*). Because it stands after a word, by युष्मदस्मदोः षष्ठीचतुर्थिद्विती (*yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthidvitī*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-20; the sūtra name is cut off in the print, as supplied) the substitute वाम् (*vām*) for the accusative form; it is anudātta.

### Printed p. 217

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 5):

- अर्चंति (*arcaṃti*)—root अर्च पूजायां (*arca pūjāyāṃ*); *laṭ* third person plural. By तिज्जतिजः (*tijjatijaḥ*) (as supplied; the sūtra name is broken) the *nighāta* accent comes.
- उक्तिनः (*uktinaḥ*)—root वच परिभाषणे (*vaca paribhāṣaṇe*). By पात्यतुदिवचिरिंचि (*pātyatudivaciriṃci*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-164) the ending *thak* in the passive sense; being *kit*, by वचिस्वपियजादीनांकिति (*vacisvapiyajādīnāṃkiti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-15) *saṃprasāraṇa* of the root, with the earlier form (*pūrvarūpa*). By चोःकुः (*coḥkuḥ*) the final *c* of the root becomes *k*. *Ukta* means *śastra* (a special mantra); when the sense "possessing it" is intended, by अतइनितनौ (*atainitanau*) (Pā. Sū. 5-2-115) the ending *ini*; by यस्यॆतिच (*yasyètica*) the elision of the preceding *a*; the accent of the ending (the supplied text has "ಆದ್ಯುದಾತ್ಮಸ್ವರ", as supplied) comes.
- नीथाविदः (*nīthāvidaḥ*)—root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*). By हनिकुषिनीरमि (*hanikuṣinīrami*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-159) the ending *kvin*; being *kit*, no guṇa for the *i* of the root; the form is *nītha*. विदः (*vidaḥ*)—root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*); by क्विप्‌च (*kvipca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2.76) the ending *kvip*. नीथं विदंति इति नीथाविदः (*nīthaṃ vidaṃti iti nīthāvidaḥ*); by अन्येषामपिदृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapidṛśyate*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137) lengthening of the earlier member in the Saṃhitā.
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—vocative dual. Being at the beginning of a pāda, the *nighāta* accent does not come; by आमंत्रितस्य (*āmaṃtritasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) the initial-udātta accent comes.
- वृणे (*vṛṇe*)—root वृज् संभक्तौ (*vṛj saṃbhaktau*), *kryādi* class. Explained in the previous mantra. By तिज्जतिजः (*tijjatijaḥ*) the *nighāta* accent comes.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The cities of the enemies were shaken by you two together, with one single effort, at one moment; I invoke you, Indra and Agni. The rest of the bhāṣya is grammar of the words नवतिं (*navatiṃ*), दासपत्नीः (*dāsapatnīḥ*), अधूनुतं (*adhūnutaṃ*), एकेन (*ekena*) (the supplied text has several slips in it, e.g. "ಜಿಹ್", "ಕೆನ್", kept as supplied).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(ಹೇ) इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni. दासपत्नीः (*dāsapatnīḥ*)—under the control of the (to us) harmful ones. नवतिं (*navatiṃ*)—ninety. पुरः (*puraḥ*)—enemy cities. एकेन कर्मणा (*ekena karmaṇā*)—(you two) with one single effort. साकं (*sākaṃ*)—at one time. आधूनुतं (*ādhūnutaṃ*) (printed so, with long ā, as supplied)—you caused to tremble (destroyed). ("ಅಂತರ ನಿಮ್ಮಿಬ್ಬರನ್ನೂ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ" [sic, as supplied]: "I praise you both.")

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, you destroyed ninety "ಪಡ್ವಣ" (sic, as supplied; presumably "cities") of the enemies at one time, with one single effort; such as you I invoke.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra and Agni, with one united effort you overthrew ninety cities ruled over by (your) foes.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दासपत्निः (*dāsapatniḥ*)—दासयंति उपक्षपयंति इति दासाः । उपक्षपयितारः शत्रवः ते पालकाः यासां ता दासपत्निः । (*dāsayaṃti upakṣapayaṃti iti dāsāḥ | upakṣapayitāraḥ śatravaḥ te pālakāḥ yāsāṃ tā dāsapatniḥ |*) The word दास (*dāsa*), formed from the root दसु (*dasu*) which denotes "destroy", is used in the sense "enemy". It is explained as: cities which have these enemies as their protectors. The Nirukta-writer has explained the word दासपत्निः (*dāsapatniḥ*) thus: दासपत्निः दासाधिपत्नः । दासो दस्यतेरुपदासयति कर्माणि । (*dāsapatniḥ dāsādhipatnaḥ | dāso dasyaterupadāsayati karmāṇi |*) (Ni. 2-18). Durgācārya says: दासः कर्मकरः तं हि ताः अधिष्ठाय पांति रक्षंति । स हि कर्मणा श्रांतः तासु पीतासु विश्रांत आप्यायितो भवंति । (*dāsaḥ karmakaraḥ taṃ hi tāḥ adhiṣṭhāya pāṃti rakṣaṃti | sa hi karmaṇā śrāṃtaḥ tāsu pītāsu viśrāṃta āpyāyito bhavaṃti |*) (the verb भवंति (*bhavaṃti*) in the plural after स (*sa*) singular, as supplied). That is: the one who does the work is the दास (*dāsa*), and when he is tired the waters remove his weariness and make him live happily; so the waters are दासपत्नि (*dāsapatni*) — this is one kind of meaning given of the word (the Kannada says "ಅರ್ಥವೆಂಬ ಒಂದು ವಿಧವಾದ ಅರ್ಥ", as supplied). See the explanation of the word दासपत्निः (*dāsapatniḥ*) in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-11 (see page 629, Part II, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā).

### Printed p. 219

Special Topics, continued: On the historical view, when war is being waged, the root दसु (*dasu*) denotes destruction, so the enemy who destroys the "ಕೃಷ್ಣಾದಿಕಮಗಳು" [sic, as supplied] is meant by the word दास (*dāsa*); the one who protects him is दासपत्नि (*dāsapatni*); so the meaning is described. Since a wife is always a nourisher, the enemies, who nourish their दास (*dāsa*) like a wife, get the name दासपत्न्यः (*dāsapatnyaḥ*) (printed "ದಾಸಪತ್ನ್ಯ:", as supplied); or, because they guard their dwelling (the city, their place of residence) as one nourishes a wife, their cities are called "ದಾಸಪತ್ನಿಯರು" .

नवतिं पुरः एकेन कर्मणा साकमधूनुतं (*navatiṃ puraḥ ekena karmaṇā sākamadhūnutaṃ*)—नवतिसंख्याकाः शत्रुणां पुरीः एकेनैवोद्योगेन युगपत् अकम्वयतं । (*navatisaṃkhyākāḥ śatruṇāṃ purīḥ ekenaivodyogena yugapat akamvayataṃ |*) (the supplied text has "ಶತ್ರುಣಾಂ" and "ಅಕಮ್ವಯತಂ", kept as supplied). The word नवति (*navati*): नवानां दशशां नवभावः (*navānāṃ daśaśāṃ navabhāvaḥ*) — nines repeated ten times become ninety. Having said that Indra and Agni destroyed at one time, with one single effort, the ninety cities protected by the enemies, the sense is explained that these two, filled with such greatness, are invited to the sacrifice for the drinking of Soma (the Kannada has "ಮಾಹಿತ್ರ್ಯ", as supplied, for presumably "greatness"; "ಆಹ್ವಾನ ಮಾಡಿದೆ", "I invoked").

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- नवतिम् (*navatim*)—नवानां दशतां नवभावः (*navānāṃ daśatāṃ navabhāvaḥ*): the ending ति (*ti*) (nine, ten); by the ending's accent it is *antodātta*. Accusative singular form.
- दासपत्नीः (*dāsapatnīḥ*)—root दसु उपक्षये (*dasu upakṣaye*); दासयतीति दासः (*dāsayatīti dāsaḥ*). After the *ṇijanta*, by नंदिग्रहपचा (*naṃdigrahapacā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134) the ending *ac* in the agent sense; by अतउपधायाः (*ataupadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) *vṛddhi* of the penultimate of the root; since the ending has *c* as marker, the *antodātta* accent comes. दासाः पतयः यासां दासपत्न्यः (*dāsāḥ patayaḥ yāsāṃ dāsapatnyaḥ*): since नित्यंसपत्न्यादिषु दासाज्ञ (*nityaṃsapatnyādiṣu dāsājña*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-35 ಗ — as supplied, "ಗ" after the number) is read, by विभाषा सपूर्वस्य (*vibhāṣā sapūrvasya*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-34) the ending *ṅīp*, printed "ಜೀಪ್" ; *nakāra* substituted for the *ikāra* ; in the *bahuvrīhi* the accent of the first member comes. Accusative plural form.
- अधूनुतम् (*adhūnutam*)—root धूञ् कंपने (*dhūñ kaṃpane*); *laṭ* (printed "ಲಜ್", as supplied) second person dual, by तस्‌थस्-भमिपां (*tasthas-bhamipāṃ*) (the line breaks after "ತಸ್‌ಥಸ್-" in the print) the substitute तम् (*tam*); by स्वादिभ्यःत्नुः (*svādibhyaḥtnuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-73) the *śnu* conjugational sign. Because it is treated as *ñit* (printed "ಜಿತ್ವಾತಿದೇಶ", as supplied), no guṇa of the *ikāra* of the root; no guṇa of the *u* of the sign either. The augment *aṭ* (printed "ಅಡಾಗಮ") to the base. By तिज्ञतिजः (*tijñatijaḥ*) the *nighāta* accent comes.
- एकेन (*ekena*)—root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) ; by इण्‌भीकापातल्यतिमर्जिभ्यः कन् (*iṇbhīkāpātalyatimarjibhyaḥ kan*) (Uṇ. Sū. 3-3-25) the ending *kan*. By सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) guṇa of the root. As the ending has *n* as marker, the *ādyudātta* accent comes (printed "ಅದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತಸ್ವರ", as supplied). Instrumental singular ("ಕೃತೀಯಾ" printed, as supplied).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the *dhītayaḥ* — the Hotṛ and the other priests who hold (guard) the Soma — go about close around our rite with their eyes on the paths of the fruit of rite; so come for the drinking of Soma. Or: the *dhītayaḥ* are the praises, which go around the rite following the paths of the sacrifice; so come, as praiseworthy ones. The rest is grammar of the words यंति (*yaṃti*) and धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(ಹೇ) इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni. धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—the Hotṛ and other priests who hold (or guard) the Soma. ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the fruit of the rite. पथ्याः (*pathyāḥ*)—the paths. अनु (*anu*)—keeping in view. अपसः (*apasaḥ*)—(of the rite done by us). परि (*pari*)—around. उप प्र यंति (*upa pra yaṃti*)—are near (hence come, both of you, for the drinking of Soma). Or: धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—the praises. ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice. पथ्याः अनु (*pathyāḥ anu*)—following the paths. अपसः परि (*apasaḥ pari*)—around this rite of ours. उप प्र यंति (*upa pra yaṃti*)—are near; (hence, being praiseworthy, come both of you here).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, the Hotṛ and other priests who hold (have kept guarded) the Soma for you, keeping the attainment of the fruit of rite as their aim, are engaged in this rite of ours; (therefore come to drink the Soma juice that is to be given by them).

### Printed p. 221

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra and Agni the pious ministers, are present at our holy rite, according to the ways of worship.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—सोमस्य पातारः होत्रादयः । (*somasya pātāraḥ hotrādayaḥ |*) The word धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*) is formed from the root धेट् (*dheṭ*), which conveys the sense "to drink"; since it means "those who drink", the meaning is described here as the Ṛtvijs, Hotṛ and the others, who drink the Soma juice. Yāska has explained the meanings of the words धीति: (*dhīti:*) and दीतयः (*dītayaḥ*) , giving examples.

The word धीशयः (*dhīśayaḥ*) is stated among the twenty-two names of the fingers beginning with आग्रुवः (*āgruvaḥ*) and अण्वः (*aṇvaḥ*) (Ni. 3-9).

इयं कुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः । (*iyaṃ kuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ |*)
पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥ (*pārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-61-2)
Here the meaning "rite" or "praise" is explained for the word धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*).

यतस्य हि शुरुधस्संति पूर्विर्यतस्य धीतिर्वृजिनानि हंति । (*yatasya hi śurudhassaṃti pūrviryatasya dhītirvṛjināni haṃti |*)
यतस्य श्लोको बधिरा ततर्द कर्णा बुधानः शुचमान आयोः ॥ (*yatasya śloko badhirā tatarda karṇā budhānaḥ śucamāna āyoḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-23-8, printed "ಮ ಸಂ. ೪-೨೩-೮" [sic], as supplied)
Here the meaning "wisdom" (प्रज्ञा (*prajñā*)) is described for the word धीति (*dhīti*). The purport is that, in the view of the Nirukta-writers, the meaning of the word दीति (*dīti*) , formed from the root धै चिंतायां (*dhai ciṃtāyāṃ*) ("to think"), has been explained.

अपसः (*apasaḥ*)—this word is stated among the names of "work" (Ni. 3-2). Sāyaṇa gave the word ऋत (*ṛta*), which means "truth" or "sacrifice", the meaning "fruit of the rite"; for अपसः (*apasaḥ*) he gave the meaning that the Hotṛ and the other Ṛtvijs, who drink the Soma in the sacrifice that is performed keeping in view the way by which the fruit of the rite comes (directly) without hindrance, are engaged in the work of the sacrifice. This is one kind of meaning. And since Yāska has explained the word धीति (*dhīti*) as conveying "praise", the second meaning is given, with the commentary यद्वा धीतयः स्तुतयः ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य मार्गान् लक्षीकृत्य कर्मणः परितः प्रवर्तंते । (*yadvā dhītayaḥ stutayaḥ ṛtasya yajñasya mārgān lakṣīkṛtya karmaṇaḥ paritaḥ pravartaṃte |*): the praises recited by the Ṛtvijs, addressed to the gods, keep in view the ways of the sacrifice and bring about activity in the sacrificial work itself.

Since the Ṛtvijs, the Hotṛ and others, praise Indra and Agni and invite them to come for the drinking of Soma, it is prayed that Indra and Agni should come to the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 222

Special Topics, continued: पथ्या—पथः मार्गान् (*pathyā—pathaḥ mārgān*)—"paths, ways": the meaning is explained thus. पथ्या स्वस्ति:— (*pathyā svasti:—*) : पंथा अंतरिक्षं तन्निवासात् (*paṃthā aṃtarikṣaṃ tannivāsāt*) (Ni. 11-45): पंथा (*paṃthā*) means the atmosphere (अंतरिक्ष (*aṃtarikṣa*)), and since one dwells in it, the word पथ्या (*pathyā*) is given the meaning "way".

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- यंति (*yaṃti*)—root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), of the अदादि (*adādi*) class. *Laṭ*, third person plural, with the substitute अंत (*aṃta*) (*ant*). *Luk* for the *śap*. By इणोयण् (*iṇoyaṇ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-81) the *yaṇ* substitution. The *tiṅanta* *nighāta* accent comes.
- धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—root धेट् पाने (*dheṭ pāne*). After it, in the agent sense, by क्तिच्क्तौचसंज्ञायाम् (*kticktaucasaṃjñāyām*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-174) the ending *ktic*. As the ending has *k* as marker, when it follows, by घुमास्थागा— (*ghumāsthāgā—*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66) the root takes *ī*. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-1993 [sic, as supplied]) the *antodātta* accent comes. Nominative plural form.
- पथ्याः (*pathyāḥ*)—the word पथिन् (*pathin*); the ending *yat*; टिलोप (*ṭilopa*) (loss of the *ṭi*, as supplied). Since the ending has *t* as marker, by तित्‌स्वरितम् (*titsvaritam*) the *svarita* accent comes.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी तवि॒षाणि॑ वां स॒धस्था॑नि॒ प्रयां॑सि च ।  
> युवोरपूर्यं हितं ॥ ८ ॥

> *iṃdrāgnī taviṣāṇi vāṃ sadhasthāni prayāṃsi ca |*  
> *yuvorapūryaṃ hitaṃ ‖ 8 ‖*

*(In the Pada the supplied text reads "ಅಪ್ಸತೂರ್ಯಂ" where the Saṃhitā has "ಅಪೂರ್ಯಂ"; also "ಚೆ" for "ಚ"; kept as supplied.)*

> इंद्राग्नी इति । तविषाणि । वां । सधस्थानि । प्रयांसि । चॆ ।  
> युवोः । अप्सतूर्यं । हितं ॥ ८ ॥

> *iṃdrāgnī iti | taviṣāṇi | vāṃ | sadhasthāni | prayāṃsi | cè |*  
> *yuvoḥ | apsatūryaṃ | hitaṃ ‖ 8 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी वां युवयोस्तविषाणि बलानि प्रयांस्यन्नानि च सधस्थानि
> परस्परमवियुज्य वर्तंते! तथापूर्यं वृष्टि द्वारा प्रेरकत्वं युवोर्युवयो-
> रेव हितं निहितं वर्तते । तस्मात्सोमपानप्रभृतिषु सर्वकर्मस्विंद्राग्योः सहैव
> वर्तमानत्वमिति भावः ॥ वां । षष्ठीद्विवचने वामित्यादेशः । सधस्थानि । ष्ठा गतिनि-
> वृत् । आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः ! सध मादस्थयोश्चंदसीति सहस्य सधादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, in you two strengths and foods dwell together, never separated; likewise the power of sending rain is placed in you two alone; hence in all rites, beginning with Soma-drinking, Indra and Agni are present together. The rest is grammar of the words वां (*vāṃ*) and सधस्थानि (*sadhasthāni*).

### Printed p. 223

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(ಹೇ) इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni. वां (*vāṃ*)—in you two. तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*)—strengths. प्रयांसि (*prayāṃsi*) (च (*ca*))—and foods. सदस्यानि (*sadasyāni*) (printed so, differing from सधस्थानि (*sadhasthāni*) of the Saṃhitā, as supplied)—are unseparated (अवियुक्त (*aviyukta*)); (likewise) अपूर्यं (*apūryaṃ*)—the power of sending rain युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—in you two alone हितं (*hitaṃ*)—is placed. (Therefore, for Soma-drinking and the like, come both of you together. [The parenthesis is not closed in the print, as supplied.])

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, strength and food are in you two unseparated (existing together), and the power of sending rain is also in you alone; therefore do you two come together to our sacrifice and drink the Soma.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra and Agni, in you, vigour and food are abiding together, and therefore in you is deposited the dispensing of water.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तविषाणि—बलानि. (*taviṣāṇi—balāni.*) The word तविषी (*taviṣī*) is stated among the names of "strength" (Ni. 3-9), and:

पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् । (*pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīm |*)
यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् । (*yasya trito vyojasā vṛtraṃ viparvamardayat |*)
(printed "ಪು. ಸಂ. ೧-೧೮೭-೧" [sic, पु (*pu*) for ऋ (*ṛ*)], as supplied: Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-187-1)

Here: तविषीति बलनाम तवतेर्वा वृद्धिकर्मणः (*taviṣīti balanāma tavatervā vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 9-25): Yāska has given the word तविस् (*tavis*), formed from the root तु (*tu*) (printed "ತು ಧಾತಾವಿನಿಂದ", as supplied), which conveys "growth", the meaning "strength" and "that which makes grow".

The word प्रयस् (*prayas*) is stated among the names of "food" (Ni. 3-9). Since it is said that Indra and Agni both obtain strength and food together, mutually, the meaning is explained that the mutual state of the two is one of non-separation.

For the word अपूर्यं (*apūryaṃ*) the meaning is explained that Indra and Agni alone are those who show favour so that rain occurs and who urge the world towards growth. Having explained thus, with सोमपानप्रकृतिषु सर्वकर्मसु इंद्राग्न्योः सहैव वर्तमानत्वं (*somapānaprakṛtiṣu sarvakarmasu iṃdrāgnyoḥ sahaiva vartamānatvaṃ*) (the supplied text has प्रकृतिषु (*prakṛtiṣu*) where the bhāṣya has प्रभृतिषु (*prabhṛtiṣu*); as supplied), it is wished that, since Indra and Agni are together in granting strength and food, in Soma-drinking, and in urging the world to growth by producing rain, the two should come together to the sacrifice for the drinking of Soma. On the companionship of Indra and Agni see Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Part 8, pages 575 to 576.

### Printed p. 224

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- तविषाणि (*taviṣāṇi*)—तव (*tava*) is a *sautra* root. By तवेणिद्वा (*taveṇidvā*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-48) the ending *ṭiṣac*. By चुटू (*cuṭū*) the initial *ṭ* gets the *it* designation and is dropped. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the *antodātta* accent comes.
- वाम् (*vām*)—the word युष्मद् (*yuṣmad*); for the genitive dual, by युष्मदत्मदोः— (*yuṣmadatmadoḥ—*) the substitute वाम् (*vām*); it becomes unaccented.
- सधस्थानि (*sadhasthāni*)—root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*). By आतोनुपसर्गेकः (*ātonupasargekaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-3) the ending *ka*. As it has *k* as marker, when it follows, by आतोलोपइटच (*ātolopaiṭaca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64) the *ā* is dropped. When स्थ (*stha*) follows, by सधमादस्थयोश्चंदसि (*sadhamādasthayoścaṃdasi*) the substitute सध (*sadha*) for सह (*saha*). The accent of the first member comes.
- हितम् (*hitam*)—root डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). The ending *kta* in the passive. By दधातेर्हि: (*dadhāterhi:*) the root takes the substitute हि (*hi*). By the accent of the ending it becomes *antodātta*.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, you, the illuminators of heaven, are adorned all around in battles, that is, you remain victorious everywhere having defeated the enemies; your valour makes known such victory in battle. Or: you overcome the enemies in battles. The rest, as before; the grammar of रोचना (*rocanā*) begins at the end of this window and continues on the next page.

### Printed p. 226

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 9.)* वाजेषु परि भूषथः (*vājeṣu pari bhūṣathaḥ*)—The word वाज (*vāja*) is stated among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Although this word has many meanings, it is said that here it is used in the sense of battle, war; and by युवां परितः सर्वतः अलंकृतौ भवथः, शत्रुन् पराजित्य सर्वतो विजयमान् वर्तेथे । (*yuvāṃ paritaḥ sarvataḥ alaṃkṛtau bhavathaḥ, śatrun parājitya sarvato vijayamān vartethe |*) it is described that Indra and Agni, addressed, are adorned in battles and, having conquered the enemies, are victorious in every way. And further: यद्वा युवां वाजेषु संग्रामेषु शत्रुर् परि भूषथः परिभवथः (*yadvā yuvāṃ vājeṣu saṃgrāmeṣu śatrur pari bhūṣathaḥ paribhavathaḥ*) —or it is said that they always overcome the enemies.

By the sentence वां वीर्यं तत् प्र चेति (*vāṃ vīryaṃ tat pra ceti*) it is described that the prowess of you two makes known to all the victory in battle that you have achieved in that manner, and the greatness of the weighty prowess of Indra and Agni is set out.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- रोचना (*rocanā*): root रुच दीप्तौ (*ruca dīptau*). Since it is an *anudāttet* root, by अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः (*anudāttetaśca halādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-149) the affix *yuc* in the agent sense; by युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the substitute *ana* for it. By पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) *guṇa* for the light penultimate vowel of the root. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the *antodātta* accent comes. By सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the case ending gets the substitute printed "ಆಕಾರಾದೇತ" .
- दिवः (*divaḥ*): by ऊडिदं पदादि (*ūḍidaṃ padādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the *udātta* accent comes to the case ending.
- भूषथः (*bhūṣathaḥ*): root printed भूष अलंकारे (*bhūṣa alaṃkāre*) *(the bhāṣya has भूष भूषणे (*bhūṣa bhūṣaṇe*); as supplied)*. *Laṭ*, second person dual form; it has the designation *tiṅ*. By the rule printed तिणिः (*tiṇiḥ*) the *tiṅanta* *nighāta* accent comes.
- चेति (*ceti*): root चिती संज्ञाने (*citī saṃjñāne*). Since it shows the sense of urging, it is a root with the causative sense included. *Laṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; by बहुलंघंदॆसि (*bahulaṃghaṃdèsi*) *luk* for *śap*. On account of *tip*, by पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) *guṇa* for the light penultimate vowel of the root. By Vedic usage there is elision of the *t* of the root *(as supplied: "ಧಾತು ತಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಲೋಪ")*. Because it stands in a verse that has an *atiṅanta* , the *nighāta* accent comes.
- वीर्यम् (*vīryam*): when the affix *yat* comes after the word वीर (*vīra*), by यस्येतिज (*yasyetija*) the preceding *a* is elided. By यतोनावः (*yatonāvaḥ*) the initial-*udātta* accent does not come to it. By तित्स्वरितम् (*titsvaritam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185) the *svarita* accent comes to the affix.

## Sūkta 13 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The thirteenth sūkta** (ಹದಿಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वितीयेऽनुवाके सप्तदश सूक्तानि । तत्र प्र वो देवायेति सप्तर्चमाद्यं
> सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रयषभस्यार्षमग्नि देवताकमानुष्टुभं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । प्र वः
> सप्त ऋषभस्त्वानुष्टुभमिति । विश्वामित्रपुत्र ऋषभ ऋषिः । मंडलादिपरिभाषयाग्नि-
> र्देवता ॥ अग्निष्टोम इदं सूक्तमाज्यशस्त्रं । पराजिध्वर्यावावृत्त इति खंडे
> सूत्रितं । प्र वो देवायेत्याज्यमुपसंतनुयात् । आ.५-९ । इति ॥ इदमेव सूक्तं
> प्रातरनुवाक आश्विनशस्त्रे च विनियुक्तं । सूत्रं च । प्र वो देवायाग्ने कदा त इति
> पंच । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥ अभ्युदयेष्टौ स यंतेत्यग्ने प्रदातुर्याज्या । सूत्रितं
> च । स यंता विप्र एषां दीर्घस्ते अस्त्वंकुशः । आ. ३-१३ । इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta (the first of the second anuvāka) begins the second anuvāka of the third maṇḍala. In this anuvāka there are seventeen sūktas; of these the sūkta beginning प्र वो देवाय (*pra vo devāya*) is the first. It has seven ṛks. Ṛṣabha, the son of Viśvāmitra, is the Ṛṣi of this sūkta; Agni is the deity; Anuṣṭubh is the metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said प्र वः सप्त ऋषभस्तानुष्टुभं (*pra vaḥ sapta ṛṣabhastānuṣṭubhaṃ*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has ऋषभस्त्वानुष्टुभमिति (*ṛṣabhastvānuṣṭubhamiti*))*. In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice this sūkta is to be recited as the Ājya-śastra mantra, as set out by the sūtra प्र वो देवायेत्याज्यमुपसंतनुयात् (*pra vo devāyetyājyamupasaṃtanuyāt*) in the section called पराजिध्वर्यावावृत्त (*parājidhvaryāvāvṛtta*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 5-9); and this sūkta is applied to the Aśvina-śastra mantras at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, as set out by the sūtra प्र वो देवयाग्ने कदा त इति पंच (*pra vo devayāgne kadā ta iti paṃca*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has प्र वो देवायाग्ने कदा त इति पंच (*pra vo devāyāgne kadā ta iti paṃca*))* of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 4-13); and in the Abhyudayeṣṭi the third ṛk of this sūkta, beginning स यंता विप्र एषां (*sa yaṃtā vipra eṣāṃ*), is to be recited as the Agni-related yājyā mantra, as set out by the sūtra स यंता विप्र एषां दीर्घस्ते अस्त्वंकुतः (*sa yaṃtā vipra eṣāṃ dīrghaste astvaṃkutaḥ*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has अंकुशः (*aṃkuśaḥ*) at the end)* of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 3-13).
