#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वो॑ दे॒वाया॒ग्नये॒ बर्हि॑ष्ठमर्चास्मै ।  
> गम॑द्दे॒वेभि॒रा स नो॒ यजि॑ष्ठो ब॒र्हिरा स॑दत् ॥ १ ॥

> *pra vo devāyāgnaye barhiṣṭhamarcāsmai |*  
> *gamaddevebhirā sa no yajiṣṭho barhirā sadat ‖ 1 ‖*

*[In the Pada the supplied text has "ಆ ' ಸಃ" where a danda would be expected after ಆ; as supplied. The Saṃhitā has देवेभिरा स नो (*devebhirā sa no*).]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वः । देवाय । अग्नये । बर्हिष्ठं । अर्च । अस्मै ।  
> गमत् । देवेभिः । आ ' सः । नः । यजिष्ठः । बर्हिः । आ । सदत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यजमानो होत्रादीन्प्रति ब्रूते । हे होत्रादयो वो युष्मत्संबं-
> धिने देवाय द्योतमानायास्मै अस्मिन् कर्मणि स्तुत्यायाग्नये बर्हिष्ठं पृथ-
> तमं प्रभूतमिदं स्तुतिरूपं स्तोत्रशस्त्रादि वोक्ष्यजातं प्रार्थ । उच्चारयत ।
> एवं स्तुतः सोग्निर्देवेभिर्यष्टव्यदेवैः सहितः सन् नोऽस्मान् प्रति आगमत् ।
> आगच्छतु । आगत्य च यजिष्ठो यष्टृतमः सोग्निर्बर्हिरस्माभिर्वेद्यां स्तीर्णे
> बर्हिष्यासदत् । आसीदतु । उपविशतु ॥ बर्हिष्ठं । बर्हितृशब्दात्तुत्पंडसीत्यतिशायन
> इष्यन् । अर्च । अर्च पूजायां । भौवादिकः । बहुवचनस्यैकवणनं । निघातः ।
> गमत् । गमल्प गत् । अस्य छंदसि बुज् लप्लिट इति लोडर्थे लुज् । ल्यदित्वात्
> क्षेरज् । नित्यं जित इतीकारलोपः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । यजिष्ठः । यष्टृ-
> शब्दात्तुत्पंडसीतीष्ठन् । तुरिष्ठेमेयःस्थिति तृचो लोपः नित् स्वरः । सदत् ।
> पूर्ववल्लोडर्थे लुज् । षड्ल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेष्टित्यस्य ल्यदित्वादज् । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer tells the Hotṛ and the other priests to chant abundant praise to the shining Agni, and prays that Agni, praised, may come to us with the gods and sit on the strewn sacred grass. The rest is grammar: बर्हिष्ठं (*barhiṣṭhaṃ*), अर्च (*arca*), गमत् (*gamat*), यजिष्ठः (*yajiṣṭhaḥ*), सदत् (*sadat*) (transcribed, not explained). *(The bhāṣya has "बहुवचनस्यैकवणनं" with the printed "ಏಕವಣನಂ" and "ज्" for "ल्" in several roots, as supplied.)*

### Printed p. 229

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे होत्रादयः (*he hotrādayaḥ*)—O Hotṛ and other priests.) वः (*vaḥ*)—belonging to you
- देवाय (*devāya*)—the shining
- आस्मै (*āsmai*) *(as supplied; the Pada has अस्मै (*asmai*))*—to this (who is to be praised in this rite)
- अग्नये (*agnaye*)—for Agni
- बर्हिष्ठं (*barhiṣṭhaṃ*)—the most excellent praises, the stotras, śastras and so on; प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—chant abundantly. सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni (praised by you)
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—with the gods to whom the offering is to be made
- नः (*naḥ*)—towards us; आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—may he come; (having come) यजिष्ठः (*yajiṣṭhaḥ*)—Agni, the best among those to be worshipped (by us)
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—on the seat of sacred grass (spread on the altar); आ सदत् (*ā sadat*)—may he sit down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Hotṛ and the other priests, chant excellent praises, stotras, śastras and the like, towards that Agni, mass of radiance, who is yours; may that Agni, praised by you and most worthy of worship, come to our sacrificial hall with the other gods to whom the offering is to be made *(the print has "ಯಷ್ಟವ್ಯರಾಡ ಇತರ ದೇವತೆಗಳೊಡನೆ"; the word ಯಷ್ಟವ್ಯರಾಡ is as supplied)*, and sit on the seat of sacred grass spread on the altar. (May he be seated.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Priests) utter devout (praises) to this your divine Agni, that so glorî-fied [sic, as supplied] he may come to us with the gods, and sit down on the sacrificial grass.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

देवाय-द्योतमानाय (*devāya-dyotamānāya*). The authors of the Nirukta, saying देवो दानाद्वा दीपनाद्वा (*devo dānādvā dīpanādvā*) द्योतनाद्वा द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा (*dyotanādvā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā*) *(the line breaks after द्योत- (*dyota-*) in the print)*, have explained that Agni is denoted by the word *deva* because he fulfils the desired ends of the sacrificers, or because he shines with his abundant glory, or because he has made his dwelling in the atmosphere or in heaven. Here the sense "shining" is set out.

अस्मै बर्हिष्ठं प्र अर्च (*asmai barhiṣṭhaṃ pra arca*)—अस्मिन् कर्मणि स्तुत्याय वृद्धतमं प्रभूतमिदं (*asmin karmaṇi stutyāya vṛddhatamaṃ prabhūtamidaṃ*) स्तुतिरूपं स्तोत्रशस्त्रादि वा उक्ष्यजातं उच्चारयत (*stutirūpaṃ stotraśastrādi vā ukṣyajātaṃ uccārayata*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has "ಪೃಥತಮಂ" (split by a line-end hyphen in the print) for वृद्धतमं (*vṛddhatamaṃ*), and वोक्ष्यजातं (*vokṣyajātaṃ*) for उक्ष्यजातं (*ukṣyajātaṃ*))*. Among the names of the great (*mahat*), बहिष्यः, बर्हिषद् (*bahiṣyaḥ, barhiṣad*) , the word *barhiṣṭha* is stated (Ni. 3-19). Agni is worthy of being praised by the priests on behalf of the sacrificer *(the print has "ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ತುನಲ್ಲಿ", as supplied)*. The sense of the command is set out: the sacrificer, addressing the priests, says (printed "ಹೇಳಿರುಹನು", as supplied) "chant abundantly the stotra or śastra and the ukthya verses that make manifest the abundant power of Agni, who is worthy of praise."

यजिष्ठः बर्हिः आ सदत् (*yajiṣṭhaḥ barhiḥ ā sadat*)—यष्टृतमः सः अग्निः अस्माभिः वेद्यां स्तीर्णे (*yaṣṭṛtamaḥ saḥ agniḥ asmābhiḥ vedyāṃ stīrṇe*) बर्हिषि आसीदतु उपवितितु (*barhiṣi āsīdatu upavititu*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has उपविशतु (*upaviśatu*))*. The wish is expressed that Agni, together with the gods who come, invited, to receive the offering in the sacrifice,

### Printed p. 230

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 1.)* may come to our sacrificial hall and be seated on the *barhis* spread on the sacrificial altar. The word *barhis* is stated among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10) and among the names of water (Ni 2-14, as printed). And Yāska, with बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् (*barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt*) (Ni 8 9, as printed without a hyphen), has explained the sense "a seat made of cut-off pieces of *darbha* grass, spread out and prepared as a part of the sacrifice" by the sentence परिच्छेदनात् लूनं हि तद्भवति, परिवृद्धं वा (*paricchedanāt lūnaṃ hi tadbhavati, parivṛddhaṃ vā*) (printed "ಪಾಕ್ಯದಿಂದ", as supplied).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

- बर्हिष्ठम् (*barhiṣṭham*): from the word बर्हितृ (*barhitṛ*) , by तुशृंडसि (*tuśṛṃḍasi*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-59) , when the superlative sense is shown, the affix *iṣṭan*; by तुरिष्टेमेयःसु (*turiṣṭemeyaḥsu*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-104) elision of *tṛc* when the affix follows. Since the affix has *n* as an indicatory letter, the initial-*udātta* accent comes.
- अर्च (*arca*): root अर्च पूजायां (*arca pūjāyāṃ*), *bhvādi*, *loṭ*. By *vyatyaya* the singular affix *sip* in place of the second person plural; the substitute *hi* for it; the *vikaraṇa* printed तप् (*tap*) ; by अतोहेः (*atoheḥ*) *luk* for it. The *tiṅanta* *nighāta* accent (printed तिजंतनिघातस्वर (*tijaṃtanighātasvara*), as supplied) comes.
- गमत् (*gamat*): root गम्‌ल्य गतौ (*gamlya gatau*) . By छंदसिलुज् लज् लिटः (*chaṃdasiluj laj liṭaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) *luñ* in the sense of *loṭ*; *tip* in the third person singular; by इतश्च (*itaśca*) elision of the vowel *i*. Since the root has the indicatory *ḷ* (printed ल्यदित्तादुदरिंद (*lyadittādudariṃda*)), by पुषादिद्युतादि (*puṣādidyutādi*)-(Pā. Sū. 3-1-55) the substitute *aj* *(printed "ಅಜಾದೇಶ" for the affix printed "ಚ್ಚಿ"; as supplied)*. By बहुलंछंदस्य (*bahulaṃchaṃdasya*)-(Pā. Sū. 6-4-75) the augment *aṭ* does not come. Since it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the *nighāta* accent does not come; the root accent remains.
- यजिष्ठः (*yajiṣṭhaḥ*): to the word यजितृ (*yajitṛ*) the affix *iṣṭan* in the superlative sense, by तुच्छंदसि (*tucchaṃdasi*); *tṛc* is elided when it follows; since the affix has *n* as an indicatory letter, the initial-*udātta* accent comes.
- सदत् (*sadat*): root षद्ल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadlya viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*) . By Vedic usage *luñ* in the sense of *loṭ*; elision of the *i* of *tip*; as before the substitute *aj* because the root has indicatory *ḷ*; by बहुलंछंदस्य (*bahulaṃchaṃdasya*) the augment *aṭ* does not come to the stem; by तिज्ञतिजः (*tijñatijaḥ*) the *nighāta* accent comes.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तावा॒ यस्य॒ रोद॑सी॒ दक्षं॒ सचं॑त ऊ॒तयः॑ ।  
> ह॒विष्मं॑त॒स्तमी॑ळते॒ तं स॑नि॒ष्यंतोऽव॑से ॥ २ ॥

> *ṛtāvā yasya rodasī dakṣaṃ sacaṃta ūtayaḥ |*  
> *haviṣmaṃtastamīḷate taṃ saniṣyaṃto 'vase ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 231

*(Ṛk 2, continued from p. 230, where its Saṃhitā stands.)*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

*[The Pada begins यतवा (*yatavā*) where the Saṃhitā has ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*) and the bhāṣya quotes ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*) (and once यतावा (*yatāvā*)); the supplied reading of the Pada word is kept as supplied. The Pada also has तं (*taṃ*) twice, as in the Saṃhitā.]*

> यतवा । यस्य । रोदसी इति । दक्षं । सचंते । ऊशयः ।  
> हविष्मंतः । तं । ईळते । तं । सनिष्यंतः । अवसे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्य पूर्वमंत्रे प्रतिपादितस्याग्ने रोदसी इमे द्यावापृथिव्य वशे
> भवतः । आग्नेः प्रकाशकत्वेन तदधीनप्रकाशके भवत इत्यर्थः । किंच ऊतयो यज-
> मानस्य फलप्रदानेन रक्षितारो देवा दक्षं यस्त्याग्निर्बलं सचंते सेवंते ।
> सचंते सेवंते। नि ७-२३ । इति यास्कः। अग्न्येर्यजमानवत्तहविषां प्रदातृश्वेन तद-
> धीना इत्यर्थः । एवंभूतः सोग्निर्यतावा सत्यकर्मा । सत्यसंकल्प इत्यर्थः ।
> किंच हविष्मंतः संभृतहविष्का यजमाना हविर्वहनार्धं तमेवाग्निमीळते । स्तुति-
> रूपाभिर्वाग्नि पूजयंति । किंच सनिष्यंतो धनादिलाभमिच्छंतस्तमवसे रक्षणाय
> तमेवाग्निमाश्रयंते ॥ ऋतावा । ऋततब्धात्तदस्यास्ति छंदसीवनिपौ वक्तव्याविति
> वनिप् । अन्वेषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः । वॆनिपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे प्रातिपदिकस्वरः ।
> सचंते । सच समवाये । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । सनि-
> ष्यंतः । ससर्लाभः । तमिच्छंतः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यो लालसा
> यां सुग्वक्तव्य इति क्यचि परशः सुगागमः । क्यचः स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two worlds are under the sway of Agni, the gods who protect the sacrificer draw on his strength, and he is true in his deeds and resolve. The sacrificers who have their oblations ready praise him, and those who seek wealth take refuge in him for protection. The rest is grammar: ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*), सचंते (*sacaṃte*), सनिष्यंतः (*saniṣyaṃtaḥ*) (transcribed, not explained). *(The bhāṣya has the references printed "ನಿ ೭-೨೩" for the Nirukta passage and several slips such as सोग्निर्यतावा (*sogniryatāvā*) and वॆनिपः (*vènipaḥ*), as supplied.)*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—(of Agni, set forth in the preceding mantra) in whose (power) रोदसी (*rodasī*)—these two, heaven and earth, (are, and) ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—the gods who (by bestowing the fruit) protect the sacrificer
- (यस्य (*yasya*)) दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—(of whom) the strength सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—they serve
- (सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni) ऋतवा (*ṛtavā*) *(as supplied; the Saṃhitā has ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*))*—he who has true action (or true resolve); (and) हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*)—the sacrificers *(printed "ಸಂಭ್ರಸಹವಿಶ್ಕರಾದ", as supplied; the bhāṣya has संभृतहविष्का (*saṃbhṛtahaviṣkā*))* (so that he may carry the oblation to the gods) तं (*taṃ*)—that same Agni ईळते (*īḷate*)—praise (and likewise) सनिष्यंतः (*saniṣyaṃtaḥ*)—desiring wealth and the like अवसे (*avase*)—for protection *(printed "ತಕ್ಷಣಗೋಸ್ಕರಲೂ", as supplied)* तं (*taṃ*)—him alone (they resort to)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The two worlds are under the sway of the radiant Agni, and the gods, who protect the sacrificers by granting fruit and the like *(printed "ಫಅಪ್ರದಾನಾದಿ…", with ಫಅ for ಫಲ, as supplied)*, have taken refuge in the strength of Agni, the bearer of the oblation. That Agni, true in his resolve, is praised by all the sacrificers who have their oblations ready, that he may bring the oblation to the gods; and, desiring wealth and the like, they resort to him alone for their protection.

### Printed p. 232

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The observer of truth, of whom (are) heaven and earth, and whose vigour the protecting (deities) assist : him, the offerers of oblations adore, and those desirous of riches (have recourse) to him for protection.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यस्य रोदसी (*yasya rodasī*)—पूर्वमंत्रे प्रतिपादितस्य आग्नेः इमे द्यावापृथिव्यौ वशे भवतः आग्नेः प्रकाशकत्वेन तदधीनप्रकाशके भवतः (*pūrvamaṃtre pratipāditasya āgneḥ ime dyāvāpṛthivyau vaśe bhavataḥ āgneḥ prakāśakatvena tadadhīnaprakāśake bhavataḥ*). The word रोदसी (*rodasī*) is stated among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22).

इमे चिदिंद्र रोदसी अपारी यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन् कारित्ते । (*ime cidiṃdra rodasī apārī yatsaṃgṛbhṇā maghavan kāritte |*) (printed "ಪು ಸಂ. ೩-೩೦-೫", as supplied). Here: रोदसी रोदसी द्यावापृथिव् धिरोधनात् । कालं रोधः निरुणद्धि स्रोतः (*rodasī rodasī dyāvāpṛthiv dhirodhanāt | kālaṃ rodhaḥ niruṇaddhi srotaḥ*) (Ni. 6-1) : because heaven and earth hold back the flow (of water) and the bank, they are denoted by the words रोदसी (*rodasī*) or रोधसी (*rodhasī*).

प्र वो महे मंदमानायांधसोऽर्चा विश्वासराय विश्वाभुवे । (*pra vo mahe maṃdamānāyāṃdhaso 'rcā viśvāsarāya viśvābhuve |*)
इंद्रस्य यस्य सुमखं सहो महि श्रवो नृण्मं च रोदसी सप- (*iṃdrasya yasya sumakhaṃ saho mahi śravo nṛṇmaṃ ca rodasī sapa-*)
र्यतः ॥ (*ryataḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-50-1). Here it is said that heaven and earth worship the praise of Vaiśvānara Agni *(so the print; the verse as supplied names Indra)*, and for the word रोदसी (*rodasī*) the sense "heaven and earth" is described.

रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हुवामहे । (*rathaṃ nu mārutaṃ vayaṃ śravasyumā huvāmahe |*)
आ यस्मिन्तस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥ (*ā yasmintasthau suraṇāni bibhratī sacā marutsu rodasī ‖*)
(printed "ಮು. ಸಂ. ೫-೫೬-೮", as supplied). Here the sense रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि रुद्रस्य विभूति: (*rodasī rudrasya patni rudrasya vibhūti:*) (Rodasī is Rudra's wife, Rudra's splendour) is explained.

Because Sāyaṇa sets forth Agni as of abundant greatness, heaven and earth being under the control of Agni, and because these two have no light of their own, he has explained the sense that they are luminous by the light of Agni alone.

ऊतयः दक्षं सचंते (*ūtayaḥ dakṣaṃ sacaṃte*)—the word ऊति (*ūti*) is stated as ऊतिरवनाश् (*ūtiravanāś*) (Ni. 5-3) : formed from the root अव (*ava*), which conveys "to protect", the sense of the word ऊति (*ūti*) is explained as "protecting". The word दक्ष (*dakṣa*) is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9).

दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि प्रते राजाना मित्रावरुणा विवाससि । (*dakṣasya vādite janmani prate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā vivāsasi |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-64-5)

### Printed p. 233

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 2.)* Here, by the statement आदित्यो दक्ष इत्याहुः (*ādityo dakṣa ityāhuḥ*) (printed "ಸಿ ೧೧-೨೪", i.e. Ni. 11-24, as supplied), the sense "Āditya" is given for the word दक्ष (*dakṣa*).

शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तु विजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंतः ॥ (*śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastu vijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃtaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1). Here the word वक्ष (*vakṣa*) *(printed so; the verse has दक्षो (*dakṣo*), as supplied)* is given the sense "one of the Ādityas".

प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचंते । (*pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacaṃte |*)
(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೧-೫೯-೬", as supplied). Here the sense of सचंते सेवंते (*sacaṃte sevaṃte*) is "they serve". The gods, who grant the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice the fruit they need, resort to the strength of Agni and serve Agni. That is, since the sacrificers offer the oblation to the gods through Agni, and Agni conveys it to them, the gods are under Agni's control; this sense is set out by the commentary यजमानस्य फलप्रदानेन रक्षितारो देवाः यस्याग्निर्बलं सेवंते । आग्नेर्यजमानदत्तहविष्पदत्वेन तदधीनाः (*yajamānasya phalapradānena rakṣitāro devāḥ yasyāgnirbalaṃ sevaṃte | āgneryajamānadattahaviṣpadatvena tadadhīnāḥ*) .

ऋतावा - सत्यकर्मा, सत्यसंकल्पः । (*ṛtāvā - satyakarmā, satyasaṃkalpaḥ |*) The word ऋतु (*ṛtu*) has the several meanings water, sacrifice, truth; here Agni is described as having a true resolve.

हविष्मंतः तं ईळते (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ taṃ īḷate*) संभृतहविष्का यजमाना हनिर्वहनार्थं अग्निमेव स्तुतिरूपाभिर्वाग्भि: पूजयंति । (*saṃbhṛtahaviṣkā yajamānā hanirvahanārthaṃ agnimeva stutirūpābhirvāgbhi: pūjayaṃti |*) . The sense is described: the sacrificers, who have made ready the materials for performing the sacrifice, praise Agni with words in the form of praise, in order that he may carry the oblations to the several gods *(the print has "ಯ.ಜಮಾನರು" with a stray full stop, as supplied)*.

द्रविणोदा द्रविणसो ग्रावहस्तासो अध्वरे । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते । (*draviṇodā draviṇaso grāvahastāso adhvare | yajñeṣu devamīḷate |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-7). Here, for the word ईळते (*īḷate*) the sense is explained (Ni. 8-1) as याचंति, स्तुवंति वर्धयंति पूजयंति इति वा (*yācaṃti, stuvaṃti vardhayaṃti pūjayaṃti iti vā*): they praise, they ask, they cause to grow (nourish), or they worship.

सनिष्यंतः तमवसे (*saniṣyaṃtaḥ tamavase*)—धनादिलाभमिच्छंतः रक्षणाय तमेवाश्रयंतॆ । (*dhanādilābhamicchaṃtaḥ rakṣaṇāya tamevāśrayaṃtè |*) The authors of the Nirukta, in

हिनोता नो आध्वरं देवयज्या हिनोत ब्रह्म सनये धनानां । (*hinotā no ādhvaraṃ devayajyā hinota brahma sanaye dhanānāṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-30-11),

have explained, for the word सनये (*sanaye*) there, the sense "for obtaining riches". Sāyaṇa *(the text breaks off here; the print has "ಸಾಯಿ", cut at the end of the supplied text)*

*[Stray line at the end of the supplied text for p. 233: "80", kept as supplied; the window ends mid-sentence.]*

### Printed p. 234

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 233. The page begins with the end of a word cut at the page break; the supplied text starts at "ಇರು" and the word "ಸಾಯಿ" at the foot of p. 233 is not completed in it.)*

इरु (*iru*) **NOTE** — he has described the sense that the sacrificers take refuge in Agni alone, both from the wish to obtain wealth and the like and for protection.

##### विशेषविषयगळु — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Grammar notes of Ṛk 2)

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* Words dealt with: ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)—the suffix *vanip* in the sense of "possessing" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 for the lengthening of the first member in the Saṃhitā; the stem accent is kept because *vanip* has the mark *p*); सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—root *ṣaca* in the sense of "to go together", the ātmanepada by *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1 85, as printed with a space for the hyphen) and the suppression of the *nighāta* accent because of the relative य (*ya*) (Pā. Sū. 8-166, as printed, with the part numbers missing); Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 for the root accent; ईरते (*īrate*) (printed so; the Ṛk has ಈಳತೇ, as supplied)—root *īḍa* "to praise", of the *adādi* class; सनिष्यंतः (*saniṣyaṃtaḥ*)—*sani* in the sense of "gain", the suffix *kyac* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8), the augment *suk* by the *vārttika*, the sense of a verbal root by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ*, and the substitute *śatṛ* for *laṭ*.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

*[The garbled printed label "ಸಂಕಟಾದಿ" has been restored in the Kannada file to the standard Saṃhitā label; the verse is as supplied.]*

> स यं॒ता विप्र॑ एषां॒ स य॒ज्ञाना॒मथा॒ हि षः ।  
> अ॒ग्निं तं वो॑ दुवस्यत॒ दात्ता॒ यो वनि॑ता म॒घं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

*[Label printed "ಪದಹಾರಃ", restored to the standard Pada label in the Kannada file.]*

> सः । यंता । विप्रः । एषां । सः । यज्ञानां । अथ । हि । सः ।  
> अग्निं । तं । वः । दुवस्यत । दाता । यः । वनिता । मघं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विप्रो मेधावी कर्माभिज्ञः सोऽग्नि रेषां कालापराधेन हविर्निर्वापं
> कृतवतां यजमानानां यथोक्तकर्मप्रदर्शनेन तत्र प्रवर्तकः । अथ किंच
> यज्ञानां ज्योतिष्टोमादीनां सोऽग्निर्नियंता फलप्रदानेन नियामकः । हि
> प्रसिद्धौ अत एव सर्वस्य नियंता खलु । किंच सोऽग्निर्दाशा ज्योतिष्टोमादिकर्म-
> फलवाता मघं महनीयं धनं । मघं रेक्ण इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तद्दनं वनि
> ता प्रयच्छंश्च भवति । वो युष्मत्संबंधिनं तावृशमग्निं हे ऋत्विजो यूयं
> दुवस्यत आहुतिप्रदानेन परिचरत । दुवस्यतिः परिचरणकर्मा नमस्यति दुवस्यतीति
> तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ यंता । यम उपरम इत्यस्य तृचि रूपं ! ऋदुशनसित्यादिना
> अनटादेशः । चित्स्वरः । अथा । निपातस्येति दीर्घः । दुवस्यत । दुवः परिचरणं । तदि-
> च्छ्यंतः । सुपः कैच् । तदंतस्य धातोर्लोटि रूपं । दाता । डुदाण् दाने । ता-
> च्चीलकस्त्रन् । नित्यादाद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the wise one, instructs the sacrificers who have offered at the wrong time to perform the rite as prescribed, and so impels them; he regulates sacrifices by granting their fruit, gives wealth, and the priests should serve him with oblations. The rest is grammar: यंता (*yaṃtā*), दुवस्यत (*duvasyata*), दाता (*dātā*) (transcribed, not explained). *(Slips as supplied in the bhāṣya, e.g. "ಅನಟಾದೇಶಃ", "ಫಲವಾತಾ", "ನಿತ್ಯಾದಾದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತಃ".)*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise (the one skilled in rites)
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—for the sacrificers who offer oblations and the like
- यंता (*yaṃtā*)—the impeller *(printed so, without a dash, as supplied)*
- अथ (*atha*)—and
- यज्ञानां (*yajñānāṃ*)—for sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- (यंता (*yaṃtā*))—(as the giver of the fruit) the regulator; (for that reason *(printed "ಆಧುದರಿಂದಲೇ", as supplied)*)
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- (यंता (*yaṃtā*)) हि (*hi*)—the regulator of all, indeed *(printed "ಸರ್ವನಿಯಾಮನಷ್ಟೇ", as supplied)*
- दाता (*dātā*)—the giver of the fruit (of rites such as the Jyotiṣṭoma) *(printed "ಫಲದಾತೃವಾದ")*
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- मघं (*maghaṃ*)—splendid wealth
- वनिता (*vanitā*)—will be the giver
- तं (*taṃ*)—such
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni; (O priests, you) दुवस्यत (*duvasyata*)—tend (him by offering oblations) *(printed "ಅಹುತಿಪ್ರದಾನದಿಂದ" with ಅ for ಆ, and "ಉಪಚರಿಸಿ", as supplied)*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who knows the rites, is the guide of the sacrificers; the same, as the giver of the fruit, is the regulator of sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, and therefore is called the regulator of all. He is the one who bestows excellent wealth upon all. Such an Agni, O priests, acquaint yourselves with by oblations and the like *(printed "ಪರಿಚಯಿಸಿ", "make known / acquaint", as supplied; the Pratipadārtha has "ಉಪಚರಿಸಿ", tend)*.

### Printed p. 235

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
He, the sage, is the director of those (who sacrifice), he is (the regulator) of sacrifices : worship him your (benefactor), the donor, who is the bestower of wealth.

*(The printed "regu-lator" is broken across a line; joined here.)*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विप्रः सः एषां यन्ता (*vipraḥ saḥ eṣāṃ yantā*)—मेधावी कर्माभिज्ञः अग्निः कालापराधेन हविर्निर्पां कृतवशां यजमानानां यथोक्तकर्मप्रदर्शनेन तत्र प्रवर्तकः । (*medhāvī karmābhijñaḥ agniḥ kālāparādhena havirnirpāṃ kṛtavaśāṃ yajamānānāṃ yathoktakarmapradarśanena tatra pravartakaḥ |*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has "ಹವಿರ್ನಿರ್ವಾಪಂ ಕೃತವತಾಂ" where this quotation has "ಹವಿರ್ನಿರ್ಪಾಂ ಕೃತವಶಾಂ"; kept as supplied)* In

### Printed p. 236

*(The sentence begun at the foot of p. 235 continues:)* this Ṛk the word यन्ता (*yantā*) is repeated. In this sentence it has been explained as "impeller". The word विप्र (*vipra*) is stated among the names of the wise. This word is used as an adjective of the word सः (*saḥ*). By this he has explained Agni as wise and as one who knows the procedure of performing rites according to the śāstra, as one who, to the sacrificers who offer the oblation, a part of the rite, at another time without performing the rite at the prescribed time, teaches the procedure of performing the rite in the proper manner, and so urges each sacrificer to perform the respective rites. Thereby the sense अग्निः यजमानानां कर्मसु प्रवर्तयिता (*agniḥ yajamānānāṃ karmasu pravartayitā*) (Agni is the impeller of the sacrificers in rites) is stated.

यज्ञानां सः यन्ता हि (*yajñānāṃ saḥ yantā hi*)—ज्योतिष्टोमादीनां अग्नि: फलप्रदानेन नियामकः । (*jyotiṣṭomādīnāṃ agni: phalapradānena niyāmakaḥ |*) The word यन्तारः (*yantāraḥ*) is stated among the words of sacrificial acts (printed "ಯಾಜ್ಞಾಕರ್ಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ", as supplied) (Ni. 3-19). Here the word यन्ता (*yantā*) is explained as "regulator", and the particle हि (*hi*) is explained as "well known". Because Agni grants the fruit of rites such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, and because, keeping the whole world under his control, he is the regulator of all, he is described as the regulator of the sacrifices and rites that the sacrificers perform.

सः अग्निः दाता (*saḥ agniḥ dātā*)—ज्योतिष्टोमादिकर्मफलदाता ! (*jyotiṣṭomādikarmaphaladātā !*) *(the "!" as supplied)* Since the word दाता (*dātā*) is well known in the sense of "one who gives", the sense is described here that he grants the sacrificer the fruit of all the sacrifices and rites that he performs.

मघं (*maghaṃ*)—मंदनीयं धनं । (*maṃdanīyaṃ dhanaṃ |*) *(so here; the bhāṣya has महनीयं (*mahanīyaṃ*); kept as supplied)* The word मघ (*magha*) is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). And मंदमिति धननामधेयं मंदशेर्दानकर्मणः । (*maṃdamiti dhananāmadheyaṃ maṃdaśerdānakarmaṇaḥ |*) The sense is described that the word मघ (*magha*), formed from the root मंद (*maṃda*) , which conveys "to give", denotes wealth as the means of giving. Thereby Sāyaṇa has described for wealth the sense "to be praised, fit for giving" *(printed "ಮಂದನೀಯಂ ದಾನಾರ್ಣವಾದುದು", the second word as supplied, doubtful)* **NOTE**.

वनिशा (*vaniśā*) *(printed so; the Ṛk has वनिता (*vanitā*))*—the sense is given that Agni will bestow wealth upon the sacrificers.

वः तं अग्निं दुवस्यत (*vaḥ taṃ agniṃ duvasyata*)—हे ऋत्विजः युष्मत्संबंधिनं तादृतं अग्निं आहुतिप्रदानेन परिचरित (*he ṛtvijaḥ yuṣmatsaṃbaṃdhinaṃ tādṛtaṃ agniṃ āhutipradānena paricarita*) *(as supplied; the bhāṣya has तावृशमग्निं (*tāvṛśamagniṃ*) and परिचरत (*paricarata*))*—the word दुवस्यति (*duvasyati*) is stated among the words of tending (Ni. 3-13). Addressing the priests, the command of the seer of the mantra is described: "Serve, by offering oblations, such a powerful Agni, the giver of the fruit of sacrifice, the regulator of sacrifice and the giver of wealth."

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar page begun.)* यंता (*yaṃtā*)—root *yama* "to restrain", the suffix *tṛc* in the agent sense, nasal assimilation of the root's *m*, the final accent by the mark *c* (printed "ಚಿತ್ತಾಮದರಿಂದ", as supplied); the note breaks off at the end of p. 236 with the words "ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಸು ಪರವಾದಾಗ" (when *su* follows it), and the rest is on the next page.

### Printed p. 237

*(Grammar notes of Ṛk 3, continued from p. 236; the sentence cut at the foot of p. 236 continues:)* when *su* follows it, the rule ऋदुशनस्सुरुदं (*ṛduśanassurudaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-94) gives the substitution अनजादेश (*anajādeśa*) . By अप्‌तृन्‌तृच् (*aptṛntṛc*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-11) the penultimate vowel is lengthened. By the rule beginning हल् ज्याभो (*hal jyābho*) the *su* is dropped, and by the rule beginning नलोपः प्राति (*nalopaḥ prāti*) the *n* is dropped *(no sūtra numbers are printed for these two)*. The form यंता (*yaṃtā*) results.

अथ (*atha*)—by अथ विपातस्यच (*atha vipātasyaca*) (printed "ಪಾ. ರೂ. ೬-೩-೧೩೬", i.e. Pā. Sū. 6-3-136 with *rū* for *sū*, as supplied) a long vowel arises in the Saṃhitā.

दुवस्कृत (*duvaskṛta*) —दुवस् (*duvas*) is used in the sense of "serving" *(printed "ಪರಿಚಂಷಾರ್ಥ", as supplied)*. When the sense is intended as "desiring for oneself दुवः (*duvaḥ*)", the suffix क्यच् (*kyac*) comes by the rule beginning सुपआत्मनःक्यच् (*supaātmanaḥkyac*) . By सनाद्यंताधातवः (*sanādyaṃtādhātavaḥ*) the stem दुवस्य (*duvasya*) gets the name "root". After the *kyac*-ending root, in the imperative middle-person (2nd) plural the form दुवस्तत (*duvastata*) *(so printed; the Ṛk has ದುವಸ್ಯತ)* results. Since it follows a non-verb *(printed "ಅತಿಜಂತ", as supplied)* the *nighāta* accent comes by the rule तिज्ञतिङ्ग (*tijñatiṅga*) .

दाशा (*dāśā*) *(so printed; the Ṛk has ದಾತಾ)*—the root डुदाळ् दाने (*ḍudāḷ dāne*) takes the suffix *tṛn* when the "habitual" sense is shown. Because it has the mark *n* it has the first-syllable acute accent.

वनिशा (*vaniśā*) *(so printed; the Ṛk has ವನಿತಾ)*—the root वनु (*vanu*) is used in many senses, so here it is used in the sense of giving. As before, the suffix *tṛn* in the habitual sense; the augment *iṭ*; by इत्यादिनिर्त्यम् (*ityādinirtyam*) the first-syllable acute accent comes. The form is of the nominative singular *(printed "ಪ್ರಥಮಾ ಏಕವಚನಾತರೂವ", as supplied)*.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स नः॒ शर्मा॑णि वी॒तये॒ऽग्निर्य॑च्छतु॒ शंत॑मा ।  
> यतो॑ नः प्रु॒ष्णव॒द्वसु॑ दि॒वि क्षि॒तिभ्यो॑ अ॒प्सा ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । नः । शर्माणि । नीतये । अग्निः । यच्छतु । शंतमा ।  
> यतः । नः । पुष्पवत् । वसु । दिवि । क्षितिभ्यः । अप्सु । आ ॥ ४ ॥

> *saḥ | naḥ | śarmāṇi | nītaye | agniḥ | yacchatu | śaṃtamā |*

*(Differences as supplied between the Saṃhitā and the Pada: Saṃhitā वीतये (*vītaye*) / Pada नीतये (*nītaye*); Saṃhitā प्रुष्णवद् (*pruṣṇavad*) / Pada पुष्पवत् (*puṣpavat*); Saṃhitā अप्सा (*apsā*) / Pada अप्सु (*apsu*) आ (*ā*). Kept as supplied.)*

> सोऽग्निर्नो हपिष्पदात्थ भ्योऽस्मभ्यं शंतमा पशुपुत्रादिसमृद्ध्यातिशयेन

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Agni give us, who bring oblations, houses that bring great happiness through cattle, sons and the like, for the performance of the Agnihotra and other rites; from him comes the wealth that grows even when spent, existing in heaven, earth and the waters. The rest is grammar. *(Slips as supplied in the bhāṣya, e.g. हपिष्पदात्थ भ्यो (*hapiṣpadāttha bhyo*), सशात् (*saśāt*), ददाकु (*dadāku*).)*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यशः (*yaśaḥ*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has यतः (*yataḥ*))*—from which Agni
- पुष्णवत् (*puṣṇavat*) *(so printed; the Pada has पुष्पवत् (*puṣpavat*))*—(even if it is spent in the form of gifts, enjoyment and the like) the one that keeps increasing
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the world of the gods
- क्षितिभ्यः (*kṣitibhyaḥ*)—from the earth-world
- अप्पु (*appu*) (ಚ)—also in the waters (the one that has arisen) *(the stray "ಅದ" after this, as supplied)*
- वसु (*vasu*)—(unique) wealth
- आ (*ā*)—arrives from all sides; सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*)—that Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- तंतमा (*taṃtamā*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has शंतमा (*śaṃtamā*))*—(through increase of cattle, sons and the like) that cause happiness
- शर्माणि (*śarmāṇi*)—houses
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—(rites such as the Agnihotra) for the attainment
- यच्छतु (*yacchatu*)—let him give (grant)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From this Agni comes the wealth that belongs to heaven, the earth-world and the waters, and that goes on increasing however much it is spent. May such an Agni grant us houses that cause happiness through increase of cattle, sons and the like *(printed "ಪಶುಪುತ್ರಾದ್ಯಭಿವೃದ್ಧಾದ್ದ್ವಾರಾ", as supplied)* and are favourable to our Agnihotra and other rites.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May that Agni bestow upon us prosperous dwellings for our maintenance, so that from him infinite wealth, whether it may be in heaven or from earth. or in the waters (may come to us)

*(The printed "mainten-ance" is broken across a line; joined here. The full stop after "earth" is as printed.)*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सः अग्निः नः शंतमा वीतये यच्छतु (*saḥ agniḥ naḥ śaṃtamā vītaye yacchatu*)—हविष्पदातृभ्यः अस्मभ्यं पशुपुत्रादिसमृद्धा अतितयेन सुखकराणि तथाविधानि गृहाणि संभजनाय अग्निहोत्रादिकर्मप्राप्त्यर्थं ददातु । शर्म वर्म इति गृहनामसु पाठात् शर्मशब्दः गृहपाची । (*haviṣpadātṛbhyaḥ asmabhyaṃ paśuputrādisamṛddhā atitayena sukhakarāṇi tathāvidhāni gṛhāṇi saṃbhajanāya agnihotrādikarmaprāptyarthaṃ dadātu | śarma varma iti gṛhanāmasu pāṭhāt śarmaśabdaḥ gṛhapācī |*) *(as supplied; अतितयेन (*atitayena*) and गृहपाची (*gṛhapācī*) differ from the bhāṣya's अतिशयेन (*atiśayena*) and गृहवाची (*gṛhavācī*))* The word शर्म (*śarma*) is stated both among the names of houses and among the names of happiness (Ni. 3.13). In the passage

स्योना पृथिवि भवान्यक्षरा निवेशनी । यच्छा नः कर्म सप्रथः ॥ (*syonā pṛthivi bhavānyakṣarā niveśanī | yacchā naḥ karma saprathaḥ ‖*) (printed "ಪು. ಸಂ. ೧-೨೨-೧೫", i.e. "Pu. Saṃ. 1-22-15", as supplied) *(a rough gloss, mine and tentative: "Be pleasant, O Earth, an abode; grant us [as supplied: karma] ... wide")*

### Printed p. 239

*(The sentence begun at the foot of p. 238 continues:)* the sense "happiness" has been given to the word शर्म (*śarma*). The word शंतम (*śaṃtama*) generally means "very pleasant". Sāyaṇa has explained that this word शंतनु (*śaṃtanu*) is a synonym of the word शर्म (*śarma*) denoting a house; he has cited the explanation of the Nirukta, and has explained the meaning thus: may Agni grant to the sacrificer and the others who offer oblations a house (a dwelling) which causes great happiness by the birth of cattle, sons and the like, and which is a means to the Agnihotra and other rites. In the Nirukta Yāska, citing this Ṛk

पत्नीवंतस्सुता इम उशंतो यंकि वीतये ] अपां जग्निर्निचुंपुणः (*patnīvaṃtassutā ima uśaṃto yaṃki vītaye ] apāṃ jagnirnicuṃpuṇaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-93-22)

has explained the meaning of the word वीति (*vīti*) as वीतये अपां पानाय (*vītaye apāṃ pānāya*)—"in order to drink water". Sāyaṇa has described it as अग्निहोत्रादि कर्मप्राप्त्यर्थं (*agnihotrādi karmaprāptyarthaṃ*).

पुष्पवत् (*puṣpavat*)—समृद्धिमत्, दानभोगादिना व्यये सत्यपि अतिशयेन वर्धमानं (*samṛddhimat, dānabhogādinā vyaye satyapi atiśayena vardhamānaṃ*) This word is used as an adjective of the word वसु (*vasu*). The meaning is: the wealth that increases greatly even if one gives, enjoys (experiences happiness) and spends, and which, since it is in heaven, on earth and in the waters, is unique. अग्नेः प्रसादात् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यमानं धनं आस्मानागच्छति (*agneḥ prasādāt triṣu lokeṣu vidyamānaṃ dhanaṃ āsmānāgacchati*) *(so printed, ಆಸ್ಮಾನ್; the bhāṣya has ಅಸ್ಮಾನ್)*—here is described the command of the seer of the mantra: "Since, by the grace of Agni, wealth reaches us, the sacrificers and others who perform the sacrifice, one should serve the Agni of abundant greatness, who obtains it for us."

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

वीतये (*vītaye*)—the root वी गतिकांत्यादिसु (*vī gatikāṃtyādisu*) . By मंत्रेवृषेषपच (*maṃtrevṛṣeṣapaca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96) the suffix *ktin*. As it is enunciated with the acute, it becomes final-accented. The form is of the dative singular.

यच्छतु (*yacchatu*)—the root यम उपरमे (*yama uparame*). In the imperative third person singular the suffix *tip*. By एरुति (*eruti*) (Pā. Sū. 3-9-86, as printed) the *i* is replaced by *u*. By इषुगमियमां छः (*iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-77) the *m* of the root is replaced by *ch*. The form यच्छतु (*yacchatu*) results. By तिच्चतिजः (*ticcatijaḥ*) the *nighāta* accent comes.

तंतमा (*taṃtamā*) —the suffix *tamap* in the sense of excess. As it has the mark *p*, the accent of the stem comes. By नपुंसकबहुवचनदश शेश्छंदसिबहुलम् (*napuṃsakabahuvacanadaśa śeśchaṃdasibahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70) the *śi* is dropped.

पुष्पवत् (*puṣpavat*)—the root पुष स्नेहससेचनपूरणेम (*puṣa snehasasecanapūraṇema*) . To it the Auṇādika suffix "nar" *(so printed; the bhāṣya says nak)*. Because it has the mark *k* the guṇa of the light penultimate does not come. Because it follows *ṣ*, the change to *ṇ* comes . पुष्पः (*puṣpaḥ*)

### Printed p. 240

अस्य अस्ति इति (*asya asti iti*) *(the sentence "ಪುಷ್ಪಃ … ಅಸ್ಯ ಅಸ್ತಿ ಇತಿ" runs across the page break: "that which has flowers")*. पुष्णवत् तदस्यास्ति (*puṣṇavat tadasyāsti*) —by this the suffix *matup*; by माडुपधायाश्च (*māḍupadhāyāśca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-9) the *m* is replaced by *v* because it follows *a*. Because *matup* comes after a short vowel, the acute should come on it by the rule beginning ह्रस्वनुड्भां मतुप् (*hrasvanuḍbhāṃ matup*) *(printed "ಪ್ರಸ್ವ…", as supplied)*, but in the Veda it does not come here. The accent of the suffix *nak* remains.

अप्पु (*appu*)—the form of the locative plural. By ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the acute comes on the case-ending.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दी॒दि॒नांस॒मपू॑र्व्यं॒ वस्वी॑भिरस्य धी॒तिभिः॑ ।  
> ऋक्वा॑णो अ॒ग्निमिं॑धते॒ होता॑रं वि॒श्वतिं॑ वि॒शां ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दीदिपांसं । आपूर्व्यं । वस्वीभिः । अस्य । धीतिभिः ।  
> ऋक्वाणः । अग्निं । इंथते । होतारं । विश्वतिं । विशां ॥ ५ ॥

> *dīdipāṃsaṃ | āpūrvyaṃ | vasvībhiḥ | asya | dhītibhiḥ |*  
> *ṛkvāṇaḥ | agniṃ | iṃthate | hotāraṃ | viśvatiṃ | viśāṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

*(Differences as supplied between the Saṃhitā and the Pada: Saṃhitā दीदिनांसमपूर्व्यं (*dīdināṃsamapūrvyaṃ*) / Pada दीदिपांसं । आपूर्व्यं (*dīdipāṃsaṃ | āpūrvyaṃ*); Saṃhitā ಇಂಧತೇ / Pada इंथते (*iṃthate*). Kept as supplied.)*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋक्वाणः स्तुतिं कुर्वाणाः शस्त्रिणो होत्रादयो दीदिवांसं दीप्यमानम-
> पूर्व्यं तेजस्वितया प्रतिक्षणमभिनवं होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं विशां विश्वतिं
> प्रजानामतिशयेन पालयितारं तमग्निं वस्वीभिः प्रकस्ताभिरस्य धीतिभिरग्नि विषयस्तुति-
> लक्षणाभिर्वाग्भिः । यद्वा हस्वीभिर्वसुमद्भिरस्य धीतिभिरेतदुद्देशेन क्रियमाणैः कर्म-
> भिरिंधते । दीपयंति । स्तोत्रकरणहविष्पदानादिव्यापारेण समृद्धिं कुर्वंति ॥
> दीदिवांसं । दिवु क्रीडादावित्यस्य कृत्वा रूपं । तुजादीनामित्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घः ।
> लोपो व्योरिति लोपः । वस्वीभिः । वसुशबाद्व्यत्ययेन जीन् । नित्सर्वः । धीतिभिः ।
> धेट् पाने । क्तिच्क्च संज्ञायामिति क्तिच् । कित्त्वाद् घुमास्थेतीत्वं । चित्स्वरः।
> ऋक्वाणः । ऋच्शज्ञानतुबर्थे वनिप् । अयस्मयादित्वादृसंज्ञात्वात्कुत्वं । पद-
> संज्ञाभावाज्जत्वाभाषः । इंथते । ज्ञौइंधी दीप्तौ । विश्वतिं । परादिश्यंदसि बहुल-
> मित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । विशां । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests who praise (the hotṛ and others) kindle that Agni—blazing, ever new, the Hotṛ of the gods, protector of the people—with fine hymns about him, or with rites performed for him. The rest is grammar: दीदिवांसं (*dīdivāṃsaṃ*), वस्वीभिः (*vasvībhiḥ*), धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*), ऋक्वाणः (*ṛkvāṇaḥ*), इंथते (*iṃthate*), विश्वतिं (*viśvatiṃ*) (transcribed, not explained). *(Slips as supplied in the bhāṣya, e.g. हस्वीभिर् (*hasvībhir*), ಪ್ರಕಸ್ತಾಭಿರ್, जीन् (*jīn*).)*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋक्वाणः (*ṛkvāṇaḥ*)—the hotṛ and other priests, makers of praise *(printed "ಸೃತಿಕರ್ತೃಗಳಾದ", as supplied)*
- दीदिवांसं (*dīdivāṃsaṃ*)—the shining one *(printed "ದೇಧೀಪ್ಯಮಾನನೂ")*
- अपूर्व्यं (*apūrvyaṃ*)—because he is radiant *(printed "ತೇಜಸ್ವಿಯಾದುದರಿಂದ")*, new at every moment
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the one who invites the gods *(the window ends here, at the end of a printed line: "ಆಹ್ವಾನಿಸು" breaks off; the rest of the Pratipadārtha follows in the next window)*

### Printed p. 241–242

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 5, continued from p. 240, where it broke off after "ಹೋತಾರಂ—ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಆಹ್ವಾನಿಸು"; the first word here, ववनू (*vavanū*), completes "ಆಹ್ವಾನಿಸು" as supplied: "the one who invites the gods".)*

विशां (*viśāṃ*)—to the people; विश्वतिं (*viśvatiṃ*)—the protector *(printed "ವಿಶ್ವತಿಂ - ಪಾಲಕನೂ (ಆದ)", "who is the protector")*; अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni; वस्वीभिः (*vasvībhiḥ*)—excellent; अस्य धीतिभिः (*asya dhītibhiḥ*)—by the praises related to this Agni; [or वस्वीभिः (*vasvībhiḥ*)—possessed of wealth in the form of oblations *(printed "ಹವೀರೂಪಧನ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟವಾದ", as supplied)*; अस्य धीतिभिः (*asya dhītibhiḥ*)—by the rites performed with Agni in view]; इनते: (*inate:*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has ಇಂಧತೇ)*—they cause to blaze.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praising priests, the hotṛ and others, kindle Agni—the blazing one, who seems new at every moment, who invites the gods, the protector of the people—with oblations and the like, by the rites performed for Agni's sake, and so make him blaze up.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The devout kindle (the fire) with his wealth-obtaining rites, (to worship) the radiant, unprecedented Agni, the invoker (of the gods), the protector of men.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋक्वाणः (*ṛkvāṇaḥ*)—this word is explained as स्तुतिं कुर्वाणाः (*stutiṃ kurvāṇāḥ*), "those who recite praise"; the meaning is set out as the priests, such as the hotṛ, who recite the śastra-mantras that describe the greatness of the gods such as Agni *(printed "ಹೋತೃವೇ", as supplied)*.

अपूर्व्यं—शेजस्वितया प्रतिक्षणमभिनवं (*apūrvyaṃ—śejasvitayā pratikṣaṇamabhinavaṃ*) *(so printed, "ಶೇ" where "ತೇ" is expected)*—the meaning is that, because Agni has great radiance, he appears new at every single moment *(printed "ಕ್ಷಣಾದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ", as supplied)*.

विशां विश्वतिं—प्रजानामतिशयेन पालयितारं (*viśāṃ viśvatiṃ—prajānāmatiśayena pālayitāraṃ*)—the meaning is described as: Agni protects the people and the whole world. Yāska, in the passage

अस्य वामस्य पलितस्य होतुस्तस्य भ्राता मध्यमो अस्त्यश्च । तृतीयो भ्राता धृतपृष्ठो अस्यात्रापश्यं विश्वतिं सप्तपुत्रं ॥ (*asya vāmasya palitasya hotustasya bhrātā madhyamo astyaśca | tṛtīyo bhrātā dhṛtapṛṣṭho asyātrāpaśyaṃ viśvatiṃ saptaputraṃ ‖*) (Pu. Saṃ. 1-164-1) *(reference printed "ಪು. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

has explained the word विश्वतिं (*viśvatiṃ*) as सर्वस्य पातारं वा पालयितारं वा (*sarvasya pātāraṃ vā pālayitāraṃ vā*).

वस्वीभिः अस्य धीतिभिः इंथते—प्रशस्ताभिः अग्नि विषयस्तुतिलक्षणाभिर्वाग्भिः यद्वा वसुमद्भिरेतदुद्देशेन क्रियमाणैः कर्मभिः स्तोत्रकरणहविष्पदानादिव्यापारेण समृद्धिं कुर्वंति (*vasvībhiḥ asya dhītibhiḥ iṃthate—praśastābhiḥ agni viṣayastutilakṣaṇābhirvāgbhiḥ yadvā vasumadbhiretaduddeśena kriyamāṇaiḥ karmabhiḥ stotrakaraṇahaviṣpadānādivyāpāreṇa samṛddhiṃ kurvaṃti*) *(printed ಇಂಥತೇ and ಹವಿಷ್ಪದಾನಾದಿ as supplied; the bhāṣya has ಇಂಧತೇ)*. Because the word धीति (*dhīti*) is used in the senses of "rite", "finger" and "praise", two kinds of meaning are given here. First, it is explained that the priests make Agni grow by speech in the form of praise, excellent in praising Agni and filled with Agni's greatness. In the second sense, since धीति (*dhīti*) is taken to mean rites performed for Agni's sake, it is described that he is made to prosper and delighted by the praises recited in honour of Agni and by the rites consisting of the giving of the oblations offered in honour of Agni.

*(Here the printed text has a stray line "31", and then the running head of printed p. 242 stands in the middle of the sentence, as supplied: "242 ಸಾಯುಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೩. ಅ. ೨. ಸೂ. ೧೩." = "242 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [Maṇḍala 3, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 13", bracket not closed. The sentence "ಅಗ್ನಿಯ ಉದ್ದೇಶ|ದಿಂದ … ಪಠಿಸುವ" runs across this point; printed p. 242 begins here.)*

दीदिवांसं—दीप्यमानं (*dīdivāṃsaṃ—dīpyamānaṃ*)—the meaning is that Agni shines exceedingly with his splendours.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes (noted briefly):

दीदिवांसम् (*dīdivāṃsam*)—root दिवु (*divu*) of the क्रीडादिषु (*krīḍādiṣu*) class; when लिट् (*liṭ*) comes, क्वसु (*kvasu*) is substituted by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-107) *(the reference is printed twice, "(ಪಾ. ಸೂ. (ಪಾ. ಸೂ. ೩-೨-೧೦೭)", as supplied)*. Reduplication of the root and so on; since the root is read in the तुजादि (*tujādi*) list, the reduplicating syllable is lengthened by तुजादीनांदीर्घोभ्यासस्य (*tujādīnāṃdīrghobhyāsasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-7); the व (*va*) is dropped by लोपोव्योर्वलि (*lopovyorvali*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-66); the suffix accent comes. In the accusative singular the *num* augment comes because the suffix has a mute उक् (*uk*) *(printed "ಉಗಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ", as supplied)*.

अपूर्व्यम् (*apūrvyam*)—by तत्पुरुषेतुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣetulyārtha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the word before नञ् (*nañ*) keeps its own accent.

वस्वीभिः (*vasvībhiḥ*)—the suffix जीन् (*jīn*) by व्यत्यय (*vyatyaya*) after the word वसु (*vasu*); *yaṇ* substitution; because it has a mute न् (*n*) *(printed "ನಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ")*, the acute on the first syllable comes. Instrumental plural form.

धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)—root धेट् पाने (*dheṭ pāne*); the suffix क्तिच् (*ktic*) by क्तिच्क्त्वा च संज्ञायाम् (*kticktvā ca saṃjñāyām*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-174) ; आदेचउपदेशे (*ādecaupadeśe*) (no number printed) makes the root end in अ (*a*); since the following suffix has a mute क् (*k*), the अ (*a*) becomes ई (*ī*) by घुमास्थागापा (*ghumāsthāgāpā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66); by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the accent falls on the last syllable.

ऋक्वाणः (*ṛkvāṇaḥ*) *(printed with a colon, "ಋಕ್ವಾಣ:")*—when the meaning "he has ऋच् (*ṛc*)" is intended, the suffix वनिप् (*vanip*) by छंदसी वनिप् (*chaṃdasī vanip*); since the word is in the आयस्मयादि (*āyasmayādi*) group and has the भ (*bha*) designation, क (*ka*) replaces च (*ca*) by कुत्व (*kutva*), and जस्त्व (*jastva*) does not come because it lacks the पद (*pada*) designation; the suffix न (*na*) becomes ण (*ṇa*) after ऋ (*ṛ*); since the suffix has a mute प् (*p*) it is unaccented, so the accent of the stem remains. Nominative plural form.

इंधते (*iṃdhate*)—root इंधी दीप्तौ (*iṃdhī dīptau*); लट् (*laṭ*) third person plural *(sic, as supplied)*; the finite-verb निघात (*nighāta*) accent comes.

विश्वतिं (*viśvatiṃ*)—विशां पतिः तं (*viśāṃ patiḥ taṃ*); by परादिशृंदसि बहुलं (*parādiśṛṃdasi bahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199) *(printed "ಶೃಂದಸಿ", as supplied)* the acute falls on the first syllable of the latter member.

विशां (*viśāṃ*)—genitive plural form; by सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-18) the case-ending takes the acute.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त नो॒ ब्रह्म॑न्नविष उ॒क्तेषु॑ देव॒हूत॑मः ।  
> शं नः॑ शोचा म॒रुद्वृ॒धोऽग्ने॑ सहस्र॒सात॑मः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । नः । ब्रह्मन् । अविषः । उक्षेषु । देव्यहूतमः ।  
> शं । नः । शोच । मरुत्स्‌वृधः । अग्ने । सहस्रसातमः ॥ ६ ॥

> *uta | naḥ | brahman | aviṣaḥ | ukṣeṣu | devyahūtamaḥ |*  
> *śaṃ | naḥ | śoca | marutsvṛdhaḥ | agne | sahasrasātamaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

*(Differences as supplied between the Saṃhitā and the Pada: Saṃhitā उक्तेषु (*ukteṣu*) / Pada उक्षेषु (*ukṣeṣu*); Saṃhitā देवहूतमः (*devahūtamaḥ*) / Pada देव्यहूतमः (*devyahūtamaḥ*); Saṃhitā मरुद्वृधो (*marudvṛdho*) (sandhi form) / Pada मरुत्स्‌वृधः (*marutsvṛdhaḥ*); Saṃhitā शोचा (*śocā*) / Pada शोच (*śoca*). Kept as supplied. A garbled line "ಹಡಹಾತಿ" stood where the Pada label belongs; it was replaced by the standard label, see repair_log.txt.)*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत अपि च हे आग्ने नो यज्ञकारिणोऽस्मान् ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मण्यस्माभिः क्रि-
> यमाणे स्तोत्रेऽविषः । स्तोत्रविषयन्यूनातिरेकदोषो यथा न भवति तथा
> पालय किंच देवहूतमो देवानामाहात्यृतमस्तु मुक्तेऽस्माभिः क्रियमाणे-
> ष्टाज्यप्रउगादिशस्त्रेष्टविषः । गोपाय । किंच मरुद्वधो मरुद्विर्वर्धमानः स-
> हस्रसातमः सहस्रसुख्याकस्य धनस्यातिशयेन दाता त्वं नोऽस्माकं शं ऐहिकमामु-
> ष्मिकं च सुखं शोच । दीपय । वर्धयेत्यर्थः ॥ अविषः । अव रक्षणादिष्ठित्यस्माल्लेट
> सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् । अस्यार्थधातुकत्वादिट् । इतश्च लोप इति सिद इकारलोपः ।
> लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । निघातः । उक्षेषु । वच परिभाषणे । अस्मात्कर्मणि पात्य
> तुदिवचिरिचीत्यादिना थक् । कित्ता त्वंप्रसारणं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । देवहूतमः । ह्वय-
> तेः क्विप् । बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणपररूपत्वे । हल इति दीर्घः । कृदुत्तरपद-
> प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । शोच । शुच दीप्तौ । आयमंर्भावितण्यर्थः । निघातः । मरुद्वधः
> वृधु वर्धने । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । मरुद्वधादित्वात्पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं । सहस्र
> सातमः । षणु दाने । अस्य जनसनखनक्रमगमो विडिति विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्ये-
> त्याकारः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, protect us in the praise we make so that no deficiency or excess comes into it, and in the śastras such as the Ājya and Praüga that we recite; you who are the best invoker of the gods, grown strong through the Maruts and the great giver of thousandfold wealth, make our happiness in this world and the next shine and grow. The rest is grammar: अविषः (*aviṣaḥ*), उक्षेषु (*ukṣeṣu*), देवहूतमः (*devahūtamaḥ*), शोच (*śoca*), मरुद्वधः (*marudvadhaḥ*), सहस्रसातमः (*sahasrasātamaḥ*) (transcribed, not explained). *(Slips as supplied in the bhāṣya, e.g. मरुद्वधः (*marudvadhaḥ*) for the Saṃhitā's मरुद्वृधो (*marudvṛdho*) (sandhi form), प्रउगादि (*praugādi*) for प्रउगादि (*praugādi*), देवानामाहात्यृतमस्तु मुक्ते (*devānāmāhātyṛtamastu mukte*).)*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- (हे (*he*)) अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us (the performers of the sacrifice)
- ब्रह्मन् (*brahman*)—in the praise made by us
- अविषः (*aviṣaḥ*)—protect (so that there is no fault of deficiency or excess); (and) देवहूतमः (*devahūtamaḥ*)—you, the best among those who invite the gods
- उक्षेषु (*ukṣeṣu*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has उक्तेषु (*ukteṣu*))*—in the śastras such as the Praüga that (we recite) (अविषः (*aviṣaḥ*)—protect); (and) मरुद्वैधः (*marudvaidhaḥ*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has मरुद्वृधो (*marudvṛdho*) (sandhi form))*—you who are made to grow by the wind
- सहस्रसातमः (*sahasrasātamaḥ*)—the giver of (unmeasured) thousandfold wealth *(printed "ಧನದಾತ್ವವೂ", as supplied; the sentence runs over into p. 244)* you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- शं (*śaṃ*)—happiness (of both kinds, of this world and of the next)
- शोच (*śoca*)—make shine (increase *(the bracket is not closed in the print)*)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

And, O Agni, hotṛ of the gods *(printed "ದೇವಹೋತೃವಾದ")*, protect us so that there is no deficiency or excess in the śastra-mantras of the Praüga type that we recite and in the other praises; you who are made to grow by the wind and are the giver of unmeasured wealth, grant us both kinds of happiness, of this world and of the next *(printed "ಐಹಿಕಾಮುಷ್ಟಿಕ", as supplied)*.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Perfect our prayer, Invoker of the gods, as well as our hymns : Agni, who increase [sic] with the winds and are the giver of thousands, augment our felicity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ब्रह्मन्—ब्रह्मणि अस्माभिः क्रियमाणे स्तोत्रे न्यूनातिरेकदोषो यथा न भवति कथा पालय (*brahman—brahmaṇi asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇe stotre nyūnātirekadoṣo yathā na bhavati kathā pālaya*) *(so printed, कथा (*kathā*) where the bhāṣya has तथा (*tathā*))*. The word ब्रह्म (*brahma*) is stated both among the names of food (Ni. 3.9) and among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9) *(both references as printed)*.

यामथर्वा मनुषिता दध्यजधियमत्नत । तस्मिन् ब्रह्माणि पूर्वथेंद्र उक्ता समग्मतार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥ (*yāmatharvā manuṣitā dadhyajadhiyamatnata | tasmin brahmāṇi pūrvatheṃdra uktā samagmatārcannanu svarājyaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-16)

Here the meaning is described as ब्रह्माणि कर्माणि (*brahmāṇi karmāṇi*), "rites".

यजां त्वः पोषमास्ते पुपुष्पान् गायत्रं श्वो गायति शक्वरीषु । ब्रह्मा श्वो वदति जातविद्यां यज्ञस्य मात्रां वि मिमीत उ त्वः ॥ (*yajāṃ tvaḥ poṣamāste pupuṣpān gāyatraṃ śvo gāyati śakvarīṣu | brahmā śvo vadati jātavidyāṃ yajñasya mātrāṃ vi mimīta u tvaḥ ‖*) (Pu. Saṃ. 10-71-11) *(reference printed "ಪು. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

ब्रह्मा.. सर्वविद्यः सर्वं वेदितुमर्हति बृंहः परि ब्रह्मः श्रुततो ब्रह्म परि ब्रह्मं सर्वतः । ब्रह्मैको जाते जाते विद्यां वदति । (*brahmā.. sarvavidyaḥ sarvaṃ veditumarhati bṛṃhaḥ pari brahmaḥ śrutato brahma pari brahmaṃ sarvataḥ | brahmaiko jāte jāte vidyāṃ vadati |*) Here it is said that the word ब्रह्म (*brahma*) conveys the meaning of one priest (ऋत्विक् (*ṛtvik*)). Sāyaṇa, stating that the word ब्रह्म (*brahma*) is used in the sense of the sacrificial rite in hand, expresses the wish that Agni protect us so that no deficiency or variation, such as may possibly occur here and there in the hymns on the deities recited in the sacrifice, arises.

देवहूतमः उक्तेषु अविषः—देवानामाह्वातृतमः त्वं अस्माभिः क्रियमाणेषु आज्यप्रउगादिशस्त्रेषु गोपाय (*devahūtamaḥ ukteṣu aviṣaḥ—devānāmāhvātṛtamaḥ tvaṃ asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇeṣu ājyapraugādiśastreṣu gopāya*). It is expressed as a wish that Agni, the best of the priests called hotṛ who invite the gods to accept the share of the oblation in the sacrifice, protect the sacrificers both at the time of reciting the śastra-mantras that praise the qualities of the deities in the sacrifices they perform, and in the praise-recitations of the Ājya, Praüga and so on.

### Printed p. 245

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued from p. 244: the discussion of मरुद्वधः (*marudvadhaḥ*) begins on this page.)*

मरुद्वधः—मरुद्भिः वर्धमानः (*marudvadhaḥ—marudbhiḥ vardhamānaḥ*)—"grown by the Maruts". The word मरुत् (*marut*) is listed among the names of gold (Ni. 2-10), and among the names of priests *(printed "ಋತ್ವಿಜ್ಞಾ ಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ", as supplied, apparently a slip for "names of priests")* as मरुतः (*marutaḥ*) (Ni. 3-19). In the passage मरुतः मित्रराविणो वा मितरोचनो वा महत् द्रवंतीति वा (*marutaḥ mitrarāviṇo vā mitarocano vā mahat dravaṃtīti vā*) (Ni. 11-14) *(मितरोचनो (*mitarocano*) as supplied)* the explanation of the word मरुत् (*marut*) is given as: those who make many kinds of sound, those who shine and blaze exceedingly, those who pour down rain abundantly. Here the meaning is set out as: Agni is made to grow either by the gods or by the winds.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes (noted briefly; the sūtra numbers are as printed):

अविषः (*aviṣaḥ*)—root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*); second person singular of the लेट् (*leṭ*) with सिप् (*sip*) (सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*), Pā. Sū. 3-1-34); the final *i* is dropped by इतश्चलोपः परस्मैपदेषु (*itaścalopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97); the augment *aṭ* by लेटोडाटौ (*leṭoḍāṭau*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94); the augment *iṭ* by अर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (*ardhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35); *ṣatva* after *iṇ*, *rutva* and visarga for the suffix *s*; the finite-verb *nighāta* accent.

उक्षेषु (*ukṣeṣu*) —root वच परिभाषणे (*vaca paribhāṣaṇe*); passive suffix थक् (*thak*) by पात्रृतःदिवचिरुचि (*pātrṛtaḥdivaciruci*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-164) *(the sūtra name is printed so)*; being mute *k*, the *va* of the root takes *samprasāraṇa* by वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (*vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-15) with the earlier form of *a*; *kutva* for *c* by चोःकुः (*coḥkuḥ*); the suffix accent makes it end-acute. Locative plural form.

देवहूतमः (*devahūtamaḥ*)—root हैञ् स्पर्धायां शब्देच (*haiñ spardhāyāṃ śabdeca*); the suffix *kvip* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76); *samprasāraṇa* of the root by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) with the earlier form ("ಪೂರೈರೂಪ" as printed); lengthening by हलः (*halaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-2); then the suffix *tamap* in the superlative sense; by गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*) the accent of the latter member in a *kṛt* compound stays.

शोच (*śoca*)—root शुच दीप्त (*śuca dīpta*) with the causative sense included; second person singular of लोट् (*loṭ*); finite-verb *nighāta* accent.

मरुद्वधः (*marudvadhaḥ*)—root वृधु वर्धने (*vṛdhu vardhane*); since the penultimate vowel is called *i* (ಇಕಾರ, as supplied), the suffix *ka* by इगुपधज्ञाप्रकरः कः (*igupadhajñāprakaraḥ kaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-135); the *k* is dropped as an *it* letter by लशक्वतद्धिते (*laśakvataddhite*); because it is mute *k*, no *guṇa* of the light penultimate vowel; in मरुद्वृधादि (*marudvṛdhādi*) words the first member keeps its final acute.

सहस्रसातमः (*sahasrasātamaḥ*)—root हुणु दाने (*huṇu dāne*) ; the suffix *viṭ* by जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् (*janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2.67 *(printed so)*); the root takes *ā* before it by विद्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् (*vidvanoranunāsikasyāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4.41 *(printed so)*) *(the sūtra number continues on p. 246)*; then *tamap* in the superlative sense; the *kṛt*-final accent of the latter member.

### Printed p. 246

*(The grammar note on सहस्रसातमः (*sahasrasātamaḥ*) continues from p. 245: "…ರಿಂದ ಇದು ಪರವಾದಾಗ ಧಾತುವಿಗೆ ಆತ್ವ" — the root takes *ā* when it follows; then the suffix *tamap* in the superlative sense, and the *kṛt* latter-member accent.)*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नू नो॑ रास्व स॒हस्र॑वत्तो॒कव॑त्पुष्टि॒मद्वसु॑ ।  
> द्यु॒मद॑ग्ने सु॒वीर्यं॒ वर्षि॑ष्ठ॒मनु॑पक्षितं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नु । नः । रास्व । सहस्रवत् । तोकवत् । पुष्टिमत् । वसु ।  
> द्युमत् । अग्ने । सुवीर्यं । वर्षिष्ठं । अनुपक्षितं ॥ ७ ॥

> *nu | naḥ | rāsva | sahasravat | tokavat | puṣṭimat | vasu |*  
> *dyumat | agne | suvīryaṃ | varṣiṣṭhaṃ | anupakṣitaṃ ‖ 7 ‖*

*(The printed Saṃhitā has नू (*nū*) and the Pada नु (*nu*); the Pada reads वर्षिष्ठं (*varṣiṣṭhaṃ*) where the bhāṣya has वर्षिष्टं (*varṣiṣṭaṃ*). Kept as supplied.)*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मिन् सूक्ते स्तूयमान हे आग्ने सहस्रवत्सहस्रसंख्योपेशं तोकवत्पु-
> त्रसौत्रादिसहितं पुष्टिमत्तोषकृत् । अनेन शरीरस्य क्षीरादिद्वारा बलारोग्यप्रदं
> गवादिकमुपलक्ष्यते । द्युमत् दीप्तिमत् । अनेन रत्नकनकादिकं परिगृह्यते । सु-
> वीर्यं शोभनसामर्थ्योपेतं तत्वत्कार्येषु व्यवहारयोग्यं वर्षिष्टमतिशयेन
> वृद्धं प्रभूतमत एवानुपक्षितं व्यये क्रियमाणेऽप्यनुपक्षीणं । एवंभूतं वसु
> रत्नकनकपश्वादिलक्षणं धनं नोऽस्मभ्यं नु क्षिप्रमनिलंबेन रास्व । दत्त्व ॥ नू नः ।
> ऋचि तुनुघमक्ष्पति दीर्घः । रास्व । रा नाने । अस्य लोटि रूपं । व्यत्ययेना-
> त्मनेपदं । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । निघातः । सहस्रवत् । मादुपधाया इति मतु-
> पो वत्वं । कर्दमादित्वान्मध्योदात्तः सहस्रशब्दः । पुष्टिमत् । पुष पुष् । अस्मात्
> क्तिच् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तः । ह्रस्वनुड्ड्यामिति मतुप उदात्तत्वं । वर्षिष्टं ।
> प्रियस्थिरेत्यादिना वृद्दस्य वर्षि इत्यादेशः । नित्वरः । अनुपक्षितं : क्षि क्षय इत्यस्य
> दीर्घाभावान्निष्ठानत्वं न भवति । तत्पुरुषत्पादव्ययपूर्वपद्मप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, praised in this hymn, quickly grant us wealth—of thousandfold number, with offspring and grandchildren, nourishing, bright, of good strength fit for worldly dealings, most abundant and therefore inexhaustible even when spent. The rest is grammar: नू नः (*nū naḥ*), रास्व (*rāsva*), सहस्रवत् (*sahasravat*), पुष्टिमत् (*puṣṭimat*), वर्षिष्टं (*varṣiṣṭaṃ*), अनुपक्षितं (*anupakṣitaṃ*) (transcribed, not explained). *(Slips as supplied in the bhāṣya: आग्ने (*āgne*), दत्त्व (*dattva*), तुनुघमक्ष्पति (*tunughamakṣpati*), वर्षिष्टं (*varṣiṣṭaṃ*) with ट (*ṭa*) against the Saṃhitā's ठ (*ṭha*), नाने (*nāne*).)*

- *(Ṛk 7.)* (हे (*he*)) अग्ने (*agne*)—(praised by this hymn) O Agni
- सहस्रवत् (*sahasravat*)—possessed of a thousandfold number *(printed "ಸಹಸ್ರಸಂಖ್ಯೋಪೇಶವೂ", as supplied)*
- शोकवत् (*śokavat*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has तोकवत् (*tokavat*))*—together with sons, grandsons and the like
- पुष्टिमत् (*puṣṭimat*)—(by giving milk through cows and the like) causing nourishment
- द्युमत् (*dyumat*)—(together with gems and the like) endowed with brilliance
- सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—*(the Pratipadārtha breaks here at the foot of p. 246 and continues on p. 247)*

### Printed p. 247

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 7, continued from p. 246.)* possessed of good strength (fit for worldly dealings) *(printed "ಶೋಭನಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯೋಪೇತವೂ (ವ್ಯವಹಾರಯೋಗ್ಯವೂ)")*; वर्षिष्टं (*varṣiṣṭaṃ*)—greatly increasing *(printed "ಆತಿಶಯವಾಗಿ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಕರವೂ")*; अनुपक्षितं (*anupakṣitaṃ*)—not diminishing (even when spent); वसु (*vasu*)—wealth (consisting of gems, gold, cattle and the like); नः (*naḥ*)—to us; नु (*nu*)—quickly; रास्व (*rāsva*)—grant *(printed "ಅನುಗಹಿಸು", as supplied)*.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, grant us wealth in the form of gems, gold, cattle and the like—immeasurable, accompanied by sons and grandsons, nourishing, shining, fit for worldly dealings, exceedingly increased *(printed "ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧವೂ", as supplied)*, and inexhaustible.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Grant us indeed, Agni, wealth (that may be counted) by thousands, and comprising offspring, nourishment, brilliant treasure, and vigour, and be infi-nite [sic] and inexhaustible.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुष्टिमत्— पोषकृत् अनेन शरीरस्य क्षीरादिद्वारा बलारोग्यप्रदं गवादिकं उपलक्ष्यते । (*puṣṭimat— poṣakṛt anena śarīrasya kṣīrādidvārā balārogyapradaṃ gavādikaṃ upalakṣyate |*) For the word पुष्टिमत् (*puṣṭimat*) the meaning "that which causes nourishment" is given. By this it is explained that cows and the like, the cause of the growth and health of the body through milk and so on, are meant as well.

द्युमत्—दीप्ति मत् (*dyumat—dīpti mat*) —since this is explained as "possessing lustre", it is also explained that wealth of this kind consists of gems, gold and the like.

सुवीर्यं—शोभनसामर्थ्योपेतं (*suvīryaṃ—śobhanasāmarthyopetaṃ*)—because wealth is the chief means both in worldly dealings and in carrying out the various rites, it is described as having great power.

वर्षिष्ठं अनुपक्षितं—अतिशयेन वृद्धं प्रभूतं आत एव व्यये क्रियमाणेपि अनुपक्षितं । (*varṣiṣṭhaṃ anupakṣitaṃ—atiśayena vṛddhaṃ prabhūtaṃ āta eva vyaye kriyamāṇepi anupakṣitaṃ |*) Since this is explained as "that which does not diminish even when spent through gifts, enjoyment and the like", the meaning is described as "very abundant".

It is expressed as a wish that Agni, praised by this hymn, grant us wealth in abundance; and since that wealth is of many kinds, its varieties are set out here. Wealth that is bounded by the number of a thousand is ordinary wealth. Good sons and grandsons are also one kind of wealth. Cows and the like, the means of milk and so on that increase the health and strength of the body, are also one kind of wealth. The ability that makes wealth fit for worldly dealings *(the sentence breaks off at the foot of p. 247, "ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುವ", and continues on p. 248)*

### Printed p. 248

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 7, continued from p. 247; the supplied text begins the page with the words below, the fragment "ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುವ" at the foot of p. 247 not being joined to them.)* Material of movable form is one kind of wealth. An inexhaustible treasure, which does not run out however much is spent but only goes on increasing, is also one kind of wealth. Agni is thus wished to grant us quickly all the many kinds of wealth made up of these varieties.

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar note, brief).*

On नू नः (*nū naḥ*): by the sūtra quoted (Pā. Sū. 6-3-133) the word नु (*nu*) takes a long vowel in the Saṃhitā. On रास्व (*rāsva*): root रा (*rā*) in the sense of giving; by व्यत्ययो बहुलं (*vyatyayo bahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85) it takes the ātmanepada; Loṭ, second person singular; the low pitch (nighāta) follows. On सहस्रवत् (*sahasravat*): the affix matup after सहस्र (*sahasra*) (meaning "that of which this is possessed"), with the m changed to v because the word stands in the Kardamādi group, so सहस्र (*sahasra*) has the accent on its middle syllable; तोकवत् (*tokavat*) likewise. On पुष्टिमत् (*puṣṭimat*): root पुष (*puṣa*) with the affix ktic, which being marked k prevents the guṇa of the short penultimate vowel; then matup, which is accented by ह्रस्वनुड्यां मतुप् (*hrasvanuḍyāṃ matup*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-166) because it follows a short vowel; द्युमत् (*dyumat*) likewise. On the next word the supplied text prints "ಸುವಿಯೆ:೯೦" *(as supplied, with a stray colon and numerals)*, then quotes a sūtra beginning वीर वीर्यौ च (*vīra vīryau ca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-120) giving the accent on the first syllable of the latter member. On वर्षिष्ठं (*varṣiṣṭhaṃ*): वृद्धः (*vṛddhaḥ*) in the superlative sense with the affix iṣṭhan, for which वृद्ध (*vṛddha*) is replaced by वर्षि (*varṣi*) by प्रियस्थिर (*priyasthira*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-157); the affix being marked n, the first syllable is accented (as the print has "ನಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ"). On अनुपक्षितं (*anupakṣitaṃ*): root क्षि (*kṣi*) in the sense of waning, affix kta; since there is no long vowel the t does not become n; as a tatpuruṣa compound it keeps the natural accent of its first member by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣe tulyārtha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2).

**The thirteenth sūkta is complete** (ಹದಿಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವು.)

## Sūkta 14 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The fourteenth sūkta** (ಹದಿನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ होतेति सप्तर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं । आ होतेत्यनुक्रमणिका । ऋषभस्त्विति
> तुशब्दप्रयोगादस्यापि सूक्तस्य ऋषभ ऋषिः । अनुक्तत्वात् त्रिष्टुप् । अग्निर्देवता ॥
> एतदादीनि दश सूक्तानि तृतीयाष्टमवर्जितानि प्रातरनुवाक आश्विनशस्त्रे त्रिष्टुभे
> छंदसि विनियुक्तानि । अथैतस्या इति खंडे सूत्रितं । आ होतेति दशानां तृतीया-
> ष्टमे उद्धरेदिति त्रिष्टुभं । आ. ४-१३ इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning आ होता (*ā hotā*) is the second sūkta of the second anuvāka; it has seven ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is listed as beginning आ होता (*ā hotā*). Because the sūtra uses the word ऋषभस्तु (*ṛṣabhastu*) with the particle tu, Ṛṣabha is the Ṛṣi of this sūkta too, as of the preceding one; the metre is Triṣṭubh; Agni is the deity. From this sūkta onward ten sūktas, omitting the third and the eighth, are to be applied to the Triṣṭubh ṛks of the Āśvina-śastra at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, as explained by the sūtra आ होतेति दशानां तृतीयाष्टमे उद्धरेदिति त्रिष्टुभं (*ā hoteti daśānāṃ tṛtīyāṣṭame uddharediti triṣṭubhaṃ*) in the section अथैतस्या (*athaitasyā*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 4-13).

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 14. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 14. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 1; Varga 14. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: printed "ಋಷಿ?—ಋಷಭೋಃ ವೈಶ್ವಾಮಿತ್ರಃ" [sic] (the "?" after the word for Ṛṣi and the visarga of Ṛṣabha as supplied), that is Ṛṣabha Vaiśvāmitra. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Ṛṣabha praises Agni: the invoker of the gods, delighter, true, most wise, sacrificer and creator, he comes to our sacrifices; with lightning for chariot and flames for hair, son of strength, he spreads his radiance on the wide earth, or takes up strength there. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होता (*hotā*)—(invoking the gods to the sacrifices) the invoker
- मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—(to the worshipper) the giver of joy
- सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)—(doer of works of true fruit) of true nature
- कवितमः (*kavitamaḥ*)—the best of the wise
- यज्वा (*yajvā*)—the (divine) performer of the sacrifice
- वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*)—(the one who) created (the world)
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- विदथानि (*vidathāni*)—(the sacrifices that we perform), having them in view; आ अस्थात् (*ā asthāt*)—arrives; (and) विद्युद्रथः (*vidyudrathaḥ*)—possessed of a vehicle that is a mass of radiance (or having lightning for chariot)
- शोचिष्कशः (*śociṣkaśaḥ*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has शोचिष्केशः (*śociṣkeśaḥ*))*—having flames for hair; सहसः पुत्रः (*sahasaḥ putraḥ*)—the son of strength
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—in the wide atmosphere
- पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—his radiance
- अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—sheds; or पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—on the earth
- पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—(his) strength
- अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—makes use of (displays)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the invoker of the gods, the giver of joy to the worshipper, of true nature, the best of the wise, the performer of the sacrifices of the gods and the creator of the world, comes to our sacrifices. And that Agni, who has lightning for chariot, flames for hair, and is the son of strength, makes known his power on the earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

एतदादीनि........प्रातरनुवाके आश्विनशस्त्रे त्रैष्टुभे छंदसि विनियुक्तानि ॥ (*etadādīni........prātaranuvāke āśvinaśastre traiṣṭubhe chaṃdasi viniyuktāni ‖*) (Sā. Bhā. Pīṭhikā, as supplied)

Sāyaṇa states in the introduction to his bhāṣya that this sūkta, addressed to Agni, and the sūktas that follow it are applied in the Āśvina-śastra, which belongs to the Prātaranuvāka. Here it is necessary to know the connection between the Āśvina-śastra and the Agni-sūkta, and the special character of the Prātaranuvāka. The story that indicates the connection between the Āśvina-śastra and the Agni-sūkta is told in the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa as follows *(the print has "ಇ. ಬ್ರಾ.")*.

प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञे दुहितरं प्रायच्छत्सूर्यां सावित्रीं तस्यॆ सर्वे देवा वरा आगच्छंस्तस्या एतत्सहस्रं वहतुमन्वाकरोद्यदेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षतेऽनाश्विनं हैव तद्यदर्वाक्सहस्रं तस्मात्तत्सहस्रं वैव शंसेद्भूयो वा प्राश्य घृतं शंसेद्यथा ह वा इदमनो वा रथो वाक्तो वर्तत एवं हैवाक्तो वर्तते । शकुनिरिवोत्पतिष्यन्नाह्वयीत । (*prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchatsūryāṃ sāvitrīṃ tasyè sarve devā varā āgacchaṃstasyā etatsahasraṃ vahatumanvākarodyadetadāśvinamityācakṣate 'nāśvinaṃ haiva tadyadarvāksahasraṃ tasmāttatsahasraṃ vaiva śaṃsedbhūyo vā prāśya ghṛtaṃ śaṃsedyathā ha vā idamano vā ratho vākto vartata evaṃ haivākto vartate | śakunirivotpatiṣyannāhvayīta |*) (I. Brā. 17-1)

Formerly, when Prajāpati resolved to give his daughter Sūryā to Soma in marriage, all the gods came, each desiring to choose her as his bride. Prajāpati then laid down a rule that the thousand mantras known as the Āśvina-śastra must be recited, and not fewer. Just as in the world a chariot wheel, once it has been sprinkled with oil, moves easily, so after drinking ghee the mantras can be recited easily; therefore one should first drink ghee and then recite. And just as a bird, when ready to fly, makes its body light, so the suitor who longs for her must have that quality.

तस्मिन्देवा न समजानत ममेदमस्तु ममेदमस्त्विति ते संजानाना अब्रुवन्नाजिमस्यायामहै स यो न उज्जेष्यति तस्येदं भविष्यतीति तेग्ने रेवाधि गृहपतेरादित्यं काष्ठामकुर्वत तस्मादाग्नेयी प्रतिपद्भवत्याश्विनस्याग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेति । (*tasmindevā na samajānata mamedamastu mamedamastviti te saṃjānānā abruvannājimasyāyāmahai sa yo na ujjeṣyati tasyedaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tegne revādhi gṛhapaterādityaṃ kāṣṭhāmakurvata tasmādāgneyī pratipadbhavatyāśvinasyāgnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājeti |*) (I. Brā. 17-1)

### Printed p. 252

*(Continuation of the Kannada explanation of the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa passage quoted at the end of p. 251.)* Then the gods, not wishing to fight one another, agreed together that all of them should take part in a contest, and that whoever won in that contest should be fit to wed her. Then they ran, from Agni, the lord of the house (Gṛhapati), as far as the Sun. Therefore one opinion is that the first mantra,

स त्वं दक्षस्यावृको वृधो भूरर्यः परस्यांतरस्य तरुषः । रायः सूनो सहसो मर्त्यैष्वा छर्दिर्यच्छ वीतहव्याय सप्रथो भरद्वाजाय सप्रथः ॥ (*sa tvaṃ dakṣasyāvṛko vṛdho bhūraryaḥ parasyāṃtarasya taruṣaḥ | rāyaḥ sūno sahaso martyaiṣvā chardiryaccha vītahavyāya sapratho bharadvājāya saprathaḥ ‖*) (the print has "ಮ. ಸಂ." for the Saṃhitā, as supplied; 6-15-3)

is addressed to Agni; and another opinion is that one should begin with the mantra

अग्निं मन्ये पितरमग्निमापिमग्निं भ्रातरं सदमित्सखायं । अग्नेरनीकं बृहतः सपर्यं दिवि शुक्रं यजतं सूरस्य ॥ (*agniṃ manye pitaramagnimāpimagniṃ bhrātaraṃ sadamitsakhāyaṃ | agneranīkaṃ bṛhataḥ saparyaṃ divi śukraṃ yajataṃ sūrasya ‖*) (the print has "ಮ. ಸಂ." again, as supplied; 10-7-3).

But this is not acceptable. [The Brāhmaṇa says:]

तत्तन्नादृत्यं ।..................तस्मादग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेत्येशयैव प्रतिपद्येत गृहपतिवती प्रजातिमती शांता सर्वायुः सर्वायुत्वाय । सर्वमायुरेति य एवं वेद ॥ (*tattannādṛtyaṃ |..................tasmādagnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājetyeśayaiva pratipadyeta gṛhapativatī prajātimatī śāṃtā sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya | sarvamāyureti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) *(the dotted gap is in the print)*

It is proper to begin with mantras such as अग्निर्होता गृहपतिः (*agnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ*). Those who know this principle obtain all wealth and become long-lived, it says. And further:

तासां वै देवशानामाजिं धावंतीनामभिसृष्टानामग्निर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यत तमश्विनावन्नागच्छतां तमब्रूतामपोदिह्यावां वा इदं जेष्याव इति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्त्वस्य वै ममेहाप्यस्त्विति तथेति तस्मा अप्यत्राकुरुतां तस्मादाग्नेयमाश्विने शस्यते । (*tāsāṃ vai devaśānāmājiṃ dhāvaṃtīnāmabhisṛṣṭānāmagnirmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyata tamaśvināvannāgacchatāṃ tamabrūtāmapodihyāvāṃ vā idaṃ jeṣyāva iti sa tathetyabravīttvasya vai mamehāpyastviti tatheti tasmā apyatrākurutāṃ tasmādāgneyamāśvine śasyate |*) *(so printed: देवशानामाजिं (*devaśānāmājiṃ*) and तमश्विनावन्नागच्छतां (*tamaśvināvannāgacchatāṃ*) as supplied)*

While all the gods were running in this contest, Agni went ahead of all. Then the Aśvin gods approached Agni and asked him: "Leave us the way; help us to win in this contest." Agni agreed to that, but asked that in the victory he too should have a share. For that reason he too has a share in the Āśvina-śastra.

On this occasion another objection is raised and the answer to it is given:

तदाहुर्यच्छस्यत आग्नेयं शस्यत उषस्यं शस्यत ऐंद्रमथ कस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षत इत्यश्विनौ हि तदुदजयतामश्विनावाश्नुवातां यदश्विना उदजयतामश्विनावाश्नुवातां तस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षते । (*tadāhuryacchasyata āgneyaṃ śasyata uṣasyaṃ śasyata aiṃdramatha kasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣata ityaśvinau hi tadudajayatāmaśvināvāśnuvātāṃ yadaśvinā udajayatāmaśvināvāśnuvātāṃ tasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣate |*) (I. Brā. 17-2)

### Printed p. 253

Since on this occasion mantras addressed to Agni, to Indra and to Uṣas have to be recited, the objection arises: how does the name Āśvina-śastra come to be given to all of these? The answer is that, because this is recited mainly with reference to the victory of the Aśvin gods, these mantras bear this name.

Here it is necessary to explain what the Prātaranuvāka is. In performing the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice the day on which the soma juice is pressed out is called Sutyā-dina or Stutyā-dina. On the morning of this day, before sunrise (the print has "ಸೂದ್ಯೋದಯ" *[sic]*), as soon as the Adhvaryu has recited the Praiṣa mantra देवेभ्यः प्रातरावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहि (*devebhyaḥ prātarāvabhyo hotaranubrūhi*) *(as supplied; the Brāhmaṇa quotation on p. 254 has प्रातरावाभ्यो (*prātarāvābhyo*))*, the Hotṛ recites certain mantras. These are called the Prātaranuvāka mantras. The Hotṛ must recite these Prātaranuvāka mantras. This is stated in the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa itself: देवेभ्यः प्रातरावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः (*devebhyaḥ prātarāvabhyo hotaranubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 2-15).

The procedure the Hotṛ follows in reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras is now described in detail. The Adhvaryu, who plays the part of the chief officiant (ṛtvij) in the sacrifice, has again and again to say to the other officiants "you must make such-and-such a recitation" and the like; such sentences are called Praiṣas. In the present case the Adhvaryu addresses the Hotṛ with देवेभ्यःप्रातरावभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहि (*devebhyaḥprātarāvabhyo hotaranubrūhi*): "O Hotṛ, recite the Prātaranuvāka mantras to the gods." Then the Hotṛ goes to the fire-pit called Āgnīdhra and there, for purification of speech (the print has "ವಾಚ್ಯುದ್ಧಿ" *[sic]*), makes one oblation of ghee, and in the Āhavanīya fire two oblations of ghee, with the prescribed mantras. Then he enters the hall called Havirdhāna by the eastern door, sits near the yoke of the carts that are there, and first recites this mantra:

आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्वः क्रतुं च भद्रं बिभृतामृतं च । रायश्च स्थ स्वपत्यस्य पत्निः सरस्वती तद्गृणते वयो धात् ॥ (*āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasvaḥ kratuṃ ca bhadraṃ bibhṛtāmṛtaṃ ca | rāyaśca stha svapatyasya patniḥ sarasvatī tadgṛṇate vayo dhāt ‖*) (the print has "ಮ.ಸಂ." for the Saṃhitā, as supplied; 10-30-12)

After that he recites the Prātaranuvāka mantras addressed to Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin gods. These are in three parts. The mantras recited to Agni are called Āgneya-kratu, those recited to Uṣas Uṣasya-kratu, and those recited to the Aśvin gods Āśvina-kratu. To show that the mantras addressed to each deity must be in all seven metres, there is a repetition (the print has "ವೀಷ್ಟೆ" *[sic]*; "it is doubled"): सप्तभिः सप्तभिः छंदोभिः (*saptabhiḥ saptabhiḥ chaṃdobhiḥ*). Accordingly the account of these mantras is as follows.

*(The following lines are set in the print as a list, each beginning with the opening words of a ṛk, then its reference, then the metre; in the print the second and later lines use ditto marks, which are not reproduced here: the Ṛgveda references are given as printed, with ditto "Ṛ. Saṃ." understood. First, for Agni:)*

- त्वमग्ने वसून् (*tvamagne vasūn*) (ditto 1-45-1) इत्यादिष्टनुष्टुप् च्छंदः । (*ityādiṣṭanuṣṭup cchaṃdaḥ |*) *(so printed: इत्यादिष्टनुष्टुप् (*ityādiṣṭanuṣṭup*))*
