तान्येतान्याश्विने प्रातरनुवाके सप्तछंदांसि । (*tānyetānyāśvine prātaranuvāke saptachaṃdāṃsi |*) These seven are the Prātaranuvāka mantras addressed to the Aśvin gods and belonging to the Āśvina-kratu. The greatness of these Prātaranuvāka mantras is described in the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa, which explains its spiritual background as follows:

देवेभ्यः प्रातरावाभ्यो होतरनुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः । एते वाव देवाः प्रातरावाणो यदग्निरुषा अश्विनौ त एते सप्तभिः सप्तभिश्चंदोभिरागच्छंति । अस्य देवाः प्रातरावाणो हवं गच्छंति य एवं वेद । प्रजापत् वै स्वयं होतरि प्रातरनुवाकमनुवक्ष्यत्युभये देवासुरा यज्ञमुपावसन्नस्मभ्यमनुवक्ष्यत्यस्मभ्यमिति स वै देवेभ्य एवान्वब्रवीत् । (*devebhyaḥ prātarāvābhyo hotaranubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ | ete vāva devāḥ prātarāvāṇo yadagniruṣā aśvinau ta ete saptabhiḥ saptabhiścaṃdobhirāgacchaṃti | asya devāḥ prātarāvāṇo havaṃ gacchaṃti ya evaṃ veda | prajāpat vai svayaṃ hotari prātaranuvākamanuvakṣyatyubhaye devāsurā yajñamupāvasannasmabhyamanuvakṣyatyasmabhyamiti sa vai devebhya evānvabravīt |*) *(so printed: प्रातरावाभ्यो (*prātarāvābhyo*), प्रजापत् (*prajāpat*); the passage and its explanation continue on p. 255, and no reference number is printed yet)*

### Printed p. 255

*(The Aitareya-brāhmaṇa quotation begun on p. 254 continues; the print has a row of dots in its middle, which is kept as "……" here.)*

ततो वै देवा अभवन्परासुराः भवत्यात्मना परास्य द्विषन् पाप्मा भ्रातृव्यो भवति य एवं वेद । प्रातर्वै स तं देवेभ्योऽन्वब्रवीद्यत्पातरनुवाकस्य प्रातरनुवाकत्वं । महति रात्र्या अनूच्यः सर्वस्य वाचः सर्वस्य ब्रह्मणः परिगृहीत्यै यो वै भवति यः श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते तस्य वाचं प्रोदितामनुप्रववंति तस्मान्महति रात्र्या अनूच्यः (*tato vai devā abhavanparāsurāḥ bhavatyātmanā parāsya dviṣan pāpmā bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda | prātarvai sa taṃ devebhyo 'nvabravīdyatpātaranuvākasya prātaranuvākatvaṃ | mahati rātryā anūcyaḥ sarvasya vācaḥ sarvasya brahmaṇaḥ parigṛhītyai yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatāmaśnute tasya vācaṃ proditāmanupravavaṃti tasmānmahati rātryā anūcyaḥ*) …… यदा वा अध्वर्युरुपाकरोति वाचैवोपाकरोति वाचा होतान्नाह वाग्नि ब्रह्म तत्र स काम उपाप्तोयो वाचि च ब्रह्मणि च ॥ (*yadā vā adhvaryurupākaroti vācaivopākaroti vācā hotānnāha vāgni brahma tatra sa kāma upāptoyo vāci ca brahmaṇi ca ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 7-5; the print has "ಇ. ಬ್ರಾ.", as supplied) *(the words भवति य एवं वेद (*bhavati ya evaṃ veda*) and वाग्नि (*vāgni*) stand so in the supplied text; प्रोदितामनुप्रववंति (*proditāmanupravavaṃti*) is the supplied joining of a word broken at a line end)*

Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin gods are the deities who move about in the early morning. Each of these deities is possessed of a sattva-metre (the print has सत्त्वच्छंदस्सन्नुळ्ळवरागिद्दारॆ (*sattvacchaṃdassannuḷḷavarāgiddārè*), "are possessed of a sattva-metre"). They come to the man who knows this principle. Once, when Prajāpati himself was the Hotṛ, the gods on one side and the asuras on the other were consecrated for the sacrifice, and both groups imagined that Prajāpati would recite the Prātaranuvāka for their own sacrifice. But Prajāpati recited it for the gods alone. By this the gods conquered, and the asuras were defeated. Because this was recited (the print has पासिद्दरिंद (*pāsiddariṃda*), as supplied; evidently "recited" is meant) in the morning, it became famous as the Prātaranuvāka; and for its power to appear in full it must be recited in the depth of the middle of the night. Since speech itself is of the nature of Brahman, if this is recited the desired object is obtained.

प्रजापत् स्वयं होतरि प्रातरनुवाकमनुवक्ष्यति सर्वा देवता आशंसंतमामभि प्रतिपत्स्यति मामभीति स प्रजापतिरैक्षत यद्येकां देवतामादिष्टामभि प्रतिपत्स्सामीतरामेकेन देवता उपाप्ता भविष्यंतीति स एतामृचमपश्यदापो रेवतीरित्पपो वै सर्वा देवता रेवत्यः सर्वा देवताः स एतयर्चा प्रातरनुवाकं प्रत्यपद्यत ताः सर्वा देवताः प्रामोदंत मामभि प्रत्यपादि मामभीति । सर्वा हास्मिन् देवताः प्रातरनुवाकमनुब्रुवति प्रमोदंते सर्वाभिर्हास्य देवताभिः प्रातरनुवाकः प्रतिपन्नो भवति य एवं वेद । (*prajāpat svayaṃ hotari prātaranuvākamanuvakṣyati sarvā devatā āśaṃsaṃtamāmabhi pratipatsyati māmabhīti sa prajāpatiraikṣata yadyekāṃ devatāmādiṣṭāmabhi pratipatssāmītarāmekena devatā upāptā bhaviṣyaṃtīti sa etāmṛcamapaśyadāpo revatīritpapo vai sarvā devatā revatyaḥ sarvā devatāḥ sa etayarcā prātaranuvākaṃ pratyapadyata tāḥ sarvā devatāḥ prāmodaṃta māmabhi pratyapādi māmabhīti | sarvā hāsmin devatāḥ prātaranuvākamanubruvati pramodaṃte sarvābhirhāsya devatābhiḥ prātaranuvākaḥ pratipanno bhavati ya evaṃ veda |*) (Ai. Brā. 7-6) *(so printed: प्रजापत् (*prajāpat*), रेवतीरित्पपो (*revatīritpapo*), एतयर्चा (*etayarcā*), as supplied)*

When Prajāpati was ready, as Hotṛ, to recite the Prātaranuvāka, each one of the deities was waiting with curiosity, thinking "he will recite it addressed to me". Then Prajāpati fell into a dilemma: if he addressed only one deity, how was he to win the other deities? Thinking so, he finally addressed the waters (the print has अप्पन्नुद्देशिसि (*appannuddeśisi*), "addressing the waters"), which embody all the deities, and recited

आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्वः क्रतुं च भद्रं बिभृतामृतं च । रायश्च स्थ स्वपत्यस्य पत्निः सरस्वती तद्गृणते वयो धात् ॥ (*āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasvaḥ kratuṃ ca bhadraṃ bibhṛtāmṛtaṃ ca | rāyaśca stha svapatyasya patniḥ sarasvatī tadgṛṇate vayo dhāt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-30-2)

### Printed p. 256

This mantra he recited. By this all the deities were satisfied. Therefore he who, knowing this principle, recites the Prātaranuvāka obtains the favour of all the deities.

तिस्रो देवता अन्वाह त्रयो वा इमे त्रिवृशो लोका विषामेव लोकानामभिजित्यै ॥ (*tisro devatā anvāha trayo vā ime trivṛśo lokā viṣāmeva lokānāmabhijityai ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 7-8) *(so printed: त्रिवृशो (*trivṛśo*), विषामेव (*viṣāmeva*))*

Agni, Uṣas (the print has उपस्सु (*upassu*) [sic]) and the Aśvin gods, these three, are the lords of the three worlds; so the mantras recited addressed to them become the means of obtaining the three worlds. This being said, another doubt arises here; foreseeing that doubt, the answer is given to it in this way.

तदाहुः कथमनूच्यः प्रातरनुवाक इति । यथाच्छंदसमनूच्यः प्रातरनुवाकः प्रजापतेर्वा एतान्यंगानि यच्छंदांस्येष उ एव प्रजापतिर्यो यजते यद्यजमानाय हितं । पच्चोऽनूच्यः प्रातरनुवाकश्चतुष्पादा वै पशवः पशूनामवरुद्धै (*tadāhuḥ kathamanūcyaḥ prātaranuvāka iti | yathācchaṃdasamanūcyaḥ prātaranuvākaḥ prajāpatervā etānyaṃgāni yacchaṃdāṃsyeṣa u eva prajāpatiryo yajate yadyajamānāya hitaṃ | pacco 'nūcyaḥ prātaranuvākaścatuṣpādā vai paśavaḥ paśūnāmavaruddhai*) …… *(a long row of dots in the print)* …… आहुतिभागा वा अन्या देवता अन्याः स्तोमभागाश्चंदोभागास्ता या अग्नावाहुतॆयो हूयंते ताभिराहुतिभागाः प्रीणातृथ यत्स्तुवंति च शंसंति च तेन स्तोमभागाश्चंदोभागाः । उभयो हास्मैता देवताः प्रीता अभीष्टा भवंति य एवं वेद ॥ (*āhutibhāgā vā anyā devatā anyāḥ stomabhāgāścaṃdobhāgāstā yā agnāvāhutèyo hūyaṃte tābhirāhutibhāgāḥ prīṇātṛtha yatstuvaṃti ca śaṃsaṃti ca tena stomabhāgāścaṃdobhāgāḥ | ubhayo hāsmaitā devatāḥ prītā abhīṣṭā bhavaṃti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) *(so printed: पच्चोऽनूच्यः (*pacco 'nūcyaḥ*), प्रीणातृथ (*prīṇātṛtha*), यच्छंदांस्येष (*yacchaṃdāṃsyeṣa*); no reference is printed after this passage here; the next reference printed is the one given below)*

To the question what is the procedure for reciting the Prātaranuvāka, the answer is that the correct procedure according to the rules is to recite it in metrical form and following the order of the prescribed metres. Why? Because the metres are the limbs of Prajāpati, and Prajāpati is himself the sacrificer. And since animals are walkers on feet, in order to obtain them the Prātaranuvāka must be recited foot by foot. Having thus explained the order of recitation, the text foresees another doubt. It is this:

अभूदुषा रुशत्पशुरित्युत्तमया परिवधाति । तदाहुर्यस्त्रीन्यत्रूनन्वाहाग्नियमुषस्यमाश्विनं कथमस्यैकयर्चा परिदधतः सर्वे त्रयः क्रतवः परिहिता भवंतीति । अभूदुषा रुशत्पशुरित्युषसो रूपमाग्निरधाय्यत्विय इत्यग्नेरयोजि वां वृषण्वसू रथो दस्रावमर्त्यो माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवमित्यश्विनोरेवमुहास्यैकयर्चा परिदधतः सर्वे त्रयः क्रतवः परिहिता भवंति भवंति ॥ (*abhūduṣā ruśatpaśurityuttamayā parivadhāti | tadāhuryastrīnyatrūnanvāhāgniyamuṣasyamāśvinaṃ kathamasyaikayarcā paridadhataḥ sarve trayaḥ kratavaḥ parihitā bhavaṃtīti | abhūduṣā ruśatpaśurityuṣaso rūpamāgniradhāyyatviya ityagnerayoji vāṃ vṛṣaṇvasū ratho dasrāvamartyo mādhvī mama śrutaṃ havamityaśvinorevamuhāsyaikayarcā paridadhataḥ sarve trayaḥ kratavaḥ parihitā bhavaṃti bhavaṃti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 7-8; as printed, the same reference as the one above) *(so printed: परिवधाति (*parivadhāti*), यस्त्रीन्यत्रूनन्वाहाग्नियमुषस्यमाश्विनं (*yastrīnyatrūnanvāhāgniyamuṣasyamāśvinaṃ*), रधाय्यत्विय (*radhāyyatviya*), भवंति भवंति (*bhavaṃti bhavaṃti*))*

Since the Prātaranuvāka has to be recited addressed to all these deities, Agni, Uṣas and the Aśvin gods, the question arises, in the present case, how, when the conclusion is spoken with the one mantra

अभूदुषा दुशत्पशुराग्नि रधाय्यृत्वियः । (*abhūduṣā duśatpaśurāgni radhāyyṛtviyaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-75-9)

all the rites addressed to all the deities are brought to completion. *(In the printed bhāṣya the words read रुशत्पशुरित्युत्तमया (*ruśatpaśurityuttamayā*); here the Ṛk quotation has दुशत्पशुराग्नि (*duśatpaśurāgni*) and रधाय्यृत्वियः (*radhāyyṛtviyaḥ*) as a separate word; the readings रुशत्पशु (*ruśatpaśu*) and दुशत्पशु (*duśatpaśu*) differ, and both are kept as supplied.)*

### Printed p. 257

The answer to that question is shown by explaining that in this very mantra there is also the praise of the three deities. This is the greatness of the Prātaranuvāka.

होता (*hotā*) — the one who invites, with the several mantras, the deities who are to come to receive their share of the oblation in the sacrifice is called a Hotṛ. Since Agni himself is designated here by the word Hotṛ, the identity (तादात्म (*tādātma*), so printed) with this Hotṛ is said of Agni. And since the function of inviting the deities belongs to Agni alone, the meaning देवानां आह्वाता (*devānāṃ āhvātā*) is explained.

Explaining the formation of this word, the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa says as follows.

यज्ञो वै देवेभ्य उदक्रामत्तमिष्टिभिः प्रैषमैच्छन्यदिष्टिभिः प्रैषमैच्छंस्तदिष्टीनामिष्टित्वं तमन्वविंदन् । अनुवित्तयज्ञो राध्योति य एवं वेद । आहूतयो वै नामैता यदाहुतय एताभिर्वै देवान्यजमानो ह्वयति तदाहुतीनामाहूतित्वं। ऊतयः खलु वै ता नाम याभिर्देना यजमानस्य हवमायंति ये वै पंथानो याः स्रुतयस्ता वा ऊतयस्त उ एवैतत्स्वर्गयाणा यजमानस्य भवंति । (*yajño vai devebhya udakrāmattamiṣṭibhiḥ praiṣamaicchanyadiṣṭibhiḥ praiṣamaicchaṃstadiṣṭīnāmiṣṭitvaṃ tamanvaviṃdan | anuvittayajño rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda | āhūtayo vai nāmaitā yadāhutaya etābhirvai devānyajamāno hvayati tadāhutīnāmāhūtitvaṃ| ūtayaḥ khalu vai tā nāma yābhirdenā yajamānasya havamāyaṃti ye vai paṃthāno yāḥ srutayastā vā ūtayasta u evaitatsvargayāṇā yajamānasya bhavaṃti |*) (Ai. Brā. 1-2) *(so printed: उदक्रामत्तमिष्टिभिः (*udakrāmattamiṣṭibhiḥ*), राध्योति (*rādhyoti*), देना (*denā*), स्रुतयस्ता (*srutayastā*))*

Once the sacrifice went away from the gods. Then they got it back by making offerings (आहुति (*āhuti*)). An offering means an oblation made by calling on the name of a deity. If it is said that the one who makes such an offering is called Hotṛ, then another question arises.

तदाहुर्यदन्यो जुहोत्यथ योऽनु चाह यजति च कस्मात्तं होतेत्याचक्षत इति यद्वाव स तत्र यथाभाजनं देवता अमुमावहामुमावहेत्यानाहयति तदेव होतुर्होतृत्वं होता भवति। होतेत्येनमाचक्षते य एवं वेद ॥ (*tadāhuryadanyo juhotyatha yo 'nu cāha yajati ca kasmāttaṃ hotetyācakṣata iti yadvāva sa tatra yathābhājanaṃ devatā amumāvahāmumāvahetyānāhayati tadeva hoturhotṛtvaṃ hotā bhavati| hotetyenamācakṣate ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 1-2) *(so printed: मावहेत्यानाहयति (*māvahetyānāhayati*))*

The one who offers the oblation is one person; the one who gives the invitation for the offering and utters the mantra is another. Even so, how is the name Hotṛ proper for the one who utters the offering mantra? To this question the answer is that, since the one who recites this mantra calls the several deities according to the measure of the several offerings, the name Hotṛ is proper for him too; and having said this, the text goes on:

मनो वै यज्ञस्य मैत्रावरुणो वाग्यज्ञस्य होता (*mano vai yajñasya maitrāvaruṇo vāgyajñasya hotā*) (Ai. Brā. 6-5)

By this sentence the identity (तादात्म्य (*tādātmya*)) of the speech that recites the mantra with the Hotṛ is stated. And further, *(the sentence is completed on p. 258; the print has a stray number "33" at the foot of the page, probably the signature mark of the sheet, kept as supplied)*

### Printed p. 258

सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वानित्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैष स्वो लोको यदुत्तरवेदीनाभिः (*sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvānityagnirvai devānāṃ hotā tasyaiṣa svo loko yaduttaravedīnābhiḥ*) …… *(a row of dots in the print)* …… निहोता होतृषदने विदान इत्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैतद्भोतृषदनं यदुत्तरवेदीनाभिः । (*nihotā hotṛṣadane vidāna ityagnirvai devānāṃ hotā tasyaitadbhotṛṣadanaṃ yaduttaravedīnābhiḥ |*) (Ai. Brā. 5-2; the print has "ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ." here and "ಇ. ಬ್ರಾ." above, as supplied) *(so printed: भोतृषदनं (*bhotṛṣadanaṃ*))*

These and similar sentences address Agni, the accomplisher of the oblation, as the Hotṛ of the gods. Therefore in the present ṛk the word होतारं (*hotāraṃ*) can be explained as होमनिष्पादकं, आह्वातारं वा (*homaniṣpādakaṃ, āhvātāraṃ vā*) ("the accomplisher of the oblation, or the one who invites"). It is an epithet of Agni.

मंद्र (*maṃdra*) — स्तोतुः मादयिता। (*stotuḥ mādayitā|*) ("the one who gladdens the praiser"). Since the word मंद्र (*maṃdra*), formed from the root मदि (*madi*), which conveys the sense of joy (हर्ष (*harṣa*)), means "one who causes exceeding joy", it is said that Agni makes those who praise him exceedingly glad. This word is read in the list of words for speech (the print has वाङ्मामगळल्लि (*vāṅmāmagaḷalli*), as supplied) (Ni. 2-23): speech that is sweet and gladdening. When the word मंद्रजिह्व (*maṃdrajihva*) is used as an epithet of Agni and of Bṛhaspati, it describes their attractive form; but the meaning differs somewhat. For example:

अनर्वाणं वृषभं मंद्रजिह्वं बृहस्पतिं वर्धया नव्यमर्कैः । गाथान्यः सुरुचो यस्य देवा आशृण्वंति नवमानस्य मर्ताः ॥ (*anarvāṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ maṃdrajihvaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ vardhayā navyamarkaiḥ | gāthānyaḥ suruco yasya devā āśṛṇvaṃti navamānasya martāḥ ‖*) (the print has "ಮ. ಸಂ." for the Saṃhitā, as supplied; 1-190-1)

In this ṛk, when it is used as an epithet of Bṛhaspati, it means "one whose speech gladdens". The same epithet, in ṛks such as

त्वामग्ने प्रथमं देवयंतो देवं मर्ता अमृत मंद्रजिह्वं । (*tvāmagne prathamaṃ devayaṃto devaṃ martā amṛta maṃdrajihvaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-11-5)

when used as an epithet of Agni, means Agni with tongues in the form of flames that are charming and gladdening. In the present ṛk the word मंद्र (*maṃdra*) means Agni, whose form is charming and gladdening.

सत्यः (*satyaḥ*) — सत्यकर्मा । (*satyakarmā |*) ("one whose acts are true"). Since the word सत्य (*satya*) is stated among the names of water (Ni. 2-24), the meaning is explained as "the giver of rain (वृष्टिप्रद (*vṛṣṭiprada*)), the one who produces water for the world"; or, सत्यं कस्मात् सत्तु तायते सत्पभवं भवतीति वा (*satyaṃ kasmāt sattu tāyate satpabhavaṃ bhavatīti vā*) (Ni. 3-13) *(the print has सत्तु (*sattu*) and सत्पभवं (*satpabhavaṃ*) across a line break, स-त्पभवं (*sa-tpabhavaṃ*), joined as supplied)*, taken as speech without deceit that is in good men, or as the pure speech spoken in the neighbourhood of good men; therefore it is explained that Agni is one who speaks words that cause no deception to others, or one whose acts are without deceit.

### Printed p. 259

These epithets सत्यः (*satyaḥ*), कवितमः (*kavitamaḥ*), वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*) all indicate the extraordinary qualities of Agni.

For the word वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*) Sāyaṇa gives the meaning सर्वस्य जगतः विधाता (*sarvasya jagataḥ vidhātā*), that is, the creator of the whole world. The word वेधस् (*vedhas*) is read in the Nirukta among the names of the wise (the print has "ಸಿ. 3-19" as the reference, as supplied; Ni. 3-19 is presumably meant). When the qualities of the wise sacrificer are described, this word is generally an epithet. In some places, although the sense "producer" is there, it can only be "producer of the fruit of the sacrifice"; the word does not seem to be used with the meaning of creator. But in the present ṛk, since it stands together with epithets such as सत्यः (*satyaḥ*) and कवितमः (*kavitamaḥ*), the meaning Sāyaṇa has given may fit the context. Moreover, in ṛks such as

स पूर्वया निविदा कव्यतायोरिमाः प्रजा अजनयन्मनूनां विवस्वता चक्षसा द्यामपश्च देवा अग्निं धारयन्द्रविणोदां (*sa pūrvayā nividā kavyatāyorimāḥ prajā ajanayanmanūnāṃ vivasvatā cakṣasā dyāmapaśca devā agniṃ dhārayandraviṇodāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-2)

there is the description that Agni, praised by the mantra of Manu, which is ancient, worthy of praise and of the nature of a hymn, created all the creatures that belong to Manu. And the account of how Agni, praised by Manu with mantras such as आग्निर्देवेद्धः (*āgnirdeveddhaḥ*) (so printed, with long ā), made the creation of all beings, and the greatness of those mantras, are described in the seventy-fourth to seventy-eighth pages of the eighth part of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā.

सत्यः (*satyaḥ*) — for this word Sāyaṇa has given here the meaning सत्यकर्मा (*satyakarmā*).

The word सत्य (*satya*) is used throughout the Ṛk-saṃhitā with the sense of an excellent and moral worthiness and power kept before the mind. The acts performed by those who have such excellent worthiness are also of the nature of truth. Expressing this very meaning, the author of the Nirukta too has explained the word सत्य (*satya*) in this way:

सत्यं कस्मात् सत्तु कायते सत्पभवं भवतीति वा (*satyaṃ kasmāt sattu kāyate satpabhavaṃ bhavatīti vā*) (Ni. 3-13)

It spreads among good men, or it is born among good men; therefore it is called satya: so the Nirukta-author has explained. According to this explanation, since even the fruit of the nature of truth must come to good men alone, the idea that the fruit is of a good nature, matching the true acts of the virtuous, is indicated by the description in this ṛk. It shows the difference between the god-fearing man who follows the path of truth and the god-reviler who follows the path of untruth: however great the strength of the god-reviler may be at the beginning, it dwindles of itself in the end, whereas the powers of the god-fearing man grow, and that growth is the fruit of his life of truth. Therefore the sacrificer,

### Printed p. 260

त्वं देहि सहस्रिणं रयिं नोऽद्रोघेण वचसा सत्यमग्ने (*tvaṃ dehi sahasriṇaṃ rayiṃ no 'drogheṇa vacasā satyamagne*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-14_6, the underscore as supplied)

in such contexts prays to Agni, who is of the nature of truth: सत्यशीलं, सन्मार्गप्रवर्तमानं पुत्रं देहि (*satyaśīlaṃ, sanmārgapravartamānaṃ putraṃ dehi*), "give a son who is true in character and moves on the good path". Thus, since the word सत्य (*satya*) is used with reference to action and with reference to fruit, it has to be explained, in both these contexts, which principle of the universe this idea reflects.

ते देना उत्सृज्यानृतं । सत्यमन्वालेभिरे । (*te denā utsṛjyānṛtaṃ | satyamanvālebhire |*) (Śa. Brā. 9. 5. 1. 13; the print has "ದೇನಾ" for "ದೇವಾ", as supplied)

तद्यत्तत्सत्यं । त्रयी सा विद्या ते देवा अब्रुवन् यज्ञं कृत्वेदं सत्यं तनवामहा इति (*tadyattatsatyaṃ | trayī sā vidyā te devā abruvan yajñaṃ kṛtvedaṃ satyaṃ tanavāmahā iti*) (Śa. Brā. 9. 5. 1. 18)

The gods gave up untruth and firmly took hold of truth. Since the three Vedas, called the Trayī, are of the nature of this truth, the gods said (the print has ಆತಿಸಿದರು (*ātisidaru*), probably for "wished"; as supplied) "let us perform the rites enjoined by the Veda and spread truth". Thus, besides showing the essential relation between truth and the performance of rites, it expresses the wish that by such pure performance of rites one may obtain the full welfare that is complete in all riches.

नाभिऋतस्य सप्रथा इति । सत्यं वा ऋतं वा ऋतं सत्यस्य नाभिः सप्रथा इत्येवैतदाह स नो विश्वायुः सप्रथा इति स नः सर्वायुः इत्येवैतदाह । (*nābhiṛtasya saprathā iti | satyaṃ vā ṛtaṃ vā ṛtaṃ satyasya nābhiḥ saprathā ityevaitadāha sa no viśvāyuḥ saprathā iti sa naḥ sarvāyuḥ ityevaitadāha |*) (Śa. Brā. 14. 3. 1. 18)

By such explanations the identity of truth with the order of the universe is shown, and it is made known that by following such truth and by performing true rites a full span of life is obtained as the fruit, which states the relation of cause and effect between good fruit and good action.

Since for the performance of acts of the nature of truth also it is absolutely necessary to know the order of the universe and the nature of the deities who are its cause, it is also stated clearly in many contexts that this knowledge too is possible only through truth.

सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवगैरभिज्ञा सत्त्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन् । (*sakhā ha yatra sakhibhirnavagairabhijñā sattvabhirgā anugman |*)
सत्यं तदिंद्रो दशभिर्दशगैः सूर्यं विवेद तमसि क्षियंतं । (*satyaṃ tadiṃdro daśabhirdaśagaiḥ sūryaṃ viveda tamasi kṣiyaṃtaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3. 39. 5; the print has a zero-width joiner in सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*), as supplied)

त इद्देवानां सधमाद आसन्नृतावानः कवयः पूर्व्यासः । (*ta iddevānāṃ sadhamāda āsannṛtāvānaḥ kavayaḥ pūrvyāsaḥ |*)
गूळं ज्योतिः पितरो अन्वविंदन्त्सत्यमंत्रा आजयन्नुषासं ॥ (*gūḷaṃ jyotiḥ pitaro anvaviṃdantsatyamaṃtrā ājayannuṣāsaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7. 76. 4; so printed: गूळं (*gūḷaṃ*))

### Printed p. 261

In all such ṛks there are many sentences that indicate earlier occasions on which people, knowing the nature of the deities who are of the nature of truth and performing rites, obtained wealth as the fruit. And along with it there is also the prayer "may it be well with us through truth".

अधा यथा नः पितरः परासः प्रत्नासो अग्न ऋत माशुषाणाः । (*adhā yathā naḥ pitaraḥ parāsaḥ pratnāso agna ṛta māśuṣāṇāḥ |*)
शुचीदयन्दीधितिमुक्कशासः क्षामा भिंदंतो अरुणीरपव्रन् । (*śucīdayandīdhitimukkaśāsaḥ kṣāmā bhiṃdaṃto aruṇīrapavran |*) (the print has "ಮ. ಸಂ. 4. 2. 16" for the reference, as supplied)

In prayers such as "as our fathers obtained good fruits by the sacrificial performance that is of the nature of truth, even so now may all our rites yield true fruits" (तत्सत्यमस्तु (*tatsatyamastu*)), the true nature of the deities, Agni and the others, whose law is truth, is also described.

अजो न क्षां दाधार पृथिवीं तस्तंभ द्यां मंत्रेभिः सत्यैः । (*ajo na kṣāṃ dādhāra pṛthivīṃ tastaṃbha dyāṃ maṃtrebhiḥ satyaiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-67-3)

कविमग्निमुप स्तुहि सत्यधर्माणमध्वरे । देवममीवचातनं । (*kavimagnimupa stuhi satyadharmāṇamadhvare | devamamīvacātanaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-7)

देवो न यः सविता सत्यमन्मा क्रत्वा निपाति वृजनानि विश्वा । (*devo na yaḥ savitā satyamanmā kratvā nipāti vṛjanāni viśvā |*)
पुरुप्रशस्तो अमतिर्न सत्य आत्मेव शेवो दिधिषाय्यो भूत् । (*purupraśasto amatirna satya ātmeva śevo didhiṣāyyo bhūt |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-73-2)

In many such places it is stated that the deities, Agni and the others, upheld the worlds, the earth and the rest, by truth; that by it they carried out the protection of the world; and that human beings too must follow the same path of truth. The same quality of Agni is described in the present ṛk also.

कवितमः (*kavitamaḥ*) — अतिशयेन मेधावी । (*atiśayena medhāvī |*) मेधावी कविः क्रांतदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्वा (*medhāvī kaviḥ krāṃtadarśano bhavati kavatervā*) (Ni. 12-13). The word कवि (*kavi*) is formed from the root कव (*kava*) meaning "to go"; by the maxim गत्यर्थानां ज्ञानार्थकत्वं (*gatyarthānāṃ jñānārthakatvaṃ*) it is explained as "endowed with wisdom", and so Agni is described as one who excels all the wise.

यज्ञा (*yajñā*) (so printed; यष्टा (*yaṣṭā*) is evidently meant, as the next words show) — देवानां यष्टा । (*devānāṃ yaṣṭā |*) The word-form यष्टा (*yaṣṭā*) comes from the root यज (*yaja*), which is used in the sense of worshipping the deities and so on. Since Agni is here called देवानां यष्टा (*devānāṃ yaṣṭā*), the meaning is described as: because, like a sacrificer performing a sacrifice, Agni carries the oblations to the deities, he is the one who worships the deities.

वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*) — सर्वस्य जगतो विधाता । (*sarvasya jagato vidhātā |*) The word वेध (*vedha*) (the print has वेध श्यब्द (*vedha śyabda*) with a stray श्य (*śya*), as supplied) is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). Here Agni is described as the wise one who creates the whole world.

विदथानि आस्थात् (*vidathāni āsthāt*) — अस्माभिः क्रियमाणान् यज्ञान् अतिष्ठति प्राप्नोति । (*asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇān yajñān atiṣṭhati prāpnoti |*) The word विदथ (*vidatha*) is used in the sense of wisdom or sacrifice.

### Printed p. 262

Here only one of the meanings of the word विदथ (*vidatha*) has been given. It is one of the explanations of the Nirukta-author. The word is read among the names of the sacrifice such as यज्ञः वेनः (*yajñaḥ venaḥ*) (Ni. 3-19). And in order to show for the word विदथ (*vidatha*) the meaning "knowledge" in the sense of विदथानि वेदनानि (*vidathāni vedanāni*) (Ni. 6-7), the Nirukta-author

होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेति मायया । (*hotā devo amartyaḥ purastādeti māyayā |*)
विदथानि प्रचोदयन् ॥ (*vidathāni pracodayan ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-7)

quotes this ṛk and shows that there the word is formed from the root विद् (*vid*) meaning knowledge. Some scholars have tried to give an exact meaning for this word, and every one of them has stated only his own personal opinion. Since each has shown a different derivation for this word and made a different meaning, it can be said that all these meanings fit their respective contexts. The scholar Max Muller,

अमादेषां भियसा भूमिरेजति नार्न पूर्णा क्षरति व्यथिर्यती । (*amādeṣāṃ bhiyasā bhūmirejati nārna pūrṇā kṣarati vyathiryatī |*)
दूरेद्यशो ये चितयंत एमभिरंतर्महे विदथे येतिरे नरः ॥ (*dūredyaśo ye citayaṃta emabhiraṃtarmahe vidathe yetire naraḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-59-2)

while explaining this ṛk, gave for the word विदथे (*vidathe*) the meaning "(sacrifice) assembly", (The great sacrificial Assembly). And while giving its explanation he stated the meanings that other German scholars have given to this word and their opinions on its root, and finally spoke thus:

Vidatha may have been the name of a sacred act, as Veda is of sacred knowledge. But the fact remains that it is best translated by Assembly, particularly an assembly for sacrificial purposes. (S. B·E. xxxii. p. 349 to 350)

Some have said that, as sacred knowledge is the meaning of the word Veda, so a sacred act is the meaning of the word विदथ (*vidatha*). But he concluded that there is no doubt that the sacrificial assembly is the principal meaning of this word.

The scholar Hermann Oldenberg, in the book called Vedic Hymuns [sic], while explaining the meaning of the word विदथे (*vidathe*) in the ṛk of the Ṛk-saṃhitā

त्वमग्ने वृजिनवर्तनिं नरं सक्मन्पिपर्षि विदथे विचर्षणे । (*tvamagne vṛjinavartaniṃ naraṃ sakmanpiparṣi vidathe vicarṣaṇe |*)
यः शूरसाता परितक्म्ये धने दभ्रेभिश्चित्समृता हंसि भूयसः ॥ (*yaḥ śūrasātā paritakmye dhane dabhrebhiścitsamṛtā haṃsi bhūyasaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-6)

stated his opinion in this way. His words are quoted and then his opinions are given. He too

### Printed p. 263

having suggested many lucid opinions on the discussion, finally stated his own opinion. It is as follows:

On the derivation and meaning of विदथ (*vidatha*) Various opinions have been pronounced in the last years which have been collected by prof. Max-Muller in his note on R. V. v. 59, 2. (S. B. E. Vol. 32. p. 349.) Without trying to discuss here all different theories, I proceed to state my own opinion. I propose to derive विदथ (*vidatha*) from वि+धा (*vi+dhā*), the root धा (*dhā*) with the prefix वि (*vi*) means to ' distribute ' to " arrange " or " to ordain " Thus the original meaning of विदथ (*vidatha*) must be like the meaning of विधान (*vidhāna*) "distribution, disposition or ordinance " In v. 3, 6. we read विदथेषु अह्नां (*vidatheṣu ahnāṃ*). This phrase receives its explanation by vii 66, 11 and we may call attention also to vi. 51, 2. within the sphere of the Vedic Poets' thoughts, the most prominent example of something most artificially विहित (*vihita*) was the sacrifice. यज्ञ (*yajña*) and विदथ (*vidatha*), Sacrifice and ordinance became nearly synonimous [sic]. (iii 3, 8.) .................... Finally विदथ (*vidatha*) comes to mean ' the act of disposing of any business" or the like; this meaning appears, I believe, in some passages like the well known phrase, बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*) may we with valient [sic] men mightily raise our voice at the determining of ordinances. Thus the word विदथ (*vidatha*) and सभा (*sabhā*) approach each other in their meaning: a person influential in council is called both विदथ्य (*vidathya*) and सभेय (*sabheya*). [Sacred books of the East. Vol. 46. p. 27].

The main substance of this writing is as follows. The meaning of the word विदथ (*vidatha*) is formed by adding the prefix वि (*vi*) to the root धा (*dhā*). विधा (*vidhā*) means "distribute" or "regulate"; it can also mean observance of rules. That the two words विदथ (*vidatha*) and विधा (*vidhā*) have one and the same meaning can be understood from the words used in the ṛks quoted below.

वयमग्ने वनुयाम त्वोता वसूयवो हविषा बुध्यमानाः । (*vayamagne vanuyāma tvotā vasūyavo haviṣā budhyamānāḥ |*)
वयं समर्ये विदथेस्वह्नां वयं राया सहसस्पुत्र मर्तान् ॥ (*vayaṃ samarye vidathesvahnāṃ vayaṃ rāyā sahasasputra martān ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-6; the print has "ಮ. ಸಂ." for "Ṛ. Saṃ.", as supplied)

This matter is understood from the equal sense of the words विदधेष्वह्नां (*vidadheṣvahnāṃ*) in this ṛk, and also of

वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञ मक्तुं चादृचं । (*vi ye dadhuḥ śaradaṃ māsamādaharyajña maktuṃ cādṛcaṃ |*)
अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अरमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥ (*anāpyaṃ varuṇo mitro aramā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśata ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-11)

the words विदधुः (*vidadhuḥ*) in this ṛk; and, the words विहित (*vihita*) and विदथ (*vidatha*) having one meaning, the sacrifice enjoined by the śāstra was called by the name विदथ (*vidatha*).

### Printed p. 264

This scholar has explained that the meaning "sacrifice" or "sacrificial assembly" remained at the end.

The scholar Bloomfield has maintained that विदथ (*vidatha*) never means an assembly, that the meaning "personal home" is the correct one, and has shown the faults in the meaning given by the two, Max Muller and Oldenberg. His opinion is as follows.

The word विदथ (*vidatha*) contains the root विद् (*vid*) in its ordinary sense of ' get, acquire ' Instead of this, the radical idea, underlying the word was generally felt to be ' come together, ' assemble ' Again, the false start, from the notion of ' assemblage ' resulted in an approximation of the word to other words for assemblage, especially to सभा (*sabhā*) with which विदथ (*vidatha*) was almost identified. We shall see that there are decided points of contact between the words विदथ (*vidatha*) and सभा (*sabhā*) but the contact is that of extreme opposites in a way. विदथ (*vidatha*) refers to home matters, सभा (*sabhā*) generally to public matters.

In the interpretation of a term that figures prominently in the mystic-hieratic sphere of the Veda, it is peculiarly necessary to search for its uses outside of that sphere, if there be such uses. In x. 85, 26, the bride after the wedding ceremoney [sic] proper, as the newly married couple are about to travel to their new home, is addressed with the words " May Pushan, taking you by the hand, lead thee home, may the Aswins lead you forth on their car. Go to your house in order that you may be the mistress of the house. "

Now, विदथ (*vidatha*) here, can but have one meaning, ' housenold [sic] ' or something very like it. It certainly cannot refer to anything in the nature of a public gathering similar to the सभा (*sabhā*). In the phrase बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*) (R. V. ii. 1, 16) the word सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*) refers to family relations, and not to public life.

Thus far, it may not be doubted, the word appears in the language of ordinary life. But it is found to a very much greater extent in the sacerdotal sphere; indeed, as all interpreters from Yaska on, have agreed, it often has a meaning very much close to यज्ञ (*yajña*) ' Sacrifice ' itself. This is as it should be. In as much as the sacrifice is a private bome [sic] affaire [sic] it is very natural विदध (*vidadha*)

### Printed p. 265

the house promises the establishment should figure prominently in connection with the sacrifice (the Kannada line ends here with ऎंदु हेळिदॆ (*èṃdu heḷidè*), "so he has said").

The substance of this writing is this: the meaning "assembly" for the word विदध (*vidadha*) , as some have given it, is not right. The meaning of this word is "personal home". One can notice in many places that the word is used in precisely this sense. For example,

पूषा त्वेतो नयतु हस्तगृह्याश्विना त्वा प्र वहतां रथेन । (*pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinā tvā pra vahatāṃ rathena |*)
गृहान् गच्छ गृहपत्नि यथासो वशिनी त्वं विदथवा वदासि ॥ (*gṛhān gaccha gṛhapatni yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidathavā vadāsi ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-26; the print has विदथवा वदासि (*vidathavā vadāsi*), as supplied)

In this ṛk the meaning, "may Pūṣan and the Aśvin deities lead you with well-being to your husband's house", is clear. Moreover,

ये स्तोतृभ्यो गोअग्रामश्वपेशसमग्ने रातिमुपसृजंति सूरयः । (*ye stotṛbhyo goagrāmaśvapeśasamagne rātimupasṛjaṃti sūrayaḥ |*)
अस्माञ्च तांश्च प्र हि नेषि वस्य आ बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥ (*asmāñca tāṃśca pra hi neṣi vasya ā bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. printed "21-16" and again, on the next line, "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೨೧೬"; as supplied, the reference is doubled and doubtful **NOTE**)

in this ṛk also, since सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*) has been explained as शोभनपुत्रादिसहिताः (*śobhanaputrādisahitāḥ*) ("accompanied by excellent sons and the like"), the meaning is "home". But since sacrificial work is carried on in the home, in the present context it can also be "the house of sacrifice". The same meaning is there in what Yāska and others have said, that it is a synonym of "sacrifice". Thus many scholars among the Westerners have stated their own personal opinions.

Thus, since the different meanings, home, sacrifice and assembly, all fit, none of them can be said to be wrong. In the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya itself all these meanings have been given. For example, in the ṛks 10-85-26 and 27, in 7-74-3 and others it is explained as "home", and in 10-100-6, 10-110-7 and many other ṛks as "sacrifice". It also comes to mean "house of sacrifice" and "sacrificial assembly".

विद्युद्रथ (*vidyudratha*) — विद्योतमानयानोपेतः । (*vidyotamānayānopetaḥ |*) When the horses and other things yoked to the chariots of Indra and the other deities are described, रोहितोग्नेः (*rohitogneḥ*) has been said. The meaning is given that Agni has a red, shining vehicle, or a chariot furnished with a vehicle of this kind.

शोचिष्केश (*śociṣkeśa*) — शोचींषि ज्वालाः केशाः यस्य सः (*śocīṃṣi jvālāḥ keśāḥ yasya saḥ*) Agni is one who wears his flames as men wear hair. Therefore he is described as ज्वालामय केशोपेतः (*jvālāmaya keśopetaḥ*) ("furnished with hair made of flames").

सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*) — बलस्य सूनुः । (*balasya sūnuḥ |*) Since Agni is produced by churning with the application of force in the two fire-sticks (araṇi), he is so designated.

पृथिव्यां वाजः अश्रेत् (*pṛthivyāṃ vājaḥ aśret*) (the print has ವಾಜಃ, where the bhāṣya and the Saṃhitā have पाजः; as supplied)—पृथिव्यां अंतरिक्षे विस्तीर्णे तेजः स्वकीयां प्रभां प्रापयति (*pṛthivyāṃ aṃtarikṣe vistīrṇe tejaḥ svakīyāṃ prabhāṃ prāpayati*). यद्वा पृथिव्यां भुवि वर्तमानः बलं सेवते (*yadvā pṛthivyāṃ bhuvi vartamānaḥ balaṃ sevate*). The word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) is stated among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10) and also among the words for the earth (Ni. 2-5). The meaning is that Agni pervades his radiance in the wide atmosphere and also dwells in his strength on the earth; thus the nature and the greatness of Agni are described.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes (noted briefly; the sūtra numbers are as printed):

मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—root मदि स्तुतिमोदमदस्वप्नकांतिगतिसु (*madi stutimodamadasvapnakāṃtigatisu*); the suffix *rak* by स्थायितंचि (*sthāyitaṃci*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-180); the root takes the augment *num* by इदितोनुम्धातोः (*iditonumdhātoḥ*); by the suffix accent the word is end-acute.

अस्थात् (*asthāt*)—root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*); *luṅ* in the present sense by छंदसि लुज्लज्लिटः (*chaṃdasi lujlajliṭaḥ*); *tip* in the third person singular, the *i* dropped; by गातिस्थाघुपा (*gātisthāghupā*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77) *sic* takes the substitute (the print has "ಚ್ಚಿಗೆ", as supplied, apparently for the *cli* of *luṅ*), which is then dropped (*luk*); augment *aṭ* for the stem; the finite-verb *nighāta* accent, as it follows a word that is not a finite verb .

यज्वा (*yajvā*)—root यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु (*yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu*); by सुयजोर्व्वनिप् (*suyajorvvanip*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-103) the suffix *jvanip*; *van* remains; since the suffix has a mute *p* it is unaccented, so the root accent remains; nominative singular form.

कवितमः (*kavitamaḥ*)—root कु शब्दे (*ku śabde*); अच इः (*aca iḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-578) gives the suffix *i* in the agent or the abstract sense (from "he sounds" or "it is sounded"); the *u* of the root takes *guṇa* and the substitute *av*; then *tamap* in the superlative sense; as it has a mute *p* the accent of the preceding suffix (*i*) remains.

विद्युद्रथः (*vidyudrathaḥ*)—by बहुप्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदं (*bahuprīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadaṃ*) the first member keeps its natural accent.

शोचिश्लेषः (*śociśleṣaḥ*) (so printed; the bhāṣya and the Saṃhitā have the form शोचिष्केशः (*śociṣkeśaḥ*))—root शुच दीप्तौ (*śuca dīptau*); अर्चिशुचिहुसृपिछदिछर्दिभ्य इसिः (*arciśucihusṛpichadichardibhya isiḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 3-265) gives the suffix *isi*; *guṇa* of the light penultimate vowel; by the suffix accent शोचिः (*śociḥ*) is end-acute; शोचींषि केशाः यस्य सः शोचिष्केशः (*śocīṃṣi keśāḥ yasya saḥ śociṣkeśaḥ*) is a *bahuvrīhi* in which the first member keeps its natural accent.

अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—root श्रिञ् सेवायां (*śriñ sevāyāṃ*); *laṅ* in the present sense, Vedic; *śap* dropped by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*); the *i* of *tip* dropped; *guṇa* of the root's *i* by सार्वधातुकार्ध (*sārvadhātukārdha*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-83); augment *aṭ*; the finite-verb *nighāta* accent.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, lord of the true sacrifice, I utter this word of homage to you; accept it; knowing the order of invoking the gods, bring those who know the rites; and sit, O worshipful one, in the midst of the spread grass for our protection. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (हे) ऋतावः (*ṛtāvaḥ*)—O Agni, endowed with the sacrifice that is true
- ते (*te*)—relating to you
- नमउक्तिं (*namauktiṃ*)—the word of homage
- अयामि (*ayāmi*)—(I) send forth (utter); (हे) सहस्वः (*sahasvaḥ*)—O mighty Agni
- चेतते (*cetate*)—to you who give knowledge of the rites
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you; (I utter the word of homage;) (that) जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—(the print continues on p. 268:) be one who takes pleasure in that utterance

### Printed p. 268

(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 2, continued:) (And;) विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—you who know the invoking of the gods in due order; विदुषः (*viduṣaḥ*)—those who have knowledge of the rites; आ वक्षि (*ā vakṣi*)—bring; (हे) यजत्र (*yajatra*)—O Agni, worthy to be worshipped; ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for our protection; मध्यॆ बर्हिः (*madhyè barhiḥ*)—upon the spread sacred grass; आ नि सत्सि (*ā ni satsi*)—be seated.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, endowed with the true sacrifice and mighty, I utter words of praise addressed to you; accept them; and you, who invoke the gods in due order, bring the wise ones; and you, worthy to be worshipped, be seated, for our protection, on the spread seat of sacred grass.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I utter to you the words of adoration, be pleased by them, observer of truth : endowed with strength, (they are addressed) to you who are the expounder (of sacred rites) : wise (as you are) bring (hither) the wise : object of sacrifice, sit down in the midst upon the sacred grass for our protection.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋतावः (*ṛtāvaḥ*)—since the word ऋत (*ṛta*) is used in the sense of truth or of sacrifice, Agni is addressed by the word ऋतावः (*ṛtāvaḥ*), which means "possessing the sacrifice". And he is addressed as सहस्वः (*sahasvaḥ*), "possessing strength", and as चेतते (*cetate*), which is explained as कर्मणः प्रज्ञापकाय (*karmaṇaḥ prajñāpakāya*), "one who teaches the rites". The meaning is that Agni, of such greatness, should take pleasure in the speech made up of praise and homage (नमउक्तिं (*namauktiṃ*)) which the officiating priests and the sacrificer who perform the sacrifice recite; this meaning is described by the sentence अस्माभिः क्रियमाणां नमस्कारोक्तिं सेवस्व (*asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇāṃ namaskāroktiṃ sevasva*).

विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—आनुपूर्व्येण देवाह्वानाभिज्ञः (*ānupūrvyeṇa devāhvānābhijñaḥ*). A wish is expressed that Agni, who knows well the order of invoking the several deities to accept the oblation in the sacrifice, should invoke those who know the sacrificial rites and make them come to the sacrifice.

यजत्र ऊतये मध्यॆ बर्हिः आ नि षत्सि (*yajatra ūtaye madhyè barhiḥ ā ni ṣatsi*)—यप्पव्य हे अग्ने अस्माकं रक्षणाय स्तीर्णस्य बर्हिषो मध्यॆ आ समंतान्निषीद (*yappavya he agne asmākaṃ rakṣaṇāya stīrṇasya barhiṣo madhyè ā samaṃtānniṣīda*) (the print has यप्पव्य (*yappavya*) where the bhāṣya has यष्टव्य (*yaṣṭavya*) [sic]; as supplied). Because Agni is worthy of worship he is addressed by the word यजत्र (*yajatra*). A wish is expressed that this Agni, in order to protect us, the sacrificer (yajamāna) and the priests (ṛtviks) who perform the sacrifice, should sit well upon the sacred grass spread on the sacrificial altar in the sacrificial hall.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

Grammar notes on Ṛk 2 (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as printed):

अयामि (*ayāmi*)—root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), a root of the first (bhū) class; *mip* of the first person singular of *laṭ*; *guṇa* of the root because of *śap*; the substitute *ay*; the long vowel of the stem ending in *a* by अतो दीर्घोयञ् (*ato dīrghoyañ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-101); being at the beginning of a pāda it takes no *nighāta* accent; as *mip* and *śap* are unaccented the root accent remains.

जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—root जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*), tudādi class; second person singular of *loṭ*; it follows a finite verb, hence the *nighāta* accent.

ऋतावः (*ṛtāvaḥ*)—ऋतावान् (*ṛtāvān*) "one who has ṛta"; the suffix *matup*; the first member is lengthened by अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapi dṛśyate*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137); in the vocative *ru* by मतुवसोरुः संबुद्धौ (*matuvasoruḥ saṃbuddhau*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-1); at the beginning of a pāda the vocative *nighāta* is not applied; the initial acute comes by अमंत्रितस्य (*amaṃtritasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198).

चेतते (*cetate*)—root चिती संज्ञाने (*citī saṃjñāne*); the substitute *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; *guṇa* of the light penultimate vowel by पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) (no number printed); the *sārvadhātuka* is unaccented by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186); therefore the case-ending does not take the acute, by शतुरनुमो (*śaturanumo*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173); the root accent remains.

सहस्वः (*sahasvaḥ*)—सहस्वान् (*sahasvān*) "one who has *sahas*"; the suffix *matup* by तदस्यास्ति (*tadasyāsti*); because the preceding member has the name *bha* by तसौ मत्वर्थे (*tasau matvarthe*) (Pā. Sū. 1-4-19), the *s* does not become *ru*; since the *a* stands before it, the *m* of *matup* becomes *v* by माधुपधायाश्च (*mādhupadhāyāśca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-9); in the vocative, before *su*, the augment *num* by उगिदचां (*ugidacāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70), placed after the last vowel as it has an *m*; loss of *su* by हल्ज्याभ्यो (*haljyābhyo*); the *t* is dropped by the loss of the final conjunct; the *n* becomes *ru* by मतुवसोः रुः संबुद्धौ (*matuvasoḥ ruḥ saṃbuddhau*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-1); at the end of the word it becomes visarga; the *nighāta* accent by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19).

विदुषः (*viduṣaḥ*)—root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*); the substitute *śatṛ* for *laṭ*, then the substitute *vasu* by विदेः शतुर्वसुः (*videḥ śaturvasuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-36); before *śas*, since it has the name *bha*, *samprasāraṇa* by वसोः संप्रसारणं (*vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-131); (the print has an unexplained "(ಉ)" here, as supplied) the earlier form by संप्रसारणाच्च (*saṃprasāraṇācca*); *ṣ* by शासिवसिघसीनांच (*śāsivasighasīnāṃca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-60); the form विदुषः (*viduṣaḥ*) results; by the suffix accent the *u* is acute.

सत्सि (*satsi*)—root षद्‌ल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadlya viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*) ; *sip* of the second person singular of *laṭ*; *luk* of *śap* by बहुलं-छंदसि (*bahulaṃ-chaṃdasi*); since no *śit* suffix follows, the substitute *sīda* for the root does not occur; *t* for *d* by खरिच (*kharica*); as it follows नि (*ni*), *ṣ* for the root's *s* by the sūtra beginning सदिर- (*sadira-*) (continued on p. 270, there प्रतेः (*prateḥ*), Pā. Sū. 8-3-66).

### Printed p. 270

(Continued from p. 269:) the sūtra ends प्रतेः (*prateḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-66), by which the root's *s* becomes *ṣ*. Because it follows a finite verb, the *nighāta* accent comes.

यजत्र (*yajatra*)—root यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु (*yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu*); the suffix *atran* by अमिनक्षियजि (*aminakṣiyaji*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-385); a vocative form; the *nighāta* accent by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्रव॑तां त उ॒षसा॑ वा॒जयं॑ती॒ अग्ने॒ वात॑स्य प॒थ्या॑भि॒रच्छ॑ ।  
> यत्सी॑मं॒जंति॑ पू॒र्व्यं ह॒विर्भि॒रा वं॒धुरे॑व तस्थतुर्दुरो॒णे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> द्रवतां । ते । उषसा । वाजयंती इति । अग्ने । वातस्य । पथ्याभिः । अच्छ ।  
> यत् । सीं । अंजंति । पूर्व्यं । हविःभिः । आ । वंधुराइव । तस्थतुः । दुरोणे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने वाजयंती वाजमन्नं कुर्वाणे उषसा उषासानक्ते अहोरात्रौ
> ते त्वां द्रवतां । अभिगच्छतां । त्वमपि वातस्य वायोः पथ्याभिर्मार्गैरच्छ तावहो-
> रात्रौ शीघ्रमभिगच्छ । यद्यस्मात्कारणादहोरात्राग्न्योः परस्पराभिगमनेनान्योन्य-
> संबंधस्तस्मादहोरात्रयोः सायंप्रातःकालयोः पूर्व्यं पुरातनं त्वामृत्विजो
> हविर्भिराज्यादिभिः सीं सर्वतोऽंजंति । सिंचंति । किंच बंधुरेव । यथा कूवर-
> स्थानं परस्परसंसक्तेषाद्वयोपेतं तद्वत्संसक्तौ तावहोरात्रौ दुरोणेऽस्माकं
> गृहेऽग्निहोत्रादिकर्मसिद्ध्यर्थमा आवृत्य पुनःपुनरावर्तमानौ संतौ तस्थतुः ।
> शिष्ठतां ॥ द्रवतां । द्रु गतावित्यस्य लोटि रूपं । पथ्याभिः । पथिषु साधव इत्यर्थे
> तत्र साधुः । पा. ४-४-९८ । इति यत् । नस्तद्धित इति टिलोपः । तित्स्वरित इति स्वरितः ।
> तस्थतुः । शिष्ठतेर्लिट्युसि रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, may day and night, the givers of food, run to you, and do you go to them along the paths of the wind; since they meet each other, the priests anoint you, the ancient one, with ghee and other oblations at both times; like pole and yoke joined together, may they keep returning to our house. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वाजयंती (*vājayaṃtī*)—givers of food
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—day and night
- ते (*te*)—toward you
- द्रवतां (*dravatāṃ*)—let them come running; (you also) वातस्य (*vātasya*)—of the wind
- पथ्याभिः (*pathyābhiḥ*)—by the paths
- अच्छ (*accha*)—(go) facing (those day and nights)
- यत् (*yat*)—

### Printed p. 271

(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 3, continued:) (as said above) for which reason (day and night and Agni have the relation of approaching one another); तत् (*tat*)—therefore in both day and night (that is, at the evening and morning times); पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*)—you, the ancient one (the priests); हविर्भिः (*havirbhiḥ*)—with oblations such as ghee; सीं (*sīṃ*)—always; अंजंति (*aṃjaṃti*)—anoint (make the offering); वंधुराइव (*vaṃdhurāiva*)—like the pole of a cart (day and night, joined to each other); दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)—in our house; आ (*ā*)—returning again and again; तस्थतुः (*tasthatuḥ*)—let them (ever) stand.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, day and night, the givers of food, run hastily toward you, and you too come toward them by the path of the wind; for this very reason the priests offer ghee and other oblations to you, the ancient one, at both the evening and the morning times. May those two, day and night, joined to one another, keep coming one after the other in our houses forever.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the food-bestowing day and night hasten to you whilst you, AGNI, meet them on the paths of the wind: since (the priests) ever worship you preceding (them) with oblations, whilst they (united) like the pole (and the yoke of a waggon), abide successively in our dwelling.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वाजयंती उषसा ते द्रवतां (*vājayaṃtī uṣasā te dravatāṃ*)—the bhāṣya says वाजमन्नंकुर्वाणे उषासानक्ते अहो (*vājamannaṃkurvāṇe uṣāsānakte aho*) (the line is carried over in the print as रात् त्वां अभिगच्छतां (*rāt tvāṃ abhigacchatāṃ*), so printed). The authors of the Nirukta say of उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) (Nir. 8-11): उषासानक्कोषाश्च नक्ता चोषा नक्तेति रात्रिनाम अनक्तिभूतान्यवश्यायेनापि वा नक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा (*uṣāsānakkoṣāśca naktā coṣā nakteti rātrināma anaktibhūtānyavaśyāyenāpi vā naktā avyaktavarṇā*) (the print has उषासानक्कोषाश्च (*uṣāsānakkoṣāśca*), as supplied). Durgācārya, showing the analysis of the word उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) as उषाश्च नक्ता च (*uṣāśca naktā ca*), explains: उच्छतीति उषा (*ucchatīti uṣā*) (from the root उच्छि विवासे (*ucchi vivāse*), meaning "to cause to dwell very happily"); the word उषस् (*uṣas*) formed from that root denotes the day (अहस्सु (*ahassu*)). भूतानि (*bhūtāni*) (beings) अनक्ति (*anakti*) अवश्यायेन (*avaśyāyena*): it drenches creatures with dew; thus, with the *a* of अनक्ता (*anaktā*) dropped, the word नक्ता (*naktā*) denotes night; or नक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा (*naktā avyaktavarṇā*): the day makes things appear clearly, while the night, because it does not show them plainly, is न आक्ता (*na āktā*) or न व्यक्ता (*na vyaktā*), अनक्ता (*anaktā*). Thus the derivation of the form नक्ता (*naktā*) and its meaning are given. And Yāska (the passage is cut off by the end of p. 271 and continues on the next page) quotes:

आ सुस्वयंती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योन्सौ (*ā susvayaṃtī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonsau*) ।
दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने (*divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne*) ॥ (10-110-6)

### Printed p. 272

(Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued from p. 271:) He has quoted this Ṛk. On this Ṛk Durgācārya has explained one meaning that refers to day and night, and, following another view, a second meaning that refers to Agni. Here Sāyaṇa, because the word वाज (*vāja*) is read among the names of food (Nir. 3-9), has described the meaning thus: may day and night, who bring about food for living beings, go on worshipping Agni. This meaning is stated here because the rule of worshipping Agni is constant: at the Uṣas time that precedes the day, and at the evening time that precedes the night.

Moreover, by such descriptions as वाजयंती (*vājayaṃtī*) and हविर्भिः सीं अंजंति (*havirbhiḥ sīṃ aṃjaṃti*) the constant connection between the sacrifice and these two is described. They have a very close connection with Agni, who blazes up at the Uṣas time and in the evening. For that very reason the description (in the print "ಆಂಲಕಾರಿಕ" [sic], apparently "figurative") is that they hold and bear Agni between them.

ನಕ್ತೋಷಾಸಾ ವರ್ಣಮಾಮೇಮ್ಯಾನೇ ಧಾಪಯೇತೇ ಶಿಶುಮೇಕಂ ಸಮೀಚೀ ।
ದ್ಯಾವಾಕ್ಷಾಮಾ ರುಕ್ಮೋ ಅಂತರ್ವಿ ಭಾತಿ ದೇವಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಂ ಧಾರಯನ್ದ್ರವಿಣೋದಾಂ ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-5)

From Ṛks such as this it is understood that they help Agni, who is of child form, to drink the oblation. Because of this connection they are said to be near the sacrificers. In general the description of this point is repeated. For example—

ಆ ಸುಷ್ಟಯಂತೀ ಯಜತೇ ಉಪಾಕೇ ಉಷಾಸಾನಕ್ತಾ ಸದತಾಂ ನಿ ಯೋನ್ ।
ದಿವ್ಯೇ ಯೋಷಣೇ ಬೃಹತೀ ಸುರುಕ್ಮೇ ಅಧಿ ಶ್ರಿಯಂ ಶುಕ್ರಪಿಶಂ ದಧಾನೇ ॥

(printed "ಪು. ಸಂ. ೧೦-೧೧೦-೬", i.e. "Pu. Saṃ. 10-110-6", as supplied; the abbreviation elsewhere reads Ṛ. Saṃ.) *[The first line reads "ಸುಷ್ಟಯಂತೀ" and "ಯೋನ್" here, differently from the Yāska quotation at the end of p. 271; as supplied.]*

In this Ṛk too the same matter is stated, a little differently. From this it is understood that the deities Uṣāsānaktā obtain no secondary place in the sacrificial acts but a very principal one.

ಹೋತಾಯಕ್ಷದುಷಾಸಾನಕ್ತಾ ಬೃಹತೀ ಸುಪೇಶಸಾ ನೃಗ್ ಃ ಪತಿಭ್ಯೋ ಯೋನಿಂ ಕೃಣ್ವಾನೇ।
ಸಗ್ ಸ್ಮಯಮಾನೇ ಇಂದ್ರೇಣ ದೇವೈರೇದಂ ಬರ್ಹಿಃ ಸೀದತಾಂ ವೀತಾಮಾಜ್ಯಸ್ಯ
ಹೋತ್ಯರ್ಜ ॥

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2) *[The text of this mantra is as supplied; the stray spaces and signs in नृग् ः (*nṛg ḥ*) and सग् स्मयमाने (*sag smayamāne*) and the ending होत्यर्ज (*hotyarja*) are printed so.]*

In this mantra the obtaining of this principal place is indicated, and moreover there is the prayer that these two should sit on the darbha seat together with Agni and with Indra and the other deities. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa they are addressed as अहोरात्रे (*ahorātre*). In the Bṛhaddevatā the nature of these deities is described in this way—

### Printed p. 273

ನಕ್ತೋಷಾಸೌ ಚ ಯೇ ದೇವ್ಯಾವಾಗ್ನೇಯ್ಯಾವೇವ ತೇ ಸ್ಮೃತೇ ।
ಶ್ಯಾವ್ಯಾಗ್ನೇಯೀ ಹಿ ಕಾಲಸ್ಯ ತಸ್ಯೆವೋಷಾಃ ತಲೇವ ತು ॥

(Bṛ. De. 3-8) *[तलेव (*taleva*) as supplied.]*

Naktā and Uṣas, these two goddesses, are both known to be related to Agni. Of these, Śyāvī (the night goddess) is closely connected with Agni; and from the Nirukta sentence उषः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (*uṣaḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ*) (Nir. 2-18) it is known that Uṣas is the latter part of that night.

ತಮ ಉಚ್ಛತ್ಯುಷಾ ನಕ್ತಾನಕ್ತೀಮಾಂ ಹಿಮಬಿಂದುಭಿಃ ।
ಅಪಿ ವಾವ್ಯಕ್ತವರ್ಣೇತಿ ನಇದ್ ಪೂರ್ವಾಂಜೇರಿದಂ ಭವೇತ್ ॥

(Bṛ. De. 3-9) *[Second line as supplied: नइद् पूर्वांजेरिदं (*naid pūrvāṃjeridaṃ*).]*

Of these two, Uṣas drives away the darkness. Night makes everything wet and pervaded with drops of dew. Or, because it has no definite colour, the root आंजन् (*āṃjan*) joined with the particle नञ् (*nañ*) gives the meaning "of unmanifest colour".

ಸಾ ಹಿ ದೋಷಾ ಭವತ್ಯಾದೌ ನಿಶೀಥೇ ಸಾ ತಮಸ್ವತೀ ।
ನಾಮ್ಮಾ ಭವತ್ಯುಷಾಶ್ಚೈವ ಸೈಷಾ ಪ್ರಾಗುದಯಾದ್ರವೇಃ ॥

(Bṛ. De. 3-10)

At the beginning this deity is named Doṣā, at midnight Tamasvatī, and before sunrise Uṣas. Doṣā, Tamasvatī, Śyāvī and Naktā are all well known in the Nighaṇṭu as names of night.

ಸಾಧ್ವಪಾಂಸಿ ಸನತಾ ನ ಉಕ್ಷಿತೇ ಉಷಾಸಾನಕ್ತಾ ವಯ್ಯೇವ ರಣ್ವಿತೇ ।
ತಂತುಂ ತತಂ ಸಂವಯಂತೀ ಸಮೀಚೀ ಯಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಪೇಶಃ ಸುದುಘೇ ಪಯಸ್ವತೀ ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3- *[the reference is cut off in the supplied text: "(ಋ. ಸಂ. ೨-೩-" with no closing; the last number(s) are missing] **NOTE***)

In Ṛks such as this, by such descriptions as तंतु ततं संवयंती (*taṃtu tataṃ saṃvayaṃtī*), the help of Uṣāsānaktā in the extension of the sacrifice is seen.

वाजयंतीः (*vājayaṃtīḥ*)—It is not easy to state the exact meaning of this word. As the Nirukta authors say, वाजयतीत्यर्चतिकर्मा (*vājayatītyarcatikarmā*) (Nir. 3-19) (the print has वाजयॆति (*vājayèti*) in the next sentence, as supplied), since this word belongs among the names of the act of worshipping, it can also be said that Uṣāsānaktā are those who worship Agni in this sacrificial act. This word is read not only among the names of food but also among the names of battle. The word can also mean strength. If the uses of this word are examined, in Ṛks such as

ಇಂದ್ರ ಋಭುಭಿರ್ವಾಜಿಭಿರ್ವಾಜಯನ್ನಿಹ ಸ್ತೋಮಂ ಜರಿತುರುಪ ಯಾಹಿ ಯಜ್ಞಿಯಂ ।

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-60-7)

it is, as said in the present Ṛk, अन्नं कुर्वाणः (*annaṃ kurvāṇaḥ*) ("making food"); and

### Printed p. 274

*[A stray line "35" stands at the end of p. 273 in the supplied text; kept as supplied.]*

ಏವಾ ತ ಇಂದ್ರೋಚಥಮಹೇಮ ಶ್ರವಸ್ಯಾ ನ ತ್ಮನಾ ವಾಜಯಂತಃ ।

(printed "ಮಿ. ಸಂ. ೨-೧೯-೭", i.e. "Mi. Saṃ. 2-19-7", as supplied)

in such Ṛks बलिनं कुर्वतः (*balinaṃ kurvataḥ*) ("making strong"); and

ಮಾಂ ನರಃ ಸ್ವಶ್ವಾ ವಾಜಯಂತೋ ಮಾಂ ವೃತಾಃ ಸಮರಣೇ ಹವಂತೇ ।

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-42-5)

in such places संग्राममिच्छंतः (*saṃgrāmamicchaṃtaḥ*) ("desiring battle"); and

ಸ ಮಾತರಾ ವಿಚರನ್ವಾಜಯನ್ನಪಃ ಪ್ರ ಮೇಧಿರಃ ಸ್ವಧಯಾ ಪಿನ್ವತೇ ಪದಂ ।

(printed "ಮಿ. ಸಂ. ೯-೬೮-೪", i.e. "Mi. Saṃ. 9-68-4", as supplied)

in such places प्रेरयन् (*prerayan*) ("impelling"). Thus used in many senses, in the present Ṛk the meaning अन्नं कुर्वाणे (*annaṃ kurvāṇe*), as the commentator says, is appropriate. The connection of Uṣāsānaktā with Agni and their help in the sacrificial work has been explained above.

वातस्य पथ्याभिः अच्छ (*vātasya pathyābhiḥ accha*)—त्वमपि वायोः मार्गैः तावहोरात्रौ शीघ्रमभिगच्छ (*tvamapi vāyoḥ mārgaiḥ tāvahorātrau śīghramabhigaccha*) (the print has a hyphen after अच्छ (*accha*), as supplied). The wish is that Agni should follow day and night by the path of the wind, the path along which the wind moves.

पूर्वं हविर्भिः सीं अंजंति (*pūrvaṃ havirbhiḥ sīṃ aṃjaṃti*) (so printed, पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*) where the Ṛk has pūrvyaṃ)—पुरातनं त्वां ऋत्विजः आज्यादिभिः सर्वतः सिंचंति (*purātanaṃ tvāṃ ṛtvijaḥ ājyādibhiḥ sarvataḥ siṃcaṃti*). The word पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*) is stated among the names of the ancient (Nir. 3-20). The particle सीं (*sīṃ*) is used in the sense of "grasping" (parigraha) and in the sense of a mere word-filler, as in सीमिति परिग्रहार्थियो वा पदपूरणो वा (*sīmiti parigrahārthiyo vā padapūraṇo vā*) "प्रसीमादित्यो असृजत् (*prasīmādityo asṛjat*)" प्रासृजत् सर्वत इति वा व्यवृणोत् सर्वत आदित्यः (*prāsṛjat sarvata iti vā vyavṛṇot sarvata ādityaḥ*) (Nir. 1-7). But in प्रसीं आदित्यः (*prasīṃ ādityaḥ*) the word सीं (*sīṃ*) is explained as meaning सर्वतः (*sarvataḥ*). The meaning is described thus: the priests satisfy the ancient Agni in every way with oblations and with ghee. Then he explains अहोरात्राग्न्योः परस्पराभिगमनेनान्योन्यसंबंधः (*ahorātrāgnyoḥ parasparābhigamanenānyonyasaṃbaṃdhaḥ*): just as day and night, the day being related to the night and the night to the day, follow each other mutually, so Agni, following and being related to both day and night, is therefore regularly worshipped by the sacrificers with oblations at the evening and morning times.

बंधुरेव दुरोणे आ तस्थतुः (*baṃdhureva duroṇe ā tasthatuḥ*)—यथा कूवरस्थानं परस्परसंसक्तेषाद्वयोपेतं तद्वत्संसक्तौ तावहोरात्रौ अस्माकं गृहे अग्निहोत्रादिकर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं पुनः पुनरावर्तमानौ संतौ तिष्ठतां (*yathā kūvarasthānaṃ parasparasaṃsakteṣādvayopetaṃ tadvatsaṃsaktau tāvahorātrau asmākaṃ gṛhe agnihotrādikarmasiddhyarthaṃ punaḥ punarāvartamānau saṃtau tiṣṭhatāṃ*). The word दुरोणॆ (*duroṇè*) is stated among the names of the house (Nir. 3-13) and is explained as दुरोणइति गृहनाम दुरवा भवंति दुस्तर्पाः (*duroṇaiti gṛhanāma duravā bhavaṃti dustarpāḥ*) (Nir. 4-5). Just as the driver's seat, joined firmly to each other by two planks, is firm, so day and night, closely joined with one another, for the accomplishment of rites such as the Agnihotra, the repeated coming round (āvṛtti) again and again

### Printed p. 275

(Special Topics of Ṛk 3, concluded:) ... that these two, day and night, attaining in our houses a fixed state favourable for performing the several rites, may stay (there) — so he has wished.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(grammar page, noted briefly)*

द्रवतां (*dravatāṃ*): root द्रु (*dru*) in the sense of going; loṭ, third person singular, ending त (*ta*); for its टि (*ṭi*) the ending ए (*e*) is replaced by the ām-substitute by the rule आमेतः (*āmetaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-90); guṇa of the root vowel उ (*u*) because of शप् (*śap*); av-substitution; being at the beginning of the pāda, no nighāta accent; the root accent remains because the vikaraṇa endings are anudātta.

वाजयंती (*vājayaṃtī*): वाजं करोति इति वाजयंती (*vājaṃ karoti iti vājayaṃtī*); the ending णिच् (*ṇic*) by the statement तत्करोति तदाचष्टे (*tatkaroti tadācaṣṭe*); then शतृ (*śatṛ*) and शप् (*śap*) after the णिज (*ṇija*)-ending form; guṇa and ay-substitution of the इ (*i*) of णिच् (*ṇic*); feminine जीप् (*jīp*) by उगितश्च (*ugitaśca*); by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the लसार्वधातुक (*lasārvadhātuka*) is anudātta, so the णिच् (*ṇic*) accent remains; before the nominative dual, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*), the preceding-similar long vowel.

पथ्याभिः (*pathyābhiḥ*): पथिषु साधवः पथ्या (*pathiṣu sādhavaḥ pathyā*); the ending यत् (*yat*) in the sense "good in it" by तत्र साधुः (*tatra sādhuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 4-4-98); since the word ends in न् (*n*), loss of टि (*ṭi*) (इन् (*in*)) by नस्तद्धिते (*nastaddhite*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-144); svarita accent by तित्स्वरितं (*titsvaritaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185); instrumental plural form.

अंजंति (*aṃjaṃti*): root अंजू (*aṃjū*) (व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिषु (*vyaktimrakṣaṇakāṃtigatiṣu*), as supplied); laṭ, third person plural; because of the connection with यत् (*yat*) no nighāta accent; the ending's first-syllable acute makes it middle-acute.

तस्थतुः (*tasthatuḥ*): root ष्ठा (*ṣṭhā*) (गतिनिवृत्तौ (*gatinivṛttau*)); liṭ, third person dual; the dual ending atus substituted by परस्मैपदानां (*parasmaipadānāṃ*) ...; reduplication of the root; त (*ta*) in the reduplicative syllable by शर्पूर्वा खयः (*śarpūrvā khayaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-61); since it stands after a non-verb word (as supplied "ಅತಿಜಂತದ ಪರದಲ್ಲಿ"), nighāta accent comes.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मि॒त्रश्च॒ तुभ्यं॒ वरु॑णः सह॒स्वोऽग्ने॒ विश्वे॑ म॒रुतः॑ सु॒म्मम॑र्चन् ।  
> यच्छो॒चिषा॑ सहसस्पुत्र॒ तिष्ठा॑ अ॒भि क्षि॒तीः प्र॒थय॒न्त्सूर्यो॒ न्यून् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मित्रः । च । तुभ्यं । वरुणः । सहस्रः । अग्ने । विश्वे । मरुतः । सुम्नं । अर्चन् ।  
> यत् । शोचिषा । सहसः । पुत्र । तिष्ठाः । अभि । क्षितीः । प्रथयन् । सूर्यः । स्वान्॥

> *mitraḥ | ca | tubhyaṃ | varuṇaḥ | sahasraḥ | agne | viśve | marutaḥ | sumnaṃ | arcan |*  
> *yat | śociṣā | sahasaḥ | putra | tiṣṭhāḥ | abhi | kṣitīḥ | prathayan | sūryaḥ | svān‖*

*[Pada compared with Saṃhitā, as supplied: Pada सहस्रः (*sahasraḥ*) against Saṃhitā सहस्वः (*sahasvaḥ*); Pada सुम्नं (*sumnaṃ*) against Saṃhitā सुम्मं (*summaṃ*); Pada स्वान् (*svān*) against the Saṃhitā ending न्यून् (*nyūn*); the Saṃhitā has तिष्ठा (*tiṣṭhā*) where the Pada has तिष्ठाः (*tiṣṭhāḥ*). Kept as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहस्वो बलवन् हे अग्ने मित्रश्च वरुणश्च मित्रावरुणौ विश्वे मरुतः सर्वे
> देवाश्च तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं सुम्मं स्तोत्रमर्चन् । वहंति । यद्वा सर्वे देवास्तुभ्यं
> त्वां सुम्मं सुखेनार्चन् पूजयंति । यद्यस्मात्कारणात्सहसस्पुत्र हे अग्ने सूर्यः
> सुष्टु आर्यः स्वामी यद्वा सर्वांतर्यामितया सुष्टुप्रेरको यद्वा सूर्यः
> शोभनवीयोर्भि क्षितीः । क्षितिशब्दो मनुष्यवाची । विशः क्षितय इति तन्नामसु
> पाठात् । मनुष्यानभिलक्ष्य नृन् मार्गप्रदर्शकत्वेन नेत्यन् आत्मनो रश्मिन्
> प्रथयन्सर्वतो विस्तारयंस्त्वं शोचिषा दीप्ता समानः सन् शिष्ठाः । तिष्ठसि ।
> तस्मादेते देवाः पूजयंतीति ॥ अर्चन् । अर्च पूजायामित्यस्य लजि रूपं ।
> अडभावश्चांदसः । तिष्ठाः । ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तावित्यस्य लेटि रूपं । यद्योगादनिघातः ।
> पाघ्रेत्यादिना तिष्ठादेशस्याद्युदात्तत्वेन निपातनादाद्युदात्तः । सूर्यः । राजसूय
> सूर्यॆति क्यबंतत्वेन निपातनात्सर्वार्थाः सिद्धा भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Strong Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa and all the Maruts (all gods) offer praise to you, or worship you with joy; because you, as the sun, spread your rays over men and shine, they do so. The grammatical tail explains अर्चन् (*arcan*), तिष्ठाः (*tiṣṭhāḥ*) and सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O) सहसः पुत्र (*sahasaḥ putra*)—O Agni, son of strength
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- सूर‍्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—(as the inner controller of all) the impeller of all, or (you) endowed with good capacity; क्षितीः अभि (*kṣitīḥ abhi*)—towards men
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—(your rays), the guides of the way
- प्रथर्य (*pratharya*) [sic, as supplied; apparently प्रथयन् (*prathayan*) of the Saṃhitā]—spreading everywhere
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with brightness (remaining equal everywhere)
- तिष्ठाः (*tiṣṭhāḥ*)—you stay
- (तत् (*tat*)—therefore) सहस्वः (*sahasvaḥ*)—mighty; (O) अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni; मित्रः वरुणः च (*mitraḥ varuṇaḥ ca*)—both Mitra and Varuṇa; विश्वे मरुतः (*viśve marutaḥ*)—all the deities
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)—praise
- अर्चन् (*arcan*)—carry (offer). [Or तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—you
- सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)—happily
- अर्चन् (*arcan*)—they worship.]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength and yourself mighty, you the impeller of all spread everywhere your rays that guide men on the way; therefore Mitra and Varuṇa, the Maruts and all the other deities praise you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Vigorous AGNI, to you, MITRA and VARUNA, and all the MARUTS, offer praise; since, son of strength, you stand a sun, shedding (your) rays with lustre on mankind.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सहस्व :—विश्वे मरुतः तुभ्यं सुम्ममर्चन्—बलवन् हे आग्ने सर्वॆ देवाश्च त्वदर्थं स्तोत्रं वहंति यद्वा सर्वॆ देवास्तुभ्यं त्वां सुम्मं सुखेनार्चन् (*sahasva :—viśve marutaḥ tubhyaṃ summamarcan—balavan he āgne sarvè devāśca tvadarthaṃ stotraṃ vahaṃti yadvā sarvè devāstubhyaṃ tvāṃ summaṃ sukhenārcan*) (the passage runs across the page break; as supplied the first word "ಆಗ್ನೇ" has a long ā)

### Printed p. 277

पूजयंति । (*pūjayaṃti |*) The word सुम्मं (*summaṃ*) is stated among the names of happiness (Nir. 3-13). The word सहस् (*sahas*) is read both among the names of water (Nir. 2-24) and among the names of strength (Nir. 3-9). Here, addressing Agni as one possessing abundant strength, one kind of meaning has been given: all the deities worship Agni, uttering praises. In the second alternative, where सुम्म (*summa*) is taken to mean happiness, the meaning is explained that all the deities worship Agni with joy.

सूर्यः—सुष्टु अर्यः स्वामी। यद्वा सर्वांतर्यामितया सुष्टु प्रेरकः । यद्वा शोभनवीर्यः। (*sūryaḥ—suṣṭu aryaḥ svāmī| yadvā sarvāṃtaryāmitayā suṣṭu prerakaḥ | yadvā śobhanavīryaḥ|*) Yāska (has said): सूर्यः सर्तेर्वा, सुवतेर्वा, स्वीर्यतेर्वा (*sūryaḥ sartervā, suvatervā, svīryatervā*) (Nir. 12-14). From the root सृ (*sṛ*) in the sense of going the word सूर्य (*sūrya*) is formed; on this view the meaning is "the one who moves about". When formed from the root "ಶೂಞ್" meaning "to bring forth", the meaning is "the one who creates". In giving the formation of the word सूर्य (*sūrya*) from the root ईर् (*īr*) [as supplied "ಈಶ"] in the sense of going or trembling, with the prefix सु (*su*), (Yāska says) वायुना ह्ययं सुष्टु ईर्यते प्रेय्यते (*vāyunā hyayaṃ suṣṭu īryate preyyate*) — that he is impelled exceedingly by the wind. Having thus explained the meaning in three ways, (Sāyaṇa) has cited, to teach the identity of the well-known Sūrya with Agni Jātavedas, the Ṛk

उदु त्यं जातवेदसं देवं वहन्ति केतवः । दृशे विश्वाय सूर्यं ॥ (*udu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ | dṛśe viśvāya sūryaṃ ‖*)

(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೧-೫೦-೧", i.e. "Ma. Saṃ. 1-50-1", as supplied)

And, to teach the all-pervasiveness of this Sūrya, he has cited the Ṛk

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अंतरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥ (*citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī aṃtarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1)

Here, it has been established that the well-known Agni has the qualities seen in the sun, and the meaning has been given: Agni is the lord of all, the inner controller of all, therefore the impeller of all, and one with excellent valour.

अभिक्षितीः न्यून् प्रथयन्—क्षितिशब्दः मनुष्यवाची मनुष्यानभिलक्ष्य मार्गप्रदर्शकत्वेन नेत्यन् आत्मनो रश्मी सर्वतः विस्तारयन् दीप्त्या समानस्तिष्ठसि । (*abhikṣitīḥ nyūn prathayan—kṣitiśabdaḥ manuṣyavācī manuṣyānabhilakṣya mārgapradarśakatvena netyan ātmano raśmī sarvataḥ vistārayan dīptyā samānastiṣṭhasi |*) The word क्षिति (*kṣiti*) is stated among the words for the earth (Nir. 2-5) and, as क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*), among the words for men (Nir. 3-7). Just as the sun shines in all places with his radiance, with rays that are like means of protection suited to the various men, rays that drive away darkness and lead men along the right way, so Agni too, with the brightness of his rays, spreads out as a guide of the way and shines; thus the comparison with the sun is stated indirectly through a common quality, and explained here in the manner of poetry. [The print has "ಹರಡಿರುವ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸುವನೆಂದು", as supplied.]

### Printed p. 278

न्यून् (*nyūn*)—आत्मनो रश्मिन् (*ātmano raśmin*): The word नरः (*naraḥ*) is stated both among the names of horses (Nir. 2-27) and among the names of men (Nir. 3-7). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as "the rays of Agni".

विश्वे मरुतः (*viśve marutaḥ*)—Here the word मरुत् (*marut*) is given the meaning "the gods". The authors of the Nirukta have read the word मरुत् (*marut*) among the names of priests (Nir. 3-19) and among the names of gold (Nir. 2-10). But if the word well known as the name of the Marut deities gives the meaning "priest", "gold" and in some places "gods", it takes some effort to learn what the root of this word is, how its formation is possible, and what its derivation is when it denotes the Marut deities. For this word, as used of the Marut deities, the authors of the Nirukta have also given the following etymology.

मरुतो मितराविनो वा मितरोचिनो वा महद्द्रवंतीति वा । (*maruto mitarāvino vā mitarocino vā mahaddravaṃtīti vā |*)

(printed "ಸಿ. ೧೧-೧೪", i.e. "Si. 11-14", as supplied; the Nirukta is presumably meant)

The name is (given) because they are of measured (regulated) sound, or of measured (regulated) brilliance, or because they run with great speed; having thus cited Ṛk 1-8-1, he has explained the nature of the Maruts.

Having said that it is difficult to give a proper etymology of this word, which has so many meanings, the scholar Max Muller has spoken as follows.

Marut or Maruta in ordinary Sanskrit mean wind, and more particularly a strong wind, differing by its violent character from Vayu or Vata. Nor do the hymns themselves leave us in any doubt as to the natural phenomena with which the Maruts are identified. Storms which root up the trees of the forest, lightning, thunder and showers of rain are the background from which the Maruts in their personal and dramatic character rise before our eyes. In most of the later native dictionaries, in the मेदिनी (*medinī*), विश्व (*viśva*), हेमचंद्र (*hemacaṃdra*), अमर (*amara*), अनेकार्थमंजरी (*anekārthamaṃjarī*), Marut is given a synonym of देव (*deva*), or God in general and so is Maru in Pali.

But, while the hymns addressed to the Maruts enable us to watch the successive stages in the development of so called deities more clearly than any other hymns, there is, no doubt, one drawback, namely, the uncertainty of the etymology of Marut. The etymology of the name is and always must be the best key to the original intention of a deity.

### Printed p. 279

With regard to Marut I have myself no doubt whatever that Mar-ut comes from the root MAR in the sense of grinding, crushing, pounding (like मृणाति (*mṛṇāti*), मृदित (*mṛdita*) etc.). There is no objection to this etymology either on the ground of phonetic rules, or on account of the meaning of Marut. Professor Kuhn's idea that the name of the Maruts was derived from the root मृ (*mṛ*) to die and that the Maruts were originally conceived as the souls of the departedo [sic] and afterwards as ghosts, spirits, winds and lastly as storms, derives ns, [sic] support from the Veda. Another etymology, proposed in Bohtlingk' [sic] Dictionary, which derives Marut from a root मृ (*mṛ*) to strive, labours under two disadvantages ; first that there is no such root in Sanskrit ; secondly, that the lurid splendour of the lightning is but a subordinate feature in the character of the Maruts. No better etymology having been proposed,, [sic] I still maintain that the derivation of Marut from मृ (*mṛ*) to pound, to smash, is free from any objection and that the original conception of the Maruts was that of crushing, smashing, striking, tearing, and the destroying storms.

[The Vedic Hymns. Sacred Books of the East Vol. XXXII—p. 24.]

In the above sentences this scholar has stated the opinions of Western scholars such as Kuhn and has also pointed out the defects in them. Giving his own opinion, he has said that this word is formed from the root मृ (*mṛ*), meaning violence, and denotes a special power that cuts down trees and the like. The use of the word Marut for priests also exists, because they press out Soma and the like. Since the authors of the Nirukta have said that the name became well known because they have measured brilliance, and since gods and gold have this quality, the name appears to have become well known on that account.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* अर्चन् (*arcan*): root अर्च पूजायां (*arca pūjāyāṃ*); Vedic imperfect (laṅ) third person plural in -jhi, loss of i, ending replaced, loss of t; the augment aṭ does not occur (Pā. 6-4-75); the nighāta accent follows. शोचिषा (*śociṣā*): root शुच दीप्तौ (*śuca dīptau*) with the Uṇādi suffix -isi, guṇa of the light penultimate vowel, instrumental singular. तिष्ठाः (*tiṣṭhāḥ*): root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*), leṭ second person singular, ending sip; the replacement tiṣṭha by Pā. 7-3-78, visarga; no nighāta because of the connection with yat (the word यत्); the word is initially acute.

### Printed p. 280

The note on तिष्ठाः (*tiṣṭhāḥ*) continues from p. 279: loss of the i of the ending by Pā. 3-4-92, the vikaraṇa śap, the replacement of the root by tiṣṭha (Pā. 7-3-78), the ending s becoming ru and visarga, the form तिष्ठाः (*tiṣṭhāḥ*). सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*): root सृ गतौ (*sṛ gatau*), formed with a final kyap by the sūtra राजसूय सूर्य (*rājasūya sūrya*) (Pā. 3-1-114); because the suffix has p as an indicatory letter, the root accent remains.
