##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, we, with open palms, offer you today the desired havis, approaching with homage; with a most sacrificial mind, being wise, worship the gods with a ceaseless, abundant hymn. The tail explains अद्य (*adya*), ररिम (*rarima*), उपसद्य (*upasadya*), यक्षि (*yakṣi*) and अस्रेधता (*asredhatā*).

### Printed p. 281

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(हे) अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. उत्तानहस्ताः (*uttānahastāḥ*)—having hands raised upward. वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we. कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—desirable (to the gods; the oblation of purodāśa and the like). ते (*te*)—to you. अद्य (*adya*)—now (in this rite). ररिम (*rarima*)—we offer [the full stop after "offer" is as supplied]. नमसा (*namasā*)—(by our) homage. उपसद्य (*upasadya*)—having become pleased. यजिष्ठेन (*yajiṣṭhena*)—with a firm wish to perform the sacrifice. मनसा (*manasā*)—with the inner mind. देवान् (*devān*)—the gods. यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—worship; (and) विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—(skilled in rites) wise (you). आस्रोधता (*āsrodhatā*) [sic: the Pratipadārtha has आस्रोधता (*āsrodhatā*) where the Special Topics and grammar notes have अस्रेधता (*asredhatā*); kept as supplied]—unwasting (abundant). मन्मना (*manmanā*)—with praise. (देवान् यक्षि (*devān yakṣi*)—worship the gods.)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, with hands holding the oblation, raising our hands upward, we now offer to you in this sacrifice the oblation of purodāśa and the like, which is dear to the gods; pleased by our homage and so on, and with a strong wish to perform the sacrifice for the gods, worship the gods; and you, who are skilled in the rites, praise those gods abundantly.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
With uplifted hands, approaching you with reverence, we present to you to day our oblation : do you, who are wise, worship the gods with most devout mind and with unwearied praise.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उत्तानहस्ता (*uttānahastā*)—हविःस्वीकरणादुत्तानपाणयः (*haviḥsvīkaraṇāduttānapāṇayaḥ*) (those whose palms are turned up to receive the oblation). Yāska has explained the meaning of the word उत्तान (*uttāna*) as उत्तान, उत्ततान, उर्ध्वतानो वा (*uttāna, uttatāna, urdhvatāno vā*) (Nir. 4-21) [the third form printed उर्ध्वतानो (*urdhvatāno*), as supplied]. Here, addressing Agni, the text expresses the wish: "We, the priests, with hands whose palms are turned upward, that is, raising our hands and holding the oblations, will offer to Agni, in the sacrifices, oblations such as the tasty purodāśa that produce pleasure in Agni."

नमसा उपसद्य यजिष्ठेन मनसा देवान् यक्षि (*namasā upasadya yajiṣṭhena manasā devān yakṣi*)—नमस्कारेण प्रसन्नो भूत्वा यागेन अच्छावता अंतःकरणेन यजनीयान् देवास् यज पूजय (*namaskāreṇa prasanno bhūtvā yāgena acchāvatā aṃtaḥkaraṇena yajanīyān devās yaja pūjaya*) (as supplied; the bhāṣya has yāgecchāvatā in the corresponding place). The wish is expressed that Agni, pleased by the homage of us priests, should worship, with an inner mind purified by accepting the oblation offered in our sacrifice, the gods who are worthy of worship in the sacrifice. And since the word विप्र (*vipra*) is read among the names of the wise (Nir. 3-19), it is wished that Agni, who is skilled in the sacrificial acts, should worship the gods with a hymn that is much to be meditated upon.

*[A stray line "36" follows at the end of this page, as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 282

अस्रेधता (*asredhatā*)—the meaning "unwasting, abundant, and therefore excessive, because it does not reach decay, that is, a state of diminution" is described.

मन्मना (*manmanā*)—here the meaning "with praise fit to be meditated upon" is described: मंतव्येन स्तोत्रेण (*maṃtavyena stotreṇa*).

This word is used in the senses "praiseworthy, worshipful". In many Ṛks, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-26-2; 1-127-2; 1-151-8 and others, the words मन्मना (*manmanā*) and मन्मभिः (*manmabhiḥ*) mean an excellent and praiseworthy movement of the mind. The authors of the Nirukta cite three Ṛks in which the word मन्म (*manma*) is used. First,

उप प्रागात्सुमन्मेऽधायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्ठः । अन्नेनं विप्रा ऋषयो मदंति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबंधुं ॥ (*upa prāgātsumanme 'dhāyi manma devānāmāśā upa vītapṛṣṭhaḥ | annenaṃ viprā ṛṣayo madaṃti devānāṃ puṣṭe cakṛmā subaṃdhuṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-7) [text as supplied, with its irregularities]

In this Ṛk the authors of the Nirukta (Nir. 6-22) have explained the word मन्म (*manma*) as "mantra": that is, a mantra fit to be thought over, fit for meditation. Sāyaṇa has explained it as "the fruit fit to be thought over".

Second,

तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समंजन्त्सदया सुजिह्व । मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृंधन् देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥ (*tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samaṃjantsadayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛṃdhan devatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-2) [text as supplied]

Here they have explained the meaning as अस्मदभिप्रेतानि स्तोत्राणि (*asmadabhipretāni stotrāṇi*) (hymns desired by us). In the same way, citing also the Ṛk 1-129.9 (the full stop in the number as supplied) (Nir. 19-42), they have shown that the same meaning applies there. In the present Ṛk the meaning is "with a praiseworthy mantra".

If the meaning of the parts of this word is to be stated, the sense is "the wish of the mind". In many Saṃhitā passages the use of this word indicates an object that shows an excellent desire. This desired object may be the fruit of the sacrifice, a hymn, or an oblation. In sentences such as अग्निः प्रत्नेन मन्मना (*agniḥ pratnena manmanā*) (Ai. Brā. 1-4) one may likewise note the superlative sense of this word.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* अद्य (*adya*)—अस्मिन् अहनि अद्य (*asmin ahani adya*); by सद्यः परुत् परारि (*sadyaḥ parut parāri*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-22) the replacement of the word idam by aś and the suffix dya are irregularly formed; hence final acute accent. ररिम (*rarima*)—root रा दाने (*rā dāne*), Vedic liṭ in the sense of the present; by Pā. Sū. 3-4-82 the ending masi of the first person plural is replaced by ma; the augment iḍ follows by the rule on kra-class roots; since the ending is kit (Pā. Sū. 1-2-5), the ā of the root is dropped by आतोलोप इटिच (*ātolopa iṭica*) (Pā. 6-4-64); the form is ररिम (*rarima*); because of the connection with hi, nighāta is prohibited by हिच (*hica*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34); the augment iḍ being unaccented, the ending accent makes the word acute on the final.

### Printed p. 283

Grammar notes continued. उत्तानहस्ताः (*uttānahastāḥ*)—by Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 (bahuvrīhi) the first member keeps its own accent. उपसद्य (*upasadya*)—upa is a preposition; root षदल् (*ṣadal*) in the senses of loosening, going, perishing; with the suffix ktvā, lyap is substituted (Pā. Sū. 3-1-37 as printed); the suffix having l as an indicatory letter, by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the acute falls on the syllable before the suffix; in the compound the accent of the last member comes. यजिष्ठेन (*yajiṣṭhena*)—the root yaj, with tṛc and then the suffix iṣṭhan in the sense of excess; loss of tṛc; initial acute by the nit accent; instrumental singular. यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—root yaj in the senses of worship, association, giving; laṭ-type imperative second person singular with sip; luk of śap; the j becomes ṣ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-26), the ṣ before s becomes k (Pā. Sū. 8-2-41), the s of the ending becomes ṣ; the form यक्षि (*yakṣi*); the replacement by hi does not occur in the Veda; the accent of a finite verb (nighāta) follows. अस्रेधता (*asredhatā*)—the root sridh is used in the sense of decay; the replacement śatṛ for liṭ; vikaraṇa śap; guṇa of the light penultimate vowel; "that which does not decay" is the negative compound; by Pā. Sū. 622 (printed without hyphens, as supplied) the first member keeps its own accent.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, son of strength, many protections (guarding the rite) and foods come to the sacrificer from you; give us a thousandfold wealth and a true son with guileless speech. The tail explains त्वत् (*tvat*), देहि (*dehi*) and अद्रोघेण (*adrogheṇa*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

सहसः पुत्र (*sahasaḥ putra*)—son of strength. (हे (*he*)) अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. देवस्य (*devasya*)—to the sacrificer engaged in performing rites. त्वत् (*tvat*)—from you. पूर्वीति (*pūrvīti*)—abundant (of many kinds). ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections, in the form of guarding the rite. वि यंति हि (*vi yaṃti hi*)—reach in various forms, indeed [the supplied text has यष्टॆ (*yaṣṭè*) for "indeed", as supplied]. (तथा (*tathā*)—likewise.) वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)—foods too. वि(यंति) (*vi(yaṃti)*)—reach; (and) (हे अग्ने (*he agne*)—O Agni.) त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you. सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—consisting of a thousand. रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth. नः (*naḥ*)—to us. देहि (*dehi*)—give; (in the same way) अद्रोघेण (*adrogheṇa*)—free from guile (sin). वचसा (*vacasā*)—endowed with speech, सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—of truthful nature (a son also). (देहि (*dehi*)—grant.)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength, you protect in many ways, by guarding the sacrifice and in other ways, the sacrificer who performs rites for you [the supplied text has नीन्न (*nīnna*) where "you" is meant; as supplied]. In the same way grant us also wealth of a thousandfold number, and a son whose speech is free from guile and the like and who walks the good path.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
From you, verily, son of strength, many and various benefactions and various kinds of food devolve upon the devout (worshipper) : grant us, AGNI, infinite wealth; and (a son) observant of truth, with speech devoid of guile.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*[The Kannada label is printed विशेषणगळु (*viśeṣaṇagaḷu*) ("Epithets") in the supplied text; the standard label was inserted and the printed word kept as a line, see repair_log.txt.]*

सहसः पुत्रः (*sahasaḥ putraḥ*)—because he is born from the power of churning, through the exercise of strength, Agni has epithets such as सहसस्पुत्रः (*sahasasputraḥ*) and सहसः सूनुः (*sahasaḥ sūnuḥ*) [the supplied text has the words आदि गॆ (*ādi gè*) before them, apparently for "to Agni"; kept as supplied].

### Printed p. 285

अयं हि द्रविणोदोऽग्निरयं दाशा बलस्य हि । जायते च बलेनायं मध्यकृत्कृषिभिरध्वरे ॥ (*ayaṃ hi draviṇodo 'gnirayaṃ dāśā balasya hi | jāyate ca balenāyaṃ madhyakṛtkṛṣibhiradhvare ‖*)

(Bṛ. De. 3-61; 3-65)

It is stated in the Bṛhaddevatā passages that this epithet belongs to Agni because he is a giver of strength and because he is born from strength. As examples,

अस्माकमग्ने अध्वरं जुषस्व सहसः सूनो त्रिषधस्थ हव्यं । (*asmākamagne adhvaraṃ juṣasva sahasaḥ sūno triṣadhastha havyaṃ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-4-8)

यस्ते अग्ने सुमतिं मर्तो अक्षत्सहसः सूनो अति स प्र शृण्वे ॥ (*yaste agne sumatiṃ marto akṣatsahasaḥ sūno ati sa pra śṛṇve ‖*)

(Pu. Saṃ. 10-11-7) [printed "ಪು. ಸಂ.", as supplied]

in many such Ṛks this quality of Agni is mentioned and described.

देवस्य (*devasya*)—देवनशीलस्य कर्मकरणप्रवृत्तस्य यजमानस्य (*devanaśīlasya karmakaraṇapravṛttasya yajamānasya*). The word देव (*deva*) has been explained as दानाद्वा दीपनाद्वा द्योतनाद्वा द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा (*dānādvā dīpanādvā dyotanādvā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā*) (Nir. 7-15). The details of this were given in the previous Ṛk. Here the word देव (*deva*), derived from the root div, is taken to mean one of luminous nature, and the meaning "the sacrificer engaged in sacrificial acts" is stated.

पूर्वी ऊतयः (*pūrvī ūtayaḥ*)—प्रभूताः विघ्नपरिहारेण कर्मपरिपालनादिरूपाः रक्षाः (*prabhūtāḥ vighnaparihāreṇa karmaparipālanādirūpāḥ rakṣāḥ*). Having explained the word पूर्वी (*pūrvī*) as "abundant" or "excessive", the greatness of Agni is shown: by the favour of Agni, son of strength (born from strength), the acts of the sacrifice performed by the sacrificer are carried out with excessive protections, so that no kind of obstacle comes. With this idea the bhāṣya describes the meaning of the words रक्षाः वियंति (*rakṣāḥ viyaṃti*) by the sentence विविधं गभृंति तमिमं यजमानं प्राप्पुवंति (*vividhaṃ gabhṛṃti tamimaṃ yajamānaṃ prāppuvaṃti*) [as supplied; the bhāṣya block has गच्छंति (*gacchaṃti*) and प्राप्रुवंति (*prāpruvaṃti*) in the corresponding place] and अन्नानि यजमानं पाप्पुवंति (*annāni yajamānaṃ pāppuvaṃti*) , namely that through the favour of Agni abundant food also reaches the sacrificer.

सहस्रिणं रयर नः देहि (*sahasriṇaṃ rayara naḥ dehi*) [रयर (*rayara*) as supplied; the Saṃhitā has रयिं (*rayiṃ*)]—the prayer is made that Agni's wealth consisting of a thousand (a thousand in number) be granted to us who perform the sacrifice [the supplied text has the genitive अग्निय (*agniya*) "of Agni" here; the sense is the prayer to Agni to grant it].

अद्रोघेण वचसा सत्यं देहि (*adrogheṇa vacasā satyaṃ dehi*)—द्रोहरहितेन पापशून्येन वाक्येन युक्तं सत्यशीलं सन्मार्गे प्रवर्तमानं पुत्रं च प्रयच्छ (*droharahitena pāpaśūnyena vākyena yuktaṃ satyaśīlaṃ sanmārge pravartamānaṃ putraṃ ca prayaccha*). The prayer for Agni's favour is made that there be born to the sacrificer a son whose words wish evil to no one, who speaks true words, and who follows the path of good men.

सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—this word is stated among the names of water (Nir. 2-24), and it is explained as सत्सु कायते सत्पभवं भवतीति ना (*satsu kāyate satpabhavaṃ bhavatīti nā*) (Nir 3-13) [printed without the full stop after नि (*ni*)]. Here it is used in the sense "of truthful nature" [सत्यशीलनादॆ (*satyaśīlanādè*) as supplied].

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* त्वत् (*tvat*)—stem युष्मद् (*yuṣmad*); before the ablative singular ending the stem up to ma is replaced by tva by त्वमावेकवचने (*tvamāvekavacane*); by एकवचनस्यच (*ekavacanasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-32) the ending is replaced by अत् (*at*); loss of the a, pararūpa; by एकादेशउदात्तेनोदात्तः (*ekādeśaudāttenodāttaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-5) the single substitute is acute. पुत्र सहसः (*putra sahasaḥ*)—by परमपि छंदसि (*paramapi chaṃdasi*) the following genitive behaves as part of the preceding word, so by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the whole gets the grave accent. यंति (*yaṃti*)—root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), third person plural of laṭ; हिच (*hica*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34, closing bracket missing in the print) prohibits nighāta, so the root accent remains. देहि (*dehi*)—root डुदाञ् दाने (*ḍudāñ dāne*), loṭ second person singular; replacement hi by सेर्ह्यपिच्च (*serhyapicca*); when the root is reduplicated, the reduplicate is lost by घ्वसोरेद्भावभ्यासलोपश्च (*ghvasoredbhāvabhyāsalopaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-119) and the root vowel becomes e; nighāta follows (the supplied text gives the reason as अतिजंतद परदल्लिरुवुदरिंद (*atijaṃtada paradalliruvudariṃda*), as supplied). अद्रोघेण (*adrogheṇa*)—root द्रुह जिघांसायां (*druha jighāṃsāyāṃ*), suffix ghañ; guṇa of the light penultimate vowel by पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86); the h of the root becomes gh in the Veda; न विद्यते द्रोघः यस्य सः अद्रोघः (*na vidyate droghaḥ yasya saḥ adroghaḥ*), and by नञ्सुभ्यां (*nañsubhyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the final of the last member is acute; instrumental singular.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O capable, all-knowing, shining Agni, we mortal sacrificers have made these offerings for you in the sacrifice; be the protector of every sacrificer with a good chariot, and partake of all this havis. The tail explains अकर्म (*akarma*), बोधि (*bodhi*) and स्वद (*svada*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

दक्ष (*dakṣa*)—capable. कविक्रतो (*kavikrato*)—endowed with knowledge of what is beyond the senses. देव (*deva*)—shining. (हे (*he*)) अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. मर्त्सासः (*martsāsaḥ*) [so printed; the Saṃhitā has मर्तासो (*martāso*)]—we mortals (sacrificers). तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you. यानि इमा (*yāni imā*)—which these oblations and the like. अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice. अकर्म (*akarma*)—we have offered. तत् सर्वं (*tat sarvaṃ*)—all that. (हे (*he*)) अमृत (*amṛta*)—O Agni, free from death. इह (*iha*)—in this rite. स्पद (*spada*) [so printed; the Saṃhitā has स्वद (*svada*)]—taste; (and) त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you. सुरथस्य (*surathasya*)—(helpful to the sacrifice) possessing a good chariot [रथनिशिष्टराद (*rathaniśiṣṭarāda*) so printed; the Bhāvārtha has रथविशिष्टराद (*rathaviśiṣṭarāda*)]. विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of all sacrificers. बोधि (*bodhi*)—be aware (that "I am the protector").

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, capable, knowing what is beyond the senses, shining: oblations and the like are offered in the sacrifices by us mortals, the sacrificers; you also, free from death, with the mind "I will be the protector of all sacrificers who have good chariots helpful to the sacrifice", accept all that has been offered by us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Divine (AGNI), mighty and omniscient, these (are the offerings) which we mortals present to you in the sacrifice : be cognizant of every respectable worshipper, and partake, immortal, of all (his offerings) on this occasion.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दक्ष (*dakṣa*)—समृद्धतया सामर्थ्योपेत (*samṛddhatayā sāmarthyopeta*) [the bhāṣya block has सामर्थोऽपेत (*sāmartho 'peta*); as supplied]. The word दक्ष (*dakṣa*) is read among the names of strength (Nir. 3-9). The meaning is described that Agni is endowed in every way with circumstances that produce every kind of excess, and with abundant capacity.

### Printed p. 288

कविक्रतो (*kavikrato*)—अतींद्रियविषयप्रज्ञोपेत सर्वज्ञ (*atīṃdriyaviṣayaprajñopeta sarvajña*). The word कवि (*kavi*) is used among the names of the wise. The word क्रतु (*kratu*) is explained as कर्म वा प्रज्ञां वा (*karma vā prajñāṃ vā*) (Nir. 2-28). Moreover the word kratu is stated among the names of action (Nir. 3-2) and is also stated among the names of knowledge (Nir. 3-13). Since it is understood from the explanation of the authors of the Nirukta that Agni is wise and possessed of knowledge, and since Agni's power would not be made manifest by this meaning, Sāyaṇa has described the meaning as: Agni is one with knowledge that directly perceives matters that cannot be perceived by the senses.

Besides, this word is used in many places as an epithet of Agni and in some places as an epithet of Soma. In the present Ṛk this epithet shows Agni's supernatural power and knowledge. To know its profound meaning one must know the exact meanings of the word कवि (*kavi*) and of the word क्रतु (*kratu*).

Sāyaṇa has given the word कवि (*kavi*) two kinds of meaning. First, following the śruti sentence ये देवा अनूचानास्ते कवयः (*ye devā anūcānāste kavayaḥ*) [no reference printed], one who has studied the Veda with the Vedāṅgas, a scholar of the śāstras; second, citing the Nirukta sentence कविः मनीषी (*kaviḥ manīṣī*) (Nir. 3-15), the wise.

मेधावी कविः क्रांतदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्ना (*medhāvī kaviḥ krāṃtadarśano bhavati kavaternā*)

(Si. 12-13) [printed "ಸಿ.", as supplied]

Thus the authors of the Nirukta have stated the etymology of the word कवि (*kavi*). Derived from the root kram it can mean one of far-reaching vision (क्रांतदर्शन (*krāṃtadarśana*)); or derived from the root kam it can mean one of lovely vision (कांतदर्शन (*kāṃtadarśana*)); or derived from the root ku it can mean a praiser who praises; this is what the explanation of the Nirukta authors shows. What is the nature of a kavi? What is his power? It is necessary to know for which nature and power the word kavi is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā.

One may say that the word कवि (*kavi*) [so printed as कविपदपू (*kavipadapū*), as supplied] serves to indicate the same power that the words ऋषि (*ṛṣi*), सुमेध (*sumedha*), धीर (*dhīra*) and रेभ (*rebha*) show as a special nature. One who has the extraordinary power of knowing all the dealings of the past, present and future times is the wise one, the seer; he is the kavi. One who has this power is also fit for the creation of poetry in the form of hymns. Therefore the praiser also has names such as कवि (*kavi*) and रेभ (*rebha*). [The slightly different meaning of the words kavi and kāvya in worldly literature and books will be explained later as the context requires.] To show the true nature of the kavi, the authors of the Nirukta (cite the verse),

विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । वि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥ (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catuṣpade | vi nākamakhyatsavitā vareṇyonu prayāṇamuṣaso vi rājati ‖*)

(Ma. Saṃ. 5-81-2) [printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied]

*[The sentence continues on p. 289; the supplied text of this window ends here.]*

### Printed p. 289

Having cited the Ṛk (the Nirukta-authors' verse at the end of p. 288), they have explained what nature of Savitṛ the word कवि (*kavi*), which is an epithet of Savitṛ here, shows. It is understood that Savitṛ has this epithet because he makes all the forms of the world shine. That is, he has the power to make those parts that lie hidden and are not visible to the eye of the world shine forth by his own power and so fall within the sight of the world. In this same sense the name कवि (*kavi*) is also well known for the praiser, the one who offers praise. This idea is indicated in the Ṛksaṃhitā in the Ṛk

ब्रह्मा कृशोति वरुणो गातुविदं तमीमहे । व्यूर्णोति हृदा मतिं नवो जायतामृतं वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥ (*brahmā kṛśoti varuṇo gātuvidaṃ tamīmahe | vyūrṇoti hṛdā matiṃ navo jāyatāmṛtaṃ vittaṃ me asya rodasī ‖*)

(R. Saṃ. 1105-15) [printed "ಋ. ಸಂ. ೧೧೦೫-೧೫", as supplied; the number looks irregular]

and likewise in other Ṛks. In this cited Ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained the word व्यूर्णोति (*vyūrṇoti*) as उच्चारयति (*uccārayati*) and प्रकाशयति (*prakāśayati*) ("makes utter", "makes shine"). The root ऊर्णि (*ūrṇi*) (the root ऊर्णञ् आच्छादने (*ūrṇañ ācchādane*), "to cover", meaning to hide, to cover over) becomes ऊर्णोति (*ūrṇoti*). Here, joined with the prefix वि (*vi*), it gives the meaning of "uncovering that has gone away", that is, removing the veil. The sense is "making manifest". From this it is understood that the power of creation, which manifests mental praise, and the power of showing by making manifest what is hidden, are the special quality of the kavi or praiser. Therefore the word कवि (*kavi*), which denotes the common property of Savitṛ and the praiser, is an epithet of both. Explaining this same nature of the kavi and the work of the kavi, in the Ṛksaṃhitā,

समानं नीळं वृषणो वसानाः सं जग्मिरे महिषा अर्वतीभिः । ऋतस्य पदं कवयो नि पांति गुहा नामानि दधिरे पराणि । (*samānaṃ nīḷaṃ vṛṣaṇo vasānāḥ saṃ jagmire mahiṣā arvatībhiḥ | ṛtasya padaṃ kavayo ni pāṃti guhā nāmāni dadhire parāṇi |*)

(Ma. Saṃ. 10-5-2) [printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied]

बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं यत्प्रेत नामधेयं दधानाः । यदेषां श्रेष्ठं यदरिप्रमासीत्रेणा तदेषां निहितं गुहाविः ॥ (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ yatpreta nāmadheyaṃ dadhānāḥ | yadeṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yadaripramāsītreṇā tadeṣāṃ nihitaṃ guhāviḥ ‖*)

(Ma. Saṃ. 10-71-1)

and in all such Ṛks this idea is expressed. It is described that the kavis, entering the path of the Ṛta, have borne in the most hidden heart the names of the highest secret, and that they make them manifest so that the world may know them. This seeing of the kavi, and his work of making manifest, are possible only by the means that has the form of the sacrifice.

यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन् तामन्वविंदन्नृषिषु प्रविष्टां । तामाभृत्या व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा तां सप्त रेभा अभि सं नवशे ॥ (*yajñena vācaḥ padavīyamāyan tāmanvaviṃdannṛṣiṣu praviṣṭāṃ | tāmābhṛtyā vyadadhuḥ purutrā tāṃ sapta rebhā abhi saṃ navaśe ‖*)

*[A stray line "37" follows in the supplied text, before the reference; kept as a note.]*

(Ma. Saṃ. 10-71-3)

### Printed p. 290

The kavis obtained, by the means that has the form of the sacrifice, the speech (वाक् (*vāk*)) that was hidden in the ṛṣis who see things beyond the senses. Afterwards, for the benefit of the people of the world, they instructed them also. This speech, which has the form of the principle of the universe, is served by the metres Gāyatrī and the others; and so, in some places, the creation that has the form of the manifestation of speech and the action that has the form of the sacrifice are declared to be identical, and in other places to stand in the relation of effect and cause. The same idea is stated in this way in the Śatapatha and the other Brāhmaṇas:

आयुरेतज्योतिः प्रविशति य एतमनु ना ब्रूते भक्षयति वा तस्य व्रत- चर्य्या या सृष्टौ । (*āyuretajyotiḥ praviśati ya etamanu nā brūte bhakṣayati vā tasya vrata- caryyā yā sṛṣṭau |*)

(Śa. Brā. 14-1-2-26) [printed "ಶ. ಬ್ರಾ."]

[The Sanskrit is quoted as supplied; the text looks corrupt in places.] There the identity of the action performed with the utterance of mantras and the new creation is stated. Thus the nature of the kavi and his supernatural power are described. In the same way the meaning of the word क्रतु (*kratu*) also explains these two elements. First one must know the special meaning of the word क्रतशब्द (*krataśabda*) [so printed for क्रतुशब्द (*kratuśabda*); as supplied], and then attend to the meaning of the compound कविक्रतुवॆंब (*kavikratuvèṃba*).

The authors of the Nirukta have read the word क्रतु (*kratu*) among the names of action (Nir. 3-1) and among the names of knowledge (Nir. 3-13). And, in the Ṛksaṃhitā,

यो जात एव प्रथमो मनस्वान्देवो देवान्कतुना पर्यभूषत् । यस्य शुष्माद्रोदसी अभ्यसेतां नृण्नस्य मह्ना स जनास इंद्रः ॥ (*yo jāta eva prathamo manasvāndevo devānkatunā paryabhūṣat | yasya śuṣmādrodasī abhyasetāṃ nṛṇnasya mahnā sa janāsa iṃdraḥ ‖*)

(Ma. Saṃ. 2-12-1)

having cited this Ṛk, they have stated there the special meaning of the word क्रतु (*kratu*) (Nir. 10-10). Although the word kratu is commonly given the meaning "action", wherever this word is used it is understood that there is in this action one very great distinguishing feature. And the chief meaning of this word is the resolve (संकल्प (*saṃkalpa*)) that impels the action. This meaning is understood from the Ṛk to be cited below.

सुप्रवाचनं तव वीर वीर्यं यदेकेन क्रतुना विंदसे वसु । जातूष्ठिरस्य प्र वयः सहस्वतो या चकर्थ सेंद्र विश्वास्युक्थ्यः ॥ (*supravācanaṃ tava vīra vīryaṃ yadekena kratunā viṃdase vasu | jātūṣṭhirasya pra vayaḥ sahasvato yā cakartha seṃdra viśvāsyukthyaḥ ‖*)

(Mi. Saṃ. 2-13-11) [printed "ಮಿ. ಸಂ.", as supplied; the print has "Mi." where "Ma." would be expected]

In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained the word क्रतुना (*kratunā*) as कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*) ("by action"). Here it is more fitting to say "resolve" than "action". The scholar named Monier Williams has taken this same example and, explaining it, has interpreted एतेन कर्मणा (*etena karmaṇā*) ("by this action") as "through the merewill" [sic: printed "through the merewill" in Latin letters, apparently "through the mere will"], that is, "by mere resolve alone". Here this is the natural meaning. For here the valour of Indra is described. Rather than saying "Indra destroyed the enemies by a single action", it is natural to say here "Indra destroyed the enemies by mere resolve alone".

### Printed p. 291

Whenever the word क्रतु (*kratu*) is used as a synonym of action, the resolve that is the root of that action and the aim (ध्येय (*dhyeya*)) that is the goal of the action are indicated, and the word shows the spiritual existence of the person (पुरुष (*puruṣa*)) and that same aim. For example—

त्वं सोम क्रतुभिः सुक्रतुर्भूर्स्वं दक्षैः सुदक्षो विश्ववेदाः । त्वं वृषा वृषत्वेभिर्महित्वा द्युम्नेभिर्दुम्म्यभवो नृचक्षाः ॥ (*tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ sukraturbhūrsvaṃ dakṣaiḥ sudakṣo viśvavedāḥ | tvaṃ vṛṣā vṛṣatvebhirmahitvā dyumnebhirdummyabhavo nṛcakṣāḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-912) [printed "ಋಂ. ಸಂ. ೧-೯೧೨", as supplied; the reference looks irregular]

In this Ṛk the two words क्रतु (*kratu*) and दक्ष (*dakṣa*) show the extraordinary qualities of the god Soma. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the word kratu as meaning action or knowledge (प्रज्ञा (*prajñā*)). Soma is addressed as endowed with the most excellent knowledge. In the same way,

ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः स्वेन युक्तासः क्रतुना वहंति । इंद्रवायू वीरवाहं रथं वामीशानयोरभि पृक्षः सचंते ॥ (*te satyena manasā dīdhyānāḥ svena yuktāsaḥ kratunā vahaṃti | iṃdravāyū vīravāhaṃ rathaṃ vāmīśānayorabhi pṛkṣaḥ sacaṃte ‖*)

(Ma. Saṃ. 7-90-5)

here the knowledge and the resolve that are the root of human conduct in the form of sacrifice are indicated by the word क्रतुना (*kratunā*). Since all the dealings of the universe are of the nature of sacrifice, the root of the sacrifice, which is universal and which is to be carried out through individual actions, is the resolve of the person. The individuality of the person must be complete through this resolve and aim. Therefore the person is described as क्रतुमय (*kratumaya*), "made of kratu". This same point is described in the Upaniṣads and other works in this way.

सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शांत उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिंल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ॥ (*sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śāṃta upāsīta | atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākraturasmiṃlloke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati sa kratuṃ kurvīta ‖*)

(Chā. U. 3-14-1)

Here the person is called kratumaya. Explaining what kratu is here, Śaṅkarācārya has given the following commentary.

क्रतुं कुर्वीत क्रतुर्निश्चयोऽध्यवसाय एवमेव नान्यथेत्यविचलः प्रत्य- यस्तं क्रतुं कुर्वीतोपासीतेत्यनेन व्यवहितेन संबंधः । किं पुनः क्रतुकरणेन कर्तव्यं प्रयोजनं ? कधं वा क्रतुः कर्तव्यः । क्रतुकरणं चाभिप्रेतार्थसिद्धिसाधनं कथं! इत्यस्यार्थस्य प्रतिपादनार्थमथेत्यादिग्रंथः। यस्माक्क्रतुमयः क्रतुप्रायोऽध्यवसायात्मकः पुरुषो जीवः । यथाक्रतुर्यादृशः क्रतुः अस्य सोऽयं यथाक्रतुर्यथाध्यवसायः यादृज्निश्चयः अस्मिन्निह पुरुषो भवति तथेतोऽस्माद्देहात्प्रेत्य मृत्वा भवति । क्रत्वनुरूपफलात्मको भवतीत्यर्थः ॥ (*kratuṃ kurvīta kraturniścayo 'dhyavasāya evameva nānyathetyavicalaḥ pratya- yastaṃ kratuṃ kurvītopāsītetyanena vyavahitena saṃbaṃdhaḥ | kiṃ punaḥ kratukaraṇena kartavyaṃ prayojanaṃ ? kadhaṃ vā kratuḥ kartavyaḥ | kratukaraṇaṃ cābhipretārthasiddhisādhanaṃ kathaṃ! ityasyārthasya pratipādanārthamathetyādigraṃthaḥ| yasmākkratumayaḥ kratuprāyo 'dhyavasāyātmakaḥ puruṣo jīvaḥ | yathākraturyādṛśaḥ kratuḥ asya so 'yaṃ yathākraturyathādhyavasāyaḥ yādṛjniścayaḥ asminniha puruṣo bhavati tatheto 'smāddehātpretya mṛtvā bhavati | kratvanurūpaphalātmako bhavatītyarthaḥ ‖*)

(Bhā. U. Śāṅkarabhāṣya 3-14-1) [printed "ಭಾ. ಉ. ಶಾಂಕರಭಾಷ್ಯ", as supplied]

*[The supplied text of this window ends here, after the quotation from Śaṅkara's commentary and its reference; the Special Topics of Ṛk 7 continue on p. 292.]*

### Printed p. 292

क्रतु (*kratu*) means resolve of mind, mental determination and unwavering faith. A person must necessarily practise the worship of such a kratu, which has the form of determination and is made of faith. A person's existence, whether in this world or after the abandoning of the earthly body, follows the nature of his kratu; and it is the fruit of that worship of kratu. The purport is also that without the worship of kratu there is no excellent fruit—such is the explanation of the Śāṅkara-bhāṣya. Discussing here whether the word kratu means determination or aim (purpose), the English scholar Edgerton (printed in Latin letters "Edgerton", with the Kannada transcription ಎಡ್ಗರ್ಟನ್) cites the passage of the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa and the passage cited above, and explains the meaning of the word kratu there in this way:

*The word क्रतु (*kratu*) is not easy to define. Eggling translates it "understanding," but with an alternative, "will, purpose" which is more in accord with the Hindu commentator on the passage who says क्रतु (*kratu*) means निश्चय अध्यवसाय (*niścaya adhyavasāya*), that is "fixed determination". It Seems to mean man's mental constitution as a whole, total 'frame of mind', but with a strong flavour of will, conscious purpose. or determination. . . . Man's क्रतु (*kratu*), therefore, would be his mental make up in general, but particularly any fixed determination he may entertain with regard to his future life. And his क्रतु (*kratu*) at the moment of death decides his destiny after death."* (Annals of the Bhandarkar Institute. Vol. VIII p. 223) [printed in Latin letters, as supplied; the print has "Eggling" here and "Eggeling" below, and ""It Seems" with a capital S, kept as printed [sic]; the line-end hyphens in "under-standing", "fixed determi-nation" are joined; the closing quotation mark has no opening mark in the print]

The gist of this is only the following. For the word क्रतु (*kratu*) in the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa (10-6-3-1) and in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (3-14-1), the translator Eggeling [as printed in Latin letters] first gives the meaning "knowledge" and then also the alternative meanings "resolve" and "aim". On the whole, it is said that this word means the resolve of the mind of the person, which decides the person's lasting condition and fortunes. Although in many parts of the Ṛksaṃhitā this word has the meaning "sacrifice", the same purport is implied and it means the sacrifice that has the nature of resolve. For example—

साकं हि शुचिना शुचिः प्रशास्ता क्रतुनाजनि । विद्वा अस्य व्रता ध्रुवा वया इवानु रोहते ॥ (*sākaṃ hi śucinā śuciḥ praśāstā kratunājani | vidvā asya vratā dhruvā vayā ivānu rohate ‖*)

(Pu. Sa. 2-5-4) [printed "ಪು. ಸ. ೨-೫-೪", as supplied; the abbreviation looks irregular]

In Ṛks such as this, this idea is expressed everywhere. Since a person's existence and his future condition rest on this action in the form of kratu, in the Upaniṣads and other works man is warned again and again about this matter.

ओं क्रतो स्मर कृतग्गस्मर क्रतो स्मर कृतग्गस्मर । (*oṃ krato smara kṛtaggasmara krato smara kṛtaggasmara |*)

(Īśa. 1)

### Printed p. 293

Thus in the Īśa and in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka and other Upaniṣads (Bṛ. U. 5-15-1) the self that has the nature of resolve is addressed and instructed. Śaṅkarācārya has given the meaning of the word क्रतो (*krato*) as "O you who are of the nature of resolve". But in the Aitareya Upaniṣad, when the nature of the spirit is explained—

संज्ञानमाज्ञानं विज्ञानं प्रज्ञानं . . . . स्मृतिः संकल्पः क्रतुः ॥ (*saṃjñānamājñānaṃ vijñānaṃ prajñānaṃ . . . . smṛtiḥ saṃkalpaḥ kratuḥ ‖*)

(Ai. U. 3-2)

saṃkalpa and kratu are mentioned as separate qualities of the self.

This word is used not only at the times when these spiritual qualities are being described but also when the material actions of a person and the oblation-actions of sacrifices and offerings are being described. For example,

नहि नु यादधीमसींद्रं को वीर्या परः । तस्मिन्नृम्म मुत क्रतुं देवा ओजांसि सं दधुरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥ (*nahi nu yādadhīmasīṃdraṃ ko vīryā paraḥ | tasminnṛmma muta kratuṃ devā ojāṃsi saṃ dadhurarcannanu svarājyaṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Sa. 1-80-15) [printed "ಋ. ಸ. ೧-೮೦-೧೫"]

in Ṛks such as this the word क्रतु (*kratu*) is understood as heroic action, and

यस्याजस्रं शवसा मानमुक्थं परिभुजद्रोदसी विश्वतः सीं । स पारिषत्कतुभिर्मंदसानो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥ (*yasyājasraṃ śavasā mānamukthaṃ paribhujadrodasī viśvataḥ sīṃ | sa pāriṣatkatubhirmaṃdasāno marutvānno bhavatviṃdra ūtī ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ) [stray line, as supplied]
(Ma. Saṃ. 1-100-14) [printed "ಮ. ಸಂ. ೧-೧೦೦-೧೪"; the two reference lines are both in the print]

in such places it is understood as sacrificial action. In the same way this word is also used in the senses of power, wealth, influence and the like.

Chiefly, it is clearly known from the preceding explanation that the word कवि (*kavi*) and the word क्रतु (*kratu*) both show the supernatural nature and power of the person. In the present Ṛk, explaining the compound word कविक्रतो (*kavikrato*) in which these two are joined, Sāyaṇa has stated that it is an epithet showing Agni's uncommon quality: "endowed with knowledge of things beyond the senses, all-knowing". This compound word is used as an epithet of Agni in seven contexts and as an epithet of Soma in three contexts. The meaning is: one endowed with knowledge that others cannot know, and one who has power. When the same glory of Agni is described,

शुक्रेभिरंगै रज आततन्वान् क्रतुं पुनानः कविभिः पवित्रैः । शोचिर्वसानः पर्यायुरपां श्रियो मिमिते बृहतीरनूनाः ॥ (*śukrebhiraṃgai raja ātatanvān kratuṃ punānaḥ kavibhiḥ pavitraiḥ | śocirvasānaḥ paryāyurapāṃ śriyo mimite bṛhatīranūnāḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-5)

in this verse, with the words कविभिः क्रांतप्रज्ञैः स्तोतवैः वा....तेजोभिः (*kavibhiḥ krāṃtaprajñaiḥ stotavaiḥ vā....tejobhiḥ*) and क्रतुं कर्मणां कर्तारं यजमानं (*kratuṃ karmaṇāṃ kartāraṃ yajamānaṃ*) [as supplied; "ಸ್ತೋತವೈಃ" is as printed], the word kavi indicates Agni's supernatural brilliance and the word kratu the power of action of the performer of the sacrifice. Since these words are used in many places both as compounds and separately, the meanings must be given according to the respective contexts.

### Printed p. 294

Since the word अध्वर (*adhvara*) is used in two senses, "atmosphere" or "sacrifice", addressing Agni with the words कविक्रतो देव (*kavikrato deva*) the meaning—"we, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, have offered oblations for you in the sacrifices"—is explained by the sentence सर्वज्ञ दीप्यमान हे अग्ने यजमाना वयं इमानि हवींषि यज्ञे हविस्तागमकार्ष्म (*sarvajña dīpyamāna he agne yajamānā vayaṃ imāni havīṃṣi yajñe havistāgamakārṣma*) .

सुरथस्य विश्वस्य बोधि (*surathasya viśvasya bodhi*)—शोभनयानोपेतस्य सर्वस्य यजमानस्य गोपायिता भवामीति बुध्यस्व (*śobhanayānopetasya sarvasya yajamānasya gopāyitā bhavāmīti budhyasva*). The prayer is: let Agni, knowing that the whole belongings of the sacrificer who has excellent vehicles belong to his protection, protect them.

For the word अमृत (*amṛta*): addressing Agni as one who has no mortality—अस्माभिः अस्मिन् कर्मणि दत्तं सर्वं हविः आस्वादय (*asmābhiḥ asmin karmaṇi dattaṃ sarvaṃ haviḥ āsvādaya*). The prayer is: let Agni accept all kinds of oblations that we, who are the sacrificers and priests, have offered in the sacrificial actions, and taste and eat them.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* इमा (*imā*)—by शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70) the ending शि (*śi*) that comes in the neuter plural is dropped (lopa) when the form is made. अकर्म (*akarma*)—root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*); ending मस् (*mas*) in the first person plural of लज् (*laj*); by नित्यं जातः (*nityaṃ jātaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-99) the s is dropped. By छंदस्युभयथा (*chaṃdasyubhayathā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-117 [closing bracket missing in the print]) the ending has the designation ardhadhātuka, so by सार्वधातुकमपित् (*sārvadhātukamapit*) the property of being जित् (*jit*) does not arise. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*), when लुक् (*luk*) comes for the vikaraṇa, by सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) guṇa of the ṛ of the root, coming with r; by अडागनु (*aḍāganu*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-71) the augment aṭ for the stem; the form अकर्म (*akarma*). Because of the connection with the relative pronoun word यच्छब्द (*yacchabda*) (यानि (*yāni*)), by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यं (*yadvṛttānnityaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) the prohibition of the nighāta accent follows. As the augment aṭ is acute, the word has the acute on the first syllable. सुरथस्य (*surathasya*)—शोभनः रथः यस्य सः तस्य (*śobhanaḥ rathaḥ yasya saḥ tasya*); by आद्युदात्तंद्व्यच्‌छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃdvyacchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119) the second member has the acute on its first syllable. बोधि (*bodhi*)—root बुध अवगमने (*budha avagamane*); by छंदसि लुज्‌लज्लिटः (*chaṃdasi lujlajliṭaḥ*) लुज् (*luj*) in the sense of the imperative; by the statement तिजां तिजो भवति (*tijāṃ tijo bhavati*) the substitution तादेश (*tādeśa*) for सिपिगॆ (*sipigè*) [as supplied; the print has the dative form, 'for sip']; by दीपजनबुध (*dīpajanabudha*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-61) चिण् (*ciṇ*) in the active; by चिणोलुक् (*ciṇoluk*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-104) लुक् (*luk*) for the ending त (*ta*) because it follows चिण् (*ciṇ*); guṇa of the light penultimate vowel of the root because of चिण् (*ciṇ*); by बहुलंछंदस्य (*bahulaṃchaṃdasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75) the augment aṭ does not come; the finite-verb nighāta accent follows. स्वद (*svada*) —root स्पद आस्वादने (*spada āsvādane*) [so printed; the root is spelled with ಸ್ಪ here, as supplied]; since the action of the instigator is shown, it is a root with the sense of the internal causative; the form is the second person singular of लोट् (*loṭ*); because it stands after a non-finite word, the nighāta accent follows.

## Sūkta 15 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The fifteenth sūkta** (ಹದಿನೈದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತ)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वि पाजसा पृथुनेति सप्तर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं कतगोत्रोत्पन्नोत्कीलस्यार्षं
> त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । वि पाजसा कात्य उत्कीलस्त्विति । कतगो-
> त्रोत्सन्न उत्कीलो नाम ऋषिः ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरा होतेत्यादिसूक्त-
> दशकं विनियुक्तं तत्रेदं च द्वितीयं सूक्तं ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning वि पाजसा पृथुना (*vi pājasā pṛthunā*) is the third sūkta of the second anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. For this sūkta Utkīla, born in the Kata gotra, is the Ṛṣi; the metre is Triṣṭubh; Agni is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said वि पाजसा कात्य उत्कीलस्तु (*vi pājasā kātya utkīlastu*). Utkīla is a Ṛṣi who was born in the Kata gotra. As stated in the application (viniyoga) of the preceding sūkta, this is the second of the ten sūktas beginning आ होता (*ā hotā*) which are used for the Prātaranuvāka and for the recitation of the mantras of the Āśvina-śastra.

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 15 *(the print has a separate line "ಸೂಕ್ತ—೧೫" after the Anuvāda)*. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 15. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 1; Varga 15. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: उत्कीलः कात्यः (*utkīlaḥ kātyaḥ*). Devatā: अग्निः (*agniḥ*). Chandas: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि पाज॑सा पृ॒थुना॒ शोशु॑चानो॒ बाध॑स्व द्वि॒षो र॒क्षसो॒ अमी॑वाः ।  
> सु॒शर्म॑णो बृह॒तः शर्म॑णि स्याम॒ग्नेर॒हं सु॒हव॑स्य॒ प्रणी॑तौ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । पाजसा । पृथुना । शोशुचानः । बाधस्व । द्विषः । रक्षसः । अमीवाः ।  
> सुशर्मणः । बृहतः । शर्मणि । स्यां । अग्नेः । अहं । सुहवस्य । प्रनीत् ॥ १ ॥

> उत्कलः स्तौति । हे अग्ने पृथुना विस्तीर्णेन पाजसा तेजसा शोशुचानोS-
> त्यर्थं दीप्यमानस्त्वं द्विषः कर्मानुष्ठानविघ्नकारिणः शत्रून् वि बाधस्व । विशेषेण

> सुखहेतोर्ब्बृहतो मरुतः शत्रुविजयेन प्राप्तमहिम्नः सुहवस्य सुष्वाह्वा-
> नोपेतस्याग्नेः शर्मण्यस्माकं सुखहेत् प्रणीतावुत्तरवेद्यादिस्थानेषु प्रणयने ।

> वृत्तौ पाशेर्बले जुट् चेत्यसुन् । जुडागमः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । पृथुना । प्रथ

> यज्लुकोरित्यभ्यासस्य गुणः । व्यत्ययेन शानच् । चर्करीतस्यादादिवद्भावाच्छपो

> त्तत्वं । स्यां । अस भुवीत्यस्य लिजु यासुट् परस्पैपदेष्टित्यादिना यासुट् । लिजः
> सलोप इति सलोपः । यासुटो जित्वात् श्नसोरल्लोपः । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Utkīla addresses Agni: blazing with wide radiance, destroy the enemies and the rākṣasas that obstruct the rite; may I be present at the ritual leading-forth of the fire. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

*[Notes on the bhāṣya as supplied: a Latin "S" (avagraha) stands in the word ending शोशुचानोS (*śośucānoS*); the bhāṣya reads सुखहेत् (*sukhahet*) and पा रक्षणॆ (*pā rakṣaṇè*) as printed.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni.) पृथुना (*pṛthunā*)—with wide *(printed "ವಿಸ್ತ್ರತವಾದ")*
- पाजसा (*pājasā*)—with radiance
- शोशुजानः (*śośujānaḥ*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has शोशुचानो (*śośucāno*))*—shining exceedingly
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—(the sacrificer's) enemies; वि बाधस्व (*vi bādhasva*)—destroy. (Likewise) अमीवाः रक्षसः (*amīvāḥ rakṣasaḥ*)—the rākṣasas, piśācas and the like, strong of body through health—(destroy them also). सुकर्मणः (*sukarmaṇaḥ*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has सुशर्मणो (*suśarmaṇo*))*—who is the cause of the pleasures of heaven and the like
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—who has attained greatness
- सुहवस्य (*suhavasya*)—who is endowed with an excellent invocation
- अग्नीः (*agnīḥ*) —of the god Agni
- शर्मणि (*śarmaṇi*)—the pleasure-bringing
- प्रणीतौ (*praṇītau*)—in the place where the leading-forth takes place, the northern altar and the like
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- स्यां (*syāṃ*)—may I be (devoted to worship)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, blazing exceedingly with your wide radiance, destroy our enemies, who are sacrificers' foes. Likewise destroy also the rākṣasas, piśācas and the like, strong of body through health. May I, being in the pleasure-bringing place of the northern altar of Agni, who is the cause of the pleasures of heaven and the like, who has attained greatness, who is endowed with an excellent invocation *(the sentence breaks off at the foot of p. 296 with "ಆಹ್ವಾನ", and the word is completed on p. 297 as "ಆಹ್ವಾನದಿಂದ")*

### Printed p. 297

*(Bhāvārtha continued from p. 296.)* be engaged in the activities of fire-worship; that is, may I also enjoy the pleasure that is the fruit of it.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Radiant with great glory, repel the hostile Rakshasas and Pishachas : may I be in (the enjoyment) of the favour of the great (AGNI), the giver of prosperity, and in the service of (him who is) easily invoked.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पृथुना पाजसा शोशुचानः (*pṛthunā pājasā śośucānaḥ*)—विस्तीर्णेन तेजसा अत्यर्थं दीप्यमानः (*vistīrṇena tejasā atyarthaṃ dīpyamānaḥ*). The word पृथुः (*pṛthuḥ*) (Ni. 22) is formed from the root प्रथ प्रख्याने (*pratha prakhyāne*). And in the passage विद्यामेषि रजस्पृथ्वहा मिमानो अक्तुभिः (*vidyāmeṣi rajaspṛthvahā mimāno aktubhiḥ*) (Ni. 12-25) पृथु महांतं (*pṛthu mahāṃtaṃ*) is explained as "great". The word पाजः (*pājaḥ*) is read among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9) and explained as पाजः पालनात् (*pājaḥ pālanāt*). Here the meaning is described that Agni, pervading everywhere, shines with his radiances with exceeding brilliance.

द्विषः विबाधस्व (*dviṣaḥ vibādhasva*)—कर्मानुष्ठानविघ्नकारिणः शत्र्नू विशेषेण नाशय (*karmānuṣṭhānavighnakāriṇaḥ śatrnū viśeṣeṇa nāśaya*) *(so printed; the bhāṣya has ಶತ್ರೂನ್)*. It is a prayer that Agni destroy the troubles which enemies cause to those who perform the sacrifice, and those who create obstacles while the sacrificial rites are being carried out.

अमीवाः रक्षसः विबाधस्व (*amīvāḥ rakṣasaḥ vibādhasva*)—रोगराहित्येन सामर्थ्योपेतानि तानि रक्षांसि कर्मविघ्नकारीणि तान्यपनुदस्व । यद्वा आगमनपरागमनपराः पिशाचिकाश्च बाधस्व (*rogarāhityena sāmarthyopetāni tāni rakṣāṃsi karmavighnakārīṇi tānyapanudasva | yadvā āgamanaparāgamanaparāḥ piśācikāśca bādhasva*) *(the print ends this sentence with "!" in place of the danda, as supplied)*. The word अमीवा (*amīvā*) is cited by the Nirukta-writers in—

यस्ते गर्भममीवा दुर्णामा योनिमाशये । अग्निष्टं ब्रह्मणा सह निष्क्रव्यादमनीनशत् ॥ (*yaste garbhamamīvā durṇāmā yonimāśaye | agniṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā saha niṣkravyādamanīnaśat ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-162)

and the explanation given there by Durgācārya is: अमीवा इत्यस्य क्रिमिः अभिधेयः क्रिम्युपहते हि योन् गर्भः न संभवतीत्युपपत्तिः (*amīvā ityasya krimiḥ abhidheyaḥ krimyupahate hi yon garbhaḥ na saṃbhavatītyupapattiḥ*) *(so printed, with ಯೋನ್)*. That is, by the word अमीवा (*amīvā*) a worm (krimi) is meant; the worm is what is conveyed. A foetus does not come into being in a womb that is spoiled by a worm. Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning for this sentence. In the first meaning, since the rākṣasas, who are strong because they are not afflicted by disease, are the ones who create obstacles to the sacrificial rites, it is explained that Agni should destroy them. It is also prayed that Agni destroy the piśācas and the like, who come and go for the very purpose of causing trouble to everyone.

सुशर्मणः बृहतः सुहवस्य अग्नेः (*suśarmaṇaḥ bṛhataḥ suhavasya agneḥ*)—here the glory of Agni is described by three epithets. Having obtained heaven for those who perform sacrifices, and also the worldly pleasures such as the pleasures of heaven *(the supplied text breaks off here at the foot of p. 297 with the words "ಐಹಿಕಸುಖಗಳನ್ನೂ"; the sentence continues on p. 298)*

*[A stray line "38" (a signature number) follows at the foot of p. 297 in the supplied text, as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 298

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continued from p. 297.)* …and as the one who brings about [them]; as the one who, by destroying enemies, has attained abundant greatness; and as the one of good invocation (suhava), since he calls the gods to the sacrifice to receive the oblation — thus Agni and his glory are described.

शर्मणि—अस्मा कं सुखहेतौ । (*śarmaṇi—asmā kaṃ sukhahetau |*) *(so printed, with a space inside ಅಸ್ಮಾ ಕಂ)* — "in the cause of our happiness". The word शर्म (*śarma*) is stated among the names of happiness and among the names of the house (Ni. 3-9). And: सुखं कस्मात् सुहितं खेभ्यः (*sukhaṃ kasmāt suhitaṃ khebhyaḥ*) — because it brings about what is beneficial to the senses, it is designated सुख (*sukha*) (happiness).

प्रणीतौ—उत्तरवेद्यादिस्थानेषु प्रकर्षेण नयनं तत्र तत्रानीय प्रक्षेपः एवं भूते अग्निप्रणयनपूर्वके क्रत्वनुष्ठाने । (*praṇītau—uttaravedyādisthāneṣu prakarṣeṇa nayanaṃ tatra tatrānīya prakṣepaḥ evaṃ bhūte agnipraṇayanapūrvake kratvanuṣṭhāne |*) In the sacrificial hall the fire is placed in three places, and those fires are called by different names. To carry out the rites that are limbs of the sacrifice, that is, the Soma rites (सोमिक (*somika*)) and the animal-sacrifice rites (पाशुकतंत्र (*pāśukataṃtra*)), that fire is taken to places such as the northern altar (उत्तरवेदि (*uttaravedi*)). This is here called by the word प्रणनयन (*praṇanayana*) *(so printed; the word used before is ಪ್ರಣಯನ)*. Here the seer, having described the leading-forth of the fire as a cause of happiness — that by performing the leading-forth of the fire at such places as the northern altar, carrying out the sacrifice, one obtains happiness — wishes that his own eagerness (औत्सुक्य (*autsukya*)) in the performance of the sacrifice may arise in him through Agni's favour.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* पाजसा (*pājasā*)—root पा (*pā*) in the sense of protecting; the suffix asun, continued from the preceding sūtra, is added to the root by पातेर्बले जुट् च (*pāterbale juṭ ca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-642) with the augment juṭ, which by आद्यंतौटकित् (*ādyaṃtauṭakit*) (Pā. Sū. 1-1-19) comes as the first part; since the suffix is nit, the initial acute follows; instrumental singular. पृथुना (*pṛthunā*)—root प्रथ (*pratha*) in the sense of making known; the suffix u by प्रथिम्रदिभृस्टां संप्रसारणम् (*prathimradibhṛsṭāṃ saṃprasāraṇam*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-28) ; samprasāraṇa of the r of the root, giving pṛthu; final acute by the suffix accent; instrumental singular. शोशुचानः (*śośucānaḥ*)—root शुच (*śuca*) in the sense of shining; by धातोरेकाचः (*dhātorekācaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22) *(a comma follows in the print)* the suffix यज् (*yaj*) in the sense of intensity (अतशयार्थ (*ataśayārtha*), so printed); by यजोचिच (*yajocica*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-74) luk of it; reduplication of the root; guṇa of the reduplicate by गुणोयज्‌लुकोः (*guṇoyajlukoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-82); by व्यत्ययो बहुलं (*vyatyayo bahulaṃ*) laṭ after the yaj-luk ending takes the replacement śānac; by चर्करीतंच (*carkarītaṃca*) luk of śap, the yaj-luk-ending roots being read in the adādi class; the suffix being cit, the final acute would result, but by अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) the initial acute comes. बाधस्व (*bādhasva*)—root बाध्य (*bādhya*) in the sense of harassing; loṭ, second person singular; (the grammar note continues on p. 299).

### Printed p. 299

*(Grammar notes continued.)* बाधस्व (*bādhasva*) (continued)—because it stands at the beginning of the pāda the finite-verb nighāta accent does not come; since by शास्यनुदात्तेत् (*śāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the lasārvadhātuka ending is unaccented, the root accent remains. सुशर्मणः (*suśarmaṇaḥ*)—root श्य (*śya*) *(so printed; the bhāṣya has ಶೃ)* in the sense of injuring; दुःखं शृणाति इति शर्मा (*duḥkhaṃ śṛṇāti iti śarmā*); the Uṇādi suffix manin; guṇa of the ṛ of the root, with r following; in the bahuvrīhi compound by सोर्मनसी (*sormanasī*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-117) the initial acute of the latter member comes. स्याम् (*syām*)—root अस (*asa*) in the sense of being; liṅ, first person singular, with am as the replacement of mip; the augment yāsuṭ by यासुट्-परस्मै (*yāsuṭ-parasmai*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-103); loss of its s by लिजिःसलोपोनंत्यस्य (*lijiḥsaloponaṃtyasya*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-29); since yāsuṭ is jit, when it follows, the a of the root is lost by श्नसोरल्लोपः (*śnasorallopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111); because luk has come for śap, yāsuṭ does not stand after ā, so the replacement iya does not occur; because it stands after a word that is not a finite verb (अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*), so printed) the nighāta accent follows. सुहवस्य (*suhavasya*)—by आद्युदात्तं द्वैच्‌छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvaicchaṃdasi*) (Pā. #### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं नो॑ अ॒स्या उ॒षसो॒ व्य॑ष्टौ॒ त्वं सूर॒ उदि॑ते बोधि गो॒पाः ।  
> जन्मे॑व॒ नित्यं॒ तन॑यं जुषस्व॒ स्तोमं॑ मे अग्ने त॒न्वा॑ सुजात ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । नः । आस्याः । उषसः । विउष्टौ । त्वं । सूरे । उत्ऽइते । बोधि । गोपाः ।  
> जन्मइव । नित्यं । तनयं । जुषस्व । स्तोमं । मे । अग्ने । तन्ना । सुजात ॥ २ ॥

> *tvaṃ | naḥ | āsyāḥ | uṣasaḥ | viuṣṭau | tvaṃ | sūre | ut 'ite | bodhi | gopāḥ |*  
> *janmaiva | nityaṃ | tanayaṃ | juṣasva | stomaṃ | me | agne | tannā | sujāta ‖ 2 ‖*

*(Differences within the supplied text: the Pada reads आस्याः (*āsyāḥ*) where the Saṃhitā has ಅಸ್ಯಾ; उत्ऽइते (*ut 'ite*) with an odd sign, for ಉದಿತೇ; तन्ना (*tannā*) where the Saṃhitā has ತನ್ವಾ; and जन्मइव (*janmaiva*) as one word; all as supplied.)*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वमस्या अद्य वर्तमानाया उषसो व्युष्टौ व्युच्छने प्रकाशने
> सूरे सूर्य उदिते च सति नोऽग्निहोत्रादिकर्मणि प्रवृत्तानामस्माकं गोपा
> गोपायिता भवामीति बोधि । बुध्यस्व । केचित्सूर्योदयात्पागग्निहोत्रं जुह्वति।
> केचिदुदिते तस्मिन्‌जुह्वति । तेषामुभयेषां पालयिता भवेत्यर्थः । तन्ना सुजात

*(The bhāṣya block continues on p. 300.)*

### Printed p. 300

> ज्वालापरिवृतेन शरीरेण सुष्टु जात देदीप्यमान । अथवा तन्ना सुजात आत्मनैव
> सुजातः स्वयंभूरित्यर्थः । तादशस्त्वं मे मदीयं स्तोमं त्रिवृत्पंचदशादि-
> लक्षणं स्तोत्रं नित्यं जुषस्व । तत्र दृष्टांतः । जन्मेवेति । यथा जन्म जनकः पितौ-
> रसं तनयं पुत्रं परिष्टंगादिभिः सेवते तद्वदस्माभिः क्रियमाणमिमं सेवस्व ॥
> व्युष्टौ । उच्छि विवासे । तमो विवास्यतेऽनयेति करणे क्तिन् । व्रश्चादिना षत्वं ।
> तादौ च निति कृत्यताविति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । गोपाः । गुपू रक्षणे । गुपूधूपविच्छि-
> पणिपनिभ्य इत्यायप्रत्ययः । तदंताद्घातोः क्विप् । अतो लोप इत्यकारलोपः ।
> लोपो व्योरिति यलोपः । धातुस्वरः । जुषस्व । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोरित्यस्य लोट
> रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, at dawn and after sunrise know yourself to be our protector in the agnihotra and the like; accept my praise every day as a father his son. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you; अस्याः उषसः (*asyāḥ uṣasaḥ*)—of this manifested Uṣas
- व्युष्टौ (*vyuṣṭau*)—also at the time of its shining
- सूरे (*sūre*)—also when the sun
- उदिते (*udite*)—has risen
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—as protector
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know (that you are)
- तन्वा (*tanvā*)—with the body (of the form of flame)
- सुजात (*sujāta*)—O Agni, of shining birth
- तनयं (*tanayaṃ*)—the son; जन्म इव (*janma iva*)—as the begetting father *(so printed: ಜನ್ಮ for the father)* loves (with embraces and the like)
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you also
- मे (*me*)—my
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—praise that has the characteristics of trivṛt and the like
- नित्यं (*nityaṃ*)—every day
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—serve with love *(the print has "ಪ್ರಿತಿಯಿಂದ" here, and "ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ" in the Bhāvārtha, as supplied)*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, know yourself to be our protector at the time of the shining of this manifested Uṣas and at the time when the sun has risen; that is, protect us. O Agni, of shining birth with a body of the form of flame, as a begetting father loves his son with embraces and the like, so you also serve with love every day the praise, characterised by trivṛt and the like, that is offered by me.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Consider yourself our protector at the breaking of the dawn to-day and when the sun has risen : AGNI, you are engenderd [sic] with (embodied) form; be pleased with my constant praise, as a father (is pleased with) his son.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The present Ṛk indicates the connection of the appearing of Uṣas and the rising of the sun with Agni's protection of the sacrifice. The relation that Uṣas, Agni and the Aśvin deities have to one another has been told in explaining the nature of the Āśvina-śastra. In this connection the following verse is quoted:

एता उ त्याः प्रत्यदृश्रन्पुरस्ताज्योतिरच्छंतीरुषसो विभातीः । अजेजवन्नूर्यं यज्ञमग्निमपाचीनं तमो अगादजुष्टं (*etā u tyāḥ pratyadṛśranpurastājyotiracchaṃtīruṣaso vibhātīḥ | ajejavannūryaṃ yajñamagnimapācīnaṃ tamo agādajuṣṭaṃ*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-28-3)

*(Translator's gloss, the print gives none: these shining dawns have been seen in the east, bringing light; they have set the sun, the sacrifice and Agni in motion; the unwelcome darkness has gone backward.)*

### Printed p. 301

In this Ṛk (the verse quoted at the end of p. 300), the birth of Sūrya, the sacrifice and Agni is described as coming from Uṣas. Moreover:

उषा उच्छंती समिधाने अग्ना उद्यन्तूर्य उर्विया ज्योतिरश्रेत् । देवो नो अत्र सविता न्वर्थं प्रासावीद्विपत्रु चतुष्पदितैः ॥ (*uṣā ucchaṃtī samidhāne agnā udyantūrya urviyā jyotiraśret | devo no atra savitā nvarthaṃ prāsāvīdvipatru catuṣpaditaiḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-1) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

Here, while the Āhavanīya and other fires are being kindled, the goddess Uṣas dispels the darkness with her immeasurable splendour that removes darkness; thus the relation of cause and effect between the appearing of Uṣas and the blazing of Agni is shown. In this way the inseparable connection between the origin of the sacrificial fire and the appearing of Uṣas is described in many places, and the picture which describes the union of Agni and Uṣas as spreading beauty over the universe and as being attractive to the whole world is, from the poetic point of view, most wonderful. For example:

अग्रे बृहन्नुषसामूर्ध्वो अस्थान्निर्जगन्वांतमसो ज्योतिषागात् । अग्निर्भानुना रुशता स्वंग आ जातो विश्वा सद्मान्यप्राः ॥ (*agre bṛhannuṣasāmūrdhvo asthānnirjaganvāṃtamaso jyotiṣāgāt | agnirbhānunā ruśatā svaṃga ā jāto viśvā sadmānyaprāḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-11) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

Here the description that Agni, shining in the upper part of the Uṣases, joins his splendour with the light of the Āditya and spreads brilliance over the whole world describes the beauty of the universe that arises from the union of Agni and Uṣas.

त्वामिदस्या उषसो व्युष्टिषु दूतं कृण्वाना अजयंत मानुषाः । त्वां देवा महयाय्याय वावृधुराज्यमग्ने निम्मजंतो अध्वरे ॥ (*tvāmidasyā uṣaso vyuṣṭiṣu dūtaṃ kṛṇvānā ajayaṃta mānuṣāḥ | tvāṃ devā mahayāyyāya vāvṛdhurājyamagne nimmajaṃto adhvare ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-122-7) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

In Ṛks like these the benefit to the world that is obtained from the union of Agni and Uṣas is described. As soon as Uṣas appears, men praise Agni, pray that he become the messenger of the gods, and worship him. There is also an explanation that the gods too worship the great-souled Agni. In the present Ṛk also the beauty and the benefit obtained from the union of Agni and Uṣas are indicated.

Sāyaṇa's words: अद्य उषसो व्युष्टौ सूरे उदिते च सति नः गोपाः बोधि केचित् सूर्योदयात् प्राक् अग्निहोत्रं जुह्वति केचित् उदिते सूर्ये । तेषामुभयेषां पालयिता भव । (*adya uṣaso vyuṣṭau sūre udite ca sati naḥ gopāḥ bodhi kecit sūryodayāt prāk agnihotraṃ juhvati kecit udite sūrye | teṣāmubhayeṣāṃ pālayitā bhava |*) — "Today, at the shining of Uṣas and when the sun has risen, be our protector; some offer the agnihotra before sunrise, others after the sun has risen; be the protector of both of them." The word व्युष्टि (*vyuṣṭi*) (formed from the root उच्छे (*ucche*), which has the meaning "destroy darkness (the gloom)", with the prefix वि (*vi*)) means the time of Uṣas that destroys darkness. At the time when it has arrived some, and after the sun has attained rising others, perform the agnihotra and make the oblation to Agni. The prayer to Agni is: may he be the protector of us, the sacrificers and others who are engaged in the rite of performing the agnihotra.

### Printed p. 302

The word तनयं (*tanayaṃ*) — Since it is read among the fifteen names of offspring beginning with तुक्, तोकं, तनयः (*tuk, tokaṃ, tanayaḥ*) (Nir. 3-2), both words तोकं (*tokaṃ*), तनयः (*tanayaḥ*) mean "son". In the present Ṛk also the word tanaya is explained as "son". From the gross point of view the meaning of the two words toka and tanaya is the same, but in usage there is the custom of saying "sons and grandsons" together. Moreover, the authors of the Nirukta have shown the subtle difference between them: तोकं तुद्यतेः । तनयं तनोतेः । (*tokaṃ tudyateḥ | tanayaṃ tanoteḥ |*) The commentators, explaining this, say: तोकं इति पुत्रः स हि नित्यं पित्राविनयता तुद्यते इदं कुर्विदं मा कार्षीरिति । तनयं तनोतेः पौत्रं । तद्धृतितरां पितुः सकाशात् ततं भवति । (*tokaṃ iti putraḥ sa hi nityaṃ pitrāvinayatā tudyate idaṃ kurvidaṃ mā kārṣīriti | tanayaṃ tanoteḥ pautraṃ | taddhṛtitarāṃ pituḥ sakāśāt tataṃ bhavati |*) Since the father who gives instruction always imposes the restriction "do this, do not do that" and makes him lead a life of discipline, such a son is called toka; and since the grandson is the means of extending and growing the line, he is called tanaya: so they have explained (Nir. 10-7).

तन्ना सुजात (*tannā sujāta*): ज्वालापरिवृतेन शरीरेण देदीप्यमान अथवा आत्मनैव सुजातः स्वयंभूः । (*jvālāparivṛtena śarīreṇa dedīpyamāna athavā ātmanaiva sujātaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ |*) — "Agni shines with his own body, which is the form of your rays (flames)": this is one kind of meaning. "Since there are no other causes, no contributing factors (nimittas), for his origin, he has appeared of himself, obtained a body and shines": this is the other kind of meaning, and both are explained.

मे स्तोमं जन्मेव नित्यं जुषस्व (*me stomaṃ janmeva nityaṃ juṣasva*): त्रिवृत् पंचदशादिलक्षणं स्तोत्रं जनकः पिता औरसं पुत्रं परिष्वंगादिभिः सेवते तद्वदस्माभिः क्रियमाणं इमं सेवस्व । (*trivṛt paṃcadaśādilakṣaṇaṃ stotraṃ janakaḥ pitā aurasaṃ putraṃ pariṣvaṃgādibhiḥ sevate tadvadasmābhiḥ kriyamāṇaṃ imaṃ sevasva |*) The Kannada says: may Agni, filled with abundant greatness, honour the praise recited by the sacrificers as a father lovingly caresses his own legitimate son, and listen to it with trust; so it is prayed. The praise is described as having the character of the stomas such as त्रिवत्, पंचदश (*trivat, paṃcadaśa*) *(so printed; the Sanskrit above has त्रिवृत् (*trivṛt*))*.

The word जन्म (*janma*) (janma) is stated among the names of water (Nir. 2-24). Also:

दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि व्रते राजाना मित्रावरुणा विवाससि । अतूर्तपंथाः पुरुरथो अर्यमा सप्तहोता विषुरूपेषु जन्मसु ॥ (*dakṣasya vādite janmani vrate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā vivāsasi | atūrtapaṃthāḥ pururatho aryamā saptahotā viṣurūpeṣu janmasu ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-64-5) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

Here for the words जन्मनि (*janmani*), जन्मसु (*janmasu*) the meaning "rising" or "origin" is given. Here the father who is the cause of the son's origin is also referred to by the word janma itself. And the authors of the Nirukta, citing the Ṛk

विद्यामेषि रजस्पृथ्वहा मिमानो अक्तुभिः । पश्यञ्जान्मानि सूर्य । (*vidyāmeṣi rajaspṛthvahā mimāno aktubhiḥ | paśyañjānmāni sūrya |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-7) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

have explained the word जन्मानि (*janmāni*) there as "the classes of beings that have births"

### Printed p. 303

(Nir. 12-27). Thus this word is used as an attribute both of the father, the cause of birth, and of the class of beings that consist of births. The meaning must be given according to the context.

The word स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*): for the word stoma Sāyaṇa gives the explanation त्रिवृत्पंचदशादिलक्षणं स्तोत्रं (*trivṛtpaṃcadaśādilakṣaṇaṃ stotraṃ*). With the sentence एकं साम तृचे क्रियते, तस्य च तृचस्य आवृत्या ऋचां संख्या वर्धनीया भवति या स्तोमशब्देनोच्यत इति । (*ekaṃ sāma tṛce kriyate, tasya ca tṛcasya āvṛtyā ṛcāṃ saṃkhyā vardhanīyā bhavati yā stomaśabdenocyata iti |*) the characteristic of the stoma is stated. Among the stomas there are nine kinds, त्रिवृत् (*trivṛt*), पंचदशः (*paṃcadaśaḥ*), सप्तदशः (*saptadaśaḥ*), एकविंशः (*ekaviṃśaḥ*), त्रिणवः (*triṇavaḥ*), त्रयस्त्रिंशः (*trayastriṃśaḥ*), चतुश्चत्वारिंशः (*catuścatvāriṃśaḥ*), अष्टाचत्वारिंशः (*aṣṭācatvāriṃśaḥ*) *(eight names are printed here, though "nine kinds" is stated; as supplied)*, together with their विष्णुति (*viṣṇuti*) they have been explained very clearly on pages 138 to 150 of part 2 of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; therefore only the benefits obtained from reciting those stomas are stated here.

Of the nine divisions of the stomas mentioned above, one can increase them by the method of āvāpa to त्रयोदश (*trayodaśa*), चतुर्दश (*caturdaśa*), षोडश (*ṣoḍaśa*) and so on. For example:

वसवस्त्रयोदशाक्षरेण त्रयोदशग्स्स्तोममुदजयनुद्राश्चतुर्दशाक्षरेण चतुर्दशग्स्स्तोममुदजयन्नादित्याः पंचदशाक्षरेण पंचदशग्स्स्तोममुदजयन्नदितिः षोडशाक्षरेण षोडशग्स्स्तोममुदजयत्प्रजापतिस्सप्तदशाक्षरेण सप्तदशग्स्स्तोममुदजयत् । (*vasavastrayodaśākṣareṇa trayodaśagsstomamudajayanudrāścaturdaśākṣareṇa caturdaśagsstomamudajayannādityāḥ paṃcadaśākṣareṇa paṃcadaśagsstomamudajayannaditiḥ ṣoḍaśākṣareṇa ṣoḍaśagsstomamudajayatprajāpatissaptadaśākṣareṇa saptadaśagsstomamudajayat |*)

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-11-44)

By these sentences of the Taittirīya-saṃhitā the order is stated in which the Vasus and Rudras, the Ādityas, Aditi and Prajāpati won in turn the stomas त्रयोदश (*trayodaśa*), चतुर्दश (*caturdaśa*), पंचदश (*paṃcadaśa*), षोडश (*ṣoḍaśa*) and सप्तदश (*saptadaśa*). The power of the stomas is very great; the matter that by reciting them one can obtain all desired aims is also read in the Taittirīya-saṃhitā itself:

पातःसवने वै गायत्रेण च्छंदसा त्रिवृते स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति त्रिवृता ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पंचदशाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति पंचदशेनौजसा वीर्येण सप्तदशाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति सप्तदशेन प्राजापत्येन प्रजननेनैकविग्ंशाय ज्योतिर्दधदेति स्तोम एव तत्‌स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधदेत्यथो स्तोम एव स्तोममभिप्रणयति यावंतो वै स्तोमास्तावंतः कामास्तावंतो लोकास्तावंति ज्योतीग्‌ष्येतावत एव स्तोमानेतावतः कामानेतावतो लोकानेतावंति ज्योतीग्‌ष्यवरुंधे ॥ (*pātaḥsavane vai gāyatreṇa cchaṃdasā trivṛte stomāya jyotirdadhadeti trivṛtā brahmavarcasena paṃcadaśāya jyotirdadhadeti paṃcadaśenaujasā vīryeṇa saptadaśāya jyotirdadhadeti saptadaśena prājāpatyena prajananenaikavigṃśāya jyotirdadhadeti stoma eva tatstomāya jyotirdadhadetyatho stoma eva stomamabhipraṇayati yāvaṃto vai stomāstāvaṃtaḥ kāmāstāvaṃto lokāstāvaṃti jyotīgṣyetāvata eva stomānetāvataḥ kāmānetāvato lokānetāvaṃti jyotīgṣyavaruṃdhe ‖*)

(Tṛ. Saṃ. 7-1-21) *(so printed "ತೃ. ಸಂ."; as supplied)*

In these sentences the power of the four kinds of stomas to be recited in the Agniṣṭoma is told. The sacrificer, at the time of the morning pressing, places the trivṛt stoma, in the Gāyatrī metre, in a place of importance. In the same way, from the trivṛt, which is of the form of light, the pañcadaśa-stoma, and from the vigour-endowed pañcadaśa *(the sentence continues on p. 304)*

### Printed p. 304

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 2 continued from p. 303.)* …by [the vigour-endowed pañcadaśa-stoma] the सप्रदशस्तोम (*sapradaśastoma*) *(so printed; the usual form is सप्तदशस्तोम (*saptadaśastoma*) as printed a few words later; as supplied)*, and by the सप्तदश स्तोम (*saptadaśa stoma*) which, being connected with Prajāpati, is conducive to procreation, he makes the एकविंशस्तोम (*ekaviṃśastoma*) endowed with brilliance. In just this way one kind of stoma produces influence and brilliance for another kind of stoma. As many kinds as there are in the stoma, so many worlds, so many kinds of brilliance and so many kinds of desired aims there are. And the sacrificer, by reciting the stoma, obtains that many kinds of worlds, brilliances and desired aims. Having thus told the power of the stoma, the text next tells also the loss that comes from not reciting the stoma:

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति सत्त्वै यजेत योऽग्निष्टोमेन यजमानोऽथ सर्वस्तोमेन यजेतेति यस्य त्रिवृतमंतर्यंति प्राणाग्‌स्तस्यांतर्यंति प्राणेषु मेऽप्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य पंचदशमंतर्यंति वीर्यं तस्यांतर्यंति वीर्येमेऽप्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य सप्तदशमंतर्यंति प्रजां तस्यांतर्यंति प्रजायां मेऽप्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्यैकविग्‌ंशमंतर्यंति प्रतिष्ठां तस्यांतर्यंति प्रतिष्ठायां मेऽप्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य त्रिणवमंतर्यंत्यतूग्‌श्च तस्य नक्षत्रियां च विराजमंतर्यंत्यतुषु मेऽप्यसन्नक्षत्रियायां च विराजेति खलु वै यज्ञेनयजमानो यजते यस्यत्रयस्त्रिग्‌ंशमंतर्यंति देवतास्तस्यांतर्यंतिति देवतासु मेऽप्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यो वै स्तोमानामवमं परमतां गच्छंतं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति त्रिवृद्वै स्तोमानामवमस्त्रिवृत्परमो य एवं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति ॥ (*brahmavādino vadaṃti sattvai yajeta yo 'gniṣṭomena yajamāno 'tha sarvastomena yajeteti yasya trivṛtamaṃtaryaṃti prāṇāgstasyāṃtaryaṃti prāṇeṣu me 'pyasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya paṃcadaśamaṃtaryaṃti vīryaṃ tasyāṃtaryaṃti vīryeme 'pyasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya saptadaśamaṃtaryaṃti prajāṃ tasyāṃtaryaṃti prajāyāṃ me 'pyasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasyaikavigṃśamaṃtaryaṃti pratiṣṭhāṃ tasyāṃtaryaṃti pratiṣṭhāyāṃ me 'pyasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya triṇavamaṃtaryaṃtyatūgśca tasya nakṣatriyāṃ ca virājamaṃtaryaṃtyatuṣu me 'pyasannakṣatriyāyāṃ ca virājeti khalu vai yajñenayajamāno yajate yasyatrayastrigṃśamaṃtaryaṃti devatāstasyāṃtaryaṃtiti devatāsu me 'pyasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yo vai stomānāmavamaṃ paramatāṃ gacchaṃtaṃ veda paramatāmeva gacchati trivṛdvai stomānāmavamastrivṛtparamo ya evaṃ veda paramatāmeva gacchati ‖*)

(Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-3)

Those who sacrifice with the Agniṣṭoma are ordained by the scholars of the śāstras to sacrifice with the सर्वस्तोम (*sarvastoma*) also. In this rule, if the तिवृत् स्तोम (*tivṛt stoma*) *(so printed; the Sanskrit above and below has त्रिवृत् (*trivṛt*))* is left out, his chief life-breath itself disappears; therefore the sacrificer performs the sacrifice with the intention "let this sacrifice be included in my chief life-breath". In the same way: if the पंचदशस्तोम (*paṃcadaśastoma*) is left out there is want of strength; if the सप्तदशस्तोम (*saptadaśastoma*) is left out there is no offspring; if the एकविंशस्तोम (*ekaviṃśastoma*) is left out the very support of his life falls away; if the त्रिणवस्तोम (*triṇavastoma*) is left out the seasons and the powers of the nakshatras, which exist for his benefit, do not become helpers to his share; and if the त्रयस्त्रिंशस्तोम (*trayastriṃśastoma*) is left out, the presence of the chief deities itself is lacking. Therefore the sacrificer performs the sacrifice by reciting the pañcadaśa-stoma for the acquisition of strength, the saptadaśa-stoma for the gain of offspring, the ekaviṃśa-stoma for the support of life, the triṇava-stoma for obtaining the benefit of the influences of the seasons and the nakshatras, and the trayastriṃśa-stoma for the gain of the presence of his chief deity. The sacrificer who (continued on p. 305) knows the greatness of the stomas

### Printed p. 305

*(Sentence continued from p. 304: "…the sacrificer who knows the greatness of the stomas…")* — the greatness of the त्रिवृत् स्तोम (*trivṛt stoma*) which has obtained the first place among all of them — that sacrificer obtains the first place among sacrificers.

In the same way, describing the greatness of the stomas beginning with the trivṛt that are to be recited in order on the six days in the Pṛṣṭha-ṣaḍaha sacrifice, *(the text)*:

त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमो भवति तेज एवावरुंधते पंचदशो भवतींद्रियमेवावरुंधते सप्तदशो भवत्यन्नादस्यावरुद्ध्या अथो प्रैव तेन जायंत एकविग्ंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्या अथो रुचमेवात्मनधते त्रिणवो भवति विजित्यै त्रयस्त्रिग्ंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै ॥ (*trivṛdagniṣṭomo bhavati teja evāvaruṃdhate paṃcadaśo bhavatīṃdriyamevāvaruṃdhate saptadaśo bhavatyannādasyāvaruddhyā atho praiva tena jāyaṃta ekavigṃśo bhavati pratiṣṭhityā atho rucamevātmanadhate triṇavo bhavati vijityai trayastrigṃśo bhavati pratiṣṭhityai ‖*)

*(No reference is printed after this quotation in the supplied text.)* It is also stated that with the Agniṣṭoma joined with the trivṛt stoma one obtains brilliance, with the pañcadaśa-stoma vigour, with the saptadaśa food, with the ekaviṃśa a firm standing, with the triṇava victory, and with the trayastriṃśa greatness; thus the benefits of reciting the stomas are told. In the Kaṭha Upaniṣad also:

स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्य स्राक्षीः ॥ (*stomamahadurugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā dhīro naciketo 'tya srākṣīḥ ‖*)

(Ka. U. 211) *(so printed "211", with no hyphens in the supplied text; as supplied)*

by this sentence the greatness of the stoma and the spiritual peace to be obtained from it are told. In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad:

येन च्छंदसा स्तोष्यन् स्यात्तच्छंद उपधावेद्येन स्तोमेन स्तोष्यमाणः स्यात्तं स्तोममुपधावेत् । (*yena cchaṃdasā stoṣyan syāttacchaṃda upadhāvedyena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāttaṃ stomamupadhāvet |*)

(Bhā. U. 1-3-10) *(so printed "ಭಾ. ಉ."; as supplied)*

by this sentence, describing the greatness of the उद्दीथ (*uddītha*) *(so printed, with a doubled d; as supplied)*, it is ordained that a man should meditate relying on that very stoma by which the praise of the praiser is complete, in keeping with the occasion. In the same way, in the present Ṛk also, by the word स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*) is meant such a hymn of praise, which is of the nature of song and gives surpassing benefit.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* व्युष्टौ (*vyuṣṭau*)—prefix वि (*vi*), root उछी विवासे (*uchī vivāse*); तमः विवास्यते अनया इति व्युष्टिः (*tamaḥ vivāsyate anayā iti vyuṣṭiḥ*): the suffix ktin in the instrumental sense; by वृश्चभृस्थ (*vṛścabhṛstha*) *(so printed, followed by a hyphen)* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-36) the root-final becomes ṣ, and on its account the t of the suffix becomes ṣṭ; since the word ends in a suffix with ṭ-sign and stands after the gati, by तादौच निति कृत्यत् (*tādauca niti kṛtyat*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50) the gati keeps its own accent. सूरे (*sūre*)—root सूज् प्राणिगर्भविमोचने (*sūj prāṇigarbhavimocane*); by सुसूधागृधिभ्यः क्रन् (*susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2182) the suffix kran; because it has a k-sign there is no guṇa, and because of its n-sign the first syllable is acute.

*(Printed "39" stands after the grammar notes at the foot of the page, as supplied; probably a stray number.)*

### Printed p. 306

*(Grammar notes continued.)* बोधि (*bodhi*)—root बुध अवगमने (*budha avagamane*); in the Vedic manner luṅ in the sense of loṭ; the form of the second person singular; in the Vedic manner the augment aṭ does not come; the finite-verb nighāta accent comes. गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—root गुपू रक्षणे (*gupū rakṣaṇe*); by गुपूधूपविच्छिपणिपनिभ्य आयः (*gupūdhūpavicchipaṇipanibhya āyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-28) the suffix āya in its own sense; by पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) guṇa of the short penultimate vowel on account of it; by सनाद्यंताधातवः (*sanādyaṃtādhātavaḥ*) the form gopāya receives the name dhātu; by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) the suffix kvip is added to it; by अतोलोपः (*atolopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48) the preceding a is dropped; before the dropping of kvip, by लोपोव्योर्वलि (*lopovyorvali*) the y is dropped; the form gopāḥ results, and the root accent remains. जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—root जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*); second person singular of loṭ; since it stands after an accented word, the nighāta accent comes *(the supplied text has the split word अति जंतदपरदल्लि (*ati jaṃtadaparadalli*); as supplied)*. तन्वा (*tanvā*)—by the rule तन्नादीनांछंदस्युपसंख्यानम् (*tannādīnāṃchaṃdasyupasaṃkhyānam*) the replacement yaṇ when the instrumental singular follows; since yaṇ stands in the place of an acute and the unaccented case-ending follows it, by उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) the case-ending receives the svarita accent.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं नृ॒चक्षा॑ वृष॒भानु॑ पू॒र्विः कृ॒ष्णास्व॑ग्ने अरु॒षो वि भा॑हि ।  
> वसो॒ नेषि॑ च॒ पर्षि॒ चात्यंहः॑ कृ॒धी नो॑ रा॒य उ॒शिजो॑ यविष्ठ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । नृचक्षाः । वृषभ । अनु । पूर्विः । कृष्णासु । अग्ने । अरुषः । वि । भाहि ।  
> वसो इति । नेषि । च । पर्षि । च । अति । अंहः । कृधि । नः । राये । उशिजः । यविष्ठ

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषभ कामानां वर्षितर्हे अग्ने नृचक्षा नृणां मनुष्याणां शुभाशुभकर्म-
> णोर्द्रष्टा कृष्णासु रात्रिष्टरुष आरोचमानस्त्वमनु अनुक्रमेण पूर्वीर्बही-
> ज्वालावि भाहि । विशेषेण प्रकाशय । वसो सर्वस्य प्रकाशप्रदानेन स्वस्वस्थानेषु वास-
> यितरग्ने त्वं नोऽस्मान्नेषि। कर्मानुरूपफलानि च प्रापय। अंहोऽस्माकं दारिद्र
> लक्षणं पापमतिपर्षि च । अतिपारय। निवारयेति यावत् । किंच यविष्ट युवतम हे

*(The bhāṣya block continues on p. 307; it breaks off at the end of this window with यविष्ट युवतम हे (*yaviṣṭa yuvatama he*), as supplied. Printed English, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha and gist of Ṛk 3 are not yet reached.)*
