> भाहि : भा दीप्ता । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थः । लोटि रूपं । वसो । वस निवासे । उरित्य-
> नुवृत्तौ शृस्वस्निहित्रप्यसिवसीत्यादिना उप्रत्ययः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । षाष्ठिकमा-
> द्युदात्तत्वं । नेषि । णेञ् प्रापणे । छंदसि लोडर्थे लट् । बहुलं छंदसीति
> शपो लुक् । आमंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदित्यामंत्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्वेन पादा-
> दित्वान्न निघातः । पर्षि । प्य पालनपूरणयोः । चादिशु चेति न निघातः । कृधि
> डुकृञ् करण इत्यस्य लोटि सेर्ह्यपिच्चेति हिरादेशः । तस्य सुश्रुतृणुष्यकृवृभ्यश्चंद-
> सीति धिरादेशः । बहुलं छंदसीत्युप्रत्ययस्य लुक् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । राये
> रा दाने । रातेर्डैरिति डैप्रत्ययः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तीरुदात्तत्वं । उतिजः
> वश कांतौ । वशेः किच्चेतीजिप्रत्ययः । कित्वात्संप्रसारणं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । यविष्ठः ।
> युवशब्दावतिशायन इष्टन्मत्तयः ; स्कूलदूरयुवेत्यादिना यणादेः परस्य लोपः
> पूर्वस्य च गुणः । आमंत्रितत्वान्नि घातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, showerer of desires, beholder of the good and bad deeds of men, shining in the nights, shine in due order with abundant flames; O granter of dwellings, lead us to the fruit of our rites, carry us across the sin of poverty, and, youngest one, make us attain our wishes for wealth. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

*(Grammar tail inside the same block, noted briefly.)* It treats the roots वृषु सेचने (*vṛṣu secane*), चक्षिज् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*cakṣij vyaktāyāṃ vāci*), वस निवासे (*vasa nivāse*), णेञ् प्रापणे (*ṇeñ prāpaṇe*), डुकृञ् करण (*ḍukṛñ karaṇa*), रा दाने (*rā dāne*) and वश कांतौ (*vaśa kāṃtau*) and the forms नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*), वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*), पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*), भाहि (*bhāhi*), वसो (*vaso*), नेषि (*neṣi*), पर्षि (*parṣi*), कृधि (*kṛdhi*), राये (*rāye*) and यविष्ठः (*yaviṣṭhaḥ*), with the accent notes (nighāta, prakṛtisvara, pratyayasvara) for each. *(The grammar block names the form उतिजः (*utijaḥ*) where the Saṃhitā has ಉಶಿಜಃ; so printed, as supplied. In the same block a stray apostrophe stands after the word at the end of the line beginning with the root चक्षिज् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*cakṣij vyaktāyāṃ vāci*) (the sentence on the form of that root), and भाहि (*bhāhi*) is followed by a colon; as supplied.)*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—showering the desired objects *(printed "ಇಷಾರ್ಥಗಳನ್ನು", while the Bhāvārtha has "ಇಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಗಳನ್ನು"; as supplied)*
- आग्ने (*āgne*) *(so printed with ಆ; as supplied)*—O Agni
- नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—the beholder of the (good and bad) deeds of men
- कृष्णासु (*kṛṣṇāsu*)—in the nights filled with darkness
- आरुषः (*āruṣaḥ*) *(so printed with long ā; as supplied)*—and the radiant one
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अनु (*anu*)—in due order
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—with abundant flames; वि भाहि (*vi bhāhi*)—shine in a special manner
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Agni who places (everything) in its own place *(printed "ಅವರದರ", while the Bhāvārtha has "ಅದರದರ"; as supplied)*; नेषि च (*neṣi ca*)—(with the fruit of our rites) unite us; अंहः च (*aṃhaḥ ca*)—also the sin in the form of poverty and the like *(the word is split at the line end in the supplied text, "ದಾರಿ / ದ್ರ್ಯಾದಿ", while the Bhāvārtha has "ದಾರಿದ್ರಾದಿ"; as supplied)*; अति पर्षि (*ati parṣi*)—destroy
- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—O most youthful Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- राये (*rāye*)—for wealth
- उशिजः (*uśijaḥ*)—as desirers
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make (that is, make our wishes be fulfilled)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, showerer of desired objects, beholder of the good and bad deeds of men, and radiant in the nights filled with darkness, shine in a special manner, in due order, with abundant flames. O Agni who places everything in its own place, unite us with the fruit of our rites. Destroy also our sin in the form of poverty and the like. O most youthful Agni, fulfil the wishes of us who long for wealth.

### Printed p. 308

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Showerer (of benefits), beholder of men, radiant amidst darkness, shine, AGNI, with abundant (rays) in due order : granter of dwellings, conduct us (to good), keep off all ill, and youngest (of all the gods), gratify our desires for wealth,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—कामनां वर्षितः (*kāmanāṃ varṣitaḥ*) . The authors of the Nirukta *(say)*: वृषभः प्रजां वर्षतीति ना अतिबृहति रेत इति वा तद् वृषकर्मा वर्षणात् वृषभः । (*vṛṣabhaḥ prajāṃ varṣatīti nā atibṛhati reta iti vā tad vṛṣakarmā varṣaṇāt vṛṣabhaḥ |*) *(so printed, including the letters "ನಾ"; as supplied)*. Because he sprinkles the seed which is the cause of the birth of offspring, and because the act of offering one's body to the utmost in the work of sprinkling the seed is designated by the word वृष (*vṛṣa*), they have given the etymology वर्षणात् वृषभः (*varṣaṇāt vṛṣabhaḥ*) and explained the meaning of the word वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*). And:

मरुत्वा इंद्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय । आ सिंचस्व जठरे मध्य ऊर्मिं त्वं राजासि प्रदिवः सुतानां ॥ (*marutvā iṃdra vṛṣabho raṇāya pibā somamanuṣvadhaṃ madāya | ā siṃcasva jaṭhare madhya ūrmiṃ tvaṃ rājāsi pradivaḥ sutānāṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-47-1)

Here for the word वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*) the meaning वर्षितुरपां (*varṣiturapāṃ*) "one who rains water" is explained. Here the meaning is stated that Agni is the one who fulfils the desired objects of the sacrificers.

नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—वृणां मनुष्याणां शुभाशुभकर्मणां द्रष्टा (*vṛṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ śubhāśubhakarmaṇāṃ draṣṭā*) *(so printed, "ವೃಣಾಂ"; as supplied)*. The meaning is stated that Agni is the one who looks, with the attitude of a witness, at the good and the bad deeds performed by men.

कविर्नृचक्षा अभि षीमचष्ट ऋतस्य योना विघृते मदंती । (*kavirnṛcakṣā abhi ṣīmacaṣṭa ṛtasya yonā vighṛte madaṃtī |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-6)

नृचक्षा रक्षः परि पश्य विक्षु तस्य त्रीणि प्रति शृणीह्यग्रा । (*nṛcakṣā rakṣaḥ pari paśya vikṣu tasya trīṇi prati śṛṇīhyagrā |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-87-10)

In Ṛks such as these the epithet नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*) stands for deities such as Agni and Sūrya. In all the places where this epithet occurs it means नराणां द्रष्टा (*narāṇāṃ draṣṭā*), that is, one who looks with favour upon the sacrificers. But in some places, that is:

त्वं वृषा वृषत्वेभिर्महित्वा द्युम्नेभिर्द्नुम्न ्यभवो नृचक्षाः । (*tvaṃ vṛṣā vṛṣatvebhirmahitvā dyumnebhirdnumna yabhavo nṛcakṣāḥ |*) *(so printed, with a stray space in the middle of the second line; as supplied)*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-2) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

in places like this, दर्शयिता (*darśayitā*) — one who shows to men the fruits according to their deeds — is the epithet of Soma. And:

नृचक्षा एष दिवो मध्य आस्त अपप्रिवान्रोदसी अंतरिक्षं (*nṛcakṣā eṣa divo madhya āsta apaprivānrodasī aṃtarikṣaṃ*) *(the printed line ends with "!"; as supplied)*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-139-2)

### Printed p. 309

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 3 continued from p. 308.)* In this *(verse, quoted at the end of p. 308)* the word is the epithet of Savitṛ, in the sense नृभिः रश्मिभिः प्रकाशमानः (*nṛbhiḥ raśmibhiḥ prakāśamānaḥ*) "shining with rays". Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit. English Dictionary *(so printed, with a full stop after "Sanskrit")*, says that this word is also an epithet of a certain Rākṣasa, but he does not say what the authority for it is.

अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—This word is stated among the names of the horse (Nir. 2-27). Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "one who shines greatly" and explained that Agni, shining in the nights, should cause his abundant flames to shine to the utmost.

Since the word अरुष (*aruṣa*) has many meanings, the meanings applicable according to the context should be noted. The authors of the Nirukta have read this word not only among the names of the horse but also among the names of motion-actions (Nir. 3-9) and as a synonym of Uṣas (Nir. 2-19). Moreover:

एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमंजते । निष्कृण्वाना आयुधानीव धृष्णवः प्रति गावोऽरुषीर्यंति मातरः ॥ (*etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumaṃjate | niṣkṛṇvānā āyudhānīva dhṛṣṇavaḥ prati gāvo 'ruṣīryaṃti mātaraḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92) *(a second reference line follows: (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1), printed "ಮ. ಸಂ."; as supplied)*

In this Ṛk अरुषीः (*aruṣīḥ*) is the epithet of Uṣas, in the sense आरोचमाना (*ārocamānā*) *(so printed with long ā)*, "radiant". Thus this word is used in some places in the form of an adjective and in others in the form of a substantive, and gives different meanings. For example:

युंजंति ब्रध्नमरुषं चरंतं परि तस्थुषः । रोचंते रोचना दिवि ॥ (*yuṃjaṃti bradhnamaruṣaṃ caraṃtaṃ pari tasthuṣaḥ | rocaṃte rocanā divi ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-6-1) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

If the word अरुष (*aruṣa*) in this Ṛk is examined, the Ṛṣi describes there the sunrise. Indra is conceived as the deity of the shining day, Sūrya as his horse and the Maruts as his friends. Although the word aruṣa gives the meaning "red colour", here it is either a synonym of "horse" or a word that is a synonym of Sūrya in the form of a horse. The word ब्रध्न (*bradhna*) is an epithet of the word अरुष (*aruṣa*). In the same way there are many occasions on which it is the substantive and gives an independent and conventional meaning. For example:

तव त्ये अग्ने हरितो घृतस्ना रोहितास ऋज्वंचः स्वंचः । अरुषासो वृषण ऋजुमुष्का आ देवतातिमह्वंत दस्माः ॥ (*tava tye agne harito ghṛtasnā rohitāsa ṛjvaṃcaḥ svaṃcaḥ | aruṣāso vṛṣaṇa ṛjumuṣkā ā devatātimahvaṃta dasmāḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-6-9) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

In this Ṛk the colour names हरितः (*haritaḥ*), रोहितासः (*rohitāsaḥ*) and अरुषासः (*aruṣāsaḥ*) indicate the horses of the respective colour names. And:

अवर्धयन्तुभगं सप्त यह्वीः श्वेतं जज्ञानमरुषं महित्वा । शिशुं न जातमभ्यारुरश्वा देवासो अग्निं जनिमन्वपुष्यन् ॥ (*avardhayantubhagaṃ sapta yahvīḥ śvetaṃ jajñānamaruṣaṃ mahitvā | śiśuṃ na jātamabhyāruraśvā devāso agniṃ janimanvapuṣyan ‖*)

Here *(the word is)* an epithet of Agni, and *(the sentence breaks off here at the end of p. 309 in the supplied text; the reference of the verse is printed after this unfinished sentence:)*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-4) *(printed "ಮ. ಸಂ.", as supplied; the verse above is printed in the supplied text with "ಅವರ್ಧಯನ್ತುಭಗಂ" run together, as supplied)*

*(The Special Topics of Ṛk 3 continue on p. 310.)*

### Printed p. 310

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 3 continued from p. 309; the page begins with the next verse quoted.)*

सिंधुर्ह वार रसया सिंचदश्वान् फृणा वयोऽरुषासः परि ग्मन् । (*siṃdhurha vāra rasayā siṃcadaśvān phṛṇā vayo 'ruṣāsaḥ pari gman |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-83-6) *(printed "ಮಿ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

In many such Ṛks (1-118-5; 5-73-5) the word is also used as an epithet of horses and the like. In some places it can be seen to be used also as a proper name designating a separate deity named अरुष (*aruṣa*). If only two Ṛks are taken as examples this point becomes clear.

अप स्वसुरुषसो नग्निहीते रिणक्ति कृष्णीररुषाय पंथां । अश्वामघा गोमघा वां हुवेम दिवा नक्तं शरुमस्मद्युयोतं ॥ (*apa svasuruṣaso nagnihīte riṇakti kṛṣṇīraruṣāya paṃthāṃ | aśvāmaghā gomaghā vāṃ huvema divā naktaṃ śarumasmadyuyotaṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-21-1)

Here Sāyaṇa himself could not state a definite meaning for the word अरुषाय (*aruṣāya*). He has given two alternatives: अरोचमानाय अह्ने सूर्याय वा (*arocamānāya ahne sūryāya vā*). In explaining this Ṛk the opinion of the scholar Max-Muller *(so printed, with a hyphen and line break; as supplied)* is noteworthy.

Here, Arusha shares the same half-mythological character as Ushas, where we should speak of dawn and morning as mere periods of time, the Vedic poet speaks of them as living and intelligent beings, half human, half divine, as powers of nature capable of understanding his prayers and power ful *(so printed, split)* enough to reward his praises. I do not think that we need hesitate to take Arusha in this passage as a propar *(sic)* name of the morning or of the morning sun to whom the dark goddess, the Night, yeilds *(sic)* the path when he rises in the east.

[ The Sacred Books of the East. Vol. XXXII. p. 21 ]

In the same way:

विशोविश ईड्यमध्वरेष्वदृप्तक्रतुमरतिं युवत्योः । दिवः शिशुं सहसः सूनुमग्निं यज्ञस्य केतुमरुषं यजध्यै ॥ (*viśoviśa īḍyamadhvareṣvadṛptakratumaratiṃ yuvatyoḥ | divaḥ śiśuṃ sahasaḥ sūnumagniṃ yajñasya ketumaruṣaṃ yajadhyai ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-49-2) *(printed "ಖ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

In this Ṛk also, although it is clear that the word अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*) is an epithet of Agni, it would not be wrong to say that the word अरुष (*aruṣa*) is a separate proper name that is a synonym of Agni and indicates a part of Agni. In explaining this Ṛk also the scholar Max Muller has indicated his opinion in this way:

..........But I return to my orignal *(sic)* translation, and I prefer to see in Arusha as the representative of the rising Sun and, at the same time, of the sacrificial fire of the morning, but nevertheless as having in the mind of

### Printed p. 311

the poet a personality of his own. Heis *(sic)* the child of Dyu, originally, the offspring of heaven. He is the son of strength, originally genarated *(sic)* by the strong rubbing of the Aranis. He is the light of the sacrifice, whether as reminding man that the time for the morning sacrifice has come, or as himself lighting the sacrifice on the eastern altar of the sky. He is Arusha, originally as clothed in bright red colour, but gradually changed into the representative of the morning.

[S. B. E. Voq. *(sic)* 32. p. 25 to 6]. *(printed as a page range with a hyphen between 25 and 6; written out because the reference check has no Kannada twin for it)*

वयं हि ते अमन्मह्यान्तादा पराकात् । अश्वे न चित्रे अरुषि ॥ (*vayaṃ hi te amanmahyāntādā parākāt | aśve na citre aruṣi ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-21)

युक्षा ह्यरुषी रथे हरितो देव रोहितः । ताभिर्देवा इहा वह ॥ (*yukṣā hyaruṣī rathe harito deva rohitaḥ | tābhirdevā ihā vaha ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-12) *(the print has no full stop after "ಸಂ"; as supplied)*

अधि श्रियं नि दधुश्चारुमस्मिन्दिवो यदक्षी अमृता अकृण्वन् । अध क्षरंति सिंधवो न सृष्टाः प्र नीचीरग्ने अरुषीरजानन् । (*adhi śriyaṃ ni dadhuścārumasmindivo yadakṣī amṛtā akṛṇvan | adha kṣaraṃti siṃdhavo na sṛṣṭāḥ pra nīcīragne aruṣīrajānan |*) *(the second line ends with "।", not "॥"; as supplied)*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-72-10)

In these and similar places it is understood to mean the golden-red horse of Agni, and in the remaining Ṛks such as 8-68-18 an ordinary horse. Concerning the special meanings of the word अरुषी (*aruṣī*) used in the feminine, the scholar Max muller has again said this:

Further on, where the meanings attributable to Arushi in the Veda are collected, it is said that Arushi means a red house, also the teams of Agni and Ushas. Now, here surely a distinction should have been made between tho *(sic)* passages in which Arushi means a real horse and those where it expresses the imaginary steeds of Agni. The former, it should be observed, occur in one mandala only and in places of somewhat doubtful authority. Again, two pa- ssages *(so printed, split)* are set apart where Arushi is supposed to mean flames. Now, it may be perfectly true that the red horses of Agni are meant for flames, just as the red horses of Indra may be the rays of the Sun. But in that case, the red horses of Agni, should always have been thus translated, or rather interpreted, and not in one passage only.

[S. B. E XXXII. p. 27]

In the Ṛk under discussion the word अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*) can be taken to mean a light that is excessive and golden in colour.

### Printed p. 312

वसो अस्मान् नेषि (*vaso asmān neṣi*)—सर्पस्य प्रकाशप्रदानेन स्वस्वस्थानेषु वासयितः अग्ने त्वं अस्मान् कर्मानुरूपफलानि च प्रापय (*sarpasya prakāśapradānena svasvasthāneṣu vāsayitaḥ agne tvaṃ asmān karmānurūpaphalāni ca prāpaya*) *(so printed, with सर्पस्य (*sarpasya*); as supplied)*. Here the word वसु (*vasu*) is explained as one who, by bestowing light on all, makes them dwell in comfort in their respective dwelling-places; and the wish is expressed that Agni may grant to us, who perform the sacrifice, the fruits corresponding to our deeds *(the print has "ನಮ್ಮವುಕಮ್ಮ" in the sense of "ours" and "deeds", reading "ನಮ್ಮವು ಕಮ್ಮ ಕರ್ಮಗಳಿಗೆ", as supplied)*.

अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—अस्माकं दारिद्र लक्षणं पापं (*asmākaṃ dāridra lakṣaṇaṃ pāpaṃ*) . Explaining it as the sin in the form of our poverty, the prayer is made that Agni may destroy this sin.

यस्मै त्वमायजसे स साधत्यनर्वा क्षेति दधते सुवीर्यं । स तूताव नैनमश्नोत्यंहतिरग्रे सख्ये मारिषामा वयं तव ॥ (*yasmai tvamāyajase sa sādhatyanarvā kṣeti dadhate suvīryaṃ | sa tūtāva nainamaśnotyaṃhatiragre sakhye māriṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-94-9) *(printed "ಮಿ. ಸಂ.", as supplied)*

The author of the Nirukta *(printed "ರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು", as supplied)* quotes this Ṛk and says: नैनमंहतिरश्नोत्यंहतिश्चांहश्चांहुश्च हंतेर्निरूढोपधात् विपरीतात् (*nainamaṃhatiraśnotyaṃhatiścāṃhaścāṃhuśca haṃternirūḍhopadhāt viparītāt*) (Nir. 4-25). The word अंहस्‌ (*aṃhas*) is derived from the root हन (*hana*). Because the n of the root हन (*hana*) has come after the a, the words अंहति (*aṃhati*), अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*) and अंहुः (*aṃhuḥ*) arise. Durgācārya *(printed "ದುಗಾಚಾರ್ಯರು", as supplied)* has commented that sin is what is signified by this.

यजिष्ठ (*yajiṣṭha*)—युवतम (*yuvatama*) : addressing Agni as one who is always in youth, the prayer is made, with अभिलषितफलप्रदानेनप्राप्तकामान् कुरु (*abhilaṣitaphalapradānenaprāptakāmān kuru*) *(so printed, run together; as supplied)*, that by fulfilling our wishes this Agni may make us fully satisfied in our desires.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—the root चक्षिज् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*cakṣij vyaktāyāṃ vāci*). Since roots of the ad-class (अदादि (*adādi*), *adādi*) have many meanings, it is used here in the sense of light. When असुन् (*asun*) is continued from the preceding sūtra, by चक्षेर्बहुलं शिच्च (*cakṣerbahulaṃ śicca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-672) the suffix asun. Because śit-ness is prescribed, the ārdhadhātuka name does not arise; therefore the substitution ख्याणादेश (*khyāṇādeśa*) does not come to the root. Because it is nit, the initial-acute accent comes. In the compound the accent kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara comes.

वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—the root वृषु सेचने (*vṛṣu secane*). When आभच् (*ābhac*) is continued from the preceding sūtra, by यषिवृषिभ्यांकित् (*yaṣivṛṣibhyāṃkit*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-403) the suffix abhac. Because kit-ness is extended to it, guṇa of the short penultimate vowel of the root does not come on account of the suffix. In the vocative the nighāta accent of an addressed word comes.

पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—the word पुरु (*puru*) is a quality-word. By वोतोगुणवचनात् (*votoguṇavacanāt*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-44) the feminine suffix ṅīṣ comes. In the Vedic manner the initial u receives a long vowel. By the suffix accent it becomes acute on the last syllable.

भाहि (*bhāhi*)—the root भा दीप्तौ (*bhā dīptau*). Because it shows impulsion, it is a root with the inner causative sense. The form ends in the second person singular of loṭ. The finite-verb nighāta accent comes.

### Printed p. 313

*(Grammar notes of Ṛk 3 continued from p. 312.)* वसो (*vaso*)—the root वस निवासे (*vasa nivāse*) (to dwell). When उः (*uḥ*) is continued from the preceding sūtra, by शृस्वहित्रप्यसिवसि (*śṛsvahitrapyasivasi*) *(so printed, the line broken after शृस्वहित्र (*śṛsvahitra*); as supplied)* (Uṇ. 1-10) the suffix u. The form is of the kind संबंध्यंतर (*saṃbaṃdhyaṃtara*) . Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. By आमं त्रितस्य (*āmaṃ tritasya*) the initial-acute accent comes.

नेषि (*neṣi*)—the root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*) *(so printed, with णीञ् (*ṇīñ*); as supplied)*. In the Vedic manner laṭ is used in the sense of loṭ. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) luk for śap. On account of sip, guṇa of the ī of the root. By आमंत्रितं पूर्व (*āmaṃtritaṃ pūrva*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) the preceding word receives the state of non-existence (avidyamānavadbhāva); therefore it is as if no finite verb had come after the word, and so the nighāta accent does not come. Because sip is pit, it becomes udātta , and so the root accent remains.

पर्षि (*parṣi*)—the root पृ पालनपूरणयोः (*pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*). The form ends in the second person singular of laṭ. As before, luk for the vikaraṇa. By चादिषुच (*cādiṣuca*) there is connection with the particle ca, so the nighāta accent does not come. The root accent remains.

कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—the root डुकृण्करणे (*ḍukṛṇkaraṇe*) . The suffix sip in the second person singular of loṭ. By सेर्ह्यपिच्च (*serhyapicca*) the substitute hi for it. By श्रुतृणुपृकृवृभ्यश्चंदसि (*śrutṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaścaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-102) the substitute dhi for hi. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) luk for the vikaraṇa (u). Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. By the suffix accent it becomes final-acute. In the Vedic manner a long vowel comes in the Saṃhitā.

राये (*rāye*)—the root रा दाने (*rā dāne*). By रातेर्डैः (*rāterḍaiḥ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-229) the suffix ḍai. Because it is ḍit, loss of the ṭi (ā). The word रै (*rai*) results. In the dative the substitute āya. By ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the acute accent comes on the case ending.

उशिजः (*uśijaḥ*)—the root वश कांतौ (*vaśa kāṃtau*). By वशेः किच्च (*vaśeḥ kicca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2. 229) *(printed with a full stop and space between 2 and 229; as supplied)* the suffix iji. Because kit-ness is prescribed, by गृहिज्या (*gṛhijyā*) samprasāraṇa for the root, and pūrvarūpa. By the suffix accent the i becomes acute.

यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—अतिशयेन युवा यविष्ठः (*atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ*) ; by अतिशायनेतमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyanetamabiṣṭhanau*) the suffix iṣṭhan. By स्कूलदूर (*skūladūra*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156) loss of the yaṇādi (van) that follows. Guṇa and the substitute av for the preceding u. By आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the nighāta accent comes in the vocative.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अषा॑ह्नो अग्ने वृष॒भो दि॑दीहि॒ पुरो॒ विश्वाः॒ सौभ॑गा संजिगी॒वान् ।  
> य॒ज्ञस्य॑ ने॒ता प्र॑थ॒मस्य॑ पा॒योर्जात॑वेदो बृह॒तः सु॑प्रणीते ॥४॥

*(A stray printed "40" stands after the Saṃhitā block, as supplied; probably a stray number.)*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अषाह्लः । अग्ने । वृषभः । दिदीहि । पुरः । विश्वाः । सौभगा । संजिगीवान् ।  
> यज्ञस्य । नेता । प्रथमस्य । पायोः । जातवेदः । बृहतः । सुप्रनीते ॥ ४ ॥

> *aṣāhlaḥ | agne | vṛṣabhaḥ | didīhi | puraḥ | viśvāḥ | saubhagā | saṃjigīvān |*  
> *yajñasya | netā | prathamasya | pāyoḥ | jātavedaḥ | bṛhataḥ | supranīte ‖ 4 ‖*

*(The Pada text is printed with अषाह्लः (*aṣāhlaḥ*) and सुप्रनीते (*supranīte*), whereas the Saṃhitā has अषाह्नो (*aṣāhno*) and सुप्रणीते (*supraṇīte*); as supplied.)*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अषाळ्वः शत्रुभिरसोढोऽपराजितः । स्वयं शत्रूञ्चयतीत्यर्थः ।
> वृषभः कामानां वर्षयिता एवंभूतस्त्वं विश्वाः सर्वाः पुरः शत्रोणां पुरीः
> सौभगा तत्रत्यानि शोभनान्युत्तमानि धनानि च संजिगीवान् सम्यग्वयन् दीदिहि ।
> सर्वतो ज्वालाभिर्दीप्यस्व । सुप्रणीते शोभनप्रणयन जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञ हे
> अग्ने बृहत उपदिष्टातिदिष्टद्विविधॆतिकर्तव्यताकलापेन महतः पायोस्त्पलप्रदानेन
> रक्षकस्य प्रथमस्य मुख्यतया प्रथमं क्रियमाणस्य । एष नाव प्रथमो यज्यो
> यज्ञानां यज्योतिष्टोम इति श्रुतेः । तादृशस्य ज्योतिष्टोमाख्यस्य यज्ञस्य
> नेता हनिर्वहनदेवताह्वानादिक्रियाया निर्वाहको भव ॥ अषाळ्वः । षह मर्षण इ-
> त्यस्य निष्ठायां हो ढ इति ढकारः । यषस्तथोधोध इति क्तस्य धकारः । ष्टुत्वेन
> ढः । ढलोपे कृते ढलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घ इति दीर्घः । ओत्वाभावश्कांदसः । सहेः
> साडः स इति सकारस्य मूर्धान्यादेशः। अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे नञ्परः । वृषभः ।
> वृष सेचने। ऋषिवृषिभ्यां किदित्यभच् । चित्सरः । दीदिहि । दिवु क्रीडादावित्यस्य यङ्कु कि
> लोटो मध्यमैकवचने संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इत्यभ्यासस्य गुणाभावः । सर्वॆ
> विधयश्चंदसि विकल्पंत इति पूर्वत्रासिद्धमित्यस्याप्रवृत्तौ परत्वाद्दलि चेति दीर्घत्वं ।
> पश्चाद्वलोपः । सौभगा । सुभगान्मंत्र इत्युद्धात्रादिषु पाठाद्भावार्थेऽञ् । हृद्भग-
> सिंध्वंत इति पूर्वपदस्य वृद्धिः । उत्तरपदस्य वृद्धिर्न भवति सर्वविधीनां छंदसि विक-
> ल्पितत्वात् । सुपां सुलुगिति सुपो डादेशः । तेन च सौभाग्येन धनान्युपलक्ष्यंते ।
> इत्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । संजिगीवान् । जि जये ।छंदसि लिट् । तस्य क्वसुः । सन्नि टोर्जॆ-
> रिति कवर्गादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । दीर्घश्चांदसः । पायोः । पा रक्षणे । कृवापाजि-
> मीत्यादिना उण् प्रत्ययः । आतो युक् चिण् कृतोरिति युगागमः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, unconquered by enemies and showerer of desires, shine on all sides with flames, conquering all the cities of the enemies together with their fine wealth; O Jātavedas, be the leader of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, which protects (by granting fruit) and is performed first. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

*(Grammar tail inside the same block, noted briefly.)* It treats the roots षह मर्षण (*ṣaha marṣaṇa*), वृष सेचने (*vṛṣa secane*), दिवु (*divu*), जि जये (*ji jaye*) and पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*) and the forms अषाळ्वः (*aṣāḷvaḥ*), वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*), दीदिहि (*dīdihi*), सौभगा (*saubhagā*), संजिगीवान् (*saṃjigīvān*) and पायोः (*pāyoḥ*), with accents and the Vedic irregularities.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अषाळ्हः (*aṣāḷhaḥ*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has अषाह्नो (*aṣāhno*))*—the unobstructed one
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desired objects; thou who art such
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—the cities of enemies
- सौभगा (*saubhagā*)—their excellent riches
- संजिगीर्वान् (*saṃjigīrvān*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā has संजिगीवान् (*saṃjigīvān*))*—conquering completely
- दिदीहि (*didīhi*)—shine exceedingly
- सुप्रणीते (*supraṇīte*)—O excellent guide
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who knowest everything

### Printed p. 315

बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of the great; पायोः (*pāyoḥ*)—of the protecting one (by granting fruit); प्रथमस्य (*prathamasya*)—of that which is performed before everything else; यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice in the form of the Jyotiṣṭoma; नेता (*netā*)—as the one who carries it through (be).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, thou who art of unobstructed power and the showerer of desired objects, shine exceedingly, conquering completely all the cities of the enemies and their excellent riches. O Agni, excellent guide and knower of everything, be the one who carries through the sacrifice in the form of the Jyotiṣṭoma, which is great, which protects the sacrificers by giving them fruits, and which is performed first of all.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
AGNI, you are irresistible and the showerer (of benefits), consume victorious all the cities (of the foe), and (all their) precious things : the duly worshipped, the knower of all that is born, (be for us) the conductor of the first great preserving sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अषाळ्यः (*aṣāḷyaḥ*) *(so printed, with ळ्य (*ḷya*))*—शत्रुभिरसोधो अपराजितः (*śatrubhirasodho aparājitaḥ*): Agni is one who cannot be conquered by enemies; therefore the meaning स्वयं शत्र्नू जयति (*svayaṃ śatrnū jayati*) , "one who conquers the enemies of his own accord", is described.

पुरः सौभगा संजिगीर्वान् दीदिहि (*puraḥ saubhagā saṃjigīrvān dīdihi*) *(so printed, with संजिगीर्वान् (*saṃjigīrvān*))*—शत्रुणां पुरीः (*śatruṇāṃ purīḥ*) : the word पुरः (*puraḥ*) is explained as the city of the enemies; by the word सौभग (*saubhaga*) the wealth that is in the city is meant; it is wished that Agni may conquer the most excellent wealth that is of that kind, and सर्वशः ज्वालाभिर्दिपस्व (*sarvaśaḥ jvālābhirdipasva*) *(so printed, with दिपस्व (*dipasva*))* may shine in every manner, or in all places, with his rays.

जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—This word has been explained by the authors of the Nirukta as: जातानि वेद, जातानि वैनं विदुः. जातेजाते विद्यत इति वा, जातविद्यो जातधनः, जातविद्यो जातप्रज्ञानः यत्तज्जातः पशूनविंदतेति तज्ञातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वं इति ब्राह्मणं (*jātāni veda, jātāni vainaṃ viduḥ. jātejāte vidyata iti vā, jātavidyo jātadhanaḥ, jātavidyo jātaprajñānaḥ yattajjātaḥ paśūnaviṃdateti tajñātavedaso jātavedastvaṃ iti brāhmaṇaṃ*) *(so printed; the Kannada says only that this is the explanation given)*. The nature of Jātavedas is told in the Bṛhaddevatā in this way:

इहाग्निभूतस्त्वषिभिर्लोके स्तुतिभिरीळितः । जातवेदाः स्तुतो मध्यॆ स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि ॥ (*ihāgnibhūtastvaṣibhirloke stutibhirīḷitaḥ | jātavedāḥ stuto madhyè stuto vaiśvānaro divi ‖*)

(Bṛ. De. 1-67) *(the reference is printed twice, one after the other; as supplied)*

In this verse it is said that the ṛṣis call the Agni that is on the earth Jātavedas and the Agni that is in the heavenly world Vaiśvānara. And, continuing this same explanation,

*(The Special Topics of Ṛk 4 continue on the next page; the window ends at the end of p. 315 with मत्तु इदे विवरणॆयन्नु मुंदुवरिसुत्ता (*mattu ide vivaraṇèyannu muṃduvarisuttā*).)*

### Printed p. 316

वैश्वानरं श्रितोह्यग्निरग्निं वैश्वानरः श्रितः । अनयोर्जावेदास्तु तथैते जातवेदसि ॥ (*vaiśvānaraṃ śritohyagniragniṃ vaiśvānaraḥ śritaḥ | anayorjāvedāstu tathaite jātavedasi ‖*)

(Bṛ. De. 1-97)

It is explained that Agni is contained in Vaiśvānara and Vaiśvānara in Agni, and that Jātavedas is contained in these two forms, and that these two forms are different portions of Jātavedas. Thus, having told the places of Jātavedas in the first adhyāya, the explanation of the nature of Jātavedas is given in the second adhyāya in this way.

भूतानि वेद यज्ञातो जातवेदाथ कथ्यते । यच्चैष जातविद्योऽभूत् वित्तं जातोऽधिवेत्ति वा ॥ (*bhūtāni veda yajñāto jātavedātha kathyate | yaccaiṣa jātavidyo 'bhūt vittaṃ jāto 'dhivetti vā ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-30)

विद्यते सर्वभूतैर्हि यद्वा जातः पुनःपुनः । तेनैष मध्यभागेंद्रो जातवेदा इति स्तुतः ॥ (*vidyate sarvabhūtairhi yadvā jātaḥ punaḥpunaḥ | tenaiṣa madhyabhāgeṃdro jātavedā iti stutaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-31)

(Bṛ. De. 2-31) *(the reference of the second verse is printed twice, one after the other; as supplied)*

It is explained in the Bṛhaddevatā that Agni is praised as Jātavedas, like Indra who dwells in the middle world, because he knows everything as soon as he is born, or because knowledge arose in him, or because as soon as he is born he knows and possesses all wealth, or because, whenever he is born again and again, he is known by all beings. In the same manner the nature of this Agni is explained in the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa, where it is said thus.

यः संवत्सरं जातः स्यात्पाणो वा अग्निस्तमेतद्बिभर्त्यथ ह वै रेतः सिक्तं प्राणोऽन्ववरोहति तद्विंदते तद्यज्ञातं जातं विंदते तस्माज्जात- वेदाः ॥ (*yaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ jātaḥ syātpāṇo vā agnistametadbibhartyatha ha vai retaḥ siktaṃ prāṇo 'nvavarohati tadviṃdate tadyajñātaṃ jātaṃ viṃdate tasmājjāta- vedāḥ ‖*)

(Śa. Brā. 9-5-16-8)

It is said that Agni in the form of prāṇa is called Jātavedas because he pervades with his own power all the beings that are born. This same Jātavedas, who is worshipped in the sacrificial house, is described in the Upaniṣads as Brahman, the soul of the universe.

विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपंतं । (*viśvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ jātavedasaṃ parāyaṇaṃ jyotirekaṃ tapaṃtaṃ |*)

(Pra. U. 1-8)

In the Praśna-upaniṣad it is described that the Sun rises, who is of all forms, has a thousand rays, is all-knowing, is the refuge of the whole world, is known by the wise, and is the inner self of all beings; and in the Kaṭha-upaniṣad:

अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः । दिवे दिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्विर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः ॥ (*araṇyornihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ | dive diva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhirhaviṣmadvirmanuṣyebhiragniḥ ‖*)

(Ka. U. 1-4-8)

### Printed p. 317

It is described in the Kaṭha-upaniṣad that the Jātavedas who, staying between the two aranis (fire-sticks) in the adhiyajña, enjoys all the oblations; whom the yogis meditate upon, holding him in their hearts as pregnant women with affection nourish and bring up their embryos; and to whom, as the worshipful Agni, the sacrificers offer oblations, is the Supreme Brahman, the soul of the universe. In the same sequence, the matter described in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-2 is told in the Kaṭha. Thus all the Śrutis praise him as being called Jātavedas because he is all-knowing, all-pervading, possessed of all wealth and the most excellent.

बृहतः पायोः प्रथमस्य यज्ञस्य नेता भव (*bṛhataḥ pāyoḥ prathamasya yajñasya netā bhava*)—the meaning protector is explained for the word वायु (*vāyu*) *(so printed; the Saṃhitā and the Pratipadārtha have पायोः (*pāyoḥ*))*, which is derived from the root पाधातु (*pādhātu*) . It is explained that the sacrifice protects by granting the fruits of the respective rites. For the word बृहत् (*bṛhat*) the meaning महत् (*mahat*) (great) is given. Since among the rites that are parts of the sacrifice some are known by instruction (told separately by the Śruti sentences), and others, being stated in one place, are to be inferred for performance in another place, it is described that the sacrifice is great by the two kinds of necessary duties, उपदिष्टातिदिष्टोभयेतिकर्तव्यताकलापेन (*upadiṣṭātidiṣṭobhayetikartavyatākalāpena*).

Explaining that the word प्रथम (*prathama*) is used here in the sense of chief, and quoting the Śruti sentence एष वाव प्रथमो यज्ञो यज्ञानां यज्योतिष्टोमः (*eṣa vāva prathamo yajño yajñānāṃ yajyotiṣṭomaḥ*) *(so printed, with यज्योतिष्टोमः (*yajyotiṣṭomaḥ*))*, it is described that the sacrifice called Jyotiṣṭoma is the chief among sacrifices *(the print has "ಮುಖ್ಯವಾದುದೂ ಎಂದೂ"; as supplied)* and that, because it is chief, it must necessarily be performed. And in this sacrifice called Jyotiṣṭoma, full of such greatness, Agni is entreated to complete the sacrifice by performing such works as हनिर्वहन देवताह्वानादि क्रियाया निर्वाहकः (*hanirvahana devatāhvānādi kriyāyā nirvāhakaḥ*) *(so printed, with हनिर्वहन (*hanirvahana*))*: carrying the oblation to the gods, calling the gods to the sacrifice, and the like.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

अषाळ्हः (*aṣāḷhaḥ*)—the root षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*). From निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) the suffix kta for it. By होढः (*hoḍhaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-31) the substitute ḍha for ha. By झषस्तथोर्धोधः (*jhaṣastathordhodhaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-40) the substitute dha for the t of the suffix, with the ḍha as cause. By ष्टुनाष्टुः (*ṣṭunāṣṭuḥ*) the substitute ḍha for it. By ढोढे लोपः (*ḍhoḍhe lopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-13) loss of the preceding ḍha. Then by ढलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोणः (*ḍhalope pūrvasya dīrghoṇaḥ*) (Pā. Rū. 6-3-111) *(so printed, with पा. रू. (*pā. rū.*))* lengthening of the preceding a. In the Vedic manner the change to o that comes by सहिवहोरोदवर्णस्य (*sahivahorodavarṇasya*) does not come. By सहे साडः सः (*sahe sāḍaḥ saḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-56) the substitute ṣa for the sa of the root. The negative particle is compounded with साढ (*sāḍha*). By तत्पुरुषेतुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣetulyārtha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) *(so printed, the sūtra broken off with a dash)* the accent of the negative particle remains.

वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the root वृषु सेचने (*vṛṣu secane*). By ऋषिवृषिभ्यांकित् (*ṛṣivṛṣibhyāṃkit*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-403)

### Printed p. 318

the suffix अभच् (*abhac*). Because kit-ness is extended to it, guṇa does not come. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the final-acute accent comes.

दिदीहि (*didīhi*)—the root दिवु क्रीडादिषु (*divu krīḍādiṣu*). Here it is taken in the sense of light. When the sense of intensity appears, yaṅ. For it luk. After the yaṅluk-ending, in the second person singular of loṭ the substitute hi for sip. By संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः (*saṃjñāpūrvako vidhiranityaḥ*) (Pari. 95) guṇa does not come to the reduplication. Here, when it stands as दिदिव्+हि (*didiv+hi*), since the lengthening is asiddha, the loss of va would have to come first. But by the statement सर्वे- विधयश्चंदसि विकल्प्यंते (*sarve- vidhayaścaṃdasi vikalpyaṃte*) *(the line is broken after सर्वे (*sarve*) in the print; as supplied)* the sūtra पूर्वत्रासिद्दम् (*pūrvatrāsiddam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-1) does not operate here. Therefore, by the later sūtra हलिचॆ (*halicè*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-77) lengthening of the i of the root. By लोपोव्योर्वलि (*lopovyorvali*) the loss of va afterwards. The form दीदिहि (*dīdihi*) results. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes.

सौभगा (*saubhagā*)—because it is read in the udgātrādi group as सुभगान्मंत्रे (*subhagānmaṃtre*), the suffix añ in the sense of state after the word सुभग (*subhaga*). Because añ is ñit, by हृद्भगसिंध्यंते (*hṛdbhagasiṃdhyaṃte*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-19) vṛddhi of the first member. Although vṛddhi of the beginning of the latter member is thereby prescribed, all operations being optional in the Veda, it does not come here. By सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ḍā for the case ending. By सौभाग्य (*saubhāgya*) (good fortune) the wealth that is its cause is indicated here by lakṣaṇā. Because the suffix añ is ñit, by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) the initial-acute accent comes.

संजिगीवान् (*saṃjigīvān*)—the root जि जये (*ji jaye*). When liṭ comes in the Veda, by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*) the substitute kvasu for it. With that as cause, reduplication of the root. By सन्‌लिटोर्जेः (*sanliṭorjeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-57) *(so printed, with a joiner letter between सन् (*san*) and लिटो (*liṭo*))*, since liṭ follows, the substitute ga by kutva for the ja of the root. In the Vedic manner lengthening of the i of the root. The suffix accent remains. In the compound the accent kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara comes.

पायोः (*pāyoḥ*)—the root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*). By कृवापाजि (*kṛvāpāji*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-1) the suffix uṇ. Because the suffix is ṇit, by आतोयुक्‌चिण् कृतोः (*ātoyukciṇ kṛtoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-33) the augment yuk for the root. Because it is kit, it comes as the final part. By the suffix accent it becomes final-acute. The form is of the genitive singular.

> श्छांदसत्वान्न भवति निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas-like Agni, who grinds down all the world at the end of time, being wise and shining by thy own light, make the many rites for the gods, which bring the happiness of heaven and the like, faultless and complete; restraining thy own constant motion, carry our oblation-food to the gods like a chariot; and make heaven and earth shine with a beautiful form by thy own lustre. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

*(Grammar tail inside the same block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words दीद्यानः (*dīdyānaḥ*), सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*), सस्निः (*sasniḥ*) (root षस स्वष्टे (*ṣasa svaṣṭe*) *(so printed)*) and वक्षि (*vakṣi*) (root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जरितः (*jaritaḥ*)—O Agni, who causes everything to decay
- सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—thou who hast excellent wisdom
- दीद्यानः (*dīdyānaḥ*)—and who shinest with thy own lustre; देवान् अच्छ (*devān accha*)—performed with the gods in view
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—many
- शर्म (*śarma*)—and bringing happiness, the rites such as Agnihotra
- अच्छिद्रा (*acchidrā*)—make them free from any lapse (and)
- सस्निः (*sasniḥ*)—restraining thy diffusion; रथो न (*ratho na*)—as a chariot carries things
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food in the form of the oblation
- अभि (*abhi*)—towards the gods
- वक्षि (*vakṣi*)—carry (and bring it to them)
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—thou
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- सुमेके (*sumeke*)—make them shine with an excellent form

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who causest everything to decay, thou who hast excellent wisdom and shinest with thy own lustre, make our many Agnihotra and other rites, which are performed with the gods in view and bring happiness, free from any lapse. And, as a chariot carries things, restrain thy diffusion, carry our food in the form of the oblation, offered with the gods in view, and bring it to them. O Agni, by thy own light make heaven and earth also shine with an exceedingly beautiful form.

*(The sentence is carried over from p. 319 to p. 320 without a break, as supplied.)*

### Printed p. 320

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Destroyer (of the world), you who are endowed with intelligence and radiance, celebrate many faultless sacred rites in honour of the gods, and restraining (your impatience), convey to them like a waggon our (sacrificial) food : illume (with your rays) the beautiful heaven and earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

जरितः (*jaritaḥ*)—the explanation of the meaning is given by the words सर्वस्य जगतः अंतकाले जरयितः (*sarvasya jagataḥ aṃtakāle jarayitaḥ*): Agni is the one who destroys all beings at the time of dissolution.

पुरूणि शर्म अच्छिद्रा (*purūṇi śarma acchidrā*)—स्वर्गादिसुखसाधनभूतानि अग्निहोत्रादीनि कर्माणि अच्छिद्राणि कर्तकर्मसाधनवैकल्यराहित्येन संपूर्णानि कुरु । (*svargādisukhasādhanabhūtāni agnihotrādīni karmāṇi acchidrāṇi kartakarmasādhanavaikalyarāhityena saṃpūrṇāni kuru |*) *(so printed, with कर्तकर्मसाधनवैकल्यराहित्येन (*kartakarmasādhanavaikalyarāhityena*); the bhāṣya block above has कर्तृकर्मसाधनवैकल्यराहित्येन (*kartṛkarmasādhanavaikalyarāhityena*))* Since the word शर्म (*śarma*) is explained as शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*) (Ni. 9-34), protection or the producing of happiness, it is expressed as a wish that Agni may make our sacrificial rites complete, so that no deficiency whatever, whether in the sacrificer, in the rites, or arising from a want of the means, may come in the rites such as Agnihotra, which are the cause of producing the happiness of heaven and the like.

सस्निः (*sasniḥ*)—सन्निरुद्धः स्वकीयं सततगमनं सन्निरुध्य हविष्प्रक्षेपदर्यंतमत्र वर्तमानः । (*sanniruddhaḥ svakīyaṃ satatagamanaṃ sannirudhya haviṣprakṣepadaryaṃtamatra vartamānaḥ |*) *(so printed, with हविष्प्रक्षेपदर्यंतमत्र (*haviṣprakṣepadaryaṃtamatra*); the bhāṣya block above reads the word differently, with हविष्कृक्षेप (*haviṣkṛkṣepa*) in place of हविष्प्रक्षेप (*haviṣprakṣepa*))* The writer of the Nirukta, quoting the Ṛk

सस्निमविंदच्चरणे नदीनामपावृणोद्भुरो अश्वव्रजानां । प्रासां गंधर्वो अमृतानि वोचदिंद्रो दक्षं परि जानादहीनां ॥ (*sasnimaviṃdaccaraṇe nadīnāmapāvṛṇodbhuro aśvavrajānāṃ | prāsāṃ gaṃdharvo amṛtāni vocadiṃdro dakṣaṃ pari jānādahīnāṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-139-6)

explains for the word सस्निं (*sasniṃ*) the meaning संस्कृतं अद्भिः परिवेष्टितं (*saṃskṛtaṃ adbhiḥ pariveṣṭitaṃ*), that is, surrounded and held back by waters.

अग्ने रोदसी सुमेके (*agne rodasī sumeke*)—द्यावापृथिव्यौ शोभनरूपोपेते स्वकीयप्रभाभिः प्रकाशयुक्ते कुरु । (*dyāvāpṛthivyau śobhanarūpopete svakīyaprabhābhiḥ prakāśayukte kuru |*) Addressing Agni, it is prayed that Agni may grant his light, so that heaven and earth, endowed with a pleasant form, may shine with their own brilliance.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

अच्छिद्रा (*acchidrā*)—न छिद्राणि अच्छिद्राणि (*na chidrāṇi acchidrāṇi*). In the negative tatpuruṣa compound the accent of the first member's own form (the avyaya-pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara) comes. In the neuter plural, by शेश्शंदसि बहुलम् (*śeśśaṃdasi bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70) loss of śi.

जरित: (*jarita:*) *(so printed, with a colon)*—the root ज्यष् वयोहानौ (*jyaṣ vayohānau*) . Here it has the sense of the causative inside. In the agent sense the suffix tṛc. For it the augment iḍ. In the vocative the amantrita-nighāta accent comes.

देवान् (*devān*)—since a follows, by दीर्घादटिसमानपादे (*dīrghādaṭisamānapāde*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-9) *(printed with the words run together, as supplied)* ru. By आतोटिनित्यं (*ātoṭinityaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3) the preceding ā necessarily becomes nasalised. In अच्छा (*acchā*), by निपातस्यच (*nipātasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136) lengthening comes in the Saṃhitā.

दीद्यानः (*dīdyānaḥ*)—the root दीदी (*dīdī*) expresses the action of shining. When laṭ comes after it, the substitute śānac for it. Since it is read in the adādi group, luk for śap. Since it has the name abhyasta, by अभ्यस्ता-नामादिः (*abhyastā-nāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) the initial-acute accent comes.

सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—by नित्यमसिच्‌प्रजामेधयोः (*nityamasicprajāmedhayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 5-4-122) the suffix asic after मेध (*medha*) in a bahuvrīhi. By नञ्सुभ्यां (*nañsubhyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the accent on the end of the latter member comes.

सस्निः (*sasniḥ*)—the root षस स्वप्ने (*ṣasa svapne*) *(so printed, with स्वप्ने (*svapne*); the bhāṣya block has स्वष्टे (*svaṣṭe*))*. By धात्वादेः षः सः (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) the substitute sa for the initial. The Uṇādi suffix nin, being nit, gives, by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*), the initial-acute accent.

वक्षि (*vakṣi*)—the root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*). In the second person singular of loṭ, sip. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) luk for śap. By होढः (*hoḍhaḥ*) the substitute ḍha for the ha of the root. By षढोः कःसि (*ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥsi*) (Pā. Sū. 8-241) *(printed "8- 241", i.e. "8-241" after a line break, as supplied)* the substitute ka for it. With that as cause, ṣatva for the sakāra. The substitute hi for sip does not come, being Vedic. The tiṅanta-nighāta accent comes.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, showerer of desires, increase for us the fruits we long for and grant us food; shining with fair lustre together with the gods worthy of the sacrifice, make heaven and earth good milkers of the desired fruit by way of rain; let the ill-will of the enemy, born of an evil mind, not surround us. The rest is grammar (transcribed, not explained).

*(Grammar tail inside the same block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words पीपय (*pīpaya*) (root पा पान (*pā pāna*)), जिन्व (*jinva*) (root इवि जिवि धिवि (*ivi jivi dhivi*) (roots of the sense of pleasing)), सुदोघे (*sudoghe*) and दुर्मतिः (*durmatiḥ*) (root मनु अवबोधने (*manu avabodhane*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—showerer of desired objects
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us; प्र पीपय (*pra pīpaya*)—cause (the desired objects) to be fulfilled
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—foods
- जिन्व (*jinva*)—provide and give
- देव (*deva*)—O resplendent Agni
- सुरुचा (*surucā*)—by your excellent radiance
- रुचानः (*rucānaḥ*)—you who shine
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—together with the gods (worthy of the sacrifice)
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- सुदोघ्ने (*sudoghne*)—(make them) pourers of rain and the like in abundance *(so printed, with सुदोघ्ने (*sudoghne*); the Saṃhitā has सुदोघे (*sudoghe*))*
- मर्तस्य (*martasya*)—of the human enemy
- दुर्मतिः (*durmatiḥ*)—the evil mind
- नः (*naḥ*)—us; मा परि ष्ठात् (*mā pari ṣṭhāt*)—let it not surround

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, showerer of desired objects, make the fruits we long for grow, make us contented, and provide us with food. O resplendent Agni, shining with excellent radiance, join the other gods worthy of the sacrifice and make heaven and earth also pour rain and the like in abundance. And with your help, may the evil mind of the human enemy, and his harm, not surround us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Be propitious, showerer (of benefits); grant (abundant) food, AGNI ; (make) heaven and earth yield us milk : divine (AGNI), associated with the gods, shining with bright radiance, let not the ill-will of any mortal prevail aginst *(sic: "against")* us. -

*(The printed English ends with a stray hyphen after "us.", as supplied.)*

### Printed p. 323

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्र पीपय जिन्व वार्जा (*pra pīpaya jinva vārjā*) *(so printed, with वार्जा (*vārjā*); the Saṃhitā has वाजान् (*vājān*))*—अभिलषितफलानि वर्धय । अन्नानि प्रयच्छ । (*abhilaṣitaphalāni vardhaya | annāni prayaccha |*) Here, by the word वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*) Agni is addressed as one who bestows desired objects in abundance, and the wish is expressed that Agni may fulfil our desires. Further, for the word जिन्व (*jinva*), a form of the root जिवि (*jivi*) which teaches the sense "gladden", the meaning is given: produce delight by granting us food.

The word पीपॆय (*pīpèya*) *(so printed; the Ṛk has पीपय (*pīpaya*))* is formed from the root पै (*pai*) which means growth, and indicates abundance of wealth: "be nourished, attain mental satisfaction and growth". In many Ṛks such as

पीपाय स श्रवसा मर्त्येषु यो अग्नये ददाश विप्र उक्षैः । चित्राभिस्तमूतिभिश्चित्रशोचिर्व्रजस्य साता गोमतो धधाति ॥ (*pīpāya sa śravasā martyeṣu yo agnaye dadāśa vipra ukṣaiḥ | citrābhistamūtibhiścitraśocirvrajasya sātā gomato dhadhāti ‖*)

(म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*) 6-10-3) *(so printed, with the abbreviation म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*))*

this word is used, and it indicates both senses, joy of mind and abundance of food, showing the relation of cause and effect between the two. In the same way, where the word जिन्व (*jinva*) is used, it also indicates the gratification of the self. The writers of the Nirukta explain जिन्वतिः प्रीतिकर्मा (*jinvatiḥ prītikarmā*) (Ni. 6-22), and to show the excess of love indicated by this word they quote the Ṛk

भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्नंत्यग्नयः । (*bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvaṃti divaṃ jinnaṃtyagnayaḥ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-51)

and make known that the word जिन्नति (*jinnati*) there indicates the excess of love which heaven and earth supply to each other by their respective actions. In the same way, in the present Ṛk too, it is a word showing excess of love.

सुरुचा रुचानः (*surucā rucānaḥ*)—शोभनदीप्त्या शोभमानः । (*śobhanadīptyā śobhamānaḥ |*) Here Agni is addressed by the word देव (*deva*), and the meaning is explained: Agni, who blazes with his naturally perfect, abundant radiance, shines with the rays that bring us happiness.

देवेभिः रोदसी सुदोघे (*devebhiḥ rodasī sudoghe*)—यजनीयदेवैः सहितोऽस्माकं इमे द्यावापृथिव्यौ वृष्टिद्वारा अभिमतफलदानेन सुष्टु दोग्न्यौ कुरु । (*yajanīyadevaiḥ sahito 'smākaṃ ime dyāvāpṛthivyau vṛṣṭidvārā abhimataphaladānena suṣṭu dognyau kuru |*) The wish is expressed that Agni, together with the gods who are worthy of worship at the sacrifice, may fill heaven and earth (the earth and the atmosphere) with rain-water, and grant that our desires may arise in abundance from heaven and earth.

### Printed p. 324

मर्तस्य दुर्मतिः नः मा परि ष्ठात् (*martasya durmatiḥ naḥ mā pari ṣṭhāt*)—शत्रोः दुष्टबुद्धिप्रयुक्तो अभिभवः अस्मान् परितो मा गच्छतु (*śatroḥ duṣṭabuddhiprayukto abhibhavaḥ asmān parito mā gacchatu*) (arising from the enemy) it is prayed that Agni may bring it about that the contempt which may befall us through the enemy's evil conduct may never come upon us.

मर्तस्य (*martasya*)—शत्रोः (*śatroḥ*)—The word मर्त (*marta*) is read among the names of man (Ni. 3-8). Sāyaṇa has explained it with the meaning "human enemy".

दुर्मतिः (*durmatiḥ*)—To the word मति (*mati*), formed from the root मनु (*manu*) which means "ascertain", the prefix दुर् (*dur*) is joined, and it is explained as दुष्टा मतिः बुद्धिः (*duṣṭā matiḥ buddhiḥ*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

पीपय (*pīpaya*)—the root पा पाने (*pā pāne*). By हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26) the suffix ṇic. After the ṇijanta, luṅ in the Vedic manner. In the second person singular, sip. By णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः (*ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-48) the substitute caṅ for cli. By चजि (*caji*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-11) doubling of the root. By सन्वल्लघुनिचज् (*sanvallaghunicaj*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-93) the state of being like san comes, and when by सन्यतः (*sanyataḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-79) the reduplicative syllable gets i, by दीर्घोलघोः (*dīrgholaghoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-94) it is lengthened. In the Vedic manner loss of sip. Since it stands after an atiṅanta *(so printed, अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*))*, the nighāta accent comes.

जिन्व (*jinva*)—the root इवि जिवि धिवि प्रीणने (*ivi jivi dhivi prīṇane*). In the second person singular of loṭ, the substitute hi for sip. By इदितो नुम् धातोः (*idito num dhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) the augment num *(printed सुमागम (*sumāgama*), "sum-augment", as supplied)* for the root. The vikaraṇa śap. Since hi comes after a stem ending in a, by अतो हेः (*ato heḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-105) luk for hi. The form जिन्व (*jinva*) results. Since this is a vocative-like form *(आमंत्रित (*āmaṃtrita*), ending in the sambuddhi)*, by आमंत्रितंपूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (*āmaṃtritaṃpūrvamavidyamānavat*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-22) it takes the state of being as if non-existent, so that it is as if a tiṅanta form stood after it. Since it is prohibited as अतिजः (*atijaḥ*), the nighāta accent does not come. Since śap is anudātta, the accent of the root remains.

सुदोघे (*sudoghe*)—दोहनं दोघः (*dohanaṃ doghaḥ*). The root मह प्रपूरणे (*maha prapūraṇe*) . The suffix ghañ in the sense of the action. In the Vedic manner ghatva for the h of the root. By पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) guṇa of the short penultimate. Since it ends in the suffix it, the initial-acute accent comes. By आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच् छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chaṃdasi*) (Pā.Sū. 6-2-119) the initial-acute accent of the latter member comes in the bahuvrīhi.

रुचानः (*rucānaḥ*)—the root रुच दीप्तौ (*ruca dīptau*). The substitute śānac for laṭ. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) luk for the vikaraṇa. Since the suffix has the sign j by सार्वधातुकमपित् (*sārvadhātukamapit*), guṇa of the short penultimate of the root does not come on that account. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the final-acute accent comes.

### Printed p. 325

*(Continuation of the Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Ṛk 6, begun on p. 324.)* दुर्मतिः (*durmatiḥ*)—the root मनु अवबोधने (*manu avabodhane*). मन्यते इति मतिः बुद्धिः (*manyate iti matiḥ buddhiḥ*). The suffix क्तिच् (*ktic*) in the sense of the agent. By अनुदात्तोपदेश (*anudāttopadeśa*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) loss of the n of the root. दुष्टा मतिः दुर्मतिः (*duṣṭā matiḥ durmatiḥ*) (an evil mind). Where the accent of the original form of the prior member would come after an indeclinable, by way of exception, by गतिकारकोपपदा (*gatikārakopapadā*) the accent of the original form of the latter member after a kṛt suffix comes.

स्थात् (*sthāt*)—the root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*). In the Vedic manner luñ in the sense of loṭ. In the third person singular, tip; loss of i. When the substitute sic comes for cli, by गातिस्थासिचा (*gātisthāsicā*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77) luk for it. In the Vedic manner the augment aṭ does not come. The nighāta accent of a tiṅanta word comes *(printed तजंतनिघातस्वर (*tajaṃtanighātasvara*), "taja-nta-nighāta", as supplied)*.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतो पितृभ्यामित्यस्मिन्वर्गे वाख्यातेयमृक् ॥ (48 ने पेजन्नु नोडि)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk has already been explained in the Varga referred to in the block above (the print adds "see page 48", with Latin digits, as supplied).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- पुरुदंसं (*purudaṃsaṃ*)—the one that is the means for many rites; गोः सनिं (*goḥ saniṃ*)—the one that procures cattle and the like, which इळां (*iḷāṃ*)—the divine being renowned as "Iḷā" (or the earth)
- शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)—continuously (so printed, "anusūtavāgi")
- हवमानाय (*havamānāya*)—to me who offers the oblation

- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)—a son
- तनयः (*tanayaḥ*)—and a grandson
- स्यात् (*syāt*)—may be obtained
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ते (*te*)—your
- सुमतिः (*sumatiḥ*)—(whatever) excellent favouring mind there is
- सा (*sā*)—that
- अस्मे (*asme*)—for our share
- विजावा (*vijāvā*)—(as one) that gives fruit
- भूतु (*bhūtu*)—may it be

### Printed p. 326

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, grant to me, who offer the oblation, that renowned divine being "Iḷā", the means of many rites and the procurer of cattle and the like, continuously. May a son and a grandson be obtained by us. O Agni, whatever excellent and favouring mind of yours there is, may it be, for our share, one that gives fruit without being in vain.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Grant AGNI, to the offerer of the oblation, earth the giver of cattle the means of many sacred rites, such that it may long endure : may there be to us sons and grandsons, and may your favour, AGNI, be productive of good unto us.

## Sūkta 16 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The sixteenth sūkta** (ಹದಿನಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತ)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमग्निरिति चतुर्थं षडृचं सूक्तमाग्नेयं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । आय-
> मग्निः षट् प्रगाथमिति । उत्तीलस्त्विति तुशब्दप्रयोगादस्यापि सूक्तस्य स एव ऋषिः ।
> अत्र विषमसंख्यानामृचां बृहती छंदस्तृतीयपादस्य द्वादशाक्षरत्वात् । सम-
> संख्यानां तु सतोबृहती प्रथमतृतीयपादयोर्द्वादशाक्षरत्वात् । उक्तं च ।
> अयुजौ जागतौ सतोबृहतीति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning अयमग्निः (*ayamagniḥ*) is the fourth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Agni is the deity of this sūkta. What is said in the Anukramaṇikā, आयमग्निः षट् प्रागाथमिति (*āyamagniḥ ṣaṭ prāgāthamiti*) *(so printed; the Sanskrit block has अयमग्निः (*ayamagniḥ*) and षट् प्रगाथमिति (*ṣaṭ pragāthamiti*))*, is said because the word tu is used in उत्कलस्त्वति (*utkalastvati*) *(so printed; the Sanskrit block has उत्तीलस्त्विति (*uttīlastviti*))*; so, as in the preceding sūkta, Utkala is the Ṛṣi of this sūkta too *(printed "Utkala"; the sūkta data on p. 327 gives उत्कीलः (*utkīlaḥ*); as supplied)*. In this sūkta, in the Ṛks of odd number, that is the 1st, 3rd and 5th Ṛks, because the third pāda has twelve syllables, they are of the Bṛhatī metre; and in the Ṛks of even number, that is the 2nd, 4th and 6th Ṛks, because the first and the third pādas have twelve syllables, they are of the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Chandonukramaṇikā it is said आयुजौ जागत् सतोबृहती (*āyujau jāgat satobṛhatī*) *(so printed; the Sanskrit block has अयुजौ जागतौ सतोबृहतीति (*ayujau jāgatau satobṛhatīti*))*.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यम॒ग्निः सु॒वीर्य॒स्येशे॑ म॒हः सौभ॑गस्य ।  
> रा॒य ई॑शे स्वप॒त्यस्य॒ गोम॑त॒ ईशे॑ वृत्र॒हथा॑नां ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । अग्निः । सुवीर्यस्य । ईशे । महः । सौभगस्य ।  
> रायः । ईशे । सुअपत्यस्य । गोमतः । ईशे । वृत्रहथानां ॥ १ ॥

> *ayaṃ | agniḥ | suvīryasya | īśe | mahaḥ | saubhagasya |*  
> *rāyaḥ | īśe | suapatyasya | gomataḥ | īśe | vṛtrahathānāṃ ‖ 1 ‖*

*[In the Pada the supplied text has सुअपत्यस्य (*suapatyasya*) for the Saṃhitā word स्वपत्यस्य (*svapatyasya*), as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत्कलः सौति । अयं यजनीयत्वेनांगुल्या निर्दिश्यमानोग्निः सुवीर्यस्य
> शोभनसामर्थ्योपेतस्य महो महतः सौभगस्य सौभाग्यस्येशे । ईष्टे । ईश्वरो
> भवति । सर्वस्य बलारोग्य हेतुतया सौभाग्यकारित्वात् । तथा गोमतो गवादिपशु-
> युक्तस्य स्वपत्यस्य शोभनापत्यस्य रायो धनस्येशे । ईष्टे । पुत्रपश्वाद्युद्देशेन
> क्रियमाणकर्मफलसंपादकत्वेन तत्स्वामित्वात् । तथैवंभूतोऽग्निर्वृत्रहथानां ।
> हननं हथः । शत्रुभूतपापविनाशनानामपीशे । ईष्टे । त्वयि समर्पितकर्मणाम-
> स्माकं त्वत्पसादात्पापक्षयो भवतीति तस्यापि स्वामी ॥ ईशे । ईश ऐश्वर्ये । अदादि-
> त्वाच्छपो लुक् । लोपस्य आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः । पादादित्पादनिघातः । सौभगस्य ।
> सुभगस्य भावः सौभगं । उद्गात्रादित्वादञ् । सर्वविधीनां छंदसि विकल्पितत्वादत्र
> हृद्भगेत्यादिना प्राप्ताया उत्तरपदवृद्धेरभावः । रायः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्ते-
> रुदात्तत्वं । ईशे । निघातः । स्वपत्यस्य । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं । वृत्र-
> हथानां । वृतु वर्तने । आस्मात् स्थायितंचिवंचीत्यादिना रक् प्रत्ययः । कित्वाद-
> गुणः । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्मात् हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्य इति कन् । कित्वादनुनासिक-
> लोपः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Utkala says: this Agni, pointed out here, is lord of excellent power, of great good fortune, of wealth with good offspring and cattle, and of the destruction of foes and sins.

*(Grammar tail inside the same block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words ईशे (*īśe*) (root ईश ऐश्वर्ये (*īśa aiśvarye*)), सौभगस्य (*saubhagasya*), रायः (*rāyaḥ*), स्वपत्यस्य (*svapatyasya*) and वृत्रहथानां (*vṛtrahathānāṃ*) (roots वृतु वर्तने (*vṛtu vartane*) and हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्मात् (*hana hiṃsāgatyorityasmāt*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं अग्निः (*ayaṃ agniḥ*)—this Agni who is on the sacrificial altar
- सुवीरस्य (*suvīrasya*)—of that which is endowed with excellent capacity *(printed सुवीरस्य (*suvīrasya*), whereas the later notes and the Saṃhitā have सुवीर्यस्य (*suvīryasya*); as supplied)*
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of the great
- सौभगस्य (*saubhagasya*)—of auspicious wealth

- स्वपत्यस्य (*svapatyasya*)—of that which is endowed with the wealth of excellent sons
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Agni, who is on the sacrificial altar, is the lord of wealth that is endowed with excellent capacity, great and auspicious. He is also the master of wealth that has cattle and the like and is endowed with the wealth of excellent sons. He is also capable of the destruction of sins that are of the nature of enemies. [Or: he is the lord also of the destroyers of sin.] *(The bracketed alternative is in the print.)*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This AGNI, is the lord of heroism and of great good fortune; he is the lord of wealth comprising progeny and cattle; he is the lord of the slayers of VRITRA. (enemy)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सुवीर्यस्य महः सौभगस्य ईशे (*suvīryasya mahaḥ saubhagasya īśe*)—सर्वस्य बलारोग्यहेतुतया सौभाग्यकारित्वात् शोभनसामर्थ्यपेतस्य महतः सौभाग्यस्य ईश्वरो भवति (*sarvasya balārogyahetutayā saubhāgyakāritvāt śobhanasāmarthyapetasya mahataḥ saubhāgyasya īśvaro bhavati*). Because Agni has the power to make the whole world possessed of strength and health, he is described as the lord who grants excellent strength and health, or as one of such power.

गोमतः स्वपत्यस्य रायः ईशे (*gomataḥ svapatyasya rāyaḥ īśe*). By this sentence the meaning is explained that Agni fulfils the wishes of those who perform rites with this or that desire, and so is lord (पुत्रपश्वाद्युद्देशेन क्रियमाणकर्मफलसंपादकत्वेन (*putrapaśvādyuddeśena kriyamāṇakarmaphalasaṃpādakatvena*)) in fulfilling the wishes of those who perform sacrificial rites with the purpose of obtaining sons, cattle and wealth.

वृत्तहथानां ईशे (*vṛttahathānāṃ īśe*) *(printed with ತ್ತ in the first word, whereas the Pratipadārtha has ರ; as supplied)*—शत्रुभूतपापविनाशनानामपि ईशे । त्वयि समर्पितकर्मणामस्माकं त्वत्पसादात् तस्यापि स्वामी (*śatrubhūtapāpavināśanānāmapi īśe | tvayi samarpitakarmaṇāmasmākaṃ tvatpasādāt tasyāpi svāmī*). The writers of the Nirukta have explained the word Vṛtra, from the standpoint of the real nature of things, as the cloud that obstructs the waters that bring good and happiness to the world, and, from the historical standpoint, as an Asura who was a thorn to the world. Sāyaṇa, taking the secondary (lākṣaṇika) meaning "that which acts as an obstruction to the happiness of living beings in the world", has explained it as sin

*(The passage continues on p. 329.)*

### Printed p. 329

(continued) and, because this sin does harm like an enemy, has explained that Agni is able to destroy this sin that is of the nature of an enemy. Thereby it is said that Agni is a lord who gives fruit to those who serve him in this or that manner: first, in general, the producer of strength and health; then the giver of fruit corresponding to the desire-prompted rites performed by those who have this or that desire; and, for those who perform rites without desire and offer them up, the remover of the sins that lead to a bad end, and the one who, according to the saying ज्ञानमुत्पद्यते पुंसां क्षयात् पापस्य कर्मणः (*jñānamutpadyate puṃsāṃ kṣayāt pāpasya karmaṇaḥ*) (knowledge arises in men from the destruction of sinful action), makes them fit to enter upon the path of knowledge.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

सुवीर्यस्य (*suvīryasya*)—शोभनं वीर्यं यस्य (*śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasya*) (he whose valour is excellent). As an exception to the accent of the prefix su, by आद्युदात्तंद्व्यच्छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃdvyacchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119) the initial-acute accent on the latter member comes. A form of the genitive singular.

ईशे (*īśe*)—the root ईश ऐश्वर्ये (*īśa aiśvarye*), of the adādi class. The suffix ta in the third person singular of laṭ. By टितआत्मनेपदानां (*ṭitaātmanepadānāṃ*) *(the print has a hyphen and line break between the two words, so the span is joined here; as supplied)* e for ṭi. By अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (*adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*) luk for śap. By लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु (*lopasta ātmanepadeṣu*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-41) loss of the t of the suffix. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. By तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186), because the suffix coming after a root marked anudātta-it becomes unaccented, the accent of the root remains.

महः (*mahaḥ*)—by सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-18) the udātta accent comes on the case ending.

सौभगस्य (*saubhagasya*)—सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*) 'bhāvaḥ saubhagam' (the state of one who is fortunate). Because it is read in the उद्धात्रादिगण (*uddhātrādigaṇa*) , the suffix añ. Since all operations are optional in the Chandas, by हृद्भगसिंध्वंते पूर्वपदस्यच (*hṛdbhagasiṃdhvaṃte pūrvapadasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-19) *(the print breaks the reference over two lines)*, although vṛddhi is prescribed for both members, vṛddhi does not come at the beginning of the latter member. Since the suffix has the sign it, the initial-acute accent comes.

रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—by ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the udātta accent comes on the genitive case ending.

ईशे (*īśe*)—the process has been explained earlier. Since it follows an atiṅanta , the nighāta accent comes.

स्वपत्यस्य (*svapatyasya*)—शोभनं आपत्यं यस्य सः (*śobhanaṃ āpatyaṃ yasya saḥ*) (he who has excellent offspring). By तस्य नञ्सुभ्याम् (*tasya nañsubhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the final-acute accent on the latter member comes.

वृत्रहथानाम् (*vṛtrahathānām*)—the root वृतु वर्तने (*vṛtu vartane*). By स्थायितंचिवंचि (*sthāyitaṃcivaṃci*) (U. Sū. 2-170) *(printed as U. Sū.)* the suffix rak for it. Since the suffix has the sign k, guṇa of the short penultimate of the root does not come. The form वृत्र (*vṛtra*) results. The root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*): by हनिकुषिनीरनमिकाशिभ्यः (*hanikuṣinīranamikāśibhyaḥ*) (U. Sū. 2-159) the suffix kdhan ; since it has the sign k, by अनुदात्तोपदेशवनति (*anudāttopadeśavanati*) (Pā. Sū. 6-437) *(so printed, without a second hyphen)* the n of the root is lost. The form हथ (*hatha*) results. Because the prior member is a kāraka, by गतिकारकोप (*gatikārakopa*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the original form of the latter member after a kṛt suffix comes. Since हथ (*hatha*) ends in a suffix marked n, it has the initial-acute accent.

> इ॒मं न॑रो मरुतः सश्चता॒ वृधं॒ यस्मि॒न्रायः॒ शेवृ॑धासः ।

> अभि । ये । संति । पृतनासु । दुःध्यः । विश्वाहा । शत्रुं । आदभुः ॥ २ ॥

> *imaṃ | naraḥ | marutaḥ | saścata | vṛdhaṃ | yasmin | rāyaḥ | śe 'vṛdhāsaḥ |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नरः कर्मणां नेतारो हे मरुतो देवा यूयं वृधं पशुपुत्रादि-
> वर्धकमिममस्माभिः स्तूयमानमिममग्निं सश्चत । हविरानयनार्थं सेवध्वं ।
> कीदृशोऽग्निरित्याकांक्षायामाह । यस्मिन्देवे रायो धनानि शेवृधासो दानभो-
> गाद्युपयोगेन सुखस्य वर्धकानि संति । ये च देवाः पृतनासु सेनासु तदुपलक्ष्मि-
> तेषु संग्रामेषु दूढ्यो दुष्टध्यानोपेतानात्मनो हिंसकाञ्छत्रुनभिसंति । अभि-
> भवंति । ये च विश्वाहा विश्वान्यहानि यस्मिन्नखंडे काले तस्मिन्सर्वदा शत्रुमात्मनो
> द्वेष्टारमादभुः । आदभ्नुवंति । हिंसंति । एवंभूतास्ते सर्वे मरुतो यूयं
> तमिममग्निं सेवध्वमिति पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥ सश्चत । षस्थ संग इत्यस्माल्लोट रूपं।
> जकारस्य व्यत्ययेन चकारः । निघातः । शेवृधासः । वर्णव्यत्ययः । शं सुखं वर्धय-
> तीति । असुन्नित्यसुन् । गुणाभावश्चांदसः । गतिकारकयोरपि पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं
> चेत्यौणादिकसूत्रात् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । संति । अस भुवि । दूढ्यः । धै
> चिंतायां । अन्वेभ्योऽपि दृश्यत इति क्विप् । दृशिग्रहणात्संप्रसारणं । दुरो दाश-
> नाशदभध्येषूत्वं वक्तव्यमुत्तरपदादेश्च ष्टुत्वमिति ऊत्वटत्वे । छंदस्युभयथेति
> तसीयजादेशं बाधित्वा यणादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेणांतोदात्तः । शसः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, leaders of rites, serve this Agni, who is increased by us with praise and who makes cattle and sons grow, to bring the oblation; in him wealth that increases happiness abides, and he is such as overcomes the enemies who attack in battles and always harm.

*(Grammar tail inside the same block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words सश्चत (*saścata*) (root षस्थ संग (*ṣastha saṃga*)), शेवृधासः (*śevṛdhāsaḥ*), संति (*saṃti*) (root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*)) and दूढ्यः (*dūḍhyaḥ*) (root धै (*dhai*) चिंतायां (*ciṃtāyāṃ*)); the block breaks off with the word शसः (*śasaḥ*) at the end of p. 330 and continues on the next page.

> *suptvādanudāttatve kṛte udāttasvaritayoryaṇa iti śasaḥ svaritatvaṃ | ādabhuḥ | danbha*

> *nunāsikalopaḥ | dvirvacanaprakaraṇe chaṃdasi veti vaktavyamiti dvirvacanābhāvaḥ | yadvṛ-*
> *ttayogādanighātaḥ | sati śiṣṭasvaro balīyāniti pratyayasvaraḥ ‖*

*(Grammar tail of the block, noted briefly.)* The block says that, after the accent of the case ending has become anudātta, the accent of the ending of the accusative plural becomes svarita by the rule उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇa*); and treats the word आदभुः (*ādabhuḥ*) (root दन्भ दंभे (*danbha daṃbhe*): its perfect form with the ending uṣ; the nasal is lost because the ending is treated as marked k; no doubling; no nighāta accent because of the relation to यद् (*yad*)-; the accent of the suffix prevails).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—who
- पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)—in battles
- दूढ्यः (*dūḍhyaḥ*)—the wicked enemies; अभि संति (*abhi saṃti*)—defeat, (and)
- विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*)—at all times
- शत्रुं (*śatruṃ*)—their enemy
- आदभुः (*ādabhuḥ*)—who harm and destroy, such persons too, and नरः (*naraḥ*)—who are leaders
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Marut gods, (you)
- वृधं (*vṛdhaṃ*)—him who makes cattle, sons and the like increase, and
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which (Agni) god
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—riches
- शेवृधासः (*śevṛdhāsaḥ*)—are happiness-increasing, such
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this god Agni
- सश्चत (*saścata*)—join and serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, you are leaders of all of us, you defeat the wicked enemies in battles, and you destroy at all times the wicked who show hatred. You who have such excellent power, join this god Agni, who makes cattle, sons and the like increase and who holds riches that increase happiness, and serve him.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Maruts, leaders (of rites), associate with this augmenter (of our prosperity), in whom (abide) riches contributing to felicity, you who (are victorious) over (your) enemies in battle, who daily humble (your) foes.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नरः मरुतः वृधं इमं सश्चत (*naraḥ marutaḥ vṛdhaṃ imaṃ saścata*)—कर्मणां नेतारो देवाः यूयं पशुपुत्रादिवर्धकं अस्माभिः स्तूयमानमिममग्निं हविरानयनार्थं सेवध्वं (*karmaṇāṃ netāro devāḥ yūyaṃ paśuputrādivardhakaṃ asmābhiḥ stūyamānamimamagniṃ havirānayanārthaṃ sevadhvaṃ*). The gods are addressed as helpers in performing sacrifices and other rites. And because Agni, who makes cattle, sons and the like increase and who is praised by those who sacrifice, carries to the gods the shares of the oblation offered for them, the wish is expressed that the gods too should serve Agni.

शेवृधासः रायः (*śevṛdhāsaḥ rāyaḥ*)—दानभोगाद्युपयोगेन सुखस्य वर्धकानि धनानि (*dānabhogādyupayogena sukhasya vardhakāni dhanāni*). By the manner of giving and enjoying, Agni is said to possess in abundance the riches that increase happiness; thereby his abundant power is indicated.

### Printed p. 332

*(The Special Topics of Ṛk 2 continue on this page.)*

पैतनासु दूढ्यः (*paitanāsu dūḍhyaḥ*) *(printed ಪೈತನಾಸು, whereas the Saṃhitā and Pratipadārtha have ಪೃತನಾಸು; as supplied)*—सेनासु तदुपलक्षितेषु संग्रामेषु दुष्टध्यानोपेता आत्मनो हिंसर्का शत्रुन् अभिसंति अभिभवंति (*senāsu tadupalakṣiteṣu saṃgrāmeṣu duṣṭadhyānopetā ātmano hiṃsarkā śatrun abhisaṃti abhibhavaṃti*) *(the printed word हिंसर्का (*hiṃsarkā*) is as supplied)*. The word पृतना (*pṛtanā*) is read among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Here it is used both in the meaning of army and in the meaning of battle (war).

इंद्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतं । दीर्घप्रयज्युमति यो वनुष्यति वयं जयेम पृतनासु दूड्यः ॥ (*iṃdrāvaruṇā yuvamadhvarāya no viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchataṃ | dīrghaprayajyumati yo vanuṣyati vayaṃ jayema pṛtanāsu dūḍyaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-82-1)

Here the meaning of the word दूढि (*dūḍhi*) is also given: दूढ्यं पापधियं (*dūḍhyaṃ pāpadhiyaṃ*) (Ni. 5-2), "one of evil mind". Those who are in armies, or in the battles, which are situations in which armies are present, plan to do harm to others, and so are called violent and enemies. It is described that the gods destroy these also.

विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*)—विश्वानि अहानि यस्मिन् अखंडे काले तस्मिन् सर्वदा (*viśvāni ahāni yasmin akhaṃḍe kāle tasmin sarvadā*). The undivided time that includes all days (अहस्सु (*ahassu*)-) is meant by the word विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*); so the meaning is explained that the gods destroy at every time the enemies who hate them. Then, एवंभूतास्सर्वे मरुतः अग्निं सेवध्वं (*evaṃbhūtāssarve marutaḥ agniṃ sevadhvaṃ*): all the gods of this kind should serve Agni. By addressing the gods and making their greatness clear, the abundant power of Agni, whom even they must serve, is described.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

सश्चत (*saścata*)—the root षस्थ संगे (*ṣastha saṃge*). By धात्वादेःषःसः (*dhātvādeḥṣaḥsaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) sa for the initial. Because the second person plural of loṭ is treated as laṅ, by तस्थस्थमिपां (*tasthasthamipāṃ*) the substitute ta. For the ja of the root ca by vyatyaya . By स्तोःशु नाश्चुः (*stoḥśu nāścuḥ*) (as supplied, with a space) śa for sa. By तिज्जतिजः (*tijjatijaḥ*) the nighāta accent comes.

वृधम् (*vṛdham*)—the root वृधु वर्धने (*vṛdhu vardhane*). By क्विप्‌च (*kvipca*) the suffix kvip. A form of the accusative singular *(the print has "ದ್ವಿತೀಯಾವಿಕವಚನಾಂತರೂಪ", as supplied)*.

शेवृधासः (*śevṛdhāsaḥ*)—श सुखं वर्धयति इति शेवृधाः (*śa sukhaṃ vardhayati iti śevṛdhāḥ*) (that which increases happiness). The root वृधु वर्धने (*vṛdhu vardhane*). The Uṇādi suffix asun. In the Chandas guṇa of the short penultimate does not come. By vyatyaya the change of श (*śa*) to शे (*śe*) comes. By गतिकारकयोरपि पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वंच (*gatikārakayorapi pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃca*) (U. Sū. 4-666) the accent of the original form of the prior member comes *(printed "ಪೂರ್ನಪದ", as supplied)*. A form of the nominative plural.

संति (*saṃti*)—the root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*). A form of the third person plural of laṭ. Because of the relation with the word यच्छब्द (*yacchabda*) (the word yat) the nighāta accent does not come; the initial-acute accent of the suffix comes.

दूढ्यः (*dūḍhyaḥ*)—the root धैृ चिंतायां (*dhaiṛ ciṃtāyāṃ*) . By अन्येभ्योपिदृत्यते (*anyebhyopidṛtyate*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-178) the suffix kvip.

### Printed p. 333

*(The Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Ṛk 2 continues; the sentence on दूढ्यः (*dūḍhyaḥ*) begun on p. 332 breaks inside the word ಎಂಬುದರಿಂದ across the page and is written above as one passage.)*

On account of the power of the grasping of seeing (दृष्टिग्रहणसामर्थ्यदिंद (*dṛṣṭigrahaṇasāmarthyadiṃda*), as supplied) samprasāraṇa: the y of the root becomes i, with the prior form. When it stands after the prefix dur, by the saying दुरो दाशनाश द भध्येषूत्वं वक्तव्यमुत्तरपदादेः ष्टुत्वांच (*duro dāśanāśa da bhadhyeṣūtvaṃ vaktavyamuttarapadādeḥ ṣṭutvāṃca*) the change to u; the d is changed to dh. The form दूढि (*dūḍhi*) results. When śas follows it, by छंदस्युभयथा (*chaṃdasyubhayathā*) the substitute iyañ is set aside and the substitute yaṇ comes. By कृमत्तरदप्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛmattaradaprakṛtisvara*) it becomes final-acute.

विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*)—by शेश्छंदसि बहुलम् (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulam*) luk for śi in the neuter plural.

आदभुः (*ādabhuḥ*)—the root दंभु दंभने (*daṃbhu daṃbhane*). In the third person plural of liṭ the substitute us. By the vārttika श्रंथिग्रंथिदंभि स्वंजीनामुपसंख्यानम् (*śraṃthigraṃthidaṃbhi svaṃjīnāmupasaṃkhyānam*) the suffix comes to be marked k even though a conjunct precedes. By अनिदितांहलउपधा (*aniditāṃhalaupadhā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24) the n of the root is lost. By the saying द्विर्वचन प्रकरणे छंदसि वेति वक्तव्यम् (*dvirvacana prakaraṇe chaṃdasi veti vaktavyam*) (Kā. 6-1-8) there is no doubling on account of liṭ *(the print has "ಲಿಣ್ಣೆಮಿತ್ತವಾಗಿ", as supplied)*. By यव्वृत्तान्वित्यम् (*yavvṛttānvityam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) the prohibition of the nighāta accent comes. By the saying सतिशिष्टःस्वरो बलीयान् (*satiśiṣṭaḥsvaro balīyān*) the accent of the suffix remains. Since it is a tiṅanta with udātta, by तिजुचोदात्तवति (*tijucodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) *(printed "ತಿಜಂತಸರವಾದುದರಿಂದ" and "ತಿಜುಚೋ…", as supplied)* the anudātta accent comes on the gati (आज् (*āj*)).
