##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने स तथाविधस्त्वं नोऽस्मान्रायः । तृतीयार्थे षष्ठि । धनेन शिशीहि।
> तीक्ष्णान्कुरु । आस्मान्फनसमृद्धान्कुरु । किंच तुविद्युम्न बहुधनोपेत अत एव
> मीढ्वो मीढ्वन् कामानां सेक्तः हे अग्ने त्वं वर्षिष्ठस्य वृद्धतमस्य प्रभूतस्य
> प्रजावतोऽपत्ययुक्तस्यानमीवस्यारोग्यहेतोरत एव शुष्मिणो बलहेतोः
> सुवीर्यस्य शोभनसामान्ययुक्तस्यान्नस्य संबंधिनोऽस्मान्कुरु । यद्वा । एतत्सर्व०
> विशेषणतया योजनीयं । एताः षष्ठ्यस्तृतीयार्थे । एतदुक्तं भवति । धनेना-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, such as you are, make us rich with wealth (the genitive रायः (*rāyaḥ*) is in the sense of the instrumental); O giver of many riches and showerer of desires, make us sharp, endowed with excellent strength-giving food, offspring and freedom from disease; the construction is then explained.

### Printed p. 334

*(The Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya block of Ṛk 3 continues from p. 333, beginning with the end of the word धनेना- (*dhanenā-*), which is cut at the page break; nothing is repeated.)*

> पत्यारोग्यशरीरबलोपेतेनान्नेनास्मान्समृद्धान्कुर्विति ॥ शिशीहि । शिञ् निशान इत्यस्य
> लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः । वा छंदसीति विकल्पेन जित्वादजातश्चेति
> हेर्धिरादेशो न भवति । दीर्घश्चांदसः । निघातः । मीध्वः । मिह सेचन इत्यस्य क्वसौ
> दाश्वान् साह्वान् मीढ्वांश्चेति निपातनात् धत्वं उपधादीर्घश्च । संबुद्धौ नुमि
> कृते हल् ज्यादिलोपे संयोगांतलोपे च कृते मतुवसो रुः संबुद्धौ छंद-
> सीति रुः । पादादित्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sense is: make us prosperous with wealth, and with food endowed with offspring, health and bodily strength.

*(Grammar tail of the block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words शिशीहि (*śiśīhi*) (root शिञ् निशान (*śiñ niśāna*), as supplied: the loṭ form, with the substitute for the suffix, the luk-like elision of the vikaraṇa and the optional non-substitution of dhi; the long vowel is Vedic; the nighāta accent) and मीध्वः (*mīdhvaḥ*) (root मिह सेचन (*miha secana*); the suffix kvasu; the form is fixed by rule, so that dh and the lengthening of the penultimate come; in the vocative the nu-augment, the loss of the case ending and of the final conjunct consonant, and ru for the final of the matup-type word); the first word of the pāda has the initial-acute accent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*)—endowed with abundant wealth
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- सः (*saḥ*)—he who has the qualities described above
- माड्वः (*māḍvaḥ*) *(so printed, whereas the Saṃhitā has ಮೀಢ್ವಃ; as supplied)*—and the showerer of desired objects
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सुवीरस्य (*suvīrasya*) *(so printed, whereas the Saṃhitā has ಸುವೀರ್ಯಸ್ಯ; as supplied)*—endowed with excellent vigour
- वर्षिष्ठस्य (*varṣiṣṭhasya*)—most abundant
- प्रजावतः (*prajāvataḥ*)—endowed with the wealth of sons, grandsons and the like
- अनमीवस्य (*anamīvasya*)—the cause of health
- शुष्मिणः (*śuṣmiṇaḥ*)—the producer of strength
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—with wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- शिशीहि (*śiśīhi*)—make prosperous

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, endowed with abundant wealth, you who are full of the good qualities described above and who shower desired objects, make us prosperous with wealth that is endowed with excellent vigour, most abundant, endowed with the wealth of sons, grandsons and the like, the cause of health and the producer of strength.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Opulent AGNI, showerer (of benefits), prosper us with riches comprising vigour, numerous progeny, health, and happiness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

By the sentence अस्मान् रायः शिशीहि (*asmān rāyaḥ śiśīhi*) the wish is expressed that Agni may make us wealthy. Addressing Agni by the word तुविद्युन्नु (*tuvidyunnu*) *(so printed, with a stray apostrophe after it; the Saṃhitā has ತುವಿದ್ಯುಮ್ನ)* the prayer is made that Agni is one who has abundant wealth and that Agni may make us very capable.

For the words वर्षिष्ठस्य प्रजावतः अनमीवस्य शुष्मिणः सुवीर्यस्य (*varṣiṣṭhasya prajāvataḥ anamīvasya śuṣmiṇaḥ suvīryasya*), which are in the genitive case, one kind of meaning is explained: may food that increases exceedingly, that is the cause of the birth of sons and grandsons, and that produces strength and health, come to us through the favour of Agni.

यद्वा एतत्सर्वं विशेषणतया योजनीयं धनेन अपत्यारोग्यशरीरबलोपेतेन अन्नेन च अर्स्मान् समृद्धान् कुरु (*yadvā etatsarvaṃ viśeṣaṇatayā yojanīyaṃ dhanena apatyārogyaśarīrabalopetena annena ca arsmān samṛddhān kuru*) *(so printed, with ಅರ್ಸ್ಮಾನ್)*. All these words are applied as qualifiers to the word रै (*rai*) which means wealth. The second meaning is stated and the prayer is made: may Agni favour us so that we are prosperous in wealth, either as persons endowed with food that is the cause of sons, of health, and of bodily strength and ability, or through the grant of abundant food.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

शिशीहि (*śiśīhi*)—the root शिञ् निशाने (*śiñ niśāne*) *(so printed, with ನಿಶಾನೇ; the bhāṣya has ನಿಶಾನ)*. When sip comes in the middle person singular of loṭ, the substitute hi for it. By बहुलंछंदसि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasi*) the substitute ślu for the vikaraṇa. By श्लु (*ślu*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-10) doubling of the root; by वाछंदसि (*vāchaṃdasi*) the marking of hi as ji is made optional, so it does not come here. By अजितश्च (*ajitaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-103) the change of hi to dhi does not come. The long vowel comes for the i of the Vedic root.

मीढ्वः (*mīḍhvaḥ*)—the root मिह सेचने (*miha secane*). When liṭ comes to it, the substitute kvasu for it. When this follows, since it is fixed as an irregular form by दाश्वान् साह्वान्‌मीढ्वांश्च (*dāśvān sāhvānmīḍhvāṃśca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-12), ḍha for the ha of the root, and the lengthening of the penultimate come. The word मीढ्वस् (*mīḍhvas*). In the vocative, when su follows, since it is marked ug, the nu-augment. By हल्‌ज्याभ्यो दीर्घात् (*haljyābhyo dīrghāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-78) loss of the case ending su that stands after the consonant ending. By संयोगांतस्य लोपः (*saṃyogāṃtasya lopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-223) loss of the sa after na. By मतुवसोरुः संबुद्धौ (*matuvasoruḥ saṃbuddhau*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-1) ru for the na. Visarga. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, by आमंत्रितस्य (*āmaṃtritasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) the initial-acute accent comes. In the vocative तुविद्युन्नु (*tuvidyunnu*) also the initial-acute accent comes, because it likewise stands at the beginning of a pāda.

अनमीावस्य (*anamīāvasya*) *(so printed, with a stray ಾ)*—by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the final-acute accent of the latter member comes.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽयमग्निश्चक्रिः सर्वस्य जगतः कर्ता स च विश्वा भुवना विश्वानि भवनान्यभि
> अभिविशति । तत्सृष्टा तदेवानुप्राविशदिति श्रुतेः । चक्रिः कर्ता सोऽग्निः सासहिः
> पुरोडाशादिहविर्भारसहनशीलः सन् दुवोऽस्माभिर्दत्तं हनिर्देवेषु यजनीय-
> देवेष्णा । आनयति । स चाग्निर्देवेषु देवनशीलेषु स्तोतृष्टा यतते । अभिमु-
> ख्येन गच्छति । यद्वा विश्वानि भुवनानि चक्रिरभिसासहिरभिभवनशीलः । आकारश्चार्थे ।
> देवेषु च दुवः परिचरणं चक्रिः कर्ता । य एवंभूतः स आयतत इत्यादि पूर्व-
> वत् । उत अपि च नृणां यज्ञस्य नेत्यणां शस्त्रिणां शंसे । शंसनं शंसः शस्त्रं ।
> तस्मिन् सोऽग्निरागच्छति । तथा नृणां मनुष्याणां सुवीर्ये शोभनवीर्योपेत-
> युद्धे तद्रक्षणार्थमागच्छति । अनेनाग्नेः सर्वव्यापकता प्रतिपादिता भवति ॥ चक्रिः ।
> डुकृञ्करणे । आदृगमहनजनः किकिनौ लिट् चेति किन्‌प्रत्ययः । लिद्वद्भावाद्विर्व-
> चनं । कित्त्वाद्दुणाभावः । नित् स्वरः । सासहिः । षह मर्षण इत्यस्माद्यजंतात्सहिवहि
> चलिपतिभ्यो यजंतेभ्यः किकिनौ । पा ३-२-१७१-४ । इति किः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । यतते ।
> यती प्रयत्ने । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । शंसे । भावे घञ् । इत्त्वरः । नृणां
> नृ चेति विकल्पेन दीर्घाभावः । नामन्यतरस्यामिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । विश्वेत्यादिषु
> न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठिप्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the maker of all the world, enters all beings; as the maker who bears the burdens of the oblation he brings our offering to the gods, goes to the devout worshippers, comes to help in the glorious battle and to the recitations of the men. (Alternatively: he overcomes all beings and performs service among the gods.) This shows that Agni pervades everything.

*(Grammar tail of the block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words चक्रिः (*cakriḥ*) (root डुकृञ्करणे (*ḍukṛñkaraṇe*); the suffix kin; doubling as in liṭ; no guṇa because of the kit-marking; a nit-accent), सासहिः (*sāsahiḥ*) (root षह मर्षण (*ṣaha marṣaṇa*); the suffix ki by the rule cited with the reference पा ३-२-१७१-४ (*pā 3-2-171-4*); accent of the suffix), यतते (*yatate*) (root यती प्रयत्ने (*yatī prayatne*); no nighāta because of the relation to the relative), शंसे (*śaṃse*) (the suffix ghañ in the sense of the action; the accent on the i-vowel), नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*) (the optional absence of lengthening; the acute on the case ending) and the compound-words विश्व (*viśva*)-: the prohibition of the genitive-accent rule is stated.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- चक्रिः (*cakriḥ*)—being the maker of the world; विश्वा भुवनानि (*viśvā bhuvanāni*)—all the world
- अभि (*abhi*)—pervades and enters
- चक्रिः (*cakriḥ*)—Agni, the creator
- सासहिः (*sāsahiḥ*)—as one with the power to bear the purodāśa and the like
- दुवः (*duvaḥ*)—the oblation (offered by us)
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—to the gods
- आ(नयंति) (*ā(nayaṃti)*)—takes and joins
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the worshippers of the gods, the reciters of praise; आ यतते (*ā yatate*)—goes to meet and joins
- सुवीर्यॆ (*suvīryè*) *(so printed, with ಯೆ)*—in the battle that shows excellent valour
- आ (*ā*)—comes (to help)
- उत (*uta*)—and
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—of the men who perform the sacrifice
- शंसे (*śaṃse*)—at the times of recitation
- आ(गच्छति) (*ā(gacchati)*)—comes and joins

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the maker of the world, pervades and enters the whole world. And, having the power to bear the purodāśa and the like, he takes the oblation offered by us to the gods and joins it to them. And he goes to meet the reciters of praise who are worshippers of the gods and joins them. He comes to help in the battle that shows excellent heroism *(printed ವೀರವನ್ನು, as supplied)*. And he comes at the times of recitation of the men who perform sacrifices and, joining them, accepts their praises.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
He who is the maker pervades all worlds ; he the enduring maker (of all) bears our offerings to the gods : he is present with the devout (worshippers) and amidst the heroism and the devotions of men.

### Printed p. 337

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*(The Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued from the Printed English translation on p. 336.)*

On the words चक्रिः विश्वा भुवना अभि—सर्वस्य जगतः कर्ता विश्वानि भुवनानि अभिविशति (*cakriḥ viśvā bhuvanā abhi—sarvasya jagataḥ kartā viśvāni bhuvanāni abhiviśati*) the meaning is explained as follows: Agni, having made (created) the whole world, entered the world he had created by a transformation of himself; and, concerning the entering of the world, the sentence of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad तत्स्वष्टा । तदेवानु प्राविशत् (*tatsvaṣṭā | tadevānu prāviśat*) (Te. U. 2-6) is quoted.

On चक्रिः सासहिः-पुरोडाशादिहविर्भारवहनशीलः (*cakriḥ sāsahiḥ-puroḍāśādihavirbhāravahanaśīlaḥ*) the meaning is described thus: Agni, who is the maker of the world, is the one who carries to the gods abundant oblations such as the purodāśa.

On देवेषु आयतते—देवनशीलेषु स्तोतृषु अभिमुख्येन गच्छति (*deveṣu āyatate—devanaśīleṣu stotṛṣu abhimukhyena gacchati*): Agni makes his own form visible to the priests who shine with lustre and who recite praise; thus the gracious, compassionate disposition of Agni towards the priests is stated here.

In the second meaning, विश्वा चक्रिः देवेषु दुवः चक्रिः देवेषु आयतते (*viśvā cakriḥ deveṣu duvaḥ cakriḥ deveṣu āyatate*): it is also explained that Agni, the maker of the world, who does service to the gods and who is of a nature to conquer enemies, is visibly present to the gods. And for the word देवेषु (*deveṣu*) two kinds of meaning are given: यजनीयदेवेषु, देवनशीलेषु स्तोतृषु (*yajanīyadeveṣu, devanaśīleṣu stotṛṣu*), namely those who are fit for sacrifice, and those who shine with lustre and recite praise.

On नृणां शंसे—यज्ञस्य नेतृणां शस्त्रिणां शंसे । शंसनं शंसः शस्त्रं (*nṛṇāṃ śaṃse—yajñasya netṛṇāṃ śastriṇāṃ śaṃse | śaṃsanaṃ śaṃsaḥ śastraṃ*): the meaning of the word नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*) is explained as the leaders (netṛ), those who provide the facilities for performing the sacrifice in the prescribed order; it is said that Agni, hearing the praises these recite, comes to the sacrifice. The word नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*) is also explained as मनुष्याणां (*manuṣyāṇāṃ*), "of men"; the word सुवीर्यॆ (*suvīryè*) *(so printed, with ಯೆ)* is taken, by सुवीर्यॆ शोभनवीर्योपेतयुद्धे (*suvīryè śobhanavīryopetayuddhe*), to denote a battle full of very powerful persons; and Agni is described as coming to the situations in which men fight. Then, by अनेनाग्नेः सर्वव्यापकता प्रतिपादिता भवति (*anenāgneḥ sarvavyāpakatā pratipāditā bhavati*): from this, that is, from Agni's majesty being described here, in that, as maker of the world, he enters the world; serves the gods who are fit for sacrifice; is visibly present to the priests who praise him; is near other worshippers at the times when they recite his praise; and is near also at the situations in which heroes fight *(the printed text has ನನ್ನಿಹಿತ, as supplied)*, it is said that Agni is all-pervading.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

चक्रिः (*cakriḥ*)—the root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*). By आद्यगमहनजनःकिकिनौ लिट् च (*ādyagamahanajanaḥkikinau liṭ ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-171) the suffix kin comes to it. Since this suffix is treated as liṭ, the root is doubled; (the sentence breaks off with the first part of the word for "doubling" at the end of the page and continues on p. 338; the break is inside a word).

*[Stray line on p. 337 after the last line of text: "43", kept as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 338

*(The grammar of Ṛk 4 continues from p. 337; the sentence begun at the end of p. 337 continues with the word beginning the first line below.)*

For the reduplicating syllable the substitute ca; since the suffix is marked k, the guṇa of the i of the root does not come, by सार्वधातुकार्थ (*sārvadhātukārtha*) *(so printed; the reference is given as "Pā. Sū. 1-7-3-84", as supplied, with four numbers)*; the substitute ya (yaṇ) comes. The form चक्रि (*cakri*) results. Since the suffix is marked n, the initial-acute accent comes.

विश्वा (*viśvā*), भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—in the neuter plural, by शेश्छंदसिबहुलम् (*śeśchaṃdasibahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70) the loss of śi.

सासहिः (*sāsahiḥ*)—the root षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*). When yaj comes after it, by सहि वहि चलि पृभ्यो यजंतेभ्यः किकिनौ (*sahi vahi cali pṛbhyo yajaṃtebhyaḥ kikinau*) (Pā. Ma. 3-2-171-4) *(so printed, "Pā. Ma.")* the suffix ki. By यस्यहलः (*yasyahalaḥ*) the loss of the ya of the yaj, and by अतोलोपः (*atolopaḥ*) the loss of the a. Lengthening of the reduplicating syllable. By the accent of the suffix the word becomes final-acute.

यतते (*yatate*)—the root यती प्रयत्ने (*yatī prayatne*); the form is third person singular of laṭ. Since there is relation to the word ya, the prohibition of nighāta comes by यद्वृत्तानित्यम् (*yadvṛttānityam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66). By the rule तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) the root is marked with an anudātta it, so the following lasārvadhātuka ending is anudātta, and the accent of the root remains.

शंसे (*śaṃse*)—the root शंसु स्तुतौ (*śaṃsu stutau*). In the sense of the action the suffix ghañ. By इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) the initial-acute accent comes. The form is in the locative singular.

नृणाम् (*nṛṇām*)—the word नृ (*nṛ*). When the genitive plural follows, since the lengthening is optional by नृच (*nṛca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-6), the long vowel does not come here. By नामन्यतरस्याम् (*nāmanyatarasyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-177) the acute accent comes to the case ending.

#### Ṛk 5

*[The Ṛk number 5 stands only at the end of the Saṃhitā; the print has no separate Ṛk heading.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, son of strength, do not make us subject to poverty that acts as an enemy, to childlessness, to lack of cattle and the like, or to reproach; and drive away the hatreds that arise from offences.

*(Grammar tail of the block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words अवीरताय्कॆ (*avīratāykè*) (formed with the suffix ac by the rule for arśas-class words and the suffix tal; the accent of the first member after the negative), रीरधः (*rīradhaḥ*) (root राध साध संसिद्दौ (*rādha sādha saṃsiddau*), as supplied: the causative with the aorist, the substitute for the cli, loss of the causative suffix, shortening of the penultimate, doubling, the sound of the desiderative, lengthening, no augment because of the particle mā, the nighāta accent), अगोताय्कॆ (*agotāykè*) (the word for cow used in the sense of one who has cows; the suffix tal), सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*) (all-anudātta by treatment as the latter member of a compound in the vocative) and निदे (*nide*) (root णिदि कुत्सायां (*ṇidi kutsāyāṃ*): the suffix kvip in the sense of the action, no nu-augment, the accent of the case ending).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*)—O son of strength
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अमतये (*amataye*)—to poverty that acts as an enemy; मा रीरधः (*mā rīradhaḥ*)—do not make us fit to receive it
- अवीरताय्कॆ (*avīratāykè*)—and to the state without heroic sons
- मा (*mā*)—do not make us fit to receive it
- अगोताय्कॆ (*agotāykè*)—to the condition without cows and other cattle
- मा (*mā*)—do not make us fit to receive it
- निदे (*nide*)—as objects of reproach
- मा (*mā*)—do not make us
- द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*)—the mutual hatred and jealousy
- अपाकृधि (*apākṛdhi*)—remove and destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength, do not make us fit to receive poverty that acts as an enemy, the state without heroic sons, the condition without cows and other cattle, and the reproach of others. Make our mutual hatred and jealousy go far away and be destroyed.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Consign us not, AGNI, to malignity ; (doom) us not to the absence of prosperity ; nor, son of strength, to the want of cattle, nor to reproach : drive away (all) animosities.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Addressing Agni as सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*), "son of strength" (because he is born when the fire-sticks are churned with force), the prayer is made that he destroy the poverty that does the work of an enemy towards us. Here the meaning "enemy" is given for the word अमतय (*amataya*).

### Printed p. 340

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*(The Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued from p. 339; the print gives no new label at the top of this page.)*

On अवीरताय्कॆ—वीरशब्देन तद्वान् लक्ष्यते। वीरस्य भावः वीरता न वीरता अवीरता अर्स्मान् अपुत्रताया विषयभूर्ता मा कुरु (*avīratāykè—vīraśabdena tadvān lakṣyate| vīrasya bhāvaḥ vīratā na vīratā avīratā arsmān aputratāyā viṣayabhūrtā mā kuru*): the meaning is explained thus: the word वीर (*vīra*) denotes one who has virility; the quality of the hero is virility; one without virility is a non-hero (avīra). It is further explained that one who possesses a son born of virility is denoted by the word for hero, and one who has no son is a non-hero; and Agni is prayed not to cause childlessness to us, the sacrificers.

On निदे मा कुरु—निंदाया विषयभूतान् मा विधेहि (*nide mā kuru—niṃdāyā viṣayabhūtān mā vidhehi*): Agni is prayed to show such favour that no kind of reproach may befall us, the masters of the house who perform the sacrifice.

On द्वेषांसि अप आ कृधि—कर्मापराधनिमित्तान् द्वेषांश्च निवारय (*dveṣāṃsi apa ā kṛdhi—karmāparādhanimittān dveṣāṃśca nivāraya*): Agni is prayed that the faults of omission and the like in the indispensable duties of the sacrifice may not come upon us, and that the faults such as laziness (idleness) in the performance of the sacrificial rites may not befall us; he is to favour us so.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

अवीरताय्कॆ—वीराः अस्य संति इति वीरः (*avīratāykè—vīrāḥ asya saṃti iti vīraḥ*): the suffix ac in the sense of possession by अर्श आदिभ्योच् (*arśa ādibhyoc*) (Pā. Sū. 5-2-177). वीरस्य भावः वीरता (*vīrasya bhāvaḥ vīratā*): the suffix tal in the sense of state by तस्यभावस्त्वतला (*tasyabhāvastvatalā*) (Pā. Sū. 5-1-119 *(the number is broken across two lines in the print)*). By the statement तलंतंस्त्रियां (*talaṃtaṃstriyāṃ*) the feminine suffix ṭāp comes. न वीरता अवीरता (*na vīratā avīratā*) is a compound with the negative; when the accent of the negative would be obtained, the accent on the first syllable of the latter member comes by परादिश्चंदसि बहुलं (*parādiścaṃdasi bahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199). The form is in the dative singular.

रीरधः—राध साध संसिद्धौ (*rīradhaḥ—rādha sādha saṃsiddhau*). By the rule हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*), when the action of the instigator is shown, the suffix ṇic comes. After the causative, the aorist (luṅ) in the sense of the imperative, in the Vedic manner. By णित्रिद्रुसुभ्यः कर्तरि चज् (*ṇitridrusubhyaḥ kartari caj*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-48) the substitute caṅ for cli, and by षेरनिटि (*ṣeraniṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51) the loss of ṇic. By णौचज्युपधाया ह्रस्वः (*ṇaucajyupadhāyā hrasvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-1) the penultimate of the root is shortened; by चजु (*caju*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-11) the root is doubled. By सन्वल्लघुनिचज् परेनग्लोपे (*sanvallaghunicaj parenaglope*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-93) there is the state of treatment like san, so by सन्यतः (*sanyataḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-79) the reduplicating syllable of the root gets the vowel i; to it, by दीर्घोलघोः (*dīrgholaghoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-94) lengthening. Because of the connection with the particle mā, by न माज् योगे (*na māj yoge*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-74) the augment aṭ does not come to the stem. The sibilant of the ending becomes the visarga through ru. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

अगोताय्कॆ—इल्लि (*agotāykè—illi*): the word for cow here conveys, by indication (lakṣaṇā), one who has cows. न गौः अगौः अगोर्भावः अगोता (*na gauḥ agauḥ agorbhāvaḥ agotā*): by तस्य भावस्त्वतल् (*tasya bhāvastvatal*) the suffix tal in the sense of state. Because it is marked l, by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the acute accent comes before the suffix.

### Printed p. 341

*(The grammar of Ṛk 5 continues from p. 340.)*

सहसस्पुत्र—सुबामंत्रिते (*sahasasputra—subāmaṃtrite*) (Pā. Sū. 2-1-2 *(so printed, with spaces inside the brackets)*): since the genitive सहसः (*sahasaḥ*) is stated to be treated as part of the same word, the nighāta accent of the vocative comes to the whole.

निदे—णिवि कुत्सायां (*nide—ṇivi kutsāyāṃ*) (the root as supplied). Since it is read in the sampadādi class, the suffix kvip in the sense of the action. By the maxim आगमशास्त्रमनित्यं (*āgamaśāstramanityaṃ*) the nu-augment does not come, though the root is marked i. The form is in the dative singular. By सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168) the acute accent comes to the case ending.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुभग शोभनधनोपेत हे अग्ने त्वमध्वरेऽस्माभिः क्रियमाणेऽस्मिन्नग्नि-
> ष्टोमादिकर्मणि बृहतो महतः प्रभूतस्य प्रजावतोऽपत्योपेतस्य वाजस्यान्नस्य
> शग्नि । ईशिषे । तादृशमन्नमस्मिन्नध्वरेऽस्मभ्यं देहि । किंच तुविद्युम्न बहुधनयुक्त
> हे अग्ने मयोभुना । मय इति सुखनाम शेवृथं मय इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ।
> तद्दानाद्युवयोगहेतुतया सुखस्य भावकेनात एव यशस्वता कीर्तिमता भूय-
> सातिप्रभूतेन राय्कॆवंविधेन धनेनास्मान् संसृज । संयोजय ॥ शग्नि । शक्ल शक्ता-
> वित्यस्य लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । हुझल्कॊ हेर्धिरिति धिरादेशः ।
> हेरपित्वादुदात्तता । राया । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । भूयसा । बहुश-
> ब्वात् द्विवचनविभज्योपपद इतीयसुन् । बहोर्लोपो भू च बहोरितीयसुनः
> सर्वस्य लोपे प्राप्त आदेः परस्य । पा. १-१-५४ ।इति प्रत्ययस्यादेर्लोपो बहो-
> र्भूरादेशश्च । नित्स्वरः । सृज । सृज विसर्गे । तुदादिः । लोटि रूपं । निघातः ।
> मयोभुना । भूसत्तायामित्यस्मादौणादिको डुप्रत्ययः । तुविद्युम्न । पादादि-
> त्पादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, rich in good fortune, at this rite performed by us you are lord of abundant food rich in offspring; give such food to us, and join us to abundant wealth that brings happiness and renown, O one of great wealth.

*(Grammar tail of the block, noted briefly.)* It treats the words शग्नि । (*śagni |*) (the root as supplied; the suffix lost by the Vedic rule; the substitute dhi for hi; the ending is acute because hi is without the marker p), राया (*rāyā*) (the case ending is acute), भूयसा (*bhūyasā*) (the suffix īyasun after the word for "much", the loss of the word and the substitute bhū; the accent of the marked n), सृज । (*sṛja |*) (the root of the tudādi class; the imperative form; nighāta), मयोभुना (*mayobhunā*) (the suffix ḍu of the uṇādi group after the root for being) and तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*) (the pāda-initial nighāta). It also states that the word मय (*maya*) is a name of happiness, because it is read among the names of happiness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुभग (*subhaga*)—O one with excellent wealth
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in this rite of the form of the Agniṣṭoma
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of the abundant
- प्रजावतः (*prajāvataḥ*)—and of that which is joined with the wealth of sons (offspring)

### Printed p. 342

*(The Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 6 continues from p. 341.)*

वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—of food; शग्नि (*śagni*)—you are lord *(printed "ಪ್ರಭುವಾಗಿದ್ದೀಯೆ." with a full stop, as supplied)*; तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*)—O Agni, lord of abundant wealth *(printed "ಧದಕ್ಕೆ", presumably for wealth, as supplied)*; मयोभुना (*mayobhunā*)—that which is a cause of happiness; यशस्वता (*yaśasvatā*)—that which is joined with renown; भूयसा (*bhūyasā*)—that which is exceedingly great; राया (*rāyā*)—with wealth; सं सृज (*saṃ sṛja*)—join (us).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, joined with excellent and abundant wealth, you are lord, in this rite of the form of the Agniṣṭoma, of food that is abundant and rich in the wealth of sons and the like. Therefore join us to riches that are a cause of happiness, joined with renown and exceedingly great, and make us rich in possessions.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Auspicious AGNI, bestow (upon us) at the rite, food (the source of) happiness and renown.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On अध्वरे वाजस्य शग्नि—अस्माभिः क्रियमाणे अग्निष्टोमादिकर्मणि अन्नस्य ईशिषे (*adhvare vājasya śagni—asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇe agniṣṭomādikarmaṇi annasya īśiṣe*): Agni is addressed with the word सुभग (*subhaga*) and the meaning is explained as शोभनधनोपेत (*śobhanadhanopeta*), "possessed of excellent wealth", that is, the owner of choice wealth. The meaning is described thus: in the Agniṣṭoma and the other rites performed by the sacrificers, may Agni, who has excellent wealth, bestow food of that kind. It is explained that the food Agni bestows is बृहतः—महतः (*bṛhataḥ—mahataḥ*), that is, endowed with the greatness of abundance, and प्रजावतः अपत्योपेतस्य (*prajāvataḥ apatyopetasya*), that it brings about the increase of the line of sons, grandsons and the rest.

On मयोभुना भूयसा राया संस्कृज— मय इति सुखनाम तद्दानाद्युपयोग हेतुतया सुखस्य भावकेन अतिप्रभूतेन एवं विधेन धनेनास्मान् संयोजय (*mayobhunā bhūyasā rāyā saṃskṛja— maya iti sukhanāma taddānādyupayoga hetutayā sukhasya bhāvakena atiprabhūtena evaṃ vidhena dhanenāsmān saṃyojaya*): here Agni is addressed with the word तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*), which conveys the meaning "possessed of much wealth", a very wealthy one. The word मय (*maya*) is stated among the names of happiness (Nirukta 3-13 *(printed "ನಿ. ೩-೧೩")*). Because wealth, through such uses as giving, produces happiness, it is designated by the word मयोभू (*mayobhū*). And because it brings fame through gifts and the like, it is also renowned, which is the meaning given for the word यशस्वता (*yaśasvatā*). The prayer is made that Agni, the very wealthy, may obtain for us wealth that produces happiness, brings fame and is abundant.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

शग्नि—शकल्य शक्त्य धातु (*śagni—śakalya śaktya dhātu*) *(the root as supplied; the printed letters differ from the root given in the bhāṣya)*. In the imperative second person singular the ending sip. By सेर्ह्यपिच्च (*serhyapicca*) the substitute hi for it. By बहुलंछंदसि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasi*) the luk-deletion of the vikaraṇa. Since hi comes after a stem ending in ru , by हुझल् भ्यो हेर्धिः (*hujhal bhyo herdhiḥ*) (6-4-101) the substitute dhi for it. झुलां जश् (*jhulāṃ jaś*) *(the sentence breaks off here at the end of p. 342 and continues on the next page; nothing further is in this window)*.

### Printed p. 343

*(The grammar of Ṛk 6 continues from p. 342, from the point where the sentence about the sibilant and the substitute of the ending had broken off.)*

By झुशि (*jhuśi*) the substitute g comes for the k of the root *(printed "ಧಾತುಕಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಗಕಾರದೇಶ", as supplied; the word in the first line is printed ಝುಶಿ, as supplied)*. Because the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. Since the non-pit state was thus laid down, the acute accent comes and the word becomes acute on its last syllable.

बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—by the statement बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानम् (*bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānam*) the case ending gets the acute accent.

राया (*rāyā*)—the word रै (*rai*); the form is given as a fourth-case (dative) singular form *(so printed; the Pratipadārtha renders it "with wealth")*. By ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the case ending gets the acute accent.

भूयसा (*bhūyasā*)—the word बहु (*bahu*) ("much"). When the sense of excess is shown, by द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ (*dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-57) the suffix īyasun comes. By बहोर्लोपो भूचबहोः (*bahorlopo bhūcabahoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-154) there is loss after the word for "much" and the substitute bhū for the word for "much"; when total loss of the following īyasun is obtained, by आदेःपरस्य (*ādeḥparasya*) (Pā. Sū. 1-1-54) only the initial long ī of īyasun is lost, and bhū is the substitute for "much". The stem bhūyas results. Because the suffix is marked n, by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) the acute accent on the first syllable comes.

सृज (*sṛja*)—the root सृज विसर्गे (*sṛja visarge*), of the tudādi class; the imperative (loṭ) second person singular. Because the vikaraṇa śa is treated as marked j, the guṇa of the penultimate does not come. Because it stands after a non-finite-verb-ending word *(so printed; "ಅತಿಜಂತದ ಪರದಲ್ಲಿರುವುದರಿಂದ")*, by तिज्ञतिजः (*tijñatijaḥ*) the nighāta accent comes.

मयोभुना (*mayobhunā*)—the root भू सत्तायां (*bhū sattāyāṃ*) ("to be"). To it the uṇādi suffix ḍu. Because it is marked ḍ, the ṭi part (ū) is lost. The accent of a compound whose latter member is a kṛt-ending word (the natural accent of the first member) comes. The form is in the instrumental singular.

तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*)—a vocative form. Because it stands at the beginning of the pāda, the nighāta accent of an addressed word does not come; by आमंत्रितस्य (*āmaṃtritasya*) (6-1-198) the acute accent on the first syllable comes.

## Sūkta 17 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The seventeenth sūkta** (ಹದಿನೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समिध्यमान इति पंचर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमाग्नेयं त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वामित्रस्य
> कतस्यार्षं । तदुक्तं । समिध्यमानः पंच कतो वैश्वामित्रस्त्विति.॥ आ होतेत्यादि-
> सूक्तदशकस्य विनियोग उक्तः प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरिति । तत्रेदं चतुर्थं । वाज-
> पेये बार्हस्पत्ये चरावाग्निं सुदीतिमिति स्विष्टकृतो याज्या । वाजपेयेनेत्यादि-
> खंडे सूत्रितं । अग्निं सुदीतिं सुदृशं गृणंत इति संयाज्ये । आ ९ - ९ । इति॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, which begins with समिध्यमानः (*samidhyamānaḥ*), is the fifth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. The Ṛṣi of this sūkta is the one named कतः (*kataḥ*) , of the line of Viśvāmitra; Agni is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said समिध्यमानः पंच कतो वैश्वामित्रस्त्विति (*samidhyamānaḥ paṃca kato vaiśvāmitrastviti*). Earlier (in the 14th sūkta), from the sūkta beginning with आ होता (*ā hotā*), ten

*(The Anuvāda continues from p. 343, the sentence running over the page break.)* sūktas have their application (viniyoga) in the Prātaranuvāka and in the recitation of the mantras of the Aśvina-śastra, as has already been said. Of those ten sūktas this is the fourth. When the Bārhaspatya caru oblation is made in the Vājapeya sacrifice, the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta, the Ṛk अग्निं सुदीतिं सुदृशं (*agniṃ sudītiṃ sudṛśaṃ*), is to be used as the yājyā mantra in the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra अग्निं सुदीतिं सुदृशं गृणंत इति संयाज्ये (*agniṃ sudītiṃ sudṛśaṃ gṛṇaṃta iti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 9-9).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Kata praises Agni, the upholder of rites, kindled first and in due order at the fire-places, anointed with ghee in order to sacrifice to the gods.

*(Grammar tail of the block, noted briefly.)* It explains प्रथमा (*prathamā*) (the substitute ḍā for the case ending), धर्म (*dharma*) (the suffix manin after the root for holding; the shortening is Vedic), अज्यते (*ajyate*) (the root for anointing in the passive), विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*) (a bahuvrīhi whose first member keeps its final acute accent), यजथाय (*yajathāya*) (the uṇādi suffix tha after the root for worship; the dative in the sense of purpose) and, in the bhāṣya, अकुभिः (*akubhiḥ*) *(so printed; the Pratipadārtha has अक्तुभिः (*aktubhiḥ*))*.

*[Further readings of the bhāṣya that differ from the Pada, as supplied: शोजिष्टेशः (*śojiṣṭeśaḥ*) for शोचिःकेशः (*śociḥkeśaḥ*), अग्यायतनेष्वनुक्रमेण (*agyāyataneṣvanukrameṇa*) in the form printed in the bhāṣya, and फृतनिर्णिक् (*phṛtanirṇik*) in the grammar tail where the Pada has घृतनिर्निक् (*ghṛtanirnik*).]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धर्म (*dharma*)—the upholder of sacrifices and the like
- विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*)—the one desired by all
- शोचिक्षेशः (*śocikṣeśaḥ*) *(so printed, with ಕ್ಷ; the Pada has ಕೇಶಃ)*—the one whose hair is of the form of flames
- धृतनिर्णिक् (*dhṛtanirṇik*) *(printed with ಧೃ, as supplied)*—the one with a wrapping of the form of ghee
- पावकः (*pāvakaḥ*)—our purifier
- सुयज्ञः (*suyajñaḥ*)—the one endowed with an excellent sacrifice
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, with them in view
- यजथाय (*yajathāya*)—for performing the sacrifice
- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—at the beginning of the sacrifice
- अनु (*anu*)—in order
- समिध्यमानः (*samidhyamānaḥ*)—being kindled
- अक्तुभिः (*aktubhiḥ*)—by unguents and the like
- समज्यते (*samajyate*)—is sprinkled and becomes adorned

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the upholder of sacrifices and the like, desired by all, with hair of the form of flames, with a wrapping of the form of ghee, our purifier, endowed with an excellent sacrifice, is kindled at the beginning of the sacrifice, in due order, in order to sacrifice with the gods in view, and is adorned with unguents and the like.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The righteous (AGNI) when first kindled on the several (altars) the object of adoration by all, whose hair is flame, and who is cleansed with butter, the purifier, the worthily-worshipped, is sprinkled with oblations for the worship of the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धर्मा प्रथमा अनु समिध्यमानः—धारणात् धर्म । तादृशो आग्निः प्रथमं यज्ञोपक्रम अग्न्यायतनेष्वनुक्रमेण सम्यक् प्रज्वाल्यमानः। अनु धर्म। (*dharmā prathamā anu samidhyamānaḥ—dhāraṇāt dharma | tādṛśo āgniḥ prathamaṃ yajñopakrama agnyāyataneṣvanukrameṇa samyak prajvālyamānaḥ| anu dharma|*) *(The Special Topics of Ṛk 1 begin here, quoted in full as far as the print reaches on this page: "dharma" is from holding; such an Agni, at the first beginning of the sacrifice, is kindled well in order at the fire-places; and then the word "anu" with "dharma" is taken up again. The text breaks off at the end of p. 345 inside the next word, which is cut at a hyphen, and continues on the next page; nothing further is in this window.)* *[The stray line "44" after the last line of the page is printed in the supplied text; kept as a note.]*

### Printed p. 346

*(The Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue from p. 345; the word धर्म- (*dharma-*) that broke off at the end of p. 345 is completed by the first word of this page.)* साधनभूतेषु यज्ञेषु प्रथमं समिध्यमानः । (*sādhanabhūteṣu yajñeṣu prathamaṃ samidhyamānaḥ |*) (*the Sanskrit sentence is quoted as supplied; it runs on from the end of p. 345*). Because the word conveys the sense "to hold", the derivation of the word dharma is stated as धारणात् धर्म (*dhāraṇāt dharma*). Here, since Agni carries the sacrifice through to its end, and since from the beginning of the rite until the sacrifice is complete he graciously grants his presence, the one who is the holder is addressed by the word dharma, with the derivation "the one denoted by the word dharma". The Vedic sentence धर्माणमग्निं विदथस्य साधनं (*dharmāṇamagniṃ vidathasya sādhanaṃ*), which conveys the same meaning, is also cited. Thus one kind of meaning is explained: Agni of this kind, at the beginning of the sacrifice, in the sacrificial hall, from the first act to the very last, is kept kindled by the sacrificers.

In the second meaning, since the means of the observance of dharma is the sacrifice as well, the first act among the sacrifices is that Agni is kindled (set alight) by the sacrificer and the others; so it is described.

On विश्ववारः—विश्वैस्सर्वैर्यजमानैर्यष्टव्यतया वरणीयः विश्वैर्यजमानैर्होतृद्वारा वारो वारणं यस्य (*viśvavāraḥ—viśvaissarvairyajamānairyaṣṭavyatayā varaṇīyaḥ viśvairyajamānairhotṛdvārā vāro vāraṇaṃ yasya*): two meanings are described. Either the one who is desired by the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, as one who offers the oblations (as the one worthy of the sacrifice) or who receives the offered oblations and carries them away; or else the one who is wished for by the sacrificers through the invocation of the gods in the sacrifice, namely Agni.

On शोचिष्केशः—शोचींषि ज्वालाः केशाः यस्य (*śociṣkeśaḥ—śocīṃṣi jvālāḥ keśāḥ yasya*): it is explained as one who has his own flames as hair (like hair); that is, the flames of Agni are like hairs to Agni.

On घृतनिर्णिक्—घृतस्य तापनद्वारा विलापनेन शोधकः (*ghṛtanirṇik—ghṛtasya tāpanadvārā vilāpanena śodhakaḥ*): the word निर्णिक् (*nirṇik*) is stated among the names of form (Nirukta 3-9 *(printed "ನಿ. ೩-೯")*). And साते जीवातुरुत तस्य विद्वि मा स्मृतादृगप गूहः समर्ये । आविः स्वः कृणुते गूहते बुसं स पादुरस्य निर्णिजो न मुच्यते ॥ (*sāte jīvāturuta tasya vidvi mā smṛtādṛgapa gūhaḥ samarye | āviḥ svaḥ kṛṇute gūhate busaṃ sa pādurasya nirṇijo na mucyate ‖*) (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-27-24 *(printed "ಋ. ಸಂ. ೧೦-೨೭-೨೪")*). In this Ṛk, तमः पंकदिग्धानि हि रूपाणि स्वेन प्रकाशोदकेन धौतानीव करोतीति निर्णिक् सूर्यः (*tamaḥ paṃkadigdhāni hi rūpāṇi svena prakāśodakena dhautānīva karotīti nirṇik sūryaḥ*): taking it to mean "he who makes the forms that are not seen properly in the mud called darkness visible with the waters of his own light", the meaning of the Sun as the purifier is described. Here it is explained that Agni makes the ghee melt by heating it with his rays and so purifies it.

On पावकः—अस्मदीयपापशोधकः (*pāvakaḥ—asmadīyapāpaśodhakaḥ*): it is explained that Agni removes the sins of us, the sacrificers, and makes us pure, and is therefore the one who brings about purification.

### Printed p. 347

On अक्तुभिः सं अज्यते— अंजनसाधनैः घृतादिभिः सम्यक् सिच्यते (*aktubhiḥ saṃ ajyate— aṃjanasādhanaiḥ ghṛtādibhiḥ samyak sicyate*): it is described that Agni is sprinkled by the sacrificers so that he is satisfied with ghee and the like, which are the means for such rites as anointing, in order to worship in the sacrifice the gods who are worthy of worship.

Because the sacrifice performed, or to be performed, for Agni is excellent and bears fruit, Agni is here addressed with the word सुयज्ञः (*suyajñaḥ*). For this the meaning शोभनयज्ञोपेतः (*śobhanayajñopetaḥ*) is explained here: Agni is joined with the sacrifice that is the cause of the excellent worship of the gods taking place.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

समिध्यमानः (*samidhyamānaḥ*) is treated thus: इइंधी दीप्तौ (*iiṃdhī dīptau*) *(printed with a doubled ಇ, as supplied)* is the root. In the passive the suffix śānac. By सार्वधातुकेयक् (*sārvadhātukeyak*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-67) the suffix yak. By अनिदितांहलउ (*aniditāṃhalau*) the loss of the penultimate of the root. By आनेमुक् (*ānemuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82) the augment muk. By तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*), since the lasārvadhātuka ending becomes unaccented, the accent of yak remains. In the compound the natural accent of the latter, kṛt-ending member comes.

प्रथमा (*prathamā*): by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ḍā for the case ending.

धर्म (*dharma*): धृञ् धारणे (*dhṛñ dhāraṇe*) is the root. By अन्येभ्योपिदृश्यंते (*anyebhyopidṛśyaṃte*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75) the suffix manin. By सार्वधातुकार्थ (*sārvadhātukārtha*) *(as supplied; the rest of the sūtra is not printed)* guṇa for the vowel ṛ, which comes with ra following. By इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) the accent on the first syllable comes. When su follows and lengthening is obtained, the short vowel comes as a Vedic usage.

अक्तुभिः (*aktubhiḥ*): अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिषु (*aṃjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāṃtigatiṣu*) is the root. अज्यते विभिरिति अक्तूनि (*ajyate vibhiriti aktūni*) . By the force of the word "bahula" the suffix ktu in the sense of the instrument. Because it is marked k, by अनिदितांहलउ (*aniditāṃhalau*) the loss of the nasal letter of the penultimate of the root *(printed "ಉಪಧಾನಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ", as supplied)*. By the accent of the suffix the word becomes acute on its last syllable. The form is the third-case (instrumental) plural.

अज्यते (*ajyate*): to the root stated before, in the passive, the suffix ta of the present (laṭ) third person singular. The substitute e for ṭi *(printed "ಟಗೆ ಏತ್ವ", as supplied)*. On account of yak the loss of the penultimate nasal. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes.

विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*): विश्वैः यजमानैर्होतृद्वारा वारं वारणं यस्य सः (*viśvaiḥ yajamānairhotṛdvārā vāraṃ vāraṇaṃ yasya saḥ*) *(the bhāṣya reads ವಾರೋ where this has ವಾರಂ, as supplied)*. वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*) is the root. After the causative form the suffix ghañ. By बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायाम् (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-106) the accent on the end of the first member comes.

शोचिष्केशः (*śociṣkeśaḥ*): शोचींषि केशाः यस्य सः (*śocīṃṣi keśāḥ yasya saḥ*); by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) the natural accent of the first member comes.

### Printed p. 348

धृतनिर्णिक् (*dhṛtanirṇik*) *(so printed, with ಧೃ, as supplied)*: णिजिर् शौचपोषणयोः (*ṇijir śaucapoṣaṇayoḥ*) is the root. By क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) the suffix kvip. धृतं नेनेक्ति इति धृतनिर्णिक् (*dhṛtaṃ nenekti iti dhṛtanirṇik*). The prefix nir. A tatpuruṣa compound of the second case; by तत्पुरुषे (*tatpuruṣe*) *(as supplied; the rest of the sūtra is not printed)* the natural accent of the first member comes. The word धृतशब्द (*dhṛtaśabda*) becomes acute on its last syllable.

सुयज्ञः (*suyajñaḥ*): शोभनः यज्ञः यस्य सः (*śobhanaḥ yajñaḥ yasya saḥ*). By नञ् सुभ्याम् (*nañ subhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-217 *(as supplied)*) the accent on the end of the latter member comes.

यजथाय (*yajathāya*): यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु (*yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu*) is the root. By the word "bahula" the suffix atha, laid down by शीज्शपिरुगमि (*śījśapirugami*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-393), comes to this root, and the form is yajatha. By the dictum तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी वाच्या (*tādarthye caturthī vācyā*) the fourth case comes when the sense of purpose is shown.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथाय॑जो हो॒त्रम॑ग्ने पृथि॒व्या यथा॑ दि॒वो जा॑तवेदश्चिक्ति॒त्वान् ।  
> ए॒वानेन॑ ह॒विषा॑ यक्षि दे॒वान्म॑नु॒ष्वद्य॒ज्ञं प्रति॑रे॒मम॒द्य ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । अयजः । होत्रं । अग्ने । पृथिव्याः । यथा । दिवः । जातवेदः । चिकित्वान् ।  
> एव । अनेन । हविषा । यक्षि । देवान् । मनुष्वत् । यज्ञं । प्र । शिर । इमं । अद्य ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं यथा पृथिव्या यजमानभूतायाः पृथिवीदेवतायाः पूर्वं
> होता सन् होत्रं होमसाधनं हविरयजोऽयाजीः जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञ हे
> अग्ने चिकित्वान् कर्मविषयज्ञानवान् त्वं यथा च दिवो यजमानभूताया
> द्युदेवताया होता भूत्वा हविरयजः । एव एवं त्वमस्मिन्कर्मणि होता सन्
> अनेनास्माभिर्दीयमानेन हविषा देवान् यक्षि । यज । किंच त्वमद्येदानी
> मस्माभिः क्रियमाणमिमं यज्ञं प्रतिशिर । अनुष्ठानसंपूर्त्या पारं गमय । तत्र
> दृष्टांतो मनुष्यदिति । यथा मनोर्यज्ञमनुष्ठानसंपूर्त्या पारमनैषीस्त-
> द्वदिमं यज्ञं पारं नयेत्यर्थः ॥ यथा । प्रकारवचने थालिति थाल् । लितीति
> प्रत्ययात्तूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । अयजः । यजेर्लजि रूपं । यच्छब्दयोगाद-
> निघातः । होत्रं । हु दानादनयोः । हुयामाश्रुभसिभ्यस्त्रन्निति त्रन्मृत्ययेनांतो-
> दात्तः । दिवः । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । चिकित्वान् । कित ज्ञान इत्यस्य क्वसौ

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, as you officiated as hotṛ for Earth and Heaven, so sacrifice to the gods with this oblation and bring this rite to completion, as for Manu.

Sū. 7-2-112)), यक्षि (*yakṣi*) (the imperative of the root for worship), मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*) (the suffix vati in the sense of "like"; because of the designation bha there is no change of the s to ru; the suffix keeps its accent) and तिर (*tira*) *(so printed in the bhāṣya; the Pada and the grammar page have ಶಿರ, as supplied)* (the imperative form with the substitute śa by variation; the substitution i for ṛ; nighāta).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the goddess Earth (being her hotṛ)
- होत्रं (*hotraṃ*)—the oblation, the means of the offering
- आयजः (*āyajaḥ*) *(so printed with a long ā; the Saṃhitā has ಅಯಜಃ, as supplied)*—you offered it (for the Earth) and performed the sacrifice
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni who know all things
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—you who possess knowledge of the rites
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—for the goddess of the heavenly world you performed the sacrifice
- एव (*eva*)—in the same manner; अनेन हविषा (*anena haviṣā*)—with this oblation
- देवान् (*devān*)—with the gods in view
- यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—perform the sacrifice
- मनुष्यत् (*manuṣyat*) *(so printed here; the Saṃhitā has ಮನುಷ್ವತ್, as supplied)*—as you caused the sacrifice of Manu to be completed
- अद्य (*adya*)—now; इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice; प्र तिर (*pra tira*) *(so printed, with a space)*—make it complete

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O all-knowing Agni, in what manner you formerly, being the hotṛ of the goddess Earth, performed the sacrifice, and in what manner, possessing knowledge of the rites, you performed the sacrifice for the goddess of the heavenly world as well, in that same manner perform the sacrifice with this oblation with the gods in view. *(The print has ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನುನ್ನುದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ with a doubled ನ್ನು, as supplied.)* As you formerly carried the sacrifice of Manu through completely, so now also make this sacrifice of ours complete.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
As you offered the burnt-offering, AGNI, (on behalf of) earth ; as you, JATAVEDAS, who are cognizant (of sacred rites, offered sacrifice on behalf) of heaven ; so with this oblation worship the gods, and perfect this rite to-day (as you did) that of MANU.

*[The supplied text has "sacri- fice" with a line-break hyphen in the printed English; joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On पृथिव्याः होत्रं अयजः (*pṛthivyāḥ hotraṃ ayajaḥ*): here Sāyaṇa has explained यजमानभूतायाः पृथिवीदेवतायाः पूर्वं होता सन् होत्रं हविः होमसाधनं अयजः (*yajamānabhūtāyāḥ pṛthivīdevatāyāḥ pūrvaṃ hotā san hotraṃ haviḥ homasādhanaṃ ayajaḥ*) (that is, that when the Earth was the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, Agni, as the priest called hotṛ, offered the oblation, the substance of the offering); hence it is indicated that the goddess Earth also performed the sacrifice. Yāska has read the word pṛthivī among the names of the atmosphere (Nirukta 2-10 *(printed "ನಿ. ೨-೧೦")*). But Sāyaṇa has explained this word as the goddess Earth. The word hotra, explained as denoting the means of the act, is used in the sense of the oblation, which is a substance of offering. *(The print has "ಹೋಮ' ನ್ಯರೂಪವಾದ" with a stray apostrophe and an unclear ನ್ಯ, as supplied.)*

### Printed p. 350

On जातवेदः—जातप्रज्ञ । (*jātavedaḥ—jātaprajña |*): the word jātavedas is explained by Yāska (the print has ಜಾತವೇದಶ್ಯಬ್ದ with ಶ್ಯ, as supplied): जातानि वेद, जातानि वैनं विदुः, जातेजाते विद्यत इति ना, जातवित्तो ना जातधनः, जातविद्यो ना जातप्रज्ञानः, यज्ञातः पशूनविंदतेति तज्जातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वमिति ब्राह्मणं (*jātāni veda, jātāni vainaṃ viduḥ, jātejāte vidyata iti nā, jātavitto nā jātadhanaḥ, jātavidyo nā jātaprajñānaḥ, yajñātaḥ paśūnaviṃdateti tajjātavedaso jātavedastvamiti brāhmaṇaṃ*) (Nirukta 7-20 *(printed "ನಿ. ೭-೨೦")*). (Its explanation has been given earlier.) Sāyaṇa here has explained the meaning as जातप्रज्ञ (*jātaprajña*), has addressed Agni with this word, has described Agni as possessing knowledge concerning the rites in the word चिकित्वा (*cikitvā*) *(so printed, for ಚಿಕಿತ್ವಾನ್, as supplied)*, and has explained दिवः यजमानभूतायाः द्युदेवतायाः होता भूत्वा हविरयजः (*divaḥ yajamānabhūtāyāḥ dyudevatāyāḥ hotā bhūtvā havirayajaḥ*): Agni, as the priest called hotṛ in the sacrifice of the goddess of the heavenly world, who is in the form of the sacrificer, offered the oblation, the substance of the offering.

On चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*): Yāska has explained that this word is used in the sense of चेतनार्वा (*cetanārvā*) . And:

समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देर्वा यजसि जातवेदः । आ च वह मित्रमहश्चि कित्वान् त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥ (*samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe devo dervā yajasi jātavedaḥ | ā ca vaha mitramahaści kitvān tvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi pracetāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-1) *(the print has ದೇರ್ವಾ in the first line and "ಮಿತ್ರಮಹಶ್ಚಿ ಕಿತ್ವಾನ್" with a space in the second, as supplied)*

Yāska has explained the meaning: in this ṛk Agni Jātavedas is described; Agni himself is addressed with this word; he is the messenger who carries the oblation offered in the sacrifice to the gods, he is the hotṛ, and he knows the wishes of the sacrificers.

On मनुष्यत् एव हविषा देवान् यक्षि आद्य इमं यज्ञं प्रतिर (*manuṣyat eva haviṣā devān yakṣi ādya imaṃ yajñaṃ pratira*) *(the heading is printed without a dash, as supplied)*: as Agni, when the goddess Earth and the goddess of the heavenly world performed the sacrifice, was the hotṛ and offered the oblation to the gods in accordance with the wish of the sacrificers, the wish of the sacrificer is described in अस्माभिर्धीयमानेन हविषा देवान् यक्षि (*asmābhirdhīyamānena haviṣā devān yakṣi*): "let him offer to the gods the oblations offered by us, the sacrificers", and in अनुष्ठानसंपूर्त्या पारं गमय (*anuṣṭhānasaṃpūrtyā pāraṃ gamaya*): "let Agni make this sacrifice, now performed by us, the sacrificers, complete, so that there is no omission in the performance of the rites that must be performed". In this matter the comparison is stated with the word मनुष्यत् (*manuṣyat*) (the Special Topics print ಮನುಷ್ಯತ್, as in the Pratipadārtha): यथा मनोः यज्ञं अनुष्ठानसंपूर्त्या पारमनैषीः तद्वत् (*yathā manoḥ yajñaṃ anuṣṭhānasaṃpūrtyā pāramanaiṣīḥ tadvat*), that is, as formerly in the sacrifice of the one called Manu Agni was the hotṛ and completed the rites of the sacrifice so that there was no omission of any kind, so in our sacrifice also let Agni be the hotṛ and complete the sacrifice; this is the wish of the sacrificers that is stated, and this is the meaning explained.

On यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*): this word is explained by Yāska, with a showing of the opinions of the Nairuktas and of the teacher called Upamanyu: यज्ञः कस्मात् प्रख्यातं कर्मेति नैरुक्ताः । याज्यो भवतीति ना यजुरुन्नो भवतीति वा बहुकृष्णाजन इत्यौपमन्यवो यजूंष्येनं नयंतीति वा । (*yajñaḥ kasmāt prakhyātaṃ karmeti nairuktāḥ | yājyo bhavatīti nā yajurunno bhavatīti vā bahukṛṣṇājana ityaupamanyavo yajūṃṣyenaṃ nayaṃtīti vā |*) (Nirukta 3-19 *(printed "ನಿ. ೩-೧೯")*). The meaning of this sentence has been explained earlier.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

यथा (*yathā*): from the pronoun-stem यच्छब्द (*yacchabda*), by प्रकारवचनेथाल् (*prakāravacanethāl*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-23) the suffix thāl; since it has the designation vibhakti, by त्यदादीनामः (*tyadādīnāmaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) the substitute a; by अतोगुणे (*atoguṇe*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form; the form becomes yathā. Since the suffix is marked l, by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. 6-1-193 *(as supplied; the print has no "Sū.")*) the acute accent comes before the suffix.

अयजः (*ayajaḥ*): य.ज देवपूजादिषु (*ya.ja devapūjādiṣu*) *(the print has a stray full stop after ಯ, as supplied)* is the root; the form is the second person singular of the past imperfect (lan). Because of the connection with the word ya (yathā), the nighāta accent does not come. Since the augment aṭ is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable.

होत्रं (*hotraṃ*): हु दानादनयोः (*hu dānādanayoḥ*) is the root. By हुयामाश्रुभसिभ्यस्त्रन् (*huyāmāśrubhasibhyastran*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-607) the suffix tran. By सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*) *(as supplied; the rest of the sūtra is not printed)* guṇa for the u of the root. By variation, through the accent of the suffix, the word is acute on the end.

पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*): by उदात्तयणोहल् पूर्वात् (*udāttayaṇohal pūrvāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) the acute accent comes on the case ending.

दिवः (*divaḥ*): by ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the acute accent comes on the case ending.

चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*): कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*) is the root. When the perfect (liṭ) comes to it, the substitute kvasu for it. Reduplication and the like for the root; by the accent of the suffix the ā becomes acute. In the nominative singular, since it is marked u-g, the augment num and lengthening.

अनेन (*anena*): the stem idam. When the third-case singular follows, by अनाप्यकः (*anāpyakaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-112 *(the closing bracket is not printed, as supplied; the print has "ತೃತೀಯಾವಿಕವಚನ")*) the substitute anā. By टाजसिजसा (*ṭājasijasā*) *(as supplied; the rest of the sūtra is not printed)* the substitute ina for the case ending. Guṇa.

यक्षि (*yakṣi*): the root yaja; the form is the imperative second person singular. Since it stands after a word that is not a finite verb *(the print has ಅತಿಜಂತ, as supplied)*, the nighāta accent comes.

मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*): by तत्र तस्येव (*tatra tasyeva*) (Pā. Sū. 5-1-116) the suffix vati in the sense of likeness. By the dictum नभोंगिरो मनुषां वत्युपसंख्यानं (*nabhoṃgiro manuṣāṃ vatyupasaṃkhyānaṃ*), since the designation bha comes when vati follows, the change of the preceding s to ru does not come. The initial acute accent of the suffix comes.

शिर (*śira*) *(so printed here; the bhāṣya has ತಿರ, as supplied)*: त्य प्लवनतरणयोः (*tya plavanataraṇayoḥ*) *(so printed, with ತ್ಯ, as supplied)* is the root. In the imperative second person singular the substitute hi for sip. By व्यत्ययो बहुलं (*vyatyayo bahulaṃ*) the vikaraṇa śa comes. Because it is marked c, guṇa does not come. By यूतइद्धातोः (*yūtaiddhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-100) *(the bhāṣya reads ಋತ ಇದ್ದಾತೋ; as supplied)* the substitute i for the vowel ṝ *(printed ಋೂಕಾರ, as supplied)*, which comes with ra following. By अतो हेः (*ato heḥ*) the loss of hi. Since it stands after a word that is not a finite verb *(printed ಅತಿಜಂತ, as supplied)*, the nighāta accent comes.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रीण्यायूं॑षि॒ तव॑ जातवेदस्त्रि॒स्र आ॒जानी॑रु॒षस॑स्ते अग्ने ।  
> ताभि॑र्दे॒वाना॒मवो॑ यक्षि वि॒द्वानथा॑ भव॒ यज॑मानाय॒शंयोः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रीणि । आयूंषि । तव । जातवेदः । तिस्रः । आजानीः । उषसः । ते । अग्ने ।  
> ताभिः । देवानां । अवः । यक्षि । विद्वान् । अथ । भव । यजमानाय । शं । योः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञ तव त्रीण्यायूंषि त्रिविधान्याजौषधिसोमात्मकान्यन्नान्याहारतया कल्पितानि हे अग्ने तस्र उषस एकाहाहीनसत्रगता उषस उषोऽभिमानिन्यस्तिस्रो देवतास्ते तवाजानीर्जनयित्र्यो मातरः। यद्वा । उषोऽभिमानिन्यो देवतास्तवाजानीस्त्वामनुजातास्ति स्रः स्वसारः । तथाच स्वस्यः प्रकृत्य मंत्रः ।
> प्रजामेका रक्षत्यूर्जमेका राष्ट्रमेका रक्षतीति । ताभिरुषोऽभिमानिनीभिर्देवताभिः
> सहितस्त्वमवोऽस्माभिर्दीयमानं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं देवानां यक्षि । यष्टव्यदेवानां प्रयच्छ । अथ अनंतरं विद्वान् जानंस्त्वं यजमानाय शं भव । सुखहेतुर्भव । योश्च सुखस्य मिश्रयिता च भव ॥ तव । युष्मदस्मदोर्जसीत्याद्युदात्तः । तिस्रः । त्रिशब्दस्य स्त्र्यर्थे त्रिचतुरोः स्त्रियावि ति तिसृ इत्यादेशः । अचि र ऋत
> इति रेफादेशः । तिसृभ्यो जस इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्त्वं । आजानीः । जन जनने । जनिघसिभ्यामिण् इति कर्तरि इण् । णित्वादुपधावृद्धिः । वा छ दसीति वर्णदीर्घः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । अवः । अव रक्षणे । असुन्नित्यसुन्। नित्वरः । यक्षि । यजेर्दानार्थस्य
> लेटि रूपं । यजमानाय । पूज्यजोः शानन् । पा ३-२-१२८ । इति यजेः शानन्
> नित्वरः । योः । यु मिश्रण इत्यस्मादन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति विच् । अर्थधातुकलक्षणो गुणः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, knower of all things, has three kinds of food that give life, namely ājya, herbs and Soma; the three dawn-deities of the sacrifices are his sisters or mothers; accompanied by them he is to offer our oblation to the gods and to be a source of happiness for the sacrificer. The grammar tail of the block (accent of तव (*tava*), तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*), the formation of आजानीः (*ājānīḥ*) with the suffix iṇ, अवः (*avaḥ*), यक्षि (*yakṣi*), यजमानाय (*yajamānāya*) with śānan, योः (*yoḥ*) with vic) is transcribed in the block and not explained here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni who know everything that has come into being
- तव (*tava*)—to you
- आयूंषि (*āyūṃṣi*)—foods that give life
- त्रीणि (*trīṇi*)—are of three kinds, namely ājya (clarified butter), herbs and Soma
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni; तिस्रः उषसः (*tisraḥ uṣasaḥ*)—three dawn-deities
- ते (*te*)—to you
- आजानीः (*ājānīḥ*)—sisters born together with you
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—together with those deities
- आवः (*āvaḥ*) *(so printed with a long ā; the Saṃhitā and Pada have ಅವಃ, as supplied)*—the oblation given by us

### Printed p. 353

देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—with the deities in view; यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—offer it as a sacrifice; अथ (*atha*)—thereafter; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) *(the dash is not printed, as supplied)*—you who are wise; यजमानाय (*yajamānāya*)—to the sacrificer; शंयोः (*śaṃyoḥ*)—a bestower of happiness; भव (*bhava*)—be.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who know everything that has come into being, the foods that give you life are of three kinds: ājya, herbs and Soma. And the three dawn-deities are your sisters born together with you. Together with those deities offer, with the deities in view, the oblation given by us as a sacrifice. *(The print has ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನುನ್ನುದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ with a doubled ನ್ನು, as supplied.)* Thereafter, being wise, be a bestower of happiness for the sacrificer.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Three are your existences JATAVEDAS; three, AGNI, are your parent dawns : with them offer the oblation of the gods, and knowing (his wishes) be the bestower of happiness on the institutor of the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On जादवेदः तव त्रीण्ययूंषि (*jādavedaḥ tava trīṇyayūṃṣi*) *(so printed, for ಜಾತವೇದಃ and ತ್ರೀಣ್ಯಾಯೂಂಷಿ, as supplied)*: त्रिविधानि आज्यौषधिसोमात्मकानि अन्नाहारतयो कल्पितानि (*trividhāni ājyauṣadhisomātmakāni annāhāratayo kalpitāni*) *(the line-end hyphen after ಅನ್ನಾಹಾರ is joined; the print has ತಯೋ, as supplied)*. The word jātavedas, having been explained as conveying the meaning जातप्रज्ञ (*jātaprajña*) (of born wisdom), Agni is addressed with this very word. The word āyus is read among the names of food (Nirukta 3-9 *(printed "ನಿ. ೩-೯")*). This word is explained by the author of the Nirukta as used in the sense of lifetime in the ṛk

वात आ वातु भेषजं शंभु मयोभु नो हृदे । प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषत् ॥ (*vāta ā vātu bheṣajaṃ śaṃbhu mayobhu no hṛde | pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-186-1)

Sāyaṇa has explained this word as food, and has explained the meaning that the three kinds of substances, ājya, herbs (and fuel) and Soma, are imagined as food in the form of nourishment for Agni and are offered by the sacrificers.

On तिस्रः उषसः ते आजानीः (*tisraḥ uṣasaḥ te ājānīḥ*): Sāyaṇa has explained two meanings for this sentence. In the first meaning, he has explained the word आजानीः (*ājānīḥ*) as जनयित्र्यः मातरः (*janayitryaḥ mātaraḥ*) (begetting mothers), and has described एकाहाहीनसत्रगताः उषोभिमानिन्यस्तिस्रो देवताः मातरॆः (*ekāhāhīnasatragatāḥ uṣobhimāninyastisro devatāḥ mātarèḥ*) *(the print has ಮಾತರೆಃ and no ಽ in the first ಉಷೋಭಿಮಾನಿನ್ಯ, as supplied)*: the three dawn-deities of the sacrificial days called ekāha, ahīna and satra are in the place of mothers, since on the respective days of the sacrifice they bring Agni into being and make him grow. In the second meaning he has described the word आजानीः (*ājānīḥ*) as used in the sense of अनुजाताः (*anujātāḥ*), sisters who have come into being following him. In this meaning उषोभिमानिन्यो (*uṣobhimāninyo*)

*[The sentence breaks off at the end of the page; the stray line "45" follows it in the supplied text, kept as printed.]*

### Printed p. 354

continues: देवतास्तामनुजाताः तिस्रः स्वसारः (*devatāstāmanujātāḥ tisraḥ svasāraḥ*): the dawn-deities of three times of dawn belonging to the sacrifices beginning with the एकाहवे (*ekāhave*) followed Agni in being born, and are therefore the sisters of Agni (the print has the word ಸ್ವಸ್ಯಗಳು, as supplied). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning so, and has quoted the Śruti, saying that this meaning is stated by the mantra प्रजामेका रक्षति, ऊर्जमेका, राष्ट्रमेका रक्षति (*prajāmekā rakṣati, ūrjamekā, rāṣṭramekā rakṣati*) ("one protects the offspring, one the strength, one the kingdom"). And: उषोभिमानिदेवताभिस्सहितः अस्माभिर्दीयमानं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं यष्टव्यदेवतानां प्रयच्छ (*uṣobhimānidevatābhissahitaḥ asmābhirdīyamānaṃ havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ yaṣṭavyadevatānāṃ prayaccha*): accompanied by the dawn-deities, may Agni, as the sacrificers offer in the several sacrifices, make the food, in the form of the oblation offered to the several deities, reach the several deities; thus the meaning has been explained. *(The print has ತಲಪಿಸಲ and ಅಯಾಯ, as supplied.)*

On निर्द्वान् जानंत्वं यजमानाय सुखहेतुर्भव । योः सुखस्य मिश्रयिता च भव (*nirdvān jānaṃtvaṃ yajamānāya sukhaheturbhava | yoḥ sukhasya miśrayitā ca bhava*) *(the print has ನಿರ್ದ್ವಾನ್ at the beginning, as supplied; the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya has ವಿದ್ವಾನ್ ಜಾನಂಸ್ತ್ವಂ)*: Agni is निर्द्वान् (*nirdvān*) , the all-knowing; and because he knows (the condition of the sacrificer and) all the matters of the sacrificer, the prayer is described that he may be the cause of happiness arising for the sacrificer, and that he may be the one who brings to the sacrificer the pleasures arising from himself.

Yāska: शंयोः शंयुः सुखंयुः (*śaṃyoḥ śaṃyuḥ sukhaṃyuḥ*) अथानः शंयोररपो दधात (*athānaḥ śaṃyorarapo dadhāta*) (the print gives no reference): he has explained the word śaṃyu as the one who mixes happiness and has indicated an example. And further: अथापि शंयोर्बार्हस्पत्य उच्यते (*athāpi śaṃyorbārhaspatya ucyate*)—in the opinion of the teacher called the son of Bṛhaspati, the two words शं, युः (*śaṃ, yuḥ*) are separately indicated; having explained so, he has quoted the mantra

तच्छंयोरावृणीमहे गातुं यज्ञाय गातुं यज्ञपतये दैवीस्स्वस्तिरस्तु नः स्वस्तिर्मानुषेभ्यः ऊर्ध्वं जिगातु भेषजं शंन्नो अस्तु द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे (*tacchaṃyorāvṛṇīmahe gātuṃ yajñāya gātuṃ yajñapataye daivīssvastirastu naḥ svastirmānuṣebhyaḥ ūrdhvaṃ jigātu bheṣajaṃ śaṃnno astu dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade*)

Durgācārya has explained that by the word शंयोः (*śaṃyoḥ*) the quieting of diseases and fears and the mixing of happiness are stated, with शमनयावने उच्येते (*śamanayāvane ucyete*) . The word शंयोः (*śaṃyoḥ*) is explained to be used in this same sense in the ṛks ओमानं शंयोर्ममकाय सूनवे (*omānaṃ śaṃyormamakāya sūnave*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-6) and तच्छंयोस्सुम्न मीमहॆ (*tacchaṃyossumna mīmahè*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-43-4) *(the print has ಮೀಮಹೆ, as supplied)*.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

तव (*tava*): the stem युष्मद् (*yuṣmad*), a form of the sixth case. By युष्मदस्मदोर्जसि (*yuṣmadasmadorjasi*) the acute accent comes on the first syllable.

तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*): the stem tri. When jas follows in the feminine, by त्रिचतुरोःस्त्रीयां तिसृ चतसृ (*tricaturoḥstrīyāṃ tisṛ catasṛ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-99) the substitute tisṛ. By अचिर ऋतः (*acira ṛtaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-100) the substitute ra for the vowel ṛ; the form becomes tisraḥ. By तिसृभ्योजसः (*tisṛbhyojasaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-166) *(the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya has ತಿಸೃಭ್ಯೋ ಜಸಃ, spaced)* the acute accent comes on the case ending.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(continued)*

आजानी— (*ājānī—*): the root jana (to be born). By जनिघसिभ्यामिण् (*janighasibhyāmiṇ*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-569) the suffix iṇ in the active sense. Because it has the mark ṇ, by अतउपधायाः (*ataupadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) vṛddhi for the a of the penultimate syllable of the root. When jas follows, by वाछंदसि (*vāchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-106) the homogeneous long vowel. In a compound with a prefix, by गतिकारकोपपदात् (*gatikārakopapadāt*) *(the sūtra is given in this form, without a number, as supplied)* the accent of the base of the latter member of a kṛt compound (कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛduttarapada prakṛtisvara*)) comes. *(The print has the stem ಆಜಾನೀ for the Saṃhitā form ಆಜಾನೀಃ; the line-end hyphen is joined.)*

अवः— (*avaḥ—*): the root ava (to protect). By सर्वधातुभ्यअसुन् (*sarvadhātubhyaasun*) the suffix asun. Because it has the mark n, by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) the acute accent on the first syllable comes.

यक्षि— (*yakṣi—*): the root yaj is used here in the sense of giving. It is a form of the leṭ, second person singular. The tiṅ-accent (तिजंतनिघातस्वर (*tijaṃtanighātasvara*)), i.e. the lowering of the accent, comes.

यजमानाय— (*yajamānāya—*): the root yaj. By पूज् यज्योः शानन् (*pūj yajyoḥ śānan*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-128) the suffix śānan. Because it has the designation sārvadhātuka, the vikaraṇa śap comes. By आनेमुक् (*ānemuk*) the augment muk. Because the suffix has the mark n, the acute accent on the first syllable comes. It is a form of the fourth case.

योः— (*yoḥ—*): the root yu (to mix). By अन्येभ्योपिदृश्यंते (*anyebhyopidṛśyaṃte*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75) the suffix vic after it. By सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) guṇa for the u of the root. The accent of the base of the latter member of a kṛt compound (कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*)) comes. *(The print has "ಯು ಮಿಶ್ರಣೇ. ಧಾತು" with a full stop after the root-meaning, as supplied.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing Agni, the knower of all that is born: praising you, who are endowed with good qualities, of goodly radiance, well seen by all and worthy of praise, we honour you with oblations. The gods, worshipped by us, such as Indra, made you, unattached to sense-objects and the navel of the ambrosia that is the food of the gods, their messenger who carries the oblations; of the two kinds of messenger, the bearer of news and the doer of work, they made you the doer of work. The grammar tail of the block (the formations of सुदीतिं (*sudītiṃ*), सुदृशं (*sudṛśaṃ*), गृणंतः (*gṛṇaṃtaḥ*), नमस्यामः (*namasyāmaḥ*), दूतं (*dūtaṃ*), अरतिं (*aratiṃ*), अकृण्वन् (*akṛṇvan*)) is transcribed in the block and not explained here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः— (*jātavedaḥ—*)O Agni of born wisdom
- अग्निं— (*agniṃ—*)who are endowed with the qualities of अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*) *(so printed; the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya has ಅಂಗನಾದಿಗುಹೋಪೇತಂ and the Special Topics ಅಗ್ನನಾದಿಗುಣೋಪೇತಂ, as supplied)*
- सुदीतिं— (*sudītiṃ—*)who have excellent radiance
- सुदृशं— (*sudṛśaṃ—*)who are seen to an exceeding degree by all
- ईड्यं— (*īḍyaṃ—*)and are worthy of praise
- त्वा— (*tvā—*)you
- गृणंतः— (*gṛṇaṃtaḥ—*)praising your qualities
- नमस्यामः— (*namasyāmaḥ—*)we worship
- अरतिं— (*aratiṃ—*)who are not attached to sense-objects
- अमृतस्य— (*amṛtasya—*)of the ambrosia which is the food of the gods
- नाभिं— (*nābhiṃ—*)who are the navel-place
- त्वां— (*tvāṃ—*)you
- देवाः— (*devāḥ—*)the gods beginning with Indra
- हव्यवाहं— (*havyavāhaṃ—*)bearing the oblation
- दूतं— (*dūtaṃ—*)as messenger
- अकृण्वन्— (*akṛṇvan—*)made

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni of born wisdom, we who praise your qualities worship you, who are endowed with the qualities of अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*) *(so printed, as above)*, of excellent radiance, seen to an exceeding degree by all, and worthy of praise. The gods beginning with Indra made you, who are not attached to sense-objects and are the navel-place of the ambrosia that is the food of the gods, a messenger who bears the oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
JATAVEDAS, we venerate you, glorifying the briltiant [sic], beautiful, adorable AGNI : the gods have made you their messenger, the disinterested bearer of oblations, the centre of ambrosia.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On जातवेदः— (*jātavedaḥ—*): although the word jātavedas has many kinds of meanings, here the meaning "one who knows all that has been produced" has been stated by जातस्य सर्वस्य वेदिशः (*jātasya sarvasya vediśaḥ*) *(so printed; the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya has ವೇದಿತಾ, as supplied)* and Agni is addressed.

### Printed p. 357

On गृणंतः— (*gṛṇaṃtaḥ—*): this word is used in the sense of त्वद्विषयां स्तुतिं कुर्वाणाः (*tvadviṣayāṃ stutiṃ kurvāṇāḥ*): the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice make praise concerning Agni.

On अग्निं— (*agniṃ—*): अग्ननादिगुणोपेतं (*agnanādiguṇopetaṃ*) . Yāska has explained the meaning of the word agni thus:

अग्निः कस्मात् अग्रणीर्भवति, अग्रंयज्ञेषु प्रणीयते, अंगं नयति सन्नममानः, अक्कोपनो भवतीति स्थौलाष्ठिविर्नक्कोपयति न स्नेहयति त्रिभ्यः आख्यातेभ्यो जायत इति शाकपूणिः । इतादग्दाद्वा नीतात् । सखल्वेतेराकारमादत्ते गकारमनक्तर्वा दहतेर्वा नीः परः (*agniḥ kasmāt agraṇīrbhavati, agraṃyajñeṣu praṇīyate, aṃgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ, akkopano bhavatīti sthaulāṣṭhivirnakkopayati na snehayati tribhyaḥ ākhyātebhyo jāyata iti śākapūṇiḥ | itādagdādvā nītāt | sakhalveterākāramādatte gakāramanaktarvā dahatervā nīḥ paraḥ*)

(Nirukta 7-15)

*(Tentative rendering; the supplied Sanskrit is corrupt in places, for example ಅಕ್ಕೋಪನೋ, ನಕ್ಕೋಪಯತಿ, ಸನ್ನಮಮಾನಃ, ಅನಕ್ತರ್ವಾ, kept as supplied, and the line-end hyphens are joined:)* "Why is it Agni? He is the leader (agraṇī); he is led at the front (agram) in the sacrifices; he leads the limb (aṅgam) ... ; he is not angry (so Sthaulāṣṭhīvi: he does not enrage, he does not anoint); he arises from three verbs, says Śākapūṇi: from ita, or from akta or dagdha, or from nīta; he takes the letter ā from the root i, the letter g from añj or from dah, and nī follows." The explanation of this has been given earlier.

Sāyaṇa has stated that Agni is one who keeps what is joined with his pervasion under his own control; and, because the sacrificers find that Agni has these qualities, namely a radiance that is auspicious, fitness to be seen by all and fitness to be praised, he has explained the meaning एवंविधं त्वां नमस्यामः (*evaṃvidhaṃ tvāṃ namasyāmaḥ*): "we worship such a one, Agni, offering oblations". By this the abundant majesty of Agni (the print has माहात्म (*māhātma*), as supplied) is made clear.

On देवाः— (*devāḥ—*): this word too is explained by Yāska:

दानाद्वा दीपनाद्वा द्योतनाद्वा द्युस्थानो भव तीति वा देवः (*dānādvā dīpanādvā dyotanādvā dyusthāno bhava tīti vā devaḥ*)

(Nirukta 7-15)

(The word deva: from giving, or from shining, or from illumining, or one who dwells in the place of heaven.) For this word Sāyaṇa has given the meaning अस्माभिर्यजनीया इंद्रादयः (*asmābhiryajanīyā iṃdrādayaḥ*): the gods beginning with Indra, who are worshipped by us the sacrificers, have taken Agni as their messenger, दूतमकृण्वन्— (*dūtamakṛṇvan—*). And दूतो हि द्विविधः वार्ताहारी कार्यकारी चेति तत्र कार्यकारिणं दूतमकार्षुः (*dūto hi dvividhaḥ vārtāhārī kāryakārī ceti tatra kāryakāriṇaṃ dūtamakārṣuḥ*): since a messenger is of two kinds, one who brings news and one who does the work, Agni, a doer of work, is described as a divine messenger controlled by the gods.

The words अरतिं, अमृतस्य नाभिं, हव्यवाहं (*aratiṃ, amṛtasya nābhiṃ, havyavāhaṃ*) are used as epithets of the word "messenger"; therefore the point is stated that Agni is a messenger different from the well-known worldly messenger, or superior to him in qualities.

For the word अरतिं (*aratiṃ*) he has explained the meaning न विद्यते रतिः विषयेषु प्रीतिः यस्य— (*na vidyate ratiḥ viṣayeṣu prītiḥ yasya—*): one who has no delight in sense-objects, in things to be enjoyed that are fit for enjoyment; and विषयेष्टसक्तं (*viṣayeṣṭasaktaṃ*) : one without attachment to sense-objects; thus the quality of Agni is made clear.

On अमृतस्य— (*amṛtasya—*): देवान्नभूतायाः सुधायाः (*devānnabhūtāyāḥ sudhāyāḥ*): since ambrosia is food for the gods, Agni is described as the navel, the place of origin, of this ambrosia.

On हव्यवाहं— (*havyavāhaṃ—*): the meaning "one who carries the oblation offered by the sacrificers" is explained. By this the difference from other messengers is stated: Agni has been made by the gods the divine messenger who has no attachment to sense-objects, who is the place of origin (उत्पत्तिस्माननाद (*utpattismānanāda*), so printed for ಸ್ಥಾನ, as supplied) of the ambrosia that is the food of the gods, and who carries the oblations for the gods. Agni, who has qualities greater than those of the other well-known messengers, the gods

*[The sentence breaks off at the end of the window, at the end of p. 357 as supplied (the last words are ಅಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನು ದೇವತೆಗಳು).]*

### Printed p. 358

has made a doer-of-work messenger; therefore the sense is made clear that the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice praise this Agni, offer oblations and worship him.
