## Sūkta 20 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twentieth sūkta** (ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निमुषसमिति पंचर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका ।
> अग्निमुषसमाद्यांते वैश्वदेव्याविति । गाथी हेति हशब्दप्रयोगादस्यापि सूक्तस्य
> गाथी ऋषिः । प्रथमापंचम्यौ वैश्वदेवताके शिष्टास्ति स आग्नेय्यः ॥ अस्य सूक्त-
> स्योक्तो विनियोगः ॥ मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रेऽग्निर्नेतेत्येषा धाय्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> अग्निर्नेता त्वं सोम क्रतुभिः पिन्वंत्यप इति धाय्याः । अ. ५-१४ ॥ इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with अग्निमुषसं (*agnimuṣasaṃ*) is the eighth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said अग्निमुषसमाद्यांते वैश्वदेव्य (*agnimuṣasamādyāṃte vaiśvadevya*). Since the word ha is used in गाथी हेति (*gāthī heti*), the Ṛṣi of this sūkta too, like that of the previous sūkta, is the one named गाथी (*gāthī*). The first and the last Ṛks of this sūkta have the Viśvedevas (all-gods) as deity, *(the page ends here; the sentence continues on p. 400)*

### Printed p. 400

and the remaining Ṛks have Agni as deity. The viniyoga of this sūkta too has been stated before. And, as for using the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta, the Ṛk अग्निर्नेता भग इव (*agnirnetā bhaga iva*), as a dhāyyā mantra at the time of reciting the mantras of the Marutvatīya-śastra, it is set out in the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra अग्निर्नेता (*agnirnetā*) / त्वं सोम क्रतुभिः पिन्नंत्यप इति धाय्याः (*tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinnaṃtyapa iti dhāyyāḥ*) (Āśv. 5-14). *[The Sanskrit introduction has the same sūtra with ಪಿನ್ವಂತ್ಯಪ (with ವ), the Anuvāda has ಪಿನ್ನಂತ್ಯಪ (with ನ); as supplied. The Sanskrit introduction has ಗಾಥೀ ಹೇತಿ and says that the first and last Ṛks are Vaiśvadevī (ಅಗ್ನಿಮುಷಸಮಾದ್ಯಾಂತೇ ವೈಶ್ವದೇವ್ಯ is printed there as ಅಗ್ನಿಮುಷಸಮಾದ್ಯಾಂತೇ ವೈಶ್ವದೇವ್ಯಾವಿತಿ); as supplied.]*

*[A line "ಸೂಕ್ತ-೨೦" (Sūkta 20) stands before the data, as supplied.]*

**Sūkta data .** Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 20. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 1; Varga 20. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: गाथी (*gāthī*). Devatā: Ṛks 1 and 5 विश्वेदेवाः (*viśvedevāḥ*); Ṛks 2 to 4 अग्निः (*agniḥ*) (printed "೧, ೫ . ವಿಶ್ವೇದೇವಾಃ ।೨-೪ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ"). Chandas: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निमु॒षस॑म॒श्विना॑ दधि॒क्रां व्यु॑ष्टिषु हवते॒ वह्नि॑रु॒क्थैः ।  
> सु॒ज्योति॑षो नः शृण्वंतं दे॒वाः सु॒जोष॑सो अध्व॒रं वा॑वशा॒नाः॥

> *agnimuṣasamaśvinā dadhikrāṃ vyuṣṭiṣu havate vahnirukthaiḥ |*  
> *sujyotiṣo naḥ śṛṇvaṃtaṃ devāḥ sujoṣaso adhvaraṃ vāvaśānāḥ‖*

*[The Saṃhitā carries no Ṛk number at the end in the supplied text; none is written. The Saṃhitā has शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*) where the Pada has शृण्वंतु (*śṛṇvaṃtu*); as supplied.]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निं । उषसं । अश्विना । दधिक्रां । विउष्टिषु । हवते । वह्निः । उक्तैः ।  
> सुज्योतिषः । नः । शृण्वंतु । देवाः । सजोषसः । अध्वरं । वावशानाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गाथी ब्रूते । वह्निर्हविषां प्रापयिताग्निर्व्युष्टिषूषसां व्युच्छनेष्वग्निं
> यजनीयं देवमुषसमुषोभिमानिनीं देवशामश्विना अश्विन् देवौ दधिक्रां ।
> दधिक्रावा नाम कश्चिद्देवः तं दधिक्रावाणं । एतान्नेवानुक्कैः शस्त्रैः शंसनसाधनैर-
> प्रगीतमंत्रात्मकैः सूक्तैर्हवते । आह्वयति । सुज्योतिषः सुष्टु द्योतमाना
> नोऽध्वरमस्मत्संबंधिनमिमं यज्ञं नावशानाः कामयमानाः सजोषसः परस्परं
> संगता भूत्वा सर्वे देवास्त्रदाह्वानं शृण्वंतु ॥ दधिक्रां । क्रमु पादविक्षेपे !
> दधीत्युपपदे जनसनखनक्रमगम इति विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यादित्याकारः । कृदु-
> त्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । हवते ह्वयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणं । सुज्योतिषः ।

### Printed p. 401

> सुष्टु द्योतमाना इति विग्रहे द्युत दीप्तावित्यस्य द्युतेरिसिन्नादेश जः । उ. २-१११ ।
> इतीसिन्मृत्ययो दकारस्य जकारः कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । बहुव्रीहिपक्षे तु नञ्-
> सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तता स्यात् । यथा । सुज्योतिषो अक्तवस्ता । अभि
> ष्युः । ऋग्वे १०-८९-१५ इत्यत्रांतोदात्तता । तस्मादत्र नायं समासः किंतु तत्पु-
> रुष एव शृण्वंतु । श्रु श्रवण इत्यस्माच्छुवः शृ चेति श्नुस्तत्संनियोगेन धातोः
> शृ इत्यादेशः । निघातः । वावशानाः । वश कांतावित्यस्य यज्लुकि रूपं । अभ्या-
> सस्य दीर्घोऽकित इति दीर्घः । व्यत्ययेन शानच् . चित्स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, bearer of oblations, invokes at the dawns Agni, Uṣas, the Aśvins and Dadhikrā with śastra-hymns; may the united shining gods hear." The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya is transcribed above, not explained.

*[Oddities of the supplied bhāṣya, kept as supplied: देवशामश्विना (*devaśāmaśvinā*), नावशानाः (*nāvaśānāḥ*) (for वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*)), देवास्त्रदाह्वानं (*devāstradāhvānaṃ*), एतान्नेवानुक्कैः (*etānnevānukkaiḥ*) and अभि (*abhi*) / ष्युः (*ṣyuḥ*) (broken across the line) look like misprints.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

वह्निः (*vahniḥ*): the Agni who carries the oblation. व्युष्टिषु (*vyuṣṭiṣu*): at the times of the rising of Uṣas. अग्निं (*agniṃ*): the sacrificial fire. उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*): the goddess Uṣas. अश्विना (*aśvinā*): the Aśvin deities. दधिक्रां (*dadhikrāṃ*): the deity named Dadhikrāvan. उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*): praying with hymns of the form of śastras (so printed; the Pada has उक्तैः (*uktaiḥ*)). हवते (*havate*): calls. सुज्योतिषः (*sujyotiṣaḥ*): those possessed of exceeding radiance. अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*): the sacrifice. नावशानाः (*nāvaśānāḥ*): those who desire (so printed; the Saṃhitā has वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*)). सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*): those who are united with one another. देवाः (*devāḥ*): the gods. नः (*naḥ*): our praise. शृण्वंतु (*śṛṇvaṃtu*): let them hear.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who carries the oblation, at the very time of dawn prays to and calls the sacrificial fire, the goddess Uṣas (printed "ಉಪೋದೇವತೆ", with ಪ for ಷ), the Aśvin deities and the deity named Dadhikrāvan with hymns of the form of śastras. May the gods, who possess exceeding radiance, desire the sacrifice and are united with one another, hear our praises.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The bearer (of the oblation) invokes with praises at the break of day, Agni, the dawn, the Ashwins, and Dadhikra : may the resplendent divinities, desirous of our sacrifice, hear in unison (the invocation).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is said that the Ṛṣi named गाधि (*gādhi*) (so printed here; elsewhere गाथी (*gāthī*)) praises Agni.

वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—हविषां प्रापयिता अग्निः (*haviṣāṃ prāpayitā agniḥ*) । Sāyaṇa explains that Agni is the one who performs the work of conveying to each deity the oblation that the sacrificers have offered to the gods. The Nirukta-kāras (printed "ಸಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು") have commented on the word वह्नि (*vahni*) showing many kinds of usage: the word वह्नि (*vahni*) is read also among the names of the horse (Nirukta 2-27). *(The page, and the window, end here; the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 and the grammar continue on p. 402.)*

### Printed p. 402

The following verse is cited as an example of the use of the word वह्नि (*vahni*):

न जामये तान्वो रिक्षमारैक् चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानं । यदी मातरो जनयंत वह्निमन्यः कर्ता सुकृतोरन्य ऋन्फन् ॥ (*na jāmaye tānvo rikṣamāraik cakāra garbhaṃ saniturnidhānaṃ | yadī mātaro janayaṃta vahnimanyaḥ kartā sukṛtoranya ṛnphan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-31-3)

Durgācārya (printed "ದುರ್ಗಾಚಾರ್ಯರು") has given here for the word वह्नि (*vahni*) the meaning प्रोढारं पुत्रं (*proḍhāraṃ putraṃ*) ("bearer, son").

*[The citation as supplied has ಸನಿತುರ್ನಿಧಾನಂ and ಋನ್ಫನ್ (the latter looks like a misprint); kept as supplied.]*

Another verse:

मेद्यंतु ते वह्नयो येभिरीयसेरिषण्यन् वीळयस्वा वनस्पते । अयूया धृष्टो अभिगूर्या त्वं नेष्वात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब- ऋतुभिः ॥ (*medyaṃtu te vahnayo yebhirīyaseriṣaṇyan vīḷayasvā vanaspate | ayūyā dhṛṣṭo abhigūryā tvaṃ neṣvātsomaṃ draviṇodaḥ piba- ṛtubhiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3)

Here the meaning is described as प्रोढारः अश्वा: (*proḍhāraḥ aśvā:*), "horses that bear a burden". *[The citation breaks inside a word at the line end (ಪಿಬ- / ಋತುಭಿಃ), as supplied.]*

दधिक्रां (*dadhikrāṃ*)—दधिक्रावा नाम कश्चिद्देवः तं दधिक्रावाणं । (*dadhikrāvā nāma kaściddevaḥ taṃ dadhikrāvāṇaṃ |*) The Nirukta-kāra (printed "ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರು", as supplied) read the word dadhikrāvā among the names of the horse (Nirukta 2-27) and explained: दधिक्रा इत्येतत् दधत् क्रामतीति वा दधत् क्रंदतीति वा दधदाकारी भवतीति वा । (*dadhikrā ityetat dadhat krāmatīti vā dadhat kraṃdatīti vā dadhadākārī bhavatīti vā |*) — "carrying (the rider) it moves about, or it makes a sound, or, bearing the rider, it takes a certain form". Yāska, after saying अथातो मध्यमस्थानदेवताः (*athāto madhyamasthānadevatāḥ*) ("now, therefore, the deities of the middle region"), cited the Ṛk

आ दधिक्राः शवसा पंच कृष्टीः सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान । सहस्रसाः शतसा वाज्यर्वा पृणक्तु मध्वा समिमा वचांसि ॥ (*ā dadhikrāḥ śavasā paṃca kṛṣṭīḥ sūrya iva jyotiṣāpastatāna | sahasrasāḥ śatasā vājyarvā pṛṇaktu madhvā samimā vacāṃsi ‖*) (printed "ಪು. ಸಂ." for "ಋ. ಸಂ."; 4-38-10)

and explained that the god Dadhikrā is reckoned among the deities of the middle region. Sāyaṇa has explained the word as a well-known god named Dadhikrāvan.

अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—यजनीयं देवं । (*yajanīyaṃ devaṃ |*) Yāska explained the meaning of the word agni by sentences such as अग्रणीर्भवति, अग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयते, अंगं नयति सन्नममानः (*agraṇīrbhavati, agraṃ yajñeṣu praṇīyate, aṃgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ*) (Nirukta 7-14). Sāyaṇa has explained it as the god worthy of the sacrifice (printed "ಯೋಗಾರ್ಹನಾದ", "worthy of yoga", as supplied), and has explained that Agni, who carries to the respective deities the oblations offered by the sacrificers, after the time of dawn has passed invites to the sacrifice, with mantras that praise and extol the respective deities, the god who receives the oblation in the sacrifice, the deity presiding over dawn (printed "ಉಪೋಭಿಮಾನಿ", with ಪ for ಷ), the Aśvin deities and the god named Dadhikrāvan.

अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—अस्मत्संबंधिनं इमं यज्ञं । (*asmatsaṃbaṃdhinaṃ imaṃ yajñaṃ |*) The word अध्वर (*adhvara*) is read by Yāska among the names of sacrifice (Nirukta 3-19) and among the names of the atmosphere (Nirukta 3-10), and is explained: अध्वर इति यज्ञनाम, ध्वरतिर्हिंसाकर्म तत्पतिषेधः (*adhvara iti yajñanāma, dhvaratirhiṃsākarma tatpatiṣedhaḥ*) (Nirukta 1-8) *[ತತ್ಪತಿಷೇಧಃ as supplied]*. Sāyaṇa has explained that all the gods, who desire the sacrifice performed by the sacrificers and shine with lustre, having assembled together, should hear Agni's invocation and come; thus the sacrificers' wish is set out.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 403, noted not translated. अश्विना (*aśvinā*): the dual, with the substitute ā by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. 7-1-39). दधिक्रां (*dadhikrāṃ*): root क्रमु पादविक्षेपे (*kramu pādavikṣepe*); with dadhi as upapada, the affix viC by जनसन- खनक्रमगम (*janasana- khanakramagama*) (Pā. 3-2-67); when it follows, ātva of the root by विड्वनोरनु- नासिकस्यात् (*viḍvanoranu- nāsikasyāt*) (Pā. 6-4-41); the kṛd-uttarapada accent by गतिकारकोपपदात् (*gatikārakopapadāt*). व्युष्टिषु (*vyuṣṭiṣu*): prefix vi; root उछी विवासे (*uchī vivāse*); the affix ktin in the sense of the action; ṣatva of the chakāra of the root by व्रश्च- भृस्टसृज (*vraśca- bhṛsṭasṛja*); ṭa-substitute for the ta of the affix by ṣṭutva; the prakṛti-accent of the gati (vi) by तादौच नितिकृत्यतौ (*tādauca nitikṛtyatau*) (Pā. 6-2-50) (the reference is broken over two lines, as supplied). हवते (*havate*): root ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च (*hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*); laṭ, third person singular, the affix ta; etva; śap; samprasāraṇa by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*); guṇa and avādeśa of the u; the lowered accent because it follows a non-finite word (so printed). सुज्योतिषः (*sujyotiṣaḥ*): the vigraha सुष्टु द्योतमाना (*suṣṭu dyotamānā*); root द्युत दीप्तौ (*dyuta dīptau*); the affix isan by द्युतेरिसन्नादेश जः (*dyuterisannādeśa jaḥ*) (printed "ಉ. ಸೂ. ೨-೨೬೭", whereas the bhāṣya on p. 401 gives a different Uṇādi number for the same rule; as supplied); ja for the initial da; ṣatva; guṇa; the kṛd-uttarapada accent, the initial acute because the affix is nit-marked; if a bahuvrīhi were made, the final acute would come by नञ्सुभ्यां (*nañsubhyāṃ*) (Pā. 6-2-172), as in सुज्योतिषो अक्तवस्ता अभि षुः (*sujyotiṣo aktavastā abhi ṣuḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-15) (the bhāṣya on p. 401 has ಅಭಿ / ಷ್ಯುಃ there); therefore a tatpuruṣa is made. शृण्वंतु (*śṛṇvaṃtu*): root श्रु श्रवणे (*śru śravaṇe*); loṭ, third person plural, anta for jhi, u for i; the vikaraṇa śnu by श्रुवः शृच (*śruvaḥ śṛca*) (Pā. 3-1-74) and the substitute śṛ for the root; ṇatva; no guṇa of the u because the affix is marked ñit (printed "ಜಿತ್ವ", as supplied); yaṇ; the lowered accent. नावशानाः (*nāvaśānāḥ*) (so printed as the head-word; the Saṃhitā has ವಾವಶಾನಾಃ): root वश कांतौ (*vaśa kāṃtau*); yaṅ with its luk in the intensive sense; reduplication; lengthening of the reduplicative syllable by आदिहल्‌शेषः दीर्घोकितः (*ādihalśeṣaḥ dīrghokitaḥ*) (Pā. 7-4-83); śānac in the place of laṭ by व्यत्ययो बहुलं (*vyatyayo bahulaṃ*); luk of śap; the final acute by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. 6-1-163), the affix being cit-marked.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, your three foods, three stations, three tongues and three bodies desired by the gods; with those bodies, attentive, protect our praises." The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya is transcribed above, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*): O Agni. ते (*te*): to you. वाजिना (*vājinā*): foods. त्री (*trī*): three. षधस्था (*ṣadhasthā*): your places (so printed, without the initial ಸ; the Saṃhitā has the same split). त्री (*trī*): three. ऋतजात (*ṛtajāta*): O Agni, born in the sacrifices that are of the nature of truth. ते (*te*): to you. पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*): those that fill the bellies of the gods. जिह्वाः (*jihvāḥ*): tongues. तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*): three. ते (*te*): to you. देववाताः (*devavātāḥ*): desired by the gods. तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*): bodies. तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*): three. ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*): with all these limbs. नः (*naḥ*): of us, your praisers. गिरः (*giraḥ*): the words of praise. अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*): with an attentive mind. पाहि (*pāhi*): protect.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the foods that you have are of three kinds. The places that you have are also three. O Agni, born in the sacrifices that are of the nature of truth, in order to fill the bellies of the gods, those that you have *[the supplied text, and this window, end here in the middle of the sentence; the Bhāvārtha continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 405

tongues are three. You have three kinds of bodies desired by the gods. With all these limbs also, with an attentive mind, protect the words of praise of us, your praisers.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, born of sacrifice, three are your viands; three your abiding places; three the tongues satisfying (the gods): three verily are your forms, acceptable to the deities, and with them never heedless (of our wishes), be propitious to our praises.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

श्री वाजिना (*śrī vājinā*)—Addressing Agni, the word वाजिना (*vājinā*) is explained as "food", and it is described that the three kinds of things offered by the sacrificers, namely ghee, herbs and Soma (these three), are food for Agni. *[The head-word is printed ಶ್ರೀ for ತ್ರೀ, as in the bhāṣya.]*

श्री षधस्था (*śrī ṣadhasthā*)—त्रीणि आग्नीध्रीयादीनि धिष्ण्यानि स्थानानि । यद्वा एकाहाहीन- सत्राख्यानि त्रीणि स्थानानि यद्वा त्रयोलोकाः । (*trīṇi āgnīdhrīyādīni dhiṣṇyāni sthānāni | yadvā ekāhāhīna- satrākhyāni trīṇi sthānāni yadvā trayolokāḥ |*) Agni is described as dwelling in the three places, beginning with the Āgnīdhrīya, prepared in the sacrificial hall in the order prescribed by the rules; or as abiding in the three kinds of kratu known as Ekāha, Ahīna and Satra; or as pervading the three worlds, earth, heaven and the nether world (pātāḷa). *[The head-word is printed ಶ್ರೀ ಷಧಸ್ಥಾ, as supplied.]*

ऋतजात (*ṛtajāta*)—With this word Agni is addressed. Yāska has described that the word ऋत (*ṛta*) is used in two senses, सत्यं वा यज्ञं वा (*satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā*) (Nirukta 4-19). Here Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as सत्यभूतेषु यज्ञेषु समुत्पन्न (*satyabhūteṣu yajñeṣu samutpanna*): Agni is born in the sacrifices that are of the nature of truth.

पूर्वीः तिस्रः जिह्वाः (*pūrvīḥ tisraḥ jihvāḥ*)—Although पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*) is read among the names of the old (purāṇa) (Nirukta 3-20), Sāyaṇa here explains the word पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*) as पूरयित्र्यः (*pūrayitryaḥ*) ("fillers"): the three varieties of Agni, beginning with the Gārhapatya, which satisfy the gods by offering food to them, are the tongues of Agni.

तिस्रः तन्नः (*tisraḥ tannaḥ*)—पवमान पावक शुच्यात्मकानि त्रीणि शरीराणि । (*pavamāna pāvaka śucyātmakāni trīṇi śarīrāṇi |*) The Nirukta-kāras (printed "ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು") cited the Ṛk

त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिस्तमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस्परि । त्वं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नृणां नृपते जायसे शुचिः । (*tvamagne dyubhistvamāśuśukṣaṇistamadbhyastvamaśmanaspari | tvaṃ vanebhyastvamoṣadhībhyastvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1)

*[The reference is printed with a closing bracket and no opening one, and the Ṛk is printed with ತಮದ್ಭ್ಯಃ, as supplied.]*

and explained शुचिः शोचतेज्वलतिकर्मणः ज्वलति (*śuciḥ śocatejvalatikarmaṇaḥ jvalati*): the root शुच् (*śuc*) gives the sense "to burn", and the word derived from it, शुचि (*śuci*), denotes Agni, and this Agni is the terrestrial fire.

### Printed p. 406

Agni is pavamāna, pāpaka (so printed, for pāvaka) and śuci: he purifies the place where he is, burns the impurities of the things connected with him and so purifies them, and is blazing; for this reason it is described that Agni pervades these three kinds of bodies.

Pervading the sacrifices of the form of Ekāha, Ahīna and Satra, or the three worlds, and being born in the respective sacrifices, Agni, with the bodies called pavamāna, pāvaka and śuci, which the gods love, offers to the gods, with the three tongues beginning with the Gārhapatya, the foods of the form of ghee, herbs and Soma that are offered to the gods, and thus produces satisfaction; in this way the place, form (body) and work of Agni are explained.

ताभिः अप्रयुच्छन् नः गिरः पाहि (*tābhiḥ aprayucchan naḥ giraḥ pāhi*)—अप्रमाद्यन् सावधानो भूत्वा तनूभिः आस्माकं स्तोतृणां स्तोत्रशस्त्रादीनि वाक्यानि पालय (*apramādyan sāvadhāno bhūtvā tanūbhiḥ āsmākaṃ stotṛṇāṃ stotraśastrādīni vākyāni pālaya*)—may Agni, being attentive (watchful), protect with his respective bodies the hymns recited by the praising sacrificers, that is, listen and hear them; thus the sacrificers' wish is described.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed page 406, noted not translated. श्री (*śrī*) (so printed for ತ್ರೀ): luk of śi in the neuter by शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulaṃ*) (Pā. 6-1-70). तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*): the word tri; in the feminine, before jas, the substitute tisṛ by त्रिचतुरोः स्त्रीयां तिसृचतस्य (*tricaturoḥ strīyāṃ tisṛcatasya*) (so printed); as an exception to guṇa, the substitute ra by अचिरऋतः (*aciraṛtaḥ*); the udātta accent of the case ending by तिसृभ्यो जसः (*tisṛbhyo jasaḥ*) (Pā. 6-1-166). जिह्वाः (*jihvāḥ*): root लिह आस्वादने (*liha āsvādane*); the affix van, by the nipātana in सेवा यह्वा जिह्वा ग्रीवा प्वा मीवाः (*sevā yahvā jihvā grīvā pvā mīvāḥ*) (Uṇ. 1-152); ja in place of the la of the root; no guṇa, because of the nipātana; the final udātta by vyatyaya although the affix is nit-marked. ऋतजात (*ṛtajāta*): ṛteṣu jātaḥ; the nighāta accent in the vocative. तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*): the svarita accent of the case ending by उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ*) (Pā. 8-2-4). देववाताः (*devavātāḥ*): root वा गतिगंधनयोः (*vā gatigaṃdhanayoḥ*); the affix kta in the passive by निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) (Pā. 3-2-102); because a word ending in kta in the passive follows, the prakṛti-accent of the first member by तृतीयाकर्मणि (*tṛtīyākarmaṇi*) (printed Pā. 9-2-48, as supplied). पाहि (*pāhi*): पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*), of the adādi class; loṭ, second person singular; the nighāta accent because it follows a non-finite word. अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*): युच्छ प्रमादे (*yuccha pramāde*); śatṛ for laṭ; when the negative nañ is compounded as a tatpuruṣa, the prakṛti-accent of the first member (nañ) by तत्पुरुषेतुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣetulyārtha*) (Pā. 6-2-2).)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the gods placed in you, the immortal, many splendours, and you hold the many tricks of the deceitful asuras; ward them off and protect our sacrifice." The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya is transcribed above, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—shining
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—knowing all
- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—being the lord of food; O Agni (अग्ने (*agne*))
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—who is free from the nature of death
- तव (*tava*)—your (the gods who are connected with you)
- भूरीणि (*bhūrīṇi*)—in great number (of many kinds)
- नाम (*nāma*)—splendours
- त्वे (*tve*)—in you
- संदधुः (*saṃdadhuḥ*)—they have placed
- विश्वमिन्व (*viśvaminva*)—O you who give satisfaction to the whole world
- पृष्टबंधो (*pṛṣṭabaṃdho*)—O Agni, who are a kinsman of the praisers who are seekers
- मायिनां (*māyināṃ*)—of the deceitful asuras
- पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—of great number; याः मायाः (*yāḥ māyāḥ*)—whatever deceiving powers there are (these also are placed in you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, shining, all-knowing, and lord of food, the gods who are connected with you, the deathless one, have placed in you splendours of many kinds. Moreover, since the power of deceit that is in the deceitful asuras is also placed in you, restrain the asuras by that power and protect our sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Divine Agni, knowing all that exists and distributor of food, many are the names of you, who are immortal, satisfier of all men, friend of the suppliant, the gods have deposited in yon [sic] whatever are the delusions of the deluding (Rakshasas).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this mantra Agni is addressed by the words देव (*deva*), जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*) and स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*). The meaning of the word देव (*deva*) is explained as "shining", glowing with brilliant splendours. Of the four ways in which Yāska has explained the word जातवेद (*jātaveda*) (printed ಜಾತವೇದಶ್ಯಬ್ದಕ್ಕೆ, as supplied), the sense जातप्रज्ञ (*jātaprajña*), "one of born wisdom, a knower", is given. Since the word स्वधा (*svadhā*) is stated among the names of food (Nirukta 3-9), the meaning "Agni possesses food" is given.

नाम (*nāma*)—नामानि तेजांसि, नमयंति सर्वानपि स्वाश्रयभूतान् पुरुषानिति नामानि तेजांसि (*nāmāni tejāṃsi, namayaṃti sarvānapi svāśrayabhūtān puruṣāniti nāmāni tejāṃsi*): because they make low (bend) the men who have taken refuge in him, the word नाम (*nāma*) is explained as "splendours". *[The Kannada reads ಪುರುಷಾನಿತಿ, the bhāṣya block above reads ನುರುಷಾನ್; both as supplied.]*

अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—मरणधर्मरहितस्य (*maraṇadharmarahitasya*): this word is explained as an epithet of Agni, and the meaning is described thus: the gods have placed in Agni, who is free from the nature of death, the भूरीणि नाम (*bhūrīṇi nāma*), many splendours.

विश्वमिन्व (*viśvaminva*)—विश्वमिन्वति प्रीणयतीति (*viśvaminvati prīṇayatīti*): because he gladdens the whole world, Agni is addressed with this word, which is understood as "satisfier of the universe". Yāska

### Printed p. 409

has cited this Ṛk:

व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयंतां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुंभमानाः । देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ॥ (*vyacasvatīrurviyā vi śrayaṃtāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śuṃbhamānāḥ | devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Sū. 10-110-5)

*[The reference is printed "ಋ. ಸೂ. ೧೦-೧೧೦-೫" (Ṛ. Sū. 10-110-5), as supplied.]*

Durgācārya has explained the meaning of the word विश्वमिन्व (*viśvaminva*) as the sacrificial implement that is the means of attaining everything: विश्वं अभिः एति (*viśvaṃ abhiḥ eti*).

पृष्ट बंधो (*pṛṣṭa baṃdho*)—अपेक्षितफलप्रश्नविषयाणां स्तोत्यणां बंधो (*apekṣitaphalapraśnaviṣayāṇāṃ stotyaṇāṃ baṃdho*): Agni is described as one who is pleased by the hymns of those who wish to attain what they desire, and as one who delights the whole world (printed ಪಂಚವೆಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ, for ಪ್ರಪಂಚ…, as supplied). Then, मायिनां पूर्वीः मायाः देवास्त्वयि संप्रयुयुजिरे तास्त्वयि संति (*māyināṃ pūrvīḥ māyāḥ devāstvayi saṃprayuyujire tāstvayi saṃti*): since the gods have placed in Agni all the abundant deceits belonging to the asuras who have practised deceit, यज्ञ विघ्न कारिणां मायिनां मायाः परिहृत्य अस्मदीयं यज्ञं पालय (*yajña vighna kāriṇāṃ māyināṃ māyāḥ parihṛtya asmadīyaṃ yajñaṃ pālaya*)—let Agni remove all the deceits of the asuras who cause obstacles to the sacrifices, and protect the sacrifices of us, the sacrificers; thus the wish of the sacrificers is described. Here the word पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*) is explained in the sense भूयसीः (*bhūyasīḥ*) ("abundant").

*[The Kannada ಸ್ತೋತ್ಯಣಾಂ is as supplied (the bhāṣya block of Ṛk 3 has ಸ್ತೋತ್ಕಣಾಂ).]*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed pages 409 and 410, noted not translated. स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*): when the sense "he has svadhā" is intended, the affix matup by तदस्यास्ति (*tadasyāsti*); va for the ma of matup by मादुपधायाश्च (*mādupadhāyāśca*); ru in the vocative by मतुवसोरुः संबुद्भौ (*matuvasoruḥ saṃbudbhau*) (Pā. 8-3-1) (printed ಸಂಬುದ್ಭೌ, as supplied); the nighāta accent by आमंत्रितस्य च (*āmaṃtritasya ca*) (Pā. 8-1-19). अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*): setting aside the accent of nañ, the udātta on the first syllable of the second member by नञ्तोजरमरमित्रमृताः (*nañtojaramaramitramṛtāḥ*) (Pā. 6-2-116). नाम (*nāma*): the root णमु प्रह्वत्वे (*ṇamu prahvatve*); the affix manin by nipātana, नामन् सीमन् व्योमन् (*nāman sīman vyoman*) (Uṇ. 4-590), with loss of the ma of the root and lengthening of the a; luk of the case ending in the plural by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. 7-1-39); the first syllable udātta because the affix is nit-marked. मायिनाम् (*māyinām*): the affix ini by व्रीह्यादिभ्यश्च (*vrīhyādibhyaśca*) (Pā. 5-2-116), the word being read in the vrīhi group; loss of the preceding a by यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) (Pā. 6-4-148); the i udātta by the affix accent; the form ends in the genitive plural. विश्वमिन्व (*viśvaminva*): the root इवि व्याप्तिप्रीणनयोः (*ivi vyāptiprīṇanayoḥ*); with the word viśva as upapada, the affix aṇ by कर्मण्यण् (*karmaṇyaṇ*) (Pā. 3-1-2); because the i of the root is a marker, num is added already at the time of the root's enumeration by इदितोनुंधातोः (*iditonuṃdhātoḥ*) (Pā. 7-1-58), so that no guṇa comes, there being no laghūpadha; no luk of the accusative in the compound by तत्परुषे कृतिबहुलं (*tatparuṣe kṛtibahulaṃ*) (Pā. 6-3-14); the nighāta accent in the vocative by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. 8-1-19). संदधुः (*saṃdadhuḥ*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*) with the prefix sam; liṭ, third person plural; prohibition of nighāta by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यं (*yadvṛttānnityaṃ*) (Pā. 8-1-66), so the affix accent remains; the anudātta accent of the prefix sam by तिजचोदात्तवति (*tijacodāttavati*) (Pā. 8-1-71). पृष्टबंधो (*pṛṣṭabaṃdho*): the root प्रच्छङ्ञिप्पायां (*pracchaṅñippāyāṃ*) (printed so); the affix kta in the passive by निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*); ṛ-vowel and samprasāraṇa for the r of the root by ग्रहिंज्यावयिव्यधि (*grahiṃjyāvayivyadhi*) (Pā. 6-1-16); ṣa for cha by व्रश्चभृस्थ (*vraścabhṛstha*) (Pā. 8-2-36) and ṭu-sound of the t of the affix, giving pṛṣṭa; the root बंध बंधने (*baṃdha baṃdhane*) with the affix u by श्यस्वस्निहि (*śyasvasnihi*) (Uṇ. 1-10) (printed so), giving bandhu; guṇa of the u in the vocative by ह्रस्वस्य गुणः (*hrasvasya guṇaḥ*); the nighāta accent by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*).)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, as the sun regulates the seasons, guides men and the divine peoples; true in action, slayer of Vṛtra, ancient, all-knowing, shining, may he carry the praiser across all evils.

*[In the bhāṣya block the Kannada has ಪುರಾಣೋ ... ವಿಶ್ವವೇವಾಃ (for ವಿಶ್ವವೇದಾಃ) and ವರ್ಷತ್ (for ಪರ್ಷತ್) in the grammatical tail, ಅಞ್, ಓಡ್ಢಾಣಞಾತಿ ಜಪ್ and ಪೂರ್ವ / ಪದಾಂತೋದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ broken across lines; all as supplied.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतुपाः (*ṛtupāḥ*)—protector of the seasons; भग इव (*bhaga iva*)—as the sun is the regulator (of the seasons beginning with spring)
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)—of human beings
- दैवीनां (*daivīnāṃ*)—of the peoples who have the form of deities
- नेता (*netā*)—is the regulator and the leader
- ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)—the protector of truth, or one who has true action
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—the destroyer of Vṛtra
- सनयः (*sanayaḥ*)—the ancient
- विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*)—the all-knowing
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the shining one
- सः (*saḥ*)—he, Agni
- गृणंतं (*gṛṇaṃtaṃ*)—the devotee who praises
- दुरिता (*duritā*)—from all sins
- अति (*ati*)—carrying across
- पर्षत् (*parṣat*)—may he bring (him) to the shore (protect him)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the sun is the regulator and protector of the seasons beginning with spring, so Agni is the regulator and leader of human beings and of the peoples who have the form of deities. May Agni, who is true in action, the destroyer of Vṛtra, ancient, all-knowing and shining, carry the devotee who praises him across sins of every kind and bring him to a safe shore.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The divine Agni is the guide of devout men, as the sun is the regulator of the seasons : may he, the observer of truth, the slayer of Vritra, the ancient, the omniscient, convey his adorer (safe) over all difficulties.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

क्षितीनां दैवीनां नेता (*kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ netā*)—the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*) is stated among the names of the earth (Nirukta 2-5). Here the meaning is explained that मनुष्याणां देवसंबंधिनीनां विशां अंतर्यामितया नियामकः (*manuṣyāṇāṃ devasaṃbaṃdhinīnāṃ viśāṃ aṃtaryāmitayā niyāmakaḥ*): Agni is the regulator of the human

### Printed p. 412

peoples and of the peoples who are connected with the gods.

ऋतुपाः भग इव (*ṛtupāḥ bhaga iva*)—concerning Agni's being the regulator of the peoples: यथा वसंताद्यतूनां पालकः सूर्यः सर्वस्य प्रकाशदानेन प्रवर्तकः (*yathā vasaṃtādyatūnāṃ pālakaḥ sūryaḥ sarvasya prakāśadānena pravartakaḥ*)—just as the sun makes the seasons beginning with spring set in, each in its own time, protects all things, and, bestowing light on all by his radiance, protects them, so Agni too, being the inner controller of all, makes them act in their own times; thus it is said by comparison. *[The Kannada वसंताद्यतूनां (*vasaṃtādyatūnāṃ*) (for ಋತೂನಾಂ) is as supplied.]*

Agni is ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*), सत्यकर्मा (*satyakarmā*) (true), one who has eternal actions. वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य हंता (*vṛtrahā vṛtrasya haṃtā*): one who has destroyed the asura Vṛtra (printed ಸೃತ್ರಾಸುರನನ್ನು, as supplied), or one who splits the cloud and gives rain. सनयः सनातनः पुराणः (*sanayaḥ sanātanaḥ purāṇaḥ*): one who has existed since very ancient times. विश्ववेदाः सर्वविषयज्ञानवान् सर्वज्ञः (*viśvavedāḥ sarvaviṣayajñānavān sarvajñaḥ*): one who has knowledge able to know everything (the omniscient). देवः द्योतमानः (*devaḥ dyotamānaḥ*): one who shines with splendours. Having thus described the abundant power of Agni, the wish is expressed in सः विश्वा दुरितानि अति पर्षत् (*saḥ viśvā duritāni ati parṣat*)—तथाविधः अग्निः स्तोतारं सर्वाणि दुरितानि अतिक्रम्य पारं नयतु (*tathāvidhaḥ agniḥ stotāraṃ sarvāṇi duritāni atikramya pāraṃ nayatu*): may Agni, of such great glory, destroy all the abundant sins of those who praise him and protect them.

वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—this word has been explained by Yāska.

प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचंते । वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वा अधूनोत्काष्ठा अव शंबरं भेत् ॥ (*pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacaṃte | vaiśvānaro dasyumagnirjaghanvā adhūnotkāṣṭhā ava śaṃbaraṃ bhet ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6)

Explaining the word वृत्र (*vṛtra*) as the cloud, the meaning is given as one who splits the cloud: वृत्रहणं मेघहनं (*vṛtrahaṇaṃ meghahanaṃ*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed pages 412 and 413, noted not translated. नेता (*netā*): the root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*), the affix tṛc in the agent sense; na for the initial ṇa by णोनः (*ṇonaḥ*); guṇa of the ī of the root by सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*); the final udātta accent by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. 6-1-163). क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*): the root क्षि निवासगत्योः (*kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ*); the affix ktic by क्तिच्‌क्तौचसंज्ञायां (*kticktaucasaṃjñāyāṃ*) (Pā. 3-3-174); no guṇa because the affix is k-marked; genitive plural; the udātta on the case ending of the nāmin (long vowel stem) by नामन्यतरस्यां (*nāmanyatarasyāṃ*) (Pā. 6-1-177). दैवीनां (*daivīnāṃ*): on the word deva in the sense of relation, the affix añ by देवाद्यञञ् (*devādyañañ*); vṛddhi of the first syllable by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (*taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ*) (Pā. 7-2-117); in the feminine the affix ṅīp by टिड्ढाण् (*ṭiḍḍhāṇ*) (Pā. 4-1-15), which is anudātta, so that the preceding affix is udātta; genitive plural. ऋतुपाः (*ṛtupāḥ*): the root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*); the affix vic by अन्येभ्योपिदृश्यंते (*anyebhyopidṛśyaṃte*) (Pā. 3-2-75); compound with the upapada by उपपदमतिज् (*upapadamatij*) (Pā. 2-2-19); since the upapada stands in a kāraka relation, the accent of the second member by गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*) (Pā. 6-2-139) (the Kannada text reads ಕೈಮತ್ತರಪದಪ್ರಕೃತಿಸ್ವರ, as supplied). ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*): the affix vasip in the sense of possession by the Vedic rule छंदसीवनिपौ (*chaṃdasīvanipau*); lengthening of the preceding vowel in the Saṃhitā by अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapi dṛśyate*) (Pā. 6-3-137); the affix is p-marked and so anudātta. वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*): the root हन हिंगत्योः (*hana hiṃgatyoḥ*) (printed so; the bhāṣya has ಹಿಂಸಾಗತ್ಯೋಃ); with vṛtra as upapada, the affix kvip by ब्रह्मभ्रूणवृत्रेषु क्विप् (*brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip*) (Pā. 3-2-87); the accent of the second member of a compound; nominative singular. विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*): a bahuvrīhi; the accent on the last syllable of the first member by बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायां (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyāṃ*) (Pā. 6-106, as supplied). पर्षत् (*parṣat*): the root पृ पालनपूरणयोः (*pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*); liṭ-like Vedic leṭ, third person singular, tip; loss of the i by इतश्चलोपः (*itaścalopaḥ*) (Pā. 3-4-97); sip by सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (Pā. 3-1-34); the augment aṭ by लेटोडाटौ (*leṭoḍāṭau*) (Pā. 3-4-94); guṇa of the ṛ of the root by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*) (Pā. 7-3-84); r follows; no nighāta because the word stands at the beginning of a pāda; the augment being anudātta, the accent of the root remains. दुरिता (*duritā*): the root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) (printed so) with the affix t; the accent of the second member in the compound; in the neuter plural loss of śi by शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulaṃ*). गृणंतं (*gṛṇaṃtaṃ*): the root गृ शब्दे (*gṛ śabde*), kryādi class; the substitute śatṛ for laṭ; the vikaraṇa śnā by क्रादिभ्यः श्ना (*krādibhyaḥ śnā*) (Pā. 3-1-81); since śatṛ is ś-marked, loss of the ā of the vikaraṇa by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Pā. 6-4-112); ṇatva of the n after ṛ; the accent of the affix śatṛ remains; in the accusative singular the augment sum because the form is ukit, and anusvāra by assimilation.)*

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द॒धि॒क्राम॒ग्निमु॒षसं॑ च दे॒वीं बृह॒स्पतिं॑ सवि॒तारं॑ च दे॒वं ।  
> अ॒श्विना॑ मि॒त्रावरु॑णा॒ भगं॑ च॒ वसू॑न्द्रा आ॑दि॒त्या इ॒ह हु॑वे ॥ ५ ॥

> *dadhikrāmagnimuṣasaṃ ca devīṃ bṛhaspatiṃ savitāraṃ ca devaṃ |*  
> *aśvinā mitrāvaruṇā bhagaṃ ca vasūndrā ādityā iha huve ‖ 5 ‖*

*[The Saṃhitā has ವಸೂನ್ದ್ರಾ where the Pada has ವಸೂನ್ । ರುದ್ರಾನ್; as supplied.]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दधिक्रां । अग्निं । उषसं । च । देवीं । बृहस्पतिं । सवितारं । च । देवं ।  
> अश्विना । मित्रावरुणा । भगं । च । वसून् । रुद्रान् । आदित्यान् । इह । हुवे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे दधिक्रावादयः सर्वे देवा होताहं दधिक्रां दधिक्रावाणमग्निमुषसं
> च देवीमुषोभिमानिनीं देवतां च बृहस्पतिं देवं द्योतमानं सवितारं
> सर्वस्य जगतः प्रेरकं देवं च अश्विना अश्विन् देवौ मित्रावरुण् भगं सूर्यं च
> वसूनष्टौ वसून् रुद्रानेकादश रुद्रान् आदित्यान् द्वादशादित्यान् एतान्सर्वान्
> हविर्भुजो युष्मानिहासदीये कर्मणि हुवे । हविःस्वीकरणार्थमाह्वयामि ॥
> दधिक्रां । दधातीति दधिः । आदृगमहनेत्यादिना किप्रत्ययः । दधीत्युपपदे क्रमे-
> र्जनसनेत्यादिना विट् । विड्वनोरित्यात्वं । देवीं । देवस्य पत्नि देवी । पुयोगा-
> दाख्यायामिति जीष् । यस्यॆति लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तः । बृहस्पतिं ।
> तद्बृहतोः करपत्योश्चोरदेवतयोः सुट् तलोपस्थेति पतिशब्दे परतो बृहच्छ-
> ब्दस्य तलोपः सुडागमश्च । उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपदित्युभयपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ।
> सवितारं । शू प्रेरण इत्यस्य तृचि आर्धधातुकस्येद्वलादेरितीडागमः । चित्वादं-
> तोदात्तत्वं। रुद्रा आदित्या इत्यत्र संहितायां शसो नकारस्य दीर्घादटि समान-
> पाद इति रुत्वं । ततः पूर्वस्यावर्णस्य आतोटि नित्यमित्यनुनासिकत्वं । भो भगो
> अघो अपूर्वस्य योशीति रोर्यादेशः । लोपः शाकल्यस्यॆति तस्य लोपः ।
> यलोपस्यासिद्धत्वात् स्वरसंधिर्न भवति । अतो रुद्रा आदित्या इति भवति ! एवमे-
> कस्मिन्नाद आकारादट परतो नकारस्य रुत्वयत्वपूर्वसवर्णानुनासिकादेशा उन्ने-
> याः । हुवे । स्वयतेर्लटि बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणं । इटष्टित आत्मनेपदाना-
> मित्येत्वं । उवजादेशः । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hotṛ calls to this rite, to receive the oblation, Dadhikrāvan, Agni, Uṣas, Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, the Aśvins, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, the eight Vasus, eleven Rudras and twelve Ādityas.

*[In the bhāṣya block the Kannada has ಅಶ್ವಿನ್ ದೇವೌ ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣ್ (for ಅಶ್ವಿನೌ ದೇವೌ, ಮಿತ್ರಾವರುಣೌ), ಜೀಷ್, ದೇವಸ್ಯ ಪತ್ನಿ, ಪುಯೋಗಾದಾಖ್ಯಾಯಾಮಿತಿ, ಸ್ವಯತೇರ್ಲಟಿ, ಇಟಷ್ಟಿತ and ಉವಜಾದೇಶಃ in the grammatical tail, and sentences broken across lines; all as supplied. The grammatical tail (from दधिक्रां । दधातीति (*dadhikrāṃ | dadhātīti*)) is transcribed but not explained.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होता अहं (*hotā ahaṃ*)—I, the hotṛ
- दधिक्रां (*dadhikrāṃ*)—the deity named वधिक्रावा (*vadhikrāvā*) (so printed, for ದಧಿಕ್ರಾವಾ)
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- देवीं (*devīṃ*)—divine in nature
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—the goddess Uṣas
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati *[the word is broken at the page boundary: p. 414 ends "ಬೃಹಸ್ಪತಿ", p. 415 begins "ಯನ್ನೂ"]*

### Printed p. 415

; देवं (*devaṃ*)—the shining; सवितारं (*savitāraṃ*)—the deity Savitṛ; अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvinī deities; मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—Mitra and Varuṇa; भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—Bhaga; वसून् (*vasūn*)—the Vasus; रुद्रान् (*rudrān*)—the Rudras; आदित्यान् (*ādityān*)—the Ādityas; इह (*iha*)—in this sacrificial rite; हुवे (*huve*)—(in order to receive the oblation) I call.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In this sacrificial rite of mine, in order to receive the oblation, I invoke the deity Dadhikrāvan, Agni, the divine Uṣas, Bṛhaspati, the shining deity Savitṛ, the Aśvinī deities, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, the Vasus, the Rudras and the Ādityas.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I invoke to this rite, Dadhikra, AGNI, the divine USHAS, BRIHASPATHI, the divine SAVITRI, the ASWINs, MITRA and VARUNA, BHAGA, the Vasus, the Rudras, and Adityas.

*[The printed English has BRIHAS- / PATHI broken across two lines; joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दधिक्रां (*dadhikrāṃ*)—दधिक्रावाणं (*dadhikrāvāṇaṃ*). Yāska has explained that he is a god famous as दधिक्रा (*dadhikrā*). This point has been elucidated in the Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-1).

उषसं च देवीं (*uṣasaṃ ca devīṃ*)—उषोभिमानिनीं देवतां च (*uṣobhimāninīṃ devatāṃ ca*). Yāska has cited the following Ṛks:

अपोषा अनसः सरत्संपिष्टादह बिभ्युषी । नि यत्सीं शिश्नथद्वृषा ॥ (*apoṣā anasaḥ saratsaṃpiṣṭādaha bibhyuṣī | ni yatsīṃ śiśnathadvṛṣā ‖*) (printed ಪು. ಸಂ. 4-30-10, as supplied)

उषस्तच्चित्रमा भरास्मभ्यं वाजिनीवति । येन तोकं च तनयं च धामहे ॥ (*uṣastaccitramā bharāsmabhyaṃ vājinīvati | yena tokaṃ ca tanayaṃ ca dhāmahe ‖*) (printed ಪು. ಸಂ. 1-92-13, as supplied)

*[The Kannada text prints the two references one after the other below the two verses, in the order 4-30-10, 1-92-13, with ಪು. ಸಂ. for ಋ. ಸಂ.; each is assigned to the verse above in the same order.]*

Durgācārya has described the meaning with the words इयं च मध्यमा मेघसंश्रयात् (*iyaṃ ca madhyamā meghasaṃśrayāt*): "this Uṣas too belongs to the middle region, because of her connection with the clouds".

एता उत्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमंजते । निष्कृण्वाना आयुधानीव धृष्णवः प्रति गावोऽरुषीर्यंति मातरः ॥ (*etā utyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumaṃjate | niṣkṛṇvānā āyudhānīva dhṛṣṇavaḥ prati gāvo 'ruṣīryaṃti mātaraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1)

In this Ṛk it is described that the rays of the goddess Uṣas, joining the rays of the sun that has risen, shine.

बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Yāska explains बृहस्पतिः बृहतः पतिः पालयिता वा । (*bṛhaspatiḥ bṛhataḥ patiḥ pālayitā vā |*) ("Bṛhaspati is the lord of the great, or the protector"), and cites

अश्नापिनद्धं मधु पर्यपश्यन् मत्स्यं न दीन उदनि क्षियंतं । निष्टज्जभार चमसं न वृक्षात् बृहस्पतिर्विरवेणा विकृत्य ॥ (*aśnāpinaddhaṃ madhu paryapaśyan matsyaṃ na dīna udani kṣiyaṃtaṃ | niṣṭajjabhāra camasaṃ na vṛkṣāt bṛhaspatirviraveṇā vikṛtya ‖*) (printed ಮಿ. ಸಂ. 10-68-8, as supplied)

*[The Kannada has ಮಿ. ಸಂ. for ಋ. ಸಂ.; the Saṃhitā text of the verse is as supplied (ಅಶ್ನಾಪಿನದ್ಧಂ, ನಿಷ್ಟಜ್ಜಭಾರ).]*

### Printed p. 416

He has cited this Ṛk. Durgācārya (Nirukta 10-12) explains: बृहतः महतोऽस्य जगतः उदकस्य वा पाता रक्षिता पालयिता रक्षितैव । उदकनिर्हरणात् मध्यमः (*bṛhataḥ mahato 'sya jagataḥ udakasya vā pātā rakṣitā pālayitā rakṣitaiva | udakanirharaṇāt madhyamaḥ*)—that he is the deity who protects the great world or the water, and, because he makes the water from the clouds favourable to rain, he is a deity of the middle region.

देवं सवितारं (*devaṃ savitāraṃ*)—द्योतमानं जगतः प्रेरकं देवं (*dyotamānaṃ jagataḥ prerakaṃ devaṃ*). Sāyaṇa explains that Savitṛ is the deity who shines with splendours and who impels the several beings in the world so that they act in accordance with their own affairs.

Yāska explains: सविता व्याख्यातः तस्य कालो यदा द्यौरपहततमस्कारीर्णरश्मिर्भवति ऎंदु व्याख्यानमाडिद्दारॆ. दुर्गाचार्यरु— यस्मिन्काले द्यौरेव अपहततमस्का भवति (*savitā vyākhyātaḥ tasya kālo yadā dyaurapahatatamaskārīrṇaraśmirbhavati èṃdu vyākhyānamāḍiddārè. durgācāryaru— yasminkāle dyaureva apahatatamaskā bhavati*) ("Savitṛ has been explained; his time is when the sky has its darkness removed and its rays are scattered"). Durgācārya:

यस्मिन्काले द्यौरेव अपहततमस्का भवति पृथिव्यां तमो भवति दिव्यपहतेतमसि विक्षिप्ता अस्यां रश्मयो भवंति स सावित्रः कालः तस्मिन्कालेआदित्यः सवितोच्यते ॥ (*yasminkāle dyaureva apahatatamaskā bhavati pṛthivyāṃ tamo bhavati divyapahatetamasi vikṣiptā asyāṃ raśmayo bhavaṃti sa sāvitraḥ kālaḥ tasminkāleādityaḥ savitocyate ‖*)

*[This Sanskrit passage has several unclear places in the supplied text (ದಿವ್ಯ- / ಪಹತೇತಮಸಿ, ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ಕಾಲೇ- / ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಸವಿತೋಚ್ಯತೇ); all as supplied.]*

The Kannada explanation says: the time when, the darkness in the sky (antarikṣa) having been destroyed while darkness fills the earth, the rays of the sun that spread light pervade, belongs to the deity Savitṛ; therefore Āditya himself is designated by the word Savitṛ.

अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—अश्वीनीदेवौ (*aśvīnīdevau*) . Yāska has explained the meaning of the word Aśvin:

अश्विनौ यद्व्यश्नुवाते सर्वं रसेनान्यो ज्योतिषान्यः । अश्विनावश्चैरित्यौर्णवाभः । द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके । अहोरात्रावित्यैके । सूर्याचंद्र मसावित्येके । राजान् पुण्यकृतावित्येतिहासिकाः । (*aśvinau yadvyaśnuvāte sarvaṃ rasenānyo jyotiṣānyaḥ | aśvināvaścairityaurṇavābhaḥ | dyāvāpṛthivyāvityeke | ahorātrāvityaike | sūryācaṃdra masāvityeke | rājān puṇyakṛtāvityetihāsikāḥ |*)

Everything is pervaded by the two deities, the one with water, the other with light; these are said to be the Aśvinī deities. The teacher called और्णवाभजट्ट (*aurṇavābhajaṭṭa*) (so printed, for Aurṇavābha) says that they pervade the world (printed ಗತ್ತನ್ನು, for ಜಗತ್ತನ್ನು) with horses. Some describe the name Aśvinī deities as Heaven and Earth; some say that day and night are the Aśvinī deities, some that Sun and Moon are; those who tell history describe two meritorious kings as the Aśvinī deities. Thus the differing views are explained. Since the author of the Nirukta has read them among the deities of the heaven-region, they are explained as deities of the heaven-region.

भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*). The author of the Nirukta (cites):

प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम वयं पुत्रमदितेयो विधर्ता । आध्रशिद्यं मन्यमानस्तुरश्चिद्राजा चिद्यं भगं भक्षेत्याह ॥ (*prātarjitaṃ bhagamugraṃ huvema vayaṃ putramaditeyo vidhartā | ādhraśidyaṃ manyamānasturaścidrājā cidyaṃ bhagaṃ bhakṣetyāha ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-40-2)

*[The Kannada text prints the reference twice, one after the other: "(ಋ. ಸಂ. (೭-೪೦-೨)" and "(ಮಿ. ಸಂ. (೭-೪೧-೨)", each with a stray opening bracket; both are as supplied, and the second (printed Mi. Saṃ. 7-41-2) disagrees in the last numbers with the first.]*

Here the meaning of the word Bhaga is said to be the sun. Durgācārya has described the meaning, explaining the light that comes after the Sāvitra time as called by the word Bhaga: सावित्रात्कालात् परतः एतदुत्तमं ज्योतिः भगाख्यं भवति (*sāvitrātkālāt parataḥ etaduttamaṃ jyotiḥ bhagākhyaṃ bhavati*).

*[The page, and the window, end here, in the middle of the Special Topics of Ṛk 5, with the sentence ending ದುರ್ಗಾಚಾರ್ಯರು ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ವರ್ಣಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ.]*

### Printed p. 417

वसून् (*vasūn*)—अष्टौ वर्सूर् (*aṣṭau varsūr*) . The meaning of the word Vasu, with Yāska's Nirukta passage:

वसवः यद्विवसते सर्वमग्निर्वसुभिः वासव इति समाख्या तस्मात् पृथिवीस्थानाः । इंद्रो वसुभिर्वासव इति समाख्या तस्मान्मध्यमस्था नाः । वसव आदित्यरश्मयो विवासनात्तस्मात् द्युस्थानाः । (*vasavaḥ yadvivasate sarvamagnirvasubhiḥ vāsava iti samākhyā tasmāt pṛthivīsthānāḥ | iṃdro vasubhirvāsava iti samākhyā tasmānmadhyamasthā nāḥ | vasava ādityaraśmayo vivāsanāttasmāt dyusthānāḥ |*) (Nirukta 12-41)

सुगा वो देवाः सुपथा अकर्म य आजग्मुः सवनमिदं जुषाणः । जक्षिवांसः पपिवांसश्च विश्वेऽस्मे धत्त वसवो वसूनि ॥ (*sugā vo devāḥ supathā akarma ya ājagmuḥ savanamidaṃ juṣāṇaḥ | jakṣivāṃsaḥ papivāṃsaśca viśve 'sme dhatta vasavo vasūni ‖*) (printed ಯ. ವಾ. ಸಂ. 8-18, the abbreviation left unexpanded)

ज्मया अत्र वसवो रंत देवा उरावंतरिक्षे मर्जयंत शुभ्राः । आर्वाक्षथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो न अस्य ॥ (*jmayā atra vasavo raṃta devā urāvaṃtarikṣe marjayaṃta śubhrāḥ | ārvākṣatha urujrayaḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ śrotā dūtasya jagmuṣo na asya ‖*) (printed ಮ. ಸಂ. 7-39-3, as supplied)

Since Agni pervades everything, he is designated (printed ವ್ಯದಿಷ್ಟ, as supplied) by the word Vasu; hence the Vasus have the earth as their place. Since Indra is accompanied by Vasus, the Vasus have the middle region as their place. The rays of Āditya, being designated by the word Vasu as they pervade, have the heaven as their place. Thus Yāska has explained the meaning of the word Vasu, and has described that a dwelling is allotted to them in all the three places, earth, atmosphere and heaven. Sāyaṇa has explained, with अष्टौ वसवः (*aṣṭau vasavaḥ*), that there are eight Vasus. The names of these Vasus are stated in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka.

रुद्राः (*rudrāḥ*)—एकादश रुद्राः (*ekādaśa rudrāḥ*). The author of the Nirukta (cites):

आ रुद्रास इंद्रवंतः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गंतन । इयं वो अस्मत्पति हर्यते मतिस्तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥ (*ā rudrāsa iṃdravaṃtaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gaṃtana | iyaṃ vo asmatpati haryate matistṛṣṇaje na diva utsā udanyave ‖*) (printed ಮ. ಸಂ. 5-57-1, as supplied)

Citing this Ṛk, he describes the Rudras as existing in supreme lordship and as coming with Indra to the sacrifice, and their power. Sāyaṇa has explained that these Rudras are eleven in number.

आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*)—द्वादशादित्याः (*dvādaśādityāḥ*). The meaning of the word Āditya is stated in the Nirukta.

आदित्यः रसानादत्ते भासं ज्योतिषामादीप्तो भासेति वा अदितेः पुत्र इति वा (*ādityaḥ rasānādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāmādīpto bhāseti vā aditeḥ putra iti vā*) (Nirukta 2-13) एवमन्यासामपि देवतानामादित्यप्रवादाः स्तुतयो भवंति । तद्यथा एतन्मित्रस्य वरुणस्यार्यम्मो दक्षस्य भगस्यांशस्येति । (*evamanyāsāmapi devatānāmādityapravādāḥ stutayo bhavaṃti | tadyathā etanmitrasya varuṇasyāryammo dakṣasya bhagasyāṃśasyeti |*) (Nirukta 2-13) स्वरादित्यो भवति । पृश्निरादित्यो भवति । नाक आदित्यो भवति । गौरादित्यो भवति । विष्टबादित्यो भवति । नभ आदित्यो भवति । (*svarādityo bhavati | pṛśnirādityo bhavati | nāka ādityo bhavati | gaurādityo bhavati | viṣṭabādityo bhavati | nabha ādityo bhavati |*) (Nirukta 2-14)

The name Āditya is famous because he drinks up the waters, because he lessens other lights, because he shines with radiance, or because he is the son of the goddess Aditi

### Printed p. 418

thus he explains; and he explains that the usage with the word Āditya applies also to other deities, namely the deities Mitra, Mitrāvaruṇa, Aryamā, Dakṣa, Bhaga and Aṃśa, and in this matter he has also stated separate examples.

Heaven too is called Āditya, because it has the qualities of drinking up the waters connected with the earth and with the atmosphere, of lessening the splendour of planets, stars and the like by its own light, and of being endowed with radiance. In the same way Pṛśni, Nāka (the heaven-world), Dyauḥ, Viṣṭap and Nabhaḥ are all designated by the word Āditya: so he has explained the meaning. Sāyaṇa has explained that there are twelve Ādityas.

हे दधिक्रावदयः सर्वॆ देवाः होता अहं सर्वान् हविर्भुजः युष्मान् अस्मदीये कर्मणि हविस्वीकरणार्थमाह्वयामि (*he dadhikrāvadayaḥ sarvè devāḥ hotā ahaṃ sarvān havirbhujaḥ yuṣmān asmadīye karmaṇi havisvīkaraṇārthamāhvayāmi*)—the priest who is the hotṛ, in the sacrificial act addressing all the deities beginning with Dadhikrāvan, invites everyone: let all these deities, who partake of the oblation, come to accept in the sacrifice their several oblations offered there. Sāyaṇa explains that the meaning is thus described.

*[This Sanskrit sentence of the bhāṣya, with its Kannada explanation, stands at the end of the Special Topics of Ṛk 5 in the supplied text, not as a separate bhāṣya block; it is kept here as supplied.]*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed pages 418 and 419, noted not translated. दधिक्रां (*dadhikrāṃ*): दधातीति दधिः (*dadhātīti dadhiḥ*), the root डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*), the affix ki by आद्यगमहन (*ādyagamahana*) (Pā. 3-1-171); reduplication etc. as in the perfect; loss of the a of the root by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (printed ಷಾ. 6-4-112), giving दधि (*dadhi*); as an upapada the affix viṭ on the root kram by जनसनखन (*janasanakhana*) (Pā. 3-2-67); ātva before viṭ by विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् (*viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt*) (Pā. 6-4-41); in the compound the accent of the final member's base. देवीं (*devīṃ*): on the word deva the affix ṅīṣ (printed ಜೀಷ್) by पुंयोगादाख्यायां (*puṃyogādākhyāyāṃ*) (Pā. 4-1-48); loss of the preceding a; the final udātta by the accent of the affix. बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*): loss of the t of bṛhat and the augment suṭ before pati in the sense of a deity, by the statement तद्बृहतोः करपत्योश्चोरदेवतयोः सुट् तलोपश्च (*tadbṛhatoḥ karapatyoścoradevatayoḥ suṭ talopaśca*); the āmredita-like udātta accent on both members by उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपत् (*ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat*) (Pā. 6-2-140). सवितारं (*savitāraṃ*): the root षू प्रेरणे (*ṣū preraṇe*), the affix tṛc in the agent sense; the augment iṭ by आर्धधातुकस्यॆड्वलादेः (*ārdhadhātukasyèḍvalādeḥ*) (Pā. 7-3-35); guṇa and avādeśa; the final udātta because the affix is c-marked, by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. 6-1-173); accusative singular. अश्विना (*aśvinā*): ā for the dual ending by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. 7-1-39). रुद्रा आदित्यान् (*rudrā ādityān*): in रुद्रान् (*rudrān*) the n of the ending -śas, with aṭ following, becomes ru by दीर्घादटि समानपादे (*dīrghādaṭi samānapāde*) (Pā. 8-3-8); anunāsika of the preceding ā by आतोटिनित्यं (*ātoṭinityaṃ*) (Pā. 8-3-3); ru becomes ya by भोभगो अघो अपूर्वस्ययोशि (*bhobhago agho apūrvasyayośi*) (Pā. 8-3-17); loss of that ya by लोपः शाकल्यस्य (*lopaḥ śākalyasya*) (Pā. 8-3-19); by पूर्वत्रासिद्धं (*pūrvatrāsiddhaṃ*) this loss counts as not having happened, so no vowel sandhi (savarṇadīrgha) arises; the same process in आदित्यान् (*ādityān*). हुवे (*huve*): the root ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्देच (*hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabdeca*), the first person singular of laṭ, ētva by टित आत्मने (*ṭita ātmane*), samprasāraṇa of the va by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*), no guṇa because the affix is j-marked (printed ಜಿತ್ವ), uvaṇādeśa; the nighāta accent after a non-verb (printed ಅತಿಜಂತದ).)*

## Sūkta 21 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-first sūkta** (ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमं न इति पंचर्चं नवमं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । इमं न उ-
> पाद्ये अनुष्टुभौ विराड्रूपा सतो बृहती अंत्येति द्वितीयातृतीये अनुष्टुभौ
> पंचमी विराड्रूपा सतो बृहती च । अनुक्तत्वात्पथमाचतुर्थ्यौ त्रिष्टुभौ । अस्यापि
> गाथी ऋषिः ॥ पशौ स्तोकानुवचन इदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । जुषस्व सप्रथस्तम-
> मिमं नो यज्ञं । आ. ३-४ । इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with इमं न (*imaṃ na*) is the ninth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said इमं न उपाद्ये अनुष्टुभौ विराड्रूपासतो बृहती चांत्या (*imaṃ na upādye anuṣṭubhau virāḍrūpāsato bṛhatī cāṃtyā*). The second and third Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the fifth Ṛk is of the metre called Virāḍrūpā Sato-bṛhatī; the first and the fourth Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. For this sūkta too the seer is the one called Gāthī. The application of this sūkta in the animal sacrifice, for the Stokānuvacana, is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra जुषस्व सप्रथस्तममिमं नो यज्ञं (*juṣasva saprathastamamimaṃ no yajñaṃ*) (Ā. 3-4).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Gāthī prays: Agni, hand over our animal sacrifice to the immortal gods, accept the oblations, and seated first on the altar drink the drops of marrow and ghee.

### Printed p. 421

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

जातवेद: (*jātaveda:*)—O Agni, of born wisdom (jātaprajña). नः (*naḥ*)—our. इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*)—this animal sacrifice. अमृतेषु (*amṛteṣu*)—among the immortal gods. धेहि (*dhehi*)—offer. इमा (*imā*)—given by us. हव्या (*havyā*)—the oblations. जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—partake (the Kannada has a full stop after the word). होतः (*hotaḥ*)—you who call the gods. अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni (printed ವಿಲೈ, for ಎಲೈ). निषद्य (*niṣadya*)—sitting on this altar. प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—as the first of all the priests. मेदसः (*medasaḥ*)—of the oblation in the form of vapā (omentum) (and) घृतस्य (*ghṛtasya*)—of the ājya (ghee). स्तोकानां (*stokānāṃ*)—the drops. प्र (*pra*)—exceedingly. आशान (*āśāna*)—eat.

*[The Pratipadārtha has आशान (*āśāna*) where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya have अशान (*aśāna*); the first word is printed with a colon (जातवेद: (*jātaveda:*)) instead of the visarga; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of born wisdom, offer this animal sacrifice of ours among the immortal gods. Partake of the oblations given by us. O Agni, who gives the call to the gods, you too, sitting on this altar, as the first of all the priests, drink up to the full the drops of this oblation in the form of vapā and of the ājya.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Convey our sacrifice, Jatavedas, to the immortals, and accept these oblations : Agni, invoker (of the gods), seated (on the altar) first partake of the drops of the marrow and the butter.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—For this word the meaning "jātaprajña" has been given. Further, addressing Agni with this word, he has expressed the wish: अस्माकं पशुयागं मरणधर्मरहितेषु यष्टव्यदेवेषु तदधीनतॆया समर्पय (*asmākaṃ paśuyāgaṃ maraṇadharmarahiteṣu yaṣṭavyadeveṣu tadadhīnatèyā samarpaya*)—that Agni may hand over the animal sacrifice performed by us, the sacrificers, in such a way that it is fitting for the gods who are free from mortality.

इमा हव्या जुषस्व—इमानि अस्माभिर्दीयमानानि हव्यानि हवींषि सेवस्व (*imā havyā juṣasva—imāni asmābhirdīyamānāni havyāni havīṃṣi sevasva*)—the wish of the sacrificers is described: let Agni partake of the oblations offered by us, the sacrificers.

होतः (*hotaḥ*)—With this word Agni is addressed. अग्निर्वै देवानां होता (*agnirvai devānāṃ hotā*) (printed ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ 3-14, as supplied): citing this sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, which teaches that Agni is the priest called hotṛ who invites the gods to the sacrifice, he has explained देवानां आह्वातः (*devānāṃ āhvātaḥ*) as: Agni is the one who invites the gods.

प्रथमः मेधसः धृतस्य च स्तोकानां अशान-सर्वेषां यत्विजां (*prathamaḥ medhasaḥ dhṛtasya ca stokānāṃ aśāna-sarveṣāṃ yatvijāṃ*) आदिमः सन् वपाख्यस्य हविषः आज्यस्य च बिंदून् भक्षय । (*ādimaḥ san vapākhyasya haviṣaḥ ājyasya ca biṃdūn bhakṣaya |*)

### Printed p. 422

Here the wish of the sacrificer is described: let Agni, seated on the sacrificial altar as the first of all the priests, partake of the oblation of the animal called vaṣā and of the drops (hani) of marrow and ājya.

हव्या (*havyā*)—हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*). Yāska, citing the Ṛk

नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुप स्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः । ये सुक्रतवश्युचयो धियंधाः स्वदंति देवा उभयानि हव्या ॥ (*narāśaṃsasya mahimānameṣāmupa stoṣāma yajatasya yajñaiḥ | ye sukratavaśyucayo dhiyaṃdhāḥ svadaṃti devā ubhayāni havyā ‖*) (printed ಪು. ಸಂ. 7-2 2, as supplied)

*[The reference is printed "(ಪು. ಸಂ. (೭-೨ ೨)" with a stray opening bracket and a space inside the number, and ಪು. ಸಂ. for ಋ. ಸಂ.; as supplied.]*

has explained the word हव्या (*havyā*) as हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 422, noted not translated. धेहि (*dhehi*): the root डुधाञ धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāña dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*) (so printed); lot, second person singular; the nighāta accent because it follows a non-verb (printed ಅತಿಜಂತದ). हव्या (*havyā*): loss of śi in the neuter plural by शेश्शंदसि बहुलं (*śeśśaṃdasi bahulaṃ*) (Pā. 6-1-70). जुषस्व (*juṣasva*): the root जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*), ātmanepada, lot, second person singular; the nighāta accent by तिज्जतिजः (*tijjatijaḥ*) (so printed). अशान (*aśāna*): the root अश भोजने (*aśa bhojane*), kryādi class; lot, second person singular, with hi substituted for sip; the vikaraṇa śnā by क्रादिभ्यः श्ना (*krādibhyaḥ śnā*); since it follows a consonant, the substitute śānac by हलः श्नः शानज्ञौ (*halaḥ śnaḥ śānajñau*) (Pā. 3-3-83); luk of hi after the final a by अतोहेः (*atoheḥ*) (Pā. 6-4-105); the nighāta accent. प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*): the root प्रथ प्रख्याने (*pratha prakhyāne*); प्रथमः प्रधंते अस्मात् द्वितीयादयः (*prathamaḥ pradhaṃte asmāt dvitīyādayaḥ*) (one more famous than the second and the rest); the affix amac by प्रथेरमच् (*pratheramac*) (Uṇ. 5-246); the final udātta accent because the affix is c-marked (printed ಚಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ). निषद्य (*niṣadya*): the root पद्‌ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*pad viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*) (so printed); after the sūtra समासेनञ् पूर्वा (*samāsenañ pūrvā*) (Pā. 7-1-37) the affix ktvā is replaced by lyap (printed ಳ್ಪ); because it follows an upasarga, ṣatva of the s of the root by सदिरप्रतेः (*sadiraprateḥ*) (Pā. 8-3-66; printed ಪತ್ವ); because the affix is l-marked, the udātta before the affix by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. 6-1-193); in the compound the accent of the final member's base.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Purifying Agni: in this sacrifice ghee-rich drops of the marrow oblation drip for you and the gods; therefore grant us the best desirable wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

*[Between the bhāṣya and the Pratipadārtha the supplied text has a stray line प्रतिपार्श्व (*pratipārśva*), in the place of the label Pratipadārtha; kept as an italic note in the Kannada file and the standard label inserted. The Pratipadārtha lines were printed as a quoted block in the supplied text and are un-quoted in the Kannada file.]*

पावक (*pāvaka*)—O Agni, the purifier (printed ಎತ್ತಿ, for ಎಲೈ). स्वधर्मन् (*svadharman*)—in this sacrifice, which is fit for sacrifice and endowed with all the limbs (printed ನಲ, for ಸಕಲ as in the Bhāvārtha). ते (*te*)—for your eating. देववीतये (*devavītaye*)—for the drinking of the gods. घृतवंतः (*ghṛtavaṃtaḥ*)—full of ghee (printed ಸೃತ). मेदसः (*medasaḥ*)—belonging to the oblation in the form of marrow. स्तोकाः (*stokāḥ*)—drops. श्चोतंति (*ścotaṃti*)—flow; (therefore) वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)—desired, श्रेष्ठं (*śreṣṭhaṃ*)—best wealth, नः (*naḥ*)—to us, धेहि (*dhehi*)—give.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O purifying Agni, in this sacrifice, which is fit for sacrifice and endowed with all the limbs, for your eating and also for the drinking of the gods, drops full of ghee (printed ಧೃತ) and belonging to the oblation in the form of marrow

### Printed p. 424

*[The page begins in the middle of the sentence of the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 2 that closes page 423; continued here without repeating.]*

—related (to it), the drops are flowing. As the result of that, give us the fruit that is desired and excellent.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The drops of the marrow charged with butter fall, purifier, to you, at your own rite, for the food of the gods : therefore grant us excellent affluence.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पावक (*pāvaka*)—With this word Agni is addressed. The meaning is explained thus: as the purifier he destroys the sins of beings and makes them wholly pure. The Nirukta-writers, addressing Varuṇa with mantras beginning "येना पावक (*yenā pāvaka*) चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*)" and so on, have explained the meaning as referring to Varuṇa (Ni. 12-22). Here the word is used as an epithet of Agni.

देववीतये (*devavītaye*)—देवानां वीतिः प्रीतिः यस्यां भक्षणक्रियायां । (*devānāṃ vītiḥ prītiḥ yasyāṃ bhakṣaṇakriyāyāṃ |*) The meaning is described as: the act of eating that brings pleasure to the gods.

स्वधर्मन् (*svadharman*)—स्वायत्तधर्मके सांगे अस्मिन् यज्ञे (*svāyattadharmake sāṃge asmin yajñe*): having explained the meaning as: performed in the manner enjoined by the rule and free of any deficiency, he gives the sense that in this sacrifice, for the satisfaction of the gods, or देवस्य तव वीतये (*devasya tava vītaye*), for the satisfaction of Agni who shines, मेदसः (*medasaḥ*) स्तोकाः (*stokāḥ*), the drops of the oblation, श्चोतंति क्षरंति (*ścotaṃti kṣaraṃti*), have been offered.

वार्यं श्रेष्ठं नः देहि (*vāryaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ naḥ dehi*) (printed ದೇಹಿ where the Saṃhitā has ಧೇಹಿ, as supplied)—वरणीयं संभजनीयं उत्तमं धनं अस्मभ्यं (*varaṇīyaṃ saṃbhajanīyaṃ uttamaṃ dhanaṃ asmabhyaṃ*) प्रयच्छ । (*prayaccha |*) Citing वृणोतेरथापि वरतमं (*vṛṇoterathāpi varatamaṃ*) (Ni. 5-1), he has explained that the word वार्य (*vārya*), formed from the root वृञ् (*vṛñ*), means that which is desired by all and which must necessarily be obtained, and he has expressed the wish that Agni may grant the sacrificers such excellent wealth.

दुर्गाचार्यरु (*durgācāryaru*)—Durgācārya (cites):

तद्वार्यं वृणीमहे वरिष्ठं गोपयत्यं । (*tadvāryaṃ vṛṇīmahe variṣṭhaṃ gopayatyaṃ |*) मित्रो यत्सांति वरुणो यदर्यमा ॥ (*mitro yatsāṃti varuṇo yadaryamā ‖*) (printed ಮಿ. ಸಂ. 8-25-13, as supplied)

Here, he has described, the word वार्य (*vārya*) is used in the sense of वरयितव्यं वरणार्हं धनं (*varayitavyaṃ varaṇārhaṃ dhanaṃ*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed page 424, noted not translated. श्चोतंति (*ścotaṃti*): the root श्चुतिर् क्षरणे (*ścutir kṣaraṇe*); lat, third person plural; the nighāta accent because it follows a non-verb (printed ಅತಿಜಂತದ). स्वधर्मन् (*svadharman*): स्वे (अंगभूताः) धर्माणो यस्य स्वधर्मा (*sve (aṃgabhūtāḥ) dharmāṇo yasya svadharmā*), a bahuvrīhi compound; by धर्मादनिच्‌केवलात् (*dharmādanickevalāt*) (Pā. Sū. 5-4-124) the affix anic comes at the end of the compound. The grammar continues on page 425.)*

Sū. 6-2-1; so printed) the accent of the base of the first member comes; by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) luk of the locative case ending. देववीतये (*devavītaye*): देवानां वीतिः प्रीतिः यस्यां भक्षणक्रियायां. सा देववीतिः (*devānāṃ vītiḥ prītiḥ yasyāṃ bhakṣaṇakriyāyāṃ. sā devavītiḥ*) (that eating in which the gods have pleasure); in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the base of the first member comes, as before; a dative singular form. श्रेष्ठं (*śreṣṭhaṃ*): अतिशयेन प्रशस्यः श्रेष्ठः (*atiśayena praśasyaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ*); by अतिशायनेतमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyanetamabiṣṭhanau*) the affix iṣṭan after the word praśasya; by प्रशस्य श्रः (*praśasya śraḥ*) (Pā. ##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, worthy of being obtained by the sacrificers, wise and a seer of supersensuous things, is kindled by the ghee-rich drops; be the protector of our animal sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

संत्य (*saṃtya*)—(to the sacrificers) worthy of worship. अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. विप्राय (*viprāya*)—wise. तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you. धृतश्चुतः (*dhṛtaścutaḥ*)—endowed with the flowing of ghee. स्तोकाः (*stokāḥ*)—drops (are ready). ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—one able to see supersensuous things, and श्रेष्ठः (*śreṣṭhaḥ*)—excellent, you. समिध्यसे (*samidhyase*)—you are kindled. यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of this animal sacrifice performed by us. प्राविता (*prāvitā*)—as protector. भव (*bhava*)—be.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, worthy of worship to the sacrificers, for you who are wise, drops endowed with the flowing of ghee are ready. You, who are able to see supersensuous things and are excellent, are now kindled. Be the protector of this animal sacrifice performed by us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The drops (of marrow) dripping with butter are offered, Agni, to you who are wise : you the most excellent Rishi are kindled : be the protector of the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

संत्य (*saṃtya*)—यष्टृभिः संभजनीय यद्वा यष्टृभ्यः फलप्रद । (*yaṣṭṛbhiḥ saṃbhajanīya yadvā yaṣṭṛbhyaḥ phalaprada |*) The meaning is explained thus: Agni is one who must necessarily be obtained by the sacrificing yajamānas, or one who grants the fruit of the sacrifice to the sacrificing yajamānas.

Having described that this word is used as an epithet of the word Agni, and addressing Agni with it, he has explained the meaning: विप्राय धृतश्चुतः स्तोकाः (*viprāya dhṛtaścutaḥ stokāḥ*)—for the satisfaction of the wise Agni, drops of the oblation filled with ājya have been offered.

### Printed p. 427

ऋषिः श्रेष्ठः समिध्यसे (*ṛṣiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ samidhyase*)—having explained the meaning as: अतींद्रियार्थदर्शि (*atīṃdriyārthadarśi*), one who possesses the knowledge of things that cannot be known by the senses, he explains that because Agni is a ṛṣi he is सर्वातिशायी (*sarvātiśāyī*), better than all; and समिध्यसे—धृतयुक्तमेदोबिंदुभिः प्रज्वाल्यसे (*samidhyase—dhṛtayuktamedobiṃdubhiḥ prajvālyase*): that in the animal sacrifice Agni is kindled by the oblations in the form of the fat of the omentum (vapā) of the animal and by the ājya.

यज्ञस्य प्राविता भव (*yajñasya prāvitā bhava*)—अस्माभिः क्रियमाणस्य पशुयागस्य प्रकर्षण पालकः भव (*asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇasya paśuyāgasya prakarṣaṇa pālakaḥ bhava*) (printed ಪ್ರಕರ್ಷಣ, as supplied). The Nirukta-writers have explained: यज्ञः प्रख्यातं यजतिकर्म (*yajñaḥ prakhyātaṃ yajatikarma*), that yajña is well known, in the world and in the Veda, as the act of worship that gladdens the gods; and from the Brāhmaṇa sentence यज्ञो वै देवानामन्नं समभूत् तं भृत्यास्समभावयन्निति हि विज्ञायते (*yajño vai devānāmannaṃ samabhūt taṃ bhṛtyāssamabhāvayanniti hi vijñāyate*), which teaches that yajña is the act of offering food to the gods and that those who desire sustenance (bharaṇa) regard it as an act worthy of worship, the word is derived as यजनात् यज्ञः (*yajanāt yajñaḥ*). Since it has thus been explained, and since in this sacrifice a rite in the form of a kind of animal sacrifice is performed by the yajamānas, the yajamānas' wish is described: may Agni protect this sacrifice so that no deficiency comes to it.

Then संतौ भवः संत्यः (*saṃtau bhavaḥ saṃtyaḥ*): by भवेछंदसि (*bhavechaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) or by तत्रसाधुः (*tatrasādhuḥ*) (Pā. ##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आध्रिगो अधृतगमन सततगमनस्वभाव । अत एव शचीवः शक्तिमन् हे अग्ने
> तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं मेदसो मेदोरूपस्य हविषो घृतस्य स्तोकासो बिंदवः
> श्चोतंति । स्रवंति । तस्मात्कविशस्तः कविभिः कर्माभिज्ञैर्होत्रादिभिः स्तुतस्त्वं बृहता
> प्रभूतेन भानुना तेजसा सहितः सन् आगाः । अस्मदीयं पशुयागमभ्यागच्छ । अगत्य
> च मेधिर 'प्रज्ञावन्नग्ने हव्या अस्माभिर्दीयमानानि वपादीनि हवींषि जुषस्व
> सेवस्व ॥ अध्रिगो । गमनं गौरिति गम्‌ल्य सृप्‌ल्य गतावित्यस्य भावे गमेर्डोरिति
> डोः । अधृता गौर्येनेत्यत्र गोस्त्रियोरुपसर्जनस्यॆति गोशब्दस्य ह्रस्वत्वं ।
> धृतशब्दस्य पृषोदरादित्वात् धिभावः । संबोधने संबुद्धौ च । पा. ७ ३-१०६ ।
> इति गुणः । अपादादित्वान्निघातः । शचीवः । मतुपो मतुवसो रुरिति रुत्वं । कविशस्त्रः । शन्नु स्तुतावित्यस्य निष्ठायामनुनासिकलोपः । यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः ।
> थाथघञ्क्ताजबित्र काणामित्यंतोदात्तत्वं । भानुना । भा दीप्तौ । दाभाभ्यां नुरिति
> कर्तरि नुः। प्रत्ययस्वरः। अगाः । इण् गतावित्यस्य छांदसे लुजु इणो गेति गादेशः ।
> गातिस्थेति सिचो लोपः । निघातः । मेधिर । मेधारथाभ्यामिरनिरचौ वक्तव्यावितीरन् । आमंत्रितत्वान्निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, of unhindered movement and powerful: drops of fat and ghee flow for you; praised by the hotṛs, come with splendour to our animal sacrifice and enjoy the oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अध्रिगो (*adhrigo*)—one whose nature is to spread without hindrance, and तजीवः (*tajīvaḥ*) —powerful. आग्ने (*āgne*) —O Agni. तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you. मेदसः (*medasaḥ*)—of the oblation in the form of marrow (fat), (and) घृतस्य (*ghṛtasya*)—of ghee. स्तोकासु (*stokāsu*) —drops. श्लोतंति (*ślotaṃti*) —flow. कविशस्त्रः (*kaviśastraḥ*)—you, praised by the hotṛs and others who know the nature of the rites. बृहता (*bṛhatā*)—abundant, भानुना (*bhānunā*)—endowed with splendour, for this our animal sacrifice, आगाः (*āgāḥ*)—deign (to come). (Having come here,) मेधिर (*medhira*)—O Agni endowed with wisdom. हव्या (*havyā*)—the oblations given by us, जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—partake of.

*[A stray "!" stands before ಘೃತಸ್ಯ and a stray "।" before ತಜೀವಃ in the supplied text.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

*[The supplied text has the garbled label ಭಾಷೆ before this paragraph (kept as an italic note in the Kannada file); the standard label is inserted.]*

O Agni, of unhindered, spreading nature and powerful, for you drops of the oblation in the form of marrow (printed ಮೆಟೋರೂಪದ, so printed) and of ghee (printed ಧೃತದ, so printed) flow. You, who are praised (printed ಸ್ತತನಾದ, so printed) by the hotṛs and others who know the rites, come to this our animal sacrifice, which is abundant and endowed with splendour, and partake here of the oblations that we offer.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Irresistible and powerful Agni, the drops of marrow and of butter distil for you . therefore you are praised by sages, come with great splendour, and be pleased, ever intelligent Agni, with our oblations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

*[The heading of the Special Topics is garbled in the supplied text (ಪ್ರೀ:ಡಪಡುಗಳು, kept as an italic note in the Kannada file); the standard label is inserted. The right-hand ends of several lines of this part are missing or garbled in the supplied text; they are translated as far as legible, with … where a line breaks off.]*

The meaning of this mantra has been explained by Sāyaṇa and by the Nirutta-writer ; **NOTE** there is a little difference.

अध्रिगो (*adhrigo*)—this word and the word शजीवः (*śajīvaḥ*) , … Agni's … (line breaks off: ಅಗ್ನಿಪದದ ವಿಶೇಷ, as supplied); अधृतगमन, सततगमनस्वभाव (*adhṛtagamana, satatagamanasvabhāva*), he of unhindered movement, of the nature of constant movement, … the nature of always moving about … (line breaks off); the meaning … शक्तिमन् (*śaktiman*), one possessed of power, thus the meaning for the word शजीवः (*śajīvaḥ*) … (line breaks off); addressing Agni with अग्ने (*agne*), मेदोरूपस्य हविषः धृतस्य च (*medorūpasya haviṣaḥ dhṛtasya ca*) **NOTE** (the following fragment is garbled) … the drops of the oblation in the form of fat and of the ājya, in the animal sacrifice … (line breaks off), thus he has explained.

कविशस्त्रः (*kaviśastraḥ*)—कविभिः कर्माभिज्ञैः होत्रादिभिः स्तुतः (*kavibhiḥ karmābhijñaiḥ hotrādibhiḥ stutaḥ*); Yāska … (line breaks off) has read it among the names (Si. 3-19, as printed). Further, उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोत्वज एकपात् पृथिवी समुद्र, विश्वे देवा ऋतावृधो हुवानाः स्तुता मंत्राः कविशस्त (*uta no 'hirbudhnyaḥ śṛṇotvaja ekapāt pṛthivī samudra, viśve devā ṛtāvṛdho huvānāḥ stutā maṃtrāḥ kaviśasta*) **NOTE** (the quotation breaks off with "_ 30:" in the supplied text, which ends here).

### Printed p. 430

In this Ṛk, for the word कविशस्ताः (*kaviśastāḥ*) the meaning मेधाविशस्ताः (*medhāviśastāḥ*), those praised by the wise, has been described. Sāyaṇa, having stated the meaning that Agni is praised by the ṛtvijs, the hotṛs and others, who know the order of performing the sacrificial rites, has described, for बृहता भानुना आगाः (*bṛhatā bhānunā āgāḥ*), the meaning that Agni should come to the sacrificial hall with his abundant splendour. The word भानु (*bhānu*) is stated among the names of day (Ni. 2-21). Here it is used in the sense of splendour. For the word मेधिर (*medhira*) he explained the meaning as प्रज्ञावन् (*prajñāvan*) (endowed with wisdom), and then explained the meaning: अस्माभिर्दीयमानानि वपादीनि हवींषि सेवस्व (*asmābhirdīyamānāni vapādīni havīṃṣi sevasva*), let Agni, who is wise, partake of the oblations, in the form of vapā and in other forms, that the sacrificers offer. Yāska has explained the meaning of अध्रिगु (*adhrigu*) in this way (printed ಅಧ್ರಿಗು ದ್ವಾರ್ಥವನ್ನು, as supplied).

अध्रिगुर्मंत्रो भवति गव्यधिकृतत्वादपि वा प्रशासनमेवाभिप्रेतं स्यात् तच्छब्दवत्त्वादध्रिगोशमीध्वं सुशमि शमीध्वं शमीध्वमध्रिगविति (*adhrigurmaṃtro bhavati gavyadhikṛtatvādapi vā praśāsanamevābhipretaṃ syāt tacchabdavattvādadhrigośamīdhvaṃ suśami śamīdhvaṃ śamīdhvamadhrigaviti*) (Ni. 5-11)

Durgācārya has explained: the word अध्रिगु (*adhrigu*) has many meanings. गवि अधिकृतो मंत्रः अध्रिगुः (*gavi adhikṛto maṃtraḥ adhriguḥ*): the mantra that is powerful in addressing the animal is also designated by the word adhrigu; and अध्रिगुर्नाम दैव्यः कश्चिदस्ति शमिता तस्यैतत् प्रशासनं स्यात् (*adhrigurnāma daivyaḥ kaścidasti śamitā tasyaitat praśāsanaṃ syāt*): there is a certain divine being who slaughters the animal in the sacrifice; for him this word is in the form of an address; and अध्रिगो शमीध्वं (*adhrigo śamīdhvaṃ*), thus there is an exhortation (sampreṣaṇa) in the sacrifice.

Further, Yāska says अग्निरप्यध्रिगुरुच्यते (*agnirapyadhrigurucyate*), that Agni too is spoken of by the word adhrigu (printed ಅದ್ರಿಗು here), cites this mantra, “तुभ्यं श्चोतंत्यध्रिगो शचीवः (*tubhyaṃ ścotaṃtyadhrigo śacīvaḥ*)”, and describes that, because he is like one of unrestrained action of going, अधृतगमनकर्मवत् (*adhṛtagamanakarmavat*), one with a continuous action of going, Agni is the one denoted by the word adhrigu.

अस्मा इदु प्र तवसे तुराय प्रयो न हर्मि स्तोमं माहिनाय यचीषमायाद्रिगव ओहमिंद्राय ब्रह्माणि राततमा ॥ (*asmā idu pra tavase turāya prayo na harmi stomaṃ māhināya yacīṣamāyādrigava ohamiṃdrāya brahmāṇi rātatamā ‖*)

(Pu. Saṃ. 1-68-1, as printed.) In this mantra, while Indra is described, आध्रिगवे इंद्राय (*ādhrigave iṃdrāya*) is stated (so printed; the mantra has a different spelling), and therefore Yāska has explained that by the word adhrigu Indra too is denoted: इंद्रोप्यथ्रिगुरुच्यते (*iṃdropyathrigurucyate*) (printed so, with ಥ್ರಿ). Durgācārya has explained the meaning as अधृतगमनाय अप्रतिहतगमनाय (*adhṛtagamanāya apratihatagamanāya*), one whose movement is unhindered. Following this, Sāyaṇa also has described the meaning. Durgācārya has described for the word शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*) the meaning कर्मवन् (*karmavan*), one who has rites (action).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ओजि॑ष्ठं ते मध्य॒तो मेद॒ उद्भृ॑तं॒ प्र ते॑ व॒यं द॑दामहे ।  
> श्चोतं॑ति ते वसो स्तो॒का अधि॑ त्व॒चि प्रति॒ तान्दे॑व॒शो वि॑हि ॥ ५ ॥

> *ojiṣṭhaṃ te madhyato meda udbhṛtaṃ pra te vayaṃ dadāmahe |*  
> *ścotaṃti te vaso stokā adhi tvaci prati tāndevaśo vihi ‖ 5 ‖*

> श्चोतंति । ते । वसोऽइति । स्तोकाः । अधि । त्वचि । प्रति । तान् । देवशः । विहि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने ओजिष्ठं अतिशयेन सारयुक्तं मेदो वपाख्यं हविर्मध्यतः
> पशोर्मध्यभागात्ते त्वदर्थमुद्धृतमुद्धृतमध्वर्यादयो वयमस्मिन्पशौ ते
> तुभ्यं प्रददामहे । उद्धृतं तद्वपाख्यं हविः प्रयच्छामः । वसो सर्वस्य जगतो
> वासयितर्हे अग्ने त्वच्यधि वपायामुपरि ये स्तोका धृतमिश्रा बिंदवस्ते ते
> त्वदर्थं श्चोतंति । स्रवंति । यद्वा ते तव त्वच्यधि ज्वालाख्यशरीरस्कोपरि श्चोतंति ।
> तान् सोकान्नेवशो देवेषु प्रति विहि । प्रत्येकं विभजस्व ॥ मध्यतः । मध्यशब्दात्
> पंचम्यास्तसिः । पा. ५-४-४४-१ । इति तसिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । उद्भृतं । हृञ् हरणे ।
> कर्मणि क्तः । हृग्रहोर्भश्चंदसीति हकारस्य भकारः । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । ददामहे । दद दान इत्यस्य लटि जात्दात्मनेपदं । अतो दीर्घो
> यञ्चिति दीर्घः । निघातः । श्चोतंति । शुतिर् क्षरणे । पादादित्वादनिघातः । अंतेर्लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणानुदात्तत्वे कृते धातुस्वरः । त्वचि । तनु विस्तारे । तनोतेरनश्च
> वः । उ. २-६३ । इति कर्तरि कर्मणि वा चिक् । आकारनकारयोर्वकारादेशः । तनोति
> तायते ना त्वक् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । विहि । वी कांतिगत्यादिष्टित्यस्य
> लोट्यदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । ह्रस्वश्छांदसः । निघातः । खिलं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The vapā oblation lifted from the animal's middle is offered to Agni; its drops flow; he is asked to share them among the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni.) ओजिष्ठं (*ojiṣṭhaṃ*)—that which is full of the utmost essence (sāra), मध्यतः (*madhyataḥ*)—from the middle region of the animal, ते (*te*)—for you, उद्भृतं (*udbhṛtaṃ*)—lifted out, मेदः (*medaḥ*)—the oblation in the form of vapā (printed ವಪಾರೂಪವಾಮದೂ, so printed), वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, the adhvaru and others, ते (*te*)—addressing you, प्रददामहे (*pradadāmahe*)—we offer. वसो (*vaso*)—O Agni who provides a dwelling for the whole world. त्वचि अधि (*tvaci adhi*)—upon the vapā (printed ವಪೆ). स्तोकाः (*stokāḥ*)—drops mixed with ghee (printed ಕೃತಮಿಶ್ರವಾದ, so printed). ते (*te*)—for you (within your flame). श्चोतंति (*ścotaṃti*)—flow. तान् (*tān*)—those drops, देवशः (*devaśaḥ*)—among the gods, प्रति विहि (*prati vihi*)—separate them and distribute them to all.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, we, the adhvaru and others, lift out for you from the middle region of the animal the oblation that is full of the utmost essence and is in the form of vapā, and offer it addressing you. O Agni, who provide a dwelling for the whole world, drops mixed with ghee (printed ಧೃತಮಿಶ್ರವಾದ, where the Pratipadārtha has ಕೃತಮಿಶ್ರವಾದ) flow for you, into your flame, upon the vapā (printed ವಷೆ here, where the Pratipadārtha has ವಪೆ; as supplied). Separate those drops and share them out among the gods, to all of them.

*[The supplied text ends with the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 5 at the end of printed page 432; the printed English translation of Ṛk 5 follows in the next window.]*
