##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ओजिष्ठं मेदः मध्यतः उद्भृतं (*ojiṣṭhaṃ medaḥ madhyataḥ udbhṛtaṃ*) (अतिशयेन सारयुक्तं वपाख्यं हविः पशोर्मध्यभागात् त्वदर्थमुद्धृतं (*atiśayena sārayuktaṃ vapākhyaṃ haviḥ paśormadhyabhāgāt tvadarthamuddhṛtaṃ*)): the oblation known as vapā, which is of the utmost essence, abundant (endowed with power) and productive of strength, being taken out separately for Agni from the middle of the animal's body, has been offered here for Agni alone in this animal sacrifice by the adhvaryu and the other ṛtvijs; thus the meaning is explained.

वसो (*vaso*)—सर्वस्य जगतो वासयितः (*sarvasya jagato vāsayitaḥ*): Yāska has explained many meanings of the word vasu. Having described the meaning that Agni is addressed by the word vasu because he makes the whole world dwell in comfort, Sāyaṇa describes अधि त्वचि स्तोकाः ते श्चोतंति (*adhi tvaci stokāḥ te ścotaṃti*): वपायां उपरि धृतमिश्राः बिंदवः त्वदर्थं स्रवंति (*vapāyāṃ upari dhṛtamiśrāḥ biṃdavaḥ tvadarthaṃ sravaṃti*), the drops mixed with ghee flow for you above the vapā; यद्वा (*yadvā*): तव ज्वालाख्यशरीरस्य उपरि स्रवंति (*tava jvālākhyaśarīrasya upari sravaṃti*), and in the form of the oblation, above the vapā (printed ವಷೆಯ, so printed), the drops of ājya trickle for Agni. Or else the drops of ājya ooze above the body of Agni in the form of flame; and the wish is expressed that Agni may convey these oblations, which are in the form of drops of ājya, to the deities who are worthy of the sacrifice and have been invited to it.

मेदः (*medaḥ*)—वपाख्यं हविः (*vapākhyaṃ haviḥ*). Yāska has explained मेदः मेद्यतेः (*medaḥ medyateḥ*) (Ni. 4-3): the word मेदः (*medaḥ*), formed from the root मिदा (*midā*) of the meaning "endowed with unctuousness" (snehena yukta), is a bodily constituent that keeps moisture in the body. Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as the oblation named vapā.

*[The quotation at the beginning of the Special Topics runs on into the Kannada explanation without a break, as supplied; the word ವಷೆಯ (for the vapā) is printed so in the second paragraph.]*

## Sūkta 22 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-second sūkta** (ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं स इति पंचर्चं दशमं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । अयं स
> उपांत्यानुष्टुप् पुरीष्येभ्योग्निभ्य इति । ऋषिः कौशिको गाथी । पंचचितिरूपा
> अग्नयो देवता । चतुर्थ्यनुष्टुप् शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरुक्तः
> सूक्तविनियोगः । अग्निचयन इष्टकाप्रणयने पुरीष्यास इत्येषानुवचनीया ।
> प्रेषितः पुरीष्यचितयेऽन्वाहेत्युपक्रम्य पुरीष्यादो अग्निय इति त्रिरुपांशु सप्रण-
> वमिति सूत्रितं । आ ४-८ ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with अयं स (*ayaṃ sa*) is the tenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said अयं स उपांत्यानुष्टुप् पुरीष्येभ्योऽग्निभ्य इति (*ayaṃ sa upāṃtyānuṣṭup purīṣyebhyo 'gnibhya iti*). For this sūkta कौशिको गाथी (*kauśiko gāthī*), that is, the son of Kuśika called Gāthī, is the seer; the Agnis in the form of the five layers (pañcaciti) are the deity; the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta has the Anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks have the Triṣṭubh metre. The application of this sūkta is in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Aśvina-śastra mantras; and in the Agnicayana, when the bricks are brought, the Ṛk beginning पुरीष्यास (*purīṣyāsa*) (the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta) is to be used as the anuvacanīyā mantra, as set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (printed ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಶೌತಸೂತ್ರದ) beginning प्रे (*pre*) (continued on the next page)

### Printed p. 435

(The Anuvāda continues:) षितः पुरीष्यचितयेऽन्वाहेत्युपक्रम्य पुरीष्यासो अग्नय इति त्रिरुपांशु सप्रणवमिति (*ṣitaḥ purīṣyacitaye 'nvāhetyupakramya purīṣyāso agnaya iti trirupāṃśu sapraṇavamiti*), (Ā. 4-8). This ends the Anuvāda.

Devatā: पुरीष्या अग्नयः (*purīṣyā agnayaḥ*) (the Purīṣya Agnis). Chandas: Ṛks 1 to 3 and 5 Triṣṭubh, Ṛk 4 Anuṣṭubh, as supplied.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं सो अ॒ग्निर्यस्मि॒न्सोम॒मिंद्रः॑ सु॒तं द॒धे ज॒ठरे॑ नावशा॒नः ।  
> स॒ह॒स्रिणं॒ वाज॒मत्यं॒ न सप्तिं॑ सस॒वान्त्सन्यू॑यसे जातवेदः ॥ १ ॥

> *ayaṃ so agniryasminsomamiṃdraḥ sutaṃ dadhe jaṭhare nāvaśānaḥ |*  
> *sahasriṇaṃ vājamatyaṃ na saptiṃ sasavāntsanyūyase jātavedaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

*[The Saṃhitā has नावशानः (*nāvaśānaḥ*) where the Pada has वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*), and ससवान्त्सन्यूयसे (*sasavāntsanyūyase*) where the Pada has सर्सवान् (*sarsavān*), सन् (*san*), स्तूयसे (*stūyase*); as supplied.]*

> अयं । सः । अग्निः । यस्मिन् । सोमं । इंद्रः । सुतं । दधे । जठरे । वावशानः ।  
> सहस्रिणं । वाजं । अत्यं । न । सप्तिं । सर्सवान् । सन् । स्तूयसे । जातवेदः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गाथी ब्रूते । आयमुत्तरवेद्यामाहुत्यधिकरणभूतावहनीयरूपतया दृश्यमा-
> नोग्निः स तथाविधः खलु वावशानः सोमं कामयमान इंद्रो यस्मिन्नग्नौ सुत-
> मभिषवादिसंस्कारोपेतं सोमं जठरे स्वोदरे दधे दधार। तस्मात्तादृशमहिमो-
> पेतः सोग्निरिति पूर्वणान्वयः । किंच । हे जातवेदः सहस्रिणं । सहस्रं नाना-
> रूपतां युद्धे यो भजति स सहस्री । तमत्यं वेगवशादतनशीलं सप्तिं न अश्व-
> मिव वाजं आज्यौषधिसोमाद्यनेकप्रकारं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं ससवान् भेजिवान् सन्
> त्वं स्तूयसे । स्तोतृभिरस्माभिः स्तूयमानो वर्तसे ॥ धधे । दधातेर्लिटि लिट-
> स्तझयोरेशिरेजिति तप्रत्ययस्य एशित्यादेशः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । प्रत्यय-
> स्वरः । वावशानः । वश कांतावित्यस्य यज्लुकि दीर्घोऽकित इत्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घः । व्य-
> त्ययेन शानच् । चित्स्वरः । ससवान् । षण संभक्तौ । क्वसाविडभावः । नलोपः । प्रत्य-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Gāthī speaks; this is the Agni in whom Indra, desiring Soma, held the pressed Soma in his belly; Jātavedas, you are praised by us.

> दीर्घः । निघातः ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

नावशानः (*nāvaśānaḥ*)—desiring the Soma juice. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra. यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which Agni. सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—endowed with the preparation by pressing and the like. सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice. जठरे (*jaṭhare*)—in his own belly. दधे (*dadhe*)—filled himself (printed ತುಂಬಿಕೊಂಡನೋ, with a comma that stands before the stop; as supplied). अयं (*ayaṃ*)—who is on the Uttaravedi. अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni also. सः (*saḥ*)—is he himself (printed with a stop after ಆಗಿದ್ದಾನೆ, as supplied). जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who know everything that is produced. सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—(on the battlefield) showing forms of many kinds, अत्यं (*atyaṃ*)—and of swift going, सप्तिं न (*saptiṃ na*)—like a horse (printed ಅಶ್ವದೋಪಾದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ, as supplied). वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food of many kinds, ājya, herbs (printed ಓಪಧಿ, as supplied), Soma and so on, ससवान्सन् (*sasavānsan*)—partaking of, स्तूयसे (*stūyase*)—you are praised (by us).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who is on the Uttaravedi is also himself that Agni in which Indra, desiring the Soma juice, filled his belly with the Soma juice endowed with the preparation by pressing and the like. O Agni, who know all the things that are produced, like a swift-going horse that obtains in the battlefield forms (and) experiences of many kinds (printed ನಾನಾರೂಪವನ್ನು ಅನುಭವಗಳನ್ನೂ ಪಡೆಯುವ, as supplied), you are praised by us, partaking of food of many kinds such as ājya.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This is that Agni in whom Indra, desirous (of the oblation), placed the effused Soma for (his own) belly: you are praised by us Jatavedas enjoying the sacrificial food of many sorts like a rapid courser (enjoying many pleasures in battle).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अयमग्निः सः (*ayamagniḥ saḥ*)—उत्तरवेद्यामाहुत्यधिकरणभूताहवनीयरूपतया दृश्यमानः (*uttaravedyāmāhutyadhikaraṇabhūtāhavanīyarūpatayā dṛśyamānaḥ*): since the Uttaravedi is the dwelling of the fire called Āhavanīya, which offers the oblation to the gods, Agni shines there visibly, endowed with his own greatness; having described this meaning, Sāyaṇa explains नावशानः इंद्रः यस्मिन् सुतं सोमं जठरे दधार (*nāvaśānaḥ iṃdraḥ yasmin sutaṃ somaṃ jaṭhare dadhāra*): he keeps (or has kept) within himself the Soma juice offered in this Agni in the form of an oblation, in order to offer it to Indra who desires it. By this the meaning is also explained that this Agni shines by an abundant greatness that produces satisfaction in the gods.

जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—by this word the Āhavanīya fire is addressed; and सहस्रिणं अत्यं सप्तिं न (*sahasriṇaṃ atyaṃ saptiṃ na*) वेगवशात् आतनशीलं अश्वमिव (*vegavaśāt ātanaśīlaṃ aśvamiva*): Agni is compared to a horse that goes swiftly because it obtains in battles changes of form of many kinds (movements)—

### Printed p. 437

(The sentence broken at the page boundary continues:) having thus compared Agni to a swift-moving horse, Sāyaṇa describes that Agni has food of many kinds in the form of oblation, such as ājya, herbs and Soma, and that this very Agni is praised by the ṛtvijs who are the reciters.

अत्यं (*atyaṃ*)—आतनशीलं (*ātanaśīlaṃ*): the word अत्य (*atya*) is stated among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27). Here the meaning "having the nature of moving about" is stated.

सप्तिं (*saptiṃ*)—this word is stated among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27).

मा नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिंद्र ऋभुक्षाः मरुतः परि ख्यन् । यद्वाजिनो देवजातस्य सप्तेः प्रवक्ष्यामो विदथे वीर्याणि (*mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyuriṃdra ṛbhukṣāḥ marutaḥ pari khyan | yadvājino devajātasya sapteḥ pravakṣyāmo vidathe vīryāṇi*) (Ma. Saṃ. 1-162-1)

In this Ṛk it is explained that the horse is born of the gods and is endowed with greatness of that kind.

नावशानः (*nāvaśānaḥ*)—वष्टेर्वा वाश्यतेर्वा (*vaṣṭervā vāśyatervā*) (Ni. 5-1): this word is formed either from the root वश (*vaśa*) with the meaning of desire, or from the root वाश् (*vāś*) with the meaning of making a sound. Here the meaning of the word is stated as कामयमानः (*kāmayamānaḥ*), one who desires.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed pages 437 and 438, noted not translated. सुतं (*sutaṃ*): the root पुञ् अभिषवे (*puñ abhiṣave*) (printed so); the affix kta in the passive; a change of the initial (printed ಸತ್ವ); no guṇa, because the affix is k-marked; final-udātta by the accent of the affix. दधे (*dadhe*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); liṭ, third person singular, the affix ta; by लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच् (*liṭastajhayoreśirec*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81); by यद्वृत्तानित्यं (*yadvṛttānityaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 8.1-66, as printed) the nighāta accent is barred, and the accent of the affix, final-udātta, remains. जठरे (*jaṭhare*): the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*); by जनेररष्यच (*janeraraṣyaca*) (U. Sū. 5-716) the affix ara; ḍa for the end of the root; initial udātta by the affix. वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*): the root वश कांत् (*vaśa kāṃt*); when yaṅ comes in the sense of intensity, luk by यजोचिच (*yajocica*) (printed so); doubling of the root by सन्यजोः (*sanyajoḥ*); lengthening of the reduplicative by दीर्घोकितः (*dīrghokitaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-83); by व्यत्ययोबहुलं (*vyatyayobahulaṃ*) śānac for laṭ after the yaṅ-luk; it is cit-marked, so final-udātta by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163). ससवान् (*sasavān*): the root षण संभक्तौ (*ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*); in liṭ, kvasu by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-107); because the affix is k-marked the nasal of the root is dropped (printed ಲೋಪ); doubling etc.; by the accent of the affix the vowel after the va is udātta. The grammar continues on page 438.)*

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ यत्ते॑ दि॒वि वर्चः॑ पृथि॒व्यां यदोष॑धीष्व॒प्स्वा य॑जत्र ।  
> येनां॒तरि॑क्षमु॒र्वा॑त॒तंथ॑ त्वे॒षः स भा॒नुर॑र्ण॒वो नृ॒चक्षाः॑ ॥ २ ॥

> येन । अंतरिक्षं । उरु । आततंथ । त्वेषः । सः । भानुः । अर्णवः । नृचक्षाः ॥ २ ॥

> *agne | yat | te| divi | varcaḥ | pṛthivyāṃ | yat | oṣadhīṣu | ap 'su | ā | yajatra |*  
> *yena | aṃtarikṣaṃ | uru | ātataṃtha | tveṣaḥ | saḥ | bhānuḥ | arṇavaḥ | nṛcakṣāḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यजत्र यजनीय हे अग्ने दिवि द्युलोके यद्वर्च आदित्याख्यं यज्योति-
> स्तत्ते तनैव ज्योतिः । पृथिव्यामाहवनीयादिरूपतया वर्तमानं यत्तेजस्तत्त्व-
> दीयमेव । प्रसिद्धं तेजोऽभिधाय गूढं ज्योतिरभिधत्ते । यदोषधीष्टस्त्विति ।
> ओषधीष्वरणिप्रभृतिषु काष्ठेषु यत्तेजः। यद्वा । ओषधीषु वनस्पत्यादिषु सोमाख्यं
> यत्तेजोऽप्पु जलेषु यदौर्वाख्यं तेजस्तत्सर्वं आ सर्वत्र वर्तमानं तेजस्तावक-
> मेव। किंच येन वायुरूपेण तेजसांतरिक्षमाकाशमुर्वाततंथ आतेनिथ विस्तीर्णं
> कृतवानसि । त्वेषो दीस्तिमान् अत एव भानुर्भासमानो नृचक्षा नृणां साक्षि-
> तया वृष्टार्णवः समुद्रवन्महान् । स तादृशस्त्वमंतरिक्षमातेनिथेति पूर्वणा-
> न्वयः । उक्तार्थे वाजसनेयकं । अग्ने यत्ते दिवि वर्च इत्यादित्यो वा अस्य दिवि
> वर्चः पृथिव्यामित्ययमग्निः पृथिव्यां यदोषधीष्टप्स्वा यजत्रेति य एवौषधीषु
> चाप्सु चाग्निस्तमेतदाह येनांतरिक्षमूर्वाततंथेति वायुः स त्वेषः स भानुर-
> र्णवो नृचक्षा इति महांत्सभानुरणर्वो नृचक्षा इत्येतत् । शत. ब्रा. ७-१-२३। इति ॥
> पृथिव्यां । उदात्तयणो हल्बूनादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । ओषधीषु । ओषधेश्च
> विभक्तावप्रथमायामिति दीर्घत्वं । अप्पु । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । आ-
> ततंथ । तनु विस्तार इत्यस्य लिटि थलि बभूथाततंथ जगृम्म ववर्धेति निपानादिडेत्वा-

> भ्यासलोपान भवंति लतीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्कोदात्तत्वं ' यद्वृत्तयोगादॆनिघातः ।
> अर्णवः अर्णांस्य स्मिन्संशीति मतुबर्थे वप्रकरणेऽन्येभ्योपि दृश्यंत इति वप्रत्ययः ।
> अर्णगः सलोपश्चेति सलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । नृचक्षाः चक्षिज् व्यक्तायां वाचि ।
> अभिव्यक्तवाग्वाच्ययं धातुरत्राभिव्यक्तिमात्रे वर्तते । चक्षेर्बदुलं शिच्चेत्यसुन् ।
> कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All the radiance in heaven, earth, plants and waters is Agni's; with the wind-form radiance he spread out the sky; the Śata. Brā. 7-1-23 passage is quoted for it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

*[In the supplied text the Pratipadārtha and the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 2 stand inside the bhāṣya block, headed by the lines कन्नड (*kannaḍa*) and भाषा (*bhāṣā*) instead of the standard labels; the garbled label lines are kept in the Kannada file as italic lines, and the standard labels are used here.]*

यजत्र (*yajatra*)—for sacrifice (printed ಯಜ್ಞಾರ್ಥನಾದ; the Bhāvārtha has ಯಜ್ಞಾರ್ಹನಾದ, "worthy of sacrifice"). अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni, दिवि (*divi*)—in the heaven (printed ದೃಲೋಕದಲ್ಲಿ, followed by a mark "!" for the stop, as supplied), यत् वर्चः (*yat varcaḥ*)—whatever radiance of the Āditya and the rest there is; पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—on the earth, in the form of the ahamānīya and the rest, in the creation, whatever radiance there is; ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—in the plants such as the araṇi, whatever radiance is contained, and अप्पु (*appu*)—in the waters; यत् (*yat*)—whatever Aurva (printed ಔರ್ವಾಸ್ಯವಾದ) radiance; आ (*ā*)—having spread everywhere, all of it too; ते (*te*)—is your own special radiances. येन (*yena*)—by which radiance of the wind-form; अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament; उरु (*uru*)—as an extensive thing; आतशंथ (*ātaśaṃtha*) (printed so, where the Saṃhitā has आततंथ (*ātataṃtha*))—you made; सः (*saḥ*)—that radiance of yours; श्वेषः (*śveṣaḥ*) (printed so, where the Saṃhitā has त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*))—ದೀಷ್ಟಮಂತಾದುದೂ ; भानुः (*bhānuḥ*)—shining; नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—that which looks upon and can know the doings of men; अर्णवः (*arṇavaḥ*)—very extensive, like the ocean.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, worthy of sacrifice (printed ಯಜ್ಞಾರ್ಹನಾದ): the radiance called Āditya that is in the heaven; the radiance on the earth in the form of the ಅರವನೀಯಾದಿ ; the radiance contained in the ವಸಸ್ಪತಿ ; and whatever Aurva radiance there is in the waters: all of it, ಗತ , is your own special radiances. By the radiance of the wind-form with which you caused the firmament to become extensive, that radiance of yours, endowed with radiance (printed ದೀಪ್ತಿಮತ್ತಾದುದೂ), ಭಾಷೆಯನವಾದುದೂ (printed so; the sense is not clear), and able to look upon and know the doings of men, is very extensive like the ocean.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Adorable Agni, your radiance that is in the heaven, on the earth, in the plants, in the water, and wherewith you overspread the firmament, that is shining and resplendent, overlooking man (vast as) the ocean.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the word यजत्र (*yajatra*) the meaning "one worthy of being worshipped in the yajanīya sacrifice" is explained, and Agni is addressed.

दिवि यत् वर्चः ते (*divi yat varcaḥ te*)-द्युलोके आदिश्याख्यं यत् ज्योतिः तत् तन्नव (*dyuloke ādiśyākhyaṃ yat jyotiḥ tat tannava*) (printed so, with a mark "!" at the end). The word वर्चः (*varcaḥ*) is stated among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) (printed ಪರಿತವಾಗಿದೆ, as supplied). Here the meaning "radiance" is explained, and

*[The supplied text ends here, in the middle of a sentence of the Special Topics of Ṛk 2, at the end of printed page 439 (the window ran one page past its end because the head of that page was garbled); the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 continue in the next window.]*

### Printed p. 440

(The sentence broken at the page boundary continues:) the radiance called the Āditya, which is seen directly by all who dwell in the heaven, is described as the radiance that belongs to Agni.

पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—आहवनीयादि रूपतया वर्तमानं यत्तेजः (*āhavanīyādi rūpatayā vartamānaṃ yattejaḥ*): in the sacrificial hall, the radiance that belongs to the earthly fire, which is well known and fit for the sacrifice under such names as Āhavanīya and Gārhapatya, is also none other than Agni's own radiance; thus it is explained.

Having explained that the Āditya and the Tretā fires (printed ತ್ರೇತಾಗ್ನಿಗಳು), which have an abundant form and shine with brilliance, exist in identity with Agni, it is described by the sentence यदोषधीष्टप्पास्वा (*yadoṣadhīṣṭappāsvā*) both how Agni pervades with his radiance in subtle form and the basis that is fit to be pervaded.

ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—in the araṇis, which are the place of origin of the Agni produced when the churning is done at the sacrifice; in what is in the form of Soma offered in the sacrifice as oblation; in the ones beginning with vanaspati (यूपस्तंभ (*yūpastaṃbha*), the sacrificial post); the radiance that is well known in the waters (अप्पु (*appu*)) by the name Aurva; and the radiance that is of subtle form in the herbs, trees and waters: all of these are तावकमेव (*tāvakameva*), Agni's own radiances; having explained thus, it is described that Agni's radiance is all-pervading.

Having described how Agni's radiance pervades in abundant and in subtle forms, it is explained, for the sentence येनांतरिक्षं उरु आततंथ (*yenāṃtarikṣaṃ uru ātataṃtha*) (वायुरूपेण तेजसा आकाशं आततंथ (*vāyurūpeṇa tejasā ākāśaṃ ātataṃtha*)), that Agni pervades the firmament too by radiance in the form of wind.

तेषः, भानुः, नृचक्षाः, अर्णवः (*teṣaḥ, bhānuḥ, nṛcakṣāḥ, arṇavaḥ*) (the first word printed so)—दीप्तिमान्, भासमानः, नृणां साक्षितया द्रष्टा, (अर्णवः) समुद्रवत् महान् (*dīptimān, bhāsamānaḥ, nṛṇāṃ sākṣitayā draṣṭā, (arṇavaḥ) samudravat mahān*): Agni is brilliant through his own radiance; he shines and causes light for everything; he is present as a witness of all the rites that men perform; as the ocean, the mass of waters, is great, so Agni is great through his majesty; thus Agni's might is described by describing the nature of his abundant radiance. This point is stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, and the sentence from there is quoted—

अग्ने यत्ते दिवि वर्च इत्यादित्यो वा अस्य दिवि वर्चः पृथिव्यामित्यय.मग्निः पृथिव्यां यदोषधीष्वप्स्सा यजत्रेति य एवौषधीषु चाप्सु चाग्निस्तमेतदाह येनांतरिक्षमुर्वाततंथेति वायुः स तैषः स भानुरर्णवो नृचक्षा इति महान्त्सभानुरर्णवो नृचक्षा इत्मेतत् (*agne yatte divi varca ityādityo vā asya divi varcaḥ pṛthivyāmityaya.magniḥ pṛthivyāṃ yadoṣadhīṣvapssā yajatreti ya evauṣadhīṣu cāpsu cāgnistametadāha yenāṃtarikṣamurvātataṃtheti vāyuḥ sa taiṣaḥ sa bhānurarṇavo nṛcakṣā iti mahāntsabhānurarṇavo nṛcakṣā itmetat*) (Ś. Cā. 7-1-23)

*[The quotation is given as supplied: the line ends with a full stop (मित्यय. (*mityaya.*)) where a hyphen would be expected, and the text has यदोषधीष्वप्स्सा (*yadoṣadhīṣvapssā*) and इत्मेतत् (*itmetat*) as printed.]*

Here the presence of Agni's radiance in the heaven, the earth, the herbs, the trees, the waters and the firmament, and Agni's being a witness of the rites and a mass of radiance, are described.

Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent comes on the syllable before the affix; because of the connection with यद्योग (*yadyoga*) the nighāta accent does not come; by तिजाचोदात्तवति (*tijācodāttavati*) (printed so) the anudātta accent comes on the gati (अ (*a*)). अर्णवः (*arṇavaḥ*): अर्णांसि अस्मिन् संति इति अर्णवः (*arṇāṃsi asmin saṃti iti arṇavaḥ*); by the statement वप्रकरणे अन्वेभ्योपि दृश्यते (*vaprakaraṇe anvebhyopi dṛśyate*) (5-3-109-1) (printed so, without the abbreviation for the sūtra) the affix व (*va*) in the sense of matup (printed मतुबर्थ (*matubartha*)); by अर्णसः सलोपश्च (*arṇasaḥ salopaśca*) the sa of the base is elided when this follows; by the accent of the affix it becomes final-udātta. नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*): चक्षिज् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*cakṣij vyaktāyāṃ vāci*); the root is of the adādi class (printed अदादि (*adādi*)); although the root has the sense of manifest speech, here it gives only the sense of manifestation (radiance); by चक्षेर्बहुलंशिच्च (*cakṣerbahulaṃśicca*) (U. Sū. 4-672) the affix asun; since शित्व (*śitva*) is laid down, the substitution ख्याञादेश (*khyāñādeśa*) does not come on account of the affix; because the first member is a कारकपूर्वपद (*kārakapūrvapada*), the accent of the kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti comes.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni reaches the waters of heaven by smoke, gathers the breath-gods in order, and moves the waters above and below the sun; Śata. Brā. 7-1-24 is quoted.

*[Printed oddities in the bhāṣya, as supplied: the sign for zero stands in place of the anusvāra in the word अर्ण (*arṇa*) (twice); the Śatapatha quotation has परस्तात्ूर्यस्य (*parastātūryasya*) with a letter missing and वस्तामउपतिष्ठंत (*vastāmaupatiṣṭhaṃta*), where a run of Latin letters in the supplied text was rewritten as Kannada letter for letter (see the repair log); the bhāṣya has ऊजिषे (*ūjiṣe*) in the quotation and in the grammar where the Saṃhitā has ऊचिषे (*ūciṣe*); and धिष्ण्याः (*dhiṣṇyāḥ*) in places where the Pada has धिष्ट्याः (*dhiṣṭyāḥ*).]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. (त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you.) दिवः (*divaḥ*)—in the heaven. अर्णं अच्छ (*arṇaṃ accha*)—towards the water. जिगासि (*jigāsi*)—you go (you unite with it). धिष्ण्याः (*dhiṣṇyāḥ*)—who are in the form of life-breath. देवान् (*devān*)—the gods. अच्छ (*accha*)—in due order. ऊचिषे (*ūciṣe*)—you gather together into one. सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the world of Sūrya. परस्तात् (*parastāt*)—in the upper part. रोचने (*rocane*)—in the world named Rocana. याः (*yāḥ*)—whatever waters there are (and). अवस्तात् (*avastāt*)—below the world of Sūrya,

*[The supplied text ends here, in the middle of the Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 3, at the end of printed page 442, after the word for "below"; the Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 3 continues in the next window.]*

### Printed p. 443

(The Pratipadārtha continues:) in the firmament world that is there. याश्च आपः (*yāśca āpaḥ*)—whatever waters. उपतिष्ठंते (*upatiṣṭhaṃte*)—are present (you animate all of them).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you spread upward and join the waters that are in the heaven. You bring together, in due order, so that they become one, the gods who are in the form of the life-breaths. In the world named Rocana, which is the upper part of the world of Sūrya, and in the firmament that lies below the world of Sūrya, whatever waters there are, all of these you animate; that is, you make them flow.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
you move, Agni, to the vapour in heaven; you congregate the divinities who are the vital airs (of the body); you animate the waters in the bright region above the sun, as well as those that are in the firmament beneath.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दिवो अर्णं अच्छ जिगासि (*divo arṇaṃ accha jigāsi*)—द्युलोके वर्तमानं अम्भः अभिलक्ष्य धूमद्वारा प्राप्नोषि (*dyuloke vartamānaṃ ambhaḥ abhilakṣya dhūmadvārā prāpnoṣi*). The word अर्णस् (*arṇas*) is stated among the names of water (Si. 2-24; the abbreviation as printed). The meaning is explained thus: Agni pervades the waters that are in the heaven in the form of smoke.

धिष्ण्याः (*dhiṣṇyāḥ*)—बुद्धुपहितं देहमुष्णंति उष्णीकुर्वंति इति धिष्ण्याः प्राणाभिमानिनो देवाः (*buddhupahitaṃ dehamuṣṇaṃti uṣṇīkurvaṃti iti dhiṣṇyāḥ prāṇābhimānino devāḥ*). Yāska has explained the meaning of the word धिष्ण्य (*dhiṣṇya*)—

धिष्ण्याद्धिष्णो णि धिषण्यो णि धिषणाभवः धिषणा वाग्निषेर्दधात्यर्थे धीसादिनीति वा धीसानिनीति ना । (*dhiṣṇyāddhiṣṇo ṇi dhiṣaṇyo ṇi dhiṣaṇābhavaḥ dhiṣaṇā vāgniṣerdadhātyarthe dhīsādinīti vā dhīsāninīti nā |*) (Si. 8-4).

*[The Nirukta passage is given as supplied, with its odd word divisions (for example धिष्णो णि (*dhiṣṇo ṇi*) and धिषण्यो णि (*dhiṣaṇyo ṇi*)); it is not corrected.]*

Durgācārya, taking the root धिष (*dhiṣa*) together with the root दध (*dadha*), has explained the word धिष्ण्य (*dhiṣṇya*) in one way as वाक् अर्धं धारयति (*vāk ardhaṃ dhārayati*) (the printed अर्धं (*ardhaṃ*) is kept as supplied): since the relation between the word and the meaning is eternal, the word holds the meaning. And since the word धी (*dhī*) has the meaning प्रज्ञा (*prajñā*) or कर्म (*karma*), he has explained the word धिष्ण्य (*dhiṣṇya*) also as one who attains understanding or rite, and as one who is in understanding or in rite. Sāyaṇa has explained the word धिष्ण्य (*dhiṣṇya*) as the gods who identify themselves with the life-breaths and who, taking the intellect as their limiting adjunct, make the body full of brilliance. And by the sentence देवान् अच्छ ऊचिषे (*devān accha ūciṣe*) he has set forth the meaning that Agni has said that all the gods who identify themselves with the life-breaths should be of one and the same mind.

सूर्यस्य परस्तात् रोचने या आपः (*sūryasya parastāt rocane yā āpaḥ*)—सूर्यलोकस्य उपरि रोचनो नामायं लोकः यत्राग्नेयं ज्योतिः तपति । तस्मिन् भासमाने रोचनाख्ये (*sūryalokasya upari rocano nāmāyaṃ lokaḥ yatrāgneyaṃ jyotiḥ tapati | tasmin bhāsamāne rocanākhye*)

### Printed p. 444

लोके याः आपः विद्यंते सूर्यलोकात् अधस्तात् अंतरिक्षलोके याः आपः उपतिष्ठंते ता उभयारपस्त्वं प्रेरयसि (*loke yāḥ āpaḥ vidyaṃte sūryalokāt adhastāt aṃtarikṣaloke yāḥ āpaḥ upatiṣṭhaṃte tā ubhayārapastvaṃ prerayasi*). Having explained that Agni impels, for the welfare of the world, the waters that are in the world named Rocana, in the upper part of the world of Sūrya, shining with the radiance of Agni, and the waters that are in the firmament, the lower part of the world of Sūrya, Sāyaṇa has quoted the sentence of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa which describes the whole intent of this mantra.

आपो वा अस्य दिवोऽर्णस्ता एष धूमेनाच्छेत्यच्छा देवा ऊचिषे धिष्ट्या य इति प्राणा वै देवा धिष्ण्यास्ते हि सर्वा धिय इष्टंति या रोचने परस्तात् सूर्यस्य याश्चावस्तादुपतिष्ठंत आप इति रोचनो ह नामैष लोको यत्रैष एतत्तपति तद्याश्चैतं परेणापो याश्चावरेण ता एतदाह । (*āpo vā asya divo 'rṇastā eṣa dhūmenācchetyacchā devā ūciṣe dhiṣṭyā ya iti prāṇā vai devā dhiṣṇyāste hi sarvā dhiya iṣṭaṃti yā rocane parastāt sūryasya yāścāvastādupatiṣṭhaṃta āpa iti rocano ha nāmaiṣa loko yatraiṣa etattapati tadyāścaitaṃ pareṇāpo yāścāvareṇa tā etadāha |*) (Ś. Brā. 7-1-24)

अयमर्थो वाजसनेयिभिः स्पष्टमुक्तः (*ayamartho vājasaneyibhiḥ spaṣṭamuktaḥ*): in this sentence the meaning of this mantra is described clearly.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the sand-pit fires, united with the digging implements, are to enjoy the sacrifice; and that the great foods, free from disease and the like, are to be given to us. The rest is grammar of the words.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

पुरीष्यासः (*purīṣyāsaḥ*)—those that are in the sand-pits. आग्नयः (*āgnayaḥ*)—the fires of the layered altar (citya). प्रवणेभिः (*pravaṇebhiḥ*)—together with the implements for digging the pits. सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—united with one another. यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice performed by us. जुषंतां (*juṣaṃtāṃ*)—let them partake. (And) अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)—those that are harmless, अनमीवाः (*anamīvāḥ*)—those that are free from disease and the like; महीः (*mahīḥ*)—abundant. इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods (let them give).

*[The Pratipadārtha has आग्नयः (*āgnayaḥ*) with a long initial vowel, as supplied. After the Pratipadārtha the supplied text has the garbled label line धनार्थ (*dhanārtha*) in place of the Bhāvārtha label; it is kept here as a note and the standard label follows.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the layered-altar fires that are in the sand-pits, united with one another together with the implements for digging the pits, partake of this sacrifice performed by us. And may they give foods that are harmless, free from disease and the like, and abundant.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the benignant fires termed purishya, together with the instruments (that have dug the pits in which they are placed) combined, accept the sacrifice (and grant us) salutary and abundant food.

*[The printed English has a line break inside "instru-ments", joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुरीष्यासः- अग्नयः (*purīṣyāsaḥ- agnayaḥ*)—Yāska has explained पृणातेः पूरयतीर्वा पुरीषं (*pṛṇāteḥ pūrayatīrvā purīṣaṃ*) (Ni. 221) (reference as printed). Gurgācārya has explained the meaning of the word पुरीष (*purīṣa*) as पूरयितृ प्रीणयितृ (*pūrayitṛ prīṇayitṛ*), that is, one who fills or one who gladdens. Sāyaṇa has explained पृणाति पूर्यते वा (*pṛṇāti pūryate vā*), and has described the meaning

### Printed p. 447

as: the fires (सिकतासंमिश्राः अग्नयः (*sikatāsaṃmiśrāḥ agnayaḥ*)) that are in the sand-pits and that fill the sacrificers with their wishes or gladden the sacrificers.

प्रवणेभिः (*pravaṇebhiḥ*)—प्रकर्षण वन्यते संभज्यते संश्लिष्यते मृदेभिरिति प्रावणानि खनित्राणि (*prakarṣaṇa vanyate saṃbhajyate saṃśliṣyate mṛdebhiriti prāvaṇāni khanitrāṇi*)—the spade and the like, the implements that cause [the earth] to be exceedingly separate; and मृत्पननसाधनभूतैः अभ्र्यादिभिस्सहिताः (*mṛtpananasādhanabhūtaiḥ abhryādibhissahitāḥ*)—the fires of the sacrifice, together with the spades that are the means of digging the earth and with the other fires, come to this Soma sacrifice, of which the Agnicayana and the like are parts, performed by the sacrificers, and partake of the oblation there: so it is expressed as a wish.

अद्रुहः अनमीवाः (*adruhaḥ anamīvāḥ*)—Having stated the meaning that the fires are those who do no harm, the meaning is explained that these fires should bestow upon the sacrificers इषः (*iṣaḥ*), food that is free from disease and the like and abundant. The word इष (*iṣa*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9).

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed page 447, noted not translated. पुरीष्यासः (*purīṣyāsaḥ*): the root पृ पालनपूरणयोः (*pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*); the affix īṣan by शृ पृ भ्यांकित् (*śṛ pṛ bhyāṃkit*) (U. Sū. 4-467), and because it is k-marked there is no guṇa; the substitution u by उदोष्यः पूर्वस्य (*udoṣyaḥ pūrvasya*) (Pā.Sū. 7-1-10) (reference as printed), with r following. पुरीषं पृणातेः पूरयतीर्वा (*purīṣaṃ pṛṇāteḥ pūrayatīrvā*) (Siru. 2-22) is cited as Yāska's (abbreviation as printed). The affix ya by छंदसिच (*chaṃdasica*) (Pā. Sū. 5-1-67); the designation bha by यचिभं (*yacibhaṃ*); elision of the preceding a by यस्यॆतिच (*yasyètica*); the affix accent makes it final-udātta; after jas the augment asuk by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50). प्रावणेभिः (*prāvaṇebhiḥ*): the root वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*); the affix gha in the sense of instrument by पुंसि संज्ञायां घःप्रायेण (*puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥprāyeṇa*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-118); the प्रवणानि (*pravaṇāni*) are the digging implements (हारॆ गुद्दलि मुंतादुवु (*hārè guddali muṃtāduvu*)); ṇatva of the root n by पुनिरंतः (*puniraṃtaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-4-5) (printed so); by वनंसमासे (*vanaṃsamāse*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-178) the final-udātta accent in the compound, or the kṛd-uttarapada accent; or, from the root पुज् गत् (*puj gat*), the affix yuṭ by चलनशब्दार्थादकर्मकाद्युट् (*calanaśabdārthādakarmakādyuṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-148). In the former alternative it must be said that the avagraha does not occur by Vedic usage. The grammar continues on page 448.)*

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इळा॑मग्ने पुरु॒दंसं॑ स॒निं गोः श॑श्वत्त॒मं हव॑मानाय साध ।  
> स्यान्नः॑ सू॒नुस्तन॑यो वि॒जावाग्ने॒ सा ते॑ सुम॒तिर्भू॑त्व॒स्मै ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इळां । अग्ने । पुरुदंसं । सनिं । गोः । शश्वत्तमं । हवमानाय । साध ।  
> स्यात् । नः । सूनुः । तनयः । विजावा । अग्ने । सा । ते । सुमतिः । भूतु । अस्मे  
> इति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने पुरुदंसं । अपोऽपो दंसो वेष इति कर्मनामसु पठितत्वा-
> द्दंसःशब्दः कर्मवाची । पुरूणि बहूनि दंसांसि कर्माणि यस्याः सा । तां बहुक-
> र्माणं गोः सनिं गवादिपशून्संपादयित्रीमिळामेतन्नामिकां गोरूपां देवतां
> शश्वत्तमं निरंतरं हवमानाय यजमानाय मह्यं साध । साधय। किंच नोऽस्माकं
> सूनुः पुत्रस्तनयः पौत्रः स्याद्भवतीति ते तव या सुमतिः शोभना बुद्धिः सा विजा-
> वाबंध्या सत्यस्मे आस्माकं भूतु । भवतु ॥ शश्वत्तमं । उच्छादिषु पाठादंतोदा-
> त्तत्वं । साध । राध साध संसिद्धौ । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थोऽयं । लोटि व्यत्ययेन
> शप् । सेर्ह्यपिच्चेति हिरादेशः । तस्यातो हेरिति लुक् । निघातः । विजावा । जनी
> प्रादुर्भावे । आस्मादन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति वनिप् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यादित्यात्वं ।
> कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । लिंगव्यत्ययः । भूतु । भू सत्तायां । बहुलं छंदसीति
> शपो लुक् । भूसुवोस्तिजीति गुणप्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that Iḷā, of many works and giver of cattle, is to be granted to the sacrificer; that son and grandson may be ours; and that Agni's favour may be fruitful for us. The rest is grammar of the words.

*[The supplied text of this window ends with the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Ṛk 5.]*

### Printed p. 449

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. पुरुदंसं (*purudaṃsaṃ*)—that which is the means for many rites. गोः सनिं (*goḥ saniṃ*)—that which obtains and gives cattle and the like. इळां (*iḷāṃ*)—the particular deity famed as Iḷā (or the earth). शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)—continuously (printed ಅನುಸೂತವಾಗಿ). हवमानाय (*havamānāya*)—to me, who offer the oblation. साध (*sādha*)—provide. नः (*naḥ*)—to us. सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)—a son. तनयः (*tanayaḥ*)—a grandson. स्यात् (*syāt*)—let (him) be obtained. अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. ते (*te*)—your. सुमतिः (*sumatiḥ*)—(which) excellent mind of favour there is. सा (*sā*)—that. अस्मे (*asme*)—for our share. विजावा (*vijāvā*)—being such as gives fruit. भूतु (*bhūtu*)—let it be.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, make the earth, who is named Iḷā, who is of the form of a cow and who gives the cattle and the like that are helpful to the many rites, favourable to us, who are constantly engaged in the performance of sacrifice; and, O Agni, may the auspicious mind that desires to bestow sons, grandsons and the like on the praisers be always unbarren for us. (May it be fruitful.)

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Grant, Agni, to the offerer of the oblation earth the giver of cattle, the means of many sacred rites, such that it may long endure : may there be to us sons and grandsons, and may your favour, Agni, be productive of good unto us.

*[The printed English is broken into four lines, joined here; the space before the colon after "endure" is as printed.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुरुदंसं—पुरूणि बहूनि दंसांसि कर्माणि यस्याः सा (*purudaṃsaṃ—purūṇi bahūni daṃsāṃsi karmāṇi yasyāḥ sā*). Among the twenty-six names of action beginning with अप्पः दंसः (*appaḥ daṃsaḥ*) (Ni. 3-2) the word दंस (*daṃsa*) is stated. The meaning is: one having many rites.

गोः सनिं — गवादिपशून् संपादयित्रीं (*goḥ saniṃ — gavādipaśūn saṃpādayitrīṃ*). The word गो (*go*) has many meanings: earth, speech, animal, ray. Since the words गोः सनिं (*goḥ saniṃ*) are qualifiers of the word इळा (*iḷā*), the meaning is described as that the deity Iḷā bestows all things beginning with cows.

इळां—एतन्नामिकां गोरूपां देवतां (*iḷāṃ—etannāmikāṃ gorūpāṃ devatāṃ*). The word इळा (*iḷā*) is stated among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5); it is stated also among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23), among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of the cow (Ni. 3-9) (the same reference twice, as printed). And the word इळा (*iḷā*) is derived from the root ईश (*īśa*). The following is quoted:

अभि न इळा यूथस्य माता स्मन्नदीभिरुर्वशी वा गृणातु । उर्वशी ना बृहद्दिवा गृणानाभ्यूर्वाना प्रथृथस्यायोः । सिहक्तु न ऊर्जव्यस्य पुष्टेः ॥ (*abhi na iḷā yūthasya mātā smannadībhirurvaśī vā gṛṇātu | urvaśī nā bṛhaddivā gṛṇānābhyūrvānā prathṛthasyāyoḥ | sihaktu na ūrjavyasya puṣṭeḥ ‖*) (printed Ma. Saṃ. 5-41-19, 20)

*[The Vedic verses are quoted exactly as supplied, with their printed spellings; the abbreviation of the source is printed ಮ. ಸಂ., and the figure 57 stands alone at the foot of the page, as supplied. No translation of the verses is printed.]*

### Printed p. 450

In these Ṛks the goddess named इळा (*iḷā*) or इडा (*iḍā*) is explained as a deity of the middle region (printed ಮಧ್ಯಮಸ್ಥಾನದೇವತೆ). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as the deity named Iḷā, who has assumed the form of a cow.

शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध—निरंतरं हवमानाय यजमानाय मह्यं साधय (*śaśvattamaṃ havamānāya sādha—niraṃtaraṃ havamānāya yajamānāya mahyaṃ sādhaya*). Agni is prayed to that the favour of the deity Iḷā may come about, who fulfils the desired objects needed by the sacrificer who is always satisfying Agni with oblations, who is filled with abundant greatness (printed ಮಹಾತ್ಮದಿಂದ) and who is in the form of a cow. (A full stop stands after ಇಳಾದೇವತೆಯ in the supplied text.)

सूनुः—पुत्रः; तनयः पौत्रः (*sūnuḥ—putraḥ; tanayaḥ pautraḥ*). Among the fifteen names of offspring beginning with तुक्, तोकं (*tuk, tokaṃ*) (Ni. 3-2) the word तनय (*tanaya*) and the word सूनु (*sūnu*) are included (printed ಪರಿತವಾಗಿದೆ).

एता विश्वा सवना तूतुमा कृषे स्वयं सूनो सहसो यानि दधिषे । वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मंत्रो ब्रह्मोद्यतं वचः ॥ (*etā viśvā savanā tūtumā kṛṣe svayaṃ sūno sahaso yāni dadhiṣe | varāya te pātraṃ dharmaṇe tanā yajño maṃtro brahmodyataṃ vacaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-50-6)

In this Ṛk the meaning "son" is given for the word सूनो (*sūno*), and Agni is called सहससूनो (*sahasasūno*) (सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*)), बलस्य पुत्र (*balasya putra*), that is, son of strength. Sāyaṇa has explained the word सूनु (*sūnu*) as son and the word तनय (*tanaya*) as grandson (the son of a son).

सुमतिः—शोभना बुद्धिः (*sumatiḥ—śobhanā buddhiḥ*). The author of the Nirukta has described this same meaning: at देवसुमतिं (*devasumatiṃ*) as देवनां कल्याणीं मतिं (*devanāṃ kalyāṇīṃ matiṃ*), the auspicious mind of the gods; at वैश्वानरस्य सुमत् सौम्य (*vaiśvānarasya sumat saumya*) as कल्याण्यां मत् (*kalyāṇyāṃ mat*); and at वयं देवस्य धीमहि सुमतिं सत्यधर्मणः (*vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ*) also, the same meaning कल्याणीं मतिं (*kalyāṇīṃ matiṃ*). Sāyaṇa has prayed that, in respect of the sacrificers who have satisfied Agni with oblations, the auspicious mind of Agni, consisting of the production, increase and the like of sons, grandsons and others whom Agni may bestow, may arise.

Sū. 6-2.119) the final-udātta accent of the latter member. शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*): because it is read in the list printed ಉಂಭಾದಿ, by उंभादीनांच (*uṃbhādīnāṃca*) (Pā. ## Sūkta 23 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-third sūkta** (इप्पत्तमूरनॆय सूक्तवु (*ippattamūranèya sūktavu*))

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> निर्मथितः सुधित इति पंचर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । निर्म-
> थितो देवश्रवा देववातश्च भारतौ तृतीया सतोबृहतीति । भरतस्य पुत्रौ देवश्रवा
> देववातश्चेत्युभावस्य ऋषी । तृतीया सतोबृहती । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । अग्निर्देवता ।
> आ होतेत्यादिसूक्तदशकस्योक्तो विनियोगः प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोः । इळा-
> मग्न इत्यस्या विनियोगोऽसकृदुपदिष्टः ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with निर्मथितः सुधित (*nirmathitaḥ sudhita*) is the eleventh sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said निर्मथितो देवश्रवा देववातश्च भारतौ तृतीया सतो बृहतीति (*nirmathito devaśravā devavātaśca bhāratau tṛtīyā sato bṛhatīti*). For this sūkta Devaśravāḥ and Devavātaḥ, the two sons of Bharata, are the seers; the third Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Sato-bṛhatī metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre; Agni is the deity. That the ten sūktas beginning with आ होता (*ā hotā*) (among which this sūkta is also included) have their application in the Prātaranuvāka and in the recitation of the Aśvina-śastra mantras has been stated before. The application of the Ṛk इळामग्ने (*iḷāmagne*) (the last Ṛk of this sūkta) has been stated before.

*[The supplied text of this window ends here, with the Anuvāda of Sūkta 23.]*

**Sūkta data .** Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 23. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 1; Varga 23. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seers: देवश्रवा देववातश्च भारता (*devaśravā devavātaśca bhāratā*) (Devaśravāḥ and Devavātaḥ, the Bhāratas; the Anuvāda of p. 451 has the dual form Bhāratau). Devatā: अग्निः (*agniḥ*) (Agni). Chandas: Ṛks 1, 2, 4 and 5 त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*) (Triṣṭubh), Ṛk 3 सतोबृहती (*satobṛhatī*) (Sato-bṛhatī), as supplied.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> निर्म॑थितः॒ सुधि॑त॒ आ स॒धस्थे॒ युवा॑ क॒विर॑ध्व॒रस्य॑ प्रणे॒ता ।  
> जूर्य॑त्स्व॒ग्निर॒जरो॒ वने॒ष्वत्रा॑ दधे अ॒मृतं॑ जा॒तवे॑दाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> निःमथितः । सुधितः । आ । सधस्थे । युवा । कविः । अध्वरस्य । प्रनेता ।  
> जूर्यत्सु । अग्निः । अजरः । वनेषु । अत्र । दधे । अमृतं । जातवेदाः ॥ १ ॥

> *niḥmathitaḥ | sudhitaḥ | ā | sadhasthe | yuvā | kaviḥ | adhvarasya | pranetā |*  
> *jūryatsu | agniḥ | ajaraḥ | vaneṣu | atra | dadhe | amṛtaṃ | jātavedāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

*[The Pada has प्रनेता (*pranetā*) where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya have प्रणेता (*praṇetā*); as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भारतावृषी स्तोत्रं कुर्वाते । योऽग्निर्निर्मथितोऽग्निष्टोमादिकर्म-
> स्वरण्योर्नितरां मथितः सन् सधस्थे यजमानगृहे सुधितो गार्हपत्याधिषु त्रिषु
> कुंडेषु सुष्टु निहितः निधाय च काष्ठप्रक्षेपेण प्रज्वाल्यमानो युवा प्रबुद्धः
> अत एवाध्वरस्य ज्योतिष्टोमादेः प्रणेता प्रकर्षेणानेता निर्वाहको नेतृत्वादेव
> कविः क्रांतदर्शी । तथाविधो जातवेदाः सर्वविषयाभिज्ञानवान् सोऽग्निर्वनेषु
> महारण्येषु जूर्यत्तु दानाग्नि संबंधाज्जूर्यमाणेषु जरा नाशं प्राप्नु वत्सपि
> स्वयमजरो जरारहितः प्रत्युत दीप्यमानः सन् अत्र एवं स्तुतिं कुर्वाणेषु
> यजमानेस्वमृतं क्षयरहितं प्रभूतमन्नमादधे । निदधाति ॥ सुधितः । दधातेः
> कर्मणि निष्ठायां सुधितवसुधितनेमधितेत्यादिना निपातनाद्धि इत्यादेशः । गतिरनंतर
> इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । जूर्यत्तु । जूरी घूरी हिंसावयोहान्योः । व्यत्य-
> येन शतृप्रत्ययः । दिवादित्वाच्छन् । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । अजरः । ज्ञ वयोहाना-
> वित्यस्माद्भाव ऋदोरबित्यप्पत्ययः । गुणः । नञ्नो जरमरमित्रमृता इत्युत्तर-
> पदाद्युदात्तत्वं । दधे । दधातेर्वर्तमाने लिटि रूपं । जातवेदाः । जनी प्रादु-

> र्भाव इत्यस्य क्ते जनसनखनां सन्‌झलोरित्याकारः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृति-
> स्वरत्वं ॥

> *rbhāva ityasya kte janasanakhanāṃ sanjhalorityākāraḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛti-*
> *svaratvaṃ ‖*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two Bhārata seers praise Agni, churned from the sticks, placed in the hearths, young, leader of the rite, who stays ageless though forests burn and gives imperishable food to the praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

निर्मथितः (*nirmathitaḥ*)—one who is well churned by the araṇis (fire-sticks). सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*)—in the sacrificial house. सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*)—one who is placed in the Gārhapatya and other hearths. युवा (*yuvā*)—the awakened one (printed प्रबुद्धनू (*prabuddhanū*)). अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—for the sacrifice. प्रणीता (*praṇītā*)—the excellent leader (printed so, where the Saṃhitā has प्रणेता (*praṇetā*)). कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the far-seeing one (क्रांतदर्शियू (*krāṃtadarśiyū*)). जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—one of born wisdom. अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni. वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—the great forests. जूरत्सु (*jūratsu*)—even though they are being consumed by forest fire (printed so, where the Saṃhitā has जूर्यत्सु (*jūryatsu*)). अजरः (*ajaraḥ*)—himself being free from decay. अत्र (*atra*)—at the time of the sacrifice, for the sacrificer who praises. अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—imperishable food. आ दधे (*ā dadhe*)—he provides.

*[A stray word, भुवनेश्वर (*bhuvaneśvara*), stands between the Pratipadārtha and the Bhāvārtha in the supplied text, in the place of the label of the Bhāvārtha; kept as an italic note in the Kannada file, and the standard label inserted.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is well churned by the araṇis, who is placed in the Gārhapatya and other hearths in the sacrificial house, the awakened one, the excellent conductor of the sacrifice, the far-seeing one, one of born wisdom, even while the great forests are being consumed by forest fire, himself free from decay, provides imperishable food at the time of the sacrifice for the sacrificer who praises.

*[The supplied text has माडक्कॆ (*māḍakkè*) before यजमाननिगॆ (*yajamānanigè*) (for the sacrificer); kept as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Churned (by the friction of the sticks), duly placed in the sacrificial chamber, the young and sage leader of the rite, Jatavedas, the imperishable Agni, (blazing) amidst consuming forests, grants us on this occasion ambrosial (food).

*[The printed English is broken into four lines, the last word across a hyphenated line break (ambro- / sial); joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

निर्मिथितः सुधितः—अग्निष्टोमादिकर्मसु अरण्यो नितरां मथितः यजमानगृहे गार्हपत्यादिषु त्रिषु कुंडेषु सुष्टु निहितः (*nirmithitaḥ sudhitaḥ—agniṣṭomādikarmasu araṇyo nitarāṃ mathitaḥ yajamānagṛhe gārhapatyādiṣu triṣu kuṃḍeṣu suṣṭu nihitaḥ*). It is described that in sacrifices beginning with the Agniṣṭoma Agni, produced by churning in the araṇis, sits in the sacrificer's sacrificial hall (in the respective places), in the places famed as Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and so on.

*[The supplied text has निर्मिथितः (*nirmithitaḥ*) in this heading where the bhāṣya and the Saṃhitā have निर्मथितः (*nirmathitaḥ*), and अरण्यो (*araṇyo*) in the Sanskrit; as supplied.]*

युवा अध्वरस्य प्रणेता (*yuvā adhvarasya praṇetā*)—By the offering of wood and the like this Agni is kindled, shines with lustre and brilliance like one who is in youth, will carry out sacrifices beginning with the Jyotiṣṭoma, and is a poet (kavi) who has seen the end of the sacrificial rites. The word कवि (*kavi*) is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19), but here the meaning is explained as क्रांतदर्शि (*krāṃtadarśi*).

### Printed p. 454

जातवेदाः अग्निः वनेषु जूर्यत्सु अजरः—सर्वविषयाभिज्ञानवान् सः महारण्येषु दावाग्निसंबंधात् नाशं प्राप्नुवत्स्वपि स्वयं (अजरः) जरारहितः प्रत्युत दीप्यमानः (*jātavedāḥ agniḥ vaneṣu jūryatsu ajaraḥ—sarvaviṣayābhijñānavān saḥ mahāraṇyeṣu dāvāgnisaṃbaṃdhāt nāśaṃ prāpnuvatsvapi svayaṃ (ajaraḥ) jarārahitaḥ pratyuta dīpyamānaḥ*). The word जातवेदा (*jātavedā*) is explained as "omniscient", and the meaning is explained that this Jātavedas Agni, even when the forests are destroyed through contact with forest fire (wildfire), himself does not diminish at all but shines with lustre; therefore it is indicated that in sacrifices and other rites Jātavedas Agni is one to be worshipped (printed यष्टव्यनागिरुवनॆंदु (*yaṣṭavyanāgiruvanèṃdu*)).

अमृतं आ. दधे—क्षयरहितं प्रभूतमन्नं निदधाति (*amṛtaṃ ā. dadhe—kṣayarahitaṃ prabhūtamannaṃ nidadhāti*). The word अमृत (*amṛta*) is stated among the names of gold (Ni. 2-2-10) and among the names of water (Ni. 2-24), and is explained as अमृतेषु देवेषु (*amṛteṣu deveṣu*) (Ni. 8-20). Here the meaning is described that Jātavedas Agni bestows on the sacrificers who praise him abundant food that does not come to an end even when it is spent.

*[The reference after the names of gold is printed with three numbers, as supplied.]*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 454, noted not translated. निर्मथितः (*nirmathitaḥ*): the root मंथ विलोडने (*maṃtha viloḍane*); the affix kta in the passive; because it is kit, loss of the nasal of the root; by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent for the gati. सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*): the root डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*) (the bhāṣya has डुधाञ् (*ḍudhāñ*) in the other place); when kta comes in the passive, since it is irregularly formed by सुधितवसुधित नेमधित (*sudhitavasudhita nemadhita*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-45), dhi is the substitute for the root; by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) the gati takes its own (prakṛti) accent. जूर्यत्सु (*jūryatsu*): the root जूरी घूरी हिंसावयोहान्योः (*jūrī ghūrī hiṃsāvayohānyoḥ*); by व्यत्ययोबहुलं (*vyatyayobahulaṃ*) śatṛ is the substitute for laṭ; by दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (*divādibhyaḥ śyan*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-69) the vikaraṇa śyan; because it follows what the print gives as अदुपदेश (*adupadeśa*), the lasārvadhātuka becomes anudātta; since śyan is nit, by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the initial-udātta accent comes; a form ending in the seventh case plural. अजरः (*ajaraḥ*): the root ज्यूष् वयोहानौ (*jyūṣ vayohānau*) (the bhāṣya has ज्ञ वयोहाना (*jña vayohānā*)); when the abstract sense is shown, by ऋदोरप् (*ṛdorap*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-57) guṇa for the ṛ of the root, which comes with ra; न विद्यते जरा यस्य सः (*na vidyate jarā yasya saḥ*), by नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः (*naño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ*) (Pā. Sū 6-2-116, as printed) the accent udātta on the first syllable of the latter member. अत्र (*atra*): by ऋचि तुनुघ (*ṛci tunugha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-133) lengthening in the Saṃhitā (printed धीर्घ (*dhīrgha*)). दधे (*dadhe*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); liṭ in the present sense by Vedic usage; a form ending in the first person (printed प्रथमपुरुष (*prathamapuruṣa*)) singular; the tiṅanta-nighāta accent comes. जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*): the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*); when the affix kta follows, by जनसनखनां सन्झलोः (*janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ*) (Pā.Sū. 6-4-42, as printed) ā as the final substitute of the root; जातं वेदः (*jātaṃ vedaḥ*) (ज्ञानं (*jñānaṃ*)) यस्य सः जातवेदाः (*yasya saḥ jātavedāḥ*); by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदं (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyāpūrvapadaṃ*) the pūrvapada-prakṛti accent; the former member becomes antodātta by the affix accent.)*

> हे अग्ने भारता भारतौ भरतस्य पुत्रौ देवश्रवा देववातश्चेत्युभौ सुदक्षं
> शोभनसामर्थ्योपेतं रेवत् रयिमंतमग्निमंगनादिगुणोपेतं त्वाममं-

> ज्योहर्वाजी वस्तोर्द्युरिति तन्नामसु पातात् । द्युननु सर्वेषु दिवसेषु नोऽ-
> स्माकमिषामन्नानां नेता आनेता भवतात् । भव ॥ अमंथिष्टां । मंथ विलोडन
> इत्यस्माल्लुजु सिच् । वदप्रजहलंतस्याचः । पा. ७-२-३ । इति वृद्दौ प्राप्तायां ने-
> टीति प्रतिषेधः । तस्थस्थमिपामित्यादिना तसस्तामादेशः । पादादित्वादनिघातः । अट्-

> इत्त्वरः । रेवत् । रयिशब्दान्मतुप् । वत्तोदात्तत्वसंप्रसारणपरपूर्वत्वगुणसु-

> पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं चेत्याणादिकसूत्रात्पूर्वपदस्वरः । देववातः । वा गतिगंध-
> नयोः । अस्मात्मर्मणि क्तः । देवैरिष्यमाणतया प्राप्तो देववात ऋषिः । तृती-
> या कर्मणेति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । द्यून् । द्यु अभिगमने द्युत दीप्तौ ना । जि-

> इति द्योतते किरणसंबंधादिति ना द्युर्दिवसः । प्रथमयोरिति सवर्णदीर्घः । तस्मा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two sons of Bharata, Devaśravas and Devavāta, churned Agni, the capable and wealthy one, for the rites; Agni is asked to look on us with abundant wealth and to bring us food every day.

### Printed p. 456

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. भारता (*bhāratā*)—the sons of Bharata. देवश्रवाः (*devaśravāḥ*)—the one named Devaśravas. देववातः (*devavātaḥ*)—the one named Devavāta. सुदक्षं (*sudakṣaṃ*)—one endowed with excellent capacity. रेवत् (*revat*)—the wealthy one. अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—you, endowed with अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*) and other qualities . अमंथिष्टां (*amaṃthiṣṭāṃ*)—the two churned and brought into being (such as you are). बृहता (*bṛhatā*)—abundant. राया (*rāyā*)—together with wealth. अभि (*abhi*)—towards us. विपश्य (*vipaśya*)—look with a favouring eye (printed as one word, where the Saṃhitā has वि पश्य (*vi paśya*)). अनु द्यून् (*anu dyūn*)—every day. नः (*naḥ*)—to us. इषां (*iṣāṃ*)—foods. नेता (*netā*)—as the bringer. भवतात् (*bhavatāt*)—be.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the two sons of Bharata, Devaśrava and Devavāta, churned you, who are endowed with excellent capacity, wealthy, and endowed with अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*) and other qualities , and brought you into being. Such as you are, come together with abundant wealth, face us and look on us with a favouring eye. Be the bringer of foods to us every day.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The two sons of Bharata, Devashravas and Devavata, have churned the very powerful and wealth-bestowing Agni ; look upon us, Agni, with vast riches, and be the bringer of food (to us) every day.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

भारता—भारतौ भरतस्य पुत्रौ (*bhāratā—bhāratau bharatasya putrau*)—The meaning is described as: because they are sons of one famed as Bharata, they are called Bhāratas.

देवश्रवाः—देवैः श्रूयते प्रख्याप्यते असाविति (*devaśravāḥ—devaiḥ śrūyate prakhyāpyate asāviti*)—the sage who bears the name Devaśravas because he is made famous by the gods, and देवैववातः—देवैरिष्यमाणतया प्राप्तः (*devaivavātaḥ—devairiṣyamāṇatayā prāptaḥ*) (printed so, with देवैववातः (*devaivavātaḥ*) where the heading elsewhere has देववातः (*devavātaḥ*); the sage called Devavāta because he was obtained by the gods as one desired by them)—both of them produced Agni, the wealthy one, who makes whatever he resorts to subject to himself, by churning in the araṇis for the accomplishment of sacrificial rites beginning with the Agniṣṭoma; so it is explained. Agni, produced in the araṇis by these sages, is wished for in this way: बृहत् राया (*bṛhat rāyā*), endowed with abundant wealth, face us, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, and वीक्षस्व (*vīkṣasva*), look on us with an exceedingly favouring glance.

अनु द्यून् नः इषां नेता भव—सर्वॆषु दिवसेषु अस्माकमन्नानामानेता भव (*anu dyūn naḥ iṣāṃ netā bhava—sarvèṣu divaseṣu asmākamannānāmānetā bhava*) (printed सर्वॆषु (*sarvèṣu*))—The word द्यु (*dyu*) is stated among the names of the day (Ni. 2-21). The wish is that Agni may bestow food on the sacrificers.

> दश॒ क्षिपः॑ पू॒र्व्यं सी॑मजीजन॒न्तु जा॑तं मा॒तृषु॑ प्रि॒यं ।  
> अ॒ग्निं स्तु॑हि दैववा॒तं दे॑वश्रवो॒ यो जना॑ना॒मस॑द्व॒ती ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दश । क्षिपः । पूर्व्यं । सीं । अजीजनन् । सुजातं । मातृषु । प्रियं ।  
> अग्निं । स्तुहि । दैववातं । देवश्रवः । यः । जनानां । असत् । वशी ॥ ३ ॥

> हे अग्ने देववातस्य क्षिपः । क्षिप्यंते कर्मकरणार्थमिति क्षिपोऽंगुलयः ।

> श्रवो मातृषु मातृभूतारण्योः सुजातं सुषूत्पन्नं अत एव प्रियं कमनीयं

> मानानां वशी वशवर्ति कर्मणां स्वातंत्र्येण प्रवर्तकोऽसत् भवति तं स्तुहीति
> पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥ दश । दन्य दशने । कनिन्नित्यनुवृत्तौ नुदशोर्गुणश्चति कनिन् ।
> नित्स्वरः । क्षिपः । क्षिप प्रेरणे । औणादिकः कर्मणि क्विप् । क्षिप्यंते प्रेय्यंते कर्मस्विति
> क्षिपोऽगुलयॆः । धातुस्वरः । अजीजनन् । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । हेतुमण्यंतस्य लुणु

> डागमः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ten fingers of Devavāta produced the ancient Agni in the araṇis; Devaśravas is told to praise him, who is master of the people.

### Printed p. 459

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

दश क्षिपः (*daśa kṣipaḥ*)—(Devavāta's) ten fingers. पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*)—the ancient one. सीं (*sīṃ*)—Agni, who is endowed with excellent qualities. अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*)—made to come into being. देवश्रवः (*devaśravaḥ*)—O Devaśravas. मातृषु (*mātṛṣu*)—in the araṇis, which are as mothers. सुजातं (*sujātaṃ*)—the one exceedingly well born. प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—the beneficent one. देववातं (*devavātaṃ*)—the one churned by Devavāta (and). यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni. जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—to the sacrificers, who are praisers. वशी (*vaśī*)—dependent. असत् (*asat*)—is. Such (Agni): अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni (the accusative). स्तुहि (*stuhi*)—praise.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The ten fingers of Devavāta, too, caused Agni, the ancient one, who is endowed with excellent qualities, to come into being. O Devaśravas, praise that Agni who is exceedingly well born in the araṇis, which are as mothers, who is beneficent, who was churned by Devavāta, and who is dependent on the sacrificer, the praiser.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The ten fingers have generated this ancient (Agni) : praise, Devashravas, this well born, beloved (son) of his parents, generated by Devavata, Agni, who is the servant of men.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

क्षिपः— क्षिप्यंते कर्मकरणार्थमिति क्षपो अंगुलयः (*kṣipaḥ— kṣipyaṃte karmakaraṇārthamiti kṣapo aṃgulayaḥ*) (printed क्षपो (*kṣapo*) where the bhāṣya has क्षिपोऽंगुलयः (*kṣipo 'ṃgulayaḥ*))—The word क्षिपः (*kṣipaḥ*) is stated among the names of the fingers (Ni. 3-9). Because the fingers are put to use for the duties that must be done, they are called by the word क्षिप (*kṣipa*). These fingers are ten, from the two hands. All of them belong to the two arms, which are the means in churning Agni; they are helpful at the time of the churning of Agni. The meaning is explained thus: these fingers have caused this Agni, who is ancient, to be produced from the araṇis.

The particle सीं (*sīṃ*) is explained by Yāska as used either in the sense of comprehension (परिग्रह (*parigraha*)) or as a filler of the pada: सीमिति परिग्रहार्थियो ना पदपूरणो ना (*sīmiti parigrahārthiyo nā padapūraṇo nā*) (Ni. 1-7). And he explains further: अपि ना सीमित्येतवनर्थकमुपनिबंधवाददीत पंचमी कर्मणां सीम्नः सीमतः सीमातः मर्यादातः सीमा मर्यादा (*api nā sīmityetavanarthakamupanibaṃdhavādadīta paṃcamī karmaṇāṃ sīmnaḥ sīmataḥ sīmātaḥ maryādātaḥ sīmā maryādā*), and gives as examples प्रसीमादित्यो असृजत् (*prasīmādityo asṛjat*) and विसीमतः सुरुचो वेन आवः (*visīmataḥ suruco vena āvaḥ*). Durgācārya has described the meaning: that सीं (*sīṃ*) is a particle without meaning, and that in the sense of an action it shows a limit.

### Printed p. 460

By the sentence मातृषु सुजातं प्रियं दैववातं अग्निं स्तुहि (*mātṛṣu sujātaṃ priyaṃ daivavātaṃ agniṃ stuhi*), addressed to the sage देवश्रवस् (*devaśravas*), a wish in the form of an injunction is described: let the sage Devaśravas praise that Agni who was produced by churning in the araṇis, which are the chief cause of Agni's arising, who is beneficent to all, and who was churned by the sage Devavāta.

जनानां वशी (*janānāṃ vaśī*)—Agni is subordinate to the sacrificers who praise him, and he carries out the sacrificial rites without the help of others; therefore the wish is that Agni, who is worthy of praise, be praised.

> नि त्वा॑ दधे॒ वर॒ आ पृ॑थि॒व्या इळा॑यास्प॒दे सु॑दिन॒त्वे अह्नां॑ ।

> दृषत्त्वत्यां । मानुषे ' आपयायां । सरस्वत्यां । रेवत् । अग्ने । दिदीहि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने इळाया गोरूपधारिण्याः पृथिव्या भूमेर्वरे वरिष्ठ पद उत्तर-
> वेद्यां आह्नां सुदिनत्वे यजनीयदिवसानां शोभनदिनत्वार्थं । येषु दिनेस्तिं-
> द्रादयो वरीयांसो देवा इज्यंते तानि सुदिनानि । तदर्थं त्वा त्वामा निदधे । आ
> समंतान्निदधामि । उत्तमानि स्थानानि दर्शयति । दृष्टद्वत्यां । दृष्टद्वती नाम काचि-
> न्नदी तस्यां । मानुषे मनुष्य संचारविषये तीरे । अपयायां । अपया नाम
> काचिन्नदी तस्यां । सरस्वत्यां नद्यां । एतेषु स्थानेषु त्वं रेवत् धनयुक्तं यथा
> भवति तथा दिदीहि । दीप्यस्व । महर्षयः सरस्वतीतीरे खलु यज्ञादिकर्माण्यकार्षुः।
> तथा च ब्राह्मणं । ऋषयो वै सरस्वत्यां सत्रमासत । ऐ. ब्रा. २-१९ । इति ॥ दधे ।
> दधातेर्लिट्युत्तमैकवचने रूपं । वरे । वृञ् वरणे । ग्रहवृदृनिश्चि गमश्चेत्यप् ।
> पित्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ' दृषद्वत्यां । दृ विदारणे । दृणातेः षुग्गु स्वश्च ।
> उ. १-१३० । इत्यादिना सुगागमो धातोर्ह्रस्वश्च । दृष्टद उपला यस्यां संतीति
> मतुप् । झय इति तस्य वत्वं । स्वरविधौ व्यंजनमविद्यमानवदित्य स्याः परिभाषाया
> अत्राश्रयणाभावान्तुप उदात्तताभावः । आदिप्रत्ययस्वरः । सरस्वत्यां । सरःशब्दोऽ
> सुनंतत्वादाद्युदात्तः । तवस्यास्तीति मतुप् । अदुपधत्वान्मस्य वत्वं । उगित्वात्
> जीप् । दिदीहि । दिवु क्रीडादावित्यस्य यज्लुकि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is told: I place you in the best spot of the earth, on the best of days; shine, wealthy, on the banks of the Dṛṣadvatī, Āpayā and Sarasvatī. The bhāṣya adds a Brāhmaṇa quotation; its grammatical tail is transcribed in the block, not explained. Differences kept as supplied: the Saṃhitā reads दृषद्वत्यां (*dṛṣadvatyāṃ*) and आसयायां (*āsayāyāṃ*) where the Pada has दृषत्त्वत्यां (*dṛṣattvatyāṃ*) and आपयायां (*āpayāyāṃ*) and the bhāṣya has दृष्टद्वत्यां (*dṛṣṭadvatyāṃ*); in the Pada a plain apostrophe stands between मानुषे (*mānuṣe*) and आपयायां (*āpayāyāṃ*) (the same mark stands once in the bhāṣya, between धातुस्वरः (*dhātusvaraḥ*) and दृषद्वत्यां (*dṛṣadvatyāṃ*)). The Latin letter S at the end of the line after सरःशब्दोऽ (*saraḥśabdo '*) is rewritten letter for letter as the Kannada avagraha in the Kannada file.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. इळायाः (*iḷāyāḥ*)—of the earth, which has assumed the form of a cow. पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth. वरे (*vare*)—excellent, and पदे (*pade*)—in the place that has the form of the uttaravedi. अह्नां सुदिनत्वे (*ahnāṃ sudinatve*)—on the good day that is the most excellent of all. त्वा (*tvā*)—you. आ निदधे (*ā nidadhe*)—I place all around. मनुषे (*manuṣe*) (printed so, where the Saṃhitā has मानुष (*mānuṣa*) and the Pada मानुषे (*mānuṣe*))—which the human beings who are sacrificers frequent. दृषद्वत्यां (*dṛṣadvatyāṃ*)—on the bank of the दृषद्वति (*dṛṣadvati*); (the page ends here, in the middle of the entry)

### Printed p. 462

आपयायां (*āpayāyāṃ*)—on the (river) आपया (*āpayā*). सरस्वत्यां (*sarasvatyāṃ*)—on the bank of the river सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*). रेवत् (*revat*)—so as to be endowed with wealth. दिदीहि (*didīhi*)—blaze forth and shine.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in the excellent place for the altar of the earth, which has assumed the form of a cow, on the sacrificial day that is the most excellent of all the days, I place you all around. Blaze forth and shine, endowed with wealth, on the bank of the वृषद्वति (*vṛṣadvati*) (printed so, where the Pratipadārtha has दृषद्वति (*dṛṣadvati*)), which the human beings who are sacrificers frequent, and also on the banks of the rivers आपया (*āpayā*) and सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I place you in an excellent spot of earth on an auspicious day of days: Agni, shine on the frequented (banks) of the Drishadvati, Apaya, and Saraswati, rivers.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

इळायाः—गोरूपधारिण्याः (*iḷāyāḥ—gorūpadhāriṇyāḥ*)—The word इळा (*iḷā*) is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5), among the names of speech (the print has वाङ्गाम (*vāṅgāma*) with a Kannada ending, as supplied) (Ni. 2-23), among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of the cow (Ni. 3-9), as the print gives it. It is explained as derived from the root ईड (*īḍa*), which means praising, and quoted: अभि न इळा यूथस्य माता (*abhi na iḷā yūthasya mātā*). Sāyaṇa has explained the sense as "assuming the form of a cow" and states that it is used as an adjective of the word पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*).

पृथिव्याः-भूमेः (*pṛthivyāḥ-bhūmeḥ*)—The word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) is stated among the names of the earth (Ni. 6-5) and among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 3-10), and is quoted: बळित्था पर्वतानां खिद्रं बिभर्षि पृथिवि । प्र या भूमिं स्रवत्वति मह्ना जिनोषि महिनि (*baḷitthā parvatānāṃ khidraṃ bibharṣi pṛthivi | pra yā bhūmiṃ sravatvati mahnā jinoṣi mahini*) (Ma. Saṃ. 5-84-1, as printed). It is explained as the deity of the middle region, who dwells in the atmosphere bearing a strength that endures the cleaving of mountains and clouds, and who is filled with greatness as rain-water falls on the earth, or who bears waters.

Here Sāyaṇa has explained the word as the earth, and has explained the sense thus: in the excellent region of the uttaravedi on this earth, येषु दिनेषु इंद्रावयो वरीयांसो देवा इज्यंते तानि सुदिनानि (*yeṣu dineṣu iṃdrāvayo varīyāṃso devā ijyaṃte tāni sudināni*) (printed इंद्रावयो (*iṃdrāvayo*) where the bhāṣya has द्रादयो (*drādayo*)), the days on which gods such as Indra, who are filled with greatness, are प्रशिसि (*praśisi*) (printed so; the sense is not clear from the supplied text, and is taken as worshipping, from इज्यंते (*ijyaṃte*) in the bhāṣya's words) and the sacrifice is performed, are determined to be the good days.

### Printed p. 463

दृषद्वत्यां—दृषदः उपलाः यस्यां संति । दृषद्वतीनाम काचिन्नदी तस्यां (*dṛṣadvatyāṃ—dṛṣadaḥ upalāḥ yasyāṃ saṃti | dṛṣadvatīnāma kācinnadī tasyāṃ*)—Because there are many stones in it, the river famous as दृष्टद्वती (*dṛṣṭadvatī*) (printed so, with the ṣṭa that the Saṃhitā and Pada do not have) flows through this excellent region fit for sacrifice; having described the sense in this way, Sāyaṇa explains that this word is used as a qualifier of the word मानुषे (*mānuṣe*), and describes the bank of the river दृष्टद्वती (*dṛṣṭadvatī*) as suitable for the movement of human beings.

आपयायां सरस्वत्यां—आपयानाम काचिन्नदी तस्यां (*āpayāyāṃ sarasvatyāṃ—āpayānāma kācinnadī tasyāṃ*)—Yāska has read सरस्वत्यः (*sarasvatyaḥ*) among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24).

इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः । पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥ (*iyaṃ śuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ | pārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖*) (Mi. Saṃ. 6-61-2, the abbreviation printed मि. सं. (*mi. saṃ.*) so). The word सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*) in this Ṛk is explained as a river.

सावका नस्सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः ॥ (*sāvakā nassarasvatī vājebhirvājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ ‖*) महो अर्णस्सरस्वती प्र चेतयति केतुना । धियो विश्वा वि राजति ॥ (*maho arṇassarasvatī pra cetayati ketunā | dhiyo viśvā vi rājati ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 1-3-10) (Kh. Saṃ. 1-3-12) [the two references stand one after the other below the two verses, as printed, with the abbreviations म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*) and ख. सं. (*kha. saṃ.*); the Ṛk numbers are as supplied]. The word सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*) in these Ṛks is explained in the sense of the deity who presides over speech.

Sāyaṇa has explained that the words आपया (*āpayā*) and सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*) are used in the sense of rivers famous by these very names, and has said महर्षयस्सरस्वतीतीरॆ यज्ञमकार्षुः (*maharṣayassarasvatītīrè yajñamakārṣuḥ*) (the great sages performed the sacrifice on the bank of the river Sarasvatī); he has quoted the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa ऋषयो वै सरस्वत्यां सत्रमासत (*ṛṣayo vai sarasvatyāṃ satramāsata*) (Ai. Brā. 2-19), and has explained that in such excellent regions, which are full of greatness, Agni is wished to be blazing forth so as to be endowed with wealth. The Kannada adds: see the description of this sacrifice in the introduction to this section.

Sū. 6-1-171) the case ending (the seventh case) takes the udātta accent.)*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, continued, printed page 464, noted not translated. दृषद्वत्यां (*dṛṣadvatyāṃ*): the root द्य विदारणे (*dya vidāraṇe*) (printed so); by दृणातेःषुग्प्रस्वश्च (*dṛṇāteḥṣugprasvaśca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-128, as printed) the augment printed शुकागम (*śukāgama*); the root becomes short. दृषदः उपलाः (कल्लुगळु) यस्यां संतीति दृष्टती तद- स्यास्ति (*dṛṣadaḥ upalāḥ (kallugaḷu) yasyāṃ saṃtīti dṛṣṭatī tada- syāsti*) (the stones, glossed in a bracket as कल्लुगळु (*kallugaḷu*), are in it; the form is printed दृष्टती (*dṛṣṭatī*)): by this the affix मतुप् (*matup*). Because the form of ta stands before a jhay letter, by झयः (*jhayaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-10) the ma of matup becomes va. By the paribhāṣā स्वरविधौव्यंजनमविद्यमानवत् (*svaravidhauvyaṃjanamavidyamānavat*) the ta between is as if absent, so that matup would stand after a short vowel and would have to take the udātta accent; but because that paribhāṣā is anitya (not constant) it is not resorted to here, the rule ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (*hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup*) does not operate, and so matup does not get the udātta accent; the earlier accent of the first affix (printed अदिप्रत्ययस्वर (*adipratyayasvara*)) comes. सरस्वत्यां (*sarasvatyāṃ*): the root सृ गतौ (*sṛ gatau*); when to it the Uṇādi affix (printed औणादिक (*auṇādika*)) असुन् (*asun*) comes, guṇa comes and the form is सरः (*saraḥ*); because the affix is a nit one, the initial udātta accent comes. सरः अस्याः अस्ति इति सरस्वती (*saraḥ asyāḥ asti iti sarasvatī*): the affix matup as before (the word "as before" is broken across two lines in the supplied text). Because it follows a word whose penultimate letter is a-kāra, by माडुपधायाश्च (*māḍupadhāyāśca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-29, as printed) the ma becomes va. Because it is ugit, by उगितश्च (*ugitaśca*) (Pā. Sū, 4-1-6, as printed with a comma after the abbreviation) the affix jīp in the feminine; because it is pit it is anudātta. दिदीहि (*didīhi*): the root दिवु क्रीडादिषु (*divu krīḍādiṣu*) (printed so); after the form ending in yaj-luk (printed यज् लुगंत (*yaj lugaṃta*)), loṭ; in the second person singular the form is दिदीहि (*didīhi*). Because it stands after a word printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) (as supplied), the nighāta accent comes.)*

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इळा॑मग्ने पुरु॒दंसं॑ स॒निं गोः श॑श्वत्त॒मं हव॑मानाय साध ।  
> स्यान्नः॑ सू॒नुस्तन॑यो वि॒जावाग्ने॒ सा ते॑ सुम॒तिर्भू॑त्व॒स्मे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इळां । अग्ने । पुरुदंसं । सनिं । गोः । शश्वत्तमं । हवमानाय । साध ।  
> स्यात् । नः । सूनुः । तनयः । विजावा । अग्ने । सा । ते । सुमतिः । भूतु । अस्मे  
> इति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने पुरुदंसं । अपोऽपो दंसो वेष इति कर्मनामसु पठितत्वा-
> द्दंसःशब्दः कर्मवाची । पुरूणि बहूनि दंसांसि कर्माणि यस्याः सा । तां बहुक-
> र्माणं गोः सनिं गवादिपशून्संपादयित्रीमिळामेतन्नामिकां गोरूपां देवतां
> शश्वत्तमं निरंतरं हवमानाय यजमानाय मह्यं साध । साधय। किंच नोऽस्माकं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is asked to provide the cow-formed Iḷā, giver of cattle, to the sacrificer, that sons and grandsons may be ours, and that his favour may bear fruit for us. The bhāṣya runs over the page break in two blocks; its grammatical tail is transcribed in the block, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). पुरुदंसं (*purudaṃsaṃ*)—that which is the means for many actions. गोः सनिं (*goḥ saniṃ*)—that which provides cows and the other animals. इळां (*iḷāṃ*)—the particular deity famous as इळा (*iḷā*) (or the earth). शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)—अनुसूतवागि (*anusūtavāgi*) (in unbroken succession). हवमानाय (*havamānāya*)—to me, who offer the oblation. साध—ऒदगिसिकॊडु (*sādha—òdagisikòḍu*) (provide). नः (*naḥ*)—to us. सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)—a son
- तनयः (*tanayaḥ*)—a grandson
- स्यात् (*syāt*)—may be obtained. अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. ते (*te*)—your. सुमतिः (*sumatiḥ*)—the excellent mind of favour that there is. सा (*sā*)—that. अस्मे (*asme*)—to our share. विजावा (*vijāvā*)—as that which gives fruit. भूतु (*bhūtu*)—may it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, make the earth, who is the helper of many actions, the giver of cows and other animals, named इळा (*iḷā*) and of the form of a cow, favourable to us, who are engaged in the constant performance of sacrifice; and, O Agni, may the auspicious intention that sons, grandsons and the rest should be granted to the praisers be always unbarren for us (सफलवागलि (*saphalavāgali*), "may it be fruitful").

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Grant, Agni, to the offerer of the oblation earth the giver of cattle, the means of many sacred rites, such that it may long endure : may there be to us sons and grandsons, and may your favour, Agni, be productive of good unto us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुरुदंसं—पुरूणि बहूनि दंसांसि कर्माणि यस्याः सा (*purudaṃsaṃ—purūṇi bahūni daṃsāṃsi karmāṇi yasyāḥ sā*)—In the series of twenty-six names of action, अप्पः दंसः (*appaḥ daṃsaḥ*) (Ni. 3-2), the word दंस (*daṃsa*) is stated. The sense is: that which has many actions.

गोः सनिं — गवादिपशून् संपादयित्रीं (*goḥ saniṃ — gavādipaśūn saṃpādayitrīṃ*)—The word गो (*go*) has many meanings: earth, speech, animal, ray. The words गोः सनिं (*goḥ saniṃ*) are qualifiers of the word इळा (*iḷā*) ... *[the supplied text breaks off at the end of this page in the middle of the word विशेषणवागिरु (*viśeṣaṇavāgiru*), so the sentence is not finished; the window ends here, in the middle of the Special Topics of Ṛk 5.]*

### Printed p. 466

(The entry on goḥ saniṃ continues:) ... because they are qualifiers (the word is completed across the page boundary), the sense is described that the deity Iḷā bestows cows and all the other things.

इळां—एतन्नामिकां गोरूपां देवतां (*iḷāṃ—etannāmikāṃ gorūpāṃ devatāṃ*)—The word इळा (*iḷā*) is stated among the names of the earth (Si. 2-5) [the reference is printed with the abbreviation ಸಿ., as supplied; the other references of this entry have ನಿ.]. It is stated also among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23), among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of the cow (Ni. 3-9). And the word इळा (*iḷā*) is derived from the root ईश (*īśa*).

अभि न इळा यूथस्य माता स्मन्नदीभिरुर्वशी ना गृणातु । उर्वशी वा बृहद्दि ना गृणानाभ्यूर्वाना प्रभृथस्यायोः । सिषक्तु न ऊर्जव्यस्य पुष्टेः ॥ (*abhi na iḷā yūthasya mātā smannadībhirurvaśī nā gṛṇātu | urvaśī vā bṛhaddi nā gṛṇānābhyūrvānā prabhṛthasyāyoḥ | siṣaktu na ūrjavyasya puṣṭeḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41-19, 20). In these Ṛks the goddess named इळा (*iḷā*) or इडा (*iḍā*) is described as a deity of the middle region. Sāyaṇa has explained the sense as the deity named इळा (*iḷā*) who wears the form of a cow.

शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध—निरंतरं हवमानाय यजमानाय मह्यं साधय । (*śaśvattamaṃ havamānāya sādha—niraṃtaraṃ havamānāya yajamānāya mahyaṃ sādhaya |*) Agni is prayed that the favour of the deity Iḷā, who is in the form of a cow, who fulfils the desired objects of the sacrificer who is always satisfying Agni with oblations, and who is filled with abundant greatness, may come about [the full stop after ಇಳಾದೇವತೆಯ is as supplied].

सूनुः—पुत्रः; तनयः पौत्रः । (*sūnuḥ—putraḥ; tanayaḥ pautraḥ |*) Among the fifteen names of offspring beginning with तुक्, तोकं (*tuk, tokaṃ*) (Ni. 3-2) the word tanaya and the word sūnu are read.

एता विश्वा सवना तूतुमा कृषे स्वयं सूनो सहसो यानि दधिषे । वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मंत्रो ब्रहोद्यतं वचः ॥ (*etā viśvā savanā tūtumā kṛṣe svayaṃ sūno sahaso yāni dadhiṣe | varāya te pātraṃ dharmaṇe tanā yajño maṃtro brahodyataṃ vacaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-50-6). In this Ṛk, having said that the word सूनो (*sūno*) means a son, Agni is called (सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*)) सहससूनो, बलस्य पुत्र (*sahasasūno, balasya putra*). Sāyaṇa has explained the word सूनु (*sūnu*) as son and the word तनय (*tanaya*) as grandson (the son of a son).

सुमतिः—शोभना बुद्धिः । (*sumatiḥ—śobhanā buddhiḥ |*) The author of the Nirukta has explained the same sense: in देवसुमतिं (*devasumatiṃ*) as देवनां कल्याणीं मतिं (*devanāṃ kalyāṇīṃ matiṃ*) (the auspicious intelligence of the deities); in वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम (*vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma*) as कल्याण्यां मतौ (*kalyāṇyāṃ matau*); and in वयं देवस्य धीमहि सुमतिं सत्यधर्मणः (*vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ*) again as कल्याणीं मतिं (*kalyāṇīṃ matiṃ*) [the full stop after ಮತಿಂ in the first case and the form ದೇವನಾಂ are as supplied]. It is prayed that the auspicious intelligence of Agni may arise, namely the birth and growth of sons, grandsons and the rest, which Agni may grant in respect of the sacrificers who have satisfied Agni with oblations.

## Sūkta 24 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-fourth sūkta** (इप्पत्तनाल्कनॆय सूक्तवु (*ippattanālkanèya sūktavu*))

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने सहस्वेति संचर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । अग्ने सहस्व
> गायत्रमाद्यानुष्टुबिति । ऋषिगार्थिनो विश्वामित्रः । अग्निर्देवता । आद्यानुष्टुप्
> शिष्टा गायत्रैः ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ प्रातरनुवाक आश्विनशस्त्रे च प्रथमा-
> वर्जितस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगः । अथैतस्या इति खंडे सूत्रितं । अग्नि इळेति चतस्रः । आ.
> ४-१३ । इति ॥ अभ्युदयेष्टावग्नेर्दातुरनुवाक्याग्ने दा दाशुष इत्येषा । अथा-
> ग्नेय्य इति खंडे सूत्रितं । अग्ने दा दाशुषे रयिं स यंता विप्र एषां । अ.
> ३-१३ । इति ॥

### Printed p. 468

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with अग्ने सहस्व (*agne sahasva*) is the twelfth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said अग्ने सहस्व गायत्रमाद्यानु-ष्टुबिति (*agne sahasva gāyatramādyānu-ṣṭubiti*) (the word is broken across two lines in the supplied text). For this sūkta Viśvāmitra, the son of Gāthi, is the seer; Agni is the deity. The first Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. The application of the sūkta is लैंगिक (*laiṃgika*) . That the Ṛks other than the first Ṛk of this sūkta are to be used at the time of the Prātaranuvāka and of the recitation of the Aśvina-śastra mantras is explained by the sūtra अग्नि इळेति चतस्रः (*agni iḷeti catasraḥ*) in the section of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra beginning अथैतस्या (*athaitasyā*) (Ā. 4-13); and that in the अभ्युदयेष्टि (*abhyudayeṣṭi*), in the homa made addressing the deity called अग्निर्दाता (*agnirdātā*), the Ṛk अग्ने दा दाशुषे (*agne dā dāśuṣe*) (the fifth Ṛk of this sūkta) is to be used as the Anuvākyā mantra is explained by the sūtra अग्ने दा दाशुषे रयिं स यंता विप्र एषां (*agne dā dāśuṣe rayiṃ sa yaṃtā vipra eṣāṃ*) in the section of the same work beginning अथाग्नेय्य (*athāgneyya*) (Ā. 3-13).
