##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, whom no one can overcome, overcoming the enemies by his own splendour, is asked to give food to the sacrificer who carries out the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. पृतनाः (*pṛtanāḥ*)—the armies (that oppose us). सहस्व (*sahasva*)—face and defeat. अभिमातीः (*abhimātīḥ*)—the enemies who, out of arrogance, cause obstruction to the rite. अपास्य (*apāsya*)—drive far away. दुष्टरः (*duṣṭaraḥ*)—the unassailable. अरातीः (*arātīḥ*)—the enemies. तरन् (*taran*)—(by your greatness) confronting. यज्ञवाहसे (*yajñavāhase*)—to the sacrificer who carries out the sacrifice. वर्चः (*varcaḥ*)—food full of splendour. धाः (*dhāḥ*)—give.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, face and defeat the armies that oppose us. Drive far away the enemies who, out of arrogance, cause obstruction to the rite. Confronting by your greatness the unassailable enemies, give food full of splendour to the sacrificer who carries out the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Repel, Agni, (hostile) hosts ; drive away (all) assailants ; inseparable, foe-surpassing, give food to the institutor of this sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अग्नि पृतनाः सहस्व—अभियोक्रीति सेनाभिभव । (*agni pṛtanāḥ sahasva—abhiyokrīti senābhibhava |*) The word पृतना (*pṛtanā*) is stated among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). In this sentence Agni is addressed. The sense is described that Agni may repel the armies that confront him.

अभिमातीः—अभितो मानं येषां (*abhimātīḥ—abhito mānaṃ yeṣāṃ*) Because they are extremely arrogant, it is wished that Agni may destroy the enemies who practise obstruction in respect of the sacrificial rites [the word ಕರ್ಮ-ವಿಘ್ನಕಾರಿಣಿ stands in the supplied text, hyphenated at the line end, before the Kannada rendering, as supplied].

दुष्टरः—दुस्तरः न केनापि तरितुं एक्यः (*duṣṭaraḥ—dustaraḥ na kenāpi tarituṃ ekyaḥ*) [the last word is printed so, as supplied] Yāska has cited the use of the word दुष्टर (*duṣṭara*) in this same sense—

### Printed p. 470

पृथक् प्रायन् प्रथमा देवहूतयोऽकृण्वत श्रवस्यानि दुष्टरा । न ये शेकुर्यज्ञियां नावमारुहमीर्मैव ते न्यविशंत केपयः ॥ (*pṛthak prāyan prathamā devahūtayo 'kṛṇvata śravasyāni duṣṭarā | na ye śekuryajñiyāṃ nāvamāruhamīrmaiva te nyaviśaṃta kepayaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-44-6). Here the sense is described that दुष्टरा (*duṣṭarā*) means दुस्तराणि (*dustarāṇi*).

अरातीः—अरातीन् शत्रून् । (*arātīḥ—arātīn śatrūn |*) Yāska has explained the meaning of the word अराति (*arāti*) as अरातयः अदानकर्माणः अदानप्रज्ञा ना (*arātayaḥ adānakarmāṇaḥ adānaprajñā nā*) (Ni. 3-11) [the last letters are as supplied]. Durgācārya, explaining the sense as अस्माक-मभिमतानर्थान् ददतो ये निवारयंति (*asmāka-mabhimatānarthān dadato ye nivārayaṃti*), those who prevent, by preaching to them, those who give us the things we desire are enemies, and explaining that there are two kinds of enemies, द्विविधाः हि शत्रवः दुःखसन्नाश्याः सुखसन्नाश्याश्च (*dvividhāḥ hi śatravaḥ duḥkhasannāśyāḥ sukhasannāśyāśca*), has also stated the details of the divisions of the अराति (*arāti*): तत्र ये दुःखसन्नाश्याः ते अदानप्रज्ञाः ये अदानकर्माणः ते सुखसन्नाश्याः (*tatra ye duḥkhasannāśyāḥ te adānaprajñāḥ ye adānakarmāṇaḥ te sukhasannāśyāḥ*).

Sāyaṇa, having said that the word ಆರಾತಿ means an enemy, wishes that Agni, scorning the enemies स्वतेजसा तिर-स्कुर्वन् तन्न तेजस्सिनिंद तिरस्करिसि (*svatejasā tira-skurvan tanna tejassiniṃda tiraskarisi*) with his own splendour, may grant food to the sacrificers who carry out the sacrifice.

वर्चः— अन्नं । (*varcaḥ— annaṃ |*) The word वर्चः (*varcaḥ*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9); Sāyaṇa has explained it here as food.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed pages 470 and 471, noted not translated. सहस्व (*sahasva*): the root षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*); sa for ṣa; loṭ, second person singular; by आमंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (*āmaṃtritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) the preceding vocative is treated as non-existent, so the nighāta accent does not come; by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-156) the root accent remains. अभिमातीः (*abhimātīḥ*): the root माज् माने (*māj māne*); by स्त्रीयांक्तिन् (*strīyāṃktin*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-94) the affix ktin; the root मा (*mā*) is read in घुमास्था (*ghumāsthā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66); in the bahuvrīhi compound the pūrvapada-prakṛti accent by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyāpūrvapadam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1); accusative plural. अस्य (*asya*): the root असु क्षेपणे (*asu kṣepaṇe*), divādi class; loṭ, second person singular; the nighāta accent comes. The grammar continues on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 471

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, continued, printed page 471. दुष्टरः (*duṣṭaraḥ*): the root तृ प्लवनतरणयोः (*tṛ plavanataraṇayoḥ*); by ईषदुःसुषु (*īṣaduḥsuṣu*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-126) the affix khal; guṇa of the ṛ; by सुषामादिषुच (*suṣāmādiṣuca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-98) ṣatva of the visarga-s of dus; because the affix has an indicatory l, the udātta accent comes before the affix by लिति (*liti*), whose sūtra number is printed with a stray letter, as supplied. तरन् (*taran*): the affix śatṛ; the root accent remains. धाः (*dhāḥ*): the root धुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*dhudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); luṅ in the sense of loṭ in the Veda; luk of sic by गातिस्थाघु (*gātisthāghu*); no aḍāgama in the Veda; the nighāta accent comes.)*

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्न॑ इ॒ळा समि॑ध्यसे वी॒तिहो॑त्रो॒ अम॑र्त्यः ।  
> जु॒षस्व॒ सू नो॑ अध्व॒रं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । इळा । सं । इध्रसे । वीतिहोत्रः । अमर्त्यः ।  
> जुषस्वः । सु , नः । अध्वरं ॥ २ ॥

*[Printed oddities in the Ṛk 2 text as supplied: the Saṃhitā begins ಅಗ್ನ ಇಳಾ where the Pada has ಅಗ್ನೇ; the Pada has ಇಧ್ರಸೇ where the Saṃhitā has ಸಮಿಧ್ಯಸೇ; and the Pada has ಜುಷಸ್ವಃ and ಸು , ನಃ with a visarga and a spaced comma.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने वीतिहोत्रः । वीतिः प्रीतिविषयं होत्रमग्निहोत्रादिकं यस्या-
> सौ वीतिहोत्रः । यज्ञेषु प्रीतिमानित्यर्थः । अनर्त्यो मरणधर्मरहितस्त्वमिळे-
> ळायामीड्यायामुत्तरवेद्यां समिध्यसे । आज्याहुतिप्रक्षेपेण सम्यक् प्रज्वाल्यसे ।
> तादृशस्त्वं नोऽस्माकमध्वरमिमं यज्ञं सु सुष्टु जुषस्व । आहुतिस्वीकरणेन से-
> वस्व ॥ वीतिहोत्रः । वी कांत्यादिषु । आस्मात् कर्मणि मंत्रे वृषेषपचेत्यादिना
> क्तिन्नुदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । जुषस्व । जुषतेर्लोटि रूपं । श-
> स्वरः । सु । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, immortal and delighting in sacrifices, is kindled with ghee oblations on the altar Iḷā; he is asked to accept our sacrifice.

### Printed p. 472

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. नीतिहोत्रः (*nītihotraḥ*)—he who is gratified by the sacrifice [the word is printed नीतिहोत्रः (*nītihotraḥ*) here, where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya have वीतिहोत्रः (*vītihotraḥ*); as supplied]. अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—free from the nature of death, you. इळा (*iḷā*)—on the worshipful northern altar (uttaravedi). समिध्यसे (*samidhyase*)—you are kindled. नः (*naḥ*)—our. अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—sacrifice. सु जुषस्व (*su juṣasva*)—accept (serve) with love.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni [printed with a long ā at the beginning: ಎಲೈ ಆಗ್ನಿಯೇ, as supplied], you who are gratified by the sacrifice and free from the nature of death are kindled on the worshipful northern altar. Accept our sacrifice with love.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, (who art) immortal and who art gratified byoblations [sic], thou. art kindled upon the altar : be pleased by this our sacrifice

*[The printed English is headed by a label in Latin letters, "English Translation.", and the first line breaks after "thou." before "art"; kept as supplied.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वीतिहोत्रः—वीतिः प्रीतिविषयं होत्रं अग्निहोत्रादिकं यस्य । यज्ञेषु प्रीतिमान् । (*vītihotraḥ—vītiḥ prītiviṣayaṃ hotraṃ agnihotrādikaṃ yasya | yajñeṣu prītimān |*) The sense of this word is described: Agni is one who has delight in the Agnihotra and the like.

अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—It is stated that Agni, who is without the nature of death, is kindled on the northern altar of the worshipful sacrificial hall by the ghee-oblations offered by the sacrificers, and it is wished that this Agni, accepting the sacrifice and the oblation of us who are the sacrificers, may serve (enjoy) them so that the sacrifice is well accomplished.

इळा (*iḷā*)—Although the word has many meanings, here, explained as इळायां ईड्यायां (*iḷāyāṃ īḍyāyāṃ*) ("worshipful"), it is used in the locative case in the sense of the northern altar.

अध्वरं—यज्ञं । (*adhvaraṃ—yajñaṃ |*) The word अध्वर (*adhvara*) is stated among the names of sacrifice, and is explained as ध्वरतिर्हिंसाकर्म तत्प्रतिषेधः (*dhvaratirhiṃsākarma tatpratiṣedhaḥ*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed pages 472 and 473, noted not translated. इळा (*iḷā*): by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the locative takes the substitute ā [the reference is printed with ಪಾ. ಸುಂ., as supplied]. इध्यसे (*idhyase*): the root इइंधी दीप्तौ (*iiṃdhī dīptau*) ; laṭ in the passive, second person singular; the tiṅanta nighāta accent comes. वीतिहोत्रः (*vītihotraḥ*): the root वी कांत्यादिपु (*vī kāṃtyādipu*) : the affix ktin comes in the passive, udātta, by मंत्रे वृषेषपच (*maṃtre vṛṣeṣapaca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96); वीतिः होत्रं यस्य सः (*vītiḥ hotraṃ yasya saḥ*); in the bahuvrīhi compound the pūrvapada-prakṛti accent comes. The grammar continues on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 473

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued, printed page 473. जुषस्व (*juṣasva*): the root जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*); loṭ, second person singular (the word is printed ಏಕವಚನಾಂತರೊಪ, as supplied); since the word stands at the beginning of the pāda the nighāta accent does not come; since the lasārvadhātuka becomes anudātta, the accent of the vikaraṇa (śa) remains. सु (*su*): by चादयोसत्वे (*cādayosatve*) (Pā. Sū. 1-4-57) it has the designation nipāta, and so by निपात-स्यच (*nipāta-syaca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136) there is lengthening in the Saṃhitā.)*

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ द्यु॒म्नेन॑ जागृवे॒ सह॑सः सूनवाहुत ।  
> एदं ब॒र्हिः स॑दो॒ मम॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । द्युम्नेन । जाग्रवे । सहसः । सूनो इति । आहुत ।  
> आ । इदं । बर्हिः । सदः । मम ॥ ३ ॥

*[Printed oddity: the Pada has ಜಾಗ್ರವೇ where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya have ಜಾಗೃವೇ; as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्युम्नेन स्वतेजसा सह जागृवे । जागर्तीति जागृविः । तस्य संबुद्धिः । लोक-
> रक्षार्थं स्वतेजसा सह सर्वदा जागरणोपेत आहुत देवताह्वानार्थमस्माभिराहुत
> सहसः सूनो बलस्य पुत्र हे अग्ने मम मत्संबंधिन्यस्मिन्यज्ञे यद्वेद्यामास्तीर्ण-
> मिदं बर्हिस्तत्रासदः । आसीद ॥ जागृवे । जागृ निद्राक्षये । ज्ञाश्चास्त्यजागृभ्यः
> क्विन्निति क्विन् । कित्वाद्गुणः । जागर्तीति जागृविः । जागृविर्जागरणात् । नि. ९-८ । इति
> यास्कः । संबुद्धौ चेति गुणः । एज् ह्रस्वात् । पा. ६-१-६९ । इति सोर्लोपः ।
> निघातः । सहसः सूनो । सुप आमंत्रिते परांगवद्भावादनुदात्तत्वे पादादित्वाद-
> निघातः । सदः । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेष्टित्यस्य छांदसे लुजि लृदित्वादज् ।
> निघातः । मम । अस्मच्छब्दस्य षष्ठैकवचने ममादेशः । युष्मदस्मदोर्जसीत्या-
> द्युदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, vigilant with his own splendour for the protection of the world, invoked by us, son of strength, is asked to sit on the barhis strewn on the altar of my sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

द्युम्नेन (*dyumnena*)—by your own splendour. जागृवे (*jāgṛve*)—the one who is awake (for the protection of the world). आहुत (*āhuta*)—the one who is invoked by us. सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—son of strength. अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. मम (*mama*)—of this altar of the sacrifice performed by me. इदं बर्हिः (*idaṃ barhiḥ*)—on this seat of darbha grass. आ सदः (*ā sadaḥ*)—sit down.

*[A stray line with the number 60 follows the Pratipadārtha at the foot of the page in the supplied text; kept as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 474

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who, for the protection of the world, are awake together with your own splendour, who are invoked by us and are the son of strength, sit on the darbha seat of this altar of the sacrifice performed by me.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, son of strength, vigilant (in the exercise of) your energy, take your seat when invoked, on the sacred grass (strewn at) my (sacrifice).

*[The label of the printed English translation is in Latin letters, without a full stop, as supplied; the first line breaks after "take" before "your".]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

द्युम्नेन जागृवे—जागर्तीति जागृविः । स्वतेजसा सह लोकरक्षार्थं सर्वदा जागरणोपेत। (*dyumnena jāgṛve—jāgartīti jāgṛviḥ | svatejasā saha lokarakṣārthaṃ sarvadā jāgaraṇopeta|*) The word द्युम्न (*dyumna*) is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9) and is explained as द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वा अन्नं वा (*dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vā annaṃ vā*). Here Sāyaṇa has explained the word as splendour (tejas). The Nirukta-author has quoted the word जागृवि (*jāgṛvi*) in the verse

प्रावेपा मा बृहतो मादयंति प्रवातेजा इरिणे वर्वृतानाः । सोमस्येव मौजवतस्य भक्षो विभीदको जागृविर्मह्यमच्छान् ॥ (*prāvepā mā bṛhato mādayaṃti pravātejā iriṇe varvṛtānāḥ | somasyeva maujavatasya bhakṣo vibhīdako jāgṛvirmahyamacchān ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-34-1) and explained it as जागृविर्जागरणात् (*jāgṛvirjāgaraṇāt*). Durgācārya has explained the meaning of the word जागृवि (*jāgṛvi*) as one who keeps awake: जागृविः जागरण-कर्ता— यो जयति सः हर्षेण जागर्ति, यो जीयते सः दुःखेन जागर्ति (*jāgṛviḥ jāgaraṇa-kartā— yo jayati saḥ harṣeṇa jāgarti, yo jīyate saḥ duḥkhena jāgarti*); that is, one who has won keeps awake with joy, one who has been defeated is awake with sorrow. Here the sense is explained that Agni is always awake, with his own splendour, in order to protect the world.

आहुत—देवानां आह्वानार्थमस्माभिः आहुत । (*āhuta—devānāṃ āhvānārthamasmābhiḥ āhuta |*) The word आहुत (*āhuta*) is explained in the Ṛk quoted by Yāska,

हविष्पान्तमजरं स्वर्विदि दिविस्पृश्याहुतं जुष्टमग्नौ । तस्य भर्मणे भुवनाय देवा धर्मणे कं स्वधया पप्रथंत ॥ (*haviṣpāntamajaraṃ svarvidi divispṛśyāhutaṃ juṣṭamagnau | tasya bharmaṇe bhuvanāya devā dharmaṇe kaṃ svadhayā paprathaṃta ‖*)

(मि. सं. (*mi. saṃ.*) 10-88-1) in which the sense is explained as आहुतं अभिहुतं विसृष्टं (*āhutaṃ abhihutaṃ visṛṣṭaṃ*), "offered" [the line that follows the verse in the supplied text begins with the fragment ಲ್ಲಿ; as supplied; the beginning of the sentence is lost].

सिनीवालि पृथुष्टुके या देवानामसि स्वसा । जुषस्व हव्यमाहुतं प्रजां देवि दिदिड्डि नः ॥ (*sinīvāli pṛthuṣṭuke yā devānāmasi svasā | juṣasva havyamāhutaṃ prajāṃ devi didiḍḍi naḥ ‖*)

(म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*) 2-32-6) In this Ṛk also the word आहुतशब्दवु (*āhutaśabdavu*) is explained, in the sense of that which is offered into the fire in the manner stated in the Śāstra, in conformity with the rule: मर्यादया विधानतः हुतं (*maryādayā vidhānataḥ hutaṃ*).

### Printed p. 475

By this word Agni is addressed as one who has the oblation offered for bringing the gods to the sacrifice.

सहस: सूनो (*sahasa: sūno*)—बलस्य पुत्र (*balasya putra*). Because Agni is produced by rubbing in the araṇis, and is born of strength, he is addressed by this word.

Durgācārya has explained the meaning of the words सूनो (*sūno*) सहसः (*sahasaḥ*) in the following way: अधिदेवताभावेन प्राण इंद्रो व्यवस्थितः तस्यॆतरो यः प्रज्ञामुत्पाद्यावशिष्टः प्राणः सः पुत्रः इत्येवमुपपद्यते पितृपुत्र- भावः । तदुक्तं “ प्राणो वा अहमस्मि प्राणस्त्वं प्राणस्सर्वाणि भूतानि” इति (*adhidevatābhāvena prāṇa iṃdro vyavasthitaḥ tasyètaro yaḥ prajñāmutpādyāvaśiṣṭaḥ prāṇaḥ saḥ putraḥ ityevamupapadyate pitṛputra- bhāvaḥ | taduktaṃ “ prāṇo vā ahamasmi prāṇastvaṃ prāṇassarvāṇi bhūtāni” iti*). (The supplied text gives no separate translation of this Sanskrit passage; the Kannada comment on it follows.)

Explaining that by the adhidevatā aspect Indra stands in the form of prāṇa, that in the matter of producing consciousness the other prāṇa-vāyus are helpers, and the relation of father and son between the prāṇa-vāyu and the other airs connected with it, he has cited the Śruti sentence that teaches this view. This explanation is concerned with Indra.

In the present Ṛk, addressing Agni by this word, the sacrificer's wish is described: मत्संबंधिन्यस्मि यज्ञे यद्वेद्यामास्तीर्ण० बर्हिः तत्र आसीद (*matsaṃbaṃdhinyasmi yajñe yadvedyāmāstīrṇa0 barhiḥ tatra āsīda*) [the word ending in ಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ೦ is printed with a zero sign at the end, as supplied], that is, may Agni be seated on the barhis spread on the sacrificial altar in the sacrifice performed by the sacrificer.

बर्हिः—बर्हिश्यब्दवु अंतरिक्षनामगळल्लियू (नि. २-१०) उदकनामगळल्लियू (नि. २-२४) उक्तवागि बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् (*barhiḥ—barhiśyabdavu aṃtarikṣanāmagaḷalliyū (ni. 2-10) udakanāmagaḷalliyū (ni. 2-24) uktavāgi barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt*) (Ni. 8-9). The word बर्हिश्यब्द (*barhiśyabda*) is stated among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10) and among the names of water (Ni. 2-24), and is explained as बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् (*barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt*).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ विश्वे॑भिर॒ग्निभि॑र्दे॒वेभि॑र्महया॒-गिरः॑ ।  
> य॒ज्ञेषु॒ य उ॑ चा॒यवः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> *agne viśvebhiragnibhirdevebhirmahayā-giraḥ |*  
> *yajñeṣu ya u cāyavaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

*[Printed oddity: the Saṃhitā line has a hyphen inside the line, between महया (*mahayā*) and गिरः (*giraḥ*), where the Pada has महय (*mahaya*) and गिरः (*giraḥ*) as separate words; as supplied.]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । विश्वेभिः । अग्निभिः । देवेभिः । महय । गिरः ।  
> यज्ञेषु । ये । ऊं इति । चायवः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आग्ने देवेभिर्द्योतमानैर्विश्वेभिः सर्वैरग्निभिर्यष्टव्यतया स्थितैरग्निभिः
> सहितस्त्वं चायव उक्तविषयस्तुतिरूपाभिर्वाग्निरनन्यमनस्कतया पूजका ये वि-
> द्यंते तेषां यज्ञेषु ज्योतिष्टोमादिषु गिरः स्तोत्रशस्त्रादिलक्षणानि वाक्यानि
> महय । पूजय ॥ मह पूजायां । चुरादिः । अदंतत्वादुपधावृद्ध्यभावः ।
> निघातः । चायवः । चाय् पूजानिशामनयोः । मृगय्दादयश्चति कुप्रत्ययः ।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, together with all the fires that stand as objects of worship, honour the praise-words of the worshippers in the sacrifices.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—luminous. विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*)—all. अग्निभिः (*agnibhiḥ*)—you who are joined with the other Agnis (who are your other forms). चायवः (*cāyavaḥ*)—your worshippers; ये (*ye*)—whichever sacrificers there are, of such ones. यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*)—in the sacrifices beginning with the Jyotiṣṭoma. गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the words in the form of praise. महय (*mahaya*)—honour and listen.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who are joined with all the other Agnis, which are luminous and are your own other forms [the word is printed रूपांतवू (*rūpāṃtavū*) here, where the Pratipadārtha has रूपांतरगळाद (*rūpāṃtaragaḷāda*); as supplied], honour with respect and listen to the praise-words, recited by them, in the sacrifices beginning with the Jyotiṣṭoma, of whichever sacrificers there are who are your worshippers.

### Printed p. 477

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, with all the divine fires, respect the praises of those who in (their) sacrifices are (your especial) worshippers.

*[The label of the printed English translation is in Latin letters, without a full stop, as supplied.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

देवेभिः—द्योतमानैः! (*devebhiḥ—dyotamānaiḥ!*) [the sign after the word is printed as an exclamation mark, as supplied]. The word is explained as देवो दानाद्वा दीपनाद्वा द्योतनाद्वा द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा (*devo dānādvā dīpanādvā dyotanādvā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā*) (Ni. 7-15). Here the meaning is explained as those who possess light.

अग्निभिः—यष्टव्यतया स्थितैरग्निभिः (*agnibhiḥ—yaṣṭavyatayā sthitairagnibhiḥ*) The word अग्नि (*agni*) has been explained by Yāska [printed वाख्यात (*vākhyāta*), as supplied]. Here the meaning is described as follows: Agni is joined with the varieties of Agni who are famous by their respective names, according to the order stated in the Śāstra, for offering the oblation in the sacrifice.

चायवः—तद्विषयस्तुतिरूपाभिः वाग्निः अनन्यमनस्कतया पूजकाः । (*cāyavaḥ—tadviṣayastutirūpābhiḥ vāgniḥ ananyamanaskatayā pūjakāḥ |*) [the bhāṣya has उक्तविषय (*uktaviṣaya*) where this has तद्विषय (*tadviṣaya*); as supplied]. The meaning of the word चावयः (*cāvayaḥ*) [so printed here, with ವ, where the Ṛk has चायवः (*cāyavaḥ*); as supplied] is described as those who praise, with one mind, those worthy of praise with the respective words fit for praising.

यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*)—Although the word yajña denotes sacrifice in general, here it is used in the sense of ज्योतिष्टोमादिसु (*jyotiṣṭomādisu*) , that is, in the sacrifices beginning with the Jyotiṣṭoma. It is explained that the wish of the sacrificer is described: may Agni, together with the other Agnis who are worthy of the sacrifice and famous in the respective sacrifices, be worshipped by those who worship with a concentrated mind, with the respective words in the form of stotra and śastra.

गिरः—स्तोत्रशस्त्रादिलक्षणानि वाक्यानि । (*giraḥ—stotraśastrādilakṣaṇāni vākyāni |*) The word गीः (*gīḥ*) is stated among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23).

मा त्वा सोमस्य गल्बया सदा याचन्नहं गिरा । भूर्णिं मृगं न सवनेषु चुक्रुद्धं क ईशानं न याचिषत्॥ (*mā tvā somasya galbayā sadā yācannahaṃ girā | bhūrṇiṃ mṛgaṃ na savaneṣu cukruddhaṃ ka īśānaṃ na yāciṣat‖*)

(पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*)81-20) [the reference is printed so, with the abbreviation पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) and no space before the numbers; as supplied] Here the meaning of the word गिरा (*girā*) is explained as गीत्या स्तुत्या (*gītyā stutyā*). In “तमूषु समना गिरा (*tamūṣu samanā girā*)” (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-3-26-1) also गिरा (*girā*) is used in the same sense, गीत्या स्तुत्या (*gītyā stutyā*).

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed pages 477 and 478, noted not translated. विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*): in the Chandas, by ना छंदसि (*nā chaṃdasi*) the substitution ऐस्‌भाव (*aisbhāva*) for भिसिगॆ (*bhisigè*) is optional, and so does not come here. For the loṭ, second person singular (sip) the grammar continues on the next page.)*

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ दा दा॒शुषे॑ र॒यिं वी॒रवं॑तं॒ परी॑णसं ।  
> शि॒शी॒हि नः॑ सूनु॒मतः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

> अग्ने । दाः । दाशुषे । रयिं । वीरवंतं । परीणसं ।  
> शिशीहि । नः । सूनुमतः H ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने दाशुषे तुभ्यं हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय वीरवंतं पुत्रयुक्तं
> परीणसं प्रभूतं रयिं धनं दाः । देहि । सूनुमतः पुत्रपौत्रादिसहितान्नोऽस्मान्
> शिशीहि । धनप्रदानेन तीक्ष्णीकुरु ॥ दाः । डुदाञ् दान इत्यस्य छांवसे लुजु रूपं
> आमंत्रितस्याविद्यमानत्वेन पादादित्वादनिघातः । दाशुषे । दाश्य दान इत्यस्य क्वसौ
> दाश्वान्साह्वान्मीढ्वांश्चति निपातनात् द्विर्वचनाभाव इडभावश्च । भसंज्ञायां संप्र-
> सारणं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । परीणसं । परिपूर्वान्नसतेव्याप्त्यर्थात् क्विप् । अन्वेषा-
> मपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः । शिशीहि । शिञ् निशाने । व्यत्ययेन श्लुः । दीर्घश्चांदसः
> हेरपित्त्वादंतोदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, give abundant wealth together with sons to the sacrificer who has offered you the oblation, and make us, with sons and grandsons, sharp by the gift of wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers you the oblation. वीरवंतं (*vīravaṃtaṃ*)—that which is accompanied by sons; परीणसं (*parīṇasaṃ*)—and abundant. रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth. दारि (*dāri*)—give [the word is printed दारि (*dāri*) here, where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya have दाः (*dāḥ*); as supplied]. सूनुमतः (*sūnumataḥ*)—accompanied by sons, grandsons and the rest. नः (*naḥ*)—us. शिशीहि (*śiśīhi*)—make (by the gift of wealth) full of splendour.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, give to the sacrificer who offers you the oblation wealth that is accompanied by sons and is abundant. Make us, who are accompanied by sons, grandsons and the rest, full of splendour by the gift of wealth (printed धनपदानदिंद (*dhanapadānadiṃda*) here, where the bhāṣya has धनप्रदानेन (*dhanapradānena*); as supplied).

*[The page, and with it the window, ends with the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 5; the printed English translation and the Special Topics of Ṛk 5 follow on the next page.]*

### Printed p. 479

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Grant, Agni, ample wealth and progcny [sic] to the donor (of the oblation).
Make us prosperous, possessed of offspring.

*[The label of the printed English translation is in Latin letters, in italics, with a full stop, as supplied.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दाशुषे-तुभ्यं हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय । (*dāśuṣe-tubhyaṃ havirdattavate yajamānāya |*) (the gloss of Sāyaṇa on the word दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)). Yāska: धाता ददातु दाशुषे प्राचीं जीवातुमक्षितां । वयं देवस्य धीमहि सुमतिं सत्यधर्मिणः ॥ (*dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe prācīṃ jīvātumakṣitāṃ | vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmiṇaḥ ‖*) (अथ. सं. (*atha. saṃ.*) 7-17-1). Here the meaning दत्तवते (*dattavate*) has been explained for the word दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*). Sāyaṇa has described the meaning as follows: Agni is addressed [the verb is printed in two parts across a line break, संचो (*saṃco*) and धिसिदॆ (*dhisidè*); as supplied], and may Agni favour the sacrificer who has offered him the oblation with abundant wealth together with sons.

वीरवंतं— पुत्रयुक्तं । (*vīravaṃtaṃ— putrayuktaṃ |*) Yāska has explained: वीरवंतः कल्याणवीरा वा वीरो वीरयत्यमित्रान् वेतेर्वास्याद्धतिकर्मणो वीरयतीर्वा । (*vīravaṃtaḥ kalyāṇavīrā vā vīro vīrayatyamitrān vetervāsyāddhatikarmaṇo vīrayatīrvā |*) (Ni. 1-7) (one word of the quotation is broken across two lines in the supplied text). Durgācārya has said that the word वीर (*vīra*) is derived from a root with the sense of going (printed विधातुविनिंद (*vidhātuviniṃda*)), or that it is derived from the root वीर (*vīra*) [printed वीरधातुपिनिंद (*vīradhātupiniṃda*); as supplied], which denotes valour, and is used in the sense of one who destroys enemies वानाविधवागि (*vānāvidhavāgi*) . Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as "accompanied by sons".

परीणसं (*parīṇasaṃ*)—प्रभूतं परीणसा (*prabhūtaṃ parīṇasā*) is stated among the names of "much" (Ni. 3-13). Here it is used in the sense of बहळ (*bahaḷa*) or बहु (*bahu*).

सूनुमतः नः शिशीहि (*sūnumataḥ naḥ śiśīhi*)— as to the word सूनुमतः (*sūnumataḥ*), the wish is expressed that Agni, by granting wealth to the sacrificers who are accompanied by sons and grandsons (मक्कळु मन्नॊक्कळु (*makkaḷu mannòkkaḷu*) , that is, children and grandchildren), may make them full of splendour [printed तेजश्वालिगळागिरु (*tejaśvāligaḷāgiru*); as supplied]. The word सूनु (*sūnu*) is stated among the names of offspring (Ni. 3-2).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed pages 479 and 480, noted not translated. दाः (*dāḥ*): the root डुदाञ् दाने (*ḍudāñ dāne*); by छंदसिलुज् लज् लिटः (*chaṃdasiluj laj liṭaḥ*) luṅ in the sense of loṭ; second person singular, sip; by इतश्च (*itaśca*) loss of the i; the fragment च्चिगॆ (*ccigè*) takes the substitute सिचादेश (*sicādeśa*) ; by गातिस्थाघुवा (*gātisthāghuvā*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77) luk of it; by बहुलंछंदस्य— (*bahulaṃchaṃdasya—*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75) the augment aḍ does not come; because an āmantrita precedes, it has the status of non-existence, so it stands as if at the beginning of a pāda and the anudātta accent does not come; by the accent of the root it becomes udātta.)*

### Printed p. 480

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, continued, printed page 480. दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*): the root दाशृदाने (*dāśṛdāne*); when the affix kvasu comes, because it is made nipātana by दाश्वान् साह्वान् मीढ्वांश्च (*dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃśca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-12), the doubling and the augment iḍ do not come; in the dative singular, because it has the bha-designation, saṃprasāraṇa and pūrvarūpa; by the accent of the affix the u becomes udātta. परीणसं (*parīṇasaṃ*): the prefix pari; the root णस व्याप्तौ (*ṇasa vyāptau*); when pari is the upapada, by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) the affix kvip; by अन्येषामपिदृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapidṛśyate*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-134) lengthening of the preceding word; by vyatyaya the ādyudātta accent comes. शिशीहि (*śiśīhi*): the root शिञ् निशाने (*śiñ niśāne*); loṭ, second person singular, hi as the substitute for sip; by व्यत्ययो बहुलं (*vyatyayo bahulaṃ*) the vikaraṇa śplu; by श्लु (*ślu*) doubling of the root; in the Chāndasa, lengthening of the i of the root; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda the nighāta accent does not come; because the apittva is prescribed in this way it becomes udātta.)*

## Sūkta 25 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-fifth sūkta** (इप्पत्तैदनॆय सूक्तवु (*ippattaidanèya sūktavu*))

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने दिव इति पंचर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं । अत्रेयमनुक्रम-
> णिका । अग्ने दिवो वैराजमुपांत्याग्नेंद्रीति । विराट् छंदः । अग्न इंद्रश्चेत्ये-
> षेंद्राग्नीदेवताका । शिष्टा आग्नेय्यः ॥ अग्निष्टोम आज्यशस्त्रेऽग्न इंद्रश्चेति
> याज्या । अग्न इंद्रश्च दाशुषो दुरोण इति याज्या । आ. ५-९ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with अग्ने दिव (*agne diva*) is the thirteenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. For this sūkta Viśvāmitra is the seer; in the Anukramaṇikā it is said अग्ने दिवो वैराजमुपांत्याग्नेंद्रीति (*agne divo vairājamupāṃtyāgneṃdrīti*). For the Ṛk अग्न इंद्रश्च दाशुषः (*agna iṃdraśca dāśuṣaḥ*) of this sūkta (the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta) Agni and Indra are the deities; for the remaining Ṛks Agni is the deity; the metre is Virāṭ. That in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, in the homa relating to the Ājyaśastra, the Ṛk beginning अग्न इंद्रश्च (*agna iṃdraśca*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra is explained by the sūtra अग्न इंद्रश्च दाशुषो दुरोण इति याज्या (*agna iṃdraśca dāśuṣo duroṇa iti yājyā*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 5-9).

**Sūkta data .** Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 25. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 1; Varga 25. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: विश्वामित्रः (*viśvāmitraḥ*) (Viśvāmitra). Devatā: Ṛks 1-3 and 5 अग्निः (*agniḥ*) (Agni); Ṛk 4 इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*) (Indra and Agni together). Chandas: विराट् (*virāṭ*) (Virāṭ).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ दि॒वः सू॒नुर॑सि॒ प्रचे॑ता॒स्तना॑ पृथि॒व्या उ॒त वि॒श्ववे॑दाः ।  
> ऋधगेवा इह यजा चिकित्स्यः ॥ १ ॥

> *agne divaḥ sūnurasi pracetāstanā pṛthivyā uta viśvavedāḥ |*  
> *ṛdhagevā iha yajā cikitsyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

*[Printed oddity: the Saṃhitā line has ऋधगेवा (*ṛdhagevā*) and चिकित्स्यः (*cikitsyaḥ*) where the Pada has यधक् (*yadhak*), देवान् (*devān*) and चिकित्वः (*cikitvaḥ*) (the bhāṣya has ऋधक् (*ṛdhak*) and चिकित्सश्चेतनावन् (*cikitsaścetanāvan*)); as supplied.]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । दिवः । सूनुः । असि । प्रचेताः । तना । पृथिव्याः । उत । विश्ववेदाः ।  
> यधक् । देवान् । इह । यज । चिकित्वः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वामित्रः स्तौति । हे अग्ने विश्ववेदाः सर्वविषयज्ञानवान् प्रचेताः
> कर्मविषयज्ञानवांस्त्वं दिवो द्युलोकाभिमानिदेवतायाः सूनुरसि । पुत्रो
> भवसि । उत अपि च पृथिव्याः पृथिव्यभिमानिदेवतायास्तना तनयोऽसि । किंच । चिकित्स-
> श्चेतनावन् हे अग्ने इहास्माभिः क्रियमाणेऽस्मिन्कर्मणि देवान् यजनीया-
> निंद्रादिदेवान् ऋधक् पृथक् क्रमेण यज । हविष्ट्रदानेन पूजय ॥ असि । अस
> भुवीत्यस्य लट तासस्त्योर्लोप इति सलोपः । निघातः । विश्ववेदाः । बहुव्रीहौ
> विश्वं संज्ञायामिति विश्वस्यांतोदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises Agni: knowing all and the rite, you are the son of heaven and the offspring of earth; worship the gods severally here with oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*)—you who know all things, प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*)—and who have knowledge in the matter of rites. दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the deity presiding over the heavenly world
- सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)—as son
- असि (*asi*)—you are. उत (*uta*)—and
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the deity of the earth
- तना (*tanā*)—you are also the offspring. इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice of ours
- चिकित्सं (*cikitsaṃ*)—you who are wise [the word is printed चिकित्सं (*cikitsaṃ*) here, where the Saṃhitā has चिकित्स्यः (*cikitsyaḥ*) and the Pada चिकित्वः (*cikitvaḥ*); as supplied]
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods Indra and the rest
- ऋधक् (*ṛdhak*)—separately (in accordance with their respective places)
- यज (*yaja*)—worship

### Printed p. 482

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who know all things and have knowledge relating to rites, you are the son of the deity presiding over the heavenly world, and you are also the offspring of the deity of the earth. You who are wise, in this sacrifice of ours worship Indra and the other gods severally, in accordance with their respective places.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni you are omniscient, and the discriminator (of acts), you are the son of heaven or the son of earth : you are intelligent; worship severally the gods on this occasion.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्रचेताः—कर्मविषयज्ञानवान् । (*pracetāḥ—karmaviṣayajñānavān |*) The authors of the Nirukta (निरुक्तकाररु (*niruktakāraru*)) quote: आ जंघंति सान्वेषां जघना उप जिघ्नते । आश्वाजनि प्रचेतसोऽश्वानमत्तु चोदय ॥ (*ā jaṃghaṃti sānveṣāṃ jaghanā upa jighnate | āśvājani pracetaso 'śvānamattu codaya ‖*) (पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) 6-75-13). Having quoted this Ṛk, they have explained the meaning of the word प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*) as प्रवृद्धचेतसः (*pravṛddhacetasaḥ*). Durgācārya has given the meaning प्रकृष्टचेतसः (*prakṛṣṭacetasaḥ*), that is, possessing excessive knowledge. Sāyaṇa, addressing Agni, has described the meaning thus: he is विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*), one who has every kind of knowledge and who knows the sacrificial rites; दिवः सूनुः (*divaḥ sūnuḥ*), the son of the deity presiding over the heavenly world; and पृथिव्याःतना (*pṛthivyāḥtanā*) [printed run together; as supplied], the son of the deity presiding over the earth. The word तना (*tanā*) is stated among the names of wealth (सि. (*si.*) 3-9), but here, he has said, it is used in the sense of offspring or son. The authors of the Nirukta have quoted that, although the word द्यु (*dyu*) is stated among the names of day (सि. (*si.*) 2-21), it is also used in the sense of the heavenly world. In त्वमग्नि द्युभिः (*tvamagni dyubhiḥ*) (ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 2-1-1), in उप श्वासयपृथिवीमुतद्यां (*upa śvāsayapṛthivīmutadyāṃ*) [printed run together; as supplied] (ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 6-47-29) and in मित्रो जनान् यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां (*mitro janān yātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ*) (ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 3-59-1) the word द्यु (*dyu*) is used in the senses of day and of the heavenly world.

चिकित्त्वः (*cikittvaḥ*) [so printed here, differing from the forms of the word in the Saṃhitā and the Pada of Ṛk 1; as supplied]—by this word Agni, who has understanding (चेतनावन् (*cetanāvan*)), is addressed as wise. इह देवान् यधक् यज (*iha devān yadhak yaja*)—it is explained that the wish of the sacrificers is described: in the sacrificial rite which the sacrificers are performing, let Agni worship, offering the oblation, the gods worthy of the sacrifice (printed यार्गार्हराद (*yārgārharāda*); as supplied) such as Indra.

चिकित्वान्— (*cikitvān—*) this word also is quoted as used in the sense of चेतनावान् (*cetanāvān*) (Ni. 8-5) in समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे (*samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe*) (ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 10-110-1).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 483, noted not translated. प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*): the root चिती ज्ञाने (*citī jñāne*), affix asun; by पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) guṇa of the light penultimate of the root; as a bahuvrīhi the accent of the first member comes. तना (*tanā*): the root तनु विस्तारे (*tanu vistāre*), affix kvip; by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the substitute ā for the ending su. असि (*asi*): the root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*), laṭ, second person singular, sip; by तासस्त्योर्लोपः (*tāsastyorlopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-50) loss of the s of the root; the nighāta accent comes. विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*): the root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*), the Uṇādi affix asun, guṇa of the penultimate; by बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायां (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-106) the word viśva takes the antodātta accent. यज (*yaja*): the root यज देवपूजादिषु (*yaja devapūjādiṣu*), loṭ, second person singular; the nighāta accent; by द्व्यचोतस्तिजः (*dvyacotastijaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135) lengthening in the Saṃhitā. चिकित्सॆ: (*cikitsè:*) : the root कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*); the substitute kvasu for liṭ; doubling of the root; because the affix is kit the guṇa of the penultimate does not come; in the vocative the nighāta accent by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*).)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, who knows the rites, gives the sacrificer powers such as cattle and sons, adorns the world, and gives food to the immortal gods; he is asked to bring the gods here.

### Printed p. 484

*[The two following labels are garbled in the supplied text: प्रदर्शन (*pradarśana*) for the Pratipadārtha and भाषॆ (*bhāṣè*) for the Bhāvārtha. Both stood inside the bhāṣya block with their texts; the garbled lines are kept as italic notes and the standard labels inserted.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—knowing the matters of rites. अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni. वीर्याणि (*vīryāṇi*)—the powers in the form of cattle, sons and so on. सनोति (*sanoti*)—he gives; and भूषन् (*bhūṣan*)—(with his splendour) adorning the whole world. अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—to the gods Indra and the rest, who are free from the nature of death, वादं (*vādaṃ*) [so printed, where the Pada has वाजं (*vājaṃ*); as supplied]—food in the form of oblation. सनोति (*sanoti*)—he offers. पुरुक्षो (*purukṣo*)—O Agni, endowed with the purodāśa-cake and other foods. सः (*saḥ*)—such as you are. नः (*naḥ*)—of ours. इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice. देवान् (*devān*)—the gods worthy of the sacrifice. आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring along with you.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who knows the matters of rites, gives the powers in the form of cattle, sons and so on. Adorning the whole world with his splendour, he offers food in the form of oblation to the Indra and the other gods who are free from the nature of death. O Agni, endowed with the purodāśa-cake and other foods, such as you are, bring along with you in this sacrifice of ours the gods who are worthy of the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The wise Agni bestows faculties (securing prosperity and descendants) ; adorning (the world with lustre) he gives (sacrificial food) to the immortals : Agni, (to whom) many oblations (are offered), bring hither to us the gods.

*[The word "descendants" is broken across two lines in the print ("descen-" and "dants"); joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अग्निः वीर्याणि सनोति—पशुपुत्रादिसंपद्रूपाणि सामर्थ्यानि यजमानाय ददाति. (*agniḥ vīryāṇi sanoti—paśuputrādisaṃpadrūpāṇi sāmarthyāni yajamānāya dadāti.*) The meaning is explained thus: Agni will bestow strength and power on the sacrificers in forms such as cattle, sons and wealth. Yāska, in the Ṛk यो अनिध्मो दीदयदप्सन्नर्यं विप्रास ईळके अध्वरेषु । अपान्न पान्मधुमतीरपो दा याभिरिंद्रो वावृधे वीर्याय ॥ (*yo anidhmo dīdayadapsannaryaṃ viprāsa īḷake adhvareṣu | apānna pānmadhumatīrapo dā yābhiriṃdro vāvṛdhe vīryāya ‖*) (म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*) 10-30-4) [the Kannada word for "Ṛk" is printed ऋत्किनल्लि (*ṛtkinalli*) here; as supplied], has described the meaning of the word वीर्याय (*vīryāya*) as वीरकर्मणे (*vīrakarmaṇe*).

### Printed p. 485

भूषन् (*bhūṣan*)—he explains the meaning: Agni makes the whole world, by his splendour, as if adorned; and having done so, he has described the meaning of अमृताय मरणरहिताय इंद्रादिदेवाय वाजं सनोति (*amṛtāya maraṇarahitāya iṃdrādidevāya vājaṃ sanoti*): Agni will convey to the gods Indra and the rest, who are free from death, the food in the form of oblation offered by the sacrificers.

पुरुक्षो—पुरवः क्षुधः अन्नानि यस्य । (*purukṣo—puravaḥ kṣudhaḥ annāni yasya |*) बहुविधान्नोपेत. (*bahuvidhānnopeta.*) By this word Agni is addressed as one who has many kinds of food such as पुरो डारवे (*puro ḍārave*) [so printed, broken across two lines; as supplied].

नः इह देवान् आ वह (*naḥ iha devān ā vaha*)—by this sentence it is explained that Agni should invite the gods worthy of the sacrifice, so that they may receive the oblation offered in this sacrifice which we, the sacrificers, are performing. The meaning of the word देव (*deva*) is described here as the gods worthy of the sacrifice (printed यागार्हराव (*yāgārharāva*); as supplied).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed page 485, noted not translated. सनोति (*sanoti*): the root षणु दाने (*ṣaṇu dāne*); by धात्वादेः षः सः (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*) the substitution of s for the initial; by तनादिकृञ्भ्यउः (*tanādikṛñbhyauḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-79) the vikaraṇa u; third person singular. Because the verb अग्नि (*agni*) stands before it, the nighāta accent comes; the second सनोति (*sanoti*) stands at the beginning of a pāda and has no nighāta; by the accent of the vikaraṇa it is madhyodātta. भूषन् (*bhūṣan*): the root भूष अलंकारे (*bhūṣa alaṃkāre*), a root with the sense of the causative included; the substitute śatṛ [printed so, with लिटिगॆ (*liṭigè*); as supplied]; because it is a lasārvadhātuka that comes after a root ending in a, by तास्यनुपात्तेत् (*tāsyanupāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) it is anudātta, so the accent of the root remains. वह (*vaha*): the root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*), loṭ, second person singular; the nighāta accent of the verb comes. पुरुक्षो (*purukṣo*): पुरवः क्षुधोऽन्नानि यस्य सः पुरुक्षुः (*puravaḥ kṣudho 'nnāni yasya saḥ purukṣuḥ*); in the Chāndasa loss of the dh of kṣudh; in the vocative, when su follows, guṇa by संबुद्धौ च (*saṃbuddhau ca*); loss of su by एज्‌ह्रस्वात् संबुद्धेः (*ejhrasvāt saṃbuddheḥ*); by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the nighāta accent comes.)*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमूरोऽमूढः सर्वज्ञः क्षयन् ईशानः सर्वस्य जगतः अत एव पुरुश्चंद्रः
> पुरुचंद्रो बहुहिरण्योपेतः । यद्वा । बहुदीप्ति स्वरूपः । वाजैर्बलैनमोभि-

> चेत्युभयोः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । विश्वजन्ने । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्व-
> पदांतोदात्तः । तत्पुरुषे तु स्वरश्चिंतनीयः । आ भाति । भा दीप्तौ । अंतर्भा-
> वितण्यर्थः । क्षयन् । क्षि ऐश्वर्ये । शतुर्लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ।
> पुरुश्चंद्रः । ह्रस्वाच्चंद्रोत्तरपदे मंत्र इति सुडागमः । श्चुत्वेन शकारः । उत्तर-
> पदांतोदात्तप्रकरणे त्रिचक्रादीनां छंदस्युपसंख्यानमित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं।
> यद्वा समासस्येत्यंतोदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, all-knowing, lord of the world, with gold or brilliance, strength and food, makes heaven and earth, the immortal makers of the world, shine.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अमूरः (*amūraḥ*)—one without erroneous knowledge (one possessed of exact knowledge), and क्षयन् (*kṣayan*)—lord of the whole world, and पुरुश्चंद्रः (*puruścaṃdraḥ*)—of manifold splendour, and वाजैः (*vājaiḥ*)—with powers, नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with foods, associated; being such, अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni, विश्वजन्ये (*viśvajanye*) (so printed जनसियरू (*janasiyarū*), where the Bhāvārtha has जननी जनकरू (*jananī janakarū*); as supplied)—the parents of the whole world, देवी (*devī*)—of divine nature, अमृते (*amṛte*)—free from the nature of death, द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth, आ भाति (*ā bhāti*)—he makes shine all around.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is without erroneous knowledge and has exact understanding, the lord of the whole world, of manifold splendour, and endowed with powers and with foods, makes shine all around heaven and earth, the parents of the whole world, free from the nature of death and of divine nature.

*[In the Bhāvārtha the word for "with foods" is printed अन्नगळिंदलद (*annagaḷiṃdalada*); as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the unbewildered, the ruler (of the world), the radiant, associated with vigour and food, illumines the divine immortal parents of all things, heaven and earth.

*[The word "associated" is broken across two lines in the print ("associ-" and "ated"); joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अमूरः क्षयन् पुरुश्चंद्रः (*amūraḥ kṣayan puruścaṃdraḥ*)—Agni is described by these words. The word अमूर (*amūra*) has been explained by Yāska—

### Printed p. 487

in the Ṛk मूरा अमूर न वयं चिकित्वो महित्वमग्ने त्वमंग वित्से । (*mūrā amūra na vayaṃ cikitvo mahitvamagne tvamaṃga vitse |*) (म. सं (*ma. saṃ*) 10-4-4) thus: मूढा वयं स्मो अमूढस्त्वमसि न वयं विद्यो महत्त्वमग्ने त्वं तु वेत्थ (*mūḍhā vayaṃ smo amūḍhastvamasi na vayaṃ vidyo mahattvamagne tvaṃ tu vettha*)—"We who are bewildered cannot know the great glory of Agni; since Agni is all-knowing, he knows it." This is explained. Sāyaṇa explains the word अमूर शब्दक्कॆ (*amūra śabdakkè*) as अमूढः सर्वज्ञः (*amūḍhaḥ sarvajñaḥ*) and describes Agni as knowing everything, as being all-knowing.

क्षयन्—ईशानः सर्वस्य जगतः (*kṣayan—īśānaḥ sarvasya jagataḥ*)—Yāska, in the Ṛk प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नामार्यः शंसामि वयुनानि विद्वान् । तं त्वा गृणामि तवसमतव्यान् क्षयंतमस्य रजसः पराके ॥ (*pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa nāmāryaḥ śaṃsāmi vayunāni vidvān | taṃ tvā gṛṇāmi tavasamatavyān kṣayaṃtamasya rajasaḥ parāke ‖*) (म. सं (*ma. saṃ*) 7-100-5), has described the word क्षयंतं (*kṣayaṃtaṃ*) in this Ṛk as used in the sense of dwelling. Sāyaṇa has said that Agni is the lord of the whole world; the word printed अथर्ववन्नु (*atharvavannu*) is left untranslated here [the sense of this word is not clear in the supplied text].

पुरुश्चंद्रः—बहुहिरण्योपेतः । यद्वा बहुदीप्ति स्वरूपः (*puruścaṃdraḥ—bahuhiraṇyopetaḥ | yadvā bahudīpti svarūpaḥ*)—the word चंद्रशब्दवु (*caṃdraśabdavu*) is stated among the names of gold, हिरण्य (*hiraṇya*) (सि (*si*) 2-10). Two meanings are explained: Agni is one who has abundant gold, or one whose form is of exceeding splendour.

वाजैः नमोभिः—बलैः अन्नैश्च सहितः (*vājaiḥ namobhiḥ—balaiḥ annaiśca sahitaḥ*)—Yāska has explained that the word वाजशब्दवु (*vājaśabdavu*) is used in the senses of strength, food and water. The word नमश्यब्दवु (*namaśyabdavu*) is stated among the names of food (नि (*ni*) 3-9). The meaning is given that Agni is possessed of strength and of food.

विश्वजन्ये—विश्वस्य जनयित्र्यौ यद्वा विश्वं जन्यं उत्पाद्यं याभ्यां ते (*viśvajanye—viśvasya janayitryau yadvā viśvaṃ janyaṃ utpādyaṃ yābhyāṃ te*)—Durgācārya has described for the word विश्वजन्यशब्दक्कॆ (*viśvajanyaśabdakkè*) the meaning "beneficial to all the world". The meaning is given that heaven and earth are the makers of the world, or the cause of the world that comes to be; and saying so, he describes them as द्योतमाने मरणधर्मरहिते (*dyotamāne maraṇadharmarahite*), that is, possessed of radiance and free from death, and says that Agni आभाति आसमंतात् प्रकाशयति (*ābhāti āsamaṃtāt prakāśayati*), makes these heaven and earth shine.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed pages 487 and 488, noted not translated. द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*): दौश्च पृथिवी च द्यावापृथिव्यौ (*dauśca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivyau*); by दिवोद्यावा (*divodyāvā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-29) the substitute dyāvā for div, which takes the ādyudātta accent; the word पृथिवीशब्दवु (*pṛthivīśabdavu*) ends in the affix जीष् (*jīṣ*) and is antodātta; by देवताद्वंद्वेच (*devatādvaṃdveca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-141) both members keep their own accent in the compound; by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) the case ending is lengthened, पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घ (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*). विश्वजन्ये (*viśvajanye*): विश्वं जन्यं याभ्यां ते (*viśvaṃ janyaṃ yābhyāṃ te*); by बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञा-याम् (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñā-yām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-106) the accent is on the last of the first member; if the compound is taken as a tatpuruṣa, the Chāndasa character of the accent must be accepted.)*

### Printed p. 488

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, continued. आभाति (*ābhāti*): भा दीप्तौ (*bhā dīptau*), a root with the sense of the causative included; laṭ, third person singular; the tiṅanta nighāta accent comes. क्षयन् (*kṣayan*): क्षि ऐश्वर्ये (*kṣi aiśvarye*); the substitute śatṛ for laṭ; guṇa of the i of the root and the substitute ay; by त्यास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tyāsyanudāttet*) the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, so the accent of the root remains; in the nominative singular, because it is ugit, सुमागम (*sumāgama*) (as printed). पुरुश्चंद्रः (*puruścaṃdraḥ*): by ह्रस्वाच्चंद्रोत्तरपदे मंत्रे (*hrasvāccaṃdrottarapade maṃtre*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-151) the augment सुटागम (*suṭāgama*) after a short vowel when चंद्ररूप (*caṃdrarūpa*) is the latter member; by स्तोःश्चुना श्चुः (*stoḥścunā ścuḥ*) the substitute ś; by त्रिचक्रा-दीनां छंदस्युपसंख्यानम् (*tricakrā-dīnāṃ chaṃdasyupasaṃkhyānam*) the accent of the last of the latter member, since the word is read in the त्रिचक्रादिगणदल्लि (*tricakrādigaṇadalli*); or, by समासस्य (*samāsasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223), the antodātta accent.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni and Indra, not harming the rite, are asked to come to the sacrificer's house, where soma is pressed and oblations offered, to drink soma.

### Printed p. 489

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. देवा (*devā*)—of divine nature. (त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you; the Kannada word is printed सीनू (*sīnū*) [so printed, where the Bhāvārtha has नीनू (*nīnū*); as supplied].) इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*)—and Indra also. अमर्धंता (*amardhaṃtā*)—(in regard to the performer of the sacrifice) not harming. सुतवतः (*sutavataḥ*)—who presses the Soma juice, दाशुषः (*dāśuṣaḥ*)—who offers the oblation, of the sacrificer. इह दुरोणे (*iha duroṇe*)—in this sacrificial house. यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—with reference to the sacrifice (that is being performed). सोमहेयाय (*somaheyāya*) [so printed, where the Pada has सोमपेयाय (*somapeyāya*); as supplied]—for the drinking of the Soma juice. उप यातं (*upa yātaṃ*)—come.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you of divine nature and Indra also, not harming the performer of the sacrifice, come, with reference to the sacrifice being performed in this sacrificial house of the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice and offers the oblation, for the drinking of the Soma juice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, you and Indra, gods disdaining not (our rite), come to the sacrifice in thc [sic] dwelling of the offerer of the libation to drink the Soma juice.

*[The word "the" is printed "thc" in the print; kept and marked [sic].]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अमर्धंता—अनागमसेन यज्ञहिंसामकुर्वंतौ (*amardhaṃtā—anāgamasena yajñahiṃsāmakurvaṃtau*)—Let Indra and Agni, making the sacrifice be accomplished by their coming, come for the drinking of the Soma to the sacrifice performed in the house of the sacrificer who has prepared the Soma juice and offered the oblation (सुतवतः दाशुषः (*sutavataḥ dāśuṣaḥ*)); this wish (आशंसनॆयु (*āśaṃsanèyu*)) of the sacrificer is described here.

*[The Kannada word after अमर्धंता (*amardhaṃtā*) is printed अनागमसेन (*anāgamasena*), where the bhāṣya has अनागमनेन (*anāgamanena*); as supplied.]*

दाशुषः—हविर्दत्तवतः यजमानस्य (*dāśuṣaḥ—havirdattavataḥ yajamānasya*)—the authors of the Nirukta, in ओमासश्चर्यणीधृतः (*omāsaścaryaṇīdhṛtaḥ*) (ऋ. सं (*ṛ. saṃ*) 1-2-3), have described for the word दाशुषः (*dāśuṣaḥ*) the meaning दत्तवंतः (*dattavaṃtaḥ*). Here Sāyaṇa explains that the word is used in the sense of the sacrificer who has offered the oblation.

दुरोणे—गृहे (*duroṇe—gṛhe*)—the word दुरोणशब्दवु (*duroṇaśabdavu*) is stated among the names of house (नि (*ni*) 3-13). It is explained by Yāska: दुरोण इति गृहनाम पुरवा भवंति दुस्तर्पाः (*duroṇa iti gṛhanāma puravā bhavaṃti dustarpāḥ*) (नि (*ni*) 4-4). Here it is used in the sense of the sacrificial hall in which the sacrificers perform the sacrifice. The meaning of the word यज्ञ शब्दार्थवु (*yajña śabdārthavu*) is explained along with a statement of other views.

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, begun on printed page 489; the page ends within it, and the rest follows on the next page. सुतवतः (*sutavataḥ*): सुञ् अभिषवे (*suñ abhiṣave*), a root; the affix क्त (*kta*) in the passive; by the accent of the affix it is antodātta; when मतुप् (*matup*) is added after it, वॆत्व (*vètva*) for the m, since it follows the ā-sound; this, because it is पित्ताडुदरिंद (*pittāḍudariṃda*) (as printed), becomes anudātta.)*

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ अ॒पां समि॑ध्यसे दुरो॒णे नित्यः॑ सूनो सहसो जातवेदः ।  
> स॒धस्था॑नि म॒हय॑मान ऊ॒ती ॥ ५ ॥

> *agne apāṃ samidhyase duroṇe nityaḥ sūno sahaso jātavedaḥ |*  
> *sadhasthāni mahayamāna ūtī ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । अपां । सं । इध्यसे । दुरोणे । नित्यः । सूनो इति । सहसः । जातवेदः ।  
> सधस्थानि । महयमानः । ऊती ॥ ५ ॥

> *agne | apāṃ | saṃ | idhyase | duroṇe | nityaḥ | sūno iti | sahasaḥ | jātavedaḥ |*  
> *sadhasthāni | mahayamānaḥ | ūtī ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहसः सूनो बलस्य पुत्र जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञ हे अग्ने नित्योऽविनाशी
> ऊती ऊत्या रक्षणेन सधस्थानि प्राणिनां निवासभूतांलोकान्महयमानः परिचरं-
> स्त्वमपां दुरोणेःपां स्थाने०तरिक्षे समिध्यसे । सम्यगीप्यसे ॥ दुरोणे ।
> अव रक्षण इत्यस्मादौणादिको नक्षृत्ययः । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना ऊट् । गुणः , मरोण
> इति गृहनाम । दुरवा भवंति । नि. ४-५ । इति यास्कः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । महयमानः '
> मह पूजायां । व्यत्ययेन शानच् । शानचो लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणानुदात्तत्वे
> णिच्‌स्वरः । ऊती । अव रक्षणादिषु । ऊतियूतिजूतीत्यादिना निपातनादंतो-
> दात्तः । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः सवर्णदीर्घः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, son of strength, of born wisdom, imperishable, kindled with his protection in the atmosphere, the place of the waters, moving among the worlds where beings dwell.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength. जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—of born wisdom. अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni. नित्यः (*nityaḥ*)—you who are eternal. उती (*utī*) [so printed, where the Saṃhitā has ऊती; as supplied]—with (your) protection. सधस्थानि (*sadhasthāni*)—the dwelling places of the beings,

### Printed p. 491

*(Pratipadārtha continued from the previous page.)* all the worlds. महयमानः (*mahayamānaḥ*)—moving about. अपां दुरोणे (*apāṃ duroṇe*)—in the atmosphere, the place of origin of the waters. समिध्यसे (*samidhyase*)—you blaze fully.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength and of born wisdom, you, free from decay and of eternal state, moving with your protection among all the worlds that are the dwelling places of beings, blaze fully in the atmosphere, the place of origin of the waters.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, son of strength, Jatavedas, the eternal, traversing the inhabited regions with your protection, you are kindled in the dwelling of the waters.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सहसः सूनो, जातवेदः (*sahasaḥ sūno, jātavedaḥ*)—for these words the meaning is explained thus: because Agni is produced by force, by churning in the fire-sticks, he is the son of force; because he is possessed of wisdom he is of born wisdom; with these words Agni is addressed.

नित्यः (*nityaḥ*)—this Agni, who does not go to destruction, protecting all by his protection, सधस्थानि (*sadhasthāni*)—moving in the worlds in which beings dwell, shines in the atmosphere, the dwelling place of the waters: so the meaning is explained. The word सधस्थशब्दवु (*sadhasthaśabdavu*) (is explained) by Yāska:—

कुह स्विद्योषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः । को नां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥ (*kuha svidyoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karataḥ kuhoṣatuḥ | ko nāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ maryaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā ‖*)

(ऋ. सं (*ṛ. saṃ*) 10-40-2). In this passage the word सभस्थ शब्दवु (*sabhastha śabdavu*) is used in the sense of "place together". The word ऊति शब्दवु (*ūti śabdavu*) is explained as ऊतिरवनात् (*ūtiravanāt*) (सि (*si*) 5-3) . Here it is used in the sense of protection. अपां समिध्यसे-अपां स्थाने अंतरिक्षे समिध्यसे (*apāṃ samidhyase-apāṃ sthāne aṃtarikṣe samidhyase*): because the meaning is explained thus, it is indicated that here the lightning-fire (वैद्युताग्नियु (*vaidyutāgniyu*)) is described. Having shown the difference among the fires as पार्थिवाग्नि (*pārthivāgni*), जातवेदाग्नि (*jātavedāgni*) and वैद्यताग्नि (*vaidyatāgni*) [so printed, where the lightning-fire was written differently a little before; as supplied], he also indicates here their identity [the sentence ends with a verb form without its final letter, as supplied].

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, begun on printed page 491. अपां (*apāṃ*): genitive plural; by ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the case ending takes the udātta accent. इध्यसे (*idhyase*): the root इइइंधी दीप्तौ (*iiiṃdhī dīptau*) [so printed, with the letter doubled; as supplied]; laṭ in the passive, second person singular; the tiṅanta nighāta accent comes. दुरोणे (*duroṇe*): the root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*); to it the Auṇādika affix नक् (*nak*) [the word before the affix is printed औणाविक (*auṇāvika*); as supplied]; by ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यवि (*jvaratvarasrivyavi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-20) ūṭ for the penultimate and the va, because of the affix, and guṇa for it. The page ends here, with the word दुरोण (*duroṇa*), and the sentence goes on on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 492

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, continued, printed page 492. दुरोण (*duroṇa*) इति गृहनाम दुरवा भवंति (*iti gṛhanāma duravā bhavaṃti*) (निरु (*niru*) 4-5): so Yāska has said. By the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta. नित्यः (*nityaḥ*): by the statement त्येज्नेध्रुव इति वक्तव्यम् (*tyejnedhruva iti vaktavyam*) the affix tyap after ni; because it is पित्तादुद (*pittāduda*) (the word is broken at the end of the line and goes on with रिंद (*riṃda*)) it becomes anudātta. सूनो सहसः (*sūno sahasaḥ*): by सुबामंत्रिते परांगवत्‌स्वरे (*subāmaṃtrite parāṃgavatsvare*), since in some places the pūrvāṅgavadbhāva is also stated, the āmantrita nighāta accent comes to the whole. सधस्थानि (*sadhasthāni*): by सधमादस्थयोश्चंदसि (*sadhamādasthayoścaṃdasi*) (Pā. When the instrumental singular follows, by सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) pūrvasavarṇadīrgha comes.)*

## Sūkta 26 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-sixth sūkta** (इप्पत्तारनॆय सूक्तवु (*ippattāranèya sūktavu*))

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वैश्वानरं मनसेति नवर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं । तत्रानुक्रमणिका वैश्वानरं
> नव तृच् वैश्वानरीयमारुत् जागत् दृच आत्मस्तुतिर्वा पूर्वात्मगीतांत्यो-
> पाध्यायस्तुतिरिति । वैश्वानरं मनसेत्याद्यौ तृच् जागतौ प्रथमस्य वैश्वानरोग्नि
> र्देवता द्वितीयस्य मरुतः । सप्तम्याध्यास्ति स्रस्त्रिष्टुभः । अग्निरस्मीति द्वृपस्याग्निः परं
> ब्रह्म वा देवता । नवम्यास्तु विश्वामित्रोपाध्यायस्य स्तुत्यत्वात्स एव देवता । सप्त-
> मावर्जितस्य सूक्तस्य विश्वामित्र ऋषिः । सप्तम्या ब्रह्मवाक्यद्वाद्यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिरिति
> न्यायेन ब्रह्म ऋषिः ॥ वैश्वानरं मनसेत्याद्यस्तृच अभिप्लविके चतुर्थेऽहनि अग्नि-
> मारुते वैश्वानरीयनिविद्वाने विनियुक्तः । तृतीयस्येति खंडे सूत्रितं । वैश्वानरं
> मनसेति तिस्सः । आ. ७-७ । इति ॥ अयमेव तृचो बृहस्पतिसवेऽप्याग्नि मारुते वैश्वा-
> नरीयनिविद्वानीयः । प्र यंतु वाजा इति द्वितीयतृचो बृहस्पतिसवे मारुतनिवि-

*[The Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya introduction of Sūkta 26 is cut off at the end of printed page 492, in the middle of a word, with a line-end hyphen; it goes on on the next page.]*

### Printed p. 493

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वानीयः । उभयमप्पुशनसः स्तोमेनेति खंडे सूत्रितं । वैश्वानरं मनसाग्निं
> निचाय्य प्रयंतु वाजास्तविषीभिरग्नयः । आ. ९-५ । इति ॥ अग्निचयने संचिताग्न्य-
> नुशंसनेऽग्निरस्मीत्येषा । अथाग्निं संचितमनुगीतमनुशंसेदित्युपक्रम्य सूत्रितं ।
> अग्निरस्मि जन्मना जातवेदा इति त्रिर्मध्यमया वाचा । आ. ४-८ । इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta beginning with वैश्वानरं मनसा (*vaiśvānaraṃ manasā*) is the fourteenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are nine Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said वैश्वानरं नव तृचौ वैश्वानरीयमारुतौ जागत् दृच आत्मस्तुतिर्वा पूर्वात्मगीतांत्योपाध्यायस्तुतिः (*vaiśvānaraṃ nava tṛcau vaiśvānarīyamārutau jāgat dṛca ātmastutirvā pūrvātmagītāṃtyopādhyāyastutiḥ*). The first two tṛcas of this sūkta (a tṛca means three Ṛks) are in the Jagatī metre. For the first tṛca (Ṛks 1 to 3) the deity is the fire Vaiśvānara; for the second tṛca (Ṛks 4 to 6) the Maruts are the deity. The three Ṛks from the seventh to the ninth are in the Triṣṭubh metre. For the two Ṛks beginning अग्निरस्मि (*agnirasmi*) (Ṛks 7 and 8) Agni or the Supreme Brahman is the deity. Because in the ninth Ṛk the seer Viśvāmitra has praised his own teacher (guru), the teacher himself is the deity of this Ṛk. Viśvāmitra is the seer of all the Ṛks of this sūkta except the seventh. Because the seventh Ṛk is a statement spoken by Brahman [the word is printed ಬಹ್ಮನು, as supplied], by the maxim यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषिः (*yasya vākyaṃ sa ṛṣiḥ*)—"he whose statement is in the Ṛk is the seer of that Ṛk"—Brahman himself is the seer of this seventh Ṛk.

The first tṛca of this sūkta (Ṛks 1 to 3) is applied, at the recitation of the Agnimāruta-śastra mantras on the fourth day of the sacrifice called Abhiplava, for the nivid mantras addressed to Vaiśvānara; this is explained in the section तृतीयस्य (*tṛtīyasya*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra वैश्वानरं मनसेति शिस्त्रः (*vaiśvānaraṃ manaseti śistraḥ*) (Ā. 7-7) [so printed, with a different last word from the form in the bhāṣya block; as supplied]. And these three Ṛks are applied also in the sacrifice called Bṛhaspatisava, at the recitation of the Agnimāruta-śastra, for the nivid mantras addressed to Vaiśvānara. The second tṛca, beginning प्र यंतु वाजाः (*pra yaṃtu vājāḥ*) (Ṛks 4 to 6), is applied in the Bṛhaspatisava for the nivid mantras addressed to the Maruts. Both these applications are indicated in the section उशनसस्तोमेन (*uśanasastomena*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra वैश्वानरं मनसाग्निं निचाय्कॆ प्र यंतु वाजास्तविषीभिरग्नियः (*vaiśvānaraṃ manasāgniṃ nicāykè pra yaṃtu vājāstaviṣībhiragniyaḥ*) (Ā. 9-5) [the Sanskrit introduction at the head of this page names this section with a differently spelled first word; as supplied].

That the Ṛk अग्निरस्मि (*agnirasmi*) (the seventh Ṛk) is applied when the sañcita fire is recited over in the agnicayana is indicated in the sentences of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra beginning संचितमनुगीतमनुशंसेत् (*saṃcitamanugītamanuśaṃset*) by the sūtra अग्निरस्मि जन्मना जातवेदा इति त्रिर्मध्यमया वाचा (*agnirasmi janmanā jātavedā iti trirmadhyamayā vācā*) (4-8).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वै॒श्वा॒न॒रं मन॑सा॒ग्निं नि॒चाय्या॑ ह॒विष्मं॑तो अनुष॒त्यं स्व॒र्विदं॑ ।  
> सु॒दानुं॑ दे॒वं र॑थि॒रं व॑सू॒यवो॑ गी॒र्भी र॒ण्वं कु॑ति॒कासो॑ हवामहे ॥ १ ॥

*[The label of the next section is printed garbled, "ಪವಪಾಠಿ", in the supplied text; kept here, and the standard label of the Pada-pāṭha is used.]*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वैश्वानरं । मनसा । अग्निं । निचाय्य । हविष्मंतः । अनुसत्यं । स्वःविदं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises. We of the Kuśika lineage, holding oblations and desiring wealth, invoke with praises Agni Vaiśvānara, true to his word, knower of heaven, giver, charioteer, shining.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*)—(for the sacrifice) possessing oblations. वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*)—desiring wealth. कुशिकासः (*kuśikāsaḥ*)—we who are born in the lineage of the sage Kuśika [the Kannada word is printed ಹುಟ್ಟದವರೂ, as supplied]. वैश्वानरं (*vaiśvānaraṃ*)—the leader of the whole world. अनुषत्यं (*anuṣatyaṃ*)—the protector of truth. स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*)—the knower of the fruits in the form of heaven and the rest. सुदानुं (*sudānuṃ*)—the excellent giver. रथिरं (*rathiraṃ*)—the swift-moving (or the possessor of a chariot). रण्वं (*raṇvaṃ*)—who goes towards the sacrifice. देवं (*devaṃ*)—and resplendent. अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni. मनसा निचाय्य (*manasā nicāyya*)—having known in the mind by meditative knowledge. गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—by words in the form of praise. हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray and call.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We who possess oblations for the sacrifice, who desire wealth and who are born in the lineage of the sage Kuśika, having known in the mind by meditative knowledge Agni—the leader of the whole world, the protector of truth, the knower of the fruits in the form of heaven and the rest, the excellent giver, the possessor of a swift chariot, who goes towards the sacrifice and is resplendent—pray and call him with words in the form of praise [the Kannada has ಅಗ್ನಿಯದ್ದು here, as supplied].

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We of the race of Kushika offering oblations, desirous of wealth, having contemplated him in our minds, invoke with praises the devine [sic] Vaishwanara, the observer of truth, the cognizant of heaven, the bountiful, the.charioteer [sic], the frequenter (of sacrifices).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वसूयवः—धनमात्मन इच्छंतः (*vasūyavaḥ—dhanamātmana icchaṃtaḥ*). Yāska—

कारुरहं ततो भिषगुपलप्रक्षिणी नना । (*kārurahaṃ tato bhiṣagupalaprakṣiṇī nanā |*)

### Printed p. 496

नानाधियो वसूयवोऽनु गा इव तस्थिमेंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*nānādhiyo vasūyavo 'nu gā iva tasthimeṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*)

In this Ṛk the word वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*) is given the meaning वसुकापूः (*vasukāpūḥ*) . Sāyaṇa has explained here that the word means those who desire wealth for themselves.

कुशिकासः— कुशिकगोत्रोत्पन्नाः (*kuśikāsaḥ— kuśikagotrotpannāḥ*) —Sāyaṇa has explained that this word is used in the sense "those born in the Kuśika lineage". The Nirukta authors—

उप प्रेत कुशिकाश्चेतयध्वमश्वं राये प्र मुंचता सुदासः ॥ (*upa preta kuśikāścetayadhvamaśvaṃ rāye pra muṃcatā sudāsaḥ ‖*)
राजा वृत्रं जंघनत्पागुदगथा यजाते वर आ पृथिव्याः ॥ (*rājā vṛtraṃ jaṃghanatpāgudagathā yajāte vara ā pṛthivyāḥ ‖*)

(पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) 3-53-11) [the abbreviation is printed so, as supplied]. Here, for the word "Kuśikas", the meaning स्तुतिक्रोष्टारः ऋत्विजः (*stutikroṣṭāraḥ ṛtvijaḥ*)—"the priests who recite praises" [the Kannada word for "recite" is printed ಪತಿಸುವ, as supplied]—has been stated.

वैश्वानरं (*vaiśvānaraṃ*)—विश्वे नरा अग्निप्रणयनादिक्रियाया नेतारो यस्येति विश्वासरो अग्निः । तस्य संबंधी वैश्वानरः । यद्वा विश्वासर एव वैश्वानरः (*viśve narā agnipraṇayanādikriyāyā netāro yasyeti viśvāsaro agniḥ | tasya saṃbaṃdhī vaiśvānaraḥ | yadvā viśvāsara eva vaiśvānaraḥ*). Because all who perform sacrifices perform the rite called agnipraṇayana, Agni, being connected with the word विश्वासरशब्द (*viśvāsaraśabda*), is denoted by the word वैश्वानरशब्द (*vaiśvānaraśabda*); or it is described that विश्वासर (*viśvāsara*) himself is spoken of as वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*). The Nirukta authors explain the sense of this word Vaiśvānara at length [the Kannada word is printed ವಿರತವಾಗಿ, as supplied].

अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च विवर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः । (*ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vivartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ |*)
वैश्वानरो जायमानो न राजावातिरज्जोतिषाग्निस्तमांसि ॥ (*vaiśvānaro jāyamāno na rājāvātirajjotiṣāgnistamāṃsi ‖*)
वैश्वानरो जायमानो न राजावातिरज्योतिषाग्निस्तमांसि ॥ (*vaiśvānaro jāyamāno na rājāvātirajyotiṣāgnistamāṃsi ‖*)

*[The second line of the quotation is printed twice in the supplied text, the second time with one letter different; both are kept as supplied.]*

Here: वैश्वानरो जायमान इव उद्यन्नादित्यः सर्वॆषां ज्योतिषां राजा वाहन्नग्निज्योतिषा तमांसि (*vaiśvānaro jāyamāna iva udyannādityaḥ sarvèṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ rājā vāhannagnijyotiṣā tamāṃsi*). Thus the fire Vaiśvānara is compared to the Āditya (the sun) [the Kannada has ಎಂತು here, as supplied]. Durgācārya has described it thus: यथा ह्यद्यन्नादित्यस्तमांसि अपहंति दिना एवमग्निरपि रात्रावपहंति (*yathā hyadyannādityastamāṃsi apahaṃti dinā evamagnirapi rātrāvapahaṃti*)—just as the sun that has risen destroys the darkness in the day, so Agni destroys the darkness at night.

And: विश्व एनं नरा नयंतीति वा, अपि वा विश्वानर एव स्यात् प्रत्यृतः सर्वाणि भूतानि तस्य वैश्वानरः (*viśva enaṃ narā nayaṃtīti vā, api vā viśvānara eva syāt pratyṛtaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tasya vaiśvānaraḥ*).

Explaining the sense of the word Vaiśvānara as interpreted by Yāska [the Kannada word is broken across two lines and printed ವೈಶ್ ನರಪದದ, as supplied], Durgācārya [the words ಅರ್ಥ ನನ್ನದುರ್ಗಾಚಾರ್ಯರು stand so in the supplied text; as supplied] gives two explanations: विश्वान् सर्रा इतो लोकात् अमुं लोकं सर्वासु प्रवृत्तिषु नयति (*viśvān sarrā ito lokāt amuṃ lokaṃ sarvāsu pravṛttiṣu nayati*)—he who impels all people in this world to practise their respective activities; or गति तस्मिन् सर्वाः प्रवृत्तयः फलवत्यो नराणां भवंतीति सर्वासु प्रवृत्तिषु अयॆमेव नर्रा प्रवर्तयति (*gati tasmin sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ phalavatyo narāṇāṃ bhavaṃtīti sarvāsu pravṛttiṣu ayèmeva narrā pravartayati*)—he who, making all kinds of activities of people fruitful, causes everyone to engage in his respective duties, and is therefore the impeller of people's activity, is Vaiśvānara. Further: विश्वे नरा एनं नयंति स नीयमानः तासु तासु क्रियासु अंगभावं नरैः (*viśve narā enaṃ nayaṃti sa nīyamānaḥ tāsu tāsu kriyāsu aṃgabhāvaṃ naraiḥ*)

### Printed p. 497

कर्म संपद्यते (*karma saṃpadyate*). In the respective sacrificial rites Agni, carried by the respective sacrificers and making the respective rites his own parts, is called Vaiśvānara; or: विश्वानि ह्यसौ भूतानि प्रतियुतः प्रविष्टः विश्वासरः तस्य अपत्यं वैश्वानरः (*viśvāni hyasau bhūtāni pratiyutaḥ praviṣṭaḥ viśvāsaraḥ tasya apatyaṃ vaiśvānaraḥ*)—he who is known as विश्वासर (*viśvāsara*), having entered into all beings in the form of the digestive fire जारराग्नि (*jārarāgni*) , the son of that विश्वासर (*viśvāsara*) is वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*): thus another kind of meaning is described.

वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम राजा हि कं भुवनानामधिश्रीः । (*vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma rājā hi kaṃ bhuvanānāmadhiśrīḥ |*)
इतो जातो विश्वमिदं वि चष्टे वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण ॥ (*ito jāto viśvamidaṃ vi caṣṭe vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa ‖*)

The words "citing this reasoning, Yāska—" follow in the supplied text, and then the reference (मि. सं. (*mi. saṃ.*) 1-98-1) , which belongs to the Ṛk quoted just before. Yāska:

इतो जातः सर्वमिदमभिविपश्यति वैश्वानरः संयतते सूर्येण राजा यः सर्वेषां भूतानामभिश्रयणीयः तस्य वयं वैश्वानरस्य कल्याण्यां मतौ स्याम ॥ (*ito jātaḥ sarvamidamabhivipaśyati vaiśvānaraḥ saṃyatate sūryeṇa rājā yaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmabhiśrayaṇīyaḥ tasya vayaṃ vaiśvānarasya kalyāṇyāṃ matau syāma ‖*) (नि. (*ni.*) 7-23)

This Agni, born on earth from herbs and trees, being the illuminator of all and the benefactor of all, regards by his splendour the sun as equal to himself [two Kannada words are run together in the print, ಸೂರ್ಯನನ್ನೂತನಗೆ, as supplied]. Therefore this Agni called Vaiśvānara is to be resorted to by all beings. The expression of the wish that we may be within the scope of the auspicious activity of this Vaiśvānara Agni, who does good to all, is described: thus the meaning is explained. In the Vaiśvānara-vidyā the Ātman himself is Vaiśvānara; and Indra, Āditya, Vāyu, Ākāśa, Udaka and Pṛthivī are each designated by the word Vaiśvānara, as is said in the śāstras. Therefore, quoting the question तत्को वैश्वानरः (*tatko vaiśvānaraḥ*), and मध्यम इत्याचार्याः (*madhyama ityācāryāḥ*), it is stated that the Vaiśvānara Agni designated in sacrifices and the like stands in the middle region: so the Nairukta view and the concurrence of the other ācāryas are stated.

प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचंते । वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वा अधूनोत्काष्ठा अव शंबरं भेत् ॥ (*pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacaṃte | vaiśvānaro dasyumagnirjaghanvā adhūnotkāṣṭhā ava śaṃbaraṃ bhet ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 1-59-6). In this Ṛk this Vaiśvānara Agni is praised with the word वर्षक्रियाकारित्वेन (*varṣakriyākāritvena*), as the doer of the activity of rain. From this, the opinion of some ācāryas who hold that this Vaiśvānara Agni is a deity of the middle region is stated.

The ancient sacrificers: अथासावादित्य इति पूर्वे याज्ञिकाः (*athāsāvāditya iti pūrve yājñikāḥ*). At the respective savanas, in accordance with the maxim रोहात् प्रत्यवरोहश्तिकीर्षितः (*rohāt pratyavarohaśtikīrṣitaḥ*) , because the śastra mantra is recited with the Vaiśvānarīya sūkta, they say that the Āditya also is Vaiśvānara: thus another opinion is indicated. Those who say that the Āditya himself is Vaiśvānara—
