अथापि वैश्वानरीयो द्वादशकपालो भवत्येतस्य हि द्वादशविधं कर्म । (*athāpi vaiśvānarīyo dvādaśakapālo bhavatyetasya hi dvādaśavidhaṃ karma |*)
अधापि ब्राह्मणं भवत्यसौ ना आदित्योऽग्निः वैश्वानर इति ॥ (*adhāpi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavatyasau nā ādityo 'gniḥ vaiśvānara iti ‖*)

[Gist: "Further, the Vaiśvānarīya offering is on twelve potsherds, for his action is twelvefold. Further there is a Brāhmaṇa: that Āditya is Agni Vaiśvānara." The word before "Āditya" is printed ನಾ where the next passage has ವಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯೋ; as supplied.]

देवतागुणसामान्येन अधियज्ञेषु गुणविधयः कल्प्यंते वैश्वानरीयश्च सर्वत्र द्वादशमासप्रविभागलक्षणं कर्म । देवतागुणकपालविध्यनुकरणात् पश्याम आदित्यो वैश्वानर इति । (*devatāguṇasāmānyena adhiyajñeṣu guṇavidhayaḥ kalpyaṃte vaiśvānarīyaśca sarvatra dvādaśamāsapravibhāgalakṣaṇaṃ karma | devatāguṇakapālavidhyanukaraṇāt paśyāma ādityo vaiśvānara iti |*)

[Gist: by the common quality of the deity, injunctions of qualities are imagined in the sacrificial contexts; the Vaiśvānarīya everywhere is a rite characterised by the division into twelve months; because the injunction of the potsherds follows the quality of the deity, "we see that Āditya is Vaiśvānara".]

The Kannada explains: because injunctions of qualities conformable to the nature of the qualities of the deity are imagined, and because the Vaiśvānarīya potsherd-offering is twelvefold, in accordance with the twelve months, they set forth the reasoning that there is also the Brāhmaṇa sentence भवत्यसौ वा आदित्योऽग्निर्वैश्वानरः (*bhavatyasau vā ādityo 'gnirvaiśvānaraḥ*) in support of this injunction of the potsherds according to the quality of the deity. And, quoting अधापि छांदोमिकंसूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवति (*adhāpi chāṃdomikaṃsūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavati*) and saying that the Chāndomika hymn has Sūrya and Vaiśvānara as its deities, [the author] quotes:

दिवि पृष्टो अरोचताग्निर्वैश्वानरो बृहन् । (*divi pṛṣṭo arocatāgnirvaiśvānaro bṛhan |*)
क्षया वृधान ओजसा चनोहितो ज्योतिषा बाधते तमः ॥ (*kṣayā vṛdhāna ojasā canohito jyotiṣā bādhate tamaḥ ‖*)

(वा. सं. (*vā. saṃ.*) 33-92)

*[Before this reference the supplied text has a stray line "(ವ", kept here as a note; the reference that follows begins with the abbreviation printed in the line below.]*

Citing this Ṛk, it is described that this Vaiśvānara Agni, stationed in the heavenly world, shines, and that he is filled with greatness by his own radiance. And further, अथापि हविष्कांतीयं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवति (*athāpi haviṣkāṃtīyaṃ sūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavati*)—

विश्वस्मा अग्निं भुवनाय देवा वैश्वानरं केतुमह्नामकृण्वन् ॥ (*viśvasmā agniṃ bhuvanāya devā vaiśvānaraṃ ketumahnāmakṛṇvan ‖*)

(ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 10-88-12)

Pointing out that the Havishkāntīya hymn too is Sūrya-Vaiśvānarīya, and quoting a Ṛk of it [the Kannada word is printed ಋತ್ಕನ್ನು, as supplied], [the author] states the conclusion: आदित्य एव ह्युदयास्तमयाभ्यामहानि करोति तेन वयमेतैर्हेतुभिः सूर्यो वैश्वानर इति पश्यामः (*āditya eva hyudayāstamayābhyāmahāni karoti tena vayametairhetubhiḥ sūryo vaiśvānara iti paśyāmaḥ*)—"the Āditya himself, by rising and setting, makes the days; for these reasons we see that Sūrya is Vaiśvānara". Saying that the Āditya divides the days and in accordance with them performs the risings and settings, they declare the conclusion that for these reasons the Āditya himself is Vaiśvānara.

अयमेवाग्निर्वैश्वानर इति शाकपूणिः । (*ayamevāgnirvaiśvānara iti śākapūṇiḥ |*)
विश्वानरावेते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी वैश्वानरोऽयं यत्ताभ्यां जायते ॥ (*viśvānarāvete uttare jyotiṣī vaiśvānaro 'yaṃ yattābhyāṃ jāyate ‖*)

[Gist: "This very Agni is Vaiśvānara," says Śākapūṇi; "these two higher lights are Viśvānara; this one is Vaiśvānara because he is born from the two."]

The ācārya named Śākapūṇi, expressing his view that this terrestrial fire (Pārthiva Agni) is Vaiśvānara, has described his conclusion with a demonstration of reasoning. He has stated the reasoning on the point that this terrestrial fire is neither the lightning fire (Vaidyuta Agni) of the middle region nor the Āditya.

कथं नृयमेताभ्यां जायत इति यत्र वैद्युतः शरणमभिहंति यावदनुपात्तो भवति मध्यमधर्म्मेव तावद्भवत्युदकेंधनः शरीरोपशमन उपादीयमान एवायं संपद्यत उदकोपशमनः शरीरदीप्तिः ॥ (*kathaṃ nṛyametābhyāṃ jāyata iti yatra vaidyutaḥ śaraṇamabhihaṃti yāvadanupātto bhavati madhyamadharmmeva tāvadbhavatyudakeṃdhanaḥ śarīropaśamana upādīyamāna evāyaṃ saṃpadyata udakopaśamanaḥ śarīradīptiḥ ‖*)

[Gist: the passage asks how he is born from these two, and answers in terms of the lightning fire, a middle nature, water as fuel, and the pacification and light of the body; the Kannada explanation follows on the next page. The first word after the question is printed ನೃಯಮೇತಾಭ್ಯಾಂ, as supplied.]

### Printed p. 499

The lightning fire reaches its own support, whether water or a tree. It is not taken up by men. It always grows only through water. By the form that is of liquid shape, or earth-related, at all times (the form) having a shape or another shape, it exists by the middle quality that finds repose in the support [so the sentence stands in the supplied text, with a parenthesis, as supplied]. Not having a nature that arises from place or species, and not being produced by any kind of cause, is being "middle". The lightning fire, being thus middle, is designated Viśvānara. The terrestrial fire connected with it, taken up by men, abandons its own quality, acquires a quality different from that of the middle lightning fire [the Kannada word is printed ಮಧ್ಯನುವಾದ, as supplied], and is endowed with the qualities of being overcome by water and of producing light in bodies. It is therefore explained that this terrestrial fire is called Vaiśvānara fire because it arises from Viśvānara (the middle lightning fire). The analysing phrase विश्वासरस्त्यं वैश्वानरः (*viśvāsarastyaṃ vaiśvānaraḥ*) is also shown.

Having supported by reasoning the difference between the lightning fire and the terrestrial fire, and having explained the origin of the terrestrial fire from the lightning fire, [the author] describes the origin of the terrestrial fire from the Āditya [the phrase "having explained the origin of the terrestrial fire from the Āditya" is printed twice in succession, as supplied]—

अथादित्यादुदीचिप्रथमसमावृत्त आदित्ये कंसं ना मणिं वा परिमृज्य प्रतिस्वरे यत्र शुष्कगोमयमसंस्पर्शयन् धारयति तत् प्रदीप्यते सोऽयमेव संपद्यते ॥ (*athādityādudīciprathamasamāvṛtta āditye kaṃsaṃ nā maṇiṃ vā parimṛjya pratisvare yatra śuṣkagomayamasaṃsparśayan dhārayati tat pradīpyate so 'yameva saṃpadyate ‖*)

(सि. (*si.*) 7-23)

[Gist: the passage speaks of the Āditya, a bowl or a gem, and dry cow-dung that is kindled; the Kannada explanation follows.]

When the Āditya is in the uttarāyaṇa, a sun-stone (sūryakānta) that comes into relation with the Āditya's rays produces fire (as fire arises in dried [the Kannada word is printed ವಣಗಿದ, as supplied] cow-dung); hence this fire, arising from the Āditya, is designated by the name "terrestrial fire", different from the Āditya. Thus it is described.

अथाप्याह—“ वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण ” इति । न चपुनरात्मनात्मा संयततेऽन्येनैवान्यः संयतत इत इममादधात्यमुतोऽमुष्य रश्मयः प्रादुर्भवंतीतोऽस्यार्चिषस्तयोर्भासोः संसंगं दृष्टैवमवक्ष्यत् ॥ (*athāpyāha—“ vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa ” iti | na capunarātmanātmā saṃyatate 'nyenaivānyaḥ saṃyatata ita imamādadhātyamuto 'muṣya raśmayaḥ prādurbhavaṃtīto 'syārciṣastayorbhāsoḥ saṃsaṃgaṃ dṛṣṭaivamavakṣyat ‖*)

[Gist: "Further he says: Vaiśvānara strives with Sūrya." The passage argues that one self does not strive with itself but one strives with another, and speaks of the rays and light of the two coming into contact; the Kannada explanation follows.]

"वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण (*vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa*)"—since the position of one ātman within another ātman is contradictory, the reasoning that the opinion of the ācāryas stated earlier is explained by the relation of the rays of the Āditya, that is, that a relation of the rays of the Āditya and of this terrestrial fire is spoken of, is refuted.

### Printed p. 500

अथ यान्येतान्यौत्तमिकानि सूक्तानि भागानि वा सावित्राणि वा सौर्याणि वा पौष्णानि वा वैष्णवानि वा वैश्वदेव्यानि वा तेषु वैश्वानरीयाः प्रवादा अभविष्यन्नादि त्यकर्मणा चैनमस्तोष्यन्नित्युदेषीत्यस्तमेषीति पिपिर्येषीति । (*atha yānyetānyauttamikāni sūktāni bhāgāni vā sāvitrāṇi vā sauryāṇi vā pauṣṇāni vā vaiṣṇavāni vā vaiśvadevyāni vā teṣu vaiśvānarīyāḥ pravādā abhaviṣyannādi tyakarmaṇā cainamastoṣyannityudeṣītyastameṣīti pipiryeṣīti |*)

[Gist: as for those hymns or portions of the highest class addressed to Savitṛ, Sūrya, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu or the Viśvedevas, the Vaiśvānarīya statements would have occurred in them, and one would have praised him with the action of the Āditya ("you rise", "you go to setting", "you fill").]

In the hymns on the subject of the highest deities, belonging to Savitṛ, Sūrya, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, the Viśvedevas and the like, Vaiśvānara Agni too is praised in the mantras in a subordinate manner (guṇabhāva). Just as the Āditya's quality, rising and setting, is mentioned in the mantras in the manner of primacy, so the reversals of rising and setting are not stated in the case of this Vaiśvānara Agni; for that reason the statement that this Vaiśvānara Agni is the Āditya is refuted.

आग्नेयेष्टेव हि सूक्तेषु वैश्वानरीयाः प्रवादा भवंति । (*āgneyeṣṭeva hi sūkteṣu vaiśvānarīyāḥ pravādā bhavaṃti |*)
अग्निकर्मणा चैनं स्तोतीति वहसीति पचसीति दहसीति ॥ (*agnikarmaṇā cainaṃ stotīti vahasīti pacasīti dahasīti ‖*)

[Gist: in hymns addressed to Agni the Vaiśvānarīya statements occur, and one praises him with Agni's action: "you carry", "you cook", "you burn".]

समानमेतदुदकमुच्चैत्यव चाहभिः । (*samānametadudakamuccaityava cāhabhiḥ |*)
भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्नंति दिवं जिन्नंत्यग्नयः ॥ (*bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinnaṃti divaṃ jinnaṃtyagnayaḥ ‖*)

(सि. (*si.*) 7-23)
(म. सं. (*ma. saṃ.*) 1-164-51)

[Gist: "This water is one and the same, going up and coming down with the days; the rain-clouds gladden the earth, the fires gladden the heaven." The verb is printed ಜಿನ್ನಂತಿ and ಜಿನ್ನಂತ್ಯಗ್ನಯಃ, and the second reference is printed with ಮ. ಸಂ., as supplied.]

In the hymns that concern Agni, the greatness of Vaiśvānara Agni is praised. Describing that the carrying of the oblation, cooking and burning are actions of Agni, stated in the manner of primacy with Vaiśvānara Agni himself as their subject, [the author] quotes:

एकमेवोदकं पर्यायेणोत्तरायणदक्षिणायनयोः जगद्यात्रासिद्धये तदुदेति चावृति च वर्षकर्मभावेन । आहुतयो ह्यग्नौ प्रक्षप्ताः तेन दग्धास्ताः स्वार्चिर्भिः कृत्योदकभावमापाद्य परमं सूक्ष्मं देवोपभोगयोग्यं द्यां प्रति वर्षभावेनोन्नीयंते तल्लोकनिवासिनां तृप्तये ततस्त इह वर्षं प्रकल्पयंति । (*ekamevodakaṃ paryāyeṇottarāyaṇadakṣiṇāyanayoḥ jagadyātrāsiddhaye tadudeti cāvṛti ca varṣakarmabhāvena | āhutayo hyagnau prakṣaptāḥ tena dagdhāstāḥ svārcirbhiḥ kṛtyodakabhāvamāpādya paramaṃ sūkṣmaṃ devopabhogayogyaṃ dyāṃ prati varṣabhāvenonnīyaṃte tallokanivāsināṃ tṛptaye tatasta iha varṣaṃ prakalpayaṃti |*)

and explains: water, for the protection of the world, attains upward and downward movement in the form of rain in the uttarāyaṇa and the dakṣiṇāyana; the oblations offered in Agni are burnt by Agni, attain through Agni's rays the state of water, and in an extremely subtle and unsurpassed form give satisfaction to the gods, thereby protecting the world of the gods, and through rain protecting creation. Describing thus, [the author] refutes the opinion of the ācāryas who said that the Āditya himself performs the action of rain, because the action of rain arises from Agni. Also quoting the Ṛk कृष्णं नियानां हरयः सुपर्णाः (*kṛṣṇaṃ niyānāṃ harayaḥ suparṇāḥ*) (ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 1-164-47) [the opening parenthesis of the reference is printed twice and not closed, as supplied], and the words यस्मिन्नग्निरादित्यो वर्षकर्मणा स्तूयते (*yasminnagnirādityo varṣakarmaṇā stūyate*), it is explained that Agni himself, in the form of the Āditya [the Kannada word is printed ಆದಿತ್ಯನರೂಪದಿಂದ, as supplied], is the giver of rain.

वैश्वानरीयो द्वादशकपालो भवतीत्यनिर्वचनं कपालानि भवंत्यस्ति हि सौर्य एक कपालः पंचकपालश्च । (*vaiśvānarīyo dvādaśakapālo bhavatītyanirvacanaṃ kapālāni bhavaṃtyasti hi saurya eka kapālaḥ paṃcakapālaśca |*)
बहुभक्तिवादीनि हि ब्राह्मणानि भवंति— (*bahubhaktivādīni hi brāhmaṇāni bhavaṃti—*)
पृथिवी वैश्वानरः, संवत्सरो वैश्वानरो ब्राह्मणो वैश्वानर इति ॥ (*pṛthivī vaiśvānaraḥ, saṃvatsaro vaiśvānaro brāhmaṇo vaiśvānara iti ‖*)

(सि. (*si.*) 7-5=)

[Gist: "'The Vaiśvānarīya has twelve potsherds' is no etymological explanation; there are potsherds, for the Saurya has one potsherd and (another) five potsherds. The Brāhmaṇas speak of many divisions: Pṛthivī is Vaiśvānara, the year is Vaiśvānara, the Brāhmaṇa is Vaiśvānara." The reference ends in an equals sign after its numbers in the supplied text, as supplied.]

### Printed p. 501

The reasonings stated earlier, that the Āditya is Vaiśvānara, and the Brāhmaṇa sentence, are refuted by the Brāhmaṇa sentence that propounds Vaiśvānara-ness also for the Pṛthivī, the year and the Brāhmaṇa which have been cited; and the meaning is explained that the hymn हविष्कांतं (*haviṣkāṃtaṃ*) [printed so, where the earlier passage has ಹವಿಷ್ಕಾಂತೀಯಂ; as supplied] is addressed to Agni.

अपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्यत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुर्यग्नियं । (*apāmupasthe mahiṣā agṛbhyata viśo rājānamupa tasthuryagniyaṃ |*)
आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥ (*ā dūto agnimabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ ‖*)

(ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 6-8-4)

In this Ṛk it is described that the mighty gods praised Vaiśvānara Agni in the atmosphere (antarikṣa); and [it quotes]

मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततस्सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् । (*mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktamagnistatassūryo jāyate prātarudyan |*)
मायामू तु यज्जियानामेतामपो यत्तूर्णिश्चरति प्रजानन् ॥ (*māyāmū tu yajjiyānāmetāmapo yattūrṇiścarati prajānan ‖*)

(ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 10-8)

*[The reference is printed with only two numbers, as supplied.]*

This terrestrial fire, by the designation Vaiśvānara, exists in all beings as chief. He holds primacy on the earth. At night he shines with his own radiance. In the morning, having risen, he shines in the form of the sun. Performing his duty in the form of the Āditya and in the form of Agni, he moves in the respective places. Thus it is described.

स्तोमेन हि दिवि देवासो अग्निमजीजनइ्भक्तिभी रोदसिप्रां । (*stomena hi divi devāso agnimajījanaibhaktibhī rodasiprāṃ |*)
तमू अकृण्वंस्रेधा भुवे कं स ओषधीः पचति विश्वरूपाः ॥ (*tamū akṛṇvaṃsredhā bhuve kaṃ sa oṣadhīḥ pacati viśvarūpāḥ ‖*)

(पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) 10-85-10)

*[The word ಮಜೀಜನಇ್ಭಕ್ತಿಭೀ is printed so, as supplied; the abbreviation of the reference is printed ಪು. ಸಂ., as in earlier references.]*

It is explained that the gods, offering oblations as sacrificers to this Agni who exists in the all-self state for the protection of the world, know him as protector in three ways, in Pṛthivī, antarikṣa and the heavenly world, and worship him.

यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्जियासो दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयं । (*yadedenamadadhuryajjiyāso divi devāḥ sūryamāditeyaṃ |*)

(पु. सं. (*pu. saṃ.*) 10-28-11)

In the Ṛk beginning thus, it is described that the gods worship this Vaiśvānara Agni as the Āditya; and by the Ṛk यत्रा वदेते अवरः परश्च (*yatrā vadete avaraḥ paraśca*) (ऋ. सं. (*ṛ. saṃ.*) 10-88-12) it is explained that this Vaiśvānara Agni himself is the one of the middle region.

यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरूप्यतेयमेव सोऽग्निर्वैश्वानरः । (*yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirūpyateyameva so 'gnirvaiśvānaraḥ |*)

(नि. (*ni.*) 7-31)

By the sentence that begins with ಎಂ followed by a stray numeral , the Nirukta authors have made it a conclusion and said that the sacrificers, preparing the oblation with the respective mantras, worship the terrestrial fire [the Kannada word is printed ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿವಾಗ್ನಿಯನ್ನೇ, as supplied] itself as Vaiśvānara Agni: the view of the ācārya Śākapūṇi. The subject of Vaiśvānara Agni has been explained in detail in the first volume.

### Printed p. 502

Sāyaṇa here shows the compound-resolution विश्वानर एव वैश्वानरः (*viśvānara eva vaiśvānaraḥ*) ("Viśvānara himself is Vaiśvānara"), says that the taddhita affix has come in the sense of the base itself, and describes the derivation of the word Vaiśvānara as being like the usage राक्षसवायसादिवत् (*rākṣasavāyasādivat*), "the rākṣasa himself is a crow".

अनुषत्यं—सत्येनानुगतं (*anuṣatyaṃ—satyenānugataṃ*): describing Agni as one who is true to his word in granting to those who serve him the fruit that corresponds to their respective actions; स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*)—as the knowing one who grants heaven and the other fruits according to the eligibility of each; सुदानुं (*sudānuṃ*)—Agni is generous; रथिरं, रण्वं (*rathiraṃ, raṇvaṃ*)—since he has a chariot he comes to the sacrifices; and देवं (*devaṃ*)—he shines with radiance. Thus the greatness of Agni is described, and the meaning is made clear that the sacrificers, the seers of the mantras, knowing it with their mind (मनसा (*manasā*) निचाय्कॆ (*nicāykè*)), praise Agni and invoke him in the sacrifices.

रण्वं—रण्वति यज्ञान् गच्छति (*raṇvaṃ—raṇvati yajñān gacchati*): since he comes to the sacrifices he is ranva; thus the meaning of the word ranva is explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 502. वैश्वानरम् (*vaiśvānaram*): by नरे संज्ञायाम् (*nare saṃjñāyām*) the former member is lengthened [the Kannada word for "lengthened" is printed with an aspirated dh; as supplied]. When the meaning विश्वानरस्य इदम् (*viśvānarasya idam*) is intended, by तस्येदम् (*tasyedam*) (Pā. Sū. 4-3-120) the affix aṇ; by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (*taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-117) vṛddhi of the first vowel; by यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) elision of the a before the affix; by the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta. निचाय्य (*nicāyya*): the root चाय्य पूजानिरामनयोः (*cāyya pūjānirāmanayoḥ*); when the affix ktvā comes in a compound, by समासेनञ् पूर्वेक्वॊल्यप् (*samāsenañ pūrvekvòlyap*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-37) the substitute ल्यबादेश (*lyabādeśa*) ; because it has the mark l, by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent comes before the affix; in a compound the accent of the former member of a kṛt-ending final member comes.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 502, continued. अनुषत्यं (*anuṣatyaṃ*): अनुगतं सत्येन अनुषत्यं (*anugataṃ satyena anuṣatyaṃ*); by अवादयः क्रुष्टाद्यर्थे तृतीयया (*avādayaḥ kruṣṭādyarthe tṛtīyayā*) (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18) the prādi compound; because it is read in the Suṣāmādi group, by सुषामादिषुच (*suṣāmādiṣuca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-98) ṣatva of the sakāra; because it is read in the group beginning with निरुदक (*nirudaka*) the antodātta accent comes. सुदानं (*sudānaṃ*): the root डुदाण् दाने (*ḍudāṇ dāne*); by दाभाभ्यांनुः (*dābhābhyāṃnuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199) the affix nu in the agent sense; by परादिश्चंदसिबहुलं (*parādiścaṃdasibahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199) [the same reference is printed for both rules; as supplied] in a compound the final member takes the first-syllable udātta accent. रथिरं (*rathiraṃ*): when रथः अस्य अस्ति (*rathaḥ asya asti*) is intended, in the possessive sense by मेधारथाभ्यामिरन्निरचौ वक्तव्यौ (*medhārathābhyāmiranniracau vaktavyau*) the affix इनच् (*inac*) ; by यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) elision of the a; by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the antodātta accent comes.)*

### Printed p. 503

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, continued, printed page 503. वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*): वसु आत्मनः इच्छंतः वसूयवः (*vasu ātmanaḥ icchaṃtaḥ vasūyavaḥ*); by सुपआत्मनःक्यच् (*supaātmanaḥkyac*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8) the affix kyac in the sense of wishing; by अकृत् सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः (*akṛt sārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-25) lengthening of the preceding vowel; by क्याच्छंदसि (*kyācchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-170) the affix u after a kyac-ending; by अतोलोपः (*atolopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48) elision of the preceding a; by the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta. रण्वं (*raṇvaṃ*): the root रवि गतौ (*ravi gatau*); रण्वति यज्ञान् गच्छतीति रण्वः (*raṇvati yajñān gacchatīti raṇvaḥ*); because it is read in the pacādi group, by नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यः (*naṃdigrahapacādibhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134) the affix ac; by इदितोनुंधातोः (*iditonuṃdhātoḥ*) the augment num; thus the form raṇva; by the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 503, continued. कुशिकासः (*kuśikāsaḥ*): on the word कुशिक (*kuśika*), when the meaning of descendant in the lineage is intended, because it is read in the Bidādi group, the affix अञ् (*añ*); the form is कौशिक (*kauśika*); when plurality is intended, by यञ्इतोश्च (*yañitośca*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-64) luk for the affix; then the vṛddhi that had come because of the affix also goes; by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-60) the augment asuk for jas. हवामहे (*havāmahe*): the root ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च (*hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*); in laṭ, prathama-puruṣa plural , the affix महिज् (*mahij*); e for ṭi; by बहुलंछंदसि (*bahulaṃchaṃdasi*) samprasāraṇa of the root, and the pūrva-form; by अतोदीर्घोयइति (*atodīrghoyaiti*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-101) lengthening of the stem ending in a; because it stands after an अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*) the nighāta accent comes.)*

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं शु॒भ्रम॒ग्निमव॑से हवामहे वैश्वान॒रं मा॑त॒रिश्वा॑नमु॒क्थ्यं॑ ।  
> बृह॒स्पतिं॒ मनु॑षो दे॒वता॑तये॒ विप्रं॒ श्रोता॑र॒मति॑थिं रघु॒ष्यदं॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । शुभ्रं । अग्निं । अवसे । हवामहे । वैश्वानरं । मातरिश्वानं । उक्ष्यं ।  
> बृहस्पतिं । मनुषः । देवतातये । विप्रं । श्रोतारं । अतिथिं । रघुस्यदं ॥ २ ॥

> *taṃ | śubhraṃ | agniṃ | avase | havāmahe | vaiśvānaraṃ | mātariśvānaṃ | ukṣyaṃ |*  
> *bṛhaspatiṃ | manuṣaḥ | devatātaye | vipraṃ | śrotāraṃ | atithiṃ | raghusyadaṃ ‖ 2 ‖*

*[Differences between Saṃhitā and Pada in the supplied text, kept as supplied: the Saṃhitā has मातरिश्वानमुक्थ्यं (*mātariśvānamukthyaṃ*) (with the preceding word joined), मनुषो (*manuṣo*) and रघुष्यदं (*raghuṣyadaṃ*), where the Pada has उक्ष्यं (*ukṣyaṃ*), मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*) and रघुस्यदं (*raghusyadaṃ*). The Ṛk number 2 is printed at the end of the Pada-pāṭha, not after the Saṃhitā.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निः पूर्वमंत्रे प्रतिपादितस्तं शुभ्रं द्योतमानं वैश्वानरं विश्वासन-
> संबंधिनं मातरिश्वानं । मातर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति विद्युदादिरूपतया चेष्टत इति
> मातरिश्वाग्निः । तमुक्थ्यमुक्थैः शस्त्रैः शंसनीयं बृहस्पतिं बृहतो यज्ञस्य पतिं
> पालकतया स्वामिनं विप्रं मेधाविनं श्रोतारं स्तोत्रशस्त्रादिमंत्रवाक्यं शृण्वंत

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We of Kuśika's line invoke the radiant Agni Vaiśvānara, Mātariśvan, lord of the great sacrifice, wise, listener, guest, swift-moving, for protection and for man's sacrifice. The block is cut at the end of p. 503 in the middle of a word and goes on on p. 504 in a new block.

> मतिथिमातिथेयपूजार्हतया यदृच्छया प्राप्तं रघुस्यदं लघुस्यदं। रघुर्लघुः

> यज्ञार्थं त्वामाह्वयामः ॥ शुभ्रं । शुभ दीप्ता । अस्मात् स्थायितंचीत्यादिना

> तांतरिक्षं । तत्र श्वसिति प्राणितीति मातरिश्वाग्निः । श्वन्नुक्षन्नित्यादिना मातरिश्वङ्बद्य
> कनृत्ययांतत्वेन निपातनात्तूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं । उक्तं । उक्तेन स्तोत्रेण
> स्तुत्यः । तत्र भव इत्यर्थे भवे छंदसीति यत् । तित्सरितमिति स्वरितः । देवतातये ।
> देव एव देवतातिः । स्वार्थिकस्तातिल् । देवतातिशब्देन यज्यो लक्ष्यते तत्संप्रदान-

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तं शुभ्रं (*taṃ śubhraṃ*)—having pure radiance, as described above
- वैश्वानरं (*vaiśvānaraṃ*)—the leader of the universe
- मातरिश्वानं (*mātariśvānaṃ*)—who moves in the atmosphere (antarikṣa)
- उक्त्यं (*uktyaṃ*)—praised by ukkas and the like [the Kannada has ಉಕ್ಕಾದಿಗಳಿಂದ here, as supplied]
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—the lord of the great sacrifice
- विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)—the wise one
- श्रोतारं (*śrotāraṃ*)—who listens with love to the praises [the Kannada word for "praises" is printed with e for u in its second letter; as supplied]
- अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—who becomes the guest in the sacrifice
- रघुष्यदं (*raghuṣyadaṃ*)—the swift-going; and such Agni (अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni): अवसे (*avase*)—for our protection
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—of man
- देवतातये (*devatātaye*)—for the sacrifice
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray and call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We pray and call Agni—who, as described in the mantras above, has pure radiance, is the leader of the universe, moves in the atmosphere, is praised by ukka and the other mantras, is the lord of the great sacrifice, the wise one, who listens with love to the praises, becomes the guest in the sacrifice and is swift-going—for our protection and for the sacrifice of man.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke you for our own protection and for the devotions of mankind, the radiant Agni, Vaishwanara, the illuminator of the firmament, the adorable lord of sacred rites, the wise, the hearer (of supplications), the guest (of men), the quick-moving.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शुभ्रं वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानं (*śubhraṃ vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvānaṃ*)—the word śubhra is used in the sense "shining with radiance", and thus the meaning is stated. For the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) Sāyaṇa [explains] मातरि अंतरिक्षे (*mātari aṃtarikṣe*) *[the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of p. 504, in the middle of the sentence; the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 go on on the next page]*

### Printed p. 505

Continuation of Sāyaṇa's explanation of the word Mātariśvan, which broke off on page 504 in the middle of a sentence: श्वसिति विद्युदादिरूपतया चेष्टत इति मातरिश्वा अग्निः (*śvasiti vidyudādirūpatayā ceṣṭata iti mātariśvā agniḥ*), or अथवा निर्माणहेतुत्वात् माता अंतरिक्षं तत्र श्वसिति प्राणितीति मातरिश्वा अग्निः (*athavā nirmāṇahetutvāt mātā aṃtarikṣaṃ tatra śvasiti prāṇitīti mātariśvā agniḥ*). Since the atmosphere is the chief cause in the making of everything, it is designated by the word "mother". Because Agni, in the form of lightning in the atmosphere, becomes Mātariśvan, or because he is born (moving) in the atmosphere, Agni is called Mātariśvan: thus Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning.

This Vaiśvānara Agni shines with radiance; shines in the atmosphere in the form of lightning; is worthy to be praised with hymns; is the lord who protects the sacrifices; is wise; listens to the hymns, mantras and the like recited by the sacrificers; has come to the sacrifice by chance as a guest worthy of worship; and is swift-going (ಶ್ರಿಪ್ರಗಾಮಿ, the Kannada word printed with ś where kṣ is expected; as supplied) by his speed. Having described Agni's abundant greatness thus, the meaning is set out that we sacrificers, born in the Kuśika lineage, have invoked Agni for our own protection, and in order that, coming to the sacrifices performed by us men, he may accept the oblation.

रघुष्यदं (*raghuṣyadaṃ*)—रघुः लघुः स्यदो वेगो यस्य यद्वा स्यदशब्देन अध्वा लक्ष्यते (*raghuḥ laghuḥ syado vego yasya yadvā syadaśabdena adhvā lakṣyate*): having explained the meaning as "one who has light speed (ಕ್ಷಿಪ್ರಗಂತಾ, the swift-goer), or one who walks quickly on the road", Sāyaṇa describes Agni as endowed with such a quality.

मनुषरि (*manuṣari*)—मनुष्यस्य (*manuṣyasya*) *[the heading word is printed ಮನುಷರಿ in the supplied text, where the Saṃhitā has a different final letter; as supplied]*. The Nirukta-writers (ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು) [cite]: युवं वृकेणाश्विना वपंतेषं दुहंता मनुषाय दस्रा (*yuvaṃ vṛkeṇāśvinā vapaṃteṣaṃ duhaṃtā manuṣāya dasrā*) (Ṛ. Sa. 1-117-21), and also in समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे (*samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-1); in both places the word manuṣya is used in the sense of "manuṣya" *[so the supplied text says: the Kannada states that the word manuṣya is used in the sense manuṣya; as supplied]*. Sāyaṇa too has explained the same meaning.

देवतातये (*devatātaye*)—यज्ञार्थं (*yajñārthaṃ*). Sāyaṇa [says]: देव एव देवतातिः देवतातिशब्देन यज्ञो लक्ष्यते तत्संप्रदानकत्वात् यज्ञस्य (*deva eva devatātiḥ devatātiśabdena yajño lakṣyate tatsaṃpradānakatvāt yajñasya*). He has described the meaning thus: the sacrificial act, in which the oblation is offered with the deities in view, is also designated by the word "deva".

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed page 505. शुभ्रं (*śubhraṃ*): the root शुभ दीप्तौ (*śubha dīptau*); to it, by स्वायितंचिवंचि (*svāyitaṃcivaṃci*) (U. Sū. 2-170) the affix rak in the agent sense; since it is marked k (ಕಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ) guṇa does not come for the light penultimate (ಲಘೋಪಧೆ) of the root; by the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta. मातरिश्वानं (*mātariśvānaṃ*): since it is the cause of the creation, the word "mother" is itself the atmosphere (the sky); तत्र श्वसिति प्राणिति इति मातरिश्वा (*tatra śvasiti prāṇiti iti mātariśvā*), "(if there is space, the one who lives is Agni)", अग्निः (*agniḥ*) श्वन्नु (*śvannu*) *[the word breaks at the end of page 505 after this and goes on at the head of page 506; as supplied].)*

*[Stray line at the foot of p. 505, kept as supplied: the number 64.]*

### Printed p. 506

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed page 506, continued. हन् (*han*) (U. Sū. 1-157): by this rule मातरिश्वन् (*mātariśvan*) is fixed irregularly (nipātana) as ending in the affix कन् (*kan*), and so the accent udātta on the last syllable of the former member comes. उत्कं (*utkaṃ*) *[the head word is printed so; as supplied]*: उक्तेन स्तोत्रेण स्तुत्यः उत्कं तत्र भवः (*uktena stotreṇa stutyaḥ utkaṃ tatra bhavaḥ*); when this meaning is intended, by भवेछंदसि (*bhavechaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) the affix yat; since it has the designation bha, by यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) the preceding a is elided; since the affix is marked t, by तित्तादुदरिंद तित्‌स्वरितं (*tittādudariṃda titsvaritaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185) the svarita accent comes. देवतातये (*devatātaye*): देव एव देवतातिः (*deva eva devatātiḥ*); by सर्वदेवात्तातिल् (*sarvadevāttātil*) (Pā. Sū. 4-4-142) the affix tātil in its own sense (ಸ್ವಾರ್ಥ) to the word deva; since it is marked l, by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6 1-193) the udātta accent comes before the affix. It is a form ending in the dative singular (ಚತುರ್ಥೀಏಕವಚನಾಂತರರೂಪ, so printed; as supplied). Here, by the figurative function (lakṣaṇā), the word देवताति (*devatāti*) must be given the meaning "sacrifice"; since the sacrifice is performed with the deities in view, the sacrifice too is a deity.)*

> नेन प्रतिदिनं सम्यक् पोष्यते तद्वत्।अमृतेषु मरणधर्मरहितेषु देवेषु मध्यॆ

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vaiśvānara Agni is kindled daily by the Kuśikas, as a neighing foal is nourished by mares; may the wakeful one give us wealth. The bhāṣya ends with a grammatical tail on the words yuge yuge, svaśvaṃ, dadhātu, ratnaṃ and jāgṛviḥ, transcribed in the block, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जनिभिः (*janibhiḥ*)—stimulated by the mothers, the mares
- क्रंदन् (*kraṃdan*)—and making the sound of neighing; अश्वो न (*aśvo na*)—like a thoroughbred horse
- वैश्वानरः (*vaiśvānaraḥ*)—Vaiśvānara Agni
- कुशिकेभिः (*kuśikebhiḥ*)—by the sages born in Kuśika's family; युगे युगे (*yuge yuge*)—every day (or in every yuga)
- समिध्यते (*samidhyate*)—is kindled by oblations of ghee
- अमृतेषु (*amṛteṣu*)—among the gods, who are free from the nature of death
- जागृविः (*jāgṛviḥ*)—who is awakened by the flame; सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*)—that Agni
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*) *[so printed, where the Saṃhitā has a different form; as supplied]*—endowed with excellent offspring
- स्वश्वं (*svaśvaṃ*)—endowed with excellent horses *[the Kannada has ಅದ after this; as supplied]*
- रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—the excellent wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दधातु (*dadhātu*)—may he give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like a thoroughbred horse that is stimulated by the mothers, the mares, and makes the sound of neighing, Vaiśvānara Agni is kindled every day by the sages born in Kuśika's family with oblations of ghee. May that Agni, who is awakened by the flame among the gods, free from the nature of death, give us excellent wealth, endowed with excellent offspring and with excellent horses.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Vaishwanara is kindled in every age by the Kushikas as a neighing foal (is nourished) by its mother : may that Agni, vigilant amongst the immortals, give us wealth with excellent offspring and good horses.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अश्वो न क्रंदन् जनिभिः (*aśvo na kraṃdan janibhiḥ*)—यथा जातो अश्वः हेषारवं कुर्वन् जनयित्रीभिः वडवाभिः स्तन्यपानेन प्रतिदिनं सम्यक् पोष्यते तद्वत् वैश्वानरो अग्निः स्तोत्रं (*yathā jāto aśvaḥ heṣāravaṃ kurvan janayitrībhiḥ vaḍavābhiḥ stanyapānena pratidinaṃ samyak poṣyate tadvat vaiśvānaro agniḥ stotraṃ*): "just as a newly born horse, making the sound of neighing, is nourished every day with suckling by its mothers, the mares, so Vaiśvānara Agni ... the hymn". *[The supplied text breaks off here, with a hyphen, at the end of p. 507, in the middle of the sentence; the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 go on on the next page.]*

### Printed p. 508

Continuation of Sāyaṇa's sentence that broke off on page 507: कुर्वाणैः होत्रादिभिः प्रतिदिनं आज्याहुतिप्रक्षेपेण सम्यक् दीप्यते (*kurvāṇaiḥ hotrādibhiḥ pratidinaṃ ājyāhutiprakṣepeṇa samyak dīpyate*): "(Vaiśvānara Agni) is well kindled every day, by the Hotṛs and the others who make the hymn, by the casting in of oblations of ghee". Like a newly born horse that is nourished every day by suckling (with the breast milk) from the mares that make the sound of neighing, this Vaiśvānara Agni grows every day by the oblations of ghee and the like offered by the priests (ṛtvijs), the Hotṛ and the others, who recite the hymn: thus the simile of the horse has been set out (the Kannada word is printed प्रदर्शनॆ (*pradarśanè*); as supplied) and the description given.

अमृतेषु जागृविः (*amṛteṣu jāgṛviḥ*)—this Vaiśvānara Agni is described as being wakeful and shining with his own brilliance among the gods, who are free from the nature of death.

May this Agni give: सुवीर्यं स्वश्त्वं रत्नं नः दधातु (*suvīryaṃ svaśtvaṃ ratnaṃ naḥ dadhātu*) *[the second word is printed so; as supplied]*: wealth endowed with excellent offspring, endowed with excellent horses and cattle, and excellent or delight-giving, to us the sacrificers (yajamānas): thus the wish is expressed.

The word ratna: रमंतेऽस्मिन्निति रत्नं (*ramaṃte 'sminniti ratnaṃ*); because it gives people joy by being obtained, it is called ratna: thus the meaning of the word ratna is explained.

युगेयुगे (*yugeyuge*)—प्रतिदिनं (*pratidinaṃ*). Although the word yuga denotes a long period of time known by the names Kṛta, Tretā and the like, here it is explained as meaning "day"; and since the repetition (dvirukti) is mentioned, it is used in the sense "every day": thus the meaning is explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed page 508. क्रंदन् (*kraṃdan*): the root क्रदि आह्वाने रोदने च (*kradi āhvāne rodane ca*); for laṭ the substitute śatṛ; since it is marked idit, the augment num. By तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the śatṛ becomes anudātta, so the accent of the root remains. युगेयुगे (*yugeyuge*): by नित्यवीप्सयोः (*nityavīpsayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-4) the doubling comes. By तस्यपरमाम्रेडितं (*tasyaparamāmreḍitaṃ*) the latter part gets the designation āmreḍita. By अनुदात्तंच (*anudāttaṃca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3) it takes the sarvānudātta accent, so the accent of the nature of the former member remains. सुवीर्यम् (*suvīryam*): by वीर वीर्यौच (*vīra vīryauca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-120) the ādyudātta accent of the latter member comes. स्वश्वं (*svaśvaṃ*): शोभनः अश्वः यस्य तत् (*śobhanaḥ aśvaḥ yasya tat*). Since the word aśva ends in the affix क्वन् (*kvan*) (printed so; as supplied) it is ādyudātta; by आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्‌छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvyacchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119) the ādyudātta accent of the latter member comes in the compound. Here the letter ya has come in addition, as a Vedic usage. Or: अश्वेषु साधनः अश्वाः तत्रसाधुः (*aśveṣu sādhanaḥ aśvāḥ tatrasādhuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 4-4-98) the affix yat in the sense "good at". By यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) the preceding a is elided. By यतोनावः (*yatonāvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-313) the ādyudātta accent comes, so in the bahuvrīhi the ādyudātta accent of the latter member comes as before.)*

### Printed p. 509

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed page 509, continued. दधातु (*dadhātu*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); the form ends in the third person singular of lōṭ. Since it stands at the beginning of the pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. By अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) the ādyudātta accent comes. रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*): the root रमु क्रीडायां (*ramu krīḍāyāṃ*). By रमेस्तच (*ramestaca*) (U. Sū. 2-294) *[the Kannada word that follows is printed ऎंबुदरिंइ (*èṃbudariṃi*); as supplied]* the affix na in the sense of the locus (adhikaraṇa); along with it the substitute ending in ta comes. रमंते अस्मिन् इति रत्नं (*ramaṃte asmin iti ratnaṃ*). Since नित् (*nit*) continues from the previous sūtra, by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the ādyudātta accent comes. जागृविः (*jāgṛviḥ*): the root जागृ निद्राक्षये (*jāgṛ nidrākṣaye*); to it the Uṇādi affix kvin, of which vi remains; since it is marked k, guṇa does not come; since it is marked n, the ādyudātta accent comes as before.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The swift fires go towards the water; with the Maruts they form drops, and the Maruts shake the clouds so that much rain falls. The bhāṣya ends with a grammatical tail on the words of the Ṛk, transcribed in the block, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)—having swift movement
- अग्नयः (*agnayaḥ*)—the fires
- प्रयंतु (*prayaṃtu*)—may go towards the regions of water (afterwards)
- तविषीभिः (*taviṣībhiḥ*)—with the Maruts, who are strong
- शुभे (*śubhe*)—in the pure water
- संमिश्लाः (*saṃmiślāḥ*)—having joined
- पृषतीः (*pṛṣatīḥ*)—the drops of water
- आयुक्तत (*āyuktata*) *[so printed, where the Saṃhitā has a different form; as supplied]*—they gathered together (may it unite into one)
- विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*)—who know everything
- अदाभ्याः (*adābhyāḥ*)—and are unobstructed
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts (the winds)
- बृहदुक्षः (*bṛhadukṣaḥ*)—pouring down water in abundance
- पर्वतान् (*parvatān*)—the clouds; प्र वेपयंति (*pra vepayaṃti*)—make move

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the fires, which move swiftly, go towards the regions of water. Afterwards, joining with the strong Maruts in the pure water, may they gather the drops of water together. The winds, who know everything and are unobstructed, make move the clouds that pour down water in abundance.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the swift fires combained [sic] with the vigorous winds proceed to the pure (region of water), uniting the drops (of rain) : the Maruts irresistible, all knowing, agitate the copious-shedding clouds.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the praise of Agni is present in general, but the praise of the Marut deities is stated as the chief thing.

वाजाः अग्नयः प्रयंतु (*vājāḥ agnayaḥ prayaṃtu*)—here the word vāja is used in the sense "endowed with speed". The Nirukta-writers (ನಿರುಕ್ತಕಾರರು) have recited it among the names of food. The meaning is stated thus: the fires endowed with speed, जलमभिलक्ष्य गच्छंतु (*jalamabhilakṣya gacchaṃtu*) (let them go with the water in view), let them be joined with the waters सेरिइरलि (*seriirali*) *[the last Kannada word is printed so; as supplied]*.

तविषीभिः (*taviṣībhiḥ*)—बलयुक्तैः मरुद्भिः । तवंति संचरंत्याकाशे इति तविषाः नायवः (*balayuktaiḥ marudbhiḥ | tavaṃti saṃcaraṃtyākāśe iti taviṣāḥ nāyavaḥ*) *[the last word is printed so; as supplied]*: the meaning is explained that because the winds move about in the atmosphere (antarikṣa) they have the name तविषाः (*taviṣāḥ*).

### Printed p. 511

But here, although the word tavisī is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9), the meaning "endowed with strength" is described, and one kind of meaning is described: the fires, joining with the strong winds and with the waters, have produced drops of water. In the second meaning: यद्वा वाजाः वेगवंतो अग्नयः तविषीभिर्बलयुक्तैर्मरुद्धिः जलमनुलक्ष्य गच्छंतु । ते च मरुतः शुभे जलेऽग्निभिःस्संगताः चित्रवर्णाः वाहनरूपाः वडवाः आयुक्त रथे मेघभेदनार्थे आयौक्षुः (*yadvā vājāḥ vegavaṃto agnayaḥ taviṣībhirbalayuktairmaruddhiḥ jalamanulakṣya gacchaṃtu | te ca marutaḥ śubhe jale 'gnibhiḥssaṃgatāḥ citravarṇāḥ vāhanarūpāḥ vaḍavāḥ āyukta rathe meghabhedanārthe āyaukṣuḥ*). When the swift fires, joining with the strong Maruts, reached the waters, the Marut deities who are with the fires (the winds) mounted, in order to split the cloud, a chariot to which were yoked their vehicles, the mares of variegated colours: thus the meaning is explained. In describing the vehicles of the several deities the Nirukta-writers have counted पृषत्यो मरुतां (*pṛṣatyo marutāṃ*) (Si. 2 28). Here Sāyaṇa has described the meaning of the word पृषतीः (*pṛṣatīḥ*) as drops of water.

विश्ववेदसः अदाभ्याः (*viśvavedasaḥ adābhyāḥ*)—it is said that these words are used as epithets of the word मरुतः (*marutaḥ*). The Marut deities, who are skilled in knowing the deeds performed by the several creatures and are not to be despised by others, यथा प्रभूता वृष्टिर्भवति तथा मेघान् चालयंति (*yathā prabhūtā vṛṣṭirbhavati tathā meghān cālayaṃti*): it is explained that they impel the clouds so that the clouds pour down abundant rain.

पृषतीः (*pṛṣatīḥ*)—बिंदून् । वर्षंतीति पृषत्यः शीकराः । पृणंति पालयंति इति पृषत्यो वडवाः (*biṃdūn | varṣaṃtīti pṛṣatyaḥ śīkarāḥ | pṛṇaṃti pālayaṃti iti pṛṣatyo vaḍavāḥ*) *[the first word of the second sentence begins differently in the bhāṣya block; as supplied]*. Having said that the word pṛṣatī, derived from the पृषधातु (*pṛṣadhātu*) in the sense of sprinkling, denotes drops of water, or that, derived from the पृथातु (*pṛthātu*) in the sense of protecting or filling, it denotes "one that protects", it is explained that, since the work of protection is accomplished by the vehicles of the Marut deities, the meaning is पृषत्यः वडवाः (*pṛṣatyaḥ vaḍavāḥ*), mares.

पर्वताः (*parvatāḥ*)—पूरयति भूमिमुदकेन इति पर्वतो मेघः (*pūrayati bhūmimudakena iti parvato meghaḥ*) "पर्व पूरणे (*parva pūraṇe*)": the word parvata is derived from the पर्वधातु (*parvadhātu*) in the sense of filling, and since it fills the earth with waters, the cloud is जोध्यवागिरुवुदु (*jodhyavāgiruvudu*) *[so printed, apparently a word for "denoted"; as supplied]* by the word parvata: thus the meaning is indicated. Describing the lightning-fire (vaidyutāgni), it is explained that through connection with the lightning-fire the winds split the clouds and make the rain pour down.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed page 511. यंतु (*yaṃtu*): the root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*); for the third person plural of lōṭ the substitute अंतादेश (*aṃtādeśa*). By एरुः (*eruḥ*) the change to u. By इणोयण् (*iṇoyaṇ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-81) the substitute yaṇ for the root. Since it stands after a word printed अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*) , the nighāta accent comes.)*

> कर्षणं नमनोन्नमनादिलक्षणं कर्म येभ्यो भवति ते विश्वकृष्टयः । एवंविधा-
> ये मरुतो विद्यंते तेषां च मरुतां त्वेषं दीप्तमुग्रमुद्दूर्णमवो रक्षण-
> मेमहे । कुशिका वयमा समंताद्याचामहे । ते मरुतो रुद्रिया रुद्रपुत्रा

> घः । तस्येयादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥ २६ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts, resting on the fire of lightning and moving trees, are asked by the Kuśikas for protection; roaring like lions, they give water. The bhāṣya ends with a grammatical tail on words of the Ṛk, transcribed in the block, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- अग्निश्रियः (*agniśriyaḥ*)—those who shine, resting on the fire of the form of lightning
- विश्वकृष्टयः (*viśvakṛṣṭayaḥ*)—those who draw all the things of the world, trees and the rest, and make them move (so they are)
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, born in the family of Kuśika
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—possessing a fierce nature
- त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—(of those Maruts) the power
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—for protection; आ ईमहे (*ā īmahe*)—we pray fully
- रुद्रियाः (*rudriyāḥ*)—sons of Rudra
- वर्षनिर्णिजः (*varṣanirṇijaḥ*)—having a form of the nature of rain
- हेषक्रतवः (*heṣakratavaḥ*)—makers of a deep sound
- ते (*te*)—those Maruts; सिंहा न (*siṃhā na*)—like lions
- स्वानिनः (*svāninaḥ*)—making the sound of roaring
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—become givers of water

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts shine, resting on the fire of the form of lightning, and draw all the things of the world, trees and the rest, and make them move. We, born in the family of Kuśika, fully pray, for protection, for the power of those Maruts, who possess a fierce nature,

*[A bare numeral, 65, stands here at the end of the page, apart from the text; kept as supplied. The sentence is carried on over the page break.]*

### Printed p. 514

and who are sons of Rudra, have a form of the nature of rain *[the Kannada word is printed वृष्टाशित्मकवाद स्वरूपवुळ्ळवरू (*vṛṣṭāśitmakavāda svarūpavuḷḷavarū*) over the line break, with a different letter from the Pratipadārtha; as supplied]*, and make a deep sound; those Maruts, like lions making the sound of roaring, become givers of water.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The fire-beautified, all-agitating Maruts : we seek their fierce radiance for protection : they, the sons of Rudra, the bountiful Maruts, whose form is the rain, are loud like roaring lions.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अग्निश्रियः (*agniśriyaḥ*)—वैद्युतमग्निं श्रयंतः (*vaidyutamagniṃ śrayaṃtaḥ*): the Maruts have attained the fire of the form of lightning. The fire that is in the waters in the clouds is there in the form of vidyut (lightning). Since the winds act so that he makes his own form manifest to others, it is described thus here.

विश्वकृष्टयः (*viśvakṛṣṭayaḥ*)—विश्वस्य कृष्णादेः । कृष्टिः आकर्षणं । वृक्षाणां नमनोन्नमनादिलक्षणं कर्म येभ्यो भवति ते विश्वकृष्टयः (*viśvasya kṛṣṇādeḥ | kṛṣṭiḥ ākarṣaṇaṃ | vṛkṣāṇāṃ namanonnamanādilakṣaṇaṃ karma yebhyo bhavati te viśvakṛṣṭayaḥ*) *[the printed कृष्णादेः (*kṛṣṇādeḥ*) differs from the वृक्षादेः (*vṛkṣādeḥ*) of the bhāṣya block; as supplied]*. Here the meaning "tree" is stated for the word viśva. Since the wind performs the acts of pulling trees, bending them and carrying them upward, it is described that the wind is denoted by the word viśvakṛṣṭi.

मरुतः त्वेषं उग्रं अवः ईमहे (*marutaḥ tveṣaṃ ugraṃ avaḥ īmahe*)—the protection of these Marut deities, accompanied by abundant strength, we, the sacrificers, have desired: thus the sacrificers' invocation is described.

रुद्रियाः वर्षनिर्णिजः (*rudriyāḥ varṣanirṇijaḥ*)—वर्षणं रूपं स्वभावो येषां ते वर्षनिर्णिजः वर्षकाः (*varṣaṇaṃ rūpaṃ svabhāvo yeṣāṃ te varṣanirṇijaḥ varṣakāḥ*). The word निर्णिक् (*nirṇik*) is stated among the names of form (Ni. 3-13). It is described that the Maruts are sons of Rudra and have the nature of producing rain.

हेषक्रतवः सिंहा न स्वानिनः (*heṣakratavaḥ siṃhā na svāninaḥ*)—हेषारवस्य क्रतुः करणं येषां ते कृतहेषारवाः सिंहा इव शब्दवंतः (*heṣāravasya kratuḥ karaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ te kṛtaheṣāravāḥ siṃhā iva śabdavaṃtaḥ*). Saying that, like lions, the Marut deities are of the nature of performing a roar (of sound), with the lion given as an illustration, the nature of the Maruts is explained. Thus it is described that the Maruts, who possess abundant greatness, bestow waters for the benefit of the world.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed page 514. अग्निश्रियः (*agniśriyaḥ*): त्रिञ् सेवायां (*triñ sevāyāṃ*) *[so printed, where the bhāṣya has a different first letter; as supplied]*, the root. By वचिप्रच्छि (*vacipracchi*) (U. Sū. 2-215) the affix kvip, the absence of samprasāraṇa, and lengthening of the root come. When jas follows, by अचिश्नुधातुभ्रुवां (*aciśnudhātubhruvāṃ*) the substitute इयजादेश (*iyajādeśa*). The accent कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛduttarapada prakṛtisvara*) comes. विश्वकृष्टयः (*viśvakṛṣṭayaḥ*): the root कृष विलेखने (*kṛṣa vilekhane*). In the sense of bhāva the affix ktin. विश्वस्य कृष्टिः येभ्यः ते (*viśvasya kṛṣṭiḥ yebhyaḥ te*). By बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायां (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyāṃ*) the accent that makes the last syllable of the former member udātta comes.)*

### Printed p. 515

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed page 515, continued. उग्रं (*ugraṃ*): the prefix उत् (*ut*). The root गम्‌ल्य गतौ (*gamlya gatau*) *[so printed, where the bhāṣya has a different spelling; as supplied]*. By ऋजेंद्राग्र (*ṛjeṃdrāgra*) (U. Sū. 2-180), since it is fixed irregularly (nipātana), the affix ra, the elision of the m of the root and the elision of the end of the upasarga come. उद्गच्छतीति उग्रः (*udgacchatīti ugraḥ*). By the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta. ईमहे (*īmahe*): the root ई कांतिगत्यादिषु (*ī kāṃtigatyādiṣu*). By व्यत्ययोबहुलं (*vyatyayobahulaṃ*) the ātmanepada comes. In the first person plural of लट् (*laṭ*) the affix महिज् (*mahij*). By टितआत्मनेपदानां (*ṭitaātmanepadānāṃ*) the substitute ē for ṭi. By अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (*adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) the elision (शपिगॆ लुक् (*śapigè luk*)) of śap. Since the affix has the status of जुत्वातिदेश (*jutvātideśa*) , the guṇa does not come. Since it stands after an अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the nighāta accent comes.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed page 515, continued. स्वानिनः (*svāninaḥ*): स्वास (*svāsa*) *[so printed; the next sentence has ಸ್ವಾನಃ; as supplied]* is a word that ends in घणांत (*ghaṇāṃta*) . The word स्वानिन् (*svānin*) results. By the accent of the affix the vowel i becomes udātta. रुद्रियाः (*rudriyāḥ*): after the word रुद्र (*rudra*) the affix घ (*gha*) in the Vedic manner. By आयनेयीनी (*āyaneyīnī*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the substitute इयादेश (*iyādeśa*) for it. By यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*) the elision of the preceding a. The ādyudātta accent of the affix comes.)*

#### Ṛk 6

*[No Ṛk number is printed after the Saṃhitā; the number 6 is printed after the Pada. Between the Saṃhitā and the Pada the supplied text has the garbled line पडॆदारि (*paḍèdāri*) in place of the Pada label; kept in kn.md as an italic note and the standard label inserted.]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व्रातं॑ व्रातं ग॒णंग॑णं सुश॒स्तिभि॑र॒ग्नेर्भामं॑ म॒रुता॒मोज॑ ईमहे।  
> पृष॑दश्वासो अनव॒भ्ररा॑धसो॒ गंता॑रो य॒ज्ञं वि॒दथे॑षु॒ धीराः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> व्रातंव्रातं । गणंऽगणं । सुशस्तिभिः । अग्नेः । भामं । मरुतां । ओजः । ईमहे ।  
> पृषत्ऽअश्वासः । अनवभ्रऽराधसः । गंतारः । यज्ञं । विदथेषु । धीराः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कुशिका वयमग्नेर्भामं भासकं मरुतामोजस्तेजो व्रातंव्रातं व्राते
> व्राते प्रतिसमूहं गणंगणं गणे गणे महति समूहे क्रियमाणाभिः सुशस्तिभिः ।
> शोभनाः शस्त्ययः स्तुतयो यैर्मंत्रैः क्रियंते ते सुशस्त्रयः । त्रैर्मंत्रैरी-
> महे । तादृशं मारुतं तेजो याचामहे । पृषदश्वासः । पृषत्यश्चित्रवर्णा अश्वा
> येषां ते तादृशाः । अनवभ्रराधसः । न विद्यतेवभ्रंशो यस्य तदनवभ्रं । अनवभ्रं
> राधो धनं येषां तेऽनवभ्रराधसः । संपूर्णधना इति यावत् । धीराः कर्मा-
> भिज्ञास्ते मरुतो विदथेषु यज्ञेषु यज्ञं यजनीयं हविरभिलक्ष्य गंतारो

### Printed p. 516

> गमनशीला भवंति ॥ गणं गणं । गण संख्याने । पचाद्यच् । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति द्विर्व-
> चनं । परस्याम्रेडितत्वादनुदात्तत्वे पूर्वपदस्वरः । सुशस्तिभिः । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्-
> सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं । भामं । भा दीप्तौ । अर्तिस्तुस्वित्यादिना मन् ।
> नित्स्वरः । ओजः । उब्ब आर्जवे । उच्चीर्बले बलोपश्च । उ. ४-१९१ । इत्यसुन् ।
> तत्संनियोगेन बकारलोपः । अर्धधातुकलक्षणो गुणः । नित्स्वरः । ईमहे ।
> कांत्यादिषु । निघातः । अनवभ्रराधसः । अनवभ्रं । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतो-
> दात्तत्वं । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । गंतारः । ताच्छिलिकस्तृन् । विदथेषु । विद
> ज्ञाने । रुदिविदिभ्यां किदित्यथप्रत्ययः । कित्त्वादगुणः । विदंत्यस्मिन्कर्मजातमध्व-
> र्यादय इति विदथो यज्ञः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Kuśikas ask, with excellent hymns, for the shining power of the Maruts; the Maruts, with variegated horses and unfailing wealth, go to the sacrifices. The bhāṣya ends with a grammatical tail on words of the Ṛk, transcribed in the block, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- भामं (*bhāmaṃ*)—that which is of the form of radiance
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of the Maruts
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—that which is of the form of splendour, the mass of power
- व्रातंव्रातं (*vrātaṃvrātaṃ*)—everywhere where there are groups (of sacrificers) (and); गणं गणं (*gaṇaṃ gaṇaṃ*)—everywhere where great assemblies have gathered *[printed with ಲ್ಲಿಲ್ಲಾ at the end of the gloss; as supplied]*
- सुशस्तिभिः (*suśastibhiḥ*)—with excellent mantras
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we pray
- पृषदश्वासः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ*)—possessing horses that have variegated colours
- अनवभ्रराधसः (*anavabhrarādhasaḥ*)—possessing wealth that is full, without deficiency
- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—and wise, the Maruts
- विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—towards the worshipful oblation
- गंतारः (*gaṃtāraḥ*)—they become goers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We pray, with excellent mantras, everywhere where there are groups of sacrificers and everywhere where great assemblies have gathered, for the mass of power which is the radiance of Agni and the splendour of the Maruts. The Maruts, possessing horses that have variegated colours, possessing wealth that is full, without deficiency, and wise, go in the sacrifices towards the worshipful oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We solicit the might of the Maruts, the irradiation of Agni with solemn prayers in every assembly and company (of worshippers); those Maruts who have party-coloured steeds, who are dispensers of unfailing wealth, firm (of purpose), and frequenters of sacrifices.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सुशस्तिभिः (*suśastibhiḥ*)—शोभनाः शस्तयः स्तुतयो यैर्मंत्रैः क्रियंते ते सुशस्त्रयः (*śobhanāḥ śastayaḥ stutayo yairmaṃtraiḥ kriyaṃte te suśastrayaḥ*). The meaning of the word susasti is explained as: mantras that are in the form of excellent praises. मरुतां ओजः अग्नेर्भामं (*marutāṃ ojaḥ agnerbhāmaṃ*): it is explained that the splendour of the Maruts makes Agni shine.

### Printed p. 517

The sacrificers born in the Kuśika gotra, व्रातंव्रातं, गणंगणं (*vrātaṃvrātaṃ, gaṇaṃgaṇaṃ*)—dividing the splendour of the Maruts, which makes Agni shine, in every group and according to each troop, praised it with mantras that make the praise of the Maruts manifest, and wished that splendour to be a protector for themselves: thus the meaning is stated.

पृषदश्वासः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ*)—पृषत्यश्चित्रवर्णाः अश्वाः येषां ते (*pṛṣatyaścitravarṇāḥ aśvāḥ yeṣāṃ te*). The Maruts have horses of variegated colours as their vehicle; and अनवभ्रराधसः (*anavabhrarādhasaḥ*)—न विद्यते अवभ्रंशो यस्य तदनवभ्रं । (*na vidyate avabhraṃśo yasya tadanavabhraṃ |*) अनवभ्रं राधो धनं येषां ते (*anavabhraṃ rādho dhanaṃ yeṣāṃ te*)। (decrease) deficiency is expressed by the word अवभ्रंश (*avabhraṃśa*). The absence of deficiency is being अनवभ्र (*anavabhra*). अनवभ्रष्टधनाः, संपूर्णधनाः (*anavabhraṣṭadhanāḥ, saṃpūrṇadhanāḥ*)। Those who possess wealth without deficiency, that is, the Marut deities possess imperishable wealth: thus the meaning is explained.

विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—विदंत्यस्मिन् कर्मजातमध्वर्यार्दयः इति विदथो यज्ञः । (*vidaṃtyasmin karmajātamadhvaryārdayaḥ iti vidatho yajñaḥ |*) *[the printed र्यार्दयः (*ryārdayaḥ*) has an extra r before d, where the bhāṣya block has र्यादय (*ryādaya*); as supplied]*. Because the occasion in which the adhvaryu and the others know the duty that must be done is the sacrifice, the word vidatha is explained as denoting the sacrifice. Explaining that the Maruts are wise (the meaning of the word dhīra) and knowers of rites, it is described that these Marut deities come, with the oblation offered in the sacrifices in view, to the respective sacrifices performed by the sacrificers.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, printed page 517. गणंगणं (*gaṇaṃgaṇaṃ*): the root गण संख्याने (*gaṇa saṃkhyāne*). By नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यः (*naṃdigrahapacādibhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134) the affix अच् (*ac*). By नित्यवीप्सयोः (*nityavīpsayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-4) the doubling comes. The latter form, which has the designation आम्रेडित (*āmreḍita*), by अनुदात्तंच (*anudāttaṃca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3) becomes entirely anudātta (सर्वानुदात्त (*sarvānudātta*)); therefore the accent पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वर (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara*) comes. सुशस्तिभिः (*suśastibhiḥ*): भा दीप्तौ (*bhā dīptau*), the root *[so printed, as in the entry for the next word; as supplied]*. When the affix क्तिन् (*ktin*) follows, the nasal (अनुनासिक (*anunāsika*)) of the root is elided. When the compound is a बहुप्रीहि (*bahuprīhi*) , by नञ्सुभ्यां (*nañsubhyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the accent that makes the last syllable of the latter member udātta comes. The form ends in the instrumental plural (तृतीया बहुवचनांतररूप (*tṛtīyā bahuvacanāṃtararūpa*)).)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, printed page 517, continued. भामं (*bhāmaṃ*): भा दीप्तौ (*bhā dīptau*), the root. By अर्तिस्तुसु (*artistusu*) (ए. सू. १-१३७ (*e. sū. 1-137*)) *[the abbreviation is printed with ಏ; as supplied]* the affix मन् (*man*); since it is nit, by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the ādyudātta accent comes. ओजः (*ojaḥ*): the root उब्ब आर्जवे (*ubba ārjave*). By उच्चेर्बले बलोपश्च (*uccerbale balopaśca*) (U. Sū. 4-631) the affix असुन् (*asun*). With it the elision of the b of the root. When it is उज्+अस् (*uj+as*), by पुगंतलघूपदस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadasyaca*) the guṇa for the light penultimate vowel of the root. Since the affix is nit, the ādyudātta accent comes. ईमहे (*īmahe*): ई कांत्यादिमु (*ī kāṃtyādimu*), the root *[so printed, where the bhāṣya block has a different last letter; as supplied]*. The form ends in the first person plural of लट् (*laṭ*). Since it stands after an अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the nighāta accent comes.)*

### Printed p. 518

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, printed page 518, continued. अनवभ्रराधसः (*anavabhrarādhasaḥ*): न विद्यते अवभ्रंशः यस्य तत् अनवभ्रं (*na vidyate avabhraṃśaḥ yasya tat anavabhraṃ*). By नञ्सुभ्यां (*nañsubhyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-17) the accent that makes the end of the latter member udātta comes. अनवभ्रं राधः येषां ते (*anavabhraṃ rādhaḥ yeṣāṃ te*), the compound follows. By बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदं (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the accent पूर्वपद प्रकृतिस्वर (*pūrvapada prakṛtisvara*) comes, that is, the accent of the former member.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, printed page 518, continued. गंतारः (*gaṃtāraḥ*): the root गम्‌ल्य गत् (*gamlya gat*) . In the sense of habit (ताच्छील्य (*tācchīlya*)) the affix तृन् (*tṛn*). For the letter m there come the anusvāra and the parasavarṇa. Since the affix is nit, the ādyudātta accent comes. विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*): the root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*). By रुदिविदिभ्यां कित् (*rudividibhyāṃ kit*) (U. Sū. 4-395) the affix अथ (*atha*). Because kit-ness is extended (by atideśa), the guṇa does not come for the light penultimate vowel of the root. विदंति अस्मिन् कर्मजातं अध्वर्यादयः इति विदथः यज्ञः (*vidaṃti asmin karmajātaṃ adhvaryādayaḥ iti vidathaḥ yajñaḥ*) (the adhvaryu and others know in it the works to be done). By the ādyudātta accent of the affix the word becomes a madhyodātta word.)*

#### Ṛk 7

*[The Saṃhitā is printed with the Ṛk number 6 and the Pada with the number 7; as supplied.]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निर॑स्मि॒ जन्म॑ना जा॒तवे॑दा घृ॒तं मे॒ चक्षु॑र॒मृतं॑ म आ॒सन् ।  
> अ॒र्कस्त्रि॒धातू॒ रज॑सो वि॒मानोज॑स्रो घ॒र्मो ह॒विर॑स्मि॒ नाम॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निः । अस्मि । जन्मना । जातवेदाः । घृतं । मे । चक्षुः । अमृतं । मे । आसन् ।  
> अर्कः । त्रिधातुः । रजसः । विमानः । अजस्रः । घर्मः । हविः । अस्मि । नाम ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> साक्षात्कृतपरतत्त्वरूपोऽग्निर्द्वचेन स्वात्मनः सर्वात्मकत्वानुभवमाविष्करोति ।
> हे कुशिकाः । भोक्तृभोग्यभावेन द्विविधं हीदं सर्वं जगत् । एतावद्वा इदमन्नं
> चैवान्नादश्च सोम एवान्नमग्निरन्नाद इति श्रुतेः । तत्र सकलभोक्तृवर्गरूपेणा-
> न्नादोऽग्निः । स चाग्निवाय्वादित्यभेदेन त्रेधा भूत्वा पृथिव्यंतरिक्षद्युलोकानधि-
> तिष्ठति । तदुक्तं वाजसनेयके । स त्रेधात्मानं व्यभजत । आदित्यं तृतीयं वायुं
> तृतीयमिति । तत्र सोऽग्निरहं जन्मनैव जातवेदा अस्मि । श्रवणमननाडिसाधननिरजी-
> क्षेण स्वभावत एव साक्षात्कृतपरतत्त्वस्वरूपोस्मि । धृतं मे चक्षुः । यदेतद्विश्वस्य
> विभासकं मम स्वभावभूतप्रकाशात्मकं चक्षुस्तद्धृतं । इदानीमत्यंतं दीप्तं
> यदेतदमृतं कर्मफलं दिव्यादिव्यविविधविषयोवभोगात्मकं तन्ने मनासन् ।

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—I, who am famous as Agni
- जन्मना (*janmanā*)—by the very form of my origin
- जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—as one who knows everything
- अस्मि (*asmi*)—I am
- धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*)—the clarified butter itself *[the headword is printed with a different first consonant from the Saṃhitā; as supplied]*
- मे (*me*)—my
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—is the eye of luminous nature
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—ambrosia
- मे (*me*)—my
- आसन् (*āsan*)—is in the mouth *[followed by an exclamation mark where a danda would be expected; as supplied]*
- त्रिधातुः (*tridhātuḥ*)—divided into three parts in the form of air (as prāṇa, apāna and vyāna)
- आर्कः (*ārkaḥ*) *[printed with a long ā at the start; as supplied]*—I am the prāṇa itself
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- विमानः (*vimānaḥ*)—I am also the presiding one
- अजस्रः (*ajasraḥ*)—*[the gloss is broken across the page; its first part, “decay”, ends page 519 and the rest is on page 520]*

### Printed p. 520

(Continuation of the gloss of the preceding word: “without decay”,) and of luminous nature; घर्मः (*gharmaḥ*)—the Āditya, who is of luminous nature, is another form of mine, and; हविः अस्मि नाम (*haviḥ asmi nāma*)—I am myself also the oblation fit to be enjoyed, am I not.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, who am famous by the name Agni, am by the very form of my origin one who knows everything. The clarified butter itself is my eye of luminous nature *[the first word is printed as in the Pratipadārtha; as supplied]*. Ambrosia is in my mouth. I am also the prāṇa that is divided into three parts in the form of air. I am also the presiding one of the atmosphere. The Āditya, who is without decay and of luminous nature, is another form of mine, and I am also the oblation fit to be enjoyed.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I, Agni, am by birth endowed with knowledge of all that exists : clarified butter is my eye : ambrosia is my mouth : I am the living breath of threefold nature, the measure of the firmament, eternal warmth : I am also the oblation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sāyaṇa has described the meaning of this Ṛk in two ways. In the first meaning he has explained that Agni exists in his state of being the Supreme Principle, and that, in the form of enjoyer and enjoyed, he exists pervading the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven worlds; in the second meaning he has said that the all-selfhood of Agni is also made manifest. And—

He has commented that Agni, praised by the sages born in the Kuśika gotra, himself explained his experience of the Supreme Principle by the mantra अहमस्मि जन्मना जातवेदाः (*ahamasmi janmanā jātavedāḥ*) and by the mantra त्रिभिः पवित्रैः (*tribhiḥ pavitraiḥ*).

साक्षात्कृतपरतत्त्वरूपः अग्निः द्वृचेन स्वात्मनः सर्वात्मकत्वानुभवमाविष्करोति (*sākṣātkṛtaparatattvarūpaḥ agniḥ dvṛcena svātmanaḥ sarvātmakatvānubhavamāviṣkaroti*): Agni, having realised the form of the Supreme Brahman, has made clear by two Ṛks the state of all-selfhood that has arisen in him from it.

भोक्तृभोग्यभावेन द्विविधं हि इदं जगत् । एतावद्वा इदमन्नं चैवान्नादश्च सोम एवान्नमग्निरन्नादः (*bhoktṛbhogyabhāvena dvividhaṃ hi idaṃ jagat | etāvadvā idamannaṃ caivānnādaśca soma evānnamagnirannādaḥ*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-6) तत्र सकल भोक्तृवर्गरूपेणान्नादोऽग्निः । स च अग्निवाय्वादित्यभेदेन त्रेधा भूत्वा पृथिव्यंतरिक्षद्युलोकानधितिष्ठति । स त्रेधा आत्मानं व्यभजत । आदित्यं तृतीयं वायुं तृतीयं इति (*tatra sakala bhoktṛvargarūpeṇānnādo 'gniḥ | sa ca agnivāyvādityabhedena tredhā bhūtvā pṛthivyaṃtarikṣadyulokānadhitiṣṭhati | sa tredhā ātmānaṃ vyabhajata | ādityaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vāyuṃ tṛtīyaṃ iti*) (Bṛ. U. 1-2-3).

This world exists in two ways, in the form of the enjoyer and in the form of the enjoyed. This matter is explained in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad: in this world, which exists in the two ways of food and the eater of food, Soma is the food and Agni is the eater of food.

### Printed p. 521

Agni, who is the enjoyer, pervades the three worlds named earth, atmosphere and heaven in three kinds of form, named Agni, Vāyu and Āditya; and the sentence of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad that is the basis of this has also been quoted *[the words for atmosphere and heaven are run together in the print, and the verb “has quoted” is spelt with a different letter from the usual one; as supplied]*.

अहमस्मि जन्मना जातवेदाः—श्रवणमननादिसाधननिरपेक्षेण स्वभावत एव साक्षात्कृतपरतत्त्वरूपः अस्मि । (*ahamasmi janmanā jātavedāḥ—śravaṇamananādisādhananirapekṣeṇa svabhāvata eva sākṣātkṛtaparatattvarūpaḥ asmi |*) In this sentence the word जातवेदश्यब्द (*jātavedaśyabda*) is explained as meaning one who has the form of the Supreme Principle that has come into being directly. The means well known in the Upaniṣads and elsewhere for the knowledge of the true nature of the Supreme Brahman are: hearing the meaning stated, reflecting on what has been heard (examining it with the mind), and afterwards meditating on that nature at all times. But Agni, without asking for the help of these means of realising the Supreme Principle, knows the Supreme Principle completely by nature and has it before him directly; that experience is explained by the words अहमस्मि (*ahamasmi*).

धृतं मे चक्षुः—विश्वस्य विभासकं मम स्वभावभूतप्रकाशात्मकं चक्षुस्तद् धृतं इदानीं तत् अत्यंतं दीप्तं । (*dhṛtaṃ me cakṣuḥ—viśvasya vibhāsakaṃ mama svabhāvabhūtaprakāśātmakaṃ cakṣustad dhṛtaṃ idānīṃ tat atyaṃtaṃ dīptaṃ |*) *[the first word is printed with a different consonant from the one in the Saṃhitā of this Ṛk; as supplied]* The word धृतशब्द (*dhṛtaśabda*) is stated among the names of water (Ni. 2-24). The word चक्षुश्यब्द (*cakṣuśyabda*) is explained as derived चक्षुः ख्यातेर्वा चष्टेर्वा (*cakṣuḥ khyātervā caṣṭervā*) (Ni. 4-3) either from the root ख्या (*khyā*), which conveys the meaning “make manifest”, or from the root चक्षिज् (*cakṣij*), which has the meaning of seeing. That form which makes the whole world shine, which is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, which makes itself and everything else shine and exists as light (the form of lightning fire), is shining in the form of unsurpassed light. By this very form Agni has made manifest the form of fire that stands in his place in the heaven world. In the preceding sentence the nature of knowledge was stated; by this sentence existence in the form of pure being is stated.

अमृतं म आर्स (*amṛtaṃ ma ārsa*) *[so printed, with letters that differ from the word of the Saṃhitā; as supplied]* The word अमृतशब्द (*amṛtaśabda*) is explained by the Nirukta authors as मरणधर्मरहितं (*maraṇadharmarahitaṃ*) (“without the nature of death”) (Ni. 2-20). It is also stated among the names of water (Ni. 2-24).

Here दिव्यादिव्यविविधविषयोपभोगात्मकं कर्मफलं (*divyādivyavividhaviṣayopabhogātmakaṃ karmaphalaṃ*), the fruit of action in the form of the enjoyment of various objects, divine and not divine, is explained as used in the sense of the respective fruit of action, which can be experienced in the heavens and other worlds or in this world, in the various ways in which it exists, and which produces pleasure that comes within the experience of everyone. This kind of fruit of action is also described as being in the mouth of Agni, who exists in the form of the Supreme Brahman, and it is said clearly that Agni exists in the form of bliss. Since by this the state of the self as being, consciousness and bliss (सच्चिदानंद (*saccidānaṃda*)) is stated in Agni, and since Agni सकल भोक्तृवर्गात्मना अवस्थानात् (*sakala bhoktṛvargātmanā avasthānāt*) (exists as the soul of the whole class of enjoyers), and a property is not separate from the possessor of the property, it is explained that Agni himself, who has the other form of the enjoyed, could take the form of an enjoyer different from himself, yet exists in his own natural form as the enjoyer fit to enjoy every kind of enjoyed thing; thus the Supreme-Brahman state of Agni, which exists in the identity of property and possessor, has been made clear.

*[A stray line, the number 66, follows at the end of p. 521; kept as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 522

अर्क:-जगत्सृष्टा प्राणः । (*arka:-jagatsṛṣṭā prāṇaḥ |*) The word अर्कशब्द (*arkaśabda*) is stated among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 3-11), and is used in the meanings god, mantra, food and tree (Ni. 5-4). Here the meaning is explained thus: the creator of the world is Vāyu, who exists in the form of prāṇa; and the Brāhmaṇa sentence that supports this meaning is quoted: “सोऽर्चनचरत्तस्यार्चत आपो अजायंत अर्चते वै मे कमभूदिति तदेवार्कस्य अर्कत्वं (*so 'rcanacarattasyārcata āpo ajāyaṃta arcate vai me kamabhūditi tadevārkasya arkatvaṃ*)” (Śa. Brā. 10-6-5).

त्रिधातुः रजसो विमानः—सः प्राणः अहं त्रेधा आत्मानं विभज्य तत्र वाय्वात्मना अंतरिक्षस्य विमाता अधिष्ठाता अस्मि । (*tridhātuḥ rajaso vimānaḥ—saḥ prāṇaḥ ahaṃ tredhā ātmānaṃ vibhajya tatra vāyvātmanā aṃtarikṣasya vimātā adhiṣṭhātā asmi |*) In the preceding sentence it was said that the state of Agni in the form of the whole class of enjoyers is on the earth. The state of Agni in the atmosphere in the form of Vāyu (wind) is stated here; this is the meaning that Sāyaṇa has explained, saying that Agni, who exists in the form of prāṇa, has three forms (Agni, Vāyu, Āditya), and so exists in the atmosphere in the form of Vāyu, one of them. The word रजस् (*rajas*) conveys various meanings. Here, according to the statement of the Nirukta authors, रजो रजते: ज्योती रज उच्यते, उदकं रज उच्यतॆ, लोका रजांस्युच्यंते, आसृगहनी रजसी उच्यतॆ, (*rajo rajate: jyotī raja ucyate, udakaṃ raja ucyatè, lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte, āsṛgahanī rajasī ucyatè,*) (Ni. 4-19) *[the spellings of the two endings are printed in that way; as supplied]*, he gives the word rajas the meaning “world”, and describes it as used in the sense of the atmosphere world in particular.

अजस्रो घर्मः— अजस्रो अनुपक्षीणो प्रकाशात्मा द्युलोकाधिष्ठाता आदित्योऽहमस्मि । (*ajasro gharmaḥ— ajasro anupakṣīṇo prakāśātmā dyulokādhiṣṭhātā ādityo 'hamasmi |*) The word घर्मशब्द (*gharmaśabda*) is also stated among the names of the day (Ni. 3-19). Here the meaning is explained as the Āditya shining in the heaven world in the form of light that is of one kind at all times or does not come to decay; and the state of Agni existing in the form of Āditya is explained, saying that Agni is in the heaven world in this very form of Āditya.

हविः अस्मि—भोग्यं प्रसिद्धमस्ति तदप्यहमस्मि. (*haviḥ asmi—bhogyaṃ prasiddhamasti tadapyahamasmi.*) The word हविः (*haviḥ*) is stated among the names of water (Ni. 224) *[the reference is printed without a hyphen; as supplied]*. It was said earlier that the prāṇa-vāyu form, the fire form and the Āditya form of Agni are forms of the enjoyer. Now the state of Agni in the form of the enjoyed (as the enjoyer and enjoyed forms of the self have been explained) is described by the sentence हविः अस्मि (*haviḥ asmi*). The thing to be enjoyed, which the enjoyer must have, is fixed as different from the form of the enjoyer. In the experience of the nature of the Brahman-self that arises from the direct realisation of the Supreme Brahman the distinction of enjoyer and enjoyed does not appear; having attained that experience Agni has made manifest his existence in the form of enjoyer and enjoyed *[the word for “enjoyer” in this paragraph is printed in a simplified spelling; as supplied]*.

In the second meaning, which is another kind of explanation by Sāyaṇa, since Agni is of the form of the directly realised Supreme Brahman, his all-selfhood is made clear.

अग्निरस्मि (*agnirasmi*) For this sentence the explanation is देवानां हविःप्रापणात् अंगनादिगुणयुक्तोऽस्मि । (*devānāṃ haviḥprāpaṇāt aṃganādiguṇayukto 'smi |*) The nature of Agni is stated thus: because he conveys to the gods the oblations offered by the sacrificers, I am endowed with attributes that have the form of the relation of part and whole.

### Printed p. 523

जन्मना जातवेदाः (*janmanā jātavedāḥ*) In this sentence the word जातवेदश्यब्द (*jātavedaśyabda*) is explained as used in the sense of जातप्रज्ञ (*jātaprajña*) (“one who has knowledge from birth”). The meaning is described thus: Agni is all-knowing from the moment of his birth; or जातं सर्वं स्वात्मतया वेत्तीति (*jātaṃ sarvaṃ svātmatayā vettīti*) (he knows all that has come into being as being of the nature of his own self), that is, Agni knows that all that has come into being is of the nature of the Self itself. Thus the meaning of the word jātavedas is explained, and the all-selfhood of Agni is established.

घृतं मे चक्षुः (*ghṛtaṃ me cakṣuḥ*) The meaning of this sentence is explained thus: what is well known in the world as ājya (clarified butter) exists for Agni in the form of an eye; यथा लोके चक्षुर्भासकं एवं मयि प्रक्षिप्तं घृतं मयि ज्वालामुत्पादयन् मम भासकं । (*yathā loke cakṣurbhāsakaṃ evaṃ mayi prakṣiptaṃ ghṛtaṃ mayi jvālāmutpādayan mama bhāsakaṃ |*) As in the world the eye shows the capacity of seeing all things, the clarified butter offered in Agni produces flame and makes the form of Agni shine; thus the eye-form of the clarified butter is supported.

अमृतं म आर्स (*amṛtaṃ ma ārsa*) The word अमृतपद (*amṛtapada*) is explained as used in the sense of प्रभारूपं अविनाशि ज्योतिः (*prabhārūpaṃ avināśi jyotiḥ*), that is, a form of light shining as a radiance that does not perish and does not give up its nature; and this shining form of light is described as being in the mouth of Agni.

त्रिधातुः अर्कः रजसो विमानः (*tridhātuḥ arkaḥ rajaso vimānaḥ*) The form of the prāṇa-vāyu, which is of three kinds as prāṇa, apāna and vyāna, is also Agni himself. The venerable form of Vāyu shines specially in the atmosphere in the very form of Agni; thus the state of Agni in the atmosphere in the form of Vāyu is stated.

अजस्रो घर्मः (*ajasro gharmaḥ*) By this sentence, नैरंतर्येण संतापकारी सूर्यश्चाहमस्मि (*nairaṃtaryeṇa saṃtāpakārī sūryaścāhamasmi*), it is said that Agni exists also in the form of the Sun, who at all times causes great heat to all, and thus the state of Agni in the form of the Sun is stated.

हविरस्मि नाम (*havirasmi nāma*) It is described that this sentence conveys the meaning that Agni exists in the form of the oblation, and it is explained: आज्यपुरोडाशादिरूपं हविरस्ति तदुपलक्षितं सर्वमप्यहमस्मि (*ājyapuroḍāśādirūpaṃ havirasti tadupalakṣitaṃ sarvamapyahamasmi*) that is, the oblations of the form of ājya, purodāśa and so on, and also the other kinds of enjoyed things, exist in the form of Agni. By this the all-selfhood of the Supreme Brahman, which is stated in the Śruti “सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म (*sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma*)” (Chā. U. 3-14-1), is also stated about Agni, and अनेनाग्नेः सर्वात्मकत्वप्रतिपादनेन परब्रह्मत्वं उक्तं भवति । (*anenāgneḥ sarvātmakatvapratipādanena parabrahmatvaṃ uktaṃ bhavati |*) It is explained that, since the all-selfhood of Agni is established, the state of the Supreme Brahman is stated here of Agni.

The Nirukta authors, making the promise अथात ऊर्ध्वगतिं व्याख्या स्यामः (*athāta ūrdhvagatiṃ vyākhyā syāmaḥ*) *[so printed, with a separate word division]*, say महांतमात्मानमेषर्ग्गणः प्रवदंति (*mahāṃtamātmānameṣarggaṇaḥ pravadaṃti*): the Ṛks describe the form of the Supreme Self, which is full of greatness; and having said so, they have cited this Ṛk by आत्मजिज्ञासया आत्मानं प्रोवाचाग्निरस्मि जन्मना जातवेदाः (*ātmajijñāsayā ātmānaṃ provācāgnirasmi janmanā jātavedāḥ*) (Ni.खं (*khaṃ*)-4) *[the reference is printed in that form, with no space; the sentence runs on to p. 524; as supplied]*.

### Printed p. 524

In the matter of making known the nature of the Self, Agni has stated his own experience of the Supreme Brahman; thus they have cited this Ṛk.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 7, printed page 524. अस्मि (*asmi*): the root आस भुवि (*āsa bhuvi*). The form ends in the first person singular of लट् (*laṭ*). The accent तिजंतनिघातस्वर (*tijaṃtanighātasvara*) comes. जन्मना (*janmanā*): the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*). The affix मनिन् (*manin*) given in the Uṇādi list; since the affix is nit, the ādyudātta accent comes. चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*): the root चक्षिज् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*cakṣij vyaktāyāṃ vāci*), of the अदादि (*adādi*) class. When उसिन् (*usin*) is carried over from the preceding sūtra, by चक्षे शिच्च (*cakṣe śicca*) the affix उसिन् (*usin*). Because the affix is treated as śit, the substitute ख्यञादेश (*khyañādeśa*) does not come for the root. Since the affix is nit, the ādyudātta accent comes. अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*): by नञोजरमर (*nañojaramara*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-116) the accent that makes the first syllable of the latter member udātta comes.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 7, printed page 524, continued. आसन् (*āsan*): the word आस्य (*āsya*). When the seventh-case singular follows it, by पद्वन्नोमास् (*padvannomās*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-63) the substitute आसन् (*āsan*) comes. By सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the elision लुक् (*luk*) comes for the seventh case. अजस्रः (*ajasraḥ*): the root जसु मोक्षणे (*jasu mokṣaṇe*). By नमिकंपिस्म्य जसकमहिंसदीपोरः (*namikaṃpismya jasakamahiṃsadīporaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-167) the affix र (*ra*). This root, preceded by नञ् (*nañ*), namely जस् (*jas*), gives the meaning of continuity (without a break). By तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣe tulyārtha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the accent that keeps the nature of the former member नञ् (*nañ*) comes. The root जस उपक्षये (*jasa upakṣaye*): if the affix र (*ra*) comes to it as before, the form becomes as before.)*
