The rest of the block is the grammar of the words (Pā. 3-2-186), transcribed but not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Agni, who is all-selfhood) हृदा (*hṛdā*)—by the activity of the inner organ. मतिं (*matiṃ*)—fit to be meditated upon. ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the radiance. अनुप्रजानन् (*anuprajānan*)—having understood by means such as hearing and reflection. पवित्रैः (*pavitraiḥ*)—purifying. त्रिभिः (*tribhiḥ*)—by the three principles Agni, Vāyu and Sūra *[“Sūra” is printed here and below for Sūrya; as supplied]*. अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—his own worshipful nature. अपुपोद्धि (*apupoddhi*)—has he not purified. वर्षिष्टं (*varṣiṣṭaṃ*) *[so printed, with ṭa]*—his own most excellent self. स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)—by Agni, Vāyu and Sūra, who sustain the worlds. रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—as something delightful. आकृत (*ākṛta*) *[so printed, with long ā]*—he made. आदित् (*ādit*)—immediately. द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth also. पर्यपश्यत् (*paryapaśyat*)—he understood as the extension of his own form.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is all-selfhood, having understood by means such as hearing and reflection the radiance that is fit to be meditated upon by the activity of the inner organ, purified his own worshipful nature by the three पापनगळाद (*pāpanagaḷāda*) *[so printed; the Pratipadārtha has the word for “purifying”; as supplied]* principles, Agni, Vāyu and Sūra. By Agni, Vāyu and Sūra, who sustain all the worlds, he made his own most excellent self delightful. Immediately he understood heaven and earth also as the extension of his own form.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, thoroughly comprehending the light that is to be understood

### Printed p. 526

by the heart, has purified himself (by the three) purifying (forms); he has
made himself most excellent treasure by (these) self-manifestations, and has
thence contemplated heaven and earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हृदा मतिं ज्योतिरनु प्रजानन्—सर्वात्मकः अग्निः अंतःकरणवृत्ता मननीयं स्वप्रकाशरूपं परब्रह्माख्यं तेजः श्रवणमननादिक्रमेण संशयविपर्यासभावनाबुद्धिनिरासेन स्वात्मरूपतया जानानः (*hṛdā matiṃ jyotiranu prajānan—sarvātmakaḥ agniḥ aṃtaḥkaraṇavṛttā mananīyaṃ svaprakāśarūpaṃ parabrahmākhyaṃ tejaḥ śravaṇamananādikrameṇa saṃśayaviparyāsabhāvanābuddhinirāsena svātmarūpatayā jānānaḥ*) “Agni, who is all-selfhood, understanding by the inner organ the radiance called the Supreme Brahman, which is to be meditated upon and is of self-luminous form, in the order of hearing, reflection and so on, by driving away the idea of doubt and of mistaking one thing for another, as being of the nature of his own self.” The heart, being the organ that grasps knowledge, is called the inner organ (sense-organ); it is considered the chief member in the body, imagined as related to the five knowledge-organs beginning with the eye and to the five organs of action, and as the place for meditating on the Self. This inner organ is of four kinds: manas, buddhi, citta and ahaṃkāra. The authorities say that it has the power to grasp doubtful knowledge through manas, determinate knowledge through buddhi, pride through the name चित्र (*citra*) *[so printed; the word is printed in that form for citta]*, and the knowledge of memory through the name ahaṃkāra, and that in both the knowledge-organs and the organs of action it is the producer of the respective knowledge.

Here the word हृदा (*hṛdā*) is given the meaning inner organ. The part of knowledge that belongs to this inner organ is stated by the word मति (*mati*), a synonym of buddhi. Since mati produces determinate knowledge, it is said that Agni, who has the all-selfhood of the Supreme Brahman, meditates by his intellect and knows the form of the radiance known as the Supreme Brahman, his own real nature, shining at all times in the form of light; and that, having destroyed the doubtful knowledge and the knowledge that takes one thing for another, which arise while he directly realises his own nature in meditation, by hearing the meaning stated in the scriptures and by examining it, he is one whose knowledge about the Supreme Brahman is fixed, by steady contemplation, as being his own nature. Thus the all-selfhood of Agni is confirmed and described.

पवित्रैः त्रिभिः अर्कं अपुपोद्धि (*pavitraiḥ tribhiḥ arkaṃ apupoddhi*) By this sentence it is said that Agni, devoted to meditation on the Self, has divided into three kinds the very form of the Supreme Brahman that he has through his Brahman-contemplation. These three forms are the forms well known in the worlds by the names Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, which are pure and worthy of worship by others; and it is explained by the sentence परिचिच्छेद खलु (*pariciccheda khalu*) *[the first word is printed in that form; as supplied]* that he shines also in his own Brahman state, which is purer than these and worthy of worship, and that he is such that others come to this kind of certainty. In this matter the illustration त्रिभिः पवित्रैः (*tribhiḥ pavitraiḥ*) is also given: as at the time of sacrifice the Soma is strained through three purifiers, so he purifies everything by his other forms, the forms of Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya.

### Printed p. 527

वर्षिष्ठं स्वधाभिः रत्नमकृत (*varṣiṣṭhaṃ svadhābhiḥ ratnamakṛta*) The word स्वधाशब्द (*svadhāśabda*) is stated among the names of water (Ni. 3-24), among the names of food (Si. 3-9) *[so printed, with a different letter in place of the usual abbreviation; as supplied]*, as “spardhā” (Si. 3-22), and among the names of heaven and earth. Here the word svadhā is explained as स्वेन लोर्का दधातीति स्वधा (*svena lorkā dadhātīti svadhā*) *[the second word is printed in that form; as supplied]*, and is used in the sense of upholding the world. The meaning is stated thus: Agni, holding his own excellent (place) Supreme Brahman nature in the three forms Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, and making all rejoice, has caused the worlds to rejoice.

आदित् द्यावापृथिवी पर्यपश्यत् (*ādit dyāvāpṛthivī paryapaśyat*) For the word आदित् (*ādit*) the meaning “after the knowledge of the Self arose” is described, and तत्र परिकल्पिते द्यावापृथिव्यौ तदुपलक्षितं सर्वं जगत् परितः सर्वतः स्वात्मतया, अदर्शत् (*tatra parikalpite dyāvāpṛthivyau tadupalakṣitaṃ sarvaṃ jagat paritaḥ sarvataḥ svātmatayā, adarśat*) Agni, being fixed in the very knowledge that knows his own real Supreme-Brahman nature, knew the world as imagined in the Supreme Brahman himself, and knew that all the worlds, and also heaven and earth, are imagined in his own nature, which exists in the form of the Supreme Brahman. Having so described it, the commentator cites the Śruti sentence “आत्मन विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवति (*ātmana vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati*)” *[the first word is printed in that form; as supplied]*, which teaches that after the realisation of the Self there arises knowledge of the real nature of all things that are imagined as different from the Self.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 8, printed page 527. पवित्रैः (*pavitraiḥ*): the root पूञ् पवने (*pūñ pavane*). By कर्तरिचर्षि देवतयोः (*kartaricarṣi devatayoḥ*) (Pā. #### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तधा॑र॒मुत्स॒मक्षी॑यमाणं विप॒श्चितं॑ पि॒तरं॒ वक्त्वा॑नां ।  
> मे॒ळिं मदं॑तं पि॒त्रोरु॒पस्थे॒ तं रो॑दसी पिपृतं सत्य॒वाचं॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतधारं । उत्सं । अक्षीयमाणं । विपःचितं । पितरं । वक्तानां ।  
> मेळिं । मदंतं । पित्रोः । उपस्थे । तं । रोदसी इति । पिपृतं । सत्यवाचं ॥ ९ ॥

> *śatadhāraṃ | utsaṃ | akṣīyamāṇaṃ | vipaḥcitaṃ | pitaraṃ | vaktānāṃ |*  
> *meḷiṃ | madaṃtaṃ | pitroḥ | upasthe | taṃ | rodasī iti | pipṛtaṃ | satyavācaṃ ‖ 9 ‖*

*[The first line of the Saṃhitā block has वक्त्वानां (*vaktvānāṃ*), while the Pada block has वक्तानां (*vaktānāṃ*); as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्मादुपाध्यायाद्विश्वामित्रो वैश्वानराख्यं परं ब्रह्माज्ञासीत्तमिनमुपा-
> ध्यायमनयर्चा स्तौति । हे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य शतधारमपरिमितजलधारायु
> क्तमक्षीयमाणं न कदापि विच्छिन्नप्रवाहमुत्सं उत्समिव शतप्रवाहोपेतं
> स्रोत इवाविच्छिन्नवाक्करणीसमेतं विपश्चितं मेधाविनं सकलशास्त्राभिज्ञं पितरं शि-
> ष्याणां विद्योपदेशेन पालकं वक्तानां वक्तव्यानां वेदवाक्यानां मे ०
> मेलकं नानाशाखागतानां वाक्यानामेकस्मिन्नर्थे संकलय्य वक्तारं पित्रोर्द्र्या-
> वापृथिव्योरुपस्थे समीपे वदंतं ज्ञानातिशयेन हृष्यंतं अत एव सत्यवाचम-
> ज्ञातार्थभावात्परप्रतारणे च कारणाभावात्सत्यवादिनं । तमिममुपाध्यायं पि-
> पृतं । अपेक्षितफलप्रदानेन संपूर्णं कुरुतं । यद्वा पालयंतं ॥ उत्सं । उन्वी

> आर्तिपिपर्त्योश्चेत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । निघातः ॥

> *kvedane | asmādunmigudhikuṣibhyaḥ kit | u. 3-68 | iti sapratyayaḥ | kitvānnakāra-*

> *vāk | vipo vācaści notīti kvip | hrasvasya pitīti tuk | tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulamiti*
> *bahulavacanāt dvitīyāyā apyaluk | kṛduttarapadasvaraḥ | vaktānāṃ | vaca paribhā-*
> *ṣaṇe | asmātkṛtyārthe tavaikennenyatvana iti tvanpratyayaḥ | coḥ kuriti kutvaṃ |*
> *nitsvaraḥ meḷiṃ | miliḥ saṃparkārtho dhātuḥ | asmādauṇādika ipratyayaḥ | rodasī |*
> *āmaṃtritatvānnighātaḥ | pipṛtaṃ | pṛpālanapūraṇayoḥ | chāṃdaso juhotyādiḥ |*
> *ārtipipartyoścetyabhyāsasyètvaṃ | nighātaḥ ‖*

Gist: the teacher from whom Viśvāmitra learned the Supreme Brahman called Vaiśvānara is praised; heaven and earth are asked to satisfy or protect him. The rest of the block is grammar, transcribed but not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रोदसी (*rodasī*)—O heaven and earth. शतधारं (*śatadhāraṃ*)—he who is possessed of an immeasurable stream of water. अक्षीयमाणं (*akṣīyamāṇaṃ*)—free from decay. उत्सं (*utsaṃ*)—having a continuous (अनुस्यत (*anusyata*) *[so printed; see the Bhāvārtha; as supplied]*) flow. विपश्चितं (*vipaścitaṃ*)—the wise. पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—the protector of disciples. वक्तानां (*vaktānāṃ*)—for the Vedic sentences. मेळिं (*meḷiṃ*)—he who shows their harmony and expounds their unity. पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*)—of heaven and earth, who are the parents of the whole world. उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—near. मदंतं (*madaṃtaṃ*)—(by excess of knowledge) rejoicing. सत्यवाचं (*satyavācaṃ*)—he who speaks truth. तं (*taṃ*)—this teacher (the sage). पिपृतं (*pipṛtaṃ*)—satisfy fully.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O heaven and earth, satisfy fully this sage, who is possessed of an immeasurable stream of water, free from decay, with a continuous (अनुसूत (*anusūta*) *[the Pratipadārtha has a different word here; as supplied]*) flow, wise, the protector of disciples, he who shows the harmony of the Vedic sentences and expounds their unity, who rejoices, by excess of knowledge, near heaven and earth, the parents of the whole world, and who speaks the true sense.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
*[The label is printed here as plain “English translation”; as supplied.]*

Heaven and earth bc [sic] kind to that sage who is as it were a many-
channelled and inexhaustible stream (of knowledge); the parent (of his
disciples), the collater of holy texts, rejoicing on the lap of his parents, whose
words are truth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is described that the sage Viśvāmitra has praised, by this Ṛk, the teacher who instructed him so that he might directly realise the Supreme Brahman form of Agni, who is famed as Vaiśvānara. It is explained that all the words in the accusative case stated in this Ṛk are qualifiers of the word पितरं (*pitaraṃ*).

*[A stray line at the foot of p. 529, a number printed as 67; as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 530

शतधारं अक्षीयमाणं उत्सं (*śatadhāraṃ akṣīyamāṇaṃ utsaṃ*)—The word उत्स (*utsa*) is stated among the names of a well (Ni. 3-19). उत्स उत्सरणाद्वोत्साहादनाद्वा उत्स्यंदनाद्वा उनत्तेर्वा (*utsa utsaraṇādvotsāhādanādvā utsyaṃdanādvā unattervā*) (Ni. 10-10): the word formed from the root उंद् (*uṃd*) meaning moistening, namely उत्स (*utsa*), is explained as conveying the sense of उत्सरण (*utsaraṇa*), उत्पादन (*utpādana*) and उत्स्यंदन (*utsyaṃdana*), that is, welling up, flowing. And—

अश्मास्यमवतं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभि यमोजसातृणत् । तमेव विश्वे पपिरे स्वर्दृशो बहु साकं सिसिचुरुत्समुद्रिणं ॥ (*aśmāsyamavataṃ brahmaṇaspatirmadhudhāramabhi yamojasātṛṇat | tameva viśve papire svardṛśo bahu sākaṃ sisicurutsamudriṇaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-24-4).

Here Durgācārya has explained, with उत्सं मेघं (*utsaṃ meghaṃ*), the word utsa as meaning cloud. Sāyaṇa has explained the word उत्स (*utsa*) used in this Ṛk as उत्सविव (*utsaviva*) , saying that it is a comparison (उप्पोपम (*uppopama*)). The teacher of the sage Viśvāmitra is सततप्रवाहोपेतं स्तोत इव अविच्छिन्नवाक्करणीसमेतं (*satatapravāhopetaṃ stota iva avicchinnavākkaraṇīsametaṃ*) *[the third word is so printed; as supplied]*. Sāyaṇa has explained him as one who is possessed of the power of uttering (by diffusion) words that never cease, like waters possessed of a flow, joined with streams of immeasurable waters, always (unceasing), imperishable, flowing at all times.

विप्रं पितरं (*vipraṃ pitaraṃ*)—Since the word विप्र (*vipra*) is stated among the names of the wise by the authors of the Nirukta, the meaning is given that the teacher of Viśvāmitra is skilled in all the śāstras and protects his disciples, as a father protects, by teaching them knowledge. *[The Ṛk has a different word at this place; the heading is printed as above; as supplied.]*

वक्तानां मेळिं (*vaktānāṃ meḷiṃ*)—वक्तव्यानां वेदवाक्यानां नानाशाखागतानां वाक्यानामेकस्मिन्नर्थे संकलय्य वक्तारं (*vaktavyānāṃ vedavākyānāṃ nānāśākhāgatānāṃ vākyānāmekasminnarthe saṃkalayya vaktāraṃ*)—It is explained that the teacher of the sage Viśvāmitra explains to his disciples the meaning of the Vedic sentences found in the many different śākhās, and teaches necessarily, in regard to the Vedic sentences, that all of them have the purport of conveying one single meaning.

पित्रोः उपस्थे मदंतं (*pitroḥ upasthe madaṃtaṃ*)—द्यावापृथिव्योः समीपे ज्ञानातिशयेन हृष्यंतं (*dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ samīpe jñānātiśayena hṛṣyaṃtaṃ*). Here the word पितृ (*pitṛ*) is explained as heaven and earth. The meaning is stated that, having obtained abundant knowledge, he is in joy, by the glory of that knowledge, near heaven and earth (in earth and atmosphere).

सत्यवाचं—अज्ञातार्थाभावात् परप्रतारणे च कारणाभावात् सत्यवाचं (*satyavācaṃ—ajñātārthābhāvāt parapratāraṇe ca kāraṇābhāvāt satyavācaṃ*)—The meaning is described thus: because he knows the whole meaning of the śāstras, and because he has no purpose of deceiving another, he speaks genuine words. It is described that the wish is expressed that heaven and earth, by bestowing the desired fruit on a teacher of such glory, may fulfil the teacher's desire, or may protect him.

### Printed p. 531

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 9, printed page 531. उत्सं (*utsaṃ*): the root उंदी क्लेवने (*uṃdī klevane*). By उद्यमिगुधि कुषिभ्यःकित् (*udyamigudhi kuṣibhyaḥkit*) (U. Sū. 3-348) [the bhāṣya block gives a different number for this rule; as supplied] the affix sa. Since kit-ness is prescribed for it, by अनिदितां हलउ (*aniditāṃ halau*) the elision comes for the उपधानकारक्कॆ (*upadhānakārakkè*) of the root. उनत्ति इति उत्सः (*unatti iti utsaḥ*). By vyatyaya the आम्यदातस्वर (*āmyadātasvara*) accent comes. अक्षीयमाणं (*akṣīyamāṇaṃ*): the root क्षि, क्षये (*kṣi, kṣaye*); laṭ in the passive; for it the substitute śānac; with yak as the cause, lengthening of the i of the root; in the nañ tatpuruṣa compound the natural accent of the first member comes. विपश्चितं (*vipaścitaṃ*): विशेषेण पातीति विपा वाक् (*viśeṣeṇa pātīti vipā vāk*); विपो वाचश्चिनोति इति (*vipo vācaścinoti iti*); the affix क्विप् (*kvip*). By ह्रस्पस्य पितिकृतितुक् (*hraspasya pitikṛtituk*) the augment tuk for the root चि (*ci*); since it has the kit property, it comes as a final part. By the power of the taking of the word बहुल (*bahula*) in तत्पुरुषेकृतिबहुलं (*tatpuruṣekṛtibahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-14), when the compound is formed here, aluk comes for the accusative case ending. Since a kāraka is the first member, by गतिकारको (*gatikārako*) the accent कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛduttarapada prakṛtisvara*) comes. The form ends in the accusative singular.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 9, printed page 531, continued further. वक्त्वानां (*vaktvānāṃ*) : the root वच परिभाषणे (*vaca paribhāṣaṇe*); for it, by कृत्यार्थे तवैकेन् केन्यत्वनः (*kṛtyārthe tavaiken kenyatvanaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-14) the affix त्वन् (*tvan*). By चोःकुः (*coḥkuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-30) the substitution of ka for the ca of the root. Since the affix is nit, by इ्नतादिर्नित्यं (*inatādirnityaṃ*) the ādyudātta accent comes. The form ends in the genitive plural. मेळिं (*meḷiṃ*): the root मिळ संपर्के (*miḷa saṃparke*); for it the Auṇādika affix i. By पुगंतलघूदधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūdadhasyaca*) guṇa for the लघूपथॆ (*laghūpathè*) of the root. By the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta. रोदसी (*rodasī*): by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) (Pā. Sū 8-1-19) the sarvānudātta accent comes. पिपृतं (*pipṛtaṃ*): the root पृ पालनपूरणयोः (*pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*); in the Veda it is read in the juhotyādi class (printed जाहोत्यादि (*jāhotyādi*)); loṭ, second person; for the dual the substitute tam; because of ślu, reduplication of the root; by अर्तिपिपर्तोश्च (*artipipartośca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-77) ittva for the reduplicating syllable. Since it stands after an अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the nighāta accent comes.)*

## Sūkta 27 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-seventh sūkta** (इप्पत्तेळनॆय सूक्तवु (*ippatteḷanèya sūktavu*))

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र वो वाजा इति पंचदशर्चं पंचदशं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । प्र वः

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मान इत्येका सूत्रितं च । समिध्यमानो अध्वरे समिद्धो अग्न आहुतेति द्वे। आ. १-२
> इति॥ आधाने तृतीयायामिष्टौ सामिधेनीष्ट्यध्यमानेद्दवत्योर्मध्यॆ पृथुपाजा इति
> द्वे धाय्कॆ। सूत्रितं च । प्रागुपोत्तमायाः पृथुपाजा अमर्त्य इति द्वे । आ, २-१।
> इति ॥ एवमन्यत्रापि यत्र यत्र सप्तदश सामिधेन्यस्तत्र तत्रैते धाय्कॆ इति द्रष्टव्यं ।
> विषुवत्येकविंशतिः सामिधेन्यः। तत्र पृथुपाजा अमर्त्य इति षडृचो धाय्काः पृथु-
> पाजा अमर्त्य इति षट् धाय्काः सामिधेनीनां । अ. ८-६ । इति सूत्रितं । महा-
> व्रतेऽपि पंचविंशतिसंख्याकाः सामिधेन्यः । तत्राप्येताः षडृचो द्रष्टव्याः ॥ अग्नि-
> षोमप्रणयने होता देवो अमर्त्य इति तृचः । सूत्रितं च । होता देवो
> अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादुप त्वाग्ने दिवेदिवे । आ. ४-१० । इति ॥ ईळेन्नो नमस्यस्तियर इति
> तिस्रः सामिधेन्यः । सूत्रितं च । ईळेन्नो नमस्यस्तिरोऽग्निं दूतं वृणीमहे ।
> आ. १-२ । इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning with प्र वो वाजा (*pra vo vājā*) is the fifteenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are fifteen Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said प्र वः पंचोना गायत्रं त्वृतव्या वाद्या (*pra vaḥ paṃconā gāyatraṃ tvṛtavyā vādyā*) [the Sanskrit introduction ends this quotation with a different word; as supplied]. For this sūkta Viśvāmitra is the seer, the metre is Gāyatrī and Agni is the deity. The first Ṛk is addressed to Agni or to the Ṛtus (seasons). The application of this sūkta, at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka and the आश्विनशक्रमंत्र (*āśvinaśakramaṃtra*) , for Ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre, is explained by the sūtra प्र वो वाजा उपसद्याय (*pra vo vājā upasadyāya*) (Ā. 4-13) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra.

In the Ukthya sacrifice connected with Abhiplava, the tṛca (three Ṛks) beginning प्र वो वाजाः (*pra vo vājāḥ*) may optionally be recited as the stotriya tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra प्र वो वाजा अभिद्यवोऽभिप्रायांसि वाहसा (*pra vo vājā abhidyavo 'bhiprāyāṃsi vāhasā*) (Ā. 7-8) [so printed, with a differently joined word from the form in the Sanskrit introduction; as supplied] of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra. The first Ṛk of this sūkta is applied as the first of the sāmidhenī mantras; this is explained by the sūtra प्र वॊ वाजा अभिद्यवोऽग्न आ याहि वीतये (*pra vò vājā abhidyavo 'gna ā yāhi vītaye*) (Ā. 1-2) [so printed, with वॊ (*vò*); as supplied] of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra.

And the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta, समिध्यमानः (*samidhyamānaḥ*), is to be recited as one of the sāmidhenī mantras stated before; this is explained by the sūtra समिध्यमानो अध्वरे समिद्दो अग्न आहुतेति द्वे (*samidhyamāno adhvare samiddo agna āhuteti dve*) (Ā. 1-2) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra.

In the third इल्लियल्लि (*illiyalli*) of the sacrifice called Ādhāna, after the fire has been kindled by the sāmidhenī mantras, the fifth and sixth Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning पृथुपाजाः (*pṛthupājāḥ*), are to be recited for the two dhāyyā mantras; this is explained by the sūtra प्रागुपोत्तमायाः पृथुपाजा अमर्त्य इति द्वे (*prāgupottamāyāḥ pṛthupājā amartya iti dve*) (Ā. 2-1) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra. And it is said that in whatever rites 17 sāmidhenī mantras are used, अश्विला (*aśvilā*) the two Ṛks beginning पृथुपाजाः (*pṛthupājāḥ*) (Ṛks 5-6 of this sūkta) are to be applied for the dhāyyā mantras. And in the sacrifice called विषुवति (*viṣuvati*) there are 21 sāmidhenī mantras. Among them, the six Ṛks of this sūkta beginning पृथुपाजा अमर्त्यः (*pṛthupājā amartyaḥ*), that is,

### Printed p. 533

*(Anuvāda, continued.)* the Ṛks 5 to 10, are to be applied as dhāyyā mantras; this is explained by the sūtra पृथुपाजा अमर्त्य इति षट् धाय्या सामिधेनीनां (*pṛthupājā amartya iti ṣaṭ dhāyyā sāmidhenīnāṃ*) (Ā. 8-6) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (the name is printed here आश्वलायनशौतसूत्र (*āśvalāyanaśautasūtra*), without the letter r; as supplied). In the Mahāvrata also there are twenty-five sāmidhenī mantras; among them the six Ṛks stated above are included as dhāyyā mantras. At the time of the Agniṣoma-praṇayana the three Ṛks beginning होता देवो अमर्त्यः (*hotā devo amartyaḥ*) (the Ṛks 79 of this sūkta [so printed, without a hyphen; as supplied]) are to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादुप त्वाग्ने दिवेदिवे (*hotā devo amartyaḥ purastādupa tvāgne divedive*) (Ā. 4-10) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra. And then the Ṛks of this sūkta beginning ईळेन्यो नमस्यस्तियरः (*īḷenyo namasyastiyaraḥ*) (Ṛks 13 to 15 of this sūkta) are to be applied for the sāmidhenī mantras (printed सामॆधेनीमंत्र (*sāmèdhenīmaṃtra*); as supplied); this is explained by the sūtra ईळेन्यो नमस्यस्तियरोऽग्निं दूतं वृणीमहे (*īḷenyo namasyastiyaro 'gniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe*) (1-2) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra.

*(Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Ṛk 1, continued from the foot of p. 533.)*

> धृताच्या । धृतमंचति प्राप्नोतीति धृताची स्रुक् । तथा च वाजसनेयकं । पशवो

> मानः सुम्नयुः। (तै.सं. २-५-७-४)। इति॥ अभिद्यवः। बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Ghṛtācī is also the ladle (sruk); with these at hand for your sacrifice, the sacrificer desiring happiness reaches the gods (Taittirīya cited); a grammatical tail on abhidyavaḥ, ghṛtācyā, jigāti and sumnayuḥ follows, transcribed but not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)—the months
- अभिद्यवः (*abhidyavaḥ*)—the half-months
- हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*)—those possessing oblations such as milk
- धृताच्या (*dhṛtācyā*)—the cattle (or the ladles)
- वः (*vaḥ*)—in your sacrifice
- प्र (*pra*)—are lords
- सुम्नयुः (*sumnayuḥ*)—the sacrificer who desires happiness—देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- जिगाति (*jigāti*)—worships and approaches

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The months and half-months that partake of oblations, the other gods, and the cattle that give oblations in the form of milk and the like, are the lords of the sacrifice. The sacrificer who desires happiness worships the gods and approaches them.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The months, the half months, (the gods) who are the receivers of oblations, with the butter-yielding cows, preside over your rite; the sacrificer, desirous of prosperity, worships the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)—Here the word vāja is used in the sense वजंति गच्छंति (*vajaṃti gacchaṃti*), "they go, they pass away", and therefore conveys the meaning "months".

अभिद्यवः (*abhidyavaḥ*)—अभितः द्यवो दिवसा येष्विति अभिद्यवो अर्धमासाः (*abhitaḥ dyavo divasā yeṣviti abhidyavo ardhamāsāḥ*). Since in every month there are days (daylights) on both sides of the respective nights, the meaning "half-months" has been given for the word abhidyu.

### Printed p. 535

धृताच्या (*dhṛtācyā*)—धृतमंचतीति धृताची गौः (*dhṛtamaṃcatīti dhṛtācī gauḥ*); धृतमंचति प्राप्नोति इति धृताची स्रुक् (*dhṛtamaṃcati prāpnoti iti dhṛtācī sruk*). The word धृताची (*dhṛtācī*) is stated among the names of night (Ni. 2-18). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning of the word ghṛtācī as a cow, because it gives ghṛta (ghee) for storing, or as a vessel for the oblation (sruk), because ghee is offered in it. And explaining the word हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*) as the gods who have a share of the oblation, or as हविषः क्षीरादेः प्रदातारः (*haviṣaḥ kṣīrādeḥ pradātāraḥ*), the cattle (cows) that give milk and the like, which are oblations, he has cited for these two meanings suitable śruti sentences: "देवाहविष्मंतो गौर्घृताची (*devāhaviṣmaṃto gaurghṛtācī*)" (Tai. Saṃ. 2-7-5-4) and "पशवो हविष्मंतः स्रुक् धृताची (*paśavo haviṣmaṃtaḥ sruk dhṛtācī*)". [The bhāṣya block gives the number 2-5-7-4 for the first of these; as supplied.]

धृताच्या सहिता हविष्मंतो देवाः (*dhṛtācyā sahitā haviṣmaṃto devāḥ*): addressing the gods, who are worthy to receive the oblation, together with the sacrificial vessel filled with ghee for the homa, [he says that] the cattle, the months and the half-months, all these are ready for the gods, that is, for satisfying the gods through the sacrifice; and सुम्नयुः देवान् जिगाति (*sumnayuḥ devān jigāti*): the sacrificer who desires to obtain happiness is ready, with these, to perform the sacrifice for satisfying the gods. Thus he has explained the meaning and cited a śruti sentence that conveys this same intention. उक्तार्थे तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मणं (*uktārthe taittirīyabrāhmaṇaṃ*)—प्रवो वाजा इत्यन्वाह मासा वै वाजाः अर्धमासा अभिद्यवो देवा हवि- ष्मंतो गौर्घृताची यज्ञो देर्वा जिगाति यजमानो सुम्नयुः (*pravo vājā ityanvāha māsā vai vājāḥ ardhamāsā abhidyavo devā havi- ṣmaṃto gaurghṛtācī yajño dervā jigāti yajamāno sumnayuḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-7-8-4) [so printed, with a different number from the earlier citations, and with the words differing from the form in the bhāṣya block; as supplied]. In this Brāhmaṇa sentence the meaning of this passage is clearly explained.

सुम्मयुः (*summayuḥ*)—सुम्मं सुखं आत्मन इच्छॆ (*summaṃ sukhaṃ ātmana icchè*) [the Special Topics print the word with a double m, and the last word as shown; as supplied]. The word सुम्म (*summa*) is stated among the names of happiness (Ni. 2-13). The meaning of the word सुम्मयु (*summayu*) is explained as: one who wishes that happiness may come to himself.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed pages 535 and 536. अभिद्यवः (*abhidyavaḥ*): बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदं (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyāpūrvapadaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1); by it the accent of the nature of the first member comes. धृताच्या (*dhṛtācyā*): the root फृ क्षरणदीप्त्योः (*phṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ*) [so printed, with the letter phṛ]; by अंजिघृषिभ्यः क्तः (*aṃjighṛṣibhyaḥ ktaḥ*) (U. Sū. 3-36-9) [the bhāṣya block gives a different number; as supplied] the affix kta in the passive; since it is kit, no guṇa comes. धृतं आज्यं अंचति इति धृताची (*dhṛtaṃ ājyaṃ aṃcati iti dhṛtācī*); the root अंचु गतिपूजनयोः (*aṃcu gatipūjanayoḥ*); with a subanta in the form ghṛta as upapada, by ऋत्विक् दधृक् (*ṛtvik dadhṛk*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-59) the affix kvin; by अनिदितां हलउ (*aniditāṃ halau*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24) elision of the penultimate n of the root; when the feminine is intended, by the rule अंचतेश्चोपसंख्यानं (*aṃcateścopasaṃkhyānaṃ*) the affix jīp; by चौ (*cau*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-222) the accent udātta on the end of the first member comes. जिगाति (*jigāti*): the root गा गतौ (*gā gatau*); जहोत्यादि (*jahotyādi*) , used only in the Veda; because of the vikaraṇa श्लु (*ślu*) doubling of the root (the sentence goes on on the next page).)*

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ईळे॑ अ॒ग्निं वि॑प॒श्चितं॑ गि॒रा य॒ज्ञस्य॒ साध॑नं ।  
> श्रु॒ष्टी॒वानं॑ धि॒तावा॑नं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ईळे । अग्निं । विपःचितं । गिरा । यज्ञस्य । साधनं ।  
> श्रुष्टीऽवानं । धितऽवानं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विपश्चितं मेधाविनं यज्ञस्य साधनं यज्ञस्य निर्वाहकं श्रुष्टीवानं सुखवंतं
> यद्वा वेगवंतं धितानानं । वानं वननीयं धनं धितं निहितं यस्य तं निहितधनं ।
> तमिममग्निं गिरा स्तुतिलक्षणया वाचेळे । विश्वामित्रोऽहं सौमि ॥ ईळे । ईड
> स्तुत् । श्रुष्टीवानं । वन षण संभक्तावित्यस्माद्विच् । श्रुष्टी वनतीति श्रुष्टीना । कृदु-
> त्तरपदस्वरः । धितानानं । दधातेर्निष्ठायां धिरादेशश्चांदसः । वन संभक्त्य । कर्मणि
> घञ् । बहुव्रीह् निष्ठॆति धितशब्दस्य पूर्वनिपातः । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is wise and the accomplisher of the sacrifice; Viśvāmitra praises him; dhita is explained as deposited wealth; grammar of īḷe, śruṣṭīvānam and dhitāvānam follows, not explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विपश्चितं (*vipaścitaṃ*)—wise; यज्ञस्य साधनं (*yajñasya sādhanaṃ*)—the accomplisher of the sacrifice
- श्रुष्टीवानं (*śruṣṭīvānaṃ*)—the happy, or the swift
- धितानानं (*dhitānānaṃ*)—having a deposit of wealth [so printed, as in the bhāṣya block; the Saṃhitā and Pada have a different form; as supplied]
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- गिरा (*girā*)—with speech in the form of praise
- ईळे (*īḷe*)—I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise with speech in the form of praise Agni, who is wise, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, happy, and the one who has a deposit of wealth.

### Printed p. 537

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I worship with praise the wise Agni, the accomplisher of sacrifice the possessor of happiness, the repository of wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

श्रुष्टीवानं-सुखवंतं यद्वा वेगवंतं (*śruṣṭīvānaṃ-sukhavaṃtaṃ yadvā vegavaṃtaṃ*). The authors of the Nirukta have explained the meaning of the word śruṣṭi: श्रुष्टीति क्षिप्रनाम (*śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma*) (Ni. 6-13), that is, śruṣṭi is a name for "quick". And they have also given the meaning श्रुष्टीवरीः सुखवत्यः (*śruṣṭīvarīḥ sukhavatyaḥ*), "the happy ones". Sāyaṇa has described Agni as one who has happiness and who has speed.

धितानानं—वानं वननीयं धनं धितं यस्य तं निहितधनं (*dhitānānaṃ—vānaṃ vananīyaṃ dhanaṃ dhitaṃ yasya taṃ nihitadhanaṃ*). Explaining the word vāna as "what is desired", he has explained that Agni is "dhitāvāna" [so printed in the Special Topics] because the desired wealth has been deposited by Agni for the sacrificers.

The seer Viśvāmitra, the seer of the mantra, praises with words in the form of praise Agni, who is wise, capable of carrying out the sacrifice, happy or swift, and who bestows wealth on the sacrificers according to the wish of each; this is how the meaning has been explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed page 537. ईळे (*īḷe*): the root ईड स्तुतौ (*īḍa stutau*), the form of the present tense, first person singular; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda the nighāta accent does not come; since the sarvadhātuka affix la comes after a root that is anudātta-it, by तास्यनु- दात्तेत् (*tāsyanu- dāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the affix is anudātta and the accent of the root remains. विपश्चितं (*vipaścitaṃ*): विपः चिनोतीति विपश्चित् (*vipaḥ cinotīti vipaścit*); by the word bahula, luk does not come to the case ending of the first member in the compound; the accent of the nature of the kṛt-ending last member comes. गिरा (*girā*): by सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-18) the udātta accent comes to the instrumental singular.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued. श्रुष्टीवानं (*śruṣṭīvānaṃ*): the root वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*); by अन्येभ्योपि दृश्यंते (*anyebhyopi dṛśyaṃte*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75) the affix vic, in which total elision takes place; श्रुष्टी वनति इति श्रुष्टीवा (*śruṣṭī vanati iti śruṣṭīvā*); by गतिकार- कोपपदात् (*gatikāra- kopapadāt*) the accent of the nature of the kṛt-ending last member comes; the form is in the accusative singular. धितानानं (*dhitānānaṃ*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); when the affix kta comes to it, the root gets the substitute dhi in the Veda, and the form dhita results; the root वन संभक्तौ (*vana saṃbhaktau*) with the affix ghañ in the passive; by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) vṛddhi of the penultimate of the root; वानं धितं यस्य सः धितानानः (*vānaṃ dhitaṃ yasya saḥ dhitānānaḥ*) in a bahuvrīhi, by निष्ठाच (*niṣṭhāca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-205) the word dhita is placed first; by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदं (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the accent of the nature of the first member comes.)*

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ श॒केम॑ ते व॒यं यमं॑ दे॒वस्य॑ वा॒जिनः॑ ।  
> अति॒ द्वेषां॑सि तरेम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । शकेम । ते । वयं । यमं । देवस्य । वाजिनः ।  
> अति । द्वेषांसि । तरेम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने वाजिनः संभृतहविष्का वयं देवस्य द्योतमानस्य ते तव यमं
> यमनमा यज्ञसमीप्तेरत्रावस्थानं कर्तुं शकेम । शक्यास्मै । वाजिनो वेगवतो
> देवस्येति वा योजनीयं । ततः कारणात् द्वेषांस्यस्मदीयानि पापान्यतितरेम ।
> पापेभ्य उत्तीर्णा भवेम ॥ शकेम । शकल्य शक्तावित्यस्याशीर्लिज लिज्याशिष्य ज्ञॆत्यज्
> प्रत्ययः । किदाशिषीति यासुट् । सलोपेयादेशयलोपगुणसलोपाः आमंत्रि-
> तस्याविद्यमानत्वेन पादादित्वादनिघातः । उदात्तनिवृत्ति स्वरः । यमं यम उपरम
> इत्यस्माद्भावे घज् । यम उपरम इति निपातनाद्वृद्ध्यभावः । इत्त्वर । तरेम ।
> तृप्लवनतरणयोः । प्रार्थने लिजि रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, holding oblations, are able to detain shining Agni till the rite ends, and may cross over our sins; grammar of śakema, yamam, tarema follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)—who have collected the oblation
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the shining one; ते यमं (*te yamaṃ*)—to keep you (until the completion of the sacrifice)
- शकेम (*śakema*)—grant that we be able
- द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*)—our sins; अति तरेम (*ati tarema*)—grant also that we cross over and become free from them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, grant that we, who have obtained the oblation and are ready for the sacrifice, may be able to keep you, the shining one, with us until our sacrifice is finished, and grant also that we cross over our sins and become free from them.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May we offering oblations effect the detention of you who are divine (until the completion of the rite), and may we (thereby) overcome all animosities.

### Printed p. 539

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here Sāyaṇa has explained the word वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*) in one way as संभृतहविष्का (*saṃbhṛtahaviṣkā*), that is, the sacrificers who have prepared the oblation for offering in Agni, and in another way as वाजिनः वेगवतः देवस्य (*vājinaḥ vegavataḥ devasya*), that is, the swift Agni.

In the first meaning, since the word वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*) is an epithet of the sacrificers, the meaning has been explained thus: we, the sacrificers who have prepared the oblation for performing the sacrifice, would be able to bring about in the shining Agni the yamana, that is, the आयज्ञसमाप्तेः अवस्थानं (*āyajñasamāpteḥ avasthānaṃ*), the state of being near at hand until the sacrifice is completed.

In the second meaning, the wish is set forth that Agni, who is swift, may be near at hand in the sacrifice of us sacrificers until the completion of the sacrifice.

द्वेषांसि अतितरेम (*dveṣāṃsi atitarema*)—अस्मदीयानि (*asmadīyāni*) (those relating to us), the sins committed by us: this is the meaning explained for the word द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*). The wish of the sacrificers is explained: because Agni's presence is in our sacrifice, may we obtain release from all those sins.

The great power of the sacrificers, who are able to make Agni, who is shining and swift, remain present in the sacrifice until its completion, is also indicated.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed page 539. शकेम (*śakema*): the root शक्य शक्ति (*śakya śakti*) ; the liṅ in the sense of benediction; the affix mas in the first person plural; by नित्यं जितः (*nityaṃ jitaḥ*) elision of sa; by लिज्याशिष्यज् (*lijyāśiṣyaj*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-86) the affix aj; by किदाशिषि (*kidāśiṣi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-104) the augment yāsuṭ, which is kit; since in the Veda it has the name sārvadhātuka, by लिजःसलोपो (*lijaḥsalopo*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-79) elision of sa; by अतोयेयः (*atoyeyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-80) the substitute iya for the yāsuṭ that comes after a stem ending in a, elision of ya, guṇa, and the form śakema results. Since the vocative stands before it and is treated as non-existent, and since it stands at the beginning of the pāda, the nighāta accent of the finite verb does not come; by the udātta-nivṛtti accent the letter e becomes udātta, so it is madhyodātta.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, continued. यमं (*yamaṃ*): the root यम उपरमे (*yama uparame*); the affix ghañ in the sense of the action; since it is irregularly formed by यम उपरमे (*yama uparame*), the vṛddhi of the penultimate does not come; since the affix is "it" , the ādyudātta accent comes. द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*): the root द्विष, अप्रीत् (*dviṣa, aprīt*); the Uṇādi affix asun; guṇa of the light penultimate of the root; since it is nit, the ādyudātta accent comes. तरेम (*tarema*): the root त्वा प्लवनतरणयोः (*tvā plavanataraṇayoḥ*) [the bhāṣya block gives a different form of the root; as supplied]; the liṅ in the sense of prayer; the form in the first person plural; since it stands after an अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the nighāta accent comes.)*

> स्माण्णत् । अस्य तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरितत्वे प्राप्त ईडवंदेत्यादिनाद्युदात्तत्वं। ईमहे ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, kindled in the sacrifice by ghee oblations, flame-haired, purifying and worthy of praise, is asked by us for the desired fruit; grammar of īḍyaḥ and īmahe follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- समिध्यमानः (*samidhyamānaḥ*)—blazing forth
- शोचिष्केशः (*śociṣkeśaḥ*)—having hair in the form of flames
- पावकः (*pāvakaḥ*)—the purifier
- ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)—worthy of praise, he is
- तं (*taṃ*)—that worshipful Agni
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask, for the sake of the fruit

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, blazing forth in the sacrifice, has hair in the form of flames, is the purifier and is worthy of praise. We ask that worshipful Agni for the sake of the fruit.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We solicit that Agni, who is being kindled at the sacrifice, the purifier, the adorable, whose hair is flame.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—The meaning of the word agni has been explained earlier. This Agni, घृताज्याहुतिभिः सम्यक् प्रज्याल्यमानः (*ghṛtājyāhutibhiḥ samyak prajyālyamānaḥ*) [so printed; the bhāṣya has a different spelling of the last word], that is, being thought of as possessing exceedingly great flames through the oblations in the form of ājya (the sentence is garbled at this point in the supplied text, where it reads as "like one who possesses"), is said to be invoked by the sacrificer; and शोचिश्केशः (*śociśkeśaḥ*) as one with hair in the form of flames,

### Printed p. 541

and पावकः (*pāvakaḥ*) as the producer of purification; thus described, this Agni स्तोतृभिः प्रशस्यो भवति (*stotṛbhiḥ praśasyo bhavati*), that is, is worthy of praise by those who praise him. Further, at ईमहे (*īmahe*), saying that this root, which is capable in the sense of lustre and so on, here conveys the meaning in the form of याज्ञा (*yājñā*) (prayer), the meaning has been explained that we, the sacrificers, pray to Agni, who is शोचिष्टेश (*śociṣṭeśa*) [so printed in the Special Topics], the purifier and the one worthy of praise, so that our wish may be fulfilled.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed page 541. समिध्यमानः (*samidhyamānaḥ*): the root इइंधी दीप्तौ (*iiṃdhī dīptau*) ; in the passive the affix śānac replaces laṭ; because of yak the nasal of the root is elided; by the rule of the accent of the nature of the kṛt-ending last member the accent of yak remains. ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*): the root ईड स्तुत् (*īḍa stut*) ; by ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (*ṛhalorṇyat*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-124) the affix ṇyat; since it is tit, the svarita accent is obtained by तित्‌स्वरितं (*titsvaritaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185), but by ईडवृंदवृ (*īḍavṛṃdavṛ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-214) the ādyudātta accent comes. शोचिष्केशः (*śociṣkeśaḥ*): शोचींषि केशाः यस्य सः (*śocīṃṣi keśāḥ yasya saḥ*) ; in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the nature of the first member comes. ईमहे (*īmahe*): the root ई कांतादिषु (*ī kāṃtādiṣu*) ; since roots have many meanings, it is used here in the sense of asking; laṭ, first person plural; the nighāta accent of a finite verb comes.)*

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पृ॒थु॒पाजा॒ अम॑त्यो घृ॒तनि॑र्णि॒क्स्वा॑हुतः ।  
> अ॒ग्निर्य॒ज्ञस्य॑ हव्य॒वाट् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पृथुपाजाः । अमर्त्यः । घृतनिर्निक् । सुआहुतः ।  
> अग्निः । यज्ञस्य । हव्यवाट् ॥५॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पृथुपाजाः प्रभूततेजोरूपोऽमर्त्यो मरणधर्मरहितो घृतनिर्णिक् ।
> घृतस्य विलयनद्वारा शोधनं येनेति घृतनिर्णिक् । स्वाहुतः सुष्टु होत्रादिभिः
> सम्यगिष्टः । एवंभूतोग्निर्यज्ञस्य ज्योतिष्टोमादेर्हव्यवाट् हव्यानां वोढा
> भवति॥ पृथुपाजाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । स्वाहुतः । जुहोतेः कर्मणि क्तः । गतिरनंतर
> इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । हव्यवाट् । वहश्चेति ण्वैः ॥

### Printed p. 542

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, of abundant lustre, immortal, purifying through melted ghee, well worshipped, is the bearer of the oblations of the sacrifice such as the Jyotiṣṭoma; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पृथुपाजाः (*pṛthupājāḥ*)—having abundant lustre
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—free from the nature of death
- घृतनिर्णिक् (*ghṛtanirṇik*)—having a form made pure by the melting of ghee
- स्वाहुतः (*svāhutaḥ*)—honoured in a special manner by the hotṛ priests and others
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice
- हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*)—is the means that carries the oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who has abundant lustre, is free from the nature of death, has a form made pure by the melting of ghee, is the means that carries the oblation of the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, the bright-shining, the immortal, the cleanser with clarified butter, the fitly-invoked, the bearer of the oblation in the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पृथुपाजाः (*pṛthupājāḥ*)—प्रभूततेजोरूपः (*prabhūtatejorūpaḥ*). The word pāja is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). The meaning has been explained thus: Agni possesses strength in the form of his abundant (excessive) radiance.

घृतनिर्णिक् (*ghṛtanirṇik*)—घृतस्य विलयनद्वारा शोधनं येनेति (*ghṛtasya vilayanadvārā śodhanaṃ yeneti*). The word nirṇik is stated among the names of form (Ni. 3-13) [printed with a comma instead of a full stop after Ni]. The meaning is that Agni has the form that purifies the things offered into him.

स्वाहुतः (*svāhutaḥ*)—सुष्टुहोत्रादिभिः सम्यगिष्टः (*suṣṭuhotrādibhiḥ samyagiṣṭaḥ*): the meaning has been given as one who is worshipped in accordance with the rules of the scripture by the priests such as the होतृवे (*hotṛve*) and others.

Agni, who has power in the form of exceeding radiance, who purifies the substance offered into him, who is worshipped according to the order of the scripture by the hotṛ priests, is the bearer of the oblations offered to the gods in sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma; this is how it has been explained. [The supplied text has an unmatched closing bracket after the word for "substance" in the first line of this paragraph; as supplied.]

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed page 542. पृथुपाजाः (*pṛthupājāḥ*): by गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*) the accent of the nature of the kṛt-ending last member comes. Since pāja ends in an affix with the mark n, it becomes ādyudātta. घृतनिर्णिक् (*ghṛtanirṇik*): घृतस्य निर्निक् (निर्नॆजनं) येन सः (*ghṛtasya nirnik (nirnèjanaṃ) yena saḥ*) in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the nature of the first member comes.)*

### Printed p. 543

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, continued, printed page 543. स्वाहुतः (*svāhutaḥ*): सु आज् (*su āj*) are the prefixes; the root हु दानादनयोः (*hu dānādanayoḥ*); in the passive the affix kta. Because it is kit, guṇa does not come. Because a word ending in the passive kta follows, by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent comes to the gati (स्वा (*svā*)). हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*): हव्यं वहतीति हव्यवाट् (*havyaṃ vahatīti havyavāṭ*); the root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*); by वहश्च (*vahaśca*) (Pā.Sū. 3-2-64) the affix ṇi in the Chandas. Since it is ṇit, by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) vṛddhi comes to the penultimate of the root. Everything in the affix is elided. At the end of the word, for the h come ḍhatva, jastva and cartva. The accent of the nature of the kṛt-ending last member comes.)*

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं स॒बाधो॑ य॒तस्रु॑च इ॒त्था धि॒या य॒ज्ञवं॑तः ।  
> आ च॑क्रुर॒ग्निमू॒तये॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । सबाधः । यत्स्रुचः । इत्था । धिया । यज्ञवंतः ।  
> आ । चक्रुः । अग्निं । ऊतये ॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सबाधः । रक्षोघ्नमंत्रोच्चारणेन तद्विषयबाधा सह वर्तंत इति सबाधः ।
> यज्ञवंतो यजनीयहवियर्युक्ता यतस्रुचः । यताः संयताः सुचो जुह्वाद्या
> यैस्ते यतस्रुचः । ऋत्विजः । इत्थेत्मनेन प्रकारेण क्रियमाणया धिया स्तुत्या
> तमेवंभूतमग्निमूतये राक्षसबाधाद्रक्षणाय आ अभिमुखं चक्रुः । कुर्वंति ॥
> सबाधः । बाध्य विलोडन इत्यस्मात् क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । इत्था । इदंशब्दात्पका-
> रार्थ इदमस्थमुः । तस्य सुपां सुलुगिति डादेशः । उदात्तनिवृत्ति स्वरेणांतोदात्तः ।
> चक्रुः । दुकृञ् करण इत्यस्य लिट्युसि यणादेशे कृते तस्य द्विर्वचनेऽचीति स्थानिव-
> द्भावाद्विर्वचनं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests, beset by the obstruction of demons, holding their ladles and having the worshipful oblations, thus turn Agni towards themselves by praise, for protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*)—those who have fallen into the trouble caused by demons and the like
- यज्ञवंतः (*yajñavaṃtaḥ*)—those who possess the worshipful oblation
- यतस्रुचः (*yatasrucaḥ*)—the ṛtvik priests who hold the suk-vessel
- इत्था (*itthā*)—of this kind

### Printed p. 544

धिया (*dhiyā*)—by praise; तं अग्निं (*taṃ agniṃ*)—Agni, who has the qualities described above; ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection; आ चक्रुः (*ā cakruḥ*)—they make (him) turn towards themselves.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The ṛtvik priests, who have fallen into the trouble caused by demons and the like and who possess the worshipful oblation, by praise of this kind make Agni, who has the qualities described above, turn towards themselves for protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The exorcisers (of the demons), lifting up their ladles, and offering sacrifice, have called upon Agni by this ceremony for their protection,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*)—रक्षोघ्नमंत्रोच्चारणेन तद्विषयबाधासहवर्तंते (*rakṣoghnamaṃtroccāraṇena tadviṣayabādhāsahavartaṃte*) । The priests, when they recite mantras in the sacrifices to remove the obstacles that demons cause, are described as those who at that time are accompanied by the obstructions that may be expected; and यज्ञवंतः (*yajñavaṃtaḥ*)—taking the word yajña to mean oblations fit to be offered in the sacrifice, they are described as those who have prepared oblations of that kind; and यतस्रुचः (*yatasrucaḥ*)—as those who hold the vessels for the homa made ready to offer the oblations in the fire, addressed to the gods. Having so described the priests, इत्था धिया तं अग्निं ऊतये आचक्रुः (*itthā dhiyā taṃ agniṃ ūtaye ācakruḥ*)—अनेन प्रकारेण क्रियमाणया स्तुत्या एवंभूतमग्निं राक्षसबाधात् रक्षणाय अभिमुखं कुर्वंति (*anena prakāreṇa kriyamāṇayā stutyā evaṃbhūtamagniṃ rākṣasabādhāt rakṣaṇāya abhimukhaṃ kurvaṃti*) । The meaning has been explained thus: by the praises recited in the various ways, in order to obtain from Agni protection in the form of the removal of the obstruction of the demons, they turn Agni towards themselves and serve him.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, printed page 544. सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*): the root बाध्य विलोडने (*bādhya viloḍane*); by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) the affix kvip to it. The accent of the nature of the kṛt-ending last member comes. The form is nominative plural. यतस्रुचः (*yatasrucaḥ*): यताः स्रुचः यैस्ते (*yatāḥ srucaḥ yaiste*); by बहुव्रीहौ (*bahuvrīhau*) the accent of the nature of the first member comes. इत्था (*itthā*): the word idam; when the sense of manner is shown, by इदमस्थमः (*idamasthamaḥ*) (Pā.Sū. 5-3-24) the affix तथमु (*tathamu*) . By सुपांसुलुक् (*supāṃsuluk*) the word gets the substitute ḍā; ṭi is elided. By अनुदात्तस्ययत्रोदात्तलोपः (*anudāttasyayatrodāttalopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-161) the ā becomes udātta. धिया (*dhiyā*): by सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-18) the udātta accent comes to the case ending.)*

### Printed p. 545

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, continued, printed page 545. चक्रुः (*cakruḥ*): डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*) is the root. For the liṭ third person plural the substitute us; taking that as the cause, the substitute yaṇ. Because by द्विर्वचनेचि (*dvirvacaneci*) (Pā. Sū. 1-1-59) the sthānivadbhāva comes, the single vowel of the root is doubled, with liṭ as the cause. By कुहोश्चुः (*kuhoścuḥ*) the abhyāsa gets cutva. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the immortal, shining hotṛ, impelling the rites, comes to us at the very beginning of the rite, endowed with knowledge of the rite; grammar of māyayā and vidathāni follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होता (*hotā*)—the accomplisher of the homa
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—free from the nature of death
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—shining, the Agni who is so
- विदथानि (*vidathāni*)—the actions fit for sacrifice
- प्रचोदयन् (*pracodayan*)—impelling
- मायया (*māyayā*)—joined with knowledge concerning the action
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—at the very time of the beginning of the action [the supplied text has an exclamation mark here]
- एति (*eti*)—comes towards us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the accomplisher of the homa, free from the nature of death, and shining, impelling the actions fit for sacrifice, joined with knowledge concerning the action, comes towards us at the very time of the beginning of the action.

*[A stray line "69" follows in the supplied text, a number that is not part of the text; kept as a note.]*

### Printed p. 546

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The offerer of the oblation, the divine, immortal Agni, comes first (at the ceremony) directing solemnities by his experience.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मायया (*māyayā*)—मिमाते जानीते कर्म, मीयते अनयेति वा माया कर्मविषयज्ञानं (*mimāte jānīte karma, mīyate anayeti vā māyā karmaviṣayajñānaṃ*) । The meaning of the word māyā is explained thus: that which is known in a limited state, or that which is the means of knowing a limited state, is māyā; and कर्मविषयाभिज्ञानेन युक्तः (*karmaviṣayābhijñānena yuktaḥ*)—Agni is one joined with māyā in the form of the scholarship fit for knowing the nature of actions (concerning action); thus it has been explained.

Agni, who is the hotṛ performing the homa, who is without the nature of death, a god shining with radiance, who impels the sacrificers to perform the sacrificial rites, and who has full scholarship in the performance of the several sacrificial rites, comes in visible form before the sacrificers at the time of the beginning of the performance of the several sacrificial rites; this is the meaning that has been explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 7, printed page 546. पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*): when the affix astāti comes to the word pūrva, by पूर्वावराधराणा (*pūrvāvarādharāṇā*) (Prā. Sū. 5-3-39) [so printed, "Prā." for the usual "Pā."] the ādyudātta accent of the affix, परादेशप्रत्ययद (*parādeśapratyayada*) , comes. एति (*eti*): the root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) , adādi. Laṭ, third person singular. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes. मायया (*māyayā*): माज् माने शब्दे च (*māj māne śabde ca*) is the root. By माच्छाससि सूभ्योयः (*mācchāsasi sūbhyoyaḥ*) (U. Sū. 4-549) the affix ya, either in the active or the passive. In the feminine ṭāp. मिमाते जानीते-कर्म मीयते अनया इति वा माया कर्मविषयज्ञानं (*mimāte jānīte-karma mīyate anayā iti vā māyā karmaviṣayajñānaṃ*). By the accent of the affix it becomes antodātta. The form is instrumental singular [the printed word for "singular" is misspelled]. विदथानि (*vidathāni*): विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*) is the root. By रुदिविदिभ्यांकित् (*rudividibhyāṃkit*) (U. Sū. 3-395) the affix atha in the passive. Because kitva is extended, guṇa does not come. The ādyudātta accent of the affix comes. प्रचोदयन् (*pracodayan*): चुद प्रेरणे (*cuda preraṇe*) is the root. When laṭ comes after the ṇijanta, the substitute śatṛ for it. Because of śap, guṇa and the substitute aya for ṇic. Because of ṇic, guṇa for the light penultimate of the root. Since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the accent of ṇic remains.)*

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वा॒जी वाजे॑षु धीयतेऽध्व॒रेषु॒ प्र णे॑यते ।  
> विप्रो॑ य॒ज्ञस्य॒ साध॑नः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वाजी । वाजेषु । धीयते । अध्वरेषु । प्र । नीयते ।  
> विप्रः । यज्ञस्य । साधनः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाजी बलवानग्निर्वाजेषु युद्धेषु धीयते । देवैः शत्रुहननार्थं निधी-
> यते । किंच । अध्वरेष्टग्नि होत्रादिषु प्रणीयते । अध्वर्यादिभिः प्रकर्षणाहव-
> नीयादिस्थानेषु, प्रक्षिप्यते । आत एव विप्रो मेधावी सन्नग्निर्यज्ञस्याग्नि होत्रादेः
> साधनः साधको भवति ॥ धीयते । दधातेः कर्मणि यक् । घुमास्थागापेत्यादिना
> ईत्वं । निघातः । नीयते । णीञ् प्रापण इत्यस्य कर्मणि यकि रूपं । उपसर्गादस-
> मासेऽपि णोपदेशस्यॆति णत्वं । साधनः । साध संसिद्धौ । नंद्यादित्वात्कर्तरि ल्युः ।
> लित्स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Strong Agni is set in front by the gods in battles and installed by the priests in the Āhavanīya and other places; so, being wise, he accomplishes the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजी (*vājī*)—the mighty Agni
- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—in battles
- धीयते (*dhīyate*)—(for the killing of foes, by the gods) is placed at the front
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—in sacrifices
- प्रणीयते (*praṇīyate*)—(by the ṛtvik priests) is set in the places such as the Āhavanīya (and therefore)
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise Agni
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of sacrifices such as the Agnihotra
- साधनः (*sādhanaḥ*)—becomes the accomplisher

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The mighty Agni is placed at the front by the gods in battles for the killing of foes. He is set by the ṛtvik priests, at the time of the sacrifice, in the places such as the Āhavanīya. Therefore the wise Agni becomes the accomplisher of sacrifices such as the Agnihotra.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The mighty Agni is placed (foremost by the gods) in battle ; he is brought forward reverently at holy rites ; for he is the sage fulfiller of the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 548

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वाजी (*vājī*)—बलवान् (*balavān*) । The word vājī is read among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27). Here it is used in the sense of one who has strength, that is, Agni.

वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—युद्धेषु (*yuddheṣu*) । The word vāja is stated by the Nirukta authors to have the senses of food and battle. Used here in the sense of battle, the meaning is explained by Sāyaṇa thus: Agni, who has strength, is impelled by the gods in battles to subdue the enemies.

अध्वरेषु प्रणीयते (*adhvareṣu praṇīyate*)—Although the word adhvara is read by the Nirukta authors among the names of the sacrifice, here Sāyaṇa uses it in the sense of the rite in which Agni is worshipped, and explains the meaning thus: in the Agnihotras the priests, adhvaryu and the others, install Agni in the divisions marked off in the sacrificial hall, such as the one called Āhavanīya .

विप्रः यज्ञस्य साधनः (*vipraḥ yajñasya sādhanaḥ*)—Since the word vipra is stated among the names of the wise, the meaning is described thus: Agni is wise, and he accomplishes the sacrificial rites for the sacrificers.

*[In the supplied text the word for "Agni" is spelled with a different first vowel in the second explanation above; as supplied.]*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 8, printed page 548. धीयते (*dhīyate*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). Laṭ in the passive. The affix ta in the third person singular. The ṭi gets etva. By सार्वधातुके यक् (*sārvadhātuke yak*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-67) the affix yak. By घुमास्थागा (*ghumāsthāgā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66) [the sūtra is printed in this broken form], since a kit affix follows, ī-substitution for the ā of the root. Because it stands after a word that is "atijanta" , the nighāta accent comes. नीयते (*nīyate*): णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*) is the root. By णोनः (*ṇonaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-65) natva at the beginning. Laṭ in the passive. The form is accomplished as before. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes. Because it stands after the upasarga pra, by उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि णोपदेशस्य (*upasargādasamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya*) (Pā. Sū. 8-4-14) ṇatva for the n of the root. साधनः (*sādhanaḥ*): साध संसिद्धौ (*sādha saṃsiddhau*) is the root. Because it is read in the nandyādi group, by नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यः (*naṃdigrahapacādibhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134) [the printed sūtra has a hyphen at the line end] the affix lyu in the active. By युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the substitute ana for it. Because the affix is lit, by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent comes to the preceding part.)*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धिया । चक्रे । वरेण्यः । भूतानां । गर्भं । आ । दधे ।  
> दक्षस्य । पितरं । तना ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निर्धियाधानपवमानेष्टिरूपेण कर्मणा चक्र आहवनीयरूपतया कृ
> तोऽभूत् अत एव वरेण्यः सर्वैर्यजमानैः कर्मांगत्वेन वरणेयः यश्चाग्निर्भू-
> तानां स्थावरजंगमात्मकानां भूतजातानामंतर्गर्भं स्वात्मानमेव गर्भरूपतया
> आदधे सर्वत्र दधार पितरं सर्वस्य जगतः पालकं तमिममग्निं दक्षस्य दक्षप्रजापते-
> स्तना तनया वेदिरूपा भूमिर्दर्शपूर्णमासाग्निहोत्रादिकर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं धार
> यति । भूमेर्दक्षदुहितृत्वे मंत्रवर्णः । अदितिर्ह्यजनिष्ट दक्ष या दुहिता तव ।
> ऋग्वे १०-७२-५ ॥ इति ॥ चक्रे । करोतेः कर्मणि लिटि रूपं । गर्भं । गृ निगरण इत्य
> स्मादर्तिग्यभ्यां भन्निति भन् । गिरति गीर्यते वा गर्भः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । दधे ।
> दधातेर्लिटि रूपं । पितरं । पा रक्षणे । नप्तनेष्ट इत्यादिना तृजंतत्वेन निपातना-
> दित्वं । पाति पालयतीति पिता पालकः । चित्वरः । तना । यलोपच्छांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, made the Āhavanīya by the rite and chosen by all, is the embryo in all beings; the Earth, Dakṣa's daughter, holds him for the rites.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni)
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by the rite that is a part of the sacrifice
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—has been made in the form of the Āhavanīya and the like
- वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—Agni, chosen (desired) by all
- भूतानां (*bhūtānāṃ*)—for all beings
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—(himself) in the form of an embryo; आ दधे (*ā dadhe*)—bore
- पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—Agni, the guardian of the whole world
- दक्षस्य (*dakṣasya*)—of Dakṣa Prajāpati
- तना (*tanā*)—the Earth, the daughter (held him in herself for the accomplishment of the rite)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni has been made, by the rite that is a part of the sacrifice, in the form of the Āhavanīya and the like; Agni, desired by all, has become the embryo of all beings; the Earth, the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati, holds in herself Agni, the guardian of the whole world.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
He who has been made by the sacred rite, the choice (of the worshipper) who comprehends (within himself) the germ of all creatures, and whom the daughter of Daksha (receives) as the parent of the world.

### Printed p. 550

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धिया (*dhiyā*)—The word dhī is stated by the Nirukta authors in the sense of wisdom or rite; therefore Sāyaṇa has explained that Agni is established by the sacrificers, under the name Āhavanīya, on the altar of the sacrificial hall, for performing rites such as the Ādhāna and the Pavamāna-iṣṭi.

वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—Sāyaṇa describes that Agni is chosen by the sacrificers as an accessory in the sacrificial rites; that, being present in a transformed form in the middle part of the bodies of beings, moving and unmoving, he sustains those beings; and that Agni, who in this way sustains everything and is therefore the protector of all like a father, is held by the Earth, the daughter of the Prajāpati named Dakṣa, in the form of the altar, the dwelling of Agni in the sacrifice, for the accomplishment of the rites of the forms Darśa, Pūrṇamāsa and Agnihotra. And he has cited the Vedic sentence that teaches that the daughter of Dakṣa-Brahman is the Earth: अदितिर्हजनिष्ट दक्ष या दुहिता तव (*aditirhajaniṣṭa dakṣa yā duhitā tava*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-5). [The spelling of this quotation as supplied here differs from the one in the bhāṣya block quoted under Ṛk 9; as supplied.]

The Nirukta authors read the word dakṣa among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9); at दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि व्रते (*dakṣasya vādite janmani vrate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-5-6) [the reference is so printed] they explain the word dakṣa in the sense of Āditya, and say आदित्यो दक्ष इत्याहुः (*ādityo dakṣa ityāhuḥ*). Then they cite this mantra:

भूर्जज्ञ उत्तानपदो भुव आशा अजायंत ॥ (*bhūrjajña uttānapado bhuva āśā ajāyaṃta ‖*) अदितेर्दक्षो अजायत दक्षाद्वदितिः सरि । (*aditerdakṣo ajāyata dakṣādvaditiḥ sari |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-22-4)

and describe the contradiction that is seen about the birth of Dakṣa and Aditi, and its resolution.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 9, printed page 550. चक्रे (*cakre*): the root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*). In the passive, the Lit form, third person singular. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes. गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*): the root ग्य निगरणे (*gya nigaraṇe*) . By अर्तिग्यभ्यांभन् (*artigyabhyāṃbhan*) (U. Sū. 4-432) the affix bhan. By सार्वधातुकार्थधातु (*sārvadhātukārthadhātu*) [the sūtra is printed in this abbreviated form, with a dash] guṇa comes to the ṛ-vowel, followed by r. गिरति, गीर्यते वा गर्भः (*girati, gīryate vā garbhaḥ*): since the affix is nit, by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the ādyudātta accent comes [the word for ādyudātta is spelled irregularly in the supplied text]. दधे (*dadhe*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). The Lit form, third person singular; the nighāta accent of a finite verb comes. पितरं (*pitaraṃ*): the root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*). By नप्तृनेष्टृ (*naptṛneṣṭṛ*) (U. Sū. 2-252) [the sūtra is printed in this abbreviated form, with a dash], since it is enjoined by nipāta as ending in the affix tṛc, itva comes. पाति पालयतीति वा पिता पालकः (*pāti pālayatīti vā pitā pālakaḥ*); by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the antodātta accent comes. तना (*tanā*): when the form is तनया (*tanayā*), the elision of the letter ya comes, by Chandas.)*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि त्वा॑ दधे॒ वरे॑ण्यं॒ दक्ष॑स्ये॒ळा स॑हस्कृत ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । त्वा । दधे । वरेण्यं । दक्षस्य । इळा । सहःकृत ।

> कर्मार्थिभिः काम्यमानं । आत एव वरेण्यं तैर्वर्णीयं त्वा एवंविधं त्वां दक्षस्य
> दुहितेळा वेद्यादिलक्षणा भूमिर्नि दधे । अग्निहोत्रादिकर्मसमृध्यर्थं नितरां

> घप्रत्यः । ह्रस्वश्चांदसः । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वादगुणः । ईड्यंते स्तूयं-
> तेऽस्यां यजमानैर्देवा इतीळा भूमिः । उदात्तनिवृत्ति स्वरेणांतोदात्तः । प्रत्य-
> यस्वरः । उशिजं । वश कांतावित्यस्माद्वशः किच्चेतीजिप्रत्ययः । कित्वात्संप्रसारणं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, born of churning-strength and desired for oblations, is held firmly by Ilā, Dakṣa's daughter, the Earth as altar, for the rites.

*[In the bhāṣya block the supplied text has the form आग्ने (*āgne*) for the vocative of Agni; as supplied.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहस्कृत (*sahaskṛta*)—born of the power in the form of churning
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- सुदीतिं (*sudītiṃ*)—endowed with excellent radiance
- उशिजं (*uśijaṃ*)—desiring the oblation, or desired by the sacrificers
- वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*)—dear to all
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- दक्षस्य (*dakṣasya*)—of Dakṣa Prajāpati, the daughter
- इळा (*iḷā*)—the Earth in the form of the altar; नि दधे (*ni dadhe*)—has sustained for the sake of the rite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, born of the power in the form of churning, endowed with excellent radiance, desiring the oblation and desired by all: you, the Earth in the form of the altar, the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati, has sustained for the sake of the rite.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, strength-engendered, Ila (the daughter) of Daksha has sustained you, the desirable, the resplendent, and longing (for the oblation).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सहस्कृत (*sahaskṛta*)—सहः (*sahaḥ*) is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). Since Agni is produced by the application of strength when the ṛtvik priests churn him in the fire-sticks, he is addressed by this word as one born of strength.

उशिजं (*uśijaṃ*)—उशिक् वष्टेः कांतिकर्मणः (*uśik vaṣṭeḥ kāṃtikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 6-61): so it is explained by the Nirukta authors. Sāyaṇa has given this word two kinds of meaning: पुरोडाशादिहविः काम्यमानं (*puroḍāśādihaviḥ kāmyamānaṃ*), that Agni desires oblations such as the puroḍāśa; or यद्वा कर्मार्थिभिः काम्यमानं (*yadvā karmārthibhiḥ kāmyamānaṃ*), that Agni is desired by those who wish to perform sacrificial rites such as the sacrifice.

दक्षस्य दुहिता इळा निदधे (*dakṣasya duhitā iḷā nidadhe*)—The meaning is explained thus: the Earth, the daughter of Dakṣa-Brahman, holds Agni, who shines with auspicious radiance and is chosen by the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, in the form of the sacrificial altar, in order to perform in great measure the sacrificial rites beginning with the Agnihotra.

इळा (*iḷā*)—This word is stated among the names of the Earth (Ni. 2-5), among the वाज्ञाम (*vājñāma*) names (Ni. 2-23), among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of the cow (Ni. 3-9), and it is explained as ईट्वेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (*īṭveḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 11-50). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as वेद्यादिलक्षणा भूमिः (*vedyādilakṣaṇā bhūmiḥ*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 10, printed page 552. इळा (*iḷā*): the root ईड स्तुतौ (*īḍa stutau*) . In पुंसि संज्ञायां घःप्रायेण (*puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥprāyeṇa*) (Pā. ##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वनुषः विप्राः (*vanuṣaḥ viprāḥ*)—The wise ṛtvik priests, who desire Agni for the success of the sacrificial rites, cause Agni, who moves swiftly, or who is the regulator of all, and who sends the waters, to be kindled with foods in the form of oblations, in order to perform sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma; so the meaning is described.

यंतुरं (*yaṃturaṃ*)—यंतारः (*yaṃtāraḥ*) is stated in the याज्ञाकर्मगळल्लि (*yājñākarmagaḷalli*) (Ni. 3-19). Sāyaṇa indicates the formation of the word as वर्णव्यत्ययः यंतारं (*varṇavyatyayaḥ yaṃtāraṃ*) and explains the meaning: that Agni is the regulator of all, and that this word, derived from the root या (*yā*) in the sense of reaching, is used in the sense of one who goes swiftly.

ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—Since the word ऋत (*ṛta*) is used in the senses of truth or sacrifice, here it is used in the sense of sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma.

वाजैः (*vājaiḥ*)—Since the word वाज (*vāja*) has many meanings, the meaning is stated here as food in the form of oblation.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 11, printed page 554. यंतुरं (*yaṃturaṃ*): the root या प्रापणे (*yā prāpaṇe*), the affix tṛc in the sense of the agent. By Chandas a letter-exchange comes. By चितः (*citaḥ*) the antodātta accent comes. अप्तुरं (*apturaṃ*): the root तुर त्वर्णे (*tura tvarṇe*), of the जुहोत्यादि (*juhotyādi*) class. By अपः तुतोर्ति त्वरयति इति अप्तुः क्विप् च (*apaḥ tutorti tvarayati iti aptuḥ kvip ca*) the affix kvip. The कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*) accent comes. The form ending in the second-case singular (द्वितीयाविकवचनांतरूप (*dvitīyāvikavacanāṃtarūpa*) [the word for 'singular' is so printed]). योगे (*yoge*): युजिर् योगे (*yujir yoge*) is the root. In the sense of the action, the affix ghañ. Since the letter gha is it, by चजोः कु घिण्यतोः (*cajoḥ ku ghiṇyatoḥ*) the j of the root is replaced by g through kutva. By इत्यादिनिर्नित्यं (*ityādinirnityaṃ*) the ādyudātta accent comes. वनुषः (*vanuṣaḥ*): वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*) is the root. Because the word bahula is taken in the उणादि (*uṇādi*) [so spelled in the supplied text], by its force the affix usi enjoined by जनेरुसिः (*janerusiḥ*) (U. Sū. 2-272) comes to this word also. By the accent of the affix the vowel u becomes udātta. The form ending in the nominative plural. इंधते (*iṃdhate*): इंधी दीप्तौ (*iṃdhī dīptau*) is the root. The Lat form, third person plural. Because it stands after अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*) , the nighāta accent comes.)*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऊर्जोनपातं (*ūrjonapātaṃ*)—Sāyaṇa explains that here the word नपात् (*napāt*) is used in the sense of नप्तृ (*naptṛ*), and he describes that Agni is हविर्लक्षणैरन्नॆः समिध्यमानत्वेन अन्नस्य पुत्रं (*havirlakṣaṇairannèḥ samidhyamānatvena annasya putraṃ*): since Agni grows by the foods in the form of oblation, Agni is the son of food; this is one kind of meaning. The other meaning he describes by यद्वा यश्चान्नादाहुतिराहुतेरादित्य आदित्यादग्निरिति (*yadvā yaścānnādāhutirāhuterāditya ādityādagniriti*) [the supplied text reads so here, while the bhāṣya block has a different wording at its start; as supplied]: from food comes the oblation, from the oblation Āditya, and from Āditya Agni. Since Agni is the fourth from food, he explains अन्नस्य चतुर्थं (*annasya caturthaṃ*): as in a lineage the fourth from the original ancestor is the naptṛ, so Agni is the fourth from food.

कविक्रतुं (*kavikratuṃ*)—The word कवि (*kavi*) is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). The meaning of the word is explained as the wise. The meaning that Agni is produced by the wise ṛtvik priests, beginning with the adhvaryu, and therefore is kavikratu, is described by the explanation मेधाविनो अध्वर्यादयः मथनेन कर्तारो यस्य । अध्वर्यादिभिः निष्पाद्यमानं (*medhāvino adhvaryādayaḥ mathanena kartāro yasya | adhvaryādibhiḥ niṣpādyamānaṃ*).

उप द्यवि दीदिवांसं (*upa dyavi dīdivāṃsaṃ*)—The meaning is stated by अंतरिक्षसमीपे अतिशयेन दीप्यमानं (*aṃtarikṣasamīpe atiśayena dīpyamānaṃ*): Agni shines with abundant radiance near the sky.

It is explained that the seer of the mantra, the sage Viśvāmitra (and the ṛtvik priests such as the adhvaryu), praises in the sacrifice, with words in the form of praise, Agni who is endowed with greatness of this kind.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 12, printed page 556. ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*): the root ऊर्ज बले (*ūrja bale*). By भ्राजभासधुर्वि (*bhrājabhāsadhurvi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-177) [the sūtra is printed in this abbreviated form, with a dash] the affix kvip. ऊर्जयति शरीरमिति ऊर्क्-अन्नं (*ūrjayati śarīramiti ūrk-annaṃ*) (what makes the body grow is food); the form ending in the sixth-case singular. Since the case ending has come after the एकाचिन (*ekācina*) , by सावेकाचस्तृ (*sāvekācastṛ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168) [the sūtra is printed in this abbreviated form, with a dash] the udātta accent comes to it. नपात् (*napāt*): by नभ्राण् नपात् (*nabhrāṇ napāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-75) [the sūtra is printed with a dash] the नलोप (*nalopa*) in the compound does not come, and the form is established by nipāta. The नञ् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वर (*nañ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara*) accent comes. दृवि (*dṛvi*) : द्युत दीप्तौ (*dyuta dīptau*) is the root. To it the Auṇādika affix ḍun. द्योतते किरणसंबंधादिति द्युः (*dyotate kiraṇasaṃbaṃdhāditi dyuḥ*): by the force of ḍit-ness the ṭi (ut) of the root is elided. The form becomes द्यु (*dyu*). That which shines through connection with rays is the sky. By the nit-accent the ādyudātta accent comes. The form ending in the seventh-case singular. ईळे (*īḷe*): ईड स्तुतौ (*īḍa stutau*) is the root. The Lat form, first person singular. कविक्रतुं (*kavikratuṃ*): कवयः क्रतवः यस्य स तं (*kavayaḥ kratavaḥ yasya sa taṃ*). In the bahuvrīhi the accent of the prior member comes.)*

- समिध्यते (*samidhyate*)—is well kindled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is worthy of excellent praise and of worship, who removes darkness and has an attractive form, is kindled as the one who fulfils the desired objects of the sacrificer.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, who is to be worshipped with praise and with prostration, the dispeller of darkness, the beautiful, the showerer (of benefits) is kindled.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ईळेन्यः (*īḷenyaḥ*)—By those who praise, Agni is praised with praises, and नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*) he is worthy of homage by all; तमांसि तिरः (*tamāṃsi tiraḥ*) having destroyed darkness with his own radiances, he is to be seen with a luminous form visible to all; thus Agni's power and nature are stated.

वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—यजमानस्य कामानां वर्षिता (*yajamānasya kāmānāṃ varṣitā*). The author of the Nirukta has explained this word as वृषा वर्षिता (*vṛṣā varṣitā*) (Ni. 11-48). The meaning is set out thus: Sāyaṇa says that Agni, who is praised by hymns, worthy of homage by all, destroys deep darkness with his splendours, and has a form to be seen by all, fulfils the desired objects of the sacrificers according to each one's wish and is kindled by the oblations the sacrificers offer. The Vājasaneya śruti teaching this same view is quoted: ईडेन्यो ह्येष नमस्यो ह्येष तिरस्तमांसि ददृशे समिद्धः (*īḍenyo hyeṣa namasyo hyeṣa tirastamāṃsi dadṛśe samiddhaḥ*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 13, printed page 558. ईळेन्यः (*īḷenyaḥ*): ईड स्तुतौ (*īḍa stutau*) is the root. By कृत्यार्थेतवैकेन् केन्यत्वनः (*kṛtyārthetavaiken kenyatvanaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-14) the affix kenya. By the ādyudātta accent of the affix it becomes madhyodātta. नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*): to the root नमस्य (*namasya*) ending in kyaṅ, by अचोयत् (*acoyat*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-97) the affix yat. By अतोलोपः (*atolopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4.48) the preceding a is elided. By यस्यहलः (*yasyahalaḥ*) the y is elided. Since the affix is kit, by तित्स्वरितं (*titsvaritaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185) the svarita accent comes.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 13, continued. दर्शतः (*darśataḥ*): दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे (*dṛśir prekṣaṇe*) is the root. By भ्रमृदृशि (*bhramṛdṛśi*) (U. Sū. 3-390) the affix atac comes to it in the karman. By पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) guṇa comes to the light penultimate of the root. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the antodātta accent comes. वृषा (*vṛṣā*): वृषु सेचने (*vṛṣu secane*) is the root. By कनिन्‌युवृषि (*kaninyuvṛṣi*) (U. Because of nit-ness the ādyudātta accent comes.)*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, who rains down desires and carries oblations to the gods as a horse carries a king, is kindled; the sacrificers who hold oblations praise him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषो (*vṛṣo*)—the one who fulfils desired objects; अश्वो न (*aśvo na*)—as a horse bears a king
- देववाहः (*devavāhaḥ*) [so printed; the Saṃhitā block has the word ending in the other form]—the one who bears the oblation to the gods
- अग्नि (*agni*) [the visarga is printed as a colon]—Agni
- समिध्यते (*samidhyate*)—is kindled
- तं (*taṃ*)—that worshipful Agni
- हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*)—the sacrificers who possess oblations
- ईळते (*īḷate*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who fulfils desired objects and who bears the oblation to the gods as a horse bears a king, is kindled. The sacrificers who possess (have prepared) oblations praise that worshipful Agni.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The offerers of oblations glorify that Agni who is the showerer (of benefits) and is the bearer of the offerings to the gods as a horse (bears his rider to his home).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वृषो (*vṛṣo*)-वृषेव कामानां वर्षिता (*vṛṣeva kāmānāṃ varṣitā*). Agni fulfils the wishes of the sacrificers exceedingly, as waters pour down abundantly in rain; this meaning Sāyaṇa, of the word वृषा (*vṛṣā*) … *[the supplied text breaks off here, in the middle of the sentence, at the end of the pages of this window.]*

used together with it, has explained the particle उ (*u*) by assigning to it the sense of 'iva' (like). The author of the Nirukta, in examining and explaining the senses of the particles, says: अथाप्युकार एतस्मिन्नेवार्थ उत्तरेण । मृषेमे वदंति सत्यमुते वंदतीति । अथापि पदपूरण इदमु तदु (*athāpyukāra etasminnevārtha uttareṇa | mṛṣeme vadaṃti satyamute vaṃdatīti | athāpi padapūraṇa idamu tadu*) (Ni. 1-5). That is: the particle उ (*u*) is used in the sense of restraint and also in the sense of filling out a word; having thus set out its use in particular senses, he further says of particles in general: उच्चावचेष्ट्यर्थेषु निपतंति । अप्युपमार्थेपि कर्मोपसंग्रहार्थेपि पदपूरणाः (*uccāvaceṣṭyartheṣu nipataṃti | apyupamārthepi karmopasaṃgrahārthepi padapūraṇāḥ*) (Ni. 1-4). Particles convey many kinds of senses; they convey the sense of comparison and the sense of combining; they are also used in the sense of filling out a word. Thus the use in the general sense is shown as well. Following this, Sāyaṇa here has defended the use in the sense of comparison and described the meaning.

अश्वो न देववाहनः—यथा अश्वो राजानं वाहयति स्वपुरं प्रापयति तद्वत् देवान् हवींषि प्रापयॆति (*aśvo na devavāhanaḥ—yathā aśvo rājānaṃ vāhayati svapuraṃ prāpayati tadvat devān havīṃṣi prāpayèti*). Just as a horse conveys a king to his city, so Agni conveys to the several gods the oblations offered into him for the gods; thus the horse is given as an illustration. Here the particle न (*na*) is described as used in the sense of comparison.

अग्निः समिध्यते—वाहनभूतो अग्निः आज्याहुतिप्रदानेन सम्यक् दीप्यते (*agniḥ samidhyate—vāhanabhūto agniḥ ājyāhutipradānena samyak dīpyate*) *[so in the supplied text; the bhāṣya block has a different word before the word for 'oblation'; as supplied.]* Here the word अग्नि (*agni*) is explained as देववाहन (*devavāhana*), that is, like a horse, देवानां हवींषि वाहयतीति (*devānāṃ havīṃṣi vāhayatīti*): the one who carries the oblations of the gods to them. The meaning is set out that the sacrificers kindle this Agni by offering ghee and other oblations.

हविष्मंत ईळते-संभृतहविष्काः यजमानाः कर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं स्तुवंति (*haviṣmaṃta īḷate-saṃbhṛtahaviṣkāḥ yajamānāḥ karmasiddhyarthaṃ stuvaṃti*) The meaning is set out that the sacrificers, having prepared oblations, praise Agni so that their rites may be accomplished.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 14, printed page 560. वृषो इति (*vṛṣo iti*): when the word is vṛṣa joined with उ (*u*), guṇa comes by आद्गुणः (*ādguṇaḥ*). By उञाः (*uñāḥ*) the उ (*u*) becomes uñ and has the designation pragṛhya (प्रगृहसंज्ञा (*pragṛhasaṃjñā*) in the supplied text); therefore, relying on the uñ in the ओ (*o*) (relying on the treatment of the single substitute as if it were the following or the preceding sound), the designation प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा (*pragṛhyasaṃjñā*) comes at the stage of the pada. Hence there is no scope for the avādeśa and other sandhi operations. देववाहनः (*devavāhanaḥ*): वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*) is the root. By हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*) the affix ṇic. By अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) vṛddhi comes to the penultimate of the root (the supplied word is उपधानकारक्कॆ (*upadhānakārakkè*)). After the ṇyanta the affix lyu in the agent. By णेरनिटि (*ṇeraniṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51) the ṇic is elided. By युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the यु (*yu*) that remains in the affix lyu receives the substitute ana. By लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent comes on the syllable before the affix. When it becomes a compound, by गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*) the accent of the final member's own base comes.)*
