##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressed to Agni, the showerer of desires: the sacrificers, pouring ghee-oblations, kindle him, the blazing and great, who sends rain through the oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—the one who fulfils desired objects
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—who pour streams of ghee-oblations
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—the one who pours down water in the form of rain
- दीद्यतं (*dīdyataṃ*) [the dash is missing in the supplied text]—the shining one
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—the one of abundant greatness, who is such
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- समिधीमहि (*samidhīmahi*)—we cause to blaze up

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who fulfil desired objects, we who offer ghee-oblations cause you to blaze up, you who pour down water in the form of rain, who are shining and of abundant greatness.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Showerer (of benefits) we profusely offering (oblations) kindle you, mighty and resplendent Agni; you are the sender of showers.

वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—by this word Agni is addressed, and the meaning is set out that Agni fulfils the wishes of the sacrificers.

वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—वृषाणः घृताज्याहुतीनां सेक्तारः (*vṛṣāṇaḥ ghṛtājyāhutīnāṃ sektāraḥ*) *[the bhāṣya block has a different first letter in the word for 'ghee'; as supplied]*: the meaning is described as the sacrificers who offer into the fire, for the sake of the gods, oblations such as water and ghee.

वृषणं—आहुतिद्वारा उदकस्य सेक्तारं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ—āhutidvārā udakasya sektāraṃ*): the meaning is set out that Agni causes rain through the oblations offered into him. Having explained so, the author also quotes: अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिस्सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आदित्याज्ञायते वृष्टिः वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः ॥ (*agnau prāstāhutissamyagādityamupatiṣṭhate | ādityājñāyate vṛṣṭiḥ vṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ ‖*) The oblation offered into Agni reaches Aditya; from Aditya comes rain; from rain, as the grains grow, the increase of food; and from the increase of food the creatures are born. The verse of the Manusmṛti teaching this meaning is quoted, and since the identity of Agni and Aditya is thereby stated, it is explained that Agni is the giver of rain.

दीद्यतं बृहत् समधीमहि—दीप्यमानं महांतं अग्निं सम्यक् दीपयामः (*dīdyataṃ bṛhat samadhīmahi—dīpyamānaṃ mahāṃtaṃ agniṃ samyak dīpayāmaḥ*) *[the word before 'we kindle' is spelled differently from the Saṃhitā; as supplied]*: the wish is described that we, the sacrificers, make blaze up by offering oblations Agni who gives rain, accomplishes the desires of the sacrificers, shines with his radiances and has abundant greatness.

Because it stands after a word ending in a finite verb-form [as supplied: अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*)], the nighāta accent comes. दीद्यतं (*dīdyataṃ*): this is a root read in the sense of shining. ## Sūkta 28 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-eighth sūkta** (इप्पत्तॆंटनॆय सूक्तवु (*ippattèṃṭanèya sūktavu*))

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने जुषस्वेति षडृचं षोडशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रमाग्नेयं । अत्रानुक्रम-
> णिका । अग्ने जुषस्व षट् तृतीयाद्युष्टिक् त्रिष्टुब्बगत्य इति । पूर्वसूक्ते गायत्रं
> त्वित्युक्तत्वादेतवपि गायत्रं । तृतीया तूष्टिक् चतुर्थी त्रिष्टुप् पंचमी जगती ॥
> अग्ने जुषस्वेति सवनीयपुरोडाशे स्विष्टकृतः प्रातःसवनीयानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> अथ स्विष्टकृतोऽग्ने जुषस्व नो हविः । आ ५-४ । इति ॥ अतिरात्र आश्विनशस्त्रे परिहिते
> सति चमसगणैः सहाश्विनोर्द्विकपालः पुरोडाशः सर्वहुतो होतव्यः । यदि पुरो
> डाशमवशेष्य स्विष्टकृतं कुर्युस्तस्य स्विष्टकृतः पुरोळा अग्न इत्येषा याज्या । य-
> द्येतस्य पुरोडाशस्य स्विष्टकृता चरेयुः पुरोळा अग्ने पचितः । आ. ६-५ । इति सू-
> त्रितं ॥ माध्यंदिने सवने सवनीयपुरोडाशे स्विष्टकृतोऽनुवाक्या माध्यंदिने
> सवन इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविर्माध्यंदिने सवने जातवेदः
> आ. ५-४ । इति ॥ तृतीयसवने सवनीयपुरोडाशस्य स्विष्टकृतोऽनुवाक्याग्ने तृती-
> ये सवन इत्येषा। सूत्रितं च।अग्ने तृतीये सवने हि कानिष इत्यनुसवनमनुवाक्या।
> आ. ५-४ । इति ॥ आश्विनपुरोडाशस्य स्विष्टकृतो याज्याग्ने वृधान इत्येषा । सूत्रितं
> च । अग्ने वृधान आहुतिमिति संयाज्ये । आ. ६-५ इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning with अग्ने जुषस्व (*agne juṣasva*) is the sixteenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are six Ṛks in it. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta; Agni is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अग्ने जुषस्व षट् तृतीयाद्युष्टिक्‌त्रिष्टुब्बगत्यः (*agne juṣasva ṣaṭ tṛtīyādyuṣṭiktriṣṭubbagatyaḥ*). Since in the matter of the preceding sūkta it is said in the Anukramaṇikā गायत्रं तु (*gāyatraṃ tu*), this sūkta also is in the Gāyatrī metre. But the third Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Uṣṇik metre, the fourth in the Triṣṭubh metre, and the fifth in the Jagatī metre.

That the first Ṛk of this sūkta beginning with अग्ने जुषस्व (*agne juṣasva*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the morning pressing in the sviṣṭakṛd-rite (printed स्विष्टकृद्योमदल्लि (*sviṣṭakṛdyomadalli*), here and below, as supplied) of the savanīya-purodāśa is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (the name is printed here आश्वलायनशौतसूत्र (*āśvalāyanaśautasūtra*), without the letter r; as supplied) अथ स्विष्टकृतोऽग्ने जुषस्व नो हविः (*atha sviṣṭakṛto 'gne juṣasva no haviḥ*) (Ā. 5-4).

It is set out as follows: in the sacrifice called Atirātra, after the Āśvina-śastra mantras have been recited, a purodāśa cooked on two potsherds is to be offered whole, with the camasas, with the Aśvin deities in view. Having offered it, the remaining purodāśa is to be used for the sviṣṭakṛd-rite.

In that rite the Ṛk beginning पुरोळा अग्ने (*puroḷā agne*) (the second Ṛk of this sūkta) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra यद्येतस्य पुरोडाशस्य स्विष्टकृता चरेयुः पुरोळा अग्ने पचतः (*yadyetasya puroḍāśasya sviṣṭakṛtā careyuḥ puroḷā agne pacataḥ*) (Ā. 5-5) *[the bhāṣya block gives the end of this sūtra as पुरोळा अग्ने पचितः (*puroḷā agne pacitaḥ*) and the reference as Ā. 6-5; the Anuvāda gives the last word differently and the reference as Ā. 5-5; both as supplied]*.

In the Mādhyandina-savana also, in the sviṣṭakṛd-rite of the savanīya-purodāśa, the Ṛk beginning माध्यंदिने सवने (*mādhyaṃdine savane*) (the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविर्माध्यंदिने (*agne juṣasva no havirmādhyaṃdine*)

### Printed p. 564

*(Anuvāda, continued.)* सवने जातवेदः (*savane jātavedaḥ*) (Ā. 5-4). In the third pressing also, in the sviṣṭakṛd-rite of the savanīya-purodāśa, this Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (the name is printed here with the letter r) आग्ने तृतीयसवने हि कानिष इत्यनुसवनमनुवाक्याः (*āgne tṛtīyasavane hi kāniṣa ityanusavanamanuvākyāḥ*) (Ā. 5-4) *[the Anuvāda gives the first word with the long vowel and the last word in the plural, differently from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]*. And in the sviṣṭakṛd-rite of the purodāśa-offering made with the Aśvin deities in view, the Ṛk अग्ने वृधानः (*agne vṛdhānaḥ*) (the sixth Ṛk of this sūkta) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra आग्ने वृधान आहुतिमिति संयाज्ये (*āgne vṛdhāna āhutimiti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 6-5) *[the closing bracket of the reference is missing in the supplied text; as supplied]*.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta (the word is printed सूकदल्लिरुव (*sūkadalliruva*); as supplied): 6. Seer: विश्वामित्रः (*viśvāmitraḥ*). Devatā: अग्निः (*agniḥ*). Chandas: Ṛks 1, 2 and 6, गायत्रि (*gāyatri*); Ṛk 3, उष्णिक् (*uṣṇik*); Ṛk 4, त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*); Ṛk 5 (a full stop follows the number in the print), जगती (*jagatī*). *[The metre of the third Ṛk is spelled with ṣṭ in the Anukramaṇikā line of the bhāṣya block (तृतीयाद्युष्टिक् (*tṛtīyādyuṣṭik*)) and with ṣṇ in the Anuvāda and in the data; as supplied.]*

> प्रा॒तः॒सा॒वे धि॑यावसो ॥ १ ॥

> *agne juṣasva no haviḥ puroḷāśaṃ jātavedaḥ |*  
> *prātaḥsāve dhiyāvaso ‖ 1 ‖*

*[In the supplied text a garbled line stood between the Saṃhitā and the Pada blocks, in place of the Pada label: हडसात्कॆ (*haḍasātkè*); it is kept as a line of its own, the standard Pada label is inserted and the block is split; as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वामित्रः स्तौति । जातवेदः जातप्रज्ञ धियावसो । धिया स्तोत्रेण वसु
> धनं यस्माद्भवति सोऽयं धियावसुः । तस्य संबुद्धिः । कर्मानुरूपधनप्रद हे

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भावे घञ् । थाथघञ् क्ताजबित्रकाणामित्यंतोदात्तत्वं । धियावसो । विभक्त्य-
> लोपश्चांदसः । आमंत्रितत्वान्निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises Agni, the knower of all who is born with wisdom and gives wealth in return for praise and rites, and asks him to partake of our purodāśa oblation at the morning pressing; grammatical tail transcribed only.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—the one who knows everything as soon as it is born
- धियावसो (*dhiyāvaso*)—who gives the fruit suited to the rite
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- प्रातःसावे (*prātaḥsāve*)—in the morning pressing, which is in the form of the Agniṣṭoma
- नः (*naḥ*)—given by us
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—in the form of the purodāśa
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—partake of it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who are born with wisdom and give the fruit suited to the rite, accept and partake of the purodāśa given by us at the morning pressing, which is in the form of the Agniṣṭoma.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, by whom all is known, you reward pious acts with wealth; accept our cakes offered with butter at the morning worship.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धियावसो—धिया स्तोत्रेण वसु धनं यस्मात् भवति सोऽयं धियावसुः (*dhiyāvaso—dhiyā stotreṇa vasu dhanaṃ yasmāt bhavati so 'yaṃ dhiyāvasuḥ*): the meaning is set out that by praise Agni grants wealth to each according to his rite, and Agni is addressed by this word. The authors of the Nirukta, on the verse पावका न स्सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः ॥ (*pāvakā na ssarasvatī vājebhirvājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-10) have described the word धियावसु (*dhiyāvasu*) in this Ṛk as meaning कर्मवसुः (*karmavasuḥ*). Durgācārya has given the meaning कर्मधन (*karmadhana*). Sāyaṇa, because the word धी (*dhī*) is used in both senses, rite or wisdom, has explained it as a praise in the form of wisdom, and has described Agni's greatness as the giver of wealth suited to the rite.

जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)— *[the word जातवेदश्यब्दक्कॆ (*jātavedaśyabdakkè*) is printed with ś and y; as supplied]*: since four kinds of meaning of the word have been set out by the authors of the Nirukta, Sāyaṇa here has explained the meaning 'of born wisdom', and the wish is described that this Agni, addressed by this word, प्रातःस्सावे नः पुरोडाशं हविः जुषस्व (*prātaḥssāve naḥ puroḍāśaṃ haviḥ juṣasva*) *[so printed, with a doubled s; the Saṃhitā has प्रातःसावे (*prātaḥsāve*)]*, accept the oblation called purodāśa which the sacrificers offer at the time of the morning pressing in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. *[A dash follows the last word in the print; as supplied.]*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 565. जुषस्व (*juṣasva*): जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*) is the root. The form is of the imperative (लोट्‌मध्यमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूप (*loṭmadhyamapuruṣaekavacanāṃtarūpa*)), second person singular. Although the word अग्ने (*agne*), having the designation āmantrita, stands before it, that word has the status of one not present (अविद्यमानवद्भाव (*avidyamānavadbhāva*)), and therefore पादादि (*pādādi*) …)* *[the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window, in the middle of a word, without a hyphen.]*

### Printed p. 566

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, continued.)* The word begun at the foot of the preceding page is completed by the ending meaning "in", and the sentence goes on: it comes as if in it; therefore the nighāta accent does not come. By the rule तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. 6-1-186) the lasārvadhātuka ending becomes anudātta, so the accent of the vikaraṇa śa remains.

प्रातःसावे (*prātaḥsāve*): the root is षूञ् अभिषवे (*ṣūñ abhiṣave*) and सवनं सवः (*savanaṃ savaḥ*); the affix ghañ is used in the sense of the state or action. By अचोञ्णति (*acoñṇati*) the u of the root takes vṛddhi, then the avādeśa. By थाथञ् क्ताजबित्रकाणां (*thāthañ ktājabitrakāṇāṃ*) (Pā. 6-2-144) the final-acute accent comes; in the compound the accent of the kṛdutta-pada-prakṛti comes; the form ends with the locative singular.

धियावसो (*dhiyāvaso*): धिया वसु यस्य सः धियावसुः (*dhiyā vasu yasya saḥ dhiyāvasuḥ*); in the Vedic language the instrumental ending is dropped. *[A stray line of the single Kannada word meaning "does not come" follows in the supplied text, with no sentence to which it belongs; as supplied.]* By ह्रस्वस्य गुणः (*hrasvasya guṇaḥ*) guṇa comes in the vocative. By आमंत्रितस्य च (*āmaṃtritasya ca*) (Pā. 8-1-19) the all-anudātta accent comes.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, addressed as the youngest, is asked to partake of the purodāśa which has been cooked on two potsherds and prepared for him by paryagnikaraṇa and the other rites; the rest is grammatical and is transcribed only. The bhāṣya reads ना घ (*nā gha*) where the Saṃhitā has वा घा (*vā ghā*); as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यविष्ठ्य (*yaviṣṭhya*)—very young
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- पुरोळाः (*puroḷāḥ*)—the purodāśa (offered by the adhvaryus)
- पचतः (*pacataḥ*)—cooked
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you; परिष्कृतो वा घु (*pariṣkṛto vā ghu*)—it is indeed adorned with paryagnikaraṇa and the other rites *[the printed ending of this word differs from the Saṃhitā; as supplied]*
- तं (*taṃ*)—that purodāśa
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—partake of it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who are very young, the purodāśa offered by the adhvaryus has been cooked and, adorned by paryagnikaraṇa and the other rites *[printed as परग्नि करणादिगळिंद (*paragni karaṇādigaḷiṃda*), with a letter missing in the word; as supplied]*, is ready to be offered to you; partake of that purodāśa.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The cakes and butter are dressed, Agni, and verily prepared for you; accept them youngest (of the gods).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यविष्ठ्य (*yaviṣṭhya*)—for this word the meaning "the very young, one who is always in youth" is given, and because Agni is always young through the burning of wood and the like, he is addressed by this word. The derivation यविष्ठ एव यविष्ठ्यः (*yaviṣṭha eva yaviṣṭhyaḥ*) is explained.

पुरोळाः (*puroḷāḥ*)—पुरोडाशंत अध्वर्य्या दयः एनं इति पुरोडाः पुरोडाशः (*puroḍāśaṃta adhvaryyā dayaḥ enaṃ iti puroḍāḥ puroḍāśaḥ*): the meaning is explained that the oblation is called purodāśa because the Adhvaryu and the other priests place it in front of Agni and offer it.

पचतः (*pacataḥ*)—पच्यते असाविति पचतः पक्वः (*pacyate asāviti pacataḥ pakvaḥ*): because it is cooked, or कपालयोः पक्वः (*kapālayoḥ pakvaḥ*), because it is cooked in two kapālas (halves of an earthen pot), the purodāśa is described as परिष्कृतः ना घ पर्यग्निकरणादिभिरलंकृतः (*pariṣkṛtaḥ nā gha paryagnikaraṇādibhiralaṃkṛtaḥ*), that is, made ready for Agni by the rites such as paryāgnikaraṇa that must be done in a sacrifice; and by तमिमं जुषस्व (*tamimaṃ juṣasva*) the wish of the sacrificers is described, that Agni may partake of this oblation called purodāśa which the sacrificer offers for him.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed pages 567 and 568.)* पुरोळाः (*puroḷāḥ*): the root is दाशृ दाने (*dāśṛ dāne*); with paras as the upapada, by the rule beginning पुरोडाशो ण्वैन् (*puroḍāśo ṇvain*) (Pā. 3-2-71) the affix ṇvini is used in the passive sense; by the statement श्वेतवहोदीनां (*śvetavahodīnāṃ*) (Pā. 3-2-71-1) the affix ḍas follows; and since अवयाः श्वेतवाः पुरोडाश्च (*avayāḥ śvetavāḥ puroḍāśca*) (Pā. 8-2-67) is a nipātana, the d of the root becomes ḍ.

### Printed p. 568

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued.)* The change of ḍ to ḷ is traditional among the Ṛgvedins. By गतिकारकोपपदात् (*gatikārakopapadāt*) the accent of the kṛdutta-pada-prakṛti comes.

पचतः (*pacataḥ*): the root is डुपचष् पाके (*ḍupacaṣ pāke*); the affix atac is added by the rule भ्रमृदृशि (*bhramṛdṛśi*) (U. Sū. 3-390) *[the bhāṣya block gives the first word of this rule as भृमृदृशी (*bhṛmṛdṛśī*); as supplied]*; पच्यते असौ इति पचतः पक्वः (*pacyate asau iti pacataḥ pakvaḥ*); because the affix has the mark c, the final-acute accent comes. घा (*ghā*): by ऋचितुनुघ (*ṛcitunugha*) (Pā. 6-3-133) the vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā.

परिष्कृतः (*pariṣkṛtaḥ*): the root is डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*); the affix kta in the passive; by संपरिभ्यांकरोत् भूषणे (*saṃparibhyāṃkarot bhūṣaṇe*) (Pā. 6-1-137) the augment suṭ comes to the root, as the first part; then ṣatva; by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. 6-2-49) the preverb keeps its own accent. यविष्ठ्य (*yaviṣṭhya*): यविष्ठ एव यविष्ठ्यः (*yaviṣṭha eva yaviṣṭhyaḥ*); through the force of the word cha in पादार्घाभ्यांच (*pādārghābhyāṃca*) (Pā. 5-4-25) the affix yat comes in its own sense; by यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) the preceding a is dropped; the vocative, having the designation āmantrita, takes the nighāta accent.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ वी॒हि पु॑रो॒ळाश॒माहु॑तं ति॒रोअ॑ह्न्यं ।  
> सह॑सः सू॒नुर॑स्यध्व॒रे हि॒तः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । वीहि । पुरोळाशं । आहुतं । तिरःअह्न्यं ।  
> सहसः । सूनुः । असि । अध्वरे । हितः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने तिरोअह्न्यं अह्नि तिरोहिते सत्याहुतमा समंताद्भुतं पुरो-
> डाशं पुरोडाशाख्यं हविर्वीहि । भक्षय । अध्वरेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे सहसः सूनुर्बलस्य पु-
> त्रस्त्वं हितोऽसि। आहवनीयादिस्थानेष्वस्माभिर्निहितोऽसि । तस्माद्वीहीति शेषः ॥ वीहि ।

*[The bhāṣya block is cut off at the foot of this page in the middle of the sentence, after the word वीहि (*vīhi*) which begins the grammar; it goes on on the next page in a new block. The gist is given after the whole bhāṣya.]*

### Printed p. 569

> वी कांतिगत्यादिषु । लोटि रूपं । हेरपित्वादंतोदात्तत्वं । आहुतं । जुहोतेः
> कर्मणि क्ते गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । तिरोअह्न्यं । अह्नि भवमह्न्यं ।
> भवे छंदसीति यत् । तिरोभूतमह्न्यं यस्मिन् काले स तिरोअह्न्यः । रात्रिकाल
> इत्यर्थः । कालाध्वनोरत्यंतसंयोग इति द्वितीया । प्रकृत्यांतःपादमित्येजः । प्र-
> कृतिभावः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, son of strength, is asked to eat the purodāśa offered at nightfall, since he has been placed by us in the Āhavanīya and other hearths; the rest is grammatical and is transcribed only.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्नि (*agni*)—O Agni *[the headword is printed in the form of the nominative, not as in the Saṃhitā; as supplied]*; सहसः सूनुः (*sahasaḥ sūnuḥ*)—you, son of strength
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in this sacrifice; हितः असि (*hitaḥ asi*)—you are placed in the Āhavanīya and other places (therefore)
- तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*)—at the time when the day is hidden (in the evening)
- आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*)—offered all round
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the oblation in the form of purodāśa
- वीहि (*vīhi*)—eat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who are the son of strength are placed in this sacrifice in the Āhavanīya and other places. Therefore eat the oblation in the form of purodāśa that has been offered all round at the time when the day is hidden (in the evening).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Eat, Agni, the cakes and butter offered as the day disappears : you, son of strength, are stationed (by us) at the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*)—अह्निभवमह्न्यं तिरोभूतमह्न्यं यस्मिन् । यस्मिन्‌काले स तिरोअह्न्यः रात्रिकालः । अहि तिरोहिते सति (*ahnibhavamahnyaṃ tirobhūtamahnyaṃ yasmin | yasminkāle sa tiroahnyaḥ rātrikālaḥ | ahi tirohite sati*) (the day having passed): the oblation called purodāśa that the sacrificers offer in the night that comes after the daytime has gone, that, O Agni (वीहि (*vīhi*)), may Agni eat; thus Agni is addressed and the wish is expressed.

अध्वरे सहसः सूनुः हितः (*adhvare sahasaḥ sūnuḥ hitaḥ*)—the word adhvara is explained by Yāska as अध्वर इति यज्ञनाम ध्वरतिर्हिंसाकर्मा तत्प्रतिषेधः (*adhvara iti yajñanāma dhvaratirhiṃsākarmā tatpratiṣedhaḥ*) (Ni. 1-8). Agni, because he is born of strength in the sacrifices, is spoken of by the expression सहससूनु (*sahasasūnu*), and this Agni has been placed by the sacrificers in the Āhavanīya and other places; having thus explained the origin and the seating of Agni, the wish of the sacrificers is described, that this Agni may eat the oblation called purodāśa.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed pages 569 and 570.)* वीहि (*vīhi*): the root is वी कांतिगत्यादिषु (*vī kāṃtigatyādiṣu*); the form is the second person singular of the imperative (lot). Because the affix hi is made apit, the final-acute accent comes. Because a vocative precedes, and the word comes at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come *[the words of the Kannada between "pāda" and "nighāta" are run together in print; the translation follows the sense; as supplied]*.

*[Stray line at the foot of p. 569: the number 72 alone; as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 570

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, continued.)* आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*): the root is हु दानादनयोः (*hu dānādanayoḥ*); the affix kta in the passive; by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. 6-2-49) the preverb (āj) takes the udātta accent.

तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*): अह्नि भवं अह्न्यं (*ahni bhavaṃ ahnyaṃ*); by भवेच्छंदसि (*bhavecchaṃdasi*) (Pā. 4-4-110) the affix yat. तिरोभूतं अह्न्यं यस्मिन् काले सः तिरोअह्न्यः (*tirobhūtaṃ ahnyaṃ yasmin kāle saḥ tiroahnyaḥ*) means the time of night. Because continuous connection is shown, the second case ending comes by कालाध्वनोरत्यंतसंयोगे (*kālādhvanoratyaṃtasaṃyoge*) (Pā. 2-3-5). By प्रकृत्यांतःपादमव्ययपरे (*prakṛtyāṃtaḥpādamavyayapare*) (Pā. 6-1-115) the o has its natural form (prakṛtibhāva), so no sandhi takes place. By बहुव्रीहौ प्र (*bahuvrīhau pra*) (Pā. 6-2-1) *[the rule is quoted only as far as its first two words; as supplied]* the accent of the first member of the compound comes.

हितः (*hitaḥ*): by दधातेर्हिः (*dadhāterhiḥ*) the root dhā is replaced by hi when the affix kta follows; by the accent of the affix it becomes final-acute.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> माध्यं॑दिने॒ सव॑ने जातवेदः पुरो॒ळाश॑मि॒ह क॑वे जुषस्व ।  
> अग्ने॑ य॒ह्वस्य॒ तव॑ भाग॒धेयं॒ न प्र मि॑नंति वि॒दथे॑षु॒ धीराः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> माध्यंदिने । सवने । जातवेदः । पुरोळाशं । इह । कवे । जुषस्व ।  
> अग्ने । यह्वस्य । तव । भागधेयं । न । प्र । मिनंति । विदथेषु । धीराः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कवे मेधाविन् हे जातवेद इहास्मिन्नग्निष्टोमाख्यॆ कर्मणि तत्र च माध्यं-
> दिने मध्यंदिनसंबंधिनि सवने पुरोडाशं माध्यंदिनसवनीयपुरोडाशं । जुषस्व ।
> सेवस्व ।हे अग्ने विदथेषु यज्ञेषु धीराः कर्मकुशला अध्वर्यादयो यह्वस्य ।
> यांति प्राप्रुवंति देवा हवींष्यनेनेति यहो महानग्निः। यह्वस्य महतस्तव भाग-
> धेयं भागतया परिकल्पितमिमं पुरोडाशं न प्रमिनंति । न हिंसंति । किंतु तुभ्यं
> प्रयच्छंति । तं जुषस्वेति शेषः ॥ माध्यंदिने । मध्यंदिनस्येदमित्यर्थ उत्सादित्वा-
> दञ् । इत्तादादिवृद्धिः। इत्ताद्वाद्युदात्तत्वं। यह्वस्य । या प्रापण इत्यस्मात्
> शेवयह्वजिह्वेति निपातनात्करणे वन्प्रत्ययः । हुगागमधातुह्रस्वौ । यांत्यनेनेशि
> यहोऽग्निः । व्यत्ययेनांतोदात्तः । भागधेयं । भागशब्दात्सार्थे भागरूपना-
> मभ्यो धेयप्रत्ययो वक्तव्यः । पा- ५-४-३६-२ । इति धेयः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मि-

> नंति । मिञ् हिंसायामित्यस्य क्र्यादित्वात् श्ना । तस्मिन् मीनातेर्निगम इति ह्रस्वत्वं।
> हिनु मीना । पा- ८. ४-१५ । इति णत्वं न भवति सर्वविधीनां छंदसि विकल्पितत्वादिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the wise Jātavedas, is asked to enjoy the purodāśa of the midday pressing; the skilled priests do not diminish his share but offer it; the rest is grammatical.

*[In the bhāṣya block the word for the Agniṣṭoma rite ends in a short e vowel sign (ख्यॆ (*khyè*)); the conversion carries it over as supplied.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कवे (*kave*)—O wise one *[spelled with a short vowel in the Pratipadārtha and with a long vowel in the Bhāvārtha; as supplied]*
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—Agni, who has knowledge from birth
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice; माध्यंदिने सवने (*mādhyaṃdine savane*)—at the time of the midday pressing
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the oblation in the form of purodāśa
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—enjoy
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—the priests skilled in the rites
- यह्वस्य (*yahvasya*)—of you who are worthy of sacrifice
- तव (*tava*)—your
- भागधेयं (*bhāgadheyaṃ*)—the oblation assigned to your share; न प्र मिनंति (*na pra minaṃti*)—do not diminish (that is, they offer it in full)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Agni, who have knowledge from birth, enjoy in this sacrifice the oblation in the form of purodāśa that has been offered at the time of the midday pressing. O Agni, the priests who are skilled in the rites of the sacrifices offer in full, without diminishing it, the oblation assigned to the share of you who are worthy of sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Wise Jatavedas, accept the cakes and butter offered in this sacrifice at the mid-day rite ; prudent (worshippers), withhold not at solemn ceremonies the portion of you who are mighty. *[The printed English breaks the word "ceremonies" across a line end; joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कवे (*kave*)—the word kavi is read among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). Agni is addressed by the words kavi and jātavedas (the second compound is printed with an extra letter; as supplied) because he is wise and has knowledge from birth.

इह माध्यंदिने सदने पुरोडाशं जुषस्व (*iha mādhyaṃdine sadane puroḍāśaṃ juṣasva*) *[the third word differs from the Saṃhitā; as supplied]*—it is described that the word इह (*iha*) here denotes the sacrifice called अग्निष्टोम (*agniṣṭoma*) (the word in the brackets in print is वाचि (*vāci*)), and that Agni may enjoy the oblation called purodāśa that is offered by the sacrificers at the midday pressing of this Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—the word dhīra, stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19), is explained in the meaning यज्ञेषु कर्मकुशलाः (*yajñeṣu karmakuśalāḥ*), that is, priests such as the Adhvaryu who are expert in performing the sacrificial rites.

यह्वस्य (*yahvasya*)—यांति प्राप्नुवंति देवा हवींष्यनेनेति यह्वो महानग्निः (*yāṃti prāpnuvaṃti devā havīṃṣyaneneti yahvo mahānagniḥ*): because the gods obtain the oblations through Agni, Agni is called yahva, it is explained. The word yahva is read among the names of the great (Ni. 2-3-13).

भागधेयं (*bhāgadheyaṃ*)—because the gods obtain, through Agni, the oblations offered for them in the sacrifice, the oblation that is separately set aside and offered for Agni is received by Agni *[the sentence is cut off here at the end of the window and goes on in the next; the last printed word is an incomplete word meaning "receives"]*

### Printed p. 572

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued.)* ... the sacrificers make Agni receive it. Thus the wish of the sacrificers, that Agni may enjoy this oblation (havis), the purodāśa in the form of an oblation, is explained.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed page 572.)* माध्यंदिने (*mādhyaṃdine*): मध्यंदिनस्य इदं माध्यंदिनं (*madhyaṃdinasya idaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ*), "this belongs to midday". Because the word is read in the utsādi group, the affix añ. By तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (*taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ*) comes the vṛddhi of the first vowel; by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the initial-acute accent comes.

यह्वस्य (*yahvasya*): the root is या प्रापणे (*yā prāpaṇe*). Since it is made a nipātana by शेवयह्वजिह्व (*śevayahvajihva*), the affix van; the augment huk; the root is shortened. यांति अनेन इति यह्वः अग्निः (*yāṃti anena iti yahvaḥ agniḥ*); although the affix is nit, the final-acute accent comes by vyatyaya.

भागधेयं (*bhāgadheyaṃ*): the word bhāga; after it, in its own sense, the affix dheya by the vārttika भागरूपनामभ्यो धेय प्रत्ययो वक्तव्यः (*bhāgarūpanāmabhyo dheya pratyayo vaktavyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 5-4-36-2); the initial-acute accent of the affix comes.

मिनंति (*minaṃti*): the root is मीञ् हिंसायां (*mīñ hiṃsāyāṃ*), of the kryādi class; in the third person plural the jhi is replaced by ant; by क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना (*kryādibhyaḥ śnā*) the vikaraṇa śnā. Since the extension of cit-ness (citvātideśa) applies to the affix, by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Ṇā. Sū. 6-4-112) *[the abbreviation is printed with Ṇā. where Pā. is usual; as supplied]* the a of the vikaraṇa is elided. By मीनातेर्निगमे (*mīnāternigame*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-81) the root is shortened, and the form minanti results. Because the preverb pra stands before it, ṇatva of the n is obtained by हिनुमीना (*hinumīnā*) (Prā. Sū. 8-4-15) *[printed Prā. in place of Pā.; as supplied]*, but by the statement सर्वे विधयः छंदसि विकल्प्यंते (*sarve vidhayaḥ chaṃdasi vikalpyaṃte*) ṇatva does not come here. Because it stands after an "atijanta" *[as supplied; the word is printed so]*, the nighāta accent comes.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ तृ॒तीये॒ सव॑ने॒ हि कानि॑षः पुरो॒ळाशं॑ सहसः सून॒वाहु॑तं ।  
> अथा॑ दे॒वेष्व॑ध्व॒रं वि॑प॒न्यया॒ धा रत्न॑वंतम॒मृते॑षु॒ जागृ॑विं ॥ ५॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । त्तृतीये । सवने । हि । कानिषः । पुरोळाशं । सहसः । सूनो इति । आहुतं।  
> अथ । देवेषु । अध्वरं । विपन्यया । धाः । रत्नवंतं । अमृतेषु । जागृविं ॥ ५ ॥

*[In the Pada-pāṭha the word for "third" is printed with a doubled initial consonant (the second word of the line); as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 573

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहसः सूनो बलस्य पुत्र हे अग्ने त्वं तृतीये सवन आहुतं हूयमानं
> पुरोडाशं कानिषः । कामयसे । अथ अनंतरमध्वरमविनाशिनं रत्नवंतं । रत्नश-
> ब्देन स्वर्गादिलक्षणमुत्तमं फलमभिधीयते । तद्वंतं फलप्रदं जागृविं जागरणका-
> रणं । प्रातःसोमो जागृविर्भवति स्वप्ननिवारक इति । तमिमं सोमं विपन्यया
> स्तुतिलक्षणया वाचा स्तुतस्त्वममृतेषु मरणधर्मरहितेषु देवेष्विंद्रादिषु धाः ।
> धेहि हि पूरणः ॥ तृतीये । त्रिशब्दात्पूरणार्थे त्रेः संप्रसारणं । पा. ५-२-५५ ।
> इति तीयप्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेन संप्रसारणं । हल इति दीर्घो न भवति । अन्निति
> तत्र नानुवर्तनात् प्रत्ययस्वरः । कानिषः । कनी कांत्यादिषु । लेटि सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ।
> तस्यार्द्धधातुकत्वादिडागमः । कांतिरभिलाषः । आकारस्य आकारो व्यत्ययेन । हियो-
> गादनिघातः । धातुस्वरः । विपन्यया । पन स्तुतौ । भावे क्विप् । विपनं यातीति कप्रत्य-
> यः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । धाः । दधातेर्धातोश्छांदसे लुजु रूपं । पादादित्वादनिघातः ।
> जागृविं । क्विन्प्रत्ययांतो जागृविशब्दः । नित्स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni desires the purodāśa of the third pressing; he is asked to place the awakening Soma among the immortal gods; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni; तृतीये सवने (*tṛtīye savane*)—at the third pressing
- आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*)—offered
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the purodāśa
- कानिषः (*kāniṣaḥ*)—you desire
- अथ (*atha*)—thereafter
- अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—that which is without destruction
- रत्नवंतं (*ratnavaṃtaṃ*)—that which gives the fruits such as heaven
- जागृविं (*jāgṛviṃ*)—the Soma that removes sleep and causes awakening
- विपन्यया (*vipanyayā*)—with speech in the form of praise (you who are praised)
- अमृतेषु (*amṛteṣu*)—among those free from the nature of death
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods, Indra and the others
- धाः (*dhāḥ*)—place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength, you desire the purodāśa offered at the third pressing. Thereafter, praised with speech in the form of praise, place the Soma, which is without destruction, gives the fruits such as heaven, and removes sleep and causes awakening, among the immortal gods, Indra and the others.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Be pleased, Agni, son of strength, with the cakes and butter offered at the third (daily sacrifice), and (propitiated) by praise, convey the precious imperishable and awakening (oblation) to the immortal gods. *[The printed English breaks the word "precious" across a line end; joined here.]*

### Printed p. 574

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Agni is addressed by the words सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*). Because force is used when the fire is churned in the two aranis, the meaning "son of force" is explained.

तृतीये सवने आहुतं पुरोडाशं कानिषः (*tṛtīye savane āhutaṃ puroḍāśaṃ kāniṣaḥ*)—the meaning is explained that Agni desires the purodāśa, in the form of an oblation, that the sacrificers offer at the time of the third pressing of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice.

अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—this word is stated among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19). Sāyaṇa explains this word as अविनाशिनं (*avināśinaṃ*), "that which does not meet destruction", and says it as an epithet of Soma.

रत्नवंतं (*ratnavaṃtaṃ*)—रत्नशब्देन स्वर्गादिलक्षणमुत्तमं फलमभिधीयते तत्फलप्रदं (*ratnaśabdena svargādilakṣaṇamuttamaṃ phalamabhidhīyate tatphalapradaṃ*) *[the last word differs from the bhāṣya, which has a different word for "giving fruit"; as supplied]*. The word ratna is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9); denoting delightful wealth, it is used in होतारं रत्नधातमं (*hotāraṃ ratnadhātamaṃ*). Sāyaṇa explains this word as the excellent fruit of the form of heaven and the like, and describes that Soma produces the fruit in the form of heaven and wealth.

जागृविं (*jāgṛviṃ*)—जागरणकारिणं (*jāgaraṇakāriṇaṃ*) *[the bhāṣya has a different form of the second word; as supplied]*. The word jāgṛvi is explained as जागृविर्जागरणात् (*jāgṛvirjāgaraṇāt*) (Ni. 9-8). It is explained that Soma is used in the sense of keeping one awake (making sleep not come); the śruti sentence प्रातस्सोमो जागृविर्भवति स्वप्ननिवारकः (*prātassomo jāgṛvirbhavati svapnanivārakaḥ*) is cited, and the wish of the sacrificers is set forth, that Agni may offer this Soma to the gods who do not undergo the nature of death, who are denoted by the word amṛta.

विपन्यया (*vipanyayā*)—स्तुतिलक्षणया वाचा (*stutilakṣaṇayā vācā*). The word विपन्यु (*vipanyu*) is read (ಪರಿತವಾಗಿದೆ is printed; as supplied) among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). It is explained that here it is stated as denoting speech in the form of praise, and it is described that Agni is praised with praises. The Nirukta authors say:

यथो एतदोजसो जातमुतमन्य एनमिति चाहेत्ययमप्यग्निरोजसा बलेन मध्यमानो जायते तस्मादेनमाह सहसस्पुत्रं सहसः सूनुं सहसो यहुं (*yatho etadojaso jātamutamanya enamiti cāhetyayamapyagnirojasā balena madhyamāno jāyate tasmādenamāha sahasasputraṃ sahasaḥ sūnuṃ sahaso yahuṃ*)

Explaining that Agni, because he is born of force, is designated by the words सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*), सहसस्सूनु (*sahasassūnu*) and सहसो यहु (*sahaso yahu*), and then the mantra:

त्वं ह यद्यविष्ठ्य सहसः सूनवाहुत । ऋतावा यज्ञियो भुवः ॥ (*tvaṃ ha yadyaviṣṭhya sahasaḥ sūnavāhuta | ṛtāvā yajñiyo bhuvaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-75.-3)

*[The text of this window ends here, after the second quotation; the Special Topics of Ṛk 5 go on in the next window.]*

### Printed p. 575

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued.)* अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानस्सहसो यहो । अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥ (*agne vājasya gomata īśānassahaso yaho | asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-4). In the Ṛks beginning thus, it is cited that Agni is designated by the words सहसस्सूनु (*sahasassūnu*) and सहसो यहु (*sahaso yahu*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed page 575.)* तृतीये (*tṛtīye*): the word त्रि (*tri*). When the sense of completion (ordinal) is shown after it, by त्रेः संप्रसारणं (*treḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 5-2-55) the affix tīya; the repha is replaced by ṛ (saṃprasāraṇa). By हलः (*halaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-111), according to the statement that lengthening applies only to aṇ (i, u), no lengthening comes here, because ṛ is present. Since the initial-acute accent of the affix comes, the word becomes madhyodātta. The form is of the seventh case singular.

कानिषः (*kāniṣaḥ*): the root is कसी कांत्यादिषु (*kasī kāṃtyādiṣu*) *[the root is printed with a different second letter from the bhāṣya block of this Ṛk; as supplied]*. In the second person singular of leṭ the affix sip. By इतश्चलोप (*itaścalopa*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-47) the i of it is elided. By सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-34) sip. Since it has the designation ārdhadhātuka, by अर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (*ardhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-5) the augment iṭ comes. By आदेशप्रत्यययोः (*ādeśapratyayayoḥ*) the s of sip becomes ṣ. Rutva and visarga for the letter na of the affix ; for the a of the root, ā is substituted by vyatyaya. By हिच (*hica*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34) the nighāta accent is prohibited, so the root accent remains.

अथा (*athā*): by निपातस्यच (*nipātasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136) lengthening comes in the saṃhitā.

विपन्यया (*vipanyayā*): the root is पन स्तुत् (*pana stut*) *[the second word differs from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]*. When the preverb vi stands before it, in the sense of bhāva, because it is read in the sampadādi group, the affix kvip. विपनं याति इति विपन्या (*vipanaṃ yāti iti vipanyā*); the root is या प्रापणे (*yā prāpaṇe*). By आतोनुपसर्गेकः (*ātonupasargekaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-3) the affix ka. By the affix accent the word becomes final-acute. The form is of the third case singular.

धाः (*dhāḥ*): the root is डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). By छंदसिलुज् लज् (*chaṃdasiluj laj*) luñ in the sense of ಬೋಡರ್ಥ *[the word is printed so; as supplied]*. When sip comes in the second person singular, by इतश्च (*itaśca*) the i is elided. By गातिस्थासि (*gātisthāsi*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77) *[the sūtra is printed in this broken form; as supplied]*, when sic is substituted for cli, luk comes for it; rutva and visarga for the s of the affix. As a Vedic peculiarity the augment aṭ does not come. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the anudātta accent does not come. By the root accent it becomes udātta.

जागृविं (*jāgṛviṃ*): the root is जागृ निद्राक्षये (*jāgṛ nidrākṣaye*). The Uṇādi affix kvin. The vi remains. Because it is kit, guṇa does not come. By इत्त्यादिर्नित्यं (*ittyādirnityaṃ*) the initial-acute accent comes.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ वृधा॒न आहु॑तिं पुरो॒ळाशं॑ जातवेदः ।  
> जु॒षस्व॑ ति॒रोअ॑ह्न्यं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । वृधानः । आहुतिं । पुरोळाशं । जातवेदः ।  
> जुषस्व । तिरः अह्न्यं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञ हे अग्ने वृधान आहुतिभिर्वर्धमानस्त्वं तिरोअह्नं।
> अह्नि भवमह्न्यं दिवसकृत्यं । तिरोभूतमह्न्यं यस्मिन्काले स तिरोअह्नो रात्रि-
> कालः । तस्मिन्काल आहुतिं, पुरोडाशाख्यं हविर्जुषस्व । सेवस्व ॥ आहुतिं । जुहोतेः
> कर्मणि क्तिन् । तादौ च निति कृत्यताविति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, who grows by oblations, is asked to enjoy the purodāśa oblation offered at the time when the day has gone; the grammar of the word for "oblation" follows. The bhāṣya block gives the word for "of the day" in a form (printed तिरोअह्नं (*tiroahnaṃ*)) that differs from the Saṃhitā (तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*)); as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—ಜಾತಪ್ರಜ್ಞನಾಡ
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वृधानः (*vṛdhānaḥ*)—you who grow by oblations
- तिरोअह्न्यं (*tiroahnyaṃ*)—offered at the third pressing *[so in the Pratipadārtha and the Bhāvārtha; the bhāṣya block speaks of the night-time; as supplied]*; आहुतिं पुरोडाशं (*āhutiṃ puroḍāśaṃ*)—the oblation in the form of purodāśa
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of born wisdom, you who grow by oblations, enjoy the oblation that is offered at the third pressing and is in the form of purodāśa.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, you are Jasavedas [sic] and are thriving upon oblations, accept the cakes and butter as the day disappears. *[The label of the printed English is a plain line "English translation" without the usual mark; as supplied.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The word जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*) is used here as an epithet of Agni. Since the meaning "of born wisdom" is explained, it is described that Agni is all-knowing, and Agni is addressed with this word.

### Printed p. 577

वृधानः (*vṛdhānaḥ*)—आहुतिभिर्वर्धमानः (*āhutibhirvardhamānaḥ*): the meaning is explained that Agni grows by the oblations, in the form of the offerings (havis) that the sacrificers offer.

तिरो अह्न्यं पुरोडाशं जुषस्व (*tiro ahnyaṃ puroḍāśaṃ juṣasva*)—the time fit for performing the work that comes after the day's work has been performed; because it comes after the day has passed, the meaning of this word is explained as the night-time. The wish of the sacrificers is described, that Agni may enjoy the oblation in the form of purodāśa that is offered at the time of night.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, printed page 577.)* वृधानः (*vṛdhānaḥ*): the root is वृधु वृद्धौ (*vṛdhu vṛddhau*). The substitute śānac for laṭ. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) luk for the vikaraṇa. By सार्वधातुकमपित् (*sārvadhātukamapit*) (Pā. Sū. 1-2-4), since ṅit-ness (printed ಜಿತತ್ವ; as supplied) is extended to the affix, guṇa does not come for the laghūpadha of the root. By चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the final-acute accent comes.

आहुतिं (*āhutiṃ*): the root is हु दानादनयोः (*hu dānādanayoḥ*). The affix ktin in the karman. Since a nit affix beginning with t follows, by तादौच निति कृत्यत् (*tādauca niti kṛtyat*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50) *[the sūtra is printed so; as supplied]* the udātta accent comes for the gati (आज् (*āj*)).

जुषस्व (*juṣasva*): the root is जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*). Loṭ; the form is of the second person singular. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. Since the lasārvadhātuka becomes anudātta by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) *[the sūtra is printed without a number; none is written]*, the vikaraṇa accent remains.

## Sūkta 29 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The twenty-ninth sūkta** (ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂಬತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्तीदमिति षोडशर्चं सप्तदशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका ।
> अस्तीदं षोळशाद्याचतुर्थिदशमीद्वादश्योऽनुष्टुभः षष्ठैकादश्युपांत्ये च
> जगत्यः पंचम्यत्विग्भो वेति । आद्याचतुर्थिदशमीद्वादश्योऽनुष्टुभः षष्ठेका-
> दश्युपांत्ये च जगत्यः षष्ठैकादशी चतुर्दशी पंचदशी च जगत्यः । शिष्टा अष्टौ
> त्रिष्टुभः । पंचमी मंथता नर इत्येषा ऋत्विग्देवताकाग्नि देवताका ना शिष्टा अग्नि-
> देवताकाः ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । वरुणप्रघासेष्टग्नि प्रणयन इळायास्त्वा

### Printed p. 578

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning with आस्तिदं (*āstidaṃ*) *[the first word is printed with a long initial vowel, differently from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]* is the seventeenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. There are sixteen Ṛks in it. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: आस्तिदं षोळशाद्या चतुर्थी दशमा द्वादश्योऽनुष्टुभः षष्ठैकावश्युपांत्ये च जगत्यः पंचम्यत्विग्भो ना (*āstidaṃ ṣoḷaśādyā caturthī daśamā dvādaśyo 'nuṣṭubhaḥ ṣaṣṭhaikāvaśyupāṃtye ca jagatyaḥ paṃcamyatvigbho nā*) *[this text of the Anukramaṇikā is printed differently from the bhāṣya block in some words, for example the last word; as supplied]*. Of this sūkta the 1st, 4th, 10th and 12th Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the 6th, 11th, 14th and 15th Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre; the remaining eight Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. Of this sūkta the fifth Ṛk, beginning मंथता नरः (*maṃthatā naraḥ*), has the Ṛtvij (priests) or Agni as its deity; all the remaining Ṛks have Agni as deity. The application of the sūkta is Laiṅgika (by the sense of the words).

In the mantras of the rite called Agni-praṇayana, in the sacrifice called Varuṇapraghāsa, the Ṛk इळायास्त्वा पदे (*iḷāyāstvā pade*) (the 4th Ṛk of this sūkta) has its application; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra इळायास्त्वा पदे वयमग्ने विश्वेभिः स्वनीक देवैरित्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (*iḷāyāstvā pade vayamagne viśvebhiḥ svanīka devairityardharca āramet*) (Ā. 2-17). In the Agni-praṇayana rite mentioned above, the Ṛk सीद होतः (*sīda hotaḥ*) (the 8th Ṛk of this sūkta) is to be recited when the fire is established on the uttaravedi; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra निहितेऽग्नौ सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वान् (*nihite 'gnau sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvān*) (Ā. 2-17). And the Ṛk आयं ते योनिः (*āyaṃ te yoniḥ*) (the 10th Ṛk of this sūkta) is to be recited when the fire is placed on the aranī with which the fire is churned; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (the name is printed here as two words; as supplied) अयंते योनिर्ऋत्तिय इत्यरणी गार्हपत्ये प्रतितपेत्पाणी वा (*ayaṃte yonirṛttiya ityaraṇī gārhapatye pratitapetpāṇī vā*) (Ā. 3-10).

Devatā: Ṛks 1 to 4 and 6 to 16, अग्निः (*agniḥ*); Ṛk 5, खत्विजु अग्निर्वा (*khatviju agnirvā*) *[the first word is printed so; as supplied]*. Chandas: Ṛks 1, 4, 10 and 12, अनुष्टुप् (*anuṣṭup*); Ṛks 2, 3, 5, 7 to 9, 13 and 16, त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*); Ṛks 6, 11, 14 and 15, जगती (*jagatī*).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer tells the adhvaryu the churning implements are ready, asks him to bring the fire-stick, and proposes churning the fire as of old; grammatical remarks on the words follow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this piece of the sacrificial post that is for Agni
- अस्ति (*asti*)—is ready
- अधिमंथनं (*adhimaṃthanaṃ*)—the stick and the rope together, the instruments for churning when placed on the aranī
- अस्ति (*asti*)—is ready
- प्रजननं (*prajananaṃ*)—the tuft of darbha needed for the production of fire
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—has been made ready
- विश्वत्नीं (*viśvatnīṃ*)—that protects the people who perform the sacrifice
- एतां (*etāṃ*)—this aranī; आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring (then)
- पूर्वथा (*pūrvathā*)—just as the ṛṣis of former times churned the fire, so also at this time of the sacrifice
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—the fire
- मंथाम (*maṃthāma*)—let us churn, so that it is produced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The piece of the sacrificial post that is for Agni is ready. The stick used for churning, placed on the aranī, and the rope are also ready. The tuft of darbha needed for the production of fire has also been made. O adhvaryu, bring the aranī that protects the people who perform the sacrifice. Then, just as in former times the ṛṣis churned the fire, so also at this time of the sacrifice let us churn the fire so that it is produced.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sāyaṇa has explained that this is a sentence spoken by the sacrificer to the officiating priests, the adhvaryu (ಅಧ್ವರ್ಯುಪೇ is printed so; as supplied) and others.

इदं अस्ति (*idaṃ asti*)—The word इदं (*idaṃ*) is counted among the pronouns. Since the meaning of the word इदं (*idaṃ*) has been determined as referring to a matter present in the mind, it is indicated in this mantra that the yūpa-śakala (piece of the sacrificial post) is what the word इदं (*idaṃ*) denotes, and that, the sacrificer's intention to perform the sacrifice being understood, the materials of the sacrifice are ready. By this sentence the meaning is explained that, in order to satisfy the gods by the sacrifice, the sacrificial post for binding the animal has been brought and is ready.

अधिमंथनं अस्ति (*adhimaṃthanaṃ asti*)—The meaning is described that by the word अधिमंथन (*adhimaṃthana*) are meant the stick placed on the upper part of the aranī, the instrument of the act of churning for producing fire, and the rope (cord), and the like.

प्रजननं कृतं (*prajananaṃ kṛtaṃ*)—अग्निजननसाधनं दर्भपिंजूलं संपादितं । यद्वा प्रजननं मंथनदंडस्य विन्यासविशेषः (*agnijananasādhanaṃ darbhapiṃjūlaṃ saṃpāditaṃ | yadvā prajananaṃ maṃthanadaṃḍasya vinyāsaviśeṣaḥ*). Having explained that the meaning of the word प्रजनन (*prajanana*) can be either a substance or an action, the text says that, so that the fire born in the aranīs may arise, the bits of darbha placed on the upper side of the aranīs have been made ready, or that the churning-stick has been made suitable, so that the act of churning may be performed for the production of fire in the aranī.

विश्यत्नीमेतामाभर (*viśyatnīmetāmābhara*) *[printed so, with the second letter different from the Saṃhitā; as supplied]*—By this sentence the sacrificer addresses the officiating priest called adhvaryu, and the sacrificer's request is indicated that, since all the means suited to churning and producing fire are ready, the adhvaryu should bring the aranī for the churning of the fire.

For the word विश्यत्नी (*viśyatnī*) the meaning is explained as प्रजानां पालयित्री (*prajānāṃ pālayitrī*): the aranī that protects the people by performing the agnihotra made possible by the fire, producing fruits that give abundant happiness, such as heaven.

पूर्वथा (*pūrvathā*)—For this word one kind of meaning is given: as the sacrificers have churned the fire at the respective prescribed times for performing the sacrifice. Or: यथा वा पूर्वे महर्षयो अग्निमंथिषुस्तद्वत् (*yathā vā pūrve maharṣayo agnimaṃthiṣustadvat*) *[the verb is printed here without the augment, differently from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]*. Now, those who have the intention to perform the sacrifice … *[the supplied text of this window ends here, in the middle of the sentence; it goes on in the next window.]*

### Printed p. 581

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)* … just as the great ṛṣis, who were earlier than the sacrificers, churned the fire in order to perform the sacrifice; thus a second meaning is also explained.

अग्निं मंथाम (*agniṃ maṃthāma*)—अस्मिन् कर्मणि मंथनेन निष्पन्नं करवाम (*asmin karmaṇi maṃthanena niṣpannaṃ karavāma*). In the rite that consists of the establishing of the fire, the wish of the sacrificer is expressed: let us churn (the fire) in the aranīs so that Agni is produced.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 581.)* अस्ति (*asti*): the root is अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*), of the class अदादि (*adādi*). A form of the लट् (*laṭ*), third person singular. Since the following अस्ति (*asti*) and this one both stand at the beginning of a pāda, the निघात (*nighāta*) accent does not come. Because तिप् (*tip*) is anudātta, the accent of the root remains.

अधिमंथनं (*adhimaṃthanaṃ*): the root is मंथ विलोडने (*maṃtha viloḍane*). When the affix ल्युट् (*lyuṭ*) comes, by युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) there is the अनादेश (*anādeśa*) for it. By लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent comes on the syllable before the affix. In the compound, the natural accent of the latter member comes, कृमत्तरपद (*kṛmattarapada*) .

विश् पत्नीं (*viś patnīṃ*) *[printed so, with a space and different from the Saṃhitā; as supplied]*: when the feminine sense is intended for the word पति (*pati*), since it is preceded by another member, by विभाषासपूर्वस्य (*vibhāṣāsapūrvasya*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-34) the affix जीष् (*jīṣ*) . The letter नकार (*nakāra*) comes as the final substitute. The form becomes विश् पत्नि (*viś patni*). By परादिश्चंदसि बहुलं (*parādiścaṃdasi bahulaṃ*) the udātta accent on the first syllable of the latter member comes.

भर (*bhara*): the root is हृञ् हरणे (*hṛñ haraṇe*). A form of the लोट् (*loṭ*), second person singular. By the rule हृग्रहोर्भश्चंदसि (*hṛgrahorbhaścaṃdasi*) the भकार (*bhakāra*) is substituted for the हकार (*hakāra*) of the root. Because it stands after an अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the निघात (*nighāta*) accent comes.

मंथाम (*maṃthāma*): the root is मंथ विलोडने (*maṃtha viloḍane*). A form of the लोट् (*loṭ*), first person plural. As before, the तिजंतनिघात (*tijaṃtanighāta*) accent comes.

पूर्वथा (*pūrvathā*): after the word पूर्व (*pūrva*), when the sense of similarity is shown, by प्रत्य पूर्वविश्वेमात्थाल् छंदसि (*pratya pūrvaviśvemātthāl chaṃdasi*) (5-3-111) *[the sūtra is printed so, beginning with the word ಪ್ರತ್ಯ; as supplied]* the affix थाल् (*thāl*). Since this is लित् (*lit*), by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent comes on the syllable before the affix.

> वेति वक्तव्यमिति विकल्पितत्वाद्द्विर्वचनाभावः । वसुस्रंसुध्वंस्वनडुहां दः । पा. ८-
> २-७२ । इति वसोः सकारस्य दत्वं । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, placed by the gods in the two aranīs like an embryo in pregnant women, is to be praised daily by vigilant men; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गर्भिणीषु (*garbhiṇīṣu*)—in the pregnant women
- सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*)—placed under protection
- गर्भइव (*garbhaiva*)—like an embryo
- जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—Agni, who knows all things
- अरण्योः (*araṇyoḥ*)—in the aranīs
- निहितः (*nihitaḥ*)—has been placed under protection
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the venerable Agni
- हविष्मद्भिः (*haviṣmadbhiḥ*)—by those who have gathered oblations
- जागृवद्भिः (*jāgṛvadbhiḥ*)—who are vigilant in the rites
- मनुष्येभिः (*manuṣyebhiḥ*)—by men, the sacrificers
- दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)—every day
- ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)—becomes one who is praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like an embryo kept under protection in pregnant women, Agni, who knows all things, has been placed under protection in the aranīs. The venerable Agni becomes one who is praised every day by men, the sacrificers, who have gathered oblations and are vigilant in the rites.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Jatavedas has been deposited in the two sticks as the embryo is depesited [sic] in pregnant women : Agni is to be adored day by day by vigilant men laden with oblations. *[The label of the printed English is printed as “English Ttranslation” without the usual mark; the word “deposited” is broken at the line end as “depe-sited”; as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 583

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

जातवेदाः आरण्योर्निहितः (*jātavedāḥ āraṇyornihitaḥ*)—सर्वविषयज्ञानवानयमग्निः देवैर्यज्ञार्थं नितरां स्थापितोऽस्ति । (*sarvaviṣayajñānavānayamagniḥ devairyajñārthaṃ nitarāṃ sthāpito 'sti |*) Having explained the meaning of the word for Jātavedas as “Agni, who has the abundant knowledge that knows everything”, the text describes that Agni, who has such greatness, has been placed in the aranīs by the gods for performing the sacrifice.

गर्भ इव सुधितो गर्भिणीषु (*garbha iva sudhito garbhiṇīṣu*)—This sentence is used as a simile regarding Agni's abiding in the aranīs. It is said by comparison that, as an embryo is established in women who are pregnant, Agni has been placed in the aranīs by the gods.

हविष्मद्भिः जागृवद्भिः दिवेदिवे ईड्यः (*haviṣmadbhiḥ jāgṛvadbhiḥ divedive īḍyaḥ*)—The sacrificers are accompanied by officiating priests who prepare the oblation for performing the sacrifice and are vigilant in the performance of the sacrificial rite. On the respective days, both for (producing) Agni *[the words “for producing” are in parentheses in the print]* and for his receiving the oblation, he is worthy of praise with the respective praises. For this reason it is described that they churn this Agni in the aranīs, perform the sacrifice and praise him.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, printed page 583.)* अरण्योः (*araṇyoḥ*): the root is ऋ गत् (*ṛ gat*). By अर्तिसृधृधमि (*artisṛdhṛdhami*) (U. Sū. 2-259) the affix अनि (*ani*). By सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) guṇa for the root, which comes followed by r. The accent of the affix comes, आमुदात्तस्वर (*āmudāttasvara*) . The form is of the seventh case, dual.

निहितः (*nihitaḥ*): the root is डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). The affix क्त (*kta*) in the passive. By दधातेर्हिः (*dadhāterhiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42) the substitute हि (*hi*) for the root. By गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent comes on the गति (*gati*), that is नि (*ni*).

सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*): when the affix क्त (*kta*) in the passive follows the root mentioned before, and सु (*su*) is the upapada, the form धि (*dhi*) comes and is fixed by nipātana through सुधितवसुधित (*sudhitavasudhita*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-45). As before, the udātta accent comes on the गति (*gati*).

दिवेदिवे (*divedive*): the root is दिवु क्रीडादिसु (*divu krīḍādisu*) *[the bhāṣya block has a different ending here; as supplied]*. Because the letter इकार (*ikāra*) is the upadhā, by इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः (*igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-135) the affix क (*ka*). Since it is कित् (*kit*), guṇa does not come. By नित्यवीप्सयोः (*nityavīpsayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-1) doubling. For the latter form in it, when by तस्य परमाम्रेडितं (*tasya paramāmreḍitaṃ*) the name āmreḍita is present, by अनुदात्तंच (*anudāttaṃca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3) it takes the accent that is wholly anudātta.

ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*): by ईडवंडवृ (*īḍavaṃḍavṛ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-114) *[the sūtra is cut off after its third word in the print, followed by a dash; as supplied]*, when it ends in the affix ण्यत् (*ṇyat*), the accent on the first syllable comes.

### Printed p. 584

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued on printed page 584.)* जागृवद्भिः (*jāgṛvadbhiḥ*): the root is जागृ निद्राक्षये (*jāgṛ nidrākṣaye*). When लिट् (*liṭ*) comes to it, the क्वसुरादेश (*kvasurādeśa*) comes for it. Because of the statement द्विर्वचनप्रकरणेछंदसि वेति वक्तव्यं (*dvirvacanaprakaraṇechaṃdasi veti vaktavyaṃ*) the doubling is optional, so here the root is not doubled on account of the affix क्वसु (*kvasu*). Since it is कित् (*kit*), guṇa does not come. The word जागृवस् (*jāgṛvas*) results. When the instrumental plural follows it, by वसुस्रंसु ध्वंस्वनडुहां दः (*vasusraṃsu dhvaṃsvanaḍuhāṃ daḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-72) in वसु (*vasu*) the सकार (*sakāra*) is replaced by दत्व (*datva*). By प्रत्ययस्वर (*pratyayasvara*) the vowel that follows the letter वकार (*vakāra*) becomes udātta.

मनुष्येभिः (*manuṣyebhiḥ*): by वा छंदसि (*vā chaṃdasi*) the ऐस्‌भाव (*aisbhāva*) is optional for the instrumental ending, and therefore does not come here. By बहुवचनेझल्येत् (*bahuvacanejhalyet*) the एत्व (*etva*) comes.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wise adhvaryu is to place the upper aranī, face downward, on the lower one that faces upward; the lower aranī at once produces Agni; grammar follows.

### Printed p. 585

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—you (the adhvaryu), who are wise
- उत्तानायां (*uttānāyāṃ*)—on the lower aranī that has its face turned upward; अव भर (*ava bhara*)—place the upper aranī, making it face downward
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—immediately after you have done so, (the aranī)
- प्रवीता (*pravītā*)—having received the seed and become pregnant
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—Agni, who showers the desired objects
- जजान (*jajāna*)—produces; (afterwards) अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- रुशत् (*ruśat*)—that destroys darkness
- पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—radiance (arises)
- अरुषस्तूपः (*aruṣastūpaḥ*)—endowed with an attractive mass of radiance
- इळायाःपुत्रः (*iḷāyāḥputraḥ*)—Agni, who is born on the earth in the form of the uttaravedi
- वयुने (*vayune*)—in the womb in the form of the aranī
- अजनिष्ट (*ajaniṣṭa*)—has been born

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

अध्वरुवे (*adhvaruve*), you who are wise, place the upper aranī, made to face downward, on the lower aranī that has its face turned upward. As soon as you have done so, the lower aranī, having received the seed and become pregnant, produces Agni, who showers the desired objects. Afterwards the darkness-destroying radiance of this Agni arises. Agni, endowed with an attractive mass of radiance and born on the earth in the form of the uttaravedi, has been born in the womb in the form of the aranī. *[The vocative is printed so, without the letter for ya; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Let the intelligent priest place the lower of the sticks with the face upwards, the upper (with the surface) downwards, so that quickly impregnated it may generate the showerer (of benefits) Agni : then the bright blazing son of Ila whose light dissipates the darkness is born of the wood of attrition. *[The label of the printed English is printed as “English Ttranslation” without the usual mark; as supplied.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

चिकित्त्वा उत्तानायां अव भर (*cikittvā uttānāyāṃ ava bhara*)—The authors of the Nirukta have given the word चिकित्त्वा (*cikittvā*) the meaning चेतनार्वा (*cetanārvā*) (Ni. 8-5, Ni. 2-12). Sāyaṇa here gives the meaning “the adhvaryu, the priest who has knowledge”, and describes the sacrificer's instruction that this adhvaryu must place the lower aranī so that it faces upward and the upper aranī so that it faces downward. From the sentence सद्यः प्रवीता वृषणं जजान (*sadyaḥ pravītā vṛṣaṇaṃ jajāna*) it is explained that Agni will be born from the lower aranī. And it is described that Agni is वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*), the fulfiller of the sacrificers' wishes, and that रुशत् पाजः (*ruśat pājaḥ*), the darkness-removing radiance belonging to Agni, arises in the lower aranī while it is churned by the upper aranī. The word पाजः (*pājaḥ*) is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9) and is used here in the sense of radiance.

*[Stray line “74” at the end of the page; as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 586

अरुषस्तूपः (*aruṣastūpaḥ*)—न विद्यते रुषः क्रोधो यस्य । क्रोधराहित्येन रोचमानः (*na vidyate ruṣaḥ krodho yasya | krodharāhityena rocamānaḥ*). The meaning is explained: Agni is shining because he is free from anger; आरोचमानः तेजस्संघो यस्य (*ārocamānaḥ tejassaṃgho yasya*); स्तूयत इति स्तूपः तेजस्संघः (*stūyata iti stūpaḥ tejassaṃghaḥ*), that is, because the mass of radiance is worthy of being praised, it is designated by the word स्तूप (*stūpa*); and because he shines (by shining) in all regions, the mass of radiance is denoted by the word अरुष (*aruṣa*).

अरुषस्तूपः इळायास्पुत्रः वयुने अजनिष्ट (*aruṣastūpaḥ iḷāyāsputraḥ vayune ajaniṣṭa*)—आरोचमानतेजस्संघोपेतः उत्तरवेद्याः उत्पन्नः अग्निः अरण्यां योनिस्थाने अजनिष्ट (*ārocamānatejassaṃghopetaḥ uttaravedyāḥ utpannaḥ agniḥ araṇyāṃ yonisthāne ajaniṣṭa*). The meaning is expounded: Agni, endowed with a mass of radiance that shines on all sides, before he blazes with abundant radiance in the uttaravedi of the sacrificial hall, comes to be born, in subtle form, by churning in the lower aranī.

वयुने (*vayune*)—अरण्यां योनिस्थाने अजति वीयते वा वयुनमंगं (*araṇyāṃ yonisthāne ajati vīyate vā vayunamaṃgaṃ*). Sāyaṇa explains it as the limb that is the support in the attaining of origin. The authors of the Nirukta read the word वयुन (*vayuna*) among the names of wisdom (Ni. 3-13), and comment वयुनं वेतेः कांतिर्वा प्रज्ञा वा (*vayunaṃ veteḥ kāṃtirvā prajñā vā*): derived from the root वि (*vi*), the word वयुन (*vayuna*) has the meaning radiance or wisdom. Having cited the mantra

स इत्तमोऽवयुनं ततन्वत्सूर्येण वयुनवच्चकार । कदा ते मर्ता अमृतस्य धामेयक्षंतो न मिनंति स्वधावः (*sa ittamo 'vayunaṃ tatanvatsūryeṇa vayunavaccakāra | kadā te martā amṛtasya dhāmeyakṣaṃto na minaṃti svadhāvaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-21-3)

they explain that in वयुनवच्चकार (*vayunavaccakāra*) the word वयुन (*vayuna*) has the meaning प्रज्ञान (*prajñāna*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed page 586.)* भर (*bhara*): the root is भृञ् भरणे (*bhṛñ bharaṇe*). A form of the लोट् (*loṭ*), second person singular. The तिजंतनिघातस्वर (*tijaṃtanighātasvara*) accent comes. Since there are two अच् (*ac*), by द्व्यचोतस्तिजः (*dvyacotastijaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135) lengthening comes in the Saṃhitā.

चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*): the root is कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*). For लिटि (*liṭi*) the क्वसुरादेश (*kvasurādeśa*) comes. The form is of the nominative singular, and the प्रत्ययस्वर (*pratyayasvara*) accent comes.

प्रवीता (*pravītā*): the root is वी गत्यादिषु (*vī gatyādiṣu*). The affix क्त (*kta*) in the passive. In the feminine, since the stem ends in a, टाप् (*ṭāp*) comes. By गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent comes on the गति (*gati*), that is प्र (*pra*).

जजान (*jajāna*): the root is जन जनने (*jana janane*). When the action of the causer appears, णिच् (*ṇic*) follows it. By छंदसिलुज् लज् लिटः (*chaṃdasiluj laj liṭaḥ*), in the sense of the imperative (लोडर्थ (*loḍartha*)), लिट् (*liṭ*). By the statement बहुलमन्यत्रापि संज्ञाछंदसोः (*bahulamanyatrāpi saṃjñāchaṃdasoḥ*) when लिट् (*liṭ*) follows, there is elision of णिचि (*ṇici*). Then, since it does not end in an affix, कास्‌प्रत्यया (*kāspratyayā*). *[The sūtra is quoted as supplied; the line breaks off here in the middle of a reference at the end of the supplied text of printed page 586.]*

### Printed p. 587

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, continued on printed page 587; pages 586 and 587.)* Continuation of the sūtra reference broken off on the previous page: (Sū. 3-1-35). By this the आम् (*ām*) does not come. With लिण्णिमित्त (*liṇṇimitta*) the root gets doubling and the like (the supplied text has here the word for “substitution” standing alone: आदेश (*ādeśa*)). Because the substitute is णित् (*ṇit*), by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) vṛddhi comes for the a of the penultimate of the root. Because it stands after the word printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the निघातस्वर (*nighātasvara*) accent comes.

अरुषस्तूपः (*aruṣastūpaḥ*): the explanation is न विद्यते रुषः क्रोधो यस्य इति अरुषः (*na vidyate ruṣaḥ krodho yasya iti aruṣaḥ*), which means shining without anger. By नञ् सुभ्यां (*nañ subhyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the accent with udātta on the end of the latter member comes. स्तूपः (*stūpaḥ*): the root is ष्टुञ् स्तुत् (*ṣṭuñ stut*). By स्तौतेर्धीर्घश्च (*stauterdhīrghaśca*) (U. Sū. 3-305) the affix प (*pa*). Since lengthening of the root and the quality कित् (*kit*) are prescribed together with it, guṇa does not come for the इकि (*iki*) of the root on account of the affix. स्तूयते इति स्तूपः तेजः संघः (*stūyate iti stūpaḥ tejaḥ saṃghaḥ*). अरुषः आरोचमानः तेजः संघः यस्य, अरुषस्तूपः (*aruṣaḥ ārocamānaḥ tejaḥ saṃghaḥ yasya, aruṣastūpaḥ*): in the bahuvrīhi, by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the पूर्वपद (*pūrvapada*) gets its original accent (प्रकृतिस्वर (*prakṛtisvara*)).

रुशत् (*ruśat*): the root is रुश हिंसायां (*ruśa hiṃsāyāṃ*). For लटि (*laṭi*) the शत्रादेश (*śatrādeśa*) comes; since the लसार्वधातुक (*lasārvadhātuka*) is anudātta, the धातुस्वर (*dhātusvara*) remains.

वयुने (*vayune*): the root is अज गतिक्षेपणयोः (*aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*). By अजियमिशीज्भ्यश्च (*ajiyamiśījbhyaśca*) (U. Sū. 3-341) the affix उनन् (*unan*) comes; it receives the designation चित् (*cit*). By अजेर्व्यघञपोः (*ajervyaghañapoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-56) the root gets the substitute वी (*vī*). On account of the affix, guṇa for its ikāra and the अयादेश (*ayādeśa*). अजति वीयते वा वयुनं (*ajati vīyate vā vayunaṃ*), that is the अंगं (*aṃgaṃ*). Since the affix is नित् (*nit*) , the आद्युदात्तस्वर (*ādyudāttasvara*) would be obtained, but here, by transposition, the आद्युदात्तस्वर (*ādyudāttasvara*) of the affix comes.

अजनिष्ट (*ajaniṣṭa*): the root is जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*). A form of लुज् (*luj*) in the प्रथमपुरुष (*prathamapuruṣa*) singular. Because it stands after a finite verb (अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*) as supplied), the निघातस्वर (*nighātasvara*) accent comes.

> जात॑वेदो॒ नि धी॑म॒ह्यग्ने॑ ह॒व्याय॒ वोळ्ह॑वे ॥ ४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, we priests place you on the uttaravedi, the central place of the earth and the place of Iḍā, to carry the oblation; the Brāhmaṇa is cited in support; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O one of born wisdom
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we (the priests)
- श्वा (*śvā*)—you (the supplied text prints this word where the Saṃhitā has त्वा (*tvā*); as supplied); पृथिव्या अधि (*pṛthivyā adhi*)—upon the earth
- नाभा (*nābhā*)—which is the central place; इळायाः पदे (*iḷāyāḥ pade*)—in the region of the uttaravedi; हव्याय वोळ्हवे (*havyāya voḷhave*)—for carrying the oblation in the form of पुरोडाशादिरूप (*puroḍāśādirūpa*); नि धीमहि (*ni dhīmahi*)—we establish you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni of born wisdom, we priests establish you, to carry the oblation in the form of पुरोडाशादिरूप (*puroḍāśādirūpa*), in the place of the uttaravedi, the central region of the earth. *[The label of this section is printed as the word ಭಾಷೆ; the standard label is supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni you are Jatavedas, we place you upon the earth in the centre, in the place of Ila, for the purpose of receiving the oblation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—This word expresses the meaning जातप्रज्ञ (*jātaprajña*), that is, Agni is all-knowing. Agni is addressed by this word.

पृथिव्याः अधि नाभा (*pṛthivyāḥ adhi nābhā*)—भूमेरुपरि उत्तरवेद्यां नाभौ तस्या नाभिस्थाने मध्यप्रदेशे (*bhūmerupari uttaravedyāṃ nābhau tasyā nābhisthāne madhyapradeśe*). The authors of the Nirukta have read the word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) among the names of the earth (Si. 2-5) and among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). [The first reference is printed with the abbreviation Si., not Ni.; as supplied.] And in the Ṛk बळित्वा पर्वतानां (*baḷitvā parvatānāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-84-1), explaining the word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) as पृथु दर्शनात् पृथिवी (*pṛthu darśanāt pṛthivī*), they describe it as मध्यमस्थाना (*madhyamasthānā*), the deity of the middle region. Sāyaṇa takes the meaning to be the earth and describes it as the uttaravedi, the central region of the sacrificial ground (the place of the navel), where Agni is placed. He explains the meaning of the word नाभि (*nābhi*) as वह्र्यतीति नाभिर्मध्यस्थानं (*vahryatīti nābhirmadhyasthānaṃ*). *[The bhāṣya reads नह्यतीति नाभिर्मध्यस्थानं (*nahyatīti nābhirmadhyasthānaṃ*); kept as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 589

इळायाः पदे त्वा हव्याय वोळ्पवे नि धीमहि (*iḷāyāḥ pade tvā havyāya voḷpave ni dhīmahi*)—मानव्या गोःपदे इडापद रूपे उत्तरवेद्यात्मके स्थाने पुरोडाशादिलक्षणं हविर्वोढुं निदधीमहि (*mānavyā goḥpade iḍāpada rūpe uttaravedyātmake sthāne puroḍāśādilakṣaṇaṃ havirvoḍhuṃ nidadhīmahi*). The authors of the Nirukta have read the word इळा (*iḷā*) among the names of creation (Si. 2-5), among the names of speech (printed वाङ्गाम (*vāṅgāma*)) (Si. 2-16), among the names of food (Si. 3-9), and in the phrase printed ಗೋನಾದ ಗಲ್ಲೆಯೂ (Si. 3-9). *[The references are printed with the abbreviation Si. and, in one place, without a full stop; the last phrase is unclear; as supplied.]* And they comment on ईट्टेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (*īṭṭeḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ*) that the word is derived from the root ई (*ī*) with the sense of praise. In the Ṛk अभि न इळा यूथस्य माता (*abhi na iḷā yūthasya mātā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-14-19, 20) the goddess named Iḍā is described as the deity of the middle region who forms the herd of clouds. Sāyaṇa takes the word इडा (*iḍā*) as related to the king named Manu and explains that, in the place of the sacrificial ground in the form of the uttaravedi of the cow (the word printed before “cow”, ಜ್ಯೋಧ್ಯವಾದ, is unclear; as supplied), the priests beginning with the adhvaryu will establish Agni to carry the oblation in the form of पुरोडाशादिरूप (*puroḍāśādirūpa*). He supports this view by citing the Brāhmaṇa sentence that conveys it: इळायास्त्वा पदे नाभा पृथिव्या आधीत्येतद्वा इळायास्पदं यदुत्तरवेदी नाभिर्जातवेदो निधीमहीति निधारयंतो ह्येनं भवंत्यग्ने हव्याय वोळ्पव इति हव्यं हि वर्क्ष्य भवति (*iḷāyāstvā pade nābhā pṛthivyā ādhītyetadvā iḷāyāspadaṃ yaduttaravedī nābhirjātavedo nidhīmahīti nidhārayaṃto hyenaṃ bhavaṃtyagne havyāya voḷpava iti havyaṃ hi varkṣya bhavati*) (Ai. Brā. 1-28).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed page 589.)* पदे (*pade*): a form of the locative singular. By the प्रादिपदिकस्वर (*prādipadikasvara*) it becomes final-udātta.

नाभा (*nābhā*): the root is णह बंधने (*ṇaha baṃdhane*). By नोनः (*nonaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-65) the initial gets नत्व (*natva*). When इञ् (*iñ*) continues by anuvṛtti from the preceding sūtra, by नहोभ्यश्च (*nahobhyaśca*) (U. Sū. 4-565) the affix इञ् (*iñ*) comes to this root, and for the हकार (*hakāra*) of the root the भकांडादेश (*bhakāṃḍādeśa*) comes . The form नाभि (*nābhi*) results. Because the affix is present , vṛddhi comes for the penultimate of the root, and the आद्युदात्तस्वर (*ādyudāttasvara*) comes. नह्यति इति नाभिः मध्यस्थानं (*nahyati iti nābhiḥ madhyasthānaṃ*) (it holds two parts of the body together). When the locative singular follows it, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute डादेश (*ḍādeśa*) comes for it; by the force of डित्व (*ḍitva*) there is elision of the ikāra.

धीमहि (*dhīmahi*): the root is डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). लिज् (*lij*) in the उत्तमपुरुष (*uttamapuruṣa*) plural, the affix महिज् (*mahij*). By लिजः सीयुट् (*lijaḥ sīyuṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-102) the augment सीयुट् (*sīyuṭ*) comes to it; by लोपोव्योर्वलि (*lopovyorvali*) the elision of य (*ya*). Because it is a part of the सार्वधातुक (*sārvadhātuka*), elision of the सकार (*sakāra*). Being Vedic (छांदस (*chāṃdasa*)), the doubling that would come on account of the श्लु विकरण (*ślu vikaraṇa*) does not come. The तिजंतनिघातस्वर (*tijaṃtanighātasvara*) accent comes.

वोळ्ळवे (*voḷḷave*): the root is वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*). When the sense of the infinitive affix appears (the supplied text runs the first word together; as supplied), by तुमर्थे सेसे (*tumarthe sese*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-9) the affix तवेन् (*taven*) comes. By सहिवहोरोदवर्णस्य (*sahivahorodavarṇasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-112) the ओकारादेश (*okārādeśa*) comes for the a of the root. By होढः (*hoḍhaḥ*) the ha becomes ḍha (ढत्व (*ḍhatva*)). By झषस्तथो (*jhaṣastatho*) the ta of the affix gets धत्व (*dhatva*) and ष्टुत्व (*ṣṭutva*). By डोढेलोपः (*ḍoḍhelopaḥ*) there is elision of the preceding ढकार (*ḍhakāra*). Since the affix is नित् (*nit*) , the आद्युदात्तस्वर (*ādyudāttasvara*) comes. Because it ends in एजंत (*ejaṃta*), by कृन्नेजंतः (*kṛnnejaṃtaḥ*) the designation अव्यय संज्ञा (*avyaya saṃjñā*) comes.
