In the grammar part of the bhāṣya block there is a stray syllable ನಾ at a line end before the word नरः (*naraḥ*), and in the citation of a sūtra a stray semicolon after ಪ್ರಾ;; kept as supplied.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests, the leaders of the rites, produce Agni by churning, the far-seeing, undivided in action, wise, immortal, bright-limbed one, and generate him at the start of the rite as the chief sign of the sacrifice; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरः (*naraḥ*)—O priests, the conductors of the rite
- कविं (*kaviṃ*)—the one who sees beyond
- अद्वयंतं (*advayaṃtaṃ*)—the one who has attained unity of rite through mind and through speech
- प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ*)—the one endowed with excellent knowledge *[the word breaks at the end of the page; continued on page 591]*

### Printed p. 591

*(Pratipadārtha, continued from page 590.)* अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—the one free from the nature of death; सुप्रतीकं (*supratīkaṃ*)—the one endowed with attractive limbs; अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni; मंथत (*maṃthata*)—produce by the act of churning; नरः (*naraḥ*)—you, the conductors of the rite; यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—for the sacrifice in the form of ज्योतिष्टोमादिरूप (*jyotiṣṭomādirūpa*); केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the indicator; प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—the one who is the chief limb; सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*)—the one endowed with excellent happiness, that Agni; पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—at the time of the beginning of the rite; जनयत (*janayata*)—cause to be produced.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, leaders of all rites: produce by the act of churning Agni, who sees beyond, who has gained unity of rite through mind and speech, who is endowed with excellent knowledge, free from the nature of death, and endowed with attractive limbs. And cause to be produced, at the time of the beginning of the rite, that Agni who is the indicator of the sacrifice in the form of ज्योतिष्टोमादिरूप (*jyotiṣṭomādirūpa*), the chief limb of it, and endowed with excellent happiness.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Conductors of the rite, produce by attrition the far-seeing, single-minded, intelligent, immortal, radiant-limbed Agni : generate him, leaders (of the solemnity), in the first place the chief standard of the sacrifice, who is the source of felicity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नर (*nara*)—Explaining the meaning of the word nara by the derivation नयंति कर्माणि, नीयंते कर्माण्यभिरिति वा (*nayaṃti karmāṇi, nīyaṃte karmāṇyabhiriti vā*), that is, those who perform the obligatory duties beginning with the sacrificial rite, or because the sacrificial rite and the like are performed by them, they have received the name nara; Sāyaṇa then describes the meaning कर्मणां नेतारो अध्वर्य्दायः (*karmaṇāṃ netāro adhvarydāyaḥ*) (the priests beginning with the adhvaryu, who perform the rites, are meant by the word nara here) and explains that by this word the priests beginning with the adhvaryu are addressed. *[The bhāṣya reads अध्वर्यादयः (*adhvaryādayaḥ*) here and कर्माण्येभिरिति (*karmāṇyebhiriti*); kept as supplied.]* Yāska has read this word among the names of men (Ni. 3-7) and explains the meaning of the word nara as नरा मनुष्या नृत्यंति कर्मसु (*narā manuṣyā nṛtyaṃti karmasu*) (Ni. 5-1).

कविं (*kaviṃ*)—क्रांतदर्शिनं (*krāṃtadarśinaṃ*). The word कवि (*kavi*) is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). Sāyaṇa explains that here it is used in the sense that Agni knows the end of the rites.

अद्वयंतं (*advayaṃtaṃ*)—द्वयं अनाचरंतं (*dvayaṃ anācaraṃtaṃ*): the meaning is stated that Agni (does not practise) makes no distinction in regard to those who resort to him and serve him; and, showing the reason in the matter of practising distinction, मनसा, वाचा, कर्मणा च एकविधमेव कर्म कुर्वाणं (*manasā, vācā, karmaṇā ca ekavidhameva karma kurvāṇaṃ*), he explains that Agni performs a rite of the nature of favour, of one kind alike in mind, speech and rite. *[The bhāṣya has मनसा वाचा चैकविधमेव कर्म (*manasā vācā caikavidhameva karma*), without the word for “and by rite”; kept as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 592

प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ*)—प्रकृष्टज्ञानोपेतं (*prakṛṣṭajñānopetaṃ*). Yāska, in the Ṛk अश्वाजनि प्रचेतसः (*aśvājani pracetasaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-13), explained the word प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*) as प्रवृद्धचेतसः (*pravṛddhacetasaḥ*). Sāyaṇa says that Agni is endowed with exceeding knowledge. *[The opening quotation mark before the Ṛk is printed, the closing one is missing; as supplied.]*

अमृतं सुप्रतीकं (*amṛtaṃ supratīkaṃ*)—Describing Agni as free from the nature of death, and as शोभनैरंगैर्ज्वालाभिः समेतं (*śobhanairaṃgairjvālābhiḥ sametaṃ*), endowed with flames that are like auspicious limbs, Sāyaṇa describes the command of the sacrificer, “produce this Agni by churning (मंथत (*maṃthata*)) in the two araṇis”, given to the priests beginning with the adhvaryu (printed ಅರ್ಥ್ವರ್ಯು, as supplied).

यज्ञस्य केतुं प्रथमं (*yajñasya ketuṃ prathamaṃ*)—ज्योतिष्टोमादेः प्रज्ञापकं, अग्निपूर्वकत्वात् सर्वेषामुत्तरक्रतूनां यज्ञानां मुख्यांगभूतं (*jyotiṣṭomādeḥ prajñāpakaṃ, agnipūrvakatvāt sarveṣāmuttarakratūnāṃ yajñānāṃ mukhyāṃgabhūtaṃ*). *[The word यज्ञानां (*yajñānāṃ*) stands here in addition to the bhāṣya; kept as supplied.]* The meaning is described thus: the word for sacrifice in general is used here in the sense of the kratus beginning with ज्योतिष्टोम (*jyotiṣṭoma*), in the form of क्रतु (*kratu*); Agni is the indicator (in regard to these sacrifices) in the correct performance of these sacrifices; and since all the kratus are performed through Agni alone, Agni is the chief limb of all the sacrifices.

सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*)—शोभनसुखोपेतं (*śobhanasukhopetaṃ*). *[This line is printed twice; the first time the word for “Yāska” stands as ಯಾಸುರು and the line breaks off; kept as supplied.]* यास्करु (*yāskaru*)—in the Ṛk अमीवहा वास्तोष्पते विश्वा रूपाण्याविशन् । सखा सुशेव एधि नः (*amīvahā vāstoṣpate viśvā rūpāṇyāviśan | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ*) (Ṛ Saṃ. 7-55-1), for the word सुशेव (*suśeva*) Yāska explains: शेव इति सुखनाम. शिष्यतेर्वकारो नामकरणो अंतस्थांतरोपलिंगी । विभाषितगुणः । शिवमित्यस्य भवति (*śeva iti sukhanāma. śiṣyatervakāro nāmakaraṇo aṃtasthāṃtaropaliṃgī | vibhāṣitaguṇaḥ | śivamityasya bhavati*). That is, since in the root शिषि (*śiṣi*) the letter va comes in place of the ṣa and guṇa comes for the i, the form शेव (*śeva*) results (instead of the form शिव (*śiva*), the letter e has come). Śeva means happiness. He explains the meaning of सुशेवः सुसुखः (*suśevaḥ susukhaḥ*) as one who has excellent happiness, or one who is enjoying excellent happiness.

पुरस्तात् जनयतः (*purastāt janayataḥ*)—कर्मणः प्रारंभे (*karmaṇaḥ prāraṃbhe*). *[The Saṃhitā has जनयत (*janayata*); the head word is printed जनयतः (*janayataḥ*); as supplied.]* The meaning described here is the command which the sacrificers give to the priests beginning with the adhvaryu: when the rites of the sacrifice are performed, first produce by churning in the araṇis, at the very time of the beginning of the sacrifice, Agni who is wise and knows the rites to the end, who through mind, speech and body bestows a fruit of one form, who is endowed with limbs in the form of flames, who is the standard of the sacrifices and has excellent happiness, so that he may bestow on us, the sacrificers, greatness of this kind.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, printed page 592.)* मंथत (*maṃthata*): the root is मंथ विलोडने (*maṃtha viloḍane*). A form of the लोट् (*loṭ*), second person plural (मध्यमपुरुष (*madhyamapuruṣa*)). Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the निघातस्वर (*nighātasvara*) accent does not come. In the Vedic manner lengthening comes in the Saṃhitā. By the sūtra तास्यनुदात्ते (*tāsyanudātte*), since the लसार्वधातुक (*lasārvadhātuka*) becomes anudātta, the धातुस्वर (*dhātusvara*) remains.

### Printed p. 593

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, continued from page 592.)* नरः (*naraḥ*): the root is णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*), a dhātu. By नयतेर्डिच्च (*nayaterḍicca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-157) the suffix ṛ is added to it. Since it is made ḍit, the ṭi of the root is dropped, and the form नृ (*nṛ*) results. नयंति कर्माणि, नीयंते कर्माणि एभिः इति वा नरः (*nayaṃti karmāṇi, nīyaṃte karmāṇi ebhiḥ iti vā naraḥ*) (those who carry out the work, or those by whom the work is accomplished). In the vocative, when jas follows, guṇa comes by ऋतोजि सर्वनामस्थानयोः (*ṛtoji sarvanāmasthānayoḥ*); the supplied text adds the word ರಸವಾಗಿ here, of unclear sense, kept as supplied. Because it has the designation āmantrita, the nighāta accent comes. *[The number of the Uṇādi sūtra printed here differs from the number cited in the bhāṣya on page 590; both kept as supplied.]*

अद्वयंतं (*advayaṃtaṃ*): when the sense "behaves like a pair" (द्वयमिव आचरति (*dvayamiva ācarati*)) is intended, by the vārttika सर्वप्रादिपदिकेभ्यः क्विब्वक्तव्यः (*sarvaprādipadikebhyaḥ kvibvaktavyaḥ*) the suffix kvip is added to the word द्वय (*dvaya*) in the sense of behaving. Because this is read in the group beginning with sana, the form ending in kvi receives the designation dhātu by सनाद्यंताधातवः (*sanādyaṃtādhātavaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-32). In kvip everything is dropped. When laṭ follows, the replacement śatṛ comes by लटः शतृशान (*laṭaḥ śatṛśāna*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124). द्वयति इति द्वयन् (*dvayati iti dvayan*); then अद्वयन् तं (*advayan taṃ*). In a tatpuruṣa, the prakṛti accent of the negative particle comes by तत्पुरुषेतु (*tatpuruṣetu*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1).

सुप्रतीकं (*supratīkaṃ*): शोभनं प्रतीकं यस्य सः तं (*śobhanaṃ pratīkaṃ yasya saḥ taṃ*). Because it belongs to the kratvādi group, in a bahuvrīhi the accent on the first syllable of the second member comes by क्रत्वादयश्च (*kratvādayaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-118). It is a form ending in the accusative singular.

जनयतः (*janayataḥ*) (the head word is printed so, as supplied): the root is जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*), a dhātu. The suffix ṇic comes by हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-24). When vṛddhi of the penultimate syllable is obtained by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*), then by the statement जनीज्यष् क्नसुरंजोमांताश्च (*janījyaṣ knasuraṃjomāṃtāśca*) this root is made mit, and so shortening of the penultimate comes by मितां ह्रस्वः (*mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-92). Loṭ follows the ṇic-ending root; in the second person plural the form जनयत (*janayata*) results. Because it stands after अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) (the supplied term, here taken to mean a word that is not a finite verb), the nighāta accent comes.

सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*): because the word शेव (*śeva*) ends in the Uṇādi suffix वन् (*van*), it has the accent on its first syllable. In a bahuvrīhi, the accent on the first syllable of the second member comes by आद्युदात्तं द्वैच् छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvaic chaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

If the priests beginning with the adhvaryu churn Agni with their own arms, the Agni thus born shines forth in the woods, swift and radiant, like a horse, and like the many-coloured chariot of the two Aśvins in its speed; unchecked, he burns stones and grasses and avoids the burnt places; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बाहुभिः (*bāhubhiḥ*)—with their hands; यदि मंथंति (*yadi maṃthaṃti*)—after (the priests) have churned, the Agni who is produced
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in wood and the like
- वाजी (*vājī*)—swift; अश्वो न (*aśvo na*)—like a horse
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—having a radiant form; आ वि रोचते (*ā vi rocate*)—shines exceedingly
- यामन् (*yāman*)—at the time of his movement
- अश्विनोः (*aśvinoḥ*)—of the Aśvin gods; चित्रो न (*citro na*)—like a chariot of varied colours
- अनिवृतः (*anivṛtaḥ*)—having an unobstructed movement (the supplied word is ಸಂಚಾಪುಳ್ಳವನಾಗಿ, as supplied)
- अश्मनः (*aśmanaḥ*)—stones
- तृणा (*tṛṇā*)—grasses
- दहन् (*dahan*)—burning; परि वृणक्ति (*pari vṛṇakti*)—moves all around (leaving the burnt place and going forward)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

After the priests have churned with their hands, the Agni who is produced shines exceedingly in wood and the like, like a swift horse, with a radiant form; and, like the chariot of the Aśvin gods with its varied colours, with an unobstructed movement, burning the stones and the grasses and leaving the burnt places and going forward, he moves all around. *[The word breaks at the end of the page (ಪ್ರಕಾ at the end of page 594, ಶಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ at the start of page 595); the sentence is continued on page 595.]*

### Printed p. 595

*(Bhāvārtha, continued from page 594.)*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
*[The label is printed in the garbled form English Ttranslation; the standard label is used.]*

When they rub (the sticks) with their arms the radiant Agni bursts forth from the wood like a fleet courser, and like the many-coloured car of the Ashwins unresisted in its course, Agni spreads wide around consuming stones and trees.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यदि बाहुभिः मंथंति वाजी वनेषु (*yadi bāhubhiḥ maṃthaṃti vājī vaneṣu*)—When the priests beginning with the adhvaryu churn with their hands so that Agni is produced, the Agni thus produced becomes pervading in the kāṣṭhas (pieces of wood); for the word वाजी (*vājī*) the meaning शीघ्रगमनवान् (*śīghragamanavān*) is described and explained.

अरुषः—आरोचमानः सर्वेषां प्रीतिकरः (*aruṣaḥ—ārocamānaḥ sarveṣāṃ prītikaraḥ*): describing Agni as shining on every side and giving joy to all, and regarding the speed with which his radiance spreads, he indicates the comparison अश्वो न (*aśvo na*). यथा अश्वः वनेषु बाह्यालीस्थानेषु वेगवानारोचमानः वर्तते तद्वत् (*yathā aśvaḥ vaneṣu bāhyālīsthāneṣu vegavānārocamānaḥ vartate tadvat*) The meaning is explained and the comparison made thus: as a horse of the best breed moves quickly in a wide region fit for roaming (in the pasture), so Agni spreads by his radiance. *[The supplied text has the garbled form ಸಂಚರಿಸುಶಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವ here; kept as supplied.]*

चित्रो न-वेगगमने देवभिषजोः नानाविधवर्णः रथः आरोचमानः वर्तते तद्वत् (*citro na-vegagamane devabhiṣajoḥ nānāvidhavarṇaḥ rathaḥ ārocamānaḥ vartate tadvat*)—regarding the very swift pervasion of Agni, and regarding his shining with light of many kinds, the chariot of the Aśvin gods is stated as the comparison and described.

अनिवृतः अश्मनः तृणा दहन् परि वृणक्ति (*anivṛtaḥ aśmanaḥ tṛṇā dahan pari vṛṇakti*)—केनाप्यप्रतिबद्धगमनः अग्निः उपलान् तृणानि च भस्मसात्कुर्वन् दग्धस्थानानि परितो वर्जयति (*kenāpyapratibaddhagamanaḥ agniḥ upalān tṛṇāni ca bhasmasātkurvan dagdhasthānāni parito varjayati*)—Because it is indicated that in this mantra Agni is described in the form of the forest fire, the meaning is explained thus: Agni, with a speed that nobody can check, burning even stones and grasses to ashes, leaves the regions he has burnt and spreads in the regions ahead. It is indicated that the terrestrial Agni is worshipped in many kinds of divisions, such as दावाग्नि (*dāvāgni*) and जातवेदाग्नि (*jātavedāgni*).

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

यदि (*yadi*): the lengthening in the Saṃhitā comes by निपातस्य च (*nipātasya ca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136). मंथंति (*maṃthaṃti*): the root is मंथ विलोडने (*maṃtha viloḍane*), a dhātu; the form is in the laṭ, third person plural. *[The page ends here with the word ಯದಿ; the grammar continues on page 596.]*

### Printed p. 596

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, continued from page 595; the sentence begins after the word yadi, with which page 595 ends.)* Because it stands before it, the prohibition of the nighāta accent comes by निपातैर्यद्यदि (*nipātairyadyadi*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30). Since the lasārvadhātuka becomes anudātta by the sūtra तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*), the dhātu accent remains.

रोचते (*rocate*): the root is रुच दीप्तौ (*ruca dīptau*), a dhātu of the bhvādi class; the form is in the laṭ, third person singular. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

यामन् (*yāman*): the root is या प्रापणे (*yā prāpaṇe*), a dhātu. Since it ends in ā, the suffix manin is added to it by आतो मनिन्‌क्वनिब्‌वनिपश्च (*āto maninkvanibvanipaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-74), and the word यामन् (*yāman*) results. When the seventh singular follows, the suffix is elided by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39); since it is nit, the accent on the first syllable comes by the statement इत्त्यादिर्नित्यं (*ittyādirnityaṃ*).

अनिवृतः (*anivṛtaḥ*): the root is वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*), a dhātu. The suffix kta is added by निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*); the prohibition of the augment iṭ comes by यस्य विभाषा (*yasya vibhāṣā*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-15). Since it is kit, guṇa does not come. The root vṛñ preceded by ni is used here in the sense of warding off. न निवृतः अनिवृतः (*na nivṛtaḥ anivṛtaḥ*); the accent on the first syllable comes by तत्पुरुषेतुल्या-र्थ (*tatpuruṣetulyā-rtha*) (Pā. Sū- 6-2-2). *[The reference is printed with a hyphen after Sū in the supplied text; kept as supplied.]*

वृणक्ति (*vṛṇakti*): the root is वृजी वर्जने (*vṛjī varjane*), a dhātu of the rudhādi class. In the laṭ, third person singular, the suffix tip is added. By चोःकुः (*coḥkuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-30) the j of the root becomes a velar (kutva). By खरिच (*kharica*) the replacement ca comes for it. By रुधादिभ्यः श्नं (*rudhādibhyaḥ śnaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78) the vikaraṇa śnam is added. Since it is mit, it comes after the last vowel (the supplied text has the word ಒರುತ್ತದೆ here, where ಬರುತ್ತದೆ would be expected; kept as supplied). Since it follows ṛ, ṇatva comes. Since there is the जित्वातिदेश (*jitvātideśa*) for it, guṇa does not come. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

तृणा (*tṛṇā*): the root is तृह हिंसायां (*tṛha hiṃsāyāṃ*), a dhātu. The suffix kṣa is added by तृहेः क्नोहलोपश्च (*tṛheḥ knohalopaśca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 5-686), and the h is dropped. Since the k of kṣa is dropped, guṇa does not come for the ṛ of the root. तृह्यते तत् गवादिभिरिति तृणं (*tṛhyate tat gavādibhiriti tṛṇaṃ*) (that which is injured by cows and the like through their eating). Because of the नित्यातिदेश (*nityātideśa*), the accent on the first syllable comes. *[The number of the Uṇādi sūtra printed here differs from the number cited in the bhāṣya on page 595; both kept as supplied.]*

दहन् (*dahan*): the root is दह भस्मीकरणे (*daha bhasmīkaraṇe*), a dhātu. For laṭ the replacement śatṛ comes. Since the lasārvadhātuka becomes anudātta by the sūtra तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*), the dhātu accent remains. The form is in the nominative singular.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, born after the churning, all-knowing, swift, wise in the rites, praised by the wise and a generous giver of the fruit of rites, shines; the gods placed him, the adorable, all-knowing bearer of oblations, in the sacrifices; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—produced after the churning, ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*)—worthy of praise, विश्वविदं (*viśvavidaṃ*)—knower of the whole world
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Agni
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—in sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma (the supplied text has an apostrophe in the middle of this word-group, as supplied)
- हव्यवाहं (*havyavāhaṃ*)—as the bearer of oblations
- अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)—they appointed (the supplied text adds a bracketed word, ಅಂತಃ)
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—produced after the churning
- चेकितानः (*cekitānaḥ*)—having excellent wisdom
- वाजी (*vājī*)—having a nature of constant movement
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—knowing the nature of rites (and therefore)
- कविशस्तः (*kaviśastaḥ*)—praised by the wise hotṛs
- सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)—a giver of the excellent fruit of rites
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- रोचते (*rocate*)—shines. *[In the supplied text the entry for the word ದೇವಾಸಃ carries the gloss of the word ಜಾತಃ (produced after the churning) and the glosses of the words that follow are run together; kept as supplied. The supplied text also has the garbled forms ಮೇಧಾಪಿಗಳಾದ here.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni whom the gods beginning with Indra appointed, in sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, as the bearer of oblations, worthy of praise and knowing the whole world, that Agni, who is produced after the churning, has excellent wisdom, a nature of constant movement, knows the nature of rites, and therefore is praised by the wise hotṛs and gives the excellent fruit of rites *[the supplied text has ಕರ್ಣ, split over a line, where ಕರ್ಮ is expected; kept as supplied]*, shines.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
*[The label is printed as English Translation. with a full stop; the standard label is used.]*

As soon as born Agni, shines intelligent, swift-moving, skilled in rites, praised by the wise, and liberal in gifts ; (and it is he) whom the gods have held as the bearer of oblations at sacrifices, adorable and all-knowing.

### Printed p. 598

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अग्निः जातः चेकितानः वाजी—मंथनानंतरसमुत्पन्नः अग्निः सर्वं जानानः, सततगमनस्वभावः (*agniḥ jātaḥ cekitānaḥ vājī—maṃthanānaṃtarasamutpannaḥ agniḥ sarvaṃ jānānaḥ, satatagamanasvabhāvaḥ*)—It is explained that Agni is produced after the churning of the araṇis and is a knowing one who knows everything. The word वाजी (*vājī*) is stated among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27), and Yāska has explained it, in the ṛk

नहि ग्रभायारणः सुशेवोऽन्यो दर्यो मनसा मन्तवा उ । अधा चिदोकः पुनरित्स एत्या नो वाज्यभीषाळेतु नव्यः (*nahi grabhāyāraṇaḥ suśevo 'nyo daryo manasā mantavā u | adhā cidokaḥ punaritsa etyā no vājyabhīṣāḷetu navyaḥ*)

(Mi. Saṃ. 7-4-8), as conveying the meaning "possessing speed" (वेजनवान् (*vejanavān*)). Durgācārya has explained the meaning वेजनर्वा परेभ्यो भयदाता (*vejanarvā parebhyo bhayadātā*) as "one who causes fear to enemies". For this word Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning that Agni has the nature of moving at all times. *[Printed oddity: the Sanskrit gloss of Durgācārya is printed with a break after a hyphen across two lines; the quotation is joined here.]*

विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—The word विप्र (*vipra*) is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). Sāyaṇa has described the meaning that Agni knows the nature of rites and the manner of performing them.

कविशस्त्रि (*kaviśastri*) (the head word is printed so, as supplied)—this word has been explained by the author of the Nirukta in the ṛk

उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोत्वज एकपात्पृथिवी समुद्रः । विश्वे देवा ऋतावृधो हुवानाः स्तुता मंत्राः कविशस्ता अवंतु (*uta no 'hirbudhnyaḥ śṛṇotvaja ekapātpṛthivī samudraḥ | viśve devā ṛtāvṛdho huvānāḥ stutā maṃtrāḥ kaviśastā avaṃtu*)

(Pu. Saṃ. 6-50-14) as कविशस्ता मेधाविशस्ताः (*kaviśastā medhāviśastāḥ*). Durgācārya has explained कविभिः मेधाविभिः शस्त्रैश्च शस्त्राः स्तुताः (*kavibhiḥ medhāvibhiḥ śastraiśca śastrāḥ stutāḥ*) as "praised by the wise, by the śastra mantras". Sāyaṇa has explained the word कवि (*kavi*) as the wise (hotṛs), the ṛtvij priests who perform the homa, and the meaning that Agni is praised by these priests.

Sāyaṇa explains that, because Agni bestows the fruit of rites abundantly, he is to be understood by the word सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*). Yāska has commented, in the ṛk असाम्योजो बिभृथा सुदानवः (*asāmyojo bibhṛthā sudānavaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-39-10), सुदानवः कल्याणदानाः (*sudānavaḥ kalyāṇadānāḥ*).

ईड्यं विश्वविदं (*īḍyaṃ viśvavidaṃ*)—The meaning is described and explained as follows: Agni is kindled and full of abundant greatness; he is worthy of being praised by the ṛtvij priests beginning with the hotṛ; he knows the whole created world; and the gods beginning with Indra have made this Agni the bearer of the oblations offered by the sacrificers in the rites beginning with the Jyotiṣṭoma. *[The supplied text has the form ಮಾಡಿಕೊಂಡಿರುವ with a missing ending where the sentence should read "have made"; kept as supplied.]*

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 7, continued from page 598.)* चेकितानः (*cekitānaḥ*): कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*), a dhātu. When yañ comes to it, luk comes to that (yañ) by यजोचिच (*yajocica*) . Because of yañ the root is doubled. By गुणोयज्लुकोः (*guṇoyajlukoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-82) guṇa comes for the ikāra of the reduplication. By व्यत्ययो बहुलं (*vyatyayo bahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-1-85) the replacement śānac comes for laṭ. By अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) the accent on the first syllable comes. *[The Pāṇini number is printed with four parts, 3-1-1-85, in the supplied text; kept as supplied.]*

कविशस्त्रः (*kaviśastraḥ*) (the head word is printed so again, as supplied): कविभिः शस्त्रः कविशस्त्रः (*kavibhiḥ śastraḥ kaviśastraḥ*); शंस स्तुत् (*śaṃsa stut*) , a dhātu. The suffix kta comes in the passive sense. By अनिदितां (*aniditāṃ*) the elision of the upadhā-nakāra takes place (the supplied text prints a word beginning with ಉಪಧಾನ, as supplied). By थाथघञ् क्ताजबित्रकाणां (*thāthaghañ ktājabitrakāṇāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-145) the accent on the last syllable comes.

देवासः (*devāsaḥ*): by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50) the augment asuk comes to jas. For the sakāra the visarga arising from ru comes.

ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*): ईड स्तुतौ (*īḍa stutau*), a dhātu. By ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (*ṛhalorṇyat*) the suffix ṇyat comes. By ईडमंदवृशंस- (*īḍamaṃdavṛśaṃsa-*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-214) the accent on the first syllable comes. *[The sūtra is printed broken over two lines and ending in a hyphen before the reference; kept as supplied.]*

विश्वविदं (*viśvavidaṃ*): विश्वं वेत्ति इति विश्ववित्, तं (*viśvaṃ vetti iti viśvavit, taṃ*) (the one who knows the whole world, him). विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*), a dhātu. The suffix kvip comes. The accent of the original form of the latter member after a kṛt comes (कृदुत्तर पदप्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛduttara padaprakṛtisvara*)). The form is in the accusative singular.

अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*): डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*), a dhātu. In the third person plural of laṅ the suffix jhi comes. Because of ślu the root is doubled. By सिचभ्यस्तविदिभ्यश्च (*sicabhyastavidibhyaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-109) the replacement jus comes for jhi. By उस्यपदांतात् (*usyapadāṃtāt*) the following form (para-rūpa) comes. The augment aṭ comes to the aṅga. Because there is a connection with the word yat, the prohibition of the nighāta accent comes by यद्वृत्तान्तित्यं (*yadvṛttāntityaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66). Since the augment aṭ is udātta, the accent on the first syllable comes.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer asks Agni to sit on the uttaravedi, establish the sacrificer in the best world, worship the gods with oblations and give abundant food; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—O accomplisher of the homa
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- स्वे (*sve*)—assigned to you
- लोके (*loke*)—in the region of the uttaravedi; सीद उ (*sīda u*)—(for the homa) sit down
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—you who are wise
- सुकृतस्य (*sukṛtasya*)—of the experience of happiness which is the fruit of good deeds
- योन् (*yon*)—in the sacrificial altar, the place of origin
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrificer, the performer of the sacrifice
- सादय (*sādaya*)—establish
- देवावीः (*devāvīḥ*)—(through the gift of oblations) you who are the protector of the gods
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblations of the form of puroḍāśa and the like
- देर्वा (*dervā*) —the gods
- यजासि (*yajāsi*)—worship
- यजमाने (*yajamāne*)—in me, the performer of the sacrifice
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—abundant
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- धाः (*dhāḥ*)—establish. *[The supplied text prints the word for the oblation as ಪುರೋಡಾರಾದಿರೂಪವುಳ್ಳ here; kept as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, accomplisher of the homa, sit down, for the homa, in the region of the uttaravedi assigned to you. You who are wise, establish the sacrificer, the performer of the sacrifice, in the sacrificial altar, the place of origin of the experience of happiness that is the fruit of good deeds *[the supplied text has the form ಯಜ್ಞನೇದಿ here, split over a line; kept as supplied]*. You who are the protector of the gods through the gift of oblations, worship the gods with oblations of the form of puroḍāśa and the like *[the supplied text has the form ಪುಶೋಡಾಶಾದಿ; kept as supplied]*. Establish abundant food in me, the performer of the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
*[The label is printed as English Translation. with a full stop; the standard label is used.]*

Offerer of oblations, sit down in your own sphere, for you are cognizant (of holy acts), and station the institutor of the ceremony in the chief place of the sacred rite : cherisher of the gods, worship the gods, Agni, and bestow abundant food on the founder of the sacrifice. *[The printed word cognizant is broken over two lines in the supplied text; joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

होतः अग्ने स्वे लोके सीद उ (*hotaḥ agne sve loke sīda u*)—The ṛtvij who calls the gods in the sacrifices, with the respective mantras, to accept the oblations is called a hotṛ. Agni carries the offered oblations to the respective gods and calls them so that he may deliver the oblations to each; understanding that he is therefore a hotṛ, Agni is addressed by this word. Sāyaṇa has explained for the word होतृ (*hotṛ*) the meaning होमनिष्पादक (*homaniṣpādaka*) (accomplisher of the homa), and that Agni is a hotṛ because he completes the homa; and that the word लोक (*loka*) is used in the sense of the middle region of the uttaravedi (the navel); and since this region is the seat of Agni, he has explained the meaning that Agni is seated in the middle of this uttaravedi. He has stated for the particle उ (*u*) the sense of emphasis, and has described the meaning that the wish of the sacrificer, that Agni should be seated in his own place, the middle region of the uttaravedi, is elaborated.

चिकित्वान् सुकृतस्य योन् यज्ञं साधय (*cikitvān sukṛtasya yon yajñaṃ sādhaya*)—the word चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*) is used in the sense of "knowing". The word यज्ञ (*yajña*) is stated in the sense of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice. The wish is described that Agni, who is knowing, may establish the sacrificer, the performer of the sacrifice, in the best world, which is the fruit of the performance of good action, so that he may experience its enjoyment. *[The heading is printed with the form ಸಾಧಯ, where the Saṃhitā has ಸಾದಯ; kept as supplied.]*

देवावीः (*devāvīḥ*)—देवान् हविष्पदानेन अवतीति (*devān haviṣpadānena avatīti*): Agni offers to the respective gods the oblations offered for the gods and protects them; therefore it is described that he is the one denoted by the word ದೇವಾವಿ . It is explained that the wish is described that this Agni may satisfy the gods with oblations which have the form of puroḍāśa.

यजमाने बृहत् वयः धाः (*yajamāne bṛhat vayaḥ dhāḥ*)—यागं कुर्वाणे मयि प्रभूतपशुपुत्रादिसमेतं अन्नं विधेहि (*yāgaṃ kurvāṇe mayi prabhūtapaśuputrādisametaṃ annaṃ vidhehi*). The word वयः (*vayaḥ*) is stated among the names of food (Ni. 3-19). The wish of the sacrificers is elaborated that Agni may bestow on the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice food accompanied by wealth of the form of abundant cattle, sons and the like.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

सीद (*sīda*): षद् विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣad viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*), a dhātu. In the second person singular of loṭ the suffix sip comes. The replacement hi comes for it. The vikaraṇa is śap. When this follows, the replacement sīda comes for the root by पाघ्राध्मास्था (*pāghrādhmāsthā*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78). By अतोहेः (*atoheḥ*) luk comes for hi. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. Since śap becomes anudātta, the dhātu accent remains.

सादय (*sādaya*): since the root stated above shows the action of the causer, the suffix ṇic comes by हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26). By आतउपधायाः (*ātaupadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) *[the page ends here in the middle of the sentence, after the word ಎಂಬುದರಿಂದ; the grammar continues on the next page. A stray line consisting of the numeral 76 in Latin digits follows at the end of the page in the supplied text; kept as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 602

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 8, continued from page 601.)* उपधावृद्धि (*upadhāvṛddhi*) (lengthening of the upadhā vowel). After the ṇyanta, in the second person singular of loṭ, the form sādaya results. Lengthening comes as a Vedic usage. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. Because the ṇic accent remains, it becomes madhyodātta.

देवावीः (*devāvīḥ*): अव रक्षणादिषु (*ava rakṣaṇādiṣu*), a dhātu. By अवित्यस्तंत्रिभ्य ईः (*avityastaṃtribhya īḥ*) (U. Sū. 4-438) this suffix ī comes. The form avī results. When su follows it, since it does not come in the position after ಜೀಪಿನ , elision does not come to it. Because the first member is a kāraka, the accent of the original form of the latter member after a kṛt (कृदुत्तरपद प्रकृतिस्वर (*kṛduttarapada prakṛtisvara*)) comes.

यजासि (*yajāsi*): यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु (*yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu*), a dhātu. In the second person singular of leṭ, sip. By लेटोडाटौ (*leṭoḍāṭau*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) the augment āḍ comes to it. Because it stands after an ಅತಿಜಂತ , the nighāta accent comes.

धाः (*dhāḥ*): डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*), a dhātu. When the sense of loṭ is shown, luj comes by छंदसिलुज् लज्लिटः (*chaṃdasiluj lajliṭaḥ*). The form ends in the second person singular. As a Vedic usage the augment aḍ does not come. The ತಿಜಂತ nighāta accent comes.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer tells the adhvaryu and the other priests to produce Agni, the showerer of desires, by churning, and to exert themselves in that contest; with this Agni the gods overcame the dasyus; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—O ṛtviks, helpers of the rite
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—the one who showers the desired objects, and धूमं (*dhūmaṃ*)—the one who is joined with smoke, that Agni
- कृणोत (*kṛṇota*)—(by the act of churning) cause to arise
- अस्रेधंतः (*asredhaṃtaḥ*)—you who have undiminished strength; वाजं अच्छ (*vājaṃ accha*)—looking to the battle of the form of churning
- इतन (*itana*)—be engaged
- येन (*yena*)—by whose help
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- दस्यून् (*dasyūn*)—the violent enemies
- असहंत (*asahaṃta*)—withstood and defeated; such
- सुवीरः (*suvīraḥ*)—endowed with excellent strength; आयं अग्निः (*āyaṃ agniḥ*) —this Agni
- पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*)—gains the strength to conquer enemies in battle. *[The supplied text has no closing stop after the last entry.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O ṛtviks, helpers of the rite, cause Agni, who showers the desired objects and is joined with smoke, to arise by the act of churning. You who have undiminished strength, be engaged in the battle of the form of churning. Then at once this Agni, endowed with excellent strength, by whose help the gods withstood and defeated the violent enemies, gains the strength to conquer enemies in battle.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
*[The label is printed as English Translation. with a full stop; the standard label is used.]*

Produce, friends, smoke, the showerer (of benefits); indefatigable persist in the contest with (Agni): the heroic Agni is able to encounter hosts, and by him the gods overcome their foes. *[The printed text is broken over lines in the supplied text; joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The sacrificer has addressed the adhvaryu and the other priests by the word सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*). Because these priests perform the work as helpers in the sacrificial rite, the meaning ಕರ್ಮಸಹಕಾರಿಣಿ is explained.

### Printed p. 604

धूमं (*dhūmaṃ*)—धुनोति कंपयति (दाह्यान्) इति धूमः अग्निः (*dhunoti kaṃpayati (dāhyān) iti dhūmaḥ agniḥ*): the word ಧೂಮ is used here with reference to Agni, since Agni shakes, causes to tremble, the things that burn, and so is denoted by the word dhūma; and since Agni fulfils the wishes of the sacrificers, the meaning वृषणं-कामानां वर्षितारं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ-kāmānāṃ varṣitāraṃ*) is explained. The sacrificer's wish is described that the priests may cause Agni, who has such greatness, to arise by churning.

अस्रेधंतः (*asredhaṃtaḥ*)—अक्षीणाः अनुपरतसामर्थ्याः (*akṣīṇāḥ anuparatasāmarthyāḥ*): when Agni is not produced by churning, the priests, increasing their strength, वाजं अच्छ इतन (*vājaṃ accha itana*). The sacrificer's command is described: carry out the battle of the form of churning and cause Agni to arise. Since the word ವಾಜ is stated by the Nirukta authors in the senses of food and strength, it is explained as a rite performed with great reliance on strength, and the meaning battle is given.

ಪೃತಸಾಷಾಟ್ (the head word is printed so, as supplied)—the word ಪೃತನಾ is stated among the names of battle (Ni. 39). Because Agni is one who bears the excess and the deficiency arising in battles, the meaning is explained that Agni is the one who can bear the rite, full of exceeding strength, that the priests perform for the production of Agni.

येन देवासः दस्यून् असहंत (*yena devāsaḥ dasyūn asahaṃta*)—having said that enemies are called by the word dasyu because they cause violence (दस्यंतीति दस्यवः (*dasyaṃtīti dasyavaḥ*)), it is explained that, because Agni grants strength to the gods so that they subdue the asuras who are their enemies, the sacrificer has told the priests that Agni can bear the rite performed with the use of strength when they churn Agni, and that the necessary duty of the form ಅಗ್ನಿಮಥನಕರಣರೂಪವಾಪ is stated.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

कृणोत (*kṛṇota*): कृवि हिंसाकारणयोः (*kṛvi hiṃsākāraṇayoḥ*) (the bhāṣya on page 603 spells the second word differently), a dhātu. By इदितोनुंधातोः (*iditonuṃdhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) the augment ಸುಮಾಗಮ . When the replacement ta has come for the second person plural of loṭ by तस्‌थस्थमिसां (*tasthasthamisāṃ*), then by तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च (*taptanaptanathanāśca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-45) the replacement tab comes to it again. By तनादिकृञ्भ्यउः (*tanādikṛñbhyauḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-79) the vikaraṇa u comes. Because tap is pit, guṇa comes for the ukāra by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*). Because it stands after ṛkāra, ṇatva comes for the nakāra. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. By the vikaraṇa accent it becomes madhyodātta.

धूमं (*dhūmaṃ*): धूञ् कंपने (*dhūñ kaṃpane*), a dhātu. By इषियुधींधिदसि (*iṣiyudhīṃdhidasi*) (U. Sū. 1-142) the suffix mak comes to it. Because it is kit (printed ಕಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ), guṇa does not come for the ukāra of the dhātu. धुनोति कंपयति दाह्यान् इति धूमः अग्निः (*dhunoti kaṃpayati dāhyān iti dhūmaḥ agniḥ*) (that which shakes what is burned, that is, fire). By the accent of the suffix it becomes antodātta.

### Printed p. 605

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

*(Grammar of Ṛk 9, continued from page 604.)* अस्त्रेधंतः (*astredhaṃtaḥ*): by the rule that in a tatpuruṣa compound with the sense of "equal" the accent of the original form of the first member comes (here after the negative nañ), that accent results.

इतन (*itana*): इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) , a dhātu. In loṭ the replacement ta comes for the second person plural. By तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च (*taptanaptanathanāśca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-45) the replacement tana comes to it. Because of सार्वधातुकमपित् (*sārvadhātukamapit*) it is treated as ṅit by extension, and so guṇa does not come to the dhātu. Because it stands after a finite verb, the nighāta accent comes.

पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*): षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*), a dhātu. By छंदसिसहः (*chaṃdasisahaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-63) the suffix ṇi comes to it. Because it is ṇit, by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) vṛddhi comes to the upadhā of the dhātu. By सहेः साडः सः (*saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-56) the sakāra of the dhātu at the end of the pada becomes ṣa; when su follows, the ha becomes ḍha, then jaśtva and cartva. By गतिकारकोपपदात् (*gatikārakopapadāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the original form of the latter member after a kṛt comes.

सुवीरः (*suvīraḥ*): by वीरवीर्यौच (*vīravīryauca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2920) the accent on the first syllable of the latter member comes in the bahuvrīhi.

असहंत (*asahaṃta*): षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*), a dhātu. In laṅ the replacement anta comes for the third person plural. The augment aṭ comes to the aṅga. Because the word yat is connected, the nighāta accent does not come. Because the augment aṭ is udātta, the form is ādyudātta.

दस्यून् (*dasyūn*): दसु उपक्षये (*dasu upakṣaye*), a dhātu. By यजिमनिशुंधिदसिजनिभ्यो युच् (*yajimaniśuṃdhidasijanibhyo yuc*) (U. Sū. 3-300) the suffix yuc comes to it. दस्यंतीति दस्यवः शत्रवः (*dasyaṃtīti dasyavaḥ śatravaḥ*) (those who cause affliction). Although the suffix is cit, by vyatyaya the word is ādyudātta.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is addressed: this seasonal churning-stick (araṇi) is your place of birth, from which you shone; knowing it, sit upon it and increase our praises, and make the praisers prosper; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ऋत्वियः (*ṛtviyaḥ*)—born in the seasons beginning with spring, (and) यतः (*yataḥ*)—from which
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—you who were born
- अरोचथाः (*arocathāḥ*)—shone, such too
- आयं (*āyaṃ*) —this araṇi pointed out here
- ते (*te*)—for you
- योनिः (*yoniḥ*)—is the place of birth
- जानन् (*jānan*)—you who know this
- तं (*taṃ*)—resorting to this araṇi
- आसीद (*āsīda*)—sit
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—speech in the form of praise
- वर्धय (*vardhaya*)—cause to increase (cause the praisers also to increase)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, this araṇi pointed out here, which is born in the seasons beginning with spring, and from which you, having been born, are shining, is your place of birth. Knowing this, be established in it. Afterwards cause our speech in the form of praise, and likewise us who are the praisers, to increase. *[The last word of the Kannada is printed ಮಾತು; the Pratipadārtha has the corresponding word ಮಾಡು; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
*[The label is printed as English Translation. with a full stop; the standard label is used.]*

This in every season, Agni, is your place, whence, as soon as generated, you have ever shone : knowing that to be so, Agni, there abide, and thrive by our praises. *[The printed text is broken over lines in the supplied text; joined here.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋत्वियः (*ṛtviyaḥ*)—वसंताद्यत्‌ भवः (*vasaṃtādyat bhavaḥ*) . Addressing Agni, it is described that Agni is born in the seasons beginning with spring and summer, and that for this Agni the araṇi, belonging to the palāśa (the muttuga tree) and the aśvattha tree, is the place of birth. Because Agni, born of these araṇis, is shining, the sacrificers' wish is described: तस्यामरण्यामारोपितः नैरंतर्येण तिष्ठ (*tasyāmaraṇyāmāropitaḥ nairaṃtaryeṇa tiṣṭha*), that is, may Agni remain hidden in the araṇis at all times.

### Printed p. 607

योनि: (*yoni:*)—उत्पत्तिस्थानः (*utpattisthānaḥ*). The word yoni is explained in the Nirukta: योनिरंतरिक्षं महानवयवः परिवीतो वायुना अयमपीतरो योनिरेतस्मादेव परियुतो भवति (*yoniraṃtarikṣaṃ mahānavayavaḥ parivīto vāyunā ayamapītaro yoniretasmādeva pariyuto bhavati*) (Ni. 2-8). Durgācārya has explained the meaning: भूतानां जायमानानां आकाशस्यॆव प्रदेशविशेषः कश्चित् वायुसंयुतः उदकयोनिभावं पुष्पाति (*bhūtānāṃ jāyamānānāṃ ākāśasyèva pradeśaviśeṣaḥ kaścit vāyusaṃyutaḥ udakayonibhāvaṃ puṣpāti*) : the region of the sky that is helpful to the beings that are born, being joined with air and a cause of the manifestation of water, is designated by the word yoni; and the female yoni, joined with flesh and sinew and a cause of the origin of the embryo, is also denoted by the word yoni. And the word yoni, formed from the dhātu yu, which denotes the act of mixing, has been explained in the sense of "place" through the general property of mixture. They have commented: अभियुत एनां गर्भः आमिश्रीभूतः (*abhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ āmiśrībhūtaḥ*). Since it is stated among the names of the house (Ni. 3-13), the meaning "house" is also described for yoni.

नः गिरः वर्धय (*naḥ giraḥ vardhaya*)—स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचः । यद्वा गीश्यब्देन तद्वंतो लक्षंते । स्तोत्यनस्मान् वर्धय (*stutilakṣaṇā vācaḥ | yadvā gīśyabdena tadvaṃto lakṣaṃte | stotyanasmān vardhaya*) . Yāska has read the word gīḥ among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23). And in मात्वा सोमस्य गल्लया सदा याचॆन्नहं गिरा (*mātvā somasya gallayā sadā yācènnahaṃ girā*) (Ma. Saṃ. 8-1-20) the meaning is described as गिरा गीत्या स्तुत्या (*girā gītyā stutyā*). *[The quotations above are printed in the supplied text with a short e (in the Durga quotation and in the mantra); kept as supplied.]* Sāyaṇa has given one kind of meaning, speech in the form of praise, so that Agni may increase the praises of the sacrificers; and in the second meaning, "those who have speech in the form of praise", so that Agni may increase the sacrificers who have such speech; thus he has described two kinds of meaning.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

योनिः (*yoniḥ*): यु मिश्रणे (*yu miśraṇe*), a dhātu. By वहिश्रिश्रु (*vahiśriśru*) (U. Sū. 4-491; the print gives the sūtra in this shortened form, as supplied) the suffix ni comes. By सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) guṇa comes for the ukāra of the dhātu. Because nit continues from the preceding sūtra, the ādyudātta accent comes.

ऋत्वियः (*ṛtviyaḥ*): the word ṛtu. By छंदसिघस् (*chaṃdasighas*) (Pā. Sū. 5-1-106) the suffix ghas comes to it in the sense "obtained". By आयनेयीनी (*āyaneyīnī*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-2) the replacement iya comes for it. By सितच (*sitaca*) (Pā. Sū. 1-4-16) the pada designation comes, so by ओर्गुणः (*orguṇaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-146), with the suffix as the cause, guṇa does not come to the preceding ukāra; yaṇ replacement. The suffix's ādyudātta accent comes.

अरोचथाः (*arocathāḥ*): रुच दीप्ति (*ruca dīpti*), a dhātu; the form is the second person singular of laṅ. By यद्वृत्तानित्यं (*yadvṛttānityaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) the nighāta accent is prohibited, so by the accent of the augment aṭ the form becomes ādyudātta.

### Printed p. 608

*(Grammar of Ṛk 10, continued from page 607.)* जानन् (*jānan*): ज्ञा अवबोधने (*jñā avabodhane*), a dhātu. In laṭ the शत्रादेश (*śatrādeśa*) comes; the vikaraṇa is श्ना (*śnā*). By ज्ञाजनोर्जा (*jñājanorjā*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-79) the जादेश (*jādeśa*) comes for the dhātu. By श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112) the ākāra of the vikaraṇa is dropped. The suffix's ādyudātta accent comes.

सीद (*sīda*): षद्ल विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadla viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*) , a dhātu. In loṭ, second person singular, by पाघ्राध्वा (*pāghrādhvā*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78) the सीदादेश (*sīdādeśa*) comes for the dhātu; by अतोहेः (*atoheḥ*) (no reference printed) the hi is dropped (luk). The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes.

अथा (*athā*): by निपातस्य च (*nipātasya ca*) (3-1-136; printed without the name of the work, as supplied) lengthening comes in the saṃhitā.

वर्धय (*vardhaya*): वृधु वर्धने (*vṛdhu vardhane*), a dhātu. Because the sense of prompting appears (the Kannada word is printed so, as supplied), by हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26) the suffix ṇic comes. By पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) guṇa comes for the light penultimate vowel of the dhātu. After the ṇic-ending form, in loṭ, second person singular, the form vardhaya results. Because it stands after a अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the nighāta accent comes. By the Vedic idiom, lengthening comes in the saṃhitā.

> यद्यदा मातर्यंतरिक्षे स्वं तेजोऽमिमीत निर्मिमीते तदा मातरिश्वा भवति । मा-
> तर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति चेष्टत इति व्युत्पत्तेः । एवंविधस्याग्नेः सरीमणि सरणे शीघ्र-

*[The bhāṣya block ends at the foot of the page in the middle of a word; it continues on the next page.]*

> गमने वातस्य वायोः सर्गः सृष्टिरभवत् । भवति । यदाग्निररणीषु गर्भरूपतया

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, while an embryo in the araṇis, is called Tanūnapāt; when born, Narāśaṃsa; when he shines in the sky, Mātariśvan; grammar follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—the Agni who is in embryonic form in the araṇis
- तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)—by the name “तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)”
- उच्यते (*ucyate*)—is called
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- विजायते (*vijāyate*)—when the Agni, produced from the araṇis, becomes plainly visible, then
- आसुरः (*āsuraḥ*)—the destroyer of the asuras
- नराशंसः (*narāśaṃsaḥ*)—famed by the name “नराशंस (*narāśaṃsa*)”
- भवति (*bhavati*)—he becomes
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- मातरि (*mātari*)—in the sky (antarikṣa)
- अमिमात (*amimāta*) —he creates (his radiance), then
- मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)—he is called by the name “मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)”
- सरीमणि (*sarīmaṇi*)—in the time of this Agni's movement
- वातस्य (*vātasya*)—of the wind
- सर्गः (*sargaḥ*)—the origin
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—came about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Agni is in embryonic form in the araṇis he is famed by the name “तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)”; when, produced from the araṇis, he becomes plainly visible, by the name “नराशंस (*narāśaṃsa*)”, the destroyer of the asuras; and when he creates his divine radiance in the sky, by the name “मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)”. In the time of this Agni's swift movement the origin of the wind came about.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गर्भः तनूपात् (*garbhaḥ tanūpāt*)—अरणीषु गर्भरूपतॆया अग्निः वर्तमानः तनूनपादित्युच्यते। यद्वा तनूशब्देनापो अभिधीयंते। नपातःशब्देनैकांतरिताः प्रजाः । तथा च अपां नप्ता । अपस्तता अंतरिक्षे । ताभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायंते तेभ्यो हैषः (*araṇīṣu garbharūpatèyā agniḥ vartamānaḥ tanūnapādityucyate| yadvā tanūśabdenāpo abhidhīyaṃte| napātaḥśabdenaikāṃtaritāḥ prajāḥ | tathā ca apāṃ naptā | apastatā aṃtarikṣe | tābhya oṣadhivanaspatayo jāyaṃte tebhyo haiṣaḥ*). *[The head is printed with the form just given, without the syllable na; as supplied. The quotation is printed with a short e sign in its second word group; kept as supplied.]* Agni, before being churned in the araṇis, while not yet manifest, is in embryonic form and is designated तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*): this is one kind of meaning that has been stated. In the second meaning the word तनू (*tanū*) is explained as waters, and by the word नपात् (*napāt*) the meaning “grandchildren” is stated. By this Agni is described as the grandson of the waters. The waters are in the sky; from them herbs and trees arise; and from these herbs or trees Agni arises: thus Agni's being अपां नप्तृत्व (*apāṃ naptṛtva*) is established, Sāyaṇa explains, and he has described the designation of Agni by the name तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*). *[The Kannada word for Agni in the last clause is printed with a long first vowel; as supplied.]*

तनूनपादाज्यमिति कात्थक्यः (*tanūnapādājyamiti kātthakyaḥ*) (Ni. 8-5). Having presented the view of those named Kātthakya, that by the word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) ājya (ghee) is stated, he has shown the explanation they give: नपादित्यनंतरायाः प्रजाया नामधेयं। गौरत्र तनूरुच्यते। तस्याः पयो जायते, पयसः आज्यं जायते (*napādityanaṃtarāyāḥ prajāyā nāmadheyaṃ| gauratra tanūrucyate| tasyāḥ payo jāyate, payasaḥ ājyaṃ jāyate*). By the word napāt the intervening (the Kannada word means “separated”) progeny is stated; by the word tanū the meaning “cow” is designated. Since from this cow milk arises, and from milk ājya, tanūnapāt means ājya, as they say. And further:

अग्निरिति शाकपूणि: (*agniriti śākapūṇi:*)—आपोऽत्र तन्न उच्यंते। तता अंतरिक्षेताभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायंते ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्य एष जायते (*āpo 'tra tanna ucyaṃte| tatā aṃtarikṣetābhya oṣadhivanaspatayo jāyaṃte oṣadhivanaspatibhya eṣa jāyate*). The ācārya named Śākapūṇi explains the word tanū as waters and says that after the waters in the sky have taken the state of rain, herbs and trees arise from them, and from the herbs and trees Agni arises. Sāyaṇa has accepted the view of the ācārya Śākapūṇi and made his commentary here accordingly.

यत् विजायते आसुरः नराशंसः भवति (*yat vijāyate āsuraḥ narāśaṃsaḥ bhavati*)—after Agni, having taken manifest form by the churning in the araṇis, has been born, he becomes कर्मविघ्नकारिणां असुराणां हंता (*karmavighnakāriṇāṃ asurāṇāṃ haṃtā*), the destroyer of the asuras who cause obstruction to the sacrificial rites; and, कर्मणां नेतृभिः अध्वर्यादिभिः शंसनीयः (*karmaṇāṃ netṛbhiḥ adhvaryādibhiḥ śaṃsanīyaḥ*), being worthy of praise by the priests such as the Adhvaryu who perform the sacrificial rites, he is designated by the name Narāśaṃsa; so it is described.

Yāska: नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यः नरा आसीनाः शंसंति । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः नरैः प्रशस्यो भवति (*narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyaḥ narā āsīnāḥ śaṃsaṃti | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ naraiḥ praśasyo bhavati*) (Ni. 8-7). The Kātthakyas say that, because those seated in the sacrificial hall (yāgaśālā) make praise *[the sentence breaks here at the foot of the page and continues on page 611]*

### Printed p. 611

the sacrifice, being the subject of the praise, is stated by the word Narāśaṃsa. Having presented this as one view, he explains the view of the ācārya Śākapūṇi, that Agni, who is worthy of the praise of those who perform the sacrificial rites in the sacrificial hall, is designated by the word Narāśaṃsa, and he has cited the ṛk “नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषां (*narāśaṃsasya mahimānameṣāṃ*)” as showing the power of Agni called Narāśaṃsa.

मातरि यत् अमिमित मातरिश्वा (*mātari yat amimita mātariśvā*)—यदा अंतरिक्षे स्वं तेजः निर्मिमिते तदा मातरिश्वा भवति । मातरि अंतरिक्षे श्वसिति चेष्टत इति (*yadā aṃtarikṣe svaṃ tejaḥ nirmimite tadā mātariśvā bhavati | mātari aṃtarikṣe śvasiti ceṣṭata iti*) . While Agni, in the sky, which like a mother is the abode of all beings, shines with his radiance, the Agni who pervades the sky itself in subtle form is called by the word मातरिश्व (*mātariśva*); so it is described.

Yāska: मातरि अंतरिक्षे श्वसिति मातर्याश्वनिति इति वा (*mātari aṃtarikṣe śvasiti mātaryāśvaniti iti vā*) (Ni. 7-26). Having explained the meaning of the word मातरिश्व (*mātariśva*) thus, he explains that by the word मातरिश्व (*mātariśva*) the wind is meant.

सरीमणि वातस्य सर्गः अभवत् (*sarīmaṇi vātasya sargaḥ abhavat*)—he explains that when Agni displays his state of swift movement, the creation of the wind has taken place.

यदा अग्निररणेषु गर्भरूपतया विद्यते तदा तनूनपात् नामको भवति । यदा जायते तदा नराशंसः । यदा अंतरिक्षे विद्योतते तदा मातरिश्वा भवति (*yadā agniraraṇeṣu garbharūpatayā vidyate tadā tanūnapāt nāmako bhavati | yadā jāyate tadā narāśaṃsaḥ | yadā aṃtarikṣe vidyotate tadā mātariśvā bhavati*). When Agni is hidden in the araṇis and not manifest, he receives the designation तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*). When manifest, he is designated Narāśaṃsa. When he shines in the sky with special brilliance (in the form of lightning-fire), he becomes मातरित्वन (*mātaritvana*) : the order in which the three kinds of names came to Agni is thus explained and established. (Yāska has said that the word मातरिश्वन् (*mātariśvan*) denotes the wind, and has explained that Vaiśvānara-fire arises from the wind itself; so a contradiction between these two statements is conceivable.) But by giving up the conventional meaning of the word मातरित्वन् (*mātaritvan*) and taking the etymological meaning, Agni is designated here by the word मातरिश्वन् (*mātariśvan*); thus the removal of the contradiction is to be understood.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)—तनु विस्तारे (*tanu vistāre*), a dhātu. By कृषिचमितनिधनिसर्जिखर्चिभ्य ऊः (*kṛṣicamitanidhanisarjikharcibhya ūḥ*) (U. Sū. 1-81) the suffix ū comes. By vyatyaya the word तनू (*tanū*) becomes ādyudātta. नपात् (*napāt*): पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*) or पत् ल्गतौ (*pat lgatau*) , a dhātu. After the ṇic-ending form the suffix kvip comes. नपातिन पातयति इति वा नपात् (*napātina pātayati iti vā napāt*) . By नभ्राण् नपात् नवेदा (*nabhrāṇ napāt navedā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-75), because it is made nipātana, the nañ keeps its original form (the loss of na does not come). तनूर्न पाति इति तनूनपात् (*tanūrna pāti iti tanūnapāt*). When the accent of the original form of the latter member after a kṛt would be obtained, by उभेवनस्पत्यादिषु युगपत् (*ubhevanaspatyādiṣu yugapat*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-140) the accent of the original form of both members comes.

### Printed p. 612

*(Grammar of Ṛk 11, continued from page 611.)* उच्यते (*ucyate*)—वच परिभाषणे (*vaca paribhāṣaṇe*), a dhātu. Laṭ in the passive, a form ending in the third person singular. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

आसुरः (*āsuraḥ*)—असुरस्य अयं आसुरः (*asurasya ayaṃ āsuraḥ*). By तस्येदं (*tasyedaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 4-3-120), when a relation of the nature of being harmful is shown, the suffix aṇ. By तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (*taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-117) ādivṛddhi. By यस्यॆतिच (*yasyètica*) (no reference printed; the word is printed with a short e sign, as supplied) the a before the suffix is dropped. By the accent of the suffix it becomes antodātta.

नराशंसः (*narāśaṃsaḥ*)—न्य नये (*nya naye*) , a dhātu. By यदोरप् (*yadorap*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-57) the suffix ap comes to it. By सार्वधातुका (*sārvadhātukā*) (the sūtra is printed in this broken form, as supplied) guṇa for the ṛkāra of the dhātu. Since the suffix is pit it is anudātta, and so by the dhātu accent the word becomes ādyudātta. शंसु स्तुतौ (*śaṃsu stutau*), a dhātu; the suffix ghañ. For the reason printed there in an unclear form , by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the ādyudātta accent comes. By अन्येषामपिदृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapidṛśyate*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137) lengthening comes for the former member (nara). Since it belongs to the vanaspatyādi group, by उभेवनस्पत्यादिषु (*ubhevanaspatyādiṣu*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-141) the original accent of both members comes. *[The number of this sūtra was printed with a different last figure on page 611; as supplied.]*

विजायते (*vijāyate*)—जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*), a dhātu, of the divādi class. In laṭ, third person singular, the suffix ta, and e-substitution for ṭa . By दिवादिभ्यःश्यन् (*divādibhyaḥśyan*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-69) the vikaraṇa śyan. By ज्ञाजनोर्जा (*jñājanorjā*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-79) the jā-substitution for the dhātu. Because of the yad connection the nighāta accent does not come. The lasārvadhātuka becomes anudātta by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) . Since śyan is sit, the dhātu accent remains. By तिजुचोदात्तवति (*tijucodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) the anudātta accent comes to the gati (vi).

अमिमात (*amimāta*)—माज् माने शब्दे च (*māj māne śabde ca*), a dhātu, of the juhotyādi class. In लज् (*laj*) , third person singular, the suffix ta. Because of the śluvikaraṇa, reduplication of the dhātu. By भृञामित् (*bhṛñāmit*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-76) the i-substitution for the abhyāsa. By ईहल्यघोः (*īhalyaghoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-113) the ī-substitution for the ākāra of the dhātu. The aḍāgama for the aṅga. Because of the yad connection the nighāta accent does not come; the accent of the aḍāgama remains.

सरीमणि (*sarīmaṇi*)—सृ गतौ (*sṛ gatau*), a dhātu. By हृभृस्पृसूभ्यः (*hṛbhṛspṛsūbhyaḥ*) (U. Sū. 4-587) the suffix īmanin comes to it. *[The sūtra is printed with a different letter group from the bhāṣya of page 609; as supplied.]* By सार्वधातुकार्थ (*sārvadhātukārtha*) guṇa for the ik of the dhātu; it comes with raparatva. The word सरीमन् (*sarīman*) results. Since the suffix is nit, by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the ādyudātta accent comes. A form ending in the seventh case singular.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is addressed as well churned and well placed, and is asked to make our rites free of harm and to worship the gods for the sacrificer.

*[In the bhāṣya block the word describing the placing on the northern altar is printed with a different ending from the same word in Special Topics on page 614; kept as supplied. The first word of the bhāṣya block (hē, the vocative particle) is printed with a short e sign; as supplied.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—you who are wise
- सुनिर्मथा (*sunirmathā*)—by the excellent act of churning
- निर्मथितः (*nirmathitaḥ*)—having been churned, you have arisen
- सुनिधा (*sunidhā*)—by a method performed with devotion
- निहितः (*nihitaḥ*)—you have been established
- स्वध्वरा (*svadhvarā*)—the rites that we perform, as free of harm
- कृणु (*kṛṇu*)—make
- देवयते (*devayate*)—for the sacrificer who seeks the help of the gods
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods Indra and the others
- यज (*yaja*)—worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you, the wise one (the Kannada word is printed with a different vowel sign from the Pratipadārtha; as supplied), have arisen, having been churned by the excellent act of churning. You have been established by a method performed with devotion. Make the rites that we perform free of harm. Worship Indra and the other gods for the sacrificer who seeks the help of the gods. *[The Bhāvārtha breaks off at the foot of the page in the middle of a word and continues on page 614.]*

### Printed p. 614

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni, you are pronounced by reverential attrition, and deposited with reverential care, and you are far-seeing, render our rites (exempt from defects), and worship the gods (on behalf) of the devout worshipper. *[The word defects is joined across the line end.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कविः सुनिर्मथा निर्मथितः (*kaviḥ sunirmathā nirmathitaḥ*)—मेधावी शोभनेन मथनेन नितरां मथितोऽसि (*medhāvī śobhanena mathanena nitarāṃ mathito 'si*). Addressing Agni, it is described that the wise Agni has been intensely churned in an auspicious manner with the churning stick in the araṇis.

सुनिधा निहितः (*sunidhā nihitaḥ*)—शोभनेन निधानेन उत्तरवेद्यादिस्थानेषु नितरां प्रक्षिप्तः (*śobhanena nidhānena uttaravedyādisthāneṣu nitarāṃ prakṣiptaḥ*). It is said that Agni has been placed (according to the rule, यथाविधि (*yathāvidhi*)), following the order stated in the injunction, by the sacrificers and the priests on the northern altar of the sacrificial hall.

सृध्वरा कृणु (*sṛdhvarā kṛṇu*) (the head is printed so, as supplied)—अस्माभिः क्रियामाणानि कर्माणि सुष्टु हिंसारहितानि कुरु (*asmābhiḥ kriyāmāṇāni karmāṇi suṣṭu hiṃsārahitāni kuru*). अध्वर इति यज्ञनाम ध्वरतिर्हिंसाकर्मा तत्प्रतिषेधः (*adhvara iti yajñanāma dhvaratirhiṃsākarmā tatpratiṣedhaḥ*) (Ni. 1-8). Yāska has listed the word अध्वर (*adhvara*) among the names of the sacrifice. The dhātu ध्वर (*dhvara*) conveys the meaning of doing violence; that act of violence is prohibited in the sacrifice, so he has explained. The sacrificers' wish is described: may Agni grant that the sacrificial rites performed by the sacrificers be free of acts in the form of violence.

देवयते यज (*devayate yaja*)—for the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice in order to gain the favour of the gods and to please them. Having explained thus the meaning of the word देवयते (*devayate*), he describes that Agni should worship, for the sacrificer, the gods who are fit for the sacrifice, Indra and the other gods. Yāska, in अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतः (*aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃtaḥ*), has explained the word देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*) as देर्वान् कामयमानाः (*dervān kāmayamānāḥ*) , that is, sacrificers who worship the gods in order to gain their favour. Following this, Sāyaṇa too has described the meaning.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

सुनिर्मथा (*sunirmathā*)—मथे विलोडने (*mathe viloḍane*), a dhātu. By संपदादिभ्यःक्विप् (*saṃpadādibhyaḥkvip*) the suffix kvip comes to it in the sense of bhāva. A prādi compound with सुनिर् (*sunir*). By गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the original accent of the latter member after a kṛt comes. *[The Kannada word for the latter member is printed as sada instead of pada; as supplied.]* A form ending in the third case singular. *[The grammar of Ṛk 12 begins at the foot of this page.]*

### Printed p. 615

*(Grammar of Ṛk 12, continued from page 614.)* निर्मथितः (*nirmathitaḥ*)—To the dhātu stated before, the suffix kta in the passive. By अनिदितांहल उ (*aniditāṃhala u*) (the sūtra is printed in this cut-off form, with no reference, as supplied) the loss of the letter n standing as upadhā. The augment iḍ for the suffix. By गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent comes to the gati (nir).

सुनिधा (*sunidhā*)—डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*), a dhātu. When the upasarga ni stands before it, by आतश्चोपसर्गे (*ātaścopasarge*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-106) the suffix aj in the sense of bhāva. By आतोलोपइटिच (*ātolopaiṭica*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64) the ākāra of the dhātu is dropped. When the feminine is intended, ṭāp. The kṛdutta-pada accent of the original form comes. When the third-case ending follows it, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) luk for that ending.

निहितः (*nihitaḥ*)—When the suffix kta follows the dhātu धाञ् (*dhāñ*), the substitute hi comes. By गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent comes to the gati (ni).

स्वध्वरा (*svadhvarā*)—By नञ्सुभ्यां (*nañsubhyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the accent making the end of the latter member udātta comes. By शेश्छंदसिबहुलं (*śeśchaṃdasibahulaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70) the loss of śi in the neuter.

कृणु (*kṛṇu*)—कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च (*kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca*), a dhātu. Loṭ. In the second person singular, the substitute hi for sip. By धिन्विक्रण्योरच (*dhinvikraṇyoraca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-80) the suffix u. Since it is idit, the augment सुमागम (*sumāgama*) for the dhātu; by उतश्च प्रत्ययादसंयोगपूर्वात् (*utaśca pratyayādasaṃyogapūrvāt*) (no reference printed) luk for hi. Since it follows ṛkāra, ṇatva for the nakāra. Since it follows an अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the nighāta accent comes.

देवयते (*devayate*)—On the word देव (*deva*), the suffix क्यच् (*kyac*) in the sense of wishing. When laṭ comes after the क्यजंत (*kyajaṃta*) , the substitute śatṛ for it. A form ending in the fourth case singular. By शतुरनुमोनद्यजादी (*śaturanumonadyajādī*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173) the udātta accent comes to the case ending.

यज (*yaja*)—यज देवपूजादिषु (*yaja devapūjādiṣu*), a dhātu. Loṭ, a form ending in the second person singular. The तिजंत (*tijaṃta*) nighāta accent comes.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The human priests cause Agni, deathless, undecaying and firm-toothed, to be born by churning; his ten fingers joined together sound with joy over him as people do at a son's birth.

*[Small differences in the bhāṣya block, kept as supplied: for example the word for "free of decay" is printed in the bhāṣya as क्षयरहिशं (*kṣayarahiśaṃ*); and the verb is printed in its explanation as आजीजनन् (*ājījanan*) and the word for the fingers as आग्रुवः (*āgruvaḥ*), whereas the Ṛk has अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*) and अग्रुवः (*agruvaḥ*).]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मर्त्यासः (*martyāsaḥ*)—the human priests
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—the one free from the nature of death
- अस्रेमाणं (*asremāṇaṃ*)—the one free from decay
- वीळुजंभं (*vīḷujaṃbhaṃ*)—the one who has firm teeth for eating the oblation
- तरणिं (*taraṇiṃ*)—Agni, who carries the sacrificers across sin
- अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*)—caused to be born; जातं अभि (*jātaṃ abhi*)—with reference to the born Agni
- स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—moving (engaged in the creation of Agni); दश आग्रुवः (*daśa āgruvaḥ*)—the ten fingers also
- समीचीः (*samīcīḥ*)—joining together
- पुमांसं (*pumāṃsaṃ*)—as fathers show joy at the birth festival of a son
- संरभंते (*saṃrabhaṃte*)—they make a sound and so proclaim him

### Printed p. 617

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The human priests caused Agni, who is free from the nature of death, free from decay, firm-toothed for eating the oblation, and the one who carries the sacrificers across sin, to be born. The ten fingers of their hands also, joining together and pointing to the born Agni, proclaim him, just as fathers proclaim the birth of their son at the birth festival of a son.

*[In the supplied text the English-translation label of this Ṛk is printed as "English Ttranslation" and stands directly after the Bhāvārtha; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Mortals have begotten the immortals, the undecaying (Agni), the devourer of oblations, the conveyance (by which they cross over sin), the ten sister fingers intertwined proclaim him born as if it was a male (infant).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मर्त्यासः (*martyāsaḥ*)—मर्त्याः ऋत्विजः (*martyāḥ ṛtvijaḥ*) The word मर्त्य (*martya*) is mentioned among the names of man (Ni. 3-8). Sāyaṇa has described the meaning as human priests.

अमृतं अस्रेमाणं वीळुजंभं (*amṛtaṃ asremāṇaṃ vīḷujaṃbhaṃ*)—The meaning of the word अमृत (*amṛta*) is explained: Agni is free from the nature of death. The word अस्रेमन् (*asreman*) is mentioned among the names of the praiseworthy (Ni. 3-13). Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "free from decay" and has described the sense that Agni is eternal, or without destruction. The word वीळु (*vīḷu*) is mentioned among the names of strength (Ni. 399). For हविर्भक्षणार्थं दृढदंतं (*havirbhakṣaṇārthaṃ dṛḍhadaṃtaṃ*) the meaning is given: one who has hard teeth for eating the oblation.

तरणिमजीजनन् (*taraṇimajījanan*)—तरणिः (*taraṇiḥ*) is mentioned by Yāska among the names of the swift (Ni. 7-9). Sāyaṇa, with तरंति यजमानाः पापमनेन (*taraṃti yajamānāḥ pāpamanena*), has explained that because the sacrificers shed their sins, Agni is the तरणि (*taraṇi*); and he has described the sense that Agni, endowed with abundant power, has been caused to be born by churning in the araṇis.

स्वसारः दश अग्रुवः (*svasāraḥ daśa agruvaḥ*)—समीचीः सं रभंते (*samīcīḥ saṃ rabhaṃte*)—With सुष्टु अस्यंति पदार्थान् (*suṣṭu asyaṃti padārthān*), the meaning of स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) is explained as: because they place things correctly. *[The word rendered "is explained" is printed as ನಿವೃತವಾಗಿದೆ; as supplied.]* The word अग्रुवः (*agruvaḥ*) is mentioned both among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-2-24) and among the names of fingers (Ni. 3-9). The word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) is mentioned among the names of fingers (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa has said जातमभिलक्ष्य सरंत्यः दशसंख्याकाः कर्मकरणार्थमग्रमंचंतीति अंगुलयः परस्परं संगताः शब्दं कुर्वते (*jātamabhilakṣya saraṃtyaḥ daśasaṃkhyākāḥ karmakaraṇārthamagramaṃcaṃtīti aṃgulayaḥ parasparaṃ saṃgatāḥ śabdaṃ kurvate*). *[The quotation is printed with small differences from the bhāṣya block; as supplied.]* Because they touch the foremost part in order to carry out the work, the ten fingers are famed as अग्रु (*agru*); having joined those ten fingers, Agni

*[The supplied text breaks off here, in the middle of a sentence, at the foot of this window; it continues in the next window. A stray line consisting of a number only follows the last line in the supplied text; kept as a note and not read as part of the sentence.]*

### Printed p. 618

*(Ṛk 13, Special Topics, continued from page 617; the sentence begun there continues:)* as soon as he is born the priests make a sound (clap their hands). With जातमग्निं दृष्ट्वा अध्वर्य्वादयो हर्षात् हस्तद्वयसंपुटेन शब्दं कुर्वंति (*jātamagniṃ dṛṣṭvā adhvaryvādayo harṣāt hastadvayasaṃpuṭena śabdaṃ kurvaṃti*) he has explained the meaning.

पुमांसं (*pumāṃsaṃ*)—यथा जातं पुत्रमुपलभ्य तत्रत्याः पित्रादयो हर्षात् उद्भोषंति तद्वत् (*yathā jātaṃ putramupalabhya tatratyāḥ pitrādayo harṣāt udbhoṣaṃti tadvat*). Just as the father and others, seeing that a male child has been born, make a sound with joy, so the priests beginning with the Adhvaryu make a sound as soon as Agni is born; thus the birth of a son is stated as an example, to indicate joy.

##### Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)

अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*)—जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*), a dhātu. In the causative sense the suffix ṇic; after the ṇic-ending form, luṅ. In the third person plural the suffix jhi; loss of the final; substitution of the end. By णिश्रिद्रुसुभ्यः कर्तरिचज् (*ṇiśridrusubhyaḥ kartaricaj*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-48) the substitution चणादेश (*caṇādeśa*) for च्छि (*cchi*) . By चजि (*caji*) the reduplication of the dhātu. Since there is सन्नद्भाव (*sannadbhāva*) , lengthening of the abhyāsa of the dhātu. Since it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. Since the aḍāgama is udātta, the word becomes ādyudātta.

अस्रेमाणं (*asremāṇaṃ*)—स्त्रिवु गतिशोषणयोः (*strivu gatiśoṣaṇayoḥ*), a dhātu (printed with a different letter group from the bhāṣya; as supplied). To it, in the sense of bhāva, the suffix मसिन् (*masin*) . By पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasyaca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) guṇa for the light upadhā of the dhātu. By लोपोव्योर्वलि (*lopovyorvali*) loss of the letter va. By नञ्सुभ्यां (*nañsubhyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the accent that makes the end of the latter member udātta comes in a bahuvrīhi compound. *[The word for "in the compound" is printed ಸಮಾಸಪಲ್ಲಿ; as supplied.]*

तरणिं (*taraṇiṃ*)—तृ प्लवनतरणयोः (*tṛ plavanataraṇayoḥ*), a dhātu. By अर्तिसृधृधम्यम्याश्यवित्यभ्योनिः (*artisṛdhṛdhamyamyāśyavityabhyoniḥ*) (U. Sū. 2-259) the suffix ani. By सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārthadhātukayoḥ*) (no reference printed) guṇa for the ṛkāra of the dhātu. By अट् कुप्वाज् नु (*aṭ kupvāj nu*) (no reference printed) ṇatva for the nakāra of the suffix. The ādyudātta accent of the suffix comes.

स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—असु क्षेपणे (*asu kṣepaṇe*), a dhātu. By सुञ्यासेर्यन् (*suñyāseryan*) (U. Sū. 2-253) the suffix ṛn to it. सुष्टु अस्यंति कर्मसु पदार्थान् इति स्वसारः (*suṣṭu asyaṃti karmasu padārthān iti svasāraḥ*). Yaṇ-substitution for the ukāra of su. Although स्वसृ (*svasṛ*) ends in ṛkāra, in the feminine there is a prohibition by नषट् स्वस्रादिभ्यः (*naṣaṭ svasrādibhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-10), so जीप् (*jīp*) does not come. Since the suffix is nit, the ādyudātta accent comes.

अग्रुवः (*agruvaḥ*)—अगि गत् (*agi gat*), a dhātu . By जत्वादयश्च (*jatvādayaśca*) (U. Sū. 4-542) the suffix ru. Since it is idit, the numāgama; by nipātana loss of that nakāra. The word अग्रु (*agru*) results. When jas follows, since it is read in the tanvādi group, the उवजादेश (*uvajādeśa*) comes. The accent of the suffix comes.

समीचीः (*samīcīḥ*)—इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), a dhātu. When saṃ stands before it, by समीणः (*samīṇaḥ*) (4-532) the suffix caṭ. Lengthening for the dhātu. Since the suffix is ṭit, when the feminine is intended

*(Grammar of Ṛk 13, continued from page 618.)* by टिड्ढाणञ् द्वयसच् (*ṭiḍḍhāṇañ dvayasac*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-15) जीप् (*jīp*). संयंतीति समीच्यः (*saṃyaṃtīti samīcyaḥ*); or, to the dhātu अंचु (*aṃcu*) (गतिपूजनयोः (*gatipūjanayoḥ*)) preceded by saṃ, the suffix क्विप् (*kvip*). By समः समि (*samaḥ sami*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-93) the substitution samy for saṃ. In the statement अंचतेश्चोपसंख्यानं (*aṃcateścopasaṃkhyānaṃ*) जीप् (*jīp*) in the feminine. Since the bha-designation is there, by अचः (*acaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-138) loss of the ākāra of the dhātu (the word for "of the dhātu" is printed with a stray letter; as supplied). By चौ (*cau*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-138) lengthening of what precedes. When a case ending follows, by वाछंदसि (*vāchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-106) pūrvasavarṇa lengthening. By the ekādeśa accent the ī becomes udātta.

पुमांसं (*pumāṃsaṃ*)—पा रक्षके (*pā rakṣake*), a dhātu . By पातेर्डु०सुन् (*pāterḍu0sun*) (U. Sū. 4-617) the suffix डु०सुन् (*ḍu0sun*) . By the power of ḍitva, loss of the ṭi of the dhātu. The word पुन्स् (*puns*) results. When the second case singular follows, by पुंसोसुज् (*puṃsosuj*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-89) the substitution asuc. पाति कुलमिति पुमान् (*pāti kulamiti pumān*) (one who protects his own family). Since the suffix is nit, the ādyudātta accent comes.

रभंते (*rabhaṃte*)—रभ शब्दे (*rabha śabde*), a dhātu. Laṭ, a form ending in the third person plural. Since it stands after an अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*) , the nighāta accent comes.
