having made (it) of even position; सदने (*sadane*)—in its own place; नि ससत्थ (*ni sasattha*)—you have established (it); वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—you, the showerer of desires; द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heaven; अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the sky; अस्तभ्नात् (*astabhnāt*)—you have held up, so that it does not fall down; त्वया (*tvayā*)—by you; प्रसूताः (*prasūtāḥ*)—impelled; आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters; इह (*iha*)—here, on this earth; अर्षंतु (*arṣaṃtu*)—let them fall and flow.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you have made the earth, which is great, endless and moves in one and the same circle, even in position, and have established it in its own place. You, the showerer of desires, have held up the heaven and the sky so that they do not fall down. Let the waters impelled by you fall and flow on this earth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You have fixed tranquil in its position the vast unbounded and wandering earth : the showerer (of benefit:) has upheld the heaven and the firmament : let the waters engendered by you here descend.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the cloud, which was weighed down by the water and was the refuge of the middle speech, split open in fear before the blow of your thunderbolt came. Then Indra made excellent paths so that the waters might come out and flow. Immediately,

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, alone and unaided, has filled both heaven and earth, which are joined and rich in wealth; he is asked, as lord of the chariot, to drive his horses from the sky to us. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words वसुमती (*vasumatī*), पप्रौ (*paprau*), इषः (*iṣaḥ*) and रथीः (*rathīḥ*) are analysed (lengthening, perfect, suffix, accent).

- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—alone, without the help of another
- समीची (*samīcī*)—both joined together, and
- वसुमती (*vasumatī*)—endowed with wealth
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- उत (*uta*)—and *[the entry continues on page 701]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, alone and without the help of another, has completely pervaded both heaven and earth, which are joined together and endowed with wealth. O Indra, endowed with strength, you who have a chariot, wishing to come near us, drive towards us from the sky the horses brought together and yoked to your chariot.

*[The supplied text has ದ್ಯಾವಾಪೃಥಿನಿಗಳೆರಡನ್ನೂ for "the two, heaven and earth"; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra alone has filled the two, both earth and heaven mutually combined, and abounding with wealth: you O hero, mounted in your car, come with your harnessed horses from the firmament, impatient to be near us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरश्वप्रसूताः (*haraśvaprasūtāḥ*)—impelled by Indra, who has the horses called Hari
- दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)—every day
- प्रदिष्टाः (*pradiṣṭāḥ*)—and assigned for the sun's going
- दिशः (*diśaḥ*)—the directions beginning with the east
- सूर‍्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun; न मिनाति (*na mināti*)—does not harm
- यत् (*yat*)—when (the sun)
- अध्वनः (*adhvanaḥ*)—the paths he has to travel
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—with his horses; सं आनट् (*saṃ ānaṭ*)—traverses completely

- विमोचनं (*vimocanaṃ*)—the unyoking of his horses

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sun does not harm the directions beginning with the east, which are impelled by Indra, who has the horses called Hari, and are assigned every day for the sun's going. When the sun fully traverses the paths he has to travel with his horses, he then unyokes his horses.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Surya harms not the quarters (of the horizon), set open daily (for his journey), the progeny of Haryashwa : when he has traversed the roads (he is to travel), then he lets loose his horses, for such is his office.

> सनि ज्ञाश्रुस्मृदृशां सनः । पा. १-३-५७ । इत्यात्मनेपदं । अभ्यस्तस्वरः । विवस्वत्माः ।
> विवासतेः संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । व्यत्ययेनोपधाह्रस्वत्वं । तस्मात्तदस्यास्ति ति
> मतुष् । मादुपधाया इति तस्य वत्वं । मतुपः पित्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ।
> जानंति । ज्ञा अवबोधने । ज्ञा जनोर्जेति जादेशः । निघातः । अगात् । इण् गतु-
> वित्सस्य लुजु रूपं । यद्योगादनिघातः । सुकृता । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृति-
> स्वरत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All people, at the departing of the dawn, wish to see the great and variegated light of the sun; when the dawn has come they know their great rites; the many good works are Indra's. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words दिदृक्षंते (*didṛkṣaṃte*), विवस्वत्माः (*vivasvatmāḥ*), जानंति (*jānaṃti*), अगात् (*agāt*) and सुकृता (*sukṛtā*) are analysed (desiderative, middle voice, suffixes, substitution, accent). The bhāṣya has a stray Latin digit after the word for night, and विवस्वत्माः (*vivasvatmāḥ*) where the Pratipadārtha has विवस्वत्याः (*vivasvatyāḥ*); as supplied. The bhāṣya also has the short vowel sign of Kannada in सर्वॆ (*sarvè*) and रात्रॆ (*rātrè*); both as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- विवस्वत्याः (*vivasvatyāḥ*)—passing away
- अक्टो (*akṭo*)—of the night
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—of the dawn
- यामन् (*yāman*)—at the time of departure
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—of many colours (or delightful)
- अनेकं (*anekaṃ*)—the light of the sun
- दिदृक्षंते (*didṛkṣaṃte*)—they wish to see
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- आगात् (*āgāt*)—the time of dawn arrives
- महिना (*mahinā*)—the great rites such as the Agnihotra
- जानंति (*jānaṃti*)—people know
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—of many kinds; सुकृता कर्म (*sukṛtā karma*)—all the good rites
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—are to be done by the power of Indra alone

*[In the Pratipadārtha the word for night is followed by a stray digit (eight in Kannada numerals), and the entry for अक्टो (*akṭo*) reads as supplied; the last entry has no closing stroke.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the departing time of the dawn, which belongs to the night that is passing away, everyone wishes to see the great and many-coloured light of the sun. As soon as the time of dawn has come, people know that the great rites such as the Agnihotra are to be performed. All the rites of many kinds, performed in the excellent manner, are to be accomplished by the power of Indra alone.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
All men are anxious to behold the great and variegated host (of the solar rays) at the issuing of the dawn after the night has been displaced ; and when the morning has come, they recognize the many great and glorious acts of Indra.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The great and bright water in the rivers has been placed by Indra. Because Indra placed in the cow, for eating, all this tasty curd, milk and the rest, gathered in itself, by that water, therefore the cow that has just calved, bearing milk and the rest, roams everywhere.

A great light has been shed upon the rivers : the cow yet immature grazes, charged with the ripe (milk), for Indra has placed in the cow all this collected sweetness for food.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, since the asuras who obstruct the path are on the way, be firm of mind and mighty. Give the desired fruits to the sacrificer, who performs the sacrifice and praises you, and to his sons and other kinsmen. The enemies who keep evil weapons, move crookedly, are violent and keep arrows and quiver must first be destroyed.

*[The Bhāvārtha begins with a misprinted word group, "ರ್ಮಾಕ್ಕೆ", before the word for obstruction; kept as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, be firm, for there are obstructors of (your) path : secure to the worshipper and his friends (the means of completing) the sacrifice : mortal enemies bearing bows, armed with mischievous weapons, and coming with evil intent, must be destroyed (by you).

> जहि । मारय । अनंतरमिमं यज्ञं रंधयस्व । पारं नय ॥ शृण्वे । निघातः । जहि ।
> हन हिंसागत्योः । अस्य लोटि रूपं। अशनिं । अशू व्याप्तौ । आश्यवित्यभ्योऽनिरित्यनि-
> प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । तपिष्ठां । तप्तृशब्दादिष्ठन्नृत्ययः । नित्सर्वः । वृश्च । ओव्रत्तू
> छेदने । तुदादिः । ग्रहिज्यादिना संप्रसारणं । सहस्व । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः । रंधयस्व ।
> रथ हिंसासंराद्योरित्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लोटि रधिजभोरचीति नुडागमः । वाक्यभेदा-
> दनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the roar of the thunderbolt flung by the near foes is clearly heard; hurl your burning bolt on them, cut them at the root, overcome them, slay the demons and bring the sacrifice to its end. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words शृण्वे (*śṛṇve*), जहि (*jahi*), अशनिं (*aśaniṃ*), तपिष्ठां (*tapiṣṭhāṃ*), वृश्च (*vṛśca*), सहस्व (*sahasva*) and रंधयस्व (*raṃdhayasva*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent).

- अमित्रैः (*amitraiḥ*)—foes
- घोषः (*ghoṣaḥ*)—the sound (of the weapons); सं शृण्वे (*saṃ śṛṇve*)—is well heard

- अशनिं (*aśaniṃ*)—your thunderbolt

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the roar of your thunderbolt is clearly heard by the foes who are near. Hurl the burning thunderbolt on these foes. Harm them, defeat them, cut them at the root and push them down. O Indra, destroy the demons and bring our sacrifice to full completion.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sound (of your bolt) has deen [sic] heard by the approaching foes: hurl upon them the consuming thunderbolt, cut them up by the root, oppose, Maghavan, overcome, slay the *Rakshasas* complete (the sacrifice),

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, uproot the obstructing demons, cut their middle, drive the roaming one far away and hurl your burning weapon at the Brahmin-hater. Yāska's explanation is quoted (Nirukta, printed reference Ni. 63). Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words वृह (*vṛha*), शृणीहि (*śṛṇīhi*), कीवतः (*kīvataḥ*), सललूकं (*salalūkaṃ*), चकर्थ (*cakartha*), तपुषिं (*tapuṣiṃ*) and हेतिं (*hetiṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, substitution, accent). The bhāṣya has a stray exclamation mark in its grammar part and the short vowel sign of Kannada in two words (one in the bhāṣya text, one in the quoted Nirukta passage); as supplied.

- रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)—the demons (who obstruct the rite)
- सहमूलं (*sahamūlaṃ*)—together with the root
- उद्वृह (*udvṛha*)—pull up (destroy)
- मध्यं (*madhyaṃ*)—the middle region of their lineage
- वृश्च (*vṛśca*)—cut
- प्रत्यग्रं (*pratyagraṃ*)—the front part
- शृणीहि (*śṛṇīhi*)—destroy
- सललूकं (*salalūkaṃ*)—the asura who roams at will; आ कीवतः (*ā kīvataḥ*)—to a very remote region
- चकर्थ (*cakartha*)—drive away
- ब्रह्मद्विषे (*brahmadviṣe*)—upon the demon who hates Brahmins

### Printed p. 709

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroy the demons who obstruct the rite, together with the root. Cut them in the middle and destroy their front part. Drive the asuras who roam at will to a very distant region. Hurl your burning weapon at the demon who hates Brahmins.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Pluck up the *Rakshasas*, Indra, by the root ; cut asunder the middle, blight the summit : to whatever remote (regions) you have driven the sinner, cast upon the enemy of the Veda your consuming weapon.

> कुरु । स्वस्तये चाविनाशाय कुरु । यदा त्वं समसत्सि अस्माकं समीपे यज्ञनि-

> नित्यत्वादिडभावः । चित्स्वरः । स्याम । अस भुवीत्यस्य लिजु रूपं । अस्मे । अस्मच्छब्दस्य
> सप्तम्याः सुपां सुलुगिति शे इत्यादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, leader of the world, make us rich in horses and secure; when you sit near us at the sacrifice may we be great, enjoying food and riches, and may wealth with offspring be ours. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words आसत्सि (*āsatsi*), वंतारः (*vaṃtāraḥ*), स्याम (*syāma*) and अस्मे (*asme*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent, substitution).

- प्रणेतः (*praṇetaḥ*)—the excellent guide
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra; स्वस्तये च (*svastaye ca*)—for our welfare

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, excellent guide, make us possessed of horses for our future welfare. When you sit facing us for the conduct of the sacrifice, we become men of great standing, enjoying abundant food and abundant riches. And may wealth together with sons be full in us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Regulator (of the world, provide us) with horses for our welfare, and when you are seated near to us may we become mighty, enjoying abundant food, and ample riches, and may there be to us wealth accompanied by progeny,

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, bring us splendid wealth; we are fit recipients of the gift of you who love to give; our desire has spread like the submarine fire; satisfy it with abundant wealth, lord of riches. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words देष्टस्य (*deṣṭasya*), धीमहि (*dhīmahi*), ऊर्व इव (*ūrva iva*), पप्रथॆ (*paprathè*), पृण (*pṛṇa*) and वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent, substitution). The word for "of the generous one" is spelled in the bhāṣya with a different consonant from the Saṃhitā, Pada and Pratipadārtha, and the word for "has spread" carries the short vowel sign of Kannada in the bhāṣya (two places); as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- द्युमंतं (*dyumaṃtaṃ*)—splendid
- भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—wealth; आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring
- देष्णस्य (*deṣṇasya*)—of the generous giver
- ते (*te*)—your
- प्ररेके (*prareke*)—to the gift; नि धीमहि (*ni dhīmahi*)—we are fit recipients
- अस्मे (*asme*)—our
- कामः (*kāmaḥ*)—desire; ऊर्व इव (*ūrva iva*)—like the submarine fire
- पप्रथे (*paprathe*)—is abundant
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—among riches
- वसुपते (*vasupate*)—lord of the best wealth, O Indra
- तं (*taṃ*)—that (desire of ours); आ पृण (*ā pṛṇa*)—satisfy (with the gift of abundant wealth)

*[A stray full stop stands inside the entry for "of the generous giver", as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bring us splendid wealth. We are fit recipients of the gift of you, the generous giver. Our desire is abundant like the submarine fire. O Indra, lord of the best wealth, satisfy this boundless desire of ours with the gift of abundant wealth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Bring to us, Indra, splendid affluence : we rely on the bounty of you who are fond of giving: our desire is as insatiable as the fire of the ocean : appease it, lord of infinite riches.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, gratify this desire of ours with cows, horses and shining wealth and make us renowned; the Kuśikas, skilled priests desiring heaven, offer you praise with thoughtful hymns. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words मंदय (*maṃdaya*), गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*), पप्रथः (*paprathaḥ*) and अक्रन् (*akran*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent, elision). The bhāṣya has a stray exclamation mark after one word and spells the word for "desiring heaven" differently from the Saṃhitā and the Pada; as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra); इमं कामं (*imaṃ kāmaṃ*)—this desire of ours
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with cows
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—with horses
- चंद्रवता (*caṃdravatā*)—shining; राधसा च (*rādhasā ca*)—also by giving wealth
- मंदय (*maṃdaya*)—gratify (afterwards)
- स्वरवः (*svaravaḥ*)—those who desire heaven

- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—accompanied by thoughtful
- वाहः (*vāhaḥ*)—praise
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you
- अक्रन् (*akran*)—will offer

*[Variants as supplied: the entry for "shining" is spelled differently from the Bhāvārtha; the entry for "also by giving wealth" has a word broken by a line end in an unusual spelling; the entry for "those who desire heaven" differs in spelling from the Saṃhitā and Pada.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, by giving us cows, horses and shining wealth, gratify all our desires. Afterwards your devotees, who desire heaven, are skilled in ritual and belong to the Kuśika lineage, offer you praise accompanied by hymns fit for reflection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Gratify this our desire (of wealth) with cows, with horses, with shining treasure, and make us renowned : the wise Kushikas, desirous of heaven, offer praise to you, Indra, with pious (prayers).

*[The printed English has the word "shining" broken across two lines with a hyphen; joined here.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, lord of heaven, split the clouds and bring water for us; then may praiseworthy foods come to us; you pervade the sky, are true in strength and rich; be a giver of cows to us. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words दर्दृहि (*dardṛhi*), गाः (*gāḥ*), अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*), यंतु (*yaṃtu*), दिवक्षाः (*divakṣāḥ*) and गोदाः (*godāḥ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent), with two printed Pāṇini references (Pā. 7-4-92 and Pā. 6-1-93). The bhāṣya has the word for "true in strength" ending differently from the Saṃhitā and Pada, and a garbled word before the words for "understand well"; as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गोपते (*gopate*)—O Indra, lord of heaven
- नः (*naḥ*)—for our convenience
- गोत्रा (*gotrā*)—the clouds
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—for water; अ दर्दृहि (*a dardṛhi*)—squeeze (make the water pour; then, as its result)
- सनयः (*sanayaḥ*)—praiseworthy
- वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)—foods
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us; सं यंतु (*saṃ yaṃtu*)—come in full
- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—O Indra, showerer of desires; दिवक्षाः आसि (*divakṣāḥ āsi*)—you, pervading the whole sky (and being great), are (therefore)
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- गोदाः (*godāḥ*)—as a giver of cows; सु बोधि (*su bodhi*)—resolve and understand

### Printed p. 714

*[The Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 21 was complete at the end of the previous page; this page begins with the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 21.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of heaven, for our convenience squeeze the clouds and make the water pour down. Then, as the result of that, may venerable foods come to us. O Indra, showerer of desires and wealthy one, you pervade the whole sky (ಅಂರಿಕ್ಷ, so printed, with a letter missing) and are therefore great. For that very reason, become one who has cows given to us, and in the same way make the resolve.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, lord of cattle, (divide the clouds and send us) rain, whence nutritious food may come to us : showerer (of benefits), you are spread through the sky, and powerful through truth ; Maghavan, consider yourself as our protector.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We call you, Indra, wealthy leader of the world, who hear our praise, terrify foes, slay demons in battles and win their wealth, for protection. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words शुनं (*śunaṃ*), हुवेम (*huvema*), भरे (*bhare*), वाजसात् (*vājasāt*), समत्तु (*samattu*), घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*) and संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent, elision). The bhāṣya has a garbled letter group at the start of the grammar of the first of these words, spells the word for "in battles" with a different consonant from the Saṃhitā, and has a few other irregular spellings in the grammar; as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra)
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—proceeding for the sake of food
- भरे (*bhare*)—in the battle
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—(by zeal) growing, or producing happiness
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—wealthy
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—(supremely) rich in lordship
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—leader; you who are such
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call with prayer; (and likewise) शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—(our praises) hearing
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—terrible to enemies
- समत्तु (*samattu*)—in battles
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—Vṛtra and other demons
- घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)—killing and destroying
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—the (enemies') wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in the battle that is fought for the sake of food, you who produce happiness, are wealthy, endowed with the highest lordship, a leader, who hear our praises, are terrible to enemies, kill and destroy Vṛtra and the other demons in battles and gather the enemies' wealth for us: you we call with prayer for our protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat; the leader in the foodbestowing [sic] (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

**The thirty-first sūkta** (ಮೂವತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, which begins with शासद्वह्निः (*śāsadvahniḥ*), is the second sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are twenty-two Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: शासत् कुशको विश्वामित्र एव वा श्रुतेरिति (*śāsat kuśako viśvāmitra eva vā śruteriti*) *[the second word is printed so, differently from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]*. The seer of this sūkta is Kuśika, the son of Iṣīratha, or Viśrāmitra himself *[so printed; the bhāṣya block and the particulars have Viśvāmitra]*; Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. On the twenty-fourth day of the sacrifice, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras to be recited by the ṛtvij called Acchāvāka, this sūkta is to be recited as the Ūrdhvamahīna-sūkta that is recited at the beginning; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra अस्मा इदु प्र तवसे शासद्वह्निरितीतरावहीनसूक्ते (*asmā idu pra tavase śāsadvahniritītarāvahīnasūkte*) *[the first word is printed so, differently from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]* (Ā. 7-4).

Further, on the first day of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭhaśi and Abhiplavaṣaḍaha, at the midday pressing, the ṛtvij called Acchāvāka must recite three Sampāta-sūktas in the place of the Ahīna-sūkta; of these three sūktas this one is the third Sampāta-sūkta. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra इमामू ष्टिच्छंति त्वा शासद्वह्निरिति संपाताः (*imāmū ṣṭicchaṃti tvā śāsadvahniriti saṃpātāḥ*) *[the third letter group of the second word is printed so, differently from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]* (Ā. 7-5).

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 31 *[a line with this number stands before the sūkta data; as supplied]*. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 31. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 2; Varga 5, 6, 7, 8. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 22. Seer: विश्वामित्रः कुशिको वा (*viśvāmitraḥ kuśiko vā*). Devatā: इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*). Chandas: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

A sonless father gives his daughter to a son-in-law whom he honours, so that her son counts as his own; Yāska says the same. The bhāṣya cites a smṛti passage (Vāsi. 17-17) and Yāska (Ni. 3-4). In the gloss of the last word the bhāṣya reads ಸಂದಧನ್ನೇ, with a different consonant from the Saṃhitā. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words शासत् (*śāsat*), दुहितुः (*duhituḥ*), नप्तं (*naptaṃ*), गात् (*gāt*), ऋंजन् (*ṛṃjan*), शग्मन (*śagmana*) and दधन्वे (*dadhanve*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent, elision). Printed spellings are kept as supplied; one word in the grammar of the bhāṣya carries the Kannada short e vowel sign inside the Sanskrit, kept as printed.

### Printed p. 718

*[This page begins with the Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 1; the Saṃhitā, Pada and Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Ṛk 1 were given on the previous pages.]*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—the father who is to hand over (his daughter to the son-in-law). शासत् (*śāsat*)—giving the instruction (that the son of his own daughter will be a son to him also). विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—himself knowing it in the same way. यतस्य (*yatasya*)—the semen that produces a son *[the headword is printed ಯತಸ್ಯ, with a different first letter from the Saṃhitā word; as supplied]*. दीधितिं (*dīdhitiṃ*)—the son-in-law who has taken (her) over. सपर्यन् (*saparyan*)—honouring and treating with respect. नप्तं गात् (*naptaṃ gāt*)—he becomes father to the grandson *[the gloss is printed ನಪ್ತ್ವಿಗೆ ಪಿತನಾಗುತ್ತಾನೆ; as supplied]*. दुहितुः पिता (*duhituḥ pitā*)—the son-in-law, who is the protector of (his) daughter. सेकं (*sekaṃ*)—(in her) the pouring of semen. ऋंजन् (*ṛṃjan*)—bringing about. शग्मैन (*śagmaina*)—with a mind whose cause is happiness. सं दधन्वे (*saṃ dadhanve*)—he unites with her.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The father who hands over his daughter to a son-in-law gives the instruction that the son of his own daughter will be a son to him also; with the same thought he honours with ornaments and other courtesies the son-in-law who begets a son on his own daughter, and (having given him his daughter) he stands in the position of father to his own grandson *[the word for "grandson" is printed ನಪ್ತಿವಿಗೆ, followed by the explanation (ಮೊಮ್ಮೊಗನಿಗೆ); as supplied]*. His son-in-law, for his part, begetting seed in her, unites with her out of desire for his own happiness.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sonless father, regulating (the contract), refers to his grandson, (the son) of his daughter, and relying on the efficiency of the rite, honours (his son-in-law) with valuable gifts : the father, trusting to the impregnation of the daughter, supports himself with a tranquil mind.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—अपुत्रो यः पिता कन्यामन्यकुलं प्रापयति स वह्निरित्युच्यते । (*aputro yaḥ pitā kanyāmanyakulaṃ prāpayati sa vahnirityucyate |*) A man without a son gives his daughter in marriage to a young man of another family (gotra). He does so with the intention that the son born in that daughter (the daughter's son) will be like a son to him. Such a father of a girl is called वह्निः (*vahniḥ*): in this way the commentator has explained the meaning of the word वह्नि (*vahni*). The verse:

अपुत्रस्य पितुः पुत्री दायादा पुत्रिका सती । (*aputrasya pituḥ putrī dāyādā putrikā satī |*)
यतः संतानकृत्तस्याः पुत्र इत्यनयोच्यते ॥ (*yataḥ saṃtānakṛttasyāḥ putra ityanayocyate ‖*)

To a father who has no son but has obtained only a daughter, the daughter herself is said to be the son. For through this daughter offspring arise and his line grows. In the Vāsiṣṭha-smṛti:

अभ्रातृकां प्रदास्यामि तुभ्यं कन्यामलंकृतां । (*abhrātṛkāṃ pradāsyāmi tubhyaṃ kanyāmalaṃkṛtāṃ |*)
अस्यां यो जायते पुत्रः स मे पुत्रो भवेदिति ॥ (*asyāṃ yo jāyate putraḥ sa me putro bhavediti ‖*)

(Vāsiṣṭhaskṛti 17-17) *[the title is printed ವಾಸಿಷ್ಠಸ್ಕೃತಿ, with a different letter from the one in the name of the same work a few lines above; as supplied]*

### Printed p. 719

*[The sentence continues from the previous page.]*

This is what is said. That is, this sentence was spoken by the father of the girl to the son-in-law when giving the girl in marriage: "I shall give you in marriage this my daughter, adorned *[printed ಸಾಲಾಂಕೃತಳಾದ; as supplied]* and without brothers. The son born in her will be to me also equal to a son"; that is, "through this may my line grow"; this is its purport. Explaining this matter, the English scholar Wilson has spoken thus:

The latter (वह्नि (*vahni*) 8) is said to be the father of a daughter only, not of a son, because he conveys away (वहति, प्रापयति (*vahati, prāpayati*)) his property through his married daughter into another family ; शासत्, शस्ति (*śāsat, śasti*)—he stipulates, that his daughter's son. *[sic]* his grandson महितुर्नप्तं (*mahiturnaptaṃ*) shall be his son, a mode of affiliation recognised by law ; and relying on an heir thus obtained, and one who can perform his funeral rites, he is satisfied.

*[In the Wilson passage the Sanskrit words are printed in Kannada script; the word after "daughter's" is printed ಮಹಿತುರ್ನಪ್ತಂ, with a different first letter from the Saṃhitā word for "of the daughter"; the number 8 after the first word and the full stop after "son" are as supplied.]*

Yāska has stated the etymology in connection with this ṛk (Ni. 3-3) *[printed ಯಾರು ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನ, "who", where Yāska is evidently meant; as supplied]*:

अथैनां दुहितृदायाद्य उदाहरंति । प्रत्रदायाद्य इत्येके ॥ (*athaināṃ duhitṛdāyādya udāharaṃti | pratradāyādya ityeke ‖*) *[the second word of the second line is printed ಪ್ರತ್ರದಾಯಾದ್ಯ; as supplied]*
शासद्वह्निर्दुहितुर्नप्तंगाद्विद्या ऋतस्य धीधितिं सपर्यन् । (*śāsadvahnirduhiturnaptaṃgādvidyā ṛtasya dhīdhitiṃ saparyan |*)
पिता यत्र दुहितुः सेकमृंजन्संशग्मन मनसा दधन्वे ॥ (*pitā yatra duhituḥ sekamṛṃjansaṃśagmana manasā dadhanve ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-13-1) *[as printed: the sūkta number is printed 13, while this ṛk stands in Sūkta 31; this quotation of the ṛk differs in several letters from the Saṃhitā block above; as supplied]*

दुहिता दुर्हिता दूरे हिता । दोग्धेर्वा ॥ (*duhitā durhitā dūre hitā | dogdhervā ‖*)
नप्तारमुपागमद्दौ हित्रं पौत्रमिति । (*naptāramupāgamaddau hitraṃ pautramiti |*)
विद्वान् प्रजननयज्ञस्य रेतसो ना अंगादंगात्संभूतस्य हृदयादधिजातस्य मातरि प्रत्यृतस्य । विधानं पूजयन्नविशेषेण मिथुनाः पुत्रा दायादा इति ॥ (*vidvān prajananayajñasya retaso nā aṃgādaṃgātsaṃbhūtasya hṛdayādadhijātasya mātari pratyṛtasya | vidhānaṃ pūjayannaviśeṣeṇa mithunāḥ putrā dāyādā iti ‖*)
तदेतदृक्लोकाभ्यामभ्युक्तं (*tadetadṛklokābhyāmabhyuktaṃ*)—this is also stated in a ṛk and a śloka:

अंगादंगात्संभवसि हृदयादधि जायसे । (*aṃgādaṃgātsaṃbhavasi hṛdayādadhi jāyase |*)
आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि स जीव शरदः शतं ॥ (*ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śataṃ ‖*)

(Gobhilagṛhya. Sū. 2-8-21 and Tai. Ā.)

अविशेषेण पुत्राणां दायो भवति धर्मतः । (*aviśeṣeṇa putrāṇāṃ dāyo bhavati dharmataḥ |*)
मिथुनानां विसर्गादौ मनुः स्वायंभुवोऽब्रवीत् ॥ (*mithunānāṃ visargādau manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt ‖*)
न दुहितर इत्येके । तस्मात्पुमान् दायादोऽदायादा स्त्रीति विज्ञायते । (*na duhitara ityeke | tasmātpumān dāyādo 'dāyādā strīti vijñāyate |*)
तस्मात्त्रियं परास्यंति न पुमांसमिति च ॥ स्त्रीणां दानविक्रयाति सर्गा विद्यंते न पुंसः ॥ (*tasmāttriyaṃ parāsyaṃti na pumāṃsamiti ca ‖ strīṇāṃ dānavikrayāti sargā vidyaṃte na puṃsaḥ ‖*)

अभ्रातृमतीवाद इत्यपरं ॥ (*abhrātṛmatīvāda ityaparaṃ ‖*)

(Ni. 3-3, 4, 5)

*[The Sanskrit quotations of this and the previous page are given in full and are not summarised; their spellings are as supplied.]*

Now let us examine the matter of the दुहितृदायादि (*duhitṛdāyādi*) (heirs through the daughter), that is, the increase of offspring through the daughter. If a man has a son and a daughter, then through them the increase of that man's offspring takes place, that is, the increase of his line. By usage, the offspring produced by a son are called पुत्रदायादि (*putradāyādi*) and the offspring produced by a daughter दुहितृदायादि (*duhitṛdāyādi*). Here it is necessary to explain the meaning of the word दायाद (*dāyāda*). दाय (*dāya*) means the share in the property that falls to a son or a daughter. ಮಿಯಾ + ಅದಃ = ದಾಯಾದಃ *[as printed; the first member is printed ಮಿಯಾ; as supplied]*: a son or daughter who has the right to enjoy that share of property is customarily called दायाद (*dāyāda*). In the present ṛk the matter of the दुहितृदायादि (*duhitṛdāyādi*) is stated.

Some experts in the dharmaśāstra say that it is just that the daughter, like the son, should receive a दायभाग (*dāyabhāga*). The father of the girl, when giving his daughter in marriage to a man of another gotra, holds the assurance that the son born in his daughter will be equal to a son for him also, that is, that after his death the son will perform the funeral and other rites as sons do; and having performed that marriage by the prescribed rite, he obtains peace of mind. The son-in-law, too, agrees that the son born in his wife may be like a son to his father-in-law. Here Yāska has explained the word दुहितृ (*duhitṛ*) as follows: because it is difficult to arrange for the welfare of one's daughter, or because the daughter (after marriage) leaves one's neighbourhood and lives far away (that is, in her husband's house), the daughter is called दुहितृ (*duhitṛ*). Or, he has stated the etymology that the word may be formed from the root दुह् (*duh*) (to milk; the root is printed ದುಹ್ (ಹಾಲನ್ನು) ಕರಿ) which suggests that, as a cow gives milk, the daughter produces a son .

Since both son and daughter are born from the limb and from the heart of the father, some hold that both son and daughter are entitled to the share. They say that this matter is stated in the ṛks quoted above beginning अंगादंगात्संभवसि (*aṃgādaṃgātsaṃbhavasi*) *[the plural "ṛks" is printed ಋಕ್ಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ; as supplied]*. In the Gṛhya-sūtras and other works these ṛks are said to be the mantras the father should say, at the jātakarma of a son or daughter, when smelling the head of the child. Svāyambhuva Manu, too, at the beginning of creation, said that because the offspring called son and daughter are born from the union (mithuna) of woman and man, the दाय (*dāya*) (the share in the property) should fall to both son and daughter. Some argue that the दाय (*dāya*) should fall to the son alone and should not go to the daughter, because if a female child is born she is not much honoured; sooner or later that child goes away to another's house; and the daughter has to be given up through gift (kanyādāna), sale and the like, whereas the case of the son is not so: he stays in the father's house. This is their argument.

*[The Special Topics are not concluded on this page; the section continues on the next page.]*

### Printed p. 721

*[The Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue from the previous page; the paragraph begins in the middle of the argument.]*

Still others argue that there are also circumstances in which a son has to be abandoned, and that the case of Śunaḥśepa is an example of this. Still others say that where a father has only a daughter and that daughter has neither an elder nor a younger brother (अभ्रातृमती (*abhrātṛmatī*)), in such a case the daughter herself is heir to the whole of her father's property. In this way Yāska has set out the many differences of opinion on this matter.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The son does not give his sister the father's wealth but has her married; the son performs the rites, the daughter is only adorned. The bhāṣya cites Yājñavalkya (2-124) and the Nirukta (Ni. 3-6). Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words तान्वः (*tānvaḥ*), रिक्कं (*rikkaṃ*), आरैक् (*āraik*), सनितुः (*sanituḥ*), निधानं (*nidhānaṃ*), मातरः (*mātaraḥ*), जनयंत (*janayaṃta*), वह्निं (*vahniṃ*), सुकृतोः (*sukṛtoḥ*) and ऋंधन् (*ṛṃdhan*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent, elision, with one printed Pāṇini reference, Pā. 1-2-67). A stray Latin letter s stood in place of the avagraha after the word for "from the prāṇi-, rajata- and other (words)"; it was rewritten letter for letter as the Kannada avagraha (logged). In several places the bhāṣya carries the Kannada short e or o vowel sign inside Sanskrit words (for example ತಸ್ಯೆ, ತಯೋರ್ಮಧ್ಯೆ, ನ್ಯತರೊರ್ಧಯಿತ್ವಾ); kept as printed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तान्यः (*tānyaḥ*)—the son born in the womb
- जामये (*jāmaye*)—to his sister
- रिक्कं (*rikkaṃ*)—the wealth inherited from the father; न अरैक् (*na araik*)—does not give. (But) सनितुः (*sanituḥ*)—of the husband who will cherish her
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—to the embryo
- निदानं (*nidānaṃ*)—as a recipient
- चकार (*cakāra*)—he makes (her)
- यदि (*yadi*)—if
- मातरः (*mātaraḥ*)—the parents
- वह्निं (*vahniṃ*)—offspring of female and male kind
- जनयंत (*janayaṃta*)—beget
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the one of male form (the son)
- सुकृतोः (*sukṛtoḥ*)—of excellent action
- कर्ता (*kartā*)—becomes the doer
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the one of female form (the daughter)
- ऋंधन् (*ṛṃdhan*)—becomes a recipient of ornaments such as garments

*[Variants as supplied: the first entry reads ತಾನ್ಯಃ where the Pada has ತಾನ್ವಃ; the entry for "as a recipient" reads ನಿದಾನಂ where the Pada has ನಿಧಾನಂ; the entry for the first ಅನ್ಯಃ carries a garbled explanation, printed ಪುಂದೂಪದ (ಪುತ್ರನು)ವನು, which is rendered here by its evident sense "the one of male form (the son)"; the entry for "offspring" reads ಪುಂಪದ where the Bhāvārtha reads ಪುಂರೂಪದ.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The son born of the body does not give the wealth inherited from the father to his sister as a gift. He gives her to the husband who will cherish her and makes her a recipient of that husband's embryo. Even if the parents beget offspring of female and male kind, of the two the son becomes the performer of an excellent rite such as the offering of piṇḍas; the daughter becomes a recipient only of ornaments such as garments and jewels.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(A son) born of the body, does not transfer (paternal) wealth to a sister : he has made (her) the receptacle of the embryo of the husband : if the parents procreate children (of either sex), one is the performer of holy acts, the other is to be enriched (with gifts).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अरुषस्यारोचमानस्य तव प्रयक्षे यज्ञार्थं जुह्वा ज्वालाभी
> रेजमानः कंपमानोऽग्निर्महः प्रभूतान् पुत्रान् रश्मीन् जज्ञे । उत्पादयामा-
> स । एषां रश्मीनां गर्भो जलात्मना क्रूडीकारो महानासीत् । किंच एषां रश्मी-
> नां मेलनं आ जातं सर्वत ओषध्यात्मना जातं महि महदभूत् । किंच एषां
> रश्मीनां प्रवृत् अनेन प्रकारेण प्रवृत्तिर्हर्यश्वस्येंद्रस्य यज्ञैर्यज्ञार्हैः सो-
> माहुतिभिर्मही महती भवति ॥ जज्ञे । जनी प्रादुर्भाव इत्यस्य लिटि रूपं । अंत-
> र्भावितण्यर्थः । जुह्वा । जुहोतेर्द्वै दीर्घश्चेति क्विप् द्विर्वचनं दीर्घश्च धातोः ।
> उदात्तस्वरितयोरिति स्वरितत्वं । हर्यश्वस्य । हरी अश्वा यस्यॆति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्व-
> पदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, blazing at Indra's sacrifice, produced the rays as sons; their watery embryo grew great, spread as plants and grows through Soma oblations. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words जज्ञे (*jajñe*), जुह्वा (*juhvā*) and हर्यश्वस्य (*haryaśvasya*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent, compound). The grammar of the word for "of Hari-horse" carries the Kannada short e vowel sign in ಯಸ್ಯೆತಿ; kept as printed.

- अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*)—of you, the shining one, to whom it is directed
- प्रयक्षे (*prayakṣe*)—for the sacrifice
- जुह्वा (*juhvā*)—with flames
- रेजमानः (*rejamānaḥ*)—blazing
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—abundant
- पुत्रान् (*putrān*)—sons in the form of rays
- जज्ञॆ (*jajñè*)—has produced
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these rays

- महान् (*mahān*)—became great (their union); आ जातं (*ā jātaṃ*)—having been transformed into plants and other forms
- महि (*mahi*)—became great

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for the sacrifice directed to you, the shining one, Agni, blazing with flames, has produced in abundance sons in the form of rays. The watery embryo of these rays, and their transformation into plants and other forms, became great. And this spreading power of theirs has gained still greater greatness through the sacrificial Soma and other oblations.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
For the worship of the resplendent (Indra), Agni, glowing with flame, has begotten mighty sons: great was the germ, and great was their birth, and great was their efficacy, for the worship of Haryashwa.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि जैत्री॑रसचंत स्पृधा॒नं महि॒ ज्योति॒स्तम॑सो॒ निर॑जानन् ।  
> तं जा॑न॒तीः प्रत्युदा॑यन्नु॒षासः॒ पति॒र्गवा॑मभव॒देक॒ इंद्रः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> तं । जानतीः । प्रति । उत् । आयन् । उषसः । पतिः । गवां । अभवत् । एकः । इंद्रः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चंत । सर्वतः समगच्छन् । ते च मरुतस्तस्मिन्वृत्रे हते महि महत् ज्योतिः सू-
> र्याख्यं तेजस्तमसस्तमोरूपाद्दत्तान्निरजानन् । निर्गतमज्ञासिषुः । तत इंद्रं
> वृत्रहंतारमुदितं सूर्यं जानतीर्जानाना उषसस्तं प्रत्युत् अभिलक्ष्यैव आयन्
> प्राप्नु वन् । अथ तत्रोद्भूतानां गवां रश्मीनामेकोऽद्वितीय एवेंद्रः पतिरभवत् ॥
> जैत्रीः । जयतेस्तुनि रूपं । गुणस्य स्थाने व्यत्ययेन वृद्धिः । नित्सर् । असचंत ।

> छंदसि द्विर्वचनस्य विकल्पितत्वाद्द्विर्वचनाभावः । चित्वरः । अजानन् ! ज्ञा अवबोधन
> इत्यस्य लजु रूपं । निघातः । आयन् । अय पय गतावित्यस्य लजु रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The victorious Maruts gather round Indra, who is contending with Vṛtra, and perceive the great light of the sun coming out of the darkness; the dawns turn towards it and Indra is sole lord of the rays. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words जैत्रीः (*jaitrīḥ*), असचंत (*asacaṃta*), the word for "contending" (printed in the grammar as ಸ್ಪ, ಧಾನಂ, with a comma inside it), अजानन् (*ajānan*) and आयन् (*āyan*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). After the word for "they knew" in the grammar an exclamation mark stands in place of the stop; earlier in the block a space stands inside the word for "they reached" (printed ಪ್ರಾಪ್ನು ವನ್). All kept as supplied.

- स्पृधानं (*spṛdhānaṃ*)—Indra, who was contending with Vṛtra; अभि असचंत (*abhi asacaṃta*)—came around and gathered together, and
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the light in the form of the sun
- तमसः (*tamasaḥ*)—from the body of Vṛtra, who is of the nature of darkness (the light issuing out and shining); निः अजानन् (*niḥ ajānan*)—perceived
- जानतीः (*jānatīḥ*)—knowing the rising of the (risen) sun
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the dawn goddesses; तं प्रति (*taṃ prati*)—towards him; उत् आयन् (*ut āyan*)—came up and gathered
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- गवां (*gavāṃ*)—of the risen rays of the sun; एकः पतिः (*ekaḥ patiḥ*)—as the sole lord
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—became

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The victorious Maruts gathered around Indra, who was contending with Vṛtra. They perceived the great light in the form of the sun going out of the body of Vṛtra, who is of the nature of darkness, and shining. The dawns, knowing the rising of the sun, gathered towards him. Indra became the sole lord of all the rays of the sun that had come into being.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The victorious (Maruts) associatedd [sic] (with Indra when contending with Vritra) perceived a great light issuing from the darkness. The dawns recognizing him (as the sun) arose, and Indra was the sole sovereign of the rays (of light).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The bhāṣya tells the story that the cows of the Aṅgirases were carried off by the Paṇis and hidden in a mountain, and that Indra, praised by them, had them found and given back. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words आत्यंदन् (*ātyaṃdan*) and प्राचा (*prācā*), then the word for "they urged" (printed in the grammar as ಅಹಿನ್ಸನ್, broken at the line end and joined here, with a consonant different from the Pada), then अविंदन् (*aviṃdan*), पथ्यां (*pathyāṃ*) and विवेश (*viveśa*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). All kept as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—the intelligent
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—and wise Aṅgirases
- वीळौ (*vīḷau*)—in the strong mountain
- सतीः (*satīḥ*)—the cows that had been kept hidden
- अभि (*abhi*)—having ascertained exactly
- अतृंदन् (*atṛṃdan*)—kept silent (afterwards)
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with a mind (full of faith that the cows were there)
- प्राचा (*prācā*)—and with the intention of praising Indra
- अहिन्वन् (*ahinvan*)—they pleased (Indra) with praises
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- पथ्यां (*pathyāṃ*)—that was on the path
- विश्वां (*viśvāṃ*)—all the cows that had been carried off
- अविंदन् (*aviṃdan*)—they obtained
- ता (*tā*)—the deeds of the Aṅgirases; प्रजानन् इत् (*prajānan it*)—Indra, having fully understood them
- नमसा (*namasā*)—honouring the Aṅgirases with homage; आ विवेश (*ā viveśa*)—entered (the mountain cave)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seven intelligent and wise Aṅgirases, having ascertained exactly that the cows had been hidden in the strong mountain, kept silent. Afterwards, with the faith that the cows were in that mountain and with the intention of praising Indra, they praised Indra and pleased him. And they obtained all the cows carried off from the path of the sacrifice. Indra, having fully understood the deeds of the Aṅgirases, honoured them with homage and entered the mountain cave.

*[The first entry of the Pratipadārtha ends with an exclamation mark where a stop would be expected; the entry for "they were silent" reads ಅತೃಂದನ್, differing from the Pada form (page 725); the Pratipadārtha has ಪರ್ವತಗುಹೆಯನ್ನು where the Bhāvārtha has ಪರ್ವತಗುದೆಯನ್ನು. As supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The seven intelligent sages (the Angirasas) having ascertained that (the cows) were concealed in the strong (cavern), propitiated (Indra) by mental devotion : they recovered them all by the path of sacrifice; for Indra knowing (their pious acts), and offering them homage, entered (the cave).

*[The line-ends of the printed English are joined. The Special Topics, if any, are not in the text of this window.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sarama, sent by Indra, found the mountain's broken door; Indra gave her the food promised earlier; she, knowing the cows' lowing, reached them. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words विदत् (*vidat*), सरमा (*saramā*) (with a reference to Yāska), रुग्णं (*rugṇaṃ*), पाथः (*pāthaḥ*), सध्र्यक् (*sadhryak*), कः (*kaḥ*), नयत् (*nayat*), सुपदी (*supadī*) and गात् (*gāt*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). The bhāṣya text reads ಕ್ರಥಮಾ where the Pada has प्रथमा (*prathamā*), ಕರಿಷ್ಯಾಮಾತಿ and ಸಧ್ರ್ಯಕ್ ಇತರೈರಪಿ; all kept as supplied.

- विदत् (*vidat*)—went and reached it, (and immediately) Indra
- महि (*mahi*)—(the entry continues on the next page)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Sarama (the Devaśunī), sent by Indra in search of the cows, had no sooner gone and reached the door of the mountain than Indra provided the food which was great, which had been promised to Sarama earlier, and which was abundant. Thereafter that Sarama of excellent feet, having known the sound of the cows beforehand, went on in the direction of that sound and reached the front of those imperishable cows.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
When Sarama discovered the broken (entrance) of the mountain, then Indra made great and ample (provision) for her young, as previously (promised) : then the sure-footed (animal), first recognizing their lowing, proceeded, and came to the presence of the imperishable cows.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, seeking the Aṅgirases' friendship, went to the mountain, which gave up the cows; with the Maruts he recovered them, and Aṅgiras worshipped him. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words अगच्छत् (*agacchat*), सखीयन् (*sakhīyan*), असूदयत् (*asūdayat*), ससान (*sasāna*), अंगिराः (*aṃgirāḥ*) (with a reference to Yāska) and the desiderative verb printed ವ ಖಸ್ಯನ್ (the Pada has मखस्यन् (*makhasyan*)) are analysed. All kept as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्रतमः (*vipratamaḥ*)—extremely wise
- सखीयन् (*sakhīyan*)—and one who desired friendship (with the Aṅgirases), Indra; अगच्छत् उ (*agacchat u*)—came and reached the door of the mountain indeed
- अद्रिः (*adriḥ*)—the mountain too (which desired friendship with Indra)
- सुकृते (*sukṛte*)—to Indra, the doer of excellent deeds
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the herd of cows that was inside its cave
- असूदयत् (*asūdayat*)—handed over
- युवभिः (*yuvabhiḥ*)—together with the ever-youthful Maruts
- मखस्यन् (*makhasyan*)—who desired to give cows to the Aṅgirases
- मर्यः (*maryaḥ*)—and destroyed the Asuras, Indra
- ससान (*sasāna*)—joined (the cows)
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- अंगिराः (*aṃgirāḥ*)—the sage Aṅgiras
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at once; अर्चन् अभवत् (*arcan abhavat*)—began to worship Indra

*[The Kannada of the entries for सखीयन् (*sakhīyan*) and for अर्चन् अभवत् (*arcan abhavat*) is broken across lines inside words (ಸಿ and ತೊ at the line ends); joined here. As supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is extremely wise and who desired friendship with the Aṅgirases, came and reached the door of the mountain. The mountain too, desiring friendship with Indra, handed over to him, the doer of excellent deeds, the herd of cows that was inside its cave. Indra, who desired to give cows to the Aṅgirases together with the ever-youthful Maruts, and who destroyed the Asuras, joined the cows. Immediately thereafter the sage Aṅgiras began to worship Indra.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The most sage (Indra), desirous of the friendship of the (Angirasas), went to the cave, and the mountain yielded its contents to the valiant (deity), aided by the youthful Maruts, equally wishing (to conciliate the sages) : the destroyer (of the Asuras) recovered (the cattle), and immediately Angiras became his worshipper.

> अर्चन् । अर्चतेः शतरि रूपं । सखीन् । संहितायां नकारस्य दीर्घादटीति रु: ।
> पूर्वस्य वर्णस्य अत्रानुनासिक इत्यनुनासिकादेशः । अमुंचत् । मुच्च मोक्षण
> इत्यस्य लजि शे मुचादीनामिति नुमागमः । निघातः । अवद्यात् । वद व्यक्तायां
> वाचीत्यस्य नञ्पूर्वस्य गर्हार्थेवद्यपण्यवर्या इति निपातनात् । पा, ३-१ १०१ ।
> यत्पत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the match of all that exists, knows all births and slays Śuṣṇa; desiring cows for the Aṅgirases, he freed us, his friends, from blame. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words प्रतिमानं (*pratimānaṃ*), पुरोभूः (*purobhūḥ*), वेद (*veda*), जनिम (*janima*), हंति (*haṃti*), शुष्णं (*śuṣṇaṃ*), प्र णः (*pra ṇaḥ*), पदवीः (*padavīḥ*), गव्युः (*gavyuḥ*), अर्चन् (*arcan*), सखीन् (*sakhīn*), अमुंचत् (*amuṃcat*) and अवद्यात् (*avadyāt*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Printed oddities kept: ಪ್ರತಿಮಾನಂ ! (an exclamation mark in place of a stop) and ಜಾನಾತಿ ' (a stray apostrophe). The Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha and printed English of this Ṛk follow in the next window.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is the model for all that is excellent and who rushes ahead in battle, knows the nature of all the beings that are born. The same Indra is the destroyer of the Asura called Śuṣṇa. Indra, who is a sage, who wished to give cows to the Aṅgirases, and who is our friend, coming from the heavenly world to us who are dear to him and joining us, honouring us greatly, may he be freed completely from the fault in the form of the slaying of Vṛtra.

*[Oddities as supplied: the Bhāvārtha breaks a word across lines (ನಾಶಕನಾಗಿ ದ್ದಾನೆ), and has ಆದರಿಸುತಾ for the participle.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May he who is the type of all that is excellent, the anticipator (of his foes), he who knows all that his [sic] born, who destroys Sushna, the far-seeing, the restorer of cattle, may he, a friend coming from heaven, honouring us as his friends, be free from all reproach.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Aṅgirases, wishing for cows, sat in the sattra with hymns, preparing the path to godhood; by that true rite they sought the months. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words गव्यता (*gavyatā*), सेदुः (*seduḥ*), कृण्वानासः (*kṛṇvānāsaḥ*), गातुं (*gātuṃ*) and असिषासन् (*asiṣāsan*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent), with a reference to Pāṇini in the entry for the last. Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has ಆರ್ಕೆರರ್ಚನೀಯೈಃ and ನಾಂತಾದೇಶಃ, ಸತ್ರಾಖ್ಯೆ, and an exclamation mark after ಪ್ರತ್ಯಯಃ. As supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनसा (*manasā*)—endowed with mind (the Aṅgirases)
- आर्कॆः (*ārkèḥ*)—with hymns worthy of reflection
- अमृतत्वाय (*amṛtatvāya*)—for obtaining godhood
- गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—the path
- कृष्णानासः (*kṛṣṇānāsaḥ*)—preparing; नि सेमः (*ni semaḥ*)—sat down, engaged in the rites; येन ऋतेन (*yena ṛtena*)—by which rites, that are of the nature of truth
- मासान् (*māsān*)—(the months arranged by the abhiplava and pṛṣṭha ṣaḍahas) the measures
- असिसासन् (*asisāsan*)—wished to arrange, such
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of the Aṅgirases; इदं चित् सदनं (*idaṃ cit sadanaṃ*)—that seat, which is part of the rite; भूरि नु (*bhūri nu*)—is of very great importance

The last entry of the Pratipadārtha has no stop at its end. The entry for ಯೇನ ಋತೇನ is broken across a line (ಸತ್ಯ ಭೂತಗಳಾದ), and the Bhāvārtha breaks words across lines (ದೇವತ್ವ ವನ್ನು); joined here.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirases, who desired cows and were endowed with mind, sat down engaged in the rites, preparing with hymns worthy of reflection the path to obtaining godhood. That seat of the Aṅgirases, which is part of the rite, and by which, being rites of the nature of truth, they wished to pass the months consisting of the abhiplava and pṛṣṭha ṣaḍahas, is of very great importance.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The Angirasas, with minds intent on their cattle, (sat down to worship Indra) with hymns, following the road to immortality : great was this their perseverance, by which they sought for months to accomplish (their ends).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Aṅgirases, regarding the cows as their own and milking them, rejoiced; their shout pervaded heaven and earth; they set brave men to guard the cows. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words संपश्यमानाः (*saṃpaśyamānāḥ*), अमदन् (*amadan*), दुघानाः (*dughānāḥ*), अतपत् (*atapat*), घोषः (*ghoṣaḥ*), निष्ठां (*niṣṭhāṃ*) (with a Pāṇini reference), अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*) and गोषु (*goṣu*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). The bhāṣya ends with the sign of the end of the Varga and the number six, as printed. Garbled readings kept as supplied, among them ಅಹ್ಯಷ್ಯನ್ and ಘಇಂತಃ.

- स्वं (*svaṃ*)—their own cow-wealth; अभि संपश्यमानाः (*abhi saṃpaśyamānāḥ*)—looking on it with affection
- प्रत्नस्य (*pratnasya*)—born previously
- रेतसः (*retasaḥ*)—for the sake of sustaining their sons
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- दुघानाः (*dughānāḥ*)—and milking (the Aṅgirases)
- आमदन् (*āmadan*)—became glad at heart
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these Aṅgirases (the entry continues in the next window)

### Printed p. 734

घोषः (*ghoṣaḥ*)—the sound of joy; रोदसी (*rodasī*)—both heaven and earth; वि अतपत् (*vi atapat*)—pervaded (thereafter); जाते (*jāte*)—in the things produced (among them); निष्ठां (*niṣṭhāṃ*)—having brought about the former state, they established; गोषु (*goṣu*)—for the cows that were brought back; वीरान् (*vīrān*)—heroic men who are protectors; अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)—appointed.

*[As supplied: the entry for वीरान् (*vīrān*) reads ರಕ್ಷ=ರಾದ (an equals sign inside the word, taken here as a damaged form of the word for protectors); the entry for गोषु (*goṣu*) has ಆಕೃತವಾದ where the Bhāvārtha has ಆಹ್ೃತವಾದ.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirases, looking with affection at their cow-wealth that had been brought back, and milking out milk for the sustenance of their sons who had been born earlier, became glad at heart. The sound of joy of these Aṅgirases pervaded both heaven and earth. Thereafter the Aṅgirases obtained their true state (yāthātmya) in their dealings. And for the cows that had been brought back they appointed heroic men as protectors.

*[Oddity as supplied: the word for "true state" is broken across two lines of the Bhāvārtha (ending ಯಾಥಾ and beginning ತ್ಮ್ಯವನ್ನು); joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Contemplating their own (cattle) giving milk to their former progeny (the Angirasas) were delighted; their shouts spread through heaven and earth; they replaced the recovered cows in their places and stationed guards over the cows.

*[The printed English breaks "progeny" across two lines with a hyphen at the line end; joined here. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, with the Maruts, the slayer of Vṛtra, released the milch cows for the sacrifice; the cows then yielded sweet milk for the sacrificer. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*), असृजत् (*asṛjat*), उरूची (*urūcī*), दुदुहे (*duduhe*) and जेन्या (*jenyā*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). A Nirukta reference (Yāska) is given in the bhāṣya for the word for cows. Printed oddities kept: on the previous page the bhāṣya has ವೇಂದ್ರೋಽರ್ಕೆರರ್ಚನೀಯ್ಯೈಃ and ಸಹಾಯತಯಂ. As supplied.

- सेदु (*sedu*)—that same one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the protector, together with the Maruts who were born for his help, becomes the slayer of the Asura Vṛtra. The same Indra, together with the Maruts who are worthy of worship and worthy of the oblation, released for the sacrifice the cows that yield milk. Therefore the excellent cows, which carry the oblation consisting of ghee and bring the oblations and other things that are parts of the rite, yield sweet milk for the sacrificer.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, the slayer of Vritra, let loose the milch cows, assisted by the Maruts, born for his aid, and entitled to praises and oblations, and the excellent (cows) contributing abundantly to sacred offerings, and yielding the butter of libation, milked for him sweet (sacrificial) food.

*[The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk. After the printed English a stray line stands in the supplied text: ಅನುಭವ; kept as an italic note.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Aṅgirases at the sattra made a great shining seat for Indra and, propping heaven and earth apart by the sky, established Indra on high. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words चक्रुः (*cakruḥ*), ख्यन् (*khyan*), विष्णभ्यंतः (*viṣṇabhyaṃtaḥ*) (with a reference to Pāṇini), जनित्रि (*janitri*), आसीनाः (*āsīnāḥ*) (with a second reference to Pāṇini) and मिन्वन् (*minvan*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Printed oddities kept: ವಿಷ್ಣಭೀಕುರ್ವಂತಃ, ಸ್ಕನ್ಭು and an exclamation mark after ಇತ್ಯಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛಾನಚ್!; a line break after a full stop inside a word (the word for entering, ending in a full stop at the line end). ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirases, doers of excellent deeds, built for Indra the protector a great and radiant high place, and made it manifest to the world. Seated in the place of sacrifice, they held up heaven and earth, the mother and father of the whole world, by the sky, which is like a supporting pillar, and established the swift Indra in the heavenly world.

*[Several words of the Bhāvārtha are broken across line ends in the supplied text and are joined here.]*

They (the Angirasas) performing pious acts made for their protector a spacious and splendid abode which they celebrated : seated (at the sacrifice) and supporting with the pillar (of the firmament) the parents (of all things heaven and earth), they established the rapid Indra on high (in heaven).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Our great praise is directed to Indra; when it has set up for the separation of heaven and earth one who grows at once and is able to support them, faultless praises come together in that Indra, and all his powers are natural to him, not sent by another. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*), शिश्नथे (*śiśnathe*), धात् (*dhāt*), विभ्वं (*vibhvaṃ*) and अनुत्ताः (*anuttāḥ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent), with the Pāṇinian rule names as printed. Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has ಇಾಧೃಷಾ and ಸ್ತತಿಃ. As supplied.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When our great praise has appointed, for the individual establishment of heaven and earth, a leader who grows at once, who is able to support them and who is of the form of Indra, then in that Indra faultless utterances in the form of praise come together. For that same Indra all kinds of powers too are not an external means but natural qualities.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Inasmuch as our devout praise has appointed a thriving ruler for the regulation of heaven and earth, to whom faultless and appropriate commendations (are due), therefore are all the energies of Indra spontaneously exerted.

*[The printed English breaks "commendations" across a line end with a hyphen; joined here. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, I desire your great friendship and the gifts of your power; many horses come to you, the slayer of Vṛtra, to carry you; to you, the wise, we bring great praise and oblation-food; know that you are our good protector. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*), वश्मि (*vaśmi*), नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*), अगन्म (*aganma*), बोधि (*bodhi*) and गोपा: (*gopā:*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, I desire your great friendship and the gifts that can be achieved by your power. For your carrying, horses in the form of "vaḍavāgnis", you the slayer of the Asura Vṛtra, come and gather together in great numbers. To you, the wise one, I offer great praise and food in the form of oblation. O wealthy Indra, know that you are an excellent protector for us.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, knowing, gave us, his friends, a great field, abundant gold, and then moving wealth such as cows; shining, with the Maruts, he produced the sun, dawn, the earth and fire. ##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दमूनाः । दांतं मनो यस्यासौ दमूनाः ; दांतमनाः । यद्वा दाम्यतीति दमूनाः। उपरत इत्यर्थः । स एष एवॆंद्रो विभ्वो व्याप्ताः सध्रीचीः परस्पर

> नित्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, self-controlled, created the pervading, commingled, world-delighting waters; purifying the sweet Soma with Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, they flow with days and nights. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words दमूनाः (*damūnāḥ*), अस्पृजत् (*aspṛjat*), हिन्वंति (*hinvaṃti*) and धनुत्रीः (*dhanutrīḥ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has ಅಸ್ಪೃಜತ್ where the Pada has ಅಸೃಜತ್, and ಮದ್ವಾ and ಸೋಮಾನ್ಯವಿಭಿಃ; the short vowel sign e stands for the long one in ಏವೆಂದ್ರೋ . As supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दमूनाः (*damūnāḥ*)—of subdued mind
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—Indra
- विभ्वः (*vibhvaḥ*)—all-pervading

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, of subdued mind, created waters that are all-pervading, that flow together and that delight the whole world. Those same waters, purifying the sweet Soma-juices with the help of the purifying Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, and being beneficial to the whole world, flow along themselves with the streams of days and nights.

*[As supplied: the Bhāvārtha has ಸೂರರ where the Pratipadārtha has ಸೂರ್ಯರ.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This lowly-minded Indra has created the widespread, commingled all-delighting waters; and they, purifying the sweet (libations) with the sage purifiers, and being benevolent (to all), proceed with (the revolutions) of days and nights.

*[The printed English is set in three lines; joined here. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By Indra's might day and night revolve; his friends the Maruts spread his greatness around to overcome the rite-obstructing demons. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words जिहाते (*jihāte*), मंहना (*maṃhanā*), वृजध्यै (*vṛjadhyai*), काम्याः (*kāmyāḥ*) and ऋजप्याः (*ṛjapyāḥ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has ಋಜಪ್ಯಾಃ where the Saṃhitā has ಋಜಿಪ್ಯಾಃ, and in the grammar tail the root of growth is given as ಓಪ್ಯಾಯಾ ವೃದ್ಧೌ; the short vowel sign e stands in ಭ್ಯಾಸಸ್ಯೆತ್ವಂ . As supplied.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, by the power of you, who impel the whole world, the day and night, both worthy of worship and bearing the world, undergo a revolution in the form of recurrence. The Maruts, who move straight, are your friends and have attractive forms; for the destruction of the Asuras they cause your greatness to spread all around.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The two adorable (alternations of) day and night, upholding (all things) by the might of the sun, successively revolve : your sincere and acceptable friends (the Maruts) are ready to encounter (your foes) and maintain your greatness.

*[The printed English is set in three lines; joined here. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

Long-lived Indra is asked to be lord of our dearest praises and to come to us with great protections and friendships. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, long-lived, showerer of desires and giver of food, be the lord of our dearest words of praise. You, the great-souled, come towards us together with protections of great qualities and with auspicious friends.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Slayer of Vritra, do you, who art long lived, the showerer, (of benefits), the giver of food, be the lord of our true praises, repairing (to the sacrifice), come to us great, with great, friendly, and auspicious protections.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra makes the ancient Indra new for worship, like the Aṅgirases, and asks him to destroy the dark demons and give us wealth. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words अंगिरस्वत् (*aṃgirasvat*), सपर्यन् (*saparyan*), नव्यं (*navyaṃ*), कृणोमि (*kṛṇomi*), सन्यसे (*sanyase*), पुराजां (*purājāṃ*), याहि (*yāhi*), स्वः (*svaḥ*) and सातये (*sātaye*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Printed oddities kept: the Pada has ಸಾತಯೆ where the Saṃhitā has ಸಾತಯೇ, and the bhāṣya has ನವ್ಯಂ ಣು ಸ್ತುತಾ and a danda written as an exclamation mark after the rule on the suffix of likeness; the short vowel sign e stands in ತನ್ನಿಮಿತ್ತಸ್ಯೆತಿ . As supplied.

- नमसा (*namasā*)—with praise
- सपर्यन् (*saparyan*)—I (Viśvāmitra) who worship; तं पुराजां (*taṃ purājāṃ*)—you, the ancient
- सन्यसे (*sanyase*)—for the sake of worshipping; नव्यं कृणोमि (*navyaṃ kṛṇomi*)—I make new

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is asked to fill the spread-out purifying waters up to their far bank, to protect us from harming enemies and quickly to make us winners of cattle. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words अभूवन् (*abhūvan*), पिपृहि (*pipṛhi*), रथिरः (*rathiraḥ*), रिषः (*riṣaḥ*) and मक्षु मक्षु (*makṣu makṣu*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the waters, which purify and are the means of sprinkling, have spread over the whole world. So that those waters may be imperishable, fill their place of origin with water for our good. You, who possess a chariot, protect us from harming enemies. Make us, very quickly, conquerors of cattle and the like.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, slayer of Vṛtra and lord of cattle, shows us the cows, destroys the rite-obstructing dark demons with bright splendours and, directing the cows to the Aṅgirases by true speech, closes the stall doors. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words अदेदिष्ट (*adediṣṭa*), गोपतिः (*gopatiḥ*), गात् (*gāt*), दिशमानऽ (*diśamāna '*) and अवृणोत् (*avṛṇot*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). As supplied.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of the cows, pointed out the cows. He destroyed the Asuras, the obstructers of rites, with shining splendours. Directing and showing the dearest cows to the Aṅgirases by attractive words, he closed all the doors of the stall and the cows.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्र सोमं सोमपत इति सप्तदशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं वैत्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । अनुक्रांतं च । इंद्र सोमं त्र्यूनेति ॥ पृष्ठाभिप्लवषडहयोर्द्वितीयेऽहनि मरुत्वतीय इंद्र सोममितेदं सूक्तं निविद्धानीयं । द्वितीयस्येति
> खंडे सूत्रितं । इंद्र सोमं या त ऊतिरवमेति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ७-६ । इति ॥
> गोसवविवधयोरपि मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । इंद्र सोममेतायामेति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-८ । इति ॥ उद्दिद्धवलभिदोरपि मरुत्वतीय एतत्तूक्तं ।
> सूत्रितं च । इंद्र सोममिंद्रः पूर्विदिति मध्यंदिनः । आ, ९-८ । इति ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, which begins with इंद्र सोमं सोमपते (*iṃdra somaṃ somapate*), is the third sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are seventeen Ṛks in it. The seer of this sūkta is Viśvāmitra; Indra is the

### Printed p. 750

*(Anuvāda, continued)* deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh *[so printed, with a lengthened vowel sign in the Kannada word for "metre"; as supplied]*; in the Anukramaṇikā it is said इंद्र सोमं श्रूना (*iṃdra somaṃ śrūnā*) *[the last word is printed so, differently from the bhāṣya block; as supplied]*. At the sacrifices called "Sṛṣṭi" and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, on the second day, when the mantras of the Marutvatīya śastra are recited, this sūkta beginning इंद्र सोमं (*iṃdra somaṃ*) is to be recited as the Nividdhānīya sūkta; this is explained in the Khaṇḍa beginning द्वितीयस्य (*dvitīyasya*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra इंद्र सोमं या त ऊतिरवमेति मध्यंदिनः (*iṃdra somaṃ yā ta ūtiravameti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 7-6). Further, this sūkta is used for the mantras of the Marutvatīya śastra also in the sacrifices called Gosava and Vivadha ; this is explained by the sūtra इंद्र सोममेतायामेति मध्यंदिनः (*iṃdra somametāyāmeti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā 9-8) *[no full stop after the abbreviation, as supplied]*. And in the sacrifices called Udbhit and Valabhit this sūkta is used for the mantras *[printed with a different first letter in the Kannada word, which reads like "duntras"; as supplied]* of the Marutvatīya śastra; this is explained by the sūtra इंद्र सोममिंद्रः पूर्विदिति मध्यंदिनः (*iṃdra somamiṃdraḥ pūrviditi madhyaṃdinaḥ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 9-8).

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 32 *[a line with this number stands before the sūkta data; as supplied]*. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 32. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 2; Varga 9, 10, 11 *[printed "9. 10, 11"]*. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 17. Seer: विश्वामित्रः (*viśvāmitraḥ*). Devatā: इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*). Chandas: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, lord of Soma, is asked to drink the midday Soma, unyoke his horses, fill their jaws with fodder and gladden them here. Grammar of the bhāṣya: the words प्रपुथ्य (*praputhya*), ऋजीषिन् (*ṛjīṣin*) and मादयस्व (*mādayasva*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, a Uṇādi sūtra cited with its number, accent). Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has मंध्यंदिनसंबंधि (*maṃdhyaṃdinasaṃbaṃdhi*) and द्रस्वश्चांदसः (*drasvaścāṃdasaḥ*) . As supplied.

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of Soma, drink this Soma juice offered at the time of the midday pressing. For the Niṣkevalya śastra mantra of the midday, offered with you in view, is pleasing. O Indra, wealthy one, who have the Soma material whose essence is gone, unyoke your horses from the chariot, fill their jaws with these mouthfuls and gladden them in this sacrificial place.

*[The Pratipadārtha has "one who drinks Soma whose essence is gone" for the entry ऋजेषिन् (*ṛjeṣin*), the Bhāvārtha "who has the Soma material whose essence is gone"; as supplied. Several words are broken across line ends and are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, lord of the Soma, drink this Soma juice which is grateful to you at noon-day sacrifice; Maghavan, partaker of the spiritless Soma, unyoke your horses, and, filling their jaws (with fodder) exhilarate them at this ceremony.

*[The printed English is set in four lines; joined here. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is asked to drink the three kinds of Soma offered for his delight and to be satisfied together with the Maruts and the Rudras. The grammar of the bhāṣya treats the compounds, the long vowel of the verb, the perfect form, the accent and the augment. Printed oddities kept: the Pada has त्वपत् (*tvapat*) where the bhāṣya and the Pratipadārtha have a different word beginning with the letters for "tṛ"; the Pada has गोऽआशिरं (*go 'āśiraṃ*) where the bhāṣya has a form without the avagraha; the bhāṣya has संगतस्तुं (*saṃgatastuṃ*) and लिट रूपं (*liṭa rūpaṃ*) ; the short vowel sign e is used in the bhāṣya in मंथसंयॆक्तं (*maṃthasaṃyèktaṃ*) and in the Pada word रुद्रॆः (*rudrèḥ*) . In the bhāṣya a Latin colon after तुदादिः (*tudādiḥ*) is rewritten as the visarga, letter for letter (logged). Line-end hyphens inside the blocks are joined (logged). As supplied.

- गवाशिरं (*gavāśiraṃ*)—mixed with milk
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma too
- मंथिनं (*maṃthinaṃ*)—the Soma mixed with curds too
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—the pure Soma too
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- ते (*te*)—your
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for the delight
- ररिम (*rarima*)—we offer (the Soma)
- मारुतेन (*mārutena*)—with the Marut host too
- गणेन (*gaṇena*)—of the form of a group
- रुद्रैः (*rudraiḥ*)—with the eleven Rudras too
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—united (with them)
- तृपत् (*tṛpat*)—obtaining satisfaction; आ वृषस्व (*ā vṛṣasva*)—fill the stomach with the juice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink the Soma juices beginning with गवाशिरादि (*gavāśirādi*) that are offered in all three pressings; we are offering them for your satisfaction. United with the Maruts and with the group of the eleven Rudras, obtain the satisfaction that comes from drinking the Soma juice.

*[Words broken across line ends are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, drink the Soma juice mixed with milk, with butter-milk, or fresh : we offer it for your exhilaration, associated with the devout company of the Maruts and the Rudras : drink it till you are satisfied.

*[The printed English is set in three lines; the word "company" is broken across a line end with a hyphen and is joined here. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts, praising Indra, increased his brilliance, strength and power in battle; he is asked to drink Soma with them at the midday pressing. Yāska is cited in the bhāṣya for the meaning of the word for "jaws": शिप्रे हनू नासिके वेति यास्कः (*śipre hanū nāsike veti yāskaḥ*). Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has सुसिप्र (*susipra*) where the Saṃhitā and Pada have a form with the sibilant ś; the Pada runs ते। ओजः। (*te| ojaḥ|*) without spaces before the dandas . Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged).

- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*)—(your) strength

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Maruts who are in the form of your enemy-destroying brilliance, who made your strength grow, those same Maruts increased your power in battle; you who hold the thunderbolt in the hand and have excellent cheeks, O Indra, united with the Maruts, drink the Soma juice offered at the midday pressing.

> मनिन् । नित्सर्वः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts, Indra's strength, urge him with sweet words; urged by them he found the vulnerable spot of Vṛtra, who thought his weak point unknown. The grammar of the bhāṣya treats the perfect of one root, the verb of being, the perfect of "to know" and an Uṇādi formation in मनिन् (*manin*). ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The same Maruts who are the forms of Indra's strength spur Indra on with attractive words. Indra, urged on by those same Maruts, came to know the vital spot of the demon Vṛtra, who had not made his secret known to anyone else and was filled with the pride that no one could harm him.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, enjoying this sacrifice as he did that of Manu, is asked to drink the Soma for perpetual vigour, to come with the sacrificial rites and, with the Maruts, to join the waters of the sky to those of the earth. The grammar of the bhāṣya treats the root, the suffixes, the Uṇādi form with its number, the sūtra reference and the accent of the words in the Ṛk. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, enjoying this sacrifice as you enjoyed that of Manu in former times, drink this Soma juice to obtain imperishable prowess. You who are endowed with horses of green-tawny colour, be gracious, together with the adorable Maruts. Accompanied by the roving Maruts, join the waters of the sky to the waters of the earth and make them flow together.

Phased [sic] with the sacrifice as if it was that of Manu, drink, Indra, the Soma juice, for the sake of perpetual vigour : come, lord of the tawny steeds, with the adorable Maruts, and with the traveisers [sic] (of the air) : send down the waters (of the firmament) to (blend with) the waters of the earth.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When Indra struck Vṛtra, the cloud lying motionless and enclosing the shining waters, he released the waters like horses let loose for a swift run in battle. The grammar of the bhāṣya treats the roots, suffixes, Uṇādi sūtra with its number, sandhi, lengthening and accent of the words in the Ṛk. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when you killed with your thunderbolt Vṛtra, who is in the form of a cloud, spread out around the shining waters, without light and lying motionless, then in the battle you released the waters, so that they might flow in abundance, as one lets loose horses that run very swiftly.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, grown great through the food of the oblation, ageless and ever young, is worshipped by us; heaven and earth cannot measure his greatness. The grammar of the bhāṣya treats the forms of the verbs and nouns in the Ṛk (roots, suffixes, the Pragṛhya designation of प्रिये (*priye*) , the accents) and is transcribed, not explained. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who has grown great through food in the form of the oblation, who has a vast form, is worthy of praise, free from old age and ever young, we surely worship. The boundless heaven and earth could not measure the glory of Indra, who is worthy of sacrifice; nor is it possible to measure it.

*[In the Kannada a danda stands in the middle of the sentence after the word for "ageless" (as supplied). The Bhāvārtha has ಅಳೆಯಲಾಗಲಿಲ್ಲ where the Pratipadārtha has the spelling ಅಳಿಯಲು; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Therefore we sacrifice with reverence to the vast and mighty Indra, who is adorable, undecaying, young; whose magnitude the unbounded heaven and earth have not measured, nor can measure.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All the gods do not violate Indra's many fair works and rites; skilful, he upholds the three worlds and has created the sun and the dawn. The long tail of the bhāṣya first explains why the word-group of this Ṛk, which was recited earlier at Ṛgve. 3-2-3 (the abbreviation is broken across a line end, the number is as supplied), is not omitted in the Pada-pāṭha here: the sentence is different and so is the case ending. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All the gods also do not injure the worlds such as the earth, made by Indra with exceeding beauty, nor the many works such as sacrifices. That same Indra has upheld the earth, the heavenly world and the firmament. Indra, the doer of excellent deeds, has created the sun and the dawn.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, free from malice, your greatness is true; born, you drank Soma at once; heavens, days, months and years do not restrain your might. The grammar treats the accent and the forms अद्रोघ (*adrogha*) , अपिबः (*apibaḥ*) , मासाः (*māsāḥ*) , शरदः (*śaradaḥ*) , वरंत (*varaṃta*) with the roots and suffixes, and is transcribed, not explained. - शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)—whether the years (they cannot hold back)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who do harm to no one, your well-known greatness is real. It is known to the world that you drank the Soma juice at once when you were born. The heavenly world and the others, the days, the months and the years cannot hold back your power, mighty as you are.

*[The Bhāvārtha spells the word for "greatness" as ಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯವು (long vowel after the first letter; as supplied). Words broken across line ends are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Doer of no wrong, such was your true greatness, that as soon as born, you have quaffed the Soma juice : neither the heavens, nor days, nor months, nor years, resist the force of you who are mighty.

*[After the printed English the supplied text has a stray line with the number 96 (kept in the Kannada file as printed); it is not a page number of this window. The Special Topics are not printed for these Ṛks.]*
