##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Born at once, Indra drank Soma in the highest firmament for exhilaration; when he pervaded heaven and earth he became the ancient maker of rites. The opening lines say that the Ṛk begins the Niṣkevalya-śastra of the one-day Sadyaskra sacrifice and cite the sūtra of Ā. 9-5 (as in the Special Topics below).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra; सद्यः जातः (*sadyaḥ jātaḥ*)—as soon as you were born; परमे व्योमन् (*parame vyoman*)—standing in the excellent firmament
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for exhilaration
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice (the word is broken across a line end in the supplied text)
- अपिबः (*apibaḥ*)—drank
- यत् (*yat*)—when (you)
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth; आ अविवेशीः ह (*ā aviveśīḥ ha*)—pervaded, as though covering them
- अथ (*atha*)—immediately after that
- पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)—as the ancient one
- कारुधायाः (*kārudhāyāḥ*)—as the maker of rites
- अभवः (*abhavaḥ*)—you have become

### Printed p. 763

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as soon as you were born you drank the Soma juice, which causes joy, standing in the excellent firmament. When you entered these worlds as though covering heaven and earth entirely, immediately after that, being the ancient one, you became the maker of all rites.

*[Words broken across line ends in the Bhāvārtha are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
As soon as born in the highest heaven, you have quaffed, Indra, the Soma juice for your exhilaration; and when you had pervaded the heaven and earth, you became the primary artificer (of creation).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the one-day sacrifice called सद्यस्क्रि (*sadyaskri*), at the time of reciting the mantras of the निष्केवल्यशस्त्र (*niṣkevalyaśastra*), this Ṛk beginning त्वं सद्यो अपिबः (*tvaṃ sadyo apibaḥ*) is to be recited as the opening Ṛk. This is set out in the sūtra of the आश्वलायनश्रौतसूत्र (*āśvalāyanaśrautasūtra*): त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्रानु त्वाहिघ्ने अध देव देवाः (*tvaṃ sadyo apibo jāta iṃdrānu tvāhighne adha deva devāḥ*) (Ā. 9-5).

*[The sacrifice is named सद्यस्क्रि (*sadyaskri*) here but सद्यस्क्रीनाम्मेकाहे (*sadyaskrīnāmmekāhe*) in the bhāṣya; the sūtra is quoted with त्वाहिघ्ने (*tvāhighne*) here and त्वाहिष्टे (*tvāhiṣṭe*) in the bhāṣya. As supplied.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, from whom many worlds were born and who is exceedingly great, slew Ahi, who lay round the water and was mighty; heaven did not know his greatness, since Indra covers the earth with one flame.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुविजात (*tuvijāta*)—O Indra, who are the cause of the arising of many worlds such as the earth
- तव्यान् (*tavyān*)—you who are exceedingly grown great (the Kannada word after the dash is ಅತಿಯವಾಗಿ, as supplied; the Bhāvārtha has ಅತಿಶಯವಾಗಿ)
- अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)—of the water
- परिशयानं (*pariśayānaṃ*)—who lay spread all round
- ओजायमानं (*ojāyamānaṃ*)—who is mighty
- अहिं (*ahiṃ*)—the demon in the form of the cloud
- अहन् (*ahan*)—you destroyed
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- अन्यया (*anyayā*)—by one (of many kinds)
- स्फिग्या (*sphigyā*)—by the radiance
- क्षां (*kṣāṃ*)—the earth
- अवस्था (*avasthā*)—you stand covering (printed with a colon in place of the visarga, which is left out of the word quoted here)
- अथ (*atha*)—therefore
- ते (*te*)—your
- महित्वं (*mahitvaṃ*)—greatness
- दौः (*dauḥ*)—the heavenly world; न अनुभूत् (*na anubhūt*)—did not experience (could not know)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, from whom, as the Lord, the many worlds such as the earth arose, you who have grown exceedingly great destroyed the demon in the form of the cloud, who lay spread round the water and was mighty. For the reason that you stand covering the earth with only one of your radiances of many kinds, for that very reason even the heavenly world could not know your greatness.

*[The Bhāvārtha spells the word for "demon" with a long first vowel (as supplied). Words broken across line ends are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, from whom many are born; you who are vigorous have slain Ahi, enveloping the slumbering water, and confiding in his prowess: yet the heaven apprehended not your greatness as you remained concealing the earth by one of (your) flames.

*[The printed English is set in several short lines, joined here.]*

> लजु रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Our Soma-sacrifice strengthens and pleases Indra; may he protect the sacrificer through it, and may it protect his thunderbolt in slaying Vṛtra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—this sacrifice
- ते (*te*)—for you
- वर्धनः (*vardhanaḥ*)—as a strengthener (of your power); भूत् हि (*bhūt hi*)—certainly becomes
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सुतसोमः (*sutasomaḥ*)—which has the pressed Soma
- मियॆधः (*miyèdhaḥ*)—and is the essence: this sacrifice
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—is most dear to you; यज्ञॆ यः सन् (*yajñè yaḥ san*)—(you) being worthy of sacrifice (the word is broken across a line end in the supplied text and reads as supplied)
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrificer, the performer of the sacrifice, the yajamāna
- यज्ञेन (*yajñena*)—with the help of the sacrifice that is now being performed
- अव (*ava*)—protect (as the giver of the fruit)
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—this same sacrifice
- ते (*te*)—your
- वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)—thunderbolt
- अहिहत्ये (*ahihatye*)—at the time of destroying the demon
- आवत् (*āvat*)—may it protect

*[The Pratipadārtha spells the word for "essence" as मियॆधः (*miyèdhaḥ*) with a short vowel, while the Pada has मियेधः (*miyedhaḥ*); as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, this sacrifice will certainly be a strengthener of your power. And because Soma juice has been pressed in this sacrifice, which is the essence, it is dear to you. You, who are worthy of sacrifice, protect this sacrificer. And may this same sacrifice protect your thunderbolt at the time of destroying the demons.

*[Printed oddities kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಯಜಮಾನನ್ನು for "the sacrificer" and the plural ಅಸುರರನ್ನು for "the demons", where the Pratipadārtha has the singular. Words broken across line ends are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sacrificers turn Indra towards them with a protecting sacrifice; so may I turn you towards me for new wealth, you who grow by ancient, middle and new hymns.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अवसा (*avasā*)—with the protecting (all sacrificers also)
- यज्ञेन (*yajñena*)—by the sacrifice
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—you, the lord
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—facing themselves; आ चक्रे (*ā cakre*)—they make for themselves (the bracketed remark that follows breaks off at the end of the page and goes on below)

(ಆಡತಂತೆಯೇ ನಾನೂ ಸಹ) नव्यसे (*navyase*)—new; सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*)—for wealth; एनं (*enaṃ*)—you, who are Indra; आ ववृत्यां (*ā vavṛtyāṃ*)—I make (you) face me; यः (*yaḥ*)—you who; पूर्वेभिः (*pūrvebhiḥ*)—ancient; स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—by hymns; ववृथे (*vavṛthe*)—you gain growth (just as); मध्यमेभिः (*madhyamebhiḥ*)—also by intermediate praises; उत (*uta*)—and; नूतनेभिः (*nūtanebhiḥ*)—by these new praises that we are making, you gain growth also.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, all sacrificers also make you, the lord, face them by the protecting sacrifice. In the same way I also make you, Indra, face me for the gain of new wealth. You gain growth by the ancient praises and likewise by the intermediate and the new praises.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The worshipper, by his conservatory sacrifice, has made Indra present : may I bring him to my presence to obtain new wealth, him who has been exalted by praises, whether ancieut [sic], mediæval, or recent.

*[The printed English is set in several short lines, joined here; the word "present" is broken across a line end.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the thought of praising Indra enters me I compose praise before the obstructing days come, that he may carry us across sin, as people on both banks hail a man crossing by boat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*)—the thought of praising Indra
- विवेष (*viveṣa*)—entered me (and at once)
- जजान (*jajāna*)—I produce (the hymn that praises Indra)
- पार्यात् (*pāryāt*)—even when very far away
- अह्नः (*ahnaḥ*)—the obstructing days (before they arrive)
- पुरा (*purā*)—beforehand
- स्तवै (*stavai*)—I praise (Indra)
- उभये (*ubhaye*)—the people on both banks; नावेव यांतं (*nāveva yāṃtaṃ*)—as they respectfully call one who goes in a boat (so we also)
- यत्र (*yatra*)—on the arising of which thought, of the form of praise
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from sin
- यथा (*yathā*)—in which manner
- पीपरत् (*pīparat*)—he releases and makes happy, in that manner
- हवंते (*havaṃte*)—they pray to Indra and call him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the thought of praising Indra entered me, at once I compose a hymn of praise to Indra. Even while the obstructing days are still very far off, I praise Indra before they arrive. As the people on both banks respectfully call one who goes in a boat, so all on both sides of us pray to Indra and call him.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಇಂದ್ರೆನನ್ನು in one place for "Indra" (as supplied). The Bhāvārtha does not render the clause about being carried across sin. Words broken across line ends are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
When the thought of glorifying Indra entered my mind, then I gave birth (to his praises) : may I laud him before encountering distant (evil) days, whereby he may guide us beyond sin ; for those on both sides of us invoke him, as (those on either bank of a river hail) a passenger in a boat.

*[The printed English is set in several short lines, joined here. The window contains no Special Topics section.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The cup is full of Soma for Indra's drinking; I pour it out as a water-carrier pours water; the dear juices gather round him, clockwise, for his delight. The opening lines say that this Ṛk is the prasthita-yājyā of the Āgnīdhra at the midday pressing and cite the sūtra of Ā. 5-5 (as in the Special Topics below).

- कलशः (*kalaśaḥ*)—the Droṇa-kalaśa
- अपूर्ण (*apūrṇa*)—is filled (with Soma juice)
- कोशं (*kośaṃ*)—from a bag full of water
- सेक्तेव (*sekteva*)—as one who fills water pours the water into another vessel
- पिबध्यै (*pibadhyai*)—for your drinking
- सिसिचे (*sisice*)—the Soma juice is poured
- प्रियाः (*priyāḥ*)—sweet
- सोमासः (*somāsaḥ*)—Soma juices
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—you, the lord
- अभि (*abhi*)—directed towards (the word is broken across the page end: the Kannada ಉದ್ದೇ stands at the foot of this page and ಶಿಸಿ at the head of the next; read together it means "having aimed at")

मदाय (*madāya*)—for (your) delight; प्रदक्षिणित् (*pradakṣiṇit*)—clockwise, with circumambulation (a hyphen stands in place of the dash after the word, as supplied); सं आववृत्रन् (*saṃ āvavṛtran*)—have gathered and spread all round.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Droṇa-kalaśa is filled with Soma juice for your drinking. As one who fills water pours abundant water from a bag full of water into another vessel, the Soma juice is poured for your drinking. The sweet Soma juices, directed at you, the lord, have gathered and spread all round you, causing your delight.

*[Words broken across line ends are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The vase is filled for him (with Soma); welcome Indra : I pour it out for you to drink, as a water-carrier (pours water) from his bag : may the grateful Soma juice flow in reverence round Indra for his exhilaration.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the midday pressing the Ṛk beginning आपूर्णो अस्य (*āpūrṇo asya*) is applied as the प्रस्थितयाज्या (*prasthitayājyā*) mantra to be recited by the priest called अग्नीध्र (*agnīdhra*); this is made clear by the sūtra of the आश्वलायनश्रौतसूत्र (*āśvalāyanaśrautasūtra*) आपूर्णो अस्य कलशः स्वाहेति माध्यंदिन्यः (*āpūrṇo asya kalaśaḥ svāheti mādhyaṃdinyaḥ*) (Ā. 5-5).

*[The Special Topics spell the first word with a long initial vowel, आपूर्णो अस्य कलशः स्वाहेति माध्यंदिन्यः (*āpūrṇo asya kalaśaḥ svāheti mādhyaṃdinyaḥ*), while the bhāṣya quotes the sūtra with अपूर्णो अस्येति (*apūrṇo asyeti*) on page 769; as supplied.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Neither the deep ocean nor the mountains around hold you back; entreated by your friends, you broke the mighty fire (Ūrva) lying in the pit.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, desired by many, neither the very deep ocean nor the mountains that spread very high obstruct your spreading. For that very reason you, entreated by your friends, extinguished, though you are exceedingly powerful, the forest fire that lay in the deep cave of the mountain.

*[Words broken across line ends are joined here.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Invoked of many, the deep ocean arrests you not, nor do the accompanying mountains (stay you); and therefore, summoned by your friends, you have repressed the strong flame abiding in the abyss.

## Sūkta 33 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The thirty-third sūkta** (ಮೂವತ್ತಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

*[The heading of the sūkta stands directly after the ornament line in the supplied text, without a line break; as supplied.]*

**Pīṭhikā (Introduction)**

Concerning the seer Viśvāmitra *[the supplied text prints the first word of the line as ಪಿತ್ವಾಮಿತ್ರಋಷಿಯ, with a different first letter of the name; as supplied]*, Yāska says in his Nirukta:

विश्वामित्रऋषिः सुदासः पैजवनस्य पुरोहितो बभूव । विश्वामित्रः सर्वमित्रः । सर्व संस्कृतं । सुदाः कल्याणदानः । पैजवनः पिजवनस्य पुत्रः । पिजवनः पुनः स्पर्धनीयजवो वा मिश्रीभावगतिर्वान् ॥ स वित्तं गृहीत्वा विपाट् छुतुद्रोः संभवमाययौ । अनुययुरितरे । स विश्वामित्रो नदीस्तुष्टाव-गाधा भवत इति। अपि द्विवदपि बहुवत् तद्यद्द्वदुपरिष्कात्तद्व्याख्यास्यामः ॥ (*viśvāmitraṛṣiḥ sudāsaḥ paijavanasya purohito babhūva | viśvāmitraḥ sarvamitraḥ | sarva saṃskṛtaṃ | sudāḥ kalyāṇadānaḥ | paijavanaḥ pijavanasya putraḥ | pijavanaḥ punaḥ spardhanīyajavo vā miśrībhāvagatirvān ‖ sa vittaṃ gṛhītvā vipāṭ chutudroḥ saṃbhavamāyayau | anuyayuritare | sa viśvāmitro nadīstuṣṭāva-gādhā bhavata iti| api dvivadapi bahuvat tadyaddvadupariṣkāttadvyākhyāsyāmaḥ ‖*) (Si, 9-24)

*[The supplied text prints the reference with the abbreviation ಸಿ and a comma; as supplied, not expanded. Line-end hyphens inside the Sanskrit passage are joined (logged).]*

Thus an old story is told. The meaning of the parts of the word Viśvāmitra is that this seer is a friend to all, or that all are his friends. This seer was the priest of the king named Sudāsa, son of Pijavana. Once, taking the wealth given by that king and setting out to go to his hermitage, he came to the place of confluence of the rivers Vipāṭ and Śatudri (the present Beas and Sutlej of the Punjab). Thieves who wished to seize the wealth he carried were following him. Knowing this, Viśvāmitra tried by some means to cross these rivers that lay across his path, but they were very deep with the water of the flood and it was not possible. Then the seer prayed to these rivers and praised them, that they should reduce their water and make it convenient for him to pass; this is said in the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33 (the supplied text adds the ordinal ending of "the 33rd" after the bracket) and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53, in the Ṛks 9 to 11.

*[Printed oddities kept: the supplied text has ಅಶ್ರಮಕ್ಕೆ for "to the hermitage" and, in the next paragraph, ವಿಶ್ರಾಮಿತ್ರಋಷಿಯು for the seer's name. As supplied.]*

This seer Viśvāmitra, in the above sūkta, that is, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-5, has said of himself that he is the son of Kuśika. It is said in the Rāmāyaṇa, the Bhārata and other Purāṇas that there was enmity and ill-will between Viśvāmitra and the seer Vasiṣṭha. There is support for this in a few places in the Ṛgveda also. That will be discussed in the Pīṭhikā of this part.

### Printed p. 774

The conversation of Viśvāmitra with the rivers Vipāṭ and Śatudri.

त्रयोविंशतिरैंद्राणि इच्छंतीति पराण्यतः । सूक्ते प्रेति तु नद्यश्च विश्वामित्रः समूदिरे ॥ (*trayoviṃśatiraiṃdrāṇi icchaṃtīti parāṇyataḥ | sūkte preti tu nadyaśca viśvāmitraḥ samūdire ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 4-105)

Beginning with the mantra इच्छंति (*icchaṃti*), there are in all 23 sūktas, that is, from the 30th sūkta of the third maṇḍala to the 52nd sūkta, that praise Indra. But the sūkta that begins with the mantra प्र (*pra*) alone describes the conversation of Viśvāmitra and the rivers; after stating this preface, the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā have then told minutely the order of the conversation, along with the historical situation that is the source of their conversation.

पुरोहितस्सन्निज्यार्थं सुदासा सह यन्नृषिः । विपाट्भुतुद्रोः संभेदं शमित्येते उवाच ह ॥ (*purohitassannijyārthaṃ sudāsā saha yannṛṣiḥ | vipāṭbhutudroḥ saṃbhedaṃ śamityete uvāca ha ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 4-106)

Viśvāmitra, as priest of Sudāsa, helped in his sacrificial rites. Once, while he was going with Sudāsa, he reached on the way the confluence of the rivers Vipāṭ and Śutudrī. Addressing those rivers, which were an obstruction to their way, Viśvāmitra prayed them to leave the way, and prayed शं (*śaṃ*) "be gracious to us and leave the way for us".

प्रवादास्तत्र दृश्यंते द्विवद्भुवदेकवत् । अच्छेत्यर्धर्चे पच्चो वा नदीष्वप्येकवन्निते ॥ (*pravādāstatra dṛśyaṃte dvivadbhuvadekavat | acchetyardharce pacco vā nadīṣvapyekavannite ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 4-107)

In this sūkta the conversation is presented in the singular, the dual and the plural, all three. In the earlier half of the verse beginning अच्छा (*acchā*) (3-33-3), and likewise in places such as निते (*nite*) (3-33-10,11) and the like, the singular is used. These are addressed to the rivers.

आद्ये द्वृचे द्विवत्सार्धे विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुतेः । एताभिर्यग्भर्वान् नद्य ऋषिं बहुवदूचिरे ॥ (*ādye dvṛce dvivatsārdhe viśvāmitravacaḥ śruteḥ | etābhiryagbharvān nadya ṛṣiṃ bahuvadūcire ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 4-108)

In the first two mantras of the sūkta and in the latter half of the third mantra the dual number is used. The Śruti tells that these are the words of Viśvāmitra. Besides, as will be told below, the rivers address Viśvāmitra in the plural.

षष्ट्याष्टम्या चतुर्थ्या च दशम्या चेतरा ऋषेः । सप्तम्यामृचि षष्ट्यां च यौ देवौ परिकीर्तितौ निपातिन् तु तौ ज्ञेयौ ॥ (*ṣaṣṭyāṣṭamyā caturthyā ca daśamyā cetarā ṛṣeḥ | saptamyāmṛci ṣaṣṭyāṃ ca yau devau parikīrtitau nipātin tu tau jñeyau ‖*) (4-109, 110)

*[The reference is printed without an abbreviation and the closing words of the verse stand on a third line; as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 775

In the fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth mantras the rivers address Viśvāmitra. All the rest are the words of the seer. The two deities named in the sixth and seventh mantras are also deities praised according to the context—

In this way the matter that Sudāsa and Viśvāmitra, both together, prayed to the rivers to make it easy for them to cross is stated in the Bṛhaddevatā. But in the sentences of the Saṃhitā the naming of Sudāsa does not occur in this context. Viśvāmitra has told in his prayer that it will be a help to the Bharatas who were engaged in the search for cows. Therefore, whether there is a difference between what is stated in the Bṛhaddevatā and what is explained in the Saṃhitā sentence, or whether the Bharatas and Sudāsa were of one and the same group, and similar matters, have to be considered here. This matter is told in the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, in the introduction of the sūkta, in this way:

पुरा किल विश्वामित्रः पैजवनस्य सुदासो राज्ञः पुरोहितो बभूव । स च पौरोहित्येन लब्धजनः सर्वं धनमादाय विपाट्टुतुद्रोः संभेद माययौ अनुययुरितरे । अथोत्तितीर्षुर्विश्वामित्रः आगाधजले ते नद्यौ दृष्ट्वा उत्तरणार्थं अद्याभिः तिसृभिः तुष्टाव ॥ (*purā kila viśvāmitraḥ paijavanasya sudāso rājñaḥ purohito babhūva | sa ca paurohityena labdhajanaḥ sarvaṃ dhanamādāya vipāṭṭutudroḥ saṃbheda māyayau anuyayuritare | athottitīrṣurviśvāmitraḥ āgādhajale te nadyau dṛṣṭvā uttaraṇārthaṃ adyābhiḥ tisṛbhiḥ tuṣṭāva ‖*) (Sā. Bhā. Pīṭhikā 3-33).

*[The Sanskrit passage is set in prose over several lines in the supplied text, one word being divided between two lines without a hyphen; the lines are joined as printed.]*

In the past Viśvāmitra was the family priest of the king named Sudāsa, the son of Pijavana. He, having obtained by his priesthood the support of the people, took all the wealth and reached the confluence of the rivers Vipāṭ and Śutudrī. Others also followed him. Then, seeing the rivers with very deep currents, the seer praised them with the first three mantras in order to cross them. Thus the context of the story is told. These sentences tell the relation between Sudāsa and Viśvāmitra. Who this Sudāsa was, who Bharata was, what the relation of Sudāsa and Bharata is, whether the priesthood common to both was Viśvāmitra's alone, and similar matters have to be examined here. To proceed with that, we must first know what the details of the conversation between Viśvāmitra and the rivers are.

Born from the lap-regions of the mountains, like horses that run vying with one another with loosened bonds because their bridles have been slackened, and like two cows running eagerly to approach their calves, the two rivers Vipāṭ and Śutudrī flow swiftly with their united streams. (1)

O rivers, as a charioteer runs with his chariot to his goal, you two, urged by Indra and obeying Indra's command, go united towards the ocean. Flowing together and showing increase by your respective waves, O shining rivers, one of you follows the other. (2)

*[The Kannada translation of the first two Ṛks of Sūkta 33 ends the supplied text of this window; the printed numbers (1) and (2) stand at the ends of the two paragraphs.]*

### Printed p. 776

I approach the river Vipāṭ, who has exceedingly great motherly love. This river, which is broad and auspicious, and the Śutudri, like cows that rush with speed to love the calf, go together and reach the shelter that is common to both. (3)

The rivers: With this our current we make the earth fruitful, and, according to the ordinance of the god Indra, we flow on and reach our abode in the form of the ocean, appointed by him. Following the path made by Indra, let there be no delay beyond the proper time for us to go and reach our destination. What may be the wish of this seer who prays to us? We wish to know it. (4)

Viśvāmitra: O rivers, filled with floods of water, for me who have set out to fetch Soma, hold back your current a little. That is my prayer. I, the son of Kuśika, desiring protection, humbly pray to the river Śutudri that lies before me. (5)

The rivers: When Indra, whose arm bears the vajra, killed the Ahi that lay across the whole flow of the waters, he made all the channels that suit our current. Subject to the control of Indra, who has an excellent hand and is the impeller of the world, we flow. (6)

Viśvāmitra *[the speaker's name is printed ವಿಶ್ರಾಮಿತ್ರ here, with a different second letter; as supplied]*: Having killed the demon Vṛtra with his vajra weapon, and having removed the obstruction to the free flow of the waters so that they flow at will, Indra, whose deeds are extraordinary, has heroic deeds that are all always worthy of praise. (7)

The rivers: O seer who praise Indra, do not forget the words of praise that you have now recited. By these same words this same praise will have to be performed in the ages to come. O seer, doer of good rites, serve us with these same words of praise, which are in the form of a dialogue. But do not deal with us in a bold manner, like human beings. Let there be salutation to you. (8)

Viśvāmitra: O rivers, who are like my brothers and sisters, be gracious to me who praise you. I have come from a great distance with my chariot and with other loads. To help me, reduce your currents a little. Make it convenient for me and my followers to cross. Regulate the current to a level a little below the level of the ಇರುಚಿ of our chariot wheel *[the Kannada word for this part of the wheel is printed so; its meaning is not settled here, so it is left untranslated; as supplied]*. (9)

The rivers: O praising seer, we grant your prayer. It is true also that you have come from a far region with a chariot that carries a load. We shall flow bending before you. As a mother bends to lift her dear child, and as a young woman bends to embrace her beloved, we flow bending. (10)

### Printed p. 777

Viśvāmitra: O rivers, you have made many conveniences for crossing you easily. May the Bharatas who are with me also cross your united current. May the whole company that follows us also, favoured by you and impelled by Indra, cross your current. We are worthy of the favour of you who are worthy of our praise. After we have crossed you, bring your current back to its former state. (11)

The Bharatas, who set out in search of cows, crossed the rivers. The seer, having accepted the regard of the rivers, was gratified. "O rivers, as distributors of the wealth of food and as those who increase that same wealth, carry on your current. Filling also your banks, flow with full current." (12)

*[The seer's words in this paragraph are enclosed in quotation marks in the supplied text.]*

Even so, let the ಮೂಕಿ of the yoke of our chariot be above the level of the current *[the word for the part of the yoke is printed so; the meaning of the first word is not settled here, so it is left untranslated; as supplied]*. You flow at that very measure. May the faultless and irreproachable Vipāṭ and Śutudri flow full. (13)

In this manner Viśvāmitra praised the rivers and crossed them: that is the subject of this sūkta. The matters that deserve consideration in the present context are these:

(1) In the sūkta the name of Sudāsa is not mentioned. But in the Bṛhaddevatā and in the introduction of the bhāṣya it is stated clearly that Viśvāmitra set out with Sudāsa. What is the basis for that?

(2) In the Saṃhitā it is stated that Viśvāmitra crossed the river along with the Bharatas. Are Sudāsa and the Bharatas of the same lineage, or different? When Viśvāmitra, the son of Kuśika, took up the priesthood of Sudāsa, the Paijavana, was there friendship or not between Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha, who was appointed in the same ಕಾವ್ಯ *[so printed; the word means "poem"; as supplied]*?

Such matters give scope for critical examination of historical subjects. If the personal nature and capacity of Viśvāmitra, the extraordinary deeds that he performed, and similar matters are understood, then a satisfying answer to the above problems will be obtained. Who were the forefathers of Viśvāmitra, how there was friendship between them and the people of the Bharata line, and the points that are absolutely necessary for the examination of these and of the above-mentioned problems, are explained in the introduction (Pīṭhikā) of this same part. The introduction is concluded *[the first word of this closing line is printed ಜೀರಿಕೆ, apparently a misreading of the word for "introduction"; as supplied]*.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seers, metre and deity are named (the rivers for the Ṛks they speak, Viśvāmitra for the rest; Indra the deity); Viśvāmitra, priest of Sudāsa, taking his wealth, came to the confluence of the Vipāṭ and the Śutudri, found the rivers deep, and praised them with the first three Ṛks in order to cross. Line-end hyphens inside the Sanskrit are joined (logged). The Anuvāda lines and the sūkta data that the supplied text had inside this block are moved out into the text below. Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has लब्धधनः (*labdhadhanaḥ*) whereas the same passage as quoted earlier in the introduction has a different consonant in the second part of that word; the Anuvāda quotation of the Anukramaṇikā reads प्र पर्वतानां सपोना (*pra parvatānāṃ saponā*) against प्र पर्वतानां सप्तोना (*pra parvatānāṃ saptonā*) in the block; as supplied.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, which begins with प्र पर्वतानां (*pra parvatānāṃ*), is the fourth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are thirteen Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: प्र पर्वतानां सपोना संवादो नदीभिर्विश्वामित्रस्योत्तीर्षोस्तत्र नदीवाक्यं चतुर्थिषष्यष्टमीदशम्यः षष्ठिसप्तमोस्त्विंद्रस्तुतिरंत्यानुष्टुप् (*pra parvatānāṃ saponā saṃvādo nadībhirviśvāmitrasyottīrṣostatra nadīvākyaṃ caturthiṣaṣyaṣṭamīdaśamyaḥ ṣaṣṭhisaptamostviṃdrastutiraṃtyānuṣṭup*). That is, in this sūkta, the fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth Ṛks being words of the rivers, the rivers are the seers of those Ṛks; the remaining Ṛks being words of Viśvāmitra, Viśvāmitra is their seer; the last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre.

(Anuvāda, continued.) Indra is the deity. But in the sixth and seventh Ṛks Viśvāmitra *[the supplied text prints a different first letter of the name; as supplied]* and the rivers are praised. Even so, Indra is the deity of these Ṛks also. The application of the sūkta is लैंगिक (*laiṃgika*) *[so printed, with the Kannada ending of the neuter]*.

(Anuvāda, continued.) Formerly the seer Viśvāmitra, the seer of this sūkta, was priest to a king named Sudāsa, the son of one named Pijavana *[printed so, without the diphthong that the bhāṣya has in the word for "son of Pijavana"; as supplied]*. Taking all the wealth gained by that priesthood, when he was going to his hermitage, the confluence of the rivers Vipāṭ and Śutudri came in his way and he had to cross it. Some wicked men followed this seer, wishing to seize his wealth. Then, since those rivers had much water and were deep, it was not possible to cross, and he praised those rivers with the first three Ṛks of this sūkta. The conversation that took place between Viśvāmitra and the rivers is told in this sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पर्वतानां गिरीणां शैलानामुपस्थादुत्संगान्निर्गत्योशती समुद्रगमनं कामयमाने । गमने दृष्टांतः। अश्वे इव । यथा विषिते मंदुरातो विमुक्ते हासमाने अन्नोन्यजवेन स्पर्धमाने । यद्वा हृष्यंत्यावश्वे इव वडवे इव त्वरया गच्छंत्यौ परस्परं हृष्यंत्यौ । तथा गावेव शुभ्रे। यथा द्वौ गावौ शोभमानौ वर्तते
> तद्वच्छुभ्रे शोभमाने। किंच मातरा । यथा मातरौ धेनू रिहाणे । अंतर्णीतसनर्थो लिहिः । वत्सं जिह्वया लेढुमिच्छंत्यौ शीघ्रं गच्छतस्तद्वत्समुद्रं गंतुं जवाद्धच्छंत्यौ पयसा संयुक्ते विपाट् । कूलविपाटनात् विपाशनाद्वा विमोचनाद्वा
> विपाट् । शुतुद्री । शु क्षिप्रं तु तुन्ना तुन्नेव द्रवति गच्छतीति शुतुद्री । एतन्नामके
> नद्यौ प्र जवेते । समुद्रं प्रति शीघ्रं गच्छतः । आत्र निरुक्तं । पर्वतानामुपस्थादुपस्थानादुशत्यौ कामयमाने अश्वे इव विमुक्ते इति वा विषण्णॆ इति वा हासमाने
> हासतिः स्पर्धायां हर्षमाणेवा गावानिव शुभ्रे शोभने मातरौ संरिहाणे विपाट्‌भुतुदौ पयसा प्रजवेते। नि. ९-३९ । इति ॥उशती । वश कांत् । अस्य शतुर्जु
> त्वाद्ग्रहिज्यावयीत्यादिना संप्रसारणं । विषिते । षिञ् बंधन इत्यस्य कर्मणि निष्ठा ।
> संहितायां परिनिविभ्यः सेवसितसयसिवुसहेत्यादिना । पा. ८-३-७० । षत्वं । गतिरनंतर
> गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः । हासमाने । हासतिः स्पर्धाकर्मा हसे हसने ना । शानच् । तस्य
> लसार्वधातुकस्वरे कृते धातुस्वरः । रिहाणी । लिह आस्वादने । स्वरितेत्त्वादुभयपदी ।
> शानच् । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । लकारस्य रेफश्चांदसः । रेफमवलंब्य णत्वं । चि
> त्वादंतोदात्तः । विपाट् । पट गतौ पश बाधनस्पर्शनयोरिति वा ण्यंतावेत् विपूर्वौ । शकारस्य व्रश्चादिना षत्वं । शुतुद्री । छांदसी रूपसिद्धिः । जवेते । जुज्
> गतौ । भौवादिकः । जुत्वादात्मनेपदं । आतो जित इतीयादेशः । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two rivers, leaving the flanks of the mountains and longing for the sea, run like loosed mares vying with each other and like two shining cows hastening to lick their calves; the names Vipāṭ and Śutudri are explained and the Nirukta passage is quoted; the grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained. Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: the Nirukta quotation in the block has the name of the second river in a form that differs from the Saṃhitā (a different first consonant and a different ending); the double danda before the first grammatical word is joined to it without a space; as supplied.

- विषिते (*viṣite*)—released from the stall (the two mares)
- हासमाने (*hāsamāne*)—contending with each other; अश्वे इव (*aśve iva*)—like two mares

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The two mares that are loosed from the stall and compete with one another run swiftly, and the two fair mother cows, eager to lick their calves lovingly, run remembering their calves; just so the rivers called Vipāṭ and Śutudri, filled with water, desire to join the sea and flow from the flanks of the mountains with a swift current.

*[The Kannada Bhāvārtha ends with a comma instead of a full stop; as supplied. The word for "cows" is printed with an extra nasal sign; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Rushing from the flanks of the mountains, eager (to reach the sea) like two mares with loosened reins contending (with each other in speed), like two fair mother cows (hastening) to caress (their calves), the Vipash and Shutudri, flow rapidly with (united) waters.

*[The printed English is set in several short lines, joined here; nothing else changed.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O rivers, sent by Indra and asking his leave, you go toward the sea like two charioteers to their goal, flowing together, swelling with waves and cooling the surrounding country; one of you joins the other. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O rivers, you two flow together and cool the surrounding country with your waves, and you are resplendent. Impelled by Indra and asking his permission, you flow solemnly toward the sea like two charioteers. One of you joins the other.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O rivers, I, Viśvāmitra, have come to you, Śutudri, the flowing one, the most motherly, and we have reached the great fortunate Vipāś; you two, like two mother cows hastening to lick a calf, flow together toward the one common place, the sea. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As mother cows, gathering together, run toward the one common shelter, the cowshed, to smell and lick their calves, so, O rivers, you flow with your faces toward the vessel in the form of the sea, which is common to you both. Among you the river called Śutudri is the foremost mother among nourishing mothers; the one called Vipāṭ is of great form and fortunate. I come to the two of you of this kind, and take refuge, for my own nourishment.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two rivers answer Viśvāmitra: swelling with water and flowing toward the place of the sea ordered by Indra, their impulse to go forward does not turn back; what does the Brahmin want that he calls them so urgently? ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We two, named Vipāṭ and Śutudri, giving full satisfaction to the whole world with our abundant water, are flowing toward the place of the sea directed by Indra, the lord. The undertaking of our flow cannot stop at all. Keeping what wish (for what purpose) is this Viśvāmitra calling us?

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
[The rivers speak] Fertilizing (the land) with this (our) current, we are flowing to the receptacle which has been appointed by the deity (Indra): the course appointed for our going (permits) not of delay : of what is the sage desirous, that he addresses the rivers ?

*[The printed English is set in several short lines, joined here; nothing else changed.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O rivers full of water, for the sake of my prayer, who have set out to bring Soma, check also your swift currents for a little while. O Śutudri, I, the son of Kuśika, desiring my own protection, humbly pray to you with great praise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
[Vishwamitra speaks] Rivers, charged with water, rest a moment from your course at my request, who go to gather the Soma (plant) : I, the son of Kushika, desirous of protection, address with earnest prayer especially the river before me.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The rivers answer Viśvāmitra: Indra with the thunderbolt in his arm struck Vṛtra, the cloud that surrounded the waters, and when he was struck the waters fell, and we, the flowing rivers, were dug out by them; Savitṛ of the good hands, the shining Indra, led them, filling the sea with water; under the command of such an Indra the broad rivers go, and do not stop at Viśvāmitra's word. *[Printed oddities kept: the first headword ("holding the thunderbolt in the arm") is printed with a colon in place of the visarga; the order of the glosses differs from the Saṃhitā (Indra and Vṛtra come first, then "our"); after the entry for "of that" the next headword is the word ಅನುಜ್ಞಾಂ, which is not a word of the Saṃhitā, so no entry stands for the word for "in the impulse"; and the last gloss is printed ಪ್ರಹಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇವೆ, where the Bhāvārtha has ಪ್ರವಹಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇವೆ; translated as "flowing"; as supplied. A gloss is broken inside a word at a line end without a hyphen ("destroyed"), read whole.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viśvāmitra, Indra, holding the thunderbolt in his hand, destroyed the demon in the form of the cloud who stood around as an obstacle to the river waters, and released our gateways of flow. Indra, the impeller of the world, of the excellent hand, and shining, made our flow favourable. We, full of that abundant water, are flowing as obedient to that Indra.

*[Two words of the Bhāvārtha look misprinted: the word for "obstacle" is printed ತತೆಯಾಗಿ (the Pratipadārtha has ತಡೆಯಾಗಿ) and the word for "water" is printed ಉವಕದಿಂದ (the Pratipadārtha has the word with the other consonant); the sense of the Pratipadārtha is translated; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
[The rivers speak] Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, dug our channels when he slew Ahi the blocker-up of rivers : the divine and well-handed Savitri has led us (on our path), and obedient to his commands we flow (as) ample (streams).

*[A space stands before the colon; as supplied.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra's exploit of cutting the cloud is ever to be praised; he struck the obstructing demons with the thunderbolt, and the waters went seeking their course. ##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहिं (*ahiṃ*)—the demon in the form of the cloud
- विवृश्चत् (*vivṛścat*)—(so that the flow of water might be favourable) "he killed", namely; यत् कर्म (*yat karma*)—whatever deed there is
- तत् (*tat*)—that great deed of Indra, and
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- वीर्यं (*vīryaṃ*)—the might, also
- शश्वधा (*śaśvadhā*)—always
- प्रवाच्यं (*pravācyaṃ*)—to be praised exceedingly

*[The gloss of the second word ends with the linking word meaning "namely" and runs on into the next entry (the deed that is the "killing"); translated as it stands.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The deed of Indra, that he killed the demon in the form of the cloud so that the flow of water might be favourable, that great deed and also the might of Indra are always to be praised exceedingly. Indra killed with the thunderbolt the demons spread all around. Afterwards the waters, desiring their own place to go to, flow.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
[Vishwamitra speaks] Ever is that heroic exploit of Indra to be celebrated when he cut Ahi to pieces, and with his thunderbolt destroyed the surrounding (obstructors of the rain), whence the waters proceed in the direction they desire.

*[The printed English is set in short lines with a line-end hyphen ("cele-brated"); the lines are joined and the hyphen removed.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viśvāmitra, the praiser, whatever words of praise of yours praise us, those you must certainly never forget. O excellent maker of śastras, in the coming times of sacrifice, at the times of prayer that take place, serve us also; among other men do not give occasion for harsh words about us. Salutation to you.

> स्रोतःशब्दात्स्रोतसो विभाषा ड्यड् ड्यौ । पा. ४-४-११३ । इति ड्यप्रत्ययः । डित्वाट्टलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

*[The label is printed twice in succession in the supplied text; the first is kept in the Kannada file as an italic line.]*

स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—you who are sisters; सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—O rivers; कारवे (*kārave*)—of me, the praiser, (the prayer); सु ओ श्रुणोत (*su o śruṇota*)—listen well and attentively; अनसा (*anasā*)—with a cart; रथेन (*rathena*)—and also with a chariot; दूरात् (*dūrāt*)—from a very distant region; वः (*vaḥ*)—to you, near you; ययौ (*yayau*)—I have come and arrived; सु नमध्वं (*su namadhvaṃ*)—become bowed down by lessening your flow; भवत (*bhavata*)—be; स्रोत्याभिः (*srotyābhiḥ*)—with the waters in the form of your streams; अधोअक्षाः (*adhoakṣāḥ*)—being bent down to below the axle of my chariot, and; सुपाराः (*supārāḥ*)—be having banks easy to cross.

*[The headword for "listen" is printed ಸು ಓ ಶ್ರುಣೋತ, with the vowel sign u after the consonant group, where the bhāṣya has शृणोत (*śṛṇota*); the danda after the fourth gloss stands without a space before it; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sister rivers, listen well and attentively to the prayer of me, the praiser. I have come and arrived near you from a very distant region with a cart and also with a chariot. Lessen your flow, and let your flow be lower than the axle of our cart. Let your banks be easy for me to cross.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
[Vishwamitra speaks] Listen, sister (streams), kindly to him who praises you ; who has come from afar with a waggon and chariot: bow down lowlily ; become easily fordable ; remain, rivers, lower than the axle (of the wheel) with your currents.

*[The printed English is set in several short lines, joined here; the word "lowlily" and the spacing before the semicolons are as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नद्यः पूर्वं विश्वामित्रवाक्यं प्रत्याख्यायानयर्चा तस्य वाक्यमाशुश्रुवुः ।
> कारो स्तोत्रं कुर्वाण हे विश्वामित्र ते तव वचांसीमानि वाक्यान्या शृणवाम ।
> शृणुमः । तव समाहितं प्रयोजन कुर्म इत्यर्थः । अनसा शकटेन रथेन च सह
> ययाथ । यतो दूरादागतोऽसि । वयं च ते त्वदर्थं नि नंस्यॆ । नीचैर्नमाम ।
> प्रत्येकविवक्षयात्रैकवचनं। रथेन गंतुं गाधोदका भवामेत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः।
> पीप्यानेव योषा । पीप्याना पुत्रं स्तनं पाययंती योषा माता यथा प्रह्विभवति । दृष्टांतांतरं । यथा कन्या युवतिर्मर्यायेव मनुष्याय पित्रे भ्रात्रे
> ना शश्वचै परिष्वजनाय नम्रा भवति तद्वत्ते त्वदर्थं प्रह्वीभवादुः । ते इति पुनरुक्तिरादरार्थ० । एतामृचं यास्क एवं व्याचष्टे । आशृणवाम ते कारो वचनानि याहि
> दूरादनसा च रथेन च निनमाम ते पाययमानेव योषा पुत्रं मर्यायेव
> कन्या परिष्वजनाय निनमा इति वा । नि. २-२७ । इति ॥ कारो । संबुद्धौ शाकल्यस्येत् ।
> पा. १-१ १६ । इति प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा । शृणवाम । श्रु श्रवण इत्यस्य लोट्याडुत्तमस्य पिच्चेत्याडागमः ! पित्त्वाद्दुणः । निघातः । ययाथ । या प्रापण इत्यस्य भूतमात्रे लिटि
> थलैकाच उपदेशेनुदात्तादितीट् प्रतिषेधः । लित्सरः । अनसा । सहार्थे तृतीया ।
> नंस्यॆ । णमु प्रहत्व इत्यस्य लेटुत्तमे लेटि सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् । वैतोन्यत्रेत्यैकारादेशः । निघातः । पीप्यानेव । पीज् पान इत्यस्यांतर्भावितण्यर्थस्य लिट कानचि
> रूपं । चित्स्वरः । योषा । यु मिश्रणे । वृत्यवदिहनीत्यादिना । उ. ३-६२ । सप्रत्ययः । यौतीति योषा । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । शश्वचै । स्वन्ज परिप्पंग इत्यस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । पृषोदरादित्वादिष्टरूपसिद्धिरंतोदात्तश्च ॥१३॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The rivers, who had earlier answered Viśvāmitra, now say that they have heard his words, and will bow low and be fordable for his cart and chariot, as a nursing mother and a maiden bend. The Nirukta passage on the Ṛk is quoted (Ni. 2-27) and the grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained. Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). ### Printed p. 793

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viśvāmitra, the praiser, we have listened attentively to your words of praise. You have come from a very distant region with a cart and also with a chariot. Just as a mother bends in order to give the child the breast, and just as a maiden bends to be favourable for a man's embrace, so, for you, we lower our flow and bow down.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
[The rivers speak] Hymner, we hear your words. that you have come from afar with a waggon and a chariot : we bow down before you : like a woman nursing (her child), like a maiden bending to embrace a man, (so will we do) for you.

*[The printed English has a lower-case "that" after a full stop and a space before each colon; as supplied.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given the explanation (nirvacana) for this *[the supplied text has ಮಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆ, "to the children"; as supplied]*:

आ शृणवाम ते कारो वचनानि याहि दूरादनसा च रथेन च निननाम ते पाययमानेव योषा पुत्रं मर्यायेव कन्या परिष्वजनाय निनमा इति वा ॥ (*ā śṛṇavāma te kāro vacanāni yāhi dūrādanasā ca rathena ca ninanāma te pāyayamāneva yoṣā putraṃ maryāyeva kanyā pariṣvajanāya ninamā iti vā ‖*)

(Si. 9-27) *[the abbreviation before the reference is printed as ಸಿ. ೯-೨೭, i.e. with another first letter, and the number with 9 where the bhāṣya (page 792) has the Nirukta reference with 2 (Ni. 2-27); the quotation has ನಿನನಾಮ where the bhāṣya has ನಿನಮಾಮ; as supplied]*

The rivers speak to Viśvāmitra thus: O Viśvāmitra, who praise us *[the supplied text prints the name as ವಿಶ್ರಾಮಿತ್ರನನ್ನು, with a different first letter; as supplied]*, we have listened attentively to your words. You have come here from a very distant region with your cart and your chariot. Therefore, so that you may cross us, the rivers, easily, just as a woman bends in order to give her child the breast, or as a newly married maiden *[printed ಕನೈಯು, an irregular spelling of the word for "maiden" that differs from the Kannada form used in the gloss of the Pratipadārtha (ಕನ್ಯಾ ಇವ—); as supplied]* bends bashfully for the embrace of her husband, we shall lower our currents and bow down for you. This is the main sense.

> श्रुकः कितीति निष्ठायामिट् प्रतिषेधः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ।
> अर्षात् । ऋ गतानित्यस्य लेटि तिपि सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् । लेटोडागमः ! एकाच
> इतीट् प्रतिषेधः । गुणः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । वृणे । वृज् संभक्तावित्यस्य लट रूपं । यज्जियानां यज्ञर्त्वग्भ्यां घखञाविति घप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra answers the rivers: since they have allowed him to cross, may the Bharatas, the host that wishes to cross, urged on by Indra, cross; he takes refuge in the praise-worthy favour of the rivers. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words भरताः (*bharatāḥ*), संतरेयुः (*saṃtareyuḥ*), गव्यन् (*gavyan*), ग्रामः (*grāmaḥ*), इंद्रजूतः (*iṃdrajūtaḥ*), अर्षात् (*arṣāt*) and वृणे (*vṛṇe*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent), with one printed Uṇādi reference, U. 1-142. Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: the short Kannada e sign appears in सर्वॆ (*sarvè*); the word for "going" is printed सर्गतक्को (*sargatakko*) (the Saṃhitā and the Pada of this Ṛk, on page 793, have other forms of it); the last word is printed यज्जियानां (*yajjiyānāṃ*) where the Saṃhitā of this Ṛk has a different spelling of the word; an exclamation mark stands for a danda after लेटोडागमः (*leṭoḍāgamaḥ*); the block ends with the danda sign and no Ṛk number; all as supplied.

- यत् (*yat*)—by that favour by which you have made an opening for me to cross, by that same favour

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you who have become one in the form of a confluence
- संतरेयुः (*saṃtareyuḥ*)—may it be favourable for them to cross

- इंद्रजूतः (*iṃdrajūtaḥ*)—those impelled by Indra
- ग्रामः (*grāmaḥ*)—the host of those born in the Bharata line

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O rivers, by that same favour of yours by which you have made an opening for me to cross, may all my kinsmen born in the Bharata family find it easy to cross you, who have become one in the form of a confluence. May the host of those born in the Bharata line, who wish to cross the water, who are permitted by you and impelled by Indra, cross you. The undertaking of those who have set out on a journey has been permitted by you. I recite fully the excellent praise of you who are worthy of sacrifice.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Bharatas who wished for cattle crossed; the wise Viśvāmitra received the favour of the rivers; the rivers are told to fill the canals, which cause food to grow, and to flow swiftly. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words अतारिषुः (*atāriṣuḥ*), गव्यवः (*gavyavaḥ*), अभक्त (*abhakta*), इषयंतीः (*iṣayaṃtīḥ*), पृणध्वं (*pṛṇadhvaṃ*), यात (*yāta*) and शीभं (*śībhaṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: आश्मन (*āśmana*) stands where one expects the word for "self"; the river-name is printed सदीनां (*sadīnāṃ*); the form for "flow" is पिन्नध्वं (*pinnadhvaṃ*) where the Saṃhitā and the Pada have पिन्वध्वं (*pinvadhvaṃ*); the block ends with the danda sign and no Ṛk number; all as supplied.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra asks that the wave stay below the ropes and the waters flow without touching the traces; the sinless, blameless rivers are to give no swollen flood, and so he crosses with their leave. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words ऊर्मिः (*ūrmiḥ*), शम्याः (*śamyāḥ*), हंतु (*haṃtu*), योक्राणि (*yokrāṇi*), मुंचत (*muṃcata*), अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*), शूनं (*śūnaṃ*) and अरतां (*aratāṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined and the Latin letter "s" standing for the avagraha in the word यतोऽनाव (*yato 'nāva*) is rewritten as the Kannada avagraha (logged). Printed oddities kept: the block ends with the Ṛk number 14, though this is Ṛk 13; the bhāṣya has अमुष्कृत् (*amuṣkṛt*) and विपाट् ळुतद्रौ (*vipāṭ ḷutadrau*) which differs from the Pada word for "not doing wrong", and the second river is named in a form whose first letter differs from the usual name; यत्पत्ययः (*yatpatyayaḥ*), नित्सर्रः (*nitsarraḥ*) and बहुह्रीह (*bahuhrīha*) stand for the usual grammatical terms; a stray apostrophe stands after ऋच्छतीत्यूर्मिः (*ṛcchatītyūrmiḥ*); all as supplied.

- (O rivers) वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊर्मिः (*ūrmiḥ*)—waves
- शम्याः (*śamyāḥ*)—the neck-ropes (of the vehicle)
- उत् (*ut*)—(so that they are) above (the water)

- व्येनसा (*vyenasā*)—sinless
- अदुष्कृतौ (*aduṣkṛtau*)—(always) doers of good deeds
- अफ्न्या (*aphnyā*)—unblameable, O rivers Vipāṭ and Śutudri
- शूनं (*śūnaṃ*)—prosperity; मा आरतां (*mā āratāṃ*)—do not obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O rivers Vipāṭ and Śutudri, let your waves flow below the neck-ropes of our vehicle, without touching them, in the part below them. O rivers, you who are sinless, doers of good deeds and unblameable, do not take on a swollen flow until we have crossed you.

*[The Bhāvārtha has ಅದಕಿಂತ where the usual spelling has a doubled consonant (for "than that"); as supplied. A word broken across a line end is joined.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Let your waves (rivers) so flow that the pin of the yoke may be above (their) waters : leave the traces full, and may (the two streams), exempt from misfortune or defect, and uncensured, exhibit no (present) increase.

## Sūkta 34 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The thirty-fourth sūkta** (ಮೂವತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रः पूर्विदित्येकादशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं ।
> अत्रानुक्रमणिका । इंद्रः पूर्विदेकादशेति ॥ अग्निष्टोमे माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्र इंद्रः पूर्विदिति सूक्तं । होत्रकाणामिति खंडे सूत्रितं । इंद्रः पूर्भिदुदु ब्रह्माणि । आ. ५ १६ । इति ॥ पृष्ठाभिप्लवषडहयोः प्रथमेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्र चातुर्विंशिकातिदिष्टस्या हीनसूक्तस्य स्थाने त्रीणि संपातसूक्तानि । तत्रेदं प्रथमं । इंद्रः पूर्विद्य एक इद्यस्तिगृंगः । आ. ७५ । इति ॥ उद्दिद्लभिदोर्निष्केवल्य एतत्तूक्तं निविद्धानीयं । सूत्रितं च । इंद्र सोममिंद्रः
> पूर्विदिति मध्यंदिनः । आ ९-८ । इति ॥

*[The Sanskrit block is the introduction of Sāyaṇa; the Anuvāda lines and the sūkta data that the supplied text had inside the block are moved out. In the block the line-end hyphens are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: the first two sūtra references are printed without a hyphen between their numbers and the last has no full stop after the abbreviation; the incipit is पूर्विदित्येकादशर्चं (*pūrvidityekādaśarcaṃ*) with a different consonant from the Anuvāda; the names of the sacrifices are printed उद्दिद्लभिदोर् (*uddidlabhidor*) (for the Uddit/Valabhit of the Anuvāda); and the Anukramaṇikā words differ slightly in the block and in the Anuvāda; as supplied.]*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, इंद्रः पूर्भित् (*iṃdraḥ pūrbhit*), is the fifth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are eleven Ṛks in it. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta and Indra the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh *[the Kannada word for the metre is printed joined to the preceding word with a non-joiner; as supplied]*. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: इंद्रः पूर्भिदेकादश (*iṃdraḥ pūrbhidekādaśa*). At the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, at the midday pressing, this sūkta इंद्रः पूर्भित् (*iṃdraḥ pūrbhit*) is applied to the śastra mantras that the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin must recite; this is explained by the sūtra इंद्रः पूर्भिदुदु ब्रह्माणि (*iṃdraḥ pūrbhidudu brahmāṇi*) (Ā. 5-16) in the Khaṇḍa beginning होत्रकाणां (*hotrakāṇāṃ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra. On the first day of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭha and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras that the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin must recite, three Sampāta-sūktas are to be recited in place of the Ahīna sūktas (the Cāturviṃśika, Atidiṣṭa); of these this sūkta is the first. This is explained by the sūtra इंद्रः पूर्भिद्य एक इद्यस्तिगृंगः (*iṃdraḥ pūrbhidya eka idyastigṛṃgaḥ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 7-5). And in the sacrifices called Uddit and Valabhit this sūkta is used for the Nividdhānīya sūkta that is recited among the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras; this is explained by the sūtra इंद्र सोममिंद्रः पूर्भिदिति मध्यंदिनः (*iṃdra somamiṃdraḥ pūrbhiditi madhyaṃdinaḥ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 9-8).

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 34 *[a line with this number stands before the sūkta data; as supplied]*. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 34. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 2; Varga 15 and 16 *[printed with a full stop between the two numbers]*. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Seer: विश्वामित्रः (*viśvāmitraḥ*). Devatā: इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*). Chandas: त्रिष्टप् (*triṣṭap*) *[printed without the vowel sign u and with no dash before it; as supplied]*.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वामित्रः सौति । पूर्विदसुरपुरां भेत्ता अत एव विदद्वसुर्वेदयद्धिः स्वमहिमप्रख्यापकैर्वसुभिर्युक्तः शत्रूनसुरान्वि दयमानो विशेषेण हिंसन् । तथा च
> यास्कः । विदद्वसुर्दयमानो वि शत्रूनिति हिंसाकर्मा । नि. ४-१७ । इति । तादृश
> इंद्रो दासं दस्यतेऽनेन तम इति दासो वासरः । तमर्कॆरर्चनीयैः स्वतेजोभिरातिरत् । समंतादवर्धयत् इंद्रस्य सूर्यात्मकत्वात् । तथा च स्मृतिः । चैत्रमासे
> तपेदिंद्र इति । किंच । ब्रह्मजूतो ब्रह्मणा स्तोत्रेणाकृष्टः । यद्वा ब्रह्मणा जगत्सृष्टा प्रेरितस्तन्ना स्वशरीरेण वावृधानो वर्धमानो भूरिदात्रः । दायते लूयतेऽनेन शत्रुशिर इति दात्रमायुधं । बहुविधायुधोपेतः । तादृश इंद्र उभे
> रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावापृणत् । सर्वतोऽतर्पयत् ॥ पूर्भीत् । भिदिर् विदारणे ।
> क्विप् । अतिरत् तरतेर्व्यत्ययेन शः । ऋत इद्दातोरितीत्वं । निघातः । दासं । करणे
> घञ् । इत्स्वरः । विदद्वसुः । विदेरंतर्भावितण्यर्थस्य शतर्यदादित्वाच्छपो लुकि सति
> प्रत्ययस्वरेण शतुरुदात्तत्वं । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । दयमानः । दय दानगतिरक्षण हिंसाग्रहणेषु । आत्मनेपदी । लटः शानच् । न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठिप्रतिषेधः।
> ववृधानः । वृधु वर्धने । कानचि रूपं । संहितायामभ्यासस्य शुजादित्वाद्दीर्घः ।
> भूरिदात्रः । दाप् लवने । करणे दामीत्यादिना स्पन्मत्तयः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । अप्पणत् । पृण प्रीणन इत्यस्य लजु तुदादित्वाच्छः । निघातः । रोदसी ।
> रुदेरसुनि रूपं । नित्स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises Indra, breaker of the cities of the asuras, bearer of wealth, who is solar, lights up the day with his rays, grows in his body and fills heaven and earth. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words पूर्भीत् (*pūrbhīt*), अतिरत् (*atirat*), दासं (*dāsaṃ*), विदद्वसुः (*vidadvasuḥ*), दयमानः (*dayamānaḥ*), ववृधानः (*vavṛdhānaḥ*), भूरिदात्रः (*bhūridātraḥ*), अप्पणत् (*appaṇat*) and रोदसी (*rodasī*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). The block quotes Yāska (Ni. 4-17) and a Smṛti line. Printed oddities kept: विश्वामित्रः सौति (*viśvāmitraḥ sauti*) at the beginning, तमर्कॆरर्चनीयैः (*tamarkèrarcanīyaiḥ*) (with the short Kannada e sign, which converts to the short Devanagari e sign; as supplied), प्रेरितस्तन्ना (*preritastannā*) and अप्पणत् (*appaṇat*) (the Pada and Saṃhitā have another form); the block ends with the danda sign; as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूर्भित् (*pūrbhit*)—destroyer of the cities of enemies, and
- विदद्वसु (*vidadvasu*)—possessed of famous wealth
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—enemies; वि दयमानः (*vi dayamānaḥ*)—harming exceedingly
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- दासं (*dāsaṃ*)—the day
- अर्कै: (*arkai:*)—with his worshipful radiances; आ अतिरत् (*ā atirat*)—lit up all around and made it increase *[the Kannada word for "increase" is broken by the page break: its first part stands at the end of page 799 and its end at the top of page 800; joined here]*

### Printed p. 800

*(Pratipadārtha, continued)* ब्रह्मजूतः (*brahmajūtaḥ*)—drawn by praises; तन्वा (*tanvā*)—with his own body; वावृधानः (*vāvṛdhānaḥ*)—growing; भूरिदात्रः (*bhūridātraḥ*)—armed with many kinds of weapons, Indra; उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth; आ अपृणत् (*ā apṛṇat*)—fully satisfied.

*[The entry अर्कै: (*arkai:*) is printed with a colon (ASCII) for the visarga; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the destroyer of the cities of enemies, possessed of famous wealth, who harms enemies exceedingly, lit up the day all around with his worshipful radiances and made it increase. Indra, drawn by praises, growing with his own body and armed with many kinds of weapons, fully satisfied both heaven and earth.

*[The Bhāvārtha has ಆಕೃಷ್ಣನಾಗಿ for "drawn", where the Pratipadārtha has ಆಕೃಷ್ಟನಾಗಿ; as supplied. Words broken across line ends are joined.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, the destroyer of cities, possessed of wealth, manifesting (his greatness), merciless to his enemies, has overspread the day with his radiance : attracted by prayer, increasing in bulk, and armed with many weapons, he has delighted both heaven and earth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वि दयमान: (*vi dayamāna:*)—विशेषेण हिंसन् (*viśeṣeṇa hiṃsan*). "Harming in a special way": this is the explanation of the commentator [Sāyaṇa]. Yāska has stated a derivation for this word—

दयते । दयतिरनेककर्मा । नवेन पूर्वं दयामानाः स्याम इत्युपदयाकर्मा ॥ (*dayate | dayatiranekakarmā | navena pūrvaṃ dayāmānāḥ syāma ityupadayākarmā ‖*)

य एक इद्विदयते वसु इति दानकर्मा ना विभागकर्मा ना ॥ (*ya eka idvidayate vasu iti dānakarmā nā vibhāgakarmā nā ‖*)

दुर्वत्तुर्भीमो दयते वनानि इति दहतिकर्मा । दुर्वतुर्दुर्वारः ॥ (*durvatturbhīmo dayate vanāni iti dahatikarmā | durvaturdurvāraḥ ‖*)

विदद्वसुर्दयमानो विशत्रून् इति हिंसाकर्मा । (*vidadvasurdayamāno viśatrūn iti hiṃsākarmā |*)

इमे सुता इंदवः प्रातरित्वना सजोषसा पिबतमश्विना तान् । अयं हि वामूतये वंदनाय मां वायसो दोषा दयमानो अबूबुधत् ॥ (*ime sutā iṃdavaḥ prātaritvanā sajoṣasā pibatamaśvinā tān | ayaṃ hi vāmūtaye vaṃdanāya māṃ vāyaso doṣā dayamāno abūbudhat ‖*)

दयमान इति ॥ (*dayamāna iti ‖*) (Ni. 4-17) (Ni. 4-17)

*[The Nirukta passage is printed in separate short lines, some broken across line ends (one hyphenated break is joined, logged). The reference is printed twice in succession; both are kept as supplied. The first line has दयामानाः (*dayāmānāḥ*) with a long vowel sign, where the Special Topics quote the same words below as दयमानाःस्याम (*dayamānāḥsyāma*); as supplied.]*

The word दयमान (*dayamāna*) is formed from the root दयति (*dayati*). This root has several meanings:

(1) In नवेन पूर्वं दयमानाःस्याम (*navena pūrvaṃ dayamānāḥsyāma*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-13-1) the word दयमानाः (*dayamānāḥ*) has the meaning "protect, guard".

*[The Special Topics of this Ṛk continue after the end of the supplied text of this window; the list of meanings is not finished here (only (1) is given).]*

### Printed p. 801

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued)*

(2) In य एक इद्विदयते वसु (*ya eka idvidayate vasu*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-7) the word दयते (*dayate*) has the meaning "give" or "divide". *[The reference is printed with a doubled opening bracket after the Ṛg-veda abbreviation and no bracket closing the first one; the numbers are as supplied.]*

(3) In दुर्वर्तुर्भीमो दयते वनानि (*durvarturbhīmo dayate vanāni*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-6-5) the meaning is "burn"; दुर्वर्तुः (*durvartuḥ*) means "unbearable". *[The word is printed ದುರ್ವರ್ತುಃ here and in the quotation, where the Nirukta passage above has a different spelling; as supplied.]*

(4) In विदद्वसुर्दयमानो विशत्रून् (*vidadvasurdayamāno viśatrūn*) (the present Ṛk, Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-34-1) the meaning is "harm".

(5) In the mantra इमे सुता इंदवः (*ime sutā iṃdavaḥ*) .... दयमानो अबूबुधत् । (*dayamāno abūbudhat |*) the word दयमानः (*dayamānaḥ*) has the meaning "to fly" or "to leap". *[The mantra is quoted with four dots in place of the middle words; as supplied. The Kannada word for the meaning is ಹಾರುವುದು.]*

> *makhasya | te | taviṣasya | pra | jūtiṃ | iyarmi | vācaṃ | amṛtāya | bhūṣan |*  
> *iṃdra | kṣitīnāṃ | asi | mānuṣīṇāṃ | viśāṃ | daivīnāṃ | uta | pūrva 'yāvā ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र भूषन् त्वामलंकुर्वन्नहं मखस्य महनीयस्य स्तुत्यस्य तविषस्य

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इत्परः । दैवीनां । देवाद्यञणावित्यञ् । अत्रापि पूर्ववत् जेप् । इत्स्वरः । पूर्वयावा । या प्रापण इत्यस्मादातो मनिन्कनिब्बनिपश्चेति वनिप् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Adorning Indra, the poet sends forth to the mighty, venerable god a mind-impelled praise for the sake of food; Indra goes first of the human and divine peoples. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words मखस्य (*makhasya*), तविषस्य (*taviṣasya*), जूतिं (*jūtiṃ*), इयर्मि (*iyarmi*), भूषन् (*bhūṣan*), असि (*asi*), मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*), दैवीनां (*daivīnāṃ*) and पूर्वयावा (*pūrvayāvā*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has ಪ್ರರಿತಾಂ and ದೇವಸಂಬಂಧೀನೀನಾಂ and ಪೂರ್ಯಾವಾಗ್ರತೋ; the form ಭ್ಯಾಸಸ್ಯೆತ್ವಂ has the short Kannada e sign, which converts to the short Devanagari e sign; as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- भूषन् (*bhūṣan*)—adorning you
- मखस्य (*makhasya*)—venerable
- तविषस्य (*taviṣasya*)—and mighty
- ते (*te*)—towards you
- जूतिं (*jūtiṃ*)—impelled by the mind
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—praise
- अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—for the sake of food; प्र इयर्मि (*pra iyarmi*)—I recite
- मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*)—born of Manu
- क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)—to the people
- उत (*uta*)—and
- दैवीनां (*daivīnāṃ*)—divine
- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—to the people also
- पूर्वयावा (*pūrvayāvā*)—as one who goes first
- असि (*asi*)—you are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, adorning you, I recite for the sake of food a praise impelled by the mind towards you, the venerable and powerful. You go first both of the people born of Manu and of the divine people (the gods).

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Decorating you, I address sincere prayers to you who are adorable and mighty, for the sake of (obtaining) food : you, Indra, are the predecessor of men the descendants of Manu, and of the descendants of the gods.

*[The supplied text has no Special Topics for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra of vast works held back the asura Vṛtra, destroyed the deceiving asuras, slew the hidden asura, and made the cows in the dark of night manifest; a Taittirīya passage and Yāska are quoted. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words अवृणोत् (*avṛṇot*), शर्धनीतिः (*śardhanītiḥ*), अमिनात् (*amināt*), अहन् (*ahan*), उशधक् (*uśadhak*), आविः (*āviḥ*), धेनाः (*dhenāḥ*), अकृणोत् (*akṛṇot*) and राम्याणां (*rāmyāṇāṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Printed oddities kept: the bhāṣya has ಅಹರ್ದೆವಾನಾಮಾಸೀದಾತ್ರಿರಸುರಾಣಾಂ (with the short Kannada e sign, which converts to the short Devanagari e sign, and as supplied); the Taittirīya passage has no reference; the printed Ṛg-veda reference in the grammar tail is given in an abbreviated form and a Yāska reference follows; both as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शर्धनीतिः (*śardhanītiḥ*)—having a growing work
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the asura Vṛtra
- अवृणोत् (*avṛṇot*)—tore apart
- वर्पणीतिः (*varpaṇītiḥ*)—Indra, able to stop the attack of enemies
- मायिनां (*māyināṃ*)—the deceiving asuras; प्र अमिनात् (*pra amināt*)—destroyed completely
- उशधक् (*uśadhak*)—Indra, who desired the slaying of enemies
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the forest; the asura who was hidden in the forest, व्यंसं (*vyaṃsaṃ*)—after making him have his arm broken, अहन् (*ahan*)—he killed
- राम्याणां (*rāmyāṇāṃ*)—that were in the darkness of night
- धेनाः (*dhenāḥ*)—the cows; आविः अकृणोत् (*āviḥ akṛṇot*)—he made manifest

*[The entry for the asuras has the word ಪಂಚಕರಾದ, which is not a word I can place; I translate the entry as "deceiving", following the Pada word for the possessors of deceit and the printed English; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, whose work is great, tore apart the asura Vṛtra. Indra, who can stop the attack of enemies, destroyed completely the deceiving asuras. Indra, desiring the slaying of enemies, made the asura hidden in the forest have his arm broken and killed him. He made the cows that were in the darkness of night visible to all.

*[The Bhāvārtha again has ಪಂಚಕರಾದ; as supplied. Words broken across line ends are joined.]*

> इत्यस्य लिटि सन्नि टोर्जॆरित्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य कवर्गादेशः । लित्स्वरः । पृतनाः, पृज् व्यायामे । कृपृभ्यां किदिति तनन्तृत्ययः । व्याप्रियंतेऽत्र योद्धार ३ति पृतनाः सेनाः ।

> स हि भावपरोऽपि भवितारं लक्षयति । तितुत्रतथेत्यादिनेट् प्रतिषेधः । शकंध्वादित्वात्पररूपत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । अरोचयत् । रुच दीप्तावित्यस्य लजि रूपं । मनवे । मन ज्ञाने । श्व स्वस्तिहीत्यादिना उप्रत्ययः । निदनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तः । अविंदत् । विद्ल लाभ इत्यस्य शे मुचादीनामिति नुं । पादादित्पादनिघातः । रणाय । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यं । म. १-४-३२ । इति संप्रदानसंज्ञा । रणति: शब्दार्थः । वशिरन्नोरुपसंख्यानमित्यप्रत्ययः । रणंति शब्दं कुर्वंति परस्परं योद्धारोऽत्रेति
> रण: संग्रामः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुतात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, with the battle-loving Aṅgirases, defeated the enemy armies, then made the sun shine for the sacrificer and gained light for the great battle. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words स्वर्षाः (*svarṣāḥ*), जिगाय (*jigāya*), पृतनाः (*pṛtanāḥ*), अभिष्टिः (*abhiṣṭiḥ*), अरोचयत् (*arocayat*), मनवे (*manave*), अविंदत् (*aviṃdat*) and रणाय (*raṇāya*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the giver of heaven, producing the days by his splendours, won victory, defeating the enemy armies with the Aṅgirases who desire battle. Afterwards he made the sun, the indicator of the days, shine for the human sacrificer. He produced light for the great battle.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra entered the enemy armies like a man, giving wealth to the warriors, showed the dawns to the singer and increased their bright colour. A Ṛg-veda passage is quoted for the sense of the word for dawn (its reference is printed in an abbreviated form; as supplied). - नर्या (*naryā*)—wealth for the men who set out for battle

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Providing abundantly the wealth that men setting out for battle need, Indra entered, like a man, the group of the enemy armies, which are harmful and grow with eagerness for battle. And for the benefit of the worshipper he made the dawn shine. He made the lustre of those same dawns grow.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra entered the confiding hostile (hosts) like a man distributing many (gifts) to (his) leaders : he has animated these dawns for the worshipper, and heightened their bright radiance (by his own).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra of such might, whose many great, well-done deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra are praised, crushed the sinful asuras by his strength and the Dasyus by deceits. ##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सत्पतिः सतां देवानां पतिश्चर्षणिप्राश्चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणामपेक्षितफलप्रदानेन कामपूरकः स इंद्रो महा महता युधा युद्धेन वरिवः । भृशं व्रियतेऽर्थिभिरिति वरिवो धनं । तादृशं धनं युद्धेन लब्ध्वा देवेभ्यो देवनशीलेभ्यः
> स्तोतृभ्यश्चकार । दत्तवान् । विप्रा मेधाविनः कवयः स्तोतारो विवस्वतो विशेषेणाग्निहोत्रादिकर्मार्थे वसतो यजमानस्य सदने गृहेःस्वेंद्रस्य तानि वृत्रहननबहुप्रदानानि कर्माण्युक्थेभिः स्तोत्रैर्गृणंति । स्तुवंति ॥ युधा । युध संप्रहारे।
> भावे संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तता । वरिवः । वृञ् वरण
> इत्यस्य यज्लुकि ऋतश्चेत्यभ्यासस्य रिगागमः । तदंतादसुन् । बाहुलकाट्टिलोपः ।
> नित्स्वरः । चकार । करोतेर्लिटि रूपं । निघातः । सत्पतिः । अस्तेः शतरि रूपं सदिति ।
> पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । चर्षणिप्राः । प्रा पूरणे । विच् । विवस्वतः।
> विपूर्वाद्वस निवास इत्यस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् ।
> मादुपधाया इति तस्य वत्वं । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । गृणंति । ग्य
> शब्द इत्यस्य लिटि रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, lord of the good and fulfiller of men's wishes, gave the wealth won by great battle to the shining worshippers, and the wise singers praise his deeds with hymns in the sacrificer's house. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The worshippers who bring gladness by their praise gladden Indra, who is possessed of the power to overcome Vṛtra and others, the worshipful, the giver of strength, the enjoyer of the illuminating waters and the world of heaven. That same Indra, gladdened, distributed the earth, the world of heaven and also this atmosphere to the dwellers of the respective worlds.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Devout worshippers propitiate Indra, the victorious, the excellent, the bestower of strength, the enjoyer of heaven and the divine waters, and who was the giver of the earth and heaven and this (firmament to their inhabitants).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra of the previous mantra gave horses to the Maruts for battle, the sun for the light of beings, cows giving food of many kinds, and golden wealth to the seekers, and, having slain the Dasyu asuras, protected the three-varṇa Ārya people. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words ससान (*sasāna*), हिरण्ययं (*hiraṇyayaṃ*), हत्वी (*hatvī*) and आवत् (*āvat*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent); a printed Pāṇini reference (abbreviated) occurs in it. ##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तादृश इंद्र ओषधीः पक्वफलसंयुक्तास्तृणगुल्मादिका असनोत् । प्राणिनामुपभोगार्थं प्रादात् । तथाहानि दिवसांश्चायुष्परिक्लृष्टर्थं प्रायच्छत् ।
> किंच वनस्पतीन्यज्ञार्थं खदिरपलाशादिलक्षणान् वृक्षानसनोत् । तथांतरिक्षं संचारार्थं प्रादात् । तथा वलं । संव्रियतेऽनेनाकाशमिति वलो मेघः । तं मेघं
> बिभेद । उदकप्रेरणार्थमभिंदत् । विवाचो विरुद्धवाचः प्रतिकूलानसुरान् नुनुदे।
> प्राणिनां रक्षार्थं तान् बबाधे । अथानंतरमभिक्रतूनां । क्रतुः कर्म । अभि अभिमुख्येन युद्धार्थं कर्म येषां तेऽभिकृतवो बलीयांसः शत्रवः । तेषामपि
> दमितोपशमयिताभवत् । एवं हितकरणाहितपरिहाराभ्यां सर्वाः प्रजाः पालयतिस्मेति भावः ॥ असनोत् । षणु दान इत्यस्य लजु रूपं । वनस्पतीन् । पारस्करप्रभृतित्वात् सुडागमः । वनशब्दो नब्विषयस्येत्याम्यदात्तः । पतिशब्दः प्रत्ययस्वतेणाद्युदात्तः । उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपदित्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । बिभेद । भिदिर् विदारण
> इत्यस्य लिटि रूपं । लित्स्वरः । नुनुदे । नुद प्रेरण इत्यस्य लिटि रूपं । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । दमिता । दमु उपशम इत्यस्य तृचि रूपं । जत्स्वरः । अभिक्रतूनां । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra gave the herbs with ripe fruit and the days for life, the trees for the sacrifice and the atmosphere for movement; he split the cloud for the flow of water, drove away the hostile asuras and became the subduer of even the mighty enemies; the sense is that he protects all creatures by doing good and removing harm. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words असनोत् (*asanot*), वनस्पतीन् (*vanaspatīn*), बिभेद (*bibheda*), नुनुदे (*nunude*), दमिता (*damitā*) and अभिक्रतूनां (*abhikratūnāṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: दिवसांश्चायुष्परिक्लृष्टर्थं (*divasāṃścāyuṣpariklṛṣṭarthaṃ*) and प्रत्ययस्वतेणाद्युदात्तः (*pratyayasvateṇādyudāttaḥ*) are printed so; all as supplied.

- अहानि (*ahāni*)—days (made manifest)
- वनस्पतीन् (*vanaspatīn*)—trees and the like
- असनोत् (*asanot*)—created

- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—became

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra created herbs and trees for the benefit of beings. He built the atmosphere. He split the cloud for the flow of water. He harmed and killed the hostile asuras. Afterwards he became the destroyer of the enemies opposed to the sacrifice.

*[The printed English translation and any Special Topics of this Ṛk follow in the next window.]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिंद्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सात् ।  
> शृ॒ण्वंत॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्तु॒ घ्नंतं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नां ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुनं । हुवेम । मघवानं । इंद्रं । अस्मिन् । भरे । नृतमं । वाजसात् ।  
> शृण्वंतं । उग्रं । ऊतये । समत्सु । घ्नंतं । वृत्राणि । संजितं । धनानां ॥

> *śunaṃ | huvema | maghavānaṃ | iṃdraṃ | asmin | bhare | nṛtamaṃ | vājasāt |*  
> *śṛṇvaṃtaṃ | ugraṃ | ūtaye | samatsu | ghnaṃtaṃ | vṛtrāṇi | saṃjitaṃ | dhanānāṃ ‖*

*[The Pada has समत्सु (*samatsu*) where the Saṃhitā has समत्तु (*samattu*) and the bhāṣya also reads the latter; as supplied.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः ।
> अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन्संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृद्धं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं मघवानं धनवंतं अत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संचितं समग्नेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य
> निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । ह्वयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते शपो लुकि
> कृते च लिजि रूपं । निघातः । भरे । भृञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः ।
> वाजसात् । षणु दाने । भावे क्तिन् जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं । बहुव्रीहौ
> पूर्वपदस्वरः । समत्तु । आद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति योद्धणामायूंशीति समदः संग्रामाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घ्नंतं । हन हिंसागत्यो
> श्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेरिति घत्वं । संजितं । जिजोयत् ।
> क्विप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Kuśikas call Indra, wealthy, supreme leader, hearer of praise, terrible to enemies and slayer of the Vṛtra-like demons, to this battle for protection. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words शुनं (*śunaṃ*), हुवेम (*huvema*), भरे (*bhare*), वाजसात् (*vājasāt*), समत्तु (*samattu*), घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*) and संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: the block has संचितं (*saṃcitaṃ*) in the explanation of the wealth where the Saṃhitā and Pada have the other consonant in the word for "conqueror"; in the grammar the root is introduced with the letters टुओश्वि (*ṭuośvi*); a word cut at a line end without a hyphen is joined (योद्धणामायूंशीति (*yoddhaṇāmāyūṃśīti*), logged); all as supplied.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in this battle that proceeds for the winning of food, we call for protection you who show your strength and are a helper, who are wealthy, the lord of all prosperity, the best guide of the world, who listen attentively to our praise, are terrible to enemies, torment the enemies in battles, and wholly conquer the wealth of the enemies.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

## Sūkta 35 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The thirty-fifth sūkta** (ಮೂವತ್ತೈದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तिष्ठा हरी इत्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । तिष्ठा
> हरी इत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ अग्निष्टुति मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रे निविद्वानं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च ।
> तिष्ठा हरी यो जात एवेति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-७ । इति ॥ इंद्राग्न्योः कुलायनान्मैकाहेऽप्येतन्मरुत्वतीयनिविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । तिष्ठा हरी तमु ष्टुहीति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-७ । इति ॥ समूढे दशरात्रे तृतीये छंदोमे मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र
> एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रिशं च। तिष्ठा हरी प्र मुंदिने इमा उ त्वेति मरुत्वतीयं। आ. ८-७ ।
> इति ॥ अतिरात्रे तृतीये पर्याये होतुः शस्त्रे परिहिते सत्याद्या तिष्ठा हरी इत्येषा शस्त्रयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । विश्वजिते तिष्ठा हरी रथ आ युज्यमानेति याज्या । आ.
> ६-४ । इति ॥

*[The Sanskrit block is the introduction of Sāyaṇa; the Anuvāda lines and the sūkta data follow on the next page. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: the block has सूत्रिशं (*sūtriśaṃ*) and एतत्तूक्तं (*etattūktaṃ*) and, in the second sūtra, तिषा हरी तमु (*tiṣā harī tamu*); the sacrifice of the ten nights is named समूढे (*samūḍhe*) here; all as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 815

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, तिष्ठा हरी (*tiṣṭhā harī*), is the sixth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are eleven Ṛks in it *[the Kannada word for eleven is printed ದನ್ನೊಂದು, with a different first letter; as supplied]*. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta and Indra the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh *[the Kannada word for the metre is printed joined to the preceding word with a non-joiner; as supplied]*. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: तिष्ठा हरी (*tiṣṭhā harī*). This sūkta is to be recited in the middle of the Marutvatīya śastra mantras of the Agniṣṭuti as the Nivid-dhāna sūkta; this is explained by the sūtra तिष्ठा हरी यो जात एवेति मध्यंदिनः (*tiṣṭhā harī yo jāta eveti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (A. 9-7) *[printed with the letter for "A", while the other references of this paragraph have the long vowel]*. In the one-day sacrifice called कुलाय (*kulāya*), performed for Indra and Agni, it must likewise be recited in the Marutvatīya śastra mantras as the Nivit sūkta *[printed ನಿವಿತ್ತೂಕ್ತವನ್ನಾಗಿ; as supplied]*; this is explained by the sūtra तिषा हरी तमु ष्टुहीति मध्यंदिनः (*tiṣā harī tamu ṣṭuhīti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 9-7). In the ten-night sacrifice named in the print ಸಮೂಳ್ವೆಂಬ, when the third Chandoma mantras are recited, this sūkta is used for the Marutvatīya śastra mantras; this is explained by the sūtra तिष्ठा हरी प्र मुंदिन इमा उत्वेति मरुत्वतीयं (*tiṣṭhā harī pra muṃdina imā utveti marutvatīyaṃ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 8-7). And in the sacrifice called Atirātra, when the mantras of the third paryāya are recited, among the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Hotṛ, this Ṛk तिष्ठा हरी (*tiṣṭhā harī*) is to be recited as the first śastra-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra विश्वजिते तिष्ठा हरी रथ आ युज्यमानेति याज्या (*viśvajite tiṣṭhā harī ratha ā yujyamāneti yājyā*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 6-4).

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 35 *[a line with this number stands before the sūkta data; as supplied]*. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 35. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 2; Varga 17 and 18 *[printed with a full stop between the two numbers]*. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Seer: विश्वामित्रः (*viśvāmitraḥ*). Devatā: इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*). Chandas: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तिष्ठा॒ हरी॒ रथ॒ आ यु॒ज्यमा॑ना या॒हि वा॒युर्न नि॒युतो॑ नो॒ अच्छ॑ ।  
> पिबा॒स्यंधो॑ अ॒भिसृ॑ष्टो अ॒स्मे इंद्र॒ स्वाहा॑ ररि॒मा ते॒ मदा॑य ॥
