> पिबासि । अंधः । अभिस्सृष्टः । अस्मे इति । इंद्र । स्वाहा । ररिम । ते । मदाय ॥ १ ॥

> *tiṣṭha | harī iti | rathe | ā | yujyamānā | yāhi | vāyuḥ | na | niyutaḥ | na | accha |*  
> *pibāsi | aṃdhaḥ | abhissṛṣṭaḥ | asme iti | iṃdra | svāhā | rarima | te | madāya ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वामित्रः स्तौति । हे इंद्र रथे स्यंदने युज्यमाना संयुज्यमानौ हरी
> अश्वावभिलक्ष्य कंचित्कालमा तिष्ठ । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वायुर्नॆति । यथा वायू रथे
> नियुज्यमाना नियुतो वडना अभिलक्ष्य कंचित्कालं तिष्ठति तद्वत् । अथ रथारूढस्त्वं
> नोऽस्मानच्छाभिलक्ष्या याहि । शीघ्रमागच्छ । अगत्य चास्मे अस्माभिरभिसृष्टोऽनुज्ञातस्त्वमंधः
> सोमलक्षणमन्नं पिबासि । पिब । स्वाहा । दत्तश्चायं सोमः । वयं ते
> तव मदाय हर्षाय स्वाहाकृतमिमं सोमं ररिम । ददाम ॥ अत्र याहि वायुर्न
> नियुतो नो अच्छेत्यत्र रथेना याहीत्यर्थः । आपत्तित्पिप्युः स्तर्यो न गावः ।
> ऋग्वं ७-२३-४ । इत्यत्र तन्न तथेति पदकाले नोत्सृज्यते ॥ तिष्ठ । तिष्मतेर्लोटि
> रूपं । तिष्ठादेशस्याद्युदात्तः । याहि । यातेर्लोटि रूपं । हेर्जित्वादंतोदात्तः
> । वायुः । वा गतिगंधनयोरित्यस्मात्कृवापेत्यादिना उण् । आतो युक् । प्रत्ययस्वरः
> । पिबासि । पातेर्लॆट्याडागमः । आगमस्यानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः । अंधः ।
> आद भक्षणे । अदेर्नु० धश्चेत्यसुन्नुमागमो धकारश्चांतादेशः । आद्यते प्राणिभिस्तद्वा
> स्वयमत्तीति । तथा च श्रुतिः । अद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यते ।
> त्व उ. २-२ । इति । नित्वरः । अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः शे इत्यादेशः ।
> ररिम । रातेर्लिटि रूपं । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises Indra: stay a little while, looking at your horses yoked to the chariot, as Vāyu stands looking at his team; then come to us, and drink the Soma that we offer with the cry svāhā for your delight. The grammar of the forms follows and is transcribed, not explained: the words तिष्ठ (*tiṣṭha*), याहि (*yāhi*), वायुः (*vāyuḥ*), पिबासि (*pibāsi*), अस्मे (*asme*) and ररिम (*rarima*) are analysed (roots, suffixes, accent). Line-end hyphens inside the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied: तिष्मतेर् (*tiṣmater*) (in the explanation of the root of the first verb form), वडना (*vaḍanā*), अगत्य (*agatya*) and नित्वरः (*nitvaraḥ*); a Kannada zero sign stands after the letter in the word ನು೦ of the grammar. The Kannada short e-vowel sign, which the script converts to the Devanagari short e-vowel sign inside the Sanskrit words, is supplied in वायुर्नॆति (*vāyurnèti*) and पातेर्लॆट्याडागमः (*pāterlèṭyāḍāgamaḥ*); as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वायुः (*vāyuḥ*)—Vāyu; नियुतः न (*niyutaḥ na*)—as he stands looking at his own horse
- रथे (*rathe*)—in the chariot
- युज्यमाना (*yujyamānā*)—yoked
- हरी (*harī*)—looking at the horses; आ तिष्य (*ā tiṣya*)—stay a little while; नः अच्छ (*naḥ accha*)—towards us
- याहि (*yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- अस्मे (*asme*)—by us
- अभिसृष्टः (*abhisṛṣṭaḥ*)—permitted (requested)
- अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)—the food in the form of Soma
- पिबासि (*pibāsi*)—drink
- स्वाहा (*svāhā*)—this Soma given with the cry svāhā
- ते (*te*)—your
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for delight
- ररिम (*rarima*)—we offer

*[The Pratipadārtha has आ तिष्य (*ā tiṣya*) where the Saṃhitā and Pada of this Ṛk, on the previous page, have a different consonant in the word for "stay"; the last word of the Pratipadārtha is printed ಆರ್ಪಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ with a long vowel at the start; both as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as Vāyu stands looking at his horses, you too yoke your horses to the chariot and stand for a little while looking at them. Then be pleased to come towards us. Being requested by us, drink this Soma juice, offered with the cry svāhā for your delight.

*[The Bhāvārtha has ಅರ್ಪಿಸಿಗ for "offered" (an extra syllable at the end); as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Stay, Indra, having yoked the horses to the car, as Vayu stops when he has put up to his steeds, and come to our presence : solicited by us to drink of the (Soma) beverage, which with reverence we offer for your exhilaration.

*[The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, for you, who are called by many sacrificers, I yoke the two swift horses called Hari to the yoke-ends of the chariot so that it may run well; may they bring you to this sacrifice, which is filled from all sides with the materials of the rite. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*), युनज्मि (*yunajmi*), द्रवत् (*dravat*) and वहातः (*vahātaḥ*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied: हे इंद (*he iṃda*) (the name of Indra is cut short), सर्पणशीत् (*sarpaṇaśīt*), हरिनामकावश् (*harināmakāvaś*) and तावश् (*tāvaś*). The Kannada short e-vowel sign, which the script converts to the Devanagari short e-vowel sign, is supplied in वहेर्लॆट्याडागमे (*vaherlèṭyāḍāgame*); as supplied.

- सप्ति (*sapti*)—suited to easy movement
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses named Hari
- रथस्य (*rathasya*)—of your chariot
- धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*)—in the regions of the yoke; द्रवत् यथा (*dravat yathā*)—so that the chariot may run fast and conveniently; आ युन्मजि (*ā yunmaji*)—I join and tie

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are called by many people: so that you may come easily to this sacrifice, which is filled with the materials of worship, I yoke your swift-running horses, the horses named हरी (*harī*), to the region of the yoke of your chariot so that it may run. May they bring you, the lord, to this sacrifice.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, showerer of wishes and lord of food: bring near to us your two strong horses, protectors against hostile enemies, and protect the sacrificer; unharness the red horses here, let them graze, and eat daily the like-formed parched grain. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: नयस्व (*nayasva*), तपुष्पा (*tapuṣpā*), सदृशीः (*sadṛśīḥ*), अद्धि (*addhi*) and धानाः (*dhānāḥ*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). The Kannada short e-vowel sign, which the script converts to the Devanagari short e-vowel sign, is supplied in आतोऽनुपसर्गॆ (*āto 'nupasargè*); as supplied.

- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—the showerer of wishes
- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—possessor of food, O Indra
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—capable of sprinkling
- तपुष्पा (*tapuṣpā*)—protecting against enemies: your horses; उपो नयस्व (*upo nayasva*)—

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, showerer of wishes and lord of food: send to us your horses, which are capable of sprinkling and protect us against enemies. And protect this sacrificer. Unyoke those red-coloured horses from the chariot in this region of the divine sacrifice. May they eat grass. You also, eat daily the grains of barley, all of one form.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two swift horses of Indra are yoked by the praise-hymn to the chariot; Indra is asked to mount the firm, comfortable chariot and come to drink Soma. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: ब्रह्मयुजा (*brahmayujā*), युनज्मि (*yunajmi*), सधमादे (*sadhamāde*) and सुखं (*sukhaṃ*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied: सुषुप् द्वारं (*suṣup dvāraṃ*) in the explanation of the word for "comfortable", and a zero-width non-joiner inside the grammar tail.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ब्रह्मयुजा (*brahmayujā*)—to be yoked with the recitation of mantras
- सधमादे (*sadhamāde*)—in battle
- सखाया (*sakhāyā*)—who are friends
- आशू (*āśū*)—swift-going
- ते (*te*)—your
- हरी (*harī*)—horses
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—with praises
- युनज्जि (*yunajji*)—I join to the chariot
- स्थिरं (*sthiraṃ*)—firm
- सुखं (*sukhaṃ*)—comfortable
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the chariot
- अधितिष्ठन् (*adhitiṣṭhan*)—mounting and sitting
- प्रजानन् (*prajānan*)—with the knowledge that you must come to the sacrifice
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—be pleased to come for the drinking of Soma

*[Printed oddity kept: the Pratipadārtha has युनज्जि (*yunajji*) where the bhāṣya has युनज्मि (*yunajmi*); as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, I yoke to the chariot, with praises, your horses, which are to be yoked with the recitation of mantras, are friends in battle and are swift-going. Mounting the firm and comfortable chariot, be pleased to come, with the knowledge that you must come to the sacrifice, for the drinking of Soma.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I harness with prayer your horses, who are to be harnessed with prayer, who are allies and swift-paced in battle : arise, and all-knowing Indra, mounting on your' [sic] firm and easy chariot, come to the libation.

*[The printed English has a stray apostrophe after "your"; kept and marked [sic].]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the twenty-fourth day of the sacrifice, called Chāturviṃśika, in the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, this Ṛk beginning ब्रह्मणा ते (*brahmaṇā te*) is to be recited at the beginning; this is explained by the sūtra of the ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಶ್ರತಸೂತ್ರ (Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, as the name is printed) ब्रह्मणा ते ब्रह्मयुजा युनज्मुरुं नो लोकमनुनेषि विद्वान् (*brahmaṇā te brahmayujā yunajmuruṃ no lokamanuneṣi vidvān*) (Ā. 7-4).

*[The name of the sūtra work is printed with the second syllable of "śrauta" lacking its vowel sign; as supplied.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, may other sacrificers not attract your vigorous, fair-backed horses; we shall fully satisfy you with pressed Soma, so pass the others and come always to us. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: वीतपृष्ठा (*vītapṛṣṭhā*), रीरमन् (*rīraman*), अत्यायाहि (*atyāyāhi*) and कृणवाम (*kṛṇavāma*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let the sacrificers other than us not enjoy and not attract your horses, which are showerers of wishes and have attractive back parts. We ourselves shall bring about full satisfaction for you with the pressed Soma juices. Always be pleased to come to our sacrifice only.

*[The printed English has "sacrifices" where "sacrificers" is expected; kept and marked [sic]. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, this Soma is pressed for you; come to it with a kind mind, drink much of it, and sit on the sacred grass at this sacrifice and hold the juice in your belly. At the midday pressing the Ṛk is the prasthita-yājyā of the Neṣṭṛ priest, a sūtra being cited. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: इहि (*ihi*), शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*), पाहि (*pāhi*), निषद्य (*niṣadya*), दधिष्ट (*dadhiṣṭa*) and इंदुं (*iṃduṃ*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied: the sūtra is cited as तनायं सोमस्य मेह्यर्नाजिंद्राय (*tanāyaṃ somasya mehyarnājiṃdrāya*); the explanation has सुमानाः (*sumānāḥ*) for the word of the Ṛk; a Ṛgveda passage is cited with a number as printed, and with the Kannada short e-vowel sign in its abbreviation ऋग्वॆ (*ṛgvè*) and in प्रवृद्धेऽस्मिन्यज्ञॆ (*pravṛddhe 'sminyajñè*) (the script converts this sign to the Devanagari short e-vowel sign); as supplied.

- तव (*tava*)—is pressed for you
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अर्वाज् (*arvāj*)—facing it; आ इहि (*ā ihi*)—be pleased to come
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—with a favourable mind

- निषद्य (*niṣadya*)—sitting down

- जठरे (*jaṭhare*)—within the belly; आ दधिष्ट (*ā dadhiṣṭa*)—hold

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, this Soma juice has been pressed for you. Be pleased to come favourably towards it. With a favourable mind drink this Soma abundantly. Seated at this sacrifice, which has seats of darbha grass, hold this flowing juice within your belly.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This Soma libation is for you : come down, and, well disposed, drink of it unceasingly : seated on the sacred grass at this sacrifice, take, Indra, this (libation) into your belly.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk beginning तवायं सोमः (*tavāyaṃ somaḥ*) is to be recited at the midday pressing, in the homa, as the prasthita-yājyā mantra by the priest called Neṣṭṛ; this is established by the sūtra of the ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಶೌತಸೂತ್ರ (Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, as the name is printed) तवायं सोमस्वमेह्यर्वाजींद्राय सोमाः प्रदिवः (*tavāyaṃ somasvamehyarvājīṃdrāya somāḥ pradivaḥ*) (Ā. 5-5).

*[The name of the sūtra work is printed with the r of "śrauta" lacking; the verb "to recite" is printed ಪತಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು; the line-end hyphen inside the sūtra quotation is joined (logged). The wording of the sūtra differs in several letters from the form of it cited in the bhāṣya of Ṛk 6 on p. 822; as supplied.]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वी॒र्णं ते॑ ब॒र्हिः सु॒त इं॑द्र॒ सोमः॑ कृ॒ता धा॒ना अत्त॑वे ते॒ हरि॑भ्यां ।  
> तदो॑कसे पुरु॒शाका॑य॒ वृष्णे॑ म॒रुत्व॑ते॒ तुभ्यं॑ रा॒ता ह॒वींषि॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्त्रीर्णं । ते । बर्हिः । सुतः । इंद्र । सोमः । कृताः । धानाः । अत्तवे । ते । हरिभ्यां ।  
> तत्ऽओकसे । पुरुशाकाय । वृष्णे । मरुत्वते । तुभ्यं । राता । हवींषि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तवोपवेशनार्थं बर्हिः स्तीर्णं विस्तृतं । तथा सोमश्च त्वदर्थं सुतः । अभिषुतः । ते तव हरिभ्यामत्तने भक्षणार्थं धाना बृष्टयवाः कृताः ।
> संपादिताः । तदोकसे । तद्बर्हिरोको निलयो यस्य तस्मै । पुरुशाकाय बहुभिः
> स्तुत्याय यद्वा बहुसहायाय वृष्णे कामानां वर्षित्रे मरुत्वते मरुतो देवविशः। तद्वते। एवंभूताय तुभ्यं हवींषि सोमाज्यादीनि राता। आस्माभिर्दत्तानि। तानि
> सेवस्वति भावः ॥ स्तीर्णं । स्तृञ् आच्छादन इत्यस्य ऋत इद्दातोरितीत्वं । रदाभ्यामिति निष्ठानत्वं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अत्तवे । अद भक्षण इत्यस्मात्तुमर्थे तवेन्प्रत्ययः ।

> *tasau mattvartha iti bhasaṃjñāyāṃ takārasya jaśvābhāvaḥ | pratyayasya pittvādanudāttatve*
> *prātipadikasvaraḥ | rātā | rā dāna ityasmātkarmaṇi ktaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ ‖*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The grass is spread for Indra, Soma is pressed, parched barley is made ready for his horses and oblations are offered; he is asked to enjoy them. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: स्तीर्णं (*stīrṇaṃ*), अत्तवे (*attave*), तदोकसे (*tadokase*), पुरुशाकाय (*puruśākāya*), मरुत्वते (*marutvate*) and राता (*rātā*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the blocks are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied: सेवस्वति (*sevasvati*) at the end of the explanation of the sense, and बृष्टयवाः (*bṛṣṭayavāḥ*) and बहुव्रीहौ (*bahuvrīhau*) in the bhāṣya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—for you, for sitting
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—the seat of darbha grass
- स्त्रीर्णं (*strīrṇaṃ*)—has been spread
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the Soma juice
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—has been pressed
- ते (*te*)—your
- हरिभ्यां (*haribhyāṃ*)—for the horses
- अक्तवे (*aktave*)—for eating
- धानाः (*dhānāḥ*)—barley grains
- कृताः (*kṛtāḥ*)—have been prepared
- तदोकसे (*tadokase*)—to you who have the barhis itself as your dwelling
- पुरुशाकाय (*puruśākāya*)—helper of many
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—showerer of wishes
- मरुत्वते (*marutvate*)—attended by the Maruts
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*)—the oblations of Soma and the rest
- राता (*rātā*)—have been offered (by us)

*[The Pratipadārtha has स्त्रीर्णं (*strīrṇaṃ*) and अक्तवे (*aktave*) where the Saṃhitā has स्वीर्णं (*svīrṇaṃ*) and अत्तवे (*attave*); as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the seat of darbha grass has been spread for you to sit on. The Soma has also been pressed. For the eating of your horses, barley grains have been prepared. For you, who have the barhis itself as your dwelling, who are the helper of many, the showerer of wishes and attended by the Maruts, the oblations of Soma and the rest have been offered.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sacred grass is strewn for you ; the Soma juice, Indra, is poured forth , the grain wherewith to feed your horses is prepared; the oblations are offered to you abiding on the sacred grass, who are praised of many, and (are) the showerer (of benefits), attended by the Maruts.

*[The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र नरः कर्मणां नेतारोऽध्वय्यादयः पर्वता ग्रावाण आपश्चैते
> सर्वे संभूय शुभ्यं त्वदर्थमिमं सोमं गोभिः पयोभिर्मधुमंतं माधुर्योपेतं समक्रन् । सम्यगकार्षुः । ऋष्ट दर्शनीय हे इंद्र सुमनाः शोभनमनस्को विद्वान्कर्माभिज्ञः स्वाः स्वकीयाः पथ्या वैदिके पथि कर्मणि साधुभूताः स्तुतीरनु प्रजानन् त्वं तस्य पाहि । इममभिषुतं सोमं पिब ॥ अक्रन् । करोतेर्लुजि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Priests, pressing stones and waters have prepared this milk-mixed Soma for Indra; knowing our rites and kindly disposed, he is asked to come and drink. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: अक्रन् (*akran*), आगत्य (*āgatya*) and पाहि (*pāhi*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddity kept as supplied: गमर्ल्यपि (*gamarlyapi*) in the grammar tail.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the Adhvaryu and the others
- पर्वताः (*parvatāḥ*)—the pressing stones (grāvas, the stones that press)
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters (all gathering together)
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this Soma juice
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—mixed with milk
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—and made sweet, so that it becomes so; सं अक्रन् (*saṃ akran*)—they have prepared
- ऋष्ट्व (*ṛṣṭva*)—O radiant Indra
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—being favourably disposed
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—and knowing our rites
- स्वाः (*svāḥ*)—addressed to you
- पथ्याः (*pathyāḥ*)—the Vedic praises; अनु प्रजानन् (*anu prajānan*)—taking note of
- अगत्य (*agatya*)—coming here
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of this Soma juice
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

*[In the Pratipadārtha a comma stands before the bar after the entry for the word for "favourably disposed"; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Adhvaryu and the others, the pressing stones and the waters, all gathering together, have prepared for you this Soma juice so that it is mixed with milk and endowed with sweetness. O radiant Indra, being favourably disposed and knowing our rites, taking note of the Vedic praises addressed to you, come here and drink this Soma juice.

*[The Bhāvārtha has ಅಧ್ವರುವೇ where the Pratipadārtha has ಅಧ್ವರ್ಯುವೇ for "the Adhvaryu"; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The leaders (of the ceremony) have prepared for you, Indra, this (libation), sweetened with milk, the stones, the water : beautiful Indra, who are favourably disposed, and who are wise, knowing well (the worship) that is according to your peculiar paths, come and drink of this libation.

*[The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is asked, united with the Maruts who serve him at the Soma-drinking and strengthened him in battle, to drink the pressed Soma through the flame-tongue of the Āhavanīya fire. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: अभजः (*abhajaḥ*), अवर्धन् (*avardhan*), अभवन् (*abhavan*), वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*) and पिब (*piba*) are analysed. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied: लजि (*laji*) in the grammar note on the first verb, and झीरार्धधातुकत्वाण्णॆरनिटीति (*jhīrārdhadhātukatvāṇṇèraniṭīti*), in which the short Kannada vowel sign e converts to the short Devanagari e, as supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra; यान् मरुतः (*yān marutaḥ*)—which Maruts
- सोमे (*some*)—at the time of Soma-drinking
- अभजः (*abhajaḥ*)—you serve in company
- ये (*ye*)—which (Maruts)
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- अवर्धन् (*avardhan*)—make you strong at the time of battle, they
- ते (*te*)—to you; गणः अभवन् (*gaṇaḥ abhavan*)—become helpers
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तेभिः (*tebhiḥ*)—with such Maruts
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—being united
- एतं (*etaṃ*)—the pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma juice
- नावशानः (*nāvaśānaḥ*)—desiring
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—by means of the flame
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

*[The Pratipadārtha has नावशानः (*nāvaśānaḥ*) where the Pada and the bhāṣya have वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*); as supplied. A line break stands inside the entry for the word meaning "the troop" (गणः अभवन् (*gaṇaḥ abhavan*)); as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Maruts whom you keep as companions and serve at the time of Soma-drinking, and the Maruts who make you strong at the time of battle, are always your helpers. O Indra, united with such Maruts, come here, desire the pressed Soma and drink it by means of the mouth, the flame, of Agni.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Associated, Indra, with those Maruts with whom you have shared in the libation, who encouraged you (in battle), and are your attendant troop,

### Printed p. 827

drink, desirous (of the beverage) the Soma juice, along with them, with the tongue of Agni.

> इंद्र॒ पिब॑ स्व॒धया॑ चित्सु॒तस्या॒ग्नेर्वा॑ पाहि जि॒ह्वया॑ यजत्र ।  
> अ॒ध्व॒र्योर्वा॒ प्रय॑तं शक्र॒ हस्ता॒द्दोतु॑र्वा य॒ज्ञं ह॒विषो॑  
> जुषस्व ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र ॥ पिब । स्वधया । चित् । सुतस्य । अग्नेः । वा । पाहि । जिह्वया । यजत्र ।  
> अध्वर्योः । वा । प्रयतं । शक्र । हस्तात् । होतुः । वा । यज्ञं । हविषः ।  
> जुषस्व ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र स्वधया । स्वमात्मानं दधाति पोषयतीति स्वधा बलं । तेन । चिद्विकल्पार्थः । बलवादपहृत्य सुतस्य सुतमभिषुतं हुतं वा पिब । यजत्र यष्टव्येंद्राग्नेर्ज्वालारूपया जिह्वाया वाहुतं सोमं पाहि । पिब । हे शक्र समर्थेंद्र
> अध्वर्योर्हस्ताद्वा प्रयतं दातुमुपक्रांतं सोम पिब । अथवा होतुर्यज्ञं
> यजनीयं वषट्कारोपेतं हविषो भागं जुषस्व । सेवस्व । सर्वथापि त्वमत्रागत्यास्माभिर्दीयमानं सोमं पिबेति भावः ॥ पिब । आमंत्रितस्याविद्यमानत्वेन पादादित्पादनिघातः । अध्वर्योः । अध्वरं कामयतीति क्यच् । कव्यध्वरेत्यकारलोपः ।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । तत एकादेशस्वरः । प्रयतं । यम उपरम इत्यस्य कर्मणि निष्ठा ।
> शक्र । शक्लौ शक्तौ । स्थायितंचीत्यादिना रक् । हस्तात् । असिहसीत्यादिना तन् । नित्स्वरः ।
> होतुः । जुहोतेस्ताच्छिलिकस्त्रन् । नित्स्वरः । जुषस्व । जुषी प्रीतिसेनयोरित्यस्य
> लोटि रूपं । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is asked to drink the Soma, pressed with strength, whether poured into the flame-tongue of Agni or offered from the Adhvaryu's hand, and to partake of the Hotṛ's oblation. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: पिब (*piba*), अध्वर्योः (*adhvaryoḥ*), प्रयतं (*prayataṃ*), शक्र (*śakra*), हस्तात् (*hastāt*), होतुः (*hotuḥ*) and जुषस्व (*juṣasva*). Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddity kept as supplied: the bhāṣya has जिह्वाया (*jihvāyā*) where the Saṃhitā has जिह्वया (*jihvayā*).

- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- यजत्र (*yajatra*)—O Indra, worthy of sacrifice
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—through the tongue in the form of flame
- वा (*vā*)—the Soma that has been offered
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink
- शक्र (*śakra*)—O capable Indra
- अध्वर्योः (*adhvaryoḥ*)—of the Adhvaryu
- हस्तात् (*hastāt*)—from the hand; वा प्रयतं (*vā prayataṃ*)—drink the Soma that has been offered

- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—relating to the sacrifice
- हविषः (*haviṣaḥ*)—the oblation
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—partake

### Printed p. 828

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink this Soma juice, pressed with strength and offered in the form of an oblation by the Adhvaryu, with the help of the tongue of Agni, which is flame. O capable Indra, drink the Soma offered from the hand of the Adhvaryu. Partake of the oblation belonging to the sacrifice of the Hotṛ.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Adorable Indra, drink of the effused libation, either by your own effort, or through the tongue of Agni; drink it, Sakra, offered by the hand of the Adhwaryu, or accept the presentation of the oblation (from the hand) of the Hotri.

*[The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिंद्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ ।  
> शृ॒ण्वंत॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नंतं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नां ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुनं । हुवेम । मघवानं । इंद्रं । अस्मिन् । भरे । नृतमं । वाजसात् ।  
> शृण्वंतं । उग्रं । ऊतये । समत्सु । घ्नंतं । वृत्राणि । संजितं । धनानां ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः ।
> अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन्संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृष्ठं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं मघवानं धनवंतं अत एनेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रोणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संजितं समग्नेतारं श्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य
> निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, wealthy, the best leader, fierce, hearing our praise, slayer of the Vṛtras and winner of the enemy's wealth, is called on in this battle for protection. The supplied text of the window ends here, at the end of p. 828, in the grammar tail of the bhāṣya (the last word is दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः (*dīrghābhāvaścāṃdasaḥ*), no stop printed); the grammar and the rest of this Ṛk follow in the next window. Printed oddities kept as supplied in the bhāṣya: समत्तु (*samattu*) where the Saṃhitā and the Pada have समत्सु (*samatsu*), and शत्रोणां (*śatroṇāṃ*), श्वामूतये (*śvāmūtaye*) and टुओश्वि (*ṭuośvi*).

- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—proceeding for the sake of food; अस्मिन् भरे (*asmin bhare*)—in this battle

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

*[In the supplied text the label of the printed English translation stands between the Bhāvārtha label and the Bhāvārtha text; the label is moved below the text (logged).]*

O Indra, in this battle that proceeds for the winning of food, we call for protection you who show your strength and are a helper, who are wealthy, the lord of all prosperity, the best guide of the world, who listen attentively to our praise, are terrible to enemies, harm the enemies in battles, and wholly conquer the wealth of the enemies.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

## Sūkta 36 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The thirty-sixth sūkta** (ಮೂವತ್ತಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमामू ष्वित्येकादशर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका।
> इमामू पूपांत्यां घोरोऽपश्यत् सा निर्दहेच्छस्यमानेति श्रूयत इति । दशम्या
> आंगिरसो घोर ऋषिः शिष्टानां विश्वामित्रः ॥ अग्निष्टोमे

### Printed p. 830

> माध्यंदिनसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्रे दशमीवर्जितमिमामूष्टिति सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । इमामू ष्वित्युपोत्तमामुद्धरेत्सर्वत्र । आ. ५-१६ । इति ॥ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवषडहयोर्माध्यंदिनसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्रे चातुर्विंशिकातिदिष्टस्याहीनसूक्तस्य स्थाने त्रीणि संपातसूक्तानि । तत्रोपात्तमावर्जमेतत्पथमं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । इमामू ष्विच्छंति त्वा । आ. ७-५ । इति ॥

> *mādhyaṃdinasavanecchāvākaśastre daśamīvarjitamimāmūṣṭiti sūktaṃ | sūtritaṃ ca | imāmū ṣvityupottamāmuddharetsarvatra | ā. 5-16 | iti ‖ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavaṣaḍahayormādhyaṃdinasavanecchāvākaśastre cāturviṃśikātidiṣṭasyāhīnasūktasya sthāne trīṇi saṃpātasūktāni | tatropāttamāvarjametatpathamaṃ sūktaṃ | sūtritaṃ ca | imāmū ṣvicchaṃti tvā | ā. 7-5 | iti ‖*

*[The Sanskrit blocks are the introduction of Sāyaṇa. The word cut by the page end (its first part stood at the end of p. 829) is moved below the new head and joined, so that the second block begins with माध्यंदिनसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्रे (*mādhyaṃdinasavanecchāvākaśastre*) (logged). Line-end hyphens in the blocks are joined (logged). The bhāṣya has several unusual spellings, as supplied (for instance इमामू पूपांत्यां (*imāmū pūpāṃtyāṃ*) in the first block); the Anuvāda below reads इमामू षूसांत्यां (*imāmū ṣūsāṃtyāṃ*) in the corresponding place. The Anuvāda lines and the sūkta data, printed inside the bhāṣya block in the supplied text, are moved out of the block and un-quoted (logged).]*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, इमामू षु (*imāmū ṣu*), is the seventh sūkta in the third anuvāka *[the Kannada word for seventh is printed ಎಳನೆಯ; as supplied]*. There are eleven Ṛks in it. For the tenth Ṛk of this sūkta the seer is Ghora Āṅgirasa; Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: इमामू षूसांत्यां घोरोऽपश्यत्सा निर्दहेच्छस्यमानेति श्रूयते (*imāmū ṣūsāṃtyāṃ ghoro 'paśyatsā nirdahecchasyamāneti śrūyate*). In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice this sūkta, leaving out the tenth Ṛk, is used for the Śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka; this is explained by the sūtra इमामू ष्वित्युपोत्तमामुद्धरेत्सर्वत्र (*imāmū ṣvityupottamāmuddharetsarvatra*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 5-16). In the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭha and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, at the time of the midday pressing, in the place of the Ahīna-sūktas, the Cāturviṃśika-atidiṣṭa ones, which the priest called Acchāvāka recites, three Saṃpāta-sūktas must be recited. Among them this sūkta, leaving out the tenth Ṛk, is the first. This matter is explained by the sūtra इमामू ष्विच्छंति त्वा (*imāmū ṣvicchaṃti tvā*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 7-5).

**Sūkta data .** Sūkta 36 *[a line with this number stands before the sūkta data; as supplied]*. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 36. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 2; Varga 19 and 20 *[printed with a full stop between the two numbers]*. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Seer: Ṛks 1-9 and 11, विश्वामित्रः (*viśvāmitraḥ*); Ṛk 10, घोर अंगिरसः (*ghora aṃgirasaḥ*). Devatā: इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*). Chandas: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मामू॒ षु प्रभृ॑तिं सा॒तये॑ धाः॒ शश्व॑च्छश्वदू॒तिभि॒र्याद॑मानः ।  
> सु॒तेसु॑ते नावृधे॒ वर्ध॑नेभि॒र्यः कर्म॑भिर्म॒हद्भिः॒ सुश्रु॑तो॒भूत् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमां। ऊं इति । सु । प्रभृतिं । सातये । धाः ! शश्वत्शश्वत् । ऊतिभिः । यादमानः ।  
> पितेऽसुते । ववृधे । वर्धनेभिः । यः । कर्मभिः । महत्ऽभिः । सुश्रुतः । भूत् ।

> *imāṃ| ūṃ iti | su | prabhṛtiṃ | sātaye | dhāḥ ! śaśvatśaśvat | ūtibhiḥ | yādamānaḥ |*

> विश्वामित्र इंद्रं स्तौति । दे इंद्र ऊतिभिः । अवंति रक्षंति सर्वमित्यूतयो
> मरुतः । तैः शश्वच्छश्वत्सर्वदा यादमानः संगतिं याचमानस्त्वं प्रभृतिं । प्रकर्षण भ्रियते धार्यते यज्ञार्थमिति प्रभृतिः सोमः स्तुतिर्वा । इमामिमं

> प्रभृतिं । तादौ च निति कृत्यतानिति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । धाः । दधातेश्छांवसे लुजु
> रूपं । निघातः । शश्वच्छश्वत् । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति द्विर्वचनं । यावमानः टुयाचृ
> याज्ञायां , शानचि रूपं । चकारस्य दकारश्चांवसः । नावृधे । वृधु वर्धन इत्यस्माल्लिटि रूपं । तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घः संहितायां । निघातः । वर्धनेभिः । वर्धतेर्णंतस्य नंदादित्वाल्युट् लित्स्वरः । सुश्रुतः श्रु श्रवण इत्यस्मात्कर्मणि क्तः । गतिरनंतर इति गतिस्वरः । भूत् । भवतेर्लुजु रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises Indra: with the Maruts he is asked to secure this Soma or praise for our wealth; he grows by offerings and is renowned. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: प्रभृतिं (*prabhṛtiṃ*), धाः (*dhāḥ*), शश्वच्छश्वत् (*śaśvacchaśvat*), वृधु वर्धन (*vṛdhu vardhana*), वर्धनेभिः (*vardhanebhiḥ*), सुश्रुतः श्रु (*suśrutaḥ śru*) and भूत् (*bhūt*). Line-end hyphens in the block are joined, and one line break inside a word (वर्धतेर्णंतस्य (*vardhaterṇaṃtasya*), hyphen lost in the supplied text) is joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied in the bhāṣya: यावमानः (*yāvamānaḥ*) where the Saṃhitā has यादमानः (*yādamānaḥ*); छांवसे (*chāṃvase*) and चांवसः (*cāṃvasaḥ*) in the place of the usual word for Vedic usage; दे इंद्र (*de iṃdra*) at the opening; the compound धिरसुरवधमेघभेवनादिलक्षण्यर्वापारैः (*dhirasuravadhameghabhevanādilakṣaṇyarvāpāraiḥ*) is not clear.

- (इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra)
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—with the protecting Maruts
- शश्वच्छश्वत् (*śaśvacchaśvat*)—always
- यादमानः (*yādamānaḥ*)—wishing for companionship; इमां प्रभृतिं (*imāṃ prabhṛtiṃ*)—this refined Soma (or praise)
- सातये (*sātaye*)—for the winning of our wealth; सु धाः (*su dhāḥ*)—acquire it excellently
- सुतेसुते (*sutesute*)—whenever the Soma juice is pressed
- वर्धनेभिः (*vardhanebhiḥ*)—with Soma and the like that cause growth
- वावृधे (*vāvṛdhe*)—you grow
- यः (*yaḥ*)—he, Indra, who has these qualities; महद्भिः कर्मभिः (*mahadbhiḥ karmabhiḥ*)—by great deeds; सुश्रुतः भूत् (*suśrutaḥ bhūt*)—became famous

The Kannada verb printed ಸಾಹಚರವನ್ನುಪೇಕ್ಷಿಸಿ is rendered here as "wishing for companionship", following the printed English ("seeking association"); the verb usually means "disregarding", so the sense is not certain; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, always wishing for companionship with the protecting Maruts, acquire this refined Soma for the winning of our wealth. (Hold it.) Grow by Soma and the like, which stimulate your strength. Indra, who has great qualities, became famous by his great deeds.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, who are constantly seeking (association) with your allies (the
Maruts) accept this, our offering, (made) for the grant (from you of riches);

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑य॒ सोमाः॑ प्र॒दिवो॒ विदा॑ना ऋ॒भुर्येभि॒वृष॑पर्वा॒ विहा॑याः ।  
> प्र॒य॒म्यमा॑ना॒न्प्रति॒ षू गृ॑भा॒येंद्र॒ पिब॒ वृष॑धूतस्य॒ वृष्णः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राय । सोमाः । प्रदिवः । विदानाः । ऋभुः । येभिः । वृषपर्वा । विहायाः ।  
> प्रयम्यमानान् । प्रति । सु । गृभाय । इंद्र । पिब । वृषधूतस्य । वृष्णः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> माध्यंदिने सवनेच्छावाकस्य प्रस्थितयाज्येंद्राय सोमाः प्रदिव इत्येषा ।
> सूत्रितं च । इंद्राय सोमाः प्रदिवो विदाना आपूर्णो अस्य । आ. ५-५ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र इंद्राय तुभ्यं सोमाः प्रदिवः प्रगतेषु पूर्वेष्वहःसु विदानाः ।
> अस्माभिर्लंभिताः । वृषपूर्वा । वृषाणः फलस्य वर्षकाः पर्वाणि कालावयवा वर्षाद्या यस्य स तथोक्तः । कालात्मक इत्यर्थः । अत एव विहायाः । विजहात्युत्सृजत्यर्थानर्थिभ्य इति विहाया महान् । तादृश इंद्रो येभिर्यॆर्दत्तैः सोमैर्यभुर्दिप्पो वर्तते हे इंद्र त्वं प्रयम्यमानान् प्रकर्षण मंत्रैरुपयम्यमानानिमान्सोमान् सु सुष्टु प्रति गृभाय । प्रतिगृहाण । गृहीत्वा च वृषधूतस्य वृषभिर्ग्रावभिरभिषुतं वृष्णः स्वर्गादिफलवर्षकमिमं सोमं पिब॥ प्रदिवः। दिवु क्रीडादौ ।
> क्विप् । कालाध्वनोरत्यंतसंयोग इति द्वितीया। दिव् शब्दो दिवसवाजी । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः। विदानाः। विद्ल लाभ इत्यस्य व्यत्ययेन शानच्। बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक्।
> विहायाः । ओहाक् त्यागे । वहिहाधाङ्छृंदसीत्यसुन् । णिदित्यनुवृत्तेरातो युक्
> चिण्कृतोरिति युगागमः । गतिकारकयोरिति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । गृभाय । ग्रह
> उपादान इत्यस्य लोटि हौ श्नाप्रत्ययस्य छंदसि शायजपीति शायजादेशः । हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं । अते हेरिति हेर्लुक् । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the midday pressing the Soma juices offered to Indra, who is of the nature of time, are to be accepted and drunk. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*), विदानाः (*vidānāḥ*), विहायाः (*vihāyāḥ*), गृभाय (*gṛbhāya*). Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied in the bhāṣya: वृषपूर्वा (*vṛṣapūrvā*) where the Saṃhitā has वृषपर्वा (*vṛṣaparvā*); यॆर्दत्तैः (*yèrdattaiḥ*) with the short vowel sign (converted to the Devanagari short e, as supplied); यभुर्दिप्पो (*yabhurdippo*) (the sense is not clear); आपूर्णो (*āpūrṇo*) in the sūtra quotation where the Special Topics print अपूर्णो (*apūrṇo*); छृंदसीत्यसुन् (*chṛṃdasītyasun*). In the grammar part of the bhāṣya the bars stand against the neighbouring words without a space (for instance after पिब॥ (*piba‖*)), as supplied.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is of the nature of time and great-souled, is made radiant by the Soma juices; to that lord Indra the Soma juices have been offered on all the former days. O lord Indra, accept with regard these Soma juices offered in abundance. Drink this Soma, which is pressed by the grāvas (pressing stones) and gives fruits such as heaven.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
To Indra have libations been presented in the days of old, whereby he has become illustrious, the regulator of time, the granter of desires : accept, Indra, these prescribed (offerings), and drink of this auspicious (beverage) expressed by the stones.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the midday pressing the priest called Acchāvāka must recite this Ṛk, beginning इंद्राय सोमाः प्रदिवः (*iṃdrāya somāḥ pradivaḥ*), as the Prasthita-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, इंद्राय सोमाः प्रदिवो विदाना अपूर्णो अस्य (*iṃdrāya somāḥ pradivo vidānā apūrṇo asya*) (Ā. 5-5).

*[The sūtra is quoted here as अपूर्णो (*apūrṇo*) while the bhāṣya quotes it with आपूर्णो (*āpūrṇo*); as supplied.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is asked to drink this Soma and grow strong, and to drink the new Soma now as he drank the old before. The grammar follows and is transcribed, not explained: पिब (*piba*), वर्धस्व (*vardhasva*), अपिबः (*apibaḥ*), पाहि (*pāhi*), पन्यः (*panyaḥ*), नवीयान् (*navīyān*). Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept as supplied: the word ending त्वदर्थ० (*tvadartha0*) has the Kannada digit zero in place of the anusvāra sign, which converts to a Devanagari zero.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पिब (*piba*)—drink this Soma
- वर्धस्व (*vardhasva*)—attain growth
- तव (*tava*)—with reference to you
- प्रथमाः (*prathamāḥ*)—the ancient ones
- उत (*uta*)—and; इमे सोमासः (*ime somāsaḥ*)—these Soma juices, new ones too; सुतासः घ (*sutāsaḥ gha*)—have been pressed, have they not
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पूर्वान् (*pūrvān*)—the ancient
- सोमान् (*somān*)—Soma juices
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way in which
- अपिबः (*apibaḥ*)—you drank
- एव (*eva*)—in the same way
- अद्य (*adya*)—even now
- पन्यः (*panyaḥ*)—you who are worthy of praise
- नवीयान् (*navīyān*)—the new juices
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink this Soma juice and attain growth. These juices, ancient and new, have been pressed and are ready. As you drank the ancient juices before, so you, who are worthy of praise, drink even now these new juices.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Drink, Indra, and thrive : yours are these (present) libations, as were the primitive libations : you are adorable ; drink to-day the recent libations, as you drank those of old.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the midday pressing the priest called Acchāvāka must recite this Ṛk, beginning पिबा वर्धस्व (*pibā vardhasva*), as a Yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, पिबा वर्धस्व तव फा सुतास इति याज्या (*pibā vardhasva tava phā sutāsa iti yājyā*) (Ā. 5-16).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, praised by all, has fierce strength and valour spreading everywhere; when Soma gladdens him, neither earth nor heaven surpasses him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महान् (*mahān*)—of exceeding strength
- वृजने (*vṛjane*)—in battle
- आमत्रः (*āmatraḥ*)—who defeats enemies
- विरप्यी (*virapyī*)—who is praised by all; in such an Indra, उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—fearful
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—bodily strength
- धृष्णु (*dhṛṣṇu*)—overpowering the enemies
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—valour
- पत्यते (*patyate*)—

### Printed p. 836

are pervading. यत् (*yat*)—when; सोमासः (*somāsaḥ*)—the Soma juices; हर्यश्वं (*haryaśvaṃ*)—Indra; अमंहन् (*amaṃhan*)—they satisfy (then); एनं (*enaṃ*)—this Indra of such majesty; पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth; न विव्याच (*na vivyāca*)—does not surpass and pervade; चन (*cana*)—the heaven also cannot surpass and pervade this Indra.

*[Printed oddities kept: the Pratipadārtha has ಆಮತ್ರಃ where the Saṃhitā has ಅಮತ್ರೋ, and ಅಮಂಹನ್ where the Saṃhitā has ಹರ್ಯಶ್ವಮಮಂದನ್; the Bhāvārtha has ಮಾರಿ where the Pratipadārtha has ಮೀರಿ; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who has exceeding strength, defeats the enemies in battle and is praised by all, has fearful bodily strength and an overpowering valour that spread everywhere. When the Soma juices satisfy an Indra of such majesty, then even the heaven and the earth, both together, cannot pervade beyond him.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The great Indra, the victorious in battle, the defier of foes : his fierce strength and resolute vigour are exerted : verily the earth does not contain him, neither (does the heaven), when the Soma libations exhilarate the lord of the tawny steeds.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mighty, fierce Indra grows for heroic deeds, joined with the poets' hymns; his cows give milk as food and are many givers of gifts.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महान् (*mahān*)—possessing great qualities
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—and terrible to the enemies
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—in order to display his power for great deeds
- वावृधे (*vāvṛdhe*)—attains growth
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the giver of fruit
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—and worthy of worship, Indra
- काव्येन (*kāvyena*)—with praise
- समाचक्रे (*samācakre*)—is united
- अस्य (*asya*)—of such a majestic Indra
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—the cows
- वाजदाः (*vājadāḥ*)—as givers of food in the form of milk; प्र जायंते (*pra jāyaṃte*)—are produced
- अस्य (*asya*)—his
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—all the cows, many in number
- दक्षिणाः (*dakṣiṇāḥ*)—are givers in many kinds of forms

*[Printed oddities kept: the Pratipadārtha has ವೀರಾಯ where the Saṃhitā has ವೀರ್ಯಾಯ; the Bhāvārtha has ಸೃದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನು where the Pratipadārtha has ವೃದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನು; line-end hyphens inside the Pratipadārtha headwords of both Ṛks are joined (logged); as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who possesses great qualities and is terrible to the enemies, attains growth in order to display his power for great deeds. Indra, the giver of fruit and worthy of worship, is united with poetic praise. The cows of such a majestic Indra are produced as givers of food in the form of milk, and are also endowed with many kinds of power of giving.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The mighty, fierce, auspicious Indra, the showerer (of benefits), augments (in power) as he is animated for heroic (acts) by praise : his cattle are generated givers of food : many are his donations.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सिंधवो नद्यो यथा प्रसवं । प्रकर्षण सूयत इति प्रसवः कामः । तमनुस्पत्य यद्यदा प्रायन् प्रकृष्टमतिदूरं समुद्रं गच्छंति तदापो महांतं
> समुद्रं रथ्येव रथिन इव जग्मुः । प्रीणनार्थं गच्छंति । तद्वत् अतश्चित्सदसोऽस्मादप्यंतरिक्षादसाविंद्रो वरीयान् । उरुतरः खलु । यदीं यमेनमिंद्रं दुग्धोऽभिषुतोऽंशुर्लताखंडरूपोऽल्पः सोमः पृणति प्रीणयति । यथाल्पा नद्योऽल्पीयांसि च जलानि महांतं समुद्रं प्रीणयंति तद्वदल्पतरोऽंशुभूतः सोमो वरीयांसमिंद्रं प्रीणयति ॥ प्रसवं । सवतेः कर्मण्यप् । थाधादिस्वरः । आयन् ।
> आयतेर्लजि रूपं। यद्योगादनिघातः। रथ्येव । रथस्येमे रथ्याः। रथाद दिति यत्।
> सुपां सुलुगिति सुपो डादेशः। तित्स्वरितः । इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः।
> जग्मुः। गमर्लिटि रूपं । गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः। निघातः । वरीयान् । उरुशब्दादीयसुनि प्रियस्थिरेत्यादिना वरादेशः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पृणति । पृण प्रीणने।
> तुदादिः । यद्योगादनिघातः । दुग्धः । दुहेः क्तः । एकाच इतीट् प्रतिषेधः । दादेर्धातोर्घ इति हकारस्य घत्वं । झषस्तथोधोऽधः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As the small rivers please the great ocean by flowing into it, so the small pressed Soma plant pleases Indra, who is vaster than this atmosphere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यदीं (*yadīṃ*)—when
- दुग्धः (*dugdhaḥ*)—pressed out, and; अंशुः सोमः (*aṃśuḥ somaḥ*)—consisting of pieces, the Soma
- पृणति (*pṛṇati*)—satisfies Indra, then
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—the rivers impelled by Indra; यथा प्रसवं (*yathā prasavaṃ*)—following their own independent course; रथ्येव जग्मुः (*rathyeva jagmuḥ*)—as charioteers rush forward at will
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—having unfathomable water
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—the ocean; प्र आयन् (*pra āyan*)—go and join; अतश्चित् सदसः (*ataścit sadasaḥ*)—more than this atmosphere
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वरीयान् (*varīyān*)—the greatest (literally, the excessive one). The line-end hyphen inside the last headword is joined (logged)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as the Soma, which is pressed out and consists of pieces, has satisfied Indra, all the rivers likewise flow at will along their own independent course, as charioteers rush forward at will, and go and join the ocean with its unfathomable water. Such an Indra has grown vaster than the atmosphere.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಅಭಿಸುತವಾದುದೂ where the Pratipadārtha has ಅಭಿಷುತವಾದುದೂ; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
As the rivers pursue their course, the waters rush to the ocean, like the drivers of cars (to a goal), so the vast Indra (hastens) from his dwelling (in the firmament), when the humble soma libation propitiates him.

> समुद्रेण । सहिता नद्यादिरूपेणापोऽभिद्रवंत्येनमिति समुद्रः । तेन यादमानास्तेन सह संगतिं याचमानाः सिंधवो नद्यो यथा तं पूरयंति तद्वद्धस्तिनो हस्तवंतोऽध्वर्याद्वय इंद्राय तुभ्यं सुषुतं सुष्पभिषुतं सोमं

> स्रवतो रसस्य धारया पवित्रैः पावनैर्भरित्रॆः । कर्मकरणार्थं पदार्थान्बिभ्रतीति
> भरित्रा बाहवः । तैर्मध्वो माधुर्योपेतान्नोमान्सुनंति । शोधयंति ॥ समुद्रेण । समुत्पूर्वाद्द्रवतेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यत इति डः । डित्वाट्टिलोपः । यद्वा ।
> उन्दी क्लेदने । संपूर्वस्य स्थायितंचीत्यादिना रक् । कित्वादुपधालोपः । उभयत्र प्रत्ययस्वरः । सुपा सहैकादेशे कृत एकादेश उदात्त एव । यादमानाः । टु

> पूञ् जवन इत्यस्य लटि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests, who have hands, press the Soma plant for Indra as the rivers longing to join the ocean fill it, and they purify the sweet juice with the filters.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समुद्रेण (*samudreṇa*)—with the ocean
- यादमानाः (*yādamānāḥ*)—with the desire to unite
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—the rivers (as they fill the ocean with water)
- हस्तिनः (*hastinaḥ*)—the adhvaryus and others who have hands (holding the Soma)
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra, the lord
- सुषुतं (*suṣutaṃ*)—pressed out
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- भरंतः (*bharaṃtaḥ*)—procuring
- अंशुं (*aṃśuṃ*)—the Soma in the form of the creeper
- दुहंति (*duhaṃti*)—they squeeze
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—with the stream of the juice
- पवित्रैः (*pavitraiḥ*)—pure
- भरित्रैः (*bharitraiḥ*)—with arms
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—the sweet Soma
- पुनंति (*punaṃti*)—they purify. Line-end hyphens inside the headwords are joined or absent as supplied; the page ends here, the Bhāvārtha follows on page 840

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Just as the rivers, with the desire to unite with the ocean, fill the ocean with water, so the adhvaryus, addressing you, Indra, and in order to offer to you, squeeze the Soma in the form of the creeper and obtain the juice. And with pure arms, with the stream of the juice, they purify the sweet Soma.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಅಧ್ವರ್ಯುಗಳು where the Pratipadārtha has ಅಧ್ವರುವೇ; the Pratipadārtha is on page 839; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
As the rivers are solicitour [sic] (to mix) with the ocean, so (are the priests) bearing the efficient libation to Indra : holding in their hands they milk the Soma plant, and purify the sweet juices (as they fall) in drops through the purifying filters.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रस्य कुक्षय उदराणि सोमधानाः । सोमो निधीयते येष्विति सोमधानाः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । ह्रदा इव । यथा ह्रदा जलाधारा भवंति तद्वत् । ईं सोऽयमिंद्रः पुरूणि सवना त्रीणि सवनानि सं विव्याच । सम्यक् व्याप्नोति । इंद्रः प्रथमा प्रथमान्यन्ना भक्षणीयानि सोमादीन्यन्नानि यद्यस्माद्वाश विशेषेण जघास
> ततो वृत्रं जघन्वान्वृत्रस्य हंतेंद्रः सोमं माध्यंदिने सवने देवेभ्योऽवृणीत । समभजत ॥ कुक्षयः । कुष निष्कर्षॆ । प्लुषिकुषिशुषिभ्यः क्सिः । उ. ३-१५५ । कुष्यत इति कुक्षिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सोमधानाः । दधातेरधिकरणे ल्युट् । लित्स्वरः । विव्याच । व्यचेर्लिटि रूपं । अन्ना । अद भक्षणे। अद्यत इत्यन्नं । आश । अश भोजन इत्यस्य
> लिट णलि रूपं । अत अदेरित्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घः । यद्योगादनिघातः । लित्स्वरः । वृत्रं ।
> न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठिप्रतिषेधः । जघन्वान् । हंतेः क्वसाविडभावे रूपं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अवृणीत । वृज् संभक्तावित्यस्य लजि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra's bellies hold Soma like lakes; he fills the three pressings; having eaten and slain Vṛtra, he shared Soma with the gods at midday.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The bellies of Indra are filled with Soma juices, deep like unfathomable lakes. This same Indra has taken part in the sacrifice at many pressing-times and has drunk the Soma. And having eaten the most ancient foods beginning with Soma, he destroyed the demon Vṛtra. He also distributed the Soma to the gods.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is asked to bring wealth quickly, so that no one may obstruct it; he is known as the lord of wealth and is asked to give the wealth that is his.

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—among all riches
- वसुपतिं (*vasupatiṃ*)—as the lord of the best wealth; विद्र हि (*vidra hi*)—we know indeed
- हर्षश्व (*harṣaśva*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—related to you and
- मंहनीयं (*maṃhanīyaṃ*)—venerable; यत् दत्रं अस्ति (*yat datraṃ asti*)—whatever wealth there is
- तत् (*tat*)—that wealth
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- प्रयंधि (*prayaṃdhi*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bring your wealth here quickly. We know that you are the lord of the best wealth among all riches. Give us whatever wealth is yours, related to you and venerable, and let no one obstruct your wealth on the way.

> षष्ठि । अस्मे अस्मभ्यं प्र यंधि । प्रयच्छ । किंच अस्मे अस्माकं जीवसे जीवनाय
> शतं शरदः संवत्सरान्नाः । देहि । शिप्रिन् शोभनहनो हे इंद्र अस्मे अस्माकं तश्वतः ।
> शश्वदिति बहुनाम । बहून्वीरान्पुत्रान्देहि ॥ जीवसे । जीव प्राणधारण इत्यस्य तुमर्थेऽसेप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । शश्वतः । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योः । अस्मात्संश्चद्वेहदित्यादिना अतिप्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातनादिष्टरूपसिद्धिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is used at the Jātakarma for touching the shoulder; Indra is asked for abundant wealth, a hundred years of life and many sons.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy one
- ऋजीषिन् (*ṛjīṣin*)—and drinker of the Soma whose essence is spent
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- विश्ववारस्य (*viśvavārasya*)—that is esteemed by all
- भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)—and abundant
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us; प्र यंधि (*pra yaṃdhi*)—give
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—in order to live (the word is split across two lines in the supplied text); शतं शरदः (*śataṃ śaradaḥ*)—a hundred years
- धाः (*dhāḥ*)—give
- शिप्रिन् (*śiprin*)—O one with beautiful cheeks
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- तश्वतं (*taśvataṃ*)—much
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—heroic sons, full of vigour; favour us with them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are wealthy and drink the Soma whose essence is spent, give us abundant wealth that is esteemed by all. Grant that we may live a hundred years. O Indra with beautiful cheeks, grant us heroic sons in very great number.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Opulent Indra, receiver of the spiritless Soma juice, give to us riches in universally desired quantity; grant us to live a hundred years; bestow upon us, Indra, with the handsome chin, numerous posterity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the Jātakarma, for the touching of the shoulder (अंसाभिमर्शन (*aṃsābhimarśana*)), the Ṛk beginning अस्मे प्र यंधि (*asme pra yaṃdhi*) is to be recited, as stated in the आश्वलायनगृह्यसूत्र (*āśvalāyanagṛhyasūtra*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-15).

> शृण्वंतं । उग्रं । ऊतये । समत्सु । घ्नंतं । वृत्राणि । संजितं । धनानां ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः ।
> अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन्संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृद्धं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखि नाम । सुखकरं मघवानं धनवंतं अत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संचितं समग्देतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्योरित्यस्य
> निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । हैयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते शपो लुकि
> कृते च लिजि रूपं । निघातः । भरे । भृञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः ।
> वाजसात् । पणु दाने । भावे क्तिन् जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं । बहुव्रीहौ
> पूर्वपदस्वरः । समत्सु । आद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति योद्धाणामायूंषीति समदः संग्रामाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घ्नंतं । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेरिति घत्वं । संजितं । जि जये ।
> क्विप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, wealthy, the best leader, who hears our praise, is terrible to enemies and destroys the Vṛtras and conquers their wealth; we call him to this battle for protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—that goes on for the sake of food; अस्मिन् भरे (*asmin bhare*)—in this battle
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—full of enthusiasm
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—wealthy
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the lord
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—the guide
- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—who listens to our praise
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—terrible to enemies
- समत्सु (*samatsu*)—in battles (the Kannada word for "in battles" is cut by the page end: ಸಂಗ್ರಾ at the foot of page 844 and ಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ at the top of page 845; joined here, as the print continues it)

### Printed p. 845

वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the enemies; घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)—who destroys; धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—the wealth of the enemies; संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*)—who wholly conquers; and so (that is) Indra, to be called ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection; हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in this battle that goes on for the sake of winning food, you show your strength and are a helper; you are wealthy, lord of all riches, the best guide of the world, one who listens attentively to our praise, terrible to enemies, one who in battles harms the enemies and wholly conquers the enemies' wealth. As such we call you for protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

## Sūkta 37 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The thirty-seventh sūkta** (ಮೂವತ್ತೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वार्त्रहत्यायेत्येकादशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं । एकादश्यनुष्टुप् शिष्टा गायत्रैः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । वार्त्रहत्याय गायत्रमंत्यानुष्टुबिति ॥ अतिरात्रॆ प्रथमे
> पर्याये ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्रे वार्त्रहत्यायेत्युत्तमावर्जं सूक्तं शंसनीयं ।
> तथा च सूत्रितं । वार्त्रहत्यायेत्युत्तमामुद्धरेत् । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥ महाव्रते गायत्रीतृचातीतावुत्तमावर्जमिदं सूक्तं पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं । वार्त्रहत्याय
> शवस इत्युत्तमामुद्धरति । ऐ. आ, ५-२-५ । इति ॥

*[The block is the introduction of Sāyaṇa. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: the reference ऐ. आ, ५-२-५ (*ai. ā, 5-2-5*) has a comma after the abbreviation ಆ; the word ಅತಿರಾತ್ರೆ is written with the short vowel sign ೆ, which the conversion renders with the Devanagari short sign ॆ, as supplied. The Anuvāda lines, printed inside the bhāṣya block in the supplied text, are moved out of the block and un-quoted (logged).]*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, वार्तहत्याय (*vārtahatyāya*), is the eighth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are eleven Ṛks in it. For this sūkta the seer is Viśvāmitra *[the Kannada word for Viśvāmitra is printed ವಿಶ್ರಾಮಿತ್ರನು; as supplied]*; Indra is the deity; the eleventh Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. The remaining Ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: वार्तहत्याय गायत्रमंत्यानुष्टुप् (*vārtahatyāya gāyatramaṃtyānuṣṭup*). In the sacrifice called Atirātra, in the first paryāya, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin must recite the Ṛks of this sūkta, except the last Ṛk, for the Śastra mantras; this is explained by the sūtra वार्तहत्यायेत्युत्तमामुद्धरेत् (*vārtahatyāyetyuttamāmuddharet*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 6-4). And in the sacrifice called Mahāvrata also, among the Śastra mantras, the use of the Ṛks of this sūkta, except the last Ṛk, for the Ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre is stated in the Pañcamāraṇyaka of the Aitareya-āraṇyaka (Ai: Ā. 5-2-5) by the sentence वार्तहत्याय शवस इत्युत्तमामुद्धरति (*vārtahatyāya śavasa ityuttamāmuddharati*).

*[Printed oddities kept: the Anuvāda spells the sūkta's first word and the quotations वार्तहत्याय (*vārtahatyāya*) without the conjunct, where the bhāṣya has वार्त्रहत्यायेत्येकादशर्चमष्टमं (*vārtrahatyāyetyekādaśarcamaṣṭamaṃ*); the reference before the last quotation has a colon after the abbreviation of the Aitareya-āraṇyaka; as supplied.]*

*[The Saṃhitā and the Pada carry the number of the Ṛk between bars. Printed oddities kept: the Saṃhitā has पृतनाषाह्याय (*pṛtanāṣāhyāya*) where the Pada has पृतनासह्याय (*pṛtanāsahyāya*); as supplied.]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वार्त्र॑हत्याय॒ शव॑से पृतना॒षाह्या॑य च ।  
> इंद्र॒ त्वा व॑र्तयामसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वार्त्रहत्याय । शवसे । पृतनासह्याय । च ।  
> इंद्र । त्वा । आ । वर्तयामसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वामित्रः स्तौति । हे इंद्र वार्त्रहत्याय वृत्रहननिमित्ताय शवसे बलायापि च पृतनासाह्याय परकीयसेनाभिभवाय त्वामा सर्वतो वर्तयामसि। प्रवर्तयामः ॥ वार्त्रहत्याय । वृत्रघ्नः कर्मेत्यर्थे ब्राह्मणादित्वात् सृञ् । हनस्तो
> ऽचिण्णलोः । पा. ७-३-३२ । इति तकारः । इत्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पृतनाषाह्याय । षह
> मर्षण इत्यस्माद्भावे शकिसहोश्चति यत् । संहितायां सहेः पृतनर्ताभ्यां च ।
> पा- ८-३-१०९ । इति षत्वं । दीर्घश्चांदसः । वर्तयामसि । वृतु वर्तन इत्यस्य ण्यंतस्य
> मस इदंतो मसिरिति मसि इत्यादेशः । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises Indra: we urge you on for the strength that serves the killing of Vṛtra and for the overcoming of the enemy's armies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वार्त्रहत्याय (*vārtrahatyāya*)—that is the cause of the killing of Vṛtra
- शवसे (*śavase*)—for the increase of strength (the Kannada word for "increase" is split across two lines in the supplied text)
- च (*ca*)—and
- पृतनाषाह्याय (*pṛtanāṣāhyāya*)—for the destruction of the armies of other enemies also
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ (*ā*)—all round
- वर्तयामसि (*vartayāmasi*)—gathering together, we pray and urge

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for the increase of the strength needed for killing Vṛtra, and also for the destruction of the armies of other enemies, we surround you, pray to you, encourage you and urge you on.

### Printed p. 847

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We excite you, Indra, to exert the strength that destroys Vritra, and overpowers hostile armies.

> यज्ञियां धुरमिति वाघतः स्तोतारः । ते तव सु अस्मदभिमतफलसंपादनेन शोभनं मनोर्वाचीनमस्मदभिमुखं कृण्वंतु । कुर्वंतु । उत अपि च चक्षुस्त्वदीयं दर्शनमस्मास्वनुग्रहदृष्टिं कुर्वंतु ॥ अर्वाचीनं । विभाषांचेरदिक् स्त्रीयामिति
> खप्रत्ययः । खस्येनादेशः । चक्षुः । चक्षेः शिच्चेत्युसिप्रत्ययः । शिद्वद्भावात् ख्याञादेशाभावः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तः । कृण्वंतु । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोरित्यस्य लोटि
> रूपं । आमंत्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन पादादित्वादनिघातः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । वाघतः ।
> वह प्रापणे । संश्च द्वेहदित्यादिना अतिप्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातनादुपधावृद्धिः । हकारस्य
> घत्वं । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The praisers are to turn your mind and your eye towards us, by granting what we desire, that is, to look on us with favour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—worshipped in hundreds of sacrifices
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वाघतः (*vāghataḥ*)—the praisers (the Kannada word is split across two lines in the supplied text)
- ते (*te*)—your
- सु (*su*)—excellent
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind
- उत (*uta*)—and
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—the sight
- आर्वाचीनं (*ārvācīnaṃ*)—so as to face us
- कृण्वंतु (*kṛṇvaṃtu*)—may make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worshipped in hundreds of sacrifices, may the praisers praise you so that your excellent mind and your sight are turned towards us (the Kannada word for "sight" is split across two lines in the supplied text).

### Printed p. 848

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May (your) praisers, Indra, who are worshipped in a hundred rites, direct your mind and your eyes towards us.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नामा॑नि ते शतक्रतो॒ विश्वा॑भिर्गि॒र्भिरी॑महे ।  
> इंद्रा॑भिमाति॒षाह्ये॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नामानि । ते । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो । विश्वाभिः । गीभिः । ईमहे ।  
> इंद्र । अभिमातिसह्ये ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शतक्रतो हे इंद्र अभिमातिषाह्ये । मातिर्मानो गर्वः । अभितो मानो
> येषां तेऽभिमातयः शत्रवः । तेषां सहनमेव सह्यं । तस्मिन्युद्धेऽस्माकमुपस्थिते
> सति ते तव नामानि शक्रवज्रहस्तादीनि नामधेयानि । यद्वा । तदुपलक्षितानि बलानि विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिः सर्वाभिः स्तुतिलक्षणाभिर्वाग्भिरीमहे । वयं याचामहे ॥ ईमहे ।
> ई कांत्यादिषु । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when the battle that overcomes enemies is upon us, we ask for your names (Śakra, Vajrahasta and the like), or the powers they point to, with all praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—worshipped in hundreds of sacrifices
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अभिमातिषाह्ये (*abhimātiṣāhye*)—in the time of the battle that defeats enemies *[a hyphen is printed after this word in place of the dash; as supplied]*
- ते (*te*)—your
- नामानि (*nāmāni*)—the endless names or powers; विश्वाभिः गीर्भिः (*viśvābhiḥ gīrbhiḥ*)—with all praises
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—praising (we pray)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worshipped in hundreds of sacrifices, in the time of battle that is made for defeating enemies, we praise and pray to your endless powers with all hymns of praise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We recite, Indra, who are worshipped in a hundred rites, (your many) names in all our hymns for strength to resist our foes.

*[The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒रु॒ष्टु॒तस्य॒ धाम॑भिः श॒तेन॑ महयामसि ।  
> इंद्र॑स्य चर्षणी॒धृतः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुरुऽस्तुतस्य । धामभिः । शतेन । महयामसि ।  
> इंद्रस्य । चर्षणिधृतः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पुरुष्टुतस्य पुरुभिर्बहुभिः स्तोतृभिः स्तुतस्य शतेनापरिमितसंख्याकैर्धामभिस्तेजोभिर्युक्तस्य चर्षणीधृतश्चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणां कर्मानुष्ठात्यणामभिमतफलसंपादनेन धारकस्येंद्रस्य । यद्वा । आकृषंति सर्वमनेनेति चर्षणि
> बलं । तद्धारकस्य तव महयामसि । स्तोत्रं कुर्मः ॥ पुरुष्टुतस्य । ष्टुञ् स्तुत् ।
> कर्मणि क्तः । थाधादिस्वरः । संहितायां स्तुतस्तोमयोश्चंदसीति षत्वं । महयामसि । मह पूजायामित्यस्य लटीदंतो मसिः । निघातः । चर्षणीधृतः । कृष आकर्षणे । कृषेरादेश्च चः । उ. २-१०५ । इत्यनिप्रत्ययः । ककारस्य चकारादेशः । यद्वा।
> कृष विलेखने । कर्षंतीति चर्षणयो मनुष्याः । धृ धारणे । क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, praised by many praisers, endowed with countless splendours, supporter of the sacrificing men, we offer you praise; or, the supporter of strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुष्टुतस्य (*puruṣṭutasya*)—praised by many
- शतेन (*śatena*)—of many kinds
- धामभिः (*dhāmabhiḥ*)—with splendours
- चर्षणीधृतः (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ*)—supporter of the performers of sacrifice
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of the lord Indra (the Kannada word for "lord" is split across two lines in the supplied text)
- महयामसि (*mahayāmasi*)—we praise the glory

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We praise the glory of Indra, who is praised by many, endowed with splendours of many kinds, supporter of the performers of sacrifice, and lord.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We repeat the praise of the many-lauded Indra the supporter of man, invested with a hundred glories.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रं॑ वृ॒त्राय॒ हंत॑वे पुरुहू॒तमुप॑ ब्रुवे ।  
> भरे॑षु॒ वाज॑सातये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रं । वृत्राय । हंतवे । पुरुऽहूतं । उप । ब्रुवे ॥  
> भरेषु । वाजऽसातये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वृत्राय हंतवे वृत्रनामकमसुरं हंतुं भरेषु युद्धेषु वाजसातयेऽन्नोपलक्षितधनलाभाय च पुरुहूतं पुरुभिराहूतमिंद्रं बलवंतं त्वामुपब्रुवे । सोमपानार्थं विश्वामित्रोऽहमाह्वयामि ॥ वृत्राय । क्रियाग्रहणं
> कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानं । हंतवे । हंतेस्तुमर्थे तवेन्प्रत्ययः । नित्स्वरः ।
> ब्रुवे । ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचीत्यस्य लज्युत्तम इट रूपं । निघातः । वाजसातये ।
> सननं सातिः । वाजस्य सातिर्वाजसातिः । दासीभारादित्वात्तूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, to slay the demon Vṛtra and to win food and wealth in battles, I, Viśvāmitra, call you, invoked by many, for Soma-drinking.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) वृत्राय (*vṛtrāya*)—of Vṛtra the demon
- हंतवे (*haṃtave*)—for the slaying
- भरेषु (*bhareṣu*)—in battles
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the gain of food
- पुरुहूतं (*puruhūtaṃ*)—prayed to by many
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—you, the powerful; उप ब्रुवे (*upa bruve*)—I call upon with praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for the slaying of Vṛtra the demon, and for the gain of food in battles, I call upon you with praise, you who are prayed to by many and are powerful.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I invoke you, Indra, who are invoked of many for the slaying of Vritra, and the granting of food (as the spoil) of battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, doer of many deeds, be one with power to defeat enemies in battles. We pray to you for the slaying of Vṛtra the demon.

Be victorious, Indra, in battle : we solicit you, object of many rites, to destroy Vrittra,

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र द्युम्नेषु द्योतमानेषु धनेषु प्राप्तव्येष्टभिमानिनो ये सपत्नाः पृतनाज्ये । पृतनानामजनं गमनं यस्मिन्निति पृतनाज्यं संग्रामः । तस्मिन्संग्रामे च पृत्सुतूर्षु पृतनासु तरणशीलेषु शूरेषु श्रवःसु बलेषु च येऽभिमानिनः सपत्नाः संति तान् साक्ष्य । अभिभव । तथाभिमातिषु सर्वतो गर्वयुक्तेषु
> शत्रुषु पुरुषेषु ये सपत्नाः तांश्चाभिभव ॥ पृतनाज्ये । अज गतिक्षेपणयोरित्यस्य
> ण्यंतस्य अचो यत् । पृतनानामाज्यं पृतनाज्यं । एकादेशस्वरः । पृत्सुतूर्षु ।
> पृतनाशब्दस्य सौ परतः । मांस्पृत्स्नौनामुपसंख्यानमिति पृदादेशः । इत्वरा संभ्रमे । ताच्छीलिकः क्विप् । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना ऊट् । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमिति पूर्वपदस्य सप्तम्या अलुक् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । साक्ष्य । सह मर्षण इत्यस्य लोटि बहुलं
> छंदसीति शपो लुक् । ढत्वकत्वे दीर्घश्कांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, defeat all rivals who are proud in wealth, in battle, among heroes and in strength, and the enemies puffed up on every side.

*[After the bhāṣya a stray word stands, printed in Telugu script in the supplied text; it is rewritten letter for letter in Kannada letters and kept: ಪ್ರವೇಶಮು. ##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- द्युम्नेषु (*dyumneṣu*)—whether in the matter of wealth
- पृतनाज्ये (*pṛtanājye*)—whether in battle
- पृत्सुतूर्षु (*pṛtsutūrṣu*)—whether in the throng of heroes
- श्रवःसु (*śravaḥsu*)—whether in strength
- अभिमातिषु (*abhimātiṣu*)—whether among enemies full of pride (all who are opposed to us)
- साक्ष्य (*sākṣya*)—defeat and destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whether in the matter of wealth, in battle, in the throng of heroes, in strength, or among proud men, defeat and destroy all who are opposed to us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Overcome Indra, those who are adverse to us in riches, in battle, in hostile hosts, in strength.

> शु॒ष्मिंत॑मं न ऊ॒तये॑ द्यु॒म्मिनं॑ पाहि॒ जागृ॑विं ।  
> इंद्र॒ सोमं॑ शतक्रतो ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तुष्मिन्तमं । नः । ऊतये । द्युम्मिनं । पाहि । जागृविं ॥  
> इंद्र । सोमं । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 853

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिने सवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्रे शुष्मिंतमं न ऊतय इति तृचो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । शुष्मिन्तमं न ऊतये श्रायंत
> इव सूर्यं । आ. ७-४ । इति ॥
> शतक्रतो हे इंद्र शुष्मिन्मं बलवतां मध्येऽतिशयेन बलवंतं द्युम्मिनं
> दीप्तिमंतं । यद्वा शुष्मिन्मं शत्रूणां शोषकतनुं द्युम्मिनं यशस्विनं जागृविं

> पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे प्रत्ययस्वरः । पाहि ! पातेर्लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् ।
> निघातः । जागृविः । क्विन्रत्ययांतः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The bhāṣya first states the liturgical use of the tṛca (reference Ā. 7-4); then: O Indra, drink our soma, most strong, bright and wakeful, for our protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O (Indra) of many sacrificial acts
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- शुष्मिंतमं (*śuṣmiṃtamaṃ*)—that which increases strength
- दुम्मिनं (*dumminaṃ*)—that which is bright
- जागृविं (*jāgṛviṃ*)—that which awakens
- नः (*naḥ*)—offered by us
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the soma
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for our protection
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

*[Printed oddity kept: the Pratipadārtha spells the word ದುಮ್ಮಿನಂ, where the bhāṣya has ದ್ಯುಮ್ಮಿನಂ; as supplied. The word breaks across a line (ಶಕ್ತಿವರ್ಧ್ / ಕವಾದುದೂ) are joined in the reading.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra of many sacrificial acts, drink, for our protection, the soma offered by us, which increases strength, is bright and awakens.

*[Printed oddities kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಶಕ್ತಿಪರ್ಧಕ and ಪ್ರಭೋ / ಧಕ where the Pratipadārtha has a different consonant in each (see the Pratipadārtha above); as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Drink, Indra, object of many rites, for our preservation, the most invigorating, fame-conferring, sleep-dispelling, soma juice.

*[The printed English breaks the word "invigorating" across two lines with a hyphen; joined here. The word "fame-conferring" has no counterpart in the Pratipadārtha or the Bhāvārtha; as printed.]*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśaka, at the midday pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin must recite the tṛca beginning शुष्मिन्तमं न ऊतये (*śuṣmintamaṃ na ūtaye*) (the Ṛks 8, 9 and 10 of this sūkta) as optional anurūpa mantras; this is explained by the sūtra शुष्मिंतमं न ऊतये श्रायंत इव सूर्यं (*śuṣmiṃtamaṃ na ūtaye śrāyaṃta iva sūryaṃ*) of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 7-4).

> निघातः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I claim as yours the sense-powers in the five peoples (Gandharvas, fathers, gods, Asuras, Rākṣasas), or in four peoples with the Niṣāda as fifth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O doer of many acts
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—related to you; पंचसु जनेषु (*paṃcasu janeṣu*)—among the five kinds of beings, beginning with the Gandharvas, as well
- या (*yā*)—of whatever kind
- इंद्रियाणि (*iṃdriyāṇi*)—powers of the senses there are
- तानि (*tāni*)—all those powers
- ते (*te*)—impelled by you, thus; आ वृणे (*ā vṛṇe*)—I understand

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, doer of many kinds of acts, whatever powers of the senses there are, even among the five kinds of beings, I understand that all those powers are impelled by you alone.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, object of many rites, I regard the organs of sense that exist in the five races (of beings dependent) on you, as yours.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may the abundant food offered by us reach you. Give us wealth that does not fall under the attack of enemies. We cause your strength to grow.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, come to us from near or from afar, and from your highest world, here to the sacrificial place to drink soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अर्वावतः (*arvāvataḥ*)—whether from a near place
- अथो (*atho*)—and
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—whether from a very distant place
- नः (*naḥ*)—towards us; आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be pleased to come
- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O (Indra) who holds the thunderbolt
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your; य उ लोकः (*ya u lokaḥ*)—whatever excellent world there is
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—from there also
- इह (*iha*)—to this place of sacrifice; आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be pleased to come

*[Printed oddity kept: the dash after ಶಕ್ರ, ಅಥೋ and ಅದ್ರಿವಃ is a hyphen; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O powerful Indra, be pleased to come towards us, whether from a near place or from a very distant place. O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt, from whatever excellent world of yours there is, from there also be pleased to come to this place of sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Come to us Sakra, whether from afar or nigh; whatever, Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, be your region, come from thence hither.

## Sūkta 38 (Maṇḍala 3)

**The thirty-eighth sūkta** (ಮೂವತ್ತೆಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभि तष्टवेति दशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । अभि तष्टेव दश
> प्रजापतिः स वैश्वामित्रो वाच्यो ना द्वौ ना तौ न वैकोऽपीति । विश्वामित्रगोत्रे

*[The page ends in the middle of the introduction of Sāyaṇa; the block breaks off after the word ವಿಶ್ವಾಮಿತ್ರಗೋತ್ರೇ and continues at the head of the next page, 857 (the next window). Printed oddity kept: the introduction speaks of the ninth sūkta of the anuvāka, as supplied.]*

### Printed p. 857

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रजापतिर्वाचः पुत्रः प्रजाप्रतिर्वा ऋषिः । तावुभावपि समुच्चितावस्य सूक्तस्य ऋषी
> इति द्वितीयः पक्षः । अथवा नोभावपि किंतु विश्वामित्र एवेति तृतीयः पक्षः । त्रिष्टुप्
> छंदः । इंद्रो देवता ॥
> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिने सवनेऽच्छावाकशस्त्रेऽभि तष्टेवेत्यहरहः शस्यनामकं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । उदु ब्रह्माण्यभि तष्टेवेतीतरावहरहःशस्यॆ । आ ७-४ ।
> इति ॥ एवं सर्वत्राहर्गणेषु द्वितीयादिष्टहःसु माध्यंदिने सवनेऽच्छावाकशस्त्र
> एतत्तूक्तं ॥

*[Continuation of the introduction block of Sūkta 38 (the first part stands at the end of the previous page). Gist: the seer is Prajāpati, son of Vāc, or Prajāpati alone, or both (second view); or neither but Viśvāmitra alone (third view); the metre is Triṣṭubh, the deity Indra; on the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the Acchāvāka recites this sūkta as a daily śastra, by the sūtra quoted (Ā. 7-4); the same holds for the other ahargaṇa sacrifices from the second day on. Line-end hyphens in the block are joined (logged). Printed oddities kept: the word ಶಸ್ಯೆ ends with the short vowel sign ೆ, which the conversion renders with the Devanagari short sign ॆ (the same in the Anuvāda quotation below), as supplied; the block writes the first word of the sūkta as ತಷ್ಟೇವ (in the sūtra ತಷ್ಟೇವ), where the Saṃhitā and the Anuvāda have ತಪ್ಪೇವ; as supplied.]*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, beginning with अभि तप्पेव (*abhi tappeva*), is the ninth sūkta in the third anuvāka. There are ten Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अभि तप्पेव दश प्रजापतिः स वैश्वामित्रो वाच्यो वा दौ वा तौ न वैकोऽपि (*abhi tappeva daśa prajāpatiḥ sa vaiśvāmitro vācyo vā dau vā tau na vaiko 'pi*). For this sūkta the seer is Prajāpati, the son of a seer named ವಚ *[the name of the father is printed in this form; as supplied]*, born in the lineage of Viśvāmitra; or Prajāpati alone is the seer; or it may be said that both are seers; or, apart from these two, Viśvāmitra alone is the seer *[the Kannada word for Viśvāmitra is printed ವಿಶ್ರಾ ಮಿತ್ರನೇ with a space inside the name; as supplied]*. In this matter there are three kinds of difference of opinion. Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. On the day of the sacrifice called Caturviṃśa, at the midday pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka must recite every day this sūkta, beginning अभितप्पेव (*abhitappeva*) *[printed as one word; as supplied]*, as the sampāta sūkta; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra उदु ब्रह्माण्यभि तप्पेवेतीतरावहरहः शस्यॆ (*udu brahmāṇyabhi tappevetītarāvaharahaḥ śasyè*) (Ā. 7-4). In the same way, in all the sacrifices called ahargaṇa, from the second day onwards, on every day at the midday pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka must recite this sūkta as the śastra mantra.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer says to the praiser: make the praise of Indra shine all round, as a carpenter works wood; I, like a swift, well-yoked horse, engaged in the rite and of good understanding, wish to see the poets, those who reached the state of gods through a sacrifice performed earlier. A passage of the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 6-20) is quoted for the same sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O praiser!) मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—the praise addressed to Indra
- तप्पेव (*tappeva*)—as a carpenter refines his wood and the like and does the work of carving; अभि दीधय (*abhi dīdhaya*)—make it brilliant
- सुधुर (*sudhura*)—which bears a good burden
- वाजी (*vājī*)—and is swift; अत्यो न (*atyo na*)—like a horse
- जिहानः (*jihānaḥ*)—performing the rites
- पराणि (*parāṇi*)—excellent

*[Printed oddity kept: the headword ಸುಧುರ ends with an ordinary colon instead of the visarga; as supplied. The Pratipadārtha breaks off at the foot of the page after the entry for the last word above; the next entry follows on the next page.]*

### Printed p. 859

and प्रियाणि (*priyāṇi*)—dear to Indra, rites; अभिमर्मृशत् (*abhimarmṛśat*)—performing with faith; सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—possessing excellent understanding, I; कवीन् (*kavīn*)—the poets who are of divine nature; संदृशे (*saṃdṛśe*)—to see; इच्छामि (*icchāmi*)—I wish.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, make the praise addressed to Indra brilliant, as a carpenter refines his wood and the like and does the work of carving. I, who perform rites like a horse that bears a good burden and is swift, who perform with faith the excellent rites that are dear to Indra, and who have excellent understanding, wish to see the poets who are of divine nature.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Pratipadārtha has ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠವಾದ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞೆ where the Bhāvārtha has ಬುದ್ಧಿ; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Repeat (to Indra) pious praise, as a carpenter (planes the wood), and engaging (zealously in sacred rites), as a quick horse bearing well his burden : endowed with intelligence, and reflecting upon the future acts acceptable (to Indra), I desire to behold the sages (who have gone to heaven)

*[The printed English has no full stop at the end; as supplied. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, ask the lords and teachers about the birth of the poets who did good deeds and reached the state of gods: by what deed they went to heaven and where they arose; those poets, of restrained minds and so doers of good deeds, fashioned heaven; and now, in this sacrifice, they (the sentence breaks off). ##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O Indra!)
कवीनां (*kavīnāṃ*)—of the seers who obtained the state of gods; जनिम (*janima*)—what the order of their origin is; इना (*inā*)—the teachers; पृच्छ (*pṛccha*)—ask; मनोधृतः (*manodhṛtaḥ*)—possessing minds endowed with restraint; सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)—doers of excellent deeds, those seers; द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the world of the gods; तक्षत (*takṣata*)—built; अध (*adha*)—in the present matter; धर्मणि (*dharmaṇi*)—at this time of the sacrifice; ते (*te*)—directed to you; प्रण्यः (*praṇyaḥ*)—which produce satisfaction; मनोवाताः (*manovātāḥ*)—which have the speed of mind; वर्धमानाः (*vardhamānāḥ*)—which are the cause of your increase; इमाः (*imāḥ*)—these praises of ours; नु (*nu*)—quickly; ग्मन् (*gman*)—come to you and reach you.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, ask the Lords, who are the cause of the creation of the world, what the order of origin of the seers who have obtained the state of gods is, and learn it. Those seers, who possess minds endowed with restraint and are doers of excellent deeds, built the world of the gods. May these praises of ours, directed to you at this time of the sacrifice, giving you satisfaction, having the speed of mind and being the cause of your increase, quickly come and reach you.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Bhāvārtha ends ಒಂದು ಸೇರಲಿ where the Pratipadārtha has ಬಂದು ಸೇರಲಿ ("come and reach"); I translate as in the Pratipadārtha sense; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ask of the lords (of earth, the holy teachers), the birth of those deified sages, who with well-governed minds, and diligent in sacred rites, fabricated the heavens : and may these propitiatory (praises), augmenting (your power) and rapid as the wind, reach you at this solemn rite.

*[The line-end hyphen in "fabri-cated" is joined. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*
