> समंजन् । ओषधीभिः पृथिवीं देवैश्च दिवं संगतामकार्षुः । किं च ते मात्राभिः ।
> मीयंते मांतीति ना मात्राः शिलोच्चयाः ताभिर्मात्राभिः सं ममिरे । ते रोदस्यावियत्तया परिच्छिन्ने चक्रुश्च । समृते परस्परं संगते उर्वि विस्तीर्णे मही महत्यौ ते द्यावापृथिव्यौ येमुः । नियमितवंतः । विष्टंभकेनांतरिक्षेणांतरुदयच्छन् । तथा धायसे तयोर्धारणार्थमंतरिक्षं धुः ' व्यधुः ॥ इदवधारणार्थे । गुह्या । गुहायां भवानि। भवार्थे यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तः । दधानाः। दधातेः
> शानचि रूपं । अभ्यस्तस्वरः । अंजन् । अन्नू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणगतिष्वित्यस्य लजा श्नसोरल्लोपः । निघातः । मात्राभिः । मा माने माज् माने ना । हुयामेत्यादिना त्रन्मत्तयः।
> नित्सर्वः । ममिरे । माज् मान इत्यस्य लिटि रूपं । चादिलोपे विभाषेति न निघातः ।
> येमुः । यम उपरम इत्यस्य लिट्युसि रूपं । तिजुत्तरत्वादनिघातः । धायसे ।
> वहिहाधाञ्छंदसीत्यसुन् । नित्सर्वः । धुः । दधातेर्लुजि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seers here on earth, doing hidden deeds everywhere, for strength or wealth joined heaven and earth with plants and with gods; they measured them with masses of rock, held them apart and set the atmosphere to support them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अत्र (*atra*)—in this world of the earth; गुह्या (*guhyā*)—deep deeds; सीमित् (*sīmit*)—in all regions; नि दधानाः (*ni dadhānāḥ*)—the poets who perform them; क्षत्राय (*kṣatrāya*)—for the increase of strength; रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth; समंजन् (*samaṃjan*)—they filled with plants and the like; मात्राभिः (*mātrābhiḥ*)—with materials such as mountains; सं मिमिरे (*saṃ mimire*)—they refined them; समृते (*samṛte*)—while they were joined together; उर्वी (*urvī*)—wide-spread; मही (*mahī*)—of great nature, heaven and earth; येमुः (*yemuḥ*)—they put under control; अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—between them; धायसे (*dhāyase*)—to hold them firmly; धुः (*dhuḥ*)—they created the atmosphere.

*[Printed oddities kept: the Pratipadārtha writes ವಿಸ್ಕೃತವಾದವೂ and ಮಹತ್ಸರೂಪವುಳ್ಳವೂ where the Bhāvārtha has ವಿಸ್ತ್ರತವಾದವೂ and ಮಹತ್ತ್ವರೂಪವುಳ್ಳವೂ; the Pratipadārtha headword is ಸಂ ಮಿಮಿರೇ, while the Pada and the bhāṣya have ಮಮಿರೇ; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The poets, who perform deep deeds in all regions of this world of the earth, filled heaven and earth with plants and the like for the increase of the strength of all beings; they refined them with materials such as mountains; while these were joined together they put under control heaven and earth, which are wide-spread and of great nature, and between them they created the atmosphere to hold them firmly.

*[The Bhāvārtha is cut in the middle of a word at the end of page 861 (after ಸಾಮಗ್ರಿಗ); the rest of the word stands at the head of the next page (ಳಿಂದ). In kn.md the fragment is moved below the new head and joined (logged); the English runs on.]*

> स्वरोचिः । स्वमेव रोचिर्यस्यासौ स्वरोचिः । स्वप्रभयैव दीप्यमान इत्यर्थः । आत

> नम्मते सर्वैर्नमस्क्रियत इति नामेंद्रस्य शरीरं कर्म वा । महदाश्चर्योपेतं
> वर्तते। तथा विश्वरूपो नानाविधरूपतां भजमानः स इंद्रो वरुणात्मनामृतानि जलान्या तस्थौ । आधितिष्ठति॥ विश्वे । जसः शी। अभूषन् ! भूष अलंकार इत्यस्य लजि रूपं ।

> णमु प्रह्वत्व इत्यस्मान्ना मन्मीमन्नित्यादिना मनिस्प्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातनादाद्युदात्तः ।
> विश्वरूप इति तस्य संज्ञा । बहुप्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All the poets adorned Indra who mounted the chariot; self-radiant, he moves everywhere clothed in splendours; great is that name of the bull-like Asura; of many forms, he stands over the waters as Varuṇa.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the bull, ancient and greater than all, created the waters; they are such as to allay thirst; Indra and Varuṇa, grandsons of heaven, hold wealth for us through the praises of the sacrificer. The bhāṣya is cut at the page break (pages 863 and 864) after the word for "thirst"; the sentence goes on at the head of the next page.

- पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*)—the ancient
- ज्यायान् (*jyāyān*)—the elder, Indra
- असूत (*asūta*)—(the waters) created
- पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—abundant
- इमाः (*imāḥ*)—these waters
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra

- संति (*saṃti*)—are; दिवः नपाता (*divaḥ napātā*)—the Indra and Varuṇa who sustain the world of the gods
- प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*)—brightly shining

- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—(rejoiced) by the praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the showerer of desires, the ancient and the elder, created the waters. These abundant waters allay the thirst of Indra. Indra and Varuṇa, the ನಪ್ತೃಗಳಾದ (grandsons, as supplied) of the world of the gods, delighted by the praises of the sacrificer who shines brightly, hold wealth to give it to us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The showerer (of benefits), the preceder and elder (of the gods), generated (the waters): they are the abundant allayers of his thirst : sovereign Indra and Varuna, grandsons of heaven, you possess the wealth (that is to be acquired) by the rites of the splendid sacrifice.

> सोमादिभिः पूर्णानि त्रीणि सदांसि सवनानि परि भूषथः । सर्वतोऽलंकुरुथः । हे
> इंद्र त्वं जगन्वान् । यज्ञं प्रति गतवानसि । अपि संभावनायां । यतोऽहमत्र व्रते
> यज्ञे वायुकेशान् वायुवच्चलनरश्मीन् गंधर्वान् सोमरक्षकान् स्नानभ्राजादीन् मनसापश्यं । ते च स्नानभ्राजादयस्त्युत्तिरीयके स्पष्टमभिहिताः । स्नान भ्राजांघारे बंभारे हस्त सुहस्त कृशानवेते वः सोमक्रयणास्तान्रक्षध्वं मा वो
> दभन् । स. १-२-७ । इति ॥ भूषथः । भूष अलंकार इत्यस्य लट रूपं । अपश्यं । दृशिर्
> प्रेक्षण इत्यस्य लजि रूपं । सादादित्वादनिघातः । जगन्वान् । गमेः क्वसौ विभाषा गमहनविदविशामितीटो विकल्पितत्वादत्रेडभावः । मो नो धातोर्मोश्चति मकारस्य
> नकारः । प्रत्ययस्वरः गंधर्वान् । धृञ् धारण इत्यस्य गोशब्द उपपदे गवि गन्
> धृञ्वो न इति वप्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेन गोशब्दस्य गनादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O royal Indra and Varuṇa, at this sacrifice you adorn the three pressings, full of Soma and other offerings; Indra, you have come, and I have seen in mind the Gandharvas, guardians of Soma, with hair of rays like the wind. The bhāṣya names these Gandharvas and cites a passage with the printed reference ಸ. ೧-೨-೭, transliterated Sa. 1-2-7 (the quotation stands in the block).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजाना (*rājānā*)—O lords, Indra and Varuṇa
- विदथे (*vidathe*)—in this sacrifice
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—all the sacrificial materials; त्रीणि सदांसि (*trīṇi sadāṃsi*)—also in the three pressings; परि भूषथः (*pari bhūṣathaḥ*)—you provide and adorn (O Indra)
- जगन्वान् (*jaganvān*)—you have come to the place of sacrifice
- आपि (*āpi*)—and; अत्र व्रते (*atra vrate*)—in this sacrifice
- वायुकेशान् (*vāyukeśān*)—having hair in the form of rays trembling like the wind
- गंधर्वान् (*gaṃdharvān*)—the Gandharvas, protectors of Soma
- मनसा (*manasā*)—in the form of meditation
- अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*)—I have seen face to face (have looked at)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O lords, Indra and Varuṇa, at all the three times of the pressings you provide all the materials needed for this sacrifice. O Indra, you have come to the place of sacrifice. And in this sacrifice I have seen, in meditation, the Gandharvas, protectors of Soma, whose hair, in the form of rays, trembles like the wind.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Royal Indra and Varuna, embellish the three universal sacrifices (and make them) full (of all requisites) for this celebration : you have gone

to the rite, for I have beheld in my mind, at this solemnity, the Gandharvas with hair (waving) in the wind.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गंधर्वान् (*gaṃdharvān*)—Who the Gandharvas, the guardians of Soma, are is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda—

स्नान भ्राजांघारे बंभारे हस्त सुहस्त कृशानवेते वः सोमक्रयणास्तान्नक्षध्वं मावो दभन् ॥ (*snāna bhrājāṃghāre baṃbhāre hasta suhasta kṛśānavete vaḥ somakrayaṇāstānnakṣadhvaṃ māvo dabhan ‖*)

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-7-1). Formerly Soma was in heaven. The Gāyatrī metre took the form of a falcon and brought it to the earth. While it was in heaven, some Gandharvas had been appointed to guard it. The names of those Gandharvas are स्वास (*svāsa*), भ्राज (*bhrāja*), अंघारि (*aṃghāri*), बंभारि (*baṃbhāri*) हस्त (*hasta*), सुहस्त (*suhasta*), कृशानु (*kṛśānu*). It is they who are indicated in this ṛk.

*[Printed oddities kept: in the Special Topics the first of the seven names is printed ಸ್ವಾಸ where the quotation has ಸ್ನಾನ; there is no comma between the names ಬಂಭಾರಿ and ಹಸ್ತ; the word ಕೆಲವ stands for "some" (as supplied); the line-end hyphen in the quotation is joined (logged).]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificers milk the named cow for Indra; reaching godhood they put on new Asura strength and fix their own forms in him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (The poets who perform the sacrifice) वृषभस्य (*vṛṣabhasya*)—of the giver of desired objects
- अस्य (*asya*)—for this Indra
- धेनोः (*dhenoḥ*) गोः (*goḥ*)—the milch cows
- नामभिः (*nāmabhiḥ*)—designating them by many kinds of names
- सक्म्यं (*sakmyaṃ*)—the milk fit for the oblation
- नु (*nu*)—quickly; आ ममिरे (*ā mamire*)—they milk. (The same poets) अन्यदन्यत् (*anyadanyat*)—new and ever new
- असुरं (*asuraṃ*)—special strength
- वसानाः (*vasānāḥ*)—as having put on
- मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*)—as wise
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in this Indra
- रूपं (*rūpaṃ*)—their own forms; नि ममिरे (*ni mamire*)—united

*[Printed oddity kept: the Pratipadārtha has ಅಸುರಂ where the Saṃhitā and the Pada have the word for "of the Asuras" ending in a different way; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The poets who perform the sacrifice, designating the cows by many kinds of names, milk for Indra, the giver of desired objects, the milk fit for the oblation. The same poets, having put on ever new special strength and being wise, merged their own forms in this Indra.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Those who, for (the sake of) the showerer (of benefits), milk the agreeable (produce) of the milch cow, (who is known) by (many) names, they invested with the diversified strength (of the Asuras) and practising delusive art, have deposited their own nature in him.

*[The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

No one marks off my golden lustre from Indra's; one who takes refuge in it, praised, embraces heaven and earth like a woman her children.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तत् इन्नु (*tat innu*)—from that great cause itself
- सवितुः (*savituḥ*)—of the lustre of Indra, the impeller of the world
- मे (*me*)—my
- हिरण्ययीं (*hiraṇyayīṃ*)—golden
- अमतिं (*amatiṃ*)—for the lustre; न किः (*na kiḥ*)—no one can find a difference
- यां (*yāṃ*)—this lustre which
- अशिश्रेत् (*aśiśret*)—the man who has taken refuge
- सुष्टुती (*suṣṭutī*)—praised by excellent praises
- योषा (*yoṣā*)—as a mother; जनिमानि अपीव (*janimāni apīva*)—cherishes and embraces her children
- विश्वमिन्ने (*viśvaminne*)—gratifying the whole world
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth; आ वव्रे (*ā vavre*)—pervades

*[Printed oddities kept: the Pratipadārtha has ಜಗತ್ಪೇರಕನಾದ, the Bhāvārtha has ಆಪ್ಪಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವಂತೆ; the Pratipadārtha has ಅಶಿಶ್ರೇತ್ followed by the man who has taken refuge, and "pervades" for the verb; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

No one can find a difference between the lustre of Indra, the impeller of the world, and my golden lustre. The man who has taken refuge in this lustre, praised with excellent praises, pervades heaven and earth, which gratify the whole world, as a mother cherishes and embraces her children.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
No one (distinguishes) my golden lustre from that of this Savitri, in which (lustre) he has taken refuge : gratified by pious praise, he cherishes the all-fostering heaven and earth as a woman cherishes her offspring.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वराज्यलक्षणं । किंच युवां नोऽस्मान्परि परितः स्यातं । रक्षकौ भवेतं । विश्वे सर्वॆ
> मायिनो देवा गोपाजिह्वस्य । गोप्री जिह्वा मा बिभीतेत्येतादृशी वाग्यस्य स
> तथोक्तः । तस्थुषः स्थिरतरस्येंद्रस्य विरूपा नानाविधानि वृत्रहननादीनि कृतानि कर्माणि
> पश्यंति । एवमिंद्रस्य विश्वरूपत्वमुक्तं ॥ युवं । युष्मच्छब्दस्य द्विवचने युवावौ
> द्विवचन इति युवादेशः । जेप्रथमयोरमिति सुपोऽमादेशः । साधथः । साध संसिद्धावित्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लटि रूपं । बहुलमन्यत्रापीति णेर्लुक् । निघातः । दैवी ।
> देवाद्यञञावित्यञ् प्रत्ययः। इत्यस्वरः । स्यातं । अस्तेर्लिज रूपं। गोपाजिह्वस्य ।
> गुपू रक्षण इत्यस्यायप्रत्ययांतस्य क्विप्यतोलोपयलोपयोः कृतयो रूपं
> गोपा इति । बहुव्रीह पूर्वपदस्वरः । तस्थुषः । ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तावित्यस्य क्वसौ वस्सेकाजाद्भसामिति प्राप्तस्यॆटः संप्रसारणं । संप्रसारणाश्रयं च बलीय इति संप्रसारणस्य बलीयस्त्वान्निवृत्तिः। वसोः संप्रसारणं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । पश्यंति । दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे
> निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra and Varuṇa accomplish for the worshipper great divine welfare in the form of self-rule and are to guard us on all sides; all the gods see the many deeds, such as the slaying of Vṛtra, of the firm Indra whose speech is protective.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रत्यस्य (*pratyasya*)—to the worshipper
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great; यद्दैवी स्वस्ति (*yaddaivī svasti*)—that welfare which is divine and has the form of self-rule
- साधयः (*sādhayaḥ*)—you accomplish (and)
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- परि (*pari*)—surrounding
- स्यातं (*syātaṃ*)—be protectors
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*)—the gods also
- गोपजिह्वस्य (*gopajihvasya*)—of him whose speech gives a protecting assurance
- तस्थुषः (*tasthuṣaḥ*)—and who is firm in his state, of Indra
- विरूपा (*virūpā*)—of many kinds
- कृतानि (*kṛtāni*)—the deeds
- पश्यंति (*paśyaṃti*)—they see

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two also accomplish for the worshipper that great welfare which is divine and has the form of self-rule. And surrounding us, be our protectors. All the gods also see the manifold deeds of Indra, whose speech gives a protecting assurance and who is firm in his state.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಸುತ್ತುವರೆದು where the Pratipadārtha has ಸುತ್ತುವರಿದು for "surrounding"; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You two secure the great felicity of the ancient (worshipper), that which is happiness in heaven : do you (therefore) be ever about us : all those who exercise illusion, contemplate the manifold exploits of the everlasting and blandly-speaking Indra.

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः ।
> अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन्संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृष्ठं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं मघवानं धनवंतं अत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संजितं समग्नेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य
> निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । ह्वयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते शपो लुकि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, lord of wealth, is invoked in this battle, fierce to foes, a hearer of our praise and conqueror of the enemies' wealth, for our protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजसातौ (*vājasātau*)—taking place for the sake of food; अस्मिन् भरे (*asmin bhare*)—in this battle
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—full of zeal
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—rich
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the lord
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—the guide
- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—who hears our praise
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—terrible to enemies
- समत्सु (*samatsu*)—in battles
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—enemies
- घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)—who destroys
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—the wealth of enemies
- संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*)—who conquers completely; (such) Indra, ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call

*[Printed oddity kept: the Pratipadārtha has the form ವಾಜಸಾತೌ where the Saṃhitā and the Pada have ವಾಜಸಾತ್; the word ಉತ್ಸಾ / ಹಭರಿತನೂ is cut by the line end; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in this battle which takes place for the sake of winning food, you show your strength and are a helper; you are rich, the lord of all wealth, the best guide of the world, one who listens to our praise, terrible to enemies, one who injures enemies in battles and wholly conquers the enemies' wealth. We call you, such a one, for protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

## Sūkta 39 (Maṇḍala 3)

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रं॑ म॒तिर्हृ॒द आ व॒च्यमा॒नाच्छा॒ पतिं॒ स्तोम॑तष्टा जिगाति ।  
> या जागृ॑विर्वि॒दथे॑ श॒स्यमा॒नेंद्र॒ यत्ते॒ चाय॑ते वि॒द्दि तस्य॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रं । मतिः । हृदः । आ । वच्यमाना । अच्छ । पतिं । स्तोमतष्टा । जिगाति ।  
> या । जागृविः । विदथे । शस्यमाना । इंद्र । यत् । ते । जायते । वृद्धि । तस्य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वामित्रः स्तौति । हे इंद्र हृदो हृदयाद्वच्यमानोच्यमाना स्तोमतष्टा
> स्तोमकारिभिः कृता मतिः स्तुतिः पतिं सर्वस्य जगतः स्वामिनं त्वामच्छाभिलक्ष्या जिगाति ।
> समंताद्दच्छतु । या मदीया स्तुतिर्जागृविः स्तुत्यस्य तव जागरणं कुर्वाणा विदथे
> यज्ञे शस्यमाना भवति । हे इंद्र ते त्वदर्थं यत्सोत्रं मत्तो जायते तद्विद्दि ।
> जानीहि । तस्यॆति द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठि ॥ मतिः । मंत्रे वृषेत्यादिना क्किन्नुदात्तः । हृदः । हृदयशब्दस्य पद्मन्नोमासित्यादिना हृदादेशः । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ।
> वच्यमाना । वच परिभाषण इत्यस्य कर्मणि यक् । संप्रसारणाभावश्चांदसः । प्रत्यय
> स्वरः । स्तोमतष्टा । तक्षू त्वक्कू तनूकरण इत्यस्य कर्मणि निष्ठा । तृतीया कर्मणीति
> पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । जिगाति । गा स्तुतौ छंदसीति जुहोत्यादिः । बहुलं छंदसीत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । निघातः । जायते । जनी प्रादुर्भाव इत्यस्य लट रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । विद्धि । विद ज्ञान इत्यस्य लोट हेर्हुझल्फॊ हेर्धिरिति ध्यादेशः।
> वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvāmitra praises: may the praise made from the heart by the praisers go to Indra, lord of the whole world, and awaken him at the sacrifice; let him know the praise made by me for him.

- वच्यमाना (*vacyamānā*)—that which is recited

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may the praise that is recited wholeheartedly, that is composed by the praisers, and that is recited in the sacrificial house so as to awaken you, come and reach you, the lord of the whole world. Know the praise that I have composed for your satisfaction.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಯಜ್ಞ ಗೃಹದಲ್ಲಿ ("in the sacrificial house", the word cut by the line end) where the Pratipadārtha has ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The praise that is prompted by the heart, and is uttered by the reciters of sacred hymns, proceeds to the presence of the lord, and is his awakener when repeated at the sacrifice: be cognizant Indra, of this praise, which is born for you.

*[Line-end hyphens inside words of the printed English are joined. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The praise, born at dawn before the shining sun, awakens Indra at the sacrifice; auspicious and clothed in white splendour, it is our ancient hymn inherited from the fathers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) दिवश्चित् (*divaścit*)—than the shining sun
- पूर्वा (*pūrvā*)—being earlier, at dawn; आ जायमाना (*ā jāyamānā*)—that which is created
- अस्मे (*asme*)—our
- पित्रा (*pitrā*)—related to the fathers
- सनजा (*sanajā*)—ancient; सेयं धी: (*seyaṃ dhī:*)—this praise
- विदथे (*vidathe*)—in the sacrifice
- शस्यमाना (*śasyamānā*)—being recited
- जागृवि: (*jāgṛvi:*)—awakening you (and)
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—auspicious
- अर्जुना (*arjunā*)—white-coloured
- वस्त्राणि (*vastrāṇi*)—the garment in the form of splendour
- वसाना (*vasānā*)—wearing (it is so)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, this praise, which is created at dawn, earlier than the shining sun, which is related to our fathers and is ancient, is recited in the sacrifice and awakens you; and it is auspicious and wears a garment of white splendour.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
That praise which is begotten before (the dawn) of day is the awakener of Indra, when repeated at the (morning) sacrifice : auspicious and clothed in white raiment is this our ancient and paternal hymn.

*[Line-end hyphens inside words of the printed English are joined. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

> प्रसंगादुषःकालं प्रशंसति । यमसूः । यमौ यमल् सूत इति यमसूरुषोऽभिमानिनी देवता । सा यमा यमलावश्विनावत्रोषःकालेऽसूत । अश्विनोस्तत्र शस्यमानत्वात्तावश्विन् स्तोतुं मम जिह्वाया अग्रं पतच्चंचलमास्थाद्धि ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Dawn bore the Aśvins at daybreak; my tongue trembles to praise them; the two dispellers of darkness meet at day's root, joining the dawn rites.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यमसू: (*yamasū:*)—the dawn goddess who bore sons that are a pair
- यमा (*yamā*)—the twin Aśvin deities
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this dawn-time
- असूत (*asūta*)—bore (in order to praise these very Aśvin deities)
- जिह्वायाः (*jihvāyāḥ*)—of my tongue
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—the tip
- पतत् (*patat*)—quivering (eagerly); आ अस्थात् हि (*ā asthāt hi*)—stands ready, waiting
- तमोहना (*tamohanā*)—these two, destroyers of darkness
- तपुषः (*tapuṣaḥ*)—of the day
- बुद्धे (*buddhe*)—at the root part of the day, in the dawn-time itself
- एता (*etā*)—coming
- मिथुना (*mithunā*)—joining together
- जाता (*jātā*)—created
- वपूंषि (*vapūṃṣi*)—with the rites
- सचेते (*sacete*)—become united

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The dawn goddess, who bore sons that are a pair, bore the twin Aśvin deities at this dawn-time. The tip of my tongue waits quivering to praise these very Aśvin deities. These destroyers of darkness come at the dawn-time itself, the root part of the day, join together, and unite with the rites created there.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The parent of twins (the dawn), has brought forth the twin (Aswins) on this occasion, (in the praise of whom) the tip of my tongue remains tremulous : they two, the dispersers of darkness, combine, assuming bodies as a pair (of twins) at the origin of the day.

*[The printed English has the Aśvins as "( Aswins )" with spaces inside the bracket; as supplied. The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र सत्रे प्रवृत्तानामस्माकं ये पितरोऽंगिरसो गोषु पणिभिरपहृतेषु तन्निमित्तं योधा योद्धारो वर्तंते तेषामेषां मर्त्येषु निंदिता
> दूषको नकिर्न कश्चिदस्ति । कुत इत्यत आह । माहिनावान्महिमोपेतो दंसनावान्वृत्रहननादिकर्मवानिंद्र एषामंगिरसां दृंहितानि समृद्धानि गोत्राणि गवां वृंदान्यत्सृजे। तेभ्योऽंगिरोभ्यो ददौ॥ निंदिता। निदि कुत्सायामित्यस्य तृचि रूपं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Our fathers the Aṅgirases fought for the cows seized by the Paṇis; no mortal reviles them; glorious Indra gave them the herds of cows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—to us
- ये (*ye*)—who
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—forefathers (fathers and grandfathers)
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—on account of the cows (carried off by the Paṇis)
- योधाः (*yodhāḥ*)—are fighters
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of such Aṅgirases
- निंदिताः (*niṃditāḥ*)—revilers
- मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*)—among the assembly of men; न किः (*na kiḥ*)—there is none
- माहिनावान् (*māhināvān*)—endowed with greatness
- दंसनावान् (*daṃsanāvān*)—endowed with works (and)
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—to these Aṅgirases
- दृंहिता (*dṛṃhitā*)—abundant
- गोत्राणि (*gotrāṇi*)—herds of cows; उत् सस्यजॆ (*ut sasyajè*)—releases (frees and gives)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is used at the Daśapeya, in the Niṣkevalya, before the Nivid-dhānīya; Indra, with the friends the Aṅgirases who sacrificed nine months and the ten who sacrificed ten months, found the true sun dwelling in the darkness of the cave.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सखिभिः (*sakhibhiḥ*)—friends
- सत्वभिः (*satvabhiḥ*)—(Indra's) companions gathered around him
- नवगैः (*navagaiḥ*)—with the Aṅgirases who performed the nine-month sacrifice and obtained its fruit
- सखा (*sakhā*)—joined
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which cave
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—going towards the cows
- अभिज्जु (*abhijju*)—making them walk bent over on their legs
- अनुग्मन् (*anugman*)—following them
- तत् (*tat*)—in that same cave; दशभिः दशगैः (*daśabhiḥ daśagaiḥ*)—together with the ten Aṅgirases who performed the ten-month sacrifice
- तमसि (*tamasi*)—in the darkness
- क्षियंतं (*kṣiyaṃtaṃ*)—dwelling
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—of the nature of true light
- सूर‍्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- विवेद (*viveda*)—obtained

*[Printed oddities kept: the entry for the nine-month sacrificers is spelled ನವಗೈಃ where the Pada has ನವಗ್ವೈಃ; the entry for the sun is written with a joiner sign (ಸೂರ‍್ಯಂ); the last entry has a hyphen in place of the dash; two words of the prose are cut by the line end without a hyphen and read whole; as supplied.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra joined the friends, those gathered around him, the Aṅgirases who performed the nine-month sacrifice and obtained its fruit; in whichever cave he went towards the cows, made them walk bent over on their legs and followed them, in that same cave, together with the ten Aṅgirases who performed the ten-month sacrifice and obtained its fruit, he obtained the sun, of the nature of true light, dwelling in the darkness.

*[Printed oddity kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಸೂರನನ್ನು ("the sun", the last syllable of the word missing) where the Pratipadārtha has the full word; as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
A friend, accompanied by the faithful friends who had celebrated the nine months' rite, and tracking the cows upon their knees, and in like manner accompanied by those ten who had accomplished the ten months' rite, Indra made manifest the true (light of the sun dwelling in (the) darkness (of the cave).

The Special Topics are not printed for this Ṛk.]*

> पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घः । नित्स्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra knew the milk gathered in the cow and found the footed and hoofed cattle; the capable Indra seized in his right hand the hidden asura moving unseen in the sky; the cattle are those seized by the asuras named Paṇi.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- उस्रियायां (*usriyāyāṃ*)—in the cow that supplies the means of enjoyment
- संभृतं (*saṃbhṛtaṃ*)—gathered
- मधु (*madhu*)—the sweet substance, milk and the like
- विवेद (*viveda*)—came to know
- पद्वत् (*padvat*)—that which has feet
- शफवत् (*śaphavat*)—and that which has hoofs: the wealth of cattle, he obtained
- गोः (*goḥ*)—those very cows
- नमे (*name*)—he brought
- दक्षिणावान् (*dakṣiṇāvān*)—the capable Indra
- गुह्या (*guhyā*)—in the cave; गुह्यं हितु (*guhyaṃ hitu*)—the one hidden
- अप्पु (*appu*)—in the sky
- गूह्नं (*gūhnaṃ*)—the one moving secretly, the asura; दक्षिणे हस्ते (*dakṣiṇe haste*)—in the right hand
- दधे (*dadhe*)—held

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra came to know the sweet substance, milk and the like, gathered in the cow that supplies milk and the other means of enjoyment. He obtained the wealth of cattle, that which has feet and that which has hoofs.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ज्योति॑र्वृणीत॒ तम॑सो विजा॒नन्ना॒रे स्या॑म दुरि॒ताद॒भीके॑ ।  
> इ॒मा गिरः॑ सोमपाः सोमवृद्ध जु॒षस्वें॑द्र पुरु॒तम॑स्य का॒रोः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ज्योतिः । वृणीत । तमसः । विजानन् । आरे । स्याम । दुःइतात् । अभीके ।  
> इमाः । गिरः । सोमपाः । सोमवृद्ध । जुषस्व । इंद्र । पुरुतमस्य । कारोः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तमसो रात्रेः सकाशाद्विजानन्विशेषेण जानन् प्रादुर्भवन्सूर्यात्मक इंद्रो
> ज्योतिर्वृणीत । जगद्व्यवहारनिर्वाहकं प्रकाशं समभक्त । यद्वा तमसस्तमोरूपाद्वत्रादेर्विजानन् प्रादुर्भवन् । वृत्रं हत्वा प्रकाशमवृणीत । वयं दुरितात्पापादारे दूरे पापवर्जिताः संतोऽभीके भयरहिते स्थाने स्याम । भवेम । सोमपाः सोमस्य पातरत एव सोमवृद्ध सोमपानेषु वृद्ध हे इंद्र पुरुतमस्य ।
> पुरून्वहूञ्यत्रून् तामयति ग्लापयतीति पुरुतमः । तादृतस्य कारोः स्तोत्रं
> कुर्वाणस्य ऋत्विज इमा: स्तुतिलक्षणा गिरो वाचो जुषस्व । सेवस्व ॥ वृणीत । वृच
> संभक्तानित्यस्य लजि रूपं । विजानन् । ज्ञा अवबोधने । विशेषेण ज्ञानं प्रकाशः ।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । अभीके । न विद्यते भीर्यस्मिन् । ततः शेषाद्विभाषा । पा. ५-४-१५४ । इति
> कप्पत्ययः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्यंतोदात्तत्वे प्राप्रे कपि पूर्वं । पा. ६-२-१७३ । इति
> पूर्वस्यांतोदात्तत्वं । पुरुतमस्य । तमु ग्लान इत्यस्माण्यंतात्पचाद्यचि परादितृंदसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra as the sun, knowing the darkness, chose the light; may we be far from sin and without fear; Indra, drinker of Soma, accept the praises of the priest.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sun is asked to light heaven and earth for the rite; may we be far from sin; Vasus, give abundant, prosperous wealth to the generous mortal.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ज्योति: (*jyoti:*)—the sun, illuminator of the world
- यज्ञाय (*yajñāya*)—for the help of the sacrificial rites
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth; अनु ष्मात् (*anu ṣmāt*)—may he make shine (we also)
- भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)—abundant
- दुरितस्य (*duritasya*)—to sin
- आरे (*āre*)—being distant
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—O Indra and the others
- सुपारासः (*supārāsaḥ*)—you who bring to the far end of happiness; भूरि चित् (*bhūri cit*)—exceedingly abundant
- बर्हणावत् (*barhaṇāvat*)—wealth accompanied by prosperity
- तुजतः (*tujataḥ*)—to him who offers oblation to you generously
- मर्त्यस्य (*martyasya*)—to the man (give)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the sun, illuminator of the world, make heaven and earth shine for the help of the sacrificial rites. May we also be far from abundant sin. O Indra and the others, you who make happiness, give the exceedingly abundant wealth accompanied by prosperity to the man who offers oblation to you generously.

*[Printed oddities kept: the Bhāvārtha has ಸುಖಿಕಾರಿಗಳಾದ ("makers of happiness") where the Pratipadārtha has an entry meaning "who bring to the far end of happiness"; the word for the sun is spelled with a joiner sign (ಸೂರ‍್ಯನು); as supplied.]*

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May light be spred [sic] throughout heaven and earth for (the promotion of the) sacrifice; may we be far removed from exceeding ill; Vasus, who are to be rendered present (by pious praise), bestow increasing affluence upon the man who is liberal of gifts.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः ।
> अस्मिन्भरे, जिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन्संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृथं यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं मघवानं धनवंतं अत एनेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोतिशयेन नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संचितं समग्नेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्व गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य
> निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट प्रतिषेधः यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । हैयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते शपो लुकि
> कृते च लिजा रूपं । निघातः । भरे । भ्रञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः ।
> वाजसात् । कणु दाने । भावे क्तिन् जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं । बहुव्रीहौ
> पूर्वपदस्वरः । समत्तु । आद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति योद्धणामायुंषीति समदः संग्रामाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घंतं । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेरिति घत्वं । संजितं । जि जये ।
> क्विप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, wealthy and the best of guides, who hears our praise and destroys the enemies in battles, is called to this battle for protection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—proceeding for the sake of food; अस्मिन् भरे (*asmin bhare*)—in this battle
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—full of zeal
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—wealthy
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the lord
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—guide
- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—who listens to our praise
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—terrible to enemies
- समत्तु (*samattu*)—in battles
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—enemies
- घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)—who destroys
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—the enemies' riches
- संजितं (*saṃjitaṃ*)—who wholly conquers (that is, Indra, so described)
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call

*[Words of this paragraph are cut by the line end and read whole; as supplied. The gloss of the entry समत्तु (*samattu*) reads "in battles" and the entry वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*) is glossed "enemies", as printed.]*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in this battle, which proceeds for the gain of food, you who show strength and are a helper, who are wealthy, lord of all riches, and the most excellent guide of the world (the word for guide is cut at the end of this page: ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶ, completed by ಕನೂ on the next page)

### Printed p. 884

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

who listen attentively to our praise, are terrible to enemies, strike the enemies in battles, and wholly conquer the enemies' wealth: you we call for protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk is recited again and again as the last Ṛk in Sūktas 30, 31, 32, 34, 35, 36, 38, 39, 43, 48, 49 and 50 of this Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda, and in Sūktas 89 and 104 of the 10th Maṇḍala. And it is also recited in these places: Sāmaveda. 329; Atharvaveda. 20-11-11; Tai. Brā. 2-4-4-3.

*[The list of Sūktas stands in the supplied text as a running sentence; the references are given as printed. No separate closing formula of Sūkta 39 is printed; the lines that follow are the closing formula of the adhyāya.]*

**Adhyāya colophon (Sanskrit; Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 2):**

> वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् ।
> पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥
> इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपाल
> साम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये
> वेदार्थप्रकाशे यक्संहिताभाष्ये तृतीयाष्टके
> द्वितीयोऽध्यायः समाप्तः
> ॥ ओं तत्त्वत् ॥

> *vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan |*
> *pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*
> *iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpāla*
> *sāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye*
> *vedārthaprakāśe yaksaṃhitābhāṣye tṛtīyāṣṭake*
> *dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ*
> *‖ oṃ tattvat ‖*

Closing line (Kannada): "Here ends the second adhyāya, in the third aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with Sāyaṇa's commentary and a Kannada translation." The Sanskrit verses give: dispelling the darkness of the heart by the light of the meaning of the Veda, may Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara grant the four human aims; and the colophon names Sāyaṇācārya, bearer of the burden of the empire of Vīra-Bukka, as author of the Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa, whose second adhyāya in the third aṣṭaka is ended. *[Printed oddities kept: the word before the compound for "commentary on the Saṃhitā" is printed यक्संहिताभाष्ये (*yaksaṃhitābhāṣye*) in its compound, where the colophon at the end of the first adhyāya has a different first word; the last formula is printed in the form shown; as supplied.]*

Then a verse of forgiveness (Sanskrit), with two closing formulas:

> यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् ।
> तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोस्तु ते ॥
> ॥ शुभं भूयात् ॥
> ॥ मंगळं ॥
